_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to leave a review for real people who love pirates who are curious about this game. This will be longish as there's a lot of thoughts and misconceptions to debunk on this game. I will just say in summary now, this game is awesome, and getting better by the season and most of its hate is unwarranted and frankly, weird. I'm not sure why this game has garnered the weirdo incel crybaby crowd that stalks it insulting it continuously but the game is actually really really good. Keep reading for deeper thoughts.1. This is not an assassins creed game. Your captain is not your main character, sure you can dress him up, but you won't be swashbuckling with a sword and pistol against other captains. It was also never advertised to be that - Most of this games hate has to do with it not being AC: Black Flag 2, when this was always designed as a new IP with nothing to do with AC. And yes, you are thinking, "well why are people mad its not Black Flag 2 then?" I do not know either, people are seriously dumb so I just attribute that as the answer.2.  This game is not a "crew" game like Sea of Thieves, you need no help controlling the biggest ships available currently and being fully combat ready, but you can group with up to 2 other captains for scaling difficulty and loot and run as a group of captains, and its encouraged to mix your builds and strengths and weaknesses to compliment each other in this way. 3. The game is not overly difficult for Solo players, you can progress through the entire thing without help after you learn the ropes and mechanics and if you have the skill. Some of the harder bosses are easier of course with other players, but that's easy to accomplish as well as you can ask for help and I've never seen someone not show up. 1. This is an MMO-Lite game, with light class based design and RPG elements. And this is probably the definitive ship combat pirate game. Your ship is 100% your main character, its what you level up by acquiring better gear, its what has a base class built into it and determines your base play style (Healer/Tank/DPS with different perks per ship) You can truly tailor a ship to play how you feel engaging, it be viable and feel rewarding. And be fully customizable down to the type of wheel you use on top of that.2. This game has very satisfying end game loop of boss grinding for drops and cosmetics mixed with opt in PvP elements and a fully fleshed out Empire building mechanic with ranks and leader board's you can climb with resource generation and management. This gets reset seasonally so the grind to be the top or in the top ranks can start anew. I honestly love this game, I didn't know if I would and I didn't play it at launch thanks to the review bombing, but Ubisoft Connect had a 6 hour free trial, I purchased it within 2 hours of that trial. The hate and vitriol that follows this game and its dev's has to be AI bots or neck-beards it's truly wild to see people stalk it on X or Reddit just to spew hate, most of which have never even played it. Play it or don't but hope to see you all on the high sea's matey!

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so... If you know what you're getting into here, you'll probably have a fun enough time with it.First, this is no "AAAA" game. The map isn't as big as you'd probably expect, and the overall scope of the game seems rather narrow for such a title. Really... it kinda feels like a decently funded indie game... But it's no No Man's Sky either.The game is worth at best 30 bucks. If it's not on sale, or generally priced down to that point, I'd tell you to hold back, unless you're SUPER into this sort of game.The whole game, is pirating naval combat. That's like, 99% of what you're going to be doing. Ever played Black Flag? That funny Assassin's Creed game? This game is built on the entire idea of that game's ship combat. But that's really it. It's just ship combat, and occasionally walking around some beach looking for buried treasure. You sail around, fight ships from multiple factions, maybe even a sea monster or three, and loot their crap to make more and better crap for yourself, and turn in contracts. This game, is going to feel a bit grindy, and it will feel unfair if you don't have the better stuff crafted to increase the level of your ship. That's how this game works. You can't just go in and sink an enemy ship multiple levels higher than you, aka, better equipped.There is hunting in the game that's a bit unique from the rest of the stuff, where you get in your little hunting boat and throw spears at animals until they die. You COULD just blast them with cannons on a bigger ship, but then you'd ruin whatever they drop pretty much.The game is no Sea of Thieves or anything like that, BUT, there is mechanics in the game for a holy trinity role based system. You have ships that act as tanks, with weapons that can provoke and keep the attention of enemy ships, DPS specializing ships, and even healer type ships, that you can equp with weapons that can be shot at allies to repair their ships.It's an interesting concept... And so far I really like it.

There are few games that endorse the theme of pirates and have open sea combat so it easily stands with some value just because there aren't much competitors other than sea of thieves, blackflag or indie games.Gameplay and some of its options seem pretty shallow, as you progress further in the game, it only presents itself as colored or (+1) upgrades to your weapons. You will find yourself using the same few weapons pretty much throughout the game and content doesn't seem to be king for such a live-service game. Yes there isn't as much content to warrant it being a paid live service game that still has microtransactions. The other bummer point, microtransactions are not pay to win and purely cosmetics but begs the question whether it is worth it or not seeing as how gameplay is shallow and repetitive in nature. There is also the existence of battle passes and any modern day live service practice you can think of are pretty much present here in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Ubisoft’s Skull and Bones has been in the works for 11 years. Reportedly starting life as an expansion for the beloved Assassin’s Creed: Black Flag before shifting into an MMO, then gradually turning into the multiplayer action game we see today, it’s fair to say such a protracted development is seldom a good sign. Yet I held out hope that this could be the seafaring simulator of my dreams. I’d envisaged venturing the seven seas, meeting and recruiting memorable crewmates, maybe even participating in pirate politics, and growing attached to – and immersed in – this time period. Sadly, the result of all these efforts is a frustrating and often boring sailing game that is devoid of personality. By the time I reached the endgame, I’d forgotten I was meant to be a pirate at all.The strongest reminder that I am, in fact, a pirate is my new boss, John Scurlock. The foul-mouthed leader of the Sainte-Anne pirate den is riddled with daddy issues that manifest in an insistence that we screw over anyone we come into contact with, mostly the French Compagnie. The extent of said screwing-over extends to a handful of jaunts across the ocean to sling cannonballs into enemy ships, maybe steal some items or treasure maps, and then return to enjoy Scurlock’s inevitable praise. I’d love to say there’s more of a story to Skull and Bones, but it seems that any inkling of a meaningful narrative or solid structure has been washed away with the years.The most obvious example of Skull and Bones’ missing personality is its soulless protagonist. While the customization options extend far beyond the initial character creation screen, with vendors selling outfits and plenty of collectible accessories up for grabs, my backstory is non-existent, and therefore so is my grounding in this world. This blank slate approach does occasionally lend itself well to unpredictability, such as the prologue leading me to become an impromptu captain of two shipwrecked sailors. With my new, totally unearned title, we board my battered boat and head for the Sainte-Anne pirate den to earn Scurlock’s trust, which he bestows upon me a little too easily. A short while later, I’m deemed worthy of a larger ship, but not before I check off some inane tasks to harvest specific materials that take an age to respawn if another player gets to them first.The frustrating inconveniences don’t stop there. Despite the game’s early warnings that you should play nice and not sling cannonballs into one another, players making a beeline for your ship is a regular occurrence. Yes, true PvP combat is reserved for specific zones and events, but there’s precious little I can do when a fellow bored player sails full-throttle into the side of my ship. When the alternative is playing Skull and Bones properly, I can hardly blame them.Cannonballs, of course, aren’t the only way to damage opposition fleets, or threats that lurk in the shallows. You’ve also got demicannons, sea fire cannons, and a long-gun… cannon. Skull and Bones even features magical health-restoring cannonballs for you to fire into your friends’ ships during multiplayer. This arcade-like silliness doesn’t quite land and – again – is indicative of a game that doesn’t know what it is or even wants to be.Tweaking your Skull and Bones ship loadout and exploring the extensive customization options offer a comparatively much better time. The excitement of spotting an extravagant cosmetic is dulled, however, by the high price of in-game premium currency. A particular bundle of cosmetics will set you back 1,200 gold, equating to around $13. It’s a tough sell for a game that already costs $60. Thankfully, I was able to unlock a healthy variety of cosmetics without spending a penny by completing contracts for silver and looting ships.Obtaining blueprints for bigger, better, meaner ships is a long-winded process, though. The hunt to find them can be tedious unless you’re using a guide and, strangely, there are currently only small and medium-sized ships to acquire. Unlocking the first of the medium-sized ship blueprints requires you to hit at least Brigand I infamy, and then you have to sail off to far-flung islands to buy them. After that, it’s a jaunt across the ocean, sinking enemies and looting their wreckage to find the required materials to build the ship. Despite the repetition of this loop, it’s one of the game’s few worthwhile endeavors.Crafting weapons is tedious thanks to the loading screen that appears every time you use the craft feature. This is one of many recurring loading screens that collectively hurt the game’s pacing. You’ll suffer them whenever you get off your ship, interact with an NPC, or dig up some treasure. Coupled with the fact you can only disembark at specific zones and have to be on land to fast travel, and Skull and Bones starts to feel less and less like an open-world game.The PvP is also wildly imbalanced at the moment, and you run the risk of meeting someone five levels above or below you, but these fast-paced encounters offer up one of the few opportunities for player-to-player interactivity. While I’m struggling for positives, the option to craft your own contraband and smuggle it via the Black Market does eventually open up more complex and satisfying contracts, provided you can stick it out long enough to get there.In the end, any fun to be had here is thrown off by the disjointed open world, a lack of personality, and the endless, extended fetch quests that seldom excite. Skull and Bones had every opportunity to win me over – it had so much promise – but I’m sad to say its launch version is painfully far from being the pirate adventure of my dreams.Verdict: 3/10

_childDocuments_.review: We really need neutral reviews Valve.BUT and this is the big contraindication, I would not recommend it for any price higher than that.It is a live service beast and it comes with all the downsides of that in terms of utterly disrespecting the player's time.One would think you could expect land based combat after such a long time in development hell but NO....you only play as your ship.This game would not even hold up if there was any serious triple AAA pirate competition. But as the market stands there is no pirate game which can  threaten it because all pirate games are janky sandboxes à la Sea Dogs and the old Pirates of the Caribbean by Akella Studio...except for Black Flag which is a far superior Pirate game.There are a few good aspects of Skull and bones and I am gonna start with those.It is a game with decent graphics and it certainly has atmospheric moments when you are sailing through a storm and fighting mythical beasts or battling elite captains on high sea while other players join in on the swashbuckling fun.The NPCs are displayed with nice blur optic; even though most of them are pretty lifeless. Yanita was one of the few exceptions.I acknowledge that they integrated different languages in the NPC dialogues; among them many have some Swahili catchphrases which positively caught me by surprise.The main game loop is the naval action and it is fun. It has to be after all since it is the bread and butter of gameplay. I just wished the combat had more fog like in blackflag from the cannon powder.Against wary expectations of Ubisoft's greedy practices when it comes to microtransactions, I can calm you down that there are a lot of cosmetics which can be obtained for free with the silver currency to customise your dream Pirate captain.Sea Shanties are nice and multilingual even though they are always randomised, THIS could have been handled better like the Radio wheel of the GTA titles.Ships offer a plethora of customisation options.Diverse array of different weaponry for your ships and furniture to supplement your weapon, hull or crew strength. This provides a certain depth for team based PVE fighting or PVP battles.By contrast these mediocre and good points are overshadowed by bugs, horrific design choices and a lackluster endgame.The NPCs are empty shells of the Pirates they aspire to be. Gameplay when docking on land is extremely simplistic and all the outposts look the same and have the same structure of having a cache, a bonfire for increased stamina and some messages in a bottle perhaps.The map would have been wonderful as a parchment styled map but they opted for a map which reeks of Ubisoft UI overload with too many World boss, resource and questing symbols. Horrific design choice. In the same vein, world boss popups break your immersion every chance they get with players asking for assistance.Treasure maps are not worth the effort as far as I could see even if they are LEGENDARY ONES!And what is the point of having a cool parchment treasure map when the map points you to the chest anyway?!The main quests and side quests are all mundane fetch quests mostly coupled with a bit background plot about two pirate Kingpins. Nothing memorable and powered by cringe dialogue cutscenes.The chat and Social functions are extremely limited.I hit endgame and a fairly decent ship by the 20 hour mark upon which a pretty mundane endgame awaited me.The epic sea battles against elite captains and mythical creatures are cool but if you have done them they get old pretty fast.The end game has two components: building your pirate smuggling empire and doing world bosses and PVP activities for lackluster treasure maps.After you are satisfied with your ship and captain customisation it just feels like the game is not worth playing anymore unless you play it with friends.Endgame is simply hell bent on keeping you playing with nasty player retention tactics like the real tedious empire building and grinding secondary currencies for tiny incremental upgrades to your ship.Not sure if I am gonna play this again....Buy it for 20 bucks if you have a faible for pirates or stay far away!Not worth the full price. The ones thriving Ubisoft seems to be stooping lower and lower in midst of angry share holders and a certain Assassins Creed Yasuke controversy...Yves Guillemot declaring this the groundbreaking quadruple title is the pinnacle of being delusional!

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a very repetitive and grind focused gameplay loop, with no real clear goals to work for outside a bigger and stronger ship. The combat against the AI ships feels pretty good.You can send your crew to raid islands while you defend the ship from other ships. The enemy ships all come from the same side, and in predictable waves which prevents you from progressing until they are killed or removed from the ring. It doesn't feel like a fun mechanic... you mostly just sit there until the bar is full.The character customization is pretty much pointless, as you are on your ship 99% of the time. Visiting islands to buy stuff ends up feeling bad and clunky since there's nothing to do. It feels tacked on, like they gave up partway through designing land stuff.Even gathering resources happens on the ship, you just move to the shoreline and hit a button to get materials. Why not just gut the land stuff entirely so I don't have to walk anywhere? You could have the NPC conversations, vending, and crafting happen in an interactive cinematic style thing or something instead.Crafting seems pretty pointless, as I get sent a better thing in the mail before I can even come close to being able to craft items half as good.Character customization happens through a fashion NPC in town, and they have paid cosmetics. You can't actually buy the paid cosmetics through them, or see how much they cost. You have to leave their dialogue, and move to a separate menu first. You'd think they'd make it easier to give them more money. (They give some premium currency for free... I wasn't actually buying anything.)Anyways, there is good parts to the game, but it ultimately feels hollow and strangely incomplete... like they lost sight of their original goal or something. I wish I could refund it, but I kept thinking there had to be more to the game than shoot ships and sell their junk.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll preface this by saying I didn't keep up to date with the development or launch problems of this game, so perhaps I'm coming into the game with a more unbiased opinion of it.I think it's reasonably fun. It's not AC4, but something else entirely. This game is more akin to some weird love child between World of Warships and something like Euro Truck Simulator 2, bringing the arcade-y naval action of WoWs with the calming (for me at least) monotony that you find in transport ("commerce") aspects of ETS2/ATS or Elite Dangerous. The combat isn't particularly difficult, but you can and will die on occasion, especially early on. Most of your time post-Captain Level 10 will be spent running transport missions for illicit goods, hence the comparison to ETS2.There's a surprising amount of depth and synergy to the ship weapon setups, though many of the best weapons look to be locked behind the lengthy end-game grind or seasonal battle pass rewards. I've seen complaints about fast travel being sparse, but I don't have too much of an issue with that. Once you've explored the map a fair bit, you'll find more than a few fast travel points to make use of. The only time you're locked out of fast travel is when doing the end-game blockade running missions, which is perfectly reasonable in my opinion. Limping away from a difficult fight and being a fair distance from the nearest port can be frustrating, but I think it's a necessity for difficulty and perfectly thematic.Performance-wise, the game actually feels really smooth. I'm running on an older system with a 1080Ti, and on High graphics it's completely stable at 60-70 fps. No hard crashes, but have had the odd map/journal UI buggyness. Nothing game breaking, and far better than what I was led to expect.Is the game worth $79.99 CAD normally? Definitely not, no. Not when compared to the major releases in that price range of the past couple years. On sale for 60% off or more? I'd say so, yes. Just know what kind of game it is and don't expect it to be something it isn't.

_childDocuments_.review: Prior to getting the game on Steam I have 1500 hours on Ubisoft Connect.This game has provided months of enjoyment since I started playing it back at launch on February 2024. I started playing via an 8 hour trial and was hooked. It looks stunning graphically and not cartoon like other pirate games. The game play of ship to ship combat also appealed to me, I've never been a fan of Assassin's Creed games or stealth games in general so it's hard for me to compare it to Black Flag but as a pirate game it scratches an itch until Rockstar make a pirate game (I can dream/hope).The single player content is limited and I've probably prolonged my enjoyment by joining a Discord group as it's in PVE co-op where this game truly shines. There are PVP element's such as Hostile Takeovers, Helm Wagers, and Cutthroat Cargo hunts but these are optional bits of fun, not forced activities. For those hunting PVP there is not a lot of it in the game so far but there is a PVP mode in the pipeline that looks interesting.I view this game as a new IP and one which is being updated weekly by the developers. Season's One and Two were great, Season Three is a bit content light so far but I think the dev's are giving newer players on Steam a chance to catch those of us who were here from the start.I've mentioned the graphics a little, I am running on an RTX 4070 ti super and sailing around drinking in the detail of the world you realise how much work has gone into the environment I highly recommend sailing around the Africa region, it is stunning.Overall I like a lot of others are impatient for more content but that's because I have hammered the game. _childDocuments_.review: When I first thought about Skull and Bones I was very sceptical. How can you build a pirate game that is all about sailing ships based on the comical and arcade experience of Assassin Creed Black Flag? A game I have abandoned 5 minutes after I got into the naval experience… Well, I thought they would try to take a step back and use the few strong sides (graphics for example) to mix them with (far) more realism. I was hoping they would look back on excellent pirate games like Sid Meier´s Pirates! and learn there. Learn what the core experience should be:1) At least half realistic sailing experience creating a tactical sea combat experience.2) Sailing around and looking for ships to target and attempt to steal from. This is the absolute core experience of pirate gameplay, right? Finding what, when and if strike a ship and claim it or its cargo for yourself and your crew.3) No fast travel. How can you build a core pirate ship experience if you can fast travel around the world as you wish.4) There should be strong crew elements if the game is about pirate ships. At very least you should be able to level up your crew gaining some advantages and if you sink, the main penalty should be the loss of your crew. That is just a very basic idea and could be worked in much more detail but lets simply repeat that in game like this the crew should play important role and you absolutely should have some incentive to not sink.But developers learned nothing from the past. What we got and what was even strengthen after release is absolute arcade experience. Sailing simulation is not existing. You hop (fast travel) from event to event and base to base. You do not care about normal ships outside of events basically at all. If you sink, you simply respawn on the spot and go on. If I had to compare the basic gameplay to other game, I would choose Fallout 76. Yet, developers didn’t even learn there. What Im talking about? Skull and bones is currently developing PvP mode (Nuclear Winter anyone) and there are already PvP activities in the game, even if you don’t really have to participate in them and most people don’t. Same like in Fallout 76 the game simply isn’t made for PvP at all. It didn’t work in Fallout 76 and its certainly not working in Skull and Bones. How can you make an interesting PvP ship combat with such an arcade approach? You cannot. If the game was made in what I have written above in mind, then maybe. But a game where wind doesn’t make difference, where you sail around with a speed of sport car and shoot and see other ships explode like you are in some parodic movie. No, just no. I would like to see the hard data. How many people focus on PvP in Skull and Bones? Is it more than 10 % of player base? I highly doubt so. From what I saw in my own sessions, the only thing PvP brings is anger and rage quits in a community that is already small enough. So will the developers learn from Fallout 76 and will they eventually remove and/or minimalize the PvP aspect and try to at least focus on the best possible PvE experience including much more easier balancing etc.? Well they should but…The core of the game sadly isn’t about piracy. It isn’t about sailing (instead its about fast travel hoping) at all, it isn’t about plundering either. Its about building your alcohol and drug empire with a restart each season. What I find very amusing is your own first ship mate that keeps telling you are some kind of freedom fighter against the tyranny of the western corporations. I cannot stress this enough – I’m not. I’m bloody sinking ships and stealing stuff, I’m not a good guy by any means and I don’t give a F word about western corporations. I’m not sure what lesson is the game trying to teach there, if you are supposed to be some kind of anarchist or democracy fighter, but naaah. The empire building isn’t that bad. I mean I would rather focus on true pirate gameplay but when I simply accept the game for what it is and see the improvements they made, it’s alright.Let’s jump into another topic and that’s season pass. Other games and especially Fallout 76 could learn there. I can finish the season pass very easily and that’s how season passes should work. In comparison in Fallout 76 I have spent maybe 2000 hours playing (Bethesda + Steam launchers) and I NEVER BLOODY FINISHED A SINGLE SEASON PASS. Season passes shouldn’t be made for the most hardcore players, I don’t want to focus on single game anymore (there will be no more World of Warcraft effect) and especially not to do something as simple as finishing a season for basic rewards. Also season passes should allow you to get your rewards for simply playing. Not by doing this achievement or that achievement, not by forcing you to play the way developers want but by simply playing as you do and wish to do. So very well done on the developer side in Skull and Bones.Cosmetics should be little more grounded, but I think developers already acknowledged that and it will be so in the future. But on the bright side you can use ship and captain cosmetics to look normal for the time period. Of course you will see many players that are looking like clowns. I don’t really care that much.Now with everything mentioned above, why did I give a thumbs up. I simply like games like these. From Sid Meier´s Pirates! through Sea Legends and Sea of Thieves. By the way - Sea of Thieves is a better game no doubt. Much better sailing experience, much more realistic and fun ship combat where even PvP makes sense and without a doubt 10x better experience if you play with a friend or two. But back to Skull and Bones. I have already spent around 400 hours with it, so it paid for itself already even if I stopped playing now. I have finished all 3 seasons. I play mostly solo when friends are not available and it’s not bad for what it is. It could have been much better but… I build my empire, after first season (I forbid myself using fast travel in season 1) I hop from event to event and see some NPCs ships explode in a spectacular unrealistic way. I grind loot and build stuff. Graphics looks nice. Hmmm. We shall see where it goes from here. Even if with recent updates developers focus on totally opposite aspects I would.

Forgive me for being blunt:1. The playability of the game is not as good as a 2005 online game called "Voyage Century". You only have one profession, which is piracy, and the only pleasure is endless shelling.After spending a lot of material upgrading, the ship's attributes remained almost unchanged, and even its appearance did not change3. The unlocked clothing still needs to be bought in the store without any attributes. To be honest, it doesn't look good. There is also a spending store where I really want to spend USD to buy something, but I don't like any of them. They are all strange and peculiar styles. I really don't know what the aesthetic of the graphic designer is4. Without land warfare and armored warfare, there can only be endless explosions, and the smoke from gun barrels and the sound of exploding ships are not as good as Total War5. The profits earned from opening factories, doing business, and so on are like sending beggars away. Imagine the ancestors of the Age of Discovery who discovered that profits were like this and probably wouldn't do any business6. It is said to be a gold game, but the gold products are not attractive or practical, and even if you want to spend money, you cannot spend it7. The map only includes the Indian Ocean, which is a scale changing feature. Many games with a 20-year budget now have global maps8. When treasure maps are dug up, they are all garbage, and the world boss drops garbage, all of which are playing beggars and wasting time9. Another thing is naval warfare, where enemy ships' attack power often inexplicably changes. Even before using the worst ship, I was able to get beaten, but when I switched to the ship with the highest health and armor, it inexplicably became very fragile10. _childDocuments_.review: So it's definitely the game you think it is... but at a sale price it's quite a bit of fun once you get into it. It can be slow and grindy but there are a lot of ship builds to explore. It's nice that it's largely soloable and then you kind of bounce off of players and assist each other when you want to. I don't feel like I always have to work with others if I don't want and there's still stuff to accomplish. It's been bug free so far, performs very smoothly and it's quite pretty. It is an online only title, and I definitely understand why some folks wouldn't want to support Ubisoft. It's a vehicle game first and foremost, it isn't trying in any way to be Black Flag like. If you don't like the style of ship gameplay that was in the AC series, this won't convince you. That said the ship combat itself (and I'm talking just ship of course, not melee/boarding as that is absent here) is better than AC and you have much more variety in things. It is fleshed out, more rpg in style, and heavily gear dependent. If you binge it, it'll probably get boring quick, if you only play a bit at a time, it might keep you entertained for a while. 70$ is steep, on sale, it's worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: A solid pirate ship game. Fun ship combat with an arcade feel with lots of ship customization, including cosmetic, but also tons of weapon, armor and loadout variety.Do not pay full price for this game. Pick it up for sub $30 and it's worth that price, assuming you're interested in the theme. The open seas, here the Indian Ocean, make for a fairly large battleground full of several different factions which include enemy ships of varied size, difficulty and weapons, as well as sea monsters. All combat is ship based and the only land, on foot gameplay is at little outposts or safehavens that act as quest boards and quest giving NPCs, as well as storefronts for everything from buying cannonballs to crafting new ships and outfitting your pirate. Some swordplay combat would be a welcomed addition but this is a ship fighting game and that's where it thrives. The ship combat is very fun, albeit, with an arcade feel. Ships have unrealistic speed and maneuverability, which makes for epic fights with constant cannon barrages and capability to dodge and pivot your way to victory. I believe that this combat works well and eliminates boring time, but is as far from simulation or realism as can be.The game has some noticeable visual glitches here and there; not a deal breaker for me but can be distracting and definitely ruins the immersion. On the subject of bugs, I've had constant issues connecting with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: Most of my hours are on the Ubisoft Connect platform. I'm reviewing this game through the lens of what it actually is, not what I wanted it to be or thought it would be. Skull & Bones is an interesting bird because visually speaking it is sometimes quite beautiful and charming, and yet at other times it looks (and plays) like a mobile game. It's an interesting bird because sometimes I want to play the game for hours because of how fun it is to sail the seas in my ship, and yet I end up only playing for an hour tops because I get annoyed at how clunky the quest system can be and how obtuse the UI is. It's an interesting bird because I think this game could have truly been a really solid experience but because of its tortured upbringing it's now a shadow of what no doubt was meant to be. All that to say though, it's still a fun game in as much as lovely looking arcade ship-shooters with RPG elements can be. That is after all what you're doing most of the time: sailing and shooting cannons. With this in mind I never once found myself wishing it was a swashbuckling third-person pirate game like Black Flag (if that's what you wanted then play Black Flag). For some reason some folks have had a hard time understanding that the ship is your "main character" just like it is in EVE Online. Yes you have a pilot (or capsuleer as is the case with EVE) but it's your ship that you form the bond with. As such I had no issue with many of the games mechanics being implemented through that lens (like the silly but simple resource accumulation that you can do in the open world). All-in-all Skull & Bones is a fun little game to dabble in but it's most definitely not the kind of game that would become my main squeeze, and I think for most people who find the game enjoyable it'll probably be just that. A simple sailing game to pass the time with. In closing: get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly not bad so far, If you are looking for a pirate game that you can play with your friends with a focus on PVE this could be a solid game for you. Don't buy this game expecting it to be AC black flag 2, that's not what this is. All of the combat is navel combat, no on foot combat and no boarding combat. The ship combat is very good tho, you have an array of weapons and ships to choose from, you've got your tanks, supports, and dps ships, and you have cannons, mortars, mine layers, long-range cannons, even guns that heal allies. You will meet an array of characters that guide you through your pirate adventure, some people say the voice acting is bad but I'm not sure what they are talking about, the voice acting is solid. While you are not glued to your ship, you will have the opportunity to walk around towns as your pirate to interact with shops and other players, They are like your hub worlds. For those of you scarred about a repeat of Sea of Thieves this game has a pvp flag that you must raise at a hub in order to attack and receive damage from other players so don't worry about getting griefed by high-level players.I did think it was weird to limit it to three players a party instead of 4. The game kind of wants to be a mmo with the way classes and weapons along with leveling are set up.The combat is fun and intense, the boarding minigame has some room for improvement as all you do it throw a hook onto the enemy ship but its quite literally hit or miss and I can figure out the method to ensure it lands.Right now the game is in a really good state as of now and I will admit it had a rough launch but look at Sea of Thieves, that game had a disastrous launch, and its an amazing game now, no doubt if Ubisoft puts in the effort this game can also be really great game. But overall I'd say the game is worth getting, haven't experienced any crashes or game-breaking bugs so its been a clean experience.Update: I've spent some time playing the game and it is extremely fun Don't listen to the bad reviews this game is worth a playend of the day if you like a focus on boarding a on foot combat but lacking inn navel combat play sea of thieves if you want a focus on naval combat but lacking on foot/boarding then skull and bones is for youI would love to see larger ships enter the game in the future

_childDocuments_.review: Caveat: I played this game during open beta so my 22.3 hours on record so far is misleading.This is an okay game if you don't mind the fact that the terrain rendering is more like a cheap mobile game at times. Seriously, the cheap parallax effect with hills bouncing up and down is jarring once you notice it. Also, the ships are far too fast and nimble, they never feel like massive sail-driven ships. How they managed to go from AC:BF to this is a mystery. Most likely, this is a result of all the different directions this game was tugged over the many years it was in development, with nobody agreeing on exactly what type of game they were making. Someone clearly wanted it to be more fast-paced so corners were cut everywhere to improve performance -- the visuals suffered greatly but somehow frame rate didn't improve.Still, if you get it really cheap on sale, and you don't mind the fact that the in-game chat that didn't work during open beta STILL doesn't work after all this time*, there's still fun to be had shooting up ships. The "empire building" part is ridiculously hard to get into, so expect to spend a LOT of time in the mid-game plateu grinding for bettter ships and equipment. PVP is opt-in and to this day I have never seen any.*) There's a Steam achievement tied to the permanently broken in-game chat system, so 100% completion is quite impossible. You have been warned.

_childDocuments_.review: I decided to give this game another chance after the beta, as I wasn't quite convinced it was for me. The game runs very smoothly, and while the character controls are a bit unusual, they aren't something you can't get used to. The main questline isn't particularly long; it's mostly straightforward, which I personally appreciate in this case because I didn't feel like in other games where you have to "kill 10 random enemies before getting to the point." The loot system is, in my opinion, perfectly fair. The fact that you're not forced into PvP but are given the option, thus allowing solo players a chance at piracy, is executed perfectly. Building your own pirate empire, capturing port towns, and thereby dealing with the ranked system (which resets with each new season) still rewards you even if you're not a hardcore grinder. _childDocuments_.review: I don't review things too often, but this particular game, I feel, deserves it. Wordy review incomingTLDR: I like it. I do not regret having bought it. It's not a AAAA game, but you can tell that (at least some of) the devs put a lot of love into the game.Now you've heard a lot about the game, and much of what you've heard has been true and fair.Its story is... short, and not very deep.It doesn't have a whole lot of content, it just... doesn't really. There's no sword fighting, no sneaking around, no swooping up damsels, nothing like that. The game almost entirely takes place on your ship with brief sojourns onto land to buy/sell/make stuff, repair your ship, or find a not too exciting buried treasure.But the core gameplay itself, your ship navigating around the Indian ocean as you pewpew other ships with a wide variety of cannons, grapeshot cannons, torpedos (yes really), mortars, and giant flamethrowers is still quite fun, if simple. My average play session amounts to deciding what I want to gather (through violence), heading to where said items are, then gathering through violence. Occasionally another player asks for help with an event boss (of which there are MANY) so I quick travel there, help out for 10 minutes or so, collect my loot, hope I get something neat, then back to pillaging.There's some manner of industry simulator thing where you can manage something of a smuggling empire, but everyone says it's kind of boring so I just... haven't done that.The graphics are very pretty and it's fun to see waves wash over the rails of your deck and then drain away. It's pleasant.So yeah. It's fun and pleasant and for the price I paid (roughly 40 CAD), I think it was worth it.

New Game Plus with Island OwnershipWhat if, after completing the story, players could start a New Game Plus where they own and manage their own island? Imagine:Customizable Islands: Build trade ports, shipyards, and fortifications. Make your island a hub for commerce or a pirate stronghold.Dynamic Growth: Expand your island over time, adding businesses like taverns, factories, and marketplaces that generate passive income or rare items.Island Reputation: Your island could serve as a symbol of your pirate empire, influencing alliances and rivalries in the game world.This would provide a reason to replay the game, giving players a sense of progression and legacy.2. Bartering and Advanced Trade SystemsAdd a bartering system where players exchange goods instead of relying solely on currency. Trade routes could evolve dynamically, with rare resources and high-stakes deals creating an engaging economy. Pair this with your island to create a thriving pirate economy.3. Secret Societies for Depth and MysteryIntroduce secret societies that players can join, each offering unique gameplay advantages and quests. For example:Mystical Orders for spiritual rituals, divine weapons, and powers.Merchant Guilds for trade benefits and exclusive barter deals.Shadow Networks for espionage and covert missions.Your chosen society could influence how you interact with the game world, adding replay value and narrative depth.4. Right-Hand CompanionsAllow players to recruit a right-hand ally who grows with them throughout their journey. Inspired by Li Tian Lin, the Phoenix Girl, these characters could:Manage your island when you're at sea.Assist in combat or negotiations.Develop unique skills over time, like trade, strategy, or morale-boosting abilities.5. Businesses and EconomyEnable players to own businesses on their island, such as:Taverns to gather rumors or recruit crew.Weapon Factories to produce gear for sale or personal use.Markets to influence regional economies.Combine this with a stock market system, allowing players to invest in or compete with other companies, affecting the in-game economy.6. Spirit Guides for MysticismIncorporate spirit guides that offer:Enhanced navigation and treasure hunting.Mystical powers in combat or defense.Protection from supernatural threats.This would add a magical element to the game, blending pirate folklore with immersive gameplay.Final ThoughtsSkull and Bones already offers a solid pirate adventure, but adding these features—especially island ownership—would make it truly legendary. A New Game Plus mode with deep storytelling, strategic choices, and dynamic gameplay systems would ensure players keep coming back for more.Ubisoft, let’s chart a course to greatness and make Skull and Bones the definitive pirate game!

_childDocuments_.review: The last time I heard about this game was 2018 and then I lost complete track of the game till a week ago where someone told me its out on Steam. So I checked it out and most people said its a trash game.What really confused me was that people who reviewed it on youtube said its a fun game and the gameplay looked fun and appealing to me. Since the game was for 24 Bucks on Steam I thought to check it out but wasnt sure. This were when someone told me that you can play a Free 6 hour demo on Ubiconnect.So I tried it out and played 4 hours straight and after that I bought it on Steam.The game is not bad. In no way. Actually the game is pretty fun. Is it a AAAA-Game? Of course not! It is a normal live service game like others it has it flaws but also it qualities. The Naval gameplay aka sailing your ship, upgrading it and fight on Sea is really well made and fun. The only little bummer is that there are many loading screens and little cutscenes/Animations which you cant skip. The loadingscreens mostly take 2 or 3 seconds which lead me to the question why you have to put a loadingscreen there and not build the game as a whole map like in sea of thieves? But well since they are so short its not that bad. The animations can be a bit frustrating. Everytime you board an enemy ship you dont do it by yourself but an animation is played which you cant skip.So unlike in Sea of Thieves you dont really play as a person but as a ship with their crew. Which is not bad. Like I said its fun but its way different than in Sea of Thieves and people should be aware of it.I personally think when Ubisoft would have been more down to earth with the marketing and maybe would it make F2P, since its a Live Service Game they can still earn alot of moneys people wouldnt be mad about the game and wouldnt downvote it so much.That there is no man to man combat with swords and pistols is not a problem. I must say I like it how it is. The fact that the naval combat is well thought makes the game more unique.And we dont need to talk about the graphic. Its stunning. The game is really beautiful.EDIT: One thing I forgot to mention is that the world feels really alive. the oceans are not empty. Beside the other player you have alot of NPC ships sailing around. Either just patroling or transport cargo which you can all attack and plunder. There are even different faction which can attack each other so you sail on the open sea and see on the horizon a few NPC ships battling against each other. There are different weather conditions too like storm and there are sea monsters and many world events.So here my Fazit:Its not a AAAA-Game but its still a good and fun game. Its not a Sea of Thieves clone since you play more your ship with crew and less a individual character but this is not bad. On this way it has more its own identity. Many loadingscreens and unskipable animations which can be a bit annoying but they are just a few seconds long so its not that bad. No man to man combat but the game dont need this.I really hope the game will survive and gets a lot support from the developer since its really a nice game. _childDocuments_.review: Think of this as a modernised Sid Meier's Pirates! (without the limited sword play) and you'll enjoy it as you sail your ship around a vast map, plundering settlements, terrorising supply lines, upgrading your ship, making rum and smuggling goods!This is a far better single player experience than Sea of Thieves and currently less than half the price too! However, forget the AAAA+ Ubisoft claims - this game isn't AAAA+. It's definitely worth £20 but if you'd bought in at £70 then you may feel a little different.However, ignore the Ubisoft hate. This is a solid game that will keep you entertained for a long time.***Update After Further Play Time***The game gets better the longer you play it. It's not all about sinking ships or running errands for people - you have an empire to expand which includes making and distributing rum, gin, opium etc.There's even the ability to "take-over" industrial settlements and turn them into your own illicit goods production centres that then generate pieces of eight for you over time. Set up a rum production industry and you can then transport the required sugar cane to increase production speed which gives you a real choice on whether to go and buy the goods legally as a trader, go out hunting them as a privateer or take on the daily supply missions which usually involve running through very hostile waters and trying not to get sunk!Map size is pretty good - it takes a long time to sail from one end to the other but once you've opened a port up you can fast travel to it which saves time but often it can be a good idea not to fast travel so that you can gather resources as you sail from one location to another.The bigger ships also handle really nicely with a good feeling of weight to them. Ship combat gets even more interesting once you've got in to the medium sized ships which have more configuration options, more guns and usually an auxiliary weapon system such as rockets or mortars.It's also worth noting that I am soloing this game just fine.1. Needs to be installed on an SSD drive otherwise you'll encounter loading screens every time you try to do something in port which quickly becomes annoying. Once on an SSD loading screens are totally gone!2. I've had a number of crashes when in port. Thankfully no progress lost.3. End Game Grind - Actually no where near as bad as it is made out to be. Once you've got your manufacturing plants up and running the Pieces 'o 8 roll in every day and these can be used to buy the more rare/exotic materials required through the Black Market!In fact, this game is turning more into a pirate game now that I've hit the end game. Silver, which is the currency you're usually swimming in mid-game, is suddenly required in greater volumes as your manufacturing plants need it to stay functional.Now I'm scouring the map deciding which areas are best to plunder for resources and silver! If I see a convoy I'm more likely to hit it for the money! Yarrr!

_childDocuments_.review: Once upon a time in the swashbuckling realm of high seas and treacherous tides, there lived a rather peculiar pirate named Captain Dark. Unlike his fearsome name, Captain Dark was an unassuming fellow with a peculiar hobby: he was obsessed with video games. Not just any video games, but the most notorious bug-riddled, glitch-infested pirate game ever conceived: Skull and Bones.Captain Dark had stumbled upon Skull and Bones during a particularly dreary evening in the local tavern, where he was nursing a mug of grog and lamenting his crew's unfortunate fashion choices. The game, notorious for its rampant bugs and clunky mechanics, was both reviled and revered among gamers. Intrigued by its reputation, Captain Dark decided to embark on a daring quest of his own: to conquer this digital sea of chaos and become the mightiest pirate kingpin in the virtual world.Armed with nothing but his wits and an ancient gaming console he had salvaged from the wreckage of a forgotten shipwreck, Captain Dark set sail into the pixelated waters of Skull and Bones. His first challenge was to navigate the treacherous waves of corrupted code and glitched enemies. His ship, the Junk Sail, was a wobbly vessel plagued by bizarrely shifting textures and inexplicable lag. Nonetheless, Captain Dark embraced these challenges with a blend of cunning and humor, delighting in the absurdity of his predicament.The path to greatness in Skull and Bones was fraught with bizarre anomalies: enemies would occasionally float in mid-air, treasure chests would spontaneously vanish, and the sea itself seemed to glitch into a surreal tapestry of colors. But Captain Dark was undeterred. He used the chaos to his advantage, learning to exploit the game's quirks with a savvy that soon became the stuff of legend among players.As Captain Dark progressed through the game, he amassed a crew of digital misfits who were as eccentric as the game itself. There was Peg-Leg Pete, who had a tendency to glitch through walls, and Scurvy Sam, whose piratical dialogue was perpetually stuck in a loop. Together, they forged an unbreakable bond in the face of absurd challenges, transforming each bug into an opportunity for brilliance.With every triumph and every glitchy victory, Captain Dark's reputation grew. He mastered the art of exploiting the game's many bugs, turning what others saw as frustrations into stepping stones to greatness. His name became synonymous with ingenuity and daring, and soon he was hailed as the undisputed kingpin of Skull and Bones.But as with all great tales, there came a time for Captain Dark to part with his beloved Junk Sail. It was not out of necessity but out of a whimsical sense of adventure. Having conquered the virtual seas and made a name for himself, Captain Dark decided it was time to sail off into new horizons. He auctioned off the Junk Sail, now a legendary vessel of both glitchy charm and unparalleled combat prowess, to the highest bidder.The sale was a grand affair, attended by digital and real-world pirates alike. The Junk Sail was sold for a princely sum, and Captain Dark, now a hero both in-game and out, bid farewell to his pixelated adventures. He sailed away, leaving behind a legacy of laughter, ingenuity, and the reminder that even in the face of chaos, a true pirate's spirit never falters.And so, the tale of Captain Dark, the master of Skull and Bones, became a legend in its own right—a whimsical yet serious reminder that with enough creativity and resilience, even the most bug-riddled of adventures can lead to greatness.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun, first and foremost, it's a damn fun game. The group battles are a blast and so far the player community as a whole is laid back, friendly and helpful. I also think it's relevant to point out the absence of toxic players which honestly has been a surprise to me simply because of my experiences in other massive multiplayer online games where the kids are so nasty and hateful to one another that it makes me weep for the future of mankind. I suspect that the community in this game is probably a little more mature (hence the positive remarks). The story is good and engaging enough to make one curious about what happens next and the graphics are beautiful. So overall this game is solid and like I said before it's just fn fun. Now, there are some "issues" that do seem to be more deeply rooted than the normal "Ironing out the kinks" type stuff you see in other games and rarely you will experience a "WTF" moment. However these things are not enough to detract from the positives IMO. Anyone that tells you that it's not "grindy" ,as the kids like to put it, is either captain of a level 12 or below ship or they are simply just ignorant. I say this because the requirements to go beyond 12, as in the material requirements, is ludicrous at best and downright sadistic at worst. Not only in quantity but availability of said materials is like nothing I have ever seen before. That alongside a few other minor irritants such as the seemingly constant headwind that exists at all times, everywhere on the map, no matter what, I can't help but to get the feeling that the devs weren't exactly killing it in high school and this is somehow some type of petty retribution lol. But despite those things it's a good game and every bit worth the $24 I paid for it.

_childDocuments_.review: played for 11 hours paid and 6 hours demo on the ubisoft launcher.good game if you are ok with being limited to sea combat.there is a sort of wanted system that makes some faction agressive towards you if you sink their ships or atack their outposts, the ships can call reinforcements if you don't sink em fast enough.There are also some enemies who atack you if you get too close called aswell.there are diffrent kinds of bosses from pirates who have a bounty on their head to megalodon sharks and in the current season gigantic dragons.there is a trading system where items change value depending on location and just rng.the game uses the mmo rpg trifecta of tanks supporters and dps for the abilities that the ships possesdps abilities are something like 25% more ramming damage while a dps ability is something like extra damage when the enemies is on fire.the specific abilities the ships posses often get supported by the crew abilitys (like the firebrands crew throws fire bombs instead of just shooting with muskets which plays into it's extra damage)the ships can be equiped with on big item that gives significant buffs like telescope that allows you to mark an enemy by hitting them from a long range to gain extra damage or cables that give you a speed buff when going full sail at the cost of 5% of you stamina when you use it,the weapons can be atached on the front, either side,the back and for some in the middle.there are some who are just direct upgrades like "long guns I" is ofc worse than "long guns II"but there are some who are more focused on effects. some cannons are focused on ripping the sails to halt their movement, some are fire or electricity based and some have special effects like dealing extra damge to ships with torn sails or firing the whole broadside.there are diffrent weapons aswell like harpoonguns and torpedosi like it but i recommend downloading the test version first to see if you like it

_childDocuments_.review: I am gonna organize this review out with sections so you can skip around to whatever you care to read.Overall personal feelings about the game:The game isn't for everyone and I wouldn't buy the game if you are expecting a remastered black flag experience or a sea of thieves experience. This is more like the division except with ships and way less grind. There are some elements that feel inspired by black flag like the ship upgrade system, looting system, and the towns. But I don't think it will be able to come close to black flag since I am a firm believer that nothing will compare to playing a game for the first or one that was the first of it's kind even if it's a second play through of that game. With that said, I feel it's unfair to compare it to black flag or sea of thieves (if that's your thing). But for me personally, I thoroughly enjoy the game and plan on playing it for a while. I do wish there were more ships and more variety in what you could use, but the game did just release in February so there's still time for it to correct and add more stuff. I get expectations were high since Ubisoft is a big name developer but honestly, this is better then what I expected when you compare it to the release of Overwatch 2 or the 16th Call of Duty game coming out that's just a reskin of a previous one. Anyway, I am gonna move on with the rest of the review. I do recommend giving the game a try but just don't get your expectations too high and avoid going into this knowing very little about it or thinking it's going to be something that it definitely isn't.Enemy ships PvE:Enemy ships are pretty weak even when ganged up on even when ganging up on you. Every combat feels pretty much the same until you get later into the game and then some of the ships can repair each other or get different weapons but even then it becomes a pretty mind numbing experience with bosses and forts being the only real challenge. There's currently just not enough variety right now.Bosses:Most bosses if not all of them can be taken out solo or with one other person if you are the correct rank or higher and take your time with it. The fights don't last very long with being able to kill them in 5 to 10 minutes at most. Some of the bosses are pretty tanky even with a higher rank ship and then they rely on calling in several other ships to kill you. The 2 hardest boss encounters are: The convoy bosses have a tendency to target your sails and immobilize you while they just run away until they escape off the edge map and call an endless number of enemy ships to swarm you and slow you down. The leviathan bosses are easy to take care but can almost one hit you while they hide under the water or behind waves so you can't fight back. You can leave the boss area at any point but have to return after a certain amount of time which makes it easy to just cheese the boss fights but is nice if you over estimated your ability to kill the boss.Player Ships:The ship designs are pretty bad, they look like the sawed a bot in half then used flex seal to glue the front of the ship onto the back of the ship. Which they did us dirty by not really showing the ships except for in first person, far away shot, or at certain angles so you can't see the full ship. There also not a large variety of the ships you can choose from especially early game. Which wouldn't be a problem if the ships looked better then they do currently. There is a decent variety of weapons and where you can equip them on your ship but it's nothing special. Every ship does have a unique passive to make things easier but it also limits you pretty hard to certain play style or weapon combo. I will definitely say some ships are way stronger then others to the point there's not really a point to grind for other ships.Quest:The quest are pretty generic and mostly go here, kill this, now come back or go here, look for this thing, now come back. In the early game this isn't a huge issue since along the way you can collect resources or kill AI ships for resources since there's always something to grind for. But late game, this gets pretty tedious pretty quickly especially when the fast travel points are pretty far from each other and you can only fast travel from somewhere you can dock at or you can fast travel to an event from anywhere. (Which I do to get places quicker and then just leave the event area.) Some of the quests either aren't very self explanatory or don't give you a whole lot to work with leaving you sometimes confused on what to do next.Cosmetics and customization:You can customize your ship, captain, and somewhat your crew. Most of the customization can be either earned or you can grind for the currency to buy it which is nice. There is very little to customizing your captains psychical appearance with only be able to select a few options from a couple of categories.PVP:(I personally prefer no PVP) There's little to no PVP that you have to participate in so you can go the whole game without ever fighting another player which is for the best since the ships aren't very well balanced to fight each other. You can choose to get into a lot of PVP action but that doesn't mean you actually will since you can choose to flag for PVP or not while adventuring around. So this ends up being more a PVE experience than a PVP one. Especially since there's only about 10 other players in your world at a time.Grind:There very little grinding in this game to where you don't really have to go a focus on grinding for certain things until you reach the end game and that is still not that bad. Now that being said, some things are behind a timer but for the most part you can avoid the timers but you can normally grind either something else entirely or you can grind a different way to get what you need. Which is probably meant to slow people down from just grinding to the end game content in a day.Events:There's 2 different kind of events, special boss events and game events. We'll start with the boss events, the boss events feel pretty generic and feel like a reskinned vanilla boss event. You get pretty good rewards from them so it's worth just shutting off your brain and dealing with them. I have yet to really participate in a game event so no idea but from the sound of the most recent on one they did, it didn't seem like anything special.Forts and Towns:You can plunder forts and towns for certain materials but you don't go with your crew, you stay on the ship with most of crew and fight waves of enemy ships trying to stop you while waiting on a bar to progress. These are pretty easy except for the towers or fortifications. They deal a lot of damage but are pretty easy to just snipe from a distance before you even start the plundering event.

_childDocuments_.review: As of writing this review, Skull and Bones is on sale for $19.20 USD. At this price, it’s a decent game if you’re into naval combat and pirate-themed adventures. The ship progression and grind are reasonable, with fun ship weapons that offer different playstyles for both casual and dedicated players.However, don't expect anything remotely realistic from this game. The biggest issue is that it feels confused—at times you’re a pirate, at other times you’re more of a pirate ship simulator, and that lack of clarity affects the experience. The upgrade and customization systems are mostly limited, with a lot of content locked behind microtransactions, making it feel like a free-to-play game disguised as a paid one.But if you go in without heavy expectations, Skull and Bones is a nice game to unwind with. Grab some rum, fire up your cannons, and have fun blowing up enemy ships. Forget the grind and just enjoy the chaos—that’s where the game truly shines.

name: Harry Potter: Quidditch Champions
detailed_description: Your next chapter takes flight! Immerse yourself in the enchanting world of Quidditch by playing solo or sharing the magic with friends and family. Plus, keep your Gringotts vault closed because there are no microtransactions! THE DELUXE EDITION INCLUDES: Gryffindor House Pack Hufflepuff House Pack Slytherin House Pack Ravenclaw House Pack 2,000 Gold LIVE YOUR QUIDDITCH FANTASY Take to the sky as one of the classic positions—Chaser, Seeker, Keeper, or Beater—each with their own unique play style. Soar into legendary Quidditch arenas, as well as maps that showcase never-before-seen areas of the wizarding world. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PLAY Career Mode: From backyard battles in the Weasley Burrow to high-stakes showdowns at the Quidditch World Cup, rise to become a champion either solo or in online co-op with teams of up to 3 friends. Exhibition Matches: set your teams, map, and difficulty and play alone or on teams of up to 3 in online co-op. Player vs Player: Test your skills in competitive online matches against other Quidditch teams. YOUR QUIDDITCH YOUR WAY Customize Your Approach: Level up and use skill points to tailor your play style for each role. Change your flight style by switching between and leveling up different brooms. Play As Yourself or as Iconic Harry Potter Characters: cosmetic customization options and classic character designs allow you to express your game-time personality.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, Quidditch Champions is a mostly enjoyable experience. The broom handling feels clean, playing the quaffle feels clean, whacking a bludger at the enemy seeker to give your own seeker the opportunity to catch the snitch, when timed right, can be exhilerating. But the bots. I have no idea who thought that adding bots to a game that has the makings of a competitive PvP game was a smart move. Most of the time, they'll play somewhat decently, but they are easily outclassed by even the greenest player on the pitch. This is even worse in the "story mode", if you can call it that, which you can probably run through in about 4 hours, as the bots barely pose a challenge.A lot of bugs also remain, although I have yet to encounter any game breaking ones. Mostly, they just look like QA oversights, e.g. my username being displayed for one of the enemy players at the end of the match, or assists not being counted correctly in the final scoreboard. Nothing too dire, but all this should've been caught.I'm leaving a positive review, because I think there is a healthy core of game is present, which I hope Unbroken can expand upon, especially once they hit their roadmap goal of adding 6v6 ranked PvP. But, even without it, I've still had a good time playing the game. If you wanna support the game, regardless of its flaws, I can recommend purchasing it now, otherwise hold off until 6v6 is implemented, and by then I hope we'll have a healthy competitive community built up around this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Now that I played it for a bit here are my thoughts.GOOD:-The game is very well optimized, you can run it on a very wide range of machines -Controls are very easy to understand yet hard to master-Brooms stats are a nice touch, it makes some brands better tailored for specific roles-You can play with your friends in 3v3 or 6v6 PVP matches but can also play Campaign mode if you just wanna play by yourselves and chill-Cosmetics are lacking but what's already available is pretty cool and started to really get interesting since season 1 started, it's more diverse now (PS1 Hagrid mask my beloved <3)-No microtransactions whatsoever! If you wanna buy or upgrade something, you'll have to play the game like everyone else! Don't worry, it's not that hard to earn money in there, just play and you'll always earn something. This also means there's no P2W stuff so you can get the same stuff as everyone else (minus some cosmetics and brooms from some limited time events of course)!BAD:-Some brooms are way too "meta" and sometimes gives a suspicious advantage because of some bugs, many people uses them and if you don't, you're screwed unless you're very skilled-Matchmaking is very weird at the moment, you sometimes get added mid-game where your team is already losing (like 20 to 80 for example). There's also a chance to get matched with people that have a waaaaay higher level than yours even as a beginner.-Some matches are for some reason extremely laggy beyond usability and you have a high ping for no reason, if it happens just leave and start another match, it's not worth trying to play in these conditions... I have fiber internet and this occurs in 10% of the games I play.-THE CAMERA ALWAYS ZOOMED IN! Why is it like this by default? I don't know!!! But it's definetly annoying to always have to press T to zoom out to be able to see your surroundings. I really wish there was an option to change that.Overall I love this game, it has some annoying problems but they'll slowly disappear as the game gets updated. All this doesn't stop it from being enjoyable though, give it a chance!

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying... "Pass the quaffle!"I'm really enjoying this thus far. The gameplay is accessible for beginners while having the depth that allows for mastery if you put the effort in. You can play all 4 roles (with slightly modified rules from the books/movies that make for a more balanced experience) and they all shine very well. The lack of microtransactions is refreshing and thus far everything appears to be earnable using in-game currency (except for a single-purchase deluxe dlc with a few cosmetics). There's a good variety of cosmetics, equipment and maps to keep things interesting and the gap between equipment/skills when you're first starting and after having put some time in isn't too great that it feels insurmountable but enough that it feels rewarding to specialize in a role. Overall, I'd definitely recommend this game. For Harry Potters fans, it's certainly a rush to play your favorite positions and feel like you're on the quidditch pitch. I think it's also different enough and fun enough that should engage others who are interested in a semi-casual, fantasy sports game that doesn't encourage sweating too much while still rewarding teamwork & skill.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel I have to lead off with the fact that I am a big fan of the Harry Potter franchise and I put an insane number of hours into the original Quidditch World Cup game. I love me some HP. This is the game I have been wanting for the last 20 years. It's not perfect, there are some frustrating bugs that they'll need to work out, and it's a very repetitive game. That said, I really do love it. I do have complaints with the character models that look like fortnite characters. I know this is a dumb complaint, but I hate how everything has started to adopt this crappy cartoon aesthetic that started with fortnite. Not wanting to stop there, they also do a battle pass style of progression with challenges and stuff. I don't care for it. I hate live service games and I believe live service games are overall bad for gaming, but that's another rant. On the bright side, you DO NOT have to pay for the battle pass so like...hooray??, but I still don't like the style of progression it's repetitive and boring. This game a really good interpretation of Quidditch and has made several adjustments to the rules to actually make it playable. They're fantastic. First, the snitch is worth 30pts vs 150 and you play to 100pts vs indefinite. There's also a 7min timer, and they removed the second beater to make it more balanced. These changes are great and the balance to a made up sport is surprisingly good, and a really fun experience. It plays like more complicated rocket league. If you don't like games like LoL, fortnite, hearthstone, dota, or heck even Fifa, it will bore you. You just play quidditch over and over again. Either mulitplayer or in 4-6 game long tournaments. TBH the single player does leave some to be desired (It needs league play like FIFA or Madden, only tournaments gets sooooo tedious lol), but the multiplayer is fun and I have enjoyed it. Game is far from perfect, but it is a very exciting and fun game. Worth the purchase 100% for ME, but would say absolutely worth it on sale. I just hope this game doesn't die because it's live service and I'm unsure if this title is strong enough to compete with so many other live service games.

_childDocuments_.review: Harry Potter: Quidditch Champions is a new chapter in the Harry Potter universe. The game itself is a sports simulator with a huge functionality even at the start of release. The game features both a story campaign, the essence of which is to pass various Quidditch championships in different locations, and multiplayer, which gives us the opportunity to compete with other players.  As I wrote above, the game has a huge number of features, such as a skill tree, various customization, both characters and flight brooms. The balance in the game is excellent, which means that all players are equal to each other and everything is based on how well you play, moreover, the game pleases players with constant events that cause the desire to return to it again and again. And, of course, the thematic soundtrack, which perfectly conveys the atmosphere of the game and brings us back to the moments when we first watched the Harry Potter movies. To summarize, I would like to say that the game is incredibly addictive and exciting, although some aspects still need to be improved.

_childDocuments_.review: After 40 hours of this game I finally need to write a review. This game is a harry potter game which means it should be a gold mine for the developers. However, this game is more coal then gold.GAMEPLAYThe game runs fine ish. It's fast paced and matches only last around 7 minutes tops. Most games end quicker because if your teams seeker gets both snitches that is 60 points right there. The issues I have experienced during games are your character will throw the quaffle backwards instead of forwards if someone is behind you on your team. So your character basically thinks you want to pass it when you dont. Your character will sometimes fly through people and the quaffle when trying to do anything from catch the quaffle to hit someone. Then on the flip side you get hit when nobody is near you. Also, rank wise, even though player account level does not matter, there are a lot of times where a level 50+ is paired with a brand new player due to how small the player numbers are.BUGS BUGS AND ALL THE BUGSAs mentioned before your character will sometimes throw the quaffle the wrong direction or you cant catch/hit someone even though you fly through them. Other bugs include colorblindness filters not working. Characters icons go away so you cant tell who is a teammate and whose not. If playing beater the ball will not lock onto people or will just launch itself the complete wrong direction. Finally, screen flickering and game crashing. Happens quite frequently.PLAYERBASEOr more lack there of... This game does not have a lot of people playing it due to how poorly it was marketed and how it performs. You will run into the same people over and over again especially if the server you are connecting to does not have a large population. The player numbers continue to go down every day. I truly think this game will be dead by Christmas if the developers do not fix its lack of marketing and the bugs.UNLOCKABLESThis game gives out a LOT of free cosmetics which is really nice. I get earning winged keys is suppose to be a process but even after doing the challenges, dailies and weeklies I just now had enough points to unlock someone with them. Would not be shocked if in the future they allow you to use real money to purchase them on top of organic unlocks.OVERALLDo I think its worth picking up? Kinda ish. Despite the bugs, lack of player, and overall issues I still enjoy the game for the most part. I am a massive harry potter fan so maybe that is why I keep coming back? I complain about this game not cause I want it to fail, but because I want it to succeed. If you are not a fan of harry potter or game breaking bugs irritate you then I do not recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: A down vote may be a bit harsh I wish I could give it a neutral recommendation more than a negative. I don't hate this game but it really needs some work yet. Too often I am aiming perfectly forward for a throw and the quaffle just goes in the total opposite direction. The log in tracking for the current event is broken and thus you can't get all the rewards for doing so. While I understand the changes regarding catching the snitch, twice in a match often enough means you're basically playing the other roles for maybe a minute or two and then straight back to seeker. Maybe 10 minute games up to 150 points instead of 7 minutes up to 100? The matches are just too short. Also can we have more than one World Cup Venue? The greatest thing about World Cup back in the day was the unique Pitch's for each Nation (which to be fair there were only 9 teams back then while there are 16 today) what about the Crowd though? How is it in 2004 there was enough attention to detail that you could hear the crowd rooting for you or your opponent's team in a manner fitting the team you played as? Chants for Japan were different than that of England of America of Griffindor. I do love the lack of Microtransactions. If in a couple months further updates roll out and we get more pitches and a bit more polish, I'll happily give a thumbs up. For now? I'd wait if you're on the fence about this game. It's pretty Okay but to be honest I'd rather unbury a PS2 and play World Cup.
