_childDocuments_.review: I'm mixed. I enjoyed playing single player career in the first 10 hours and managed to win the World Cup at Advanced level while still discovering how to play at my best. After the first enthusiasm I started to lose interest, to notice the defects. Even the multiplayer didn't change my mind and I'm not so interested to keep playing.It's not a matter of content. For sure a longer career would keep me more interested, but that's not the problem. I would keep playing the multiplayer or wait for updates if my interest were still high. The problem is the gameplay.They changed some rules. It's ok, I'm not purist. I can enjoy new rules if they give more fun, but that's not the case.In the old PS2 game Quidditch World Cup, catching the snitch ends the match and gives 150 points. But the snitch appears after long time from the beginning, and in the meanwhile it's easy to score hundreds points. So, when the snitch comes in and someone catches it, the result of the match depends not only on the 150 points but also on the points earned with the quaffle, precisely on the points difference between the teams.The snitch is the crucial event that ends the match and gives you more chance to win and it's exciting. However it's too easy to score goal with the quaffle, so you get tired soon. That's the defect of the old Quidditch game. What if on the contrary it were too hard to score goal? You would have less fun again, you would get frustrated. That's the defect of Quidditch Champions. Match is too short, it ends in 5 minutes, or ends when one of the teams gets 100 points. However you're lucky when your three chasers score 5 or 6 goals in the whole match, that makes around 50 or 60 points! It means that if you play as one of the chaser, don't expect to score more than one or two goals on the average! It's frustrating and boring! The snitch comes in two or three times and each time gives you 30 points when you catch it.  Chasing snitch is as important as scoring the goals. Chasing snitch needs longer time, more than one minute for each chase and it's hard to catch it everytime. On average you take 60 points from the snitch while spending more than half match to chase it. You can see that developers gave the same importance to quaffle and snitch, in opposition to the original rules. Chasing the snitch keeps you engaged for almost the whole match, while in the books is a rare but crucial event.The lack of crucial event makes the game less catchy. While chasing the snitch for the whole match is boring on the long run. At the same time scoring very few goals in the whole match is frustrating. It's not the only problem.In QC there is quite no teamwork, no strategy. I was thinking it was a matter of low AI of your team mates. Not the case; even in multiplayer mode with human players it is the same. The very huge pitch is another problem, it's too dispersive. Broom's speed is too low in comparison to the huge pitch despite the upgrades. It's too hard to tackle the opponents in such huge pitch. Most of time you see your opponents or team mates as little dots on the far distance; sometimes you cannot understand what's happening and where the quaffle is. Sometimes you exchange the dot-like players with quaffle or bludgers; it's very confusing because of similar colors and too small icons. Very hard to pass the quaffle to your mates. As you see, more frustration.They put just one beater in the team; and one bludger for each team, red and blue. The beater can summon his own bludger and lock it onto his bat; that's weird. On such huge pitch wouldn't it be better to have two beaters for each team trying to intercept two free flying bludgers as in the original concept? I don't know, weird choice indeed. However the beater is the easiest role, less frustrating. You can play as the keeper but it's not so fun, just as in books, that's not a defect of the game, it's the same in real soccer. To make it more interesting, developers added a new feature: the keeper can summon magic rings along the pitch to give energy to his team mates. However it adds more confusion.To score many more goals before the crucial snitch appearance would be more fun and the golden snitch would put end to the match but would not always decide the final result. At most you would calibrate the game slightly decreasing the points. It would be great to add special moves with the broom or combos for different shots or combined strategy with your team mates. Shrinking the pitch or making the players biggerwould be a good ideaI give thumb up because there are no microtransactions and had some fun at the beginning. Playing against the characters of the movies is very cool. But I think we could have a better Quidditch gameplay. Maybe there is room for a major update.EDIT: I noticed another problem: there are no penalties. Contacts between players are so rare because of huge pitch, so developers decided to not put penalties. There is no referee! Tbc, where is Madame Hootch? This detracts to fun. It would be better to have more contacts with opponents and have penalties, as in books. Again a problem of gameplay. Developers can do better.

_childDocuments_.review: Quidditch as it was first introduced in the Harry Potter series is a strange game thats balanced to make the hero Harry Potter good in sports at school. I look forward to see future customisations.- Online only causes a suprising count of different server side issues, but devs already fixed some without client updates in decent time.Negative:- Online only. I doubt they will ever add an offline mode, altough I hope they do for game conservation.- Too few voicelines will make you hate the commentators.- rare crashes- some progress is currently not being tracked correctlyEdit: The last Patch boosted progression on the season pass. Stuff unlocks at a good speed now.I hope the developer Unbroken Studios continues fixing current issues of the game, because I enjoy the game a lot. I doubt I will grind this game for thousands of hours, but I'm looking forward to play a few matches a week for a long time.For Harry Potter fans that want a casual PvP sports game, this is a good pick. _childDocuments_.review: I’m really glad I bought the game. I think the Quidditch feeling has been captured very well, and in the 5 hours I’ve played so far, I’ve had a lot of fun. _childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the HP universe, this review may be pretty biased so take it with a grain of salt. I will also focus on the Multiplayer experience since I've found the Solo Campain not to be worth mentioning. Online gameplay is split into 3 roles:- Keeper & Chaser- Beater & Chaser- Seeker & ChaserMany people were ranting about this concept prior to the release of the game, but it works surprisingly well in my experience and opinion. You can switch between both of these roles seamlessly while the remaining role is taken over by AI. The AI is, for the most part, pretty well balanced. I've seen AI chasers score in "high level" lobbies (Level ~45 as of writing this review). The only AI role that seems way too weak is the Seeker, but if you pick that role and decide to leave it to the AI, you're trolling anyway. The mechanics are all pretty basic. People who compare this game to Rocket League are hopefully referring to the graphics and and UI of the unlockables, otherwise they can't really be taken serious. However, once you get more experienced in the game, all these mechanics that are basic in itself, can go pretty in-depth thanks to skill trees that allow various playstyles.The unlockable cosmetics are all free, there are no micro transactions, but the amount and variety is pretty lean while the time it takes to unlock them is pretty absurd.They've announced a 6v6 mode and a Defence Against the Dark Arts update later this year, so that sounds promising. Overall, I'm personally enjoying the game a lot.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game during one of the beta tests, and it was incredibly fun. It was, as I have seen other comments remark, very similar to Rocket League. My friends and I would periodically remind each other of the release date when it was officially announced, that's how excited we were. I bought it on release day, which was my mistake, because they somehow backtracked and made the game WORSE.Instead of a full party of friends to play a fast-paced, competitive game, able to swap roles among your team if people are doing poorly / not having fun in a role, it somehow became a 3v3 with AI bots that you have to manage and control by swapping between separate characters on the field... I have no idea how they got from the beta to here. They say they have a "roadmap" for 5v5 and 6v6, when the beta test I participated in clearly was centered around that very concept. I strongly recommend NOT purchasing the game until they either fix this, or update the game to a more complete state. TL:DR; beta was much more fun, official release did not deliver on what beta presented

_childDocuments_.review: I play tested this game about a year ago and in its current state I simply can't recommend this game to anyone. The original play test I did ran 5v5 multiplayer games with what felt to be extremely balanced matchmaking. In the current state of this game, this has been changed to 3v3 multiplayer (keeper, beater, and seeker each also playing as a chaser) with horrible AI to pick up whatever role you are not currently active in. To add to this, teams now have a skill point progression system to level up characters abilities and broom stats in game. While I think this was a nice addition to the story mode portion of the game, my team found that these features also carried over into multiplayer without any form of MMR based matchmaking to compensate. The entirety of my group's playtime consisted of being paired against teams with faster brooms, health regen, and damage making for what felt like an unfair curb stomp every match.The only solution I could find to this problem is either completing the single player campaign to gain a ton of team XP, or continue losing online matches while I invest the 1-2 skill points I earn per match into a team of 6 characters each with at least 15 points worth of skill trees. The entire reason I purchased this was for the simple, fair multiplayer that I experienced during the testing, but now I am finding that I will need to complete a bunch of extra hours into other portions of the game that I do not care about to even have a balanced chance at winning an online match. I hope that the devs continue to work on improving the multiplayer functions but idk why I should pay 30 dollars to have a game make me this angry when Dota2, Overwatch, and Rocket League are completely free.

The old review below is obsolete.This game has 0 Anti Cheat (Cheaters/Hackers running rampage)The servers are unstable and can be DDOSd during the match.The balance is so bad it's not even a joke.How this game is even managed by the Devs is a mystery to themselfes.So after some time it's time for a review.Harry Potter: Quidditch Champions is best described as a mix of Rocket League and FIFA.You target is to reach 100 points before the opponent or reach time limit of 7 minutes.There are four roles:Chaser - you use the Quaffle to make goals for 10 pointsBeater -  the Bludger is your friend and used to disturb/knock out oponents for a short timeKepper - you're the one who protects the goalChaser - every now and then you're there to chase the Snitch for 30 pointsAnd i can't recommend the game in this state right now.This is to some simple fact that two roles are not well designed and very fun to play.The chaser is most times useless and only usefull when the snitch is in the field. And if that happens you fly in circles chasing the snitch and trying to be faster than the oponent. Other than that there is not much to do. Which is kinda meh. They can't do it much better I guess.But the real problem is the keeper.The chasers are able to make moves and making goals where you can't really do anything.Your counterplay is extremely limited and you can be right next to the opponent but your kicks to disrupt them are not registered! Your "power safe" barely does anything due to the fact that the chaseres can fly around your goals without consequences and make stunts where this move is practically useless to prevent a goal.This position needs a hard tweak or rework to be enjoyable.But the hitboxes/hitreg are a general problem in the game in my opinion. Noticed it multiple times during matches. You have to be in the opponent so that the hits register and are doing what they are supposed to do.Another problem is the AI in the 3vs3. This AI is bad, not absolutely horrible but plain bad. During campaign they can cheat with the AI so it's not that obvious but in the 3vs3 it's very obvious. This need some proper work.You notice that with the beater too. You can take out the opposing AI very simple during the matches since they barely react to the incoming Bludger. Especially the keeper is an easy target for that.Oh and don't mention the gameplay breaking bugs like not able to change your position. Weird flying Quaffles. Missing target lock. Wrong recognition of thrown Quaffles or Bludgers and a few more.And don't play this game with a gamepad. Mouse and Keyboard are way superior in terms of agility and aiming at goals. So better not tray that. You'll have 0 fun with a gamepad maybe you can get some use as keeper out of a gamepad but that's it.Besides all of that you'll have sometimes random crashes for unknown reasons or you're stuck in an infinite loading scree.Another massive problem is the netcode. Your opponents are sometimes warping around for some distance because the netcode can't tell you exactly where they are. This is a no go! This is extremely noticeable while playing vs people overseas or other server regions. Their servers are a clusterf... right now. Missing attacks on other players, disappearing quaffels from your chaser and other stuff. What is this shi*?This is a decent game, don't get me wrong. You can have some fun from time to time but to be really succesful this game has some way to go.So an update after the patch:It still remains the same. Keeper is extremely unfun and mostly useless.Even if they have "buffed" the position it still needs a hard rework or tweak to be considered acceptable in terms of fun and gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: successfully captures the magic and excitement of the beloved Harry Potter series. The game's nostalgic appeal is undeniable, with its faithful recreation of the Hogwarts schools and iconic quidditch elements. The absence of microtransactions is a refreshing change, allowing players to enjoy the game without feeling pressured to spend extra money.However, the game's gameplay could benefit from some improvements. The forced role-switching during matches can disrupt the flow of the game. Allowing players to choose their preferred role before the match starts would provide a more tailored experience. Additionally, the difficulty level feels too easy, and the AI-controlled bots could be more challenging. While the golden snitch mechanic adds an interesting element, it would be more satisfying if catching it could directly end the game while being really difficult, making it a more impactful goal. Finally, the camera and orientation options could use some refinement to provide a more immersive experience.Overall, Harry Potter: Quidditch Champions is a fun and nostalgic game that fans of the series will appreciate. However, the repetitive gameplay and lack of challenge may limit its appeal to casual players.Rating 3.5/5 Stars.

_childDocuments_.review: As a long-time fan of the Harry Potter series, I was thrilled to dive into Harry Potter Quidditch Champions, and I must say, it did not disappoint. The game beautifully captures the magic and excitement of Quidditch, bringing back nostalgic memories of Harry Potter Quidditch World Cup. The controls and gameplay feel refreshingly familiar yet modern, allowing players to jump right into the action. Initially, I found the controls a bit different from the older game, but after a short adjustment period, they became intuitive and fluid.Currently, the game offers an engaging 3v3 online mode, which has been a blast to play. However, I'm really looking forward to the upcoming 6v6 matches, which I believe will add an even deeper layer of strategy and excitement. One of the standout features of Harry Potter Quidditch Champions is the absence of microtransactions. All in-game items and upgrades must be earned through gameplay, which is a welcome change in today’s gaming landscape.While the game is already very enjoyable, there are a few things I hope the developers will consider for future updates. An online ranking system, whether for individual players or teams, would add a competitive edge that many players, including myself, would appreciate. Additionally, I’d love to see the point cap for matches increased from 100 to something higher, like 250, to allow for longer, more intense games. The current 6-minute time limit is reasonable, but extending the points cap would make the matches feel even more rewarding.Overall, Harry Potter Quidditch Champions is an incredibly fun and well-crafted game that brings the beloved sport of Quidditch to life. I’m excited to see what the future holds for this game and what other surprises the developers have in store for us.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:-Fun Gameplay-Graphics are simple but look beautiful-Crossplay-No Microtransactions-Runs really well, physics aren't buggyCons:I think they rushed the release and didn't have time to implement all of feedback from the final beta, but that doesn't make it a bad game. It has a lot of potential, I experienced it firsthand during the first beta. That was SO fun. I hope the devs make the right decision and listen to the community more now that the game is out.EDIT:It has been over a month since release, and the devs have done nothing to fix the game or give any incentive to keep playing this game. They keep doing timed events and double xp weekends to entice players to play again, but this week I saw the concurrent players dip into the double digits. Only competitive players play this game now, and there is no competitive gamemode. Meaning if you're a casual player that only has so much time to game in a week, you'll be screwed over in matchmaking when you go up against the same 50 players that organize teams on discord etc. All random matchmaking lumps you with other noobs. There is no balance and after seeing how much constructive criticism was given on the discord, the devs just seem to not care or wanna listen. Adding 6v6 wont even save the game because of how many people stopped playing. 6v6 is just going to ruin matchmaking even further now. So no I will not recommend this game until they stop acting like ubisoft and activision's lovechild. I cant even think of a way to revive this game anymore.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, the game is still enjoyable! But I would recommend gathering a team for online play as so far, the matchmaking system isn't kind to anyone. You'll sometimes experience 3-4 matches in a row against obvious better players . These needs to be resolved as soon as possible, as I can already notice  people quitting the game for losing 10 matches in a row because of opponents who are more experienced. It ruins the fun for most of those players.That said, if you do get a little experience, it's a super fun game to play among friends. The community itself is pretty friendly and there are LOADS of customization options to choose from. Good to know too is that, yes: the game makes use 'Seasons', but you can also get all past seasonal items in the Market. Don't worry about missing out.The developers, so far, have been pretty responsive to the feedback and gave updates along with them. However, I do feel like I'm still playing a half-baked game. The controls are OK, but there are some questionable choices when it comes to action animations not being able to cancel out & sometimes too small/big hitboxes. I do experience lag in some matches, resulting in some questionable matches as the Quaffle sometimes get teleported across the pitch. The game is fun, yes: but you should also know the game is not finished yet. I feel like the developer 'Unbroken Studios' got too little time from it's publisher 'Warner Bros. Games'. But, as mentioned before: the developers are working hard to make the game better with every update. And they deliver.  Yes, it's worth your money. Especially when you have played Quidditch World Cup in 2003. Nostalgia is definitely there and the game really captivates Quidditch in a magical way. That said: If you haven't watched Harry Potter, I genuinely think you can like this game as it perfectly explains Quidditch.  Think of it as soccer, but more violent and on flying broomsticks.The current 3vs3 matchup, and switching roles with bots, is actually pretty fun. I can see it as 'training' until we receive the update for 6vs6 by the end of 2024. My worry for this game was that the positions  weren't diverse enough to enjoy for a full long match. I can safely say that this is not the case. Every position on the Quidditch field feels wildly different, and I can already see people go ALL IN on their abilities to be the best.

_childDocuments_.review: OK so, here goes. Yes, I am a Potterhead, yes, I spent a ridiculous amount of time playing HP Quidditch World Cup when I was a kid, yes, I was expecting a somewhat of a "remake" of the aforementioned game. The review may be slightly nostalgia-biased, but I will try my best to keep the bias down to earth. TLDR belowA few words about HP Quidditch World Cup:This is not HP Quidditch World Cup (let's call it HP:QWC, so I don't have to retype the whole name everytime). HP:QWC focused on single player, it was super-arcade-y and relied on cutscene-y gameplay with powerups (tackles, beaters, team specials - oh and some teams had clearly better ones - ). Fun back then, but completely unbalanced and clunky for online play (oh I tried... . I honestly don't see how you would be able to make the expected high-octane action necessary for today's average gamer and have the original HP:QWC mechanics work. Although, I do think that the "snitch boost gage" was a cool mechanic and felt like the snitch race was an amazing culmination to the match determening the winner in 99% of the cases.About HP: Quidditch Champions (HP:Champs)Overall:The game feels fluid, animations are cool, broomstick flight feels very fun (love the drift mechanic) - I recommend inversing Y-axis from default, feels more natural. It's dynamic, chaser gameplay feels right. The quaffle is ACTUALLY A BALL that when fumbled can fall to the ground and be intercepted in mid-air. I've played almost 6 hours and I loved every second of it. I can see how this will eventually get repetitive, but hey - I had fun, and that's what matters. Can it be an amazing multiplayer experience in its current state, probably not yet, let's see where they go from here.Here are my thoughts about all positions:I actually feel like I am playing a chaser, passing is fun (once you unlock the charge perk). Fast, dynamic, you somewhat get the feel of the chaotic battle for the quaffle. Frequent intercepts, tackles and bumps all add to the fun of the game. Probably the most fleshed out position in the game. However, controller control scheme has some questionable choices, Y+Right stick for hand off pass --> very awkward thing to actually do. Having Y to be call for pass AND one-off kick (final perk in attack for chaser) is weird, since one-off overthrows the call for pass, it's a pity as the one-off kick is the only way to do any sort of combos as chasers (arguably one of the very fun mechanics from HP:QWC. Give me a way to better see my teammates and give me an opportunity to combo passes for more attack options and I'll be maining chaser.My second favorite, different controls, different movement, can be very interesting from a competitive point of view. The kick and defense is a fun design. A close second favorite.OK, I can see you are building towards a 6v6 experience, the seeker needs to have something to do during the downtime and the gameplay must feel engaging. OK, let's not overpower them and knock it down to 30 points. I CAN see how that makes sense. You had a choice, either make seeker a minigame and finish the match on that, or make them an actual playable position and give it something to do. Let's be honest, in a real qudditch setting (movie real... duh), what does Harry Potter do before he spots the snitch, just kinda fly about looking for the little bugger, dodging an occasional bludger and avoiding the Quaffle chaos below... So yeah, choices were made. I will quote a review I saw earlier, it doesn't feel like a race, I think the Seeker role can benefit from a roundtable discussion at the devs' office to see how they can make it feel more fun and less of a chore. If we eventually play 6v6, a good team of chasers can easily outscore the 30points in simple goals. I don't know... it's weird. When playing solo it seems like the bots are playing bad chaser game while you are catching the snitch and barely score anything.By far the worst imho. First of all, why is he alone? What ever happened with a pair of beaters? Don't want to make it 7v7, fine... suggestion: have the beater role control two characters? The one engaged with the bludger and one not engaged with the bludger. Second, summon the bludger? SUMMON? That son-of-a-gun-whack-your-head-off-crazy-a**-metal-whack-a-ball should not listen to anyone and just wildly fly around the field. Beaters should be able to hit in a predictable direction and kind of ping pong it between each other and have an opportunity to skill-shot snipe other players. The beater as it is now, feels useless, like one bludger hit doesn't knock the player of the broom, the cooldown to summon (ffs...) the bludger feels long, so you have to catch up to the chaser carrying the quaffle to kick them? Come on.. they already score by then.I have my opinions about this game, some worse than others. However, I still had a lot of fun, I will get my potterhead friends and I will play with them and we will have fun. I cross my fingers and hope that the devs will make the necessary reworks, and then I'll have more fun. I do recommend this game, it's a welcome change of pace, and for once, it actually feels very polished upon release. I do have a juicy rig, so this might not be the case for everyone, but I haven't had any problem running the game.Thank you for reading :)TLDR: Fun game, I recommend, fly your broomstick and vibe out. Has its shortcomings, not all positions feel equally fun,

_childDocuments_.review: Game is fine-it's just boring, it's incredible bare bones, not much to do other than zip up one size of the field, score 10 points, zip down the other side of the field, score 10 points. Don't bother wasting 25 pounds on this game yet. I have no idea how people are recommending this game and saying it's worth the money. There are 6 playable roles however you can only play 3v3 so you have to keep switching between 2 roles over and over which is really stupid-bots take over in the meantime and they are complete garbage so you're constantly scrambling to cover every single role. As soon as a chaser makes a break, that's it-you have no mechanics to effectively defend (because you're having to switch roles 24/7) and scoring passed a keeper is so stupidly easy if you play with a mouse because you can change which goal you're going to shoot into on a dime. People are saying "no microtransactions is a W"-no it isn't?? The lack of a poor mechanic does not make the game good. That's like saying "it didn't crash for me, therefore it is a good game". Fundamentally this game is a yawn festival-the easiest way to win in online is just to dash up with your chaser then reset and do it again over and over. The beater is useless, the keeper is useless if you're playing against someone with half a brain cell and the seeker isn't even involved with the core game-they're off doing a mini game in the background whilst the match is happening. Maybe it will be better later in the year with 6v6 but for the time being this game should be F2P-it does not have the depth to warrant the price and you can discover ever inch of the game within a MAX of 2 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a lot of fun! Its mechanics are simple, but getting to grips with all the nuances can take a few matches. However, those who have played “Harry Potter: Quidditch World Cup” or have experience with “Rocket League” will adapt quickly. It offers a few co-op and PvP modes, and best of all, there are no microtransactions, at least for now. Everything you need can be earned by playing, accumulating coins and keys to buy items and skins in the store, or unlocking them by reaching certain levels. Here are some suggestions to improve the game experience. 1 - 6 vs 6 mode: Implementing a 6 vs 6 mode where each player controls a position can add an interesting layer to the game. 2 - Ranked matches: Less experienced players may get frustrated with the game’s learning curve. Implementing a ranking system can help balance the matches, providing a fairer and less intimidating experience for new players. 3 - You can’t fly high enough: You can’t fly too high and you can’t fly out of the stadium. At least for the seekers, it would be nice to unlock them outside of the field during the chase for the snitch, especially considering the scenes from the movie. The game is working well, despite some bugs in the initial interface that will probably be fixed in future updates. The game also needs more content, after a few hours you find yourself collecting coins to buy something in the store, but there is not much interesting, we need more items, more customization for the characters. Overall I recommend it, it is a very cool game and worth checking out!

_childDocuments_.review: I did my waiting! Vingt years of it, in Azkaban!I 'member when this game was first announced and 'twas one of the happiest days of my life for it. Now that they've let the games begin, I can dedicate my time to the sport I've dreamt of playing since childhood.Keep in mind, however, this is more or less the same Quidditch, for now, as the game you grew to love in the books and movies. There are, however, a few rules that differ. First off, the Golden Snitch no longer wins the entire match. It only awards your team 30 points out of the winning score of 100, which is another change itself, rather than 150 winning each game. Also, each team is only 5 members, rather than 7. Furthermore, until 6v6 is added later this year, 'tis actually 3v3, where each player shares their two roles with a bot.Worth the price? Entirely. Yes, there are in-game currencies. Yes, you can earn 'em. No, you cannot buy 'em. 'Tis the price we pay for this paid game, rather free-to-play. While, yes, you can purchase the Harry Potter: Quidditch Champions Launch Bundle by supporting a Twitch streamer, that's the only loophole, if you will.In my experience, there is never a dull moment and I'm always having a thrill! As a Seeker main, I wish I didn't have to start off as Chaser, but I understand the changes as they are for now. Here's to 6v6!

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the Quidditch sport from the Harry Potter universe, there's much to appreciate here.Gameplay & Mechanics: The game features 6v6 matches where you can play various roles—Chaser, Keeper, Beater, or Seeker. Each role is essential to the match's outcome, and the game does a good job of balancing these roles. The Seeker role, however, feels more like a mini-game rather than a crucial part of the match, which may disappoint those who loved the thrill of chasing the Golden Snitch. (However I personally do find in enjoyable, but I do see that there is room for improvements) That said, the gameplay is intuitive and engaging, though the controls, particularly for flying, might take some getting used to. Graphics & Visuals: Visually, the game is stunning. The maps are beautifully crafted, and the fast-paced motion effects add to the immersive experience. The customization options, though currently limited, allow you to create and personalize your character, with potential for more variety as the game evolves.Online Play & Features: Currently, PvP matches include AI players, which some might find disappointing. However, a future update promises full 6v6 human matches, which could significantly enhance the tactical depth of the game. The lack of an offline mode and custom matches might be a letdown for some, but the absence of microtransactions is a big win in today’s gaming landscape. All items are purely cosmetic and can be unlocked through gameplay, giving players a sense of achievement as they progress.Community & Longevity: The game has a solid foundation with great mechanics. However, the community seems divided on certain aspects, with some players frustrated by the game’s presence of AI in PvP matches. Nonetheless, if you’re a Quidditch fan, this game is worth trying, especially as it continues to evolve with more updates and content.Final Verdict: Harry Potter: Quidditch Champions offers a fun and visually impressive experience with a few rough edges. While it may not yet reach the heights of a perfect Quidditch game, it's certainly enjoyable and holds promise for future improvements. If you're a fan of Quidditch or looking for a new competitive game, this one is worth a spin.

_childDocuments_.review: At first I was really looking forward to this game and the first few hours were a lot of fun. But unfortunately that's it. The game is quite buggy and the developers take a long time to fix bugs. By the time they actually manage to fix some major bugs, there are already several new bugs in the game that make a match simply frustrating.Another problem is how incredibly long it takes for new content to appear and then it's already uninteresting again after 5 minutes. Here 1-2 skins and emotes and that's it. This is a far cry from a high-quality service game. The game started with only one mode and it took almost 3 months until the community's request was finally met and a 6v6 mode was added. I can understand that the development of a new mode takes a lot of time but at the same time it leaves the impression that the developers really assumed that 1 generic mode would be enough and didn't really plan for the future. The new mode is nice, but comes way too late considering that the game was already dead after less than 2 weeks. And why? Because there is still no skill-based matchmaking, which would be much more important. Nobody enjoys being taken apart by a player who is 300 levels higher and plays nothing else but this game. Probably one of the main reasons why the game is dead. I don't need to talk about the “campaign” either. It's pretty thin, but that's ok considering that it's mainly intended as a multiplayer title. But if you can't even do that then I wonder what the point of this game is. Grinding the campaign for a few cosmetics is definitely not it. The game would have had so much potential if it had been released with more content and if more than just cosmetics were added, quite a shame.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing for 20+ hours, I find the game very fun and engaging. It feels like it could become one of the competitive games in its genre. There's so much potential for cosmetic content that they could draw from.For now, I hate to say it, but I do see the potential for this game to struggle. _childDocuments_.review: I can no longer recommend this game. You'll get around 10-20 hours of entertainment, but it's lacking in so many areas.  First of all, why is this game ONLINE ONLY? Licences will eventually fall off, causing the game to go offline, and you'll no longer be able to play at all. Even single player content, and characters take hours on end to get one, so you'll do all this grinding just for it to disappear.  I've played a good mix of single players and multiplayer, both solo and in a party. The campaign and single player modes are way too easy, even on the hardest difficulty. I can go 100-0 without much effort, and if you just sit as a keeper, you can just let your AI team do everything and still win. I'm only around level 21 on the rewards pass, and you can't get all the vaulted characters at the moment, and some require so much grinding it's not fun at all.  Online play is a massive miss, and it sucks because some challenges for characters require you to play it, and you'll find bad connections or massively higher or lower level players who just mess around and don't help at all, and finally it will crash a lot or kick your party back to the main menu for no reason.  At the time of this review, the game doesn't have any microtransactions, but I feel 2 things could happen, and that's 1 they will add micro transactions and leave the game at full price, or the player base will start to die off, and they will swap it to free to play with microtransactions and offer people who paid maybe some credits and skins.  I regret buying the game even as a massive Harry Potter fan it feels more like a free-to-play title and is poorly put together, at least at the time of this review.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good but I have a bone to pick with a lot of these reviews.The people saying that the snitch rule change ruins the game simply don't know what they're talking about from a game balance point of view. I very much hold the opinion that if the snitch acted the way it did in the book/movies the game would be much worse for people looking to play seeker and for the chasers/keepers (I think beaters would stay relatively similar/happy). I am a huge Harry Potter fan, but I will say it: EVEN IN THE BOOKS/MOVIES THE SNITCH IS A STUPID RULE. Chasers go up 100-0? Doesn't matter. Same thing would be the case in this game. There would be so much pressure put on the seeker that it would be the single most strongest role in the game and its not very close. The snitch rule changes WORK for a competitive multiplayer game. Anyone saying otherwise has their nostalgia glasses on wayyyy too tight. All that being said, if the devs want to release a single player mode with the original snitch rules I think that would be a good compromise. Now that the rant is over, the game is a lot of fun. The controls feel really great and flying feels really good and responsive. All the roles behave exactly as you would expect (snitch changes aside) and I feel like I am playing each role how I would if I was in universe. The chasers mad dash for the quaffle and sprint up and down the field is as chaotic as the books made it sound. Being a beater and being a human bludger is easily the most fun. The keeper, even though its by far the hardest role, got some nice changes to where you aren't just sitting back doing nothing all game, and it feels good to make saves like how Ron describes in the books. The seeker (my personal favorite role) is exactly what you would expect. You fly around the field chasing the snitch ignoring everything else, weaving through the other players, dodging bludgers (you better get good at it if you want to play seeker). This game scratches the itch for actually playing quidditch way more than the early 2000s game did. I think a lot of the complaints about the "lack of teamplay" is more of a side effect of people just picking up and learning the game. When you get paired with players that actually want to play as a team, it is extremely fun to play with, and extremely frustrating to play against. Also, being able to swap between roles helps keep the game fresh and always gives you something to do. I understand the desire for the 6v6 PvP from the play test (which has been confirmed to be added later this year/early next year), but 3v3 with role swapping keeps the game fast paced and reduces your downtime if you're not a chaser.Rocket League on brooms is a really fun game and I am excited to see what comes of it. I will admit that the $30 price tag is maybe a bit steep in its current state, but with the current road map (and no microtransactions) I am confident it will be worth that in the very near future. If you're on the fence, definitely check this game out.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, so this is actually the first time I´ve ever written a review for a game here on Steam because I just have to say a few things about this game.First of all, I was a MASSIVE fan of Quidditch World Cup that I played on Gamecube 20 years ago. The teams were awesome, the maps were all unique and cool and the gameplay was damn near without equal when it comes to sports games (because yes, this is absolutely a sports game). So when I heard they were gonna make a new one I was really excited about it.Now, a few days of playing and I have to say that I have mixed feelings about this game. I like some parts for sure, but other things are just not good. For example, I don´t like the new rules for Quidditch in this game. One Beater? First to 100 points wins? The Golden Snitch not only gets the team a meagre 30 points, but it comes back again and again? No, I didn´t like any of those things. The whole point of catching the GS is that it´s SUPPOSED to be very difficult! It´s tiny, quick and barely visible, not to mention that the two seekers have to find that thing in all the mayhem around them. And I hate the fact that the tournaments are so damn short. Why can I become the World Champion in less than 10 games, meaning I´ve not even faced half the teams available in the game so far? That´s just lazyI do like the fact that there are no micro-transactions at all. I think everybody were quite surprised to hear those news and I´m glad they actually kept that word. I also like the artstyle, which I´m sure others will disagree on, but go back to Quidditch World Cup and you won´t exactly see the most realistic artstyle there either. But the sad fact is that so far this game is underwhelming and feels incomplete. It needs the classic rules back, at least as an option, where the Seekers get some kind of bonus to their search after the Chasers score or something like that. You know, make sure the entire team directly and indirectly helps their Seeker find the GS. I also want way more maps. I mean, having different skins for Hogwarts and Weasleys home is not nearly enough. Every team should have their own Quidditch field.So as it stands now, despite the fun gameplay, I honestly can´t give this game higher than 6/10, which is kind of generous to be honest. I hope things get better real fast or this game is going to die before New Years Eve.

_childDocuments_.review: Quite honestly I was looking forward to this game and was truly excited. After playing it it has MANY glaring issues and is not at all fun to me.Firstly, the tutorial is unnecessarily long. They have you play a few mechanics of each position but make you play a game against bots after EVERY player position tutorial. It would make far more sense in going through each position then do ONE game at the end of all of them.The matches themselves have almost zero skill ceiling. They artificially lower your skill level to "simulate" being bad at quidditch by locking away game mechanics and making your character SO SLOW. The matches are 6v6 but you are matched with 2 other real players and 3 bots per team where you can switch between a bot you alone control. You are FORCED to play chaser and a different role even though you may not like chaser and you cannot play seeker until later in the match.The bots programming are worse than sports games from 2002 and are easily broken, exploited, and manipulated. I have seen many instances where the keeper was facing the wrong direction  or the AI was doing synchronized flying around the ball but never touching it. Every aspect of this game is buggy, even so much so that matchmaking sometimes puts one of your teammates on the other team and it being 7v5.The skill tree system is fine other than the actual skills. when you get enough points to get all the skill levels, you finally feel fast enough to play the game but there are skills in the trees that just make no sense and do not create a balanced and fair environment (an example is with seekers where if you fly through the rings first you remove the ability for the other seeker to get boost, effectively bullying them out of the match.The game is really just a horribly buggy team death match game with a quidditch skin and I absolutely hate the game for that. It's really boring and even single player is only 3-4 hours long (total) with 4 different cups you can play that they expect you to do SIXTEEN times to unlock all the content against really badly coded bots.Also as a note- I was a part of the play tests and spent over 100 hours in them, I do not love what they released.

_childDocuments_.review: A really strange experience. You can't free look. Can't bind R joystick to look around figure where your people are. There's little visibility of team mates, very frantic ways of identifying them. There's no mini-map. You're passing to people directly in your fov whatever altitude you're at. The aim/lock/pass system has a very short range, quickly and erratically moves between targets at same distance. You can't just play one role without worrying what happens in the other. Calling for pass is the same as cam lock, and there's no effective rebind without losing something else. So you're double clicking it? The broom control and camera movement is also just something. I thought you were making a game, like a high quality game equipped for competitive play. Characters keep saying these cringe things, mid/post game I don't understand why these dialogues are necessary. For example, end of a game the announcer decides to thank her deceased father without whom she wouldn't be there in the commentary box. What? The individual celebrations post win are dances and back flips with a very broadway-ish landing, arms spread apart big toothy smile eye contact with camera. Makes me feel this game is targeted at a much younger audience, possibly teens, and tries to be an incredibly inclusive and wholesome experience rich with overly cheery characters and childish dialogues. This is incomplete and strange. Maybe I'll purchase again in a few dozen patches. Or not idk.

_childDocuments_.review: ----DAY ONE REVIEW:----This game has serious potential. It will be interesting to see what they make of it. A new game dynamic with new mechanics that create a new gaming experience.If they play their cards right, it wouldn't surprise me if this became the new Rocket League in terms of competitive play. No competitive play as of yet so I hope they add it in in the future. So far, so good.----EDIT: 400 hours update----I am changing my recommendation from Yes to NoThis game would suit casual gamers looking to invest a few hours over a few weeks but that is really all it is suited for. Given that, I would not recommend it even to casual gamers.GOOD:- Soundtrack. It's well composed and fitting with the world. Props for that.BAD:- Everything else:PRICEThe price is outrageous for the content within. This is marketed as a campaign with an online mode and yet neither are suitable or worthy of their titles.CAMPAIGNThe "campaign" consists of 3 cups - The Hogwarts Cup, The Triwizard Cup & The World Cup. That is all. There are a total of 7 maps in the game. A few of these have day/night variations. The opponents all have the same cosmetics merely with different textures applied for their respective teams. There are no changes in gameplay or tactics across teams. Challenges consist of stretching out the game as much as possible. Including requiring you to play the same World Cup as each of the 16 teams available. These challenges and career objectives are lazy, repetitive fillers.SKILLS:This will be debatable from person to person. Some like, some hate. Essentially character have skill points earned by levelling up which allow different types of perks. In of itself, not a bad idea for a campaign, BUT, this carries across to Online too. Meaning if you started a new account and jumped into online, there is no physical way of matching higher levels with their abilities. The same goes for brooms. You level up your brooms and each broom has different stats assigned, but these also carry into online. Not only do different brooms have different stats which you cannot transmog so are forced to use a broom that appears ugly because of it's stats, but across all available brooms, these stats are not evenly distributed. The result is only ONE broom is optimal across EVERY role type - the FIREBOLT. Which, without advancing to a certain stage in the game or paying for the Early Access, you will not have access to.ONLINEThis is where the majority of the problems lie. It is completely unstable. Crashes are frequent. Disconnects are common. Desync issues are in every game. Server ping is shockingly poor. Anyone outside of NA is done for. The issues are so vast that they cannot be listed here but many are packing it in until significant changes are made.GAMEPLAYA handful of the mechanics simply don't work as intended. Target locks fail, switch to other characters, binds stop working mid game, inputs simply don't register. As a Triple A IP, this is absolutely pathetic. The studios in charge are incompetent and should not be in their position. The AI is enraging and players are avoiding using them in any way to somehow ensure they have an idea of what plays to make. The UI glitches either not appearing or not going away and covering the screen.IMMERSIONThe commentators are the most bareboned voice lines they could have done. Initially they would talk over each other and even themselves. No dialogue has alternate expressions or inflections and there are only a handful of lines to begin with. Imagine commentating on a World Cup final with no enthusiasm or care for anything that's going on. They sound bored and fed up. Like the playerbase at this point. Listening to the same 5 lines of dialogue over and over is mind numbing. Not to mention the commentators try to make comments in banter form but fail and simply sound like childish brags or completely irrelevant information about their own life. The writers put minimal effort into this and it's blatantly obvious.DEVSThis is likely the most insulting and troubling part of the whole situation. Their incompetance or straight up negligence is on another level. They released the game with broken mechanics they knew were broken and yet did not mention it until questioned on Discord weeks into it's release where they just went " yeah my bad"The servers went offline for 6 hours without warning, making access impossible as the entire game is a "service" not a "product" which incorporates Denuvo and requires a constant internet connection to play.6 hours without a single word from anyone in charge. After they finally came online, they brushed the entire situation under the rug and moved on.Originally, no patch notes at all, we had no idea what was being done, now we get 3 lines of text if we're lucky. They make changes no one asked for yet fail to even acknowledge the countless bugs in game.A limited time challenge is currently bugged, at least 10 to 20 people a day will ask about it in their Discord and this has been 2 weeks now, yet they can't even make a post in their "announcements" channel to inform people of the issue.NO accountabilityNO communicationNO respectThe sooner the studios are bought out by a company capable of doing their jobs the better. Or this game WILL FAIL.This could end up ranking alongside Concord with one of the biggest game disasters ever. Only WB and UBS are to blame here. The community are doing everything they can to keep this alive and they are losing motivation very quickly now.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game for the sake of ps2 nostalgia. I can see devs were clearly inspired by that game but key features are missing that made it a 10x better game.1) Most important: Lack of fast paced gameplay. While in the ps2 game you couldn't switch to beater/keeper/seekers on command, the original game made up for it in adding a supermega fast gameplay experience. Different types of passes, passing combos, volley shots, etc. made the chaser game feel dynamic and genuinely challenging. Here the chaser game boils down to: 1) Broom go fast 2) Make broom go faster 3) Pass (if any AI player even dares to go forward) 4) Shoot. That's it. No combos, no volley shots, no fast gameplay etc. It feels like a game of Rocket League on a flying broomstick.2) NO OFFLINE MODE. Can't play the game without connection. Not even against AI. You're out of luck.3) Lorewise there should be two beaters per team. You only get one. 4) World Cup Teams: WHERE IS BULGARIA?? WHERE IS IRELAND?? Two of the biggest teams lore-wise are absent. Everybody wanted Bulgaria to make a comeback and Ireland to appear for the first time. I get the world cup is limited to 16 teams but look at the countries they decided to include: India, Uganda, Jamaica, Brazil, Mexico and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ CANADA???!!! ARE YOU HAVIN A LAUGH?!! They took Bulgaria and Ireland out for these??? Also visibly due to the lack of character customisation in this game, the players of the original ps2 teams LOOK NOTHING LIKE THEY USED TO.5) They made it in the career mode so that you have to play with your own characters against the AI who plays the actual characters of their teams. Wanna play as Viktor Krum? Too bad. I guess they will add these players later to the store to buy as hero replacements, but for the career mode you can't even use hero replacers.So yeah. If you're here looking to get high on member berries of the glorious ps2 game, you're looking at the wrong game.I would have been willing to give this game a positive review for what it is: Rocket League on broomsticks... But I don't like Rocket League.Maybe if the devs could add the stuff that's missing I could change my mind. But for now, it's not worth the 30 quid.

Aiming the quaffle with flying instead of having its own aiming reticle is a major blow to the complexity that this game needs. You should be able to fly left and shoot right. This system is silly. I can forgive the automative passing, but that's another reduction of the skill ceiling. This all goes for the beater position as well. The seekers flying through rings is possibly the lamest system in the game. Just let the chase be natural. You should be able to catch the snitch head on if you make a clever route. I was most looking forward to playing the keeper. I enjoyed it at first, but I think it's because everyone barely knew how to play, and I was saving almost everything. Few days later, everyone reached the height of the skill ceiling, and it is now nearly impossible to save any shot. The keeper dash is not fast enough and the controls don't give the keeper enough control over challenging shots or coming out aggressively.  It is way too easy for chasers.tl;dr version: This game was made for children. This isn't Rocket League on broomsticks. Servers will die within 3 months. P.s. I almost want to give it a positive review for not having microtransactions though. Major props for that.

_childDocuments_.review: Overview"Harry Potter: Quidditch Champions" takes one of the Wizarding World's most beloved sports and brings it to life in a fast-paced, competitive multiplayer experience. With its focus on PvP action, the game offers an exhilarating ride for fans of Quidditch. However, while the core gameplay shines in competitive matches, there are some aspects that could use improvement to make it truly magical.Gameplay and MechanicsHaving spent five hours with "Quidditch Champions," it's clear that the PvP gameplay is where this game truly excels. The 3v3 matches are fast, challenging, and highly engaging, offering players a chance to fully immerse themselves in the high-speed, aerial action of Quidditch. The controls are smooth, and the game mechanics are well-designed, allowing for a variety of strategies and playstyles to emerge during competitive play.However, the solo/PvE gameplay leaves much to be desired. The AI in these modes doesn't allow players to fully explore the game's mechanics, often making these matches feel underwhelming compared to the excitement of PvP. For those who thrive on competition, the solo mode may feel more like a warm-up than a true test of skill.Multiplayer ExperienceThe multiplayer aspect is where "Quidditch Champions" truly shines. The thrill of going head-to-head with other players in intense, fast-paced matches makes for an exhilarating experience. However, the current 3v3 mode, while fun, feels somewhat limited. The need to control two characters in a match can be a bit cumbersome, and a 6v6 mode would provide a more dynamic and team-oriented experience. Such an addition, along with a ranked mode, could significantly enhance the game's competitive appeal.Graphics and DesignWhen it comes to graphics, "Quidditch Champions" takes a different approach compared to the stunning visuals of "Hogwarts Legacy." The art style leans more towards a Fortnite-esque aesthetic, which may appeal to a broader audience but can feel like a step down for fans expecting the same level of visual fidelity as seen in other Harry Potter games. While the graphics aren't a deal-breaker, they might disappoint those who were hoping for a more immersive, visually rich experience.Pricing and MonetizationAt £25, the game is reasonably priced, but there's a valid argument to be made for a free-to-play model. Offering the game for free with a cash shop for cosmetics and characters could have opened the door to a larger player base and potential esports opportunities. A free-to-play model could also have driven greater community engagement and increased the game's longevity.Conclusion"Harry Potter: Quidditch Champions" has a lot of potential, particularly in its multiplayer gameplay, which is both thrilling and challenging. However, there are areas where it could improve, such as the addition of a 6v6 mode, ranked play, and perhaps a rethinking of its art style. While the solo gameplay is not as compelling, the PvP matches are more than enough to keep players coming back for more. If the developers continue to build on this strong foundation, "Quidditch Champions" could become a standout competitive title in the world of esports.Rating: 3.5/5 to 4/5Pros:Fast-paced, exhilarating PvP gameplaySmooth controls and well-designed game mechanicsReasonable pricingCons:Underwhelming solo/PvE gameplay due to lackluster AIGraphics may disappoint those expecting "Hogwarts Legacy" level visualsLack of 6v6 mode and ranked play limits competitive depthOverall, "Harry Potter: Quidditch Champions" offers a fun and engaging experience, especially for those who love competitive multiplayer games. With some key improvements, it has the potential to become a well-loved title in the gaming community.....

_childDocuments_.review: Quidditch Champions is a game that is built around multiplayer. At present, you can play 3 v 3. This means you need to play as two roles. There's a goalie and chaser, beater and chaser, and lastly seeker and chaser. You essentially swap between these, meaning there's always a dopey AI playing in your other role. This is a bit of bummer, because the AI is not altogether that hard. The hope is 6 v 6 will be available by 2025. So far, the lag and performance online has been pretty darn good, so I am hopeful they deliver on this this promise.The single player features are very limited, with a tutorial and few competitions. You will be mostly done with the single player within around 2 hrs. The AI is not really much competition. You will gravitate to the hardest difficulty within a few matches. The overall single player offering is very limited indeed. I believe the purpose of the single player is preparing for multiplayer. It's really only good for warming up, trying new stuff, and, essentially, grinding for XP, crystals, and gold. You use the XP to earn skill point, and to progress through the battle pass (more on this in a moment). The crystals are used to upgrade brooms, and gold is used to buy stuff in the store. There're also 'keys' which are a special currency you earn at junctures in the battle pass. These can be used in the shop to get special items and packs. The skill points are really what I think makes this game good. You can use 10 on any one player (or role). There are three categories, with six possible points in each category (18 total). This means you'll have to be selective which perks you want. This makes the playing field more open. People will have different combinations of perks. For example, my beater is great at tackling chasers and seekers. Someone else may focus on countering their opposing role or maybe playing the Quaffle (ball).  If, after a bit of experience you want to switch around, you can do, but it costs quite a lot of gold, meaning you'll have to play a few games before you can change things up. The battle pass is not a commercial thing. They do not sell this pass or charge for gold/keys. Essentially, it is a season ladder, meaning if you have play a lot, you'll get everything. At the end of the season, some things may change in the store and there maybe a different pass. That's it. Nothing more or less. And that is the problem....At the moment, the game is focused on multiplayer, but there isn't any real incentive to play. There is the battle pass thing, but that's just lame. There's no ranking system, meaning you don't feel any progress. It's a great game and the matches I have had have been intense battles. It has truly been great. However, I can only really play for an hour or so. There's no ranked ladder to climb. They need to improve the multiplayer aspect of the game. The ranking system could be a simple gain points when you win and lose when you lose. This would enable a simple ranking system, where you achieve certain ranks at X number of points. Then just have the plain ole matchmaking you have now. Of course, the dream would be a proper ranking and ELO system, but I don't think there's the player base for this. Overall this game makes a great sporty MOBA. You have your roles, builds and team strategy. I tell you no lies when I say that I've some of the most competitive matches I've ever played online. The match length is also very good, with matches being all done an dusted within 10 mins or less. Heck, if you are against a weak team, you can shut them out 100 to 0 within a few minutes. All we need to really make this game great is 6 v 6 and ranking (and maybe leaderboards).

_childDocuments_.review: Hearing that Quidditch got narratively cut from Hogwarts Legacy last year, I knew that meant WB was planning to set up another game, primarily multiplayer & live service, to fill that niche they deliberately left for us. I was dreading it. From Mortal Kombat to Suicide Squad to Multiversus, the last thing I wanted was the company doubling down on the worse of modern gaming to drag one of my childhood IPs through the mud, even moreso after the great success of Legacy’s single player. Seeing it revealed in June, with the In-App purchases tag, only amplified my fears (the art style change didn’t help it) and I wrote it off as not worth my time or money. Cut to late August 2024, I’m browsing through Steam and I see Quidditch Champions as soon to release. I see they make a public post declaring no microtransactions in the game at all, even removing the implicative store tag from before. All of a sudden, I’m …. . They wouldn’t have said this unless they wanted to be caught lying or genuinely meant it. Tie that with a simple $30 price tag with the usual deluxe edition. Now I’m morbidly curious to try it. I did enjoy the 2003 Quidditch World Cup on CD-ROM back in the day, so I wasn’t against the idea of a new Quidditch game. I just didn’t trust modern WB Games to make it. The product we got was surprisingly … decent. It consists of a simple single player vs. bot campaign of Hogwarts, Triwizard, and World Quidditch cups, with various teams and difficulties, simple multiplayer of 3v3 (unranked as of writing this review), and exhibition matches & practice. Its content isn’t going to blow you away, and it’s UI looks very reminiscent of a game that USED to have microtransactions involved (3 currencies, a market, and “premium” vault, huh?) but truthfully has none, just as promised. Hope they keep it that way.You have a team of 3 chasers, 1 beater, a keeper, and seeker, all of which can be customized visually  and modified by role with brooms of various stats (similar to that of racing cars) that can be upgraded, and skill trees for each role. You earn skill points with your career level that can be spent on any tree, but they are few, almost meant as supplemental buffs to roles you don’t feel as comfortable with or to roles you love that make your impact more significant to a match. The various brooms are unlocked from challenges, and use earnable moonstones to upgrade their stats up to max of 5 levels per broom. It’s fine, and can give the game just a little more strategic depth, but sometimes I wonder how necessary it is. Just seems like the bare minimum they thought of to give some sense of progression outside cosmetics.Gameplay is streamlined compared to prior games, but still feels like a good spin on Quidditch. Brooms are nimble, and with some practice, make dodging, tackling, and drifting feel really good. A problem Quidditch always faced was the Snitch being essentially so important, it nullified any significance of the Quaffle Chaser part, so they reworked it to be a nice boon of 30 points that happens twice a match, instead of a game ender. Whoever reaches 100 or more points in 7 minutes wins. In single player, the roles can be swapped around at various times that don’t feel terribly klunkly, but still not as smooth as some might like (especially with controllers), and the bots taking over the other roles work well enough. In multiplayer, it’s a bit better with only 2 roles to focus on, and I’ve seen a surprising amount of synergy between keeper’s playcalling, beater’s stuns, and chaser tackles. I compare it a lot to Rocket League in simple, team sports fun.The big qualm I see many either find tolerable or hate, is the PvP setup: 3v3 where each player chooses a pair of roles to play throughout the match, a Chaser and some specialty (Beater, Keeper, or Seeker). This keeps the chaos one player has to deal with low, so they can focus on their playstyle better, but sometimes it’s still too much to jump between the action. I’ve heard that initial playtests did consist of the 6v6 team play which many more seemed to enjoy focusing on role specialty, but Unbroken may have changed due to player count expectations with the changed monetization and appeal. I’m not quite sure, but I fall in the middle. I do enjoy the compromise made, but I wish the full team of 6 allowed me to really learn to be the best at the role I want. Maybe that’s why the gameplay feels more streamlined to handle the role swapping.But with gameplay being decent, is that enough value? For 4 cup campaigns that only change visuals & setting, it will probably get repetitive after the first 10 or so hours once all skill points and brooms are unlocked. After that, it’s just a bunch of PvP that could go either way, with a pretty bad & overdone season grind of cosmetics to earn (still don’t know why wands are in a game like this though). It’s fine, especially for HP fans like me that find the world and references charming. It may be mediocre to the average person looking for a multiplayer focused sports-like experience however, even at $30.

_childDocuments_.review: The controls are over complicated. The camera, turning and ascend/descend controls all being one stick is possibly the stupidest decision ever made. And the steering is locked to the right stick so we can't even change it or properly map our own custom preset. The Chaser's AI is too slow and too stupid on the player's side, you get the quaffle and none of them are around or available, you're just waiting to be tackled, so you have to turn around, except at maximum sensitivity the turn speed is a disgrace and given the fact you can't look around besides the immediate behind camera, 99/100 times you will be tackled/hit/etc. The drifting mechanic looked cool in the trailer and it is in the game  It's the only fix I can see for the horrendous camera and turning except it doesn't make sense because it is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ slow even at the fastest speed.The Seeker is a partial role, being swapped to mid-game for a mini-game of fly through the circles that has been the standard since the first Harry Potter game that had Broom Flying. What isn't broke cant be fixed, yet somehow has been made tedious and uninteresting. There's no sense of tension or struggle or competitiveness with the opposition Seeker because the way to check progress is a tiny progression bar. It doesn't feel like it requires skill or is challenging in any way. The snitch starts off a long distance away from you and then when you've flew through a number of rings, it is still a long distance away. However, with a button press you can catch it! It left me with a hollow feeling. It's arguably the worst role in the game and extremely disappointing that the easiest formula for success was failed to be followed.The Keeper and Beater Roles are pretty damn good if you ignore the camera turning problems. Summoning a bludger or straight up battering an opponent with your club is excellent. Diving to make saves and *just* making it is extremely satisfying. One thing that I believe could do with more work however is the Playcaller Feature. As it is right now, not great. It's awkward and only works if your chasers or beaters are very close to your hoops. A suggestion I would make is to create custom plays, in a menu where you get 4 options of placements. Then during the game you as the keeper cycle through them and choose which one to use. That way you can make plays and work together with your team mates in Co-op.Why is there not an option for Original Rules, i.e. No Time Limit and Snitch ends the match? I understand the 150 points rule is too much as it guarantees a win or near enough does. For multiplayer it makes sense for a time and score limit and the snitch points severely reduced but for single player you should be able to choose.The commentary is also bland and uninteresting. There's no sense of excitement or tension at all.There's been too much time gone into customization than actual gameplay. A lot of work needs to go into fixing the controls, specifically the turning, camera and just flying in general. Where are Ireland and Bulgaria in the International teams? The World Cup winners from the Books (1994 and 2014 respectively). While I know it's probably for a later Event or season, I think that decision is stupid. The seasonal rewards and in game currency is fine but it's based off a model that requires good gameplay to keep players interested and unfortunately right now that isn't what they have here.Also the Firebolt, touted as the Best, Fastest, most Agile broom and having worse stats than a cleansweep seven makes no sense.No Professional Clubs, a whole book (Quidditch Through The Ages) and no Professional Clubs. Instead trying to tack on the Tri-Wizard Tournament with the three school teams as an interim stage between that and the world cup is disappointing. I for one wanted a player career, not a campaign.HP and the Quidditch World Cup, a near 21 year old game managed to make Quidditch fun, interesting, challenging and engaging. And there weren't any customization options besides what team you could pick. Somehow the magic of Quidditch is lost in this game. A decision to make no micro-transactions is admirable and respectable. Now it's time to fix the problems with the game. I cannot recommend the game at this time. I hope improvements are made because there is a lot of potential.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge fan of this game. Been playing since one of the playtests and am glad to finally have the full game in my hands, even if it does feel like very early days for the game. I really look forward to following its continued development over time. No MTX and a lower-cost entry fee for the game, make it worth all that it offers.The gameplay overall feels great to play and engaging. While it still has room for improvement in some areas, there is a great baseline here.Currently, there are single-player and online co-op & multiplayer modes. Full Crossplay and Cross-progression do this game many favours. Online multiplayer is limited to a 3v3 mode for now until later this year. Each player plays two positions and switches between the two while a bot takes your place in the role you are leaving. This does give the player always something to do, if you were a keeper, you can now play Chaser for a bit while you have downtime. On the other hand, it really does make matches feel "3v3" because the bots who replace you are very basic players that won't do anything really substantial. While this game mode can be a good option to choose from in the future, I am looking forward to a full 6v6 game mode. In the playtest I played, you could also fill empty roles or request to switch positions anytime in a match, which gives the game more strategy routes and tries to save a game with a last-minute switch.For a couple of improvements the gameplay could use, when throwing a bludger, you used to be able to adjust its speed rapidly to make it harder to dodge, but now you can only do that once it's travelled a certain distance which is usually already at your opponent by that point. Reverting that change might make people fear the bludger once again. Also, a big thing that missing that inhibits the gameplay is there’s no quick camera side view, to my knowledge. You can look behind you, but not the sides. So when you want to pass, you really have to rely on arrows that point to someone who’s near you, which is really not ideal.I love playing Seeker and trying to have that "movie" moment with the last-second clutch to win the game. Another seeker is also trying to do the same thing, so you're both racing to catch it first while attacking each other and both beaters are chasing you with bats in their hands. As this game lives on, I’d love to see custom ruleset matches, fun arcade modes (Unlimited boost or Quaffle handling timers so you have to constantly pass it or bludgers are 2x speed etc..), and a ranked mode. I can really see the potential and I hope it gets the love it deservesNo MTX, PS1 hargid mask, and the seeker gameplay paying homage to the PS1 games with flying through the hoops the snitch leaves in its trail, really made me feel that this game is in good hands.While not as high skill-ceiling as something like “Rocket League”, you can jump in and have fun straight away and as you’ll face tougher players, games can be quite exciting and intense at times. Having a modern, multiplayer quidditch game is a niche that needs to be filled for quite some time. To me, it doesn't matter about who's playing it or its popularity. It's a concept that's made sense for a long time and finally, we have it in our hands and it’s there for people to play it. If you're a Harry Potter fan, you’ll love it. If you are a sports game fan, you’ll get enjoyment from it. And if wondering what sweaty quidditch would be like, you’ll just have to see for yourself.
