I'm not a fan of rhythm shooting or perfect release "green" mechanics, but real % is available in the SP modes for those of us that like the strategy more than the timing. Multiplayer is heavily focused and match making sucks. I don't know why they don't have better lobbies and queues. The squad finder has literally never found me a squad. Highlighting each person in REC to find out what and how they play is tedious. There is no focus in finding 1-3-5 or 1-2-4 or 2-3-5 balanced teams. And why the heck do I need to sit in REC waiting to be invited into a team, just let me queue with my preferences and then walk about the city buying stuff or racing (very cool side activity btw). We need more mini game activities (darts, billiards, squirt guns, find the hidden item) to waste time while queued. I have no interest waiting court-side burning my XP boosts. Too much focus on squads and not enough focus on no-squads. I would love to be in a pro-am team, but getting an invite never happens and I don't want to build my own team. Where is the draft board that let's people select others (in their region, low latency, etc) based on their player DNA/Ratings/playtime/etc. ? If you are going to focus on multiplayer, for the love, make the queues and lobbies better. Wasting time standing around is not fun and doesn't promote game activity, it promotes idleness. Too many times I'm in a REC game and we have an idler which then turns into an AI, which then is exploited because they don't seem to have the same shot mechanics problems the rest of us are forced to use in MP games. AI players should use the player DNA of those that it's acting for. I expect the idle cutting 3 to play like that, not hold the ball and try to run plays (which never happens in MP). MP (online) is kind of a crap show anyhow, because it's just Big C rebounder/blocker and stupid long transition passes that are either dunked or stolen. Again, not fun. At least it's 5v5 though, 3v3 and 2v2 modes are even less fun, but somehow doesn't seem to suffer from the transition passing as much. I have so much more to say, so I'll edit it later. Oh and BTW I had 111hrs in before ever buying any VC stuff and was at lvl 22 in the season. I'll give more on the VC stuff later but tldr, bonus MT is decent, HOF is not worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: So first of all : I've played 2K forst the first time in 2011 with 2K12, I bought it every year until 2K17 on console. I came back on PC when 2K23 was on sale, but it was old gen that was just to play offline and enjoy it alone.As 2K25 is finally next-gen on PC, I bought it day one, as I wanted to experience another full year of 2K since day one, and honestly I'm not surprised but still disapointed about ONE thing : 2K has the worst playerbase in all sports game industry.2K has finally worked on gameplay, and not just a little bit, they made the pro-play, which is a huge improvement, and even more if you play offline, that thing makes the game much more enjoyable as players really have their own style of dribbling.You may think this is the biggest addition gameplay-wise but it's not, in recent years, 2K have struggled with cheaters, and not just on PC but also on consoles with something called " Zen " which was basically an shooting-bot that was based on the timing of your shot, cheaters couldn't midd an open shot. Since the timing was always the same, a cheater could never get banned as the cheat was litterally coming from their modded controller.So 2K said " **** that " and made 6 different shot timings depending on your shooting form, and made a new way of shooting called " Rhythm shooting " that's where the true game changer is. It's a new way of shooting based on your skill level and instead of releasing the shot based on a timing that you'd know by heart, it forces you to release the shot based on your shooting animation. Rhythm shooting is a new way to shoot with stick that makes the game much more skill based, old sweaty players in the majority hate it cause they hate that they have to learn something new, but they got what they finally asked for which is the end of cheaters using third party controllers, and also a new shooting system that creates a skill gap and that FEELS like shooting instead of just mechanically repeating the same shot with the same timing. You can still shoot with the button press, it's still possible and to this day, I think most players still shoot with this, but mostly because they're not accepting to change their habits ( Proof that they didn't want a new game from 2K since whenever they make a major change, they just ignore it ) If you're a new player I recommend you getting used to Rhythm shooting as you'll be rewarded with a larger " green window " and a funnier way to play.For us, PC players, we also received some recognition. During the first days of playing I did encountered some cheaters in park ( Not zen users ) with 60 overall players that suddenly had all the badges once the game started. I thought " **** the game is already plaged with cheaters " not even one week after day one, 2K released a patch, that ban-waved a lot of cheaters, and I never met any cheaters since then ( Let's hope it continues that way ) and I think SOME of the negative reviews are actually some of the cheaters that got banned, I've seen some reviews saying they were ban for " nothing " ( Sure we all get banned for nothing )On the negative points, yes I would add that indeed, in MyCareer, grinding VC can feel long, especially since nowadays a lot of people accepted the idea of micro-transactions and are willing to pay to max their player even if their build is failed, so it can feel frustrating if you're not willing to pay for VC but still wanna play Park or other online MyCareer related modes.I didn't have any regular crash as some of the other reviews says, I have no idea why or if I'm " lucky " I didn't even touch any settings related to performance and everything was set to maximum in graphics. I'd say that if you feel like your PC won't handle the game don't buy it or you can still refund if you crash during your first 2 hours, but I have a feeling this kind of reviews are from either people who think they can play on potato or those who have been banned from the banwave for cheating.So to make everything short : This playerbase will complain if the game don't change, but will also complain when the game changes and forces to change their habits. Make your own opinion, if you're a player from previous editions, open your mind and accept to play a different way, if you're a new player have fun, and play the tutorial before everything.

_childDocuments_.review: While overall there are general improvements when comparing to 2k21 (last played 2k), still can not recommend this game due to various flaws the online play has.To list some of them:- Controller settings reset randomly, in result, you almost automatically lose the match;- Impossible to rebind buttons, it would always say that something is unbound when everything is obviously still bound to every recognized controller;- Hands up defence is weaker than running into people's faces or space, makes 0 sense;- Events and event courts are broken (too many issues to list here, plus do not forget about your controller settings resetting randomly during a streak). Overall poorly executed (minus the blackout one, but that also had some very tedious tasks, if you were unlucky). And you also have skill based matchmaking here, so the best strategy is to cheese the system by creating new characters which have 0 skill level, even 60 overall characters being strong due to bugged courts;- Skill based matchmaking is present in casual game modes (e.g. Rec, Theater), while missing in the more competitive ones (e.g. Pro-AM), in result, it is almost impossible to find matches in Theater, the same goes for Solo Rec;- There was an active VC glitch for at least 24 hours (or longer), not sure if anyone got any punishment for abusing it, but there was no public statement about it as far as I know.- Still missing crossplay, which would be a great improvement.- VC can be somewhat quickly acquired, if you know the best mycareer grinding method. But it is a mindless grind, and still you need to grind a decent amount to max out one character to 99. Online play modes offer really low VC rewards (maybe minus 3x3 Pro-AM). Also, the daily and weekly quests are almost impossible to complete, even for a regular player.Some positives or improvements noticed:- There is less blatant cheating present;- There are less connectivity or crashing issues;- The shooting change is overall a good change;- The steals are really good this year (but sometimes a bit inconsistent and illogical), idiots can no longer get away with really bad passes;- Badge progression and system is much better than in the older versions;- The new rebirth also is a good improvement for people who want to play more than a single build;- The city looks nice and is overall compact without much wasted space, plus the kartings are cool. The 1 mil first place VC prize in the track is not though, should give something to top10 instead, maybe a bit more for top3.

_childDocuments_.review: NBA 2K25, the latest installment in the long-standing basketball simulation series, unfortunately falls short of the high expectations set by its predecessors. Despite the game’s potential, it emerges as a disappointment for both longtime fans and newcomers to the franchise.From a technical standpoint, NBA 2K25 struggles with several persistent issues that undermine the overall experience. The game suffers from noticeable bugs and performance inconsistencies that detract from its realism. Frame rate drops and stuttering, even on high-end systems, are frequent and disruptive. Additionally, the AI behavior, which is crucial for a sports simulation, remains problematic. Opponent and teammate logic often feels erratic and unrealistic, leading to frustrating gameplay scenarios that detract from the immersion.The graphical enhancements, which were anticipated to be a highlight, fail to deliver a significant upgrade. The player models and animations, while detailed, do not exhibit the level of refinement one would expect from a modern release. Furthermore, the presentation elements, including the commentary and in-game visuals, lack innovation and feel recycled from previous versions. This stagnation is particularly disheartening given the rapid advancements in gaming technology.NBA 2K25’s MyCareer mode, a fan-favorite feature, is marred by a convoluted progression system and an excessive focus on microtransactions. The monetization strategy employed within this mode feels particularly intrusive, overshadowing the enjoyment of the core gameplay. Similarly, the MyTeam mode’s reliance on card packs and additional purchases has shifted the focus away from skill-based play, which diminishes the overall satisfaction.The game's attempts at introducing new features and modes fall flat, as they often feel underdeveloped or poorly integrated. The lack of substantial innovation and the failure to address longstanding issues contribute to a sense of stagnation rather than progress.In conclusion, NBA 2K25 does not meet the expectations of a franchise known for its attention to detail and commitment to delivering a high-quality basketball simulation experience. Its numerous technical issues, outdated graphical presentation, intrusive monetization practices, and lack of meaningful innovation render it a disappointing entry in the series. Fans of the NBA 2K franchise may find themselves disheartened by this release, which fails to advance the series in a meaningful way.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't pick up the last couple 2K's since they were still porting the obsolete version of the game to PC instead of the Next Gen version for PS5/XBSX. This move is so baffling to me since PC is where players have access to even *more* power than console players. Boneheaded move that hopefully cost them millions of dollars. But at last! We have the updated next gen fancy edition on PC! Rejoice! But is it a better 2k than last generation? Honest answer: probably?The simulation aspect of this game has always been the best in sports games and continues that tradition in 2k25. With the graphics cranked to max, my wife constantly double takes when she catches some gameplay. Movement and physics feel like they have weight to them unlike years past which felt more floaty. Dunks and tricky layups feel earned when you nail one in traffic and makes the game more engaging. The game just feels good to play and replicates what being Luka or Joker or Dame or Steph would feel like. Gameplay is solid and rewarding if you use your noggin instead of just driving or pulling up from 3 off an iso. Playing the point or main offensive facilitator is satisfying in a way unlike other 2k's. Passing and making plays are key to winning with smarter AI that can capitalize on your mistakes more often, creating a more complex game of getting guys open, making good passes, and spacing the floor.I've dabbled in MyTeam and MyEras a bit, and they're mid to pretty lackluster. MyTeam is still an absolute scam and a mini casino marketed to a player population filled with literal children. I don't know about you, but that is abhorrant to me. There's more of a reason to get into MT (MyTeam) with the addition of Triple Threat, where you can use your MT cards to hoop in PvP pickup games like you would in The City with your created character. It's honestly pretty fun and a good excuse to check out MT if you're interested. MyEras is very poorly integrated and the incomplete rosters hold back what could be an honest to God innovation in a sports game (!). Thanks to the community rosters, the mode is saved for the most part. Getting the rights to use players likenesses is always an issue, so this isn't really 2k's fault, but it always sucks seeing my 04 Pistons without that legendary starting 5. The franchise mode that boasts RPG elements is hollow and more of a rough outline than anything. It's just not fun. Not much to say other than that.MyCareer (MC) is...man I don't even know dawg. The revamped story is grounded and feels like a glimpse behind the scenes unlike every experience before. Heart of a Dynasty is fun to hone your skills in and connect to the larger story being told in the current day. It's not super deep, but it's fun and rewards you for doing light roleplaying in certain moments. There's incentive to keep playing the single player mode to the very end of your career with the promise of creating your own dynasty. The new streetball mode is a neat distraction if you want to step away from the grind of the NBA. I wish I could skip the intro Lil Wayne or whatever is annoying good golly. Online is...well...2k online. Nothing new to report. I love the player builder and the ongoing evolution towards a more accessible experience. It's been downright fun to cobble together a player that's tuned to play exactly how I want to play hoops. If progression was tied to gameplay, I'd put 3,000,000 hours into this mode. It is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ shame this mode is corrupted by the VC scam and a dystopian nightmare of a City to roam in. The amount of ads and product placement feels like a joke. Wow! I'm so excited to do the State Farm Challenge so I can look like Jake from State Farm! Time wear my American Express merch (that costs 10,000 VC) for extra XP! It sounds like a joke when I tell people who don't play 2K. VC should not be tied to stats anymore and the overall experience suffers heavily from the reliance on a purchasable currency. It costs over 20 bucks to get a usable character and it doesn't get cheaper from there. You don't earn VC in a fast enough fashion to justify this system and needs to change more than ever.This *feels* like a game worth $70 with the amount of stuff packed in here. You can lose hundreds of hours digging into every aspect of this game like always and feel like you weren't ripped off. It's so unfortunate that the game tries to nickle and dime every moment you are in it. I don't feel good spending money in this game because it doesn't feel like I'm willingly doing it. The return is the same as feeding quarters into an arcade cabinet or a slot machine: you pay to keep playing.

Please watch a single real life Pacers game and then fix this to make it accurate.It just crashed again, deep into the 4th quarter on a career high performance. I have lost at least 40 hours of progression (and potential VC) to crashes. %75 of these crashes have happened in the 4th quarter on career-high performances.Controller settings are sometimes reset. Layup Timing is sometimes reset back to RealPlayer% after user has set it to User Timing.One minor issue is that the half-time show with Shaq and Kenny and Ernie runs at a terrible framerate, it always brings up "LOW VRAM" during it, and FPS drops to about %25 of normal gameplay FPS.Broken Steam achievement: "WINNING - Win a Game" achievement on Steam? I have won 90 consecutive games. Did you maybe mean to say "Win a Multiplayer Game"? If so, you need to rename the achievement. Rename it or fix it, one of the two.Broken Steam achievement: "Share the love - have all 5 starters on your team score double-digit points" All players in the starting lineup for my team scored double-digit points and yet the achievement was not given.Some outdoor city courts will give 300 FPS when on offence and 5 FPS on defence. City FPS will often drop below 1 FPS."MyPlayer makes the All-Star team, no surprises there." was shown in the social media and GOAT moments section, I received the 7,500 GOAT points for being selected for the All-Star team ("+7,500 - Make the All-Star team"), and yet I was not in actuality selected for the All-Star team, I was not able to play in the game, I cannot view the box score for the game, only the final team totals, and I did not receive the "Make the All-Star team as a rookie" GOAT moment.MyPlayer and teammates will celebrate for a made shot even if the ball was taken out of bounds before the shot was attempted, let alone made. In such a scenario, the basket is not scored, and therefore, in real life, no celebration would occur. (Issue observed in Brickley's Gym 5v5 Scrimmage.)Commentators do not take into account the Trent Tucker Rule. They say "and he got it off in time", even when he did not get it off in time, i.e. when 0.2 seconds in on clock and ball is inbounded and the shot is not a tip in or high-lob.Commentators will call a two a three if the shooter has their dominant foot behind the line and their non-dominant foot in front of the line.The officiation system can sometimes erroneously and egregiously call an out of bounds off the incorrect player.In the playoffs, during video of the outside of the stadium, it allows the player to hold the "A" button to skip it, and it does not skip it.Game does not distinguish between team-specific and league-wide playoff statistics records. "MP got 38 points, which breaks the single game record of 68."Please, alongside the 16 JPEGS, maybe a hyperlink to the patch notes as plain text.There is no way to reliably cancel a steal attempt once the steal animation has begun, even if that animation takes 5 seconds.Sometimes MyPlayer will throw the ball into an opposing players back.Sometimes MyPlayer will refuse to pass the ball even when every pass button is pressed multiple times.There is no way to skip goat skill activation slowdown, you must wait 5-10 seconds every single time. This usually causes at least 30 seconds of pointless waiting every single game.And the game just crashed again, 3rd quarter, second game of the NBA finals. It showed me a very far zoomed out shot of the entire crowd, froze on that while the commentators kept talking, then it shut itself down and returned me to the desktop.Where is Gravity Ball?Typo "All those folks who booed his drafting seletion....." Should be "selection", not "seletion"FPS drops to an unplayable amount after changing shot meter size.Shot meter size reverts to defaults with no user consent.*** MyTeam Bugs and Issues ***Trying to use the Create a Court feature can crash the game.The game will sometimes say that a lineup is not complete, even though it shows as valid, and has a full 13 players in it. So I go in to "replace with best available" which changes nothing, and it still doesn't work. So then I will select the autofill team to create a lineup of the exact same 13 players, and then the autofill option will work and I will be able to play the game.The Invalid Lineup Bug is (usually) due to not having an equipped ball, the game should show the player an option to select a new ball for their lineups once a prize ball is broken open. It should also give the player a (functional) apply to all lineups option here, which is directly related to/caused by the next bug....The "apply to all lineups" function does not work for balls.The season XP level indicator bar and number ALWAYS shows the incorrect value.Typo: Exhibitions: "Twin Falls Gorge": "Klakdu Nation Park" is incorrect, this should say "Kakadu National Park"Error 300 something (not sure the exact number) causes no progress to be saved after a won game. Issue observed after completing a dynamic goal in domination vs GSW. The dynamic goal was duplicated in the pause menu 5 times, might have something to do with it.*** My General Thoughts about 2k25 ***This franchise on PC has never been a good experience, and the very very late transition to the new-gen version for PC was not enough to bring the experience into line with what is expected of a triple-a developer selling a $99 dollar base price game with an option to pay $250 for the ultimate version, not including the price of each season pass. I like that the stamina bonus lasts forever after completing every exercise once. But I liked playing the exercise minigames, I just didn't like the fact that doing them was functionally compulsory. No, phenomenal isn't even the word that could possibly describe this game's graphical fidelity. This game's visuals are nothing but a marvelous feat; for instance you can see the individual beads of sweat shimmer in the arena lights as they drip from Anthony Edwards’s marvelously pristine forehead or the planar reflections on the crispy-clean hardwood floor. The visuals are nothing but a sheer ball-tingling experience, and I give nothing but props to 2K Sports for not only crafting realistic visuals in an NBA experience, but also setting the industry bar for absolute photorealism. _childDocuments_.review: 2K finally updated PC to next gen and introduced a bunch of changes making the game much more accessible for offline and casual players like me. It seems like they implemented many more ways to get VC compared to previous years. If I ever felt the grind was too much I could just lower the difficulty or play a different mode and still get a decent amount. The WNBA modes are some of the best in the game. the W career mode is like the offline MyCareer that I would have wanted, similar to way back when before microtransactions became so invasive in the rest of the game. MyCareer was fun, having to only play key games which affect badges and your dynasty is a great idea. The offseason options helped keep the career mode interesting too. I managed to influence some trades by suggesting expendable players with high potential who could grow with me after my team aged up. It took me 5 seasons to get goat status and grind to 99 overall with no money spent on VC. I liked the city as it didn't affect performance much and we got the go kart early on. The streetball challenges were fun and prepared me for coop and park games even though usually stay away from multiplayer modes. MyNBA and Eras with the next gen upgrade are a welcome change and has kept things interesting. MyGM mode is arguably worse than before with just a minor design change. There's a lot to be done to make this mode even decent. MyTeam is still microtransaction heavy but its where I spend most of my playtime now as the auction house is back and helps to avoid the pack market. That said, the auction house is pretty empty and I don't think the time lag between transactions helps. I also tried a couple of multiplayer challenges which went smoothly except that the park was very empty whenever I logged in. Overall, one of the best NBA2K games in recent memory. Every mode is fun except MyGM. Great for offline or casual players. 8/10

My review is completely centered around the high level casual-competitive environment this game provides and is not related to the experiences on the MyCareer and MyTeam gamemode.This 2k has been really hit or miss so far.Through the attempt to nerf a consistent and overpowered meta that has existed since the inception of MyCareer, that being playmaking sharpshooters, they have severely crippled the overall game experience. In this 2k, they have taken many steps to stop even the best players from shooting consistently. Unless setting your game to the shot-profile that makes it impossible to hit non-green shots, you can not time your shot in a way that guarantees a green (shot with 100% chance of going in) without super-human consistency. Even on the high risk shooting profile you have 30m/s to guarantee a green shot. The rest of the green-window for your shot has an RNG % chance of coming out as a green or white shot. To add insult to injury, they have made it so shots this year choose between 8 different timings every time you go to shoot. While overall they are minor changes to timing, they completely shift the green window. Due to this system,  It is completely ridiculous and idiotic to change someone's shot timing randomly every time they shoot. This is all without mentioning that community testing has shown that after making too many shots in a row the game forces you to miss when in a live game.This system has been an overall negative to shooting, reducing it to a luck contest where even at the top level players struggle to green consistently. In my personal experience my play-style has been completely shattered and I don't even take 3's. I focus on creating high efficiency mid-range shots while creating threats in the paint. Even this simple and effective shot selection is completely ruined by the RNG shooting and it's very disappointing for anyone that likes to do anything other than dunk.However, it is important to note that while the RNG is a terrible and regretful decision to re-implement into the series, the poor shooting itself does create some fun in the game and if the game proceeds to heavily limit shooting while completely removing RNG the playstyle they are trying to cultivate can be very fun.Despite the flaws in the structure of the game, it is very refreshing for a more grit-and-grind style game, 3 pointers have become exciting and risky again rather than the go-to plan like it has been for so long. While some players still stick to and succeed in range-centered gameplay, the majority of the community has spent a lot more time playing physically and in the paint. It really is a refreshing experience for a 2k game and is not the overall negative the community makes it out to be. The only problem is the RNG.We should not be failing to green a wide-open corner 3 with Steph Curry because 2k rolled a green window that is significantly outside the normal timing of our shots. We should not be having the visual cue's on our player's jump shots completely desynced from the actual timing of our shots because 2k rolled a green window that is significantly outside the normal timing of our shots. We should not have a chance to get a white shot with perfect timing down to the exact millisecond.With my main team that I have spent thousands of games on and know everything about the timing of by heart, I am now afraid to take the same wide open fade-away mid range shots I have hit with 80-90% accuracy for years now. Let alone a stand-still mid range. Every shot is a risk forced by the game regardless of skill level.TLDR: A refreshing 2k experience with a focus on physical play that is marred down by a terrible RNG system meant to artificially limit player skill. Skill expression from range is tarnished and even smart and safe shots are interfered with by the game to make them virtually impossible to hit.

_childDocuments_.review: WE FINALLY GOT NEXT GEN ON PC!!!Rating: ★★★★☆ (4/5)Pros:Enhanced Visuals with TrueView Technology: NBA 2K25 introduces TrueView, a new graphics engine upgrade that brings even more realism to player models, lighting, and crowd dynamics. Faces and movements have an uncanny realism, and the enhanced court environments make each game feel like watching a real broadcast. Stadium lighting and even arena-specific details contribute to an impressive overall look.Fluid Gameplay with Refined ProPLAY: Building on last year’s ProPLAY, NBA 2K25 has expanded real-life animations across more player movements and interactions, making transitions between actions smoother and more responsive. The result is a fluid experience where dribbling, shooting, and defending feel polished and natural, giving players more control in every possession.Legends Mode - Celebrating NBA’s Greatest: This new Legends Mode allows players to control the greatest players from various eras in NBA history, from Larry Bird to Shaquille O’Neal, with era-specific teams and rivalries. It’s an in-depth, nostalgic experience for long-time fans and a great introduction to NBA history for newcomers, featuring challenges and storylines based on iconic games and moments.Balanced MyCareer Progression: This year’s MyCareer mode has made notable improvements in progression balance. While VC is still part of the system, the grind for badges and attributes feels less intense, allowing players to develop their character without relying heavily on microtransactions. The storyline includes deeper branching narratives and more impactful choices, adding a nice RPG element.Crossplay & Enhanced Online Stability: NBA 2K25 has refined its crossplay capabilities across PC, Xbox, and PlayStation, improving matchmaking and enabling friends on different consoles to play together seamlessly. Server stability has seen noticeable improvement, and disconnects are less frequent, making online games more enjoyable and competitive.MyTeam Seasons & Dynamic Events: MyTeam has introduced seasonal challenges and dynamic events that align with real NBA events, like special challenges during the All-Star Weekend. New weekly rewards and updated card themes keep things fresh, and the removal of contracts continues to make team management more streamlined.Cons:Microtransactions Still Prominent: While progression has been balanced somewhat in MyCareer, the game still includes a heavy emphasis on microtransactions. VC is still used in nearly every mode, and while it's now slightly easier to earn, it can feel difficult to stay competitive in online play without spending real money.Limited Innovation in Core Gameplay: Though ProPLAY improves animation fluidity, the core mechanics remain largely unchanged. Veteran players might feel the gameplay loop has become predictable, with only minor adjustments from NBA 2K24. More variety in play styles or strategies would have helped keep the experience fresh.AI Inconsistencies: While the game’s AI has improved, there are still occasional moments where teammates make questionable decisions or the difficulty curve spikes unexpectedly, especially in MyCareer. Opponents sometimes feel overpowered in certain game modes, which can disrupt the overall balance.Grinding in MyTeam: Despite the addition of seasonal events, MyTeam remains grind-heavy. Unlocking high-tier cards without spending on microtransactions requires significant time investment, which could deter more casual players who want to stay competitive in the mode.Minor Server Lag: Although server stability has improved, minor lag persists, particularly in high-stakes online matches. This issue can impact shot timing and responsiveness, which is crucial in competitive games.Verdict: NBA 2K25 pushes the series forward with stunning visuals, refined animations, and exciting new features like Legends Mode, which is a treat for fans of the sport's history. The balanced progression in MyCareer is a welcome improvement, although microtransactions are still prominent. With better crossplay and more stable servers, the online experience is also more reliable. NBA 2K25 is a solid upgrade for both returning fans and new players, but the lingering reliance on VC and the familiar core gameplay may leave some wanting more substantial innovation.

No more cutscenes to get you hype — just grind, grind, grind.Yo, I’m not gonna lie, Rec and Pro-Am are still where it’s at for squad ball, but they got their issues. The . And Pro-Am, while fun, can still feel a bit .I gotta say it: MyTEAM this year? . It feels worse than *2K24*, no cap. The grind to get decent cards is straight-up painful unless you’re dropping your hard-earned cash on packs. If you're not willing to drop some bread, you’re pretty much cooked. It's tough to stay competitive when you’ve got dudes with God squads after Day 1. Honestly, it’s become a game of  rather than skill.Let’s talk about that VC grind because 2K did nothing to make it better. In fact, it feels even worse. You need to either put in  or drop cash if you want to get your player to 99. It's the same old pay-to-win system that keeps getting worse with each release. _childDocuments_.review: This is the first game I have gone out of my way to write a review for if that says anything. I bought this game on sale for about $40 hoping to enjoy a game that I have not played since 2k18 or so... The game constantly crashes, it has happened at least 10 times so far. I have only played MyCareer and about 10-15 times a game the mechanics begin to bug out and you (including teammates) cannot pass the ball to anyone further than 2ft away from you. This issue has resulted in several turnovers, costing me games; there were even instances where the ref was stuck in an animation attempting to give a player the ball to in-bound, causing me to have to close the game and restart because the player would never get the ball. The online "lobby" that you have to traverse in MyCareer is frustrating as well, this is about where half of my crashes have occurred. When playing a game the frame rate is fine, but the "lobby" drops to anywhere from 15-40fps.  I requested a refund after 11 hours and was denied (understandably) due to the time put in, but I was hoping that I could eventually enjoy the game as intended within that amount of time. It has crashed twice in the last 10 minutes while simply attempting to traverse to an activity in MyCareer, which has finally prompted me to write this review. I have never had a game crash this much in such a short amount of time. Will I still (try to) play it? Yes, because I spent money on it that I cannot get back and the constant stress of trying to play it will only result in my sweet release from this life arriving much sooner. Do not buy this unless it is 90% off and you absolutely love the sport. Please consult with your doctor prior to purchasing if you are at risk of a stroke or heart attack.

_childDocuments_.review: I would not recommend this game over 2k24, for the following reasons.1 - Foul out in co op multiplayer (6 fouls)?  Nope, doesnt matter your game performance or how much time is left in the game, you're immediately booted to the lobby.  If you're playing with one other person, the game ends outright and abrupt.  No VC earned at all.  Doesnt matter if the character you have fouled out has 7 points, or a 50 point quadruple double.  As an example, I received this game as a gift from a friend to mostly play co op with in quickplay.   The first time this had happened to me, I had a 35 point triple double and had an A player rating, and when I received my sixth foul with two minutes left in the fourth quarter, we were booted immediate. Whether it be two people on the same team, or two on one team one on another, if you foul out 6 fouls you are immediately booted to the lobby.2 - Unreasonably graphically demanding with long load times versus 2k24.  I REALLY enjoy formatting shaders every single time I launch this stupid game.3 - Server stability.  When doing quickplay, theres about an 85% chance at some point the game will encounter some error at some point or another and forcibly kick you back out to the lobby, indiscriminate of time in the game.  It could happen with 9 seconds left in the fourth quarter, or 2 minutes into the second quarter.4 - HUD does not apply changes you create.  First and foremost, there is no actual shot meter bar like in 2k24.  Now its all the arrow, or the dial, and even if you change them in the HUD?  Good luck getting them to apply for more than one game.  Yes, I have launched the game as administrator and attempted to apply settings to no avail.5 - The game boots you from the lobby for having a poor game performance.  This is absolutely atrocious for those of us just getting to learn the game and changes from 2k24, and basically promotes stat padding.  Not everyone wants to play as 85+ rated characters.With the above all being said, I could understand some of the changes being applied to rec or to pro am or to my career in general, or even to myteam.   And I'm all for that. But when you're playing co op with a friend in quickplay and you have 4 fouls in the third quarter and you arent allowed to play defense because of risk of fouling out and getting kicked to the lobby?  Absolutely sours the game in general.In short, would I purchase this game?  No.  I would ask for this game to be refunded if steam were to allow this.  If changes were fixed?  Sure, it could be warranted to buy the game.  The shot meter, yeah its a personal gripe but I could work around that.  Every year the shot meter changes to something different.  The instability, and the fouling out, and being kicked out for poor performance?  As someone who chooses to play only multiplayer co op? Absolutely not, and those are deal breakers for me.

Reopen it and do it until they are at 100% because the first time they load is the slowest. I have an SSD so that helps but after they installed it only took a few seconds for them to load to 100% on launch2) Skip the second set of shaders by pressing "cancel" and go straight to the graphics settings3) Turn the setting to their lowest setting and put the game on "Windowed" *not* "Windowed Fullscreen" then close the game (if you don't it will crash inevitably)4) Reopen the game and let the second set of shaders load (it only loaded about 4% for me at a time, so yes, this is the longest step). The main issue I see right now for myself and others, is crashing. Especially in The W, which is primarily what I play.I can play a game without any trouble and the game crashes loading back to The W. Other times, loading to The W crashes twice and then I can play a full game. It's pretty absurd for the price tag and all the talk about increased production costs. Unfortunately, The W is still the only experience for women. I don't mind The W, it's definitely a lot better than not being included at all. I do wish they would just make WNBA a main story and stop holding back what they obviously intend to do eventually.I can deal with all that. However, the mostly universal experience with crashing is completely unacceptable for this brand and a $70 price tag.. If they fix the bugs and crashes, would recommend. Until then, 2K25 seems like I'm paying more for a worse product just because layoffs were more important for the shareholders than quality. The game is the same great basketball sim we know, but the crashing makes it impossible to recommend.Performance is great with good hardware, but only if it doesn't crash. I get a stable 100fps at 4k Ultra with DLSS set to Quality. I get about 65fps average at 4k Native or with DLAA.That means you could typically expect a stable 60FPS at native 4K with max settings when using my hardware. I prefer using DLAA for anti-aliasing at 4K60, but to each their own there.I don't play The City, but it performed bad in the previous games and I hear it performs bad in this one too. I'd expect half the above performance in The City with frame stutter or lag spikes likely.Building ALL shaders is really important if you want to avoid stutters when playing. If a shader gets called that isn't cached, the game will hitch for a half second. I've not experienced any stuttering which others have complained about after building all shaders.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who only really plays the offline modes like MyNBA and MyGM, this is the most enjoyable NBA 2K I've played in a long time.MyGM is back, MyNBA has more eras than ever with the eras feature now being on PC, lots of little quality of life changes have been made to MyNBA such as the ability to actually offer rookies contract extensions, or actually play all 15-17 guys off of your bench, much improved coaching rotation and substitution AI, and more small but notable changes.The shooting this year is a little strange when you first get ahold of it, but it pretty quickly became my favorite shooting mechanic of any 2K that I can remember. Shooting just feels intuitive and I feel like I can get a better rhythm for it this time around than in years past. There are some quirks such to the overall feel such as the rim physics, which just seem a bit... off. A lot of shots seem to like bouncing all around the rim even when they're made shots, which always feels a bit bizarre and is not something I remember being so noticable in previous entries. Performance can occasionally be an issue as well. The halftime show with the Inside the NBA guys is locked to 30 fps and seems to have some sort of shader issues, unlike the rest of the game. Make sure to turn cloth simulation OFF in your settings for significant improvements to performance, although even with it off there is an occasional stutter when a timeout is called.Also worth mentioning that the game works pretty decently on the Steam Deck. The graphics and performance are obviously much better when running it off a proper gaming PC, but being able to take the game with you on the go and still get a passable experience is a really nice touch. At this point I've probably played a bit more on my Deck than on my machine.Haven't touched the Career mode yet as I usually play it sparingly, but it seems like multiplayer in the PC version has issues with cheaters and the like. I've never really cared for the multiplayer online stuff in 2K but it's clearly a very popular part of the game and it's a shame 2KSports hasn't addressed this and made this aspect of the game worthwhile for PC players. Please beware of this if you're looking to purchase the game for that stuff. However, all in all, really enjoy this game for the offline and single player content, and the mods being rolled out make it an even better experience.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:  Next gen engine on PC.  Playing defense has improved drastically and the player movements are responsive.  Skipping halftimes and timeouts take a couple of button presses, but it does move forward without forcing you to watch or wait too much.  There are still situations where your player will get animation locked.  I.E. you go for a steal, but the reach doesn't register until after the animation is complete.  Same thing with other moments, but it's to be expected and you can often break the animation by moving your player away from the other player.  MyCareer has a similar grind as before.  Other reviewers have mentioned that the amount of MP points needed to be a star has increased a lot.  So far MyPlayer is a 75 OVR and we're halfway through the season.  He doesn't move like a superstar until a Badge is activated, but then his stats jump to the 90s in enough categories that you'll be able to make some good plays.  Practice increases your Badge level and Overall stat cap.  Unfortunately, once you've maxed a Badge in practice you can't play that mini game anymore.  You have to practice the badges that aren't fully upgraded yet.  At least this was the case for all my offensive badges.  I'm stuck practicing boxing out until I increase my rebounding stat high enough to go to the next badge level.  I like this game a lot and it's the best 2k I've played (most recent was 2k22; I've been waiting for next gen on PC).

_childDocuments_.review: I have been passionately playing basketball in all forms for almost 40 years now, i feel like i will never lose that love for the game itself, being in real life or in a digital form. Why am i not recommending it then? Well, 2k over the years has been trying REALLY hard to kill my love for the game in the digital form. But since there are actually more positives this year then there are negatives, i will start of with the positives. First of all, i should mention that even though i have 30+ hours in already,  there are certain modes i haven't tried (my gm, the W,...) as i have rarely played them in the past. My usual go-to games are the online games in my career. But that only speaks volume as to how many different kind of game modes there are. The amount of content across the game is ridiculous. I mean seriously, there would be absolutely no shame if the game was being released only once in like 4 years or so. I have started the game by only playing the play now and play now online modes and i went through the tutorial mode which is actually well done this time around. It will teach you practically everything you need to know about the core mechanics. Also all the "main menu modes" would probably be enough to keep anyone entertained for the whole year on their own.Then there's my career of course. The city is really well done, it's just small enough for all functions to be quite readily accessible and just large enough so exploration doesn't get an overextended welcome. There is A TON of content and game modes and the experienced players will be right at home with stores, items and progression even though it looks vastly different at first glance. I won't get into details about each game mode as it's all pretty self explanatory and everyone should just take the first day to get acquainted with everything on their own. I will say though, that even with the "next-gen" labeling, certain elements of the game are ancient and obsolete and just ridiculously bad. For example, visually creating your player is the least fun thing i've done this year. The generic faces available are just atrociously bad and ugly and facescan has never produced expected results either. And the hair is just extremely bad. No amount of directx candy can hide the age of the engine itself. Back to the game modes themselves, if you like competitive play, there is no doubt you will find something for you in The City, i have no doubts there. As for the mycareer itself and the story, well... I have to say the story always got on my nerves in previous years as it was a literal cringe-fest, but this is absolutely not the case this year. I mean it's not an oscar material but it's efficient, it's straightforward and ABOVE all...it's not trying to be "socially or politically pleasing" as so much content in movies and games is trying to be last few years. There are no "agendas", no one is trying to subtly convert you into a vegetarian or make you transform your gender or accept people identifying as flying pink pandas or anything like that. And that alone is worth an A+ to me (looking at you DISNEY for ruining Star wars for me). The career part of gameplay is pretty bad in certain elements but more on that later. As for the myplayer builder itself, it's probably the best it's ever been done, especially with the pre-made builds that it has available now and should make life easier for people who don't want to dissect every nuance the builder offers, or they just simply don't know what they're doing. Even though i made a completely custom build, i have yet to fully realize how good it will be. I am around 85 ovr for now. I never watch youtube videos on the "perfect archetype and build", because i believe this is part of the fun, to figure it out on your own. Even if you make a mistake or two. And i've never created more than 1 build per yer, so i'm not the right guy to judge how good the laboratory really. I was pleased with it. If you take your time you will see in real time how each single change will affect your badges. It's very intuitive but it's probably a good idea to have a basic understanding of yourself, how you like to play the game, what your basic basketball behavioral tendencies are, etc. As i've mentioned  certain aspects of graphics, let's continue with that note. I am running an i7 9700k which is starting to show its age, a 3080ti gpu and 32gb of ram and a samsung 980 pro ssd. While we have become used to 2k being riddled with bugs over the years and even more so with bugs that persist for MANY years, i would NEVER defend 2k just solely on pure fact how they've treated bugs over the years. But man, reading all these negative reviews here really is mind boggling as to what on earth people are doing with their machines. In my 30+ hours i haven't encountered A SINGLE (mark that word down!) bug, a SINGLE crash, not even a TINY little glitch for which i could hold 2k accountable. I am really sorry for people who are either unable to play or have constant problems, but i strongly advise those people to call someone who will be able to get their system in shape, perhaps even do a clean install of the OS. My system is neither high end, nor new, if it was really as bad as many people claim i should have ran into at least one crash or other problem. I have a 1440p monitor but i'm running the game supersampled to 4k resolution and DLSS enabled and set to DLAA which i didn't expect to produce completely fluid framerate but it is. Certain arenas are more intense so i lowered the resolution back to 1440p and i NEVER drop below 60fps in games. I have all graphic options set to maximum. The raytracing is not well optimized so the City has a pretty poor framerate if it's enabled but as soon as you get to any part where you actually play, the framerate is stable and high. The lightning and shadows and player models are actually pretty nice looking but i personally would not call them next gen. The game looks solid, but can't visually compare to modern graphics in AAA games, especially the unreal engine 5 games. However the motion of the game is amazing. 2k has never been this fluid before and that itself boosts the immersion immensley. I can't wait what modders will be able to do with the game this year as i have pretty high expectations in that regard. Now finally, let's touch on the gameplay itself. Letting all the hate of a typical long term 2k baller aside, i personally never had gripe with how the game is being played. The core of 2k games has always been a pretty solid blend of realism and arcade. And i don't want to sound like someone on 2k's payroll but man, i really like gameplay this year. I've not enjoyed digital basketball this much probably since 2k16. I was actually pleasantly surprised by 2k in that regard as i have lost all hope over the years. I won't go into specific details, but gameplay elements are top notch in my books. The only real gripe i have with the game is AI which is ridiculously bad and has always been. And i mean ridiculously bad. I will end off by saying that i've had my doubts if i should even buy 2k when i saw  it won't support cross play as it was instantly clear to me this means nothing has been done about the cheating issues (shocking, i know). However, going to next gen, i had my hopes that something has been done to the engine that will prevent cheating at least in the easiest form. Sadly, it wasn't. And this fact, coupled with the predatory MXT is still enough to never recommend this game to anyone. You WILL need to feed around 30-50 euros into the game minimally, if you want to actually have fun online. MXT that affect skills in a full priced game? I will NEVER EVER accept that. And the fact that 2k doesn't even protect you from cheaters after that is even worse, and it's just sad because of how good the game itself is. And until that gets addressed, i cannot recommend anyone buys their products. No matter how much you love basketball.

_childDocuments_.review: **Edit notes: I left the original review here for anyone who wants to read it, however I have placed the update at the top of the old review**Updated Review:  So after hours of being crushed in the MyCareer, I have finally found the solution. If you are a newer player, or someone who doesn't want to do the grind, do yourself a favor. Go into Settings > Controller Settings > Shot Profile, and change your profile to Real Player %. This makes the game lose the shot meter, and use your skills in game to determine the success of your shots. Believe me, this makes a world of difference. I wont ROTY, Finals MVP, NBA Cup, and NBA Championship with a 61 overall using this method. So normally, I'm not a review guy. But just in case anyone reads this review, and it helps them, then it is worth it.@k25, as an overall game, is great. MyNBA, WNBA, and MyTeam are all smooth as silk and same as ever. However, MyCareer seems to continuously stumble down this path, switching from one side to the other. I started playing 2k in 2016, back in the Orange Juice time frame. I loved that game, and if I could still find a way to play it, I would, because that MyCareer was the most fun, and most entertaining, out of any we have played since. However, even last qyear's last-gen MyCareer was better than the garbage sandwich we were handed this year.First, Heart of a Dynasty seems cool, until you jump in to what is effectively supposed to be a High School game, and yet the players on the opposing team are playing like NBA all stars (literally, P. Wells shot two three pointers, back-to-back, from beyond half court, and suck them both!? Name one NBA player who can do that consistently!?), you're teammates play like senior citizens, and if you haven't leveled up your character, you are as good as useless on defense. Then let's throw in the fact that badge progression in the practice facility has been made 1000% more difficult, as you cant repeat exercises, and the new drills are outright impossible for early leveled characters. Finally, the actual NBA games are mostly okay, but I still can't score consistently with my low level character, because I cant level up the badges that would normally help me. There are plenty of ways to make VC, but they require you be able to perform well with your character, which you cant do unless you can level them up. Long story short, if you are like me, and want a decent MyCareer, wait until this game goes on sale, then use the money you save to buy VC and get a huge starting boost on your character.Now on to the good stuff. First, there are plenty of ways to earn VC, and several of them are repeatable methods. However, none of them give enough VC to really feel worthwhile, unless you play on HoF difficulty. Both the Rec and Pro-am are pretty full right now, so it's a good time for those matchups. I also really enjoy the layout of the City, its far easier to navigate.Gameplay is fine, although I'm not a fan of the new shot meter.

_childDocuments_.review: Just avoid the online stuff, it's pure cancer. Play MyNBA Eras, it's by far the best mode. Want to recreate Jordan's dominance in the '90s, make it even crazier, or maybe prevent him from winning with Utah Jazz and the beautiful duo of Stockton and Karl Malone? Want to play the 76ers of Julius Erving and Moses Malone in the mid '80s and stop the Lakers - Celtics dominance? Maybe you want to convince the mediocre Bulls team to trade their exciting rookie in '84 and create an alternative reality where the '90s Bulls never existed? Or maybe you want to actually win an NBA title with that mediocre Bulls team in the '80s with just prime Jordan (with Hall of Fame difficulty lmao)? You could also try to trade Charles Barkley in '92 when he becomes a free agent and make an insane trio of Jordan - Pippen - Barkley (you'll probably need to trade half of your team to just manage the salary cap hahaha)Or play as Allen Iverson in early 2000's and actually win a title against the mighty Lakers' duo of Shaq and Kobe? Or more recently, stop Steph Curry from dominating? (impossible honestly lol)And yes, some rosters in some eras are not 100% complete, but you can load custom rosters made by the community and you'll have a greater experience (notably Charles Barkley and Blake Griffin are missing in the official roster due to some licensing issues). All in all, just this mode is fantastic honestly, no sports game comes close to recreating a historical era so well. It's quite immersive, including rule changes that actually happened in real life, teams relocating and actual historical drafts (witness a rookie Shaq, Kobe, Duncan, Iverson, McGrady, Irving coming into the league) and most importantly, team tendencies and styles being so different — if you play ball in the '80s era, there's almost no 3's, the game is slower, more inside baskets and intense defense and closer game; in the '90s there's some 3's being thrown but they are almost negligible compared to the current era, the pace though ramps up compared to the '80s. And the current era is just splashing 3's most of the time lmao which can be annoying but it's also much harder on defence in my opinion. Players are so well-rounded in the current era it's actually insane, before you had just a few well-rounded players and it was mostly about role specialists. Now you can have a center like Jokic that can do basically anything. Just having this sandbox of options is fantastic and worth getting the game. If you actually play like real basketball with pick and roll and calls (and broadcast camera) it's basically watching real ball, it can get very immersive. And again, I just don't care about online, tried MyCarreer a little and all the cutscenes and the low rating of your player (incentivizing you to buy currency with real money) is just cringe as hell, so I just avoid it. Pro tip: if you want to "simulate" a MyCareer like gameplay without all the predatory stuff just turn on the "player lock" setting and set it to a specific position (PG if you want to play Iverson in the 2000's 76ers, for example), it can get a bit annoying when subs are automatically done as you'll basically be forced to play another player temporarily, but you can manage that with manual subs. This way you can have a "MyCareer" without the flashy stuff and cutscenes that I mostly don't care about. Also, playing as a historical player is much more immersive than a random custom player you generated, but that may be just my preference.TLDR: play MyNBA eras, avoid online. Actual gameplay on the court is immersive, realistic and highly customizable.

My only issues are the odd antialiasing and crashes (but that just might be my rig). You can dominate the paint this year with no dunk and high layup. Being big/strong actually matters this year, but also diminishes you in other ways (slower, more stamina consumption). Being small may be a disadvantage on defense, but offensively, you are almost un-guardable. Shooting has been changed to combat "zens" so, even if they are cheating, they can no longer be prolific cheaters. The game has introduced elements that award team play and discourages one man shows. Although you can still dominate the game as a one man army, you will lose against a team of skilled team players.I have yet to run into a cheater, but if I did, I dont think I would know. The dribbling is easier, most dribble combinations will auto-play for you while still giving you the ability to be creative and add your own flavor.  If you like basketball, and 2K, I say 2k25 is a must have. Especially if you are able to find a discord group with people willing to run proam 5v5, 3v3 to filter out any cheaters. If you play one MyCareer game on Hall of Fame difficulty (highest difficulty) on 12 minute quarters, you earn a little more than 1000 VC for a single game.If you want to upgrade your player to just 85 (which is the first time you will be capped and have to play multiple games to be able to increase your rating to 86 and so on), you gotta spend about 190k VC! With a few quests that you can complete here and there, a daily wheel spin with a chance to earn a little VC every day, you still gotta play about 150 games, that's almost 2 complete seasons, not including playoffs.-OR-Buy 200k VC with real money. It just costs 50€! But if you don't like how your build ended up playing for whatever reason, there is no way to refund at least some of that VC that you spent on your player, so if you wanna create a new player, start all over again with the spending!And if you care about customization and how your player looks, you gotta decide: make MyPlayer playable or spend your hard earned/payed VC on NBA Accessories, online play accessories, stamina boosts, animations, emotes, traversal items, basketballs, clothes, tattoos etc.! And let me tell you, these ain't cheap!I will not even touch on the ridiculous Pay2Win mechanics in MyTeam, the card collecting game which will can found in every sports game.- GAMEPLAY ISSUES - I haven't bought a 2k since 2K19 because i got tired of all this, but this year was so much better, they said. 2k now has a new ProPlay System to record NBA player movements and put them in the game, which is pretty cool! The issue is, the game is still so heavly animation based that you find yourself stuck in an animation for so long causing 3 second violations, make bad passes because your teammate isn't open anymore, miss seemingly wide open layups/dunks because a defender just slides into the play from behind etc. And then other times, mostly when playing defense, the animation to defend your opponent doesn't trigger and they just walk right through you for an easy layup/dunk. Your team in MyCareer STILL sucks compared to the opponent, who make every wide open shot almost guaranteed, but with their new contest system (if you are smaller, they shoot just over you) they now make the contested ones. If you're trying to play realistic, you will get frustrated by your teammates not switching after a pick and roll, passing out of wide open shots under the basket, missing wide open shots repeatedly etc. - The City and online play - The City is an area designed to steal your time. There are hundreds of different courts to play 1v1, 2v2, 3v3 or 5v5, hundreds of different shops to buy clothes, tattoos, accessories etc., there is an open gym for weekly workouts to increase stamina, quests with people to talk to that reward you with a jacket, 500 vc and/or some XP. Most of this would've been so much better in a menu. Gameplay in the online modes is absolutely ridiculous in my opinion. Players will just spam dribble moves from left to right until they get open for 3 or the defender falls over. Latency has always been a huge issue here and this hasn't changed, making it harder to time your shots/layups.The only reason i bought this game was a so called VC-Method, where you have to spend about 3 mind-numbing hours to get the quickest 50-60k VC possible, or spend about 4-5 hours to get around 150k VC. That's the length NBA 2k Players are willing to go. It is a full priced mobile game for PC and consoles. It will be my last 2K i will buy and i suggest you never buy one of these yourself because it will not change.

_childDocuments_.review: "NBA 2K25: A Love-Hate Slam Dunk (That'll Still Drain Your Wallet)"Okay, folks, let's talk about NBA 2K25. This game is like that ex you just can't quit, even though they keep asking to borrow money and "forgetting" to pay you back.  Yeah, the microtransactions are worse than a flagrant foul, but dang it, the gameplay is just so smooth.Look, I'm not gonna sugarcoat it. 2K25 is a love-hate relationship. On one hand, you've got the MyPLAYER mode, which is basically basketball role-playing at its finest.  You create your own baller, grind your way to the top, and live out your NBA dreams (minus the million-dollar contracts, sadly).  And then there's Eras, which lets you relive the glory days of basketball with classic teams and legendary players.  It's like a time machine for hoops fans, and it's pure nostalgia gold.But on the other hand, you've got those microtransactions lurking in the shadows like a shady sports agent. They're everywhere, tempting you to spend your hard-earned cash on virtual currency (VC) so you can upgrade your player and dominate the court.  It's a slippery slope, my friends, and I've lost more money to this game than I care to admit. (Don't tell my wife.)So, why do I keep coming back for more?  Because when 2K25 is good, it's really good.  The gameplay is tight, the graphics are slick, and the atmosphere is electric.  When you're draining threes and breaking ankles, it's easy to forget about the predatory monetization.  But then you remember you need to grind for hours or shell out more cash just to improve your player's free throw rating, and the frustration comes flooding back.Here's the bottom line: If you're a die-hard basketball fan who can resist the siren song of microtransactions (or you have a trust fund), then NBA 2K25 is worth checking out.  But for the rest of us mere mortals, I'd recommend waiting for a sale.  Trust me, your wallet will thank you.Now, if you'll excuse me, I need to go beg 2K for some free VC.  Maybe if I write them a heartfelt poem about my love for the game...  Nah, who am I kidding? They'll just tell me to open my wallet.

_childDocuments_.review: ***I was looking for a more arcade style game and that was my mistake.*** I am not the target audience for this game. I bought it to play with friends that were really into this franchise and what I bought was a game that will take hundreds of hours for me to get just average at it. Everything I am saying is my own perspective and will only be for those that don't usually play 2K games. My LARGEST issue is the cost to get into the game. You can either spend over $100 dollars (after purchase of the game) to increase your players stats buy buying skill points. OR you can level your character up by playing the game and earning points. So, it is kinda pay-to-win(ish). It will always have more to do with skill than stats and that is what keeps most people coming back, IMO. BUT in order to level up without spending real world money, you will be spending a very significant amount of time grinding out progress (probably 100+ hours). That is not a commitment I am willing to make. Some will be fine with that and actually enjoy it - different strokes.The HUB city area is just chaos to me. It seems like a terrible version of an open-world RPG. You have to walk from store to store (and other areas) in order to buy, train and practice. It is not something I appreciate. I would just prefer to purchase items in a menu that does not require that I memorize a specific store's location. The map and fast travel are poop-doodie and seem to ignore all of the clever ways RPGs have learned to make an open-world map. I also did not much care for the music library as a whole. There are some bangers, but there are also a lot of music I can do without. You can choose what songs play and can mute the music overall, which is good. I only have selected like 15-20 songs that I am willing to listen to and after hearing them 3-4 times in a play session, I am done with all of them.THIS IS NOT A VERY LEGITIMATE COMPLAINT (as much as it is just something that I would like to see)- with AI language technology being where it is, why do we still have to select from such a limited library of recorded names/nicknames? It reminds me of Fight Night and that game is 13 years old and Fight Night had many more nicknames available at that time. I h8 hearing my character called "MP" as default if I chose not to select from one of the available nicknames and have a name that isn't already recorded. BASICALLY: If you are a 2K fan, you are probably good with this game. Some of my friends are all about it. For a person that is a casual sports gamer I have to encourage you to stay away. You may get some playable hours out of the campaign and quick matches. But when you find yourself playing multiplayer it will not take you more than 2 matches before you realize the learning curve is as dramatic as playing the sport IRL. If you can get it on sale, give it a try. If you spend full price, you are just going to get a more expensive lesson in humility. Prepare to be faced with the choice to slog through the hundreds of hours it will take to "GIT GUD"; or get used to being clowned by some pretty "toxic" 2K-bros on how garbage you are.

Fix: Let me drop step people and pound the right stick up for the rise and down for the dunk instead.Your physics engine is still trash but I've come to the conclusion they care more about recycling the same garbage than fixing stuff that should've been fixed 10 years ago. _childDocuments_.review: As of right now, I have mixed opinions about this game. From experience of playing religiously since 2K18, this definitely feels very smooth and balanced *so far* gameplay wise. I haven't came across a build or certain attribute (dunk, steal, etc.) that needs tuning. Shooting is difficult this year in my opinion, if you feel hopeless in your shot, just go to Controller Settings and switch to "Low Risk Low Reward" as it will help you hit more slightly early/lates at the expense of lowering your green window.The game runs perfectly for me personally, I see a lot of reviews talking about performance, and more complaining about load times/launching the game itself. We need to consider the possibility that it may not be a developer issue on this one, as I have not experienced anything remotely similar to what some are complaining about. It literally says you need an SSD to play this game, and even if you have one and are still running into trouble, I'm sure there's something you can look into to find the fix.Now here's the real problem that I was worried about. Cheaters. I knew it'd come but I wasn't expecting it in the matter of hours. This is my first 2K on PC, as it's now Next Gen and I don't see a point in having a console anymore just for 2K. I'm starting to regret that decision. Launch night was fine, played a handful of park games and didn't see anything suspicious besides some of your guy's basketball IQ (park randoms are trash). It was tonight that I had seen at least 3 players with a 99 overall (on day 2 1/2, this is very unlikely) so I checked their player card. They are 60 overalls with nothing upgraded but they injected cheats into their game files to give them 99 in every stat. To avid 2K PC players, I'm sure you're used to this, but coming from console that's unacceptable.Besides the inevitable cheating issue that this game is bound to have, I recommend giving this year a shot if you enjoy past 2Ks. This one definitely seems promising gameplay wise.All we can do is bring awareness to the one person in charge of PC and pray they make a change, just report the cheaters.

_childDocuments_.review: 100 Hours over 2 accounts so far, here's my thoughts.-"MyCareer"/MyPlayerThe actual "Career" part of the MyPlayer mode is more in-depth than last year despite the smaller city and less meaningless quests (none of that fashion & rap stuff.)When you get your endorsements there isn't anything extra you have to go out of your way to do to obtain them, and VC is "easier" to come by than previous years.So far the monetization feels much less "In Your Face" and more so blends in with the environment of the basketball-focused city.This year the game has an Anti-Cheat and to no avail I haven't heard of a cheater problem this year on this platform, however I couldn't really give you a good assessment on this since I don't really play Online modes.-"MyTeam"/MyCasinoDon't bother playing this mode in ANY 2K unless you're good enough to make money from 2k by playing it.I can't tell you anything positive about this mode, if you like fantasy/arcade basketball, go for it. But from what I've heard MT is hard enough to come by as is and you're not really going to be having the best teams without paying.-MyNBAOverall my favorite mode to play.2K will always have my good graces in this category since what they've did with 2K23.Eras is a phenominal addition, and the Curry era is another stepping stone towards getting a year-by-year roster selection.Unfortunately, the people who weren't in the game last year, still aren't in the game.A few players who retired left the NBAPA therefore 2K lost the rights to them, so some players are missing from the roster.Players like Blake Griffin and Andre Iguodala are still in the game with their cyberfaces, available through modded rosters, and more players can be downloaded from the NLSC Forum.Fortunately, this game supports modding, althought it lacks Workshop support. With the platforms that have been given to modders this year, this mode will probably end up being the best there ever was.However, all good things must have a bad side."MyGM" (???)This is the worst it's ever been. It's never been more over.This mode is absolute Donkey Kong Shlong.I genuinely have no idea how they even let this ship.You have an office,and 5 characters (Your Staff and Top Rated Player)Those 5 characters have 2 lines each (No Voice)The decisions you make and and how you talk to people have almost ZERO impact on the game.And you can't even pick what era you play in.This mode has NO depth whatsoever.-PlayNow/QuickplayIf you play this game mode you should come to expect absolutely zero changes.Certain rewards and sub-modes have been slightly altered and tinkered with.Rating system remains the game.Player Control still not in the game.Non-Mode changesIn order to stop the Chronus Zen and other Automatic-Greening scripts and software, 2K has added an Animation-Based shot queue that isn't stable forcing you to watch your animation while you shoot instead of having a specific timing you memorize. It will be hard to get used to at first, but eventually you will be able to shoot at around the same percentage you used to.The Anti-CheatExpect less cheaters than previous games.I believe the era of unfiltered rediculous player-modding where people had the 76 foot tall players and 3 inch long arms is done.Overall - 6/10, best 2K that I've played. (Started in 2K22)

_childDocuments_.review: A VERY cautious recommend from me. I'm in my 30s, with plenty of free time to burn playing video games, and was a 2k/Madden/NCAA fan from the start until about 2016. Last 2k I played was 2k20, and the hard lean into the Park/City/Rec play modes with resources was, while logical, from a business perspective, given live services popping off at the time, the end for me. I loved the games despite the very obvious flaws with it, but, for me, it peaked in the year that they had Spike Lee direct the MyCareer mode (2016, maybe?).This game is a lot of the same stuff I didn't like about 2k20; VC is all but mandatory for Career, just to avoid the slog of leveling slowly to 70. I bought this on a 50% sale, knowing I'd be spending the other 50% I saved on VC to avoid hours of tedium. What really attracted me back, aside from the news I heard that there was at least some effort put into MyCareer this year, was the introduction of MyWNBA/The W modes, especially since they're offline; in theory, they can't take these modes away from you when they inevitably shut down the services for this game. It is very obvious they gave it very little investment, financially, but there was a good deal of honest effort on the part of The W mode; build archetypes are few/lacking, but it's a sacrifice I can handle for it's permanent nature. I cannot speak to any of the versus (Rec/Park) stuff, nor can I speak to the MyTeam mode (assuming it's the same old gatcha trash), but I find The W and MyCareer serviceable enough to justify a purchase on a half-off or deeper discount.5/10, 2k Basketball NEEDS a competitor again, they've been getting worse ever since Live died.

I played about 20 mins offline mycareer gameplay, it was solid no complaints. I dont play MyTeam or MyLeague mode so I can't speak on that. PlayNow Online seems good although I did not play it myself but based on mypark gameplay it should be fun. 2k to me is about half basketball realism(concepts like spacing, ball movement, shot selection etc.) and half stupid fun(like the old days) 2k25 delivers on both ends solidly. Rewarding gameplay for skilled and high IQ players. No game is without its flaws, those are noticeable as well, but overall nothing has ruined my experience. Final review:2k24(4.5/10)     2k25(7.5/10 so far)
