_childDocuments_.review: Do you love the good old days when games would just borrow random words from Norsk mythology because it sounds cool while not being related to the myths at all?HELL YEAH BROTHER, ME TOO!Jokes aside this game was and probably still is my favourite JRPG This game was originally released for the Wonderswan Color. Then Ported to the Gameboy Advance.Then ported to the PSPAnd now ported to Steam (Mobile and Switch JP only)The game has a level up system that requires you to diversify your play style between different weapons, and the durability system never feels like it's there just to be a nuisance. It had proper planning put behind it with how you'll progress through the game and plan out your next fightsOn top of being a JRPG though, the game also has some dating simulator elements, where your party members react to the choices you make and grow an affection for you, said reactions can lead to new items or different story paths and makes replaying the game well worth itThis steam release also comes with a lot of quality of life fixes and additional challenges for returning players making it something that's great to pick up even if you've already beaten the game.And yes, you can turn off the pixel filter.
_childDocuments_.name: Riviera: The Promised Land

_childDocuments_.review: An incredibility charming JRPG that progresses similarly like a Choose-your-own-adventure novel.The main path is set, but each screen is littered with things to poke at that'll grant you funny scenes, power-ups, items, extra battle encounters, minigames, and QTEs. You won't see it all on a first run, but the game is meant to be replayed over and over due to its multiple endings and score system (if you're so inclined).If you're a story enthusiast, take note that it's basically a slice-of-life journey where all the fun is in the character interactions, which there is a /ton/. Just relax and enjoy the ride~I do want to highlight the battles though. You take in a pool of items and each party member does their own thing with it. Bringing an iron Sword? One character will strike the nearest foe and one will use it randomly target. Bring an Egg? Why, one will literally just start cooking it over-easy on the battlefield and another will  it for a whopping..... Needless to say, I love this system. It brings quite a bit of life into combat that I really appreciate.And yes, The soundtrack slaps. Heck, this release literally allows you toggle between the older variations or even the arrange ver. which is amazing! Try it out if you're not feeling the default setup.I've played the GBA and PSP versions way too much and to this day nothing hits quite like it, if you're an avid RPG enjoyer, do give it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Riviera: The Promised Land

_childDocuments_.review: Having played this game practically yearly since I stumbled upon it on the PSP, obviously this was going to be bought the moment it launched. It's basically a turn based JRPG with a focus on character interactions. Personally I adore the cast and how present they are all the time, but if you don't get along with JRPG girls then you should know you spend a lot of time interacting with the cast. There are just a lot of quirks. Weapons and items for battle have limited uses and different functions for each character, so deciding how to use your inventory most effectively for a fight has some puzzle qualities. You can see what the enemies are weak to before a fight, so you can always plan accordingly. Battles reward you for finishing them quickly or with flashier special attacks, so there's incentive to think about what you're doing. There are a number of quick time events that can impact how a stage plays out. I don't think they're too egregious since they never impede your progress, but they are both there and pretty common.The exploration elements in stages are definitely one of the high points. Individual scenes can play out very differently based on what you choose to do in them. Some of them might even impact other choices much later into the stage. Even failing QTEs isn't always a straight up punishment since you can get different character interactions out of them. Even six odd plays in, I was still stumbling onto scenes I'd not seen before.I am pleasantly surprised by how many additions have been made. The battle UI shows more pertinent information at all times and being able to speed up battles is a welcome addition. There are a number of options for the music and sprite art, even one to make the sprites match their character art more closely, which isn't something I've seen before. Also super easy to switch between audio tracks on the fly. If there's anything I'd want to see added, it would be some more granular control of the difficulty options. Being able to ease up the QTEs without also lowering the general difficulty at least. While I appreciate having the general difficulty separate from the settings for how your inventory and items work, I think more variety between the original restrictions and basically no restrictions would be nice too.Good game with a good port that actually adds meaningful quality of life features. I look forward to playing for all the endings again, after getting best girl's of course.
_childDocuments_.name: Riviera: The Promised Land

_childDocuments_.review: This was one of my favorite games back when i was a teenager, it came out both for the game-boy advance and the playstation portable. You had to get stronger by getting new items and using practice before going into battle because the enemies could sky rocket in strength if you just went through the level. This game is in the same universe as Yggdra Union, Knights of the Nightmare and Gungnir. If you love turn based games you should definitely enjoy this. Who you let strike the last hit in battle raises that characters affection points and will help determine your ending. Also try not to get to reliant on any specific character you can at times be forced into battle with a random team. Lastly Practice is key, you will find items that brake easily but help gain skills. Use those only in Practice until all characters who can gain skills from that item have learned it. Then decide if you want to use it or not. Hoping they decide to translate and bring Blaze Union and Gloria Union as well (all the games help explain the lore better). Extremely underrated gem..... truly hope you all enjoy (and the soundtrack is awesome)

_childDocuments_.review: It's kind of a hybrid RPG/visual novel/dating sim. I don't know how to describe it, but it's a classic. A lot of the dialogue and scenes take place while the characters are exploring dungeons and interacting with objects they find, which makes dungeon exploration seem like a pretty lively social activity. It's fun. I recommend this game strongly. The port is great. You can get the wonderswan soundtrack, the GBA soundtrack, the PSP soundtrack, and two more besides, and yes, you can turn off the pixel smear filter. You can play a mode that keeps the 15 item limit or you can play a mode that removes that sort of inconvenience.You can also set it so you max out experience for an item the first time you use it, so you don't spend so much time on practice combat (note that this option is separate from the game mode options and is set while playing).

_childDocuments_.review: The first and best Dept. Heaven game is finally on Steam and it was worth the wait.Not much to say about the game itself as it's the same as on other platforms - it's a jRPG/visual novel/dating sim hybrid with excellent music and entertaining story. If that sounds good to you, you should check it out if you haven't played any of the console releases.The port itself is very well made, there is a lot of QoL functions that helps with multiple playthroughs, you can chose between modern and retro soundtracks, adjust visual filters, displayed buttons and other stuff. Honestly it's a pretty solid selection of options.There are some minor gripes however. The terrible english voiceover is here - which is not that much of a problem because game defaults to JPN one but there is a button in game that dynamically switches you to ENG and I cringed visibly whenever accidentally hitting it. Honestly it's so bad that I wouldn't be against removing it completely.Speaking of removing things - it was to be expected but bathing scenes were censored which is just a crying shame ToT. With how much effort the port took to preserve original music it's weird that it doesn't allow to switch to GBA or WonderSwan CG and portrait sets.Despite that I'm very happy with this release and glad that more people can experience it now.Fia best waifu.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the GBA version a long time ago, and knew of the various changes in the PSP version.  This port honestly feels like a rerelease of the PSP version, but with various toggleable features like not having a puny inventory anymore.  I do miss some of the GBA versions of the songs, but the soundtrack is as nice as ever overall.  I haven't seen all that many issues with lag or whatever, and I'm running this on an eight year old gaming laptop, so if my about-to-be-a-potato PC can run this, yours might  be able to too!The game isn't all that difficult, the main features are interacting with the characters through dialogue choices and the relatively unique for its time idea of "level ups" and gaining abilities through grinding out items.  The slug monsters that delete item uses are still the worst, but the various QoL features do help make the experience seem better than it was.  All in all it's a decent portUpdate:  After clearing the game once with Fia's ending (she is best girl, though I really really like Cierra too), this review is unchanged.  Yes the Quick time events are annoying, but this game also has toggleable QoL features that are really nice.  They even out.  If you only care about gameplay, maybe you will like this game less than I do, but it has great vibes, great characters, great music along with an ok battle system and an interesting level up concept by training with weapons/equipment.

Very similar appearance, demeanor and even the same voice actor, too. _childDocuments_.review: Absolutely great port of the Switch/mobile version, which is in turn an upgrade of the PSP version.For those who are not familiar, Riviera is an old adventure game from the Wonderswan that aged well due to its unique item and field mechanics, and as well as the story that unfolds based on your choices. Unlike Yggdra Union, the difficulty in this game is much more forgiving and has an easier curve to most people.For those already familiar, this version of the game has many QoL differences from previous versions of the game. Those listed are from my observations from the PSP version:- As advertised, you can speed up to five times or super-speed with "Skip"- You can save on the field now (whenever you can open the menu) as opposed to only between sub-chapters and the book in the house- Auto-saves are present for  outside battle- You can merge items in the inventory menu, up to 99 of the same named item- You can even save mid-battle on any of your character's turn- You can choose between five versions of the BGM, with the default using the PSP version- There are three difficulty settings (Easy, Normal, Hard), plus two modes (Casual, Original) which makes it the most accessible possible- Just like Yggdra Union, you can switch between JP and EN voices anytime. Oddly enough, the game defaults to JP the first time I start- You can use the mouse and keyboard to play - haven't tested this myself, been playing with a DS4 just fine- You have access to the gallery in the title screen without needing to find the key items in-gameIf you're coming from the GBA version then you should know these few things:- You can select the encounters in the practice menu instead of the selection being random- There are more illustrations to see and collect- A lot of voice acting in dialogue outside the title screen and battle scene- The list of QoL from above

_childDocuments_.review: As someone with 100% completion (steam achievements and EX library), I very much enjoyed the game. I highly recommend you play through the game blind one time just to have fun first. Then if you want to aim for all the items and secrets you can look up a guide.The game has a different way of "leveling up" that ties stats to mastering weapons. By getting enough exp from using a weapon, the character gains stats and learns an overskill, a powerful skill or utility also tied to that weapon. Weapons and items have durability, but I never found it to be a limiting problem. You might consider that this system requires you to hoard a lot of weapons and items, but you can pick a new mode that increases your inventory size and the base durability of weapons.In terms of difficulty, the game tends to be easiest in the middle of the story. It's more difficult in the beginning (where you haven't learned enough overskills and stats) and towards the end (where the enemies are really strong). This is magnified in higher difficulties. Your mileage may vary depending on which of the cast you decide to train.Gameplay outside of battles involves switching between a movement mode to explore and an action mode to interact. Interaction causes events that can earn you items, find new ways to traverse, or lead to dialogue between the characters. There's even QTEs. It was fun to figure out the means of getting certain items and outcomes by changing the way or order in which you with interact with things. If you make a mistake, the remaster has an autosave function that allows you to go back to a point before you had taken a certain action.The story is whatever. It's the trope where there's one guy and actions you take affect how much the other characters like him and which ending he gets. I can't lie though, it did make me laugh. If you want 100% completion, you will eventually have to beat the game multiple times to get all the endings, which can wear out the story on you. It definitely did for me.The game isn't without some flaws. Exp gain towards mastering weapons can be slow, but isn't too much of a problem if you keep to three characters. However, there are enemies and bosses where certain characters have an advantage, and you might not have trained them. Furthermore, near the end of the game there's a *spoiler* that can severely punish you if you do not train of lot of people. There's a practice mode where you can infinitely fight with no stakes to gain EXP, but it gets boring after a while. Luckily, the game has an exp multiplier function in which you can change how much exp you get for using a weapon. I recommend you turn it up in later playthroughs and harder difficulties.Despite being a remaster, there are still some oversights, like dying in a scripted battle you have no control over leading to a game over.After beating the game, you are able to transfer certain things to future playthroughs: stats, items, and overskill exp. While nice, it can be inflexible. if you transfer your overskill exp progress to a new game but not stats, your characters do NOT keep the stats from the overskills you learned already. This can result in an unwinnable position at some point in the game. However, if you transfer your stats, you also keep stats gained from story events, which leads to an extreme snowball that makes the game too easy.I was able to move past these issues thanks to the QoL the remaster provides, and overall, I really recommend you give the game a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Riviera: The Promised Land

_childDocuments_.review: a young boy created to be a living wmd is brought out of storage in order to preemptively destroy an entire world that the heavens have deemed to be a threat. every time he tries to air his suspicions that maybe this plan ain't it chief, yknow, perhaps genocide is a little cringe, his coworkers slap a hand over his mouth lest he be deep-sixed as a traitor by their authoritarian boss. luckily for the boy, he is snatched away from his cohort, bonked on the head, and dumped into the laps of local girls. granted the freedom to become his own person and make his own choices, the boy decides to pursue what he believes is right... while getting up to all sorts of goofy hijinks with the local girls along the way.riviera is one of those rare games that truly has something for everybody: there's lots of lighthearted comedy for players who want a laugh, but the overall plot arc is serious, and the deep lore is both quite dark and completely unhinged. one playthrough is fairly short, but the game has about six times as much replay value. gameplay mechanics are easy enough for a casual player to make it through without worries but have enough depth that the real truck freaks have plenty to gnaw on. there are cute girls for the cute girl enjoyers, cute boys for the cute boy enjoyers... and a marriage of point and click style exploration with turn-based battles, inventory management, and quick time events that could only have come from the mind of director ito shinichi.PLUS this edition of riviera has got a lot of quality of life changes that improve the experience overall. grinding taking too long? annoyed at having to reroll chests over and over to get that last dang item? the boost menu is here to save you. want to compare line reads between the original voiceovers and the atlus usa dub? there is a whole new button to change voice language on the fly AND you can replay lines in either audio in the shiny new backlog. AND steam functionality makes it really easy to change the overall game language if you happen to be multilingual and aren't in the mood for atlus' gag translation.TL;DR if you have yet to experience riviera......... you should buy it, you Will find something to enjoy.MORE DETAILED FEATURES GUIDE FOR FOLKS WHO'VE PLAYED PREVIOUS RIVIERA ITERATIONS:the steam port is based on the psp special edition, which is the version of the game that the PAL region got. this means that the bonus chapter has cgs, you can save anytime you like rather than only between areas, and that the fanservice events have inexplicable swimsuits rather than nudity per decree of CERO. the sort of boobie devotee for whom this is a dealbreaker may be better served trying to find a copy of the north american psp release rather than complaining.so, what else is new? this riviera rerelease features the easy/normal/hard/nightmare difficulties first introduced in knights in the nightmare, but it's also got four different play modes you can freely choose from (though two of those must be unlocked) that can do things like change your overall inventory capacity, restrict available save points to between areas a la the standard psp release and previous, and allow you to bench ein/ecthel instead of being forced to deploy him in every battle.i mentioned the boost features above, but once you've beaten the game once you also have the option to skip battles if you're willing to accept the lowest score and therefore not receive any item drops. this can be useful if you don't really care about your score/already have 100% items and are just trying to collect endings. furthermore the configurations menu lets you choose whether you want to listen to the wsc, gba, or psp editions of the bgm (or remixes of the wsc tracks), pick between gba and psp sfx, and even turn off the cat noises.additionally delicious is the fact that you can new game plus and choose what things you want to carry over from your chosen file; you can keep your stats and your inventory AND allow your characters to relearn all their skills if you love to be op, or eschew one or more of these for a challenge.oh and did i mention that the art that's used for the steam trading cards was only ever used for an obscure limited edition collectable and has never been released in full, let alone digitally???????????literally the ONLY thing that prevents me from calling the steam port the single most perfect iteration of riviera to ever exist, no notes, is the fact that sting did not have some of the illustration assets available at large sizes and had to blow them up and then smooth them out to make them fit chungo hd resolution. this is USUALLY less noticeable than it was for the recent blaze union port because of tobe sunaho's less ornate shading style, but if you're a returning fan you Will notice, and there are a few cgs where the forced resizing is so obvious even a new player will be able to see it.this doesn't cause any problems with the gameplay of course, but tobe's lovely artwork and sixty squillion cgs are one of the selling points of riviera for me personally and so i would've liked for sting to use a smaller screen resolution for the steam release if possible. they didn't really have a choice for consoles, and recreating the new ui at a smaller scale for this release alone would have taken extra effort, so i can understand why they didn't, but it takes what would have been a 100/100 rerelease and knocked it down to a 95. alas.this is absolutely the easiest way to get your hands on riviera through official channels nowadays though, so even with my singular gripe i still recommend that you buy it. then stream it to your friends. stream it to your followers. stream it to your enemies even. haul them into the dept heaven quicksand do it do it. incentivize sting to release even MORE games to this platform. the future of rereleases is in our hands!!!!!!!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Played and loved the GBA game, played and loved this. New QoL features, difficulty settings (including a Lunatic difficulty you obtain after clearing the game once) and a new $35 pricetag... Yikes, that didn't go over well, did it? The developer has also ported Yggdra Union to steam, a much more popular game, for less. Riviera is a JRPG that bucks most of the conventions, instead focusing on a stage-oriented game with a scoring system, CG gallery. Enemies drop better loot if you kill them with style, which you will be graded on at the end of every encounter. Oh, and there's no leveling.Pro-tip: When you unlock a skill, make sure to actually *use* it once, so it carries over into the extra chapter!

_childDocuments_.review: 1000 years have passed since Ragnarok, the war between Asgard, realm of the gods, and Utgard, home of the demons. Recently, the floating island of Riviera has been showing signs of the demons’ return. With the gods no longer present, another Ragnarok would mean certain doom for Asgard. The decision had been made to evoke the Retribution and destroy Riviera; the Grim Angels Ein and Ledah were appointed as the executors of this task. Now, two angels descend upon the Promised Land. [Atlus Software]

name: Elrentaros Wanderings
detailed_description: The dual life where Fantasy meets Reality begins! A brand-new action RPG, “Elrentaros Wanderings”! The story is set in Elrentaros, a remote town far away from the capital of Melvania. The adventure begins as the protagonist visits this town and tries to help the residents, each with distinctive personalities. Suddenly, a mysterious light appears that leads the protagonist to a completely different world. Could it be that this world is the real world? Learn the secrets of the two worlds! You may select a male or a female protagonist. You are able to build a deeper relationship with the townspeople in Elrentaros by helping them solve their tasks. Among all the people in this town, there are 10 “Partner Characters” with whom you can develop a closer relationship. A useful battle feature “Alliance” can be unlocked when you send them gifts and elevate your friendship. If the relationship becomes more intimate, you can also invite them over for a meal or have them come and visit your tent. Prepare your “Build” with the Alliances, weapons and armor obtained during your journey, and take on the upcoming dungeons. When a dungeon is cleared, a more difficult “Challenge Level” will be made available to you. As higher-level weapons and armors can be obtained in more difficult dungeons, be sure to create a strong “Build” and challenge the dungeons as much as possible.

A new fantasy × reality adventure begins. Introducing the all-new action RPG, Elrentaros Wanderings. Welcome to Elrentaros, a hinterland town far from the Melvanian capital. Visiting on a journey, you mingle with the colorful locals
and embark on a quest to find ways to help them. But your adventure takes a sudden turn when a strange light surrounds you and you wake in a different realm. Could this be the real universe? Unravel the secret of the two worlds!


Choose your protagonist, male or female,
and forge deep connections with the people of Elrentaros as you make conversation, listen to their troubles, and come to their aid.
There are ten ""partner characters"" to form bonds with.
Giving gifts to partners can deepen your friendships and unlock battle ""alliances"" in return.
Grow closer, and they might even invite you home for dinner or visit your tent to talk.

When you gain weapons and armor through alliances and dungeon raids, you can combine them into arsenal ""builds"" to tackle the dungeons as they grow ever more formidable!

Cleared dungeons can be faced again at higher ""challenge levels"" to snag better gear.
Tougher dungeons offer higher-spec weapons and armor, so keep taking them on to find your ultimate build!

Unravel the mysteries of your travels between realms and save Elrentaros from a terrible fate with the help of your new friends!

name: UberSoldier
detailed_description: Get ready for an epic World War II adventure like no other with UberSoldier! Immerse yourself in a gripping first-person shooter that will transport you to the heart of the action. This game developed by Burut Creative Team will have you on the edge of your seat. Picture this: the Nazis have made a chilling discovery, a technique that brings the dead back to life. But there's a twist - these revived soldiers possess incredible powers and are under the control of the first person they encounter. As the Allies fight to win the war, the Nazis start unleashing their fearsome UberSoldiers - super-soldiers with unimaginable abilities. Step into the shoes of Karl Stoltz, a German soldier who was killed in combat but resurrected by the Nazis. Now, Karl is seeking vengeance against his former masters and has joined the Allies to turn the tide of the war. Embark on a thrilling 12-mission rampage against the Third Reich, wielding 16 authentic WWII weapons, from the powerful Browning automatic rifle to the mighty Panzerschreck. But that's not all - as Karl, you have access to a unique 'temporal shield' that temporarily freezes bullets in mid-air, protecting you from enemy gunfire. Take down enemies with precision headshots to extend the duration of your supernatural shield, or unleash fury by stabbing three foes in quick succession to increase your health. Build up your rage and destruction to maintain your powers and unleash chaos on the Nazi threat. This special Steam release of UberSoldier has even removed the original DRM Starforce, giving you a seamless and unforgettable gaming experience. Join Karl in his quest to bring down the Nazi regime and take control of World War II. Are you ready to rewrite history? Get your copy of UberSoldier today and embark on an adrenaline-fueled journey into the heart of the war!

_childDocuments_.review: I've had  sitting on my Steam account for a while, and every time I go on a Eurojank binge I always feel its siren call, but being the type of person who can't just play the second game in a series before the first I've left it sitting as the first game hasn't been available on Steam... until now! I've once again succumbed to my addiction to low budget Eastern European FPS games so I was pretty happy to see they finally have this game available, and after playing through it I'm glad I waited because skipping this really would be missing out on something special.All things considered,  is pretty solid with a lot to like, especially compared to something like  games, which might have interesting vibes, but are borderline unplayable. The gunplay is about what you'd expect from an early-to-mid 2000's WWII shooter and the typical lineup is here and feels good to use. Aiming down sights can be a bit stumpy and if you make the mistake of trying to switch weapons while aiming down sights the game freaks out on you, but overall the shooting is good. While the enemies aren't the smartest, they do have some interesting behaviors such as shooting explosive barrels you're standing near, and I was pleasantly surprised at how well both the enemies and allies do at navigating levels.What makes the titular Ubersoldier Uber though, is his "temporal shield" which is basically Neo's bullet reflection ability from . At low levels, you simply stop bullets in their tracks and let them fall to the ground, but once you've charged the shield enough you can re-aim them and send them back. You charge it by getting three consecutive headshots, which is a bit of a challenge, but reasonable, and once you've got enough of a charge to start reflecting bullets back at enemies the game becomes deliriously fun. Once you've mastered the shield, you can start clearing rooms in the span of seconds and it feels fantastic. The shield doesn't drain particularly quickly either, so once you've got it build up to a full bar, that's enough to make it through a level or two just quickly spamming bullets back at bad guys. Machine Gun nest causing you trouble? Return to sender. What's also fun is that headshots you score from deflecting bullets also count towards the three headshot count, it's tricky to get them this way but really satisfying if you do.What also impressed me are some little details you might not expect from a game of this budget and scope. One thing I thought was cool was if you get hit by a grenade but survive, it actually knocks you down for a second and you have to get up, which is one of those things that seems obvious when you think about it, but I can't really think of an FPS that's really done that. The Submarine mission also has a surprisingly fun torpedo minigame, though I found the anti-aircraft section that follows it went on a bit long.My favorite aspect of  though, has to be the levels themselves. A big part of the appeal of so-called "Eurojank" games is the atmosphere in their environments, and every single level in this is gorgeous. The lighting isn't quite as robust as City Interactive's Lithtech powered games, but there's still some great dynamic effects and industrial hellscapes you're shooting through are peak Eastern European environment design. Some of the environments, particularly toward the end, almost feel liminal, and I got a lot of the same vibes I do from the wartime levels of .That said, not everything about  is a great time. The later levels have a particularly cruel tendency to put explosive barrels and tanks in corners where you won't see them as you come out of a door, so there's a tendency for you to seemingly randomly explode before realizing there's a barrel you need to shoot first. The obsession with random explosions really ramps up in the final level or two, to an almost absurd degree since buildings are being bombed all around you and random debris is flying all over the place, but it was worth pushing through. I also think that because of the weapon accuracy, the larger outdoor areas don't play as well as the tighter indoor environments, and while your shield can help you cover ground, it can get tricky if you've depleted it.That said though, there was never a point where I felt like it was impossible to progress and it wasn't nearly as frustrating as some of the other Eurojank games I've played. I mostly had a really fun time with this and I enjoyed the very goofy, but earnestly delivered story.As far as technical aspects go, the game generally worked well but I did run into an issue where for whatever reason the graphics menu wouldn't let me change the display resolution, so I had to edit the game's config file. The method for doing that is really weird too, instead of typing in the width and height you want, you have to do an insane math problem in which you multiply the height you want by the number 65536, then add the width. I decided to play in 1920x1440, so I had to set the r_resolution value in config.ini to 94373760. Why anyone in their right mind would hide the resolution behind a such a system is beyond me, but once I put that number in everything worked fine. I was actually really surprised that the UI scaled properly since even if you keep a 4:3 aspect ration, some games (like  tend to have the UI ridiculously small, and thankfully the game had no issues running at 144 FPS either.This was a pleasant surprise and something of a hidden gem, and I'm glad it finally made it to steam. I hope more backlog titles like this will be re-released and hopefully they find an easy way to fix the resolution issue in the graphics menu, because otherwise this actually runs really well.  is apparantly somewhat beloved in certain circles, so I'm excited to move onto that one soon.

_childDocuments_.review: Played the 2nd game first as this wasn't available on Steam at the time, but man do I regret it, I even wonder how the sequel became reality when this is sooo bad in comparison. _childDocuments_.review: ÜberSoldierPositives:+ Acceptable graphics (for its time)+ Ok shadows and lightning effects+ Weird physics engine (resulting in some fun moments)+ Good sounds+ Some parts are quite fun+ Got some low budget charm to it+ Ok temporal shield to useNegatives:- Unstable framerate- Bad voiceacting- Monotonous and repetitive gameplay- Below par gunplay- Overly use of special effects- Bad animations- Some bugs and glitches (but nothing serious)- The story is just bad- Weird head-bob that cant be disabled- No proper widescreen or fov fix out of the box This is a low budget russian game thats got some charm to it. Its in the so bad that its good category.So if youre into that stuff, play this game. Otherwise there are plenty much better WW2 shooters out there.This title is a tad better than the sequel.Total Score: 6/10NB! If you want to fix the game for widescreen with the right resolution and fov, do this:Go to: C:\Program Files\steam\steamapps\common\UberSoldier\config.iniOpen it with notepad and change the numbers behind: r_resolutioncl_hudfov cl_fovSome examples: 16:9 format: cl_hudfov 0.65 cl_fov 90 (keep the numbers between 80-106)Resolutions:             1920 x 1080p = r_resolution 707808002160 x 1440p = r_resolution 943744003840 x 2160p = r_resolution 141561600Save the file and set it to read-onlyNow you need to download HxDStart HxD and in the program open this file: C:\Program Files\steam\steamapps\common\UberSoldier\platforms\common\XTend3D.dllGo to offset 21E9B0 find 61 0B B6 3B and edit it to 61 0B E6 3BThe FOV will now be correctedThen go to offset E950 find AB AA AA 3F and edit it to 39 8E E3 3FThe aspect ratio will now be in 16:9 widescreen formatSave the changes and exit HxD.Now you can start and enjoy the game, have fun!

_childDocuments_.review: It is a fun simple shooter, with for its time good environments, a fine enough story and satisfying gunplay. And let's not forget the tons of over-the-top destruction moments and countless awesome explosions. Way better than its sequel as it does not share most of the sequel's problems.Though, just like the 2nd game, I do not like the upgrade system. You have to kill 3 enemies with a knife in a short time pediod to get a health upgrade or perform 3 headshots for shield power upgrade. As far as I know you can have infinite amount of upgrades as without trying too hard, I managed to get my health to 202 and my shield's energy line was fully white, yet I could still "upgrade" it somehow. But the problem with these is that game basically forces you to play a specific style, you start not to think how can you survive, but how to melee 3 enemies to get the next health upgrade. I had the same problem with the sequel, but they made it even worse there. At least here, the upgrades aren't as mandatory and you could beat the game just fine without any upgrades. Though if you get too many shield upgrades you basically become overpowered, and it is very easy to achieve that even on the hardest difficulty.I'm surprised that this game got released on Steam many years later after the first one. But I'm happy. I really wish Specnaz 2 (game which runs on the same engine) was on Steam too as it was my favourite of the bunch.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: While this is not the worst game ever it's only very mediocre at best and quite janky. This is a neutral/medium review because it is not straight up bad game but its so-so at best.Übersoldier I first played back in the day and it had some serious issues due to the old useless and infamous russian copy protection system called StarForce. Game also had insane amount of crashing. Thankfully now available steam edition has gotten rid of the former and also crashing hasn't happened one single time here either.You play as german hero Karl who gets killed and awokened by an evil german scientist. With this rebirth you gain a power to create a force field in front of you lol. So that's where this game's gimmick relys on. You have limited amount of forcebar that you can deploy in front of you and you gain more of the forcebar by killing enemies with a headshot. You also gain hp or something releated to hp by doing melee kills..ini editing is required to get modern resolutions and so forth working in this. But by enabling modern widescreen, breaks the in-game menu cursor finding. With widescreen you have to click in places that would seem like there isn't anything to click in order to select the gui elements. Inorder to change aspect ratio from 4:3 to widescreen and different FOV, you have to hex edit the game. That's something I left undone as it proved to be too much of an hassle but according to people it should be possible. Just know what youre getting into.Graphics are somewhat decent for 2006. This game has heavy Painkiller and Half-Life 2 look to it considering all lighting is static and lightmaps baked into the textures. Soundwise this supports EAX but this is the kind of perfect example where developer just quickly slapped in the reverb and didn't bother actually testing if it truly worked and sounded logical at all. There are in places heavy reverb where you would expect to be cramped and "muddy" and places you'd expect to echo like a huge cave there is absolutely zero of it.Actual sound effects themselves are very basic and nothing to write home about.Level design is kinda more typical mid 2000's linear style with some rooms to explore and check. Gunplay while this unfortunately does have aimdownsights, doesn't seem to punish you for not using them. I seem to hit from the hip quite accurately but the game has absolutely insane size muzzleflash which makes it hard to always see the enemies while youre firing. Also playing on hard difficulty it really becomes an issue since this is one of those games where the enemy will terminator vision you thru the walls and soon as you show 1 millimeter of your skin behind the wall, they will hit you with 100%accuracy from all directions.Gets really tiresome playing since this game does nothing that is amazing. The gunplay is dull cause you always have to prepare to take few shots when going into a new area due to the before mentioned A.I with terminator vision. Level design is so basic and just there to be played, no amazing eastereggs or any memorable sceneary. Guns are you basic WWII era designs.+Cool concept and art style/aesthetic+Couple cool tunes (Martin Kesici menu music)+Forcefield stopping bullets in realtime looks nice-Terminator vision enemy A.I-Guns don't really pack punch-Missed opportunity with use of EAX-Overall just too dull to keep playing

_childDocuments_.review: I've liked this game and revisited it from time to time ever since its original release. Really glad to finally see it on steam; the retail release has the later version StarForce DRM that will make any version of Windows newer than XP bluescreen and refuse to boot until you remove it.It's not really a hidden gem - it's a janky singleplayer WWII shooter with the twist, "you have a bullet shield." the sequel has been available on here for years, but I think it was a step back in gameplay from this one. the guns do a good amount of damage here and headshots take some aiming - in the second one, it felt like enemies were bullet sponges unless you were aiming at their huge heads. headshots are a game mechanic; three consecutive ones give you more bullet shield power, and with enough power it will fling the bullets where you're pointing when turning the shield off.you can aim down the sights of the guns, but your view sways enough that sometimes you're better off firing from the hip.the in-engine cutscenes are unintentionally funny, with awkward delivery and poorly edited timing. think The Room.all that said, the gameplay is solid at its core, and I've been coming back to it for... at this point, 18 years! I think that's worth a thumbs up.

_childDocuments_.review: i changed my review on this game like 3 different times. But I cant ignore how awful this video game is.the 3 headshot or 3 knife idea is a really bad idea, then you are focusing on getting 3x headshots before the timer runs out, completely ignoring how much HP you have left. This got me killed many times. the developers really enjoy insta-killing the player for no reason, thats a big part of this game. And the loading screens are LONG for an old game.you cant fire your gun if your finger is holding down the right mouse button, i never realized how often i do that until i played this game.. You had one job to make a gun game and the gun cant even shoot? when you press 1, 2, 3, or 4 to swap weapons, pressing the number isnt enough, you have to confirm the weapon switch as well by clicking left mouse. Horrible. Who is going to accidentally hit 1,2,3,4 on their keyboard??? Literally one of the stupidest thing ive ever seen make its way into a PC shooter gamethe game is just overall very.. stupid. Imagine a game where the fake doors, that you know are fake doors, because you attempted to open them 1000 times and now you know are FAKE doors. Well guess what? In one of the main quests you need to open one of them... But not just regularly, You have to look inside a window and shoot a red barrel nearby to destroy said door. HOW ON EARTH DO YOU EXPECT A PLAYER TO BE ABLE TO KNOW THAT?worst case ive ever seen of expecting the player to be psychic these developers should make a whole standalone game based on the turret defense segment, that was almost as fun as cod:waw zombies.. But instead of zombies you are running around a boat to different turrets, shooting torpedos and planes as they pass overhead. That was an incredible segment of gaming. Good job on that part.

_childDocuments_.review: At the height of World War II, with the outcome still very much in doubt, secret Nazi experiments are searching for a way to bring life back to the dead. name: Crime Boss: Rockay City
detailed_description: Welcome to the 90’s Rockay City! Heist, loot and shoot your way to the top of the criminal underworld! Build your criminal empire in the singleplayer rogue-lite campaign or put together a crew with your friends in action-packed co-op multiplayer heists! Heist, steal and rob it all! Become a notorious criminal legend in this tension-packed, over-the-top, first-person shooter. Use a wide range of weapons and equipment to combat police forces and rival gangs while you make off with the score! Go guns blazing or undetected with immersive stealth gameplay in highly randomized heists. Build your squad and successfully rob banks, hold up stores, raid armored trucks and more! The game comes with numerous big and medium heists, dozens of quick jobs and a variety of turfwar battles. Choose from 3 difficulty options to match your skill level. New adventures await, buddy! After the demise of the previous crime boss, this city is yours for the taking! Welcome to Rockay City, Florida – a city full of quirky characters, 90s gangster pop culture and cheesiest dialogues since VHS. Take on the role of the legendary Travis Baker in the single-player, rogue-lite campaign. Earn money in heists, manage a team of criminals and conquer the other gangs' territories to rule the underworld of Rockay City. Every strategic decision has its consequences – but failure doesn’t mean it’s over. Unlock permanent buff cards, to help you make the next run and complete your objective. Can your crime empire take over the city before Sheriff Norris stops you in your tracks? Be the top dog, solo or with friends. Create and customize your own boss and become a true crime legend! Play offline with helpful bots or team up with friends in 4 player PVE co-op multiplayer. Earn money and experience in single missions, Shuffle mode or the mini-campaigns in Urban Legends. Find a reliable crew using quickplay matchmaking, session browser or by inviting your friends. Unlock weapons, equipment, skins and teammates by gaining XP for completing missions across single and multiplayer modes. Form a crew with your friends and climb to the top!

_childDocuments_.review: Well worth a discounted price with all DLCs for free. 7/10Visually very good and with a good mechanic. Would have been higher if it was more polished, some bugs keep happening. Maybe not content-wise but the rest, including the bots, are better than PayDay 2 and so much better than PayDay 3. Heists are pretty quick so far, get in and get out style. Police becomes stronger, similar to a GTA wanted system during the heist so it prevents you from spending too much time in a heist.It feels pretty balanced and sometimes a little difficult which is great, PayDay 2 felt like a damn drag for the first 3-5 hours which this game evades You can change difficulties later on to make it more challenging.I do like the reward system a lot and you don't get some ♥♥♥♥♥♥ mods for weapons you don't own unlike PayDay 2. _childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I thought the game was going to be all memes when I got into the playtest, but I hyperfixated on it like a mother ♥♥♥♥♥♥. I have been craving a decent crime boss type game where you fight for control over city territory and work to protect your assets. This game really scratches the itch without needing to turn the whole game into an isometric turn based top town game. The game's mechanics do a pretty good job of letting you feel useful and capable without gating a bunch of skills or talents necessary for a particular heist type behind a lengthy grind (looking at you payday 3). You can stealth or play your missions aggro and you aren't punished by the game if you need to switch from stealth to aggressive. For the purposes of this review, I am going to assume that the devs intentionally love the cheesy over the top dialogue and the action movie tropes, so I won't be including that in my further breakdown. It's not the way I would write dialogue, but it's clear to me this game is a love letter from the devs.-The Good-The mechanics of the game are pretty good. They could use a little bit of responsiveness tweaks, like sometimes your bots will get confused or stuck, but largely, the systems work really well together in my experience.Looting things and packing bags feels satisfying. Something about the sound design and the visual of loot flying towards you while you gently caress it with your hand feels pretty damn satisfying. The sound design in general is really great. The guns, voices, music, etc it all sounds pretty good to me.The devs very clearly care about this game and want it to succeed. Prolific closed testing, good price point, and embracing the meme-ability of the game. The fact that it seems like people who bought the game on Epic and participated in the closed tests seem to have gotten steam copies for free is really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cool imo. The incentives to play the multiplayer function with random people, indicates to me that the devs care about fostering a good and respectful community. It seems to me that they want people to play together rather than alone. BUT they also empower you to play the game by yourself too if you prefer that! Which is such a nice change from all the controversies surrounding 'always online' style games. -The stuff that needs a little work-Some of the weapon animations, such as checking the revolver's cylinder every single time you pull out your sidearm, needs to go away. It is so frustrating to be in the middle of a fight for my life with a tiny sliver of health and for my ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ character to open the weapon to check the ammo while in the middle of a life or death moment when he already knows it's loaded. One time when you first pull out the weapon would be good. No more than that. The animation team did a good job, but you don't have to beat me over the head with how sick your revolver animations look.Loading screen/skip jankiness. The loading screen/mission start up screen needs a little TLC imo. Not much to say about this other than sometimes the skip button doesn't work as intended or the start of a mission hiccups a little bit. Nothing game breaking but would be a nice quality of life improvement.The game runs a little hot. My computer is not top of the line and up to date right now by any means, however, I am not experiencing any of the stutters, freezes, or frame issues other people seem to be having. But, the game does use quite a bit of hardware resources and can sometimes make my pc chug a little bit.-What I would like to see-This part is very subjective to me, but I have been playing with and streaming for a discord full of my friends and they largely agree with many of these things.1. I want an endless difficulty for the campaign. I want the ability to toggle the campaign into an endless state so that I can make a run last as long as I possibly can. I'm honestly not sure exactly how that would work given the current way the campaign is structured, but man that would be so fun.2. In addition to the nice rogue-like mechanics of the campaign, let me get temporary buffs that affect only the next run. Let me buy something or unlock something that has mutator effects for my next run, like "20% more cash from heists next run, but the Cognali robots begin the campaign helping the police from the start" or "The boss starts with a weapon of your choice, but he only gets one weapon slot" or even "If you hit the green zone when speeding up a drill or saw for the first time, it stays sped up permanently, but when you alert the police they start at one star higher than normal" stuff like that.3. Let us make a custom boss for the campaign, and allow us to change the look of our unlocked characters in both multiplayer and single player. I want to spend my cash on dumb stuff like shirts and pants and hairstyles too in addition to weapons and perks. That about does it for me. I have to say I really love this game already and I have a blast while I am playing it. I easily get sucked into a campaign run and time just flies by while I'm focused on that. Thanks to the devs for making a good, affordable, well crafted game. Keep on working on this game, and I think it'll go down as one of the most legendary multi-genre games in recent history.

_childDocuments_.review: First let’s get the notable cast out of the wayMichael Madsen (Travis Baker the Candyman Boss)His handlers and planners consist of Michael Rooker (Touchdown)Kim Basinger (Casey)Danny Glover (Gloves)Damion Poitier (Nasara and Payday’s Chains)Rival gang bosses areDanny Trejo (Dragon)Vanilla Ice (Hielo)Law Enforcement isChuck Norris (Sheriff Norris)This will no doubt get me smited by Chuck Norris but his voice acting is absolutely horrendous, it’s so monotone and badly done that I was under the impression that it was done by A.I, everyone else listed imo done a really good job with their rolesGameplay wise this game will no doubt garner the comparisons with the Payday franchise but your not here to read about that game since your on this pageHere’s the rundownThis game is good for people who want to do short 5min heists or longer heists, you can extract from missions anytime even if you haven’t met the quota which will result in a failure but you will still keep what you have looted, this is handy but it doesn’t apply to all missions, this is for the short quick heists such as robbing a truck or a jewellery storeYou can holster your weapon at anytime provided you haven’t gotten to the point where the police are called or you have decided to “start heist” and you have unlimited throwables such as bricks, grenades or emp grenades but they have a recharge meter, you also have unlimited zip ties and you can have up to 3 hostages follow you at once and you can also zip tie security guards but you have to hit them first to get them to drop their weapon just don’t use the regular melee button otherwise you will kill them which will give you one strike to the 3 strike stealth system in placeYou have 3 strikes when it comes to stealth, things such as getting spotted in a restricted area, shooting a security camera and killing guards will affirm to the strike systemOnce the police are called to the scene the game has 5 levels of difficulty when it comes to the swat with it increasing evermore the longer you take to the point robot police will come into play to deal with youThe game has a few bugs such as intimidating a civilian can sometimes make them warp behind you or they don’t follow you correctly and decide to take a longer path around as well as your A.I bots getting stuckYou can carry up to 2 loot bags or 3 if your playing as Jupiter, carrying 1 loot bag allows you to still use your primary gun but the moment you carry 2 bags you can only use your secondary weaponThe A.I are a lot more useful whereas they can loot for you and even carry bags you throw either at them or on the ground and even transport them to the van on their own which is a great QoL featuresUnfortunately during the much longer heists such as robbing the bank vault and the kings gold bars I found myself at a loss of what I was doing, I couldn’t find the keycard to the elevator on the tellers desk for the lift in bank heist and and the bots were no help with that either, I had no idea where I was looking apart from Nasara saying it but I gave up in the end cause nothing helped to indicate where I should go after a prolonged search, same with the gold heist, I had no idea what I was doing when it came to opening the cages where the gold bars were kept and all I knew was that the drill was involved somehow.Playing in a public lobby will also give you an additional 10% rewardUnfortunately as you level up your account each level reward is RNG and you get to pick one of 3 choices that pop up ranging from weapon skins, characters and weapons.Sadly the weapons as of current are not modifiableThe campaign is a roguelite so if any of your gangsters die or are arrested they’re gone for good and if your using Travis Baker he’s a double edged sword, you can use him twice per day for a 50% bonus in loot but if he dies the run is overAttacking other terrorities: You hire gangsters to take over other territories so it’s more favourable the more you hire, if you die you switch to another gangster until either all your gangsters die or you kill the enemies.Defending your territories: You take control of Touchdown armed with a light machine gun and whatever amount of gangster your hire, it’s the same as attacking other territories but sometimes things like an attack helicopter that you need to takedown comes into playRegular Heists: These consist of you forming a team of 1-4 to rob places such as jewellery stores, banks etc etc each getting more difficult as the story progresses, the more members you have recruited the more you have to pay towards their cut when the heist is successful, if you think your about to be overrun sometimes it’s better to extract early to live to fight another dayThe campaign consists of day cycles and when you decide to mate a day as over it’ll also reduce the amount of heat the police have towards you and sometimes progress the storyAll in all a really great game that I’m having a fun with, don’t go into this game expecting it to be a poor Payday clone as that will just ruin your experience due to your expectations, instead go into it with a fresh mindset without the comparisons to give yourself a better outlook experience and determine the good and bad things from that perspective otherwise your just gonna have a bad time

_childDocuments_.review: I really like the IDEA of this game: the execution could use a multi gigabyte patch to the performance, enemy damage and spawns, the glitches, and the weapons. Player weapons don't do enough damage, enemy weapons do too much damage, there are way too many heavies on normal difficulty, enemy swat are too tanky, the AI is totally useless and WILL get themselves killed rushing the enemy at the earliest opportunity unless you shout at them constantly. I have had so much fun in this game, and I have also experienced more unfettered rage and frustration than trying to beat The Last of Us on Grounded difficulty. At least I can say that left me with a sense of satisfaction:all this game gives me is pain. This game in it's current state is way too frustrating for me to recommend: there's so many cool and great things in this game, and it's completely ruined by the enemy balance and the complete uselessness of the AI: stealth missions are extremely fun to figure out how to solve, loud missions make me want to shoot myself in the head. A lot of things need to change in order for me to be able to recommend this game in it's current state. I hope the devs pull their heads out of their butts and look at the influx of negative reviews after their difficulty rebalance: ROLL IT BACK FFS.

_childDocuments_.review: When Crime Boss released on the Epic Launcher awhile back I considered it and ultimately decided not to get it yet as I had other interests at the time but after seeing it release on Steam given my overplayed boredom of GTA5 along with the poor release of Payday 3 with the same repetitive nonsense as the first two games while I eagerly await GTA6 I must say that Crime Boss fills that void quite well as it is one hell of a fun game that doesn't disappoint! Here's why...+ PROS +++++++++++ Outstanding Visuals!+ Outstanding Audio!+ Outstanding Gameplay!+ Outstanding Characters and some based on Real Hollywood Actors!+ The Rogue-like Campaign gives the game infinite replay value!+ Fantastic Story and Plot+ Hilarious Moments+ Choice and Consequences+ Random Unexpected Events+ Increasing Mission Difficulty+ Singleplayer and Multiplayer+ Legitimate quick-join co-op and not some lame only join if you host and have friends+ Excellent Skills+ Excellent Equipment+ Excellent Upgrades+ Decently Open Maps+ Future Planned Roadmap from Dev Team+ Turn-based Events are very involving for players- CONS - ------------- The AI is questionable at times such as on Easier and Normal the AI can often easily be outgunned usually- Theres a lot going on in the game so it can be overwhelming at first even though the game does teach you- Buying more AI Soldiers at first isn't really taught very well other than needing them so this created some problems later for me until I realized I was supposed to be doing that all along during each turn- I wish that there was some more larger-scale open-world like missions such as actually Driving to a Mission, parking a Van in a suitable spot, getting out, and then going on the mission then later being able to drive off after completing a mission which would make the game feel way more immersive- I do kind of wish that the game was more real-time and not-so-much turn-based but I guess that is the only way to make it happen effectively as I am a huge fan of realistic dynamics- I'm currently halfway through my first campaign and that worries me slightly as I feel like I might beat it quickly which makes me question its full-replay value as to what will happen when I play again if I will be bored and stop playing= VERDICT ============== Crime Boss is an outstanding game with a lot of replay and value that delivers some serious fun and I can highly recommend it. I really hope to see some great updates in the near future as well as a sequel way down the road, it deserves a lot of attention and is a hidden gem in its own right!

_childDocuments_.review: Crime boss: Rockay city; a not so nice experience. Ill keep this as short as possible as I dont really feel like writing a long a*s review but to sum it up, the game just.. isn't great in its current state.The voice acting is god awful. The 90% celeb-cast they hired for this game are a complete joke regarding the voice acting. It really seems like none of them cared about their roles and just wanted a quick pay check. Comparing this to payday 2; you can hear the characters yell and panic as if they're actually under fire. In crime boss, they sound like they're having a normal conversation. When you zip tie NPCs and tell them to follow you, you are met with casual "okays" instead of panic'd responses.The gameplay I didnt really get to experience that much because it LAGS. and HARD. Even on the lowest graphical settings Im met with constant stuttering, long loading times, and even huge FPS drops whenever I pull out a weapon. Cutscenes seem to forget to play audio unless I right click my screen, and even then its not like they're worth watching because all the voice lines are delayed instead of.. y'know, actually being synced with the cutscene.The gunplay itself is... fine? Like its nothing to write home about IMHO. I just dont care for it. The game as a whole is pretty boring, it really failed to grab my attention like payday 2 does.The game looks fine from a visual standpoint. again, nothing to write home about but it has a nice atmosphere. (when  you are running it at the highest settings, anyway)I honestly would not recommend this game in its current state. Terrible voice acting, horrible performance, and overall just boring gameplay. I had heard great things about it and was hoping it would be "Payday 3 but actually good" however I am left disappointed. Will be refunded. 3/10

_childDocuments_.review: The campaign is a mess. The map does a poor job of almost everything, there is too much information trying to be translated as icons all over the map and makes it confusing on what your next move should be or what "move" your opponents might do next turn, mission length varies wildly, some are easily done within 2 minutes, some start you off getting shot at instantly.Its like if Deathloop completely butchered its game loop and made you only play as premade bosses even in multiplayer which also sucks because even in multi you cant create your own character.It has some confusing features that shouldn't even really be features, I'm not really interested in collecting bosses and team members like playing cards, its created a convoluted system that doesn't really feel that rewarding either as some perks are clearly superior to others with not that many perks or ranks to them as of now. I think the rougelite campaign and no way to play as yourself or your own character/boss in either mode are big misses, hard to know at this point if its worth the time investment. The value in the game seems to be in the multi where you can take on the bigger missions and heists when you want even as solo. Its not bad value with all DLC included but needs work and direction for both campaign and multi

_childDocuments_.review: I will admit. When I first saw this game exclusive to the Epic Games Store, I ridiculed it for what it was, but after having played it now on Steam I can right my premature joviality a bit. Because this game is actually pretty entertaining now.For one, I've heard that the game now has a much better sense of direction and progress compared to its launch, and I appreciate that there is actually some coherence to the story, even if it is "so badly voice acted that it is funny".Some of the story missions are absolutely hilarious, at times ridiculous premises, and have strangely high production value for what they are. The voice acting almost speaks for itself in ambition.While there are also smaller shorter heists and daily jobs that don't seem to vary as much, overall it is a positive experience to play through, if you don't mind smaller odd jobs between the big heists.-What has hampered my experience with the game is the performance, and ultimately I blame modern day Unreal Engine for a lot of it. I don't want to sit a whole minute or two in the main menu waiting for the shaders to build every single time. When I try to run the game at DX11, which I've always found to be most stable DirectX in the past, Unreal crashes whenever the cops show up and start shooting.I'm playing on a GTX 1660 SUPER, i5-10600K and 16 GB of RAM, and I get a very playable experience at Low settings. I feel like many of the Unreal Engine bells and whistles are not worth it on this game. If it was more approachable on lower specs, it would definitely find a bigger footing of players that host their own servers and have a good time, like other heisting games that are still alive today.-In summary, this game is worth it, especially with the pretty reasonable launch offer, but try to get a better PC (especially GPU) than mine before you purchase. I'm hoping that the devs can cut a lot of the unnecessary glitter out and in turn also make the game run better at lower specs, given how awful Epic has made the Unreal Engine nowadays.

_childDocuments_.review: Well I'm having fun.And yes, disclaimer I won a key in a giveaway. I then bought three more copies for friends. Yeah, I like it enough to pay anyway.The roguelite mode is a very light XCOM-y management space with building an army, hiring and practicing with a gang of heisters, all the while contesting various turfs and operations of rival gangs, and avoiding too much notoriety, lest Sheriff Chuck Norris wakes up from his 80-year-old slumber and actually busts someone for a change. I don't think it has great ROGUELITE variety, but the management bits result in unique, skill-driven outcomes, and the game can really surprise you with a curveball once in a while.Beyond that, the jobs themselves are very neat and varied. This is more than a pure heisting game - tasks vary from simple gang hits and moshpit turf wars, to pinching valuable informants from right under the detective's nose, to genuine big jobs like raiding luxury yachts or running an entire train full of cash off the rails. The jobs vary greatly in length, easily satisfying both a 5 minute break and a lengthy, stealthy endeavour.Not to say the stealth is anything special - detection meters are very generous, and most every obstacle can be completely removed from play, leading to the classic PD2 scenario of twiddling your thumbs while the drill does its job. I find it a pleasing solution, though - an ultimate reward for efficiently casing the bank and locking everything down.You won't always have to contend with guards and warning "strikes," however - gang-busting operations involve no police at all, allowing for efficient silenced kills and a much swifter pace. The game compensates with much higher packs of goons to handle (even including a mini-boss at times!), and a more strict alarm condition, where thugs open fire immediately, thus attracting a call to the police. However, with the same generous meters and delays for detection, dealing with it is still a breeze. Extra credit to level designers for consistent working cover - everything you expect to hide you, does.Though you'll want to engage in combat eventually - it's tight and punchy, with good camera movement and a lot of comfort features in place, such as naturally leaning around cover, or maintaining ADS while reloading. Some consideration always has to be given to stance and reloading - you crouch lower while static than moving, potentially saving your pretty face from a nasty lead surprise, and reloads prevent any high-mobility stunts, though they CAN be activated in the middle of a slide or sprint-jump, giving it a bit of tech alongside the usual reload cancelling.Though this is where the game's atmosphere rears its head, and it's definitely for specific taste - dialogue is very corny and often poorly acted, the menagerie of voices and silly lines during heists can get draining, cutscenes seem to be stitched together from barely related animations and voice lines, and I've heard complaints that the constant "cop radio" drone during assaults is a huge ear sore to some. The game does not look fantastic, either - poor graphics options and anti-aliasing choices lead to a game that's either constantly muddy, washed out looking, or covered in "screendoor" style half-finished shadows and hairlines. I wish the game had an option for pre-set times of day with pre-baked shadows, which would avoid much of this. At the very least I would appreciate a more substantial, accurate form of AA.Performance is not good either - for its relatively plain looks, the game seems to struggle on anything below the 20-series cards. While my own 3080 is handling it admirably, the other computer with a 980 Ti is a lot less fortunate, and with lower framerates comes inconsistent mouse movement which leads to complications aiming. Once again its lack of solid graphics settings is a bummer, with many effects crammed together under one dial, and performance impact fluctuating wildly with no easy way to tell which options help the most.Still, that's just technical stuff, and I'm having a great time with the game itself. Great blend of stealth and combat, with lots of unique jobs and layouts for each, its easy to pick up roguelite mode with lots of neat decisions and outcomes, plus its ADORABLY cheesy dialogue just keep me smiling as I go along.I get. You get too.

_childDocuments_.review: I put 20 hours into the play test and really liked it. I've played both Payday: The Heist and Payday 2 for over a hundred hours combined. Surprisingly, the bots in this game are more competent than my teammates in any Payday game (lol).This game is designed with solo play in mind. As a solo player, I can play solo with bots in both the campaign and solo multiplayer matches. I can switch and control them anytime, setting different loadouts for heists. Even if my main character dies in solo multiplayer, I can still switch to bots and complete the heist successfully. It's awesome.You can order the bots to loot, subdue guards, wait, follow, tie up civilians, break and loot stuff automatically, and take the loot to the van while you’re busy shooting cops.Weapon customization is limited; weapons come in presets. You can only choose primary, secondary, and equipment for your loadout. Weapons come in different colors and tiers as you level up. Similarly, urban legend heister bots are unique and have their own skills and play styles, but you can't customize them.I don't want to compare this too much to Payday, as it's more "inspired by" Payday, but Crime Boss: Rockay City is different in its own way. Heists are short, gameplay is more casual, weapon animation is good, and the visuals are stunning and stylized in a colorful way on ultra settings.Overall, I love this game. It's very affordable, with all free DLC on Steam launch. For $19 with another 20% off, it's really fun and worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: "If I was a pedantic art critic, I'd call it 'Earnest.'" ~ Jontron or something.Jokes aside, this game is exactly what it says on the tin: A 198X - 200X roguelike heisting game with a compelling solo mode that strikes above it's weight and challenges every other game in the heisting genre to step their game up. Absolutely worth it's price base, gun DLCs are pretty cheaty though when you are starting out, while Cagnali's Order is dang good. As a base package, it's VERY MUCH worth whatever it is solo, but since you can only buy the set? 20 dollar is a steal.++PROS+++ Terribly phoned in celebrity performances that range from god awful to iconic. Chuck Norris, Danny Glover, Stallone? Yes please!+ Gunplay is basic but very fun. Have a killer time destroying every object while in a shootout in a gas station.+ Stealth is relatively simple but VERY much improved over say Payday as nonlethally forcing guards to surrender prevents alarms from being rung.+ Heat management via limiting your actions per day is fun, map management to get districts is intuitive and fun, money management and stock market financing? REAL good. Truly in love with this singleplayer roguelike mode.+ Lots of maps and cutscenes that not only was not expected but are actually good, not just in looks but layout and level design.+ LOTS of RNG elements, a must.+ A mix of stealth and loud is how a lot of missions play out and you can very easily screw up leading to a loud encounter, or you can pull it off in stealth in minutes, it's so so so good. I got to a target after minutes of sneaking, blew him away with a shotty and fought my way to the van over the course of a handful of minutes and it was hectic fun.+ Cover shooter regen health... It's good here, but usually I'd say it's a detriment. Leans into the sprint and crawl nature of fights.+ Cops and their assaults feel far more fair and "Real" than Payday or other ones, as you don't slaughter the entire cloning factory of cops but instead fight a handful of [Very lethal] enforcers before they back off and regroup. Individual gun fights are short, but the AI will flank you aggressively and only back off when casualities are a bit too much to handle. Again, hits the perfect FPS mark here.+ Minigames for stealing, overheating the saws, etc. Quite good.--Cons--- Customization is solely multiplayer, which is a little lame. I don't even mind if the boss was always in the cutscene in singleplayer, but it'd be nice to swap him to a different model for missions and apply sprays that I get to my guns in solo.- Difficulty feels all over the place and run starts can happen BEFORE the gangs have every territory or after, which is just weird.??Misc Critiques / Things I noticed??? Glass doesn't break properly, which is sad.? Hostages should hug the floor, right now some will just stay kneeling which, while it doesn't hamper gun fights, is just weird when shots are going past their heads.? Hostages also don't really serve ANY purpose in loud from what I have found which is just weird and makes tying them up pretty pointless.? Why is there not a "New Run" button? Would be nice is all I'm saying.? I'm extremely confused on who the multiplayer is for given that I just don't see the appeal. Again, not to say the Multiplayer is bad but that it's kinda weird how much stuff is locked to it while I have no idea why I'd want to play it given how the appeal, to me, is all located in singleplayer.Overall, love this game.
