_childDocuments_.review: So you may be wondering what the heck is 'Crime Boss: Rockay City'?Well the short answer is: The Payday 3 we should of got.The long answer is a little more convoluted and in depth But bare with me, an hopefully I can clear some things up for you.If you are looking for something to fill that Payday 3 void. This may be the game for you. So first things first, lets get the obvious out of the way. do i need an epic account? I can very gladly say, No! you do not! Now onto the rest of the info. The game play is fairly simple and straight forward. You don't have to worry about complex trees/ builds like you did in Payday 2. But you can equip skills/weapons to make like pseudo builds. Different skills and different characters are better at different things. Just something to keep note of.The Stealth is easy to get into but hard to master at least from my short time playing it. Stealth was one of my favourite things of Payday 2 and here I can quite confidently say. This really scratches that same itch, sneaking around is pretty much the same. Cameras are just as scary but well executed shouts can take down crowds easily.  Bricks can be thrown to distract guards and help you get them into better positions to make your moves. Melee weapons are great early on because if you get detected you can melee a guard to death (if you don't have a silenced gun.) to save your self from going loud. Oh and there is a really cool lock pick mechanic and for the most part, doors can be opened and closed!Which may not sound like a big deal but if you have played as many hours in payday 2 as I have. There are many stealth heists where i wished i could do something as simple as that. Oh and levels are very dynamic, if you fail to complete some objectives in an allotted time or mess up stealth. Then the direction of the mission may change drastically, Which I found really cool. I wont spoil anything but I will move onto more mechanics.Drills and saws are always loud but never jam on there own. If you start one in stealth it will attract all the non tied down guards in a certain area. However for the most part Civvies don't give a ♥♥♥♥. You can Interact with said equipment to boost the cutting speeds but at the risk of over heating them. I can not tell you how good it is to not NEED to baby sit drills. No more  *insert PTSD broken drill beep noise from payday 2 here* unless you want them to go as quickly as living-ly possible. Loud is straight forward, Shoot the enemies dead. Try not to become the un-alived yourself and get the loot out. However I will say be prepared for some humbling experiences. You have a very watered down version of Payday 2's build system when it comes to combat. Combat is either ON or it is Off. Basically as you fight the meter on the screen will slowly increase showing the level of Police, that you will be facing. An 5 badges is *SPICY*. You will want to be well equipped and have levelled characters if you plan on wading through tier 5 combat. Thankfully most jobs can be completed well and truly before that. CB:RC works on haste more then drawn out gunfights with literal armies of cops like Payday. So you really want to be matching the flow of the game in your movements, work on looting and things while the cops retreat. Focus on defence and combat when they are attacking. Strong Team work and good choke points are key to holding your ground. Now on the topic of loud, most of the weapons feel decent to use. Shotguns in CB:RC are so good. Popping heads with the streetsweeper is just *chef kiss*. I will say there are some weapons that feel weak but that's usually on the lower grade tier any way. Now onto the things you may be wondering about in other reviews: The Rogue-lite Single player.So simply put the Single player is what it says on the tin. You are working on taking over Rockay City. A chunk of territory at a time. As you work through the campaign you will likely face odds you are ill-equipped to deal with. Usually causing you to fail and worse case loose a run. But the game in intended to be this way, You are supposed to level up your boss and your station to better improve your odds of your next run. It makes you work for the progress which I personally like, it also gives the campaign some replay-ability. Multiplayer can be fun, but honestly the game lacks a large player-base ATM. So quick-play will likely put you into lobby by yourself. But it is worth just playing side missions or skirmishes to better level your account so you will have the money and things to unlock characters or weapons. Even solo i would say it is worth doing.Other things I like about CB:RC:Your characters can carry TWO bags. Yes you read that right, two whole ass duffel bags. You want to know the penalty for this? you move slower and can only use your secondary weapon. But there is a skill that once levelled can help you move faster while carrying bags. But carrying one barely slows you down and you can still use your primary! No more running single bags all the way to the drop point just to run all the way back to the loot. *Don't get me wrong you still kind of have to do it But at least you can do it quicker.*Characters have animations so you can see NPC models actually doing things. Whether they are throwing bags, helping some one up, picking locks etc.Maps will reuse area's but have different structures to break up the similarity between area's an missions. You also often have a wide area to flank or manoeuvre to better get at objectives. Which is a real nice touch.Cars will explode if they cop enough fire. Yes i know, not super realistic but its a nice touch to have destructive terrain during combat.Now onto the things that I don't like:CB:RC, is a live service game. Which really *really* sucks. I hate live service games for all the obvious reasons.It is a little buggy, it has its issues. But nothing that has caused me to stop playing.Having civvies or guards panic over spotting nothing is a little frustrating. And losing the ability to shout down guards because the prompt bugs is also a little problematic.The Film-clips/Cut-scenes are REALLY cheesy and I find myself usually skipping them as I roll my eyes at the some what poorly delivered lines or questionable dialogue. I understand they are meant to be larger then life characters and things but it feels overdone. Payday 2 I think, had the in game dialogue nailed. For the most part, ya know... Bain never shutting up was standard fair. However the characters voice lines suited them and if you felt they were grating. You could just switch characters. The looping lines and the character dialogues in CB:RC however, I find quite grating and can be a bit much.Over all is Crime Boss: Rockay City worth it? I would say yes. If you are a fan of the Payday games you may like this. Also For the price point it's not a hard sell and if you can get it on sale, even better.Edit notes: I found this super handy guide which covers all the aspects of CB:RC. Hopefully this will help you out if there are parts you are struggling with.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't the faintest idea where Jupiter is from with the inscrutable accent, and I don't care, she's an absolute doll, my favorite character, the team's designated 6'5" tall, 3-loot-bag-holding, roided out hard carry and never needs to change. Her voice actress' performance was phenomenally and unironically endearing, and she should be brought back for more lines for her own personal DLC. Nothing about her should change.It's nearly impossible to play this game without making immediate comparisons to Payday 2, and CBRC comes out on top. The shooting mechanics are smoother, the user interface more friendly, the heists less BS, and even the DLC has more bang for your buck. The missions where I'm forced to go loud are few and far between. Network issues as described by other reviewers are anecdotal, as I've not had issues, but if it concerns you just hop into multiplayer immediately and figure out if you're one of the unlucky ones and need to return in the 2 hour window. Speaking as someone with nearly 300 hours in Payday 2 from its release, and has 90 hours as of review time, this is a must buy for any fan of Payday 2 looking for anything to soothe the sting of Payday 3's launch and monetization.There are some negatives - Chuck Norris' voice in game is either AI or one of the most stilted performances I've been forced to bear witness to since I had to watch my nephew have no lines in a 4th grade class rendition of Fiddler on the Roof. Danny Glover is better, he seems to only be sometimes AI instead of always. There could be more locations, but they just added some in the new update so they're on top of it. Guard and camera placements on Hardcore difficulty, during the high risk Warehouse on Watch mission specifically, can be so dense and overlapping that I can feel the devs sarcastically telling me to go ahead and stealth this bulls**t. Randomized elements in general are usually reasonable on each difficulty though, enough to keep things interesting, not so much that you're getting bodied by shockers every other mission. The highest level characters in the game each has a set of missions that detail their respective backstories, I love this. You have to do these missions within 3 days of them popping up, even if you've beaten the whole set of missions, or you won't have access to that high level character for the rest of the run, I hate this.Devs, I am begging you - I appreciate what you were doing with the big names, all huge names in the 90s when this game is taking place, it's thematic, most of them did a fine job. But please hire professional trained voice actors like you did for the iconic heisters, and use whatever money you save to hire more level designers for more heists, more modelers and artists for new ♥♥♥♥ to put on those maps, and more programmers for interesting mechanics. I will buy every damn DLC you put out so long as I'm getting new maps, weapons, and interesting characters.

_childDocuments_.review: I see alot of people saying this game is not as good at payday 2 but way better than payday 3whilst the later is true I think this game is a slightly different playstyle to payday 2infact this game has a lot more in common with Payday: The Heist than payday 2.As someone who has an absurd amount of hours in the payday games I can say that I didnt enjoy the arcade-y route payday 2 took with its combat. You fight literally hundreds of cops constantly that it feels way too much even for a big action film. it makes combat kinda boring, police arent a threat at all and the game loses its immersion.What i enjoyed about PD:TH and this game is that you fight less police, it actually feels like a proper police operation, and they do way more damage. there's no armour or dodge system, cover actually matters. the gameplay feels more realistic which funny because the story of this game is on par with an cheesy 80s action film. BUT that doesnt take away from the gameplay.whilst its true there isnt the sheer amount of content that PD2 has it feels better, the heists are big set pieces, there's more interaction from the players with objectives. YOU DONT HAVE TO REPAIR A JAMMING DRILL FOR EVERY OBJECTIVE. Also not every mission is a "Heist" this game is a crime game not a a heist game so there are different types of mission and story mission to go along with the heists. Very Based.This game feels like what payday 3 should of been.that being said i feel this game is sorta like the Vermitide 2 to L4D2same genre different game. and people should enjoy this game for what it is instead of going into it expecting to play payday.now, cons.Content: but this will come with updates so, moot point. but what content there is does have a nice amount of RNG to it, so each play can be different even if not massively, its nice that it does change stuff.progression: having to earn everything through the pick-a-magazine system after each mission where you could not get any skills for a long time is not a very good system, and i hope they add a real progression system.Some of the guns feel weirdly arcade-y, this is mostly my own opinion but if you wanted realistic feeling weapons you're not really gonna get that here.a lack of customisation in terms of attachments is annoying, guns have variants with attachments on. also annoying, what if wanted to remove a scope or forward grip. you cant.annoying.being able to make / customise your own "boss" would also be coolThe voice acting is genuinely awful. They somehow made chuck norris as a badass police sheriff the least threating person ive ever met.He talks as if hes talking to child, its really weird.i do feel like the devs spent way too much time and money getting celebs into the game rather than just hiring some good voice actors and spending the remaining money on adding more content and QoL to the game. although i know basically nothing about development so take what i say with a grain of salt.Regarding campaign (rougelite) missions they dont say beforehand if they start in stealth. first time i did the armoured truck heist i assumed it would be a smash and grab. so i bought a full team, assault rifles, grenades you name it.and it was a lone truck. the mission started in stealth and i could of done it quietly ok.So then i did another armoured truck heist, different name or something. bought 1 guy with a silenced pistol and a brick. but this time it was straight into blowing up a city block and getting swat teams firing at me.Just add a little logo that says can be stealth'd or no stealth at all or only stealth. so players know beforehand.and finally, bots have a tendacy to get themselves killed, get you killed or just fail the mission.I do enjoy that they will loot, carry bags and offload bags themselves. that's very good but i think survivability needs to be looked at. i found downed AI crawling out of cover away from me into the line of fire. Not Very Based.all in 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Friendship with Payday ended, Crime Boss: Rockay City is my new friend nowNo but seriously: the singleplayer campaign is great, the stealth, while perhaps not as smooth as Payday's, has its own merits in the form of smart ping mechanics that can command your AI-controlled team to do objectives or neutralize threats alongside you on the fly, bringing a fresh modern feel to the heisting genre. My first thought was "most things calling themselves roguelites aren't this fleshed out". My experience with the multiplayer is so far limited, but I'm trying to get my friends to jump on this train while they can, so maybe I'll update that review in the future; The shared progression between multiplayer and singleplayer unlockables means there's something for both kinds of players here long term, and you won't be punished for liking a good mix of both either. A common complaint I've heard is that throwing all the DLC weapons into the usable item pool right from the get go throws off the sense of progression, but realistically, they are all so expensive on average that you are not buying them all anywhere close to right when you've started and you'll be working for what you want. The devs are active on Discord and seem to care that this game should only be going up from here, I would say it's vastly improved from its former Epic exclusive phase of being a "literally who" game, and would suggest if you're interested, give these guys your money while it's on sale and they're still giving you the DLCs for free, with a base price as low as it already is, as that's a good deal you don't see every day anymore.

_childDocuments_.review: Worth the price of admission, the team behind Rockay City has proven they understand what this genre means as well as how to make it (mostly) work without fuss.  It isn't perfect, but it's much better than most of the AAA games I've picked up in teh last year.  It isn't a Payday equivalent, but it has the same feel, similar gameplay, has a great singleplayer line along with various multi-player options, and in total gives me exactly what I want versus the unfortunate experiences from earlier titles.If you go in with an open mind, and don't expect a carbon copy replacement of other games existing in the same space, you'll hopefully be pleasantly surprised.  The actors and actresses alone in this game make it worth the price - especially on sale!  And getting every bit of DLC alongside the reduced price was an all-time high coming from a game purchase for something that launched in the last 6 months or less.Pros:* Familiar gameplay, missions, and overall flow* Great voice acting and characters* Gunplay doesn't feel too overworked - it just plain works* Multi-player drop-in/out works great, and having a pseudo-campaign in multi-player is a bonusCons:* Some NPCs feel a little canned in the voice line department* A couple minor bugs crop up occasionally.  Nothing deal-breaking, but can be a brief annoyance.* AI just got retweaked, but it had felt a bit braindead at times.  We'll hope it's moving in the right direction now!* Buying 'new things' can feel a bit grindy due to rewards vs. purchase price.  I don't mind it, but I understand statements in this space.* A few visuals seem aligned to 'only the Boss / leader' in multi-player, meaning that only the Boss sees and effect.  We've been attempting to verify this in group in multi, and seem to have verified at least between the last few parties.And to address concerns from other reviews: I have never once had an issue finding a match.  The player count doesn't seem to hinder playing the game, and I also have friends that like to play as well, so best of both worlds.  My experience doesn't support those complaints, so YMMV.If it seems interesting, I'd say go for it.  It's not perfect, but it's certainly leaps and bounds better than some of the critics give it credit for.  And for the sale price and free DLC, it's extra worth it in my book.

_childDocuments_.review: I finally beat this game's singleplayer after a few days and to say I was surprised would be an understatement. Is this music good? No, not really. Is the voice acting good? While I actually like a few of the characters' voices, not at all (Baker's lines are all so damn ridiculous and you can tell the VA isn't a VA). Is the gameplay good? It's super straightforward and simple, but also kinda fun if you aren't looking for too much depth. This game is "alright" in the best way possible. I would 100% not go into this expecting Payday 2 levels of heisting, but rather as just a heisting game doing its own thing (which it does pretty well I may add). I have my complaints about the AI (everyone seems to, which is understandable) such as the fact that it tends to sort of ignore gaurds and cameras when moving around in stealth, or the fact that when you retreat or push in combat they tend to stay hunkered down to inevitably get blasted by the police due to a lack of supporting fire. However, whether it was through sheer luck or just the way I was playing, I didn't run into *too* many issues with the AI in this regard. I like how they are actually somewhat proactive and in certain circumstances will actually *DO* things. On top of this, they are useful in stealth unlike in Payday 2 (not dunking on payday 2 in any way, simply just giving credit to the AI). The game also has a ton of variety and replayability, with tons of different variations to each mission and some random events here and there. Sure, its annoying when you're in stealth and some idiot npc lights a propane tank up with a cigarette, but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ if it isn't cool. Speaking of stealth, I almost enjoy it more than in Payday. Failing a stealth attempt doesn't feel like the end of the world and due to a lack of a pager mechanic allows for some *interesting* playstyles. For example, in gangster missions, you don't gain any strikes for killing gangsters, unlike with killing security guards. So, if you have a silenced weapon, you can very much just waltz in and light them up (which makes you feel like a badass if you pull it off btw). It might be a bit *too* easy sometimes, but if you don't really mind the difficulty then you could have as much of a blast with it as I did. Personally, I love casing out the entire place and figuring out patrol patterns and locking down the security methodically, or just cheesing with the brick because it's honestly pretty funny. If you can tolerate the voice acting and the music, this is 100% a game I can recommend to anyone who is a fan of Payday but maybe just wants to move on from it. And if you're worried about not having friends, don't worry, I don't either (None who have this game at least.), but also the game has a very well done singleplayer mode. It is a permadeath game mode though so if you aren't into losing characters, then maybe it isn't for you. Personally though, I'd take the losses on the chin and move on, it is much more enjoyable if you do that rather than resetting the game over and over to get a "perfect run". And even when you lose, its not for none. By investing in assets, playing as Baker, or just really doing things in general, you contribute points to your boss level, which gives you permanent upgrades for your next campaign attempt. Also, don't expect a story. There isn't one. Not a deep one at least. I have no problem with this, but I can understand what it might be like going into this game expecting a fantastic story to make up for the bad VA's and music. Overall, I think this is, at worst, a mediocre game that isn't a bad pickup if its on sale. But if you're someone who sees these flaws as charm or character like I do, then you'll probably love it like I do. It is not a great game. But I love it, and I can not wait to see what they do in the future. I'm glad the devs didn't give up on this game when it flopped on release and I hope things only go up from here. If a friend has this game, go ahead and buy this. If not, probably still buy it just to give it a try. It might just be a game that grows on you. Or not. Now go do things and stuff or whatever.  Good game. Nothing mind-blowing. But it didn't need to be.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really good alternative to the much-hated Payday 3.The gunplay feels about on-par with Payday 2, which is serviceable- but very "early 2010s".Don't go into this expecting Rainbow Six Siege or Modern Warfare gunplay, it's fairly shallow and forgiving.It could definitely use some balancing for enemy spawn rates, and the more bullet-sponge-y enemies that break immersion a bit.Still, when it's put in the context of the rest of the game, I've been enjoying it a lot (as someone that's played an ungodly amount of Rainbow Six Siege).The writing is bad. Not good-bad, not entertaining-bad, just bad.There's a couple rules when it comes to good-bad entertainment:A bad comedy can't be good-bad. Jokes failing to land aren't funny.A self-aware movie/game that's TRYING to be good/bad will fail 90% of the time.There's a few moments here-or-there that might get a smile out of you- Chuck Norris riding a horse while carrying a Civil War cavalry sabre is one of the only moments that got a chuckle out of me, but that was about the peak of it.The casting feels very thrown-together.I can appreciate the intent of trying to create of sort of "Expendables: The Game" theme with people like Chuck Norris, Danny Trejo, and Danny Glover in the cast, but their performances are so phoned-in that it's more depressing than it is funny or entertaining. It feels like they paid each of them $5,000 to record some lines over a Discord call.Not to mention that the actual voice lines seem to be few and far-between.Also, it feels like they ran out of options when it came to casting...I love Michael Rooker, but he doesn't exactly fit the theme of "Campy 90s Action-Hero" game.Same goes for Michael Madsen, Kim Basinger, and Vanilla Ice... it feels like they were thrown into the game just because "They worked in entertainment in the 90s, and they're available".It'd be like randomly casting Kelsey Grammar to reprise his Dr. Frasier Crane role in this game, because the only stipulation seems to be "You existed in the 90s, yeah?"No hate to any of them, love them all, just a little wishy-washy on the theme of the game's casting.The overworld stuff is a lot of fun (seems to only be available in the single-player mode, be aware).Managing your gang, taking over territories (which results in a short gunfight between your gang and a rival gang), managing finances, keeping the "heat" low so that Chuck Norris doesn't find you and stomp you into the ground, it's a good time.Not particularly deep, but a good time for sure.Overall, for $20 (or the current $15.99 on sale) including all of the available DLC in the base price, it's been very worthwhile for me.Recommended highly for someone looking for a Payday alternative with a different vibe / offline gameplay- with some light multiplayer aspects on top.

_childDocuments_.review: Well made game, taking pages from heist games/movies very well. Fun concepts, and decent gameplay loop, which sadly can get repetative at times, to the point of it being boring.My main issues with the game are:- Few heists; while it does have a great selection of them, and even has a small amount of RNG to them, after a while you won't get the same joy out of heists like you did in the beginning- A.i.; a very underlying issue, they are more advanced in some aspects, like being able to loot and grabbing and moving bags, but sometimes the behaviour is so severe, that you cannot stop the bot from going into the waves of cops for a bag, even though you are spamming "Follow me" or "Stay there"- Campaign and DLC campaigns; this is the main selling point for the game to be honest, and even though it's fun for a long time, it gets stale very fast, factoring in the number of heists in the game. _childDocuments_.review: There isn't feature bloat like Payday, where you have several systems working together to make a character strong at loud or stealth missions while ruining them for the other kind. It is ok to fail stealth since you can take weapons off corpses and probably complete missions in under 5-10 minutes. Drilling goes by quickly since it doesn't break every minute.There are several game modes like roguelite, random mission set, and character missions where you use a preset crew to do a handful of missions. Roguelite is you actually taking over the city by fighting turf wars and doing random missions scrounging up money to support it. It's different from the other modes and has its own leveling system and is meant to be replayed with better gear each time. A solo effort.The money sink is being able to customize your character in appearance, weapons, perks, and colors. Your boss also has their own level where random items are introduced each level up. Those then appear in the other modes.

_childDocuments_.review: Observed pros and cons with a few hours of gaming, at least on the default difficulty:PROS:-You can play as Danny Trejo, up to four(4) Danny Trejos at once all using a Machete™.-Shooting stuff feels great, almost everything seems viable and thus boils down to what mood you're in. Also includes throwing bricks for caveman strategies.-You can pick up enemy weapons if you want to change gear, and ammo pickups seem generous.-You can carry up to two bags, and you can also carry half a bag worth of loot without penalties.-Seemingly infinite sprinting and generous sliding to move around, even while hauling two bags, so moving around isn't a slog.-Stealth works on a 3 strike system, so even if there's 2 mistakes you can still beat it in stealth instead of a one-and-done system.-You can blow up cars and kill a bunch of enemies in one fiery swoop.-Has an option for solo offline mode, and if playing solo, you can command or even swap bots. Handy if you fall down and you want to switch to another character that hasn't fallen down to keep a run going.-You can speed up the drilling/sawing with a simple timing minigame, so you always have something to do while waiting for doors to open up.-Price is attractive: $20 maximum, and a generous discount+DLC offer until July 11th, 2024.CONS:-Somewhat frequent and random stuttering/framerate drops, though this self-corrected after about 20 seconds later in-game.-Matchmaking was down for the first hour I played, but came back when I played again later. Unsure how frequent this is, likely due to the game running on epic game servers.-Suffered at least one unreal engine crash at the start of a heist.-Loadout customization is locked on random variant weapon drops. IE a Desert Eagle with a scope is a separate equippable item you can bring with you, but you cannot manually add a scope onto a regular Desert Eagle.-Most of the heists are quick smash-and-grab styles of missions, though this can be a pro if you want to cycle through a bunch of missions swiftly or just want a quick hit of action.-Sometimes enemies seem sparse and the heists seem empty because of it. Good for just getting through a mission, bad if you are itching to blast something.Ultimately, the pros outweigh the cons, especially considering the price, and this can be at least considered a Good Game™.

_childDocuments_.review: I solely bought Cwime Bowbs because of my favorite foxu ( Kirsche Verstahl ) and found a payday 2 clone that I enjoy more.Crime boss at it's core is a streamlined payday 2 experience, there's far less grinding, there's some mechanics cut, some of the mission types are much shorter with a speed bonus for completing them under 5 minutes and the class build is more about picking perks rather than a cluster♥♥♥♥ of perk trees where you're min maxing stats changes for builds. If you're a die hard payday 2 fan look else where. Payday 2 requires you to put your friends through a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ 3 day to put them up to speed.  If you want a simplified experience that you can play solo through the campaign or have some friends drop in from time to time this is a great choice, you can get someone with no clue up to speed and playing well in a couple hours. The missions are your classic stealth heist to cargo ambushes where you fight off enemies while breaking into armoured trucks or trailers to steal loot. The Campaign has a fun enough spin with character stories you can experience which is at least a fun change of pace. Living through a character experience in Vietnam or wandering through the bayou is a good time despite how corny it is. I'm not going to complain about a "lack of content" because payday 2 has had 10 years, at least give these devs a chance to catch up and experiment.They managed to get a bunch of celebrity voice actors in to play roles and as expected the voice acting is awful. This happens every time you get famous actors because they don't know how to translate that acting into voice work. The characters are all pretty stereotypical. It's like playing a B grade movie with your buds, stupid but fun. I've heard people complain about the AI, last time I played payday 2 their AI was ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ too. Here you can switch between characters easily and give them orders to follow you, stay put, subdue enemies, loot stuff and drop off loot bags quickly and easily. their only problem is their pathing which is easy enough to work around. Progression and weapons are my biggest disappointment in this game. Progression is done buy picking one of 3 options each level which can be skins, weapon camos, weapons and characters and sometimes you'll get a choice of 2 camos and a character. I'd prefer you get to choice which category and get a random item from their. Leveling up is pretty fast but it's an annoyance when you get 3 items you give zero ♥♥♥♥♥ about. The weapon balance is kinda weird because some guns are just awful and others feel really good, it's going to take time to refine. The general gun play and handling is pretty good. Unfortunately you buy guns pre configured because that's how their doing their tiered system.Personal preference, we should unlock the gun then buy attachments for it rather then buy a pre built. I also think attachments system would allow for some fun systems like dragons breath or AP ammo. Even if the attachments had to be unlocked by doing tasks, surpressors for intimidating so many people, sights after so many headshots etc etc. Some people are complaining about a lack of suppressed pistols. If you're playing one you really don't need one. I think I've covered all the necessary parts. Overall the games easy to jump into, a lot of fun and plenty of potential if the devs keep working on it. It's damn cheap and doesn't have ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ 80+ DLC and requires you to own them to not get ♥♥♥♥♥♥ by the difficulty creep. Also for the devs, Please add the part time super terrorists, Kirshce, nano bytes, bagman and moonshine animations. It would be hilarious, it would fit the game and I'm certain all 4 of them would be down to do it. I would pay for that dlc.

_childDocuments_.review: A pleasant surprise. This is better at the Payday formula then Payday itself.That being said, don't expect Payday 3 going in. (Also features a server browser!) There is no real downside to playing multiplayer as a solo, as the bots and AI are competent most of the time, and you still progress if you private your lobby and fill it with bots. I highly recommend this to people who enjoyed Payday but were let down by 3, and are seeking a heisting game to fill that void.

_childDocuments_.review: Me and a few friends bought this game during the bundle deal, and we've been having a lot of fun with it.It's also one of the worst games I have ever played in my life.There is absolutely no excuse for this game to be in such an absolutely abysmal state after using Epic as an open beta for a year. In addition to running about as well as a dead raccoon that's had all four legs smashed into pieces by an aluminum bat, it's plagued by an overwhelming myriad of bugs, many of which are outright gamebreaking.In the short time me and my friends have played, we have encountered a bug that disables nearly every individual mechanic in the game, including but not limited to;-Losing the ability to fire weapon-Losing the ability to use ladders-Losing the ability to use equipment (Which I personally experience roughly every three to four games)-Losing the ability to move, turn camera, or really anything besides jump in place.And keep in mind, this is not one bug causing all of this at once. This is a multitude of different bugs occurring at different times under different circumstances, all fairly frequently. Not to mention the incalculable amount of smaller visual bugs, such as the van despawning when looked at from certain angles, frozen particles, elevators (visually but not mechanically) failing to move, doors (visually but not mechanically) failing to open, guns turning invisible, and your character turning pink for some reason?But wait, there's more! There's also plenty of awful game design that has nothing to do with bugs. For example, one mission begins with a cutscene of you hang gliding onto a roof. During this cutscene, you are actually already on the roof, and it is entirely possible for the game to spawn a guard directly in front of you, who will spot you while you are still stuck in the cutscene, and thus unavoidably fail stealth immediately before you even have control of your character. Me and one of my friends particularly encountered this at the end of a shuffle, which was especially frustrating considering said mission is arguably the hardest loud mission in the game.Oh, that also reminds me of a mission that starts you on a moving platform, in which I once spawned in late, the platform having already left, and resulting in me falling to my death the moment I spawned.Speaking of failing stealth, another bug we encountered was guards becoming fully "alerted" by nothing. They would remain like this until they actually saw something suspicious, at which point they would instantly, actually alert.Now, lets talk about the game closing. Yes, these devs somehow even managed to butcher closing the game, demonstrating a level of incompetence I wouldn't even expect from a rock that somehow acquired brain damage. In my personal experience, closing the game from the menu closes the window, but does not actually end the process, leaving it to eat thousands of megabytes in memory and bring my computer to a snails pace until I close it from Steam or the task manager.But why close the game when I can close my entire computer? Because upon leveling up after one match, my primary monitor died, my secondary monitor froze, and my computer completely locked up, all while the last sound to play from the game rapidly stuttered as is typical for a game crashing like a Boeing plane heading for a whistleblower convention. It didn't end there however, because upon manually restarting my entire computer and rejoining my friend ingame, I discovered my level had been reset to 1. What made this extremely interesting however is that I still had all of my money and unlocks. It had not reset my save, only my level. I cannot fathom how this even happens. Why is the level stored separate from the rest of the save? Why? Why? Why? Regardless, I initially believed this was a good thing, as it only meant I would unlock rewards faster due to my newfound lower level, but I was quick to learn that despite still possessing my unlocks, they were all also re-added to the drop pool, meaning many of my levels would effectively result in no reward due to being offered things I already have.In summary, the devs have somehow spectacularly fumbled in just about every possible aspect you could imagine to create one of the most horrendous games I have ever made the mistake of spending money on in my life. I genuinely cannot even begin to understand how some of these catastrophic errors even came to be, or how they are still in the game after so long. All I know is if I had to trust the building of a bridge between this dev team, or a headless chicken supplied only with a toothpick and a piece of string, I would ask where the dead raccoon from the beginning of the review had gone to, because they would clearly be a better option than either. This game is objectively garbage and frankly it's an insult they have the audacity to ask you to pay them for this atrocity.I can't wait to play more.

_childDocuments_.review: Crime Boss: Rockay City is more than just the anticipated Payday 3; it incorporates numerous quality-of-life (QOL) elements, offering a refreshing and dynamic gaming experience. This game brings a unique blend of strategic gameplay and action-packed heists, making it a standout in the genre.One of the key QOL improvements is the ability to carry a second bag, at the cost of reduced speed and the inability to use primary weapons. Additionally, you can command bots to neutralize guards or gather loot, adding a layer of strategic depth.The roguelike campaign is a highlight, featuring not just heists but also a strategic component where players must capture territory, avoid bankruptcy, and evade full-scale police investigations. This mode adds significant replayability and challenge, making each playthrough unique.Despite its simplicity, the story campaign complements the game well. It doesn’t burden players with complex moral dilemmas but instead enhances the gameplay with narrative-driven, planned heists. Notable missions include  each presenting intriguing scenarios, high difficulty, and substantial rewards.One of the most praised features is the removal of pagers, a popular mod in Payday 2. However, this doesn’t mean players can kill indiscriminately; murdering guards or breaking cameras raises the alert level, summoning the police at level three. Disabling cameras via a computer and tying up guards instead of killing them helps maintain a low profile. On missions against rival gangs, players can freely eliminate enemies without affecting the alert scale.Though the game has fewer locations, their procedural generation ensures that even familiar settings feel fresh and varied. This distinction sets Crime Boss: Rockay City apart from Payday, where repeated missions often felt monotonous due to unchanging environments. Here, the ever-changing layouts keep the experience exciting and unpredictable.The game's optimization is commendable, delivering stable FPS with high-quality graphics in single-player mode. However, multiplayer performance significantly drops, with FPS plummeting by six to seven times on my system, rendering the game unplayable even on minimal graphic settings. This is a significant drawback, especially since the multiplayer mode lacks the main campaign, preventing cooperative play in this engaging mode.Crime Boss: Rockay City offers a compelling blend of strategic and action elements, enriched by numerous QOL improvements and innovative features. While the single-player experience is robust and engaging, multiplayer optimization needs improvement. Nonetheless, its dynamic environments and varied gameplay ensure it stands out as a refreshing and enjoyable title in the heist game genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Tldr a Paydaylike that's better than PD3 but different from PD2 with a lot of little quirks that keep it down.First off, the offline/campaign is a management sim broken up with heists, so if you came here for the PD aspect, don't do it. It seems like you're meant to grind losses before you can actually do wins, which doesn't seem very fun and wasn't fun when I tried it.Second, the multiplayer is... Weird. Quickplay doesn't match you with games in progress that have 1-3 people in them, it matches you only to people waiting in lobbies, which, if you know humanity, means that the Quickplay button will typically force you to create a new lobby rather than joining anyone else. There's also no difficulty selection, which, if this is ever fixed, it really needs one, because......Third, the characters and hireables in multiplayer specifically are weird. You're clearly meant to use your Boss because they can use anything instead of a premade loadout, but, the thing is, the boss can only have level 1 perks and is actually incredibly weak, so what ends up happening for everyone is hiring one of the three pink-rarity hireables with more health, more regen, more damage, more bullet resist, and a predefined loadout, and just playing those instead. Wackily, this completely hamstrings the entirety of the multiplayer just because you can only apply skins to your boss and their weapons (and you have to buy the color/skin on each individual weapon, which is pretty nutty aswell when there's no skins unique to certain weapons), but since there's no reason to use your boss unless you want a challenge...The multiplayer itself is tight, though, like I said, it's above PD3, but then different from PD2. You've got the cameras, guards, patrols, the usual, but here, you can actually subdue guards without some arbitrary limit of 4 pagers. The stealth limit is actually on things that make sense, which is to say, it's a limit of 4 suspicious actions- killing a guard or breaking a camera will take one pip but won't fail the heist, instead, like PD3, if you lose all the pips or get caught in any of the sensical ways, it just turns the heist to loud, and guess what, most people don't leave if you fail stealth! Yay! Loud is comperable to PD loud but has more actual breaks and genuinely ramps up instead of being a constant flood of units (though it does become that at the end of each heist and in scripted moments) , with an emphasis on actually being in cover and managing your health instead of just tanking everything... (but people do try to do it with those 3-4 pink hireables- me included, as a Buddy player.) <Side note, yes, almost every lobby has a yellow or red connection marker, but I've not seen all that many lag issues or otherwise, so, I'm not sure it matters.>This all leads to a weird alt-payday type feeling, but the better visuals, better characters, better stories, better world, they all somehow make it feel more cohesive, generally better, and more immersive than Payday ever was... and I say that with fully-terminator-type-robots being in this world and somehow not breaking the lore. Somehow.

_childDocuments_.review: Crime Boss: Rockay City sounds like a cheap mobile game, but that couldn't have been farther from the truth. It got me seriously hooked with it's addicting gameplay loop. It brings a fresh take on the whole heisting formula with it's roguelite campaign which is unique every run you do. The game is packed with unlockables for you to unlock in a gacha-style level up system, which worked fairly well to keep me coming back to the game for more and more. The game will kick your ass the first few tries, but you'll keep getting better and better, and the game rewards you with permanent unlocks to make your next run slightly easier. It's all a learning experience, and I enjoyed all of it, it helped me get the most out of this game.The campaign has you taking over the city, turf by turf. To get turfs, you need money, that's where jobs come in. These are fairly varied and range from warehouses, compounds, armored trucks, banks, jewelry stores, malls, etc. And then you also get the BIG jobs which are more elaborate heists with greater rewards. The campaign has multiple options for a variety of aspects, such as making other bosses leave the city in alternative ways or capturing multiple turfs with 1 attack, in short the campaign provides enough variety for you to keep coming back to it.When you're done with the campaign, there's also multiplayer, which lets you experience the single player jobs in a more traditional, payday-style experience, with friends or with bots. Multiplayer has it's own progression system, and while it's a little bit on the grindier side, it also helped with providing content for me to keep playing to unlock.The devs have made great efforts to make this game as Single Player-friendly as possible, EVEN the Multiplayer mode of the game. I'm a Single Player type of guy, I very rarely play multiplayer, these days almost not at all, so this is greatly appreciated. The bots in this game, while they have their own quirks, are already pretty solid when compared with other games. They work as a team, do objectives, collect and deliver loot, among other things that make my experience as a single player that much more enjoyable.A big part of this game is the gunplay, and the gunplay in this game is TIGHT and PUNCHY! Enemies don't suffer from the spongy syndrome, and guns feel and sound STRONG! Animations are great, and so are all the other effects that complete the whole gunplay experience. Shotguns in particular are straight up porn, the devs made sure to not mess up the shotguns in this game. A FPS game with terrible shotguns is not a FPS game.The stealth in this game is fairly basic and braindead, but it's the kind of stealth that I enjoy. This is a game you're meant to replay a lot of times, so stealth doesn't need to be too complex.The game also has a very strong B-Movie feel, with it's cast of celebrities. The dialogue of this game is straight up cheese from the 90s, but in a good way (except Sheriff Norris' lines, which are straight up ASS). It makes the game feel unique and not take itself too seriously. The licensed soundtrack they've picked also complements this. The devs seem to have fully embraced the cheese.The glow up this game has had from it's almost-disastrous launch to the addicting fun experience that it's become today is to be commended. The devs have shown that they're very passionate about the game, they've listened to feedback and have implemented improvements with various updates, and they're still doing this today.Now I did mention that this game has issues, and boy does it have SOME issues! AI glitching out or getting stuck, optimization issues, softlock issues, the game still needs work. But like I mentioned above, the devs are actively listening to feedback and improving the game with each update they release. And I'm still tolerating these issues whenever they show up, just because of how damn fun this game is.

_childDocuments_.review: Crime Boss has more sauce than Payday 3. As a whole Crime Boss feels less sterile and has the same underdog studio feel that Payday 2 had at launch. Is there jank? Yup. _childDocuments_.review: Crime Boss came out swinging after its stint in gay-baby jail (I mean the Epic game store), I fully expected this game to have its single player component be completely phoned in and rely on the multiplayer to round out user enjoyment (in true 90's fashion of course) only to be surprised that the game treats not only the Rogue-lite campaign but even its cast of unique characters with some level of reverence that I wish Payday 2 could have given their cast while they were still breaking the diesel engine over their knee to accommodate new gimmicks.Much of the Voice cast sound just the right shade of phoned-in, where you can tell many of the cast and writers had the time of their lives recording some of the dialogue in this game. A good bit of this game's re-playability comes from its unpredictability, you aren't always going to the same warehouse or jewelry store because of how the tile-sets can get swapped out, sometimes stuff just goes haywire and you got to adapt on the fly which is a wild departure from the meme culture of restarting if someone's toe fell out of place and got seen by a camera that was cultivated & popularized by Payday 2.Solid game, especially now that the DLC is not at a nonsensical 20$ per item, absolutely a steal when I got it as a bundle, and at time of writing a steal while on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: When I saw the first few trailers for it I thought that the entire budget was just blown on the actors and I wouldn't like it, but I'm having fun with it. I've played PD3 through in it's entirety and I was bored almost all the way, and to this day that game doesn't have anything to offer the moment you finish the heists. (Apart from a plethora of server related issues.) You can also play this game properly solo and offline with a roguelite mode, so that's also a win in my book. Multiplayer also works fine, had no disconnects or desyncs or server errors throughout 6 hours of playtest and 2 hours of release gameplay.The only thing that I would like to see implemented one way or another is weapon customization and maybe deeper appearance customization. I'm a sucker for those. But seeing that the devs are pro-modding, once the modding scene takes off the game is golden for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Having a blast with this game. While the various jobs certainly lack the length and depth of Payday heists, the short and concise nature really complements the overall campaign. Makes for a really chill experience where you can kinda blow a stealth job and just power through the rest of the heist rather than have to start over and have blown like a half hour. Fairly fun in multiplayer to play random jobs, just disappointing that the campaign is not co-op.Big complaint is that there is no clear indication whether a mission starts quiet or loud, which can make it difficult to prepare accordingly. For example, there's one mission type where you're looting an armored cash transport, but there's no good indication whether you're crashing the convoy and looting it while shooting at cops, or just quietly intercepting it while its stopped at a motel. They should really just add a clear tag to all missions that start loud.Not really a complaint because it kinda falls into the "so bad its good" and in general plot for these kinds of games really doesn't matter but... Wow, the writing, voice acting, and just all around presentation for this game is pretty bad. I thought the actors were just randoms they brought in at first to pretend to be these big names like Chuck Norris, Danny Trejo, Danny Glover, and so on, but they're actually all the real actors. Just giving the absolute worst performances ever, for some reason.Really fun game despite that stuff, decent replayability and much more casual than Payday 2, which is a nice change of pace.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a bad game. But its a fun bad game.As a first person shooter its fun. Enemies aren't in anyway smart but neither am I so it equals out. It gets compared to Payday frequently and I suppose that's unavoidable. There is more here than just heisting though. Deathmatches in the streets for turf. Low scale store knock offs, crew and gang management. Its a full crime em up.But, and I say this without an ounce of hyperbole, this is the worst writing and voice acting I have ever heard. The devs got big name actors (from the 90s and before) and not actual VAs. Listen Chuck Norris has never been a good actor. VA or otherwise. The script is written like an edgy middle schooler learned a new swear word and that has become his whole life. This is not how people talk. Edit:I've played for a bit now and while I do say that this game is overall still fun, the cracks are showing. Lets start with the single player roguelike.Baker's battle is fun when it works. It doesn't always work and it makes even less sense. I have had multiple runs end due to various bugs. Had one where police robots showed up completely at random on low heat early in the run before they are introduced. Had another where I ended the day and it skipped multiple days in one go, timing out heists, skyrocketing my investigation and losing my territories. One time I hit 100% investigation and...nothing happened. Norris never showed up. Continued on with the game. The logic of this game is frustrating. This is due to the complete lack of it. For example, as you progress, one of your assistants comes to you with an offer to buy a new car to raise your rep. So you shell out six figures for one....then break into a DMV so its not registered as stolen. I DIDNT steal it. We bought it. Money exchanged hands. Next is during one of the heists we have to scout a port to see what boat is carrying a load of drugs into the city. After we discover when and where the boat will be, the worlds worst assistant goes "yes, looks like the usual boat in the usual port." IM SORRY? We already knew? It has a routine?  We gathered intel and spent money on info we already knew?This is due in part to the absolutely abysmal writing. It appears this game's budget went to hiring expensive actors instead of actual writers and VAs. Every line is off. Either it doesnt make sense in context, or goes on way too long or its being delivered by someone 3/4 of a way through a whiskey bottle. There is ONE exchange late in the game that sounds like two people having a convo. If you fail your run but survive and escape Madsen and Rooker will have talk about starting over. It feels (and sounds due to the sudden drop in mic quality) like this was a candid convo that just happened to get recorded. And if you read into what they are saying about "this is bad and a nightmare" following Madsen's disappointed sigh and Rooker's laughing, it almost comes off as they are making fun of the game candidly. Some lines go on way too long. Someone will make a point and then there will be another 3 or 4 shot and reverse shots of each character just making an awkward quip or saying something completely out of pocket and unrelated. Sometimes, especially with Madsen and Nasara, their lines will turn into complete gibberish. Just a random assortment of words. I think, I cannot confirm, but my headcannon is that the devs got these big name celebrities to say a line or two then used AI to do the rest. Including writing their script. There are so many moments where I had to stop and think "no human would say that." Overall though, its still fun. I like the combat. I like the more free take on stealth vs Payday. I do think the game is very easy. Early in the run you will blitz through missions. Even late game when you get a decent crew together, you'll chew through enemies. The only difficult part is the investigation meter, which I honestly really dislike, and turf wars. Turf wars are more difficult because you are playing as a random soldier. This means you cannot build them or choose their equipment. I do like the randomness of it but I am tired of spawning into a gunfight armed with only a knife. The investigation meter constantly ticks ahead and Norris for somereason only focuses on you. You can do nothing but stealth and keep under the radar but Norris will still find you and ignore everyone else. Its terrible and sucks.I do recommend it. Especially with all the free DLC. There is a surprising amount of game here given the price. Just be ready to put your head in your hands whenever Chuck Norris chokes out a line like a illiterate 3rd grader.
_childDocuments_.name: Crime Boss: Rockay City

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fine game overall, kinda mid, but certainly has enough enjoyable moments.If you can get it on a sale, definitely worth it.What I liked: - Singleplayer roguelite campaign overall, and the style of it, felt like almost "perfect" realization of that fantasy of "operating a criminal organization", and imo is the best part of the game- Heist are quite variable in gameplay, especially stealth feels like gives a lot to do, and a lot of ways to do it- Heist and mission RNG in general is really great and lends itself to be quite replayable- When playing in solo, being able to switch between any part of your team you brought to the heist is great, and in general AI of the ally bots is great in stealth heist when lootingWhat felt "meh"/indifferent:- Shooting and gunplay is serviceable, but not much more than that - guns feels like in a generic run-of-the-mill shooter from a decade and a half ago- Movement and traversal same as shooting - just doesn't bring satisfaction when playing- Loud heisting gameplay in general felt kinda "meh" - not terrible, but just lacking... something, didn't quite figure out, what felt "off" to me, just that it started to feel stale and boring really fast- Lackluster customization for guns/characters - every gun is "set", you get attachments only by getting a higher quality gun, you can't modify guns you already have. The skins for guns is a "full dip", with no option to customize wear/what parts are painted. Same for characters - every character is just a set "skin", with no option to change outfits (not even talking about different parts of the outfits)- Shallow build creation system in general - you get some boosts with perks, but most of them are just generic stat boosts, which, while do provide a noticeable buff, just don't feel like they provide for good replayability (which contrasts a lot with how replayable the heists are)- UI is generic looking and is just "serviceable" - doesn't work on improving the "crime boss fantasy", but doesn't subtract from it either. Best part of it is probably the city board in the roguelite, but team and asset management UX felt "eh", and some nested menus felt unnecessary. For example, when initiating a turf war - surely you can just give the ability to select number of soldiers and display the cost of it directly from the board, without the need for an extra menu. Another example is not being to properly switch between team members when in the character selection, and customize the loadout - you need to back out from selected character, select another character, and only then you can view what they have, and customize their loadouts, it feels like selection should be simpler, What I didn't like at all:- Voice acting and cutscene are just bad. It's not "funny cringe", it's just cringe, with only a couple funny moments, but mostly due to how much memed they were. And imo it doesn't even really work as an homage/a riff on 80s-90s B-tier action movies, as it feels like even those had much better acting and writing than whatever this is- Performance is kinda bad, at times it worked worse than how Cyberpunk 2077 and Starfield worked on my PC (with 5600X, 6900XT, 64GB RAM, running on NVME SSD), dropping below 60 FPS, while not having much to show for it comparatively- Turf wars feel like just "filler content" to make the playthrough longer. While it has some "fine" mechanics like switching to a different soldier if you die, and some mini-bosses are cool, overall it's just boring and extremely repetitive, and imo having an option to either make it random chance, based on amount of people you send, but giving an "instant" result, skipping the combat, or to take part in it yourself, would improve it a lot.- More of a minor thing, UI related - it doesn't seem like there's a difference in hitmarkers between hitting an enemy or an explosive object (be it a car or explosive canister of some kind). With cars it's especially bad since the arriving cops usually use it as cover, and, from far enough away, you can't tell if you're hitting a cop or the car. Sure, you can make the car explode, but it takes a lot of time and bullets to do so. If there was a different color/size/type of hit indicator for hitting environmental stuff (maybe make it yellow/green, or make it a circle instead of an X. or make it bigger/smaller in size), or just an option to disable it for those, it would've been nice

_childDocuments_.review: This really feels like what I hoped Payday 3 was going to be. Solid gunplay and mechanics, graphics and sound-design are great (save for Chuck Norris' voicing, though it IS hilarious,) and there's a good amount of variety as it stands now. I just want more of everything, which is the best compliment I can give a game. There do, however, still seem to be quite a few bugs present that only my friends who joined my game would encounter, such as ladders being unusable, lootbags desyncing, them being unable to do anything sometimes (looking around, aiming, and interacting,) and semi-frequent crashing. I never had any such issues, but they're certainly worth mentioning. Buddy's vision having this awful red filter is my #1 complaint, I appreciate the thought behind it but it just makes him miserable to play despite being a really fun and unique character. Maybe just tone it down (or ideally, just remove it please.) My little gripes would be that, firstly, the friendly bots are pretty useless in firefights and often don't do quite what you want them to do, but it's good that they're there, and secondly, the DLC weapons make using anything else feel like a waste of time since there aren't really any that are up to par with them. Maybe buff some weapons or give them pink variants, something.Solid 7.5/10 as it stands- fix Buddy's vision, add some more content, and squash the bugs and this game will be one I'll come back to for years.

_childDocuments_.review: About as close to that OTHER heist game I'll ever get to these days.I won't lie, this game is rough around the edges (performance issues on otherwise-capable hardware, weird desync in certain places), but the enthusiasm by the development team feels palpable, they've fully embraced the modding scene (and the memes!), and it's a fun time in multiplayer and even the single player rogue-like mode, a mode I didn't have much interest in, does have me a little curious. _childDocuments_.review: Played about ten hours during the pre-release playtest and absolutely worth coming back to. Game is great fun and the highlight for me is the roguelite mode, that feels like a cross between Payday and XCOM, where you have a limited amount of time to take over the city and eliminate your rivals, controlling a map screen and managing your crew between missions. If someone dies in a mission, they stay dead until your next playthrough.The multiplayer modes are lot more relaxed, all modes count towards you multiplayer progression and there's no worry about perma-death or losing your unlocked items. Some of the heists in the game were clearly designed for the single player campaign, and are very short, lasting only a few minutes, however there are large scale ones that can take upwards of twenty.You can choose to bring AI crew with you even in the multiplayer modes, and they are generally very good, actually helping you collect and secure loot as well as control civilians and guards even during stealth. They fall apart in actual gun fights, where I've noticed they like to stand out in the open, but they're a mark above the AI teammates of similar games.There are caveats that need to be known before going in, however. The online is peer to peer, but still requires an Epic account for matchmaking. When Epic's verification servers go down, you just get error messages and crashes.But the biggest concern are the performance issues, even beyond the usual shader compilation, the game will randomly just stutter a lot at times, I suggest making sure the game is installed to an internal SSD and you turn off background processes like Geforce Experience. The game doesn't do a whole lot to justify being as demanding as it is.At the time of writing, the game comes with all the previously released DLC for free, and it's incredible value for what's on offer. Looking forward to sinking more time into the game.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: An excellent co-op heisting FPS that's inspired by cheesy 80s/90s action movies and shares similarities with PAYDAY. I'd recommend this game to anyone who's a fan of the PAYDAY series or just wants to rob some banks with friends and listen to old Hollywood actors deliver cheesy lines. Also the game is bizarrely cheap, all the DLC is free to keep if you get it now, and future DLC will be the same way.The devs must've done a complete 180 because I recall people giving the game scathing reviews last year when I can't really find any major flaws with it now. The dialogue is very cheesy and Chuck Norris clearly did not care whatsoever when delivering his lines, but that made me laugh and every other celeb does a pretty good job (even Vanilla Ice!). Otherwise I don't see why this would've deserved being labeled one of the worst games of 2023.In some ways Crime Boss: Rockay City is like if you took the neat ideas from rough gems of the Xbox 360/PS3 era and polished them up. Overall the game is heavily inspired by 80s/90s action films like Heat, Lethal Weapon, etc. The campaign is a roguelite (permanent progression is available so it's not a roguelike), each time you start a run you'll be met with a different cutscene, a different main heist to work toward for that run, different missions, etc. etc.This aspect of the campaign is fun, though it does also feel like they had a normal-styled linear campaign during development and then chopped it up. The cutscenes that play feel totally random and confusing at first, there's no real "intro" to the campaign either (anymore, apparently when this first released on EGS there was a sorta-intro mission that's no longer available for some reason?). I'd like to see this fixed down the road, along with co-op support for it.The multiplayer on the other hand is very similar to PAYDAY, and I can see why so many other user reviews compare the two. I've played all three of that series and after the disappointment of PD3 I do think Crime Boss is scratching that itch nicely, but it feels different enough that it doesn't come off as a PAYDAY "clone," it's more like "we enjoyed PAYDAY but want to make our own game in that style."I like the 80s/90s movie vibes (including with some of the missions), stealth isn't obnoxious and limiting (infinite zipties!), and I think the gunplay feels really good and weighty.I only have a few bits of feedback at the moment, and the ones that are complaints/negative are pretty minor:

_childDocuments_.review: Crime Boss is the superior successor to the idea of Payday The Heist: a (cooperative) robbery shooter from an indie studio who unabashedly admits which movies they're trying to crib. Crime Boss notably improves upon Payday in a few ways:* Indie game pricing with no overpriced DLC or on-disk content moved to "DLC" as an attempt to pad sales.* A developer who cares about updating their release and knows how to have fun.* The mood and tone is vibrant and *fun*. Rockay is fun to fight through as a bright Miami resort city and the game is fueled with some delicious cheese. Treat the game more like Kill Bill or Lethal Weapon rather than The Godfather or Heat and you'll enjoy yourself.* The big heists actually feel grand, in scale with several missions/tasks of buildup and execution and they carry the refreshingly  simple premise of stealing anything not nailed down, as opposed to fighting ancient aliens or murky conspiracies. * There is an actual single player mode that is not only offline playable, but has a surprising amount of strategy akin to turn based strategy games.* Money is actually useful in this game, rather than Payday's money for nothing. You steal money to buy stuff, which then allows you to steal stuff faster/better with the stronger items you bought.* The developers don't care if you want to cheese the game (to an extent) and generally wont try to patch your fun out. If you wish to lure the guards one by one into a corner with the brick, knock yourself out.* The Crime Boss bots will help you with a lot of the busywork of Payday, like picking safe locks, ziptying lobbies of civilians, or moving bags of loot (not that this doesn't create its own problems).* Multiplayer has a simple server browser to get into/create the games you want, rather than trying to funnel you into crossplay/quickplay.Be warned, this game has some poor programming/has some design oversights and it does make the experience frustrating.* The allied bot AI is incredibly dumb despite being more useful. You can't command them to use their throwable, the allied bots like standing in the open, or the bots try to be helpful with picking up two bags but the decide to charge cops with just their sidearm. You can slightly mitigate this by swapping to a different bot, but please IGS, let me command bots akin to Mass Effect's squad system.* The game may just randomly break at times. During the playtest session, a hard crash on my computer randomly reset my entire save file, and one Gold Cup run randomly changed to the loud objectives of fending off the helicopter, despite the actual gameplay being in stealth.* Another example is when the stealth guards bafflingly turn into Robocop and can see behind their skulls, or can suddenly can find any guards/civilians you ziptied behind 2 walls, or can randomly see a broken laser underground despite the cops being aboveground.* There is no restart mission button in single player. I get this was a choice for the roguelite nature of the game, but the various AI bugs/lack of information can lead you to a situation you never were supposed to be in. You can work around this with Alt+F4/Task Manager to quit the game, but I'd rather the devs just put in a restart button by default so I don't need to deal with their programming breaking my runs.* Some of the single player tasks can quickly feel exhausting when there's no way to pay a resource cost to just skip them. If you have conquered most of Rockay except for 1 gang, you have to keep playing the Turf Defense instead of just paying $200,000 to automatically succeed. * The multiplayer mode progression feels awful due to the poor rewards scaling. You can rob entire trucks' worth of gold, empty grand vaults, or steal a yacht of coke from the cops and just get ... $200,000 for your effort. When most of the multiplayer unlocks cost hundreds of thousands of dollars, if not millions. (At least the payout for these in single player is in the millions and feels great.)If you can deal with some of the poor programming, Crime Boss is worth your money. So worth the money, that a friend gifted me the game (thanks hibestie) the moment it came out on Steam, before I had a chance to buy it myself.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE 10/31/24 - Unfortunately the devs have succumbed to the trend of using AI generated art in the new Rockay Rumble map, which screws over artists and their work. Hopefully something is done about the art and this does not become a trend for the game. A shame, because the game is still fun, and the new map/event is fun as well, but its hard to recommend in good consciousness knowing that the devs intend on using AI generated art. Until something is done about the art (or im just wrong about it being AI generated in the first place) ill be changing my recommendation to No, A real shame, because everything in my original review down below still stands.ORIGINAL REVIEW -This game is very silly but very fun. The roguelite campaign in the core of the game, and its fun to see how far you can get or how much money you can make. Some slight crust in regards to performance, both of the game and actors who appear in the game, who give performances ranging from chuckle worthy to bone chillingly cringe. It kinda honestly feels like a PS2 or early XBox game plucked from nearly two decades ago and dropped it into today.I bought and played the game while it was on Epic, and comparing the game from then to now, theres some things that have changed a little for the worse (each of the unique heisters used to have special perks that made them stand out from the generic goons you can hire) and for the better (new heists, new maps for the existing smaller jobs). There was also a decent amount of story cutscenes in the first few runs you did that are either cut or spread throughout multiple runs, which makes the story feel a little disjointed or clunky.Gameplay wise, it feels and plays more closer to an arcadey style shooter like Call of Duty, with sliding and regenerating health that requires you to use cover effectively, compared to the slower and more methodical gameplay that Payday 2 has to offer. Theres a fun risk reward mechanic with the drills and saws on heists that have them, where you can speed the drill up at risk of overheating the drill and needing to restart it. Your AI companions flip between being very useful friends and nearly sabotaging a stealth run when they decide to grab a bag or zip tie a civilian who isnt relevant.Overall, fun and worth some of your time, especially considering the price of the game at this time.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright here's the gist of it:It's far better than Payday 3, but no where near as good as Payday 2. It basically sits right in the middleHowever, unlike the current version of Payday 3, the game very much has a Soul, you can tell the studio actively WANTED to make this game.And quite frankly, after a year of constant love from the devs, it's in a very good place right now.Because here's the thing... this game, isn't just a cheap Payday clone, there are plenty of cool and unique ideas that makes this game stand out on its own 2 feet, like the rogue-lite campaign mode with character perma-death, the bigger heists having some pretty cool Cooperative mechanics that makes it easier to complete, the AI bot system actually being one of best in the entire genre.To me, this game went from a crappy 3/10 at launch to a solid 7/10 now, which is damn impressive considering it was achieves in the span of a single year.Overall, this thing went from a complete slop at launch to an actually enjoyable and surprisingly good coop experience, for 20 bucks, you're getting a very decent product that'll last you for a while, with more updates/DLCs on the horizon.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR 6.5/10. Needs more updates and fixes, but a good time waster for the price point. A game with potential that needs to be worked on.Crime Boss is a game I'm seriously mixed on. On one hand, it's very fun and for the price tag currently ($15.99 USD until 07/11/24) it's not a bad deal. On the other, there's a lot of flaws in this game that hinder the experience drastically and need polishing; like a Diamond that's stupid cloudy and jagged, but something can be made of it.My major concerns are the AI. The AI for friendly units need to be fixed or tweaked heavily, they constantly decide to run into the line of fire, ignore all semblance of danger and decide to eat 200 exploding propane tanks for breakfast, and get lost or stuck on random areas. Heists that are loud only, especially the "Big Heists", can easily fail because the AI decided to try to drive a car that's on fire and spray painted "DO NOT DRIVE, BOMB IN CAR". The friendly AI need either more damage resistance against explosives or just actually need to learn fire bad do not touch.My other concerns also come with gunplay, as guns are on a binary system here: Good or Utterly pointless. Most SMGs feel like peashooters due to bad feedback and even worse damage while shotguns are just stupidly broken, as even the most tanky enemies, like bosses during Territory attacks or Bulldozers fall over in 2-3 shots. Pistols also feel the same way, automatic pistols feel very poor due to harsh dropoff and weird recoil whereas revolvers consistently 1 or 2 taps at decent ranges. If Auto pistols or the SMGs get buffed and feel better, as well as the wonky balancing gets sorted out, I think gunplay would massively improve.

_childDocuments_.review: Loving the game, feels like a direct upgrade to Payday's gameplay with more forgiving stealth (infinite zip ties and body bags my beloved). My only complaints based only my experience in the campaign:-AI isn't very reliable. They don't use equipment like grenades on their own, need constant baby sitting so they don't get overwhelmed, on rare occasions they get bugged and stand in the open getting mowed down. The later happens when they try to carry loot bags to a drop off point. -No breathing room between police attacks. In Payday, having hostages increases the time between assaults. Nothing like that in Crime Boss. Stealth as much as you can before going loud. -Enemy alertness in stealth is bugged. Not sure why, but some enemies are able to detect things that are not in view and out of range. Meter fills up but the alarm isn't raised. You need to distract by throwing a none explosive weapon (brick, throwing knife, etc.) near them and that'll reset their alert state.  I only survived the Hidden Vault mission due to one of my crew members health glitching and became immortal, I had to use him as a distraction after the other two got overwhelmed and downed repeatedly. Despite the flaws and speaking as a Payday veteran, I highly recommend the game for the price alone (especially for the Steam launch special, an absolute steal).
