_childDocuments_.review: What Payday 3 should've been. As an avid player of Payday 2 who was utterly disappointed at the outcome of Payday 3, I found this game on a whim a day before it dropped. I playtested it, not expecting much, but six hours went by and I was enjoying the hell out of the Baker's campaign. It has high replayability value due to nature of the turn-based mechanics, it's pretty, decently optimized, and the AI are actually capable of following instructions, looting, and being immersive enough to keep the game fun and fresh. For the price (which currently includes the DLC), it's highly worth it. Take it from someone who excitedly pre-ordered PD3's Gold Edition and has sunk in maybe ten hours total, if even that, this is much more fun. It can be quick, the combat mechanics are varied and fun, there's load out customization, weapon skins, the heists aren't tiresome or pointlessly elongated, there are drills and saws that you can choose to accelerate (if you screw up, that's on you), and a variety of different playing modes and heists of which there's more to come! Seems like the devs listened to everything that was mildly infuriating about Payday and turned it into something good. Find some friends, take it online, or play by yourself. Worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: It really depends on WHAT you like about PD. Someone else pointed this out well; it's not a complete "heisting simulator" but rather a "gang going on a heist simulator". I'll start with the cons and end with the pros for a specific reason.Cons: - Horrible voice acting. Honestly, it doesn't even feel "so bad it's good" level to me, it's just painfully bad. The experience was actually degraded until I turned voices to 0% in options. The game then became way better.- There are definitely the occasional bugs, not the "this game just works a little differently" type, moreso the "I just outright can't use my throwable in this play session" type. However, for me and my friends, it hasn't been every session. - The game could definitely be waaayyy better optimized. 3060Ti shouldn't be at 5FPS on the main menu with a couple of characters and a map loaded, even if it's "max settings" by default, it doesn't look quite complicated enough for that.- Sometimes the AI does some very ridiculous things.Pros:- Very solid gameplay loop. "Multiplayer" and "singleplayer" are actually two different types of games. Singleplayer is a roguelite while multiplayer is just about the heists and making piles of money. It helps use the same gameplay for different mechanics and progression types, keeping the game feeling fresh (at least to me so far).- Game is pretty nicely balanced towards still keeping a good amount of pressure on the player, despite the time-regenerating health. I was concerned they'd be as bad as One Armed Robber is about it, but fortunately not.- Non-dumb AI pathing. AI actually does help with carrying bags and even deposits them for you. Not completely reliable but better than Payday's. - Bag system may be liked or disliked. Personally I like it though. Bags are just bags, you can hold one bag with little consequence, but holding a second bag prevents you from using your primary and slows you down a bit. I have my concerns on the longevity of the gameplay and whether the devs can update it to keep it well-maintained and listen to the right feedback. Hopefully they do well with it, though. I heard others say the devs are very pro-modding, but I don't know how much you can mod the game considering it's Unreal Engine (unfortunately). The game, while it has technically existed for a year, has only just now came to Steam, making it to where it'll actually start having attention. There's been a few simple UI and model change mods, so hopefully we can have some gameplay changing mods as well.

_childDocuments_.review: For a game that launched what, a year ago, and was terribly received, it's actually really good. Now I didn't experience it at launch so I can't say whether it was as bad as it sounded and there has been massive fixes and changes, or if it was just review bombed by everyone and everything and it was fine from the start, but really what matters now is the state that it's currently in which I consider to be pretty amazing.First off, rougelites, I love em. Not only will the missions be similar to PD:2 where locations are randomized, but the city map and who controls what will be as well. The whole point of the original non-DLC campaign is simple, take over the city before the police have enough evidence to shut you down. Raise funds through large and small time jobs, take over and hold territory, eliminate entire enemy factions, all against the ever climbing investigation meter. You also have the daily heat meter which rises when things go south. If your first job of the day attracts the attention of the police, and you hold your ground or don't get out soon, this meter will begin to rise from 1 to 5 stars. Starting with normal patrol officers and ending with heavy units like shields, juggernauts, and special units. If you get jobs done quiet like, the police response will remain minimal. If every job of the day has been an extended shootout with the police, as soon as the alarm is raised special units will have boots on the ground incredibly quickly. When you advance the day, this meter will reset, unlike the overall investigation meter. Second, guns and gameplay. I really have no complaints here. The movement is solid and the guns feel punchy. The biggest issue I have is, where are the silencers? Although not strictly necessary, silencers can save you from going loud under certain circumstances. For hire characters come with their own gear, so I say, just keep a lookout for any with a silenced pistol just in case. Maybe there is a way to unlock a purchasable gun with a silencer that I could distribute to all team members that I just have not gotten to yet. The stealth system is also satisfying. One of the biggest plus sides here is the ability to holster your gun after taking it out. I don't even think these guys wear masks like our Payday crews, but it's apparent that the Payday crew applies their mask with Gorilla glue to ensure it can not fall off and their identities exposed during their heists. Here, you can unholster and holster your weapon as necessary during the stealth phase, which is great.AI: Pretty darn good. But keep in mind this game does have strictly single player modes as well as multiplayer so I would expect no less. They will come in and help gather loot, tie down civilians, and carry things to the van. You can order them to do specific tasks as well if needed. Bugs: Incredibly rare and thus far never game breaking. I think I've seen 2 civs kinda phased into a wall slightly but they came out and resumed normal behavior after being shouted down. There was also one mission about freeing a prisoner or something from a transport and once released he just kinda got stuck by the truck but it made no difference, mission still complete and everything was good. I'm assuming he should have run off of the map. Overall with the release here on Steam that kinda reminded us yes, this game exists, plus the low price for the base game and all current DLC, it's 100% worth it. I think it would be worth it even without a discount. And this game isn't over yet. There is still more to come. I'm not sure exactly what the devs plan for this game is, whether it be supporting it for a long time like PD:2 or a much shorter lifespan, but I'm here for it and definitely welcome new content and maybe one day a second entry in the series since now I do consider it a good game, worth the time and worth continuing to make. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: I bought this game myself on EGS and all DLC and received a free Steam copy because I assisted with beta testing roughly a month prior to the Steam release. I am not affiliated with or paid by 505 or IGS.This game was good at launch on EGS, though lacking a bit of polish and content, as opposed to some of the games released in the same time frame that didn't even work for most players. Yet somehow those AAA title got better reviews than this game from 'influencers' and 'journalists'. I guess it doesn't matter as long as you get the clicks and views. Anyway, that's water under the bridge, so let's take a look at the Steam release!Fast forward from 2023 to 2024 and many updates and content updates later. The game is in a really great state at the moment, whether it's performance, content or balance. It's over the top, a bit cheezy, but good fun. Heisting in 90's Miami, euh I mean Rockay City! Single player roguelite campaign stays fresh replay after replay due to the well-implemented procedural generation and well-executed story and heist content. The expansions add major heists as well as new characters/skins and weapons. Playable offline too, none of that live-service stuff in here!Multiplayer offers a variety of heists and jobs and the unlock/progression system is well-thought-out. Did I mention Michael Madsen and Michael Rooker being amazing? (Can't say the same for Norris, but somehow it fits in with the cheese). The other characters are varied, with each their own character and voice lines, and when used as bots, work well to assist the player. Last, but not least: devs have been very committed with updates and new content and there's another year of that planned.Performance wise: it runs on Steam Deck and my ROG Ally has no problem with it too. Doesn't need a hefty PC to play.Anyway, if you're looking for a good heisting game, either single or multi player, and for a really nice price (at launch also includes ALL the DLC), then Crime Boss: Rockay City is a no-brainer.

_childDocuments_.review: Rockay City manages to hit the sweetspot for several niches:sneaking around and be a silent ghost, orrush in with guns blazing and carve a bloody swath trough to your objective.build your organization from humble Beginnings to controlling the whole city, and of course,LOOT!the great thing is you dont fail a mission just because stealth was lost. and its also not always the better option - you almost always have a choice on how to approach the situation.In most cases you have to pick your prefered Risk/Reward ratio, with a lot of ingame mechanics encouraging you to take more risk. Every crewmember you bring on a mission makes it a lot safer, but also eats into your profit margin. Going in alone is means fewer people to share with, but if things go south or you run into a trap, be prepared to say goodbye to an expensive operative.Or, bring the boss on a mission to imayimize payout, but beware: if he falls, your run is over.Overall, great learning curve, great concept, great execution.Also, the entire Voice-cast (and Chuck Norris in particular) is an absolute win. _childDocuments_.review: I have no idea where anyone that honestly thinks this is better than Payday is coming from.Yes this game is certainly inspired by Payday. There's some good mechanics here that had me going hmm why doesn't Payday have that. The ability to carry 2 bags of loot makes you slower and unable to use primary, UI and interaction for locks, and loot that dynamically fills bags are great simple adds. The graphics are good albeit a bit unoptimized atm. Campaign missions are somewhat interesting.AI teammates have good mechanics being able to give them commands like to help you bag loot and even switch to play as their character. Though it is a bit annoying how atm they can trigger the alarm when they roam by cluelessly walking into guards.Ofc Payday not only has a prestige and build system that make you want to maximize and try cool builds but also pull off perfect runs for XP bonuses and the most loot. Most importantly, it's also a strategy game at least when going stealth. Which guards will you take down? Will you have to drop an unexpected guard? Do you have enough time to page the guard? Will a guard unexpectedly check a room or did you soft alert a guard that will now investigate an area? The answer to all those questions in this game are no.Even if your impatient in stealth Payday gives strong value in just partially stealthing missions or even rushing stealth with risky moves thanks to it's strong gameplay. It has something for everyone.Guards are dumb as rocks here, yet the gameplay lacks the ability to rush stealth missions and pull risky plays in a similar way as Payday does. Guard and cam pings last forever meaning that a guard will never give you a surprise scare. In combo with the ability to just bonk infinite guards here makes stealth just a boring test of patience and a snooze fest.I don't like whatever the gun system is. Seems like there's no customization and you just have to find special versions of  a weapon even to get basic things like a suppressor. Granted if you've read up till here you know suppressors are useless anyways since this game is just bonking whatever guards you need/want to and easily slipping by.Same boring ass music everywhere. Seriously heist music in Payday is certainly a nice piece, and is nice in any kind of game like this.The reason I can't recommend this game are primarily 21.  While even Payday 3 lacks some simple neat mechanics this game has the same is true the other way around. Hostages serve no value here. It's not a strategy game at all. Many missions you stealth are a measure of your patience in just taking down as many guards as you want, which leaves no risk or fun and makes stealth just boring. It also makes mission design much lazier since they don't need to pay so much attention to patrol paths and tuning their difficulty. In short, this has potential in it's mechanics but is as shallow as a puddle. I can't understand how this is even in the same realm as being compared to Payday by many reviews.2. More importantly is the Coop truly sucks. The Coop missions are extremely repetitive and overwhelmingly short, basic, and boring. Bank heists are easily completed in 5min and armored cars can be done in a couple min as 2 examples. I'd have to imagine the positive reviews only come from campaign (which is not Coop) bc from the perspective of it as a MP game it's just bad. Ofc again the campaign seems decent here for solo but Payday has actual story line and plot in it's missions.This is besides the bugs and unoptimized graphics, which are playable but can sometimes partially break missions at least. The game ultimately has some potential with the mechanics and graphics it offers so there is some hope if they add Coop campaign or actually good MP missions. However, even if it improves in these areas it's hard to say it'll have close to the same longevity and replayability as Payday thanks to it's build and prestige system.

_childDocuments_.review: I have  played the multiplayer at the time of writing, only the singleplayer roguelite campaign which is what I originally bought the game for.Honestly, with how abysmal Payday 3 was, I am happy to see Payday-likes appear. I don't think one game should be able to monopolize a genre just because it did the formula first, if someone else wants to take a crack at it I think they should be able to.Now, do I think this is a  Payday-like? Yes, actually.It's not perfect, it definitely has its issues and I don't think there's the same level of depth as even Payday 2 had. , as a simple dumb fun heist game to play as an alternative, I do think it's enjoyable and worth buying. Guns felt pretty alright (to me at least), I actually  enjoy the roguelite campaigns, and the game does have some neat stuff going on like some unique missions or some story plotlines changing based on the player's actions (like what Wiz' missions play out like depending on if you screw up the data disk heist or not).The story of the game is also just... not really that bad. Honestly, it hasn't detracted from my own experience so far because the actual gameplay (the part that actually matters) feels solid. And if you think of the story like it's just a b-movie turned into a videogame, it really becomes a lot more enjoyable. Things like the dated celebrities giving questionable performances just add to the b-movie feeling.The game is also being actively supported by the developers at the time of writing, and there's a roadmap for future content, some of which looks really interesting. I personally like the game already as-is, but with some time the game can very well mature into something better.

_childDocuments_.review: Game needs some serious ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ work. Despite it's payday inspiration, it clearly has not learned several important lessons from both Payday 2 and Payday 3, namely what made PD2 one of the best horde shooters to ever exist and how PD3 ♥♥♥♥♥♥ that all up. First and most importantly your AI teammates have to not suck ♥♥♥♥, or if they have to suck ♥♥♥♥ they have to not be an active hindrance. This game fails in that entirely. I'm constantly having to neurotically watch the AI health bars like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hawk because of the way this game handles its revive system. On hard during high risk loud encounters it can be difficult to effectively take cover as the player, let alone the AI doing anything even remotely like that. Even while trying to hold a solidly defensive position the AI will gladly stand broadly in the open and eat all of the enemies gunfire, and because this game has the AI have the same rules as the player they die pretty much instantly die unless you frantically switch between everyone to get them behind cover constantly. Stealth is easy to fail and has no quick restart function, and feature from PD2 that blows my mind it isn't here. I understand this is supposed to be a roguelite, but these kinds of stealth games require lots of practice for each heist/tile set, and without a quick restart that means failing these extremely frequently per run. _childDocuments_.review: Section 16 of the EULA includes forced arbitration, preventing you from being able to take part in any lawsuit, class action or otherwise, should you be wronged by the company. You get random loadouts for turf war missions missions and no option for silenced pistols at the start of the game outside of the tutorial for the heist missions, which pretty much forces you to go loud all the time. The entire cycle is: 3 minute "heist" (Heist being a kind word for running into a warehouse, shooting 2 guards, breaking some boxes and escape before the cops even show up) then a "turf war" (which is just shooting 10 guys with your randomly given weapon and nothing else). Then rinse and repeat.Then there are bigger heists, which in my experience was just shooting more bad guys. There are no objects other then grab loot and shoot bad guys. No objectives or obstacle or anything except maybe the occasional door that requires a saw or drill, but that's it.Apparently there should be heists that have a bit more depth, but I encountered none of it so far. And if it takes me doing hours of useless grind with no challenge to get the occasional fun heist, what is the point of playing? Better to play Payday 2 or even 3.There is nothing that makes me want to play this game. And this is coming from a life long Payday fan. I would rather play payday 3 then this.

_childDocuments_.review: I was one of those that picked up PD3 at launch and I was one of the many that was left very disappointed. I was previously aware of Crime Boss: Rockay City and when the playtest arrived on Steam I jumped straight in. The playtest left me with very good impressions and had such an impact that I was sold without a doubt in my mind. Crime Boss: Rockay City was offering fun and enjoyable heists that had me hooked.Multiplayer wise I stand by my original assessment of it being an excellent coop shooter and a vastly superior alternative to the disappointing PD3. There are a variety of options for multiplayer heisting that range from Quickmatches the include an experience boost to mini-Campaigns. The heists themselves appear to have a good degree of randomisation when it comes to various elements and you'll typically be assigned additional bonus objectives.Where the game has caught me off guard is with it's singleplayer modes. The primary mode is a "roguelike" mode which sees you vying for control of the city against rival gangs while attempting to deal with increasing pressure from the law. This roguelike mode appears to offer the potential for a lot of replayability. In addition to the roguelike campaign the DLC also adds a campaign focusing on Dollar Dragon (Danny Trejo) and a more sci-fi themed campaign.When all is said and done, Crime Boss: Rockay City feels like a very polished product with a great soundtrack, some  fantastic appearances from actors such as Norris, Glover and Trejo along with some incredibly fun gameplay that can be enjoyed both solo and in coop.At this point in time the only thing I really miss from PD is weapon customisation but I can live without this given the vibrant, fun game that Crime Boss brings to the table.

Which is great (and hilarious).The voices in general are fun.The guns sound good (for once in a videogame).Just a very FUN and fairly priced game (also for once).This game is one of the very best surprises in recent times for me.If the theme and gameplay looks like they interest you even a little bit, don't pass on it.

_childDocuments_.review: Better than Payday (in most ways). The gameplay is satisfying, smooth, graphics are good, easy to find a match and people to play with.I find it a little refreshing but also annoying that in order to unlock more weapons, you need to level up and you randomly pick from 3 options of something new to unlock. I'd kinda much rather prefer everything have a set level to unlock it, simply because all I want is a silenced weapon and i'm almost level 20 and still don't have one (excluding melee weapons). _childDocuments_.review: In case you, like many, were disappointed by Payday 3, Crime Boss: Rockay City is an extremely enjoyable, if very janky and silly heisting experience. The main emphasis is put on the singleplayer roguelite mode, which has strategic elements in between missions. There is a big variety of missions to take on, far, far more than Payday 3, however a majority of these are smaller robberies, though there are still a lot of the big high-stake heists like it's competition. Bot behaviour is, compared to every Payday game on the market, Highly advanced. You can freely swap between any characters you bring onto your mission in loud or stealth, and bots will help with most objectives, such as bagging loot, pacifying civilians, and even delivering loot to the escape for you. The voice acting and storytelling will either be a source of constant annoyance or endless entertainment, as the big hollywood actors they had hired for the main characters in cutscenes where likely given not very good acting direction, as most, if not all, voice lines are very poorly acted. The main two exceptions are Nasara, voiced by Payday's very own Damien  Potier, and Dollar Dragon, voiced by Danny Trejo. Overall, though, Crime Boss is very enjoyable. If you're sick of Payday, just remember that new adventures await, buddy!

_childDocuments_.review: Was very skeptical going into this game. However, I am very impressed with how it turned out. It's almost like the game is what Payday 3 should have been. It 100% feels like an addition to the Payday universe that takes place in Florida with some futuristic elements added.I was worried it would feel more like a cyber punk given from the footage and the trailer on the store page, but it only makes up a small fraction of the game. The rest of the game has a modern setting to it.The looting was very satisfying, and by far one of the biggest improvements in this game when comparing to Payday was the AI. The NPC companions are so smart and are actually useful. They help move bags and gather loot, and even just throwing a bag down a hallway, the NPC Heisters already know to go and grab it and move to the extraction point. One of the coolest features is the ability to switch to another companion mid heist and play as them or position them in a certain area for standby.The investigation bar that increases as you commit crimes and move throughout the days is sick. The heat system to make levels harder when committing too many heists in one day (in-game day) is also cool.The Turf War system was super interesting, and took up a bit too much of the game (more then I liked). Having to constantly go and defend turfs and take over other turfs was a very annoying and repetitive task.One of the biggest negatives with the game has got to be the voice acting, or atleast the animations for the characters when talking. It isn't synced pretty well with the audio and seems very off.The ability to pickup guns from dead bodies mid missions despite not owning them was a great idea.Lastly, the stealth was very cool, maybe a bit too easy. And the gunplay was some of the best I've every seen. The guns feel heavy but also smooth, and just has an immersive feel to them. The recoil with the guns is perfect.Amazing game. Needs some more missions though.And dammit, get a new logo for the game cuz my eyes bleed when looking at it during loading screens. Terrible logo.

_childDocuments_.review: For $20 at release, this game is amazingly solid. Keep in mind. For $20. This is a co op (or solo) heist action/stealth game. Sure. There's others that are similar, but this one brings it's own spin on it. First what this game does well...Solo mode. Multiple different ways to play solo! Different game modes, but the highlight is the roguelite campaign that's honestly decently engaging. For the gameplay. The story...yeesh...we'll get to that in a minute. But you'll play as...you guessed it, a crime boss. You're taking over Rockay City (stupid name, but whatever, move on) and you'll go about this by hiring crew, buying weapons, completing heists to fund your illegal activities. You'll be fighting for gang territory and evading heat from the police. It's a balancing act, but it's decently fun. There's random events to encounter, factions will react to you attacking them or even call for a truce, which you have the option to break. The heists and territory battles are relatively short and sweet. Nothing so intense you'll spend a lot of time on, but meaty enough to still feel like you're actually playing a game. The multiplayer is a little more of a traditional stealth/shoot'em up heist. It's mindless fun, you earn money, upgrade, customize, and that's kind of the loop. There's not a ton of customization for your guns, but it's still kinda fun to just unlock stuff. So the things I don't like. Sweet baby jeebus the writing for this is god awful. Like there's campy. And there's bad. Then there's this. The "humor" and believe me. "humor" is a very generous stretch is something that of a middle school child in the 90's wrote. I think it's trying to be campy. But some of the voice lines of this asinine script is truly headache inducing. If there was anything of a good idea of a storyline, it's completely washed out by the juvenile humor written by a robot that was told "make this funny, slightly edgy, and in the style of something the kids will like, but from the early 90's" and this is what it spat out. Very dated references. I...don't THINK the voice acting is bad? It might be. I can't tell if it's the writing or the voice acting. Considering I know these voice actors have other work that's great, I'm inclined to think it's the writing. Okay, Since I barfed out this paragraph about the writing. What else do I not like?....I guess if I were to be a bit picky, the random perks you get for promoting your crew kinda stinks. Maybe some weapon customization would be nice? I do like the little breadcrumbs of a reward that the grind could offer, but sometimes you just need that hook of seeing some upgrades that look really nice, and you're really motivated to play "just one more round" to unlock some cool stuff. This doesn't really have that. Overall, the $20 VALUE is great. I would gladly have paid $30 for some decent writing though.

_childDocuments_.review: This game elicits mixed feelings for me and I do feel pretty sorry for the devs - who seem to actually care about their game. If there were a "mixed" rating button, I'd definitely use it. On one hand, the campaign is quite repetitive, and the story is almost non-existent. However, it seems clear that storytelling wasn't the primary focus here, and fortunately, the gameplay compensates for it. The gunplay is genuinely fun. I just wish the level design were more varied. Additionally, the AI isn't the sharpest, but they manage to get the job done.The game has a very small player base. This is probably due to the rough launch and notoriety this game had for being absolutely horrible on release. The lack of player base has made the multiplayer mode almost completely deserted, making it impossible to get a full squad match. As a result, you're often forced to play with bots, which becomes monotonous and feels no different than the campaign.Overall rating: 6.9/10. It's on sale right now and I would say it's worth the price if you are really craving a heist game and don't want to put up with payday3, just make sure you know what you are getting into first.

_childDocuments_.review: It's just an extremely subpar game. Matchmaking sucks. Regenerating health is too forgiving. Enemy spawn rates are unrealistic. Game balance in general sucks. And it would be one thing if this offered unique mechanics or had it's own identity but at the end of the day it's essentially a reskin of payday. It shares so many similarities with Payday that I genuinely wonder how they were legally allowed to make it; or how they landed literal A list talent for mocap and voice work. Maybe that's what they blew their budget on. Who knows.I genuinely wanted to like this game. And for what it's worth, I enjoy the single player roguelike mode. That's probably the only redeeming quality this game has to offer and the turf war mechanic of taking over the city is a solid idea in concept and would lend itself almost perfectly towards a mode akin to risk where you sieze territory from other players as you progress and yet they lock that mode into only being accessible in single player and you can only go up against AI opponents. That's probably the worst of it.I picked this up on sale for like 15-20$ and I don't find it living up to that price tag. This game isn't a steaming pile of ♥♥♥♥, it actually has redeeming qualities and interesting ideas, but in the state it exists in right now I think you should stay away from it. It suffers from poor management, poor decision making, and poor implementation and I wouldn't recommend it to anyone, even to die hard fans of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just good old school fun. I've only played the singleplayer campaign so far, so I can't speak on the multiplayer. Having said that, this campaign has a suprising amount of depth and replayability. The cutscenes with their voice acting delivery, odd animations, and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ dialogue has me laughing often. The gunplay is solid, not excellent, but servicable considering stealth is the optimal approach usually. Finding loot and robbing it is even more satisfying here than in Payday, which is the game that will inevitably draw the most comparisons with Crime Boss. The only thing Payday does better in my opinion is the cool mask mechanic, other than that Crime Boss is the superior heist game. Not to mention it costs less than most indie gamesDon't let the complaints about the friendly AI scare you off. For one, you can control your bot teammates and position them before/during a mission. And two, they're actually quite competent at gunplay and especially loot management. The pathfinding is manageable if you order them effectivelyMichael Madsen is the standout among all the great actors in this game, and they give him all the best dialogue. Not to mention he's probably who you'll play the campaign as most of the time, so it's just cool that we have a game where Mr. Blonde is the player character. The progression feels great, both within your campaign, and with the permabuffs you get as you advance rank. Overall this is just a solid package and it's the most fun I've had in an FPS in a long time. For it's price, I'd say definitely give it a shot

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very solid 7.5/10 title for $20, but there are a number of massive cracks that stop it from being the best it can be.It's a B-movie heisting game with B+ design and execution. It's got a number of good things going for it and I've heard that there's work to make this game worthy of it, which I appreciate.This game has some slight bugs and kooky AI at times, and some bad designs at points that have resulted in me failing a few missions because it didn't properly explain certain mechanics. It seems designed around an already existing familiarity with this title/similar titles in order to smooth out the on-boarding experience. This game was very obviously made by people who use English as their second language, and while the localization doesn't render the game unplayable or anything, it does make the game's UI and visual language counter-intuitive at times and it makes the writing and voicelines god-awful, even from the perspective of a purely gameplay-focused person like myself. Even the voice direction in a mission can come off as extremely inconsistent. I'd call for retakes if I were Ingame Studios.All that aside, the trailers and screenshots don't do this game justice, and that's a shame because it's got a really interesting campaign system with its "roguelike mode", (It's more like an ironman gamemode with roguelite progression elements sprinkled in) and a multiplayer mode that makes it a decent standalone coop shooter title. It reminds me of those Gen 7 console titles that'd have multiplayer-exclusive content but it's clear that it's not the main focus, especially with its extremely effective reuse of assets to make the most out of what it has.This game still needs a ton of work to make it as good as i'd like, but what's here right now is definitely worth the $15-$20 asking price, but if the devs and publishers maintain the momentum they have with this title, I can see this game filling the void of heisting games left by the disappointment that was Payday 3.

_childDocuments_.review: Bouy. Rockay City? What can you say about this game that isnt already scrawled on a tile floor in a public restroom? The game seemed like it was pitched to the numerous actors from days past as their digital time machine where hey could play themselves in their prime. Vanilla Ice could go back to be a respected member of "the culture", Micheal Madsen could go back to beating the bottle and tugging back on his girlfriends. Wait! Scatch that. Reverse it. Heck they even have chuck norris who has recorded over 8 minutes of dialogue. Lets be real the voice acting is shamefully and clearly where all the money went and long before anyone thought to write a script. I will say that Micheal Rooker is a consumite professional and will deliver his appaling lines with aplumb, even though he is an American Football themed criminal who you get to play weilding a Light machine gun whenever someone attacks your turf. Im getting a bit ahead of myself so Ill just say the plain truth about this game. The main gameplay loop is fine. Maybe even kinda addictive good. Like a live service game that keeps your attention until they feel like they have you and pull out inevitable money grab, but these guys knew they had a flop for a year on epic so no cash grab is in the works thankfully. As it stands this is simply a Paydayesque single player (unless you do the multiplayer thing) with a cringe worthy story that is lead by a man who clearly has been having a rough couple years because if those line deliveries were from a sober man I will eat my hat. Micheal Madsen is quite clearly drunk in nearly all his line reads and has been given no stage direction. Its all done in that verbatum style of cold reads that make it so so horribly unnatural you will want him to stop at some point. I give it a couple stars. I had fun and I am glad it seems to have been better recieved as the uniquely compelling dumpster fire it is. Slow down and look at the dumpster burn even though it is for sure making traffic worse for everyone else. I support buying this game simply so that the actors involved can continue to purchase the self medications that got them into this game in the first place.

_childDocuments_.review: I usually don't really write actual reviews but the devs for this game clearly want to make it better despite the status it had when it came out.Also, I'm gonna try my best to avoid comparisons to Payday 3 unless it's a really good one. To also say I've played this game a bit on EGS (up to level 10) and I played PD3 on Xbox.What's Good:-Price: Even without the sale (and honestly the extra DLC) $20 is a good deal for a game with both a full on story mode and coop mode. Add on currently, as the time of writing, that it's $16 and all DLC is free for now and it's an absolute bargain.-RNG: When it comes to coop heist games like these, RNG is key. This is the one time I'll make a comparison to Payday 3. In PD3, RNG means very little, at most it's some items being in a different area, but for the most part every heist never really changes. In CB, whole level layouts can be completely different for the same heist. Whether it's the smaller jobs having completely different locations for the same "job", to the major heists having 2 to 3 different layouts along with different item/loot locations, different camera/security room locations, etc. It really varies up the gameplay to where you don't always exactly know where to go for everything without even looking.-Voice Acting: Is it *good* good? Not, mostly not at all. Some of the random team members have decent VA but for the most part it's Not Great. Is it so bad it's extremely funny and joke worthy? Yes, 100%. "New adventures await, buddy!" has become a saying in a discord I'm in. If you can sit back, laugh, and embrace the B list cheesy as all hell action movie level dialogue (which, from how the devs act, seems to be somewhat the point) you'll enjoy the cutscenes.-Guns/Gunplay: The gunplay itself is pretty good, nothing extremely noteworthy but it plays well and guns have a good feel to them. Some uh Strange designs for some guns but overall you have a decent selection that even includes melee weapons (unlike...yeah). Whats interesting is the fact that you can pick up guns during a level. You picked a team member that only has a shovel for a primary? Replace it with a dropped shotgun. Not to mention some levels have weapon caches on the map, not only giving you an extra option but also making the map feel a bit more alive.-Story Mode: The story mode is the definition of Good. Not amazing, just good. It's a roguelike where you try to capture every territory in Rockay City and, of course, get rich. It's got permanent upgrades that help on each run along with a different set up of characters and missions each time.-Heist Flow: Almost every heist has a very clear 3 stage progression in it's heist flow. Most noticeable are the new Cagnali DLC (which, btw, are 2 of the most insane and eventful heists I've played in a shooter like this). This type of flow just makes the maps actually feel like you are doing something.-Team AI: Not only will they smash and bag by themselves, put loot into the van, AND revive teammates, you can also coordinate with a ping system, telling them *exactly* what to do. Not to mention if playing solo you can even switch to a teammate and play as them.-Server Browser-Solo ModeCould Be Better:-Level Reward System: When you level up you are able to choose between 3 random choices as a reward. Rewards being appearances for your customizable character, team members, weapons, grenades/usables, and gun camos. The problems lie in that sometimes you can just have some bad luck and get some really bad choices or you can have the opposite problem where you have 2 good choices but can only pick one. While not a *bad* system it would be nice to have a set reward system or at the very least let us pick 2 options.-Leveling: Right now you can only level up once at a time. Meaning if you get 400 xp or 1600xp you are only gonna level up once. While I understand, so its not to just blow through the lower levels in insane time. It can feel a bit meh when you complete a big heist and only get a level. Maybe 2 levels would be better?Not Good:-Optimzation/Performance: Yeah, this is kinda the biggest problem with the game. While I can get it to run fine on a Deck, you will notice some studders and lags even on capable PCs. While not the absolute worst performance (it definitely runs better without Denuvo), I feel like it definitely needs some improvement.Overall, this is a great deal for a 7/10 game at just $20, let alone $16

_childDocuments_.review: Game is genuinely fun and immersive. The only Current issues i have with the game is it's mechanics such as movement, interactions, weapons, and armour. Movement is still fun and somewhat smooth only issue is A) you can slide to Paris and back on one slide sometimes making it difficult to stop where your trying to go like behind cover or to a cop or thug who had spotted you but you've underslide or overextended in distance giving them time to shoot you and alert nearby enemies. B) Leading into interaction such as trying to vault certain objects that aren't vaultable which should like fences or walls. For some reason npcs can but you cant. stopping or hitting npcs/cameras that are next to each other are extremely difficult as the game will get confused with what your trying to do example there is an npc under a camera so your trying to break the camera inorder to get the npc on the ground without being spotted, the game gets confused to instead of hitting the camera your character hits the npc under the camera which the camera will instantly picks up and everything goes loud (happened to me). second example trying to backslap two guards walking in a line if you attempt to hit one the other guy will instantly notice (makes a lot of sense as theyre behind each other) so then you attempt to hit the guy infront but the game still thinks that your trying to hit the previous guy you just knocked one the ground giving the guy infront enough time to let a shot go off alerting other guards in nearby area (happened to me). _childDocuments_.review: Simple fun game whose name sounds like a fake mobile game, no real bs just straight up gameplay.The graphics are gorgeous and vibrant, the gameplay is simple and the guns are stupidly addictive to shoot. I'm very glad stealth is optional and the game doesn't punish you for going loud, because shooting in this game is half the fun. Every weapon feels and sounds heavy and powerful, with the LMGs in particular feeling incredibly overpowered and fun.The single player campaign is a roguelite, where you grow your criminal empire through missions and events of your choosing, where characters and their weapons, bought with your hard earned crime money, can be lost in a permadeath system. In theory it sounds bad, but in practice it's actually quite fun (and very forgiving, mind you, as characters can be rezzed indefinitely in a mission) once you realize the whole thing is meant to be replayed over and over, and the lack of permanence is its biggest feature.I know lots of negative reviews complain about the system but in my experience it's actually quite fun, with how chaotic and hectic the missions can get once you go loud, it truly makes you fight for every inch in the hardest difficulties, where you'll often question yourself if it's worth going back in for another bag or two of loot, or risk more characters and your haul trying to save another character from death. Adding to the system is the main character and boss, Travis, who gives you a 50% bonus on all the loot you get in a mission, with the drawback being that if he dies during a mission the whole run is over and you start from scratch.You'll win and lose many characters and money throughout the course of your criminal empire, and at the end of the session you'll be left feeling like no matter what, you did things your own way, even if you bit off more than you could chew then clawed out of a bad situation or died trying, losing the whole run.The multiplayer mode has a f-ton of gamemodes and absolutely 0 drawbacks for losing, so it's really fun to mess around with too, but in my opinion the singleplayer and it's permadeath system are the highlight of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: 4 hours in...Story: I'm enjoying the little campaign. Its not really a campaign, its like... little filming cuts between missions that are all pretty much unrelated to each other, though based in the same city. Gameplay is super fun though, I disliked Payday series but this one has a "charm" about it. The different mission styles of heists are great and levelling up your characters is fun with different perks etc. I like the famous actors for the different main characters. The script writing has a lot of work for another game but it'll do for now as I'm more focused on shooting the $%!& out of everyone when robbing whatever it is I'm going to be robbing. You will be surprised with the amount of stuff available to do on the story so that alone I would say is a good purchase. Multiplayer: Even though its a common issue of people just sitting in lobbies (same with a lot of hosts in games) You can host matches yourself and even select bots to take the place for the missing players. The bots are very intelligent and will actually go grab the bags of loot and run with them to the van with you. You level up your character with the heist money that you collect from the mission (new guns, skins, characters etc) So a fun game to grind in general with or without friends. Final Thoughts: This game is worthy of a 4/5 for the price and replay-ability. This will not be my go-to game to play, but it's a great time waster in between other games that I enjoy also. Great work Devs, this is the first game on steam in a while that I've taken a chance on and actually enjoyed.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the 'Rockay' start, Crime Boss has definitely proven as the spiritual PAYDAY successor.  I played PAYDAY 3 and found it to be so bland and disappointing.  After reading some reviews talking about giving this game a chance I decided to take the plunge.  It's definitely worth picking up at $15 w/ DLC - probably fair up to $25.  One thing I liked from PD3 was the "zones" mechanic like being in Public/Private/Secure and that same mechanic is in this game, except now you can holster and and equip your weapon as needed.  Guards can be subdued which wont count against your 'suspicious action' (pager) limit.  The maps make sense logically and I liked how there was always a plan B for loud heists if you mess up.  As long as they release solid content and improve on what's here they will follow in the footsteps of the legendary PAYDAY 2.  This game does have a lot of stark difference from PAYDAY, like preset characters vs the 'Boss' characters, weapon rarities, and the Saints Row 3 like story.  Initially it was kind of annoying, but all the dumb lines and characters have grown on me.  I also like that this game has a single-player themed strategy mode that helps to add to the variety found in the game.  If you are a veteran PAYDAY player and are also disappointed with the state of PAYDAY 3 I'd recommend giving Crime Boss: Rockay City a shot.  *Last note I forgot to add in the body: This game does have some performance issues.  I have a 5800x3D, 3070ti, and great internet and I get ridiculous studders in the game if playing multiplayer.  Lowering settings helps but it seems to be present no matter what.  Hoping that some optimizations come out soon.

_childDocuments_.review: Look, I have no clue how this game was a year ago when it released in EGS jail. I heard it was bad. It probably was. And Rockay is a stupid name. But the game I just got on Steam with all the DLC for $15? That game whips ass.Gameplay-wise it's another AA shooter, basically a smoother Payday 2 with regenerating health. Lockpicking, drilling, filling bags with loot, it's all there and it works just a bit smoother than P2, which you'd expect considering it came out 10 years later but it still bears mentioning given how badly Payday 3 blew it. You can actually give your bots orders so they can do objectives for you! Imagine!Multiplayer is what you'd expect, though the heists are generally less elaborate and more meant to be chained back to back. It's good, it's fine, it's mostly what you think it is. What impresses me is the single player. It's a roguelite, and for whatever reason it's a mix of Dope Wars and instanced FPS combat? I never knew I wanted that until now.Basically you have a map with a bunch of turf to take and ♥♥♥♥ to do. You can only do so much in a day and all of it costs resources. Turf battles are handled by your soldiers, one of whom you're always piloting, and their gear improves as you invest in them. Heists are for your team of named guys/gals and require more finesse, especially if you want to complete them in stealth to keep your heat down. It's not a wildly complicated setup, but there's a lot more going on there than you'd think. You'll be judging which heists to do based on what goods you'll steal, because those don't just convert to cash, you need to actually check their current trending value and sell when the time is right. Lots of heists require significant investments to even start but certain goods can often be used in lieu of cash, which is way more efficient if you can arrange it. You see the Dope Wars comparison? There's stuff here!Multi-step jobs are really nice, but what's impressed me so far are the mostly random character events that pop up like regular missions and very much aren't. I had a guy named Ranger who was a beast, my favorite squaddie by a mile. Eventually I see he gets a special mission, only it's for him alone because he was having a 'Nam flashback that I needed to handle before too many days passed. This put me in his shoes fighting in a rice paddy as he saved his unit from a sniper Rambo-style. Also his captain was Danny Trejo. What? What the ♥♥♥♥? This is awesome, why is no one talking about this???I'm not gonna say that Crime Boss will change your life or anything, and it's definitely got those AA rough edges (many of which are made manifest in the awful celeb performances), but if you want something genuinely different and you like heistin' I see no reason why you shouldn't at least try this thing. _childDocuments_.review: When Rockay first launched I had heard it was a disasterous low budget Payday rip off, and Epic exclusivity didn't help it. Having played it now I have to assume 505 have pulled off a No Mans Sky or something. Although this game has a multiplayer mode it plays far better IMO as a single player Roguelite take on the old Payday premise, heists are smaller and faster but with no trading hostages or doc bags to refresh downs the thrill is really kept up. There are still larger heists on par with Payday's Big Bank and they really lean into the cool heist asthetic but they are comperatively rare.The game has a lot of refreshing refines on core gameplay compared to Payday 2, gunsmithing is sadly gone and there are no huge RPG leveling systems but almost everything else is dramatically improved. Drills now encourage player to guard them by giving you the ability to speed them up, rather than random breaking and requiring lengthy interactions to repair, instead you can hold the drill to boost it for a time with a needle moving towards a green zone that will 3x the speed of the drill however the boost wears off after a few seconds so players will need to maintain their presence and if a player overshoots the green zone the drill will break and need to be restarted however this is far quicker than the old Payday 2 system. Bots are now far more useful and independent, with many missions they will dive in on the loot and bag it then run to the van on their own with little handholding from the player needed although they can be a little overly brave when doing so. You can also pick up fallen weapons from enemies now too!Player characters, with the exception of Troy Baker the boss, are mostly generic feeling but are meant to be disposable and function on a tier system. Common low tier characters will try their best with shovels and crowbars but can be upgraded with experience and reequiped with weapons from a shop. Some characters however are even given full on stories from a Vietnam war vet going through flashbacks to a cursed Jamican drug smuggler tracking down a voodoo witch. Stealth is also subtly reworked but for the best. You have a 3 strikes and your out system before stealth is broken and the cops are called. Eliminating guards or cameras will count as a strike, as well as trespassing in secure areas. However cameras can be disabled by finding a computer in a security room and simply shutting them off, and guards can be pacified by sneaking up on them and "intimidating" them through a sharp shoulder punch. These refinements feel a lot more rewarding and fair compared to trying to dodge guards while worrying about your 4 pager limit. Alternatively some missions have you infiltrating the territory of rival gangs which is a very different situation, gangsters do not warn you and shoot on sight but in return there are no off limit actions with them either and killing them with a silenced pistol or throwing knife is not penalized so long as the body is out of sight. This actually gives stealth gameplay two fun and different feelings to it.It's also worth mentioning the game is down right charming: inspired by 90s action movies and proud of it with many characters just being almost perfect copies of classic actors (in many cases voiced by them even); the game knows it's cheesy and is happy to have fun with it but never jumps the shark into being annoyingly goofy. The characters laugh with each other and shoot goofy one liners but it's played like friends having fun with each other; one particular scene featuring "Gloves" (Danny Glover) giggling to each other about Gloves wearing gloves was so goofy their laughter became infectious. Gloves as your heist planner and coordinator frequently chews up the scenery and it's clear Mr. Glover had a lot of fun with his role... unfortunately Chuck Norris, voicing the main antagonist Sherriff Norris either clearly did not take a video game role seriously at all, or regretted agreeing to the project; in either case every single line from Norris is bored and monotone, as if he just read through the script once not even trying to do more than say the right words, before stepping out of the recording booth and warning the devs his contract only required him to do one take. If he got paid a turkey sandwich with just tomato for this performance it was too much. Aside from him though the voice actors all do a great job with their performances; MIchael Rooker as Touchdown, the gang's enforcer is another stand out performance.Overall for 20 dollars I thought this was a great game and I'm happy to find myself coming back to it.

Your only GOOD options are shotguns, melee, or being an incredibly good at head shots. Anything else and you are better off avoiding any scenarios where fire fights are involved.The enemies either have too much health or your automatic weapons do too little damage. I'm not entirely sure which is true but it is incredibly annoying and frustrating when I can mag dump an enemy, lose half of the rounds because I'm fighting recoil and ADS sway, manage to not kill the enemy, and then spend however long it takes to reload just to do that all over again. The alternative of hipfiring is arguably worse since that means I either lose my shots to inaccuracy or be well within shotgun range, out in the open, still mag dump them, and then get downed because I have to reload with no cover.My overall opinion is that the sneaky stealth/puzzle like elements of the game like figuring out the best order to take out the guards are fun and enjoyable albeit a bit repetitive while the shooting and fending off waves of gangs/police is frustrating. _childDocuments_.review: Gonna keep it short because I just wanna drop a positive review.It's an XCOM-esque roguelite heisting game. Basically, you take the role of a wannabe gang leader and attempt to take over a city, one turf at a time. Attacking rival gangs, robbing stores/banks to fund your army/team. There's actually a surprising amount of detail put into this thing. Everyone thought this was just a cash grab to capitalize on PAYDAY 2's success, but It really isn't. Crime Boss does a lot to distinguish itself with it's 80s/90s over-the-top cheesy VO and cutscenes, as well as the strategy portion of the game. While the actual act of heisting is pretty simple in it's mechanics, it does everything it sought to do well. Gunplay feels good. Stuffing a bag full of loot is satisfying as hell. There's enough variation in heists to keep things interesting. The random events and branching paths that can happen in the Roguelite mode are surprisingly expansive as well. Summary: PAYDAY 3 disappointed me tremendously. Crime Boss Rockay City Surprised me immensely.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know how to feel about it. I had more fun playing this game than i had playing the 2 hours of Payday 3 before i refunded it but i still found myself going back to Payday 2.It may become a great game eventually but right now for that price it's like a 5 out of 10.Here are my goods, bads and in-betweens:+ Control multiple characters in a heist+ Better allied AI pathfinding and intelligence than Payday (usually)+ More randomized heists than Payday+ Loose loot you pick up gets merged into a bag when you collect enough (more realistic than Paydays loose loot but more bags to carry)- Guns and characters get unlocked by leveling up (which is not too different to Paydays heist rewards) but guns have set sights and attachments. You have no way of customizing your loadout the way you would in...well... Payday.- There are no perks or skills you unlock by leveling up. Your entire playstyle is bound to the equipment you bring. Which you unlock randomly. This not only eliminates the need of planning before doing a heist but makes the gameplay feel more arcade-like. Select and equip your characters, do the heist, repeat. The Reward = some skins maybe.- gun sound is a a bit mushy and lacks punch-/+ The gameplay loop is not too different to a Payday heist but has a few key differences.Going in loud is not too different to Payday. You've waves of enemies you fend off until you can extract with your loot.Stealth gameplay however is where the differences are notable and (in my opinion) not for the better.You have guards patrolling the area but instead of taking them out and answering the radio to avoid triggering the alarm you sneak up to them push em down and cuff them. And there is no limit to how many of them you can cuff.You could clear an area of 20 guards and no alarm is going to trigger. So what does trigger an alarm? gun shots (no silencer)being spotted (obviously)killing or destroying a total of 3 guards/cameras (???????????)You can deactivate cameras by turning off the monitor. Why do i need to turn it off if no guard is still around to watch the monitor? In Payday you could use those cameras to your advantage but here you basically beeline to the camera, turn it off then clear the guards. I can get behind the idea that when 3 cameras get destroyed the operator may get a bit suspicious but when you shoot a guard then someone knows that something is wrong but when 20 guards are cuffed in an alleyway then that's okay?And it is way too easy to clear the guards. You can have a brick as equipment that has a few seconds cooldown. Throw brick > Guard walks to brick > cuff guard > move guard away > repeatCongratulations, you completed the heist.-/+ They have a rougelike campaign mode that i won't go into detail about. Not a big fan of roguelikes. But that's not the problem. The problem is the god awful voice acting... especially of the main character... which you are forced to play. There are 3 "different" campaigns and all of them are his campaign with different settings. Animations are so stiff and voice acting so generic that i'm not sure if this is some AI generated mess. From the writing to the voice acting to the animations. Just god awful. It's so bad i recommend to buy the game, experience that trash for yourself and refund it afterwards.

_childDocuments_.review: So far, i'm surprised by how much fun i'm having with this game.I haven't done much of my own single player but i've watched my friend go through his a few times and it looked pretty good. If you haven't started your single player run yet then a good trick to start it off with a boost is to start the Cagnali's Order dlc, buy assets, restart campaign and repeat till the starter money from the DLC won't be enough for any assets.I've dipped my toes further into multiplayer and enjoy doing the heist with my friend plus bots. If you don't want to deal with randoms or have no friends then bots can help too. If you plan doing anything stealthy then don't bring bots, just do it solo. Bots have the tendency to run in front of active cameras and guards alerting everyone when you throw your bags on the floor while looting a bank vault for example. It was great to build my own boss in multiplayer however you can only have one build. I end up manically swapping perks and guns around so my boss would be set up for stealth and the same when going loud. It would be great to create a second boss (like buying a new boss slot for example) so I can create a loud boss and one for stealth.All in all i'm finding the game fun and will be great to see what comes next.

_childDocuments_.review: So... First off, I should say this review so far is only for the story mode. I Have yet to try the multiplayer...This game is totally a Payday Rip-Off, but a fun one at that. Heists don't take a hr like some of the Payday ones do, unless you want it to. Graphics are pretty good, and I like the blood spray. Language is on par with GTA5, (So dont let your kids play it), and the voice acting doesn't always read like its vocalized. (Kinda like when you turn on dubbing on a film and leave the subtitles on...) And for some of the actors, you can tell they are just reading from a script, with no visualization of what their character was doing at the time... **AHEM, MICHAEL ROOKER AND MADSEN!!**  Kinda glitchy at times, like vans not wanting to show up during a heist, or not getting your items to chose from when you level up, but a force close and restart usually fixes that. Shooting gets better with progression, and so do your crew/gang. The progression system is good, but not always very rewarding. I love that if you mess up and your boss dies, you get some permanent perks for the next run through. Missions are pretty similar, but I don't mind that because they never play out the same.

_childDocuments_.review: Current state of the game has the potential to be really good. But it is still held back by serious bugs or poor enemy behaviour.-Dying while using your gadget in campaign turf wars, sometimes makes you unable to shoot or melee. Dying allows you to use melee again. Quit game & click campaign again, to auto-restart the turf mission(does NOT work once the result screen shows).-Multiplayer Results screens frequently get stuck on-screen when it SHOULD take you back to the lobby screen. You can however, still interact with the lobby functions, but you'll basically be clicking on memory.-. This is so bad & happens basically every day, it's almost on par with Helldivers 2 before they finally started fixing extremely common crashes.-Save. Data. Corruption: I Got to level 60+, beat the campaign 3 times, bought most of the campaign-boss assets. My whole computer Freeze-crashes when i try to start a multiplayer shuffle, so i hold my power button. Next time i start the game, i've fully reset. I don't even know if the freeze-crash was caused by the game, but this game is the only one where i have problems that severe. The gadget lockups, multiplayer result screen & pc freezing all happened so often with this game, i wasn't even blindsided by the data erasure, though i was still frustrated my 60 hrs of gameplay were wiped by something entirely the game's fault.-Alt+f4 during a mission asks if you want to surrender. (Why would you even do this when you could use the pause menu?)-The difference between heat ratings does not show the enemy equipment, armor strength or possible enemy types-No Pre-map planning or display of the Pre-mission map to show objectives.-Some objective tasks are vague or do not state that there is a possible penalty, such as the Vertigo Hidden Vault. Nasara tells you to find the Night manager's desk, he does not tell you an alarm will trip if you get the wrong one. First time players will struggle a lot with many missions that have no direction or warnings of dangers.-Police can use LETHAL GRENADES in civilian areas. I see them grenade my civ groups very regularly.-Civs are useless in loud, your AI teammates won't even try to ziptie them during loud.-Friendly AI cannot/Will not use their gadgets. not even the ones that don't do damage like the berserk or Mule booster. Your soldiers in turf war won't use them either.-Friendly AI Heisters will prioritize dropping off their bags higher than listening to your orders to stay with you, isolating them & getting them killed.-Friendly AI heisters cannot be told to ignore bags you don't want picked up, such as bag groups near the escape when you would rather they run to collect loot until the escape arrives, or only carry 1 bag so they can still use their primary.-Friendly AI heisters will aggressively subdue & tie down anyone even slightly suspicious, even if the act of tying them up is much more dangerous for a stealth detection domino effect.-Guns are SO inaccurate, you can't even hit an idle enemy in the head consistently 10 meters away from you because the accuracy is that poor. This is probably to compensate for the tightly packed maps, but this just causes frustration when my gun sight says it's on target, but the bullet fires off-target. Being detected from outside your vision is really hard to notice. You only get a small icon at the EDGE of your screen. & when you're playing online, you can hear the detection SFX for your teammates too, rather than ONLY yourself. There's no big centre HUD showing your highest detection either, so even if you're TRYING to keep an eye out for it, you're guaranteed to miss it at some point when playing online due to shared Detection SFX.-Shooting non-armored enemy parts has no extra effect aside from helmets protecting from headshot damage unless you shoot it off. But if your gun isn't strong enough, you still won't kill with 1 headshot to the exposed head.-Enemy Animation Smoothness: Horrible. 90d+ snap-turns are frustratingly common & massively affect your ability to hit the target.Pathetic, adding together all your AI Soldiers' kills is unlikely to surpass 5 Gear loadouts are randomized, sometimes making you spawn with shurikens instead of something like a grenade. Or an smg instead of a shotgun.(shotguns are really good) Bullet sponge central. A SINGLE one is ALMOST guaranteed to takedown ALL of your turf-war soldiers if you do nothing, even if there were no other enemy Turf Soldiers supporting them. I know they're captains & supposed to be tougher, but 2/3 captain types are straight up UNFAIR for your ai to takedown, those being the chainsaw or Mini-gunners. Both have really high HP, DMG & movement Speed.-Turf war captains may spawn at 10 soldiers remaining, if not, you can fully clear the area. If they do, you now have infinite enemy soldiers supporting up-to 3 captains. can have their chainsaw destroyed, but melee 1-shot your soldiers & sprint faster than you could with Swift-3. In Turf Wars, melee units are actually more dangerous than guns because they rush the target & are guaranteed to land the hit, & kill in 2 hits at most. whereas guns, have something like a 10% hit rate. A single Melee Soldier will take out 3 of your people easily if you don't kill it yourself. These ones shoot so many bullets they're guaranteed to kill every 2 seconds.Edit: The Backpack Sparks & they DO take more damage if shot there. For some reason, their miniguns don't have any speed penalty, they are literally SPRINTING AS FAST AS YOU, if you were to carry a pistol with swift-3.

_childDocuments_.review: Increasing Police Spawns and difficulty while barely (if at all) improving the Ally AI was a huge mistake. The majority of assaults quickly turn into repeated grenades and flashbangs at your feet almost nonstop, all the while sending 3-4 heavies at you  With VERY little downtime between waves now. Likewise, Robot police also arrive MUCH sooner too.Before: Hard and Extreme difficulty were annoying at times but i honestly found it fun despite the Ally AI often being complete dead weight during firefights. 1-2 heavies coming at you at once every once in awhile seemed about fair and pulling through and getting extra money was nice, ESPECIALLY in a super grindy game like this. There was also a lot of time to pick up Ally AI members to prevent them from dying completely (They don't defend themselves well so it Happens A LOT MORE than it should!!!)Now: 3-4 Heavies come at you at once, You have to CONSTANTLY run from grenades/flashbangs being tossed at you, police spawn in larger clusters MUCH FASTER, and there is almost NO DOWNTIME between assault waves. Oh, and the Dying timer goes by VERY fast now, have fun trying to pick up A downed henchman when they suddenly decide to stand and do nothing in the middle of 3 heavies and a squad of robo-police before they die.  Good luck trying to survive because theres a good chance the Ally AI will STILL stare and do nothing but let itself be shot. Even when they are shooting and trying to help it feels like they barely make an impact on the enemy count compared to when its just you firing on them and often just end up getting shredded and downed.I was hoping we would see some actual AI improvements but they seem to function about the same as before. PLEASE ACTUALLY buff the Ally AI. I don't even care if its just a temporary AI damage reduction/increase when they aren't being controlled, I'd just like a mission with 4 Elite henchman to ACTUALLY FEEL like i'm not the only one defending across the entire mission length.

_childDocuments_.review: In single player you play as a ‘crime boss’ attempting to take control of Rockay city after the former kingpin met an untimely end. You send soldiers out to get control of different regions (turf) in the city while competing with 4 other factions. If invading a turf occupied by another faction you select a number of troops to send in and take direct control of a soldier as you try to kill enough enemies before you run out of soldiers. These generally take less than 2 mins with a hard deadline of 10 mins.Each day 2-4 robbery opportunities are available to send a team of 1-4 people using your boss character and/or other specialists to steal cash or other goods to fund your expansion. These can also be fairly quick, though if you are going slow in stealth they can take 20-30 mins. After a day or 2 a big heist opportunity will become available that requires you to do multiple missions, buy equipment and setup, to take on a mission that will have a significant payout. The spoils from these can usually be pocketed for personal gain, or used to pay off a faction and take them out of the campaign.All the while the police will be investigating your crimes. If their investigations gets too far along before you gain control of all the turf, you will be forced to leave the city and will have to start the campaign over again. Since this is a roguelike game you will gain experience that helps unlock permanent upgrades that make future runs easier no matter if you win or lose.As long as your ok with roguelike staples like the inability to quicksave/quickload as a way to deal with mistakes made in a mission it works fairly well. Oh that guard spotted you and called the police, well time to go loud and get out with whichever loot you can. Wiz took a few too many bullets and died in the mission, well they won’t be available till your next campaign. Generally this works well, but there are occasions where the game just plain ♥♥♥♥♥ up and things like the distraction brick will be spotted by guards and called in as if they were staring at a zip tied hostage for no understandable reason. This sucks when it happens but after having played more than 20 campaigns I have only had this happen in 4 missions, and it did not stop me from completing the mission.The randomization of the missions works fairly well. There are 2-3 base layouts for most mission types with several changes to guard/civilian patrol patterns, camera setups, safe/loot locations, and security room locations. Even after 14 successfully completed campaigns I am still seeing new layout alterations and alternate patrol/camera configurations. And the roguelike campaign has random events that can occur during missions as you get further into a campaign that throw curveballs into otherwise solid plans.The multiplayer consists of picking a mission, or selecting 3-5 mission shuffle runs. Missions are generally fairly bite size and can be completed 5-10 mins with the largest heists maybe taking 20 mins or less with a team that knows the basics of what the mission is. If you are looking for a more bite sized version of payday, this does a fairly good job of it.The voice acting is a mixed bag at best. Most of the big name male actors for this phoned it in at best. Chuck Norris is absolutely awful, with the rest being anywhere from good for the lines they were given to drunk/stoned on set. Don’t know how much was down to poor directions given as they were recording or if they made all their request through Cameo with no directions, but generally most of the big name actors for this can’t have been worth the money spent for them unless they were impossibly cheap. So generally I have enjoyed most of what I have discussed above, other than the odd glitch making missions harder than they should have been (with a few times where it got me killed). The big pain point in my opinion is the way the game locks progression for gaining new guns, teamates, and equipment through a fairly slow XP grind that is shared between single player and multiplayer. Every time you get enough XP you will be given a choice of 3 items that pulls from several different unlock types. These can be purely cosmetic character skins exclusive to multiplayer (not usable in single player), weapon skins that are mainly for multiplayer (only indirectly used in single player with update 11), new guns available for single & multiplayer, New team hires for single & multiplayer, and new equipment like deployable turrets, grenades, or throwing knives.You start the game with no silenced weapon available until the you get lucky and one is offered as one of the 3 level-up unlocks, but given that there are less than 10 silenced guns in the game and there are over ~100-200 other things that the game can offer you each time your odds of being offed one are very small for many of the early level-ups. This means that if you are mainly playing single player, you are likely to have completed the campaign 2-3 times before you are ever able to unlock a single silenced gun. This can severely limit your options in several stealth missions until they become more available.Personally I would make it so the silenced Swiss (the weak starter pistol) was unlocked by default at the start of the game to give players an option, even if it’s horrible when things start to go loud. Instead you are left praying to the RNGesus every time you gain a progression level to not be given 3 options that consist only of player/weapon skins that are useless for giving gameplay options.

_childDocuments_.review: If you spoke to me a year ago, I would have wrote this off as cheesy, PD2-ripoff schlock that didn't have enough substance for the pricetag. Now, though, I have a lot further appreciation & interest into just what the hell In Game Studios were up to with this game.This isn't PAYDAY, rather a hybrid of GTA SA's gang takeovers, mixed with Payday-like FPS combat and roguelike stat & resource management. A gang simulator of sorts, all in a cheesy 90s B-movie wrapper, that's has more actual humor than the current state of Payday 3. You have a choice between a single player rougelike campaign, with substory mission "heists" that have more linear missions & cutscenes, and full peer-to-peer multiplayer of all mission and heist types with a game-wide career progression system. Loud and stealth gameplay are very mechanically simple coming from other heist games, but that's I think that actually works here with how often you'll be repeating missions, keeping tedium fairly low, with the turf war & crew resource management (kinda like XCOM I guess?)  breaking up the firefights. The point being it's serviceable enough to get the job done, but never overstays it's welcome, knowing how shallow it can be. Hell, it's enough of an innovation here that bots here can subdue guards & civs, loot, and bag transport all on command, or automatically on their own. I honestly enjoyed it.It's kind of a fascinating idea for a single player game, seeing all these mechanics in one place, even if's not trying to outdo Grand Theft Auto's or PAYDAY's legacies. It's seemingly just trying to be entertaining. Seeing Danny Trejo, Vanilla Ice, Michael Madsen, etc. all quipping the dumbest lines out of a bootleg Tarantino picture just puts the charm cherry on top for me, personally. To be clear, this game isn't trying to pretend it's better than what it is, and the devs seem to know this by now. They have fully embraced the memes, and seemingly just want more people to give it a try, thus the lower price and DLC giveaway. It's simply a fun time if your into silly co-op shooters, especially the few heisting games out there.
