_childDocuments_.review: Its all right first few hours.Its a heisting game mixed in with this rogue like campaign where you have a map and do thigns like taking over turfs, selecting missions and hiring folk, its not entirely explained well but you will quickly learn it all once you do a couple of heists.Although general gameplay is mixed, guns feel weak like there is almost no impact, to compare, and since almost everyone does, all 3 Payday games feel better with their guns. Things you shoot at also don't feel that great, this game has specials like your usual Payday or similar Horde shooter but i do not think they stick out that well, they feel more like normal cops except with stuff like a Shield or Taser, they just don't make me go 'Oh that is that special unit' they just blend in.AI partners are cool tho, you can give them orders and they seem very good at killing, plus they can stealth, but they have problems. They can on their own take loot, take down enemies and pick up guns but sometimes this makes them B Line out in the open and take lots of damage, potentinally killed. Sometimes they also get left behind and you are just wondering where they went, so bassicaly even if they have improvements over many other games you are still going to have to sit around to help them... constantly.Missions are varied, even when i visited same missions or in similar places they felt pretty good, the variation is on par with some of the best PD2 heists. Like a simple werehouse was used for a couple of different missions but in different ways and it was very good.Visually its also pretty good... except its a TAA mess and with FXAA its jagged, so all detail and nice models are vasted on whatever poison you pick, tho there are lot of options so you can probably get around it with something like Resolution scaling.Anyway, ill re do this 'first impression' after a 100 hours, but for 20 Euros this game is very good.

_childDocuments_.review: Payday on a random sliding scale. Graphically? This is gorgeous, especially compared to Payday. Running it maxed out and it's extremely fluid and smooth.Gameplay? Only played Singleplayer so far, the AI is not awful. The fact you AI team will pick up and use other weapons on the field that the game "classifies" as better? Total improvement on the heist genre for AI. A couple things are annoying, the movement feels sluggish, and some of the missions could use a set up mode that gives you better ideas of what you are looking for. Started a heist and immediately failed it because I was supposed to find something but zero indications of what I actually needed to find. That's a major annoyance for sure.The boss upgrades that make it a Rogue-Lite are extremely handy. I like Rogue-Lite in general, and this one has some really nice major and minor perks that get carried over. There is some weight to the choice.Storywise, it looks like you get completely different story options each time you start a new run. That's just awesome on many levels. Love the amount of hollywood names in this. Chuck Norris, Danny Trejo, and Danny Glover? Love it. There are more, but those are my favorite 3 so far.At the moment, definitely recommend it. At 20 bucks it's head and shoulders above Payday 3. It's no Payday 2, but there is a certain charm to it. I binged my first 5 hours, and if it wasn't for life getting in the way then I would still be on it.

_childDocuments_.review: FFFFFFREAKING CHROMATIC ABERRATION TURN IT OFF TURN IT OFF TURN IT OFF* No way to turn off chromatic aberration. It is not a cheat code for looking good. It looks bad and it hurts my eyes. (I should be able to edit engine.ini as usual, but it doesn't seem to be working... genuinely confused as that usually does the trick.)* Lens flares are also mandatory, because everyone loves J J Abrams.* UI elements like quest markers hang out in the middle of the screen to distract you from combat rather than moving to the edge for when I want to see them. The game doesn't care what I want to see. It has a Vision.* No way to restart a heist in progress (in single player, with no bots present). No way to even leave a heist in progress. You either finish it or you quit the game.* Obnoxious psuedo-strategic map jank when I just want to do crimes.* Can't highlight things for myself if bots aren't present.* No filter or sort options for buying guns, not even "show me what I can afford".* Inconsistent mantling of objects and obstacles. Sometimes you can, sometimes you can't.* You get a brick. Your brick has a cooldown. You may not pick up the brick you threw. You may not pick up other random objects. You must wait for your brick to reincarnate.* If a guard is aware of you, your punches are lethal. You kill with one punch. There is no beatdown into submission option.* Speaking of which: between melee weapons, stealth shoves, and lethal punches, I have 2-3 different melee keybinds at all times where one would suffice.* You get a silencer for the first tutorial and then it is taken away without warning and you can't get it back. Google tells me they'll show up with certain weapons and certain heisters later. In a stealth game. With specific instructions to go silent.* You are shown how to enter a security room and disable cameras. I enter the security room and tie up the guard. Cameras will not be disabled. Out of spite I smash the nearby camera. Everyone in the level goes on alert. No one is in the security room to see it. No one is there to see it. It is simply divine inspiration.* Enemies exiting a vehicle are bulletproof until they finish their animation.* No autofill of your team roster if you want the bots. I have to go in, select a heister, select to confirm, back out, four times in a row. This is terrible.* UI: "Hold enter key to purchase". Hold enter key. Nothing. Hold other enter key. Nothing. Have to click it. Clicking is not onerous, but don't lie to me.* Windowed fullscreen performance is fugly. True fullscreen helps things immensely. Guess which it starts with?I want to like this game. _childDocuments_.review: A surprise, to be sure. But a welcome one.I gotta tell ya, I saw the $15 price tag and had low expectations. But I remember it being advertised a while ago, and thought I'd give it a shot.In the roguelite/single player mode, you get to go up against Vanilla Ice, Danny Trejo, while having Michael Rooker in your corner. Tell me that's not awesome.The ability to carry one bag and use primary or sacrifice switching to your secondary and getting a second bag of loot is a nice feature I wished the Payday games had. Not sure if PD3 does this, but pinging teammates to grab loot is a VERY nice feature, as well.I think my only gripe so far is how few maps there are, and how small they are. I understand heist games focus on a smaller area map, but I do hope some larger and varied maps get added down the road.I hope the game does well enough that the devs continue to support the game. It has good bones, it's just lacking variance in terms of voice lines and maps.At $15, you can't go wrong. _childDocuments_.review: It's a simple game, but it's a fun game too....Concerning Multiplayer;The heists are pretty varied, a bunch of bigger ones that will take you 10-15 minutes or so, and a bunch of smaller jobs and such that can be completed in 5 minutes or under. Then there are 2 systems to engagewith to make that content more interesting, one being a story-driven mode (term used extremely loosly) that sees you complete sets of 3 missions with cutscenes in between. And a shuffle mode that randomizes missions based on preferences. Both are pretty good, and overall it's a really fun experience to play this Coop with my spouse, alongside 2 (surprisingly capable) bots. Single player seems good to, haven't played it yet, but progression seems to largely carry over between modes, which is a nice touch by the devs.The progression is pretty neat, it's nothing groundbreaking, but it feels satisfying and there is plenty to unlock to keep you busy for a good few hours.PERFORMANCE:Since this seems to be hit or miss for folks, on a Ryzen 5800x and RTX3060 12gb this runs PERFECTLY for us, but only while using Vsync at 60fps, menus at 30fps at ultra settings. With DLSS at Quality we get smooth 60fps, no drops in sight, temps keeping under 70c. Make of it what you will, but for us, the game performs extremely well.OVERALLIt's a fun, adrenaline fueled ride full of dumb action, even dumber writing and a bunch of corny, badly construed characters. It's glorious, it's the 80s all over again, like a cocaine fueled rampage through neon and bloodsplatter.It's also 16 bucks on launch including all DLC, which is a steal.

_childDocuments_.review: Like Payday 2 if it was focused on single player instead of multiplayer and with tons of 90s cheese.I haven't found a single thing I disliked about this game.The gameplay loop could be considered somewhat repetitive, but in the game's defense, this is broken up by having a strategic layer (the map, teams, resource management) and a tactical layer (the missions and turfwars). It's almost got a Total War sort of energy in that regard, albeit with very different gameplay. Most importantly, though, it's just fun. Very easy to get lost in it, and for the bargain base price, you can't really accuse the devs of trying to misrepresent it.The other criticism a lot of people have is of the voice acting from the big names. Yes, it's ridiculously bad to the point that I'm convinced that a lot of it is quite literally phoned in, but whether through design or serendipity, it only enhanced the 90s campy, cheesy experience for me rather than breaking the immersion. In fact, Chuck Norris' poorly-delivered one-liners ("You've been Chuck'd") even make me look forward to losing a campaign.Huge props to the devs and publisher for this one. It deserves a lot more love than it's getting.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: I originally owned the game on EGS, where I played it for more than 60 hours. Since I tremendously dislike that launcher, I decided to get the game here instead and transfer my save, so don't be fooled by my total playtime here.That said, Crime Boss is a really good game in the heisting FPS genre and a strong competitor to Payday 3 (not that that's saying much anyway), but try seeing it more as "Payday 2 with some nice QoL changes". It's super easy to get into and has improved a lot since its original release.The roguelite mode rewards persistence, there are a lot of guns to choose from, and a decent amount of missions with surprising randomization that can drastically change the layout of even the simplest jewelry stores.The AI is very helpful as well, capable of looting and transporting said loot on their own, and you can give them orders by holding the middle mouse button. Being able to swap between your AI crewmates is a huge help and a great QoL feature in single-player.Multiplayer is almost plug-and-play levels of easy, and the connectivity issues present during its EGS days are mostly fixed, thankfully. Even in high-ping lobbies, the only issue I had was not being able to use grenades, but that's it.The voice acting and cutscenes can be silly at best or cringy at worst. If you have a soft spot for cheesy movies, I guess you can get past that.On top of all that, the game is quite cheap even without discounts, giving you good bang for your buck.

_childDocuments_.review: Crime Boss is a very solidly put together game with an enjoyable and addicting gameplay loop. Looking at how the game originally launched a year ago and seeing where it’s at now is honestly nothing short of impressive. The game won’t blow your mind or anything, but for the price it’s going for? it’s honestly a steal.Whether you’re in it for the Roguelite campaign or the multiplayer heisting (which brilliantly – can still be enjoyed alone), there’s a lot of worthwhile stuff to sink your teeth into in this package, doubly so if you grab it in this limited time period when the DLCs are free.I gotta say, mad respect for the work on the bots in this game. They may not be human-level intelligent, but they're actually useful. I was honestly shocked to see they even go so far as to bag loot and even take it to the van all by themselves. When I boot up a game with bots these days I often expect them to be absolutely useless, but not in Crime Boss. Good stuff.Progression is simple but rewarding. You play the game, you get progress. No infuriating challenge-based progression in sight. The developers seemed to take community feedback seriously and constantly addressed it to make the game better than the solid foundation it had in its original launch.The writing and voice acting are simply hilarious and it’s clearly intentional, the whole thing feels like someone watched an 80\90s action movie while high on something strong and turned it into a game. I know it sounds horrible, but it’s actually entertainingly bad, and even if “so bad it’s good” isn’t your thing, you can still enjoy the game perfectly fine because the gameplay plays it 100% straight.I personally love the cheesy characters and dialogue. It’s so hilarious, it often feels like a fever dream.Good on IGS for not giving up on this. Their commitment to making Crime Boss a fun experience shows, and I’m excited to play it some more and equally curious what its future holds because the game is already a well-rounded experience that’s easy to recommend.Don’t hesitate to try this one! Preferably sooner rather than later.

_childDocuments_.review: This rating covers the state of the game currently along with the content, technical side and everything that's currently functional in the game. My review might miss some details in the game, but I'll note every one I can think of.To preface, I think the game is in a great state as is, has great multiplayer, singleplayer and I like a lot of how it works, but there are some weird things like a lack of a gunsmithing feature.Multiplayer, the multiplayer plays really well. The netcode itself isn't optimised, and as someone from South Africa it's going to be difficult to find games on 200 ping or less due to the ping being listed as a bar and not a number. The gameplay itself is very satisfying, reminiscent of payday 2, and for me the gunplay feels better. Headshots matter, but you won't run out of ammo if you don't hit them, I mostly played on hard and normal though. A good comparison would be: what if Ravenfield and Payday combined with a good campaign, better graphics, good humor and great gunplay. Note that during the campaign you can upgrade your team as well as the protagonist.Singleplayer, the Singleplayer is fun, you can choose "multiplayer" then play offline with bots essentially in small matches, or you can go on the campaign which is basically a very fast paced gang war style campaign. You get loot, recruit soldiers, take territory, defend it, and weaken enemies. There's also a roguelite aspect to it as well, i'm personally not a fan of roguelites(despite it literally stating that on the steam store page I know), but it's fun enough that I'm able to overlook it. The weapon balance isn't too leaned on the roguelite aspect so if you like a gun you can still use it, even if it isn't the best.Technical, as mentioned you can play multiplayer with yourself and bots, or with friends. Steam invites are a way you can use to get friends in, or with quickplay(which doesn't work that well), you can join game sessions using the session browser so it operates on session based servers. Weapon unlocks and skins are all RNG, there's no pay-to-win aspect or pay-to-get the best weapon or advantages in that sense(unless you don't buy the DLCs which are free right now, so this might become an issue in the near future)I find that I can play the game really smoothly on a 1080ti, but I have shadows turned down lower. Whether it's due to lack of optimisation or shadows just being really realistic, it might help if your game isn't running smoothly.There's a lack of a gunsmithing feature due to the roguelite elements, meaning that every gun and it's attachments are separate, I'm fine with it as is, but if the weapon pool gets bigger, there might be a need to have some sort of sorting or grouping feature.Appearance, You can pick the boss appearance you want, as well as the teammates you want, in the campaign the teammates are limited to a certain set of guns that can be exchanged between each other(so a weapon pool). The multiplayer aspect of this I forgot, but I'm pretty sure it's locked. The graphics are good, but not AAA so no realistic facial expressions or the like. It feels thematic and well made in the aspect of graphics. There are skins which are more like coloured versions of camo.Overall it feels like a game that has a lot of the technical inspiration drawn from earlier 2000s games(which I preferred over how badly modern games do it sometimes) where sometimes it feels like you have to jump through hoops to just get into a game, or that you're locked to online only like in most games nowadays. The music is literally from the 90s which I find enjoyable. The gameplay feels innovative, fun, and great even ignoring the early access state that it's in. I would recommend it, unless it gets worse.A list of features I think would make the game a bit more user friendly:Note: There are bugs which are covered in other reviews I have personally not encountered any so far. The only bug that I've seen was in multiplayer when my friend randomly got stuck and couldn't move.And stealth, normally I don't play stealth in games. I prefer to just go in shooting, hoping i'm hitting and trying to march through to victory. But in this game stealth feels enjoyable, you're still paranoid, but it's not like if you bump one pebble that a nuclear reactor goes off and it's just "well you should've watched where your boot was at that moment", it feels great.

_childDocuments_.review: I have to say, this is by far the WORST game I’ve ever played.In my opinion, it’s seriously bad.I was bored within 30 minutes because it’s just the same repetitive gameplay. The heists are identical, and the turf wars are nothing more than being dropped into the middle of a battle where you kill a set number of gang members to "win." There’s no real depth—just a bunch of NPCs shooting at each other.There’s barely any story, and if there is, it’s buried under poorly voice-acted cutscenes and must be further in the game, because the cut scenes so far are nothing like what they are showing in their videos to sell the game (like - they are little small little tiny things). The small in-game announcements before and after missions is just more annoying than helpful, and they feel completely disconnected from the player.Overall, this feels like a even worse Payday 2 knockoff but with some famous voices from actors slapped on it (and even then - they sound AI in places). The game plays like a series of repetitive mini-quests, which is nothing like the exciting game-play shown in their trailers.And if there is more of a story later in the game, it’s poorly presented and I couldn't be bothered to continue. Right now, it’s just about choosing between two boring activities: turf wars or heists. Both are repetitive, dull, and lack any real engagement.Requested Refund.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: This Review is now my thoughts post beating the standard campaignAs a player of all 3 payday games and generally enjoy the heist game ascetic I have some words both good and bad but thankfully the good outweighs the bad. Little background info about me: I personally am a stealth solo player in the payday franchise and while I enjoy the crazy builds in Payday I don't min max for stats or hardest difficulty. (Unless it's a stealth heist and then I'll go hardest difficulty). I will break this review down into Sections and will modify the review as I gain more hours. Singleplayer: The single player is a turn based map where you have to take / defend territory from the other gangs along with doing missions and heists to gain capital to fund taking over the city. While this is all going on you have a sheriff who is trying to stop you and acts as a game timer preventing the game from going dozens of turns. What I enjoyed about the singleplayer is as follows: - It has plenty of repeatability even if the number of heists / maps need to be sorely increased over time. - The aspects of a roguelike I feel have been done with good but not great success and it feels like they very much want you to fail and try again. - The idea of a perma-death team is very interesting I just wish instead of completely dying the character just went to prison and had to be broken out. - The overall basic difficulty took me around 13 hours to complete and the other difficulties will likely expand this to far longer. What I didn't enjoy about the singleplayer: - The voice acting even with Hollywood actors feels very bad and while some are noticeable exceptions the overall writing and acting feels very hollow. - Once you understand all the mechanics the game doesn't really throw any extra curveballs at you and so you basically march your way to victory and I would imagine as you level up your boss this will be made easier and easier. - I wish the single player had Coop I feel it would be made a lot more enjoyable if you could bounce missions and objective ideas off another player rather then having to do it alone. - I wish their was a way to tell before entering a mission if it will be stealth or loud because many times I've lost  a run because I brought a weak stealth character into a loud mission and then they die and I lose all my stealth progress. - I also would have liked to see weapon attachments on your teams weapons as opposed to having to buy a modified gun with the attachments. - While fun the Defense missions are generally super easy if you have even a basic level of PC aim and the enemy AI will basically group up and get mowed down by your LMG fire. - Lastly I wish there was a visible list of things that would increase the heat level because some missions increase it and others don't and that's very up in the air about which does and doesn't. Multiplayer- (I haven't done this yet but I plan to and will edit my review when I have more time) Stealth: What I enjoyed: - The missions are of decent quality and they remind me of payday heists with a little less complexity. - It's a 3 strikes system as opposed to pagers so you can zip tie down entire maps and get full range of looting. - I like the idea of carrying 2 bags of loot but that lowers your speed and forces you to only use a secondary weapon. - There are random events that occur in some missions that I think really spice up the heists. (I just wish there was more of them and in higher frequency) - I like that there are a selection of gadgets you can employ in stealth but I think they need to be reworked a little as the basic Brick can basically lure guards to the edge of the map as it is now. - I love the added features they gave to the NPC's such as switching which character you play or being able to assign tasks to NPC's to say pick up loot or subdue a guard. - The Guard AI is pretty dumb which makes for easier stealth but they make up for this by putting TONS of guards on bigger maps. What I didn't enjoy in Stealth: - Cameras need to have that cone of vision that other games employ because you'll step into a cameras view and then have to run super far away for it to stop seeing you. Not to mention the cameras take far too long to revert to a searching state. - The Level variety is pretty bare and you will commonly see other heist locations in the background of whatever mission your doing. - Some of the Gadgets have an AOE effect that is far too large and actually ruins the point of using them cause it'll attract guards that are far away from where you used it. - I wish there was more open loot scattered around the map. - I wish the silenced pistol had more of a point since killing guards or cameras raises the strike meter and generally it's just easier to use a brick or ziptie to solve the problem. Loud: The gun play is OK but I can tell there's some jank involved kinda like Payday 2 before it got patched into what it is now. Enemies are pretty dumb and your friendly AI will get themselves killed either by playing dumb or by being bugged. it is for this reason that on missions you plan to go loud with I'd bring 2 or 3 guys instead of all 4 due to the fact that you may lose one or two if ♥♥♥♥ hits the fan. Also I should mention in single player if your main BOSS dies the run ends so that's a thing to consider.. I find the level of difficulty in gunfights ranges from super easy against other gangs and then pretty difficult against cops since your health regens but the cops don't hold back.  TLDR: This is a solid game that if you give it a chance could be a game to keep you heisting at least until 2-3 years when Payday 3 finally becomes what people wanted from it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game spent a year in EGS and should have spent the time fixing flaws in the game that detract it, or otherwise does not value you time. All i can say is that the content is worth the price and it does provide a unique experience on the single player side albeit flawed due to bad AI goons that more often then not will ruin your entire run. They may burn your rogue-lite run anywhere from 0 to 10 hours wasted; note there are unlocks tied to this campaign completion.There is an overarching multiplayer progress where most unlocks are tied to RNG choices upon level. This is a terrible progression system all character skills and the authority to get the option to buy guns is through this system. I did not get a single skill card until level 40 and that already 30 hours into the game. I did not get a silenced weapon until 20 hours in the game. Much with these kinds of systems devs are trying to pad content and maintain player retention but at the same time not valuing player time. Your bots ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ suck. I'm sorry i could equip these things with LMGs and it would not matter bots will just randomly decide  to stray off from you or away from cover and then die. IF you have a mission with a lot of bags they will constantly try to pick up the bags you placed in a strategic position. And when they do carry 2 bags at once this blocks off the use of the primary weapon which overall locks off firepower because they constantly pick up bags. Note that bots still have a limited number of downs so once they are gone they just die permanently on that run. I also do not appreciate the game locking away my goons when the game suddenly decides you need to play some kind of back story mission . Multiplayer, decent vary of missions and heists. The issues? Same nonsense as early pd2 days and pd3. You have issues finding games with people that want to play loud or you join a randomly lobby and they don't say anything and then they kick you for making it loud.  vice versa. Weird sync bugs like looping loot grabbing animations and view model locking caused by interrupting people's lock picking by opening the door from the other side; You know seemingly small bugs that you think would have been fixed after year? 3 difficulties; normal, medium and hard. Enemies don't seem to buff through difficulties from what i read and played. Player attributes get nerfed; like lower health and longer times between hp regen. Pick the difficulty you like and if you have some mates i think the game is decent fun. This is Payday at home.Voice acting is bad from 90% of the characters except for Nasara. His scripting seems a step up from the rest and he is voice by the voice actor of Chains from payday. The meme of so bad it's good only gets you so far.  Aside from Nasara and Maybe Gloves the rest of the caste seems to be just reading the scripting with no proper context given.

So far I am 51 hours into the game, on extreme difficulty.Some times AI characters of your team get stuck in places and if you are to switch to them, then you can not switch back to your other character. _childDocuments_.review: This game is just terrible. I've tried my best to give it as good of a shot as I can, but it's just not worth your money.- Numerous game-breaking bugs are often an unavoidable consequence of core gameplay.- Abysmal movement. Everything shy of running forward halts or restrains your character's momentum in this game. Mantling is automatic along ledges, which also kills your momentum. Sliding is restrictive, bland, and clunky.- The netcode hurts my soul. Unless the host is your neighbor, you're going to feel the pain of teleporting everywhere and generally not certainly knowing where you're actually located relative to your surroundings.- The game performs terribly even on the lowest settings, and doesn't have the visuals to justify it. Framedrops are frequent, and you shouldn't expect to get more than 80FPS without a high-end rig.- Bots are stubborn, and prioritize grabbing/holding loot bags over their safety or your own. Bots would rather grab a bag than revive others, and will end up only using their secondary weapon because they can't hold a primary with two bags.- Automatic peeking during aiming and moving hurts the game. Your character will peek when you don't want to at all.- The health system isn't fun, and combined with the crouching peeking mechanics, makes it often impossible to find time to breathe or fight back when at a disadvantage.- The roguelite campaign is lengthy and repetitive. It's either too hard or too easy, and always for the wrong reasons.- Heist variety is lacking, even with all DLCs. With all DLCs, there are only 10 large-scale heists in the game. PAYDAY 3 launched with 8, and added 3 more free heists along with 4 DLC heists for a total of 15 large-scale heists. Most other heist variety comes from miscellaneous smaller-scale jobs that simply aren't comparably memorable or fun. The most they do is pad for time when the core content is severely lacking.And last but not least, revenue from this game goes to Bo Andersson. Don't buy this game, please.
_childDocuments_.name: Crime Boss: Rockay City

_childDocuments_.review: Because the devs have shown actual dedication to fixing this game over the past year it's been out, Crime Boss honestly feels like the Payday 3 we were waiting for. Bots are smarter (for the most part), heists are way more interesting and there is a much wider variety to choose from.The campaign is really cool after you get the hang of it. It's a rogue-like crime simulator where you do jobs every day trying to take over the city from the rival gangs while also balancing your money and your "heat". As you do more jobs in one day your heat rises, thus making heists more difficult if you attempt them that day. Some heists are only available the day you see them on the map so it makes it very interesting trying to determine if the heat is worth the potential reward you get for doing the heist.Your crew members are expendable as well, meaning if they die on a heist they are GONE for the rest of the run. If you aren't careful you will very quickly find yourself soloing heists that are near impossible to complete and if the main character dies (Travis Baker) the run is OVER and you have to start over. There is so much replay value it's actually insane.Is it perfect? Hell no. But its genuinely a fun time and has some very interesting mechanics.Voice acting ranges from passable to godawful - looking at you, Chuck Norris. BUT I think it teeters on the "so bad it's good" in a way where it's kind of exciting to see which performance you are going to listen too next. Damion Poitier (VA for Chains in Payday) is the highlight, as expected.While there are still some glitches I've found, I wouldn't say there is anything game-breaking. I've only played for about 6 hours by now so your mileage may vary.Give it a try. Especially while it's on sale and you get all DLC for free, but honestly Crime Boss is worth the full price either way. I will update this review when I've put more time into it and if my opinion on anything has changed.

_childDocuments_.review: Payday meets Roguelite, but worse.They took everything that was fun from Payday, tried to remove all the dumb stuff and ended up being worse off.I will only sum up the deal breakers for me and refrain myself from describing the entire game:There are no pagers to answer during stealth, since this was a major gripe in PD2. Now you get a magical strike, whenever you kill a guard or civ. Stealth is as simple and barebone as in PD2, but there are virtually NO other stealth options or mechanics, besides the mighty brick. Which is the best item in the game, but also the only stealth item, which is also in a separat item slot that you have to bring with you. You can lure guards away to tie them down or outright kill them with it. No brick, no stealth. There is nothing else you can do to manipulate the AI. There are sometimes safes and vans to drill open. And again, they made the PD2 Drill session more fun, because you can increase the drill speed by 3 by interacting with it. But that's it. No skills, no mods, no nothing. Besides, drilling a safe will literally lure in EVERY.SINGLE.GUARD on the map to said location and then .... what? You go loud I guess. Or you kill/ cable-tie every mofo on the planet beforehand. At least cable ties are infinite and the NPCs don't spot "illegal lock picking" from a mile away or call the army, because you tossed a sports bag onto the streets. Except, when they do spot you hiding behind a barrel, that somehow doesn't hide your character. Sometimes guards spot you from behind, even though they aren't even turning their heads (You know, like in Payday 3) I though sprinting was the issue, but I could literally run everywhere without getting botherd, so who knows. Plus, you have these big open maps you can run around as you were playing an immersive sim, but there is NOTHING there. I never found additional safes, secrets or loot. Only more civs, that might as well be absent for the lack of impact or relevance they have for your current heist.Silenced pistols are as rare as a pink elefant and I never got any throwing knives or something similar. In addition, whenever you use a character for a mission, they have to recover making them unavailable for the rest of the day. But they also keep ALL their gear for themselves. Which means, you can't get the godlike brick back for any other character. And you can't buy a new one. I re-reolled the shop like 10 times and it never showed up. Why is this a thing? The roguelike-type shop doesn't add anything, anyway. There are no special effects or stats. They are always the same. Guns are basically unique gear (alla PD2) with different colored "rarity" that only costs you more to buy them. But no modding or buffing whatsoever. Mission descriptions are lackluster and offer no real important information of the mission ahead, even though you pay top dollars to "plan" them. You don't know if the mission is loud or stealth (no, I never once saw these icons everybody talks about in the forums), you don't get to know the general layout, no preplanning, no mission modifier, no assets. Nothing! If you guess wrong, than you run around with the wrong equipment, or the wrong character. For example: You would guess that a cash transporter heist is a loud heist? Which is true in this game, expect when it isn't. THEN you run around with hand grenades, pump guns and your slow as heck "brute" characters and you can't properly stealth the mission. Remember the mighty brick? Yeah, you can bring a brick OR a hand grenade, IF you ever get another one during your playthrough. The same is true the other around and much worse: Wanna stealth, nope it's a loud mission. Expecially, when you already have 4 wanted stars and the only brick was on a character who died last mission, because she took 7min to cross the road. So they buried them with it.And there is no restarting the heist, either. Which is odd, since it's a roguelike and reseting and randomizing the map is part of the genre. You have to quit the game and load back in to try the mission again. Oh, the game also permanently looks you in the current heist. So, if you have the above mentioned issues... I am really dissapointed by this game. I takes the great ideas from the Payday Series and put them in an 80s grind house charmed roguelike. I REALLY like everything about the game, besides it's polish, balancing issues and nonsensical gameplay elements that adds nothing to it.I'll wait for a major update before playing again and play Payday 3 in the meantime (which is improving on a weekly basis)What are your thoughts?

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to be talking about campagin. Multiplayer is just multiplayer heists. Pretty straightforward.After having beaten the story on Extreme I could easily say it has been a while since I had this much fun playing a game. Although beaware it is mainly due to a certain combinations of things that I like many people won't. This is a super unique game for a super unique taste.Crudely to put it, Imagine a roleplaying rougelike board game where it requires you to partake in the battles and some plans you initiate on the board in person. Your capability in these missions will determine if your action will be a contribution or the opposite. To enjoy this game, you will need to enjoy decision making, strategy and LEARNING as you play (super important). Going through tons of trial and error to figure out how to consistently get good outcomes from missions to better yourself is a part of the fun, becoming more capable through your internal knowledge rather than in-game buffs and bonuses. (even though they do exist they mostly help out) Personally I like games that rely on my mechanical capability more than anything, which is another reason why I liked this game this much. I can't just "equip a meta OP build" for my campagin, I actually need to get good but the difference between another roguelike game and Crime boss is, in other rogue-like games, where you'd learn enemy attack patterns, in here, you'll be learning how to cleanly complete missions, consistently. You will enjoy a 'good run' and must be willing to let go if you goof and watch as the game wipes your hours of work the ♥♥♥♥ out, plus you should know that your runs can be quite long in this game.As expected in games like these you must be okay with some degree of repetition. The game however does a really good job to consistently pull out new elements to keep you engaged. Level variety is very good even though it is the "same level" it doesn't feel to be. The general principle of completion more or less remains the same but not on a 1:1 scale. Things change in a way where you just need to adapt. (interior design, sometimes layout, guard civ and camera positions...) Which for me were different enough to keep the engagement as I will try it as hard as I did the first time. At no point I felt as if I was autopiloting. I simply knew the "main premise" and how a mission will generally play out.Because your campagin hangs on a balance, it helps me remain as engaged as I could be while playing it. I found this game engaging and as you get to mid-late game you get some stuff pop out that's besides robbing places and attacking gang territories. This could be a unique character story or a lead on some big heist. Which are good attention grabbers to reset your attentionspan.Last words...The game does have bugs still, AI can be a VERY retarded on loud. If you get thrown a grenade by the enemy they could decide to charge into them instead of falling back degree retarded. You tell them to camp and they keep pushing out the vault or whatever space you normally want to camp in. They pretty much don't have any coding for survivability and for some reason they somewhat value charging into enemies more than sticking close to you. If AI was coded the otherway around I believe majority of the problems could be easier to manage. The way it is, I can't tell them to "follow" and then "stay" because they care about other stuff more than those two crucial commands which would allow me to ensure their survival personally and I could gloss over them standing in the open if I were to not do that. Though the problem is, I outright can't so easily. Game does have its flaws with bugs which are neither common nor rare.In the end. I genuinely had fun and I don't see myself having the same kind on another game. (this is due to my specific taste in specific games and crimeboss being a mixture of them all)Excuse me if my paragraphing is bad i was sleep deprived by the time I wrote this.

_childDocuments_.review: Why Crime Boss: Rockay City better than Payday 31.Stunning Graphics: Crime Boss: Rockay City delivers a visually stunning experience. The detailed environments and character models are a feast for the eyes, making every heist feel immersive and lifelike.2.Hollywood Star Power: This game features a stellar cast of Hollywood actors, bringing an unmatched level of charisma and authenticity to the characters. Their performances elevate the narrative, making you feel like you're in an action-packed blockbuster.3.Voice Acting and Humor: The voice acting is top-notch, filled with memorable lines and witty banter that keep you entertained throughout. The humor is spot on, adding a delightful layer to the intense heist scenarios.4.Unique Story Mode - Roguelike Elements**: The story mode introduces an exciting roguelike twist. Each day is a challenge, and failure means starting from scratch. This adds a thrilling level of difficulty and replayability, as you strategize to make every move count.5.Diverse Missions: Unlike the repetitive bank robberies in Payday 3, Crime Boss offers a variety of missions. From attacking rival gangs to strengthen your position, to more complex heists, the gameplay is always fresh and exciting.6.Team Management: You can hire and manage your own team of criminals, adding a strategic layer to the game. Each teammate brings unique skills to the table, allowing you to plan heists more effectively.7.Upgrade Your Base: Customize and upgrade your office and vaults. This feature adds a personal touch to the game, giving you a tangible sense of progression and accomplishment as your criminal empire grows.In summary, Crime Boss: Rockay City not only looks better but offers a richer and more varied gameplay experience than Payday 3. From its star-studded cast to its challenging roguelike story mode, this game is a must-play for fans of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Not the perfect heist game, but a great experience OverallWhile this game isn't flawless, it offers a fun experience. The developers clearly have a vision, and they've executed it well. It feels more like a worthy successor to Payday 2 rather than the soulless husk that Payday 3 is.The Positives:-Roguelike Campaign: Surprisingly enjoyable with some cool mechanics that add depth to the gameplay.-Stealth System: Instead of pagers you have 3 strikes. Killing guards, breaking cameras, or generally being careless with civilians will cost you a strike. but if you subdue guards and turn off the cameras in the security room it wont cost you a strike. Its easier than it is in payday as you can slowly controll the entire map instead of having to deal with random stuff in the bigger heists but I truly enjoy the stealth as it feels dynamic and fresh.-Functional Bots: The AI can loot, suppress, intimidate civilians and guards, and deliver bags for you unlike payday where they are decoration until the heist goes loud.-No circles to stand around, truly a visionary gaming experience.-Actual good armor system-Decent Gunplay: While not revolutionary, the gunplay is solid and does its job well.-Varied Heists: The game offers a decent selection of heists, keeping things fresh.-Map Randomization: A lot of randomization within the maps -Weight-Based Loot System: Every loot in this game is *loose lot* if you played payday, you dont just get a bag from a loot point. Instead each loot has its own weight and fills your bag. You can carry 2 bags at once but for the penalty of not being able to use your primary.-Fair Pricing: No microtransactions and a reasonable price point.-Dedicated devteam who actually wants to provide a cool experience unlike others who seemingly operate on a "your opinion, my choice" kind of way. *cough* mio *cough*The Negatives:-Voice Acting & Celebrity Focus: The voice acting can get annoying quickly, and the celebrity appearances, especially Chuck Norris, feel unconvincing.-Unnoticeable Perks: The perks don’t stand out and there is little customization-Random Progression: For each level up you get 3 random choices which can include a crewmember, a weapon, a weapon skin, a boss skin. Its not bad per se but i have yet to unlock a single silenced weapon after 3 campaigns.-No customization: Theres no customization for heisters and guns. Guns come with attachments from the shop and heisters are each their own characters.-Robot Faction: The inclusion of a robot faction feels out of place, even in this crazy setting.-Turf Wars in Campaign: Turf wars can be fun, but they get repetitive. An autocomplete option would have been appreciated.-AI Issues in Loud Play: The AI can be frustrating, often dropping bags to switch to their primary weapon, leaving them behind as cops swarm in. Additionally, the AI tends to path straight into danger and die if youre not babysitting them constantly.Summary:This game gets more right than wrong and provides a lot of fun for the price. For just 20€, it offers more content than Payday 3 likely will in three years, and without the need for additional purchases. If you’re into co-op or heist games, or if you’ve already sunk 1,000 hours into Payday 2, this game is a much better value. Payday 3 won’t come close in terms of fun for the foreseeable future, if it doesn’t get canned at one point.

_childDocuments_.review: After logging around 12 hours and completing most of the Urban Legends campaign, along with trying out several other modes, here are my thoughts:Pros:  The game introduces a fresh twist to the heist genre, a welcome change since the days of "Payday 2." The dynamic maps, engaging storyline, intriguing voice acting, and high-octane gunfights bring a unique flavor to the gameplay.Cons:Unfortunately, the magic is frequently broken by numerous bugs. Let's start with the AI:The player-controlled bots are erratic at best. Sometimes, they behave like brain-dead guinea pigs; other times, they resemble trigger-happy chimpanzees, barely following instructions. When playing with friends online, they have the intelligence of a two-year-old, but in solo play there responsiveness brings them up to "Monkey with a Gun" complex which is "decent" but not great . The enemy AI is equally inconsistent, with difficulty levels not matching their labels—normal can feel like hard, hard can feel like normal, and extreme is a toss-up.Game Crashes: The frequent game crashes are incredibly frustrating. Halfway through a three-mission Urban Legends campaign, the game might freeze, leaving you stranded if you're playing online or completely freezing up if you're solo. This issue is severe enough to deter me from wanting to play again.Conclusion: While the game delivers a high-energy, explosive bank heist experience, the numerous bugs significantly hamper the enjoyment to the point of near unplayability. I am willing to push through the grind to unlock more gameplay and story elements, but this should be a choice driven by my love for the game, not marred by technical issues. Developers, please address these problems. I genuinely like this game and want to see it reach its full potential, but there's a lot that needs fixing.

_childDocuments_.review: This game may be not perfect, may be not for everyone, but its still good.Bought it after the Steam release while having experience from Payday 2 (~400 hrs, 53% achievements) and can tell that this game has its own charm.This game has a singleplayer Campaign and various Multiplayer Modes.For the start, lets talk about Campaign. There are 2 types of Campaigns - Roguelite and Story Lines.Roguelite - is a main campaign mode that allows player to take part in a Turf War for the Rokay City. This mode consists of 4 main parts:Story Lines are a singleplayer story-driven sets of missions featuring almost all key characters from the Roguelite mode, but instead of random events and fighting for turn you take part in the particular events made in the style of the film.Multiplayer has its own progression and connected with the caimpaign mode only by unlockables and leveling.MP has 3 main modes - Missions, Shuffle and Urban Legends.Crime Boss: Rockay City is a heisting game, but its not like a Payday 2. It has a lot of stuff you can find in 80s-90s crime films and has its own charm with its dialogues and actors. It may be not for everyone, may not have crazy weapon and perk customizations like Payday 2 has, but its a good game with own gems and surprises. I havent even told about other gameplay features those present in the game.Crime Boss does have some problems, most of them are caused by the AI of your own bots - sometimes they can just stay AFK after switching, or they can just stay in the middle of the open area and get absolutely destroyed, but those are not critical if you know how to play.

_childDocuments_.review: For the most part, I don't think it's possible to even look at the cover of this game and not know at least partially what you're getting into. Pretty much its entire cast is made up of actors (and Vanilla Ice, for some reason) you probably thought were either dead or retired, and frankly none of them sound like they were even trying. If you're the sort of person who will scoff at the cutscenes and go "Wow, I hope someone got fired for that blunder!", this is not the game for you. For everyone else, the voice acting can only be considered a net positive. You get Michael Madsen sounding like he's reading every line in the script for the first time, Danny Glover mumbling as if the studio called him in the middle of the night to record lines, Chuck Norris giving such a monotone delivery that you'd swear it was just AI if it weren't for the fact that AI would probably sound more like Chuck Norris, and more -- without even having to hook up your VHS player! It's beautiful and hilarious, and this was the entire reason I originally bought the game.What surprised me, though, is that beyond the inherent comedy of its premise, this is actually a pretty fun game after a year of consistent updates and overhauls. There's a full singleplayer campaign that's presented like a roguelite, with lots of unique story missions and a turf war element against various other gangs, and while I didn't really understand why it needed to be a roguelite at first it started to click over time in a way that makes it pretty interesting to play. You can hire a variety of crew members with unique voice lines that vary in hilarity, buy loads of different guns and equipment items, and unlock things that carry over into the multiplayer mode along the way. It is a little bit on the easy side, so if you're coming into this as a Payday veteran I'd recommend cranking it up to Hard from the start, and while the teammate AI is generally a step above Payday's bots (and you can order them around pretty consistently) they do have a few annoying quirks like routinely loading up with two bags just to drop one in what may or may not be a convenient spot when they swap to their primary weapon. But problems like that one have been few and far between in my experience, and if you think they might be a hindrance for a particular mission you do have the option of going in with a smaller crew or completely solo.In terms of the multiplayer, there's a surprising amount of content at its current sale price (which ends sometime in July 11th, to my knowledge), thanks to the addition of all the current DLC for free. You get at least 8 or 9 small jobs, 4 regular jobs, 10 proper heists, and 9 urban legends campaigns, which are like short mini-campaigns made up of a few different jobs. You can mix players and hired bots or just go in as a group of two or three if you want, and instead of being stuck with bots with default equipment you're able to choose who you hire from the same broad pool as the campaign, with a variety of weapons, skills, and personalities. And yes, you can unlock and play as the celebrity cast -- with the exception of Chuck Norris, as far as I can tell. I went into this game thinking that it would be funny if it were just total garbage, and hilarious if it were actually really good. But I think that it being not good enough to stand up to a juggernaut like Payday 2, but still pretty comfortably better than Payday 3 might be the funniest possible outcome that could have come from this. For $16 you get more content, smarter AI, all the QOL you didn't know you even needed, and a bunch of your dad's favorite actors treating you to the worst vocal performance you've ever heard in a video game, and to me, that's what it's all about. New adventures await, buddy!

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a  game, but I'm not entirely sure it's a good game either. Like many others leaving reviews like this, I only wish there was a way to leave a 'Mixed' recommendation instead of outright Yes or No. This game, as I've heard, is reportedly better than PAYDAY 3. I wouldn't exactly know because that game was borderline unplayable for me, with a somewhat spotty internet connection. That's a leg up for Rockay City - I can actually  it. The teammate AI is no doubt leagues more helpful than something like the OG PAYDAY 2, able to secure loot and down enemies in stealth and whatnot, but that's about as far as they go. AI likes to get directly into the line of fire a lot, and is generally only marginally helpful in a firefight. Stealth feels weirdly half baked, good in some ways (believe it or not I don't like the pager system in PAYDAY 2, but I know why it exists) and not so great in others (three strikes feel weird at times). The jobs themselves are hit or miss, either ludicrously easy if you have half a brain or just sort of braindead. Taking territory is an interesting thing, but it really just ends up being a money sink (why do all of my men disappear after a job. why does it cost tens of thousands of dollars to take a dozen men into a neighborhood?) with not too much reward, besides finishing the 'roguelike' campaign.I've only taken part in one 'big' heist, and so far I am not too fond of them. I went through four setup missions, dumped about a hundred thousand dollars into prep, only to get three strikes and FAIL the heist. No going loud, full stealth or you lose out on the job completely. Does it come back later? No idea. Is that a dumb way to handle a heist?  It feels counter-intuitive, but maybe I just didn't listen to a hint or some dialogue saying that I could outright fail. All in all, I'd give Rockay like...a six? Maybe? It's not horrible by any means, but it doesn't really function as a PAYDAY game as much as a PAYDAY inspired game. It doesn't feel like there's much focus on normal heists in the roguelike mode, and really my first experiences with the game aren't super positive. But it was cheap, and they generously bundle all the DLC into the single price, so that's nice.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a Payday 3 which isn't...scuffed? This is just that perfect balance for your game library! It's great both singleplayer and multiplayer.This game has been absolutely brilliant to play so far. I love the roguelike take on the campaign which absolutely makes your early planning crucial to decide how it will play out for your entire run, I love the dynamics and random events. Stealth is superb and really gets me annoyed when I mess up solely by my own stupidity. :')One of my most favourite random events during a heist has been  Really had my blood pumping when I went solo with Travis.My only issue in regards to singleplayer is that the game should have a better system to prevent you from just cheesing it if you have something go wrong. (Imo I will admit I have done a few times due to some bull crud reasons like orange/green wires being next to eachother and getting the two confused waaay too easily) Possibly punish the players for doing this by taking a hefty chunk off the income?There are a few silly bugs here and there but it's no where near frequent enough to be noticed, I did softlock myself getting stuck on some AC pipes which was semi-out of bounds but that's entirely my own fault lmao. Hopefully the devs are aware and are working on a fix as I typed this! 🤞I believe this is just UE5 and Nvidia being weird, but if you have a transparent taskbar, turn it off!! It breaks this game strangely and instead focuses on your taskbar rather than the game; this resolved a lot of stutters for me which was nice. It also solved my shadowplay recordings from just recording my entire desktop.The multiplayer framework could be improved a little, it'd be nice to know if our lobby is using Steam's API or the EGS' API. _childDocuments_.review: I don't know what the legs on this is, but I would say its certainly an experience.  It's almost surreal seeing so many recognizable actors in the game and clearly were all reading their scripts on different days.  Like, the dialogue is borderline nonsense most of the time, but it's charmingly stupid to hear it coming from janky digital likenesses.  In the vein of bad B-action movie fare it has that going for it.  In the gameplay department you get a series of maps and various "heists" which are the manner by which you obtain money.  These maps are used well enough as a jewelry store during the day or night has different people around and, to some degree, affects how you approach the mission.  It's lightly randomized, and missions quickly begin to repeat but there is a bit more to it than the surface suggests.Where the game gets its momentum is from the roguelike aspect.  It doesn't really make sense, but it is a good enough motivator as its interesting how quickly a job can go sour.  If you forgot your heat was maxed and you slip up during a job, even a simple heist may quickly devolve into a nightmare scenario of tank cops.  This also makes Baker an interesting player character since his ability is extra loot, which you want, but if he dies its game over.  Hence you are appropriately incentivized to bolster your roster as well as decide who you should send or what order you should tackle missions.  Maybe keep Baker home even if that gas station robbery seems like an easy mark but you maxed your heat, or hell, maybe do that mission before you run an all out turf war.I played Payday a *looooooooong* time ago so my comparison point is fairly limited and I can say I get those vibes, but the purpose of effort here feels better.  Like, it has a nice flow between missions you spend time on and missions that are fairly snacky.  Again, I don't know if this offers up hundreds of hours of fun (a metric that's kind of goofy to begin with) but it did encourage me to keep playing.  Ultimately it's a pretty fast-paced first person shooter with some randomized elements to keep things fresh and on pace, with the draw of watching recognizable actors say slightly nonsensical lines as you try to take over the city.  Serviceable is the word of the day here as it's all functional in my experience.  As far as solo play goes I didn't run into any game breaking bugs though the lack of good team commands is a shocking omission.  You can work around it, but if you asked me to complain that's where I'd point.I can definitely say twenty bucks is a reasonable price.

_childDocuments_.review: (Game received for free ON STEAM - I have purchased and played it before on epic games' launcher)This game is sleeper hit. This game started as basically a meme, even before it came out originally on EGS it was that one weird game announced at a Game Awards show that looked like a weird GTA parody, where Michael Madsen showed up, said some words and left. But the devs took it to themselves to make this an actual fun experience, even if I'll admit I only really started playing the game myself on the previous update (Update 8 on Epic), at that point it was a much different and more interesting experience than it was at launch.You'll probably see it just about everywhere when people talk about Crime Boss that the voice acting is phoned in, badly done and even cringe, and yeah it kinda is when you really look into it, but when the game is so fun to play, it sort of wraps around into being really funny. All these big names ended up turning themselves into even bigger memes and the devs totally embrace it, celebrating things like MarioInATopHat's hilarious videos and making their own jokes like tiny Travis Baker with a high pitched voice walking around some guards (look it up on the dev's twitter, I'm not joking).They get to do that and have the community laugh *with* them because the game is genuinely good and fun to play, IGS took the opportunity to turn the potential this game had into real value and they've been absolutely nailing it! Sure, it's not a full on "No Man's Sky" situation but it's close! Of course, the game isn't perfect (yet), it has its issues like any other, but what's there so far is great.Guns feel nice to shoot; looting isn't just grab a bundle of some random thing and throw it around; you can actually try to mess around with different loot weights in one bag and optimise how many you take; there's build variety not only with your own "boss" character (in multiplayer), but also in the many crew members you can get through leveling up and purchasing them afterwards (the unlock method is reliant on RNG though which can be unfortunate when you want something specifically); the heists themselves can go from your usual robbing a bank, to going into a heavily guarded facility to steal a ton of gold bars, or even to  storming through a high-tech robot factory to blow it up and kill the owner.All in all, if you want a campy heisting game that takes itself seriously but not really, play this game, you won't regret it. New adventures await, buddy

_childDocuments_.review: Short answer: no. Long answer: also no. While Crime Boss shares many ideas and gameplay mechanics with Payday, it stands on its own merits. It features multiplayer with a surprising variety of game modes, and a roguelite campaign with challenge, strategy, and humorous writing (albeit cheesy).Loud gameplay feels distinctly different from Payday, focusing more on realism and Is less arcadey by nature (though I personally prefer PD2's loud style). On the other hand, the stealth mechanics are a clear improvement from PD2 (I've only played PD3 in beta and played PD The Heist very little, so I can't compare extensively with those two), allowing you to move zip-tied hostages and employing a 3-strike system that surpasses the pager system.The campaign alone justifies the game's $20 price tag (which, I might add, is a steal—pun intended hurhur). Crime Boss offers a more grounded experience than Payday 2; rather than fantastical heists like robbing the White House, it (The campaign) focuses on gang turf disputes, wars, and controlling territory.It also includes random events including but not limited to Most missions are diverse and incorporate enjoyable elements that are enhanced by these random events. Importantly, there's minimal insistence on stealth or loud-only missions, aside from certain campaign and multiplayer missions. This is refreshing change to PD2, where repeated failures due to random team members or bad setups often necessitate restarting  specific stealth missions.There are occasional issues with stealth sightlines and detection mechanics, but they're generally manageable and not as severe as they might initially seem.Unlocking weapons and equipment can be a bit tedious initially, but once you establish yourself, it becomes less of an issue. Compared to Payday, Crime Boss offers less weapon customization—weapons come pre-built with attachments based on rarity. This limits build variety slightly, though Payday 2's endgame build diversity often hinged on specific skills. Crime Boss doesn't achieve perfection in build variety, but it's far from bad.The music in Crime Boss varies between really good and forgettable, though it's unfair to directly compare it to PD2's iconic soundtrack.While Crime Boss doesn't yet match PD2's sheer variety of heists, it's a relatively new game with tremendous potential. In summary, Crime Boss: Rockay City is fun, affordable, and offers a unique take on the heist video game genre—a worthy investment of your time and money. As of this writing, all DLC is also included for free.

The core gameplay loop has a lot of good ideas to it, both in multiplayer, and in the highly addictive roguelite mode:At the same time, however, there's a lot that bogs the experience down:I'd place it as a solid 6-7/10. Far from a perfect game, but one that I will still be playing for more dozens of hours, at least for its fun singleplayer campaign. _childDocuments_.review: A game I didn't expect to like but now I'm pretty sure I... love?Its odd. The big, hetero chest pounding machismo of hiring largely middle-aged "badass" actors from the 1980s and 1990s was why when I first saw the trailer for this game I wrote it off but after the abject failure of Payday 3 I decided that, hey, its got the right price point so even if it blows chunks it'll be worth it, right?And it is. Even if I don't like the roguelite singleplayer mode and with it was elsewise, the actors who are clearly not good voice actors (hi chuck norris, your line reading is so bad it makes me laugh) stand out in a cheesy 1980s mid-tier action movie kind of way rather than an issue of development. Likewise with the game: any scuff marks on this diamond are flatly because its a mid-tier game, not a AAA powerhouse release. The further we get from the 2010's the happier I am that mid-tier games are returning and the anachronistic, odd Crime Boss: Rockay City is the epitome of why we need them. The gameplay loop is fun and satisfying, feeling like an evolution of the heist game genre while not having eyes bigger than its stomach in terms of what they could accomplish with their budget, the gunplay is snappy and fantastic and the fact that it can be entirely singleplayer is phenomenal and really helpful for me and a game of this price point. Nobody can say what multiplayer games will live and breath forever, but ensuring that there's a healthy and robust singleplayer that more or less has the same features (and then some, tbh) was inspired on INGAME STUDIOS' part and I applaud them.The part of the game that really rocked me most noticeably was that it allows you to tell the bots what to do and even control them directly depending on what part of the heist your on. You're not pigeon holed into playing as Michael Madsen's titular crime boss, and thats good because a lot of situations will ask for different gadgets, guns, or perks. My first run was dominated by a southern belle in heels named Alleycat who straight-up was as fast as a motorcycle thanks to her perks and it was capital-F fun to just be allowed to exist and experiment in this gameplay loop.I'm also not a roguelite/rogue-like fan in general but the fact that almost immediately after the first run it feels more manageable is a nice change of pace. A lot of roguelites feel like you're just supposed to die, die, die and die until you have a good set-up but on my second run alone I was able to get more of the stories and characters than before and that was really nice! I didn't feel locked into a "forever game" where I'd have to sit and suffer for nine million runs to experience a fraction of the game bits and pieces at a time.My largest complaint is that in the single player mode you really can't experiment without consequences, and sometimes some heists are a little less intuitive to me than others. More than once I've ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up because I misread something or other, particularly in taking down the defenses of the more in-depth heists - this isn't just a problem with Crime Boss: Rockay City, though, I can firmly say that this is just a problem with a lot of heists. The man-on-the-radio exists to ameliorate this from becoming too present of an issue and for the most part this game doesn't do it too often but the few gaffes I've made have felt cheap or otherwise out of my control than a screw-up of my own making.There is also a specific job type where it glitches out and a gas tank starts to explode shortly after spawning in for no reason, immediately forcing the job to go loud. Pretty sure its not intended, and its on a smaller game map so its not TOO bad but when I bring a solo character to a map like that I'm expecting being able to actually utilize my awesome stealth abilities. Disappointing but not spirit breaking, I've not experienced many other downsides beyond a typo in one of the cutscenes, some UI faffery such as me trying to buy a crew member and then inexplicably buying the member next to them (might be an issue with mouse controls? Not sure.) This is probably one of my longer Steam reviews just because its bewitched me in the same way that other charming budget-friendly titles like Road 96 have. The clearly non-American spin on Americanism pipe fed by pop culture is truly a delightfully fun setting, and Crime Boss: Rockay City avoids the misogynistic and homophobic tendencies of similarly set settings like Grand Theft Auto. Its just genuinely a fun setting that is enjoying itself, not ripping down others.Overall this feels like a solid, AA, mid-tier heist shooter with a laughably juvenile 1980's story that sweats popcorn, spits bullets, and has Michael Madsen laconically slurring one-liners while better voice actors like Danny Trejo, Danny Glover, and Michael Rooker chew the scenery whenever they're allowed to.

_childDocuments_.review: My name is not Crime boss: Rockay City!Gotta say that the game has surprised me. From a barely coherent meme game that spilled onto epic, to a relatively fun heist game with pretty good replayability.The previous footage back when it first launched just gave me the idea that the game was a paycheck for old/inactive actors from the 80s. Although the voice acting is a bit stiff, it's not too bad considering it is all background noise for the gameplay that makes up for it.The good:-The gunplay is very satisfying and the guns feel just right for the most part.-The missions and heists are pretty replayable with things changing sort of like PD2's heists (objectives changing spawns, set-pieces varying and enemy type spawns changing).-Loot feels good. Filling bags with a meter instead of single items is something that I personally like.-AI can be very useful at times and work as individuals to a degree.-Enemies mimic that of the PD series with police/guards being squishy, swat being a fair challenge along with shields and specialists being a fair threat that can open up your defences and finally the Juggernauts and bots being real thorns in your side if you fail to go for their weak spots.-Leveling up to get rewards is something that I personally like. Getting a better tiered weapon, equipment, skins or a useful skill by chance always entertains me. Although it would be cool to get a random resource reward to pick from like money or XP too.-I like the stealth systems in place and the fact that the security cams are animated to move and change their viewing angle. Another animation I like, while on the subject, is the drill being animated to move forward towards the doors as it progresses.-The unique characters with special perks are a fun idea, especially of you wanna change up your loadout from your boss character.The meh:-Some of the level design is a real pain. For instance, in the dragon dogs heist, I can stealth all of the way into the vaults only to alert EVERY guard in the map and they then ALL single file path directly to the drill. It feels a little synthetic when that happens.-Some of the difficulty spike in the single player is a little disheartening, then again it IS a roguelite.-Quickmatch has it's moments where there isn't any way to connect to any other lobbies and just fails. I mainly play with a friend or by myself in a private lobby so not too much of an issue for me.The bad:-The AI can tank a whole heist thanks to their obsession with grabbing bags, dropping them and running off to get shot while trying to grab a random bag or dropping them and forcing you to backtrack all the way to try and secure it. In single player, you can somewhat control them by restraining their movement but in multiplayer, they just run rampant and screw up your plans of looting or storing bags until ready.As it stands, the game is very reasonably priced for the base content. Even more so as it is 20% off with all current DLC included until the 11th of July. There are also more expansions planned later on and the devs have shown that the game has promise for the future and that they are still working on it.-Edit 28/7/24-AI is now controllable, at least in invite only games, and they somewhat seem a bit more proficient? (That last part might be just my perception)-Edit 19/8/24-The latest update added some welcome additions but also new issues that I've experienced. The AI is generally worse now, making them unresponsive to commands in favour of finding where I leave loose bags and going to pick them up. This happens even when we are nowhere near them like on the upper floor of dragon dogs waiting for the chopper with the bags at the explosive wall to the sewers. They just rush over to them through gunfire and heavy enemies.The difficulty has also been tweaked to make things even more chaotic on extreme. This included random robots showing up and 3-4 juggernauts half way through, instantly killing the 2 bots and me and my friend. One thing that happened to my friend was that his cluster grenade was not throwable. This forced us to cower from the police around corners instead of being able to use equipment to create a stop gap and gain control of the fight again.Due to this and how frustrating it was, I have to change my review to a negative. The fun has been turned into anguish.Note: Just tried to do an armoured truck ambush solo and it was horrible. On extreme with bots, I notices that the bots refuse to fight back and just go down. The constant stream of police with no reprieve is unplayable, especially considering the hoards of specialist units that are not just more tanky but also destroy you in seconds. I did;nt even get to open the trucks let alone have any team members alive by the time that the saws were done.I don't think I'll be revisiting this until things are properly balanced or at the very least have the bots able to attack enemies that are more than 2 meters away. Not sure who asked for these changes but I don't think that they speak for the majority of players.
