_childDocuments_.review: Not quite baked yet.Gets stale fairly quickly because the four turtles don't feel truly unique mechanically. Odd power-spikes in enemies makes the first three zones really easy, and then you get burst down in the fourth. Decent number of glitches, such as enemies not despawning after they die. Needs some work on map design as well because art can hide enemies, leading to attacks you can't dodge because you can't see it coming. Artwork needs an update to higher resolution textures now that it's on PC and consoles. Music is uninspired.Feels like there absolutely could be something here, but it isn't here yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Splintered Fate

_childDocuments_.review: TMNT: Splintered Fate is a decent rogue-lite with a few minor issues slightly holding it back. On the positive side, the art style, voice acting, and animations for the characters in the game are top notch. Enemy attacks are clearly telegraphed and easy to spot even when the level is crowded with foes. The numerous enemy types, various character build options, and occasional change of environment keep the runs from getting stale too quickly. Perhaps the biggest thing the game has going for it is the co-op experience which, to be honest, is a frenetic blast of awesomeness that makes the flaws forgivable.On the negative side, the overall story is rather forgettable, but serviceable enough for what the game is. The dash system along with the lack of any sort of auto targeting can make it frustrating to land attacks in certain situations with the player overshooting the intended enemy. Finally, the players in co-op rounds can be hard to keep straight when certain status effects are applied to the characters.With all that being said, this one is an easy recommendation for any action rouge-lite, or TMNT fan.
_childDocuments_.name: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Splintered Fate

_childDocuments_.review: I hope this game shapes up, because I see a lot of potential. It's just confusing to see some of the My First Video Game mistakes put on full display here. The UI is pretty gosh darn ugly and looks like it's been stretched to fit my very modest, standard definition screen size. The text the game wants you to read doesn't even fit where it's assigned, so sometimes you will be told that you just upgraded a superpower that belongs to MichaelangeloIt's just so many weird bugs that you would never expect to see from Hades, so it's wild to see a much larger company look so much less professional than a small indie studioAlso, I definitely beat Shredder and the game didn't give me the Shredder claws, so the bugs in this game WILL affect your progression
_childDocuments_.name: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Splintered Fate

_childDocuments_.review: If you love Hades, and TMNT then you owe it to yourself to play this game. Based off the amazing IDW TMNT comics this game is everything I want in a turtles game. Addictive gameplay, fast combat, fun story. The only downside is the game can be glitchy. Controller randomly locks up and you can't stop running. Lose a run and it doesn't take you back to the lair. Hopefully these things get patched, but I can live with it for such a fun game
_childDocuments_.name: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Splintered Fate

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game a lot. I wasn't sure what to expect but the Ninja Turtles have been a favorite since I was a kid and this definitely did not disappoint. The gameplay is fun and the boss mechanics are interesting. They've found several ways to make this game continue to be fun and have succeeded at creating a fun turtles-themed rogue-like.  I definitely see myself easily playing this for many hours.The only "complaints" or suggestions I'd have would be:1. The character movement feels a bit too floaty, like they're a bit light or something.2. It'd be cool if the items/skills you get after each battle worked the same way as the very first one, where you walk over to the purple pizza to pick up items. I've accidentally clicked on the first item several times due to the sudden pop-up. So having an item claim to interact with would be great instead.But neither of those minor things are super important or make it any less fun.Edit: After playing it quite a bit, it definitely continues to be fun. I'm still enjoying the gameplay and continue to work towards all of the achievements. I think you get a great amount fun for the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Splintered Fate

_childDocuments_.review: This game is seriously addicting! As someone who loved Hades, I can say that this has a similar sense of progression, challenge, and strategy/variety of builds per run. The co-op is incredibly well designed to ensure ease in navigating the map and combo-ing. We stayed up for hours, promising "just one more run!" I find it hard to find any good co-op games or roguelikes, so to find one that perfectly combines both is like Christmas Morning! Fantastic!
_childDocuments_.name: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Splintered Fate

_childDocuments_.review: If you really like roguelikes, and you really like Hades, you're going to love this. I have been obsessed with this game since buying it. The combinations of powers (albeit a few a LOT more powerful than others) are fun to find the combinations. The only complaint I would have is some of the hard mode bosses aren't really indicating just HOW hard they are. First time I activated the first bosses' hard mode I was not even close to prepared how much of a buttwhooping I was going to receive. Even with that, this game is incredible, especially for the pricetag. It very much scratches that TMNT nostalgia itch as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Splintered Fate

_childDocuments_.review: A lot better than I thought it was gonna be. The price tag is a bit steep, but if you can afford it definitely buy it. Its like TMNT with a Hades-esc flair. Even though its a Nickelodeon game its not  ababy's game, as a seasoned vet of action roguelikes I sometimes die when taking all the de-buffs. Its got some jank but all in all its damn good for what it is, and theres future DLC planned which is a good thing in this case.
_childDocuments_.name: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Splintered Fate

_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion, the biggest flaw a game can have is simply not being enjoyable. Unfortunately, the combat here becomes repetitive quickly, and the upgrades feel uninspired, barely impacting gameplay in any meaningful way. Although the inclusion of voiced story segments is a nice touch, they end up feeling unnecessary, often interrupting the flow with unimportant dialogue.The levels also lack variety; they all feel too similar in layout and design. Even classic beat-'em-ups like Turtles in Time broke up the action with unique stages to keep things fresh.I found myself losing interest after just half an hour, so unfortunately, I can’t recommend this one.

Leo is by far the weakest turtle to play and he has the worst special and starter tool, meanwhile Raph and Mikey sometimes feel almost too OP.I’ve run into some sort of glitch where NPC’s keep triggering dialogue and giving me items that I already have. I’m not sure what’s caused this, but it’s kind of annoying.Multiplayer is simple, but almost too simple. The selecting lacks any form of depth.
_childDocuments_.name: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Splintered Fate

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has been a TMNT fan since I was born in the late 80s, and LITERALLY owns everything TMNT related for games, and still the original VHS tapes and toys from the 80s. _childDocuments_.name: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Splintered Fate

_childDocuments_.review: I put a few hours into the demo, and I'll update this review as needed over time.  For now I just want to give it a thumbs up on launch day.This game rocks! _childDocuments_.review: The game is really cool, i'm having fun with it. See it like an Hades like, in the world of TMNT :).The "rooms" stages are nice but feels empty in the begin, but got crowded in later stages.But the game REALLY need polish and QoL (Quality of Life) adjustments :- All animations have kind of "lag" between impact and visuals.Just play Donatello and use basic attacks to see it. The stick move is finished and you'll notice the impact like 0.5sec after. _childDocuments_.review: Foreword of caution: right now it's early days after release - this game has been previously released on multiple other and was recently ported to Steam with improvements for PC gameplay (like wide-screen support, etc.). During the week and some after release there are multiple technical issues arising on Discord support channel and the team is working on them. It is my estimate as player and gamedev there may be something limiting the current/initial speed of their work (could be part of the team is on vacation after a busy release, could be anything), but I don't judge - I wish them best of luck on now stabilizing and polishing this otherwise great game!Other than the the few issues I've run into with my friends playing in private online co-op (a couple of soft-locks that didn't lose us any rewards, a couple times one of three players had some item unlock issues and we had to change host to fix it) the game is radical, dude! Hades-style action roguelike with the Turtles and all that it entails - there's a few branches of permanent progression systems that unlock after you play and progress further (or fail enough times, and various other conditions), and the during-run progression of Turtle Powers, Masteries, Tools, Max Health and the during-run resource management of your health (roguelite style, your health tracks as you progress from room to room, so taking hits early limits your chances towards the end) and Scrap. Scrap is used at interval of a few rooms as you're given a chance to purchase from a random selection of items like healing, max health, Turtle Powers, etc. Turtle Powers are always offered as a black box where you only know what element/type of Turtle Power you're getting, and only when you commit to the choice you'll see a random selection of powers within that category. Masteries are like Turtle Powers in that both offer you some new ability like a limited shield, incremental bonuses to stuff like max health or damage of specific attacks or all damage, etc., but Masteries are much stronger and found less often. There's a fair amount of possible synergies across different Powers and Tools, and each Turtle has a couple of their personal traits they begin with (sometimes you're given the chance to pick one of some other Turtle's characteristic/personal traits).The online multiplayer works well if you have good latency (me and my friends play in Northern Europe, no problems here) and we've all agreed so far that the game's good fun just chatting and smashing our way through for the fun and pretty relaxed gameplay (some fights offer fair challenges, but the overall loop is nice and it's very relaxing to embrace that defeat is just another way towards progress as you get your rewards and shop for permanent progression perks).I have no regrets for my purchase and am certain to keep playing with my friends as soon as I hear on the Discord that some patch note mentions they've taken care of the gnarliest possible progression resetting bug, so we'll hold off for a bit just now. Maybe I'll order a pizza when it's time to put our surfs up again.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't expect much given TMNT games are miss more often than hit and the game has to live up to the unflattering comparison with Hades right out the gate, but it's honestly pretty good. Obviously not as polished as Hades, but the visuals, art style, voice acting, heck even the music are really good. Combat is a little looser and more arcadey, and they lifted a lot of mechanics straight from the obvious inspiration (the way barriers on enemies work, the entire power up system, the structure of beating a room > picking an upgrade belonging to one of several categories (water/fire/ooze), the meta progression) but it's got enough unique little ideas and fun synergies to offer its own distinct flavor, and build variety seems good (though balance could use another look, ooze for example feels distinctly weaker than fire even when I had significantly more synergetic upgrades). Additional modifiers and difficulty levers for the player to crank after first completion justify the current length of individual runs/the current content scope. I'm pleasantly surprised as of day 1, it's a comfy roguelite with charm and fanservice aplenty and a lighter tone than most of its kind. Crossing my fingies to maybe eventually see Armaggon my beloved in this game someday, and/or a playable Slash. Though one of these two feels significantly more likely, and it's not the stupid, eldritch shark abomination :(

_childDocuments_.review: Co-opable HADES in the TMNT universe, with a storyline and dialogue that feels pretty spot-on to the old cartoons. And I haven't had any bugs or stuff breaking on me or being horribly imbalanced or anything, either. Which is always a plus!The game allows local and online co-op (I think it allows both simultaneously, though I've not tried that out personally), and has the four main Turtles playable at the time of this review, but their roadmap for 2024/25 includes "Exciting DLC" next up on the menu, with new playable characters, levels/enemies/bosses, and continuing story stuff.Cannot recommend this game enough, honestly. It's a fantastic game, even playing solo (Basically HADES with TMNT skin), but being able to play this co-op is where it really shines. It reminds me of playing the old Arcade beat-em-ups in ye olden times. I don't remember a TMNT one, but I vaguely recall one for The Simpsons and for X-Men, and both of those were great.If you've been looking for a great roguelike beat-em-up, and with co-op to boot, then this is absolutely something you should check out!

_childDocuments_.review: For what it is, it's quite fun. A Hades clone ported from mobile to Switch to PC. Though I hope they add more stuff as it is little "bare-bones" right now compared to said game.One annoying thing is that attacks of the turtles magnetise seemingly to a random or the closest enemy. This also affects your tools (throwables and such). Also most of the attacks push you forward. Because there is lots of enemy AoEs, this will make you take unnecessary damage or make encounters annoying waiting games of AoE avoidance. All of this makes precision control in a game that requires quite a lot of it quite hard.The difficulty is clearly out of whack. On normal the first 2 stages are complete jokes and you usually just fly through them. Stage 3 can get somewhat tough depending on the random elements you get. Stage 4 can instantly get insanely difficult with all the shurikens, ranged beams, AoEs, bunch of armored lightning fast minibosses etc. Not as big of a problem after you know what works and not (and unlock the challenge versions of the rooms) but still quite bizarre for a somewhat casual game.Some of the hitboxes are completely whack and some non game breaking bugs are present. The UI is clearly made for mobile and Switch, as it is quite huge and some graphical elements are not fitted for monitors/TVs.The co-op multiplayer uses annoying number ID based connection in which you have to manually input a 6 digit code that your friend has to tell you. As the developer has spent some time porting this over to steam, it is quite bizarre that they didn't include a super basic thing like connecting through Steam friends list. Haven't encountered any disconnects or game ending bugs in co-op at the time of writing. Though there is a quite aggressive time-out feature in multiplayer and no possibility to pause the game. So no pee breaks or the run is over.Overall though it's a fun game for the price and gives you enough stuff to do for said price. I have enjoyed it quite a lot. There is enough variety for different power-ups and such. Nothing close to Hades but enough to be satisfying. The "co-op Hades" part is probably the main draw here. There is planned DLC coming out, so at least the game isn't being abandoned outright. Lots of potential to be amazing in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Bottom line: I recommend the game to anyone that likes games like Hades.That being said, it does lack some polish in a few places. The game relies on AOE damage too much as a means of slowing/punishing the player. It can get extremely hard to tell where the actual pulse of the AOEs are at times. You can stand in the same AOE two times and take damage one time and not the other because it's not precise on when and where the damage actually applies.- You can accidentally take a power if you're trying to dash when the screen comes up. that's on the devs and is not good for a roguelite.- You can cause other players to lose a power up if you talk to an NPC while they are selecting a power in a shop. - The story is pretty lame, but oh well. - There is not much of extra dialogue. Don't expect HADES levels of NPC interaction.- Controls are generally good, but since spam dodging is sometimes required I think the dodging can leave a little to be desired, maybe that's just me.- The AOEs in the game are sometimes not able to be dodged. "perfect" gameplay is not reasonably possible because of the constant large area AOEs that mobs will continually stand in and dash through.- Donatello attacks so slow he's practically worthless as far as I'm concerned. His dash attack leaves you in the air for over a full second.- Leonardo's special attack is INCREDIBLY worthless. Worst special in the game. His starting tool is also pretty lame unless you plan on going full shuriken build (and even then you'll want to replace it anyway)- Power randomization is HORRID. I've gone 15 full games without seeing a NINJA ability. That shouldn't even be possible, but it happens, a lot.- Tooltips leave A LOT to be desired. You don't know what applies to what skills or abilities. I imagine there is a wiki for it somewhere, but the tooltips should have been updated. There is no way to check what your current stats are. No way to know what you crit % is, damage, attack %, etc.- There are a few big bugs that haven't been addressed. I don't know if they ever will. Things like the shop saying "double power" when opening it is one. There is a bug with bebop and rocksteady. - It really seems like the game was not remotely checked for bugs at all. It does reek of "lazy port money grab" a bit. - The UI leaves A LOT to be desired. Good luck trying to figure out what you combined stats are.There is more, but as my first line says, it's still worth buying. It's a good game plagued by little details by a lazy-ish port.I hope they fix some of it, but I'll still play it either way.As a last bit, even though it's a "new" game for steam it seems like it's abandoned as far as actual updates go. They got their money from the mobile/console releases and that's that. So if you're ok with all of the above and just want 6-20 mindless hours of button mashing with friends it can still be worth it. (just depends if you want to try to do achievements)

_childDocuments_.review: Mixed review. I've played a decent chunk, cleared numerous runs, have most of the achievements, and I know I'll play it for quite a while still.  But many things just feel off or unpolished with the game that just make it feel like it's not a good game. I just love the Turtles so I keep playing.Gameplay tries to mimic Hades very much, which is great because Hades might be the best Roguelike ever. But that forces all aspects of the game to be compared to Hades where it just falls short many times. The movement and combat isn't perfectly crisp. There's a lot of stupid BS that can happen that feels very frustrating.You move forward when you attack instead of standing still, even if they're in your range, and sometimes you inch into contact damage for no reason.The dash cooldown feels wonky. If you have 0.1 seconds left to recover your dash when you use your last dash, suddenly ALL dashes go on full cooldown. So you never feel like you have enough because even if you space them out they all get locked out.Sometimes you can dash through walls/obstacles and sometimes you can't. Sometimes you ZIP through one super fast and that can mess up your timing too.Sometimes you get helpers that are clones of enemies and you spend half your time dodging friendly attacks as not every attack has a visible difference. I'd rather never have helpers.Bosses are too easy, standard rooms are more difficult. Especially anything with lots of range.You can choose to enter portals that add difficulty (and rewards) and some are negligable while some make the game unplayable. Especially most Boss Gauntlet challenges - the game switches from too easy to nearly impossible.The portals are NOT crisp. You need to be close to read what the challenge is, and then whoops you went in. Run might be over now. Gotta be careful if you're dashing to the exit after clearing a room, you might accidentally accept your end of room reward because one button does everything in the game and there's no Confirms or delay or forgiveness. There's way too much dialog and story, and much of it is repeated a LOT. Hades has essentially zero repetition and never feels like it drags on. Even in your first few runs of the game you find yourself just mashing the skip button.Vast gap between some turtles and some abilities/builds in terms of usefulness. Stuff is either insane or useless with little inbetween.tl;dr: I'm sure there's complaints I'm forgetting, but there's just LOTS of little things that aren't good, and it all adds up. The game just isn't great, though it could be. If it wasn't because the TMNT are so darn cool I would have wanted a refund and just played more Hades.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is getting a recommendation though buyers should beware of a few things.Normally I don't care much for rouge like games in part that they are very one dimensional and I get board rather quickly with them. However with this game that isn't the case strangely.For what story there is, albeit a short one, it fits nicely with most TNMT cannon. You will see a sizable selection of past heroes and villains from a variety of sources. Interactions between the main cast and support characters are nicely done. Graphics to are pretty good though "stage" and enemy designs are pretty generic.The dislike are the uneven balance among the characters and how the game handles explaining stuff. Each turtle is suppose to have a different skill set for player variety but some are just so horribly unbalanced that there are clear choices to go with and ones to avoid. Leo is always a winner while Raph is pretty crap. On the explanation, there is very little. You are just given things with certain key words like "light shell" (as one example) with nothing to tell you what these are. A lot of the discovery does amount to trial and error unless you spend time having to look up online what these do. In all a fun little game but certainly not without some major improvements needed.

_childDocuments_.review: The comparisons to Hades II are inevitable, and this game just doesn't stand up. 1) It's overpriced for a mobile port, by a lot. 2) While the game isn't as challenging as Hades II it's also much cheesier. 99% of the time, outside of boss-fights, you will have very little idea where you just took damage from. Many of the attacks, I'm looking at you homing ninja stars, blend into the background. 3) You spend so little time actually attacking. From the constant AOE attacks to the eleventy billion regular enemy attacks, you spend most of the time dodging. Which leads to point 4) The dodge button also picks your upgrades, the menu with which you pick said upgrades pops up, randomly, when the level ends. Leaving you to accidentally choose the top option when you just meant to dodge. 5) Shut the hell up! Constant inane chatter while you're in control, and ridiculously verbose dialog scenes. This game uses 100 words when 15 would have worked. This game wastes your time so much I have to assume the mobile game had time-gates implemented at some point 6) Hit boxes for attacks and enemies are whack. _childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute unbalanced train wreck. It seems really fun at first but the more you play it, the more you start to realize what you're in for and it's basically just a ridiculously long grind out for coins so you can unlock all of the games mechanics / bonus'... the game doesn't even really start until you unlock everything and then start gimping yourself with crappy artifacts that make the game harder on you... it's just a never ending cycle of frustration from start to end.The turtles are all unbalanced and all require each others synergizes to succeed. Donatello is the most broken though just due to his shield tool and his innate ability to reduce it's cool down by 80%... he's absolutely broken in the defense department but you also need Raph's critical hit bonus' to do any kind of substantial damage on hard mode... It really is just a balancing act of farming for coins and farming for distance so you can win rare materials to unlock higher tier bonus'... you'll end up replaying the same boring missions over and over ad nauseam in order to finally progress... by the 50th run of the first couple areas I've kind of had it... The enemies are also insane when it comes to dealing damage, they either do nothing or they kill you instantly it seems... it's just a mess. I wouldn't pay $35 for this... definitely grab it on sale for less than $14.99 or even lower... playing the game online with more players also seems to make the game exponentially more difficult from what I've experienced.... unless everyone is on the same page, otherwise you're carrying.It's unfortunate the maximum potential of your power all has to be unlocked by grinding and boring yourself to death with turtles you may not even want to play with. So far from what I've seen, Don and Mike are the best turtles to play as and Raph has some of the best bonus' in the game for dealing the most damage... Leo has a lot of utility skills but they're almost inconsequential when compared to Don and Mikes upgrades...It definitely needs a re-balance because the enemy scaling gets way too out of hand after the first two stages. Level 3 and 4 need a huge adjustment to make the enemies much weaker in power so they don't just 1 shot kill you.The rogue like elements also make or break your entire run... if you get unlucky enough to never get Raph's flame abilities or Don's shield to replace some of the more useless tools like Leo's Shuriken or Raphs chain thing... it's a nightmare.Don't buy this at full pop, the game is also a buggy mess and random crashes / glitches happen CONSTANTLY while playing which will make you lose most of your progress... and the time spent playing this is already absurd as it is, so when you're wasting it on zero gains, it just becomes a migraine.

_childDocuments_.review: Where the heck did this absolute gemstone of a game come from!?Great voice acting, surprisingly well-written dialogue, fantastic banter between the siblings, AMAZING action... I've been playing TMNT games intermittently for decades. This one is by far the very best I have personally played. I was immediately overjoyed by how fun the combat was from the beginning of the tutorial.It's so rare to find a good hack-n-slash game that is not riddled with blood, gore, profanity, and pornography that not everybody wants to see. I'm delighted at the chance to enjoy a Hades-style game without all of that stuff. I'm especially delighted at the idea of playing this game with my kids over the weekend. They're gonna love it. I was honestly surprised to see the roguelike genre be applied to TMNT. I must say that the devs understood the assignment wonderfully well - each upgrade feels meaningful, and a number of the percentage boosts seem so high as to feel like they ought to be unreasonable, but they apply very well into this rather well-balanced gameplay loop. Confidence very quickly bleeds over into an unexpected death, perfect for the genre. It is already hard to put this game down.This is such an incredible gem of a game that I was not expecting to run into, let alone that it would be THIS good. Not sure I can recommend this game enough - this is a game I may well play for a number of years.EDIT: 16 hours in and it's STILL a blast

_childDocuments_.review: Basically Co-op Hades - Highly recommend it!I've done a few runs solo, and a BUNCH duo with my wife. Super fun to play together, the different turtles can combo some of their starter stuff together which makes coordinating feel really good. All the resources/upgrades are individual, so you aren't fighting for loot or anything. Within a run, you unlock upgrades veryyyyy similar to Hades' "boon" system (they even have "dual boons"). You can end up with some pretty crazy combos (I got one where stuns did a ton of damage, I dealt frost damage on my attacks, and frost damage stunned, so as you can imagine that combo was really cookin'). I'm still chasing the high of that build. In-between runs, you can spend some currency to upgrade various aspects of your turtles (similar to Hades, it unlocks after you do more and more runs). One thing that's really distinct about this from Hades is you have 4 differerent characters with different basic attacks, special attacks, and "passives". They also all start with their own unique tool, but you can swap it out for other tools during the run. The characters are fully voiced, and I'm sure the story and everything is exciting if you're a TMNT fan. I only recognized a few characters because I'm not that familiar with the story, but it's definitely still a great game to play even if you're just skipping the cutscenes.The difficulty is solid. It gets easier as you unlock more and more upgrades, but I still have yet to get all the way to the end. The baseline enemies are decently hard, scaling up as you get further along. The bosses all have very interesting patterns that are challenging to master, and they start changing up their attack patterns on subsequent runs (I'm not sure what triggers it, but when a certain boss starts using flame powers.... ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ it gets hard). Even if you're quite good at games, it's probably going to take you a good number of runs to beat the whole thing. Definitely recommend playing on a gamepad. It's good on KBM too, but gamepad feels like the best experience. There's lots of cool little quality-of life stuff built into the game, you can tell the devs really cared to make a good experience and not just make a crappy copy of another game. Critiques:-I accidentally select powers all the time because I'm spamming dash after an encounter ends so I insta-select the first power-Wish I could get health more often during a run, it feels really hard to top back up-Certain levels (the one with the rat and tons of lasers especially) have the foreground environment blocking your view within areas that you can put your character, which really sucks when you're forced down there and taking damage from stuff you can't see-Some enemies just absolutely SLAP and it's hard to know that they are going to hit really hard sometimes-The little mouser buddies that come help are sooooo annoying! I can't see which are enemies and which ones are buddies >:( I know they are supposed to help but I don't like them

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: It's the kind of fighting game where you'll be pressing the dodge button 50x more often than the attack button. The AI get to play the game while you dodge around trying to sneak in extremely unsatisfying quick hits between extremely long attack routines with very brief windows to punish. Do you like combos and beat em up games? AVOID THIS GAME if you do. Do you like Dark Souls, Elden ring, and other souls games where you spend 85% of your playtime dodging around while watching the cool attacks the ai throws? Then this is right up your alley.This is one of the most unnecessarily hard games I've ever played in my life. It's one of the most grindy rogue-likes I've ever played. In addition to extremely long ai attack windows, there are an absurd amount of persistent damaging area ground effects. You will end up dodging and running away for 80% of the time only to do 1/3 of a basic attack chain or a special move before resuming nonstop defensive measures. The ONLY fun and fair boss is Shredder.BEWARE: THE DEMO HIDES THIS ASPECT OF THE GAME FROM YOU! I found out too late and as a result my refund was denied.Enemies scale hp, damage etc based on number of turtles. This sounds fun but in practice, most teammates you get are going to make it harder because their performance won't result in a net positive when compared to the inflated scaling the enemies receive.Reduce ground effects by 75%Decrease the length of AI attack combos by 50%Decrease enemy scaling from multiple turtlesIncrease punish windows by 50%If you did those things, this game would be good.

_childDocuments_.review: I like it, but I don't recommend it.For starters, within the first hour I've had several bugs.First, starting the game completely disabled the controller...the first two times the game was launched. Not just within the game... steam could no longer detect it properly. It's unclear why or if this will happen more down the road, and I don't know what fixed it.Once play resumed, losing to sewer boss triggered a soft-lock. Force closing and restarting triggers the boss's opening cut scene with the turtle dead on the ground, then immediately transitions into loss and continues properly.It was also observed at this point in the game that when switching turtles as a single player idle turtles sometimes go missing. Each of the four turtles has an in-base animation when not selected. When first arriving at base, all of the animations for the other three turtles are displayed properly. However, after swapping to a different turtle, the previously selected turtle will not be displayed anywhere in base. (EX: 1. User returns to base as Mikey. Can view Leo, Donnie, Raph. 2. User swaps to Leo. Can view Donnie, Raph. 3. User swaps to Raph. Can view Mikey, Donnie. Etc.)It was also noted during a few points in the tutorial that Leo got stuck facing screen left. The right-stick is not used for facing input, so there was no way to force him to change facing.There's also some design oversights. For example, the layout of the Dragon Coin upgrades: There are three types of upgrades. The layout within each is designed so there are four columns, and the price increase goes from left to right, top to bottom. However, within the Specialty section, the 'wrap' crosses pages. So, the top row has a single-medallion cost for three of four turtles. Then the next row has three-medallion costs for three turtles. However the top left upgrade on the second page is the fourth turtle's single-medallion upgrade. It's a very minor inconvenience, but also could've been avoided with a bit of planning and care.There's other areas which could use more clarity as well. For instance, viewing equipment outside of upgrades is done with the back/select/two-square button, opposite the three-bar/start button. This is not mentioned during the tutorial. Similarly, it does not seem that the purpose of elemental upgrades is ever explained. Or if it is, the explanation will be coming quite late (or somehow got skipped in the tutorial). Are there elemental strengths and weaknesses? Or are they just for different effect with no further reason for planning? What elements even are there — so far I've noted I think five? Is this information in the game somewhere? Uncertain.I love the turtles, which is the whole reason I got the game. But, as a game, it's not groundbreaking and the experience so far has not been smooth.

_childDocuments_.review: So, first of all, this game is Hades with a turtle skin on top. Here is a bunch of super facts:* In Hades you are seeking out Persephone who you briefly speak with at the end of runs. In TMNT you are seeking out Splinter who you briefly speak with at the end of runs.* In both the third boss fight is a comic relief pair, one of whom spends the fight charging you while the other shoots at you with ranged attacks.* In both the final boss is a two health bar fight where the boss mostly just dashes at you and does big attacks with occasional summon phases.* The basic mechanics of the game are obviously inspired by Hades in ways too numerous to name.Now, that's all fine--it's part of why I bought the game. But my big problem is that the ways in which the game has changed mostly seem to make it worse:* The power system in TMNT doesn't feel very good. Powers don't seem to do very much to increase your abilities unless you get a lot of stuff stacked up, but it's also hard to figure out the synergies as there's no list of powers to plan against. I had one run where I stacked Leo up with shruiken powers and one run where I stacked Raph up with crit, and those are the only runs so far where I've felt powerful. Otherwise it's just chip-chip-chip all the day long. Maybe that's a metacurrency issue, which reminds me:* HOW DID THEY MAKE THE META GRIND SLOWER? jfc. Hades was already too slow to grind to endgame power level and pumping endless dragon coins into +5% attack damage is an even worse version.* Enemy attack timing and/or dodge timing seems off sometimes--the game encourages you to basically play every turtle like you play fists in Hades: hold down the attack button and dash iframe through attacks. But I find that playing this way gets you hit so much because attack animations don't seem to match up with hurt frames like I expect. Maybe it's a skill issue, but that was always my favorite way to play Hades, so I like to think that my timing isn't so bad.If you haven't finished Hades, that's the better choice rather than playing this, frankly. The co-op here is a lot of fun though, and that isn't a small advantage, but unless you've got 2-3 friends who want to play this to GRIND IT, I don't know if it'll work.

_childDocuments_.name: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Splintered Fate

_childDocuments_.review: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Splintered Fate delivers an exciting, action-packed experience that will appeal to fans of roguelikes like Hades, but with the added charm of the beloved TMNT universe. If you're a fan of fast-paced combat and strategic gameplay, this title is a great choice.One of the standout features of Splintered Fate is how it borrows from Hades, particularly its combat mechanics and progression system. The gameplay feels satisfying with tight, responsive controls, and the wide array of power-ups and build options allow for deep customization. Whether you're stacking damage buffs, enhancing your movement, or boosting your defenses, there are plenty of ways to tailor your playstyle to your liking. This system ensures that each run feels fresh and rewarding, with new synergies to discover every time.The co-op feature is another major advantage that sets Splintered Fate apart from Hades. Being able to team up with a friend (or multiple friends) for some couch co-op or online multiplayer action adds a lot of fun and replay value. The ability to share the chaos and strategize together makes the experience even more dynamic, offering a cooperative twist that is largely absent in Hades. The game's flexibility in this regard will appeal to fans looking to enjoy the roguelike genre with others.However, the game does have some drawbacks. As you progress, the difficulty ramps up, and the enemies, while varied and engaging at first, become somewhat bullet-spongy in later stages. This can make certain sections feel frustrating and drag out the pacing, as it often takes longer to defeat foes that earlier in the game would have been much easier to take down. This change can disrupt the flow and lead to moments of tedium.Overall, Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Splintered Fate is an enjoyable experience for fans of action roguelikes and TMNT. Its deep customization, fun co-op mode, and familiar combat mechanics make it a solid game, though the bullet sponge enemies later on can take a bit of the shine off an otherwise exciting experience. If you're into roguelikes and the TMNT franchise, this one is definitely worth checking out.
_childDocuments_.name: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Splintered Fate

_childDocuments_.review: ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️☆Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Splintered Fate is a fantastic blend of fast-paced roguelike action and the charm of everyone's favorite heroes in a half shell. The game nails the TMNT vibe with phenomenal voice acting that brings each turtle to life and a soundtrack that perfectly matches the energy of the action and the franchise's classic feel.The gameplay feels like a cooperative Hades, satisfying, and brimming with variety. Each run is packed with exciting combat, unique abilities, and plenty of replayability as you take on enemies with your friends. While the mechanics are solid overall, the controls and animations can feel a little clunky at times, but it’s a minor nitpick in an otherwise stellar experience.Whether you're a fan of roguelikes, TMNT, or both, Splintered Fate is an absolute blast to play. Cowabunga, dudes! 🐢🎮

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a TMNT fan since the 1987 series, and have loved most of their games.  TMNT works very well as a run-based action RPG similar to Hades.  The overall gameplay seems a little more streamlined, and more friendly to beginner players, but there is still plenty of depth, with the 4 turtles, and variety of upgrades.  The story works too.  I originally grabbed this on my Switch, since the PC version didn't come out until much later, but I love that I can now play this on my desktop gaming rig, and my Steam Deck OLED.
_childDocuments_.name: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Splintered Fate

_childDocuments_.review: You can definitely see the Hades inspiration here.  I can very much understand if someone would call it a Hades clone with a TMNT coat of paint on it.  But I've been a TMNT for a long time (starting with the original 80s/90s cartoon), and that TMNT coat of paint seemed to be what I needed to appreciate this game genre as a whole.  I tried and struggled to get into it (even when trying something as well regarded as Hades), but just couldn't quite get there.  But playing it with characters I've known and loved since I was really young?  Yes please!If you've played and enjoyed Hades, you can probably enjoy this.  If you like TMNT, I'd call this game worth trying at the very least.  If you're hesitant to try it, then just wait for a sale.  I like the designs of the Turtles themselves, I do tend to prefer when they look more or less the same except the colored headbands and/or the exact shade of green used for each of them.  They look mostly inspired by the 2000s era cartoon.  I've played all single player thus far so I can speak to any of the issues some have experienced with multiplayer.  I've also played only on Steam Deck, with 0 issues.  Looks and runs fine on Deck, and the coloration works nicely on an OLED display.Would recommend overall.  Asking price might be a bit steep but in that case, just wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Is it a Hades clone? Absolutely. Is it fun? It is for a bit and has its moments. While the formula does work for TMNT, the upgrades just aren’t as exciting as Hades. If you take the final section of Hades, where you spend most of your time trying to avoid poison all over the ground, and make that the majority of the game…you’ll have an idea of what you’re getting into with this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, Chaotic, ARPG Madness. The negative reviews mentioning how bad the combat is hilarious. You mostly view the enemies animations and hit-box window the enemy creates. You have a circle around your character that helps avoid damage. As the game progresses, you get more complicated challenges to do once you complete a run for the first time, (four chapters). The comparison to Hades is a little off, but in the same ball park when it comes to boons/turtle powers. It does push for a good multiplayer, its so much fun watching how people just rush enemies without a second thought, you'll learn from mistakes very fast. All that this game has to offer for repeatability is here, and the grind for upgrades feels good. If you enjoy grinding upgrades in ARPGs, you'll enjoy TMNT:SF.

_childDocuments_.review: I love TMNT and Hades-like gameplay, so this game would be a sure win, yes?Well, sadly, no.  There was no love spent in making this game and it sure feels rushed.Let me start with the annoyances and little bugs:1. Bugs that should be easy to correct were completely neglected. Sometimes, the text gets behind the headers and footers; the last option of the vendor (when there are four options) cannot be seen, etc.2. Some upgrades request an item you get when you successfully complete a run, but the first time you win, you don't get one.3. Talismans get you a guaranteed element on the next reward. For instance, you can use the Water talisman to get once a Water Upgrade. But the game does not tell you that you have used the talisman power. You have to memorize it. So far, no prob. It's a single use, so it should be easy to remember. But then, you switch to another talisman. Let's say, Fire. Suposedly, the next reward should be Fire, but, as you have already used a Water talisman before, now Fire isn't guaranteed even once in the rewards. So, basically, switching talismans midrun is kinda pointless.4. The story goes nowhere. (At least till the point I got, which is two victories.) Only crypt sentences, made by cryptic characters that act in strange ways that make no sense. For example, why make everyone give you a gift instead of just giving it directly to you? None of the gifts come from the secondary characters. They are just delivering because they were told so. They didn't make it, they didn't get it for you. They are just the delivery team. Likewise, the archvilain motivation seems completely nonsensical. Supposedly, in the end, all will make sense, but I wouldn't keep my hopes up.Now for the truly sad part:5. The stages are beautifully rendered, but they and much bigger than required and completely uninspired. Maybe a barrier here or there, but mostly empty. With no traps, or interactibles or anything that would impact in a significant way the fights.6. There are several factions of enemies, and they often fight among themselves. At first glance, this seems fun, but as the stages are really big, as mentioned before, you just go to a corner and wait. You dont get to see anything, because they are all off screen, but at some point, only one faction is alive, and then you deal with these last survivors. It gets so silly to the point where there are two midbosses you have to fight at once and they just kill each other if you let them.7. No time was spent in making the enemies feel unique. In all worlds you get to fight the same enemies. Elite enemies are the same as normal ones, but with yellow bars and midbosses are the same just with an extra long red bar. No new moves, no nothing. Just more damage and more life. And all worlds are the same. Just more enemies at once in latter worlds.8. Almost all power-ups are about dealing more damage. A very few are about getting more life or dodge and that's it. Nothing that would allow for diferent strategies, like some crowd control, or slow or weak, or a shield, etc. Sure, there are tools that do some of this, but it is very limited because you need to charge them. So all the elements feel the same. Sure, each one have its own way to make you deal more damage, but in the end, they are just this. more damage. Almost no strategy at all.9. Finally, the worst sin possible. The bosses are so lame and easy that to make the fights harder, they spawn infinite goons. No point in killing them because they just respawn as soon as you kill them. In some fights, you get a few seconds of respite, but in most, all you get is the the spawning animation time. In the end, the battles become an almost infinite dash marathon in a bullet hell. There is no strategy. no option. The only thing that matters is staying alive and damaging the boss. There is no crowd control, no elimination of the most annoying goons so that only the weak ones remain, no cleaning the room before attacking the boss, no nothing. Just keep dashing and hitting the boss when possible. Boring as hell.In conclusion. I really wanted to love this game. When I started playing, I loved it. But as the game continued, the deficiencies started making themselves clear. I'll probably play more, because I really, really like this kind of game, but I cannot in good conscience recommend it to my friends.
_childDocuments_.name: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Splintered Fate

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely a lot of fun for the price.  For the amount of time I've put in grinding achievements and trying to 'complete' the game it feels worth it.  There are minor glitches from time to time (player disappearing after a boss fight and minions not despawning) but I haven't had one that stopped my run or made things unplayable.  It really is like Hades in the style of story playing out and getting easier with each run.  There's a fair amount of diversity with each run but certain builds feel more consistently powerful compared to others which can be frustrating.  The later levels can be quite difficult if you can't get a good build but insanely satisfying when luck is on your side.  Each turtle has some differences that lead to different play styles that do better with certain elements.  I don't know if they are different enough but the simplicity is nice so it's not too hard to jump into another game with another turtle.For those that want challenges they are definitely there if you choose it during a run.  The dialogue might be cliche but it's fun nostalgia as a turtles game.  I do hope they add more content in the future but for the price this was great.  Even after the many hours of playing there's still many things to upgrade so for the ones that want to get everything maxed it will definitely take a while.
_childDocuments_.name: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Splintered Fate

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game to play solo or with friends. The game starts to get pretty hard when portals are introduced which is a great way to play. Highly recommend spending Dreamer coins on getting more scrap per run - opens up ways to buy more coins and abilities. Use your dice to refresh shops to buy more pizza for health or more abilities!
_childDocuments_.name: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Splintered Fate

_childDocuments_.review: Fun but it definitely needs work. Enemy AI will sit in corners hidden by buildings and spam ranged abilities that cover the whole arena, forcing you to choose between trading damage to get rid of it or sit back and wait, hoping for it to finally step away from the edge (it won't). Arena borders are not clearly defined and you can end up dashing in place cause that space you see isn't really there. A not insignificant portion of the difficulty comes from unavoidable damage from enemies setting the arena completely on fire or lightning or whatever and then standing in the damage zone. More grind based than skill based, most of the progression comes from getting the stats to kill quickly and tank the unavoidable damage. Hit boxes are questionable. Avoid the Lightshell power; from what I can tell it only works on shurikens, lasers and lobbed projectiles will still hit you. of before buying.The presentation of the comics could have been done better, it is done in a similar style to Hades but only in that one small aspect and I never really did like Hades for its comic presentation or its combat, I dont like the overall feel of the presentation of how the characters talk, I think its the abrupt transition between characters talking with pauses making it feel like its less of an authentic conversation and it just feels more exaggerated paused and standoffish is the best way to describe it, it rubs me the wrong way and reminds me of Hades which I did not like for its comic feel at all. it just doesn't feel as good as it could.But the combat on the other hand is great, probably perfect which I was honestly skeptical of at first and was cautious before reach and feels good to be more precise with your attacks although button mashing is acceptable for all styles the longer reach and precision attacks feels satisfyingRaph hits like a truck but is a _childDocuments_.review: What an inspiring recreation of this IP!  We've evolved out of the side-scroller and into a bold & modernized mutation of isometric play. We're introduced to a multiversal baddie, while still layering our favorite heroes and villains with life lessons, a lot of style, and a couple iconic lines - if you like Mayhem, get ready for June-hem and July-hem.A new DLC is also on the way!  Bossa nova!  I'd like more elemental powers (earthen & wind).  I'd also enjoy a better sense of control as I move through portals, so hopefully they include a way to isolate powers I want or banish ones I don't while building.  Chevy nova?  And lengthen the story so I can spend more time designing the perfect build - I'd fight a few more bosses for the opportunity.  Acapella!I found this title on iPad, but I'm thrilled it was ported to Steam with couch-cooperative and online play.  Let's play over a pizza or two.  See you in the lair!

_childDocuments_.review: Initial impressions a few hours in on release day. I'll probably come back in a month after I get more time (and so do the devs). Pretty fun. Not quite as compelling as Hades, but definitely decent, with some bugs out and about.Gameplay is fairly basic. You have a dash, attack, tool, and super button, and tool/super get charged through attacks. The tool can be swapped or upgraded during a run, and like most of these arena roguelites, each room gives you some kind of upgrade... maybe just some currency, often a power. The core of why Hades was so nuts was because each weapon was very different, and the stacks got funny and developed a custom playstyle very quickly. Three levels deep in the Turtles game and it's mostly just little buffs... yeah, maybe throwing three shurikens on dash and they return for a damage debuff, but it's not the bonkers stuff Hades offers. And that's kinda fine. It feels more like a Turtles beat-em up, maneuvering and attacking and a bit of kiting. Enemies are decently challenging... interestingly, mousers might be the most dangerous thing, because they can spawn in and start throwing whole webs of lasers down, which means you absolutely need to stagger them or get outta there to kill other enemies first. Shuriken foot projectiles do some light trajectory adjustment, and many enemies do the stupid armored phase thing where they just tank damage without stunning so you have to learn to dash through their attack patterns again and again. Fine for a dude or two, but this becomes more just "every enemy" a couple levels in.Some enemy attacks can be pretty ambiguous. The enemy shurikens versus your own is just a size difference. When you start getting friendly Mousers, you need to pay attention to their green health versus the red health bad ones. Enemies can be hidden by scenery, with no way to tell except your attacks that try to auto-focus on something nearby. At 4k resolution, I started having screen glitches. It wasn't tearing, rather the characters that were talking would swap with the other character in the conversation for a few frames and switch back. I've got a dual monitor 4k setup, but run them in 2k resolution, so sorta suspect the fact it automatically went to 4k but seems to be a borderless fullscreen means the two resolutions was freaking the game out. By swapping down to 2k resolution in the settings this went away. I wouldn't recommend it wholeheartedly at the moment. Probably around 15 bucks I would say go for it unless you're just a huge turtles fan who likes a roguelike.

_childDocuments_.review: Its definitely a pretty well done game, gives super hades vibes, can feel a bit clunky at times. Love what I have played so far. Definitely worth the price.So far in the game, theres really only one path, I think offering risk/reward differing paths or options to choose from instead of just one linear direction as you play would be a better benefit, albeit I have only played about 2hrs of gameplay, maybe it does that later on after you beat the game for extra content. So time will tell.Edit 1: With 24hours of playtime now, the callout of really only one path kind of changed but its still there, after you beat shredder the first time you can do modifiers to enhance the remainder of the game. I still wish you could see like different rewards through and choose different options, maybe see more mousers one way, or foot another. But it doesnt mean its not fun or done well how they have it currently.Each of the characters plays a bit differently which is to be expected. Solid pickup, I cant wait if theres DLC. #hurryupEdit 2: With allied spawn ins, theres no way to differentiate from them to enemy when they have full armor, even if they are off screen, they will appear like hey an enemy spawn in so you go there to find out, oh not an enemy.With all the modifiers given in the mix, it can make some of the fights infinitely harder when there are multiple elite enemies so you will take quite a bit of damage and can mean you lose that much quicker, which isnt a bad thing but can make you feel frustrated. Maybe tone down how many spawn at one time, if you dont have a way to stun them you are going to just walk in, do an attack and zoom out. Rinse repeat for 5minutes or so, it doesnt feel very engaging to do when one does a focused attack, another does a focused attack a third one does an aoe attack, so you are forced to take something or make the fight go on. While you can escape with minimal to no damage, it just feels weird to deal with it. Either that or when they are all clumped together, allow friendly fire to take hold as an added benefit, they do take some damage from other faction, but it feels like its not enough comparatively.I think there is opportunity to improve the final boss, on hard mode, it is so much easier and quicker than normal mode. Having two phases and him refreshing his hp on normal makes it harder and more tedious, whereas on hard mode he has one health bar, gains immediate access to his extra abilities and enemies spawn, making the fight that much easier to do, now its not as telegraphed as the normal mode because you can evade all his attacks with ease. _childDocuments_.review: Edit:actually, the thing with controls is even worse now. Don't bother playing w/o controller. Works perfectly on Steam Deck, but using mouse and keyboard - when you hit space, you'll use two dashes about 60% of the time, one will get you away from danger, the second will snap you RIGHT BACK AT IT.So, not only controller is recommended - its unplayable without it.Its great, except for one thing - controls.So lets get bad out of the way first:first, there's an odd, inconsistent lag with your movement inputs. I don't know what it is, my assumption is that its related to complete lack of optimizations.Second, your attacks do not follow your mouse - they autosnap to the nearest enemy. While this makes it easier to attack in some instances, you will end up in a lot of situations where you dodge out of the way of are attack, and you want to attack the enemy down the line - but the autosnap will zoom you right back to the enemy you dodged away from, straight into his AoE.it is quite frustrating when you're on the screen with +10 enemies throwing ranged attacks at you and couple of medium or large size buddies doing constant attacks. You get hit, you lose health, and it doesn't feel like its my own fault.Third, there's no real graphics options, such as - you can't vsync or choose a framecap.That on the side - it is a really, really cool roguelike. Every character plays in a different way, and powers you unlock are fun and will either support or modify that playstyle. The perma-unlocks are noteworthy and really make it far easier to grind through initial levels even after only few upgrades.Graphics are great, sound is great.Perhaps the only thing I'd wish extra, is a bit more secrets in levels. Right now its just one arena straight to the next, so exploration isn't a thing at all.But, with all this, its a very solid TU - personally, I like this game far better than Shredder's Revenge.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! To me 60 fps is great, but 100+ is really smooth and nice. So going from a game that feels like it goes to 15 to 20 fps on the switch to having 160 fps on PC, with better graphics, I don't know how I can not recommend this.It plays like Hades, which was an awesome game. I like the Ninja Turtles, so I like this better. Instead of different weapons, you alternate the turtles, each have their strengths. Ralph, he has critical hit chance and damage that makes him great, but then there's Mike, who has long range buffs and a chance for multi hits. It's pretty cool and I used to love this show as a kid, but this story is really interesting and is introducing me to lore I guess I missed. It's a great game, and I did see people say it deserves to be less money. I don't get this. It's such a quality game. It's not full price, you can get so many hours in it, there's so much to unlock and the gameplay loop is addictive.Even if you dislike rogue games, this one has an easy mode and it's easy to rack up the currency to level things like health and other buffs.I haven't played Hades 1 in so long, that game was great, but I think this game is easier and maybe because I love the Ninja Turtles, I don't know, the combat feels more satisfying here.It's a great beat'em up. _childDocuments_.review: This game is excellent! The voice acting is great, the controls are tight, and the game puts up a challenge. I initially thought it was a bit too easy, but that changes pretty quickly as you acquire upgrades and powers. I've put hundreds of hours into roguelikes in general, and while this game doesn't necessarily do anything new, it's a really solid game. It does borrow the same formula that is used in Hades, but it does it very well. And it's TMNT-themed! On top of that, there is online co-op!There is a specific quirk that I wish would be addressed. At the end of an encounter, instead of walking over to the reward/power-up (like in Hades), a popup to choose a power shows up pretty abruptly and I've accidentally chosen the first option on several occasions because I was unaware that the encounter actually ended. It would be great if you could walk over to the power-up and pick it up like you do for the very first power-up in the run. Aside from this, I've got no real complaints about the game.

_childDocuments_.review: YouTube Link:Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Splintered Fate is an amazing new roguelike. It takes place in an original universe that’s not linked to any of the TV shows. In this fantastically developed world, the Turtles are more experienced heroes at the top of their game until a mysterious enemy kidnaps Splinter and forces them through twisted trials to try and get him back. The lore and story elements are subtly dropped through dialogue, so listen carefully if you wish to learn more. The portals and roguelike elements fuse its way into the story which is quite funny at times. TMNT Splintered Fate mixes beat ’ 'em-up action with roguelike mechanics. You will never finish this game on your first attempt and have to continuously play through runs to collect more currency to grow stronger. You need to defeat all the enemies in a room before advancing forward. You have your basic attacks alongside a tool, special ability, and a dash. The tool is like your sub-weapon, it helps you clear a room of enemies but won’t insta-kill them. That would be the special ability, dealing a ton of damage in a single shot. The tools, special abilities, and passive abilities called Inspirations are unique for each Turtle. Other Turtles can learn each other’s moves if you find them during the run. Just like the personalities in the story, how each Turtle functions in-game is what you would expect. Donnie is the long-range attacker while Ralph likes to get up close to deal damage. I personally gravitated toward Leonardo at first because he’s my favorite Turtle but quickly moved to Ralph and Mikey because of their close-range combat offering a ton of damage. At the end of each major area, there’s a boss fight. From Leatherhead to Bebop and Rocksteady, all the fan-favorite villains are here to stop your run. They’re definitely going to eat away at your health bar. Try your best to dodge and dash incoming attacks as much as possible. It feels very satisfying to take them all down with each boss fight getting progressively harder. Even the mini-bosses are tough opponents as well. It’s good to see the Turtles in a game that’s not ostensibly a brawler, and I was surprised by how well they took to the roguelike genre.

_childDocuments_.review: *Assassin’s Creed Mirage* returns to the franchise's roots, offering a focused, stealth-oriented experience reminiscent of the original games. Set in 9th-century Baghdad, players take on the role of Basim, a young assassin navigating a beautifully recreated world rich with culture and history. Mirage emphasizes stealth and parkour, bringing back classic mechanics like blending with crowds, rooftop chases, and silent assassinations. The combat system is refined and responsive, favoring a more tactical approach rather than brute force. The game encourages exploration and precision, rewarding careful planning over aggressive playstyles. The storyline dives into Basim's journey from a street thief to a master assassin, delving into themes of loyalty, revenge, and redemption. Baghdad is vividly portrayed, with bustling markets, ancient architecture, and a rich, atmospheric setting that captures the essence of the time period. Visually, *Assassin’s Creed Mirage* is stunning, with intricate details in character models, environment design, and lighting. The sound design enhances immersion, from ambient sounds in the streets to the immersive soundtrack, which complements the Middle Eastern setting perfectly. *Assassin’s Creed Mirage* offers a streamlined, immersive experience that pays homage to the series' original stealth mechanics. It’s ideal for fans of the classic Assassin’s Creed formula and those looking for a richly detailed, story-driven adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: Assassin’s Creed Mirage brings the series back to its roots, which is great for anyone who loved the older games. Set in 9th-century Baghdad, this game feels like a throwback to the classic Assassin's Creed formula, focusing more on stealth, parkour, and assassinations rather than the huge RPG-style worlds from recent entries like Valhalla or Odyssey.What’s Good:1. Awesome Setting:Baghdad looks stunning. The city is full of life, from busy markets to narrow alleyways and towering buildings. It’s not as big as some of the recent games, but it’s packed with detail and really gives you the vibe of the time period.2. Stealth is Back:If you miss the days of sneaking around and planning the perfect kill, Mirage has you covered. It feels like old-school Assassin’s Creed—blend into crowds, parkour across rooftops, and use the environment to your advantage. The assassinations are a lot of fun to pull off.3. Focused Story:The game follows Basim (you might remember him from Valhalla), and the story is much more tight and personal. It’s a straightforward, engaging plot without the massive bloat of side quests and grindy missions.4. Simple Progression:Gone are the overwhelming RPG elements. You don’t have to worry about grinding levels or a huge skill tree. The upgrade system is much simpler, which makes the game feel more accessible and keeps the focus on the action.5. Great Atmosphere:The sound, music, and voice acting all help create an immersive world. Whether you’re running across rooftops or walking through the crowded streets, the sound design really pulls you into the experience.What’s Not So Great:1. Smaller Scale:If you loved the gigantic open worlds in the last few Assassin’s Creed games, this one might feel a bit small. The world is more compact, and there aren’t as many side activities to do. That said, the tighter focus works well for this kind of game.2. Combat is Just Okay:While the stealth mechanics are solid, the combat isn’t very deep. It gets the job done, but it doesn’t have the complexity or challenge of some other action games. If you prefer fighting over sneaking, you might find the combat a bit repetitive.3. Minor Bugs:There are a few bugs and technical issues, like frame drops in busy areas or the occasional visual glitch. Nothing too serious, but it can be a bit distracting at times.4. Not Much New:Mirage is more of a return to basics than a game that introduces a lot of new stuff. It plays it safe, so if you’re looking for fresh ideas or big changes to the series, you might not find them here.Should You Play It?If you’ve been missing the older style of Assassin’s Creed, Mirage will feel like a breath of fresh air. It’s a shorter, more focused game that brings back the stealth and parkour we loved from the early days. However, if you prefer the giant open-world RPGs of recent games, this one might feel a bit too stripped down.Overall, it’s a solid return to form, but it’s not going to blow your mind with innovation. It’s great for a more focused, old-school assassin experience.Rating: 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Alright.  is done and dusted. Two things I think are particularly noteworthy when considering playing this game. First, although it definitely has aspects of a lot of previous titles in the series, Mirage has most in common with the original Assassin's Creed than the other titles from a gameplay perspective, but with a world design that has more in common with the latest trilogy. Nice blend there.Second is that while this game can definitely be played as a standalone, some aspects of the story will be lost on you if you haven't played Valhalla. On the other hand, if you have played Valhalla, there will be a few "Ohhhhh, that's why "x" happened the way it did in Valhalla" moments. It definitely serves to fill out some of the details that were vague about Basim and his motivations in Valhalla.So, with that out of the way, I thought the gameplay was tight in Mirage. There is still the ever-present danger of unintentional parkour as is the case in most Assassin's Creed games. You know how it goes. You accidentally walk into a crate and next thing you know, you are climbing something whether you want to or not. It can be particularly inconvenient at times and comical at other times. Another unintentional feature of Assassin's Creed games is getting stuck on random objects or not being able to climb something because your angle is not quite the way the game wants it to be. But otherwise, everything works as intended, and the sense of familiarity can feel like warm blanket. Something comfortable and satisfying.The writing is a mixed bag. Initially, the writing, and especially the dialogue, is very heavy handed and clunky, to the point where the emotions they're trying to convey were mostly lost on me. As the game progressed, the writing did get better, and by the end, the writing was actually quite good. I wouldn't say it ever reached the excellent tier, but it was good overall. Now, the actual overarching story, in contrast, was cool from start to finish. That was very well done.As a result, the voice acting takes a similar path of progression, from a bit wooden and clunky, to full on believable. And the voice actors themselves, once they warmed to their roles, were actually excellent. Additionally, the other audio really breathed life and helped craft a living breathing Baghdad and surrounding area. And the music was really cool, from the orchestral pieces to the street musicians. Everything was well done in that regard. There was however one weird thing of note. Most of the animals had the same audio track, a somewhat startling roar. Which is incredibly weird when it is an antelope, lol.The graphics were top tier. This game looks great. And despite being a more limited map than a lot of the series features, there were plenty of unique areas with their own unique presentation, which was nice. This game is definitely a screenshot archers dream, and there is a photo mode, which is something Ubisoft pretty much always gets right.The skill trees and equipment upgrades will be familiar to series vets. Nothing new here, although everything is useful in this iteration. One thing that did stand out was the token system. In order to receive special favors, you need faction tokens, and the appropriate token will net you things like shop discounts, information, reduced notoriety, hiring mercenaries, and so on. Tokens can be earned by doing faction quests, pickpocketed from people, etc...It took me about 33 hours to complete the story and do a fair amount of exploring, breaking and entering, and such, lol. And that was 33 hours well spent in my opinion. I had a great time playing through Basim's backstory, and it will be interesting to see if they continue to develop Basim as the modern-day character in future Assassin's Creed games. I wouldn't want to pay $50 for this, and definitely wouldn't buy the Deluxe Edition costume upgrade, lol, but for $25, this was a great game to buy and enjoy, which is what I did. And it's easy to recommend you do so as well, especially if you have already played Valhalla. Btw, you can pet cats in this game. Just thought you should know. :)

_childDocuments_.review: I would only recommend this game to Assassin's Creed fans or if its on a deep discount. What the game does well is what you would expect from Ubisoft and all other Assassin Creed entries such as the stealth and the open world which in this case happens to be the city of Baghdad. Sadly thats where the pros end and the cons begin. Basim is a boring protagonist plain and simple with very little that compels you to see his story through other than the moment to moment gameplay. The actual combat is the worst I have ever experienced in the Assassins Creed franchise. Its a janky mess somewhere inbetween valhalla and the parry combat styles of Assassins Creed one and two. Unlike the previous entries it lacks the depth of combat systems such as Valhalla, Odyssey or Origins and doesn't have the same cinematic feel and flow of the older entries such as one, two, three, Black Flag, Unity or Syndicate. What your left with is a combat systems that feels worse and looks worse than any other Assassin's Creed game by far. The movement system being built upon the bones of Valhalla is very prevalent here with Basim feeling slow, clunky, hard to control and the games parkour in general just lacking any sense of flow despite the city of Baghdad being designed around parkour and having plenty of opportunities to do so with how tightly woven and well designed the city truly is. If I had to describe Mirage in one word I would say its disappointing. Maybe not bad but just disappointing. Overall score 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: Assassin's Creed Mirage is like trying to make the best Lego construction by using playmobil. Utter compromised abomination. The main concept of Mirage is a "go back to roots" homage to the first Assassin's games, where the stealth and not the combat was the main focus of the game. However, they made it with ANVIL engine, an engine that is so animation based, that it all breaks apart in the first thirty minutes. Anvil is all about the animation and the spectacle, but lacks in precision. That could work with Odyssey and Valhalla where the combat was the main focus, but in Mirage where you want maximum precision in stealth and parkour it breaks badly. So you will have the clunky controls, falling through gaps, get stuck in the geometry, missing grabs, abruptly changing direction, missing the cover because the movement animation got you exposed and the lack of cover/corner mechanics. The battle (which the engine was made for) is bad, because it isn't the target of the game. So you have a game that could do battle well, but never does, and that does stealth badly but is all it wants to do. The story is mediocre, is too fast and too thin, mostly because it was supposed to be an expansion and not a full game. Once again, the lack of direction in narrative terms is obvious since, as many reviewer put it, the structure dictates the story and not the story that dictates the structure. The road to Hell is paved with good intentions. And this game has good intentions. But then Ubisoft being Ubisoft kicked in and produced this compromised abomination of a game.
