_childDocuments_.review: EDITS BELOW.I got it on sale for $25, but it's still not really worth it. I was expecting a bit of a return to form with the emphasis on parkour and stealth over outright combat, but then it drops you into a huge forced enemy encounter where you have to deal with their janky combat system and controls, conveniently just a bit after the 2-hour refund window closes. Also, the combat buttons are RB to attack, LB to parry, and... X to dodge??? I cannot convince my fingers to adapt to X being dodge, and I refuse to believe I'm the only one who feels this way. The parkour is also clunky, but less so than the combat. Most of the time I find myself frustrated when trying to descend with the B button, because it doesn't seem like there's a way to tell your character to jump down somewhere. It's either "press A to spring like a gazelle over the place you want to go" or "press B to do the slowest climb down imaginable, and only when the game feels like it". The end result is that I feel like I'm constantly fighting with the character like he's an unruly dog pulling on the leash in the wrong direction. The game is also buggy, and assassinating people frequently involves you floating weirdly over to them and then stabbing them in the knee for an instantaneous death. Faces look bad, haircuts look like a handful of ribbons, and they're still doing the thing where they replace random words with the in-setting language equivalent, which makes me think of the "just according to keikaku" meme. It feels like a budget title in the series, which isn't actually a bad thing, but $50 is not what I'd call "budget" pricing. If you're still interested in the game, do not under any circumstances pay full price for this game, I suspect it'll be on deep discount for basically every major sale going forward.It's been very frustrating to watch this series fall from grace, and I have to admit I was hoping that this would be more of a step in the right direction.EDIT:I'm gonna add some stuff as I notice it, because I'm too stubborn to just not play a game I don't like. This is a game that paper cuts you a lot and diminishes the overall experience as a result, and something that helped my experience immensely is just deleting the videos that play at startup from the game's install location. Having the game go right to the loading screen saves at least 20 seconds of previously-unskippable video playback, and prevents me from feeling annoyed before I even start playing the game. If that sounds dumb to you, I urge you to try it, and see if it doesn't make your experience better.I've beaten several milestone levels now, none of which really felt like boss fights or even especially hard skills tests. I'm starting to realize that they're not going to bother to set up any meaningful big bad or characterize anyone at all, even the protagonist. Basim is bland and very shallow, and I have no reason to care about him or his story without having played Valhalla (which I didn't play and didn't realize would be necessary in that way). This is definitely a Valhalla DLC that Ubisoft pawned off as a full game, and that makes some of the issues much more understandable, but also more noticeable. I suspect the prologue was added after the decision to make this a standalone game, because it's pretty lackluster in gameplay and has the most bare-minimum establishment of characters and story they could get away with. I don't think there will be any new enemy types beyond the four or five I've seen so far, and most of the time there's not much need to use any tools, other than throwing knives for solving certain puzzles. On that note, I like the environmental puzzles. They're fun, even if the gear rewards are basically useless. The gear system in general is WAY underutilized, and aside from getting slightly more damage, I mostly just treat new swords and daggers as new skins.

_childDocuments_.review: Assassin's Creed Mirage is Ubisoft's attempt to bring us back to the series' stealthy roots, but does it hit the mark? Eh, kinda.The story? Pretty mid. It’s there, it moves, but it’s not going to blow anyone away. Graphics are cool but nothing groundbreaking, not bad, but not exactly next-gen either. Honestly, it’s about time Ubisoft upgraded their engine. It’s starting to feel a bit dated.They tried to recapture the magic of the original Assassin’s Creed gameplay (movement and fighting), but instead, we get something choppy and unpolished. It’s a shame because the series usually nails this aspect.However, if you hated the bloated feel of the recent AC games, this might just be your thing. Mirage goes smaller, tighter, and stealthier, much more like the first game. A breath of fresh air in that regard.But for the full price? Hard pass. It’s fun for a few hours, sure, but it’s buggy, undercooked, and feels like Ubisoft’s focus is more on cosmetic skins than game mechanics. If they want the fans back, they need to start paying attention to the actual gameplay.Verdict: Fun, but not worth top dollar, grab it on sale if you’re feeling nostalgic.

_childDocuments_.review: Assassin's Creed Mirage masterfully transports players to the heart of the Middle East, capturing the rich culture and architectural beauty of 9th-century Baghdad. The game immerses you in a world where the bustling markets, intricate alleyways, and majestic mosques are brought to life with stunning detail. The soundtrack, influenced by traditional Middle Eastern music, adds to the authenticity, making you feel truly connected to the era. With its focus on stealth, parkour, and the rich historical backdrop of the Islamic Golden Age, AC Mirage not only delivers thrilling gameplay but also pays homage to the rich heritage of the region. It’s a perfect blend of action, history, and Middle Eastern charm, making it a standout in the series.

_childDocuments_.review: Assassin's Creed Mirage delivers exactly what fans of the classic games have been waiting for. From the moment I stepped into the vibrant streets of Baghdad, it felt like being back in the good old days, where parkour and stealth took center stage.You play as Basim, a character with a complex background and a determination that makes him incredibly engaging. He's smart, cunning, and his journey from a street thief to a feared assassin is truly compelling. His growth feels natural, and he brings back the classic "assassin mindset" – it's all about being discreet, tactical, and always having a plan.The story is gripping and keeps up the pace, though it’s on the shorter side compared to other recent titles. However, despite the shorter runtime, the experience is rich, and every moment feels carefully crafted. It's a game that respects your time and keeps you fully immersed from start to finish. For me, it was absolutely worth the price.Back to stealth and parkour: The focus on stealth and parkour is a great return to form. It feels like the classic Assassin's Creed we know and love.Authentic setting: Baghdad is beautifully crafted and feels alive with vibrant details and historical accuracy.Tight narrative: Even though the story is shorter than in other titles, it's well-paced and keeps you invested without unnecessary filler.No overwhelming RPG elements: I appreciated that the game dials back on the heavy RPG mechanics from recent installments and sticks to the basics.Short length: While the story is engaging, it feels a bit short compared to previous games in the series.Limited exploration: The map is smaller, and exploration doesn't feel as rewarding as in other Assassin’s Creed games with larger open worlds.AI inconsistencies: Sometimes, the enemy AI can feel inconsistent, with guards being either too easy to trick or unrealistically sharp.The gameplay is tight and focused, without the unnecessary RPG elements from the more recent titles. This is all about being a crafty assassin again – sneaking around, planning your strikes, and taking out enemies one by one.If, like me, you've missed the old Assassin's Creed, Mirage is a must-play. It feels like a loving tribute to what made the series great in the first place.

They force the story to go to an end point that they need it to reach, and they don't care if it's a good story that takes you there. _childDocuments_.review: (I bought it and refunded to write a review since I already have it on Ubisoft Connect)Most of the reviews show negativity in context to Ubisoft's overall reputation, not the game itself. Game is very well made as Bordeaux brought back the classic Assassin's Creed experience, (Parkour not so much). In contrast to AC Shadows slowly tearing Ubisoft apart, Mirage demonstrates what the company is capable of: Historical and cultural accuracy. Keep in mind that this game was planned to be a DLC for Valhalla so do not expect any major changes from the previous titles. Combat is horrible, stealth is improved, there are no boring missions and with each mission, we get to know more about our protagonist, Basim which I really like. Basim is a straightforward character to those who did not play Valhalla. Just a generic Assassin who wants to serve justice, a bit repetitious in my opinion. The character is a bit more enjoyable to those who have finished Valhalla. For the history geeks, the game offers a codex menu where it teaches the history of The Round City as well as the everyday life of an Iraqi citizen in the 9th century Baghdad7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Read this if you want honest review of someone with AC Odyssey background I would rate this game 2 / 10 AC Mirage falls short on almost every front when compared to Odyssey. Right away, I noticed that there’s only one mercenary targeting you in Mirage, which just feels empty. In Odyssey, four mercenaries could be on your trail at once, making every fortress raid tense and unpredictable. You’d be taking on captains and polemarchs, only to have high-level mercenaries jump in. And Mirage has stripped out the level mechanic, along with any real progression system. In Odyssey, you’d stumble upon ruins or tombs, solve enigmas, and level up by collecting loot and finishing objectives—there’s none of that here. You can’t even loot. Weapons racks, pots, and shelves would yield swords, bows, or daggers matching your level in Odyssey. Here? Nothing.Combat is a mess. One successful parry leads to an automatic kill, which gets boring fast, and there’s no critical assassination to give you that well-planned one-shot against tough enemies. And then there’s the stamina bar—just feels restrictive and pointless, adding frustration without depth. Meanwhile, higher-level enemies in Odyssey would be marked with a red skull, signaling a serious challenge. Touch them unprepared, and you’d be taken out with a single hit. Mirage lacks that sense of danger.The map size is disappointing, about 20% of what Odyssey offered, with Baghdad as the only setting, and it lacks the variety or thrill of exploration that made Odyssey’s world feel alive. What’s worse, you can’t even build your playstyle. In Odyssey, you could choose to be an assassin, fighter, or archer, customizing your approach. Here, they’ve gone “back to roots” in a way that just makes the game feel stripped down.Overall, Mirage was a waste of 1300 INR, and I ended up deleting it. If this is Ubisoft’s idea of returning to the series’ roots, they’ve completely missed the mark.

_childDocuments_.review: ("In my opinion") One of the best AC games hands down. Ubi Bordeaux NEEDS to be given another AC project with a bigger budget.Edit: I added the "In my opinion" cause I realized this is Assassin's Creed we're talking about and saying which game is the best is very divisive here.I'm also going to add some more info/points about the gameThe World: for me it's probably the best this franchise has seen. Baghdad is beautiful and lively. It feels perfectly crafted for an Assassins Creed game while still being very historically grounded even though the devil were working with very limited information about it since what we see in the game does not exist anymore.Parkour: the more I dive into it the more I'm loving it, it honestly feels like the best variation of this system that we had since like 2012/2013. Unity kinda ruined the feel of the parkour and it seems like the devs are slowly (very) trying to actually make it work. Hopefully Shadows improves it even more (wishful thinking since its world might not be as well designed for parkour as Mirage's)Combat: it's very very simple and it gets the job done. Nothing crazy about it but it definitely is NOT clunky, just simple and easy but still working as intended 99% of the time (you might find and occasional bug I guess)Stealth: Great stealth is something we've been lacking for a long time in this franchise and Mirage is making huge step to bring back the greatness of AC stealth. Adding many tools to your advantage which greatly improves the experience. The game is definitely mostly designed around stealth and that's why the combat system is so simple, you're not really meant to interact with it that much. If you think the game is too easy, try a permadeath run on the Master Assassin difficulty. You'll need to do way more thinking and planning if you want to pull it off.Lastly there's the story: it's great in the beginning and the end (especially while knowing what's coming for Basim) but the middle of the game is more like a sandbox that doesn't progress Basim's journey all that much. Still to me it's very enjoyable because of the core gameplay and the world around it.The game is a lot shorter than the previous 3 entries. Take that as you will, some love it because of that and some hate it because of that - that's the Assassin's Creed way.

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed Valhalla, Odyssey, and Origins - all fantastic games, each a masterpiece in their own right. However, Mirage was, and I do not mean this lightly, a demotivating struggle and a disappointment all around - expect for the graphics.As with the the Big 3 AC games as I've listed them, Mirage's graphics were genuinely beautiful. The world was wonderful, full of life and color and culture. But that's where the good ends. The combat was stagnant and not at all intuitive. The moves did not flow, both dodging and parrying were God awful, and both health and stamina run out far too quickly. As well, health does NOT regenerate outside of combat.Skill points are few and far between as leveling is not based on experience -- that is, the concept of "experience" in Mirage is nonexistent as killing animals/enemies and completing side quests earns you nothing, like, absolutely nothing -- and so skill points are ONLY gained from completing Main Quest missions. Which might be fine for certain players, but for those players like me who charge off in the opposite direction at the first opportunity to explore and conquer the world before ever starting the Main Quest Mirage's lack of leveling outside the Main Quest quite literally makes venturing off into the """"open world"""" without reward or fun for no matter how much you accomplish you will never level up outside of the Main Quest.In the same tone, Mirage has introduced a concept so limiting to the player experience I am absolutely shocked it made it through production: certain chests require special coins to open them. Imagine exploring outside the parameters of the Main Quest and coming across a chest that requires a special coin to open it, only thing is that coin is only given to you by completing events in the Main Quest. Once again, the """"open world"""" concept is defeated.And I know I'm nitpicking with this one, but Basim's eagle, Enkidu. might as well not even exist in this game they're so useless without Main Quest-earned skill point upgrades. Enkidu is about one-millionth of a percent as helpful as start-of-game Sýnin in Valhalla. ---TLDR; Hard pass! Devolved UI, choppy combat, and lack of true open world makes Mirage a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ disappointment I'm furious I paid $22 for and wasted 8 hours on.

_childDocuments_.review: Stepping away from the former RPG titles, Mirage brings back classic AC gameplay where patience and precision are everything. The level designs encourage creativity, with multiple paths, environmental traps, and plenty of opportunities to blend into crowds. And it gives you time, mostly, to think and strategize carefully before you strike -- especially with the help of Enkidu. Combat is alright. You've got fewer weapon options and a greater focus on dodges and counters. While the variety of enemy types is limited, thankfully, there's no XP or level-gated enemies. Additionally, the notoriety system makes a welcome return, adding a layer of tension that keeps you immersed.For me and my nerdy heart, the true star of Mirage is Baghdad itself. As always, the devs have really put their whole heart and soul in carefully recreating a city to feel alive and intricately detailed (a la Unity or Syndicate). Visually and sound-wise, it is a masterpiece. The vibrant colors and intricate details bring Baghdad to life, from sunlit rooftops to bustling bazaars. Pair this with phenomenal music and voice acting, and it’s a feast for the senses. On the narrative front, Mirage finally gives fans insight into Basim’s enigmatic character after his initial appearance in Valhalla. The game connects threads left untied, offering glimpses into his past and motivations. However, I found myself wanting even more from Basim’s arc, especially given his intriguing role in Valhalla. While Mirage works as a standalone, its ending and connection to the Isu storyline are best appreciated by fans familiar with previous titles.Despite some brevity in character development, Mirage delivers a focused, stealth-driven experience that masterfully balances nostalgia with fresh gameplay. It’s a stunning homage to the golden age of the franchise and a compelling narrative bridge for fans. A must for AC fans. new and old!

_childDocuments_.review: Assassin's Creed Mirage ReviewAssassin’s Creed Mirage brings a refreshing return to the classic Assassin’s Creed formula. Set in 9th-century Baghdad, the game captures the city’s vibrant history, architecture, and culture. It’s a more compact, story-driven game than recent titles, and it’s clear the developers prioritized accuracy in representing Arab culture, which enhances the immersion.As a fan, you’ll appreciate how Ubisoft has crafted Baghdad’s neighborhoods, blending historical accuracy with adventure. The bustling streets, marketplace sounds, and people’s clothing reflect thoughtful attention to detail, creating an authentic atmosphere. From the flowing robes to the Arabic phrases and traditional structures, it feels like a respectful tribute to Arab culture.Pros and ConsPros:Authentic Atmosphere: The city’s design and cultural details are accurate and engaging, making players feel immersed in the world.Return to Stealth and Parkour: The game leans back into classic stealth mechanics and fluid parkour, adding a nostalgic touch for long-time fans.Focused Storyline: Shorter and more focused than recent Assassin’s Creed entries, with an emphasis on the journey of Basim, the main character.Beautiful Graphics and Sound: From vibrant lighting to ambient sounds, the game does well in creating a visually and sonically rich world.Cons:Limited Open World: Some players might feel constrained as the map is smaller and less open than recent Assassin’s Creed games.Simplified Combat: The combat mechanics feel basic compared to previous titles, which might make it feel repetitive over time.Few Side Activities: Those who enjoyed the variety of missions in previous games might find the side content lacking.Short Length: The game’s shorter story may be a drawback for players looking for an extended experience.I would recommend the game when its ONLY on discount.

_childDocuments_.review: Assassin's Creed Mirage is a breathtaking return to the roots of the franchise, blending the beloved stealth and parkour mechanics with fresh new elements that keep players completely captivated. What's more, the meticulous and masterful craftsmanship in capturing the historical essence of the era transforms this game into a veritable work of art—a breathtaking journey through time that immerses players deeply into the heart of ancient Baghdad.From the dazzling architecture to the rich ambient sounds that fill the bustling streets, Mirage creates an immersive experience that feels both vast and intimate. The game’s refined combat and stealth systems make every encounter pulse with tension. You can seamlessly leap across rooftops, blend into crowds, and execute precise, exhilarating assassinations. Each mission brings a new challenge that demands skill and strategic planning, rewarding players with a sense of mastery.Visually, Assassin’s Creed Mirage is a masterpiece. The cityscape, with its warm hues and intricate details, is brought to life with extraordinary fidelity. The storyline is equally compelling, filled with political intrigue and characters who feel genuine and complex, making every decision impactful. For fans of the series and newcomers alike, this game offers an experience that is not just a journey through history but a thrill ride that pushes the boundaries of immersive storytelling. _childDocuments_.review: Eh, so, AC Mirage.Pros:> Main assassinations were pretty good and very engaging.> Mechanically did feel like an older AC title like 1 or 2, but far less clunky.> Story was pretty damn good, full stop, but that's always a matter of opinion, your mileage may vary.> Even though I kind of already knew the main twist of the ending, still managed to keep things interesting.> Tools were very nice, and I found myself inevitably using all of them, which is good, since some older games I had a tendency to just spam the dart gun and ignore everything else.Cons:> Way too damn short. I missed being able to hunt whole gigantic cults of people. The current number was not satisfying, to say the least.> Side contracts felt near pointless to complete. Were it not for extraneous equipment upgrades being locked behind them, you could ignore them entirely. The strange attempt at a story through some of them was placid at best.> The weapon and armor choices that were offered were cosmetically quite nice, but mechanically not encouraging to use or even experiment with, due to either overly polarized stats or mediocre benefits. At most, I changed up my dagger the one time and kept it that way, but none of the swords or armor offered any benefits or advantages I felt inclined to utilize, so I just stuck with the starter sword and armor the entire game, rejecting every new choice available, to my dismay. Feels like the devs were too afraid of making something overpowered. > Ending relied a bit too much on someone having played AC Valhalla to understand it in full. A newcomer would be completely confused and annoyed.> Certain items were locked behind post-game. Items that realistically should not have been, considering most of it is cosmetic, and also considering the status of the equipment I mentioned above.----Overall, good game, can't say it was ever worth full price, though. Valhalla tried and did pretty good in its own right, but hard to fill the shoes of a titan like Odyssey, or even Origins.I'd say to newcomers of the series: Feel free to play it, just don't expect any sort of explanation on the more outlandish elements. _childDocuments_.review: What to say about Mirage... It's like one step forward three steps back.On one hand we were told this was a return to form and at face value it does indeed seem to be the case but then you have mixed systems that are shallow, gutted and incredibly boring as a result. For one we have "RPG elements" such as a talent system but no experience system to get skill points - from my understanding in the first three hours you get skill points tied to story progression. This makes the risk/reward system completely moot. Why bother killing/knocking out anyone if you don't get experience to build toward a skill point? If you do a story mission you get a skill point. No matter what you do during the mission or outside of the mission you don't progress your character at all bar bland equipment.Then we have the notoriety system - it's like a three strike rule. If you get seen by a civilian killing a guard or an enemy you get an instant mark against your character where you get patrols looking for you and on the third strike an elite patrol spawning in to find you. So now not only do you have to keep an eye out for threats(actual enemies) but you have to keep an eye out for civilians who stand in place in every area. Very, VERY bad system to implement and I have ZERO idea why the devs decided to introduce this system. There was no need to introduce something that is anti-fun like this. Now I'm going around an enemy camp worrying about being spotted by a neutral NPC I can't interact with, distract, wait for them to move because I'll be punished for taking out actual enemies.The game is also very buggy. So far in my three hours of play I've regularly experienced issues such as: 1. Not being able to dismount from my mount - the option to dismount just isn't there and they key input is not registered, 2. Not being able to open doors - the icon is on the door but the key press is not registering and 3. Meeting NPC's to progress the story does not progress even when they are on front of you. Each time any of these issues have happened it's required a reload. I've never come across something quite so buggy in a very long time.The only saving grace from the bugs is that the game runs very well. No stutters, there's a high smooth framerate, the game genuinely plays well.Graphically the game looks dated. Character models are not good. Period. Character models look worse than character models from six or seven years ago. Your equipment floats by your character's side and the equipment doesn't connect to anything on your character. It's fairly bad. The scenery looks decent but everything else does not look great.The parkour is a bit of a mixed bag. Recent AC games have done this where trying to parkour up and forward is fluid but trying to drop and parkour downward is delayed and requires more of a conscious effort. I can only guess the idea of this is that in most cases the player wants to travel up instead of down and the devs made the parkour movement down require a bit of a longer press to confirm the player actually wants to parkour down - it doesn't feel great and is very jarring as a result.Honestly, at first it felt this game would be fun but after getting into the meat of it it's not fun at all. Notoriety system should be done away with - they should have given an option to turn this off at this point. It's stupid, a waste of time and makes areas that should be fun very unfun. The solution to lowering notoriety? Either pay to reset it or roam around randomly ripping up wanted posters - really bad micro game design that's just a complete waste of time.Skills system is terrible and should be done away with if there is no experience system in place.Parkour is so and so and, personally, the setting is interesting and something I would like to see more of but there's just too many downsides to this game.I can't recommend this game. If you're looking for a good game in the series just play the older ones. Assassin's Creed Unity, Syndicate, Origins and Odyssey are all very good games if you're new to the series. If you're an old school AC fan then unfortunately you're just going to have to come to terms with the fact that the series is not going to be as good as it once was.

_childDocuments_.review: Bad points first: The story kind of sucks. The assassin's plot line is straightforward and lacks most of the suspenseful prolonged conclusion most AC titles offer. It's sufficient to keep you playing, but nothing particularly noteworthy.  The Isu plot line was worse (and this is from someone who actually liked the Isu plotline from the Desmond games).  It may be better if you recently completed Valhalla, but if you're playing this on Steam 2-3+ years after playing Valhalla, you probably don't remember Valhalla's ending well enough for Mirage's ending to make any sense.  That ends up being a pretty big let down given how much the overall plot line builds toward it.  (One point in the story's favor - the twist is well hinted at and falls into place nicely when it's supposed to.)Story aside, I'd still recommend this game for anyone who enjoyed pre-Odyssey Assassin's Creed titles, especially the Ezio trilogy. The game does a great job returning to the more traditional gameplay while pulling in some of the more modern quality of life improvements.  (I was irritated that there are still enemies you can't assassinate with any amount of stealth, falling back to a "stealth attack" instead, but at least there's only one infrequently appearing generic enemy and one storyline assassination target.)  The parkour is fun as always, the assassination missions take a more modern free-form puzzle-solving approach while still rewarding creativity, and the stealth gameplay is still more of an extra reward for success than a strict necessity.  Being stealthy definitely makes the game easier, but while Basim isn't quite as OP as Ezio, he can still certainly kill 10 enemies who have detected him instead of running away if that's your preference.Overall, I think this game is worthwhile, particularly if you enjoyed the older AC titles and/or can pick it up on sale. 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Assassin's Creed Mirage brings a refreshing return to the series' roots with an emphasis on traditional stealth mechanics, engaging storytelling, and streamlined gameplay. Fans of the series who found the RPG-heavy elements of recent titles a bit too much will appreciate Mirage's commitment to simplicity. It’s an Assassin’s Creed game that doesn’t require constant weapon upgrades or leveling up to progress through the story.Mirage has a straightforward focus on the world of assassins. The narrative is gripping, drawing players into a story that manages to capture the intrigue and mystery fans love without getting bogged down by unnecessary distractions. From start to finish, the game feels like a genuine tribute to the older AC titles, striking a balance between classic and modern Assassin’s Creed gameplay elements.While it's not the best entry in the series, Mirage is far from disappointing. It shines as a solid, standalone title that lets you focus purely on the main story without forcing you into countless side quests. You can play the entire game with your starting weapon, which feels like a nod to old-school fans who miss the days of simpler, skill-based progression.In conclusion, Assassin's Creed Mirage is a refreshing blend of nostalgia and innovation, delivering an assassin-focused experience that both veteran fans and new players can enjoy. It’s a solid addition to the franchise that stays true to the spirit of Assassin’s Creed while making a few modern tweaks. If you’re looking for a pure, stealth-driven Assassin’s Creed game, Mirage is definitely worth a try!

Why does Basim care about templars or the assassins? What really motivates him? There is no backstory, no context to our protagonist's actions or motivations. First 2/3 rd's of the game we are just a hired killer going around killing targets. The story doesnt get good until after the last leg of the story. Faces look horrible, which is a surprise as the rest of the game looks really beautiful. But it can be excused given that this game was initially a DLC for Valhalla. The voice acting and script just goes to a 100 in the last 2-3hrs of the story, which just grips you in.The gameplay is actually quite good, only bad thing being the parkour, which is the buggiest, most jankiest thing I have had to deal with in quite some time now. The setting is beautiful, Baghdad ranks as one of the best AC settings for me. Its the one game where I rarely use fast travel. _childDocuments_.review: Game Review: A Return to Assassin's Creed RootsFor those who miss the tight, grounded feel of the original Assassin's Creed games, the latest release offers a nostalgic dive back to where it all began. With this entry, Ubisoft has trimmed down the vast open-world mechanics and RPG layers that recent titles were known for, bringing us something refreshingly familiar. In fact, this installment is the shortest Assassin’s Creed game I’ve played, but in the best way possible.Gone are the exhaustive quest lists and endless maps; instead, the game hones in on core gameplay elements reminiscent of Assassin’s Creed 1 and 2. The parkour feels intuitive, the stealth mechanics make a big comeback, and even the story delivers with a focused, personal tale that’s all about the creed.For anyone looking to revisit the roots of the series—when it was all about lurking in the shadows, planning assassinations, and executing them with style—this game is a perfect pick. It’s not a sprawling RPG adventure but a compact, well-paced experience that truly pays homage to Assassin’s Creed’s origins.

Although similar to many AC games the quest is engaging and fun and the Brotherhood, in the case The Hidden Ones again, feels alive in this world. The new tokens and pick-pocketing system as well as the more engaging and fun side quests make Baghdad a world worth exploring. I love that there is no level up system or hundreds of weapons and armor to collect but rather the game focuses on upgrading a solid few options given throughout the game as you progress. I wouldn't have bothered writing a review if I didn't enjoy the game as much as I have and thought that other old school AC fans would enjoy it too. Verdict: Recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed Odyssey and Valhalla, so when I heard that Mirage would be smaller, I was a bit sceptical. I will say though, that when I finished those other two, I was a little fatigued and needed a break from AC. In contrast, after finishing the main story of Mirage in about 35 hours or so (yes, I take my time), I felt like having a go at NG+ to see if I could find the bits I had missed. Halfway through that second round, I feel it's time to leave a review to balance out some of the unfair criticism.This is the first AC game where I've felt the emphasis is really on stealth from the very beginning, for the simple reason that combat is a lot more involved and being outnumbered really means something. In my first playthrough, there were a few encounters where I thought the game was forcing a combat approach but armed with some more knowledge about the surroundings, my second playthrough has so far been 100% stealthy. It also helps that I have some more tools and skills at my disposal, obviously. Even the bits that seem to force you into combat can be turned to your advantage with a few dirty tricks. I get to that wonderful state where the game becomes clay and I am the sculptor, carefully picking off the enemies one by one. Maybe, just maybe, I'll have a go at the permakill option and the highest difficulty level for my third playthrough.Technically, I've had zero(!) crashes, no memorable glitches and the game world feels authentic with just the right mix of dense city and open terrain to explore. There's really nothing negative that stands out once you get over the pointless Connect launcher that Ubisoft still insists on putting between us and their games. If you enjoyed the previous AC games, there's no reason you won't also enjoy this one, because in my opinion they've refined all the good parts while cutting or improving the annoying ones.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed playing Assassin's Creed Mirage. It is not as long as Origins, Odyssey or Valhalla. All of which I enjoyed. For comparison, my first play-throughs (obviously, it may vary individually): Origins: 113 hours (100%)Odyssey: 206 Hours (100%)Valhalla: 316 Hours (90%)Mirage: 50 Hours (100%)It doesn't bother me that it is shorter. Sometimes I want a longer game. Sometimes I want a shorter game. Mirage also has less RPG elements than the last three games. It feels like a middle-ground between the older games and the newer games. For me, that was neither a Pro or Con because I started at Origins (I have played some of the games before that, but I don't have rose tinted nostalgia towards the older games that some do). I enjoyed exploring 9th century Baghdad, stabbing people, setting them on fire, sneaking up and assassinating people etc.  The controls and mechanics aren't difficult to get used to.I only encountered one amusing bug where a dead body convulsed for a bit before flying off. I would recommend Assassin's Creed Mirage.

_childDocuments_.review: I 100%ed this game to tell you that it is genuinely not worth the price for the amount of content in the game. This is a clear step backwards in the series. The only way this game is returning to the roots of Origins is because the game is buggy, god awful sound design, and the animations are so floaty there is no gratifying feeling of autonomy. I tried to engage with the game the way the developers intended, but the developers are overworked and understaffed so it was genuinely a miserable playing experience because there wasn't enough time or resources given to make a polished game. The first thing I noticed when I played the game, was the fact that the animations were not responsive to the keys I press. Genuinely just as bad, if not worse than Origins, because the two games in between didn't really have these issues. Like they remove the bow, so you can't stockpile long ranged assassination tools, and it doesn't matter cus the map is so small, you won't be having long ranged assaults anyways. But the fact that you can one shot literally every enemy in the game makes it such a non-threat that before I even played the game I selected the hardest difficulty knowing full well it was not going to matter. The DLC adds a weapon that makes combat trivial. All you have to do is parry once, and then the enemy gets set on fire and they stop attacking you as they flail around. I genuinely don't know what they were thinking. The combat is genuinely some of the worst. They added a stamina system which you can't upgrade. This is not a 1v1 game. You are fighting multiple enemies if the stamina ever comes into play, the game wants you to run away, or rather forces you because you dont have the stamina to keep up. Not to mention how quick animations fly, that half the time you can't react, or even if you do, the game is so poorly optimized that the choreography doesn't sync with the hit and hurt boxes. And that's not me being bad. There is so much snapping when it comes to animation. The game will arbitrarily position an enemy several paces forward from where they landed their attack so even back stepping or backrolling, which you seem to have no control which you do, twice, will still cause the enemy to land their hit. Or just rolling into an unparryable attack somehow makes you immune to the damage. Or like if you don't parry a parryable attack the enemy can chain multiple attacks which is stupid. The parkour element of this game is also dogsh*t. The interaction triggers are lazy. And even if the game trains you that certain textures are scalable, they intentionally misleading. You can't scale castle walls, but there are certain parts with exposed brick which you are supposed to be able to scale. The game reuses this texture in other places, yet despite this, you cannot scale all of these textures. Same goes for bricks jutting out of houses or towers. Sometimes there is a clear brick you should be able to grab and the game does not see it. Or how finicky the game is that in order to go to the left you have to go all the way right around a pole in order to scale up which is ret*rded. So many times I just get stuck on an object and I can't climb down or jump off. There are so many small props on the ground that if you walk over a sack of flower you can't walk off like you walked onto it and have to jump off for no reason. Or better yet, the game being inconsistent on whether you were crouched or not before vaulting over a wall. There have been so many times where I just want to pop over a wall and fall in the foliage on the other side but the game decides, "you wanted to be standing straight up right so the enemy can see you?" ret*rded. Don't even get me on the AI. The AI is genuinely a step back. The AI cannot traverse the map. There are so many places where you can get to, and they can't follow and immediately lose you. While other times there are areas where it doesn't matter how well you are stealthy, for whatever reason, even if you are hidden, the AI will just spot you from a safe distance away. If you hire Mercenaries to kill guards, the guards they kill, respawn, while you are in the area you are exploring. If you are doing a story mission, and you decide you want to go the PVE route instead of the espionage route, the game will respawn enemies the moment you turn your back. I have killed the same npc 5 seperate times during a mission because they are positioned at a choke point. And it's beyond retarded because their corpse is still there and its the same model. Which is another thing. NPCs don't give a sh*t if you kill in front of them. Their reaction speed is so slow. Or they are so nonchalant, They don't care. It's mystifying to me that they decided that in addition to NPCs being ret*rded. You needed a smoke bomb which makes all npcs inside forget you exist, allowing you to drop a smoke bomb at you feet while charging into a group, and allow you to chain assassinate everybody in the smoke and leave before NPCs path over and discover the bodies. Shouldn't they be alarmed that everyone is dead? Shouldn't they go into high alert when the POI is assassinated? There are so many times where NPCs just commit suicide investigating a murder. They jump off a high place and take fall damage and die, or just get themselves stuck on a platform that not even I can access without getting stuck. It's abysmal how bad their pathing and AI routes are. Like you can stab and grab someone from a hay bale, and their partner doesn't care. What's the point of having duos wander together if they can't even have object permanance or care their partner mysteriously vanishes. Godforbid you actually add upgrades or skills that add new ways to play the game. You add swords and daggers that basically don't do anything interesting since you're limited on stamina. And you add armor that either muffles the sound of assassinations or your movement but it doesn't matter because NPCs are deaf because the devs didn't program the sound of a body falling, yet alone pots breaking. Like genuinely, how did they mess up weight. Bodies and objects used to have WEIGHT when you THREW THEM. Bodies float. They're like feathers. They make sounds like you dropped a pen or a blanket instead of a f*cking corpse. You have to be sh*tting me. Odyssey was such a good game aside from the DLC's why the f*ck did they go, "yeah let's re-release Origins without fixing the bugs. When they could've done another Odyssey. This game doesn't even have 30 hours of content in it. Most of my playtime is d*cking around to see all the bugs of magically respawning enemies, or the fact the horses have magic hitboxes and send explosive pots flying with incredible velocity and seeing just how much I could mess with an npc until they jumped off a ledge and died. You can beat the game 10 hours or less. The side content is non existant. There's no fun challenges.Other than like contracts which are mandatory to get skill points to unlock skills. Genuinely, "don't kill anyone" is such a sh*t is such a terrible objective. The game forces you to kill people, You have no nonlethal options other than gadgets. Odyssey, you could knock people out. This game forces you to kill after the prologue. You can not be force me into stealth in a mission where all of the stealth routes except 1 is blocked off, and you have to carry somebody constantly sneezing and alerting the guards to my position constantly.I have so much more to complain about but you have to keep these things "consise" Play a different game. Poorly optimized, Terrible AI, floaty animations, inconsistent level design, lazy back and forth gameplay, nothing special or new that makes it stand out as unique from the other games. Literally, I mean genuinely, copy and pasted Origins and did NOTHING, and I mean NOTHING new.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd like to start by saying that whilst I have enjoyed the new gameplay direction of AC post-Origins, it has been incredibly refreshing to play a game that has returned to it's stealthy roots (Including the return of the meme-worthy tailing missions from the Ezio era). Baghdad is a fantastic (albeit small) map, with a heavy focus on parkour to traverse the city. The streets always feel bustling with NPCs, there are plenty of opportunities for stealth and hiding around every corner, and it was nice to see the return of posters to remove notoriety. Most immersive city setting in an AC game since Paris/London in Unity/Syndicate so I will give it high praise.While Mirage still has some of the clunky parkour and RPG-style combat (BUT heavily toned down from the powers of the previous 3 titles), it's main focus for accomplishing missions is stealth. You can fight your way out of every situation, however 3 hits will kill you and your "health potions" are limited to a total of 3 by late game. I won't pretend that this is Dark Souls type of difficult, but I appreciate Ubisoft making an attempt to find a balance between the two combat mechanics that the franchise has seen over the past two decades.The negatives however. As I said earlier, parkour is clunky af. Running feels slow and sluggish (for a protagonist who is 20 I think the game says). Assassination animations are slow. It's not game ruining, but it DID kinda put a dent in the vibe of being a sleek killing machine.Other issue I had with the game is that it's SHORT for an AC title. Now while being a short game in itself isn't necessarily a crime, charging £45 for what is essentially a 24-30 hour story is NOT worth it imo. I was fortunate to get it during a sale, so definitely keep a look out for that.Either way. Super refreshing experience. Slightly flawed but nothing that ruins the experience. Solid 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game, good graphics, and it runs well. Solid action/stealth game all-in-all. The gist of the concept for this one is that it is set in Baghdad during the 900s (I think? it might be the late 800s; have to fact-check that, but...meh, it is around that time lol) during the time of the Abbasid Caliphate. And it's kind of like they took the folk character of Aladdin and were just like, "What if we re-imagine him to be recruited by the Hidden Ones?" In a weird way, too, kinda reminiscent of the original Mafia game, where you're a taxi driver or w/e, and the mob ends up recruiting you. Either way, I like it.Nice throwback to the old style of Ass Creed games too. No enemy levels, no "mmo-lite vibes" to the game design etc. Just you, your gear and your wits versus your targets. It's a smaller world than something like Odyssey of course, but it's still a relatively large map with plenty of side quests, weapons to upgrade, and secrets to root out while you gank the Temp-sorry-Order dudes for the main story. I have really enjoyed it, and I would recommend it if you hadn't bothered picking it up until it was on Steam, like me.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd wish I could give this a  rating review. For it's a relatively decent assassination game with a lot flaws that I'd like to address for any potential buyers in the future. Anyway!Assassin's Creed Mirage is another game franchise title with the same formula as its predecessors. Though, the main course this game has to offer is that it is short and sweet, and DEFINITELY not worth the money Ubisnot is offering you.  Do keep in mind, if you're interested, get it on sale like I did!Assassin's Creed Valhalla was already the last straw for me, beating the already dead horse and milking this franchise dry towards a total unworthy experience. Vikings are a historical interest of mine all my life, and Ubisnore made its gameplay so unforgivably boring and uninspired, that I don't remember a single thing from that game at all...In comparison to the previous titles, Mirage is a short game, which isn't altogether "positive". Though, the great city of Baghdad is big and it's easy to get lost, and it's admirable that it still offers you a certain scale of feeling you're really there. To be almost immersed in the streets of the poor, or the big Bazaar, merchant stands with wares and perfumes... Pickpocketing the rich and use it for your own benefit. It's really just another game to turn your brain off and relax a bit, which is probably not really what the average gamer is looking for, meaning it caters to a much lesser audience. Those are the only positives I can provide for now, up to the next topics...Don't worry, I won't spoil anything. But, it's not good at all. You're not missing anything! Characters are forgettable, some characters are annoying to listen to... No heart... No soul story. Dull and bland like cheap perfume, and Ax deodorant. It's clear as soapy bathwater that making a story was not on the planning at Oophbisoft HQ!On a personal note: I must admit, if  didn't add any achievements for this game, I'd probably skipped this title completely. They also added them for Valhalla and I might give it another shot in the far future if I really have nothing better to do, which is rare in my case.On the other hand, the achievements are very doable for any completionist out there, I got everything in 35.5 hours of playtime. Most of them are very easy to obtain, and some of them are not hard, but pretty annoying. Small tip, get  as soon as possible, as it is damn near impossible to obtain it if you pickpocketed any quest related NPCs.For a short game, it has a HUGE map. You mostly play within the walls of Baghdad, but there's a whole empty wilderness out there with nothing interesting going on.Chests, historical , artifacts, enigmas and lost books... I don't have time for chests give me ass, the orbs are out there but do I really need to invest time and effort to parkour my way there? Pickpocketing artifacts is way too easy if you've got quick reflexes, lost books are quest related... Enigmas? ENIGMAS! How the HECK are you suppose to solve them without a guide!? From crude drawings that bring you to the edge of the wilderness, to cryptic text that brings you nowhere... For completionists, you need to collect them all and solve ONE enigma if you want 100%Guards getting on your ass? Can't do any crimes without anyone looking? Woe to you, you're going to get a bounty on your head. The higher your bounty, a Shakiriyya will come looking for you, a bloodthirsty bloodhound, an Arab bounty hunter if you will. Defeating them is quite a challenge, once defeated and your bounty fades away completely like a camel's fart in the desert's wind.If that's not your thing... You can rip wanted posters off the wall, OR you can pay up services of a Mu'lin to clear your bounty altogether!Other than the Mu'lin, there're other services you can buy with the help of tokens you gain from completing mission or pickpocketing NPCs. You can lower the prices from Merchants (up to 30% off), you can buy musicians to distract the guards, you can buy groups of merchants to masquerade you past the guards unnoticed, and you can buy the assistance of mercenaries to fend off any guards nearby in combat.Available at any Hidden Ones bureau, you can do contracts to gain coins, tokens and components. Win a little extra if you perfect a mission by completing a random optional objective, like no killing, stay undetected, etc. Though, the extra reward is small, it's a challenge worth doing. It's way more fleshed out compared to missions in let's say Odyssey, that's for sure! However after some time you've seen it all, done it all, and it becomes repetitive.More like upgrading gear to level 3, with 3 kinds of components, one "rarer" than the other. I did not bother at all with this feature, since the upgraded gear adds so little benefit behind progressing the story.Perks are decent, not too shabby, though not all too interesting. Tools on the other hand are way more interesting and helps a great deal in the whole sneaking around and avoiding combat. Not a whole lot of variety, but it's better than nothing. Blowdarts to put guards asleep or make them berserk and throw a temper tantrum, throwing knives for quick workarounds, noisemakers, traps, smoke bombs... Surely makes the whole ordeal a tat more enjoyable.Now this is where I get a little pissed off...Deluxe edition... Master edition... At the end of the day it's extra wasted hard-earned money on a bunch of useless, crappy micro-transactions. From gold skins to the overpowered Fire Demon Pack that makes the whole gameplay way too easy from an already short game overall. Like, mount and eagle skins? Who'd cares!?And to wrap this up, the Ubischeiße store has an unlockable, bug-riddled quest related to the legendary Ali Baba and it's broken from the start, at least, for me it was. Which is too bad, it could've been good quest that's I didn't got to complete... So more left-over slob thrown in the feeding troughs, ready to feed the camel customers.I'm personally really fed-up with the waste of money editions that Ubislob has to offer, and I'm definitely pulling points away for the end rating!Even after ♥♥♥♥ talking the game... It's after many titles, finally a decent assassination game again (sort of), but adding a bunch of cool and interesting new features is not the case in Mirage. If by any means this review did not help you, and you're after all this still in any way interested, get this game on sale since it's, again, very short for an Assassin's Creed title. Ubi got way too soft and played it very, VERY safe this time around. Safe doesn't bring potential greatness, but as crazy as it sounds... I'd still recommend it for the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10, the game itself and story are good, but the combat is atrocious. Sometimes the game just freezes up, I press click to attack or Q to parry, nothing happens. Also at one point I assassinated a guy, the guy somehow survived with 3/4 health and then just killed me as my character stood there as I was spam clicking to attack. If it's gonna be a true old style Assassin's Creed game, except for bosses assassinate should always insta-kill. Also this won't have any standing on the score but the fact ledge assassinations aren't a thing is unfortunate. I whistled to draw a guard over, Basim just hung at the ledge like "hey, how's it going?". But I get canonically why this wasn't a thing so it doesn't matter.Stealth portions really lend to the fact you're an assassin again, unlike more recent open world variants. I just wish the combat wasn't so frustrating in the fact it feels super unfair when you're trying to attack and you just stand there doing nothing. Everything else was great, combat is single-handedly the thing dragging the score down.

_childDocuments_.review: After 10 hours have to say it's just okay. Of all the AC games I'd put it somewhere in the middle but I'm sure I have a lot of progressing to do. I'll give some pros and cons of what I have taken in so far...Pros:-The game is beautiful and great world design. Feels very authentic walking through the streets.-Well optimized and Runs great. I get 60 FPS and my PC fans barely go on. That's a very good sign. -Story is fairly interesting as far as AC story lines go -Voice acting I'd put near the top of the list. Accents feel very genuine compared to a lot of AC foreign voice acting.  No quirky accents, at least none as bad as a lot of older titles. Cons:-My biggest con is that while the world design and look is amazing, it's very lackluster and boring. Doesn't have much life to it. There's not much to do as far as activities go, besides pick pocketing -Not many side quests (or side characters) that you naturally run into in your travels.  It's almost all done through the mission board. I think I only ran into one pedestrian activated side quest and I don't even remember what it was about.-Combat is a little wonky. I've played every AC title and never had this hard a time parrying attacks. Even the most basic enemies utilize power attacks so don't expect some kind of cinematic parry-fest where you feel like a combat god. (Maybe I'm just getting old, or maybe this title is just focused more on stealth, but taking on groups of enemies is a lot more difficult than recent titles.)All in all, so far, it's pretty good. Nothing spectacular, but well polished. Valhalla, Odyssey, and Origins were much better experiences in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: I love it!!!! I have played most assassins creed games but I wouldn't call myself a pro since most of the lore goes over my head. It has a beautiful setting and feels like Origins, odyssey and valhalla because of how pretty and immersive it feels, which is what I loved when life felt boring and I love history . But it also feels like an actual assassins creed game which those listed had drifted from. You play as Basim who was featured in valhalla. You start as him being a simple thief and novice. We get to see the process of him becoming an assassin and him being trained (the whole rags to riches thing) . Then he gets the big promotion and are introduced to the main quests and more. Again, I only have 4 hours right now but the map and world feels a lot less overwhelming. You can have notoriety level so guards might run after you or look for you if you are getting up to no good. There's a pickpocketing system so you can pickpocket people and see if they have a coin bag attached to them through 'spidey sense'. You can get rid of notoriety by destroying your wanted posters (1-3 depending on how bad they are after you) or you can bribe guys to get it down too. I cannot emphasize how much you feel like an assassin, or at least how much I did. You aren't wielding battleaxes or bows and you cant always take on 3 guys like its nothing. You can 'hire' other people to help distract enemies so you can sneak around them. Lastly, I have not played super long but I feel like I've barely scratched the surface. I have heard this game is shorter than the others so my only worry is that it won't be long enough!

_childDocuments_.review: Do not understand the mid reviews of this game. It delivers on many levels. It's focused, not bloated, has a lot of great stealth options -- and I never feel railroaded in terms of my approach to a mission. Got it for half price on Steam launch and feel it's more than worth my time and money. I'm a fan of the worldbuilding, the way everything feels alive, the amazing inclusion of historical detail (with references to actual art pieces and museum catalog references). 20-some-odd hours in and enjoying it immensely.Only issue so far has been a couple of random crashes which stopped once I applied nvidia optimizations and turned off Ubi game overlay.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve been playing every single major entry in the Assassin's Creed series and reviewing them. But I did not review Valhalla. Because I did not finish it. I will never finish it. It’s insufferably boring and I was falling asleep while forcing myself to play. That’s the bonus review out of the way, so let’s talk about Assassin’s Creed Mirage – a game that started development as a big expansion for Valhalla. A fate it thankfully avoided, because it’s quite good.Mirage is a yet another reminder that Assassin’s Creed as a franchise has no idea what it is. It has been “missing the point” ever since the very first sequel and its best entries have forged a place of their own in spite of the supposed identity, not because of it. Mirage is doing the same – while utilizing the blueprint that was first introduced in Origins it is attempting to use it for creating the gameplay from the first 4 games (not 4 numbered titles, but all games before AC3… yeah, I know). And while this approach is far from perfect, the intent is strong and the results are fun.With this “going back to the roots” approach, the game returns to the  city environment as its main setting, ditches the focus on open combat in favor of stealth, removes experience and leveling up for the player and enemies and scales down the amount of side activities and icons on the map. It doesn’t completely remove the idea of an inventory or unlockable skills, unfortunately, but these concepts are simplified enough to be just additional flavors for the type of approach in completing missions you prefer. The game also still contains “flat” locations around Baghdad that you will get to explore, but most of the missions happen inside the city. You can still use an eagle to survey the locations, and while useful, I feel that it could’ve been cut entirely this time around.When the game works as intended, everything clicks almost perfectly. And as a result you get the cool newer mechanics and UI elements of the more recent titles as quality of life improvements and strategy expanding elements on top of the classic mission design. Even the general game progression is built like it was in the original entry, where you perform missions to gather intel on the target and when all of that is done it culminates with the assassination. Though, of course, this time with no utterly pointless “race me to the spot” and the like repeating missions that plagued the very first game. Some of the story beats repeat the original tale as well, though with far less style – those cool “Animus hacking” effects and digital glitches still feel incredibly cool and unconventional in comparison to the far more plain presentation of Mirage.But, of course, things often work not as intended. The freerunning system and controls are based on the Origins blueprint which was designed for the more flat locations. Due to that the familiar issues that plagued the classic titles return with character jumping in odd directions or refusing to climb down as they should. Which is especially sad, since this problem was already solved back in AC Unity – its “Run Up” and “Run Down” options (when they weren’t glitching) were the perfect solution for parkour in city areas. Game has plenty of odd glitches here and there too, and while most of them are just visual, some may temporarily block your progress.And some things are just disappointing. The story and characters, for example, never do anything good with how they are originally built up to be. Part of the issue might lie with the need to fit the main character into the role he has already played in a different game. But I feel that it could’ve been done better, with some semblance of a “journey”. Instead, you see him start as one potentially interesting character, until in the last act he must suddenly become a different one. The music hinges on being very very good, but never quite gets there. And you may notice some odd issues that happen when the sandbox elements get in the way of the story in your playthrough.I did like playing Assassin’s Creed Mirage a lot. But as you might’ve understood by now, it’s more of a “yeah, this is quite good” praise than a glowing recommendation. With this title being the 13th main entry in the franchise you’d think that being “quite good” cannot possibly land you among the best of the series. But the franchise is so full of bloated and disappointing entries that Mirage easily lands in my top 5 AC games. It’s a bit sad, but I am also glad that this franchise can still produce titles I can enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: Assassin's Creed Mirage is a welcome return to form for the series, focusing on stealth and parkour in a smaller, more focused open world. The story, while not groundbreaking, is engaging, and the setting of Baghdad is beautifully recreated. While the game could have benefited from more depth in combat and character development, it offers a satisfying and nostalgic experience for fans of the classic Assassin's Creed games.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest, I didn't expect too much going into this and only bought it because it was 50% off. But I actually thoroughly enjoyed this game. I'm not a Ubisoft fanboy, and I haven't really played any of the other games in the series, but I am a stealth-game fan and personally this game scratched that itch.My main complaints:* The movement is sometimes pretty clunky, I'd jump somewhere I wasn't planning on or drop to my doom instead of climbing down slowly.* The skills on the skill tree are a bit lack-luster. In my playthrough I ended up maxing out the stealth skill tree, then just putting points into other stuff randomly.* I won't hark too much on it as I see a lot of reviews complaining about it, but some of the voice acting wasn't that great. It didn't ruin the experience for me, but if that tends to bother you it's worth keeping in mind.* Although it's not as bad as some games I've played, this game does suffer from yellow paint syndrome. The solution to every puzzle or problem basically involves turning on your character's wallhacks or using your eagle to highlight the enemies and points of interest.Some of the things I enjoyed:* I know it's considered a staple of the genre, but every section of the game has different ways to sneak around and I found it most enjoyable to not follow the most obvious path and find my own way.* I found it interesting how the notoriety system works. With high notoriety citizens will point you out to guards. So having to always be aware of doing assassinations or stealing in front of civs* The story was alright, It didn't change my perception of reality or anything, but it was interesting enough to see Basim develop as a hidden oneOverall the game was pretty fun, not life changing, and sometimes a little too simple, but an enjoyable experience and a steal for the price I got it. If you like doing side quests and exploring every nook of the city then you'll get a few more hours out of the game than I did.

_childDocuments_.review: Assassin's Creed Mirage is an amazing return to the roots of the franchise, skillfully combining elements of classic gameplay and modern technology. I was struck by how the game recreates the atmosphere of9th-century Baghdad, with its vibrant streets, bustling markets, and majestic architectural structures. The graphics are top-notch, and the attention to detail in the environment and character animations perfectly captures the spirit of the time.The storyline is captivating and well-developed. The story of Basim, balancing between past and present, is full of unexpected twists that make each mission compelling. The characters, both positive and negative, are deeply fleshed out, and most of them have their own motivations and secrets, adding layers of complexity to the narrative.The gameplay mechanics also deserve praise. The return to a more stealth-oriented approach in Assassin's Creed, without excessive reliance on combat systems, allowed me to feel like a true Master Assassin. The ability to blend in with crowds, use the environment, and devise strategies for eliminating targets brings great joy.I can't overlook the magnificent soundtrack, which only enhances the atmosphere of what is happening. The music emphasizes the seriousness of the moments and helps immerse you in the world created by the developers.Overall, Assassin's Creed Mirage is a game that not only respects the traditions of the franchise but also offers a fresh perspective on familiar mechanics. It’s an unforgettable adventure that will not leave any fan of the series indifferent, and I eagerly await what Ubisoft will offer next. If you're looking for an engaging and deep experience in the world of Assassin's Creed, then Mirage is definitely worth your attention!

_childDocuments_.review: Having played this a fair bit on Xbox it was nice to finally pick it up on Steam and transfer my save over. So the good - this is indeed a return to the AC games of old. It's a stealth game set in a single city a long, long time ago. You really do need to creep around and kill from the shadows, as the main character is pretty weak and can be taken down quickly when spotted.  As someone who has played AC since the very first one this is great, as I really didn't care for the massive, bloated open world ones such as Valhalla and Odyssey where stealth was pretty much gone.Now the not so good - the game is visually a real mixed bag. The city is fine, it's well done enough, but after the glory days of Unity's baked lighting (still by a country mile the best looking AC game ever made) the realtime lighting is pretty weak here. It's flat and uninteresting. There is an AC 1 colour filter which marginally improves things, but still, this is unimpressive stuff. Then there are the characters.  There's really no kind way to describe them, other than to say they look like they didn't cost much to make. And the facial animation is very basic and crude. AC Unity again, set the bar sky high here and every AC game since has been getting worse on the character front.Now the bad - Ubisoft Connect.  Why does this exist? Steam is the launcher, there is no need for another launcher which I have to log in to.  Keep it if you want Ubi, but make it optional.  And the game itself can feel rather like the characters models - cheap and low budget. Some of the missions are fine, but others feel like they had very little time spent on them.I'd say if you're an old school AC fan this is worth a play, but be ready for the lower budget look of it all.

_childDocuments_.review: Assassin's Creed Mirage returns to the series' roots with a focus on stealth, assassinations, and a more condensed, narrative-driven experience compared to recent titles. Set in 9th century Baghdad, the game features Basim Ibn Ishaq as the protagonist, offering a rich character arc as he evolves into the assassin we met in Valhalla. The narrative is tightly crafted, blending historical elements with Basim's personal journey, making it one of the more engaging storylines in the franchise.Gameplay-wise, Mirage emphasizes stealth mechanics, with options for creative infiltrations, reminiscent of earlier entries in the series. However, combat is more challenging, with Basim being vulnerable in direct fights, encouraging players to rely on stealth over brute force. Parkour, while visually pleasing in Baghdad’s detailed environment, can feel awkward at times, with some control limitations that may frustrate fans of older titles.One of Mirage's standout aspects is its vibrant depiction of Baghdad. The city feels alive with cultural details, historical accuracy, and environmental interactions, though it doesn’t rival other open-world titles in terms of depth. Still, the compact design makes it immersive and enjoyable for those seeking a more traditional Assassin's Creed experience.Overall, while Mirage doesn’t offer vast innovations, its strong character focus and return to classic gameplay elements make it a satisfying entry for long-time fan

name: Pirate Hunter
detailed_description: In the middle of the South Pacific: modern pirates are making the waterways that are so important for international trade unsafe. In order to deal with this ever-growing threat, a mercenary group called The Pilgrims appears on the scene, earning their money with protection missions and the passing on of expertise. Their newest member is Eddie Jackson, a former US Navy SEAL whose wife was kidnapped on a cruise ship by unknown assailants. There Seems to be no motive for the attack on the ship and no ransom demand has been made. The player takes on the role of Eddie and embarks on a desperate search for his beloved wife. He fights on the side of the Pilgrims against various pirate and terrorist groups that are making the area unsafe. Little by little, he discovers more and more clues that lead him to his wife and the incredible secret behind her disappearance. The story comes from the pen of experienced designer Matthew Miles Griffiths, who has managed to write a gripping, deep and intriguing story with several storylines. Features: • Extensive story, divided into 20 missions • More than 20 high-tech weapons from all over the world, from grenade launchers to sniper rifles • Tropical locations with lush vegetation, sensational water effects and countless interaction possibilities interaction possibilities • 4 completely individual squad members with their own history and weapon specialization, who fight for the player in certain missions

name: Apartment Story
detailed_description: Apartment Story is a feature-length, single-player, third-person thriller set in a single apartment. You play as Arthur, a person alive in 2023 trying to keep his head above water, when you receive an unexpected call at the door from your old roommate, Diane. She stays, you party, but soon you will meet Blondey and good times turn bad very quickly. Will you participate in a dangerous and dramatic narrative? Or keep the front door closed, eating and masturbating until you’ve shut the world out for good? Whatever you choose, the cold metal of a gun is hidden within the darkness of your apartment somewhere. Features Absorb yourself in a fast-paced, dramatic thriller that centres around 3 distinct personalities which develop as the gun is introduced and stakes are raised. You are invited to take an active role in Arthur’s life and welfare through a deep and immersive needs management system. Eat food, pee, wash your hands, sleep, smoke, write, watch TV, shave, change clothes, nap, shower, take drugs, wash the dishes, turn off the lights, drink beer, listen to music, top up your electric, answer the door and shoot someone with a real gun. Engaging in these activities will keep your Life stats up and Arthur poised for the drama coming his way. Tidy and organise the objects within your apartment however you desire by picking up any small object and placing them anywhere within reach. Real-time night and day cycles. This Videogame is a feature-length experience, which means you can grab yourself a drink and complete the game within a single night. Playtime: approximately 90-120 minutes.

Navigate escalating real-time narrative events whilst managing Sims-esq stats to stay strong for an inevitable showdown. You play as Arthur, a young man trying to make it day to day before a gun turns his life upside down.

_childDocuments_.review: I was fortunate enough to play an advance copy of this game. I had been watching the development for a couple of years through whatever snapshots of progress were being shared online.For me, this game sits somewhere in between a life simulation, visual novel, and third person adventure. It pulls pieces from different genres to create a unique experience that is probably best enjoyed in a single session.The game will take around two hours to complete, and while there is a story to be told here, much of the real meat of the game is in the quiet time between the big story beats. The game compels the player to take time for reflection, time to take in the atmosphere, time to take a peek into another life. It's a quiet-loud-quiet-loud-quiet type flow.I really enjoyed my experience playing through Apartment Story, and it ran smoothly on my Steam Deck. I don't really have any nostalgia for PS1 style graphics, but I felt that the game utilized the look effectively, allowing for more complex ideas to be communicated through a simplified visual language.I think that discerning players looking for a story driven experience with rich atmosphere should give this one a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Apartment Story

_childDocuments_.review: There are aspects of this game that I really liked - the attention to detail in the apartment furnishing, the lighting, and the music were all great.Other than those things, this game really didn't hang together for me unfortunately. I like the idea of having Sims-style bars that you have to manage, but was disappointed with how little effect they had on the game. There are a couple of nice moments when narrative events impacted them but I found they didn't add much to the overall experience. In general the lack of reactivity present in the game makes me feel like there is a lot of wasted potential here. I appreciate that adding bespoke reactions based on the current game state is costly, but I think Apartment Story just serves as good example that games are not suited to the type of storytelling seen in linear media. There were multiple occasions where the seams of the narrative scripting were visible, with the game waiting for me to do the exact interactions it wanted in order to progress, and I don't think it dealt with any deviation from that well. It feels like this would have worked much better as a short film or written story.I'm quite tolerant of bugs and jank, especially in small indie titles, but I found there were enough of them to get in the way of my enjoyment. The lo-fi animations, while charming, did undermine the tone I feel the game was going for.Pacing wasn't great and there were long stretches of time where I felt like I was just waiting around for stuff to happen. If the waiting was intentional, it didn't work for me. The level design in the final scene was also confusing and kind of killed any impact the narrative may have had at that moment.Despite writing about the things I didn't like at length, I'm going to give a thumbs-up. I think it is really important that games keep trying to push the boundaries of what types of experiences they can give players and I think Apartment Story is an ambitious attempt at doing so. I'm looking forward to seeing more from the developers with the suggestion that the next thing they make is scoped a little bit more appropriately for their budget.
_childDocuments_.name: Apartment Story

_childDocuments_.review: It's more an art piece than a game, but it works really well. Mechanically, I like the way the game handles interacting with the world / objects and the cooking aspect. Could be a solid proof of concept for a more ambitious game.I finished in just under 2 hours, and it was a complete story, as straightforward as it was.

The tale unfolds slowly, revealing its mysteries like a worn scroll, while the world within resonates with a beauty both dark and fair, echoing the secrets of the lives that dwell within its walls.The hands that crafted this indie gem did so with care beyond measure, for every detail sings of devotion and labor. Know this: 'tis not merely a game, but a journey—one that calls to those with strength and spirit, leaving them forever changed.Magnificent!
