_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, but I encountered bugs within the first few minutes. The very basics of picking things up and combining items to eat (which you need to do) are needlessly janky--the very first meal I made got bugged and stuck to the dinner table, I couldn't eat it. Oh well, I moved on but eventually got to a moment in the game where something was obviously supposed to occur...but it didn't. The game was running and I could move around, but time was no longer passing and my meters weren't going down. Basically I was two hours in and realized I wouldn't be able to progress and there's no way to back up or reset the moment or whatever. Not about to wade through the first two hours again.There's charm to this game for sure, but it's just too clunky and janky to recommend in it's state. It was cool that my avatar was able to watch porn and blast it while my friend waited right by my side. A true NPC buddy indeed.
_childDocuments_.name: Apartment Story

_childDocuments_.review: A playable A24, minimalist, atompsheric flick - for good and for ill. It's more of a walking sim than its trailers imply. If you're fine with that you'll have a good time. If not, maybe wait for a sale and skip it.It genuinely makes the most of its limitations. It changes scenarios and oozes atmosphere. The Sims stat bars are extremely easy to manage, but they nonetheless invite you to ♥♥♥♥ around, take a break, reflect, and even create dread. Make food, smoke a joint, pee and shower in between the relationship drama. It's hard to explain how, but it works and immerses you into the setting.The bad part is that it's slow. REALLY slow. The game discourages skipping time by going to sleep, and doesn't have very many things to do even when you're at your best shape. This means a lot of the game's downtime is essentially filler, and it becomes extremely obvious when a scripted event happens instead of it being organic.The so-so part is the plot. It's well structured and explained, with good guys to cheer for and a bad guy to hate. Dialogues are short and sharp, and it's really cool how game mechanics are used for little character moments. That said, it's also very predictable, and ends on a bit of a "that's it?" note.P.S. There aren't multiple endings nor dialogue choices. All conflict is mandatory. Dying is a failure state. That's not good nor bad, and I realize it's a whole can of worms to accommodate for those choices. But it is just this little bit disappointing considering the infrastructure is already there for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Apartment Story

_childDocuments_.review: Apartment Story is a standout gem in the indie gaming scene, offering a fresh and unique experience compared to many smaller titles out there. The game transforms the everyday lives of apartment dwellers into a captivating narrative filled with meaningful choices and well-crafted characters. Each interaction feels significant, drawing you deeper into the story.The pacing is one of the game’s greatest strengths. It doesn't rush, allowing you to immerse yourself in the world and its characters at a natural, enjoyable pace. The narrative unfolds in a way that feels organic and rewarding, making you truly care about the people you meet and the choices you make.What sets Apartment Story apart is how it balances simplicity with depth. It doesn’t rely on flashy mechanics but instead uses thoughtful storytelling and character development to pull you in. The branching narrative and replayability give it a richness that’s rare in smaller games.Overall, *Apartment Story* is a refreshing and memorable experience—a must-play for fans of narrative-driven indie games.
_childDocuments_.name: Apartment Story

_childDocuments_.review: The latest coffee-drinking, cigarette-smoking, beer-supping, dancing-in-the-living-room simulator from indie creators of The End of the World+, finding optimism in the claustrophobic apartment of a broke millennial. It feels like a small indie movie or single set play with it’s 3 characters and setting. The diegetic music nails the vibe, especially when you have a visitor. The dialogue feels human and contemporary. The art direction speaks for itself!This is unapologetically an artsy ‘’walking sim’’ style game, and some sections are about doing the fundamental chores that go along with being trapped in a Meat Prison inside an Apartment Prison, if you don't like that. If we get another similar game, I’d love to see more internal thoughts (Disco Elysium, 13 Sentinels) with voice acting and deeper characterisation.This game costs £6, and you should consider purchasing it. It is ridiculously ambitious - the flavor interactions are familiar from your Quantic Dream, Kojima Productions or a GTA - but conjured from blood, sweat and pixels rather than mocap studios. If you want to see more interesting games made in the UK, start here.

_childDocuments_.review: This was brilliant. It's a nice little piece that's entirely based on vibes, until it's very very not. Since I heard about this, I was always curious how the whole sims-like life sim aspect plays into it, but it plays really well. There's some brilliant bits where actually looking at your stats while stuff is going on adds to Arthur's character. It's a very micro story about some crazy things, while keeping that almost low droning "life goes on, gotta get food, gotta take a shower, etc etc" kind of feeling. It's difficult to say more without spoiling things, and it's already a feature length experience as it is. I would say this though, if you're up for having well crafted downtime woven into your story telling, and down for something unexpected and different and potentially bizarre (at least in this medium), give this a go. This game isn't for everyone, but I am glad it's for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Apartment Story

_childDocuments_.review: Apartment Story offers a captivating atmosphere and a truly unique experience that immerses you in someone else’s life. Though the game is short, I actually appreciate that—it fits perfectly into my schedule since I don't often have time for longer games.The characters and environment feel authentic, and the art style is spot on. While the story can be a bit predictable at moments, the overall experience left me satisfied. If you're intrigued by what you've seen, I definitely recommend giving it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Apartment Story

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not for everyone but I think some will REALLY vibe with it. This game deserves way more attention.There's a lot of jank here. The characters don't have a ton of depth. But this game made me feel anxious and powerless in a way that was pretty unique. And then a little frustrated by the end as my save file glitched and I wasn't able to finish the game. I ended up watching the final minutes on YouTube.As the story builds, I found the sims like, stat management elements helped build tension. Washing the dishes while you wait in paranoia for the consequences of what took place the previous day was quite interesting and made me feel surprisingly anxious. The characters weren't particularly intriguing and their conversations felt pretty short. There seemed to be so little connection between them that the ending conversation felt pretty botched, as did the drop of the ending screen considering how much style the game has overall.The game looks INCREDIBLE and definitely has the sauce. I would've loved to spend more time just hanging out in the apartment. It definitely passes the weird/chill/dreary atmosphere vibe check and for $7 and two hours of my life I found it to be a pretty interesting game and great way to spend my weekend.
_childDocuments_.name: Apartment Story

_childDocuments_.review: A day in the life of Arthur:- Wake up.- Urinate for approximately 2 seconds.- Take a shower.- Prepare cereal on the chopping board (naked, because you forgot to put clothes on).- Write on the computer.- Look at explicit content on the computer.- Do…other stuff at the computer (tissues are there for a reason).- Smoke a joint with your roommate’s ex.- Discuss what to do with The Gun.Apartment Story is a short narrative-driven simulation game. Your character, Arthur, has recently lost his job, is drowning in debt, and struggling to find purpose in life. You must keep Arthur alive by making sure he eats, sleeps, goes to the bathroom, keeps his hygiene in check, and looks after his mental wellness using a sort of Sims-esque system of health bars. If these needs drag Arthur's Life bar down, it’s game over, so keeping them balanced is crucial (though not at all difficult).You control Arthur in 3rd person as he wanders around the apartment, using a targeting crosshair to highlight things you want him to interact with. Though all of the controls are a bit fiddly (picking multiple items up is particularly clumsy) and there’s a degree of jank to every element of the design, it somehow works with the low-poly aesthetics - plus the sheer volume of interactable “stuff” is impressive. The soundtrack is beautiful, composed of drifting electronic tracks from TRAAPS. There are several scenes of nudity and explicit content which feel somewhat gratuitous to me, but inoffensively so.At certain points, events will happen: the doorbell will ring, your phone will beep, or your electricity meter will cut out. What will you do? These choices feed the narrative, which is thrilling and completely believable. I swung between laughter and nail-biting tension as situations unfolded, desperate to make the “right” decisions. There are several ways your story can “end”, which makes for some replayability. All in all, I enjoyed this: it’s not perfect, but it is entertaining!(Notes: Works fine on Steamdeck. Multiple saves are not supported. Approx 2 hour run time. Well worth the asking price IMO.)
_childDocuments_.name: Apartment Story

_childDocuments_.review: A moreish tone piece about soaking up the glittering mediocrity of a English flat — the sparkling rain on a window and the coloured light of electronics painting beauty onto the overcast and beige. Rupturing the quotidian is a sudden violence and passion that culminates into a genuinely suspenseful and effecting waiting game.There are quibbles with some awkward tangibles and the friction of some interactions chafe against the sheer elegance of its presentation from typography to UI but in less than a feature length film I found myself invested in the cleaning up of someone else's apartment, wanting more fictional television and knowing the depths of a character's psyche.Hell, it's worth it for the utterly charismatic materials and lighting alone.

_childDocuments_.review: It's three in the afternoon, I'm stoned, I'm hungry but I don't feel like cooking or cleaning. I pick up a slice of pizza off the floor and eat it. But enough about my life, I have some thoughts on this game to share.Short experimental game that is surprisingly affecting for how short and simple it is. A relatively mundane setting and set of verbs makes the moments of tension and violence feel that much more shocking. The visuals really bring it to life, every detail of the apartment exudes personality and the lighting is gorgeous. The devs have said they plan on releasing more shortform games like this and I'm excited to see what else they come up with.

_childDocuments_.review: The Sims expansion you've always dreamed about! Taking the dramatic moments to the next level! LOL. ok ok I jest, but this is actually a fun little Sims-like game.You play as Arthur, someone who was laid off a few weeks ago and has been holed up in his apartment everyday doing nothing. The game lets you play three days of his life. You control Arthur like a character in Sims, he can cook, take shower, use toilet, making coffee, watching pxrn on the computer, eating dinner while watching tv after shooting somebody. That last part is not in Sims but it sure as heck is in this game! Like I said, taking the dramatic moments to the max. There are character dialogue cutscenes that unfolds each day to tell the story between Arthur and other characters in the game.The game can be completed in about 90 minutes to 120 minutes. My first run I encountered a bug where the gun disappeared after cooking/eating meal, which eventually caused me getting a bad ending since my gun was gone. Had to replay the whole game. I was thinking about leaving a negative review because of this, but this game was really fun up to that particular point. So I'd still give this game a positive, recommended review.2nd time playing the game since I knew what to do, the game could be completed with about 60 minutes. The trick of passing time faster is to tell Arthur watch pxrn on the computer all day, which makes him sleepy, and then he can go to bed, sleep, and the game time passes way faster that way.if you like this game, I recommend checking out "12 Minutes"Like I said, a wild little Sims-like, slice of life game. Recommended, 7.1/10

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely loved the game! Brought back so many memories of playing Remedy games as a child. Glad to be hearing the director/developer of this title wants to create many more of these short story experiences. I think that is what the world needs more of these days. Highly recommend adding this to your collection if you enjoy the type of melancholic titles that are comfy and can be enjoined on a rainy day whilst sipping a cup of coffee.

_childDocuments_.review: I mean this in a positive way, this is a perfect game to chill out to. The amount of stuff you can interact with is pretty wild considering how short the game is. How much enjoyment you get from the down time is dependent on how much you like SIMS-style character management but I dug it! I experienced a few glitches here and there (being unable to pick up an item again after I set it down somewhere, and being stuck for a little more than a while trying to turn off a light because there was an item in front of it). Nothing game breaking by any means, but worth mentioning. TLDR: I recommend it! A good, short game for a great price with an interesting story, replay-ability, chill soundtrack, and visuals I really dig.

_childDocuments_.review: Introduction: In the vast and ever-evolving landscape of video games, it’s often the simplest concepts that capture our attention and imagination. “Nut,” a clicker game available on Steam, epitomizes this notion. At first glance, it may seem like a trivial and absurd endeavor, but beneath its simplistic exterior lies a surprisingly engaging and community-driven experience.Gameplay: “Nut” is, at its core, a clicker game where the primary objective is to click on a nut. Each click increments a counter, and every few hours, players are rewarded with a digital nut image. These images, created by the community through the game’s official Discord server, add a layer of charm and uniqueness to the game. The simplicity of the gameplay is both its strength and its weakness. While it lacks the depth and complexity of more traditional games, it excels in providing a low-effort, high-reward experience that can be enjoyed in short bursts.Visuals and Sound: The visual presentation of “Nut” is minimalistic, with a dark yellow background and a prominently displayed nut. The lack of intricate graphics or detailed animations might be seen as a drawback, but it aligns perfectly with the game’s straightforward nature. The sound design is equally minimal, with subtle clicks accompanying each interaction. This understated approach ensures that the game remains unobtrusive, allowing players to engage with it passively while multitasking.Community and Social Interaction: One of the standout features of “Nut” is its vibrant and active community. The game’s official Discord server serves as a hub for players to share their nut images, discuss strategies, and participate in design submissions. This sense of community fosters a collaborative environment where players feel connected and invested in the game’s ongoing development. The community-driven aspect of “Nut” is a testament to the power of social interaction in enhancing the gaming experience.Monetization and Value: While “Nut” is free to play, it incorporates a unique monetization model where players can buy and sell digital nut images for real money. This feature has contributed to the game’s popularity, as players are drawn to the potential for financial gain. However, it’s important to approach this aspect with caution, as the value of these digital items is highly speculative and may not be sustainable in the long term.Conclusion: “Nut” may not be the most groundbreaking or innovative game on the market, but its unexpected rise to fame on Steam proves that simplicity can be a powerful tool in the gaming industry. The game’s minimalistic design, coupled with its engaging community and unique monetization model, creates an experience that is both entertaining and thought-provoking. Whether you’re a seasoned gamer looking for a lighthearted distraction or a newcomer seeking a low-effort entry point into the world of clicker games, “Nut” offers a delightfully absurd experience that is worth exploring.

name: Stranded Deep
detailed_description: TEST YOUR SURVIVAL SKILLS IN THIS OPEN WORLD ADVENTURE In the aftermath of a mysterious plane crash, you are stranded in the vast expanse of the Pacific Ocean. Alone, without any means to call for help, you must do what you can to survive. BUILD. CRAFT. SURVIVE. ESCAPE. Explore underwater and on land as you hunt for supplies to craft the tools, weapons, and shelter you’ll need to stay alive. Stay sharp: hunger, thirst, and exposure conspire against you as you brave treacherous elements and the dangerous creatures of the Pacific. Live long enough, Stay Alive! Health, Hunger, Thirst, and sunstroke. Manage and monitor these vitals through an interactive survival watch. Cure poisons, heal broken bones, and bandage bleeding to stay alive. Spears, Axes, Bows, Spearguns, and so much more can all be crafted through an interactive crafting menu or by the quick-craft selection wheel. Items in your inventory and on the ground around you can all be crafted into something useful. Harvesting, Craftsmanship, Cooking, Physical, and Hunting can all be levelled up for maximum efficiency or to unlock different crafting combinations. With dozens of tiers and building pieces to choose from; craft your very own home away from home. From a weak and flimsy palm frond shack to a solid clay brick house. Customise your own raft with sails, canopies, storage, anchors, boat motors, and more. If sailings not for you - fly in style by constructing a gyrocopter! Explore the procedurally generated world with no two islands the same. Dive for sunken shipwrecks, abandoned shelters from previous survivors, or search for rare sea creatures like whales. Build and manage your farm with water management and plant growth cycles. Hunt, Fish, Trap, and Skin animals for food or kill to insert your dominance over the pacific islands. If you’re looking for a challenge then take on one of the three bosses to obtain a wall trophy and a very important reward. Unlock Steam achievements! Compare statistics with your friends from the in-game leaderboards for whose the best survivor. Play online or split screen co-op modes! Customise your world through the map island editor. Play as Female or Male. Change your game difficulty. Play split-screen co-op, and so much more! Create your own custom island and add it to your survival world! Hand sculpt the terrain and manually place each individual tree, rock, and creature to create the adventure island you want! You can even share it with your friends!

_childDocuments_.review: I have only played roughly 30-40 minutes of this game but hear me out. My first play through that lasted a whole 2 minutes or so consisted of me throwing crabs into the air and trying to bash rocks against rocks. I was confused. Look on the steam community while you're in-game to view a couple guides to get you started. I ended this first play through because I had accidentally thrown my knife somewhere into the water (lol). You need the knife to get started so I had to end it. My second play through which I am currently in is going pretty well. It's not too hard to survive yet but than again I have only been in for a half hour. I just eat and drink coconuts and eat potatos. I have not ventured into the water yet because I am deadly afraid of sharks in real life. So for me this is Deepest Fear Simulator 2015. Other than that the game is pretty good! Not a whole lot of features but It is pre-alpha. Still a fun game with amazing physics and a great physical crafting mechanic. PROS----------Graphics - 8.5/10 The graphics are pretty amazing for an indie game. I know they plan to improve so im sure it will be a 10/10 soon enough! Reminds me of "The Forest" graphics... not to compare the two.Crafting - 8/10 Not too much to craft but hey.. its just pre-alpha.Environment - 9/10 Seriously makes me think of Tom Hanks. I found a "DeadEx" package on my island so I will keep it until I find the woman in the farmhouse that creates things out of metal when I become saved.Gameplay - 9/10 Fun game so far, just needs more features. Which as I have said before is because it is a pre-alpha game. I have nothing but high hopes for this game and I believe the developers will achieve them.Now im not a usual reviewererer so im not sure if i covered all of the normal category's but I tried my best!! As for CONS----------------Nothing too bad about this game. You have to cut it some slack because it is a pre-alpha game. So as far as a Con list goes I really don't have anything to say. Maybe add in a tutorial so you can prevent idiots like me from trying to bash rocks together hahah.Now getting to the bottom line.. Should you buy this game? In my opinion yes you should. But keep in mind that it is extremely early in its release. There isn't much to build but there is plently to explore. It's a survival game so it isnt going to be easy. So if you are not patient and if you didnt like games like "The Forest" or "Rust" than probably don't pick this one up. But overall in my own personal opinion I think it is worth a buy. Maybe wait a couple months though if you dont want to get it in such an early state.Thanks for reading! Like I said this is a first serious review for me!

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Game is great, but has some problems to be expected in EA. Overall: 8/10 (for early access)Since many of the reviews that I've seen for this game are mostly people trying to be funny, or just people leaving reviews that are short, I decided to share my thoughts about this game as in depth as possible. That being said, this game is currently early access so of course it isn't complete. Normally I'm against buying games in EA or pre-order, but I couldn't resist this one. Also, this review was written with about 3 hours of gameplay under my belt. It may not seem like much time to get an idea of what a game is like, but with the limited content, I did almost everything you could. Anyway, let's begin:Pros:- Survival/Open world/exploration- graphics are great, but still could be a little bit better- very atmospheric and immersive even as it is- day/night cycle- random weather (really forces you to adapt in some situations)- player is actually pretty hardy, doesn't die too easily (I haven't died yet with 3 hours of gameplay)- supplies are scarce, just like they would be in a real situation like this- sharks seem to be attracted to blood- sharks add a great sense of fear when exploring the ocean- really makes you feel like you have to survive by picking and choosing everything- even the temporary UI looks great IMO- night time isn't so dark you can't see, moon lights up the island a bit- doesn't hold your hand, throws you right into itCons:- VERY small islands- no caves (devs, I would really love to see bigger islands with caves in this game)- not much to craft- not much to do (island hop and dive, forage for food - that's about it. It's survival, sure, but it feels like it's missing something still- tiger sharks are SO aggressive. They'll constantly knock you off of your raft and force you to fight them to leave an island- no other animals except for aquatics (fish, sharks, turtles, and stingrays - that's about it)- some weapons are weaker than they should be (machete is almost useless for chopping down palm trees, use it for sharks only)- very limited in what you can do/what there is to doNow that is just a list of things that are good and bad about this game, as for my experience with the game, I must say that I'm impressed. The game itself is visually compelling - the underwater scenes are glorious and the textures are pretty great everywhere else. Also, it's VERY atmospheric. I really felt like I was lost on an island trying to survive while playing this game. That's a huge plus for me. I just wish that there was more to experience within the game. I would love to see bigger islands with cave systems that are inhabited by animals like rodents, monkeys, deer, etc. It would be really cool to be able to hunt and trap them. The items that you can craft are pretty functional, but other than the few items that you can craft, there's not much more you can do in that category which is a bit of a disappointment.There were also a few bugs that I've come across like getting stuck inside your life raft, but after jumping, I was able to fix that. Also, sharks seem to defy the laws of physics, glitching right through the boundaries of shipwrecks occasionally. This can be a little scary when you're first starting out or in dire need of first aid.Overall, this game is simply amazing, but I'm hoping that the devs expand on it quite a bit. I'm hoping to see a lot more content and a lot of interesting sites to explore.A note to the devs:Here are my suggestions for content, hopefully this is seen.- CAVES - I really want to see this implemented- bigger islands - the small islands are kind of boring, bigger would be better because then there's more to explore- multi-storied shelters - ability to customize shelters in general really. Also, ladders and stairs.- fishing - It would be great to be able to craft a fishing rod and fish with it- hunting - bigger islands, throw in some animals and let us craft bows and traps. It would be epic.- binoculars that actually work - Seriously though, currently they're useless.- more items to eat/forage for - maybe add some banana trees and the likes- SCUBA/snokel gear - I think some of this is already in the game, but if not, DO IT.Thanks for the development of this game. I really enjoy playing it and it's a lot of fun!

_childDocuments_.review: Considering I played this game for 140+ hours I cannot vote anything but "Yes". But...there are quite a few things I did not like. The random world isn't very random. An island has a rock and pine saplings or it has palms and ficus trees. If it has a rock it will have 1 hog, 2 boars, 2 snakes, 2 giant crabs. And they respawn every 3 days which is stupid. All island seem to have 3 yucca trees and 1 or 2 rocks. So that gets boring eventually. Steering a boat larger than 3x2 is bothersome. Too many sharks in the game, there is always 1 or 2 around. You can walk through tables, you cannot sit on a chair or sleep in a bed. It storms a lot and the lightening is so bright, I walk away (irl) until it is gone. Some minor issues with building a house (half walls and triangle foundation). Storyline is very weak. The number of shipwrecks is ridiculous.  The loot is predictable. Now on the plus side: it's scary in the water with the sharks. Swimming in the coral (jay! shark repellent) is beautifully done. The repetitive sound track isn't annoying and the music warns you of certain events which is nice. You can build a house, a boat, farm food, hunt and fish. You can store stuff in a nice OCD manner thanks to container shelves. You do get a sense of being all alone, lost and in danger. I think if you want a better "being lost" experience you should never click on cartographer. The game is enjoyable and entertaining, but in my opinion it's a shame the developers did not focus more on a story line with a complimentary loot system and some minor quests.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to love this game, I so wanted to love it.  I loved Ark and Long Dark, this seemed that it could be something like these but new and exciting.  However after playing for a few hours and trying things out.  This is just boring.  It has SOO many weak points in the design.  There is a significant lack of any kind of progression.  Sure you can build a bigger and bigger shack, but why?  Literally nothing needs to go in your shack.  You can't build storage to put in there.  The decor and furniture is all basically non-functional.  Basically the entire point of this game is to build a raft to go collect the same basic resources from small islands and bring them back to your "base" by hand.  The only "survival" element here is that there is no way to catch all the copious amounts of rain, so you have to constantly harvest pawn frawns to put into your water still.  So many years in early access, such a great disappointment.

I do strongly believe that if online multiplayer became a thing, this game could have a nice burst of popularity. I'd have much more fun with friends than alone.In all, Stranded Deep is a potentially incredible game, and with the right additions and MUCH more consistent updates, it can reach it's peak yet. _childDocuments_.review: Stranded Deep is pretty unique. I find it very chill and relaxing. I truely feel a sense of adventure traveling from island to island on my thin yellow life raft, oar in hand braving the elements. One such time I can remember being halfway to another island and suddenly getting caught in a huge storm. I paddled in what I hoped was the same direction for a few minutes but couldn't resist looking behind me to try and glimpse sight of my "home" island to get my bearings. After that point I was lost. The clouds were so thick I didn't know which way I was facing. Then as night came I was not only lost in the fog, I was also lost in the dark. I had mentaly maped out the nearest islands to my "home" but now was way off course. This was hillarious to me. It was like finding a brick of solid GOLD when I finally opened a chest with a COMPASS inside!  I eventually gave up on my mental map and grabed a piece of scratch paper and started maping my discoveries. I even started using real world triangulation to chart my discoveries with my new compass. I loved this. No minimap with red dots to tell me where to go. No yellow brick road to follow. You are just LOST, using your wits, this was great.Now with all that said, I will say this...At one point several months back (maybe a year ago?) there was an update that in my opinion drastically altered the game, and it really put me off at the time. The crafting menu's were foreign to my original experience, there were several glitches, and the world seemed much much smaller. I basically shelved the game after that for some time, with the intention of coming back to it later when the new changes had become more polished. I am happy to say, things have improved.If I could change/add one thing to this game It would be to add a Rip Curl (so I can hang 10 with a surfboard) the ocean graphics are great but sometimes the shoreline breaks immersion for me. (High and low tide would be cool too)I would recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Ever since I was little, I've loved survival games. The thrill of life and death in your hands... Stranded Deep has good graphics and that was one of the first things I liked. But after 4 hours, I feel as if I've experienced all there is to offer, and that's disappointing. There has to be more than just surviving day after day. Survival games can notoriously fall into monotony if there isn't good balance. For example, it needs story, direction, and/or more that you can build. Games like Lost in Blue 3 have story and more interactive building/cooking. It could even try to be educational like Oregon Trail or be able to make more things like Minecraft. But just like Minecraft, the game falls flat without direction. Maybe some puzzles or actual places you can find, like Myst, would even be good. Bottom line, this game left me wanting more.(I know it's in Beta but that's my advice. If it was improved, it definitely has potential.)

_childDocuments_.review: A lie by omission..Yes you can give a game a negative review even after 60 hours if it's been in early access for years and never fulfilled the promise of adding multiplayer.The extra time since release has given proper context for a review that at first was optimistic based on promises that would never come to fruition, this is part of the reason Early Access is terrible.1. Devs will lose the incentive to actually finish their game as they've long since seen their highest income from the project.2. Consumers don't judge the game for what it is, because then of course you'd expect a vast amount of negative reviews, instead they give the game the benefit of the doubt regarding future improvements such as adding multiplayer to name 1 example.Now we get to the part where the game is tagged has having "Multiplayer", it's technically true that maybe some folks would consider splitscreen "multiplayer" but you're insulting and taunting the vast majority of people who will look at that and reasonable assume that means at least 4 player CO-OP obviously on 4 separate machines, at worst 2 player proper co-op.But to market that title with the lazy split screen CO-OP from decades past running on 1 client? All you have is 2 character and Cameras on the same machine with different controls..Yes you're not lying, but you're also deserving of reviews like this.So be warned, this game does NOT have the multiplayer you'd expect after seeing that it's marketed as a multiplayer game, when it says it has Splitscreen CO-OP it means it ONLY has Splitscreen CO-OP which constitutes it's "Multiplayer" feature. They're not technically lying but it's obviously sneaky and as such negative reviews are completely warranted.If you rely on the fact that most people will look at the store and reasonable assume the game has a true Multiplayer feature beyond 2 characters on one machine, then I'll rely on User Reviews to warn people.This is fair game, if you don't want reviews that YOU would consider to be petty, then correct the petty tags on the store page.Play stupid games, get stupid prizes.. This game could have much more warranted positive reviews merely on the basis of the single player experience, no need to mislead people.PS: Am I to believe that the promised Multiplayer feature is already here in the form of the half ***ed single Client CO-OP mode? Is that where the years of promises for Multiplayer ended up? If so then it's obvious to me that such feature was ONLY developed so the devs could add a Multiplayer tag to the store since that feature meets the lowest possible bar one needs to justify said tag and also to claim they made good on their promise/user requests to add Multiplayer?!That's a whole other community relation issue of it's own.. In any event, I must not recommend this game on the basis that I know any of my friends would see the Multiplayer tag and reasonably assume that means at least 2-4 player proper CO-OP and thus they would get their hopes up and possibly waste their money if they were to first play more than 2 hours before trying to play with someone else.If someone is aware that the game doesn't in fact have a REAL multiplayer feature then I would say it's a worthwhile single player survival game if you assume that essentially nothing will change in the long run, in other words buy it if the CURRENT features make you happy because time has told us little will change as with most EA games aside from the Unity upgrade which honestly was a side grade if I'm being honest since they took that time to kinda mess up the UI.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game, but I can't.The game gets off to a rough start: the unskippable starting cut-scene. Fine for the first time, but when you're playing a SURVIVAL game, odds are you're going to die at least once or twice. Sometimes the starting island screws you over (more on that in a bit) and you need to reset back up, or maybe you're a permadeath player. Either way, sitting there waiting for the rather loud cut-scene to finish is tedious at best. Okay fine, you make it past that. The game has a straightforward tutorial that teaches you how the survival mechanics work-like any good game of this genre-but as I mentioned above, you could have a short lived attempt depending on your starting island. More than a few occasions did I have to restart the game simply because I didn't have enough vital resources to survive the time it takes for said resources to respawn. That alone is why I quit playing when I first got the game. When some friends brought the game up again, I figured I'd give it another shot. Imagine our surprise to discover a game this old still had a two player cap, despite the community clearly hoping for more. We decided no big deal and I attempted to play solo again for the first time in years.Y'all, this is where I honestly can't even attempt to enjoy this game anymore. The physics are HORRIBLE! In a game where that surviving is the POINT OF THE GAME you'd think they would have refined this to be actually playable! Alas, it is not. From crafted rafts refusing to follow the laws of physics, to trees shooting off into the sea, to the annoyance of not being able to simply jump in a reasonable manner (once again, to SURVIVE and avoid danger), this alone is enough of a reason for me to uninstall, hide, and try my best to forget this game even exists. Thanks for reading if you stuck around! Even if this game was free I'd STRONGLY recommend against it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first game review so I don't enter this lightly.I'm 130 hours into Stranded Deep, release December 2018. So far I can say the experience IS WHAT YOU MAKE IT. If you expect zombies, action games, long story modes, multi-player death matches, then you will be disappointed. If you like excellent graphics, thoughtful survival games, then this could be for you.I just recently watched Tom Hanks again in Castaway. Play Stranded Deep for about 15 hours, then watch the movie. You will be saying to yourself "Build a water collector!" "You need a fishing spear!" "Get a smoker going!". Literally the game follows the movie; washed up on a desert island in a life raft, having to scavenge to survive. Keep all items, they may come in useful!If you like a challenging game without the bad guys, but with sharks you have to build spears and spearguns for, you will enjoy this. If you like hoarding supplies and building a base that keeps you alive and lets you explore without worrying about food and water, you'll like this. 130 hours can't be wrong. Collect the crates from the wrecks underwater and build you chosen island up. If you hate a particular shark, well he is leather and food when you decide to use your speargun. 8 )If you like continuous combat or a story line that leads to a conclusion, you won't like this. Be prepared it's early access so won't be supported to endgame regularly. But I had great fun and the moment I speargunned a great white shark was the best ever. 8 )

_childDocuments_.review: Stranded Deep is not a bad game. Its actually one of my favorite single player survival games (im not counting remote play together. that is not a substitute for online multiplayer and its laughable that the devs treat it like it is) The idea, setting, and gameplay are all good for the most part. The issue with stranded deep is the developer. Its been in early access for 6 years now with very long periods of silence from the devs and inconsistent updates. for a while i thought that Stranded Deep was dead, or at least i did until the devs stabbed their PC playerbase in the back. They ported the unfinished, unpolished game to consoles for a cash grab and then proceeded to create and release poorly planned, rushed, time exclusive content to consoles that does not make sense or fit the game so they could claim that the game had a half assed ending. They finally got around to releasing the content for their PC playerbase (who make up most of the sales of their game btw, we funded the company by buying this game) but its the fact that they treated their PC players as second class citizens. If this game was the developers priority it would have been out of early access a long time ago, they made more than enough money through PC sales alone (youre welcome Beam Team) and have had more than enough time to fund a team of extra devs and finish the game. If you want to buy the game because you just enjoy survival games then by all means purchase stranded deep, like i said its a fun game. But dont expect the game to go much farther than it already is, its been 6 years and the game is still relatively the same save for the previously mentioned "ending" and a couple of untimely bug fixes. If you dont want to support lazy ungrateful developers that treat their primary playerbase like garbage then dont bother wasting your hard earned money this game.

_childDocuments_.review: How To Start A Car:Before you start the car: Locate the gas pedal and the brake pedal.  Get your foot in position with your heel on the floor so you can swivel back and forth between the brake and the gas comfortably.Make sure that the car is in PARK.  Now start the car.  With your foot on the brake, put the car in ‘Drive’.  Slowly lift your foot off the brake.  Do not give the car any gas.  The car will move forward slowly.This will be all the speed you need for some maneuvers.  Hover your foot over the brake in case you need to stop suddenly.  Lift it slowly off the brake to start moving again.  You can practice as you learn to drive in an open parking lot.Repeat the same maneuver in ‘Reverse.’  This slow speed is all the speed you’ll need for backing up in many cases.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend you get this game at the asking price, assuming you can afford it and it's the sort of game you enjoy playing ;)  Yes it is unfinished but this does not mean the game is sub-par in its present state.  The game is excellent already and is getting better with every update.  You can see that the graphics are pretty top notch, and it's optimised nicely too; I can run it on "medium" graphical settings on my laptop (which does meet the recommended system requirements, so don't go getting it if your rig genuinely lacks any grunt).  What I like about this game probably more than anything is that there's a lot of stuff it doesn't do for you.  Not only do you have to figure out mechanics for yourself (lots of good guides out there) but there are psychological aspects of survival which the game manages exceptionally well to implement from inside the player's mind, as opposed to the frequently-seen alternative of quantifying every aspect of your physical and mental health and presenting you with detailed information.  Above everything the game forces you to face a constant dilemma of whether to endure boredom or risk adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: First I'd like to say that this game has a very interesting game concept and game design, though nothing completely unique with the other dozen games of the survival genre that have come about the last year or so.  It is a nice change from the zombie / apocolyptic theme in a more serene tropical setting.Unfortunately I would not recommend purchasing this yet in its current state.  I would class is as somewhere between a proof of concept / tech demo and a pre-alpha release.The game is graphically polished and very appealing on the eye (probably why its has sold around 500,000 units),  however once you get past the nice polished graphics of the game,  the actual content is lacking.   - The crafting system is very primitive with a only a handful of thing to actually craft.  - The survival aspect is almost non-existent.  You can survive indefinitely without any problems.- The exploration aspect is repetetive as there is only a handful of biomes / islands that can be generated and they are finitely randomly generated so once you've seen 5 or so islands, you've seen them all.- Item discovery is done by exploring ship wrecks, etc of which there's around maybe 50 items to find  with half of them pretty much having no actual purpose in the game.The game is in its VERY early stages and quite honestly,  should not be released to the public let alone make anyone pay to play it.  The game has potential, so keep an eye on it,  but don't hold your breath.

_childDocuments_.review: So I haven't really achieved much in terms of survival or crafting, but each time I last a little longer. The game has its ups and downs, like all.Pros: True survival, no map, no stat bars, realistic inventory space, interestingly unique, yet primitive, crafting system, spectacular animals, great graphics, sickness.Do not expect to have your hand held through this. You get a few moments of learning on the plane before it goes down, and you have to get up to the surface. You do not get stat bars, i.e., health, stamina, hunger, thirst. Just gotta stay hydrated and fed at all times. There is no map, you are stranded. At most I have found a compass, and still have gotten confused and lost. You can only carry 8 items, some stack, stack max being 4. The crafting is all done in front of you. No need to waste materials on a silly crafting table. The wild life is great, sharks, stingrays, fish, crabs. Well made, too. The graphics are wonderful, nice water, nice weather, no complaints. Sickness... Always cook your food if you can. You can get sick, I am not sure of the side effects, since you are all alone with no guide to tell you why you just threw up. Weird pro, but its nice to actually have to let a crab sit on your fire for a while, at which point it makes a microwave 'ding', no matter where you are. Not realistic but mildly amusing.Cons: Physics, warning time, placement of items, no bags?, no shadow, achievements not working.Not many issues I have here. Some of the physics are off, you can move four felled trees with a potato if you pull it into them. C'mon now. Warning times are hideous, you have roughly ten minutes, give or take, before you die of hunger or thirst after getting a warning saying you are weak and should eat something. Really difficult when you are traveling between islands, makes inventory space a hassle, which brings me to the final two issues. Some items, on pick up, vanish. Torches and buckets are the only two I've managed to get so far, but they vanish, and are just 'passive' items I think. Waterbottles are filled by buckets which are filled by the ocean and you can do it anywhere. Filtration isn't fast, so I'm not sure on the logic there, along with the fact I have no idea where the bucket/torch is being held, seeing as it isn't in one of my 8 slots. No bags. There is a question mark because I'm not sure if I'm missing something, or just haven't collected the materials for it yet. Would be nice to have in instances of island travel, for food/water/tools. Not having a shadow is pretty big in terms of good gameplay. I can see both of my arms, yet all the shadow is is the tool I weild. I've noticed that I should have gotten almost all the achievements by now as well, but they seem to not be working.That's all I've got now, but it really is a great game, and despite some of the horrendous, fatal issues I've had, I can't stop playing. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is an updated review after I replayed it early 2023. I would still avoid this game. It is visually appealing, but that is about as far as it goes. The game feels like it is still in early Alpha stage with so many bugs and glitches it just makes it a frustrating experience. From snagging on scenery and jarring transitions between water and land, it just breaks you out of the immersion the game tries to give you. Simple physics like jumping and climbing is just too strange a process. For example, to get on top of a boat, there is a ladder, but the ladder isn't usable. For some unknown reason you have to climb up the wall, which is a combination of running headlong into the wall while randomly mashing jump. Only occasionally will your character even jump. If you are in water, you will randomly find yourself unable to surface as you get snagged on a stray atom that means you have to WASD yourself like mad to get free.Building is a nightmare. It goes white when you can build and red when intersecting with scenery. Makes sense. Except when it doesn't. Want to build a raft base on that flat bit of beach? No chance. There is a grain of sand that is too high. You have to wade out into chest-deep shark infested water and try to put some planks down. How about building a home? Nope. Same issue. That non-interactive leaf in the way means you will have to have a 2m x 2m hole in the floor where you cannot place that piece of floor. I can't believe the game still has these issues since 2015. I think they just got bored of it and decided to release it. There are mods out for the game, but they are so unsupported they often crash the game. Save your money.EDIT: 2023... Still very much the same. Placing objects is still a very frustrating process. Leaves still hamper you putting down items. You have to hack the entire tree down and clean up the debris just because a single leaf is blocking your path. I am swearing at this games physics more than I am enjoying it. Avoid.

_childDocuments_.review: Review updated on December 2022 - Same old issues.... Not impressed with this game at all. The graphics are beautiful but the crafting and inventory system/menus are HORRIBLE. After playing games like 7 days to Die, Minecraft, the long dark, and many others, this game is unplayable. For example, why not just allow players to harvest yucca with a click of the mouse? Instead you need to hack at the leaves as if you are cutting it down, then the leaves (which are tied with string??) fall on the ground. It's then very difficult to see where they are, you need to find the white outlines. Very bad. When picking something up it goes into your hands not into your inventory. When dropping something it automatically puts the next item in your inventory into your hands, like a tarp....WHY!? The game makes decisions for us when we play. When entering the crafting menu, you are left with a shopping list that goes off the screen with multiple lists, no tabs, and no search option. 2/3 of the crafting menu shows the background which is useless.  The more difficult a game is, the less likely people will play it. This game can have so much more potential, I hope the Dev's learn from other games that have a large following. Two frustrating thumbs down!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm just gonna come out and say it: This game is not fun anymore. It used to be a challenge to get started, with an eventual point you'd reach where things would stay level. Now, it feels like nothing more than a constant war against the food/water meters.  Others have complained about the new water system and I have to join in: The water filter object is terrible. It requires fiber to continuously supply water, which is just plain ridiculous when a good rainfall hits and anyone with half a brain would keep their coconut halves to catch rainwater, or even use the tarp on some sticks. There were buckets before, and while I do feel they were far too abundant in the past, having just one or two would make a huge difference in not having to constantly deal with the thirst meter.This is not the game for you if you feel like having a casual castaway experience as the sole survivor on a bunch of tropical islands. It's more of a "let's see how many pieces of my shelter I can build before I have to pay attention to my food/water" simulator. Honestly, the greatest Castaway type game I ever played was The Sims 2: Castaway Stories for the Nintendo Wii, and I wish someone out there with mad game programming skills would learn from it and come up with something I would love to buy.

_childDocuments_.review: I've bought this game on January . Twice. One copy for me, one for a good friend.The game had just come out a few days prior and seemed challenging and interesting enough to check it out.15€ invested and we started.A few almost fading keyboard notes reached my headphones. A waving Stranded Deep logo appeared on my screen. As I sat out to start my new game I was crushed by how amazing it looked. It was 2015 and those ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sun shafts and shaders still haunt me until this day.The game looked amazing and it felt amazing. Yes, , the intro, I know. The Forest came out sometime in 2014 and this intro was basically a one point copy. But everything after the intro. .You are flying to a unknown destination in your plane, private jet I guess, when you suddently crash. Stranded with only the emergency boat and your clothes, you arrive on a nearby island. A small, coconut rich island. From here on out, .✓ Incredible visuals since 2015✓ (Used to) Minimalistic design✓ Easy crafting system (Now bound with a skill system)✓ Fairly simple to get into and progress✓ Generated islands with different sizes and stuff✓ Sharks & other fish you can hunt & hunt you✓ Now with animals on the islands you can hunt✓ Old, rusty ruins of ships and other sunken buildings to explore✓ Swimming and diving mechanics are really nice✗ ✗ The new skill system breaks immersion for me✗ Sometimes necessary things (Like a hammer) are hard to find✗ Your items break ✗ I loved this game. I could always start it up and simply roam around my island with so much to do and so many more things to explore; every update. New gadgets, new animals, new weapons, more stuff to craft.I used to put coconuts or just scrap I didn't need at the place I left my island, swam a straight line to the next island, planted stones and looked for loot. That way I could always find my way back.In the last few updates the game has changed . That's not always a bad thing.The minimalistic swimming, diving and surviving game I once knew and loved has been replaced by a game that tries too hard to reach The Forest's state.Don't,  ruin this masterpiece. The menu has been massacred and the lovely tune of keyboard notes has vanished. Where did the minimalistic game from 2015 go? Don't get me wrong, the game is still incredible fun to play. But it's just not the same anymore. Back then I was able to play hours and hours, swim around islands, explore sunken ships and fight sharks. Now I have to skill up for ages before being able to build a base. That's not...no. That's not what we wanted.

_childDocuments_.review: Hi,Please read this honest review before buying the game.My dad and I sit in the shed most weekends and week nights hiding from Mother Aunt Moredeborah watching Castaway.It is our best movie and all that Mum has sanctioned us to watch.We used to talk about how Moredeborah would follow us no matter where we went in the city and that the only way to get away from her was on a dessert island. Most times we would hug and cry after that conversation, most times. Then along comes this game. I remember I was hiding in the chicken coupe when Dad came scurrying in (he knew all my hiding place because he used them as well). I thought it was a routine fleeing of my Moredeborahs wrath. Not this time. He had urgent news to tell me and I could see how excited he was, as he had wetted his pant fronts and scraped his elbows. He gripped me, digging in his unkept nails, and he, pulling me in close said, "I have a way to escape Mother Aunt Moredeborah." I blinked back tears and choked out a whimpering "thank you father."That night we loaded up this game with a title that reflects our hearts sentiment. My father and I played for hours huddled under the blankets safe from the Mother Aunty. Without this game I think we wouldnt be here today.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually write reviews, but I feel like this one needs it. When you first boot up the game, everything is great. The survival is fun, the graphics are pretty good, and it is just an all around fun game. It is also worth a mention that the physics are great. Just being able to drag a tree or paddle a raft dynamically is great. The crafting is also intuitive and nice. It gets a bit grindy at times, but if you are into serious realistic survival games, without zombies or guns, this is for you. The problem lies in the little things, that eventually build up into huge glaring issues. The sad part about it is, they are usually things that were put there on purpose by the devs to add a “survival feel” to the game. The most obvious one that comes to mind is the one save slot. I know you want to make it so we have to see how long we can survive on an island, but really? Thankfully this is easily bypassed by manually backing up the save game, but we should be able to have multiple games going at once without having to do actual work to save our games. There is also no “creative” mode, in case you get bored of the survival aspect and just want to build a house or go fishing. There is an option to change your game to “survival” or “builder” modes, but when you click on these, they do nothing. I found a thread on steam support asking what these buttons did, in November. Meaning that there has been close to five months since the buttons were implemented, and they still do nothing. Another issue is the building. Before I got the game, when you wanted to build a house, you would place down a foundation block, then walls and a roof on top of that. Now you need a separate foundation block, then a floor block on top of the foundation block. This means that building houses requires a lot more wood, which means more grinding trees for 10 minutes until they fall down. Beyond this, for me, it just doesn’t work. Whenever I try to place floors on top of foundations, they glitch out and disappear. So I can’t build anything. The game technically has a “create an island” feature. Which sounds pretty good, right? Except it is completely broken. For one thing, you are limited to a tiny size for your island. To give them the benefit of the doubt, all islands are tiny in the game, and they are working on getting bigger islands. Also, you lag out when you approach a regular island, much less a huge one. The next problem is that you have to place each asset individually, including trees. I can understand placing assets like ships and barrels down individually, but having to place down each individual tree and then rotating it takes hours. Maybe i’m just used to the Cities Skylines map creator, which is absolutely great. In the Cities Skylines creator, you choose the type of tree and then spread it over the landscape with a brush. If stranded deep had that option, as well as the individual placement option, the map creator would be a lot more useable. Don’t even get me started on the camera for the map creator, there are too many problems with it to list here, such as having to hold down right click to pan up or down, and then it still taking a minute to get to a top down view because it is so unresponsive. basically, what were the devs smoking when they designed it? Once you have done all that, you can use the “cartographer” mode to place it. You could also download a map off the internet because the game doesn’t have steam workshop support. Half the time the maps are outdated (not the devs fault). The cartographer mode is also a stupid idea to try and make the game feel more ”survivally”. Basically, you can place down your custom island in little squares on a map, then you have to actually travel to the island. This could be bypassed by just spawning at the island, but again, you only have one save slot.In the end, i’m still going to recommend the game, despite it’s shortcomings, because it is still in early access. It has a lot of potential moving forward, if the devs fix the issues the game has currently. It is worth a mention that when i mention “devs”, I mean two people. It is absolutely amazing that two people could make a quality of a game as good as this.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that had genuine promise and opportunity. A visually great experience and the simple idea of just being stranded on a small desert island. The foundation of the "survival" concept.Except it's riddled with problems, and has remained in 'early access' for now half a decade, proving that the early access system is so easily abused.In a survival game, the idea of crafting is near enough its most vital gameplay. Yet this game will hamstring you with the fact that almost NOTHING respawns. You need rocks? Sticks? Food? none of this will respawn. The only thing, the single, one object, that will respawn in this game is palm sprigs. So leaves. Thats it.More importantly, there will come a point when you can no longer create tools, harvest food, get water. Building and crafting anything is entirely worthless because it uses vital resources you need and will never get more of.Then there's every other aspect of this game. This game has character leveling, yet you'll never know what that means. Harvesting, fishing, athletics... After 13 hours of playing I still have zero understanding of what this effects as nothing has changed.The same goes for survival statistics. Food, Water, Sunburn (yes really), and then poison and various effects. I assume most of these will kill you... slowly. Even drowning is such an insanely slow effect on health. But these are made even more painful as resources DO. NOT. RESPAWN. You could accidentally be tapped ever so gently by a puffer fish and get poisoned. It will take like an hour to die from this, but will never be cured without making it yourself.Your game could easily no longer have antidote plants in the game, but you wont know. Save your game and bam, your entire save file is destroyed.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first bought this game over a year ago, I was very excited to see how it would develop over time, and I was looking forward to a more polished survival game that didn't rely on zombies or zombie-like creatures to create tension. However, it's been over a year, and this game, as other reviews have stated, still struggles with some of the same issues it had when it first entered Early Access. Don't get me wrong, the game hasn't been abandoned (far from it), but the focus seems to be mainly on new content and not on fixing the current content as it is. (You can still get stuck on/in things, or get flung into the air to your death.) The mechanics have changed, sometimes for the better and sometimes very much not (it used to be a lot easier to break rocks and coconuts, for example). New content is great, especially in a game that is admittedly plagued by a lack of anything to really do after you get the basics down, but there has to be a balance between fixing the old stuff and adding something extra.All that said, I haven't given up on this game. I do still occasionally fire it up just to see how it's been developing, and some of the things I've seen have been promising. As it is right now, however, I can't say I would recommend it. Save your money until the game has had a chance to mature a little more. Maybe after they've fixed the glitch that allows you to chop trees at four times the normal speed.

Multiplayer needs to be enhanced, additional players would be great, but just fixing the connectivity/syncing problems would be appreciated. The menu should be explained in the tutorial missions, so as to avoid a complete dependence on player guides elsewhere online. Having items that can't be picked up and stored, namely tires and barrels used to craft raft bases is redundant and more annoying than "creative" on the dev's part.The game is in alpha, but that's been a while to keep saying that's the reason it's still unstable. Decent game with potential, personally worth buying and investing some time into, but it still has a long way to go.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, here we are again with another Early Access Alpha release ( and review ) on Steam, lol!  This review will be rather long as most people want more of an analysis to base their purchasing decision on instead of just: "This game rocks! 10/10 would get stranded again!"  I've only played about 6hrs so far and as much as I would recommend this game I would also NOT recommend it.  Let me explain:  The controls, at least for me, are flawless and I haven't noticed any issues so far although it takes a bit to get the scheme down.  The graphics aren't groundbreaking but nontheless acceptable and the animations are smooth.  The crafting system if pretty intuitive and easy to use, instead of dragging and dropping like DayZ and going through an animation you have to manually move and manipulate the items OUTSIDE your inventory and the system is not too picky about whats on the ground as a small menu will pop up and show you what you can build with what you have in your pile and you can drop more craftable items in your pile to craft other stuff.  There isn't a lot going on at once onscreen since you are, ya know, stranded in the middle of the South Pacific with dozens of islands all around you in just about every direction.  Most islands are small with a few larger ones here and there but YOU WILL run out of resources on your little island getaway and will be forced to get out in your raft and explore the other islands and the sea for sunken ships and other very useful items.  There is a way to make a motor for your raft to GO A HELLEVA LOT FASTER than paddling along between islands at half the speed of smell but you will do metric ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of paddling just to find all the gear and loot you need to have fun with the game and its system.  I mean, IT IS a game about being stranded and surviving but I hope for ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ they speed up the paddling, it gets REALLY boring paddling for ever to get to the next island, but what are ya gonna do, ya know?  Anyway, if the devs keep on it and keep improving upon the mechanics and the crafting system and add new elements and depth it will be a fantastic game, especially if they somehow eventually incorporate multiplayer into it.  So far I haven't found a map or anything in game that helps you navigate around the island or helps you get back to your HOME ISLAND, I suppose since every game is different that would be a tad difficult to put in.  However, if you find the blue compass for the love of GabeN don't lose it!  It is like the "Wilson" of Stranded Deep!  Happy Gaming!

_childDocuments_.review: This game has great potential, I would like to see larger islands with more areas to explore.  The process of taking logs back to the main island is a bit boring, so larger islands with more plant life, trees, food, etc.. would leave more exploration time and less travel/hauling time.  The crafting is fine, not great but it is an alpha game and I do expect to see more items in the future, such as larger rafts/boats.  I would definately recommend this game to anyone who likes survival/crafting games, but is ok dealing with alpha bugs.  I do have give the devs crediti, they seem to fix things quickly.  The ability to grow food from seeds and hunt wild animals (boars, rabbits, birds etc..) would make this game more interesting and replayable.  Maybe even some land threats, bears or whatever would give it a little more excitement.  The distance between islands makes for some boring trips back and forth with little to do other than avoid sharks and paddle.  I would also like to see a crude map function, as of now I just had to keep paper and write coordinates down on paper, which works, but I would rather see this as an in game function.  Also a coop maybe 4-8 players would be fantastic for those of us who like to play with others.  I read another review and agree, the server only would be crap due to hackers and people who generally like to ruin other peoples game time.  Other than that is generally a fun and interesting game, I look forward  to the future updates.

I was forced to go to the forums to learn about these attributes.  I prefer my games to be more inclusive and not reliant upon outside sources of information.Then it got boring.  I would travel from island to island, doing the same old thing.  I want to discover clues.  I want to discover treasures, beyond flashlights and axes.  Why can't storms wash crates on shore?  I want the ability to build markers to tell me to which Islands I have traveled from my "home".  I want the ability to break up large rocks into smaller ones.  And where are the bananas???I have given this a thumbs down, but so far the developers have done a great job and the fact that I want more is a good sign.  Done right and this will become a great game.

And Traveling on the life raft an hour after creating a character because there wasn't more than 4-5 rocks on the starting island is bad.In addition you can build massive rafts which is very cool and does give you something to aim for but you cannot build walls, half walls, or any building structures on your massive raft. Even something so obvious as a bed, or in this games case a shelter cannot be placed on the surface of a raft.I like the game but I can't play more than a few hours before it annoys me in more than a few ways, to push me to uninstall until a new update. _childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable survival game, nice game play loop. There are bugs/glitches, though they don't "significantly" detract from enjoying the game. Things like fish flying above the water, watching a boar render in the distance - 20 feet in the air, abruptly fall, then run circles in the air. Cutting down a tree to watch it go flying across the island. Re-arranging barrel scrap 50 times before the game allows you to build it in to your raft. You know, funny bugs/glitches - minor irritations at worst.Navigating by compass and still getting lost.. feels bad. It's very fortunate that the "Cartographer" option is there to see where in the world the player is, but seeing that your base is due East, you go due East, then find you're on the bottom of the map... yeah.All this being said, minor irritations aside, I still recommend this game. It's fun, picturesque, enjoyable and frankly (regardless of the annoying potato grind) - I am very much looking forward to flying the Gyrocopter! That being said, I've had my raft motor for ages but absolutely no fuel because finding potatoes was.. challenging (after the one on my starter island died before I knew how incredibly important it was).OH! Don't step on purple star looking things! Lost my first game file that way because I couldn't level up fast enough to make poison Antidote.

_childDocuments_.review: At Release date 2015-01-23, the game shows a lot of promise already, at the start its fun trying to find out how you can survive on your little island and figuring out crafting recipes. But after you run out of resources its really hard to just go to another island and bring back stuff, since from a distance the islands look practicly the same. The Devs said theres no end goal right now, so to keep ourselves bussy we can do stuff like surviving, exploring, base building or fighting sharks... which haven't really gone successful for me yet.The surviving part gets easy when you realize all you need to do is eat a few coconuts to get your fill of water and hydration. Exploring gets tedious when rowing to another island takes ages and have a high risk of bugging your raft out so you are left out in the dangerous open water without refuge. But diving into the waters to search through the various ship wrecks around is quite exciting, especially when you realize a shark is just outside waiting for you to come out. Another bad point though is the very limited backpack space you have, and putting stuff in your raft just ends up with them disappearing eventually.Base building/Home making isn't really a great option right now since you can only chop down coconut trees which are quite limited on your island, also rocks are also few on your island and as mentioned above, going back and forth between islands just fetching rocks is not a fun process.So at its current state its not something I would play for hours with no end, but I feel that it has a great start already and would love to play more of it after a few feature updates.

_childDocuments_.review: DAY ONE: Found a crab.. Named him Bob. Bob is my friend. DAY TWO: Bob and me cut down a palm tree to gain coconuts.DAY THREE: Bob is a little sad today, we ate the last coconuts.DAY FOUR: Well, today was fun.. We started our first fire, accedently burning our raft. DAY FIVE: Bob attacked me today, he even cut my arm a little... I think it's because we run out of food.. And water..DAY SIX: Today bob decided to run away, he tried to swim away from me. He failed and I have now build a cage for him.DAY SEVEN: I build a house for myself, I caught a fish for me and Bob to share.DAY EIGHT: Bob ate most of the fish, I only got the tail.DAY NINE: I'm starting to feel the hunger... Bob also told me that I looked handsome.DAY TEN: I saw a ship today, it didn't see me. DAY -.. What day is it? DAY TWELVE: I ate bob today, he was getting on my nerves.DAY THIRTEEN: I miss Bob.DAY FOURTEEN: What have I done.. I'm still hungry.. It wasn't worth it.DAY FIFTEEN: I can't live without Bob, I can't take it anymore.DAY SIXTEEN: I'm going to drown myself today.(Also, I rate this game 8/10, amazing fun when you make up random stories. - Needs more things to craft + more animals)

I was super stoked to dive back in and play only to realize that everything I worked so hard for is gone! I would have thought that it saved to Steam cloud but obviously that's not the case. Its quite unfortunate that if you get a new PC or have a serious hardware issue that requires a restore, you will lose all your progress.

_childDocuments_.review: Not yet a finished product, but looks and feels awesome. There are a couple of bugs, like the despawning raft when traveling, or the sharks swiming under the beach, or getting stuck in the shipwrecks, but those will be fixed very soon from what i have heard. Looking forward to playing this again when i can fully explore all islands. Oh... and this is not a Bear Grylls game.. if you try to eat a raw crab, you will be puking instantly :)Found out that if you are not saving, your raft or boat will not despawn while traveling to another island!!!So here i am eager to survive! I start fresh on a small island, gather all rocks i could find, make a hammer, a crude axe and a spear. My pocket knife gets all worn up, but im not worried, i have the crude axe and the crude knife to chop down palm trees. I start building my shelter, drink and eat few coconuts, i am FINE! Storm is coming and my shelter is not yet build, i hurry up and make 2 pieces of the roof, and get inside waiting till morning with fear that lightning may strike me. Next morning the sun lights up my face. I continue making a bed, searching nearby shipwreck and i find a pair of binoculars. Ill use them to scout the sea for ships. Next i am building a bed so i dont get bitten by the many crabs that are crawling around.I start to feel hungry so i am quickly breaking some coconuts and get fed. I feel fine, but suddenly i realise both my crude axe and crude knife are all worn off. I desperately need a rock to make a crude axe!!!! Or else ill starve to death. I am afraid to hunt for fish and eat them, some may be poisonous. I look at my watch, full HP, full bar for hunger and full bar for thirst. I decide to travel to next island to get a rock. At this point, i am unable to scavenge for potatoes nor break coconuts nor cook fish or crabs. After 10 minutes i am on the next island, looking around for rocks.....NOTHING!!! The shipwreck has a hardened case but when i go near it, it despawns and i am unable to loot it. Must be a mirage. I search the island again, pick up some wood and get back to my boat. I aim for the island to the right, while making sure i will remember where my main island is. I start traveling with caution. I arrive on third island at dark and go look for rocks. I am happy to find 4 rocks, i check my watch and my hunger has only 2 bars left. Im not worried, ill be fine! I get back to my boat and triangulate the main island from where i have left. I need to get back and get myself a crude axe crafted and eat some coconuts or else i will die. At this point i realise i should have taken some ropes with me. I could have crafted the crude axe and get some food on this island. I check my watch again: 1 bar left. I start to feel worried. No time to waste! I start rowing towards the first island. Three huge sharks are easy to spot somewhere to the left, im not afraid of them. Suddenly i hear the engine of a boat.. i look around fast - I should have taken my binoculars with me!!!! I dont see anything so i look at the sharks and start rowing again. On the horizon, on the direction i was heading i see 2 islands now. I am confused and i dont know which one is mine... i look back i look front im going for the island on the right....no.. it must be the left one....or the right.. i dont know.... ill go for the one on the left. While standing up in my plastic boat, i trip and fall over the board. I have to go around so i can climb up while making efforts to maintain my orrientation. I feel weak now, i am hungry. The islands seem to be the same, sharks are gone.... or no.. they are behind me. Desperately i am pushing with my last bits of strenght towards the closest island. At this moment even a raw crab would be good. I look back at my watch, half of my life bar is gone. I know i am about to die. My last thought: I should have carried some ropes! GAME OVERI feel like starting again!
