_childDocuments_.review: There are some nice ideas and the graphics and core gameplay loop are serviceable BUT (a) survival isn't that challenging, in the beginning you mostly need to ration rocks (b) the interface is awful. Some of it is due to being designed for both PC and console, which on the one hand does increase the userbase and thus developer ressources. On the other, you still end up with a poorly designed PC interface which should mean worse reviews and lower PC sales. Either way, I ended up fighting the interface much more than the environment for no discernible reason. The radial inventories are merely wasteful, the biggest issue is that you can't carry big stuff with both hands (at, for instance, the price of losing access to the rest of your inventory while you do so) but have to drag everything awkwardly holding right mouse button. This extends to smaller stuff as well, you can place meat in the smoker, but have to drop it on the floor and then right mouse fling it onto the hobo stove. There is a skill levelling system but it's no barrier to crafting (which is good) but also doesn't for instance allow you to bypass annoying animations at higher levels so not sure what it is needed for.The loot is weird, lots of compasses and motor parts, very few stones and most importantly, little in the way of dual use. You either have the part you need or you don't. You practically never end up regretting a particular crafting decision because later finds open up different opportunities, it's very simple and linear in that respect. Still, if the interface was good, this wouldn't matter much.

_childDocuments_.review: This game really immerses you on a stranded island and does a great job making you feel like you truly need to manage your character's health while not being too demanding to where you feel you can't do anything else except watch your health, hydration, and hunger bars (like an Amazon based survival game I can think of...). There are still lots of glitches, such as sharks simply swimming into land and disappearing, and the crafting/inventory systems forcing you drop something you just crafted before you can pick it up, but they're minimal and really don't affect game play. I do wish there was a little bit more to do other than explore, as after two islands you've already discovered all animals, loot, and sunken ships (besides the bosses). I still highly recommend this game to any survival genre enthusiasts.

_childDocuments_.review: Stranded Deep is an enthralling open world survival game that offers players an unforgettable adventure. Developed by Beam Team Games, this game will test your survival skills as you find yourself stranded in the Pacific Ocean following a mysterious plane crash. With no means to call for help, you must craft, build, and hunt for resources to survive.In Stranded Deep, players are tasked with exploring the vast expanse of the Pacific Ocean while collecting supplies, crafting tools and weapons, and building shelters to stay alive. You will need to manage your character's hunger, thirst, and exposure levels through an interactive survival watch. The game also allows you to level up skills such as harvesting, craftsmanship, cooking, physical, and hunting to increase efficiency and unlock new crafting combinations.The game features an interactive crafting menu that allows you to craft various tools and weapons such as spears, axes, bows, and spearguns. You can also quick-craft items from your inventory or the ground around you. The crafting system allows you to turn almost anything into something useful, making resource management a crucial aspect of the game.Players can build their own homes away from home with dozens of tiers and building pieces to choose from. You can start with a weak and flimsy palm frond shack and upgrade to a solid clay brick house. Customizing your raft with sails, canopies, storage, anchors, and boat motors, or constructing a gyrocopter, are also great ways to explore the vast expanse of the Pacific Ocean.The game's procedurally generated world ensures that no two islands are the same. Players can dive for sunken shipwrecks, search for abandoned shelters from previous survivors, or search for rare sea creatures like whales. Hunting, fishing, trapping, and skinning animals are other ways to collect food or assert your dominance over the Pacific islands. There are also three bosses to take on, which offer rewards upon defeating them.Stranded Deep allows for online or split-screen co-op modes, making the game even more enjoyable to play with friends. You can also customize your world through the map island editor, which allows you to manually place trees, rocks, and creatures to create your own adventure island to share with friends.Overall, Stranded Deep is an excellent open-world survival game that offers players a unique and exciting experience. With its immersive gameplay, stunning graphics, and challenging survival mechanics, it's definitely worth playing. So if you're looking for a game that will test your survival skills and provide hours of entertainment, then Stranded Deep is the perfect choice.

Because of this, the game leaves you "Stranded Deep" In Frustration!.......................................................................It's a great start, but it lacks so many features and common sense that so many other similar games have already mastered. As of now though, it is lacking to be honest, but I definitely understand that it is early access and that if why I am recommending some changes that I think are really important for the future of this game. A lot of stuff has already been recommended in other reviews, but this is what I think some people may have missed and could add a great deal to the game.- A variety in food and nutrition should be needed in order to sustain ones health as I'm pretty sure living of coconuts would make you lack in essential nutrients- Land animals on larger islands e.g. monkeys, tortoises etc. (maybe you can tame them?? :D)- Digging would add a great deal as it would allow for landscaping and better construction of homes- A variety in islands- Throwable objects e.g. rocks, spears etc. (maybe you can i just haven't figured it out yet haha)- More deadly environments e.g. deadly animals and insects (when you're on land you're pretty much invincible if you have coconuts)- Deadly weather (wind gusts could hurl debris at you, rain could blur your vision and make you prone to illness etc.)- Item storage e.g. a chest or somesort in which you can store a limited amount of items- Waves (can toss you around a bit and make paddling more difficult)- A shadow for your person haha- Character customization - Destructable environments e.g. You could use you lighter to set alight a palm tree and use the charcol that it makesThat's all i can think of for now that hasnt been comonly mentioned. _childDocuments_.review: Gender, MaleName, Samuel Smith. Age 35Day 1, 12th AugustPaddle and inflatable life raft, I paddled to shore, unsure of what to expect from such a small and barren island. On arrival I notice the only local inhabitants I can find is a population of what I would now describe to be extremely delicious crabs. Armed with just a knife, paddle and lighter I managed to construct a fairly crude fire in order to cook the local population on. My hunger levels are starting to ease, however I am extremely thirsty and I do not wish to waste the precious water I managed to carry from the wreckage of my plane.With my remaining time I have managed to construct a bed in which to sleep. I will continue the journal tomorrow.Day 2, 13th AugustI awoke blinking and almost blinded by the sun and overwhelmed by the heat. I had only forgotten for a brief moment my current situation. After gathering my senses I set out to start creating some crude tools with which to hunt, cook and craft. I do not yet know how I am going to make a spear, as there appear to be very few rocks around the shoreline on this barren hell I now call home.I managed to somehow scrape enough stone together however to make a crude yet effective axe. Again, night time beckons and I have already eaten my fill of crab for the day.Day 3, 14th AugustI awake to yet again be smacked in the face by the damning reality of my current predicament. With no-one to socialise with, I feel I may become more and more like the crazy stranded hermits I had seen in motion pictures before the crash, talking to coconuts and dancing around fires during the middle of the night. I will not let myself succumb to this.I had spotted just off shore a small sunken vessel, browned with metal decay from the salty waters of my surroundings. I waded out to the vessel to search the cabin and to my surprise, found a woodcutting axe, a lantern and some bandages. Whoever was stranded here in the past or whoever left these supplies clearly perished. I feel their misfortunes are now my savior.Day 4, 15th AugustAfter yesterday's apparent success I have made a formal decision to abandon the idea of living the remainder of my time out on this sandy, dusty hell and I have chosen to gather the supplies I have and make for land...or at least just somewhere else.So far I have not encountered any other wildlife, aside from crabs and sardines just off the shore and continue to rely on that to be my main source of survival. I managed to open some coconuts in order to drink the succulent milk from within. It was like nectar as I had used the remaining fresh water I still had yesterday. Night has dawned...dreamless sleep awaits...Day 5, 16th AugustRising early, I made for the raft and paddle and begun pushing it out to sea. My pack is filled with cooked crabs as I realised this may be a long journey. After eating some food I set out for new horizons, not fully understanding what I was about to run into. I had believes my solidarity from living things had been my great advantage so far, however things were about to change very quickly.Paddling towards a small speck I could see in the distance and at this point could only determine to be another god forsaken island I stopped for a moment to observe the scenary. There are many of these barren wastelands dotted all over the sea and I do not know how far I am from the main land at this point. I think to myself, where could I possibly go to be safe? At this very moment the raft moves from underneath me. Startled by the feeling of what was a fin I could only look over the edge of my raft slowly, trembling with fear and anticipation of what may arise from the depths. In this moment there was silence, only the sound of the ocean's waters lapping against my raft. Still trembling I waited, with bated breath, when suddenly a Tiger Shark appeared from the side of my raft and began swimming quickly towards me. Panicking, I swung wildly with my axe, however this made no difference. The shark knocked me into the water and sent my raft veering away from me. I am now officially in hell. With the shark slowly circling me and moving ever closer I feel the need to get back to the raft, so I do. Quickly I swim towards it and manage to board it. With my hands now shaking uncontrollably I reach for my paddle and begin frantically paddling towards the shore of a nearby island.On arrival I come to an understanding that it was my lack of preparation that caused this inevitable scenario.Day 6, 17th AugustIt's raining. It hasn't stopped raining all morning. All throughout the night it continued to pour as I had spent all night hacking away at the local foliage, in order to gather enough resources to construct a crude dwelling. From my watch, it says it is 7:30am. I am now squatting uncomfortably in my shack, wondering where I go from here. Over my breakfast of crab...again...I come to the idea that perhaps the best way to survive is to hunt the very thing I have now learned to fear. Perhaps this will be my downfall. Now, it seems like the only option.Using a rock I smashed earlier this morning and some sticks found lying on the beach, I have managed to make myself two crude, yet sharp spears to combat my underwater foe. Climbing into my raft with my paddle, spears and axe I make my way to open water. Whilst paddling, I notice a brown pipe breaking the top of the water. This can only be the top of a mast of a ship sunken underwater. After gathering my bravery, I took the decision to dive into the water, completely unaware of any danger in my immediate surroundings. Diving deeper, I open the door to the ship, just touching the sea bed and make my way inside. After opening a couple of lockers I have found a torch, a propeller and a jerry can and within a chest in the main room of the ship's interior I have found some flares. Making my way to the surface to find my raft, I then paddle back to shore and deposited my loot into my shack and waited out the rest of the day. It's now too late to go hunting sharks and I do not wish to do this at night time.Day 7, 18th AugustThe days are starting to blur together, it feels like a week has now passed and I am still no closer to rescue. My idea to hunt sharks is my objective today, so with spear in hand I make my way to the open ocean once more in my trusty life raft. Here I sit, waiting for my prey...or demise...After no longer than 3 minutes on the water I see a dark fin making it's way towards me. With a steady hand I waited until my prey moved closer and then delivered a short, sharp stab with my spear. A solid strike. The shark twitched in irritation. This has clearly angered the beast as he quickly circled back and begun heading towards me once more. Another few strikes as he passed the raft, he is clearly now extremely angry and has begun attempting to ram me from my raft, diving after each attempt. However, during each attempt I manage to land a few blows here and there, wounding the shark. He makes his way for deeper waters and just as he begins to swim away, I land the strike that kills him. I had done it. I had done the impossible. My predator has been vanquished and I have dragged his carcass aboard my raft. With my paddle in hand and my prey laying on my lap, I make my way for shore swiftly, so the beast has no time to foul from the wounds suffered.Upon arriving on shore, I drag him towards my crude hut and fire and begin to butcher him for the meat. I realise now I will be eating shark soon and will not go hungry for a number of days. As I begun to cook the portions of shark, I could not help but feel elation at my victory and began to laugh uncontrollably. After a brief moment of insanity I regain my composure, only to look across the ocean for a brief moment to spot another two fins...It would appear I won't go hungry again for a long time yet......

_childDocuments_.review: This is an Early access review of course; and it should be noted that the review is also being written only about a week since the game was initially released upon STEAM so I've played the "bare bones" version so far with only a few updates or content added.  Will have a "TL;DR" at the end for anyone that wants to see my underlying thoughts.Stranded Deep is another classic survival game, but this time it takes place upon the open ocean with small islands scattered about with the supplies you need to survive.  You start off on a plane and it crashes, leaving you afloat in a life raft.  This is where the game currently starts and requires you to go from island to island to gather materials needed to survive and build.  Now before anyone pushes aside the game as just "another survival game", there are a few things that are unique to the game however that I personally quite enjoy that I want to make note off.  First off is the crafting system.  As with many other survival games you are able to craft and make new things to help you survive longer.  Most of the time, most games have a UI or type of tab pull up that you simply throw your supplies onto, and then craft.  Stranded deep does it differently; you have to actually pull your items out of your inventory, place them on the ground, group them with whatever other "ingredients" you need for the crafting recipe, and then craft it that way.  No longer do you simply craft a camp fire and have it instantly placed in your inventory for placing; no, you gather the sticks, throw them down into a pile, then craft it right there in front of you where it will then immediatly be placed.  It's rather a pleasent change from the usual crafting schemes that most survival games have.  Coupled with this is cooking; you don't just use a user interface to throw a fish on the fire, have it cooked, then pick it back up from said UI.  No, in this game you have to hold the fish over the fire and actually wait.  It won't cook immediatly; it will sizzle, smoke, and take a while before it will finally be cooked.  Now, you can either hold it over it manually, or you can craft a type of rotissery, but either way, its nothing simple like "fish + fire = instant dinner in UI".  Second thing that is largely unique to the game is the exploration factor.  At the surface, yes, going from simple island to simple island doesn't seem very exciting.  But in this game there are many a boat that has been wrecked in the ocean depths below you, holding tools, treasures, and weapons that you need to go diving down into to loot.  The underwater world is beautiful, and often (if you have a good enough graphics card/the sea bed is shallow enough) you can catch glimpses of coral formations and fish swimming about underneath your raft as you move around the ocean or as you are on a beach.  Some areas may be very shallow, others much deeper.  And of course, while you do this, you have to worry about predators; sharks like to pop up and go after you for a quick snack as you treasure hunt, or even as you are on the beach.  They are tough predators to take down and they like to tease you a bit it seems with they way they act.  Lastly the world is rather beautiful.  For an early access game, the environment is great and I love seeing the sun rise and fall because of the great graphics engine and how beautiful it can be.  Fog can roll in, heavy rain can pound down on you at any moment; the environment is great and very beautiful.  And this is coming from a guy that doesn't have the best graphics available either.  I can only imagine how great it looks with the proper system and build.   Crafting itself is fun; nothing too unique to be honest here.  You can make tools, build certain items for a small house or base, etc.  The real world crafting system is thrown in here too; you have to place sticks onto a foundation for instance to be able to craft supports that will allow for roofs or walls.  You can make a bed to sleep through the night, a spear for fishing, axes for cutting down wood/keeping away sharks etc.  Combine this with you have to figure out the recipies/being able to further break down items (for instance break a rock in two and make rock shards which are necessary for the spear) and you can spend a good amount of time trying to figure it all out.  Now, sadly, to the Negatives.  First and foremost, the game IS Early Access.  I PERSONALLY (this is my opinion) have lost faith in Early access games.  Too many here on STEAM start off strong, then die away slowly till they are no longer updated and taken care of.  I'm not saying this will happen to this game, but its always a possibility.  Again, the game has only come out recently, so the developers have not had time to post up any time maps, guides, or similar tools on Steam to help show whats coming up, their development, etc.  Its possible they have a website that does this, but I have yet to look myself for such.  Combine this with the fact that as this is the initial early access release, and after a few hours of gameplay, you will have largely done most of what you can at the moment.  Not that it isn't fun, but until updates come in and more content is added, don't expect a huge world full of possibilities just yet.  As said above, while crafting is fun, it is limited.  So far, from what I have found, there are a good amount of recipies but stop rather short of what I'd personally like to see.  You can craft everything thus far, but again, you'll be done in a while after you find the required materials.  The islands are FAR FAR away from each other.  I know that Islands are not going to be uber close to one another, but I mean they are FAR.  Now, this may have been a developer's choice to do such, but it can get rather long and tedious of just having to row for such a long time from one island, clean it of the supplies it has (which, is a good amount but nothing huge that allows you to spend a good day in the world on the island) and then have to go to the next.  This is also coupled with that most islands are the same with one another; some are actual copies, some are different, but most are all teh same size and have the same features except for maybe a few wrecks here and there that are in the ocean close to it.  Game is currently buggy; I've seen rafts dissapear out from under you leaving you in open water randomly at times.  Sharks behavior, while good at times, seems slightly sporadic as well, and the spawn rate is high.  Items can glitch at times through floors if you leave them in a safe place for instance, and at times I've found loot that I couldn't carry, but when I came back, the loot mysteriously dissapeared.  I can only assume a shark swam off with the flashlight for who knows what...TL;DR/ The bottom LineI'm still playing the game, still working at it.  Bottom line, I personally enjoy it.  It's a survival game yes, but its different then most out then with the concept and I think with enough hard work it can become quite a gem.  Can I say buy it now at it's current state?  That is up to you.  Its fun and will pass the time for a while.  But if you are wanting a more developed game or one with more options/more features added in for the support of the game, I'd suggest you follow the game and wait till more has been applied to it and it has been patched/added too.

_childDocuments_.review: Being such an incomplete game (look at the dev's road map for a list of awesome upcoming features!), it will leave you with a smile. _childDocuments_.review: By far one of my favorite games. I played Stranded Deep way back when it came out and it was pretty decent, a little but and lacking but still loved it. I'm now playing it for the first time since 2015 and I am absolutely blown away with all of the updates. This is one of the best survival games on the market right now. I'm way excited for the future updates! Read below for positive/negatives about the game.First off, this game is gorgeous. I'm running on the "high" graphic settings and it looks phenomenal. The scenery is beautiful. There are many different types of weather such as cloudy, sunny, rainy and even severe storms and they all look great aesthetically. Secondly, the survival aspect is very realistic. This game is single player only (for now) and it really immerses you into the daily life of an lonely island survivor. You have to battle the elements as well as some wildlife. You must avoid sunburn on sunny days and stay warm on the cold nights. You also must avoid venomous snakes and vicious sharks which makes this game that much harder to stay alive. I hope to see new animals added in the future! I'm excited for co-op but I'm totally satisfied with the solo aspect of it. Finally, the crafting is endless. Back when I first played years ago, there wasn't really much you could craft so it's great to have much more crafting abilities. The game makes you work (a little grindy but not so bad as each island is different). I could do with more variety of islands but I'm sure the devs are working on that. This game is a challenge and is very unforgiving, I really enjoy that as many modern games baby you through the entire game with handouts & hints. This is a game you can play for many hours and still be crafting and discovering new things. I also heard there might be an end-game rescue type scenario added into the future, super stoked for that!  Stranded Deep is a very well rounded game so far but it does have its negative points, just like every game. Don't be turned off by the long paragraph here, much of the content of this part of my review is explaining my in-game experience! Right off that bat I will tell you that it's a tiny bit buggy at points (still in early access so it's to be expected). The bugs/glitches I've experienced are very minor but it can get frustrating when you crack open a coconut and the pieces go flying. Considering that it's still early access, this game is very stable. Another thing I'm not too fond of is the respawn rate of certain resources. I'm not sure if coconuts are supposed to respawn but I'm 10 days in, have travelled and explored several surrounding islands and my home island has yet to respawn the coconuts. I still haven't found a bucket so I'm solely living off of coconut water and it makes it very hard to survive when you have to travel 3 islands over just to stay hydrated. Another negative point worth nothing is that it takes quite a bit to kill any animal. I chucked 4 crude spears into a boar and it was still running around like nothing happened (took 6 spears to take it out). This game is very realistic in many aspects but damn, I've never seen a small boar take that many spears and live. Good thing crude spears are very easy to craft. There are higher tier spears you can craft that do much more damage but still a pain in the booty. None of these points are game-breaking in any way. Still an amazing EA game!All in all, Stranded Deep is a fantastic game so far and I'm beyond excited for the future content. The devs have been busting their butts for the past few years and have kept up with frequent updates. I bought this game for $10.49 during Summer Sale but it is most definitely worth full price if not more! I  recommend this game to anyone that enjoys a solid survival game.

_childDocuments_.review: Review for alpha version 0.02.H1:First of all, if you liked the movie "Cast Away" with Tom Hanks, you will love this game very much.This game is just so beautiful, it has just extraordinary good graphics, very detailed and also the light- and shadow-effects look so good, you will fall in love with the sunrise/sundown and maybe with the bright shining moon, too. The whole carribean island setting is just amazing. Also the underwater-world is super detailed and beautiful. I haven't seen a game looking this good very often, especially when it's an early access alpha game.You play a lone survivor stranded after a plane crash on the ocean. After landing on the first island with your life-raft, you have to do, what every survivor has to do in this situation: find water, find food, build a shelter, make a fire. You will find lots of resources to achieve your goals. Also you can search in the water for useful stuff, dive down and maybe you'll find a shipwreck and discover a real treasure (no gold). And of course you can also paddle to other islands around you, there are dozens of them, BUT watch out for the hungry SHARKS! They will overturn your raft (if you're lucky enough) and then you have real problems! Better get back on the raft ASAP!In my current game (6,5 h) I survived for 9 days so far, found lots of food (crabbes, fish, potatoes, coconuts), crafted some tools, started to build a house and a bed and checked out a few islands.  I even got my raft flipped over by a shark (almost ♥♥♥♥ my pants), but was fast enough back on there.And I still have to learn things to survive longer, there is just so much do discover already. Because in this game you have to find out everything yourself, there are no plans of how to craft this or that, you have to try it out, what I find pretty cool, just put every craftable item on a stack and see, what you can do. Same with the exploring, just keep your eyes open for everything useful on land and in the water. I think, I still haven't seen all of this game yet, but I am very impressed so far!I actually can't understand people, who rate this game negative, just because it's an alpha version and because there is so much work to do. People, it's an early access alpha build, just v 0.02, that means, the game is not finished and the developers want YOU to try the game and help them with the developing process by telling them what you like and what you would like to see in this game, report bugs and stuff! If you like the game so far, but think, it needs some work, than SAY IT, you can rate it positive AND say, what you don't like!My conclusion: This game ist just amazing, very nice concept, great graphics and lots of things to do and to discover so far, even in this early stage. I bet, when it continues getting updated regularly, than this one will probably become the best survival game in gaming history, even if it takes a lot of time! I will wait for it!And the 15 bucks for this game are well invested, because you will get everything that's still to come for free, a finished game of this kind will cost you at least 30 bucks! Actually, just the beauty of this game is worth the purchase!

_childDocuments_.review: This is very early access game.  It is similar to The Forest, except it is a bit more mellow, and it takes place in the ocean.  One thing that I noticed with this game is that it is very difficult to create a sense of security.  The ocean is all around you, and building a fort is basically useless.  There is no sense of security.  There are limited resources, so the need to keep moving to survive is necessary.  I don't normally get freaked out in games, but when you dive 30-40ft down to inspect a wreck, and sharks show up... geez does that make my heart race!  Another thing that happened to me was a bug caused my raft to disappear..... in the middle of the ocean.  So I had to swim to the closest island (which was pretty far away).  I made the mistake of diving and swimming under water as I headed to the island.  Below me, the ocean was so deep that you couldn't see the floor.   So eerie!!  Just floating there in the middle of the ocean, bobbing up and down, helpless.... so scary!  Then a shark showed up.  I started to swim frantically!  I tried to kill it!  I kept dodging its teeth and trying to attack it! I finally made it to shore.  If it were real life I would've fell to my face and kissed the sand. Only this game could make me feel this way.  Hopefully the developers add tons more content and actually complete the game someday.

_childDocuments_.review: I dont often write reviews but in the case of this game I felt I should. Let me start off by saying this game is fun. I just got it and already at 16 hours. Just like any game it takes a few hours to figure out the mechanics and learn the tricks and it has been an enjoyable journey so far. A few ideas though to improve upon the gameplay would be in my opinion first and foremost you should add binoculars or something similar to the game. They ould eventually lose their usefulness but mainly at the start when you are first learning your bearings it would help to identify your main island you set up your base on. Also you should add a pole you can craft with the solar lights to sit atop to act as a sort of beacon for your island in the night sky. I currently set all my solar lights around my home island so when i am heading home at night its easy to say yup thats my island all lit up. Now my next suggestion is for the farming. As far as i know it seems only one plant per garden plot and those plots are huge and you telling me i can only put one plant in them???? Seems I should be able to get at least 2 but really 4 would be more realistic as those plots take up a lot of space. The most important thing I would like to see changed is the amount of fuel the gyrocopter uses, I can make it to the nearest island and back on a single tank of gas and I feel I should be able to go at least 2 or even 3 islands out from my base before im like crap out of fuel. My third point about fuel consumption also goes with my comment abot garden plots only holding one plant. With as much fuel as the chopper burns and only one plant per plot Im going to need tons of plots if i dont want it to take FOREVER to get fuel made. Its already almost borderline ridiculous how long it takes just to get everything needed to craft and the back and forth travel with sharks literally flipping you into the air off your boat that once i finally do get all the parts for a motor boat and chopper i dont want it to take yet several more hours just to make enough fuel to enjoy my new motorized toys. Yes I know thats kinda the point but I think with a slightly better fuel efficiancy and more plants per garden plot it would make all the effort that much more satisfying. I really hope this game continues to develop with new features like The Forest is bc it has the same satisfying seach collect and craft as The Forest just without the Mutants. Anyways keep up the great work!

_childDocuments_.review: The game looks great and has potential. But in it's current state you basically beat the game after being 5 minutes in the game. Because that's how long you need to have unlimited food, shelter and a campfire. There is no built in need-to-do-next-tier. There are tons of coconuts and potatoes around. And they regrow faster than you can eat them. So what to do next? Why even doing something at all? All the islands look the same and are the same. There is nothing happening either. No hurricane destroys your camp, no wild animals threatening you. Just sit there and enjoy the beach for the rest of your days.... boooooring!Also some game flaws are annoying. Want to go treasure hunting and discover other islands? Well, be prepared that your life-boat can't even carry an empty water-bottle, a lighter and two sticks without sinking. That's annoying at best.The things to build are very very limited as well. Is it worth it? Well, it's beautiful... and I had my "oooh" moments. But good looks isn't everything.I would wait. With current development speed it may be something in a year... maybe.---------Edit after 6 years: The game is more fun, especially because of the coop possibility. But the amount of bugs and the little progress the game made in such a long time span is .... without words. Bugs make it painful to play. Single player might be way less of an issue though.Maybe better get something like Raft first and only this after you run out of games with a tropical survival boat kinda style I'd say. There is not THAT much to do in the game still, even though the first hours will probably amaze you if you touch it for the first time.

_childDocuments_.review: I found this game way back, somewhere in its early access phase around the end of 2015 / Start of 2016, through a small let's player on YouTube I watched at the time. And over the years I really enjoyed getting back to it, see the big progressions the whole development made and slowly grinding my way up to the 100% finish.I think stranded deep is a perfect example of a good / quality "early access" game - which kept its promises and accelerated over the years.The Gameplay is somewhat typical for a survival game - farming resources, hunting animals, defending of predators, building a base & finally make it out alive. But due to the fact that Stranded deep also already came out back in the days with some of the bigger household names in the "survival" genre, it definitely kept steadily improving on Gameplay, in game content and overall look & feel and for me always struck a very nice niche in this column.Sure, here and there some bugs can still appear - bugging items, Glitching Object & Texture Collisions etc. but none of them was Game breaking or heavily disruptive & definitely got a lot of polishing and attention over the past years.To sum it up quickly:+ Nice & Fun, not to story driven / more exploration focused gameplay loop.+ Very immersive & beautiful visuals+ Unique Castaway / lord of flies’ type setting+ ca. 20 bucks for about 150h of playtime to 100%- The small (but for me often funny) bugsI think this game is definitely worth every buck and I can recommend it to everyone enjoying a good & immersive survival experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Stranded Deep is about as generic a survival game as you can get these days. The overall feel of play-style sways towards simplicity, relying on resource shortage and brutal forward planning in order to hold up the game play mechanic. The world doesn't really feel like it wants to open up to the player, instead opting for a feeling of helplessness and an inevitable grind towards success.Crafting is, at best, basic and, at its worst, frustrating. Creating a raft (your primary item of choice if you wish to survive) is simple, but also tricky to undertake because of physics collisions, weight distribution problems (placing a single vehicle tyre onto your raft can have the entire construction spinning out of control, or cause it to drown) and space restrictions. It's meant to be realistic, but the execution of it is glitchy and immersion-breaking, often adding frustration to your task. On top of that, there is very little you are allowed to add to the raft as a vehicle, ending up with your final creation being uninspiring and boring. Want to build a little sleep area that's enclosed, with maybe something to cook on - Nope! You can construct a shelf system for your crates, a sail, a rudder, a simple stone anchor and, if you're really feeling fancy, you can build an outboard engine. The latter of which requires a contrived, painfully slow process of farming potatoes (from limited resources) in order to distill them into fuel. It all feels a bit over-the-top., while also being incredibly underwhelming.Crafting on land is marginally more involved, with basic structures that you'd expect from a castaway survival situation. It's not terrible, but it's not particularly inspiring either. With resources being cruelly sparse, requiring plenty of island hopping to support any form of player home settlement, it soon becomes tiring to have to travel vast distances just to get some sticks or enough fiber for crafting  water production. Some might enjoy the challenge - indeed I did at first - but it soon becomes a grind, taking away the thrill of exploration and discovery and replacing it with necessity. Not really good for anything but die-hard survivalist wannabe's.As for the story - I honestly haven't come across anything so far that gives me a clue of what I am supposed to do to get home. It might be something added on final release, but as yet it's a big mystery to me. I see hints of what I can craft from the story (4 items) but there's no connection to them in any form so far in my 21 hours of this play-through (Day 32) that I am attempting in July of 2022. Hopefully that will change. People shouldn't have to look up spoiler guides and sift through forums just to find out what they should be doing. Short of that you will likely just float aimlessly around the game world until you bump into something, which could take little time for the bold explorer, or tens of hours for the cautious gamer.Now to the bugs; There's plenty! Physics causing catapulting of trees when cutting them down, physics glitches with your raft, instability issues and (for me) a flickering shadows problem that has existed for 7 years, with no progress made by the developers to fix it. I am not alone with this glitch. It's apparently quite common, especially the further you explore and on the larger islands. It's not the end of the World, but it breaks immersion considerably and is extremely uncomfortable on the eyes,Visually (aside from technical bugs), the game is very pretty to look at. The water elements are quite beautiful and there's plenty of wildlife to make it feel alive and atmospheric. Colour use is decent, giving a truly tropical feel to the environment. Indeed, graphically it is a great showcase of what modern game engine technology can produce. Especially when it's designed by a fairly small team.My gripes: 1)  It's not good to have a screen output that's uncomfortable to look at or that ruins all the hard work that's gone into creating this beautiful environment.2)  There's too much emphasis on forcing players to island-hop for resources. Encouraging the player to explore can still be achieved without brute force. The island sizes never offer enough space for a player to get comfortable in the game and create something special as a home. It feels like the developers are keen for the player to simply keep moving until the end of the, erm... story?!?3)  I want at least some direction when I play games. It doesn't need to hold my hand, but zero information just makes it aimless and uncertain. Not a good way to design a story. This needs significant work.4)  Making a player hop islands (taking up significant time, depending on distance) just to get a few logs to make planks, or resupply an island of wooden sticks for cooking and crafting, because there's nothing left to cut down on the island the player has decided to settle on, is contrived, boring and grindy. There's no need for this. Look at Green Hell or Subnautica for reference. There's an abundance of resources everywhere (for the most part) but it doesn't lock the player into position. Instead it makes preparation for exploration more enjoyable - heightening the excitement of discovering new places.5)  Staying alive is what this game is all about, but the grind added to make it fit into this genre is bordering on lazy design instead of thoughtful complexity. This is a tricky aspect that I also cover in my likes as well, but needs to be mentioned.6) My likes:1)  The world looks beautiful and the water is realistic feeling and immersive. The developers have done a great job with the overall visual and dynamic environment.2)  It sounds nice and there's plenty of atmosphere created around the player from the various audio elements.3)  A truly tropical vibe. A lovely water pallet and a vibrant and inviting overall feel for the world space.4)  With the exception of over-sized crabs, the overall look and feel of the wildlife is so good you'll likely want to spend time (especially under water) just drinking it in and experiencing the flora and fauna of a tropical dream holiday. It's not at all safe, but it's incredibly immersive. Enough that you don't really need a story if there was more space to explore on land and more emphasis on taking in the wonders of the tropics. Very nice indeed.5)  There's quite a selection of things to build, even if the game doesn't balance it well or give it purpose. It's not enough for impressive creativity, but it lends to the game enough to warrant a mention.6)  Staying alive is tough. You need to look where you are going and pay attention to your needs. it's what the game centers around and it, almost, works. I prefer thoughtful survival mechanics over brute force, lazy design. It's a bit of "love it and hate it" as far as this aspect goes.I'd give this game a somewhat generous 7/10, but must warn of glitches that can potentially ruin your experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Tons of promise, currently very rudimentary.  At $15, I am happy to fund the development of a really neat and unique survival game.  I haven't played Rust or the Forest or those others, so take this with a grain of salt.For starters, I love the immersion of the intro.  You fix a martini before the dreaded plane crash, then hop on a life raft and wash onto a small s. pacific island.From there, you can do some basic crafting (axe for chopping, hammer for building, weapons), and get to the core of the game - exploration!  Initially, it's a pretty scary world with somewhat odd clipping/collision mechanics (how many times have I fallen off the boat into shark infested water?).  Sharks are everywhere, and not wanting to lose my progress, I stayed the hell away from them.  Turns out they are just the gumbas of this game - you can outswim them, dodge them easily, and mostly ignore them when boating between islands.  In the current build, there's basic vegetation like yucca and potatoes, plus some creatures like crabs, some small fish like sardines, and some bigger fish that I haven't gotten to yet.  I had a humpback whale beach itself on my lagoon home (not really, just a clipping thing, rather hilarious though to see a giant whale swim through my island).  The idea of foraging, hunting, and scavenging wreckage to thrive-not-survive is cool.  There is good risk/reward, for example you can loot flippers and an airtank to do more robust diving, longer runs and faster swimming.  In the 6 hours I played, I was able to:-Sail around at least 12 different islands, explore 6-8 unique wreckage, avoid sharks and collect loot.-Build a 3-hut home with a spitfire and some other conveniences-Construct a motor-driven raft that is oddly rewarding to pilot, perhaps just because the controls are so good.  -Stab a tiger shark 15 times with my spear, only to have it coming back for more.  Do these things die?########################### DEVS - IF YOU ARE READING THIS!  Here's what I'd like to see implemented: ############################-A Few Bigger, more sustainable "rare" islands.  This is paramount.  The island hopping is kind of fun for a couple hours but the ultimate goal of any builder is to make an awesome base to thrive, not just survive.  This is one that could collect enough fresh water, grow enough crops (potatoes?  Pineapple?  Mangos?) to eat, perhaps even have a lagoon with a collection of seashells and other oddities.  - Environmental effects that affect the character.  e.g. getting "drenched" in the rain lowers your temperature, possible hypothermia, lower health etc.  Dry off by a fire or stay under your hut!  Or die.- More flora and fauna.  Both threatening, and domesticatable.  How about wild boar to hunt, or lemurs/rodents to feed and perhaps domesticate?  How about variety of sharks, some incredibly threatening that will have you carrying a just-in-case harpoon gun, others more for hunting/food?  How about more fruit with seeds that can be cultivated?  How about medicinal herbs?-Expand the structures to allow frond-bridges between platofrms, have multi-level huts with firepole slides, etc.  Add the concept of furniture, or at least allow the bed/hammock to go inside.  Currently the hut is just for looks, no function whatsoever.  -Since multiplayer would ruin the lonely vibe that is so crucial to the game, having some remnant of human culture would add to the ambiance (like tikis or moari statues).  Maybe it's letters or notes found in the wreckage.  Perhaps a journal that can be collected/reconstructed.  Maybe add an indiginous people that can eventually be contacted, fought, or otherwise encountered.-An eventual path to "victory" - or some implementation of an endgame.  Maybe its building a large whale-oil fueled signal fire, maybe its a megaraft with the boatmotor that can hold enough coconuts for a year's food.  They don't have to work 100%, but we all know the human endgame is to get out of Castaway.  Lots of fun and I look forward to the continued development.

_childDocuments_.review: Stranded Deep starts off great, its early game is fun, immersive, with lots to do. Though once it hits mid to late game, it becomes very repetitive. It's ending is also one of the worst out there.The good:*Very fun at the start of the game*World is immersive at the start*Lots of fun things to do at the start*Sharks in this game specifically add a great horror element that I have never seen in another game that I have played*Shark AI for the Tiger Sharks and Great Whites is really good*Graphics are quite noiceThe bad:*Mid to late game is the same thing over and over, very repetitive. Collecting clay, dealing with creatures the same way, travelling long distances... the same way*Random World Generator causes too much meshing with wrecks, making many non accessible or causing the player to get stuck*Sharks, when moving fast, have more animations. Looks like they are moving in 15 fps, which breaks immersion*Shark AI for Goblin and Hammerhead Sharks is annoying, they are too rapid*There is no difference to building out of clay vs building out of sticks or planks, only visual differences, no reward for making stronger buildings*Hurricanes/storms are annoying, they pose no threat, lightning creates unpleasant flashes*Hard mode is annoying as it increase water consumption to insane levels*Nights are too long, day is too short, underwater visibility is too limited with a in game 5 hour window to be able to see well*No diving/swimming equipment, no fins, snorkel, goggles, armor, etc*Collecting clay is tedious and boring after awhile, mining pick the whole game*The games ending needs improvement*No fast travel, it needs it because travelling across the map is boring and takes a long time*Respawning snakes, crabs and large boars will knock your stuff around on the island, and you don't know when they have respawned, they often get you while you're in the middle of something.How the game could improve:*Add a map*Add more story elements, unique elements about each island, things to break up the grind*Add upgrades for equipment and buildings to improve their use*Add water tanks for collecting water, water filtration, water purification, gutters for collecting water, water tank storage for rafts*Make a polished world as the main world, and use Random World Generators for everything else. The main world could be polished, bug free, no meshing, add extra story elements, larger land masses, other deceased survivors and their stories*More upgrades for rafts, better rudders for turning, better engines for faster movement, better storage system, compass holder, etc*Essential storage for the raft that is visual and you can see how many you have without having to open every storage box. It could hold food, water, fuel, medical items, fuel etc*Add automated notes of what the player has done on an island*Add fast travel for islands you've discovered or add a marker the player can make and place so they can.

_childDocuments_.review: Played for the first time a while ago and quit because I got poisoned by a Lionfish a half hour into it and gave up. Came back 2 weeks ago and really took my time to figure everything out and now I love it. If you're thinking about buying this know that there is a learning curve, as with most sandbox survival games, and it's very punishing if you don't take your time to learn the mechanics and items. The one that frustrated me, poisoning, is one  such mechanic you need to prepare for or else you're screwed. Even something as simple as touching a purple starfish, which can happen easily since they spawn in shallow water, can end you if you aren't prepared. Something as simple as eating can also prove deadly as drinking or eating too many coconuts can make you sick and put you in a tough spot if you don't have plenty of extra water around. I'd compare this game to The Long Dark but in the tropics. It explains very little beyond crafting which may turn some people off but makes it that much better when you figure things out for yourself. Take it slow, enjoy the scenery and watch our for the wildlife.

_childDocuments_.review: It's very mixed, I wish there was a "meh" rating. It feels half-baked, it's not great and also not bad. I have played about 7h so far. You have crafting, base building and survival elements and combat with wildlife. Animations of attacking wildlife are jittery but acceptable, although the boar is especially janky.Playing the game in co-op and it's pretty rough with a bunch of disconnects and it takes about 5-10min to rejoin while both are just waiting for a loading screen to go away. There's objects that "vibrates" a lot, like you usually see in multiplayer when desync is happening, sometimes the raft throws a tantrum and launches you like a catapult. There's a lack of information about how the game works and I randomly died while having 50% health and breath underwater whilst being poisoned. It was also unclear whether I died or not the first time, the UI just vanishes and you're stuck only being able to rotate the camera, scratching your head.The UI and crafting is rough, needlessly clunky even though I'm starting to get a bit more used to it. We figured out you could get to a specific category of crafting depending on what tool you have in hand. I would rather have an overview of all categories at least instead of the system they have now where you gotta click several times until you hopefully see what you want.  You have a hotbar showing tools/weapons that arent necessarily there, gotta check the "wheel inventory" if it's actually there or not. Many small negatives adding up and large gaps between game updates is the reason why I decided to not recommend it.If you are really interested in the game, I would recommend checking out gameplay before deciding.Edit: I decided to try multiplayer mode (MP) a second time after a QoL update, but sadly we still had the same issues with crashes and desyncs. So I decided to play the game in single player mode (SP) instead.  The game is much more playable in SP and haven't encountered any crashes. Summary still remains essentially the same although the game is decent, if the game was SP only I might've given it a recommendation. However, since MP is broken, I can't recommend it as the feature is not fully functioning.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, I finally bought this game yesterday after like 5 years of deliberation and it was... a roller coaster ride.I boot up the game with expectations high because I've always been a huge fan of castaway narratives. I see there was procedural map generation, exciting! I see a perma-death option, very exciting! I start a new game, learn enough about it to fully understand all the early mistakes I made.Start another new game, get poisoned early, run out of resources early, no antidote. I die on-route to a bigger island. Start another new game. This time I am fully ready. No poison for these feet. First island stripped of important resource, I set out for a bigger island to start building my new home. 4-5 hours later, I have a hut built, loads of resources and loot saved up, cooking setup, hunting, tanning some hides. Life was good, until I ran out of stones. There's no two-ways about it. I need to risk travel to another island to gather more. But it's almost my bedtime. I risk it. Gun it for the nearest island on my blow-up raft. Spend a good 30 minutes there gathering all I can, and set back in the same direction I came from. But something goes horribly wrong. In my tired, delirious state I lost sight of my home island, and went the wrong way. I arrive on this foreign shore scared, my heart sunk with the thought that I've gotten myself completely lost. What follows is a lot of paddling, I hopped between 4-5 islands trying desperately to find the small haven I'd built for myself, but couldn't find it. I messed up bad. This game is bad! Why so easy to get lost? Please noooo.  I think to myself "Maybe I'll just die and start a new playthrough tomorrow cause @#%* this.", at this point I just want to go to bed. But no, I can't. I paddle that crummy little raft away from the  as fast as I can, getting pelted repeatedly by  , on the brink of death. Somehow I get away, and make for the nearest island. At least I have a shot at starting a new life.You may not believe this, but I kid you not that the island I found myself on was the one on which I had so lovingly crafted my home. The elation I felt in this moment was so uplifting that I had a hard time getting to sleep after.I will never forget this moment. If this sounds fun to you, chances are you will like the game. But keep in mind that it can sometimes be a bit rough around the edges since it's made by a small team.

_childDocuments_.review: UI is terribly clunky and unintuitive, the inventory/storage system is kind of ridiculous and convoluted. Yet still, once you get used to its systems, the game grows on you. You build your little shelter, get some food and water to survive the first few nights, then paddle over to another island with more plentiful resources. You build your little hut, a raft, begin to explore the network of islands that surround you. You find salvage on the scattered islands and diving into shipwrecks, build ever increasingly better stuff to survive, then thrive. It's Survival Gaming 101, and it is done well.There is zero story here, so it's pretty much a castaway simulator. But the crafting progression is fun and addictive, orientation is tricky with just a compass and a pair of binoculars, but it adds to the immersion. I feel like this game is a bit of a wasted opportunity, could have been so much more (like Subnautica or Green Hell), but it does scratch the survival itch well, and you'll get your 20-30h of tropical survival fun out of it.

_childDocuments_.review: ^ In-depth review by my boyfriend after I showed him the game; I agree, but am going to add a bit.Pros:-I personally love the idea of a physical in-game crafting system; it adds to the immersion.-In some aspects, the realism is very much there. The way the sharks attack is terrifying and accurate -- they approach if you splash around in the water or are wounded, knock into your raft to try and make you fall in, and will drag you deepinto the ocean if you're in shallow water. And the different species of sharks have different behaviors -- Tiger sharks are aggressive and act as previously stated, but others don't really care about you as long as you don't attack them. Other than the sharks, the injuries sustained make sense -- falling from a tall tree can cause you to break a bone; if it's your arm, looking at your watch is a bit difficult.Meh:-I'm pretty okay with it, but it isn't for everyone, so it's not really a pro or a con, but you get dropped into this game with basically no idea what you're doing or how to do it. To me, that's part of the experience -- I mean, if you were stranded on an island, it'd be the same thing: you'd have a vague idea of what you need to do (get food and water, make shelter), but wouldn't quite be sure about how to put it into practice.Cons:-Only one save slot. To start a new game, you have to overwrite your other one. For a game that boasts an almost infinite amount of randomized worlds and different chances of coming across important items in each one, I feel like it's a bit of a slap in the fact to only have one save game. You can, of course, go into the files and move your save to a different location, and then start another game, but that's a lot of effort for just wanting to play again.It has a lot of potential, but it isn't quite there yet. Of course, Standed Deep isn't a finished game. There's still more work to be done, and considering how well done it is right now, I'm hopeful.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I used to absolutely love this game. I remember ~4 years ago when Stranded Deep and Subnautica completely dominated all my computer time. Both were mysterious, early access, survival games and both were unique from the other. Subnautica now is out of early access and about to release a brand new expansion, it was optimized, it had a story added and even a form of "Multiplayer". It was amazing. And then there's Stranded Deep, I don't know how fair it is to compare the two but Stranded Deep seems to be the type of thing people are afraid of Early access games for. This game was projected to be finished in 2015, then in 2016 the developement period was left kind of open. It's 2019 at the time of writing this, and having played the game both now and then I can say- It looks "Better" but it plays almost the same. I think it used to have a bit of indie charm in the way it looked, and in the years of development they've updated the models to be higher quality with the downside of looking like any generic survival game. On top of that as far as I know, the game gives you no reason to play. Subnautica has you trying to scan everything, to learn about this alien planet. The Forest has you collecting clues about your son, or what's going on on the island, or even trying to put together a gun. Stranded deep has you, survive. Like I said I used to play this game years back, and the fun came from the potentiel, what I thought might get added, the magic and mystery of what could be going on. Playing it recently, I traveled to an island I like, got a store of food, built a shelter and then. I was done. What more was there for me to do, I could explore but there wasn't much avaliable I didn't have, there wasn't much new for me to explore, and there wasn't a reason to seek out any upgrades. The game doesn't give you a reason to play it, it doesn't draw you in, and it doesn't warrent you buying it.

_childDocuments_.review: I recently decided to pick up this game again, after leaving it on the shelf for a few years, and while there's been a little improvement here and there I'm sorry to say that there are quite a bit of flaws still with the game.First, I'm happy to say that Multiplayer has finally been added to the game.  That said, they've basically done it in a co-op format so it's limited to 2 players only.  I really don't get this, since there are other games that use the same story intro mechanic (like The Forest) and allow many more players.  One theory I have is that adding more than one additional player would make the game virtually impossible, due to...Secondly, they still haven't resolved the most common player complaint. That being, major resources don't respawn.  I certainly understand that when you pick up a rock another rock shouldn't just pop into existence at that spot.  That said, coconuts don't regrow on trees?  You can't plant and regrow trees?  I mean, come on...  These are crops, and in the real world they're certainly renewable crops.  With each player required to craft the same objects to unlock more recipes, having these resources limited is quite a large problem, especially early game.Third, the health system is still completely broken.  You can stand in complete shade and still be overheating and getting UV stroke.  You have to move around until you find one tiny little spot, sometimes not even in the shade, where the UV meter shows you're in the "shade".  You can step on an urchin and get poisoned, but it's a roll of the dice if you can even drink the antidote you craft from the rare flower you had to find, because sometimes it goes buggy and can't actually be drunk.  You're given a limited quantity of coconuts, as mentioned before they don't respawn.  That said, if you drink more than one within a certain amount of time you get sick from it.  Oh, and you'd probably still get more "hydration" by drinking sea water or beach sand.  Coconuts, in this game, are practically useless as a drink.The inventory system is still fairly odd.  You get a limited number of slots, but what you can put in those slots sometimes doesn't make sense.  Some things stack, other things don't.  Thankfully some objects can be placed in "piles" now, however instead of the game just doing it you have to go through the crafting system to tell it you want to create a pile.  It's far from intuitive, and if you didn't already know you could do this you're not likely to realise you can.  In addition, piles are only for major resources and somewhat useless because, as said before, major resources are extremely limited and don't regenerate.  In this game, if you actually need to "pile" a major resource, you aren't working on survival.  It almost would have been better to give us a larger storage chest option.All in all, this game is still missing pretty much everything that I'd require to give it my recommendation.  It needs regenerative resources, even if those resources take a long time to regenerate (10-20 days) and can be toggled on/off by the host.  It needs multiplayer that's more than just a 2 player co-op existence.  The survival and inventory systems also still need some fixes, because right now they feel broken.  I'm not saying make the game stupid easy, because survival shouldn't be that way, but at least make things follow some form of common sense.I purchased this game early, back before there was even a half-decent crafting system.  Normally I write up well thought out reviews, but I simply can't here.  This game is so horrible.  This could be an excellent game, but there's just so much wrong with it that I simply can't recommend it.  It's a complete patchwork of ideas originating from other games.  That said, the ideas have been mashed together and executed so badly that it's not worth playing.------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------For more no-nonsense reviews check out my curator page at;

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good, it's fun, keeps you busy. BUT there are so many inconsistencies and missed opportunities. Here are some of the things that stand out to me:1.) You need a hammer to build structures. Even for brick structures you wouldn't need a hammer. All wooden structures should need rope and wood. There are no nails, so why would you need a hammer? Punch posts into the ground? That can be done with a rock tied to a stick.2.) 2 wooden sticks make a small hook to put on a wall to hold a torch/lantern. But you need 4 sticks to make an entire wooden foundation? 3.) Sharks just attack. This cliche needs to die out. I understand there needs to be some challenge, but sharks just attacking is an easy way out.4.) You can build a loom, a water still, a raft or a shelf to hold containers, but...you don't know or can't build a container yourself? Hmm. It's obviously in the game as a progression/reward system, but it's inconsistent and silly.5.) Missed opportunity: Tool belt - it doesn't add to your inventory, it just gives you hotkeys. With an inventory of only 10 slots (Or 30 if you hold 10 containers on your person, which doesn't make any sense)...it's just odd.I'm sure I will find more points to make as I continue to play, but I've made it clear the inconsistency issues here. Don't get me wrong, the game IS FUN!! It is relaxing to be on an island surviving. I indeed DO recommend the game, but these inconsistency issues do frustrate me enough to mention them. Take them as you will!

_childDocuments_.review: I posted a negative review a few years ago, but now i feel like revising it. I wasn't expecting the devs to actually continue production, but they've made a lot of great improvements.PROS:~Very immersive~survival mechanics (i.e., how long it takes to starve, etc.) are actually very realistic feeling.~Sea travel feels real. I started making a map with compass headings on paper just to remember where things were.~Pretty fun as a building/exploration/survival game~More map modes than just the vanilla scenario. This is something every survival explorer game needs!CONS:~It has the same feel as "No Man's Sky". There's some cool things to see, but every island is essentially the same in the vanilla edition.~Controls are NOT very intuitive compared to other similar games. You can get them to be muscle memory, but it's still a little clunky.~Total lack of realism when it comes to the sharks. All the shark are ***holes and want to eat you the second they see you. it would be more pracitcal to have them attack you if you're injured or are carrying meat, etc.~still very buggy in terms of entity fixation to other entities. Putting boxes on the raft works, but small glitches can make the raft move lightning fast and fling your stuff across the ocean.~Also unrealistic in terms of raft weight. I had basically a floating fortress, and a little tiger shark still flipped it. It's too big to flip back, so i lost my pride and joy. I would still recommend waiting for a huge sale, or the full release. Still, it's a fun game to kill some hours, especially if you like authentic survival.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll say this game is a lot of fun.It has more realistic oriented features of survival such as needing water more readily than you need food, as opposed to most survival games where your character dies after half a day of not eating... A definite welcome change of pace there.Hunting animals is fun and the game looks and feels really nice IMO.Sure, animations when hunting fish and the mechanics when climing trees and orienting yourself towards that desperately needed coconut are a bit odd, but forgivable all the same.The graphics are great and you are ALMOST fully immersed in this pseudo-tropical archipelago. I say ALMOST because I just feel there's a little ambience missing from the game. You almost feel like there should be a little more audio ambience to flesh it out abit more. Having said that, it doesn't ever feel like you're playing a barebones survival game which has no atmosphere whatsoever.The game doesn't feel easy OR hard, on the normal settings, which to me, shows they got it right there. You definitely need to be comfortable with how the game works and then use that knowledge to plan ahead so you're not left short of any necessary supplies but at the same time, there is definitely enough about the game where you can improvise as you go along.But alas when all is said and done, not having an online co-op is a big stinger, I've had alot of fun playing with a friend via steam remote split screen, but it just isn't the same and I wouldn't expect anyone to settle for just that.If you're a solo player I'd recommend this game, if you want to play with a friend and CAN put up with sharing the same screen and streaming it at the same time then I'd also recommend it. If you want to play via standard multiplayer means then it's definitely not going to hit the spot.Game gets a 7/10 from me, multi player co-op would make this an 8 or a 9/10 easily.

_childDocuments_.review: A great survival game for beginners to the Genre. The music type and tropical ambiance will please and cheer you up if you are down! The sights are lovely and the ocean, islands, and sealife look very much alive.However! This is certainly not a game for Hardcore Survivalists as it is very light on ACTUAL Survival. Food is aplenty, water can easily be accessed once you build one water collector, and animals are easy enough to avoid/kill. Compared to Green Hell, this game is hardly worth the challenge and more of a passing of time. The Devs have a surprisingly small amount of items that can be found to benefit you, and there's no true sickness or exposure enough that would kill you. All-in-all, it's very soft on the pains it delivers. Item-wise, it's pretty basic and only the most surface level of survival things can be made/found, and you can live without 99% of them.They have a weather system that goes according to a Calendar system, which is pretty cool, but really doesn't do enough to make the game replayable as much as it could. If overheating/freezing were added, however. . And if the storms ACTUALLY threatened you in any way, or harmed your raft, or any shelter you might have built, it would be quite impressive. -- But it's not. Feels quite empty infact.Here's hoping the Devs will continue their efforts to make this game harder, seem more alive, for Pacific Storms to be frightening and enough to wreck damage on you, your raft, shelter, then it'll be a good 10/10. At the moment, it's rather more like 6-7/10.  Also, the current ending is really. . bad. They should work on a real one. .

_childDocuments_.review: It was a very mixed experience for my wife and I. Here's the good, bad and ugly.Good: Pleasant to look at most of the time, gameplay loop is fun (though gets repetitive after about 6-12 hours), user interface is more intuitive than some other games in the survival genre (though very dated and clearly for PC gamers). Has a giant squid boss battle!! Can have an eerie atmosphere one moment, and very calm the next moment.Bad: Days are WAY too short and there's no way to change it by default. Lots of glitches, very limited on difficulty or custom settings (starving or getting thirsty "quicker" just makes needs more annoying, not actually harder), and that ending... WORST ending in gaming history. DO NOT bother finishing the game, you will be disappointed).(Small spoiler*)Ugly: Variety of animals, tools, and crafting is somewhat limited and survival needs are oversimplified to a pass/ fail kind of feeling that isn't very involved (which is good to brand new players unfamiliar with survival games and bad for anyone who has ever played a survival crafting game in their life- including Minecraft). It's a good "start" to a game and the idea is sound; although, the game's mechanics & lack of any compelling story handicaps its potential. Surviving and eventually thriving has little meaning beyond the next step in the 1 linear mission this game has, which is to escape on a conveniently placed airplane your guy suddenly has the skills to fix out of nowhere upon discovery.Overall: 7/10. Not winning any awards, but at least it's not just a cash grab.

_childDocuments_.review: Stranded Deep seems like a cheap rip-off of 'The Forest' or a video game adaptation of the movie 'Cast-Away' at first glance, but truth be told, this randomly generated cluster of islands offers loads of adventure and exploration that is virtually limitless.Recently I started the game once again after a short hiatus only to discover new achievements, items, craftable objects, and house components as well as new mechanics for performing any task that takes more than one second in real life. It's amazing to bear witness to the numerous updates that this game frequently has, with a lot of the updated content being suggested by players. The development team is really involved with the community and it shows.Now on to the actual review where I point out good aspects and some flaws within the game:PROS-The game looks stellar! Every model and texture has huge amounts of detail especially for an indie game and it helps immerse you in the world that Stranded deep has to offer-The game runs incredibly well, especially for the amount of detail in all of the models and textures-The realistic shark A.I. does glitch from time to time but generally scares you when travelling from one island to the next. The sharks will often bump the boat but that doesn't mean they will attack you... unless it's a great white!-Something that I picked up on was the shape of the ocean floor. The drop-offs and sea-shelfs are very true to life and once again immerse you in the lonely world of Stranded Deep -The player controls very fluently both above and below the water. It doesn't feel rough or unresponsive at any time-The realistic mechanics such as breaking your legs or being poisoned by a lionfish do add some difficulty to a pretty simple game, but none of these mechanics feel unfair-The transition between above and underwater is smooth and automatically tells your brain that the game has changed and now the aquatic creatures have the upper hand-The sounds aren't distracting but they do the job well providing another extra step of realism to the gameplay-The crafting system is simplistic, but it makes sense once you get used to it. You can just find new things because everything is made from the same four to five materials. You'll love finding new combinations in the creative but easy to use crafting system!CONS-Glitches. Seriously they are everywhere. A lot of the hotfixes seem to have removed some of the more notable ones such as boats disappearing or flying around and sharks and other animals swimming through the islands, but I wouldn't be surprised if more glitches appeared when new content is added-The game is repeditive as all hell, which means that you will most likely play it every day for about 20-40 minutes for about a week and then take a three week break before doing it all over again. This sin't really an issue but I do wish there were different types of islands (bigger, smaller, volcanic, foresty) than just the standard sandy dinky island to add some variety to the game-There is only one type of building unlike the forest, which makes sense due to the modular style of building that the game features. This is a minor issue because new stuff related to building and crafting has been recently added so i wouldn't be surprised if a new type of house such as a treehouse was added in another updateOverall, this game is definetely worth your hard earned money. All of the immersive and easy to use aspects of the gameplay complimented with the incredible graphics and sounds outweigh the minor glitches and redundancy that you will encounter from time to time. Stranded Deep gets a solid:8.5/10
