_childDocuments_.review: May 16 2018: TLDR; don't bother.  I recommend The Forest or Subnautica instead. Update, I thought I'd check in on this, especially since Raft is coming out, and I'm sorry to say nothing's really changed.  Some things have been updated, crafting's a bit better, UI's nice too.  Animals, etc. etc.  etc.  But... the game is still unplayable.  The way that things switch around from having to hold space to tapping space to get onto things, what button to do what with, same old island after same old island.  No goals still, and despite adding a storage container to your lifeboat you can't... actually... store things in it...  Overall this game still feels like it was made by people who don't play games.  The premise is cool but the mechanics are so impossible to utilize that it just becomes an excercise in frustration.  Not to mention that the graphics are just SO glitchy now.  Every fish turns into a stretched polygon disaster, which makes it much harder to escape from sharks.  Also, I really wish the sharks were more realistic, or could at least be scaled in that regard.  Sharks don't just kill people for funsies.  Anyway, don't buy this.  Waste of time and the money I had back in 2015.I've had this game for a good long time, and all I can say is that it's disappointing.  It has so much potential, but once you've seen one or two islands you've kind of seen them all.  There's nothing to aim for, no end game, no interesting discoveries to make, and the controls are incredibly clunky.  It's fun for the first little while, but once you've played it for a bit the novelty wears off.  If the updates that came out actually added gameplay elements or plot then I'd definitely be more gung ho about it, but they don't and nothing's really changed from last year.  You're still just a guy on an island, and then just a guy on a slightly different island, and then a guy on an island where there's weather now.  The updates have only added aesthetic things like weather and crabs that don't make apple noises when you eat them.  That's all well and good, but it isn't a sign of progress.  It's cosmetic at best, and I'd rather have had some kind of end goal or more interesting things to investigate; items, chances of rescue, that sort of thing.  This game isn't even that bad, it's just boring and pointless.  I get no sense of acheivement from it like other survival sims give you. I'd bought this in the hopes that it would eventually be like Subnautica in that there's a sort of questline (not to mention consistently fantastic updates)  but so far Stranded Deep has stagnated and just not lived up to expectations over its development.  It's in my library, so I'll keep coming back to see if it's improved, but I'm not holding my breath.  I really hope it gets better, since the concept is a solid one and I want to like it, but as it is, I just can't.

_childDocuments_.review: The ongoing love / hate of SD.EDIT: January 29, 2020 I have to say. In regards to my long Love / Hate relationship of years, this game is now sliding back to my Love list. The many changes over all this time has made a very interesting time kill / casual survival game. The core of it lies at avoiding death / injury from wildlife and managing non-replenishing resources. ------------- The latest updates did provide a nice change. ( as usual I was on XP branch before the general toss out ) Gone for the moment are finding everything you need to live forever on two islands. The complete removal of buckets, meaning you have to actually plan some water system a bit at first, and be ready for figuing out how to craft the new clay items, such as a water bottle / jug.However the game still suffers from the most major downfall of all.There is absolutely no reason to do anything beyond 1 to 2 game days .. 3 tops.By day three of my new game, I had 4 water stills collecting more than enough fluid for living and stockpiling. A smoker stacked over half full of fish. A box by the stills filled with full coconuts, and of course my bed for save / sleep.So once agian. 3 days in game of playing. Zero reason to go anywhere for any reason. Explore? Not needed, there is nothing I ' have ' to try and find. Wood? Covered for days. Shelter. Still not needed for any reason at all. Clothing? Not integrated at all.Love this game for the look, the idea of pure survival with no SyFy elements, no horror.Hate this game for the simple, there is no survival to it. No drive to do anything beyond the initial setup. It does not even require the " 3 " THREE main elements of actual survival that would make you a hero if you had all established in 3 days really. Food / Water ( has that ) Shelter ( not needed at all still ) Clothing ( not even mentioned )My ongoing opinion. A neat play for a very casual player. A neat play for an extremely casual survival genre fan. Still think its a neat idea and a cute game. But would have really thought that by now the core of survival would have been in place to build on. Survival involves a lot more than food / water and a save bed.I have to rate it down now, simply because it's not worth the price with so little gone into making much of a survival genre game. EARLY ACCESS REVIEW2/8/17 ** New EDIT **This game.. and my love / hate relationship. I WANT to love this game. I really do. I was deep into it on release.. spent all my time then on the old experimental game.. slugged thru' hours of no game to play and testing issues only there.. THEN came the SD as it progresses now..Which, ' aint ' much. Its not a survival game... since you have nothing to fear. Not even the need for rest, food and hydration.Its not a exploration game... well it could be. But only if rowing from one island to the next to the next is your thing.The building is nice.... but other than a bed to save / sleep.. you dont need to build anything but a water catcher and the occasional new knife or axe.It would be a really fun casual game, except that there really is no point to do anything. In the last round on experimental with this new update I am trying, trying to enjoy just a calm, peaceful play around game.. and its just simply no reason to even try.. but try I am still. There is absolutely no reason to do anything now. My smoker is filled with meat. I have two water catchers and rain catching buckets, plenty of fish in shallow water for small meat, a giant crab family on the isle and an easy drop off access to deeper water fish with low danger of sharks. Plenty of wood still to burn.. and the building of the shack I have done was needless.. still no reason to even have a shelter at all. WX has no affect on the player. SO why play it? I have no idea. Other than for me, I want to see it become something.. I want to like this game. And it is really good for a simple time kill that looks nice, and plays nice.. but has zero challenge. It could have challenge. If there really was a reason to ever venture beyond the first two islands. In 4 starts now before saying.. screw it.. I am going to play for a bit, they were all the same in giving me everything I need to live. Tarps, tools, buckets..... I ve not had to cringe once in hopes of finding survival. Its all on the second beach. I like the idea of it being a casual little play. But having all you need dropped on you at the beginning really removes anything ' game ' about this game. Heck even A' cant play it... as she said " I found everything everytime.. thats boring. "Well, back to see if I can just linger in it a bit, because if nothing else, it looks nice, and it is relaxing..I really do hope it evolves a bit tho'.. or at least stops giving you more in the beginning than using cheat codes does.8/15/2016 ** EDIT**Well.. been supporting this one since day one. Now I admit. I am wondering exactly where its heading....Today, monthly update brought us!! Not much. The ability to craft upgraded crude tools from regular crude tools. The need to make a "NEW" special spear for fishing... and another special spear for defence and hunting.. of which there is really nothing to hunt but some pigs..AND an amazing SPEAR GUN ( DIYS) made from a component you need to go deep diving to find.... so you can have a SPEAR GUN to go deep diving.. Ok.. thats nice.. BUT:After all this time, this ' survival ' game still has little to offer survival wise.You still start on an island where you can find all you need to live in 5 mins.You can craft all you need to live within 20 ( not counting this fascination that some have with building Aztec sun temples )Unless you just kill yourself.. or insist on doing everything counter to a ' survival ' game.. you cant die. Which is still moot since its a scrub save / load game.Weather ( this is a big one to me! ) Still has zero effect, other than fill your buckets ( which today I have 5 of after 30 mins ) NOW THIS IS BIG BIG to me... no drift. You dont even have the worry of things floating away. After all this time, the ocean has no drift. Drop buoys, your raft.. whatever in the ocean.. it wont float away.. So scratch the lose stuff or worry over your raft as you tinker around in the water.. ( which outside of fishing you dont really need to do.. unless you just seek things you really dont need.. medicine... which you only need if you do something to yourself.. etc etc )Billboards of distant islands.. or close ones even. Dont matter. They are all the same still.What should be global events do not work. IE Rain storm.. if your not on your island.. your buckets dont fill. Row off your island.. just far enough away to see the billboard.. return.. zero has changed. Time passes, but things like buckets dont fill, fire burns.... God I want to like this game.. I badly want to like this game. A survival game whose premise was survival.. no zombies, no freaky Sci Fi events.. just survival on islands in the ocean.But after a year.. all we have is, spawn, pick up stuff.. build sun temples. Unless you just want a zero threat, zero purpose casual island living sandbox.. or really want to support this game.Not advised at all anymore to anyone.4/22/2016 NEW EDIT:THIS is a game I ve supported since it first popped up EA. The team still trudges on, and the game has truly evolved.. slow but steady over the course..I DO NOT play it alot in sittings still, as even now there is just not that much meat and potatoes wise to hold you if your actually after what the selling point has been.. survival Castaway style... NO, NO.. SD currently, and most likely even in the end will now be a new category of game.. The Casual Gamers, No Problem, No Stress Survival, Non Survival Game DO NOT get me wrong.. it IS a good idea, it IS a neat little game.. but unless you just want to build rafts, look for engine parts and build beach houses just to do it.. it has little else to offer.

Stranded Deep is about survival and surviving on 1 island is not possible, also catching fish with a crude spear is near impossible. Because you need to travel to other islands, it is easy to get lost, because there is no mapping ability in the game. you don't know where you are in the world and it is easy to lose track your home base. _childDocuments_.review: The concept for this game is good and has potential but right now it's just not very good. The movement of your character is all messed up and there really isn't very much for you to do.The islands are way too small... If you're going to make an island survival game, the island you're stranded on needs to be bigger than like 15 X 15 feet... Theres like 5 or 6 trees on each island.The only difficult thing about this game is finding something to do, and playing it for more than thirty minutes. You can tell by my hours that I really gave it a try, but it's just not fun right now. There is literally no challenge to this game except finding resources and things to do because the islands are so ridiculously small. The most prominent danger to your survival in this game is getting food which isn't even hard. The only ways you can die are starving, drowning, and getting attacked by sharks or snakes. Both of which are insanely easy to avoid and the sharks and snakes are extremely glitchy and just plain annoying.You could probably play this game for about an hour before there was literally nothing else for you to do. There is like no goal whatsoever, which wouldn't be as big of a problem if it weren't for the fact that there is literally like nothing to explore. There are maybe 2 or 3 very generic shipwrecks that you can find (both of which kind of suck, I might add) but other than that there isn't anything to discover. Exploration is a huge part of open-world survival games and there is nothing to explore in this game... well, other than the multiple islands that are all pretty much the same and also are too small to explore. I literally can't stress enough how depressing the islands are, especially considering this is a freaking island survival game. If you're thinking about buying this, I would at least wait to see if they add anything better because it's currently not worth the money.Things that would make this game bearable or even good:1. More sea creatures- It's an ocean game and literally the only ocean life you see are very generic fish, like one type of shark, really small, boring turtles, and sometimes a whale that doesn't do anything.2. MAKE THE ISLAND BIGGER!!- There is nothing to explore on your island! It is a literal pile of sand with some trees on it with the occasional glitchy crab or snake.3. Add more goals and things you can make- Honestly, the most advanced thing you can really shoot for in this game is a square house. That's pretty much it.4. Exploration- Currently, there is nothing to explore. The shipwrecks in this game are incredibly lame and they are sadly the most exciting thing you can find anyway.5. Add more dangers- This game is way too easy which makes it very boring and if there isn't going to be any goals to work toward because there isn't like anything cool or advanced that you can make, at least make it somewhat difficult to survive.It is still in early access so, who knows, maybe it will get better but for right now, spare yourself and don't pay for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I've had this game for a long time. I've played this game for a long time. I've pretty much beaten the game as it stands right now and I feel conflicted. This game was beautiful and a load of potential. Sadly, it seems that the developers for some reason updated this game backward from whence it started, most likely due to formatting to console release. I remember when this game had a beautiful life under the water where you could find sunken ships anywhere even in the deepest parts of the water. I also remember when worlds used to be infinite and very fun to explore. Now the oceans lay barren and empty and the world a limited with an out of place yellow floating ball border with nothing but empty ocean after it. I know that the world is limited for reasons of bosses and island creations, but I still can't help but feel that something great was taken away from me. Something that could have grown into something beautiful.        I bought this game near the moment of this release, and I was really excited, I would even go on to play this game for hours on end. I remember when the community for this game was booming and everyone was excited to see what would come next. And for the most part, we were not disappointed. But there was one thing everyone was begging the developers to implement every sing update they posted. Multiplayer, the thing everyone wanted because no one wanted to survive alone. But as the days, months, and even years grew on, they never added it, but they added plenty of things that people never asked for. Eventually, the community started begging and pleading, but as time went on, so did people. The hype died down and the most abandoned hope. What went from people giving great ideas and sharing love with the game soon became people giving small comments of pity as they clung to what little hope they had left for the game. And while the developers watched their fan-base shrink, they decided to take action, but not to give the people what they want, but to instead bring out a console release. At which point I knew they had given up and decided to run for a cash grab before it was too late.        The game itself at first is very fun and exciting with plenty of things to look forward to. But after playing long enough you start to realize the grind and just how annoying it is to find the one thing that you need to start doing things that could be actually fun. Like building fun creations. But the building has changed for the worst as they implemented the leveling system that stopped you from building things if you were not high enough level. This leveling system has to be the worst feature I've ever seen in their evolution going backward. The sharks are fun to fight, but they don't even seem to tip over your raft while you sail to another island. Which in my opinion made the game before very challenging in scary. Now sailing to another island is just boring and feels like a waste of time. They also seemed to make the game more complicated as to get the fuel you need to get potatoes, farms, fuel machines, and Jerry Cans. Whereas before you just needed to find a Jerry can with limited fuel already in it. The progression in this game feels more like it's holding you back from experiencing the fun parts until you've experienced the rough buggy hard parts. It took days just to level up enough just so that I could create something that I've wanted through the entire game which I could also acquire in the previous updates just through perseverance and luck.        Overall this game is dying if not already dead, and though it may seem harsh to say and I may just sound like an old bitter man saying it, I feel that I have been betrayed too many times to have any hope for this game. Though it was fun and I enjoyed myself, I don't think that this game is worth it, it felt like a cash grab in the beginning, and it stayed a cash grab until what looks like the end. This game has betrayed and left it's fans alone for so long to play a game that can only provide so much fun. Is it really too much to ask for one thing? The one thing that everyone wants? I've said it more than once, everyone's said it, but I'll ask one more time...                              Beamteam, won't you please add online multiplayer so that I can just                                                                                        have fun with my friends and we can all know that you listen.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll just cover the main reasons as to why I wouldn't recommend this game:-The plane crash scene at the beginning of a new world was deafening even with the master volume set to 20% (the in-game music however wasn't deafening). -The life raft got stuck on the island leaving me no other way to push it out into the ocean meaning that I basically had to start a new world because of this bug. Just to add the cherry on top, when using the life raft, you can't use the escape key to change any settings.-The game has overall went downhill since I last played it. the islands about a year or two ago were like cornucopias holding resources that can last you days, now you'd be lucky to even find an island nearby that has the necessities for survival. The controls were more intuitive leaving me with fewer controls to tamper with. The life raft wasn't broken and was effortless to use because you didn't have to hold the "e" key as much. The experience two years ago just felt more fluid and more appealing.With these cons listed, it's very hard for me to begin listing the pros within this game today because of either all the flaws that I've encountered only ten minutes in the game (as listed above), or because I'm just too impatient in this game to even continue playing with the flaws. After taking a two year break in hopes that the game would be at its prime, it just then struck me two years later to find out that the game was at its prime two years ago.

_childDocuments_.review: The concept for this game is pretty good. The graphics and the setting are okay. As someone who has dived in both Southeast Asia and Australia however, I can tell you that the developers put very little realism or attention to detail in this game. Sharks have been very demonised in this game. I have swam with sharks before and the only way to get attacked by sharks as often as you do in this game would be to wear a wet suit made from freshly caught fish meat. Other inconsistencies are:   - Wild pigs may be aggressive if you approach them by surprise but they would not track a human all over an island to attack them.   - Giant crabs don't spend a lot of time on land and when they are on land, they cannot run due to the weight of their shells.   - In this game you can make a raft base out of tyres. TYRES?? They don't float. Their inner tubes might but the tyres don't.   - Light from the sun can penetrate much deeper into clear Pacific waters than it does in this game. The developers have also released this game as the finished project but there are still some very noticeable glitches in it. When I started my game there was a humpback whale in the water near my first island. It wasn't swimming, it had its front half in the water and its back half was just sticking out of the water motionless. Kind of an immersion breaker.

_childDocuments_.review: Short version: You can't collect rain. With your water collector. This is WAI (!)Long version: I normally love survival games and especially this kind of setting, but this game feels just too shallow, un-intuitive & unrealistic. During my first 2 hours in the games this happened, in chronological order:- Your body, when visible (while rowing for example) looks super weird and distorted- I had to google several times to find out how very basic things in the game are working- Collecting items from the (forest-) ground is a nice "highlight the correct pixel"-minigame- The inventory- and crafting menu is very non-intuitive- I fell while climbing on a palm tree without any reason and lost the half of my healthbar- I crafted a water collector and shortly after it started to rain. I was wondering why there is no water collected, as the setup is visually totally fine and should be able to collect rain.I googled once more and found out that this device isn't collecting rain (rain is ignored in this game), instead  of that you need to place plant material below it to slowly collect water. At this point is quit and requested a refund. I am not sure why this game has so many positive reviews, sorry.

_childDocuments_.review: After about an hour of sitting on an island wishing I hadn't accidentally used all of my rocks to craft tools, I finally resigned myself to my plan of paddling out to a distant island to see if I could gather up some more. I paddled for ages and was incredibly excited to see the new shore. It was a small island with a wrecked ship on both it's east and west sides. After gathering a sizable pile of rocks to take back to my sad little home island, I decided to pull out my knife and explore the shipwrecks.As I swam down into the tiny fishing trawler, I wondered how long I could hold my breath. Long enough to discover a hatchet stuffed away in a locker, and a fuel tank stored in the ship's console, and a spare lighter stored away in a toolbox. I excitedly tossed my treasure on the ground by my raft, eager to see what was located in the other ship.This ship was much larger, maybe a crabbing boat or something. It had at least two decks. I couldn't discover the hidden gems in this thing. Oooh! Is that another hatchet? Yes! Awesome! Whoa, a machete?! Sweet, I should probably go up for air. Alright, air is sufficient. Let's go back down. Wait...what is this music? There hasn't been any music before...this sounds...ominous. Please tell me there aren't sharks in this game...OH CRAP, THAT'S A SHARK. SWIM DAMN YOU, SWIM.After escaping what was certain death, I went back to my raft and settled on what to take back home with me. The rocks, the fuel tank, and my beautiful new machete. The rest, I left on the beach for easy access if I ever decided to grow a pair and finish exploring that boat.As I began paddling back to my island, I reflected on my performance while I experienced extreme fear after spotting the shark, quite happy with myself. I escaped the wrath of a frightening creature while stupidly swimming around in his home turf. I can outperform sharks, man. I'm awesome.It was at this moment of smug satisfaction that I heard the ominous music again and immediately reverted back to fear mode, and looked around my raft in a panic, trying to spot my tormentor. Suddenly my raft was violently pushed by something below me. I flipped out and started mashing buttons in an effort to pull out my new, prized machete treasure. In my panic, I managed to press Q instead, which resulted in my hurling the tiny plastic paddle I was using to transport myself home directly at the shark's head.Realizing I was now stranded in a raft with no way to paddle back home, being circled by a large sea creature with enough teeth to completely ruin my day, I quit the game and decided to sit in bed for awhile wrapped in a cozy, warm blanket.8/10 will most definitely play again.

_childDocuments_.review: This game when it first came out showed an immense amount of potential. Now this game only shows disappointment to me. The idea of surviving on islands in the Pacific is cool but the game suffers from lack of content and slow developement time. I was hoping the game would live up to being called a survival but I've never felt challenged on making sure I'm hydrated and not starving. You find a bucket, make a fire and a spear, spear whatever you desire (even crabs) and you eat your cooked crab and drink your distilled water. It feels like they have only added in waves and some new things and ways to craft. Why craft new items if the game is already easy, why not actually add in some more challenges to overcome or maybe do some new island types instead of expecting us to make them with the island creator? I feel lied to as this game has only become more and more of a "creative survival" which I feel is the result to the developers wanting to finish the game as soon as possible so they've changed their plan to a more traditional, uninspiring, "crafting survival". There was once a period where people thought this game was abandoned and with good reason (there wasn't any updates for almost 2 months and no word from the developer). They take forever to update and none of it is meaningful. The game runs and looks worse from when it was first released. There hasn't been enough content added in 4 months of updates to even want me to check it out for more than an hour. At this rate, the game might take several years to make. Due to how long it takes for them to add anything, they could just be trying to work out some crafting ideas first and then focus on the core of the game (which i still would hope it's surviving) and that makes it seem like the game is going in a direction I didn't think nor wanted it to go in. Regardless that doesn't make this product any better or anymore promising. I've lost hope on this game as it is forced to rely on its looks and ideas (ideas that seemed to have replaced the ones that was released with the game). I can only guess on where the game is going based on the past year and that is nowhere. I've waited a year to see what it has done and all there was to have been seen is money taken from me and now I can only hope the developers get their act together in 2016.

_childDocuments_.review: Day 2: Tomorrow I have to swim to that wreck I saw earlier. There will be something there I can salvage, surely? Got an axe yesterday. Had to use it to get back.  The sharks!! They scare me. Day 3 : Lucked out. The wreck revealed a torch. Flat batteries.  I got back to the island. I find a rock. A stick. A potato plant. I'm feeling vibrant.Day 4: It rained last night. I had nothing to catch the fresh water. Coconut milk again.Day 5: Axe is getting worn. I have plenty of wood. For now. Fire just went out. Must light another. Day 6: I despair at ever drinking fresh water ever again. Day 8: Went swiming today to get some fish. I FOUND A BUCKET!!! Rejoice. Need rain.Day 10: No rain. Tomorrow maybe.Day 12: Still no rain. Coconut milk and cooked crab. I want chocolate. And a burger. And fries. And... coffee..Day 13: Somehow I threw my knife away. I spent all day looking for it. How stupid!!!Day 16: Must. go. to. new. island. Nothing here. Can't last.Day 22: New home. Broken arm. Fell. Getting coconuts. Why did I jump?Day xx: Axe is broken. I don't know anymore. What should I do? Another island?Day xx+1: I'm dying. Broken arm, still.  No water. No food. No axe.Day 27: I woke in a daze. It's... raining. Raining!! I just might survive this. I look at my watch, it's 27th December. I didn't even remember Christmas. I sprinkled sand on a coconut and called it a pudding. It still tasted like.....coconut.. just... gritty. I laughed until I cried. I need a hat. Obviously.Day 28: Decided to live. Feel that it's better to die trying than to just...die. Swam to a new island. Met a whale on the way. It's song stirred me. I'm right. I.must.live.to be continued......

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really fun game. It's definitely lacking polish, but for the price it's exactly what you want out of a tough survival sim. It's challenging (surprisingly so, especially on Hardcore) and the crafting system is pretty slick once you get used to it, just takes a little practice. It looks really pretty and although there are some funny images to be found in the way the physics of objects interact, overall it seems pretty stable. The co-op is a little wonky, I STRONGLY recommend that you play several single player games before trying co-op. The game is difficult and complex enough that you might get pissed off with your buddy trying to learn it and stay alive together at the same time LOL.  I do want to give a minor criticism:The status effects such as poison are a bit over-tuned in my opinion, to the point where they make the game prohibitively difficult on your first few runs (even on Normal difficulty). I suggest the devs should either reduce the number of environmental objects/creatures that cause these effects or make the restorative consumables more accessible. It's possible if you step on a poison thing with full hp and a good base to just lose because you got unlucky and no Antibiotics/Pipi happened to spawn before the effect kills you. If you are playing this one the Hardcore mode, it's basically a guaranteed waste of time unless you get really lucky early with Pipi plant spawns or consumables from shipwrecks. Overall, give this game a try. I think it will only improve as time goes on.

_childDocuments_.review: 2/10The game, while showing some potential, is more than flawed. The combat is unresponsive and unfair, gameplay is barebones, lacks fun milestones or ways of significantly changing what you do(Throughout the game you gather the same resources, loot the same places and craft the same stuff, without real improvements or changes to the gameplay loop).Crafting, while present, is no fun. New structures do not advance your progress by any meaningful degree, you can't customize your raft and there is no incentive to progress to the "higher tiers" of buildings.The fact that you can't build any of the production stations on your vessel, yet the game requires constant island-hopping to gather new resources feels just wrong. The islands lack variation and seem to be always based on one of two blueprints you quickly learn to identify. The fact that you can tell what the resources, enemies and layout of every island is gonna be, before even setting a foot on shore kills any fun exploration might bring. The "story" adds 3 bosses but in combination with the unbelievably flawed combat system makes you dread every single encounter. And for every technical problem that the game has, the multiplayer makes it 10 times worse. It has everything: Absurd long loading times on high end systems, random disconnects, bugs, synchronization issues.The game needs work. At times you can see the potential: General Gameplay idea, Nice graphic effects, the water behavior, atmosphere during thunderstorms, yet all of that pales in comparison to the issues.

_childDocuments_.review: Stranded Deep is one of the unique survival games on Steam.You play as the role of a castaway stuck in the void of Pacific ocean.: Since every island has limited resources, you'll find yourself constantly wandering around the vast open ocean to find another island with yet another scarce resources.There are three ways in which you can travel from island to island: Swimming, paddling, and using a motor boat.Not to mention, sharks will occasionally draw an interest unto the player.You can do a lot of things on an island: Build simple structures, find/cook food, and sleep.In the vast deep sea, you can: loot shipwrecks, and hunt fish/shark for food.The crafting in this game is very unique compared to other games; You craft materials in front of you instead of the traditional craft-it-in-your-inventory/backpack.You need to watch out for three things: Your Health, Hunger, and Thirst.Everything that you do is a necessity for survival.: The graphics of this game is breathtaking. The water's effects are some of the best I've seen. Seeing water quality in other games is rarely done. In fact, they do not act like water at all. This game is an exception to that; moreover, this is an Indie game.The islands are filled with flora elements which makes up the beautiful island scenery.The water world is also perfect.You'll see tons of detailed biomes and aquatic fauna.The only disturbing thing to see in the game is when the player is poisoned and your flashlight/torch is opened. This gives me goosebumps whenever I see this.In conclusion, The graphics is superior in proportion to the file size of the game.: Throwing things around and cutting trees are the most realistic scenarios I can think of.There are many flaws in the Physics of the game: •Raft sinking in the presence of light objects, •You can climb a tree while chopping it down, •You can chop a tree while freely walking afar from it, •Swimming is faster than paddling, •You can use a tree as a raft, • and many more...: Most of the fish travels in schools.The three types of sharks has their own attitude towards the player.Great AI script.There are still a lot of bugs and glitches present in the game since it is still on Alpha stage.I would gladly share how to reproduce those bugs and glitches, Just message me.Stranded Deep is an extremely promising Early Access Game!Rating: Disclaimer: Everything is purely based on my opinion.Thanks for reading!~

name: Suicide Squad: Kill the Justice League
detailed_description: Suicide Squad: Kill the Justice League - Digital Deluxe Edition Jumping into the Digital Deluxe Edition unleashes even more mayhem with the Justice League Outfits for the Squad, 3 Notorious Weapons, 4 Weapon Dolls, 1 Battle Pass Token*, and 4 Color Swatches. *Battle Pass Token redeemable for Premium Battle Pass access (Seasons 1-4 battle passes, subject to availability). One Battle Pass available per season. WB Games may modify or discontinue online services with reasonable notice at any time. About the Game From Rocksteady Studios, the creators of the Batman: Arkham series, Suicide Squad: Kill the Justice League is a genre-defying third-person action shooter where the ultimate band of misfits must do the impossible to save the world: Kill the Justice League. Join the newly “recruited” members of Amanda Waller’s infamous Task Force X (aka the Suicide Squad), Harley Quinn, Deadshot, Captain Boomerang and King Shark, as they set out on an impossible mission to Kill the Justice League. Drop into an expansive and dynamic open-world Metropolis ravaged by Brainiac’s invasion and terrorized by the heroes who once protected it. Each Squad member brings their own traversal mechanics to help them navigate a sprawling and battle-torn Metropolis, combining free-roaming exploration and combat verticality for an unforgettable experience. Players are free to experiment with a variety of different play styles to unleash maximum damage on their enemies. Whether in single player or online with up to three of your friends, players can take on this suicide mission their own way. Post-launch, players can expect a continuously evolving Metropolis with free new playable villains, environments, weapons, in-game events, and more, all included with purchase of the base game.

_childDocuments_.review: Unexpectedly, this game came out blazing, the biggest issues as of 1 day after launch, are performance on old rigs (1060 runs it at 40-60 FPS always) minor bugs here and there that could ruin immersion, annoying voice lines that repeat too much here and there, and the skill trees aren't really customizable, just one big linear tree split into 3 segments.However, the PROS heavily outweigh the *very fixable* CONS.- Very Good story, with really funny bits sprinkled in.- Well meshed mix between combat and movement, both really fun- Interesting elemental mechanics that defy industry norms and provide important combat style changes, and several layers of combat depth- Heavily detailed world with tons of references to comics, previous games, and such. - Enemy variety is probably perfect for combat complexity, I just wish they weren't all purple aliensAfter having just finished the Main Story (hyped to try the endgame content), I believe this almost the best game we could've gotten about the Suicide Squad.So far it deserves a solid 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: THIS REVIEW IS FOR PEOPLE WANTING TO PURCHASE AFTER SEASON 1 (JOKER UPDATE) AND CURRENT EXISTING PLAYERS!Story Experience: So I purchased this game after the Joker update because It's just what I wanted to do. I played through the whole story and did extremely minimal side missions. I figured grinding a game that I only cared about the story for sounded ridiculous. I got through 90% of the game using the weapons I had at the literal start. At some point during the end of the story I got some pretty nice weapon drops that were impossible to not use.Characters: I mainly play Harley but found myself bouncing back and forth from her and Joker. In my opinion those are the two most fun characters to use. However I did give a try to every character in the game and they are absolutely done well through and through. Great abilities and movement for each character AND some characters can have access to weapons that others cant if I'm not mistaken.Gameplay Experience: The appeal for this game 100% comes from the arcady design (keeping up combo score, flashy movement, doing time based challenges, etc). My biggest takeaway from this game is that it ground up feels like a do over of Sunset Overdrive. I started playing Sunset Overdrive because of Suicide Squad and I must say that both games hit right at home with each other. Unlimited fun to be had there. I found myself forgetting to do missions because I'm just flying around with Harley like an idiot having fun and killing things. I think people are extremely critical of this game (Understandably so. Rocksteady has a big reputation to keep with Batman games) but I think you should just relax, turn your brain off, sip on some juice and shoot some bad guys. This game is one of the most fun experiences I've had in any superhero title.Cut scenes: So while I understand that we had some BS thrown in the game from "Sweet baby inc" (from what I could tell only 1% of the game was affected by them but it was obvious when it was shown to you) and the story has some pretty sickening plot holes and doesn't make total sense... however the cut scenes of the game are absolute GOLD. Comedy is so on point. I had so many laughs. The suicide squad were so well scripted, cute, and even had 18+ humor (Boomer pulling out his PP to piss on Flash's dead body and Harley giving him a salute for his size along with the rest of the squad complimenting him LMAO).FORM AN ORIGINAL THOUGHT: I wish more people would get off twitter and stop spewing the same words because its trendy to say "game bad" instead of forming an actual original thought. Unfortunately not everyone is as insanely passionate about games as I am and wont give something a chance the way I would. But hopefully this review can change some minds. I know a bad game when I see one and this one is just great fun. It's not bad, not terrible, not a triple A insane experience. It's just great fun. This review doesn't go insanely in depth because I dont feel like writing a novel. I did touch on most things I wanted to though but... that's all. Buy the game on a sale lolAlso RIP Kevin. Thank you for everything <3W Game

_childDocuments_.review: A weird one to review to say the least. So lets start simple.Visuals: 9/10Open World: 7/10Combat: 11/10 (Boomerang in particular)Story: 7/10 (maybe an 8 but i need to think more)Endgame: 6/10 (I'm addicted but its super repetitive and grindy)Customisation: 7/10 (not as good as Borderlands or Destiny, but who doesn't love a good dopamine hit?)Performance: 10/10 (14700kf and 3080, the best day one performance in years. no bugs, zero crashes and a very stable frame rate)I'm hooked on this game. It sucks that so many people are crapping on it without playing it. It has many issues, the endgame is kinda boring for example. It's balanced out by the absolutely incredible movement and gunplay. I feel like a badass everytime I start playing.If you enjoying fun characters, kinetic and fluid combat, looter shooter mechanics and the idea of playing new content on and off over an extended period of time; this is for you. Is it worth $80-$110? (CAD) that's up to you. Personally I got a discount through my humble bundle subscription and I don't feel like a single cent was wasted.Wait for a sale if you're uncertain. If you love DC and the Arkhamverse, or looter shooters and binge-ing games for 8 hours straight then play this ASAP.Overall I give it a 7.5/10 and I can't wait to get back into the city of Metropolis to grind some repetitive end game quests and prep for season 1.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty awful. Not gonna lie. I wanted to like it, I really did but it becomes apparent in the first couple minutes why it has the reputation it does and why no one is playing it.One of the worst forced tutorials I've played in a long time followed by immediate game breaking bugs forcing you to exit out to the menu to reload and hope is works. Tons of other bugs and glitches, one prominent one being invisible characters. And the game is riddled with them from start to end. It makes the playing experience pretty poor.After all that what you get is a pretty poor looter shooter with a sometimes funny but awfully stupid story that often makes no sense based on any DC lore. The writers clearly had no idea what they were doing or how anything in the universe works from kryptonite to lantern rings. The traversal is abysmal all around. Like literally atrocious and it's such a major part of the game, that it should have been the most enjoyable part, but it's by far the worst. The combat is okay to bad, but pretty scripted and just doesn't feel fluid or fun.They don't understand loot or how to reward it. You often get things that are far worse than what you received LEVELS before. I was even still using the first 2 guns I got 6 hours later because not one drop was better. You can't join anyone's game, only be invited. Even if you get booted or crash, you have to wait for the person to re-invite you. If you're not the host you can't do anything in the Hall of Justice. No upgrading or rerolling, nothing. You're locked out from a pretty important part of the gameplay just for not being player 1.It's like this with everything in the game, every single little detail is done wrong or badly. It honestly feels like with every single aspect of the game they asked themselves what would piss off the players the most and went with that. This game is not worth $60, this game is not worth $20. Maybe MAYBE $10 would be a good price point for this pile, but even then you won't get much time out of it before realizing why it's so hated. It deserves it. Rocksteady deserves to be closed for even trying to put forth this garbage as a real game.In the infamous words of the Nerd, WHAT WERE THEY THINKING!?

_childDocuments_.review: When it comes to playing Suicide Squad I'm something of an anomaly. I have zero experience playing any of Rocksteady's Arkham games. I also have very (very) little exposure to super hero/villain video games as they're not my style. What I do have experience with, however, is playing looter shooters with similar gunplay/traversal (such as Warframe, The First Descendant, etc.). This last aspect is key because it's the gunplay/traversal in Suicide Squad that initially drew me to the game to begin with, despite the controversy and complaints. I eventually decided to give it a try and so far I am glad I did. I think visually speaking the game looks really good. In terms of character development the rag tag squad of idiots that you play as are on-brand and not nearly as annoying as I thought they would be. The missions of course can feel recycled but to me the gameplay itself is fun enough to overcome any annoyances I may have with the same mission structure repeated over and over again. This game feels like a mix of Warframe, Gotham Knights, and The First Descendant and I dig it.

_childDocuments_.review: Suicide Squad Review EDIT APRIL 2ND 2024:Please don't buy this game, the season model is insanely grindy and it adds basically no story content. Save your money. Don't support this game till they acknowledge these issues, such a sad way to see rocksteady go down.TLDR;6.5 out of 10    (EDIT: 2 out of 10)GAME IS MIDThe gameplay is super funThe story is below average Not worth $70, get it on sale This game is “something”. I've played all the Arkham games, and I have enjoyed what Rocksteady has done with that world. This is a huge step away from what they've done before. After beating the story, if you enjoy DC IP and these suicide squad members you'll be entertained. The story has its moments but it is a little stale. It is a rocksteady story though that can't be missed. The humor was pretty good but at the expanse of characters, I wish we had more time with them. The gameplay is honestly the most fun I've had in a while with a game like this, it is super chaotic and fast-paced pace but it is so much fun. Traversal is super fun and just fast. All the characters are unique in traversal and abilities, but the gunplay on all of them is similar enough. This is 100% a live service game and you can't escape that aspect of the game. It's always online, weapon rarities, resources, contracts, dailys, and loadout crafting. If you just wanna play the story and play the next game in the “Arkham Series”, you can do your best to ignore this aspect of the game but it will always be there, offline play is set to be coming at a later date post-release. I can best describe this game as if Destiny, Borderlands, Sunset Overdrive, and Warframe had a baby and slapped an Arkham coat of paint on it. If you enjoy those games you will enjoy this game if you like DC. Overall I give this game a 6.5 out of 10. Not worth the full price, and would be more fun with friends. Pleasantly surprised with the gameplay and traversal but slightly disappointed with the story. Addressing the big giant bat in the room, Yes I am Upset with how they treated Arkham Batman but it's whatever. I'm just glad I got to hear Kevin Conroy reprise the role of one of my favorite Batman adaptations one last time after his passing.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to love this game so bad, but I just can't. You can tell that Rocksteady really did not want to make this, executives at WB saw the Arkham games' success, and likely just ordered Rocksteady to make it. They made the story entertaining, there aren't really any bugs I've come across, but my god is the story itself just bad. I haven't even completed it yet, but its hard to enjoy unless you're playing with someone else. The gameplay is mediocre, the best way I can describe it as a Captain Boomerang main is fortnite mixed with the speed of titanfall. $70 for the price of this is such a scam. It's a looter shooter but just feels like they crammed the loot system in last second. I can't believe I'm saying this, but as an Arkham veteran, I genuinely hope that this game fails completely so they'll go back to making single player non live service games. This failure is definitely on Warner Brothers, not Rocksteady. I really, really wanted this game to be good, I was excited and bought it on day one. But It's just not worth it right now. I don't consider this game at all cannon to the Arkhamverse in the slightest, either. It completely removes the point of Batman's joker story arc in Knight. The lines that Batman has does not make him feel like Arkham Batman, but Kevin Conroy still had a fantastic performance with them.The boss fights are laughably easy, if THIS is the real Justice League you're killing, I think they would've died long before the suicide squad got to them. It is crazy to think that Batman, in Arkham Origins, in his SECOND YEAR of crime fighting, took down a significant amount of his rogues gallery who were also completely only out to get him, would die to a couple of idiots, a magic shark and one actually competent assassin. Especially when here, in this game, he is not holding back at all! He has brainiac's army at his disposal, he is not afraid to kill in the slightest, and he's also dealt with criminals far more powerful than these four.  And the first time we see the whole Justice League in an "Arkhamverse" game is one we have to kill them in? What a load of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Superman hardly even has a full page of dialogue in total, hell, even Green Lantern had significantly more screen time(no hate on Green Lantern, but he's usually a pretty minor character in comparison to Superman). This game does nothing for DC or its fans to be excited about. Oh, cool, we get to kill an evil Justice League and get a kind-of sequel to Arkham Knight! That doesn't matter, let's be honest, the only reason you're even thinking of buying this game is because it's in the Arkhamverse and is from Rocksteady, not because it genuinely looks fun(which, by the way, it's not. Mission design is very repetitive). And, even for Arkhamverse nostalgia, it's not enough for $70 PLUS MICROTRANSACTIONS! The league members almost all die in the same, boring-ass way, with hardly any tribute to their characters after their deaths(maybe like 10 seconds at most, yikes). The story is super flat, and does what the Harley Quinn show did but worse; ♥♥♥♥♥ on every superhero in the least funny, most boring, uninteresting way imaginable, except maybe Wonder Woman. Come on WB, bring that cancelled batman beyond game back into development! Give us superman, or flash, or hell, even green lantern games(not mentioning wonder woman because she's getting her own game outside of the Arkhamverse) instead of whatever the hell this is. Make an actual justice league game for crying out loud, that'd sell and play far better than this! Even as a live service! A co-op Justice League game with Arkham's freeflow combat where theres a focus on fighting different villains each season? I'd rather it not be live service, but THAT is SO much better than this! That would probably make infinitely more money than this!I genuinely cannot believe how good at making bad decisions like this game Warner Brothers is. This is a disgrace to the Arkhamverse and anything related to it. Rocksteady may have been dealt a bad hand by greedy WB execs, but man, did they not even really try to do anything interesting with it other than some small references to previous Arkham games here and there. And all this for 8 1/2 years of waiting for something new from Rocksteady? I think that part is a funnier joke than any of the lines in this game, which is so sad. I could not be more disappointed. ♥♥♥♥ Warner Brothers. Go play the arkham games if you haven't, you'll have infinitely more fun with those than this mountain of ♥♥♥♥.

_childDocuments_.review: Major mainstream review sites are calling the game's campaign too short, saying it clocks in at around 10 hours. 10 hours into the game on the hardest difficulty, I am 30% of the way through the campaign and having a great time. I disagree with all the bad you've heard about this game. Rocksteady has given us a well-written, well-acted evolution of the Arkham formula. The slower pacing of Batman's stories has been replaced with a Doom 2016 style of constant offense to move through each encounter, and I think it's really enjoyable to see how the studio has developed over time.Rocksteady delivered a very fun, sometimes challenging, well-told story. The only negative outside the typical complaints about GaaS is that the UI can be a little too much at times. Luckily, the menus allow for a great deal of turning off the UI.Not a perfect game, but one worth the asking price. Looking forward to Joker's debut and how Season 1 pushes the game forward.

_childDocuments_.review: From start to finish I honestly enjoyed playing this game, some aspects were truly memorable and stood out for me. Knowing this game had mixed reviews on release and considering how much fun I had playing it I felt compelled to share my experience. Suicide Squad: Kill the Justice League is everything you would expect from a Rocksteady game and more. This full force action adventure will keep you on the edge of your seat and coming back. Accompanied with exhilarating combat, over the top executions, next level cut scenes and graphics, a silly yet exciting story line, tons of weapons and loot, and the list goes on. Buckle up you are in for one hell of a ride.To begin, the story was well done and kept me hooked throughout its 20 hour or so kill spree. The cut scenes and character animations were next level and felt cinematic, some of the best I have seen in a game thus far. The writing and personalities of the characters felt spot-on and a lot of the time had me laughing while still being compelling. I never wanted to miss or skip a cut scene they were so good. The story is on the darker side with some rated R moments, though it never takes itself too seriously. It really feels awesome and is a unique twist to play as the supervillains to help save the world and kill the justice league.The all-around game play was frenetic, stylish, destructive, and delightful, a definite highlight of the game. Even though it's a third person shooter a lot of the time you will be getting up close and personal, utilizing melee combos and powerful abilities to vanquish Braniac's hordes of minions. There is an endless number of weapons and loot, and many other ways to customize your character. The game also has a fair number of enemies and even more have been added in. The combat effects are insane, the speed and kill animations with all the colors, glitz, and glam, it's really a pleasure to watch and even more so to play. You can suit up as any of the available Suicide Squad members and each have a distinctive feel and play style. When I thought one character was my favorite, the next I tried soon became my new favorite. Once you level up your squad, they truly feel a force to be reckoned with. The open world in Metropolis is a nice size map you can freely roam with plenty of missions and activities to partake in. The mobility of the different characters are highlighted when traversing through the city and was fun in itself. The world can seem a tad lifeless besides enemies, but based on the plot it feels fitting though still could be improved on. Once you beat the game there is a seemingly endless amount of content to play and you can upgrade your squad even further. The end-game missions can feel repetitive, but there is still a good variety to choose from. And since you can play with up to four friends it feels like a new playground at your disposal. There are some micro transactions, but they are minimal, unnecessary, and dont interfere with the game in any way. Every season there is new content and a new theme to Metropolis which makes it fun to go back in and play. Since I started the game, the developers seem to have added quite a few updates which is nice to see. I have mentioned this game to quite a few people while playing it letting them know how much I am enjoying it and I feel it has plenty to offer. I highly recommend giving this game a go and getting a group of friends together to maximize the fun.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great.The  story is really good. I am someone who represents the opinion that campaigns could be left out all together from 99% of the games I play because I dont care about the characters, their motives, etc.. I just want to enjoy the game and not be interupted by some random NPC or boring cutscene. However in this game the characters are intersting and dont "stall" the conversation with unnecessary dialogue and get straight to point or at least fast enough at times. I went into this game with the intention to skip all cutscenes and watched all in the end. The story missions themselves are mostly the same with some variations but due to the gameplay it is fine.The gameplay is just amazing and reminds of Sunset Overdrive at least when playing as Harley. Every character has his own unique movement. Captain Boomerang teleports and dashes, Deadshot can fly and King Shark can leap and dash. Traversing the city is fun to some degree but where the gameplay really shines is in combat. When you just stand around or strafe you will eat damage easily on higher difficulties so you are encouraged to use your movement all the time while in combat and keep your momentum while shooting and dodging. For example as Harley you grapple onto a ledge then overshoot to get some air time then when you fall again you swing with your drone to keep the momentum after which you enter slide or grapple again to reset the cooldown all while shooting and dodging bullets or other stuff.The endgame is ok at best. You basically repeat 3 missions over  and over again with the only variation being the objective moving 10m right or left and the enemies getting stronger. One thing I think is pretty nice is gear can be made "elite" which means you can re-roll or choose every augment you want which just costs a bit more ressourses.For it beeing a looter shooter though the game doesnt have many different legendaries and uniques and even less are viable. It contains enough to create a few cool builds but it needs way more. Also the "skill-tree" is honestly just 30 rows seperated to make it look like one from games like Borderlands. Each row containes up to 3 skills of which you can choose one per line and you get 30 skillpoints so can pretty much skill everything.All in all I definitly recommend the game but if you arent the person to grind and just want to play the campaign wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: In general a game with a lot of potential that was completely wasted by developers focusing on things that nobody actually cares about (but hey it generates a lot of articles and brownie points with people that won't buy the games!) instead of focusing on what fans want and to create a game and product that delivers value to them - so I will be waiting eagerly for Rocksteady to be closing soon so that they stop wasting WB money and hopefully we can see way better DC projects one of these days by other companies - Update: seems like this is almost underway and deserved.■  The game has a lot of potential and a solid base with the gameplay traversal accompanied with the combat mechanics that together created a really fun gameplay loop plus the characters although similar due to the fact that all use ranged weapons (for the long ranged combat, while for short range combat they each use their own weapons) with the traversal and weapon limits they still felt different enough from each other to make sense to change to another one from time to time (although the level up should be shared to avoid having a difference in power). ■  The graphics are quite nice specially considering the entire story is using pretty much just real time cutscenes and delivers on what it needs there and the world is detailed enough that you can go to any area and see that each area has a defined mood and style, plus along with this in terms of performance it never became an issue specially considering that it's an open world and more the fact that you can move quite fast through it without getting into stutters or similar.■  Following the perspective and premise of a Suicide Squad team being created on the spot to save the world by having to try and kill the Justice League is a really interesting and funny premise, the four members all have their time to shine individually and together plus they all bounce well of each other and this accompanied with the high quality cut-scenes being quite decently length (not to long to forget you are playing a game but not so short that are meaningless) in the end they were able to deliver the story with quite some highlighting moments. Some aspects of the premise were criticised by people but this premise is nothing that new and usually repeated in many of the comics and other media, in which Batman always prepares a plan in case the Justice League gets compromised and also always voices his wishes to get taken down and eliminated in case if he also gets compromised (e.g. the plot in Justice League Dark Apokolips saga), plus all of this makes sense since the people for this job would be the people on Suicide Squad, they are all villains that just want to do what is best for them - in this case to get their freedom and saving the world is just an indirect consequence of them saving themselves and their close ones.■  In a open world the missions and specially secondary missions are the bread and butter of what you will be doing most of the time, the devs couldn't even put some proper effort in making a nice variety of basic objectives here that would support a normal open world, with the fact that this was a GAAS this could have been fulfilled but pretty obvious that no effort was put into doing that aside from adding end game-change-color-of-boss-and-et-voila type of missions.■  Probably the the biggest red flags aside from the aforementioned repetitive nature of the missions which aligs with the fact that the game was sold as to be a fully fledged Games As A Service (GAAS) which didn't deliver at all since simply it never had enough variety of initial content to be sold as such and also wasn't fed and kept up-to-date to get to a good point over the past months in order for that standard to be achieved by retaining players but also try bring new people in - 6 months after release and all we had was just 1 character and a few meager updates to the game with an upcoming character that nobody wants.■  Along with the failed GAAS the biggest issue is that the few pieces content that they are working and releasing are simply nonsensical	■ ■ First character out of four was a Variant of Joker which is an obvious marketing ploy but at least it has a justification due to the obvious popularity of Joker and still fitting easily into a Suicide Squad type of story.      ■ ■    Second character will be Ms Freeze that's not even using anything similar to the original design of the original character (even considering as a variant) so it's not even a variant of the Original Villain.	■ ■ Third character will be Lawless/Zoe Lawton the daughter of Deadshot which is pretty much an unknown character with no marketability or interest from anyone since it's a badly made up retcon.■ ■ 	Fourth and last character will be Deathstroke which is a quite popular character but not in the scale that it justifies a slot as it was the case with Joker. 	So in the end, arguably one of four characters actually made any sense to get added instead of focusing on creating and adding proper Suicide Squad members which was what people were hoping to have when buying this game. If they wanted to do a character focused on cold why would they not add the fan favorite and well known Suicide Squad member Killer Frost or you could even go with Captain Cold, again both are members of SQ and are actually well liked characters and then fill the rest of the slots with the obvious popular and fan-favorites such as Peacemaker, Killer Croc, Enchantress, Katana, etc.■  All they could monetize they tried to do it (battle-pass, buy levels, buy characters, buy skins, etc) and failed miserably at it and the most basic thing that they could do with success they haven't done, 6 months later after the release and you still don't even have any decent character skins from other versions of media (e.g. Killing Joke Joker, Harley Isekai, Deadshot variant from the original Arkham, etc) which they could easily sell to fans plus they could even leverage them to add more team members as echo characters without having to add anything to the story or missions just to satisfy fans of the characters (e.g. premium skin for King Shark of Killer Croc since they could traverse and fight in the same way, Bloodsport skin for Deadshot, etc).

_childDocuments_.review: I hate that I've enjoyed it as much as I have.But the looting aspect of the game doesn't have enough variety. The weapon ratings seem very arbitrary when you're given legendary rated weapons from your first, second, and third missions. I may have just been lucky but with how easy it is to craft more, I doubt it.I've only gotten to the first major boss of the game, so I can't really say much for the bosses. I thought that the boss was quite good though I've seen a lot of people think the opposite. It might have been because I was setting myself up for failure with difficulty, character choice, and weapon.The story is very standard, it starts off quite strong and aside from a few very minor complaints, it is still fine at least up until this point.The movement in the game is great. I've been mostly playing as Harley since her swinging is somewhat reminiscent of the Arkham games before this.But I've left a negative review on this game because it has some pretty bad performance issues. My device generally has higher specs than the recommended, so I should have no issue running the game. But I was met with a lot of freezing and frame rate dropping. Especially when going in between cutscene and gameplay. The game being live service also is weird. It doesn't feel like one in any aspect that I've seen so far. It just seems like a way for them to excuse features not yet being in the game. The UI is also pretty ugly.The game is just too expensive for what it is. Especially since there are in game purchases already for skins. It seems like they're trying to juggle between monetization practices by putting it at the price of a AAA game (which it is) but with the micro transactions of a free to play game. If the price was even brought down 20% this review would probably be positive.Updating: Batman's boss fight was disappointing. Superman was a good boss fight. There is a whole lot of bugs that I've encountered especially in regard to projectile hit boxes. Tanks should not be able to shoot you through any surface. Any of the missions that require critical hits to do damage should not exist. Non critical hits will heal them and your allies will actively screw you over by healing bombers and tanks to full health whenever you get them low. Also the explosion on critical hits that they give also is disadvantageous since the explosion isn't a critical hit so it just knocks them in the air sometimes while healing. Terrible mission condition.

My opinion of this game, with what I have done so far as I'm waiting for the ALTERNATE Joker launch, is that this could be an alternate timeline of the Arkham-verse. Note, this is if you're playing with keyboard and mouse.Gunplay and melee- guns feel too forced with melee being a secondary feature rather than an alternative to using guns, especially for King Shark and Harley. However, all guns feel great!Shields- I both like and hate this mechanic. I like it because it is unique for a Batman game. I hate it because Waller decided to go, in-universe, "Screw you criminals I've forcefully conscripted! You don't fight, you die!". Meaning, you have to avoid getting hit, shoot the enemies in the legs to get them ready to be hit by a melee attack to get a shield boost, and keep moving around. _childDocuments_.review: Yeah, I don't recommend this game at all.Just like everyone else is saying, it costs way too much for something so skin deep and actually short. BASE GAME (Finite Crisis):The bosses are paradoxically too easy and too hard at the same time, with Flash and Superman really being the two "hard" bosses that I wish would just stop moving more often without something exploding or hitting/knocking you back before you can get a decent shot in, but then, if you DO use a sniper or pistol against them in frustration (they both deal insane damage on single shots, which is all you'll get in against those two) then they get trivialized and die in around 6-12 hits, or perhaps actually die as quickly as intended, because otherwise they're unhittable, don't stop moving, and barely take any damage (literally over 2,000 hits if you use a minigun, rifle, smg, or shotgun, for some reason). On the other hand, Green Lantern and Batman are fine fights, because both are still a lot of the time and don't need to constantly be countered with the counter gimmick at very specific times in order to become damageable, and in batman's case, is the one boss big enough to be hit decently with any weapon. Tldr, it's all over the place, and Flash and Superman really only die to Snipers and Pistols.UNLIKE everyone else, however, I really do get and see what they were going for here outside of that. The tone of the game is far brighter, casual, and goofier than the Arkham games, and all the characters are either cracking jokes that may or may not be funny to people, or... are Waller, Brainiac, and the generic second-in-command guy who are all really overbearing and annoying. That bright, casual goofiness, as well as the annoyance, actually extends into the playstyles, skill trees, and even the loot system, and yes, it's a lot to go through.Each character has their own playstyle, movement option, 3 innate skills, and like 2 skillpoint builds each that actually make sense for them. They've also got restrictions on which weapons each one can use for some reason, which is more annoying than it is helpful. In the end, though, the majority of your build will ignore the skill tree completely (totally not because half of every tree is based on the combo mechanic that doesn't work that well with the minion spam and op single units the game has) and will rely mostly on the loot you get, which...Loot in this game is probably confusing to most people. Instead of following the usual upgrade styles where you get better loot as you play, nah. If you get a legendary in the first few missions, you're basically set into the endgame, which is both silly, but also kinda nice, as it cuts out the extreme farming that a lot of other games have, BUT......then you get to the extremely repetitive and gated endgame. My god it's actually worse than Warframe's grinds. You initially get 3 missions to get some currency to do 3 other missions, then you kill Brainiac, who's a repeat of Flash with extra mechanics (although his arena does allow for more than a sniper to be used, I still reccomend using a sniper or pistol, minigun if you're playing king shark) except his flash fight is better than the one that came before it, I think it's down to the arena being better, but, anyway, you kill him, and then... Get a screen saying that's it until they release the next season, then you get into the boring, rotating grind of doing the 6 missions you already did, one at a time, at very, very gradually harder difficulties so you can unlock more difficulties over and over and over until you get to 20 on all of them, except, instead of going by, say, 5s, they went by 1s. You do all the missions on Mastery 3 and you unlock mastery 5. You do them all on 5, you get difficulty 7, and all the while, your gear isn't changing, and all you're getting are skillpoints for a meta tree straight out of a roguelike, if you actually got anyone to 30 and kept playing them. The gear is randomly dropped and higher levels give higher tiers for SPECIFIC BUILDS. (This is important going into Joker's season.)Thus, in the end, it's more bad than it is good, sadly. The loot system is nice, the guns and traversals feel great, but the characters are 50/50, and the grind is terrible, even for just leveling everyone to 30, and it gets stagnant way too fast. You can't even directly matchmake with other people to somewhat alleviate this, you have to go out of your way, into the matchmaking menu, open up YOUR game to other people, and then either wait for them to filter in and start doing things if they chose the same option, or go in and have them go along with whatever you're doing at some point, point being, there's no quick-joining here despite the flat loot and power scales and the genuine opportunity to just drop in and go regardless of level, skills, or what have you. There's even clans/guilds ffs, but no real reason to get them together. (You can just use other people's characters in your game with a wacky social bot system, so, it's just weird, though maybe also helpful..?)It also likes to freeze randomly for varying amounts of time as you traverse the city.ELSEWORLDS: (Currently just Joker's ill-fittingly-named Season of Fear that focuses on... *Scarecrow*, who in-lore is currently horribly mentally damaged and traumatized beyoned belief somewhere in or out of Arkham.)Say it with me now: epic grind with no progression, battle pass grind, grind for the character, grind until you drop dead. I went into it with 1 or 2 level 30 characters and very little equipment from the basegame grind and once I saw "Dazed/Crazed immunity" , I was glad I DIDN'T grind it at all... (This was recently changed to 50% resist, but is still grating if you really went for the Finite Crisis grind) and then you basically get put into ANOTHER grind to raise "episode rank" that's also your Mastery Rank once you hit 35 and kill Green Lantern- sorry, Brain Lantern , with the added downside of Episode Rank going up regardless of if it's one of the purple missions or not, but Mastery Rank only going up if you do the purple missions on harder and harder difficulties... But there aren't really tank builds and winning missions is essentially fully RNG coupled with if you got the full sets of the current season. ICK.Oh, and by the way, you get one animated cutscene for joker's prehistory at the start, and one cutscene for his admittance into the squad after you do the grind. It's a nothing sandwich inbetween.Oh, and it's still Online Only with Guilds, but you can't randomly matchmake with other people, you can only have them match with you, so... What's the point of the guild.0/10, there are better and more rewarding games/grinds out there that don't put their characters behind 20 hour empty grinds.

_childDocuments_.review: Im not sure I understand the negativity towards this game.  I can only surmise that most of the negative reviews are people of the following:-Big time Arkham series fans that really enjoy their single player DC superhero experience.-Big time DC fans that cannot fathom the "justice league" being corrupted.  Seriously, I've seen some articles and posts with people saying one of the reasons they dislike the game is because Batman would never succumb to this...hell, he survived scarecrow and his mania!-People who vehemently despise live service games with a cash shop.  This one I can understand more to a degree. If you strip all of that away...It has a decent story, at least I thought so.A fleshed out endgame (Seriously, I dont see what people could possibly complain about here).  Metropolis missions to farm promethium to then jump into incursions in order to raise mastery in order to raise finite crisis rank so that you can access higher tier gear.  Every now and then, sprinkle in some killing time missions and you also have 13 braniacs to kill across the nexus as true challenges.  What is lacking here?  Looter/looter shooter/arpgs have launched with FAR less.  Division 2 launched with a lot less.  Destiny 2 launched with WAY, WAY less (Seriosuly here, we had like...earth for the first year or so with absolutely nothing to do. It wasnt like how destiny 2 is today.) The endgame is there.  Its a grind like any other looter.Decent build customization, although they should have launched with more than just the bane set.  You almost feel compelled to lean into Venom/Craze for every build but you can venture out.I thought the dialogue between the characters is pretty comical.  And not just in a "oh hah thats funny", some lines had me cracking up.Additionally, I understand that sweetbaby had a hand in writing this.  I've only seen one true area where the wokeness is present.  I havent seen anywhere else.  Maybe Im blind or deaf.Looking at the game for what it is:  A live-service looter shooter in a super hero universe (street villains, nice spin) I give it a 7.5/10.  It does what it needs to do as a looter shooter fairly well.
