_childDocuments_.review: This is a biased review based on other metroidvania games played. It will also have spoilers so beware. I have completed an ending of the game with 52% of achievements completed. Overall, this game is disappointing. For the prices, this game is better than Itorah, somewhat on par with Souldiers but far behind Hollow Knight (HK). The game feel short and lacks polish.For the pros:Nice environment/background artNice sprite workNice soundtrackFor the cons:Character PortaitsLength of gameplayStoryWeapon balanceAnimationCombatBased on a first time playthrough, I know I missed some sections which seemed impossible to get to based on the items I had. However, I reached the end without exploring them. For reference  This ending felt unsatisfactory and leads me to believe/hope there was more. I hate how some dialogue is voices but most isn't and is just text. Compared to the beautiful background, the character portraits suck. I feel Souldiers character dialogue scenes are better. Combat is passable with enemies having enough pattern recognizance on when to dodge/run away. Allocating your stats make it seem like an important task but its not, just make sure your strong and any enemy will die eventually. Melee only seems a playstyle but some enemies explode making shooting at a distance much more viable. The  seem to be the best special weapons with others not dealing enough damage or being completely useless. There's a luck stat that seem entirely useless as I only found one item to upgrade it and it costs 8,000 nanogel. Nothing but two collectibles seemed to be drop by standard enemies and I got those near the beginning of my playthrough. Animations seem stiff. With the running and walking animation being similar to adobe flash bone tools. For the details/beauty on the background and the soundtrack, the animations looks stiff. There is some world building in the narrative, but nothing that makes you wonder or creates a want to know more. From what I gathered . There's some mystery about the world but nothing that really hooked me to care or see the lore explained.There some unique mechanics in the game that make it interesting, but not enough to make use of them (overheating making your melee stronger, certain melee weapons having unique moves   a rechargeable special bar for alternate fire. Unfortunately, the game doesn't make these options favorable due to lack of balance.I would recommend this game on a sale which make me believe HK being $15 and being so polished has set the bar high for new metroidvanias. Still, I do hope for a sequel that builds upon the mechanics set out in this game does come out but based on the ending I got, I don't see that happening. Close but no cigar
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: I wish this was better, because the core gameplay is fun but it has too many negatives which bring it down.The story just peters out with no proper conclusion. There's a large amount of story that was told through side missions that were easily missable and explained some of what was actually happening. Not that it matters because it didn't come up in the ending.Most of the sub weapons are bad. The usual process was:Final a new sub weapon> Is it better than the rocket launcher?> No> Keep using the rocket launcher.Later on in the game when I got the double & wall jump abilities I was able to scale a large cliff to the right of the landing site. But there's nothing there, just multiple empty screens. You really couldn't put a place a few enemies to shoot?It's impossible to buy all the weapons/ equipables from the shop without grinding. By the end of the game I needed at least 5000 currency to afford the last item (13000 if you include the overpriced luck seed.)The merchant even makes a comment about how he shouldn't be charging and should just give the player the items he is selling. Of course the offer is immediately turned down by the protagonist.Unnecessary padding which seems to only exist to add to the short game length. Whenever a ship part is found, fast travel is disabled. This could have been an interesting challenge, but in reality it seems to just exist to waste time. A few easy enemies are spawned on the way back to the ship, but it never escalates and never felt like it couldn't have been skipped without losing anything from the game as a whole.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: The instant people hear metroidvania, certain expectations pop into their head, and I think if you go into Ghost Song with those expectations, you might be disappointed. The combat doesn't have the most depth to it, there is a decent amount of options for combat but a lot of it feels like personal choice rather than needing any real strategy or tactics.  You do progress with a fairly standard set of exploration skills but there isn't an incredibly big world here to explore and there's only a few differences between areas.However, what I got out of this game was a moving set of personal stories. This is a game not about surviving alone, but surviving together, and that's a tone I haven't experienced too much of in games of this genre, so I was happy to go through it. And I especially like how much characterisation is given to the main character using very, very few words.Do I want more of...basically everything? Sure, I'd have loved to have more in depth conversations and interactions with characters, to see more of this universe they've made, or to follow up on some of the wild plot threads and concepts that are happening in the background. But it's enough for one game, especially one game from a small team, and I do hope we see more from them sometime.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: This game is simply ... just not good. I think that is a hard to swallow pill that people who backed this game or have been following its development will just have to accept. If you are looking for a good metroidvania, look elsewhere.The good: - The art. Probably the only thing that is good, but the best art in the world cannot carry the bad design that come with this game.The bad: - Gameplay design. For some reason the creators decided that your primary weapon would be a gun, while at the same time deciding that a large bulk of enemies will be a knee height meaning that all your shots go right over them unless you decide to crouch. And if you crouch you are unable to move. - Clunky controls. This is by far my biggest gripe with this game, everything is bad. Sprinting not only consumes stamina, but is overall slower than dashing since it requires 3 seconds to actually ramp up and then still does not feel like a sprint. The wall jumps are inconsistent, sometimes you think you are wall jumping but you end up doing a double jump. The player character is slow as HECK, meaning even simple jumps across small gaps become a tedious task.- Platformer design. Boy oh boy, the poor platformer design combined with the clunky movements leads to the biggest wombo combo of annoying gameplay. There are many instances where the level screens look like they were made by a child, including repetitive vertical shafts with one-block wide platforms acting as a ladder, or just rooms with nothing but an empty corridor. Many cases of platforming were clearly not well tested, with distances between platforms being just far enough that you need to time the jump very well to land on the tiny midair platform, while using your dash means you overshoot the same gap.- Story/narrative. The entire game is a massive fetch quest, and the game establishes that one hour into it. One hour into the game and you already know what the remaining 10 hours of your gameplay is going to be. No rising tension or build up to a dramatic climax, just a long arduous fetch quest for 10 hours, leading to a huge copout of an ending. This tedium further accentuated by the conscious decision to block fast travelling when delivering the fetch quest items, serving no gameplay purpose outside of padding your play time. - Lack of meaningful progression/upgrades. There is no rhyme or reason behind any of the upgrades obtained, which are usually just randomly located across the map. Aside from the fact that the game does not introduce anything new to the default metroidvania abilities of only dash, mid air jumps, and wall jumps, these upgrades are rewarded with no context after a boss fight. Every location of every ability could have been put through a metroidvania randomiser and I would not have known the difference between the randomiser and the base game, since no ability fits in thematically with the area or boss it comes from. - Evident lack of playtesting and polish. I encountered many bugs and/or potential softlocks. These include the map markers, where the keys used to navigate the cursor around the map ALSO change the map marker being selected simultaneously. As well as the map markers appearing in the layer beneath the map, so sometimes it becomes partially obstructed. The dialogue locks you out of any actions, meaning you cannot for example, open a shop while an NPC is talking to you. One particular area requires you to deliver an item back to the camp site after you obtain the item after defeating the boss. However, the game automatically saves when you defeat the boss and initiate this delivery quest. What it doesn't do, however, is topping up your health and resources. This lead to me having to navigate my way out of the area with literally 1 hp because that was how much hp I had left after defeating the boss.There is so much more that is just ... executed poorly but I think I will end my review here.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: After I put 10 hours of game play in I felt my teeth starting to sink into this delicious Metroidvania. My teeth didn't sink too far though as the game ended an hour after this awesome feeling of environmental/lore discovery.  I feel as if this could have been a 10/10 Metroidvania if were about 20 hours longer with expanded lore, but as is a 7/10 for me. I enjoyed everything about this game, and honestly my only gripe is the end and how fast things conclude. I felt huge potential for the lore of this game as there were many interesting ideas and concepts, but ended very abruptly. I guess I wanted a book but got a short story, in which in itself is an awesome experience worth 20 dollars.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

I picked it up on a whim after seeing it on the home page, and I have to say that it probably one of the best games I have played this year. It's so hauntingly beautiful, from the art to music the and sound design perspective. The game is dripping with atmosphere and I cannot recommend it enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: Disappointed to not care for this one. Might be worth a try if you like the melancholy vibe, but it's otherwise a pretty middle-of-the-road Metroidvania that struggles to really define itself.There's nothing fundamentally  here, aside from some boring map & enemy design that puts it a few steps behind its peers.  that's enough for me to give a thumbs up to an indie. But it's also just... not weird enough? This didn't swing for the fences and make some missteps, it just kinda riffed on Dark Souls (including bringing over a few things that didn't work well there either, but  don't work here) with an underdeveloped Metroidvania as its framework.For close to a decade, I've been forgetting that I'd kickstarted this game only to be pleasantly surprised by a developer update about it. Now, having played it, I think I'm just going to forget it again, and that may be the saddest possible outcome.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: Is it everything I hoped for after kickstarting it nearly a decade ago and hyping it up with every small snippet of video released for years on end? Of course, not. It was made by one guy basically, how could it be? But it's a really good experience marred by some glaring flaws and an underwhelming ending. But I enjoyed it more than 90% of the metroids and dark souls out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: What a game. I finished it a few days ago and my head is still buzzing. Mechanics are good and enjoyable, but the real standout is the art, music, and story. Be sure to engage in all of the dialogue options you can. It's so incredibly well written and heartfelt. Also nice to have a break from the decision based stories that are becoming more popular. Not that a decision-dependent story isn't fun, it's just a nice change of pace every now and then to just play a game without worrying about how each action I take will hide or reveal certain endings. Just play the game and experience the world and story. Loved it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start with the cons because I'm currently tilted my 'souls' were locked behind a boss fight i took a wrong turn into and I couldn't recover them without having to stop what I was doing. -Your corpse must be recovered, ala Soulslike. Potential for tension but also frustration. Have to worry about stuff like, " If i save and take a break will my body still be there?" +-Good amount of backtracking. _childDocuments_.review: Ethereal, melancholy, searching... fighting to survive, if you are in some sense alive. And looking for something beyond just survival. It's a peculiar existence in Ghost Song, but that's okay. The experience is unique enough to be worth the occasional stubbed toe on rough edges of game design or difficulty smoothing.The narrative is fairly fleshy, especially for a soulsy game. And this is a souls-like, without a doubt - a 2D platforming metroidvania one, but with the same spirit of evasion, maneuvering, timing and tactics to determine whether combat will go well... or result in a hike back from the nearest save spot. Expect to die a lot, and remember to learn something every time if you can - this should help you through.You have a basic ranged attack from your blaster gun, and with sustained fire your gun will overheat and fire slower until it cools. But in a neat twist of game design, this grants you a damage bonus if you whack enemies in melee combat while your gun heat is high, so one series of attacks flows smoothly into the next. This isn't always easy to pull off, but it provides opportunities for satisfying, skilful combat - the heart and soul of the souls genre.It's a shame there's only partial voice acting. What there is, however, is well done and helps pull you into the world, its characters and their struggles. The sound and music are good. The visuals are strange, varied and interesting, as well as quite beautiful.Some areas feel fairly empty, which I read as a sign of good pacing, atmosphere, even realism - not  needs to be full of belligerent creatures, after all - and not all creatures in the game are belligerent. It makes the world feel more like a world, yes?All in all, I'd recommend this game to fans of the metroidvania soulslike genre blend, who enjoyed games such as Salt & Sanctuary (or its sequel), Ender Lilies, or that Vigil thing. As a caution, the game could arguably be more polished. At the same time, though, its heart is in the right place, it has a good amount of action and exploration of a strange alien world through the eyes of a mysterious being... so yes.Heartily recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: I was a backer for Ghost Song years ago and ultimately I enjoyed the game. The game does have its fair share of real flaws though, namely that Dark Souls was the worst thing to happen to indie Metroidvanias because they made indie devs think tedious ass mechanics like loads of backtracking and getting you into a penalty loop for dying in your attempts to get better were good game design. Regardless, I liked the game in spite of this and it also really helps that if you play Explorer Mode most of the mechanics that punish you for dying are cut. I’d seriously suggest playing Explorer right now too because the game needs a couple of balance patches when it come to a couple stuff like some boss hitboxes and better placement of warp zones, I can see how parts of the game could potentially be a major pain in the ass on Normal Mode. For the positives Ghost Song nails what I think is one of the most important things to get right in Metroidvanias, it rewards exploration. There are very few areas of the map that don’t reward you in some noticeable way, may it be through currency, sub-weapons, equipment modules that give you different benefits, and permanent stat buffs. The game also rewards experimentation too as you can get some real powerful builds if you combine your sub-weapons and modules in certain ways. The game starts off rather slow and clunky but once you start getting more abilities it starts to flow better. One real cool thing is that the game is pretty open-ended in you how you collect ship parts which are required to get to endgame. There’s a bit of an annoying mechanic where you have to make the whole journey back to the ship to return the parts though. Ironically, the first part the game tells you get to is the hardest due to the walk back being weirdly kind of brutal and long compared to pretty much every other one which are much shorter and are less of a hassle. I would actually recommend not picking that one up until later because you can unlock the other movement abilities first. Combat gets better as the game goes along and you get more sub-weapons and modules. The focus on switching between your gun and its sub-weapons and the melee weapons you pick up is a neat one and gives you some freedom in how you approach combat.The level design is mostly okay though it has few standout areas compared to others in the genre like Bloodstained and Hollow Knight. The music is also just kind of there. The writing is decent with your interactions of the survivors of a stranded ship, though the ending is just kind of a nothing anti-climax. The game looks pretty good though and nicely atmospheric.Still as I said overall despite its flaws I had a fun time with Ghost Song and it did fill some of that Metroid shaped-hole in my heart because I was really disappointed by Dread. Worth checking out.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: Ghost Song isn't a bad game, but it was disappointing. To preface, the devs are very competent with their game ideas, however, I think there are so many ideas that the combination doesn't work. The game is a Metroidvania, but while I initially thought it would be more along the lines of a Metroid-esque game, it's stat-based with respawning enemies when you reach save points.This isn't necessarily a bad thing in itself, but the damage output is so poor, that even with upgrading your gunpower stats, the basic enemies you first see in the game will still at least 3-4 shots. Either the enemies are massive bullet sponges or the weapons are too ineffective. And while I like the idea of the modules allowing for customization, having the long-range enhancement not be a permanent upgrade was a letdown.One thing I will definitely praise is that the melee damage does do damage. This is something that I wanted to see in Metroid Dread. It wasn't enough to just counter attacks, but I wanted to also be able to deal damage. The one drawback to melee attacks in Ghost Song, though, is that because it has no ability to cancel it, you will leave yourself open to attacks until the animation completes, so it's really best to only use on slow enemies.Exploration is encouraged to gain new abilities/modules, but only a handful are really needed to beat the game. However, it can be easy to accidentally walk into enemies that can easily wipe you out in only a few hits.The weakest part of the game was the characters and story. The premise is simple: Wake up unsure of who you are and help some stranded people escape the planet. However, while you can learn who you are in the true ending, how you got to be that way is never explained. And I found most of the characters to be unlikable or be so contrasting to the tone/atmosphere. The only ones who I enjoyed were Matilda (because she took the situation seriously) and Mutt (because of his eccentric nature that fits the tone of the game and whose questline is reminiscent of a Dark Souls character). Mabec's demeanor was understandable due to her situation (also eccentric like Mutt), and while I don't really like how open-ended his story is/how little it relates to the main plot, Saymund was decent enough.I think that if the devs had another go, they could refine their ideas and be more concise with them: have a Metroid-like game or work on the damage output and make a Souls-like game (which the game does have some influence from). But with Ghost Song, there were too many ingredients in the soup to make it exceptional.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: This was a metroidvania I wasn't expecting to enjoy as much as I did. The storytelling is the big selling point for me here. The way in which this game delivers it's lore through such well written dialogue really kept me playing and wanting to learn more. The gameplay is fine, a little easy, but it kept me entertained for the entire playthrough. I'd recommend this game if you find yourself with a little bit of time.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: This game does some things pretty well. The atmosphere is moody and well-defined. The story, once you put the pieces together, hits some good notes. The characters are rich, full of life, and very unique to the world of Ghost Song.With that said, other aspects of the game are very frustrating. The dialogue sometimes drags, with at least 5 sections of dialogue per unique character encounter, dialogue that can't be sped up because of the voice acting. Furthermore, some dialogue is missable if you don't meet the characters at just the right time, so you'll surely need to do multiple playthroughs or check a guide if you want to get all the content.In terms of gameplay, it's passable, but there is much to be desired. The module system, both for weapon modules and standard suit modules, allows various different load-outs. The melee weapons and the game systems that encourage swapping between ranged and melee are a nice touch. Unfortunately, combat itself feels like a slog. Many bosses, and even just basic enemies, feel like bullet sponges. I found myself making mistakes, not because the bosses were especially difficult, but more because the fights dragged on for so long that I would zone out and lose focus. Outside of some basic dodging and jumping, the bosses don't require much in the way of acrobatics, and there's also a sad lack of gimmicks and weak points. I never really had an "A-ha" moment when fighting a boss.Overall, while I did somewhat enjoy the game, I think I am biased toward the Metroidvania genre itself. If you've already played some of the titans of the genre and want more, give this a try. Otherwise, you won't be missing much.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this somber little adventure, and am glad it finally came out and as well as it did. This was the oldest game in my wishlist.This is a metroidvania with souls-like elements in an alien world with beautiful artwork and music. Gameplay wise there are some annoyances, some enemy encounters can be akward without any sort of soft lockon for shooting. Some save points are pretty far from the bosses and the map could have used at least a couple more teleport points. Otherwise it was quite fun, the upgrades feel meaningful. There are some cool modules/weapons you can get and either go gun or melee route, or a bit of both which the main combat mechanic of your gun heating up charges up your melee incentivizes.The highlight for me however was the cast of characters and getting pieces of the interesting story/backstory from them. You'll find them around the map and after certain events have been met and it pulled me into the experience more than just the gameplay ever could. I do think some bits at the end could have been handled a bit different, there is a pretty big lore point thats hidden behind a not very intuitive action. But overall was good. And I like the main characters little comments on some things she sees in the world, dialogue overall juggles "down to (not-so) earth", "dreamlike", and "cryptic". Its a contemplative experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm about to tear into this game something fierce. It doesn't matter how good you think your writing is, hire an editor, hire some QA people. It's alright fun, but I'm left groaning at the end.I'll start with the positives, though. The gameplay is fine. Being 2D, a common problem is enemies just flipping without any frames to attack, and this is not one of those instances. There's an okay variety to how you end up building your Deadsuit. But there is also only objectively one good way to progress through levels. This is where the positives end.Continuing from gameplay, if you don't focus most of your levels into GunPower, you quickly feel the burn of spongey enemies. As you progress through the story, enemies also all level up, too. If you aren't careful, you might be shooting some electric sponges for far too long and leveling is becoming tedious. Thankfully, I changed courses very fast early on. I can see how some people could also fall into that trap... It would be okay if you could respec and learn the error of your ways, but if you invested even two hours, you might not wanna restart.Contact damage is an archaic idea, and while it wasn't an issue for most of the game, there was one boss in particular, Ogre, that made it particularly frustrating. Even if you were to have contact damage, having the damage be the same amount as a full attack is just egregious. It can make some fights feel completely unfair. I'm in power armor, why isn't a BUG being hurt?Fast Travel feels like a late addition, and one added in reluctantly. There are story points where you can't use fast travel, and that's fine. But when you CAN use fast travel, there are so few points available on the map that you'll end up running a quarter of the map any time you need to get anywhere. And if you need to backtrack for something, that becomes a bit more tedious...Fast Travel seems like it could have been an easy fix, so why wasn't it? Well, that's because of Dark Souls style NPC quests. Souls generally has NPCs in your path that you need to go to to continue their quests. Not Ghost Song. In fact, there's two times you need to revisit one specific room that is in the starting area that you will enter one more time for sure, but a second time is really pushing it unless you're just... wandering for no reason. And these places are random as ♥♥♥♥, too. There's even an entirely out of the way room that I ran into on a whim while just re-exploring because of this that I would have never entered if I just was focusing on what paths I missed or loot I missed.Speaking of paths, some hidden walls are too hidden. At the start, there's some hinting with little plants here and there, or you walk on something and it shakes... That's dropped almost completely later on. In fact, one of the only extra charges for healing is under a floor that doesn't shake and blends PERFECTLY into the rest of the floor. Am I expected to just run around shooting every wall and floor?The indistinguishability also comes from the fact so much of the world is just flat blobs, uninteresting landscape. I'm gonna shamelessly compare this to Hollow Knight and Super Metroid and just say treat every room like you would an actual room and decorate it to have some purpose, not slag filled hallway with more slag.The writing.In the fourth stage, I just started mashing through some of the dialogue with the crew. "Bloat" does not begin to describe it. So the characters all love talking. At length. Conversations are mostly one sided, driven by Deadsuit being generally curious. And they go on and on and on about whatever's plaguing them. Imagine scrolling through a white girl's twitter feed. I can understand their problems, but the lengths to which it's hammered in.Not only that, but dialogue will flip between text and voice. Text you can mash past at least, but once voice starts, then you have to listen through it all, even if it's dull, all in favor of completionism, but what a chore. And what is with the ship characters? So much of Gamber's dialogue comes off like a failed liberal arts degree's best attempt at being whimsical. And why is a ship even talking like that?And like I mentioned before, quests are all over the place. Make sure you catch everyone as their next location every time.Finally, the actual plot: The entire premise of what's going on is laid out to the character after a point. Some flowery dialogue is added but otherwise 'this is exactly why all this is happening'. There isn't room for any kind of interpretation, there is just something in the sun and also there's forces above sun worm gods that can just set bounties and send bug dudes. So the most bizarre things are just explained outright to you.But the most frustrating is the inconsistency. Deadsuit is consistently shown as curious, helpful, inquisitive... But knows nothing about herself. And when presented, time and time again with opportunities to do so, refuses to look inward. Why is this the one thing someone so curious is not at all curious about? One boss even yells 'deadsuits aren't real' at one point even though you ARE one and what the ♥♥♥♥ a deadsuit even is is never explained at all.And to top it off, spoilers mind you,  but that only ends up creating more questions, like why  Nothing satisfying ever comes from the mystery of the Deadsuit and is entirely unexplained, while the entire premise of the world is in turn, which could have been more interesting. But it's just *thrown* at you.Skip all the dialogue, you'll have a better experience. I'm not exaggerating. Do buy it on sale, level up GunPower primarily, and if you want completionism, there's a 100% map for all the quest markers and other stuff if you need.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: Dont understand the hype for this ... the art and music and atmosphere are all well done but the core gameplay mechanics of exploration and combat are so bad, and it ends in a crappy "what?"-style anti-climax that just craps all over your character.There is so much forced backtracking with poorly placed fast travel. Most of your combat will be spent dashing in hyper-armor waiting for your guns to come off cooldown. The map is designed in a way as to not show what is in the rooms, even though you need to know how to get to each room's exits separately. There are missable quests because you are just supposed to revisit every single room on the map after random parts of the "main quest" to advance them. Skipped some dialogue? too bad.This game needed another pass and it's rather short for a metroidvania. It's an absolute shame because the art, music and atmosphere are so good, but what is the point when half the rooms are empty and you spend your time playing fetch ? There's a sprint mechanic that doesn't do anything because your dash is faster, and the sprint even wastes stamina.Dust or Bloodstained get it right, this game doesn't.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: The art direction and atmosphere are great.Controls and handling are fine. Though some of the hit-boxes were a bit wonky.Cons:The game's balance is very out of wack. Normal mobs are very tanky and boss kills take a long time. Your damage doesn't even scale as you progress through the game and most equipment you get are worthless other than the mandatory ones you need to progress the story.This game forces you to back track a ton for every little thing and side quest in a very Dark Souls NPC-like fashion to progress questlines. It's very easy to forget or even miss quests entirely because of this. And even disables fast travels constantly to progress the main story to the point it's extremely annoying.The experience gain is abysmal and hard to farm.----While Ghost Song is fine as a game by itself it pales in comparison with other, far better, Metroidvanias in the genre.In other words, get it while on sale. Otherwise, look at other games in the genre for your metroidvania fix.

_childDocuments_.review: This is like a minimum viable product as far as metroidvania's go for me.  There was a LOT I didn't enjoy about this game and yet it managed to keep me long enough to see credits.  I don't recommend the game.  Its combat is dull.  It has a ton of backtracking that's not compelling.  Bosses aren't fun.  Your character doesn't control great.  The story has some okay moments but wasn't the draw.  Almost nothing about this game worked for me.  Yet something about the exploration was just enough to keep me playing.  I never looked forward to playing more...but it was a suitable time sink.  4.5/10.  I'm a big fan of modern metroidvania's and of the 15 or so I've played this is at the bottom of the ones I was willing to finish.  I'm actually surprised it was so positively received. Glad others could enjoy it more than I did.

After so much wait I got it as a gift from a friend and... well... IT'S AMAZING.The combat is sublime and satisfying, the art is unique and very pleasing to see, the music is amazing. _childDocuments_.review: Ghost Song is probably one of my favorite games of 2022There's a very certain kind of melancholy that envelopes the setting that made the experience generally relaxing for me. This game is one of the few games where the soundtrack really sells the experience tenfold, so I really recommend playing in a quiet environment.The voice acting is great; as is the writing for the characters. By the end of the journey everyone feels like an old friend, and I was rather sad to have to let go. I found the main character extremely endearing as well. Combat is good. I don't think the bosses or enemies have any particularly rough patterns, and I beat most of them on my first try except for maybe two of them. This game doesn't set out to be an extremely hard experience. It's easier than most Metroid games. The exploration is a pretty standard affair as well. Mechanically everything is very competent. I was not expecting the story to hold onto me as much as it did, though. I recommend for anyone looking to pick this game up to be sure to wander and speak to all of the NPCs, let the dialogue run, and absorb yourself into the atmosphere a bit. I took a little longer to go through everything, but it's more than worth the asking price.I hope in the future we maybe get a bit of expanded lore for the setting because there were a few things that I felt weren't explained as well as I would have liked, but maybe I just missed the explanations as well.

_childDocuments_.review: It is beautiful game with beautiful peaceful music and has great potential but this beautiful world is too empty. Not many enemies, also you need to fight like 2 bosses? Rest of them are optional. Way too short and map too small, especially being so empty. The emptiness made this game very atmospheric tho, you will often watch backgrounds or talk with NPCs with pleasure.Leveling system, abilities and weapons, healing are cool ideas taken from best metroidvanias.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games for which I wish there was a more complex system of rating than yes or no.I can't say I didn't enjoy playing it or that it's a bad game but there is this lack of sense of progression, of leveling up. You just have to shoot and shoot and shoot from your underpowered gun and the enemies are getting more and more bullet-sponge. The bosses are also uninteresting, just big enemies with huge hitboxes, tremendous attacks that can kill you in one hit and a lot of life. I would have liked some weak spots or something else to snatch you from the same shooting experience. The fact that you have to be immobile to aim makes these fights harder just for the sake of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very beautiful, voice acting is nice, game play mechanics feel fluid, and pretty easy to understand plot. You can tell the developers really put a lot of effort into this game and it reflects that. It kept me on my toes and I wanted to finish playing it to know how it ends. Blue (the MC) is a very sweet character and I enjoyed playing as her in the game from a personal aspect. I would say the main thing that kept me glued to the screen is 'the want' to know what happens next. What new ability will I get. What new weapons will I get. The typical feelings you get when playing a metroidvania and the game definitely hit that itch for me. The combat was definitely interesting to experience. You can shoot your blaster continuously, but if you do it overheats and slows it's rate of fire down. It overheats which decreases your blaster's strength, but it increases the strength of your melee ability so it was fun to adapt and switch between melee and blaster. The balance between those two was appreciated and you never felt as if one attack was more overpowered than the other. Overall, I really enjoyed this game. There were some areas that could be improved of course, but nothing really made me not enjoy it. Ghost Song is basically a giant fetch quest game, but it was fun to get them. I'd say if you like Metroidvania's with a hint of story then you'll like this one. TLDR; 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: To justify my short play time - I've already beaten this game through Game Pass, I just repurchased it on Steam to have it permanently.This is easily one of my favourite games of 2022, in part because it has clear strengths, but no obvious weaknesses to distract you from what the game does best.The visuals in this game are gorgeous - it feels like playing through a concept art book. I'm sure that many have seen beautiful key art pieces and wished they could play through something like that, but the reality is that technical limitations and gameplay restrictions often forbid such a practice. Here, however, the artist, programmer and the game designer got along swimmingly. It probably helped that they're the same person. The game is beautiful, but it never feels like a compromise - the gameplay never suffers just to show you something cool, or vice versa,Speaking of gameplay, it is very good. It's not something that feels extremely tight, making me wanna replay the game over and over. But it definitely deserves a better grade than 'fine'. Controlling Deadsuit feels good from the start, becoming increasingly fun as you collect more upgrades. The idea of synergizing melee with ranged combat is a really smart one (as your gun overheats, melee gets stronger), so fights stay dynamic for a long time. Admittedly, melee loses value as you progress, but other mechanics come in to fill in the gap. The balance also might've changed in a patch at some point, I've played at release. The enemies are tanky, but to me, it never felt like a tedium to fight them.This game is a classic metroidvania in terms of map structure, wherein you gather upgrades while exploring, which then allow you to explore maps, or backtrack to the previous maps to get upgrades. You can also teleport to a small number of locations, but the game isn't too generous with that, so get ready to walk.Backtracking through visited maps doesn't feel too dull though - the game doesn't tend to have any rooms designed to annoy you (think Castlevania and the rooms with flying medusa heads). What's more, enemies drop 'nanogel', which can be used to upgrade your character, soulslike-style. And similar to a Souls game, you drop your nanogel when you die and you have to pick it back up.Music in this game surprised me - I had certain expectations going into a sci-fi Metroidvania game, but they were subverted in a pleasant way. OST is comprised of mostly chill and ambient-like music, which feels kinda analogue (idk how to better describe it). It's a joy to listen to in-game, as the music perfectly sets the tone of the game and accentuates what's going on. Outside of the game, it sounds just as good, and the OST often plays while I do work.I'm afraid to speak on the story, because after two years, I don't remember much. I only recall that I enjoyed it. The main story is focused on helping a crew fix their crashed ship and escape the moon. There is also a sub-plot going on, where you can learn more about the backstory of the place, and the conflict which devastated it.I'd absolutely recommend that you give this game a shot when it's on sale. If you're looking to scratch a metroidvania itch, with fantastic visuals and music, that isn't afraid to slow down sometimes and smell the flowers, this could be it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: I had a wonderful time playing Ghost Song. I feel like this metroidvania is wildly underrated. I recommend it to anyone interested. It is one of the best metroidvanias I have played since Hollow Knight. I really mean that. The story is really interesting, the worlds are gorgeous, the shooting mechanics are really fun, and the leveling-up system is awesome. That's not to mention the amazing music, animations, and effects. It is such a beautiful, atmospheric game that has entered my favorites list. I like how it is a game you can just get lost in. It felt so rewarding to just discover whatever I wanted to whenever I wanted to. My favorite aspect of this game was the exploration, the world felt so rich and full of life despite the setting being a dying world. The world tells a story without being heavy-handed. Also, the story of Ghost Song is both thought-provoking and melancholy, without being depressing or nihilistic. Stories that strike that balance are very impressive. I specifically found a new appreciation for the characters during a second playthrough. They are well-developed in a way that makes them all memorable and recognizable. While the names may be difficult to assign to each character, each character will feel distinct by the time you finish the game. The dialogue between the main character and the NPCs all felt very natural. All of the characters feel like they have rich lives that happened before meeting the main character and that they will continue to after the story.  On a second playthrough, I was able to spend more time with characters that I hadn't gotten to know very well which was very rewarding. I will mention some critiques I have of the game. While I love this game, I felt it was much more fun for me on a second playthrough with New Game+. Having more modules up front makes the combat more fun and less of a grind. Which was nice because I personally really liked the feel and mechanics of the combat, but felt it was held back by specifically the overheating mechanic and a lack of variety, both of which were nullified in New Game+. I also felt that the final battle and the ending were a little anticlimactic to me. The final battle was disappointing in comparison to, say, the old singer battle or the Henrietta the changed battles towards the middle of the game. I understand why the creators took that route, as there is a theme on the importance of reasoning with people who pose no threat to you. However, a more climactic final battle does not detract from that theme. The character you are supposed to reason with takes place after the boss, so why not make the boss more difficult and have more variety with the battle phases?  I don't know, the fact that I had more difficulty with weaker/secret bosses and finding collectibles is saying something.  The ending of the entire game is very abrupt.  No spoilers, but I wish they spent a little more time to let certain moments linger at the end. While I was able to get answers for a good chunk of my questions on a second playthrough, I wish the information I wanted was not such a grind to find. If you don't run into certain characters during specific points and exhaust their dialogue multiple times by the end of the game, you miss a lot of essential information to finish the plot. You need to grind for certain abilities to get essential plot info as well. Secrets are a lot of fun to find in games, and I enjoyed finding the ones I did! However, I personally feel that they should be the icing on the cake that rewards a dedicated player, not what ties the story together. There are a lot of loose threads to the story that are unresolved if you don't try to do a completionist route. I wish that specific intrigue on the deadsuit's origin was explored more and was more readily accessible to a casual player, as it would make the story feel more complete upfront. As is, it sometimes feels like the game was forcing me to chose between finding about the deadsuit's origin or exploring the world. That was frustrating because I wanted to explore the world because of its richness and beauty.At the end of the day though, these flaws were very minor. This game felt very special to me in multiple ways. I think it is a wonderful game and a very impressive first outing by a very talented developer. It deserves more love. It deserves more attention. It is a sci-fi game that I had an excellent time with and I wish there were more games like it. I have played a lot of platformers, but this one was very unique. From the combat to the art to the level design, this game felt different in a special way. I found a new appreciation for platformers again, as it reinvented the wheel while staying true to why those games are great. It is definitely in my top 10, so please, check it out if you have the time/money. To the developers: Thank you! :D

_childDocuments_.review: I really had high hopes for this one, and it starts out great, but after a while it just starts falling apart. The excessive backtracking is fine, because you can level up with the resources from beating the same enemies over and over again, but at one point every boss just take a thousand shots, and it feels like they were just using everything they could find to get 10 to 12 hours out of the game.  There are long stretches that there isn't even anything there and it's the only way to the major hub. The fast travel points need to be doubled, because none of them are anywhere near where  you need to go. Finally, at a point there's a boss that you need to avoid long enough to sneak past like 4 times, and that ended up being the final nail in the coffin. _childDocuments_.review: There'a a lot to love here - the art style, the story, and the soundtrack are all amazing. However, the game is severely hampered by questionable game design choices. - The runs between save rooms are punishing, even by souls-like standards.- The maximum health reduction on death is, likewise, baffling. Why would you punish a player for dying, making their next attempt even harder?- Disabling fast-travel after each boss is blatant padding, and adds nothing but tedium and frustration to the game. - Fast travel being limited to so few locations serves as additional padding, forcing long, repetitive runs through the same areas. A simple tweak of allowing fast travel between all save points would do the game wonders.With a few more months in the oven and proper balancing, this could have been an amazing addition to the Metroidvania genre, but as of right now I sadly can't recommend this title.

_childDocuments_.review: I will start this review by stating that I am a veteran Metroid player.I quite enjoyed the game for what it was. I did not need to look for any guides in order to find my way around, or figure things out on my own. The controls of the game play pretty much like a Metroid, with a twist: The dash button is used to avoid attacks, as well as traversing. The game does not allow you to turn on all the features and weapons at your disposal, making you choose which ones to to have active at any given time. The game has a roguelike mechanic where if you are defeated then you lose all your currency, and receive a semi permanent debuff to your total health, but that can be repaired at a very low cost. In terms of difficulty, I only found myself losing about once or twice to the most difficult bosses, but most I could defeat with ease. Which is not to say the game is easy for a beginner. The game has an ample variety of enemies and boss attack patterns to keep you on your toes.I will not spoil any of the story. I will simply say that there is a lot of melancholy in the world of Ghost Song. It was a lovely, atmospheric time, and you can tell the developer poured his soul into it.Strongly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I initially heard about this project years ago, and I had been sort of following it's development in the background ever since then. When I heard it had gone through some setbacks and a reboot, I was initially a bit concerned about it, but as soon as I was able to hop in and play it, I knew it was something special. Everything about it went well beyond my expectations, and I feel like it should be getting way more recognition.The game world itself is very eerie, moody, and desolate, and I love the atmosphere that has been built through the environment art, audio design, and fantastic soundtrack. It strikes an excellent balance between something like Hollow Knight and Super Metroid. The overall art direction is great as well, and I really liked all of the different character designs.The overall narrative unfurls in an interesting way, keeping things fairly cryptic and mysterious early on, while revealing bits of lore through NPCs you find throughout the map. The mysterious nature of the main character had me guessing throughout the whole game, and kept me playing just to find out more details about her. The game also tackles some interesting themes of , which was really cool. I appreciated that the game had some really interesting side stories to engage with as well outside of the main narrative. The voice acting in the game was also very good and a nice surprise!The gameplay itself is also really solid, with a lot of different weapons and effects to play with in different combinations. Combat uses 3 different resources that deplete and regenerate based on which weapon you're using, which helps to encourage you to swap between different strategies in the middle of fights, keeping things fresh. There are some nice secrets to find as well, helping to encourage exploration. I also appreciate that the main objectives can mostly be tackled in any order, although some of them are fairly difficult to try and achieve early on in the game.The game also has a good sense of when to let the player just take in the world. Some metroidvanias like this tend to just shove enemies in your face all the time, but there are some sections of this game that just let you explore and take in the surrounding world. I think it's important for games to take moments like that and let the art and sound breath for a bit.The world itself also feels fairly dynamic, where certain bosses and enemies would appear based on your current step in the story. One boss that appeared caught me entirely off guard, and it was a really neat moment in an area that I had otherwise been mindlessly traversing through. Another boss , which was incredibly neat to encounter. Some of the bosses in the game are a bit difficult if you're not careful, and I did get frustrated with one or two of them at certain points, but overall they are fun encounters.Overall, this game really fires on all cylinders, and I couldn't put it down once I started it. If you're a fan of this genre, I'd say pick this up ASAP! For $20 it's an excellent experience, and it was probably one of my favorite games of 2022.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr - I really love the atmosphere and storytelling so far, but gameplay makes it hard want to keep trying. Overall it's a beautiful game and I can see why so many enjoy it, even if it's not for me :) (EDIT: ignore this tl;dr because this game is incredible and I would absolutely recommend everyone play it)I was initially drawn to this game by the art style and atmosphere, but unfortunately some key gameplay elements just weren't right for me. I'm still pretty early in the story as far as I know, so it's a good idea to take all this with a grain of salt. Just got the first "major" objectives (not sure if there's more after I complete these). All that being said, a couple problems made it hard for me to want to keep coming back and trying.The most glaring problem for me was just how slow the Ghost Suit moved  almost every boss I came up against. I know the slower, more methodical combat speed is an intentional design choice like Super Metroid, for example. But it felt like it put me at a unfair (and frankly not enjoyable) disadvantage compared to a number of progress-blocking foes.Even if I'd react in time and jump/dodge, somehow I'd still get clipped by the attack, or couldn't recover in time to also dodge an immediate follow-up attack. This early on, that chunks near half or more of my health bar. I know it's supposed to feel like a hostile world and no where is safe, but getting two-shot by a boss without any clear mistakes just feels unbalanced in my opinion. Which makes the next problem all the more painful...Here's where I know it's going to be controversial: I hate boss run backs. Absolutely despise them. Even so, I love Dark Souls 3, Bloodborne and Dark Souls 1. All of these have run backs, but they're fair and, after a couple attempts, rather painless with some exceptions (looking at you Nito lol). I only mention this to say that even with my distaste for run backs, if they're done well enough I can accept it just fine. However, the run backs in this game tend to put unavoidable enemies in the way that chunk your healthbar and ensure the runback itself is long and tedious. It completely removes you from the flow of the fight and makes it even harder to identify and improve upon mistakes, while also frequently putting you at a disadvantage before entering the arena. This is especially confusing given the game The Dark Souls 2 style "shrink the healthbar for every death" mechanic isn't an issue by itself (in fact I love it for tension during exploration), but the fact that there's never a statue near boss arena's where I can recover this health seems like either an oversight, or maybe a little trolling by the dev lol not the worst, but definitely makes death even discouraging.Overall I think this game has a lot of potential, and I'm sure I'll finish it one day. But for now, the frequent appearance of these two issues make it just not fun for me. For those who love the Metroidvania genre, love atmospheric and lonely experiences, want a real challenge and have the time to dedicate to it, this game is probably a dream come true! But if my thoughts and preferences resonate with you, then this may not be something you'd like to dedicate time to.P.S. that title menu song gives me CHILLS. That alone is 10/10!EDIT: I've since played a handful more hours and, while I still do have the criticisms listed above, I have to change my answer and recommend this game to others. The first few hours can be extremely challenging to get through, and some points may be more frustrating than enjoyable. However past that, it's near impossible to put down. A few reason for that are:- Chilling, ambient soundtrack- Satisfying and incredibly rewarding exploration- Charming NPC's, many of which will travel the world like you, add even more depth to the world and storyI won't delete any of my previous feedback as I think it's important for others to make informed decisions, but all I can say is that it's worth it to move past gripes in order to experience a true work of art.

_childDocuments_.review: Been waiting years for this. And has it been worth it?Absolutely and undoubtedly yes.The somber and dreadful atmosphere juxtaposed with the charming personalities of the characters you meet feels so fresh. _childDocuments_.review: Great if somewhat short Metroidvania, much heavier on the Metroid aspect with run & gun sci-fi than on Iga-style RPG elements. Sound and graphics are excellent and absolutely bleed atmosphere. Controls quite well with some novel combat elements where firing your ranged weapon overheats it over time and you can use various melee attacks to both dissipate the heat and deliver heavy blows. I found this an interesting twist but it probably isn't for everyone because it does put a pause on the action and require you to wait out the cooldown, move in close for high risk / reward damage or use alternate means of dealing with the heat.The visuals and story are a weird collision of classic sci-fi eldritch horror mixed in with a hint of spirituality and some philosophic concepts like what defines the self. It's deliberately vague and confusing at times but does mostly make sense despite being a weird premise, but... forewarning, you'll have to get the true ending to really make much sense of it. A casual playthrough is probably going to leave you scratching your head about what just happened if you care more about coherency than action.This is not an especially easy game but does reward precision and practice. Most mid to later bosses are quite hard but still end up feeling reasonably fair and you are expected to make the most of all the abilities you've got. Having said that, there are a handful of bosses that feel really over tuned with either too much RNG in their patterns and one particular very large late-game boss whose hitbox on his swings is way, way too big and even with pixel perfect dodging you still won't be able to evade these attacks and for some reason most of his attacks knock you the wrong way so you'll frequently take double hits. Literally the only way I could beat him was to cheese the fight by doing passive damage and waiting while staying away from him which was really bizarre because everything else felt challenging but reasonable.Overall an excellent offering from a tiny indie dev and there have even been a few spaced out updates since launch with extra (free) content added, including fleshing out some initially sparse NPC interactions and some optional bosses.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Ghost Song is a pretty typical Metroidvania experience. If you're looking for something to scratch your Metroidvania itch, this will certainly do that. It wasn't innovative or anything. It's a good Metroidvania, and that's that. For the most part, I found it decently balanced and not as frustrating as some others I've played recently.The one complaint that jumps out to me is that the save points are pretty stingy. They're often pretty far from arena-style challenge rooms and boss fights, which makes tracking back to the point you fell unnecessarily annoying. The game features a kind of Hollow Knight-ish penalty for dying where you drop all your money where you fell. To get your money back, you track back to where you fell to pick it up. Money is needed for upgrades and equipment, which would make the battles easier. Each death also causes a semi-permanent health cap loss which you need to pay money to repair. The statues that do the upgrades and repairs -- which are incidentally also the fast-travel points -- are usually found with save points but even less commonly and usually farther from boss rooms. This creates a bit of a stilted gameplay dynamic: you either track a significant distance with lower HP back to the boss fight and attempt it with increasingly reduced health until you manage to both pick up your money and survive the fight so you can repair the damage and buy upgrades; or you forgo the dropped money and go grind out new money to repair the damage somewhere else entirely. I don't dislike the basic concept. I just found that the access to the resources stretched things out into relatively boring grinds. That said, there is a lower difficulty that I think turns off that penalty. In any case, I obviously didn't find the game unplayable or even super frustrating. I needed to adapt my playstyle more and make regular stops to buy my upgrades. Again, that would require longer travel times, but that's not a fatal flaw. I wouldn't see the difficulty as being degraded by having more statues and therefore more opportunities to buy upgrades and fast-travel. Maybe fast travel would have a monetary cost and only a few super-statues or something could do the repairs, so that would preserve some of the challenge level as it is now without as much of the grind padding.Nevertheless, the game was basically fun. It certainly gave me something entertaining to do for hours at a time while I'm stuck at home off work with COVID, so if you're looking for a solid Metroidvania, I would recommend this.

_childDocuments_.review: We’re definitely not short of stellar metroidvanias on Steam.  Bloodstained, Blashpemous, Ori, Infernax, Castlevania advance collection, Axiom Verge… however, Ghost Song is a very special title that you should make time for if this genre is your jamYou could be very crude and write this off as a Metroid clone, and to be fair, Ghost song takes a bucketload of inspiration from Samus.  However, Ghost song also pulls quite liberally from Bloodborne/Dark Souls, with an interesting shooting/melee combat loop and a lot of focus on NPC dialogues and side quests that really sets it apart from Nintendo’s classic.I was honestly astonished to learn the Ghost Song was mainly a solo developed work.  The whole thing is just bursting with a staggering amount of detail, creativity, colours and vibrance.  The way that the outside scenery bobs and ebbs in the wind.  The way that little trails of smoke follow the character.  The excellent (and at times downright creepy) sound effects and atmospheric sound design.  The exquisite enemy designs and animations. The staggering use of colour and shading.  The evocative soundtrack. It’s all just dripping with such a wonderful attention to detail, making almost every moment a joy for me to play.Ghost Song is not, however perfect.  While I generally enjoyed combat (dear me that giant robot gauntlet is fun) I did find that certain bosses and elite enemies became quite a chore due to their extreme sponginess. Second, there’s perhaps a bit too much backtracking, with fast travel points being a bit too few and far between for my liking.  Finally SPOILERS the conclusion of the story felt quite underwhelming and didn’t really deliver on what it seemed to be leading up to.  There may alternative endings that I didn’t find though…All in all, though, Ghost Song was an absolute blast to play and really struck me as one of the best looking and best sounding 2D games I’ve played in a while, and can easily recommend this to fans of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm still just getting started, of course, but so far this is a pretty striking game. It's clearly something of a love-letter to the early Metroid games and does a good job of evoking that specific sense of lonely alien exploration while still very much being its own thing.The setting is the high point here. It's absolutely striking and if you, like me, found the greatest pleasure of old Metroid games was just exploring and seeing the sights of the alien world then I don't think you'll be disappointed here. The whole thing oozes a dreamlike quality which I greatly enjoy.The combat system is pretty basic, but still reasonably interesting. In some regards it's a complete improvement over the old metroid formula. I think the enemies are too sluggish, though in groups they can be overwhelming at times, and I think the melee attack could be a little more quick and snappy, but it's still quite good. Overall there's a nice flow and sense of strategy to combat.In the end Super Metroid still holds the champion belt for this sort of game, but Ghost Song is an exciting new entry in this genre. Well worth it, in my opinion. I'm excited to see where this setting takes me.

_childDocuments_.review: I remember in 2013 when this game was first revealed and the kick starter went live. It was around a time Metroid fans were starved of quality 2D Metroid games. So when I found this game, needless to say I was excited. I followed it for as long as I could before it became lost on me and I had forgotten about it. Much to my surprise 9 years later the game would finally see a release. So did it live up to my excitement and expectations after all this time? Well... kinda.The good. The game does a good job with atmosphere and the feeling of being lost in a strange world. NPCs are present but few and far between. The characters you meet are voiced just enough to give them a larger sense of personality and I think that worked well for me to get more immersed in the game and it's characters. The gameplay is mostly snappy and responsive. The exosuit for the most part does exactly what I ask it, and responds *nearly* perfectly to my inputs. There are however a few moments that a quick snap of the analog stick after a dash or wall jump would result in the exosuit not changing directions for a second.  If I were to do a quick motion of jumping off a wall to the right, then immediately snapping the stick to the left and pressing dash, it would result in the exosuit just dashing to the right again. It's a small gripe and so far this is the only thing I can think of that hindered my gameplay with the exosuit. The boss fights were challenging and engaging. I had a great time hunting down the bosses, and there are a handful of bosses that I haven't encountered as some boss fights require a specific quest or prerequisite to be done before encountering them. I really enjoy that even after finishing the game there is still more that I missed and more bosses and loot to hunt down. Finally my biggest praise for this game is the sheer amount of freedom and sequence breaking you are allotted. You can go wherever you like and do whatever you like. I played through 90% of the game before I realized there was a  upgrade that I was supposed to have found right after , but instead I went completely out of order and found the  upgrade instead. I never even needed the  at all. The freedom to explore and find my own path was integral to my enjoyment of this game and I'm very happy it has that freedom. The bad. After all this time waiting for this game I wish there were only good things to say about it, but sadly there are several things that bothered me. Firstly some of the voice acting is just not that great and that's jarring since other characters are voiced quite well and sound completely normal. The enemies in this game are generally not fun to fight whatsoever. They are bullet sponges that take so much time and energy to kill that I can't think of a single enemy in the game I liked fighting. I enjoyed most of the bosses in this game, however some of the bosses are just amplified versions of regular enemies that you have to fight in a room filled with the enemy they're based on. For instance, during , you could jump and just be just outside of the arch of it's swing at you and still be hit by nothing you can visually see. During the game's most challenging events, it feels frustrating to believe you have dodged an attack only to be hit anyways. Finally the game despite it's difficulty and time spent being developed is very short. I finished my playthrough at 9 hours before starting a new game + file. I've seen some folks less thorough than I finish the game in even less time.At a $20 price point, I believe Ghost Song is worth it's asking price and is sure to have more people enjoy it than not. _childDocuments_.review: Barring one glaring issue, this became one of my favorite Metroidvanias (coming from someone that's been playing these titles since the original NES Metroid and Castlevania). The visuals and sound are enthralling and it was unusual to have a Metroidvania with a decent narrative - both through evolving NPC relationships and environmental storytelling. Just about everything was thoroughly intriguing and I couldn't wait to find out more. As far as action goes, a variety of movement abilities, melee, and ranged weapons kept the minute-to-minute play interesting.Buuuut, the game just ends. No anticipated climax. Only one resolution. Little explanation. Cheap artwork and no meaningful dialog. Not even a hint of a pre/sequel to fill things in. It's like the devs ran out of time or threw up their hands while shouting, "Bored now!" and left the Friday afternoon janitor to draw and write the closing scenes while everyone else went to Vegas. And I say that after nearly 100%-ing the game, using no guides, and getting the "good" ending. I spent 20 hours on a single playthrough, loving nearly every minute of it, and this was the disappointing return. Does that change my recommendation? Absolutely not - but know you'll have fill in a ton of loose story threads on your own.Another thing to note is that unlike me, you may get sick of backtracking. The game has limited fast travel and the primary loop involves fetching parts from the ends of the map and manually returning them to base (usually with new enemies on the way). That's not terrible, but NPC's and minibosses spawn and move around with each part returned. This means to 100% the game in terms of items and story, you're going to have to re-explore the  map six or so times. I personally felt that the carrot-on-the-stick was enticing enough for this activity, but you may not and I wouldn't blame you for it.+Beautiful artwork, decent animation+A lot of nice touches all over the place (I love that water cools your gun)+A number of unique or rare mechanics+Voice acting pretty good+Very relaxing music. Absolutely love it. Available on YT, Bandcamp and Amazon.+Great sound design, attacks and explosions "feel" weighty+Controls are generally responsive+Encourages a mix of ranged and melee combat, tailorable to your preferences+Bosses have multiple phases, often show damage and telegraph pretty fairly+Fascinating lore+A number of genuinely creepy enemies and areas+Many NPC's - friend and foe - have personality+Most secrets have subtle audio or visual clues+Ability cooldowns also have audio and visual clues+Can disable controller vibration+Normal and casual (less death penalty) difficulties+Multiple save slots+New Game++RPG elements and mostly open world, so you can work around tough fights+You can also simply run away from or past many bosses~Some blood, no gore or swearing, very minor statue nudity~Not a lot of documentation of the game available online~Devs seem to have abandoned game?~Unusual number of "empty" hallways with not much of anything to see or do~Save point frequency inconsistent at the start~Could use another one or two fast travel points~A number of enemies require awkward crouching to hit~Screen transitions could be a bit smoother~Mouse cursor occasionally appears on screen~A few enemies can get stuck in walls~A number of permanently missable items and conversations if you're not thorough~Game doesn't hold your hand and expects you to find hidden mechanics and lore~One UI element I never figured out the purpose for~No end-game item/ability for finding secrets you missed?~No completion %'s listed anywhere before or after credits?~You have to re-explore the entire map each phase if you want 100%~I appreciate the purpose of the Curious Gizmo, but I wish the intent was at least hinted at in the description. Wasted a ton of time re-exploring the entire map, hoping to find its use - only to look on the forums later and see that I didn't need it due to earlier exploration.-Unskippable splash screens-One softlock attempting to access  forcing an Alt+F4-Ogre being able to instantly turn around and change his massive hurtbox is cheap-Map markers have a number of bugs that devs haven't fixed for more than a year-So much lore is left unresolved, and not in a good kind of way-The final minutes of the game are an enormous, effortless letdown, even with pre-hinted "good" ending revelationPlayed on:Win11, i7-14700K, RTX4060 Ti 8GB, 32GB DDR5-6000 @ 1920x1080Using PowerA Enhanced Wired Controller for Xbox Series X|SExplorer difficulty

_childDocuments_.review: is a Metroidvania with Souls-like elements. The story follows a newly-awakened Deadsuit who took upon herself to assist the surviving crew of a crashed spaceship. There are no story-related choices (the main character auto-replies in dialogues), though some of the mandatory objectives can be achieved in different order. The story and the dialogues are written well, and the characters are likeable, so the protagonist’s lines are fitting and going along with the objectives comes easy.The combat is functional - the main default weapon is a gun with rather limited range, while the damage decreases the farther the target is. There are other ranged weapons with different attack types and abilities, as well as melee weapons. Also a combat drone. It should be noted that there is contact damage and it hits as hard as a normal attack from the respective foe, which usually makes ranged combat preferable. The main character has few attributes which can be upgraded at the infrequent fast travel points, while the save points are much more plentiful. Additionally, there are modules, which provide quality changes to the protagonist’s abilities, such as healing while attacking in melee, double jumping, or being able to see foes’ health bars. The bosses are diverse, challenging, and have some background story. Most of them have several stages or additional mechanics. A few are the same as the regular enemies, but larger. The main aspect of a Metroidvania is exploration, and the world is interesting and engaging to explore. There are a lot of optional paths and secrets, while the traversal is comfortable. There are very fast travel points, but the map is not too large. Additionally, the locations change slightly as the story progresses, most notably, during the return-to-camp sequences, while new abilities allow to access previously unreachable areas. The visual design is stunningly beautiful and easy to read at the same time. The music is pleasant and does not block foes’ attack cues nor distracts from the game. The dialogues are partially voiced, with the VA being of good quality. The controls are reasonably comfortable and rebindable. No significant bugs have been encountered during the playthough, only a couple visual ones. The only technical flaw I can see is auto-saving in the same slot, which is typical for Souls-likes and can be circumvented by copying the save files with Windows Explorer manually. Overall, highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful atmospheric game with intriguing story lore. I genuinely enjoyed the dialogue (but you can skip past it and not have the extra engagement). Good fun. Combat was challenging and I found myself dying and retrying over and over for some of the bosses (some of which I came back to slightly later). You pick up different modules and different weapons, and based on your level you can choose how many and which ones to equip, and then you can toggle through the equipped weapons during a fight. This enables you to adapt to different enemies, but will also challenge you to approach familiar enemies with different loadouts and adapt accordingly. I don't play metroidvania normally. I bought this game because I played the Swapper and Ghost Song promised me the same vibes. I did find it frustrating having to go back through previously explored areas once I had new abilities unlocked - but most of that frustration may have been because you cannot sprint or dash in the early game. During late game play it was easy to move through the map.I really value how you can play the game your way and your style, because the skill development isn't linear, but cumulative (and you must choose what you have active at any given time).I absolutely wanted more from the game. I approached the final boss fight really hoping it would unlock some new chapter instead of finish the game. I didn't want to begin a New Game + BUT after writing this review I think I will afterall. There's more modules and weapons to find and play around with and the difficulty has already shown itself to be adaptive. Plus there are some resolutions for some characters which I did not find in my first play through.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't write many reviews, but wanted to write on for Ghost Song.I've been following this game since 2016, and I feel like it was worth the wait for sure. The game is absolutely beautiful. The music fits in perfectly to where I always enjoyed it, but it always felt so smooth to be that I barely noticed when it was coming and going. Very seamless, very appropriate, very good. The art is wonderful as well. Each area and scene has so many layers to it that give the world so much more depth, immersion, and distinction. I really loved the combat system, seeing what all sorts of combinations I could use between the melee weapons and various alt blasters. I really enjoyed the gun heat mechanic that forced you to be more strategic in combat and not just rely on a blaster from far away. Finally, I really enjoyed all of the characters and their stories. I loved the writing and the development of the overall story and the stories of the characters. It was really fun to piece it all together.There are certainly some things that couldn't have been done different, but I know the dev team is listening and changing what they can, and its also their first game. I discovered after beating the game that it was easy to miss a number of character interactions, some that are necessary for the full ending and deeper lore. That said, this isn't too unique with most Soulsborne type games, but I think there could have been a bit more guidance. I didn't feel like the game was a huge challenge, but it was so fun to explore, and I'm already excited about my NG+ playthrough.
