_childDocuments_.review: A WiiU Nintendo eShop game from 2015-now a free Steam game. 	Armillo is surprisingly decent for what it is. It has decent length to it; unlockables; 'hidden' levels. A plot with some twists. And the central game mechanic is an interesting blend of monkey ball with some speedier segments and light platforming. People call it a mix of Sonic with Mario Galaxy and Monkey Ball. Which is slightly misleading, but I get where it comes from. The dashing and speedier segments give it the Sonic comparison. It being in Space gets it the Mario Galaxy one.	It's still a game that is slightly rough. Setting up your controls is weird. The dialogue feels a bit rushed at points. The 2D levels are especially awkward to control. 	But despite all of that, it is surprisingly competent. The music is shockingly decent to good. Game itself looks good. Each level has a unique gimmick or new game mechanic. On the surface it looks like a budget game. Even in-game its not exactly a triple A production. But the developers really put in some effort in the areas that matter.	I'd pin this at the 10 dollar range if they were to put a price on it. If they can clean it up a bit, I'd definitely buy a sequel.	I'm not calling this a must-play, but if you do you'll be pretty shocked at how good it actually is.

_childDocuments_.review:
Rolling Platforming Game. Sci-fi parallel Universe theme. Massive amount of gameplay elements.

Armillo is a unique, fun rolling platforming game with a sci-fi parallel universe theme. It features a massive amount of gameplay elements. For one, there is the regular 3D world, followed by a bonus stage on the moon. Then there is the evil parallel universe, and special 2D speed-run inspired worlds. Lots of unexpected deadly twists, and surprises await! The star of the game features a space armadillo named Armillo. He's not your usual armadillo as he's capable of blasting off to space in order to travel from planet to planet. He's joined by his little blue critter friends and his brother. What's supposed to be a peaceful galaxy becomes ruined by the invasion of the robotic Darkbots. Where are they from? Why are they here? But one thing is for sure, they certainly are not the friendly type.

name: Black Mesa
detailed_description: Join Our Community About the Game Relive Half-Life Black Mesa is the fan-made reimagining of Valve Software’s Half-Life . Black Mesa: Definitive Edition Update 1.5 brings together all the improvements to graphics and gameplay across 15 years of development to create the final version of Black Mesa. There has never been a better time to pick up the crowbar and play! Single Player Campaign You are Gordon Freeman, a theoretical physicist at the Black Mesa Research Facility. When a routine experiment goes horribly wrong, you must fight your way through an interdimensional alien invasion, and a bloodthirsty military clean-up crew in order to save the science team... and the world! Features A completely reimagined and refined single player campaign, including all new and expanded Xen levels 19 chapters of fighting through top-secret labs, running atop harsh desert landscapes, sneaking into abandoned railways, and leaping across dimensions Mind-Blowing graphics and effects, never before seen on the Source Engine Face off against an army of classic enemies, updated with new features and engaging AI Wield an arsenal of military hardware, scientific prototypes, and the iconic crowbar through incredibly detailed environments The all-new soundtrack and voice acting create a more immersive experience than ever before 50 Fun and challenging achievements Multiplayer Frag your friends across 10 iconic maps from the Half-Life universe, including: Bounce Gasworks Stalkyard Undertow Crossfire Workshop Create your own mods, models, and maps with the Black Mesa Source SDK, then share it with the community on the Steam Workshop. Steamworks Collect the full set of trading cards, backgrounds, emoticons, and achievements! Featuring Steam Cloud, Steam Workshop, closed captions in multiple languages and full controller support.

_childDocuments_.review: I have pretty mixed feelings about this game.On one hand it is probably the single greatest remaster ever made because unlike *deep breath*Bioshock remastered, Bioshock 2 remastered, Dark Souls remastered, Resident Evil Remastered, Red Faction Gurellia Re-Mars-tered, Skyrim Remastered, and Half Life 2 Update or pretty much any other 'remaster' out there. Black Mesa not only resells me Half Life 1 but actually ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ improves it in away that any player can observe. Going beyond the traditional 'HD" textures that look no different to the original and in which no improvement can be seen without a side by side comparison, Black Mesa adds whole new models, new sound effects, new dialog, and everything. Whole sections of the game have been completely redone while still preserving the original's vision, other sections have been mildly tweaked to make them that much more better. However. This remastering doesn't come without drawbacks. Three of which are very cutting in my mind and almost make me not want to recomend the game.1: Xen hasn't been out and at this point I'll probably be in an old folks home before it does. I do not understand why so much effort is being put into Xen while chapters like Residue Processing remain as terrible as they were in the original.2: Residue Processsing is still a complete maze that I have no idea how to navigate and still need a walkthrough after playing through it three times before. Why this chapter was passed over for an overhaul but Xen has had multiple years of development dedicated to it is a mystery. Other new sequences are a thousand times harder than the original, pretty much any level with Marines as a focused enemy is going to be a lot harder because of the improved AI (♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Surface Tension Dam)3: THE SOUND EFFECTS ARE TOO ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ LOUD AND I THINK I'VE GONE DEAF BECAUSE OF THEM HOW HARD IS IT TO MAKE A SOURCE GAME THAT DOESN'T MAKE MY EARS BLEED!?!?!?!?!?!?!?!?!?!?!?!?Seriously though point 3 is a huge issue as the music and sound effects are so high it actually hurts. Even after adjusting the volume levels in the opitions the sound effects still feel too loud even though they no longer hurt my ears now the volume levels are just annoying with footsteps being as loud as gunshots in any other game and bodies hitting the floor with enough force to be heard from several dozen feet away in the middle of a chaotic battlefieldBut the game also has a lot of improvements, better graphics, better models, some levels have been redesigned and now look and feel a lot better, new achievements finally got added, more awesome easter eggs.I cannot stress how awesome it is to see Half Life given the rebirth it deserves and that a team of people exist who are dedicated enough to bring it into the modern era, though I question their time management and why some parts of the game earn a massive rework while still having the glaring cancerous cyst that is Residue Processesing remain completely unchanged. I do believe this game will be worth your time.I say will because at this rate the game is probably not going to enter a completed state untill sometime around the second coming of Christ. I know that a lot of people complain about "Xen when?" but when your looking at an early access game to buy and all you've got for assurences that it will leave early acess are a list of changed launch dates a mile long, and some nice looking screenshots you tend to start seeing shades of No Man's Sky or Mighty no.9 all over again, and my usuall faith in kickstarter projects, is around the same level as my faith that jaming my thumbs into my eye sockets and tearing my eyeballs out then tying my optic nevers around my penis while I masturbate into a blender will be a painless processes.In short I can't recomend this game in its current state as it is simply incomplete and I have serious doubts that it ever will be completed. Even if the Crowbar Collective does manage to complete it I'm still going to hold the amount of time it took agaisnt them, and it won't change the fact that I feel their time could have been better alocated to improving some of the earlier chapters.Edit: Not really counting this because this could just be me being a dumbass but, how did they manage to make Half Life's akward ladders even harder to dismount? I mean sure they used to have even odds of you flinging yourself to your death whenever you tried to get off so I'm glad that doesn't happen but I can't be alone in experiencing a slight hanging up whenever I try to get off a ladder

_childDocuments_.review: A love-letter to one of the greatest shooters of all time. Black Mesa does not seek to reinvent the original, rather it stays true to its core brilliance of gameplay, atmosphere, and storytelling but with a visual upgrade. The biggest difference to this, however, is Xen. Black Mesa takes the weakest area of the original and turns it around on its head. Where Xen was once bland, rushed, and out of place before, it is now beautiful, expansive, and an absolute labour of love.With that said, Black Mesa does not replace Half-Life. It compliments, revitalizes, and celebrates the original. It offers a new-old experience for veterans of the series. But is it ?? No, I don't think it is. Despite it's faithfulness to the original, much of it feels like an imitation or perhaps, counterfeit. Every footstep, every gunshot, every swing of the crowbar - a mere counterfeit. A fantastic counterfeit, a beautiful counterfeit, a much-needed godsend of a counterfeit in the face of Valve's enduring silence and seeming abandonment of the franchise, but a counterfeit nonetheless.10/10 would play counterfeit Half-Life again.

_childDocuments_.review: Remember back in 1998 when you first tried a new game called "Half-Life"? I do. As a kid, I remember where I was, who I was with, the circumstances of me trying it, and the eventual purchasing of it as the first PC game I ever received. I remember the smell of the box, the look of the old console menu, and the sounds that the menu buttons made when you clicked on them. I remember the events surrounding every moment that I witnessed this game being played, or played it myself. I remember the countless hours talking about it with friends, showing it to them at home, and even being fearfully reluctant to move forward at some points. I even remember all the make-belief sessions of playing this game with my friends.Although games come and go, and new favourites surfaced out of the changing times, this one kept coming back to me. I had made too many memories about it. I can safely say that Half-Life influenced my early life in significant ways, and that makes it my favourite game of all time. We can all think back about a game that influenced us in our childhoods. Half-Life was that game for me.Black Mesa captivated the essence of everything that made Half-Life that game for me and made it special for me. Playing through Black Mesa, I felt as though it was my first time playing it again, back in the late 90's. Every detail of it made it feel like the first time I was discovering Half-Life. The developers even went so far as to include period-accurate props in the game, such as old computer monitors, microwave models, and wall-art. Everything about it made me feel like I was back in the 90's, playing it for the first time.Black Mesa brought back some feelings and fond memories, and I appreciate the work that has been done to get it to feel so close to what it was once. With new twists and story elements to discover if you know where and how to look, Black Mesa truly honours the original title of Half-Life.To qualify my personal opinion, I would like to state a few issues I experienced during the game. Possible spoilers ahead:The first is hardly an issue, but one that I even appreciated. The Xen levels were repetitive and lengthy in their puzzle formula. But I appreciated this. I remember playing the game and wondering when the story would move forward, so every extra minute I spent solving puzzles on the Xen map made the story content draw out, and made me yearn in anticipation at what would happen next, even if I was familiar with the original story.The second thing is the Alien Grunt pods getting stuck in the portion right before the Alien Controller elevator level in Interloper. After I destroyed the middle red power tube, the pods began to accumulate and overload the game in terms of props. I had to complete it quickly otherwise it would crash. During this time, frame rates fell very low. Almost unplayable in terms of being able to time movements and attacks, if I was lucky. If I was unlucky, the game would just crash.Otherwise, the textures, the gameplay, the voice acting, the amazing music, and the hours of content true to the original's quintessence, were all fantastic. For it, I would absolutely recommend any fans of the original, and even new players, to discover and rediscover the story of Gordon Freeman and his heroic acts in Black Mesa and beyond. I personally give this game 9.8 / 10 in terms of the rating. The bugs on Interloper were immersion-breaking. Hopefully these will be fixed soon so future players can play without any issues.

_childDocuments_.review: After over 16 years in development, Black Mesa: half remake, half reimagining of the original Half-Life, is a fantastic fan-made revision of the complete HL1 experience, greatly extending the campaign as well as outright expanding it. Xen goes from a minor footnote comprising a set of 5 shipped maps, barely tied together to the rest of the game with duct tape... to a grand 4-hour FPS epic of many maps: quiet exploration, mild survival horror vibes, more ludo-narrative cohesion, as well as actual storytelling, culminating in a series of high-skill challenges and puzzles ample in both size and scope. Then you've also got the multiplayer, which is a great and very well constructed throwback to classic 1990s deathmatch. It's a lot of fun and though the map selection right now isn't too good, more levels are on the way. It's a shame that not a lot of people actually play it.Back to the singleplayer: well, you've got a remake/reimagining of one of the greatest and most innovative games ever made. For one, it looks, feels and for all intents and purposes, plays better than the original, which sometimes suffered from issues inherent to games made in the late 90s. You've got a few clever surprises on the way that subvert player expectations in really cool ways. Overall, the story has been improved and in some ways expanded, a lot of new dialogue has been added, the environmental "mise en scene" storytelling has been conserved if not massively improved. In a lot of respects it's simply a better experience - with all the amenities, details and mechanics of HL2 but the satisfying difficulty, diversity, setting, atmosphere and engagement of HL1. On the whole, this is light-years beyond anything AAA-supported studios put together these days (that includes Valve until they finally get around to making another non-VR singleplayer game).Overall, after its 16+ years in development, Black Mesa is worthy of the Half-Life mantle, living up to HL1 faithfully and serving as a great new entry in the series. Highly recommended and every bit as great as HL1 and 2. One of the best games ever!

_childDocuments_.review: Never played the original Half Life 1, but when I saw this looming around on Steam I was drawn in instantly.Whilst there are a few small bugs here and there, it's ultimately miniscule when compared to how well the game mashes together. Interactive environments, creative and fun boss fights, diverse weapons arsenal and decent replay value make this a good game overall.If you're planning on buying this as a first time player, here are some quick tips:- Explore every room, corridor and crevice. You'll find secrets and plenty of gear to make the next areas so much easier.- Do not use walkthroughs or strategy guides.- If you're well and truly stuck? Go play something else or take a short break. Come back to it later, that button or lever you needed was probably right in front of you but you were too frustrated to see it.- When you reach Xen, just spend a few minutes admiring the environment before you go about killing.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game. The original was groundbreaking for its time and this game is remade lovingly using the source engine. It may not hold up to the best of modern titles graphically but it is a huge improvement on the original. Lots of improvements made to the game with some redesigned areas and improvements across the board. Music, controls, environments and level design are all stellar.Enemy AI is drastically improved from original also. Only negatives I have are ammo was far too plentiful for the most part meaning I rarely felt the need to conserve anything and health stations were all over the place meaning I rarely felt in real danger until some end sections. (I did play on normal difficulty however so maybe hard mode solves this) Lastly there are some wonky platforming sections that do detract from the game somewhat especially toward the end. They would have been better off removing 70 percent of the platforming from this game imo.Unfortunately there is loading everytime you reach a new section just like in the original which is a pity. It breaks immersion when your falling down a pit or being chased by a monster only to have the game pause and load for 6 seconds. This happens every half hour or so. 8/10 Would highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: Played through the game and finished it 2 times. Allow me to say how amazing Black Mesa is for its good graphics and its environment it has around places re-imagining Half-Life 1. The most part I love about it is how to makes the NPCs Security Guard and Scientists for example feel alive for it's voicelines and AI. I really enjoy playing around the chapters and don't get me started how amazing it is playing chapter Xen and Gonarch Lair. It is a stunning and sweeting chapter to look around it on how amazing it's places are. The last part I like about it is the soundtrack for any combat, action, puzzles, and atmosphere. It feels good to listen to that I sometimes listen to it more than the gameplay sometimes. I strongly recommend this game to any Half-Life fan who wants to re-experience playing Half-Life 1.Thank you, Crowbar Collective!
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: After playing this game, I think it's safe to say that it's ALMOST a masterpiece. To describe this game in one word, however: "incredible." I loved everything about it, especially Crowbar Collective's take on Xen. The sheer beauty is breathtaking, and the soundtrack for Xen is amazing. Words cannot fathom how thankful I am for Crowbar Collective releasing this as a FULL GAME. Never again will we have to play through the bug infested world of HL1, except for nostalgia's sake. The reason I consider this game "almost" a masterpiece, is because of the optimization in certain areas. For example, there's a section near the end where the player is taken up a long elevator and is forced to fight those big head alien things. My PC is pretty decent, and it had a harder and harder time running that section as I went further up the elevator. I was forced to turn my graphics to "potato" just to finish it. This might be the only negative issue I had with the game. I had no need to look anything up, except once on this one Xen section during chapter 17. Great game, please play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed the original Half Life and want to relive all the glory and excitement of this series again, I highly recommend Black Mesa. Although the graphics are a little outdated (because, you know, it's made on Source Engine), the visuals are still absolutely gourgeous. Small improvements were made, making the gameplay feel similar to Half Life 2 rather than the original Half Life (this is a good thing). My only "problem" with the game so far is that the HECU Team don't have that opressive radio chatter anymore.9/10 would cause a resonance cascade again
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa takes the best out of Half Life 1 and makes it better! If you ever think of playing the Half Life series again, start with Black Mesa! The game itself still entertains better than most contemporary games - over two decades after it's release Half Life still manages to entertain the player in a way that most titles just can't. There's just no boring moment in this game and even though I never really enjoyed the story itself, the setting and atmosphere become the story. Half Life always has been about that and thanks to the crowbar collective we finally can experience this classic again. Just better.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best remakes of a video game I've ever played. Crowbar Collective have taken the original blueprint of Half-Life and updated it almost masterfully. They've made everything more detailed, epic, and cinematic while never losing the roots of what made the original game in 1998 work. I especially love the re-imaginings of the Xen levels (although some of them do go on longer than necessary). The fact that the team at CC have been working on this since 2012 should speak to how dedicated they are to making the best product they can make, and as well as to how influential the original Half-Life was. Unfortunately, I only saw one crowbar during the entire game, which was the one Gordon uses. This is disappointing since this game is made by a Crowbar Collective. As such, 0/10 from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: If you played Half-Life 1 before, then you need to play this. If you HAVE NOT played Half-Life 1, then you NEED to play this. Seriously, what a great job revitalizing the OG fps game that gave us all the goodies we have today. HL1 is def one of the best games ever made and now it's totally 2020. check it out. worth the $20.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: Well I just "finished" Black Mesa, the graphically improved version of the original Half-Life, and I have to say I was very impressed! Not only is the game Graphically enhanced but the voice lines are all redone and it really is a new game consisting mostly of new textures with a few pulled from HL2, there's also a variety of new npc models made exclusively for Black Mesa. They even included unique models specifically for Dr. Kliener and Eli Vance as their models for HL2 were originally based off the 2 or 3 models for scientists in the original.Although, you might be wondering why I put "finished" in air quotes and that's because the game isn't actually 100% completed yet, they have everything done up until you go into the portal to get to the Borderworld of Xen. Once you go into the portal you get a message saying the assignment has been postponed as they're gathering more research. Essentially what they're saying is that it's not done yet but once it's finished it will be added to the game free of charge!However even without Xen the game is a fantastic deal! It really helps bring the original Half-Life into the modern age of gaming whilst staying true to the story and game play of the original! As a result I can whole heartedly recommend Black Mesa to anyone who would like to revisit the original Half-Life or to anyone who has never played Half-Life but would like to try it out and find out the origin of the series!

_childDocuments_.review: I was playing Black Mesa long before the highly anticipated Xen update on a much worse rig than I have now, but even back then in early access it was a really good game that was incredibly faithful to the original Half-Life while also ironing some of the level design and general jankness in the original game.I stopped playing around 1.0 because my machine literally couldn't handle Xen and came back around the time the Definitive Edition was released. I intended to start a new playthrough and end the game in the new Xen, but now I don't see that happening. For reference, I played the game through the 1.0 release because the most recent update as of writing will randomly wipe your savegames for no reason.For starters, marines have been turned into Super Aimbot Death Squads and can hit you reliably from halfway across the map. Marines are ridiculously fast and deadly accurate with shotguns as well, making the issue even more prevalent as getting within about 6 feet of a shotgun marine is pretty much instant death because they seem to have a way faster fire rate than you do with your shotgun. It makes some combat encounters a chore because you can't play nearly as aggressively as you could in Half-Life 1 (I've played both games on Hard difficulty) and are instead forced into a corner where you take potshots at the enemy until either of you is dead. Black Mesa becomes diet Call of Duty.This ultimately makes the shotgun worthless as you can't get very close to other enemies, meaning for most of my playthrough I've had a surplus of shotgun ammo and nothing to do with it.This isn't even beginning to mention the amount of times I saw AI hitch and break. I've seen a marine dedicate his entire life to shooting at one wall indefinetely, while I saw another look directly up at nothing and shout while not firing. These are issues I never saw in the early access version of Black Mesa.In its current state I cannot reccomend Black Mesa. I admire the massive efforts over a 12 year development cycle and all of those involved, but if you want classic Half-Life, go play classic Half-Life.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely at least as good as the original, but more modern - somewhat better graphics, and a physics system (which is not nearly as relevant as in Half-Life 2, but they did go somewhat overboard in that, hehe.)As of 26/05/2018, the last 1/8th or the game is not finished, and there are a few things that may be polished up in the future - the only significant thing being the fact that the Vortigaunts sometimes can't attack effectively because their attack is blocked by guard rails (which does little to block bullets, making these encounters sometimes too easy). And while it's obviously a "recreation" of Half-Life 1, they have put a ton of effort into improving some of the levels... Much, if not most, of the game is so reminiscent of the original that you might not notice the differences, while some areas are significantly visually different, and a few are different in gameplay terms - mostly, in my view, for the better. Black Mesa does include quite a few characters with unique audio that I don't remember from Half-Life 1, and a few of the jokes are slightly raunchy, so I think they're original to Black Mesa. The quality of the voice-over is impeccable. Overall, I highly recommend playing this game, either as a replacement for Half-Life, or for the memories, or just because it's a pretty good game. Judged by a modern standard, or the post-Half-Life 2 episodes, a soulless, mindless game critic could sneer at many aspects of the game, but we're not soulless, mindless players. We actually liked Half-Life 1, and Black Mesa is definitely living up to its namesake.I hope Valve throws some assets at these guys to get them to make Half-Life 3. ;) Valve is running out of excuses!!

_childDocuments_.review: Half Life 1 is a classic but very flawed game now when you consider the advancements in technology. Many of the puzzles feel strange and archaic and I found myself relying heavily on online guides, but this fan made remake seems to eliminate any issues. Just by exploring the environment and trial and error, I've been able to understand the solve the puzzles here and the newer graphics look downright beautiful. Xen isn't out and probably won't be out for quite a while, but what is here is very satisfying and great. If you want to play Half Life but can't get over the graphics or have some issues with either combat or the puzzle solving, try this version.

_childDocuments_.review: NOTE: At the time of writing this review/opinion  i'm at Surface Tension level which is a little bit more than half way through the game . If my opinion will shift strongly after playing remaining portion of the game i will update this review to reflect my opinion.Now , a good question to start with would be ' Is Black Mesa a REMAKE,REMASTER or REIMAGINING  of original Half Life ' ? I think it's all of those at the same time but none of them entirely. ' What does that even mean?' you could ask. Well ... while if you have played the original you will recognize all the areas, events and everything in between with ease they have redesigned some of the areas so much they sort of are different levels all together with hit and miss accuracy.That said nothing stands as plain 'bad' in this game , i'm just not sold on some of the redesign choices they have made. But once that is out of the way i couldnt recommend Black Mesa more. I'm so glad it actually exists and that i have chance to play it. For someone like me who have played Half Life 1 last time probably a decade and a half ago this brings so many great memories back and it just holds up so well to this day . I think they left the core of the FPS game from that time untouched and the fact that it is so enjoyable to play in 2019 speaks volumes of how timeless this formula is and what monumental game Half Life was and still is. I feel more investment in this basically two decades old game i have beaten several times than most of modern FPS games with all they modern design and bombastic cutscenes. To me Black Mesa is just a perfect way to relive and renew my appreciation for this genre and this francize in 21st century . I'm really glad this project did happen and even though it's still in EA after 10 years or so and well i dont agree on some of their changes i'm super greatful to Crowbar Collective for caring and doing this for us folks.

_childDocuments_.review: This game, well..Lets see..Black Mesa is a HUGE improvement of Half Life 1.Sad that I enjoy the Fan-Made game gives me more joy than the original games or even the Half Life 2 games.Black Mesa is the Fan-Man game of well I already said it before which is of Valve's Half Life 1 (Would be cool to see a remake of the other 2 Half Life 1 games)Everything about this game seems completely fresh.The Scientist, Guards and even the Soldiers feel so lively and real instead of feeling like the same lifeless NPCs they were in the original Half Life 1.The Weapons models look great and sound pretty damn great like they were back in Half Life 1.The effects and graphics in the game are VASTLY improved than back in Half Life 1's days.And all and all, I VERY much recommend this game to any Half Life Fan or anyone who is looking to try Half Life at all.

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa is Half-Life, but in a 2019 version of the Half-Life 2 engine, with accordingly remastered graphics, level design and physics.What are you waiting for? It may say it's still in Early Access, but as far as i'm concerned, It's DONE, buy it and play it NOW.I purchased Black Mesa in summer 2017 because we were promised the final third of the game, Xen in time for xmas of that Year.  I decided to wait until the Xen update  to write a review.  It's December 2019 and Xen has  finally arrived (looks like Crowbar Collective work in Valve time too).I didn't think it could possibly be worth waiting this long, but they proved me wrong.  This is not your daddy's Xen.  Black Mesa's Xen has scenes that filled me with awe and wonder, backed by a hair raising soundtrack and breathtaking action.It's got more 3D platforming than you would find in any other 2019 game, but what the heck it's Half-life.

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game on the strength of the Xen maps alone. These art and design of these sections feel worthy of a game on its own, yet represent what felt like the latter half of the game, going above and beyond how this world was imagined in the original Half Life game. I chose to play the game on the hardest difficulty, and boy, was it punishing, yet still enjoyable throughout. The skeleton of the original Half Life is evident throughout Black Mesa, with many additional twists and turns, Easter eggs, and puzzles that bring the old familiar maps back to life, but not always how you remembered them.Props to the devs for sticking with it through all these years. For me it was worth the wait.

Crowbar Collective's remake of the original 'Half-Life' game from Valve deserves all the praises one can only think about.From visuals to sounds; from the smoothness of gameplay to cloud support, achievements integration and badges; from a total bug-free experience to the joy a player gets since the first chapter to the last… this title is perfect even without the final part which will be released in 2019.One warning, though. _childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa is a very good FPS game, especially for it's time. Most of the genre (at the time) consisted of games like DOOM 2016 & Wolfenstein: The New Order which are still great influential games but the most influential at the time was Half-Life which added a well told story to these games there are many iconic SFX in this (Namely the memed death sound) but the game also has a lot of atmosphere & intense moments. As a big fan of movies like Alien (the Facehuggers definitely inspired the Headcrabs) I really enjoyed the survival horror elements in the game I also liked the mysterious factors like The G-Man character & the Xen border world. Although it's a great game it's definitely without it's flaws such as the chapter "Surface Tension" which is boring although I don't have problems with a challenge in the game because I did enjoy the final chapters of the game set in Xen & also the NPC's are pretty good but the game is from 2020 & it's fun to play around with them. Overall I really do love this game it's got some amazing use of environmental storytelling & some kickass action.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa is phenomenal, with a few quirks and very few legitimate complaints. As a fan of the original Half-Life (warts and all), I have to say I felt right at home in this excellent remake.The visuals are nothing short of stunning, the HL2 engine is pushed to its absolute limits and everything looks crisp, detailed and in general you can tell there has been a LOT of love poured into the visual aspect of things. Especially Xen. Xen is so incredibly oozing with style it's... I can't really put it into words you just have to see it for yourself.In terms of sound, I'm also impressed. The sound design in general is also top-notch, great weapon sounds (especially the Gluon Gun, wow), pumping action tracks, cool ambient music.The story is largely left intact (save for the two marines that capture Freeman, that was a bit of a strange departure), so I won't waste words on it. Moving on.The gameplay carries over very well. The aliens behave more or less identically to the original. The marines are relentless, even more so than in HL1, and some areas are the cheap kind of difficult as a result, but overall, I enjoyed the action-packed middle section of the game, it felt a lot more natural than in the original. That said, I could've sworn the MP5 had 50 rounds, that the pistol wasn't so strong, that the shotgun had a faster rate of fire and so on - so in the weapons department, some things feel different, but not in a way that I'd say they feel "off" or "worse. You just have to get used to it.The maps (save for Interloper, more on that shortly) are just amazing as well. I can't get over how well they managed to expand upon the ideas in the original with a tweak here and there to make the whole thing even more palpable, tangible and flowing super-smoothly. Black Mesa in Anomalous Materials feels a lot more teeming with life, the survival horror is soup-thick thanks to the excellent lighting and layout of the first third of the game, Surface Tension and Forget About Freeman are awesomely brought to life, On a Rail is shorter (yay), Lambda Core and Xen are amazing too, just nothing but good things to say, again.Any negatives, then...? Well... not really, no. I didn't have any performance drops, bugs, I had the odd ragdoll spaz-out but that happened in HL2 as well, nature of the beast etc. The weapon and story departures aren't significant enough to make up a worse experience. The only thing that really ticked me off was Interloper. That map was tedious to begin with and for some arcane reason, they decided to stretch it out even more. The whole organic factory shtick grows old really, really fast and all the puzzles are just a variation on the same thing over and over again, just... annoying, is the word I'm looking for. The initial vista, the Vortigaunts and the crystals powering the Gluon Gun were nifty and all but other than that, it's just utterly forgettable platforming with some hasty combat sections.All in all, if you haven't played Half-Life one and graphics are what is putting you off, well, no more excuses for you! If you played and loved the original, you'll love this as well (and hate Interloper even more). Win-win. Limitlessss potential!

_childDocuments_.review: Although it definitely still has the same issues in level design that I have always had with Half-Life games in general, its atmosphere makes up for that entirely and I recommend playing the game just for that alone. _childDocuments_.review: The definitive Half Life 1 experience. Completely refreshed with the Source engine and all of the benefits included, but preserves all of the original game. _childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: I loved every second of it.I've been a fan of Half-Life 2 since the day it was released but I never brought myself to finish the genre-defining original. Too clunky and at parts just frustrating. Black Mesa was so well made, everything I remember to be annoying has been either polished, cut, expanded, or completely remade. First, it felt like playing a chapter of HL2 which is good enough for me and then you get to Xen which just blew my mind. Thanks, Crowbar Collective for creating this work of art and allowing me to feel everything people must have felt when they first played HL1 in 1998.

_childDocuments_.review: Great remake of the original from the ground up. Basically made HL1  look like HL2. Only problem I have is that it is plagued with micro stutters and screen tearing even with GSync (found some work arounds but still not silky smooth). Also "Escape" key stops functioning occasionally (can't access menu). Despite the issues, I still recommend this game as you can't go wrong for the price and nostalgia factor.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: As a long time HALF LIFE fan, I was very impressed by this BLACK MESA game, which is Half Life original remade. I had played the free mod released back in 2012 and also the Early Access commercial re-release back in 2015. The EA re-release wasn't the full experience since the playthrough stopped right when you go into the Lambda's Core teleporter. Years later, the game includes the XEN CHAPTERS. I had to hold playing it since I kept having issues, especially with my ultrawide resolution which wasn't displaying the font properly.Having waited longer than I thought, I periodically checked whenever CROWBAR COLLECTIVE would fix it and at last, it is now!So what's BMDE compared to the free mod version released way too long ago?As for this paid version, not only it makes the game feel more modern, but Black Mesa offers a few differences worth of mention during gameplay, compared to Half Life and even the free Black Mesa mod.Pretty much the same as the free mod version, except improved visuals mostly, there is a new multiplayer portion included as well. Finally, XEN is included and it is way bigger than I imagined! Compared to the original Half Life, XEN chapters takes about two hours for a chapter, for a total of three chapters. So, a good 6 hours of gameplay, give or take more/less depending on your playstyle and achievements hunt.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: This is how you do a remake of a classic FPS in Source.After Valve's rather disappointing and lackluster "Source remake" of the first Half-Life game several years ago, a group of dedicated fans made it their goal to recreate Half-Life as it should have been in Source and then release it as a free mod.And now we have gotten to this point with this stand-alone remake that don't force you to have a Source game like Team Fortress 2, Half-Life 2 or any other Source powered games in order to play, you can still however download the free and older mod version via Moddb.Also this whole thing is just about complete, except of course for the Xen part which the devs have promised will be remade to be as enjoyable as possible and not a frustrating jumping nightmare like in the original as most people might recall.This is a perfect example of when Early Access is done right, you really should get this especially if you're a Half-Life fan, casual or hardcore, it doesn't matter as you will still get one heck of an enjoyable experience as you revisit Black Mesa.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: Black MesaRelease Date:  5 May 2015Strengths: -A great Half-life-1 remake with improved graphics-Long levels and playtime average around 14 hrs-Great fire fights thanks to good AI-Additional content and expanded levels as compared to the original Limitations:-Badly optimized and frequent FPS drops-Still has bugs that leads to crashes (especially in Lambda Core level)-Some situations and puzzles can be frustrating (but so was Half-life wasn't it?)Conclusion:This game is a remake of the Half-Life-1 made by valve in 1998 which was one of the best seller games of all time. Surprisingly, this remake is worthy enough to be associated with Half-life as it successfully preserves what made the original game unique and adds content on top of it. The most significant improvement is the expansion of the levels Xen, Gonarch's Lair, Interloper which are now vast. AI is brutal and all original weapons have been preserved. The game uses the new Source engine so it appears better but it is poorly optimized and FPS drops are common. Nevertheless, the game is pretty much enjoyable and playable as new areas are included with glimpses of the original ones well preserved. Overall, the game is a must buy for Half-Life fans and if you haven't played that, it stands good as a latest replacement for the same.Graphics: 7/10 Gameplay: 8/10Replayability: 5/10Story: 5/10Sound: 6/10Level Design: 8/10Overall rating is 6.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa is a remake of the original Half-Life, staying faithful to the original while having subtle changes and the new and improved  levels, which I'd argue is the main selling point of this game. In advance, this is coming from someone who's never played the original but has watched plenty of gameplay, so comparisons will come from what I've seen/remember.I don't really have anything bad to say, so I'll just mention things that bothered me personally but never felt like it ruined the game in a negative way.Black Mesa is the one exception I can make where you don't need to play the original. Why? Because it's janky and old as heck. Black Mesa is so faithful that it's the same experience but on a new engine. Better Xen levels, gameplay and graphics If you're planning on doing a Half-Life binge like I currently am, play this instead. You'll thank me later. Thank you CC for this masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: Things i liked:-the puzzles-the combat-the graphics-the atmosphere-the storyThings i Didn't like:-the length of certain parts (the factory section in Xen)I would give this game 9/10. This is a fan-made reimagining of Half-life. Please do not let the term "fan-made" fool you, this game is one of the best games I've played in a long time. It fixes problems with certain chapters like on a rail and upgrades almost all of the assets and models. Something I also want to note, this game is a reimagining, it isn't a replacement for half-life. These games include different enemies and different level layouts. These are very different games. I strongly advise people to play both Half-Life and Black Mesa.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great, until it is not. I wish I could rate it as neutral. The original half life is challenge, but it never gets annoying and tiresome like the bugs and strange level design in black mesa. My main gripes are with Zen levels. Zen looks great, and new levels are welcome. BUT, a lot of them are visually confusing, long puzzle-mazes, and buggy experiences. The long jump suit made slip and slide all across the levels where I had to use it; sometimes it would flat out not work when trying to activate. I feel like these parts could of been more polished. The whole zen-factory-lab levels made me want to just say ♥♥♥♥ it and quit. In addition, the levels seem large and there are a lot of visual confusion where to go making me error test a lot of the parts to see where I actually need to go. The worst bug I had happen to me was in Gonarch's Lair and Interloper levels, where the level loading bricked the game I could go to my previous quicksave since it was the level loading save and had to load an earlier manual save.Get it, if you are a fan.

But it has filled this up with quite interesting elements like the Laser Crystals in Interloper.

_childDocuments_.review: What to say? The first half of the game is updated, improved version of the old classic that we know and love. Until we get to Xen. The first time Gordon teleports in, it is absolutely gorgeous. Xen is now half of the game, and is worth the asking price on it's own - it is completely re-designed, re-scored and refreshed. I found myself spending a good few minutes standing there, looking up at the environment each time after emerging from a cave system, with the score swelling around me taking in everything. It really is excellent. Joel Nielsen has done a superb job on the soundtrack - it is very hard to believe that this is a fan made game in every aspect - and is a credit to everyone who worked on it for so long.There are a few ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ - getting stuck on scenery occasionally, some of the sections felt a little bit too long and in one later battle with the Alien Controllers my 970 struggled with all the particles, dropping to 10fps (at 1440p) but a game restart cured that after finishing the section. I'm nitpicking, however. Don't let it put you off, the experience is worth it. Completed in February 2020.Everything leads up to the Nihilanth fight, an exposition which is tremendous. A climactic battle in it's truest sense, with the amount of destruction that rains upon you as it gets closer to the end being truly awe inspiring. No hyperbole. I was very impressed.Crowbar Collective should be very satisfied with themselves. Well done all of you!
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: So, i am a big fan of the Half-Life series and i must say that if there is any con on it,they are the graphics. Yes, i know that it came out in 1998 and it's pretty decent for the time. I honestly find the graphics not a major point in games like these that have a high replayability value, but there will always be a "IF" there were good grahpics, this game could be even more enjoyable...So now, let's move on to Black Mesa itself. They use Source Engine and best graphics. Logically. But apart that, what is there to note? From the original gameplay i could find a lot of diferences between the original game and this fan-made remake:->Some puzzles have different ways to be solved;->Some areas are accessed in a diferent way (took me a few minutes in the lab to realize that the door i normally would pass through in HL1 is closed and i had to go a way around through a freezer);->Some areas have some different music themes for (for example) when you are fighting, in the middle of a puzzle or in a new area. I don't know about this change, i think it's a bold move since in some cases it increases the thrill and "mood" and others simply is a bit...uncessessary.->Some new events were created, not much, small stuff.->Some details in HL1 that weren't explained "properly" (and by that i mean not getting our attention for being extremely little details) are actually more...clear so to say. Like the cooking pot in the microwave that you make explode. Now seriously doe, i never heard of Eli Vance until the second game. There is one thing to add down about Black Mesa: the game ends (for now at least) on the portal to XEN. The developers said that there was a problem with the organic textures and Source engine. They are also expanding XEN. Again, a bold move since a lot of the players didn't really liked that area. There are taking their time and honestly, i can't blame them. They are making a remake of one of the best FPS/Horror/Sci-fi games of all time. Valve's Serie have a powerfull name in the industry.So as a final review: ->Is it worth it?Yes, but keep in mind it's a growing game. If you are afraid of it, consider either purchasing it on sales or downloading the Black Mesa's mod from the official team website (keep in mind XEN won't be included, so if you want future releases, buy the game).
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: This was my first (full) experience with any of the Half-Life games and it was fantastic... until the Interloper chapter. I still highly recommend this game because it is very fun and really engaging BUT I think Interloper by FAR the weakest section of the game and tainted the experience as a whole. It's essentially the last traditional chapter of the game and since it drags on and on with a lot of cluttered environments and repeated puzzles, there is a really bad taste left in your mouth before completing the game. A lot of the chapter felt like community made obstacle course/jump puzzle maps you could download in Halo 3 Forge. Questionable environment designs and routing that didn't feel coordinated with the "factory" you are set in. It breaks the immersion and became more like a run-on sentence rather than the streamlined and clean experience that I had with the majority of the previous chapters. Overall, an extremely well done game. Definitely made me a fan of the universe and gave me a greater appreciation for the Source Engine, Valve and all their influence on games today. Just wish Crowbar Collective tightened up those Xen chapters a little bit more.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: This game is for everyone. If you played Half-Life back when it came out in 1998, you're in for a big treat. This is more than a remaster. Nobody is trying to rewrite Shakespeare over here. What the Crowbar Collective has produced is the culmination of over 20 years of industry shaping and user experience expertise. Even our favorite games from the past can have suffered in respect to clarity and wayfinding. They suffered to some degree from "quality of life" issues. Black Mesa is a beautiful world, wonderfully and tactfully reimagined in a way that has not only sated my nostalgia, but nourished my waning dedication to the series. If you DIDN'T play it back in the 90s, you owe it to yourself (or your uncle) to join the club.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: Although this is essentially a reboot of the original Half-Life, it has been built completely from the ground up with only a grain of reused assets. The devs have not spared any effort to that end, either, as this game brings Black Mesa to life like never before. Everything seems to have been done right here, from the level recreation, gorgeous environments, sound design, and overall loyalty to the original game. All the dedication and hard work of the devs has created something that is truly worthy of Valve's legacy and the Half-Life franchise. Make no mistake - this is the way Half-Life was meant to be played.

Really loved the Xen part of the game. The only thing I would say that I hate about this game are the water levels (except the one in Xen). Overall, an amazing game 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I was never into video games when I was a young kid. I had other hobbies. When I was living in England when I was in middle school, a buddy gave me a "Demo Disk" from the British PC Gamer, and told me to load the game Half-Life on it. The demo was a stand alone level (if anyone here is in their thirties and can remember), and this was at a time where you could fit a few demos on a CD included with a magazine.     Half-Life changed my life. I became a life long PC Gamer. All these years later it's always there. We played it on my five PC LAN growing up; moving onto HL:OP, CS, DOD, and NS. And I played through HL2 a thousand times in High School, College, and the Army. Now my son watches me play them.     Point in fact, the original HL is a master-piece, but dated graphically (textures, models, and effects). Normally, I never buy early access on Steam, but I was willing to take a chance for this. This game is missing Xen, but to be honest, I always thought the Xen levels were a pain. Black Mesa is gorgeous and true to it's source material. I felt the people who made this product were life long fans like myself, and put their talents to good use. The attention to detail makes it a labour of love. In an age of COD madness, this game has a soul, and is worth your time and your money.

_childDocuments_.review: JUST BUY IT!An incredible remake for one of the best games of all time.Black Mesa improves Half-Life with improves graphics, changes the gameplay and tactics adding new rooms, and adds the Havoc physics, something that the original Half-Life didn't have.This game will give some good nostalgia to the old-schoolers, and the new generations will have a taste of the original game.Totally recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic remake of the original Half-Life. If the old game from 1998 seems a bit too old and out there, this is perfect. The story is still amazing, while the graphics of this game is amazing, and while the basic gameplay hasn't changed much, just getting it in a nicer and fancier package makes it much easier to swallow. Even if you still enjoy the original Half-Life and have no problems with that game, this is still worth it. _childDocuments_.review: Best way to re-experience the original Half-Life from 1998.  This reiteration on the Source engine is truly a work of love.  The voices, the sounds, the music, graphics are all up to date for today's expectations, but still hold true to the original game it's attempting to remake.Nothing has changed from the original game so far, except that the alien world, Xen, has not been completed yet.  I was able to get to the portal and jump through and finish what's been made so far and the experience was spectacular.  I played it on hard, or expert or whatever the hardest level was and the game was truly difficult in certain locations.As a whole though, the feel, the pace, the guns, and all the puzzles you need to solve are all there.  The levels have not been changed whatsoever.  This means some of the key points of the game still persists.  The point where bullet holes show up and tear down the duct that you're crawling through still occurs, the part where a marine through a detonating pack in the pipe you're in and closes the door where a fire inferno starts when it blows up still occurs.  Every signature moment is perfectly recrafted for this version.This may be an old game, and I may be knee deep in nostalgia, but kudos to the team who put this together.  Highly recommended if you have not had the chance to play this game.  Also, I'm close to getting all of the achievements for the game, but there is one just like in Half-Life 2 where you have to carry an item with you throughout the game.  Sounds annoying, but I figured that I would try it out when the Xen world portion of the game was released.

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of the original Half-Life, I was excited to play this remake. From the very start Black Mesa captures the distinctive Half-Life gaming experience. It goes without saying that if you are a fan of the original, then Black Mesa is a game you really should have in your collection.

_childDocuments_.review: Crowbar Collective have done an incredible job here. It's a tall order to take one of the most beloved PC games ever made and update it for the modern era and they have probably done this more successfully than I've ever seen anyone do it before. THIS is how you remake a game.CC have walked the knife edge of staying true and updating that results in a piece of work that is how you REMEMBER Half-Life being when you played it twenty years ago, not how it actually was. Every level, texture, enemy and sound are faithful to the original, but higher res. No improvement made struck me as taking too much license. Small things like a range of different faces, some slightly expanded dialogue add to the experience instead of making it feel too different. All the changes and deviations serve only to make the setting for more real, more human and more nuanced.Finally... Xen. Just wow. They took what was one of the least loved sections from one of the best loved games and completely turned it around to be, in my opinion, the very best part of the remake. Xen lives and breathes. It is beautiful and disturbing. Parts of it feel like a dream, others like a nightmare. They cut down on things we hated (less insanely difficult jumping puzzles) and expanded the parts we loved. The Gonarch battle is a MUCH larger part of the game and it's one of the most incredible, tense hunt and be hunted experiences I've ever had. Better even that the antlion queen from Episode 2. And the final battle with Nihilanth was awesome. The factory section introduced so many awesome and enjoyable synergistic gameplay elements it's hard to believe they weren't in the original. And the final battle with Nihilanth, after all that, STILL manages to be a satisfying climax to the experience instead of a let down, as so many games end bosses are these days.All in all, perfect. 10/10. Thank you, Crowbar Collective.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't play the original Half-Life when it was released, but after playing the 2nd and becoming interested in the series I definitely wanted to go back and see what I missed. I decided to play Black Mesa for the modern visuals. I can't say how well it replicates the feel of the original since I never had that experience, but judging it on its own I think it's very good.It does take a while to get used to if you're accustomed to modern shooters. The unnaturally fast movement speed and first person platforming is something that a lot of titles have abandoned, probably for good reason, but once I got the hang of it I viewed those sequences as a nice change of pace.I also appreciated the ability to quicksave at virtually any point, and you probably will need to use that feature at least a few times. In particular, the combat against soldiers felt unbalanced. Even on medium difficulty they are basically just walking aimbots. In a game that's very atmospheric, this was probably the one thing that would consistently break my immersion. All of the other enemies felt grounded within the world. There's a lot of variety in the monsters you'll face, with different strategies being ideal for taking each of them down, so that helps keep things fresh. I didn't play multiplayer, so I won't talk about pvp combat.The level design is one of the strongest points of the game. There are a lot of aesthetically distinct environments that you'll spend time in, some of them small and confined, others that are very big and give you an open-world feel. You'll have moments of relative silence and peace while solving environmental puzzles, as well as orchestrated action sequences and big battles where you've got 2 different factions besides yourself fighting each other. It's unique in its ability to be cinematic while still allowing the player to move freely around the environment. There are almost no cutscenes, but still a ton of "wow" moments. The only real problem is that the last portion of the overhaul, which takes place on an alien planet, has not yet been finished. This is somewhat forgivable since it's still listed as early access, but it's becoming a controversy within the game's community. I decided to just download the user-created Xen mod from the workshop since I couldn't wait to see the ending, and I have to say that it worked fine and was done very well. Overall this is a respectable project, and if you can look past a few points of frustration, this is a great way to experience a game that every FPS player should try.

_childDocuments_.review: 15 years in the making, and I'd say it's worth it.Looks, sounds, and plays quite great, an impressive effort to say the least.As for the campaign it's a fantastic recreation of the original Half Life campaign, but with some minor changes here and there, even some sections are partially redesigned for pacing reasons (mainly On A Rail and Xen chapters).I do have some gripes with it, mainly the feel of the weapons which feels similar to Half Life 2 for very obvious reasons which didn't exactly have my favorite gunplay of the first two installments, and I have some small problems with the art style which feels a bit too photorealistic for my taste, the original Half Life was quite colorful and to some degree almost cartoonish, but Black Mesa goes for more gritty realism (which it does succeed quite well with).Black Mesa is a great introduction to the Half Life series, as it retains the story of the original but more accessible due to the  graphical fidelity and just having an overall more modern feel.

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa, as advertised. An excellently done and faithful recreation and revamp of the original Half-Life, this game brings a previously ancient and rusting experience into the modern day, with all the love and attention it deserves.Visuals: 10/10     Excellently done graphical effects, UI and menus are high quality, no bugs, no glitches, simple to use and understand.Game looks like a treat, and generally runs like one too, although this is a rather demanding game.Audio: 10/10     Audio is a treat as well, excellent ambience, variety of configurations to support surround sound systems, well balanced, and very well chosen sounds mean that it never gets old either.Gameplay: 9/10     No significant gameplay issues. Mostly straight forward combat (with varying difficulty, encounters, a vast number of enemy types, and some stealth and surprise opportunities), simple puzzle solving, A few boss fights, and linear game progression. Confusing level layouts occasionally leave something to be desired. Did experience crashes multiple times involving the controllers and vortigaunts when they're being controlled. Keeps things fresh as the game progresses, you're never dealing with the same enemy encounters more than you can handle.---/// Overall: 9.7/10 ///---If you enjoyed the other half life games and their respective experiences, you're certain to enjoy this. Cannot recommend enough, if you have the computer to handle it.

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa is a stunning remake of the classic 1998 first-person shooter game, Half-Life. Developed by Crowbar Collective, the game aims to capture the essence of the original game while updating it with modern graphics, improved gameplay mechanics, and other enhancements.One of the standout features of Black Mesa is its faithful recreation of the original Half-Life experience. The game follows the same story as the original, with players taking on the role of scientist Gordon Freeman as he battles his way through the Black Mesa research facility, fighting off alien invaders and navigating the complex's many dangerous and mysterious areas.But where Black Mesa truly shines is in its updated graphics and gameplay mechanics. The game features stunning high-definition visuals that breathe new life into the game's iconic locations and enemies, making the experience feel fresh and exciting even for players who have played the original countless times. The game also features new and improved mechanics, such as updated physics, improved enemy AI, and new weapons and items that give players even more ways to take on the game's many challenges.For fans of the original Half-Life, Black Mesa is an absolute must-play. The game's attention to detail and commitment to capturing the spirit of the original make it a truly unique experience that feels both familiar and new. It's a game that will bring back fond memories of playing the original Half-Life as a child, while also providing an updated and enhanced experience that is sure to captivate a new generation of players.Overall, Black Mesa is an outstanding game that is well worth checking out for fans of the original Half-Life, as well as anyone who loves first-person shooter games with compelling stories and challenging gameplay. It's a true labor of love that captures the essence of the original while elevating it to new heights, making it one of the best remakes of a classic game ever made.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent experience, a remake done well. The general path that you take throughout the game roughly follows the one of the original Half-Life, but many areas have been expanded or revamped to give it a fresh feel. Xen, the last section of the game, has been completely overhauled, and in my opinion, it is a major improvement over the section from the original game. The gameplay is solid, the classic Source Engine shooter experience that you'd expect, with puzzles every now and then throughout the game. I can't think of anything negative to say about the game; the default difficulty is perhaps a little too easy, but one can always bump up the difficulty or add a difficulty mod through the Steam Workshop.It took me about 15 hours to finish the game, as I enjoyed exploring the detailed world. I'd recommend the game to both people who have and have not played the original Half-Life, but I recommend playing the original at some point as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: Normally, I was going to recommend it because I really love Black Mesa but the things that has changed since the mod version sometimes bother me. Of course there has been positive changes as well but the negatives do bother me a lot.+Improved AI makes the game more fun and more challenging+Better graphics but despite being a source game it doesn't work on some of the older computers which is a bummer, it used to work on my older device but no longer does since 2017(?) graphical update? If the year is wrong please correct me+Addition of the lost parts of surface tension make the game feel more like Half Life 1 experience and the scripted events does make you  pity the marines fearing their lives in this carnage+XEN is very beautiful, it was worth the wait.-Interactivity is lowered, you can no longer pick up many things you used to be able  to pick up or break-Some of the weapon models are downgrades of what they used to be, I don't know what actual variant of MP5 this is, I prefer the EOD version, luckily there is modding for it. Of all the transitions, the crossbow has the worst scope it ever had, this thing is ugly and weird to use-You can no longer have stains and marks of the liquids you were exposed to on your weapons, I know it was buggy but instead of fixing the issues people had with it instead of just removing it or not even adding it as a graphical setting was disappointing-New UI is hard to get used to but I'm actually neutral about it. -Some paths are blocked from what I've seen, you can't backtrack in a shootout easily, if the developers want you to see something, you will see it and you will see it at the spot you want them to see it. Examples are the Abrams in the Lambda Complex, you can no longer access it through the door and have the ability to retreat to cover and have the HECU and Aliens kill each other, you have to crawl a vent and forecefully engage both sides because they will attack you. Another example is the battle after exiting the tunnels and facing an abrams and the marines while the aircraft are retreating above you before the entrance of the lamba complex, you no longer can retreat back into the small armoury because there is a barbed fence and you can't just shoot the lock to go back, another bummer. It feels less of  a source game compared to the downgraded interactivity. -The weapons like shotgun and the magnum has a stupid delay. Shotgun doesn't fire instantly when you pull the trigger, it makes shooting the headcrabs mid air extremely hard and annoying, the enemies  dodge your shotgun because how slow it fires, the magnum doesn't  fire instantly when you zoom, in the mod it was faster because Gordon was logically using single action to fire the magnum and it was much better than this illogical delay. You press the button on your mouse, the gun doesn't fire.-A problem I had with the mod which seems to have carried over to the base game but in a worse condition is how underpowered the abrams tank, the RPG and the  tow launchers are. If I can willy nilly dodge tank shells by just walking sideways, that tank is not done right. Alien controllers can dodge what appears to be a man portable ATGM which is realistically at MACH speeds. TOW is even worse, what kind of an ATGM nest is this, no wonder HECU lost control, this is just cringy. At least in the mod skill.cfg, you could edit these without breaking the game, my attempts to fix the rpg and the tank just made it unplayable, if I increase the speed the shells just don't spawn or despawn after 2 feet in front of you.If you were going to make the interactivity with the physics this low, why even use the Source engine? You could use any other game engine to have even better graphics. The game doesn't even run that well on older devices anymore so I don't see the point of it being in Source other than making it related to Half-Life series as if it is not a remake already.My point is, I love the game but my problems are that every part until XEN is downgraded from the mod version and the updates seem to keep pushing it that way. Xen is worth the money but I really hope the developers will actually make it a source game again. Because of these downsides, many improvements just don't feel like improvements anymore. It is worth the price but it is still a downgrade from what it used to be even with improved lighting and graphics.If you have any criticism about my opinion or if you can correct any mistakes I made, please do so :)

_childDocuments_.review: The new Interloper chapter is a complete disaster in my opinion. There are way too many puzzles to solve and they just repeat themselves over time and that makes it so boring to play. I almost quit playing the game rather than finishing that chapter. _childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: If a studio is remaking a game and it doesn't go to the lengths Black Mesa went to do justice to the original Half-Life, that studio is making a money-grab. This is the quintessential remake against which all other remakes should and ought to be compared. It's damn near perfect. The only complaint I have is the same I had with the original game: Xen. Where the Xen levels in the original Half-Life were sloppy and unpolished (Valve did confess to rushing them through development), the Xen levels in Black Mesa draaag on and on and on and on and on and on and on and on and on and on and on and on and on and on. The mechanics and level design for Xen are improvements by every measure. However, Crowbar Collective over-corrected by making the Xen levels so long they end up outstaying their welcome. Make no mistake, Xen is great fun to play through, but it gets exhausting.I only recommend you buy and play through the original Half-Life first if you want to fully appreciate the masterpiece Crowbar Collective so lovingly put together for us to enjoy. Black Mesa is a testament to the skill and passion of the team at Crowbar Collective, and an incomparable tribute to what is arguably the greatest, most significant game ever made.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: A creative reimagining of the fps classic.Black Mesa is a great game. The graphics, especially on the Xen levels, are gorgeous. Voice-actors did an amazing job on replicating the sound and feel of the original lines, while bringing the additional character flair alongside with it. The soundtrack only shines on the Xen levels. In other places it's really hit-or-miss. I still prefer the superior Kelly Bailey score for the original Half-life. I really like the saturated look Crowbar Collective went with the graphics for Black Mesa. They redid the all the textures in the game, while at the same time giving them a spin. Saddly, not all is great about Black Mesa. The gameplay sufferes in comparison to Half-life. Most notably the AI of the Marines. They are basically a straight port of the Combine forces from Half-life 2 — which were more "artificial" than "intelligence".Black Mesa is something, that I personally think cannot be truly appreciated without first beating the original Half-life series.It's somewhat of a tribute honestly, and I love that. You will want to beat this game after beating Half-life. The series as a whole has a lot of a replay value, and Black Mesa succeds at replicating that, along with the aforementioned.I highly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa is one of the rare fan-made remakes that leaves Early Access and ends up being pretty great. While it is not perfect, particularly near the end, this is not a bad way to experience Half-Life today. It is probably still best to play the original first, but Black Mesa is far from the worst way to experience the Half-Life universe...PROS:- Vastly improved visuals that (mostly) retain the original art style- All the great, weapons, enemies, level design, and uninterrupted gameplay from the original- Great plot with somewhat improved lore- Improved boss fights- Developers seem to have known when to change and when not to change things- Good value at ~ 11 hours to completeCONS:- While this does improve on the Xen levels, Interloper in particular is still terrible- Some really bad load times- Decent amount of crashes and shaky performance in the later levels- Some janky hitboxes and movement
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa is representation of what remake should be. It doesn't bring big difference into the story, but brings new mindblowing visuals, expands levels with many new puzzles, cleaner sound design and voice acting and realistic physics of the Source engine.Even though the offices didn't get a big change, they look great, of course, but haven't changed in general look and feel of them, the surface levels do. The canyons and clear skies of New Mexico feel way more real than in the original, but the true mindblowing aspect of this remake is..., my god...Months ago, I knew there is some remake of HL1, that is slowly being finished, but I wasn't much interested. But recently, when I came back to play through older titles from Valve, I looked it up, and I gotta say, once I saw how Xen looks like, I couldn't hold my wallet still. I just can't comprehend how someone managed to turn few flying rocks, into a living organism. While in HL1 you just jump from rock to rock, walk through some caves, find off some enemies from to time, in Black Mesa, you gotta walk through whole islands, abandoned bases full of scientific equipment, and dead scientists in HEV suits, walk through flooded  dark caves and tunnels, green and blue jungles, and the place is just so unnatural to our kind, that you generally feel like you're the alien. And the cherry on top, is it's fantastic soundtrack. Once you see the gorgeous nature and amount of alien creatures of Xen, with purple skies, full of stars, nebulas and galaxies, and also hear the phenomenal soundtrack, you want the moment to last foreverBlack Mesa's Xen may be the most beautiful place I've ever visited in a videogame, or any other kind of media, and is truly unforgettable experience.I gotta admit, I haven't finished the game, so far, but that's because my toaster has hard time running later chapters on surface and in Xen, so I don't really want to get into boss fights, but still, in chapters that run pretty well, I have trouble with random FPS drops, I would blame my potato, but I've seen even people with great machines complain, so, be aware of that. But I am sure the team is working on it. - Beautiful piece of pure passion
