_childDocuments_.review: I can't believe that it's finally here after all these years, but it is, and it is glorious. If you played the original Half-Life then enjoy this love letter to it by the fans, for the fans.  If you haven't played the original Half-Life, you can safely skip it and play this remake instead.  You won't be missing out.I won't have to go too deep into detail here, since many other reviewers have covered this title very effectively.  My take is that this long-overdue (but seriously, they weren't getting paid until now) remake is a remarkable achievement, and improves on the original game in a huge number of ways.The most obvious improvement is the graphics, which while they're still dated by today's standards due to the limits of the Source engine, they still have several jaw-dropping visuals to enjoy in the level design.  This remake is worth playing just for re-discovering Black Mesa Research Facility in the way our childhood memories did when Half-Life first came out.The physics engine is leveraged well, and there's more interaction with objects than the original, but without too much of a gimmick factor.  There are jumping scenarios, as always, but some much more engaging mechanical puzzles to work out along the way which don't take too much from the pacing.Now that we know more about the universe of Half-Life, having a chance to actually "save" Vortigaunts was a nice touch, and indeed there has been some additions which decrease the linearity of some of the levels slightly, yet in respectful ways.  The original game had some sequences which could be challenging, but if you knew what to expect you could bypass them entirely with some strategically-placed satchel charges.  Black Mesa will offer you no such recourse in the majority of your encounters, and remains continually challenging as you progress.  One of the most significant areas I found to be improved were the boss fights.  Gonarth and Nihilanth in particular have far more epic and dynamic scenarios for you to fight them in.  That said, there are so many areas on Earth where scenes that were mildly challenging in the original will be gruelingly difficult and require you to experiment with different tactics in order to successfully defeat.  The difficulty ramp-up has a steep curve, and is consistently tough, so buckle up!The final comment I'll make is about the part of Half-Life that every PC gamer loves to hate:  Xen.  The borderworld levels were the bane of the original game because they broke up the pacing and tension in a distracting way, and some parts were even downright drudgery.  Personally, I really enjoyed the art design of Xen in the original, but shared the complains gameplay-wise.  The Crowbar collective took Xen and made it so visually (and acoustically) beautiful that I legitimately wanted to just hang out there and meditate, in a way its name would imply.  The levels were interesting and fun to discover, and unlike the original, some of the time I spent in the borderworld was legitimately fun!  However, that fun ultimately stretches into a series of annoyed groans...because in Black Mesa, the Xen levels seem like they go on forever...  The improvements are fantastic, and if they had kept the length of content the same, it would have been near-perfect.  Unfortunately, there's just far too much of Xen in this game for it to be a net overall positive effect on the game.  (I swear if I see another alien conveyor belt....)Overall, I have to say Black Mesa is fantastic, and worth a buy.  It is both a wonderful re-discovery of the story of the original, and a terrific fast-paced narrative shooter in its own right.  Kudos to the team, and a tiny kudos to Valve for not being jerks and allowing them to get some compensation for all their hard work by letting them sell it on Steam.  Great job, Crowbar Collective!

_childDocuments_.review: Half-Life and it's sequel are my favorite first person shooters. The franchise offers a unique experience to the genre that has yet to be surpassed. I have replayed them hundreds of times!Black Mesa offers an incredible re-imagining of Half-Life. Both in terms of it's gorgeous visuals and spectacular audio. The people who were responsible for it's detailed  environments, sound design and character development are a top notch level of talent! The Crowbar Collective has offered a stellar tribute to one of the greatest games of all  time. I wouldn't change anything about what the game offers in terms of its presentation.What I would change is the most important part of any fps, the combat. The developers have decided against an exact replication of the original game. There certainly is nothing wrong with that choice. In fact I am overjoyed they decided to optimize some of Half-Life's more tedious and unnecessarily long chapters. While this has worked to improve the games pacing, it has hurt a crucial area of it's mechanics.Black Mesa's redesign of the weapons makes fighting enemies far more aggravating. This is partially due to the larger number of enemies that have been included into the new ambush sections. Dealing with these new threats is particularly difficult because the reduced amounts of ammo that can be carried. Also, the damage in certain weapons (Specifically anything using explosives) has been reduced substantially compaired with the arsenal in Half-Life. Let me use the submachine-gun as a perfect example.The SMG from Half-Life One:Ammo: 50 round clip - 250 reserve - 10 grenades. Fairly accurate with a fair amount of recoil that was automatically compensated by Freeman.As anyone knows the amount of ammo and number of guns was reduced significantly from half life one to its sequel. However whatever Valve took away they added something to replace it.The SMG from Half-Life Two:Ammo: 45 round clip - 225 reserve - 3 grenades. Very accurate and faster firing speed with a small amount of recoil that was automatically compensated by Freeman.While we lost a small amount of bullets and large number of grenades, we gained a far more accurate SMG with a higher rate of fire.This is what the SMG looks like in Black Mesa:Ammo: 30 round clip - 150 reserve - 3 grenades. Accurate in small bursts with a fair amount of recoil that is NOT compensated by Freeman. Grenades damage and area of effect was also reduced.By these numbers the new SMG should be pin point accurate, no recoil at all and should fire even faster. The alternative being that the grenades should be at least 2 times more powerful than either of the Half-Life's.While I could certainly go over the issues I have for each of the weapons, I won't.Instead I will offer a quick list of changes that, in my opinion, would make for a better tribute.1: Pistol - Half-Life 2 - Semi-Auto is love, Semi-Auto is life.2: Magnum - Half-Life 2 - Suit Zoom + Accuracy = Head shot.3: SMG - See Above... :-)4: Shotgun - Half- Life 1 - Needs interruptible reload animation.5: Crossbow - Remove the arch, faster reload, 25 ammo.6: RPG - Please fix the laser guidance. Rockets bounce off enemies.7: Explosives - Half-Life 1 level of devastation!8: Exotic Energy Weapons - No issues.9: Xen Weapons - All good.10: Sprinting - Half-Life 1 - Let me sprint in ALL directions.This is one of the times I wish the recommendation system had a mixed option.I LOVE what has been done with the games graphics, sound and characters.Not a big fan of the combat...

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly dont remember the original Half Life having anything like this much platforming, and quite frankly I am no fan of such things in my shooters. Theres also a lot of puzzles that are pretty obtuse just for the sake of lengthening the game (I assume), many of which are pretty much the same thing in different locations.However, its still Half Life and as such Black Mesa is an updated version of a classic. It plays much the same as the original (at least as far as I can remember) and genuinely looks stunning. One of the most problematic parts of HL1 was Xen and here its had less of a face-lift and more of a complete re-imagining. It looks amazing and is one of the most creepily alien environments I have ever seen in a game. Everything from the lighting, the flora and fauna to the sound design screams that you "arent in Kansas any more". When you stumble onto the normality of a human science station or camp it reinforces just how out of place you are. Once again, Xen does fall into the trap of having rather too much in the way of (very similar) puzzles and platforming. I dont mind plugging in machines to unlock my path but when you have done this over and over again it gets a bit much.Anyway, its a worthy remake. It looks fantastic and the world and backstory are just as interesting as they have always been. Shame about the platforming.

_childDocuments_.review: A stunningly beautiful game that breathes fresh life into the already fantastic game Half-Life. This is more than just a remake or a mod, this is the complete rebirth and refinement of Half-Life. With greatly improved combat, incredible visuals and the terrific soundtrack to match, this masterpiece from the Crowbar Collective allows players to either relive the joy of playing Half-Life or to experience it for the first time, but in fantastic quality, with a high-fidelity, well optimised game that honestly is a joy to play. Whether it be crawling through dark vents fighting headcrabs, out in the desert fighting marines or in an alien world fighting who knows what, Black Mesa is a wonderful masterpiece of a game that excels in creating a vibrant and colourful modern version of the original Half-Life game.

_childDocuments_.review: Full disclaimer: I've never played the original Half-Life, but I'm familiar with the story.Black Mesa in one word - grandiose.Story, though not original, is still phenomenal by today's standards.Graphical execution is top notch. And then the F***ING pizza. With sprinkled Source engine physics voodoo on top. There's a special place in hell for people who decide to inflict so much frustration on other people. And this special place is reserved for Half-Life 2: Episode Two's Gnome achievement guys. CC, you've decided to put TWO of those in the same game. Not a short game, by any stretch of the imagination. _childDocuments_.review: I put off playing Black Mesa for a long time, but recently I decided to satisfy my craving for some nostalgia and finally beat Black Mesa. I deeply regret this decision.The Good:The early game is really, really strong and strikes an awesome balance between faithfully recreating the original and polishing some of the rough edges.Some of the enemy and weapon changes really help provide new challenges and new tools to old veteran players, such as the improved soldier AI and the ability to aim down sights with the revolver.The art direction is absolutely gorgeous, especially as you get to Xen.They cut out a pretty massive chunk of On A Rail, which was a brilliant decision on their part. I also think they cut down Surface Tension a little as well, but it may have just been better pacing. Solid improvements on both partsThe Bad:The enemies are absolute damage sponges and it's not unusual to have to spend and entire SMG magazine to kill a single human grunt. The weapons have really, really odd random spread that you have no control over, so accurately placing shots is a near impossibility with the SMG and the shotgun seems to be biased to the lower half of the crosshair around 60% of the time.Sometimes, the damage feels random as well.A lot of the new environment detail makes the maps less readable, since a lot of the interactive switches and doors you need to go through are marked with green lights. This also happens to be the art team's favorite color light to put next to decorative switches that don't do anything.Interloper. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. INTERLOPER. I HOPE YOU LIKE SPENDING A SOLID TWO HOURS RIDING CONVEYOR BELTS, DOING SOURCE ENGINE PLATFORMING, FINDING WEIRD RED BLOB THINGS TO BREAK TO TURN OFF FORCE FIELDS AND FIGHTING WAVES OF ALIEN CONTROLLERS WITH A GLUON GUN WITH INFINITE AMMO ONLY TO SPEND MORE TIME RIDING CONVEYOR BELTS TO FIND MORE RED THINGS TO SMASH TO TURN OFF FORCE FIELDS THIS IS YOUR LIFE NOW READ THIS BIT OVER AND OVER AND OVER FOR THE NEXT TWO HOURS THEY MADE XEN WORSE HOW DID THEY MAKE XEN WORSE HOW DO YOU DO THAT?!?!?!?In summary, Black Mesa starts strong and has a pretty solid middle, but manages to absolutely donk it up at the end making it a very faithful reproduction of the original. Needless to say, I cannot recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: It's worth the $20.Oh my gosh. This game is phenomenal! I had already played everything leading up to Xen on beta, but thought I'd give it a whirl again since I was in the mood to play through Half-Life again - so glad I did! The details they've added throughout the game are incredible, while maintaining the core of the level design, etc. which is what we expect.I was NOT expecting what I found when entering Xen, though. My jaw was literally hanging at almost every turn. I was expecting a more direct port, similar to what they did with the rest of the game - just with updated visuals. I was pleasantly surprised. The levels, the art direction, the execution - everything about it was utterly on-point. This is true of the whole game but the liberties taken stand out more in Xen. The System Shock-escque research base was particularly memorable. After coming back to it, getting to experience the last chapters made it worth the purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: The game that defined FPS shooters as we know them today, but remade to fit modern standards.Spoiler-Free reviewBlack Mesa is a great remake, not always as faithful to the original, but for people who desire Half-Life after finishing them all, this is what you need.Black Mesa is actually comparable to Half-Life 2, due to sharing the same engine, physics engine, things like that. With some few differences. Physics puzzles are lessend due to them not being a focus in Half-Life 1, and the game focuses a lot more on action compared to the previous titles. You are Gordon Freeman, a scientist working at Black Mesa. An important test is scheduled today. But you're late! In your haste you go to the test chamber immediately after putting on your radiation suit named the "HEV". However, the test goes horribly wrong. Perhaps you should've stayed home today. In other words, this story is the exact same as the original Half-Life, with only extremely minor changes to fit the world/gameplay.I am not sure if I should compare this to the previous Half-Life's, or see it as a standalone. Compared to the previous Half-Life's, this game delivers mostly. Not always, but it's got that Half-Life vibe on it. As this is Crowbar Collective's first game, it is quite spectacular.Black Mesa still runs on the Source Engine, and while that keeps the gameplay very faithful, the graphics can only go so far. For Source Engine standards, Black Mesa is beautiful. For modern standards in 2020, it's average. However, this is not meant to be an AAA game, and as such, I believe it's looks really good if you were to call it "Indie". Performance wise however, is a different story. Some parts of the game truly push the Source Engine, and as such, the framerate can't keep up. While 90% of the time it stays above 60, in heavy scenes it can drop to the 40-30s. In the Xen chapter there was even a point where my framerate was at 7 FPS for a short period. For reference my CPU is a i5 3470, and my GPU an GTX 1060.Black Mesa sounds absolutely great. It is a massive update compared to the original Half-Life which uses compressed sounds from the 90s. Use headphones, your ears will thank you.Black Mesa is a great game. Should I call it a Half-Life game though? I am unsure. It's faithfulness is up to debate. Some parts are added to pad out the gameplay, or improve where the original failed, yet I feel like I would've enjoyed this game more if it was even more faithful. I especially felt this at the Xen chapters, where the levels were so much longer than the original game, and so different that it felt like a different game all together. But on the positive side, yeah. This game is wonderful. However, please, play the original Half-Life before this. That's all.This game gets a solid 7.5, the performance issues prevent it from being an 8 or higher. For any future players: Enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game around 2015 expecting to wait maybe a year for Xen to release. Over four years later, after playing through it several times, the game has finally been released from early access, and this game is truly something special. Half-Life is one of my all-time favorite games, but the Goldsrc engine really isn't what it used to be and Half-Life: Source breaks quite a few things. so a modern way to play the game was sorely needed. However, this game isn't just the graphical overhaul most of us were expecting, but is instead a reimagining that improves upon the original in a number of ways while remaining true to the Source material (pun intended). The game is beautiful, simple as that. Despite running on what is essentially a 15 year old engine, the team's efforts to upgrade it shine through with the use of improved shadow maps, impressive modeling, great post-processing effects, and some breathtaking art design. Nowhere is this more apparent than in the long-awaited Xen, where the opening scenery and incredible score left me in utter amazement. It truly is a sight to behold. Probably the most underrated improvement to the game is its revamped combat. Compared to the original and Half-Life 2, Black Mesa's weapons are far more satisfying to use and enemy AI (as of the latest update) is actually challenging to face instead of feeling like bullet-sponges. It is very well-balanced experience that turns the series' weakest aspect into something far more enjoyable. Side note: if you go into the skill.cfg file in the game's directory, you can alter how much ammo the weapons carry. While most of the game is perfectly balanced with the default values, I recommend increasing the MP5's grenade count to 5 to afford you a little more freedom in using the game's most satisfying alt-fire.As for Xen, the team took the most questionable chapters of the original and reworked them into some of the most exciting set pieces in the entire game. Aside from the aforementioned graphical improvements, the gameplay and level design is all incredible, with the exceptions of a few overly-long sequences in interloper. This is where Black Mesa takes the most creative liberties when compared to the rest of the game, undoubtedly for the better, as the original Xen chapters were more of boring endurance test that could be knocked out in 30 minutes. This game is great. The few faults that can be levied against it are almost entirely products of the game's roots, and even the most die-hard Half-Life purist would be hard-pressed to complain about the changes that are made. In conclusion, ♥♥♥♥ first-person platforming.

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa is an FPS developed by Crowbar Collective, and the Definitive Edition was released in 2020.This is the Source Engine Remake of the cult first Half-Life published in 1998.The least we can say is that the talented developers have masterfully revisited Valve's masterpiece.The great scenario of the game originally written by Marc Laidlaw remains unchanged.The player embodies Gordon Freeman, a brilliant scientist recently graduated from M.I.T., working at the Black Mesa Research Center in New Mexico.During an experiment aimed at analyzing a crystal of unknown origin,an immense catastrophe of unprecedented scale occurred: a resonance cascade.Dimensional portals open here and there from which unfriendly aliens emerge.The army was called in to help stop the invasion, but seems determined to cover up the whole affair.You must do everything to try to get out of there, help your colleagues in difficulty, and destroy what is at the origin of this disaster...Black Mesa lives by Half-Life's motto of "Run, Think, Shoot, Live."The game retains the charm of yesteryear, oscillating between combat, reflection, and platform making it original.Unlike the sadly unloved Half-Life Source, Black Mesa is not a simple port of the first Half-Life to the Source Engine.Although the maps, enemies and plot are similar, the developers have taken some liberties, refreshing the original work.The very essence of the game is respected, and even embellished in many areas.The pace of the combat is much more frantic, the shootouts are dynamic to say the least.Some complex sequences have been simplified, while others have been largely redesigned.The game has a much more elaborate and spectacular staging than its glorious ancestor, and sometimes offers great moments of bravery.We are amazed at every moment, since the effect of nostalgia is enhanced by all the new things.Half-Life has never been more beautiful and immersive than in Black Mesa.The game pushes the limits of the ancient but still very effective Source Engine.The graphics are sublime, the lighting and reflections magnificent, the particle effects striking… The weapons become covered in blood when you pulverize an enemy in close combat, the game can be very gory, almost giving the impression of playing a modern version of Brutal Half-Life.The game accentuates its connection with the other illustrious Half-Life games, by borrowing various elements from them, including gameplay mechanics.It's possible to pick up various objects to clear your path, to burn Zombies using flares, to look for a valve to place on its support in order to use it, to reconnect a cable to a socket, to launch a flammable barrel on the tongue of the Barnacles so that it explodes once it reaches their mouth... The sprint system and the flashligt are similar to Half-Life 2, except that they no longer drain the battery of the H.E.V. Suit.The NPCs are much more numerous and detailed than in the past.First of all, scientists have a plethora of models, including female ones for the first time.Female scientists should have appeared in Half-Life 1, but only a few leftovers remain in the Half-Life Alpha and Half-Life Source files.The models of security guards are also much more diverse and better armed.Indeed, if they are often equipped with their famous pistol, some have revolvers and even shotguns! From time to time you can even lead a small squad of "Barneys" and Scientists.These valuable allies often interact with each other and have new lines of dialogue, in addition to those already well known.Some recognizable characters and elements now appear in Black Mesa.Gordon meets the likeable Issac Kleiner and Eli Vance early in the game.Vortigaunts communicate the same way as in Half-Life 2. Galanga!Don't forget Dr. Magnusson’s famous "microwave casserole"…The enemies are essentially the same as in Half-Life, but with models that resemble some of those in Half-Life 2, including their animations.In addition to the already well-known Xen creatures (including the iconic Headcrabs, the intelligent Vortigaunts, the fierce Bullsquids and many others), Black Mesa introduces :the Zombie Torso previously seen in Half-Life 2,the Zombie Security Guards and H.E.C.U. coming straight from Opposing Force and Blue Shift,two new variants of Houndeyes, the first one is explosive and kamikaze, while the second is a larger and beefier,and a sort of underwater Barnacle, undoubtedly drawing inspiration from the unfinished Sand Barnacle from Half-Life 2 Beta.The Military H.E.C.U. and Black Ops are as tough as ever, and can give you a hard time.They communicate constantly, attack in groups and are not there to make up the numbers.Female Assassins are extremely agile and flawlessly precise, and have the same Long-Fall Boots as the protagonist of Portal 1 and 2, Chell ! Additionally, there may be enemies where there were none in the original game.Black Mesa is much larger than before, and teeming with life and little details that will delight even the biggest fans.The weapons are exactly the same as in Half-Life, but are not necessarily picked up in the same place.Some have a few difference differences in their gameplay, such as:The 357 Magnum has an Iron Sight, similar to Half-Life 1 in multiplayer.The crossbow has a real scope at the scope, making it more practical and more realistic.However, all those guns seem much more powerful and impactful, giving a more dynamic combat feeling than in the past.The last part of the game, taking place in the "Border World" Xen, has been completely remade.The artistic direction is totally original and splendid, it's a perpetual visual feast.It almost feels like we're on the planet Pandora from the Avatar, one of James Cameron's masterpieces of the Seventh Art.This alien universe is adorned with its most beautiful shimmering colors, mixing caves worthy of HL2: Episode Two, lush jungles, and settings similar to the abyss. The firmament is covered with clouds of sparkling stars and a multitude of celestial objects.This ecosystem made up of several biomes is teeming with life and details of the highest quality.The flora is colorful, accentuating the exoticism of this distant land.The local fauna is variegated, and while Boids fly peacefully in the skies, other species are much more harmful.The aliens that we slay throughout the game are there have new variants.The Vortigaunts are much more surprising beings than we might think at first glance...Some areas are very industrialized and mechanical, while others are tribal and primitive, like in the Oddworld games.Xen contains traces of human activities, there are some installations and devices of all kinds.The original soundtrack by Joel Nielsen is simply masterful. It magnificently accentuates the feeling of strangeness and drama of the events suffered by Gordon Freeman with quite calm and mysterious sounds. During the fights, the music is very rock or orchestral and emphasizes the epic feeling of this atypical and mythical sci-fi shooter.On Xen, the music is as unique as it's breathtaking, composed of captivating sounds and exquisite lyrical female vocalizations.Black Mesa respects the authenticity of Half-Life by providing it with the necessary new features and accessibility.Newcomers will love the intriguing storyline, the masterfully orchestrated staging, and its anthology sequences.While veterans of the Half-Life franchise who have completed the first game countless times will appreciate the improved graphics, realistic physics, dynamic combat, subtle references to other episodes, and all the elements brought by this remake. The original work from 1998 is in no way stripped of its charm and is brilliantly modernized, with a delicious touch of fan service added.This is a must-have game.

_childDocuments_.review: Making this edit for the Steam Awards 2020. I'm impressed they continue to update this game and making it even better. Truly the definitive Half-Life 1 experience. It's been 5 long years waiting for Xen, and I'd have to say it was worth the wait! Not only is Xen longer than the original, it introduces many new things including new enemies. Pretty much the entirety of Xen was redone and it is fantastic. Not only that they also touched up the Earthbound levels and improved the AI of the soldiers and Vortiguants. My only complaint is that in the original Nihilanth fight he could throw teleporter orb things at you which would tele you to one of I believe 3 different areas. You would have to fight enemies, find supplies, and find the teleporter back. The new Nihilanth doesn't do that. Oh well, not a huge deal considering how much bigger Xen is. They also gave us 3 different ways to deal with the Gonarch whereas in the original you could only shoot it to death.Now is the time to buy and play this, or replay it if you already own it. One of the best shooters of all time now remade even better and finally complete.  everything that made Half-Life the classic it is today, and the few things missing are greatly overshadowed by everything else which is improved. You've got much better graphics, better sounds, really awesome reskinned guns, and the same level layout we all remember and love.**A few areas have been slightly redesigned and some long, drawn out areas have been shortened seamlessly. Ultimately not a big deal to me, especially since there's workshop mods you can download that restore the cut areas.The main thing I didn't like was the new voice acting. It's all right, I just prefer the original. I also prefer the music of the original but the new music here is good too.It should be noted that currently the game only goes up to the portal that sends you to Xen; Xen will be finished at a later date and added to the game for free (of course). What is here is still many hours of fun with the promise of more to come! Also there's multiplayer but I didn't mess with that.So is this game worth $20? It's a complete reimagining of Half-Life, FAR more than a simple graphics mod. Therefore yes I feel it's worth it, especially if you're a huge fan of the Half-Life series and want more.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first Steam review, because I really think this game deserves more praise. The developers took the original Half Life and applied an amazing fresh coat of paint; bringing the game into the modern era near seamlessly. if I had to level any criticism towards Black Mesa, it would be regarding Xen. The updated version of the final chapters of HL1 is visually staggering, a real beauty to look at, and the gameplay is generally solid - I absolutely adore the Gonarch fight in particular. Outside of that, though, it suffers in several places from heavy repetition. "Do X thing 3 times to progress" is used in no less than 4 places before the end. Once or twice is fine, but done to this extent, it really felt like padding.In my mind, this is the definitive way to experience HL1. If you've never played and want to see what all the fuss was about, or want to experience the classic again in a brand new way, Black Mesa is the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a staggering achievement.As I rode the tram into the Black mesa Complex, I felt the old magic, the same way I did when I was a much younger, more innocent man, playing Half life 1 on a computer that likely couldn't interface with the internet today.The scale of the game is unequaled in an FPS. Black Mesa Complex is huge, and Xen, ever bigger.  It's not for show either, the player maintains a sense of moving through the world.Now however, the visuals resemble those of the games successor Half Life 2,  which arguably ranks among the greatest first person shooters of all time, and has aged like a fine wine thanks to the love and dedication of it's community.  The image was widescreen 1080p, textures are updated...  but it was HALF LIFE, and I felt like I had left Kansas once again.Crowbar Collective have made a faithful update toHalf Life 1 that inspires the same sense of awe and wonder that I felt the first time I stepped into Gordon's HEV suit.They haven't made it a full "AAA" style update with pointless graphic features, Mo-Cap and animated every little thing. The interactivity is as high as Valve ever made it, imo, no one was better.  However, the game loses NOTHING without all the bells and whistles of a modern production.  If anything Black Mesa feels even more immersive without those distractions, and runs wonderfully, likely even on lower tier systems.The overall effect highlights the absolute genius of Valve during their heyday, a development team who did nearly EVERYTHING right, and deserves all the good fortune, accolades and wealth that they've garnered in successive years. Simultaneously, the brilliance and devotion of Crowbar Collective, who made it their mission to faithfully update one of the most immersive, beloved gaming experiences of all time for modern audiences, is on full display.Side note, Black Mesa is a Master Class in how modern developer's should treat classic properties, they have not "reimagined" the experience, subjected it to the whims of modern politics or taken excessive creative liberties. Crowbar Collective's love and devotion for the original title shines through on everything they've done, and I am grateful.To people who have never played HL1, do yourself a favor, and play this, and while you are doing so, marvel at how many things you have seen in other games found their origin here, and in many cases, failed to live up to Valve's Timeless creation.Then play Half Life 2, and you will understand why  legions of devoted fans are still so perplexed and frustrated  that Valve Never released half Life 3 and finished Gordons story.  (No matter how brilliant it is, ALYX does NOT count).  You will understand why even to this day, 15 years after HL2, there are still those who dare to hope.Don't miss this.  Worth it at twice the price.(apparently, they have added at ton of additional content, MP and custom maps.  I am not sure, but it can only make the game BETTER)20 out of 10, go grab your crowbars.Addendum:Perhaps the only subpar section of the original game, underwhelming after what was an outstanding Adventure, it felt like Valve rushed through Xen.The same clever puzzles were there, interaction and combat wise, it was a worthy ending to the title.Visually however, Xen was a disappointment in half life.NOT ANYMORE.After I passed through the Lambda portal, I knew I was in for a treat, hell, the visuals from the portal itself are jaw-dropping...  and perhaps i was misremembering, but the level itself is MASSIVE, alternating between puzzles, combat, platforming and running for your life.Crowbar Collective has improved on every aspect of Black Mesa's Final chapter.The entirety of the realm feels alien, yet believable.  Weird and wonderful, everywhere you look you are greeted with pure visual spectacle, surreal, deadly eye candy.The Flora and Fauna are believable, with the exception of the entirely gravity defying nature of the landscape, but I suppose that's part of Xen's phantasmagoric allure.  Despite this, it still comes across as a believable biome, the various monsters that had tormented you on your journey through the Black Mesa complex are shown in reasonable context, intrinsic parts of the environment, both in locomotive capability, and camouflage.  The creatures appearances and offensive capabilities are explained, without a single word, by their unnatural habit.The environmental puzzles that allowed Gordon Freeman to Weave his way through the Black Mesa complex also exist in Xen, I have to commend the developers on the fact that none of it felt obvious, the pathways you would need to take to get where you were going are intrinsic parts of the environment, they look like they belong there, not that they merely exist to facilitate Gordon's Passage.The sound design is fantastic, blending the odd noises of the creatures with further environmental sounds, creating the impression of an alien rainforest, brimming with life, and very much seeking to take yours.Xen's natural properties explain why Black Mesa was so interested in researching the place, both for it's levitating materials, as well as elements of a natural origin which were capable of generating tremendous electrical (and otherwise) energy.I recommend moving cautiously through the area, visually identifying Environmental hazards, and how to use them on your enemies. Even on medium difficulty, ammo is scarce.There are a few surprises, and I'm going to leave it at that.Like every other part of the game, the completion of a puzzle leaves you with a tremendous feeling of satisfaction....  it's an added bonus, that the entire time you are more than happy to stop and take in the scenery.No one has done first person puzzle-platforming better.The Gonarch is the Gold standard for boss fights. Nihilanth is also fantastic.

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa is a Half-Life 1 remake which has been around for many years now but its completion nearly turned into a sheetstorm (!) due to never-ending development process of Xen chapters. Although calling this game a remake may not do justice to the game itself but since developers themselves also call it a remake, we can safely proceed doing so, albeit I’d like to call it more like a reimagining.Black Mesa was first released in 2012 as a free mod, then it arrived in Steam in 2015, but last three chapters of the game, which are called “Xen chapters” were missing. Until very recently, the game was ending in the final chapter of Lambda Core, which we depart from Black Mesa Research Facility and get teleported into the alien Xen world for 5 years, but March 2020 saw the completion of Xen chapters and release 1.0 was finally with the gamers. I was only able to complete these new episodes very recently, partly because of the ongoing pandemic since March 2020 around the globe.As to talk some about the already-present parts of the game since 2015, Black Mesa really managed to capture the spirit of original Half-Life and carried it forward. Since Black Mesa is a reimagining of a game from a bygone age, in which the games seldom took the players’ hand and carried them forward, it had difficult chapters compared to today’s standards. However, carefully sculpted chapters from tip to tail, heavy atmosphere brought by the game’s story and Half-Life’s world which started as an extremely ordinary day morphing into complete chaos were brought to life very exquisitely.Meanwhile, I’d like to give a brief summary about the game’s story, since the game is now 22 years old and some of the people here were not even born yet then. Black Mesa Research Facility is a high-tech underground research laboratory (there really is a mesa there in the real world in New Mexico). You are playing as a 27-year-old scientist called Gordon Freeman, who is already late to a very unusual experiment that day. After a train ride and changing outfits, getting into the iconic HEV – Hazardous Environment Suit and greeting your fellow colleagues, you enter the giant experiment room where the Anti-Mass Spectrometer device is located. This is where all the ordinary and normal parts of the game end. As soon as you start the experiment, portals start to open to an unknown world and unidentified creatures storm the facility. After this event, which is called as a “resonance cascade” in the game, you get up and try to find your way out of this giant facility as one of the few survivors. After some time you learn that military has arrived to the facility but your hopes of rescue shatter to pieces when you understand they are not here to help exactly but to silence any and all personnel in the facility, primarily you, so all hell starts to break loose.I’d like to emphasize something about Xen chapters without too much detail. The most boring parts which I have avoided to play in the original game that I have finished numerous times were the Xen chapters in the original Half-Life. But Black Mesa transformed the Xen chapters to another level, also the recently added three chapters nearly equal the length of all the previous chapters which are around since 2015, such is the magnitude of these new maps.Of course some people will be bored to death of the repetitive puzzles after a while but Half-Life was a puzzle game as much as it was action-packed. As someone who remembers and gets frustrated by the puzzles from the original Xen chapters, I can say I find Black Mesa’s puzzle mechanics much more feasible.Graphical capabilities of this game which runs on Source engine is seriously extraordinary. Black Mesa was not looking this good when it first came out but the developer team made many corrections, additions and lighting improvements in the following years and the chapters which take place in the facility itself are already looking great compared to today’s standards, but the environment of Xen chapters is really breathtaking (of course not as much as Keanu Reeves). I stopped in my tracks and gazed around the endless space with colors and void too many times in the first chapter, which is also named “Xen”.From the new enemies developed from scratch by Crowbar Collective to many altered chapter designs, Black Mesa not only gives credit to its predecessor and original, but stands tall in the shoulders of the already solid Half-Life legacy, raising the bar further. Newly composed soundtrack for this game is really successful and captures the spirit of original game, which is available on different platforms like YouTube and Spotify.Caution with mild spoilers here. I want to talk about Gonarch and Nihilanth, who are the bosses of new Xen chapters. Gonarch battle is much longer than the original, some people complained about this, but I really liked it. Some of the pursuit scenes are forced and the fact that Gonarch is invulnerable in many of those moments can easily escape the player, causing them to waste ammo, but playing hide and seek with this gigantic, single balled creature surely created a feeling of struggle which was definitely absent in the original game.Nihilanth is ultimately more majestic than how he was in original Half-Life, like he is supposed to be, since he is the endgame boss after all. Entire battle with Nihilanth really gives the vibes that this is the endgame boss and you have reached the ultimate end of the journey. Also, they removed his frustrating ability of teleporting player out of the room, instead they blessed him with many different abilities which he uses in various phases according to his remaining health, lower the health, higher the abilities. This really helped Nihilanth to become the ultimate endgame boss Half-Life had deserved in the first place.About the insanely criticized Interloper chapter, I must say that I got tired in some places of that chapter too. Repetitively jumping from conveyer to conveyor, plugging the sockets, avoiding the lasers, shutting the shields down; all of these mundane tasks almost killed the pace, particularly nearing the end of the chapter. But many people do not know that Interloper was always a chapter like this in the original game. On the contrary to the public opinion, I actually thank Black Mesa dev team for Interloper because the newly introduced mechanics and the final elevator section of the chapter, which is the penultimate encounter before the endgame boss really jolted my brain, which was getting numb because of the repetitive puzzles throughout this long chapter, and sprung me back to action. They also hinted players the mechanics of the crystals they need to take care of in Nihilanth fight with smaller crystals protecting the Controllers throughout the episode here, something which the original game never did and caused some awkward situations in the predecessor Half-Life. So, that elevator literally ascends you to the final boss of the game and game itself throws everything it has at you to make you aware of that fact. Of course, that section may be several leagues out of reach of today’s players who are used to getting everything they need on a silver platter, but this is the real deal here anyway, you are playing an old legend, updated to today’s standards.For closure, Black Mesa surely helped thousands of people from new generation who were never able to play Half-Life when it came out and never would have played it otherwise due to really outdated graphics compared to our day. It deserves praise only because of that, but the fact that the game itself independently is very solid and well-detailed from the graphics to voice acting, soundtrack, sound engineering, designs, undulant atmosphere, fine details and easter eggs really requires a salute and applause to devs for the immense effort they put into this game and transforming it into a masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: Still in Beta but practically finished end to end, Black Mesa is a modern remake of Half-Life. Starting out as an ambitious project for a group of modders back in the mid-2000s to being one of the first Greenlight games for Steam's platform, it has been worked on for many years. Some of the development team, now known as the Crowbar Collective, have come and gone and many hands have touched it but their combined work has actually paid off.Black Mesa, treads in the footsteps of the classic, genre-changing, Valve game Half-Life. It is a mix of horror, action, exploration, and puzzle solving as you shoot your way through the underground facility that has been invaded by inter-dimensional beings. A lengthy single-player game taking roughly 13-17 hours on a first playthrough but it can be finished in just under 12 hours. The devs have streamlined some of the more tedious chapters, which helps with the pacing, but they've also gone to town on others such as Surface Tension and the later levels set in off-world. Generally the maps are larger which aids in showing off the size and scope of the facility. The chapter Lambda Core, for example, contains towering equipment that thuds into life as you clamber maintenance ladders to scale it. Other areas contain huge aircraft hangers and large storage warehouses. However, some maps are, at times, a bit too open. This causes the tight, frantic, in your face, close combat from Half-Life to get a bit lost and you feel exposed to enemies. For a Source engine game it looks incredible. The devs have done some true witchcraft and improved lighting with better shadow maps, colour correction, dynamic lighting, god-rays, lens flares and other more modern tricks. The use of particle effects, cinematic physics, smoke and fog create a visual stunning game at times. They've squeezed what they can out of the old engine. The final chapters have had huge amount of work put into the environments and through iteration Xen feels completely different to it's original levels. Much of the teams focus appears to have gone into the visuals and details of the facility and they've used Valve's method of environmental story telling very well.Sound is generally good across the board. Weapons are punchy and have good bass, ambient noises are great in most levels, the soundtrack is very good and at times brilliant. Voice acting is very close to Half-Life. Black Mesa has kept the eccentric scientist voices and friendly guards with only one or two voices that don't quite cut it. The HECU marines sound more human but unfortunately don't always use their audio barks so firefights involving them can feel deathly quiet or muffled. Clear audio barks from enemies can inform the player where the enemies are and what they are doing. They cause a sense of anticipation but are also memorable. Across the board though, when the sound design all comes together it creates some fantastic moments.The majority of set pieces are as enjoyable as in Half-Life. A good amount are vastly superior. The unforgiving insta-death moments of the original game are gone, but there are still some lethal trial and error gameplay. I've found that the Black Mesa devs have been heavily inspired, almost to the point of downright ripping some scenes, puzzles and moments from other Valve games and also DOOM 2016. It may be done in homage as there are only a few, but there are times when you think, "This is like Portal 2, this is from Episode 1, this looks very familiar etc". The devs have however have been creative and improved areas with their own ideas. There is a sniper section that plays out nicely and incorporates some tricks, and the final boss battle is enjoyable. Throughout the game you may notice slightly different levels of polish, this is due to some chapters being expanded or re-added and others have come later in the cycle. Notoriously Xen has been left until last. It plays like a Greatest Hits of what the team can do. It could almost survive on it's own and mainly it flows really well. The Interloper chapter is the least polished but was also last to be completed. Xen, Gonarch's Lair, and Nihilanth play out better and perform smoother. The game is still in beta and is being worked on. I do hope that they can revisit the chapters set on Earth as some need a bit of a touch up. I also hope they can look at Residue Processing as it is a carbon copy and still a chore riding conveyor belts with perilous falls. The puzzles in Black Mesa usually revolve around solving an access issue, this could be locked doors due to a loss of power or something is blocking your way or a grate that needs opening with a wheel. Most of the puzzles are placed for a bit of downtime and generally you don't think twice about them. However, later in the game and the final chapters repetition does set in. Another cable puzzle is presented or you have to do something three times to activate a sequence. It's hard to invent new puzzles and to be fair the Half-Life series popularised them, but when a goal is in sight and puzzle room behind a vent is in the way, eye rolling can occur.So there are some improvements with Black Mesa. I feel some music tracks play too early or don't quite represent what is onscreen. The helicopter fights need to give more openings to shoot back. The AI of enemies and some animations do need a bit of a rework. The HECU now have a tendency to charge you and relentless fire, which for hitscan enemies cause you to hold back behind cover. They also have some problems navigating around objects or can run back and forth between the same location. Little moments do stand out and engagements can feel odd as enemies get stuck in two minds. It's partially down to level design but also something seems off in the programming. Shootouts can suddenly devolve and you feel a bit deflated as they didn't... quite... get out of first gear.I will commend the work done in later chapters as the devs have utilised early game enemies, such as Barnacles and Headcrabs, in creative ways. For experienced Half-Life players there are a few surprises. I believe that if some more work is put into the animations to help telegraph what actions the enemies will carry out and if timing of their attacks are changed it will give the player opportunity to move around like an old FPS. Better pathfinding, looking at some sound issues, and changing enemy start positions could improve the feel. It may appear slightly antiquated but also tried and tested.Regardless of the above nitpicks but I would definitely recommend Black Mesa based on the quality of other released games. With one or two more patches and bug fixes and it could be a true, polished, gem.

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa is clearly a loving recreation of a beloved game that will spur all kinds of memories and, at times, amaze in the way the original did back in 1998 with inspired and beautiful new maps, creature designs, and content. Ultimately, however, the game overstays its nostalgic welcome and loses a player's goodwill by becoming an endurance test in tedium.The signs of the international developing team Crowbar Collective's taste for maximalism show themselves early, but are sugarcoated by both the inherent positivity toward a group of volunteer fans undertaking such a project and by graphics I consider gorgeous. The first clue is that the tram ride that kicks off the game is noticeably longer than Half-Life's version, and seemingly with good reason: There is so much to look at in this vision of the Black Mesa facility. The facility throughout the Earth portion of the game appears much more vibrant and alive than technology allowed it to be when the original game was released. The scientists and guards have not only a wider variety of faces and expressions but carry on conversations with one another hinting at underlying individual personalities which really adds to the increased immersion factor this improved engine wielded by dedicated designers can provide.It would be irrational and childish of me not to give credit where it's due, and until the Interloper level on Xen, I was going to give this game a "Recommended" rating with major reservations. There has been so much work done on expanding this world and making it so much better and bigger, to flesh out what could only have been fleshed out in our imaginations back in 1998.Xen itself, as a setting and not a portion of the game, is the most impressive reimagining. What was once bland, seemingly lifeless and disappointing in the original fleshes out into an alien wilderness that is a joy to explore and examine. The artists and art designers in this project have done great work.The kitchen sink approachThe problem here, though, is that the developers outside the art department did not know where and when to stop (not including whoever was responsible for the vastly improved long-jumping mechanic). This game is about taking Half-Life to levels and heights these true fans always believed it deserved, but at the cost of cohesion and, yes, fun.Black Mesa was in development for fifteen years. It’s not just the extraordinary length of the development that calls to mind Duke Nukem Forever, but the final product. This could be called a “kitchen sink game,” since the developers clearly believed there was not only room in the mix for every idea over that 15-year period, but for the grandest possible imagining of every one of them.There is no balance. Every aspect of this game has been jacked up to the point of overload that I found myself playing without joy after the sixth or seventh hour. Artistically-rendered environments were let down by the unprofessional designers' knack for "improving" the game by turning it into Doom 2016, but with guns of obviously diminishing power (or the hit points of opponents so artificially and suddenly boosted from level to level) as to be a frustrating slog.I had seen development notes talk about the expanded environments and increased enemy counts being there to inspire a player to "slow down" and become more tactical, but the experience belies that intent. Enemies throughout the game move like hell-inspired speed freaks, forcing the player character to run and gun and NOT take cover. In several instances, the game presented characters far away, clearly calling for a long-range weapon but undermining that inspiration for tactics because the NPCs were moving like Benny Hill on fast forward. This makes hitting them with a weapon like the revolver or the bow, with their low rate of fire and slow reload times, a Sisyphean task that leaves you feeling empty of spirit.Puzzle me NOTMore glaring than the joyless enemy encounters, though, are the puzzles. Half-Life jumping puzzles were often a nuisance then (as first-person games naturally leave you in the dark about exact body positioning), but Crowbar Collective must have found the puzzles of the original the ONE aspect of the game to really double—no, quadruple down on. I already found the recreations of the original jumping puzzles a bit of a bore that hurt game pacing and led to needless frustration, but the new ones in Black Mesa make this the least enjoyable gaming experience I have had in memory. To call what you find, especially in the closing levels in Xen, "puzzles" would be to throw the definition of the word out the window. A puzzle requires a goal or a motivation, and this game's "puzzles" leave the player character totally in the dark. Without any idea what your goal or motivation is, you will find yourself Mr. Magoo-ing your way through hours and hours of repetitive and miserable busy work.While it could be argued that Xen’s factory is such a nightmare to operate in and is so epic in scope because that promotes the alienness of the environment, that misses the point. This is a game meant to be enjoyed, not a real-life scientific scouting expedition to compare notes on corporate and industrial design. To make an argument that the game was designed with plausibility in mind would also ignore why a PhD in theoretical physics from one of the world’s elite universities attempts to solve an interdimensional catastrophe with the same tactics a drunk couch potato takes in fixing a TV on the fritz: pummel it until something happens. But that’s what Gordon Freeman does because it’s a game.  Here is the only hint you need: Shoot everything and push every button, and if something big isn't happening yet, then jump on things or shoot things that you didn't know you could, then you'll be firing on all cylinders and ready for the next several hours of pain.Quality control problemsThe pain of exhaustion is exacerbated by the lack of quality control. If the game is to have this many puzzles, then more polish is needed for traversing the obstacle. It does not feel smooth to move in the more precarious puzzle scenarios in this world and it especially does not feel smooth when encountering a terrain clipping area following a loading screen. Save often, because you’ll never know when you’ll have to revert to an earlier save through no fault of your own after you became glued to the floor because you didn’t stand in the right place just before an unexpected loading screen. There are also glaring errors that show scripted happenings, too. You cannot kill the Gonarch until after it has chased you—seemingly for hours—into its final den. Don’t waste ammo shooting its sac until the final arena. I know this to be true because I got to a section where it couldn’t reach me and emptied all of my ammunition into the sac to no effect. In the final section, I killed it without difficulty.ConclusionThere is a philosophy in design, and art in general, about highlighting. If every scene and every encounter is a set piece, then none of it is. Not every part can be the best part, because if every enemy encounter is huge and every puzzle is epic, then none of them stand out as exemplary moments in the experience.Look at my hours invested: More than 20. Look at the hours invested by many of the more positive reviews. I, too, was enjoying the game with rose-tinted nostalgia for the first four or five hours, but found not new innovation but repetition and bigness for bigness's sake with each new hour. Black Mesa is less than the sum of its largely impressive parts and serves primarily as an object lesson that "more" and "bigger" do not mean better.

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10Black Mesa is nothing short of incredible; An ode to Half-Life fans, and a showcase of pure talent from dedicated developers Crowbaw Collective. 16 years in the making, Black Mesa not only faithfully recreates the chapters and events of the first game, it expands upon them; adding alternate routes, completely redesigned level spaces, unique NPC dialogues upon completing objectives with or without them, among others. But ignoring everything short of Lambda Core, Crowbar Collective went above and beyond for Part 2 of Black Mesa's launch; the release of the Xenian chapters. With this, not only would Black Mesa finally be complete, but Xen would be recreated from the ground up in a completely unique art style, blending cosmic fantasy with eldritch overtones. While many complained of Xen in Half-Life for it's bland, rushed development that showed; the opposite can be said of the new Xen. It is fleshed out, expanded upon with new regions like the Vortigaunt Ghettos, and lives up to what I imagined Valve initially envisioned in 1998. TLDR: Black Mesa is a modern masterpiece, both with it's storied development over the course of nearly two decades, to the game's faithful, yet phenomenally creative take on the Xenian chapters. You might as well consider this canon, because this is the most faithful Half-Life game ever made.

_childDocuments_.review: Ah, Black Mesa: Source. The original mod that I followed since post Half-Life 2 release. Constantly winning "vaporware" awards, it released years later to people like myself that never stopped believing.This IS the hands-down best way to play the original Half-Life (unless you need to have the old school textures/polygons, which is understandable).I really only have a few nitpicky criticisms of Black Mesa: Source (the original title until Valve made 'em change it).1) The Source engine physics present are kind of "Source-engine-lite," if that makes sense. If you've recently played HL2 and then play this, you can experience it for yourself. This may have been a strict design decision to not deviate too far from the original source (pun unitended) material.2) Interacting with objects/clutter feels choppy & janky. To pick something up or interact with an object, you have to get really, really close and make sure your reticule is targetting exactly what you want to interact with. This really shows its ugly head when multiple items are atop of one another3) There isn't a dialog volume option, unfortunately. During sequences where contextual music plays, it often drowns out any dialog that NPCs are expressing. There IS a music volume slider, however, but I'm reluctant to turn it down becuase the score is excellent.4) Movement can feel too "floaty," especially when you are trying to precision crouch-jump or hop onto that thin metal girder.5) Well, I have to say it out of principle: Xen, the second-half of the game is still missing (BUT IT'S ON THE WAY!!!)Beyond the above, Black Mesa: Source ***ABSOLUTELY*** belongs in your Steam library. It's fantastic, it stays true to the original, and is an overall great expereince to play!
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: While not a direct port of Half-Life, Black Mesa does well to remake all of the wonders and highlights of Half-Life, while following it as closely as necessary. As a veteran of Half-Life, I would highly recommend this to anyone after playing the original, as it is a beautiful game and definitely worth the time and money spent. Only complaints would be that the final chapters of Xen and the occasional Surface Tension map would run poorly on my PC. In addition to this, recent changes to the game in my opinion don't make it better and just bloat the game's playtime (minus a few exceptions). It's definitely not a Half-Life Remaster, but it's a very fun remake that felt like I was playing Half-Life for the first time.rip black mesa beta glock noise, you will be missed

_childDocuments_.review: WOW. Over and over I kept saying "WOW." This was so well done - different enough from the original half life game that it was a whole new adventure, but similar enough that you were reminiscing. Valve would be proud! I hate to say this out of respect for Valve, but Xen was better than the original.The original half life Xen was a little too weird sometimes. I know, it was supposed to be fantasy/alien/out of this world, but Black Mesa Xen I think really outdid themselves in balancing the fantasy/alien factor with a little more logic for the puzzles and the experience in what you saw and had to do. The graphics and gameplay were phenomenal. The musical scores were not just appropriate, but inspirational and added so much to the game. *Spoiler alerts*Nice touch with the hazard suit zombies.

_childDocuments_.review: I've never played the original Half-Life so this won't be a comparison review. The graphics are modern compared to some of the screen shots I've seen of the original game. I'd say they look like a game that came out in the 2010's. Some of the later areas in Xen look gorgeous but suffer some frame-rate issues and lag even on a 1080ti but I did have all the graphics cranked up. It's a re-imagining of one of the grand-daddies of First Person Shooters. Fundamentally, you shoot things, find new weapons, solve puzzles, and do some light platforming. There are some intense firefights with some decent AI that hides behind cover, and tries to flank you. The couple boss fights were well developed and had a good amount of difficulty. The voice overs for the NPC scientists and guards are fine, nothing great but they sound like they were done by the same voice actor. The music that plays during some of the more intense moments and in the Xen chapters are excellent. Something I'd actually want to hear outside of the game. I particularly liked the otherworldly tranquil feel of the Xen music.I decided to get this game because I saw it on sale and wanted to immerse myself into the Half-Life universe prior to starting up the new Alyx game in VR. The game has a lot more play time than I expected for an FPS single player experience. Even though this is a remake of a classic, I can see how the original disrupted and changed the industry. Crowbar Collective did a superb job modernizing Half-Life for today's audience!2 thumbs up!

_childDocuments_.review: Long awaited, definitely worth the wait. Combines both beauty and quality game length. Hands down the most beautiful FPS-game I ever played (especially the final half). Also can't remember last time post year 2000 that I ever played an FPS-game-campaign longer than this (25+ hours straight). Kept being surprised that they still had more quality content. Can't see that there will ever be a better, more well-made Half-Life game released after this. This has its own spot on the pedestal. 16 years is a long time, but given the magnitude of this ginormous game and the level of detail; it's time well spent.  Deepest thanks to the Half-Life team - what a fantastic job and such a blessing! Warmest recommendations --- enjoy !

_childDocuments_.review: A gorgeous remastering of the original half life. In development for an extremely long time, but finally finished and definately worth the wait.Black Mesa is not simple a reskin of the original half life, it does look less out dated than it's previous form, but that is the smallest difference in comparison to what crowbar collective have managed to accomplish.The devs have faithfully recreated and improved parts of the original game that were considered to be brilliant, most early levels, especially those within the labs, have been kept almost identical but with beautiful improvements and clear attention to detail, such as scientists conversations being changed and improved, labs being more detailed than they originally were, and a much better sense of world building than the original.Later into the game changes have varied from small improvements, to total reworks of previously boring areas such as certain military zones and especially Xen, which is completely unrecognisable and incredibly enjoyable.Pros:1.Significant graphical improvement (yes it still looks outdated by todays standards but not in comparison to the original half life)2.Great level rework, fleshing out more dud areas such as the lambda laboratory in half life which was pretty boring considering how much of an important part of the story it was meant to be.3.Excellent gun play, guns feel alot nicer to use than in the original, the only feature I found strange was being able to ADS with the revolver, but since this was the only gun with that added feature it wasn't too unfaithful to the original, guns are simply made to feel more powerful and enjoyable to use, especially the gluon cannon.4.Nice animation updates, a clear sprinting animation, nicer jumping and pretty reload animations to top it off.5.The ending Unfotunately not all is pretty, there are some unfortunate issues that hopefully can be fixed in time.Cons:1.Bugs, there are quite alot of bugs specifically to do with enemies, some get stuck in walls, they don't seem to move from their original spawn locations like they were meant to e.g. the 2.Xen is abit too long. The creation of Xen was beautiful for sure, the world was fleshed out lovely and it's nice seeing a world that seemingly couldnt care less about you, random creatures, roam and sleep and hunt eachother without taking a notice in you. Seeing all the random experiments and descimated camps is also a nice touch. But, and this is a big but, when you get inside the alient temple? I guess thats what it is. The game just seems to keep going, you repeat the same puzzles and fights over and over again and it just outstays its welcome by at least an extra hour.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing remake made by very dedicated fans which only started as a mod now released as a proper game and its great! This is the best way to experience the original half life if you are new to the series, the combat of the original has aged extremely well but some of the levels just haven't that much. The gameplay and combat is very good and the visuals are stunning. The story is also improved and is better told with better dialogue and characters have more of a presence. Besides character model animations on NPCs and some other stuff I would say this is absolutely just as good as if Valve themselves made it.  The devs of this game have done a great job a recreating the weapons and how they feel. The gameplay feels fluid and there are very minor bugs that you encounter sometimes other than that its great. The combat is really well done, it is a very faithful recreation of the original game's. The weapon variety is also great and all the weapons feel great to use. I think the grenade launcher on the SMG needs a little bigger radius and the grenades feel underwhelming other than that everything is awesome. They have made great improvements to the story. The dialogue is better and the characters have more of a presence and personality, They also have a cameo of Eli Vance in the early section of the game. I would say that they have done great in the story department I just hate that the tramp ride from the beginning of the game is even longer than in the original and it gets boring just sitting in there.All the levels from the original game have been recreated super well. It feels really awesome to see the old levels in such great graphics and the way you transverse through each of them has also been changed a little bit to give them a modern touch. The xen area from the original has been recreated entirely here because it was hated in the original game. They did an incredible job with Xen now it is an awesome level. I like all the chapters that take place in black mesa's Xen except Interloper, it starts off great but just takes a nosedive in quality halfway through it. Black Mesa's Xen is easily the most beautiful looking area in the entire half life franchise!This game's soundtrack was composed by Joel Nielsen and he did an incredible job! Almost every track in the game sounds great this might even be the best score of the franchise. I hope Valve gets this guy to do music for HL3 if they make it. This game's soundtrack destroys HL Alyx's. All of the tracks are hype and give you an adrenaline rush when they play during combat sequences. The only thing wrong here I would say is that sometimes when the music plays it is a bit too loud.Buy this game, it is great and is one of my favourite remakes ever only beaten by the first two incredible resident evil remakes and shadow of the colossus. If you can get it on sale then its even better but do buy it and support the devs, they worked hard on it and poured so much love into this project and it shows! I would give Black Mesa in its current state a 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Shooters like the original Half-Life, where exploring the levels and solving puzzles is at least half the fun, are not really made anymore. Enter Crowbar Collective and their remake of Half-Life. It's crazy to see how well the structure and ideas of the original hold up even today. Of course, this version is vastly improved, both in terms of graphics and (most of) the level design. It even greatly expands and improves upon the last act, where the original was running out of breath. Beware, however: some might think it even extends the original a bit too much in the last few levels. Some of the very minor gameplay tweaks are also a bit controversial.But overall, this is an amazing accomplishment. Whether you never played the original back in the 90s and want to see what the fuzz is about or whether you want to revisit the escape from Black Mesa almost 25 years later with all the bells and whistles we expect today but without sacrificing any of the original's concepts to modern sensibilities - this is the real thing right here!

_childDocuments_.review: I love the Half-Life universe and games. I’ve replayed each part of the series multiple times. I played Half-Life: Source once, which didn’t impress me much as a remake. I didn’t expect much from a fan-made remake of the game, but boy, was I wrong!I played Black Mesa even before the Xen part was released, and I already liked it back then. But with its official announcement, I decided to replay it. This is the best remake among the games I’ve played! It’s clear that the game was made by fans for fans.The gameplay has even been improved! New music was written for the game, new character lines were added, and many new models (for example, female scientists) were introduced. The enemy assassins (women in camouflage suits) wear special devices on their legs, like the characters from Portal, which explains their speed and agility!There are more "physical" puzzles now. For example, in one episode, they made it possible to shoot from a stationary rocket launcher, which needs to be manually loaded with shells. The Source engine allows you to use the environment to your advantage: I defended myself from vortigaunt shots using a barrel I was carrying, or threw objects (and even body parts) at enemies, and signal flares can be used to set enemies on fire!Some levels from the original game didn’t make it into Black Mesa, but there are new ones! For example, watching the confrontation between the invading army and the US army is a complete pleasure now. These battles look much more interesting than in the original.The game now features achievements, some of which are quite original. For example, the task of finding and gathering all the scientists and guards on a level. There are achievements inspired by Episode Two of Half-Life. If you had to send a garden gnome into space there, here you need to carry a hat, a pizza, and a canister of toxic gas! Try carrying them all at once!The game's story has improved. The scientists and guards you meet give more information about what’s happening. And Xen was a real surprise. If it was a short adventure in the original, here a lot of content has been added, about a quarter or even a third of the game. Xen is very beautiful, the artists and animators did a great job. New creatures and ecosystem details were added. The authors explained why the Vortigaunts are so grateful to Gordon for saving them. The human presence in Xen suggests that their invasion attracted the Covenant’s attention to Earth. Yes, this wasn’t in the original game, so it can be considered an addition, but it’s so good that you want to believe it.My only complaint might be the soldier production factory. Despite the attempt to show another world with its own laws and rules, the factory looks dull and boring.If the encounter with Gonarch was relatively short and uninteresting, in Black Mesa they did their best! The battles with Gonarch and Nihilanth became more interesting and challenging. The levels are well-designed, there are several possible outcomes (for example, you can kill Gonarch in one of two ways, or leave it alive), and the number of Nihilanth’s attack types has significantly increased.Overall, this is a very cool game, made not only with regard to the entire Half-Life series (and even Portal), but also with the authors’ vision of the alien invasion events on Earth. I highly recommend it to all fans of the universe.
