_childDocuments_.review: forever changed the way I play and appreciate first-person shooters. While it wasn’t the first FPS to feature a (good) story, I was impressed by how you get to experience the entire narrative from first-person perspective, by its scripted events, and by its deliberate pacing.  was intense, cinematic, suspenseful, complex, and fun. It raised the (crow)bar of excellence very high.Nowadays, some developers remaster or remake their hit titles for modern gaming systems. Valve did port  to run on the Source Engine in 2004, but the resulting product --  -- was generally considered inadequate. Consequently, a group of dissatisfied fans, branding themselves as Crowbar Collective, decided to volunteer their time to remaster  properly. It was in this way that the  project began. started out as a fan-made mod of  for . Released in 2012 after 7 years of development, it’s still available to download for free at the time of this review. However, the mod only goes up to the end of the “Lambda Core” chapter. The developers spent an additional 8 years converting the mod into a standalone game powered by the Source 2013 engine, adding more details to many of the levels, and re-imagining and completing the Xen levels. The final product of that Herculean effort is . is a notable achievement. The developers essentially remade  so that the story and aesthetics align with those of the sequels. Because of that, the game’s narrative is more cohesive with the  lore. This includes formally introducing players to Dr. Kleiner and Dr. Vance at the Black Mesa Research Facility, and showing the Vortigaunts being enslaved on Xen. I believe these changes will not only satisfy many long-time fans, but also ease unfamiliar players into the  game series.My memory of  isn’t as exact as those of players who play it on a regular basis, or who have played it recently. What I remember most about  is the general thrill from playing it, and being in awe of a few prominent set pieces (e.g., stepping out of a drain pipe onto the cliff of a mesa as a fighter jet zooms by). What  successfully accomplished is letting veteran players experience similar excitement, suspense and tension when playing it, as if they are playing  for the first time.The original graphics of  haven’t aged well. Even the level designs, which were ahead of the curve back in 1998, are rudimentary by today’s standards. To remake  properly, the developers couldn’t simply insert models with higher polygon counts, slap on new, high-definition textures, and call it a day. The challenge of remaking a game like  is that it needs to feel contemporary, but also deliver the spirit of the original. I was very happy to see that despite the new visual presentation,  is similarly paced and subversive as .The developers interpreted the original material, remixed level designs to make them feel more modern and less rigid, and spruced everything up with advanced lighting and water effects. They did such a good job with the visuals and elaborating on the levels that I was convinced that  had always looked and played this good. It took me watching playthroughs of the original game to snap myself back into realizing how rudimentary  looks in comparison, and how much work the developers had put in into making .Yet, the developers did show restraint on the interpretation and remixing. They couldn’t and didn’t rearrange the layout of Black Mesa Research Facility too radically, and didn’t add new elements that are too disparate from the original concepts. Some levels are likely easier to contemporize (e.g., “On a Rail”, “Surface Tension”), and some harder (e.g., “We’ve Got Hostiles”, “Lambda Core”). What we end up getting in  is some unevenness throughout the many levels, which may be an unforeseen consequence of modernizing a classic game while staying faithful to the source material.Let’s address the elephant (or Gargantua if you will) in the room: how are those re-imagined Xen levels? For those unfamiliar with , the original Xen levels were not very good to say the least. Even my co-worker who enthusiastically recommended  to me back in the day advised me stop playing upon arriving at Xen. I didn’t listen, and got to experience first-hand how mechanically and tonally different those last levels were. I believe that many people still hold  in high regard only because the first 85 to 90% of the game was so good.Crowbar Collective did a really great job re-imagining Xen. They expanded the scope of each level visually and structurally. In fact, the new designs bare very little resemblance to what Valve delivered back in 1998. Instead of sticking with the original pukey yellowish-brown shades, the developers assigned each level its own colour scheme. There’s tranquil, mysterious purple in “Xen”, followed by earthy orange and brown in “Gonarch’s Lair”, and finished off with dangerous red and alien green in “Interloper”.Significant changes were also made to the terrain and flora, with “Xen” partly inspired by the forests of Pandora from the movie, , “Gonarch’s Lair” featuring an elaborate underground labyrinth reminiscent of Shelob’s lair in , and “Interloper” having an industrial look that reminded me of . The expanded variety of colours and environment is a much welcome change.In spite of the creativity and effort, some purists will not like how these newly designed levels greatly deviate from the original. I didn’t mind it, but my biggest complaint about the new levels is that they’re just too long, so much so that I found they overstayed their welcome. Plus, these levels are much more challenging than what the first 70% of  presented. Ironically, Xen in this game feels very much like an afterthought as in .In the end, Xen is Xen. Despite Crowbar Collective’s best efforts, these last few levels just don’t fit well with the first part of . The transition from Black Mesa Research Facility to the alien world is still as jarring as before. Xen feels like it belongs to a different type of game, like ones that star alien-killing space marines, who make their enemies tremble with fear. You can’t fault the developers too much though, because a remake of  just isn’t complete without these divisive levels.I love , and I will enthusiastically recommend this game to anyone interested in the  game series. Coincidentally much like the co-worker who recommended  to me, I love this game up to the end of the “Lambda Core” chapter only, for I’m rather apathetic about the Xen levels. Yet, I recognize that no matter how you slice it, Xen -- in its original or remastered form -- will be divisive among  enthusiasts. So who knows, you may actually enjoy them more than I did! No matter what, the creativity and hard work that Crowbar Collective had put in into modernizing , and redesigning Xen from scratch are praiseworthy. And for that, they deserve not only our thanks, but also our financial support.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes. Yes. Yes.Now, first I would like to say that I don't recommend this before you ever play any other Half-Life game (even though that's kind of what I did). I recommend starting with the original Half-Life - NOT HALF-LIFE SOURCE (it's extremely buggy, and you're better off playing Half-Life). Black Mesa is pretty much exactly the same as Half-Life, but with a fully completed and polished last few chapters - that I won't spoil in case you don't know already - which are beautiful compared to the original, but I believe the additions in Black Mesa are considered non-canon.Now to the actual review:I love this game, it sticks as close as it can to the original game, yet using the Source engine to update puzzles and fights etc. This game makes the not-so-great end chapters of the original into what seems like a beautiful bluish-purple masterpiece (my Steam profile picture is a small part of said end chapters). The game adds new physics puzzles, cuts a few things out (most notably the maze from "On a Rail" that the majority of players disliked from the original game) and, of course, the usual properties of a remake, like improved graphics, voicelines, models and mechanics (still trying not to deviate too far from the original game).          Though, no game is without it's flaws, and why would this game be an exception?          This game takes away from some of the puzzles from the original, and replaces them with plug puzzles. Then there's a puzzle that I remember being stuck on for about five minutes where you need to shoot a plank of wood stuck in an electrical box, that's causing electricity to flow through a metal door, blocking your path, and never once in the game are you taught to do this, not just that, but it was also fairly unclear what was needed to be done at the time. I'm not entirely sure if this puzzle is in the original game, but I don't remember it being there when I played the original game. Another flaw is that the final boss felt slightly easy compared to the hard battles that came before, though it does somewhat make up for this by adding so much going on at the same time. This flaw doesn't necessarily apply to everyone, but in the final few chapters especially, there is a lot of framerate problems. Though I will say that my PC isn't great, I asked my friend (who has a much better computer than me) and he said that there was a few framerate problems as well.Anyhow, overall, the game (in my opinion) hasn't got many huge flaws, however my friend has had a few bugs, such as: vital objects disappearing (valves etc), random models spawning in vital places so you can't progress, and an enemy dropping their weapon???In the end, I'd rate this game 8/10, but, it is still a remake, and it still takes from the original game - which is where it gets a lot of it's greatness from.

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10I never played the original Half-Life and bought this after seeing a review that praised it for making Half-Life feel more modern. I went in knowing nothing of the story of Half-Life, and wondering why I'd seen memes comparing Master Chief to Freeman.Now, I get the memes. I highly recommend this to anyone who didn't play the OG Half-Life. This game has made me think about trying it, but I worry the experience will feel too dated. Either way, the universe and story are timeless and I was sad when Black Mesa ended. I can't recommend this enough and I've now started Half-Life 2. The gameplay does feel dated at times, to be fair, but not necessarily in a bad way. The mechanics aren't what you'd expect to find in other, more modern games, but they give the game charm. The game is challenging, sometimes frustrating, especially if you're also a smooth brain and don't immediately figure out all the puzzles, but never boring or lacking engagement. Music: 10/10, story: 10/10, environments: 10/10, gameplay: 10/10, level design: Some levels go on longer than maybe they should have, but after doing some research I discovered they were kept true to the original (good) or completely remade to be better. Because of Black Mesa, I fully understand why Half-Life is so iconic, and honestly consider it one of if not the best (story) games of all time.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: I've been totally blown away by the Black Mesa experience and can't recommend it highly enough.No, it doesn't have cutting edge graphics or totally innovative gameplay ideas.  That's okay though because it brings us back to the story of one of the most iconic games in PC history, Half-Life, and it's silent protagonist Gordon Freeman.Black Mesa brings Half-Life into the Source engine with all those capabilities.  It isn't id Tech 6 but it looks great and more importantly, runs great on a wide range of hardware.  It's a huge upgrade over the 1998 game for sure (to include the Gearbox's HD pack), as well as Half-Life 2.I'm only up to Residue Processing in the story but so far it's been that classic Half-Life experience.  The developers have adjusted the level design and environmental puzzles so it isn't a carbon copy of the original game.  You have an idea of what's coming, but it's an entirely new experience.  Some of the annoying bits from the original game have been tweaked and the Source engine gives them some new options for other puzzles.  From what I understand, the long-awaited Xen levels are even better than Valve's ho-hum rushed ones, so I can't wait to see what's coming.Edit on Jan 10: Finally played through to Xen and completed the game.  The Xen levels are MUCH better than Valve's original version.  There were a few times when the environmental puzzles got a little repetitive but the overall atmosphere was really engaging.  I didn't exactly enjoy the Nihilanth fight, but it was a lot better than the original take.  They did an excellent job filling in history of the human presence in Xen, though I do wish we had some additional backstory on the Xenian creatures aside from "some massive power must be holding open the portal, you must stop it!"All in all, this is an awesome game.  Valve will probably never revisit Gordon Freeman, so at least Black Mesa lets me have another shot at his earlier adventures.  (Though based on some of the rumors for HL3 story ideas, maybe it's best we don't get there.)  I'm having a great time with Black Mesa and can recommend it to anyone that loves the original Half-Life, is a fan of science-fiction adventure, or loves FPS games in general. You won't be disappointed!

_childDocuments_.review: The reason I don't recommend this game is because of frequent crashes and bugs that I experienced. Fair warning: I wrote a bit too much text, so only bother if you are interested. Should contain none to very slight spoilers.I spent about 60h on this game and played it through multiple times, also in order to get all the achievements - I would not have done that if I did not enjoy the game itself. What I did not enjoy however where that on my first playthrough the game crashed on me more than a hundred times. And this is no exaggeration. It would just crash at random points, and with crashes of different nature. Most commonly it just closed down without any error or notification whatsoever, sometimes the game would grey out and stop responding, other times the audio would freeze and then subsequently the game would crash. There were more but you get the point... crashing all the time ain't fun. Those aforementioned crashes also happened a few times (I think 5 times on my first playthrough) with quicksaves. Meaning, it would crash on loading the save, leading to me losing progress, the biggest hit I got with that was losing a big chunk of progress in the chapters Xen and Interloper, which are quite long. Another thing that bothered me were bugs. I have seldom played a game so riddled with bugs as this, and while this partially might be attributed to me exploring a lot in video games I informed myself about some of the more grave issues that made it impossible to progress and found that actually quite a few people ran into them. Be it cables being impossible to be plugged in and me searching half an hour for what to do only to find out the cables sometimes bug and I had to reload an earlier save or be it a cable or another required object just falling through the map or a locked door. The last part that annoyed me were some of the achievements. There is one in which you have to kill all of a certain type of creature found in the later part of the game. There are some which can be seen from both sides of adjecent maps but it only counts from one side, for whatever reason - I wasted 2 hours till I found that out. And then there are the transporting achievements.... while the hat is rather unproblematic, the pizza box is a whole other thing. Getting up ladders and teleporters with this is just annoying, I am really not sure why they added such an achievement in a game were you just know the physics will screw it up. And the gas cannister required for another achievement would get literally stuck midair when moving it through zones so the only way to get the achievement was creating that object anew every time it got stuck. I could also just have created it at the goal, but I wanted to do it the right way. So every area switch I had to create the achievement item new... and also some additional times as it just randomly got stuck on the ground, or while falling down, just floating midair. I know that some might consider achievements issues not issues with the game itself as those are not part of the game per se, but for me they are integral, I tend to do them in games I like and enjoy and I like completing games 100%. Having achievements that are bugged or are badly designed is just something I dislike and that will clearly reduce my enjoyment.On another, more positive note, I enjoyed the gameplay, even tho I think the mechanics are a bit clunky at times and hitscan enemies always suck. The story and ambience is very well done but some might consider a few sections a bit drawn out, especially comparing to the original. The graphics are neat, nothing world moving compared to contemporary games but it is impressive what they managed to do within the limitations of such an old engine. If not for the bugs and especially the crashes I would definetly recommend this (especially for fans of the franchise), but remembering how it crashed on me so many times and how that sucked the fun out of it I cannot do that with a clear conscience.

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa is a love letter to Half Life, a glimpse of how far the FPS genre (and video games in general) have come since HL1, as well as being one of the finest games I have ever played. Being an authorised fan remake of the original Half Life, the game shares a lot in common with said game, but also adds in brand new assets, levels, and brings the game into the modern age. Pros:- The Black Mesa Research Facility looks better than ever. While maintaining roughly the same layout as it did back in the '90's, the modern incarnation benefits from modern graphics technology, more detailed environments, as well as the physics of the modern Source Engine. - A host of improvements to gameplay make Black Mesa a highly enjoyable experience. While core mechanics still focus on blended puzzle and gunplay segments; Black Mesa both reuses and improves segments from the original game, while also adding new and original content to existing segments. - Brilliant audio and FX design. 'nuff said. - XenCons:- There's a few minor bugs, but these can potentially be attributed to the age of the Source Engine, and I didn't encounter any that were game-breaking. Most bugs are related to physics or AI for certain opponents. - Some of the new additions to levels feel a little too formulaic and underwhelming. I haven't played the original Half Life in years, so I can't figure out whether all of the bits I thought were rather poorly done were necessarily new, but a few of them I definitely don't recall being in the original. Regardless, none were overtly bad, or deserving of mention, so YMMV. Overall, Black Mesa is one of the best games I have ever played. If you love video games, get this game.

_childDocuments_.review: THANK YOU.The first time I got to play Half life was just a few weeks after release, around the holidays in '98, and it was a glorious experience. Every level, every aspect, every new weapon was like having a minor orgasm, something you remember vividly even after 22 years. So as they announced Black Mesa, and the early versions started to pop up, I maintained my distance, not installing it. Hell, not even watching a vid on Youtube. Why? Because I wanted my re-experience to be perfect.I simply didn't want to be disappointed in something that was so dear to me. It took an iron will not to cave in, but alas, today the long-awaited mail came; "Black Mesa is now available on Steam!"So, was it worth it?FV<K YES.I'm twenty minutes in, just got into my HEV suit, and at that scene I cried a little, had to alt-tab out, and get a beer from the fridge, because I'm eighteen again.Dear Crowbar Collective: Thank you. Truly, from my heart and soul, thank you for doing this.

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa is a lovingly crafted remake of one of the most revolutionary first person shooters to exist. The improved graphics and lighting help to add immersion to the dark and mysterious world, on the source engine for a much smoother experience too. Being faithful to the original while also taking some liberties in the correct places, like turning Xen into a more beautiful landscape. I only encountered a couple glitches and was otherwise a great experience. Gunplay felt nice although on playing on hard sometimes the enemies could feel like bullet sponges. If you played Half-Life before this would be a wondeful trip down memory lane, and if you never played HL before, this would be a great way to get into the series.

_childDocuments_.review: Should I play Black Mesa? I think if you have played Half Life before or Half Life 2 the answer is most certainly a yes. If you have not then its harder to say. Black Mesa absolutely delivers on the promise of Half Life in the source engine, for me though it is obvious it is built on the frame of a game released in 1998. There are times when the platforming is just to fiddly to be fun, or where the momentum of the game is lost because I had to hunt around for the way forward. These are minor gripes to someone who has loved the Half Life series since I was 13 but players trying to dip their toe into the Half Life universe to find out what all the fuss is about might find themselves thrown off by the platforming and level design. One major praise here is the amazing set piece moments within the game. Those times when the music kicks in and the enemies swarm an arena for you to charge down is just epic!The Devs deserve full credit here to painstakingly rebuilding this classic. Would recommend to any fan of the Half Life series

_childDocuments_.review: I don't disagree with most of the positive comments people have made about this game, but there were a few things that spoiled it for me.  An update blew away my game save files, but that probably won't happen to you.  Twice my PC completely locked up and I had to power it off and back on again to recover.  As for the game itself, there were good parts and bad parts.  It starts slowly, but that's more the fault of the story than this particular telling of it.  Once it gets going, it's of similar quality to Half Life 2, minus the close interaction with other players and plus more detailed models of the game world.  But towards the end it starts to get repetitive, predictable and even tedious.  Xen and Interloper are far too long.  Although the world is beautiful, it is constructed around the puzzles, rather than the puzzles being constructed out of pieces of the world that would naturally be there anyway.   This destroys immersion and decreases enjoyment.  There are sections where you just blast away at stuff with the gluon gun, which gets automatically recharged, and as long as you don't die you get charged back up to 100% heath and armor before the next section.  If you like this, well, fine, but I prefer a little more imagination in the map design.  So, overall, I think you should buy it when it's on sale and try it out, but be prepared for disappointment.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic way to experience Half-Life, whether you played the original or not. My only real gripes are some minor things they changed around that confused me - but only because I was so used to original, having played it through countless times. Otherwise really solid, keeps the core of what made HL good intact while making some smart updates. Can't wait for Xen.EDIT: Have now played through the definitive update, including Xen. I can't really say whether Black Mesa's version of Xen is an improvement over Half-Life's, but it's certainly a lot... more. The issue for me was that the quality varied drastically from one part to the next.On the positive end, they've obviously put a lot of effort into the look of it, and for the most part it paid off. The more exploration and puzzle-heavy segments (while maybe a bit too conveniently laid-out) were mostly really fun. Finally, some of the parts they added and fleshed out to account for the events of HL2 are pretty cool!On the more negative side, it features some truly interminable sections which were made much lengthier than the original for no good reason. Fights which were merely frustrating in HL1 are now absolutely infuriating. Aesthetically there are some rough spots, too. There are some added sections that feel a little out of place, but worse than that is the music. Earlier in the campaign there are some eyebrow-raising tracks, but in Xen it's just grating. I really have no idea how they thought this was appropriate for a game trying to ape Half-Life's feel in most every other respect, but every time it kicked in it took me out of the experience in a pretty visceral way.All in all a much more mixed experience now, but still overall positive. I respect the scope of what they tried with Xen, I just wish it was more consistent.

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa is a fan made recreation of the original 1998 Half-Life game.It isn't exactly a reimagining but there are certain elements that are,I will try to keep this as spoiler free as possible.So anyways here are my thoughts and opinions of this game's qualities:==================================================================Story is very awesome! (10/10)>> There isn't too much to say here except they recreated the HL1 story perfectly!>> Crowbar Collective really made every NPC sound and look more alive with uniquedialog to every each and one of them.Gameplay is fantastically designed! (10/10)>> I will later get into more details but for now, I can only say I love the movement,combat, level flow and feedback!>> There is only a single setting missing, I couldn't really turn off the autoswitchsetting when you pickup new weapons.>> I really feel that every element works perfectly with the other one.>> The crosshairs also go very well with the type of weapon you are holding!The weapons are very fun (10/10)>> The redesigned weapons are so much more fun than in HL1!>> Most of the weapons feel so much more punchy and with a lot more power!>> When using the Shotgun, Gluon-gun and the Magnum I really feel their strength, powerand feedback!Combat is improved and very fun (10/10)>> The new AI makes for a better enemy that feels more real!>> The new Vortigaunt and Grunt AI are a great addition to the game!>> The weapons combined with the AI make up for a great combat experience!>> I could only complain about how strong are the HECU soldiers, ofc they are trainedmarines but holy crap they are too strong!NPCs/Enemies are one big improvement (10/10)>> There are new enemy types in Black Mesa.>> Lots of retextured variety of the human NPCs>> Overall they just add to the immersion of the game!Graphics are Amazing! (10/10)>> Of course because this is a remake with better technology, the graphics look waybetter than HL1, with an improved game engine and better hardware.>> I found that Xen looks very cool! but at some areas really lazy and out of place.>> The redesigned NPCs also look so good, I remember being a bit sad that VALVe didn'tinclude houndeyes in HL2 and when I saw them in Black Mesa I was excited!>> I also really appreciate the different types of zombies/scientists/guards!>> Every chapter has its own theme and look, I find that very interesting!>> The weapon models and textures also look great I really like every single on of them!Game setting/atmosphere is excellent (10/10)>> Like I said every chapter has its own setting that is being executed astonishingly!>> The levels also never stray away too much from the games atmosphere.>> I personally really liked the "questionable ethics", "lambda core" and the first chapterof "Xen", mostly for their setting!Soundtracks are amazing (10/10)>> I really love every single one of this games soundtracks!>> They fit the game perfectly and help set the right settings!>> The soundtracks aren't annoying or repetitive!Optimization is fantastic! (10/10)>> I play on a fairly low-end PC and still run this game at low-mid 60 FPS at heavyareas!>> The game still looks great and plays even better!>> In a bit lighter areas I can even get 60-100 FPS with nearly max settings!Workshop content doesn't disappoint (10/10)>> I do not count the workshop score but I just wanted to mention that the workshopsupport is amazing, the content there is entertaining with great mods and maps!Level design is almost perfect! (9/10)>> Most of the levels are redesigned slightly to work better in todays standards.>> They are more clear with dumbed-down puzzles(for the better and the worse).>> I could only complain that some later areas have worse clipping than the beginning.>> I also feel like the game would've been a lot better if the chapter interloper didn'tdrag on for so long, the puzzles aren't fun and the combat feels really dry there.> however the elevator combat sequence was very cool(in interloper)!Sounds are amazing (9/10)>> Sounds fit the game and its atmosphere in a beneficial way!>> Even the little details are designed with professionalism and love!>> The voice acting also feels perfect and immersive!Movement is well done (9/10)>> In Black Mesa you can still crouch jump and Bunny-Hop which is awesome!>> I also found the sliding mechanic very fun!>> And everything else is pretty much still there as in HL1.>> Nothing more to add here, I really like the movement of source games.Achievement are fun for the most part (8/10)>> I completed all of the achievements to 100%, and if I can say one thing to someone whowants to complete them is: be patient, and make the most research about how manyachievements you could do in a single run.>> I found myself replaying the same sections of the game just for one or two achievementsat once, really a waste of time.>> The 3 achievements that you have to carry objects are fun but holy crap they made mehate ladders so much. Please crowbar make it somehow a bit easier!Also the pizza box has it's collision enabled so sometimes when falling I would get stuckmid air because of the box.> When teleporting with those objects you could get stuck inside of them, if you do, justhit those props with your crowbar until you get out.> Also I'm not sure if it exist but in case not, please crowbar add someway to teleport theprops to the end of the interloper chapter.Puzzles are a bit on the weaker side (8/10)>> In HL1 the puzzles were more challenging and interesting, but here in Black Mesait feels like "go get this, plug it here and press that". Don't get me wrong thepuzzles aren't bad but are repetitive and boring most of the time.>> I really miss some of the HL1 puzzles but feel like the newer puzzles are a bit moreclear at what you should do and I can appreciate it.Multiplayer is ??? (?/?)>> Haven't tried it and don't really plan to do so, I won't be able to give it a score.Other:Cons:- some very small areas have clipping textures.- some areas in Xen feel too flat compared to the other places.- too many houndeyes in XenSide comments/notes:- I played through the campaign about 7 times and still enjoy it!- One serious playthrough without any major skips would be around 10-15 hours!==================================================================So after all of that, finally, I would give Black Mesa a solid (9/10).

_childDocuments_.review: I had an absolute blast playing Black Mesa. The team has faithfully re-created the original Half-Life in terms of gameplay, movement, atmosphere, etc., but changed enough for it to feel like a new experience. This might be Black Mesa's greatest merit: Allowing you to play one of the best shooters of all time for the first time again. If I'm not mistaken, they also ramped up the difficulty level quite a bit - "normal" felt like Half-Life on "hard" to me, which is fine. Looking forward to the Xen levels!(Edit for full version: Crowbar Collective really outdid themselves with the Xen levels! They are re-designed from scratch and add a sizeable chunk of gameplay easily on par with the best of the Half-Life franchise. The music in particular is phenomenal!)

_childDocuments_.review: One of the easiest recommendations from me. I'm not a hardcore fan of the Half-Life series but I recognise its importance for gaming as a whole and the cultural impact it made more than 20 years ago. The original HL was definitely a revolutionary game for its time but I doubt I'd play it today. I'm too spoiled by the modern graphics and gameplay gimmicks that it lacks. You just can't immerse yourself in that blurry, gnarly low poly world with very few details compared to the modern games. No high res textures can fix it, unfortunately.Enter Black Mesa. A small team of really hardcore fans remade HL1 from scratch and made it a modern, vibrant game that still is THAT Half-Life with the same (and even improved) atmosphere, story, friends and enemies. Despite it was in the making for 14 years, the visuals still look good. Yes, it's not a fresh pop-a-mole shooter from Activision or something that would put your GPU to its virtual knees, but everything looks good enough to not distract you from the gameplay process. Until Xen. Because if the main part brought back memories from playing HL1 back in 2000s, Xen doesn't. That's why it plays and feels like a sequel to the Earth part, it's so unlike anything you played before it, and absolutely not like the boring floating islands in HL1. The graphic there is totally up to the today standards (at least it's the best the old Source engine can do, the FPS overall is like 4 times lower than in the Earth levels), it's alive, it breathes, it tells a story that connects Black Mesa with Half-Life 2.If you played HL1 before you'll still have a lot of fun revisiting the familiar locations. They're not copypasted of course and only the most iconic rooms are recreated close to the originals. Everything else is new. In Xen you'll meet only two well known bosses (but the battles with them are completely different) and that part is so long it could easily be a standalone game.Another important part of the game is music. At times it discords with the scene and suddenly brings unexpected emotions and understanding of what's really happening right now. I won't spoil it but you'll see and feel it I hope. Xen's music organically enhances the intense parts and creates a unique atmosphere that's drastically different from the boring and hostile feeling of HL1's Xen. Here you're like a guest that came not to destroy but to understand this world (and destroy. A bit).It's really an AAA game for a very low price considering the amount and quality of the content. It doesn't matter that a small team made it, you can't tell if you don't know it. The game is solid, it keeps the good tempo, the difficulty of fights and puzzles is polished, you're never bored. I'd say even HL2, the official Valve game, pales in comparison with Black Mesa. Go play it and you won't be disappointed.Played the game through on Debian Linux, i7-7700k, 32 Gb RAM, NVIDIA GeForce 1070. There are some broken shaders or textures in the Linux build (black polygons in some areas) and a severe FPS drop in the portal tower (lambda generator) area. FPS drops to 5-10 and since this puzzle requires a good reaction this renders it unplayable. Fortunately, you can play on Proton (force it in the game properties) but you'll need to put -oldgameui to the launch parameters or else you'll have no main menu for some reason. Then DXVK (D9VK) kicks in and you'll have a great performance and hopefully no graphical glitches anywhere. Or you can wait until this is fixed in the native Linux build.

The shooting is reminiscent of the Counter Strike, which is very engaging. Yeah yeah, we all know this. For one's who don't: You'd travel thorugh a variety of close quater maps seeing a multitude of enemies, but get repetitive later. The boss fights are not the ones you see nowadays, you'd have to find ways to defeat it by intercating with the game world. That's it, all you need to know for now.What's new in this game is, improved graphics and physics. Since it is based on the acclaimed Source engine.Play this game for:Its story.The environmental based puzzles.Unforgiving action.Memorable characters.This game is tough if you play it in higher difficulties and will instill multiple rage quits. _childDocuments_.review: Holy Macaroni this is good.Black Mesa is a remake of the original half life which has been in development for over a decade. Now, finally it is released in its full form and this is absolutely a must play.Not only is the base game lovingly recreated, remastered and rebuilt in certain areas to take advantage of the source engine and iron out some kinks with the original levels but the Xen levels have been COMPLETELY redesigned to become in my opinion the absolute highlight of the game.The Xen levels have been in development for years and now having finished Black Mesa from start to finish I can say it was absolutely 100% worth the wait. The Xen levels are amazingly good and you really feel like you're exploring an alien planet from beyond, helped a ton by the drop dead gorgeous visuals and aesthetic design along with the incredible musical score by Joel Nielsen.The music in this game deserves a special mention because it isn't something that plays all the time, rather it kicks in at certain moments during the game and is used to build up certain scenes. In the base on earth portion of the game the tracks are a mixture between Melodic Piano tracks and more heavy slow rock style tracks and the two genres often cross over.On Xen the music becomes a lot more euphoric with some amazing vocals done by Joel's wife, Kala Nielsen, being one of the highlights of the soundtrack. A lot of the time in the Xen levels you'll reach a moment where you stumble into a new area and you're met with an amazingly beautiful sight coupled with the music beginning to kick in and you just can't help but stop and gawk at what you're seeing. It's truly incredible what Crowbar Collective have managed to pull off in the Source Engine here.Really my only complaints are that I hit a few bugs and glitches here and there, most of them were minor, like the autosave kicking in at the wrong place causing it to autosave while I was falling to my death (thankfully you can quicksave on the fly and quicksaving does not overwrite your previous quicksave so if you happen to quicksave mid fall you can roll back to the quicksave before that) but I did hit one glitch where an NPC got stuck in the Surface Tension chapter and I was forced to NoClip my way through a door in order to trigger the next NPC event to get him unstuck (this is a known issue apparently).It's a bit awkward but thankfully these glitches are very few and far between. You may not run into any of them at all.With all that being said, Black Mesa is an incredible experience and an incredible way to experience Half Life, either for the first time or for the fifteenth time. So what are you waiting for? Because they're waiting for you Gordon, in the test chamber...

_childDocuments_.review: A must play for fans of the original. Updated textures and graphics alone would have been a welcome addition but they go further still to slightly tweak and rework parts of the game to keep it fresh.Updated: A few more comments on the bigger and better Xen missions.I have to commend the developers on the lengths they went to improve upon the Xen portion of Half-Life. While I don't think it necessarily needed to be lengthened or modified I was excited to see what they had in store. They expand the final levels in some very interesting ways.Story telling takes a front seat in these final hours--let's say passenger, because the gameplay is still driving here. Through some environmental story telling so well executed in the likes of Left 4 Dead, you get a glimpse of what an enslaved Vortigaunt's  pitiful existence might look like--they are put to work by the controllers, live in hovels under tight survellance and are discarded when their utility has been fully exploited. These moments fill in the gap of the canon not really explored by Valve, where between Half-life and HL2 Gordon Freeman becomes a living deity to the Vortigaunts through his actions at the end of this game.Gameplay wise, you can expect some extremely tightly designed levels and puzzles that rival, if not surpass the work of Valve themselves. An extensive look into what the industrial machine behind an invasion of earth looks like provides an environmental palette for the level and puzzle designers to work with -- a lot of standing on pumps to reach higher areas, or crawling through tunnels to reach that final cable in a puzzle. They created two (maybe three) 'marathon' set pieces that test your ability to run and gun. There were a couple interesting puzzles added around the controllers too. As for the two boss fights they have expanded those mechanically as well. All great stuff!My gripes with this final stretch are few, but they might prevent me from coming back to play through this portion ever again. Firstly, the length. I understand there might have been so many good ideas for puzzles--again, I saw quite a few--and an overarching urge to get a lot of use out of all the great assets created however these levels just started to drag. Some mechanics, while smartly used may have been used on too many times, or there was just too much of a good thing! Secondly, in some high intensity fights and spaces the game got quite 'framey' for the first time ever. I wonder if there's anything that could be done to optimise them more.Ending on these points of feedback shouldn't dissuade you from playing one of the best first-person shooter campaigns ever. I hope this team gets the green light to give a similar treatment to Opposing Forces or Blue Shift, or make something entirely of their own in the Half-Life universe, but actually come out -- Arkane's 'Ravenholm' anyone?Play this game! You won't regret it!

_childDocuments_.review: The first ten chapters of this game are a faithful reimagining of Half-Life 1; apart from the graphics and physics obviously being better, and the maps looking much prettier and having actual architecture instead of just being 'rectangly', it doesn't add or take away anything from the original.However, once the game gets to Surface Tension it really comes into its own and you can tell the developers all of a sudden went "Hey, why constrain ourselves to the original, why don't we come up with new stuff since we're on a much better engine and have more capabilities now". In some ways, it's a shame they didn't have this thought process for the entire game from the beginning, I guess that's the downside of spending over 10 years in development?We see puzzles that make use of the physics in a way that couldn't be done in the original, there's a stealth section (which can be done guns blazing) that wasn't present in the original, a really cool sniper sequence on a rooftop that I'm pretty sure wasn't in the original (They shoot away the walls etc, very exciting), and they've made the Xen section of the game actually cool instead of being a bit of a drag as the original was.I could type a lot about Xen alone but the important thing is apart from being visually impressive, it just introduces so much that's not in HL1. New items like the crystalline suit chargers and energy weapon chargers, new areas like the field laboratory (Which I've seen other people singling out for praise) and Vortigaunt Village, new enemies like the HEV Zombies and explosive Houndeyes; it actually tells story in a way HL1 didn't, in that it shows the Alien Slaves are slaves, and that when they're not being controlled they're actually passive and friendly (the story being they're helping you because they want to be free from Nihilanth; this did not happen at all in-game in HL1), oh yeah and now the Alien Controllers actually control aliens, who would've known! There's sequences where you're given unlimited ammo for energy weapons, so you get to have Gluon gun killing sprees... I think I've said enough, the point is they made Xen The soundtrack is unremarkable, not really worth mentioning. The voice actors for guards and scientists sound surprisingly like the ones in HL1, the voices for Nihilanth and G-man don't quite hit the mark. It also would've been nice if they had the grunts voice lines in the style of the Opposing Force grunts who have more fleshed out lines and personality, but instead they went for the more generic HL1 grunts who only say things like "Contact!" "Grenade!" "Reloading!".Good!Definitely a reimagining on the original maps. Most of it will feel somewhat familiar but not quite, and is without doubt a remarkable improvementGood; a bit of a generic shooter in most of the first several chapters. We all know the existing puzzles etc from HL1 so there's nothing truly new until later in the game.  Once you get to the 2/3rds way mark they do a really great job of balancing gameplay between combat, puzzle time, running for your life, and specific sequences which are cool.Absolutely dead. I was hoping maybe it would have a slight revival with the game coming out of Early Access and having a sale, but nope. Every time I log in there's only one server in the entire world with players, and it has 260 ping so I can't play. The brief time I was able to play the other year, the actual MP was decent enough.So overall I'd give Black Mesa a I would definitely buy an Opposing Force or Blue Shift DLC should they make one. If only Black Mesa had a Sven Co-opOh, and if you get the game, check out my mod which replaces the voice of all the alien slaves with Morty from Rick and Morty ;)

_childDocuments_.review: What a phenomenal remake! No few words can describe how epic and adrenaline charged this game is. It’s almost hard to believe that this is a fan-made passion project that has been in the works since 2005.A solid effort by the guys at Crowbar Collective, the long road to its full release has definitely been worth the wait. At the risk of triggering the Half-Life fans, I’ll declare that this game rivals and maybe even surpasses the almighty HL2, and I wouldn't say that lightly. Proving to be so much more than a 1:1 rebuild, this rendition of the monumental classic not only restores cut content from the original game but also contains brand new sections and altered level designs that deliver seamless improvements. The team fully utilised Source Engine’s physics system to introduce intricate puzzles and interactive environments. The combat remains progressively challenging and at times incredibly punishing, even on medium difficulty. The music is sublime, intensifying many unforgettable moments across the game’s eighteen hour runtime.The first fourteen chapters of the game still hold their own after five years of being playable through early access. “Surface Tension” (a gruelling 2-3 hour slog) stands out as the most riveting, although the final shootouts in "Questionable Ethics" and "Forget About Freeman" deserve an honourable mention. The highly anticipated XEN update converts the last hour of Half-Life into a remarkable 4-5 hour adventure, with the newest chapters succeeding a steady difficulty curve after "Lambda Core". The planet Xen has been reimagined as a strange yet beautiful alien world, home to bizarre wildlife and paved with treacherous terrain. “Gonarch’s Lair” is by far the most badass boss battle in the entire game, starring a big mama headcrab that persistently hunts you. “Interloper” now features the trickiest platforming puzzle in the whole game, which is a testament to how inventively the developers approached the layout of this instalment.It would be a sin not to give this game a perfect score. One of the best I’ve played in my life, impeccably recapturing the essence and glory of Valve's groundbreaking debut, and I’m eager to see future third party productions like “Project Borealis” (an interpretation of what might have been HL2: Episode Three) gather momentum and receive a supported release on Steam too.10/10 without a doubt.EDIT: Deathmatch servers were mostly empty last I checked, Mac OS port coming soon apparently.

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa is a good update to the original Half-Life, but it's not a replacement. There are many alterations in the game's levels so if you want to play the authentic experience, stick to Half-Life or Half-Life: Source.That caveat in mind, Black Mesa is a great time. Everything you remember from Half-Life is in here and it works well, and the graphics are easily up to par with Half-Life 2. One thing I really like is how all NPCs now have unique faces and there is a lot of unique dialogue, too.Play this if you like Half-Life, but if you never played the original, make sure to play that first.

_childDocuments_.review: Half-Life is one of the most important games ever. Not even just FPS games, though it's insanely important to the entire genre for being one of the first to not be arcadey (a-la Doom or Quake) and to merge a coherent story with gameplay to make a whole experience. Before, you'd get a text crawl if you're lucky, or else you'd just have to go to the manual. Or there'd be Cutscenes. The game itself is a masterpiece in almost every way, so in 2005 or so, a group of crazy people wanted to remake the entire thing in the source engine (as opposed to Gold Source which was built off the quake engine) and the results we have are Black Mesa.What can you say about a game that so lovingly recreates a game like Half-Life. It doesn't change what made Half-Life good, even keeping in jank like crouch jumping and other similar quirks of the source engine. It looks and plays like a dream. It follows the game to the letter but sprinkles in some added stuff to make it stand out in a way. The biggest addition is the expansion of Xen, which I'm torn about. On one hand, it feels great and looks beautiful. You can see how much effort into making the alien world look as breathtaking as it does. It's long enough to feel like it's own game separate from the rest of running around Black Mesa. On the other hand, it still kinda has the same problems Xen had, that being that it's not really a satisfying conclusion to running around the Black Mesa compound. Making it longer just has the same issue.Another issue i had was getting it to run. It gave my dang 3060 ti a run for its money and i was chugging a lot at some spots. Particularly during the outside segments and some parts in Xen. Granted, i was playing on the highest graphics but still, be weary.Overall, i would say to play the original Half-Life first, but don't skip over this if you're a fan. It's a 15 year love letter to one of the most important games ever made. You can feel it in every inch of the game. Cant wait for them to remake it in Source 2 now in another 15 years.

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't played Half Life before but I can understand why it is considered a classic. Comparing this to the original in youtube is night and day. The guys at Crowbar Collective have done a brilliant job with the graphics, and especially Xen is breathtaking. The soundtrack is atmospheric and spot on. Gameplay wise the game is your classic FPS but with excellent weapons that are all useful at some point. The riddles are quite fun with the proper difficulty for an fps, and platforming stages are also solid and a nice break from battle. The setting and pace of the game is excellent without cutscenes and too much dialog which I prefer in games. But Lore is there and presented very smartly during gameplay.Minor glitches and bugs do exist but nothing game breaking. A tad annoying is the framerate drop that happens on 2-3 very busy fights towards the end of the game but I played with the graphics maxed out.Overall I think every FPS gamer should experience this game at some point. It is made with great attention and love and I am sure you will love it as well.

_childDocuments_.review: I am really impressed by the job done by the Crowbar Collective. I hardly remembered how good Half-Life was when I played it the first time. It was only a souvenir of a good game. After replaying the whole game, I can say that it does not get old. It still has everything you could expect from a modern FPS and that is why it was such a break through at the time. You don't have to simply shoot all your enemies, you have to think a lot. _childDocuments_.review: I played this when it was just a fanmade mod. I was so pissed after they wanted to turn a mod into a paid game. I was so sure they were going to change the game into something else. I was right, for the wrong reasons.Black Mesa is not only a fan remade of Half Life, it's also has its own unique flavour. New textures, great gunplay, high immersion, improved HL maps, keeping the legendary moments of the original... It's just great and you have to play it.I wasn't one of those "xen when?" people, but it actually bothered me how long it took just to get new textures to slap on the existing maps and puzzles. So, is it the same Xen we know and love?♥♥♥♥ NO! NEW XEN IS UNIQUE AND IT IS A MASTERPIECE.I was just expecting a reskin of the original maps, and what did I get? Totally new maps with new puzzles! I love the atmosphere, models and everything, it took me hours to finish the Xen maps. I was checking EVERYTHING, from a rock on the ground to stars in the skybox. _childDocuments_.review: Still Half Life. Still immersive and atmospheric as hell. Goes to show just how inspired the original was if it's still able to captivate me years on. I've been looking to replay the series, but having played the original several times over the years, I figured I'd wait until this 'remaster' to give it another go. I'm glad I did. The added level bits and characer interactions are welcome little distractions and don't take away from the experience or feel 'tacked on'; the guts are still the same old Half Life you know and love, just with a that shiny nice look provided by a fresh audio-visual coat of paint. _childDocuments_.review: After years in development, it was definitely worth the wait.What can I really say about this game besides calling being a masterpiece? Everything about it is great. It takes Half-Life 1 and improves on it. Instead of blocky corridors and rooms, the levels feel like an actual research facility. Each level has new things to experiment with; new things to interact with- I spent 20 minutes alone playing with the grinders in Residue Processing. Crowbar took liberties in detailing and expanding the game, and it shows. Speaking of expanding... Xen. Holy Headcrabs. I watched a playthrough of the original, and it doesn't have ANYTHING on Black Mesa. The amount of worldbuilding that was created for Xen is astounding.-It's a lush, but dangerous alien world. -The conditions the Vortigaunts are living and working in actually shows their enslavement better.  -The final boss battle is super climactic, and is a lot more fun to fight.-The Gonarch looks even more like a Scrotum Spider- and that's a good thing!The only bugs I ever encountered (besides aliens) were some subtitles not lining up with audio, some occasional crashes (but that's to be expected, thanks autosave!), and some occasional jank with terrain.Overall, Black Mesa is a great remaster and rework of Half-Life, and was exceptionally fun. The game rewards exploration and creativity in some parts, and even has achievements for those who want to enjoy their experience. 10 of the World's Smallest Coffee Cup  10.

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa is so good and professional, it's impossible to tell that this is actually not an AAA-title with big publisher but a fan-made game that baked 14 years in the oven. Black Mesa is brilliant, utterly professional reimagining of cult classics. Equally good for old dogs like me and newcomers.I salute to the bravery of the Crowbar Collective, really. There are tons of changes. Good changes. Essential changes. It's not even on par with Half-Life. It's tad betted. It's Half-Life as you remembered it. Minus the ugly models, jank, poor Xen chapters and abysmal movement systems from 1998.Black Mesa is fun, beautiful and engaging FPS game with great pacing and surprisingly competent visuals. It's a good FPS game even without the Half-Life legacy. Long one too. Took me 20 hours with Xen on Normal.Honestly, if you love good FPS games or good games in general, you should definitely pick Black Mesa up. Even if you're not into the Half-Life craze, it's a crime to miss such focused and honest single-player shooter w/o service bullcrap, fp2 BR mode or mtx.Support the devs! _childDocuments_.review: I bought Black Mesa because I had never played the original Half-Life and wanted to experience it but with better graphics.  I am okay at FPS games, and I played the game at its default difficulty of normal.I thoroughly enjoyed my time overall with this game.  I had only one crash late in the game, and don't recall any bugs or glitches while I played.  From the beginning up to Xen, I really got immersed in feeling like I was making my way through a gigantic complex.  There are times that feel claustrophobic, and others that feel epic and genuinely brought a smile to my face.  There are times where you are working your way down corridors, and there are huge battles in open arenas.  I enjoyed that there were times that were low key, where you were doing some platforming or exploring or puzzling, so that it wasn't constant action.  The game "breathes", and I prefer that style immensely.Xen onward was a mixed bag.  I loved the first couple areas of Xen.  It looks fantastic, and you are given plenty of opportunities to enjoy the alien flora and fauna.  From the first big boss fight onward, my excitement started to wane--but it wasn't terrible by any means.  The difficulty definitely jumps up.  You start having combat that is a bit different than before in that you really need to continuously move quickly.  Previous to this, I felt I could duck in and out of cover.  You start having long chase scenes where you have to puzzle out your path while instant death is constantly on your heels, which can lead to what feels like trial-and-error with little actual strategy or skill involvement.  Epic feeling once you know where you are going, but annoying until that point.  Levels start to feel long and repetitive, and felt more like gaming challenges than immersive experiences.  Some are fine with that, but for me the level and encounter designs felt lesser than what came before.  Final boss battle is intense and will give you a challenge but feels very epic and I enjoyed it.If you like FPS games, it's a good one.  Just be ready for a difficulty jump at the end, and remember that when in doubt, run like hell.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll begin by saying that I didn't play the original game. I did play HL2 and all episodes, so I was waiting for Black Mesa to finally play all HL games. And it was worth it. Even if u compare current FPS games with HL, it immediately becomes clear how simple and empty the games are. They have almost no challenge, u will always be shown where to go and what exactly to do. In HL u have no mini-map, no objective reminder, only HP and ammo counter. The enemies are also very aggressive and u have to strafe and parkour to get to the next level. Yes, modern games can surprise you with excellent graphics, animation, sometimes even great stories. But there's nothing like HL. And I'm absolutely sure that there aren't so many games that even 20 years later I would like to re-run. There are some minor glitches and performance issues (especially on Zen level), but I think it's mostly because of the Source engine. If u still didn't play HL, now is the perfect time to start.

_childDocuments_.review: Not only does Black Mesa present a distinct makeover of a historically noteworthy FPS to a modern audience, but it adds enough of its own spice to merit the unique title.Visually, the two-decades' shift in technology facilitates a grander scale to the game's events. Outdoor segments have more expansive and populated backgrounds which help to show the size and destruction of the conflict. The active storytelling that made the original Half-Life a game-changer is iterated upon with great new characterization. Plenty of new background events and dialogue add flavor and direction to the story. Humans are more tangible thanks to the more diverse and less comical voice acting. Texture and model work has of course received a satisfying upgrade, yet the addition of lighting overhauls is what best enhances the atmosphere in a way that just wasn't possible before.That said, Black Mesa is often held back by the requirements of its  material. Part of the impact of the original game came from its new ideas that have since spread to the rest of the industry. Without that pioneering context, Black Mesa faces an unequal level of scrutiny projected by its prestigious parent. Staying faithful to its legacy means that the blocky hallways and dreary industrial buildings remain a staple of many chapters. While many rough patches of gameplay have been streamlined, many backtracking areas remained disorienting even when assisted by knowledge of the original. Features such as quicksaving are a part of the source engine but, as always, the cumbersome system is self-destructively incentivized. It promotes insecurity and is a detriment to pacing that infects the level design. As it was, Black Mesa came across as a faithful and clearly dedicated homage worth recommending to those who were perhaps put off by the original's age. That is until Xen twists the game’s stagnation on its head.In the final act of Black Mesa, the remaster becomes a masterful reimagining as the game takes advantage of the creative potential provided by exploring an alien dimension. A litany of unique gameplay situations is spawned from discarding the details of the weakest portion of its predecessor. Gordon puts that Ph.D. to use while puzzling out extraterrestrial constructs in scenarios that expertly escalate. Additional movement via the long jump coupled with Xen’s bizarre environments brings new energy to combat. The composition and lighting of Xen, especially in its early hours, has no right to be as astonishing as it is. The presentation here is above and beyond the standards set by dusty New Mexico. Not a word is spoken throughout Xen yet its narratives, for both gameplay and story, are the most compelling of the whole game. Here, the term ‘chapter’ is an appropriate way to label each of Black Mesa’s levels.  all overshadow the premises of prior settings, making for a true climax to a true classic.Remakes and remasterings, especially ones described as 'built by fans', establish themselves on ground that is immediately vulnerable to comparative and biased critique. It's one thing to repaint and polish a game, but a far more demanding task to redesign and expand a game using its own principles. Black Mesa's studious reconstruction and its superb take on Xen show the competency of a team worthy of being a part of an essential series' legacy, not just 'fans'.

_childDocuments_.review: -ENG LanguageHalf-Life 1 is a remake of the original Half-Life game, and it's made by fans. There was no big studio involved, just a small team of people who were passionate about the game. It's amazing to see how much they were able to accomplish with such a small team. This is easily one of the best fan-made remakes ever made, and it's one of the best remakes in general. Half-Life was already a great game, but this remake takes it to the next level by enhancing the visuals, making the story more cohesive, and making some significant changes to certain levels. The visuals are stunning, the Zen section is especially beautiful, and the physics are just as you'd expect from Half-Life. There are a few small things I could nitpick about the game. One is that objects can be carried from the beginning to the end of the game in achievements, and the other is a few minor bugs. I didn't encounter any game-breaking bugs, but there were a few that were a bit annoying. I think this game is definitely worth the price of 100₺ or less, but whether or not it's worth more than that depends on how much you love Half-Life. Overall, this is a very successful remake.-TR LanguageHalf Life 1 oyununa yapılmış bir remake, üstelik bir fan projesi, büyük çaplı bir stüdyo yok işin içinde, sadece bu oyuna remake için oluşturulmuş bir ekip. Bu kadar küçük bir oluşumdan böyle harika bir iş çıkması gerçekten muazzam. Fan yapımı remake yapımlarında çok rahat en iyisi, genel remake yapımlarında ise bana göre en iyi remake oyunlarından biri. Half Life başlı başına zaten güzel bir oyun ancak burada oyunu görsel açıdan zenginleştirerek hikayeye daha uygun şekilde ve bazı bölümlerde çok ciddi değişiklikler yaparak sunmak bu oyunu zirveye taşımış. Görsel açıdan güzel, zen kısmı ayrı bir güzel, fizikler alıştığımız half life yani gayet başarılı. Oyunda eleştirebileceğim çok ufak kısımlar var. Bunlardan biri başarımlarda oyun başından sonuna taşınan objeler, ikincisi de ufak tefek buglar. Oyunu oynadığım süre içerisinde benim canımı sıkacak türde bir hata yaşanmadı ama. 100tl altı fiyatı kesinlikle hak edeceğinin düşünüyorum, üstü Half Life a olan bağlılığınıza göre değişir. Son derece başarılı bir yapım.

_childDocuments_.review: Having been introduced into the Half-Life franchise by HL:Alyx, I decided to finally experience the rest of the franchise. I wanted to get a complete understanding of the games' origins, I decided to play both the original HL and its remake.With both under my belt, I can safely say that Black Mesa is, in my opinion, the definitive way to play HL1. That's not to say that the original is bad. Far from it. It's very easy to see why people still love it and its importance to gaming history,However, having experienced it with more recent eyes, I can say that it hasn't aged well. BM takes what makes the original good, throws in a few spices, and cleans up it's rough edges. The two are somewhat different experiences, so I still encourage a playthrough of both games, but if you MUST choose between one version of the game to play, this one is easily the best way to experience one of gaming's giants. Great remake and the team should be proud.Post game edit: This game was, simply put, a masterpiece. This and HL: Alyx have cemented me as a fan.

_childDocuments_.review: With the release of XEN, Black Mesa is finally complete. I played this for the first time when this was a mod for Half-Life 2. The devs did an excellent job back then but I wondered why XEN was missing, you could say the ending felt very anti-climatic since the game was abruptly cut with a "Will Continue" message after you jumped into the portal.Talking about the main sections of the game, this recreates faithfully the original Half-Life in almost every aspect. You will feel right at home if you played the original. There's new gameplay aspects like Iron Sights for the revolver and whatnot, but you probably already knew that.Now on to XEN.I see why they took so long to release XEN in Black Mesa. The original Half-Life Xen was the most weak part of the game, technically speaking, as it felt very rushed, short and incomplete compared to the rest of the game. In Black Mesa's iteration, however, they didn't just remastered the already existing segments, they added a lot of new gameplay mechanics, stages, new segments that pushed the use of the Space Jump Module for a more exciting combat experience and expanded much more to the already existing lore of Half-Life... all of this essentially for free, if you already bought the game.I'm so glad this exists and I would wholeheartedly recommend to anyone, already existing and new Half-Life fans alike, to purchase this masterpiece. It has been a hell of a ride saving the world while being late to work in Black Mesa.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game with a super intriguing story that's revealed through dialogue and gameplay rather than exposition. _childDocuments_.review: I bought the original Half Life as soon as it came out. I had to upgrade my PC but it was worth it. I really think Black Mesa captures most of that feeling although I'm not calling my friends about it, I miss those days.Before I continue I need to mention Stalker. _childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa is an interesting modernized version of Half Life. It has beautiful level design and interesting visual storytelling. I understand Crowbar Collective's intent to remake the Xen levels, but the Xen levels feel off and unnecessarily extended, especially Interloper and parts of both Xen and Gonarch's Lair. The same could be said to a degree for Nihilanth which feels like a bunch of flashy particles but is still a fun boss fight for the first two stages. _childDocuments_.review: is a lovingly crafted re-creation of the 1998 classic  that adds a modern shine & smoothness to the graphics and gameplay, while retaining the core  gameplay experience. retains the classic FPS gameplay feel of  and as such is pretty distinct from more precise-feeling modern shooters. It is not, however, overly clumsy or cumbersome. Gunplay is fairly basic by design, but solid and satisfying. The player is given a large variety of different weapons with their own strengths and weaknesses, and is encouraged to make use of their full arsenal due to limited ammo supplies and varied enemy types. Loadout includes typical firearms such as pistols and shotguns, explosives such as grenades and trip mines, plus more exotic items such as a scoped crossbow, a projectile-firing alien creature, and an experimental beam-cannon.Movement, while not precise, flows well and provides a good sense of momentum, allowing the player to quickly navigate their environment.Original  level design has been faithfully recreated in , with all the puzzles, platforming and vent-crawling that entails. With the exception of the  section of the game, the basic level aesthetic has also been retained from the 1998 classic. This aesthetic coupled with the far more modern and detailed level decoration helps to maintain the player's sense of playing a classic game without making it feel too dated. Expect linear levels across a variety of environments, each with their own hazards, puzzles and environmental features the player can make use of.The  section of  has been expanded and improved beyond what was in the original , making it a more fulfilling and enjoyable experience that contrasts considerably with the themes seen earlier in the game.The enjoyable story of  is accurately recreated in  with the bonus of modern graphics and audio to help tell the story of Gordon Freeman. This makes quite a difference, as the game does not feature cutscenes or lore snippets for the player to read. is a total visual recreation of the original game, with vastly improved models, textures and shaders. As  was built on the relatively dated  engine, visuals are not on par with today's stunners like , but are still very nice and obviously a great deal better than the 1998 original.The recently completed  section of the game is the real visual treat of . What was originally a dull green and brown wasteland is now a stunning and vibrant alien world, rich in colour and life.Using the hardware listed above I was usually able to play  at maximum settings with a smooth framerate well in excess of 60fps, though it would dip considerably when there were a lot of particles on screen, and in some areas of .Sound effects in the majority of  are adequate and of decent quality, though don't seem to have much reaction to the environment and don't travel far. Many times I would throw a grenade a short distance, duck back around the corner and wouldn't hear the explosion at all. I also had trouble hearing NPC dialogue unless I was very close to them.Music plays rarely during gameplay, leaving the player to enjoy their adventure in silence most of the time. When the music does kick in, it's for a special gameplay section like a boss fight or a dramatic reveal. This serves to give the player the sense that a significant event is going on, and makes every one of these events a little bit more special. This is aided by the quality of the soundtrack itself, which is excellent.As with the visuals,   section contains the best of all.Ambient sounds are excellent, giving the alien location a real sense of being a vibrant place packed with strange life. Music in  is simply beautiful, and plays at exactly the right moments.Aside from the audio distance issue I mentioned above, I have encountered only two very minor technical issues, both related to level design not working quite the way it was intended. In both these cases, I was only slowed down very briefly and as such they did not affect my overall experience.  not only recreates the original  experience, but arguably improves upon it in almost every way. It's enjoyable not just as a nostalgia trip, but as a good game in its own right.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, absolutely yes. If you've played the original Half-Life, then this is the perfect homage to the game. Once you get there yourself, you'll see.For newcomers to the Half-Life series, this is the perfect introduction to it. While I do recommend the originals, the old school graphics and Quake/Doom like movement might not suit everyone and this does away with new graphics and refactoring of the movement(though knowing Source games, it still retains some of old-school movement). _childDocuments_.review: A brilliant reimagining of a timeless classic. If you've never played the half life series before but are turned off by the dated-ness this is a great way to get the same experience with a more modern feeling. It stays true to the original but it's also not a carbon copy.For those of you who are familiar, this is not just a fresh coat of paint or some HD textures. It's the entire game redesigned and remastered. The levels and puzzles will be familiar, but the entire thing feels different; it's a totally new experience and  absolutely worth playing.Now for the thing on everyone's mind: is it worth $20? As a standalone product, absolutely. It delivers enough content with the quality to justify that price tag.The point of contention here is that the game was released earlier as a free mod. I haven't played much of the mod, but the money and valve's support here seems to have been used to take the mod a bit beyond what it could achieve as a mod alone - full use of the latest source engine, a multiplayer mode with steam workshop integration for maps, graphics and sound improved even further, gameplay stability improved greatly (I haven't encountered a single bug or glitch on my playthrough). Certainly, this is an improved experience from the mod and not just the same thing with a price tag slapped on. I'm given to understand the devs have kept the mod release (now legacy version) available for free so it's up to you to decide whether $20 is a worthy asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: when i first heard about this when it was still a mod, i was honestly a bit skeptical. i mean, let's be honest, the fact that crowbar collective even did this was amazing, considering the original mod was done as a side project, if i remember correctly.during the first few minutes of the mod, i was already extremely impressed with how realistic everything looked compared to the original half-life's graphics. and the soundtrack was very memorable for me. the intro had a surprising amount of impact, though im assuming that was done purposefully for half-life fans.this mod does the half-life series justice in an incredible way, being remade from scratch in the updated source engine using brand new models, sounds, textures, lighting, voice clips, soundtrack, etc. etc.and the (not quite) full, retail release of black mesa is somehow even better than the original mod, with even better looking textures, models, and lighting, new scripted events, amazing voice acting...as a longtime half-life fan, it's very hard to find words good enough to describe how amazing black mesa is.crowbar collective deserves some serious credit and recognition for having the determination and effort to remake a cult classic from the ground up.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not really one to play First Person Shooters (Aside from TF2) and honestly these kind of games usually don't interest me. In fact, FPS games are my least favorite genre. But when I finally decided to play Black Mesa (Which I had come to learn about through my brother), I couldn't put it down! I've never played the original Half-Life, however I can really see how much the developers of Black Mesa loved the original and their passion for it. Their love and dedication to this game is something I really felt and has won me over. There's really a feeling of tragedy and disaster in the game; to which I find myself doing my best to protect the scientists and security partners. You feel sad and helpless when you watch another scientist and/or security guard get killed and there's nothing you can do about it. I don't know how many times I've tried to save one scientist from falling to his death only to watch him die and have myself die several times in the process! At least until I realized there was literally no way to save him.I can't wait to finally visit Xen and complete the game! I'm just having a hard time figuring out whether I should wait until Black Mesa is complete to play my recently purchased copy of Half-Life 2 or to just play it now!Update: July 4th 2021:After five years, I finally found time to complete this game. I did end up playing the original Half-Life all the way through and Half-Life 2 before Xen was released for this game. I think that was for the best because Xen absolutely blew me away. They took the alien border world  with vaguely different areas (I don't blame Valve at all, it's originally from the 90's after all) and turned into a living and breathing world and ecosystem. I adore this game and since I originally wrote this review, I have become a Half-Life fan. I can't recommend this game enough.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is better than the original. I'll go over the pros and cons and give a summary at the end.PROS:-Made the guns look like real guns-Made New models for evreything-Made a Zombie Guard-Added new voicelines and character interactions-Made new animations for all the guns, including sprinting, reloading, fireing, and made a animation for when you pick up the gun for the first time-Made objectives clearer-Made Female and Black Scientists so they're all not the same 3 models-Hired some diffrent voice actors for scientists and gurads so they don't all sound the same-Looks great-More Interactions with guards and scientists-Got rid of a ton of stupid bugs in HL1-Made it modeble via Steam Workshop-Added new tons of new sounds-The Achievements are actually cool, and you don't get them just by playing the gameCONS:-Diffucult, but not much more than HL1-Sometimes NPC's bug out -The music is a little worse than HL1 but still excellant-Hazord Suit still talks for 5 minutes when you put it on-Xen levels aren't realeased yet but I don't really care about thoseSUMMARY:It was tons better than I expected, I spent my first 20 minutes maxing out all the dialougue.
