_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa: Definitive Edition (November 2020 – based upon the developers’ final big update) was created by a group of modders named the Crowbar Collective and is the remake of Valve Software’s 1998 first-person shooter, Half-Life. The development for Black Mesa started around 2005 as a mod, with modders recreating the Half-Life levels up to Forget the Freeman. The Black Mesa mod was released around September 2012 for free on their website or Moddb website. Since, then the mod was released to the Steam platform in 2015. There were tweaks, major revamps on level designs, and the long-awaited Xen levels were released. Black Mesa and its developers garnered significant praises from critics and Half-Life franchise fans alike while criticisms on some level designs, shortened levels in some areas, and instances of broken AI. Is Black Mesa considered one of the best remakes ever made?Black Mesa utilizes the Source engine like it was with Half-Life 2 and the two episodes that came after HL2’s release date. When I play the game and look at the graphical feature, the developers seem to enhance the game engine as polished and contemporary as possible. There were notables features like the god rays, unique and original texture design (XEN-related), lighting effects, and unique shadow settings. I do admit the developers’ graphical features were highly impressive. Black Mesa is not 100% back-to-back rendition to Half-Life, but Crowbar Collective did an excellent job on designing the levels for the modern demographics and those who played Half-Life. Surface Tension is, arguably, the best level in Half-Life. For Black Mesa, Surface Tension cranked up the intensity up to 11 as Gordon Freeman fights to survive in the surface against overwhelming odds with original soundtrack from Joel Nielson. There are some reviewers who compare Joel to Kelly Bailey, but in my view, I think it is an unfair comparison. Bailey’s soundtrack is, without a doubt, a godsend for the Half-Life franchise. Nielson’s soundtrack for Black Mesa is very impressive and I usually listen to Nielson’s during gym workouts. I do have the commend Joel Nielson for creating such an outstanding soundtrack with notable examples from We Got Hostiles, Surface Tension, and XEN. The gameplay is the same as the Half-Life franchise, therefore I will not go further details on it. What impressed me the most in Black Mesa is how the HECU (Hazardous Environment Combat Unit) felt more humanize than the original Half-Life. If the player pays attention to military radios and dialogue interaction among HECU, the HECU were placed in an unwinnable battle with a mixture of grave desperation on leaving the facility, conflicted thoughts on killing Black Mesa personnel, and frightful emotions on fighting against the XEN creatures. Half-Life shows the HECU as one-dimensional NPCs groups only came to kill Freeman, Black Mesa personnel, and all living groups without thought. Black Mesa portrays the HECU a lot better. This feature is subtle, but I really appreciate the voice acting for the HECU as genuine since the voice acting sounds very familiar to me, probably from modern first-person shooter, Insurgency?There are some criticisms for Black Mesa. For me, the primary criticism is the enemy artificial intelligence. Usually, when the enemy detects the player, the enemy starts to shoot the player until the player is out of the enemy’s line of sight. In Black Mesa, there were some notable instances. An example is when a HECU NPC was shooting the .50 caliber MG at me across the map in the level, On the Rails. The second example is when the entire HECU patrol of 10+ personnel already knew where I hid and still shoots at the player across the map and when the player is out of sight. I believe the enemy AI behaves the same as the Combine AI in Half-Life 2 and the following two episodes. There are three difficulty modes: Normal, Black Mesa (default), and Hard. The difficulty modes are unbalanced as the “normal” mode is normal mode but the weapon damage against the player is inconsistent. Black Mesa difficulty feels more like Hard mode with a single hit can cost you roughly around 10 health points or takes out most HEV charge points. The player can be killed in a matter of seconds even at full health. Playing the game on hard mode is asking to commit suicide. I enjoy a difficult challenge like playing Halo games in Legendary difficulty, but some instances in Black Mesa where the enemy can shred you before the player can react baffles me. Another criticism is some of the level design and can feel a bit of a drag. The notable example is the level – Interloper. I appreciate the beauty for Crowbar Collective creating the XEN world, but Interloper wants me to pull out my hair. I thought the modders can simplify the Interloper level with shorter time for platforming and puzzles before meeting Nihilanth. There are other examples on criticizing level designs from different levels in Black Mesa, but it will take too long to complain.At the end of the day, Black Mesa was developed by modders who are Half-Life fans, and probably want to make a proper remake for the first game, unlike Valve’s lazy port – Half Life: Source. I do have to commend the modders on finally finishing and polishing the remake for this long. The XEN world is very mystifying but beautiful. The portrayal of the HECU in Black Mesa is certainly better than the original. The general level design is good for most of my experience in Black Mesa accompanied by the outstanding original soundtrack by Joel Nielson. Seeing the end credits made me emotional, particularly when looking at the “former developers” section. Black Mesa really took this long to develop and has fully blossom to its highest potential. For me, Black Mesa is one of the best remakes I play so far and has a solid recommendation on getting this game regardless of the $20 USD default price or on a discount. An essential purchase for your Steam library.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent fan-made remake of the original Half-Life game. I thoroughly enjoyed the first part where Freeman has to escape the facility; It kept true to the original story and maps while also adding some additional rooms and spaces to explore. The introduction, just after the Resonance Cascade event, is even more atmospheric and spookier than the original - adding in the half-zombies was a great touch. The soundtrack is also marvellous; Internal Conflict by Joel Nielsen goes too hard.However, this game is not without its flaws. It did crash on me a couple of times, but most often during the Nihilinth boss fight. Unfortunately, I did spend a good chunk of time relaunching my game and reloading uncorrupted saves before the crash trying to figure out how to defeat the boss. It took me far too long to realise that the rocket launcher was doing negative damage to its brain (makes sense) so once I swapped to the tau cannon I easily overcome it and was able to finish the game. Getting thrown out of bounds may have also added salt to the wound...The Xen level is absolutely gorgeous (so beautiful in fact there are entire guides on how to farm it for screenshots). Visually extremely stunning and rich in fauna and flora I actually preferred this over the original. The alien levels do drop off a bit in quality as they go on. The Interloper chapter was particularly tedious and repetitive, some parts poorly construed and thrown together. Perhaps the developers were also running out of steam towards the end.This game is well-worth a play-through but is by no means a replacement to the original which I believe remains the GOAT.

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa is a fan-remake for the Half Life game from 1998 with improved graphics,new areas and some bits of story changed  but with the same original atmosphere . The question is should you play the original or the remake? The answer is different for everyone ,it's up to you to decide. For me it was simple ,i went for the remake for more content and better graphics. Made with Half-Life 2's Source engine,this was the perfect foundation for me to start a entire Half Life series playthrough. It's amazing Black Mesa is allowed to be sold as a standalone game, Valve earned a lot of respect and popularity from gaming community because of this. To be honest Black Mesa was my guilty pleasure to delve into the Half Life universe,a perfect excuse to try an old title for the first time and a perfect introduction to Half life 2. What stands out from the original game is the final chapters of the remake for me. The Xen section and some boss fights are on another level of quality and design and some areas are completely new. The visuals are breathtaking ,you just don't expect something like this from a Half Life remake. Experiencing the story for the first time was beautiful,it's sad they don't make games like this anymore. The multiplayer lobby most of the time are empty but from time to time you'll find some people to play with.In my opinion this is a must-play ,if before people like me had an excuse to skip the Half Life 1,with Black Mesa remake it's almost mandatory.Pros:-one of the best remakes -good story (same as original with some changes to fit better with rest of the series)-solid fps experienceCons:- sometimes it's not clear how to complete a puzzle or how to progressMy review score:Story   - 10Gameplay- 9Graphics- 9Sound  - 9Overall - 9.25

_childDocuments_.review: It was a long journey; It all started in 2008, when it was called Black Mesa: Source. Black Mesa: Source was basically a fan made recreation of the 1998 classic game made by VAVLe called "Hλlf-Life". The mod team shared it's first trailer in 2008. But after delays and pushback to date, Black Mesa: Source was released in 2012 on ModDB. The mod initially set Black Mesa Source as a free modification. Skipping to 2015, that's when it really kicked off as VALVe (the creator's of Hλlf-Life) has given the approval of the game being green lit via it's service "Steam greenlight", which as of now has been defunct. Black Mesa Source was renamed to "Black Mesa" and became an Early Access Game, being sold on the Steam Store for $20 USD. It was an amazing thing for the developers, but one thing was still missing from the remake, Xen. Xen is the last levels in Hλlf-Life where you travel to the unknown borderworld, known as Xen. The reason why Xen wasn't added in the early days (as in 2008 - 2015) because the dev team wanted to recreate the Xen levels as in Hλlf-Life, the level design was really poor, it got Gabe Newell, CEO of VALVe to say the he didn't like the design of what Xen looked like in the 1998 Hλlf-Life. The Dev of BMS wanted to make sure that the mod wouldn't have poor level design of Xen. Black Mesa would receive basic small updates, not constant, but little content that could add stuff in the game, like the Crossfire update, which as the name suggests, adds 1 new map to Multiplayer mode, Crossfire (a Hλlf-Life classic map) That was one to name a few.Years and years have passed from 2015 to 2018, that's when the Black Mesa community and fans were given it's first look at Xen with a Trailer showcasing, the beauty nature in Nov 19, 2018. Into the year of 2019 on June 26, the dev team released 3 chapters of Xen to the public in a Beta test stress for Xen levels, see how different player computers were to one and another, this test was implemented for number of reasons, the most common was to see game performance, bug fixes. In December 6, that when all the Xen levels was released. Into the new year, new decade of 2020;After the huge full beta announcement, we would have thought of something that the team would do, but, in February 24, 2020 an article on Steam news for the game was published titled "Fear Not The Long Road" by Adam Engels. The article was him describing his years on how he started and what he encountered in the years. However, what was really intriguing was on before the last line "Black Mesa 1.0 will launch Thursday March 5th on Steam." This confirms that Black Mesa will now exit Early Access Game, which has been in for the past 5 years, and after from reading that, I think to myself going back to the Source era of Black Mesa, we have to appreciate the devs at Crowbar Collective. As a fan of Half Life and this mod, it makes me tear up to the point of now, realizing how far it was from completion, and now how close it's now to completion. I want to say, from the bottom of my heart, thank you @Crowbar Collective. The team that worked on the game, whether it was code, sound, visuals. You all have to give yourselves a pat on the back and a thank you from the community. What a journey it was and still going to be a journey after the March 2020 release.Feel free to correct any thing that I may have forgotten or mixed up.Article news -

_childDocuments_.review: I completed the tedious achievement tasks of carrying a purple hat and pizza box to the end of the game. I would still recommend the game despite some moments of sheer frustration with said objects. In fact, if you're a Half-Life veteran looking for a solid challenge, try to earn those achievements in your playthrough! Half-Life was a fantastic game which still holds its own today. Black Mesa gives it a pretty facelift, but the core game mechanics feel unchanged. Movement is fast and free, and it remains one of the best feeling FPS games out there. The development team that transferred this game to the modern era did so with care. Even though I still appreciate the original Half-Life game and would still happily play it, this Black Mesa update is beautiful. Some may complain that the updated graphics are already outdated due to the lengthy development time the game experienced, but I seriously don't know how one could choose this aspect to whine about when you consider the price point while also remembering that the original objective of the development team has been achieved: they updated the graphics of Half-Life!In the end, if you're a gamer who missed Half-Life's original release, you need to buy this game to experience one of the greatest and most important games of all-time. If you just enjoy playing shooters, this game is also for you because the movement of your character is light yet tight while also providing you with a fun, wide arsenal of weapons to choose from. Finally, if you liked Half-Life, then purchasing Black Mesa should be an easy decision for you!

_childDocuments_.review: This is so much more than what I expected from a Half-Life reboot, This is so amazing, the graphics are beyond what I was hoping for, even without the Xen levels it's still so fun, This has blown my expectations through the roof, Thank you Crowbar Collective for making this amazing reboot, even on my old laptop with a core i3 processor and a terrible CPU Black Mesa runs very well with little to no lag or freezing.I think this game deserves the even better then I expected award because It blew my expectations out of the water....I decided to check this game out since I last played and reviewed it in early access. To say the least what I said before still holds up. This game is a really good port of Half Life to the source engine. The graphics still hold up too. And... (Finally Xen is added to the game) I also like how it makes changes to the core gameplay of Half Life to make some minor improvements. (Some major even like the Gonarch's Lair chapter) I specifically really like how the gonarch really seems like a big threat with how it can knock you off from the part that it first shows up if you're not careful. Yet it's still a fun battle. And the fact that you can use gas to kill the gonarch in the lair. Just creative, a really nice touch. The sound design for that chapter really adds to the battle too.Overall I really liked most of the changes to Xen and feel like it made some improvements over the original Half Life. However, I don't like some of the new enemies in Xen. (The exploding houndeyes specifically.) Additionally the pacing of Interloper is WAY TOO SLOW! To say the least... I like the idea of adding in puzzle elements to that chapter but I feel it's kind of overdone and the pacing bogs down the chapter. The final boss with the Nihilanth was great too though. I didn't like how the Nihilanth could teleport you to different areas in the original Half Life. I still feel like that slowed the pacing a bit too much. So that not being there in Black Mesa was a plus. I also really liked the addition of a shield around the Nihilanth that you had to destroy to even do any damage to it. It added a challenge that made the boss battle feel more satisfying. Oh and the way the Nihilanth blows up too at the very end. Chefs kiss. Just how that looks in the source engine. The scenery in Xen too is just beautiful and looks so great in the source engine. This is a really great remake of Half Life in the source engine... Still! I highly recommend this game to anyone who has already played the original Half Life and wants a fresh spin on the game. However, it does not replace the original Half Life for me. Half Life will always be an iconic shooter for years to come. There's a reason it has lasted the test of time (even with the dated graphics) So regardless, I recommend playing Half Life before you play Black Mesa. Doing so made me appreciate both games way more.All the rambling aside I love this game. It's a great remake that still holds up. It has it's short comings but to be fair so does the original Half Life. A strong 8/10 No less!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a rare thing when I choose to actually play the campaign of a first-person shooter three times within the space of a couple of months because I couldn't stop thinking about it. I thought it was just nostalgia and yeah, that contributed in the first play through but I went through the second and third times simply because I enjoyed the game. It's just so damned good! It keeps all the vital elements of the original game; the puzzles, the action, the set pieces, the story and its ever expanding stakes and expands on them - it's big and bold. And while it's can't be said to be original since it's a remake of Half-Life- this isn't a simple remake, this is probably the most imaginative remake (a re-imagining?),  I've ever played.The original was criticised for the Xen levels since compared to the rest of the game they felt rushed, bland and less detailed but I'm happy to report that on the subsequent play-through's I  looked forward to getting there. Your introduction to "Xen" is glorious, and gives you the sense that this is place where the xeno's thrive in the wild, and where scientists came, set up camp, observed and gathered specimens way before things went south... In the original game "Interloper", the penultimate level before the battle with the main antagonist was remarkable in one regard: It was a long boring slog in unimaginative arenas which served no way to drive the story. In Black Mesa, yes, it's still long, but it reinforces the idea that the thing that you are in is this massive bio-engineered factory used to build more bio-weapons and that its a place of research and science. The puzzles are stream lined the battles are tough but its well paced and I enjoyed the verticality.Crowbar Collective and all the developers who contributed to this masterpiece deserve all the success and credit they get and AAA developers really need to take a look at this and ask themselves whether they do the industry and the FPS genre, easily the most accessible game genre, justice when they ship their 8-level, 6 hour (If you're lucky) lack-lustre campaigns. The original half-life came out in 1998, with the sequel two years later. I would defy you to suggest that FPS's have moved on since then because as far as I can tell the only thing that's been added is quick-time event and unimaginative stories.  It's genuinely the best FPS I've played since probably Doom 2016 and easily the best remake I've played this year. It's simply  that good.This is a classic FPS in the best possible style, a monument to one of the biggest games in history and stands testament to what FPS's can be. It's more than worthy of your cash at a mere £15.Glorious!

_childDocuments_.review: It was worth the wait, last time i played Black Mesa was during the first public release of the mod way back in the day, even back then we've already waited ages to play it and now we've waited even more for it finally be fully done and it was indeed worth it.It's an absolutely excellent way to re/experience the first game's story be it as a newcomer or a fan , it was improved in basically every way, especially the Xen part of the game, apart from one area in Xen which is the factory chapter where the vortigaunts are enslaved to work at. That area starts off fine but as it progresses the quality start dipping sharply and it was unnecessarily made longer then the original chapter but as i mentioned, apart from that bit, the rest of xen is better in every way versus the original and it looks gorgeous, downside is since they're pushing this old engine by force to do things it was never ment, Xen runs a lot worse then the research facility chapters of the game, i can dip as low as 40 or 50 fps in some areas of xen which considering this is a source based is pretty bad, since source games tend to easily hit 200+ fps even on low end PCs of today, still the visuals on display on Xen do justify the dip and especially considering its being pushed on such an aging engine.Worth every penny, good job to the guys and gals at the crowbar directive.

_childDocuments_.review: The original Half-Life has not aged very well, but many of the core components remain strong. Black Mesa draws upon these components, re-imagines the familiar settings and encounters, and brings the old classic into the modern PC gaming landscape. While the engine is showing its age, the gameplay is as strong as ever and the team behind Black Mesa successfully captured and distilled what made the original title so remarkable. The big moments are still there and they feel as amazing as ever, while the more dull and tedious portions of the original title- such as the On a Rail -have been redesigned to make them more engaging and fit seamlessly into the title. The first two thirds of the same are spent at the Black Mesa facility with only a few changes to the overall design.XEN, the climax of Half-Life, ended up being one of the worst sections to play through in the original game. Black Mesa redesigned the entire XEN experience from the ground up, and this new iteration is stunning. XEN becomes a living, breathing environment. The previous teams that crossed over before Gordon have an actual presence on XEN and their fates are revealed through chilling environmental storytelling. "Lord Pendulous" also has more of a presence and its portion of the remade XEN experience is thrilling- if not occasionally frustrating. In fact, there are several times when Black Mesa stumbles. The paths you must take in chase sequences, especially in XEN, are not always clearly telegraphed and it takes me out of the experience when I die half a dozen times because I missed a turn in my haste not to get squished. In addition, while some portions of the original game have been trimmed and redesigned to make them more fun to play through, it feels like they transplanted some of that tedium to XEN. Interloper, especially, began to drag on during the second half and  could use some trimming. Less assembly line navigation, please.While nothing is perfect, the redesign of XEN was astounding and sparked my imagination in ways the original design never did. The changes made to the Black Mesa facility were a welcome redesign. The game looks good and I am very pleased with my purchase. I've been waiting for this title for over a decade. I stuck with it as a mod, lost interest for a bit, bought it when it hit greenlight, lost interest again when I heard XEN wasn't complete, and just recently discovered everything had finally been completed. The wait has been long but it has been worth it. Half Life has come a long way since the scrappy little FPS that made my 16 mb video card wet its circuits every time I turned the flashlight on.Hats off to the Crowbar Collective. You guys did a great job. I can't wait to give the Definitive Edition a good shakedown.Did I mention the music in XEN was phenomenal? Because it was. Joel Nielsen killed it.

_childDocuments_.review: Back in 2012 it was already an impressive feat to see this come alive as a full mod release, as I was used to impressive looking mods to barely or ever release at all. Browsing Moddb as a youngin I encountered lots of crushed dreams and lost hopes. Had you told me it would go all these lengths to feel like a full AAA title and more, I probably wouldn't have believed you. But it's done now, with the addition of a reimagined Xen chapter, the game has finally reached it's 1.0 release. I put it off for a while bc I was kinda occupied with other things since then, but I finally finished it again during my summer vacay. this marks a 3rd time for a full playthrough.Having played it way back I remember it being fun, but a bit jank in places. Jumping was particularly wonky as you got stuck quite a lot on common surfaces and props. Luckily, most of the jankness has been ironed out here and I barely ran into any issues in this playthrough compared to any previous ones I've done. I still think the AI is kinda lacking though, as grunts and aliens don't behave as "interestingly" as they did in the orignal. For the rest, well, it's Half Life as you know it. Not entirely faithfully recreated, but the changes are very much for the better as lots of issues I've had playing the first game MANY years ago aren't really present here anymore. Weapons all feel and look great, the updated environments from the first build (or the first store release) are really nice, and the reimagined Xen chapter is a sight to behold. Xen is a whole new otherworldly beast altogether, and yet...it doesn't feel out of place when I consider the game as a whole. I was there for it all the way til the end. It's neat.Sure, the game might feel a little dated in some areas when you think about it's mechanics or gameplay, but that's how Half-Life was back then too. And while the original graphically hasn't aged well, this updated version is a good alternative to experience the game, you could definitely do much worse (Half-Life source, gross).

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa is a fan-made, Valve-approved remake of the original Half-Life. Originally released as mod for Half-life 2.There's many improvements to the core game mechanically as well as narratively as one of the scientists that Gordon passes by in the introduction is actually Alyx's father from Half-Life 2. The original game only had a few character models for both the scientists and security guards.There's a not a lot to say about this, if you've never played the original Half-Life, this is the one to play now unless you're a purist.The game is not without its faults, I believe the game goes on for far too long, especially without any real explanation as to what is really happening. This was an issue in the original as well. The “ludo-narrative dissonance” is strong in this one. The story is told through Gordon's perspective but the overall world of Half-Life has much more going on it — even with the Black Mesa Compound. These things are alluded to with the presence of G-Man, but ultimately the story is told told “in the dark”. Gordon is more or less just trying to escape the facility after an experiment goes wrong.The game will bounce back and forth between heavy action sequences, creepy and dark horror sections and mix in some first-person platforming and environmental puzzling solving.While Half-Life will always have its place in gaming history, I'm not sure even this remake holds up to modern standards, or at least expectations. It's just sort of feels inherently old — the original game is from 1998 after all. I don't feel as though it's a must play, however. If you're feeling nostalgic or just want to see what all the fuss was about way back when, I think grabbing it on sale is a fair course of action. That said, I think it'd be pretty cool see Blue Shift and Opposing Force get remakes. Expansions for the original game from the perspective of a security guard and military grunt respectively.

_childDocuments_.review: My review: while an impressive achievement and definitely a visually updated look for Black Mesa, it manages to miss a lot of what made the original game good, as well as the sequels.Issue 1: the areas have all been made much larger out (to the benefit of the soldiers). This isn't a problem in terms of navigation, as the player can now sprint, but the enemy soldiers have much better aim than in the original, and the levels have drastically less cover than in the original. Exiting out into the surface in "We've Got Hostiles" kind of demonstrates the lack of understanding in level design, as the hangar no longer has the scattered crates you could use to circle around and hide behind cover. Enemy damage has been increased too, seemingly, making a single soldier from a mile away a significant threat that's hard to eliminate, even with the crossbow. One moment that comes to mind is when soldiers descend from a helicopter and simply mowed me down several times, with seemingly no viable way to eliminate them. I ended up lowering the difficulty to medium, which helped, but it was still ridiculous to see two guys with wooden animations slide into frame and push me with knockback into the back wall, killing me from full health/armor in a matter of seconds. The Questionable Ethics lobby fight was perhaps the worst culprit. You're trapped in a room with soldiers entering from above, the left, and the right, with almost no explosives, no rifle grenades, and with no cover in the arena, except a few boxes in the corner. I'm not sure if anyone even playtested that fight, as it devolved to hiding in the corner and waiting for the enemy to come into view, and peeking through a tiny gap in the crates. Another moment that comes to mind is the descending lift in Power Up. The lift exit in HL1 is surprisingly small, while the one in Black Mesa is a more distant and difficult encounter, especially with the blind corner. There are a few explosive barrels scattered around, which makes it seem like a prime way setting a trap, but its actually surprisingly hard to bait them into following while not taking significantly damage.Issue 2: alien enemy AI is worse. Bullsquids no longer charge at you (or move at all it seems), rather becoming stationary shotguns, with deceptively timed projectiles. Vortigaunts have terrible aim that can be dodged simply by sidestepping, and they rarely seem to recognize the player is in melee range. Owing to this, vortigaunt fights are less the peeking and ducking of the original, but rather a circular dash to blow them away with the shotgun. This was strategy in the original too, but it was guaranteed you would be hit by lightning if you missed your shotgun blast. In their updated level design, Office Complex suffers greatly. Where there was once a circular network of offices with you and four vortigaunts playing a game of cat and mouse, there's now a few cubicles in the middle, making it trivial to rush them. The disparity between soldier and alien difficulty is massive, moreso than in the original, despite houndeyes and bullsquids being useless in that one.Issue 3: missing setpieces from the first game. Most of the big moments are there, but there are a bunch of little scripted bits and environments that were a treasure in the original. They cut short On A Rail which was a common complaint in the original, but when you're remaking a game, they could have easily fixed the issues with it rather than cutting it entirely.Issue 4: no hazard course. Not a big issue but it wasn't a difficult thing to include, especially for a goldsource franchise staple.Issue 5: lack of puzzles/hl2 design advancements. HL2 excelled when it came to incorporating optional mini-puzzles into the maps, which definitely made the experience a little wooden. HL2 set the gold standard for physics based interactivity. Check out this video to know what I mean: . Physics only came into play in a handful of places, including a poorly telegraphed puzzle where the player has to use floating barrels to lift a sunken platform, which is only intuitive if you've played hl2. Hell, I almost got stuck on that part because they had barely acknowledged bouyancy before that point and I happened to notice the barrel container hallmark. Overall, some additional moments of interactivity could have been nice. The crate situation is also puzzling: the item rate has seemingly been lowered from the original game, making it feel pointless to try to smash open crates.Issue 6: ladders. I don't know what compelled them to create one of the most obnoxious and finnicky climbing systems of all time, and this is coming from a half-life fan. At least those behaved in a predictable way once you understood the mechanics.Issue 7: very buggy. It's easy to sequence break, get out of the map, or otherwise experience a ton of lighting, AI, or physics errors. Going through a vent with a physics object in them is a nightmare, as the shadow turns into a black blob that envelops the whole screen as you pass by it. Over all, it just feels like it's lacking final polish. If you manage to save a scientist they don't even acknowledge you, opting to stare into space, which isn't really a big issue but having some extremely basic "rescued" AI or voicelines would have gone a long way. Loading screens seem excessive or poorly positioned in a few areas. Soldiers endlessly shoot tracers through props and solid walls, and I had them lay waste to me straight up through a concrete fenceThere's probably a couple things I missed, but I'm not done the entire game yet. I did appreciate the dynamic lighting in several spots, like the rocket launch or laser test, and the game landscapes look terrific, but the texture quality is starkly lacking and many decals are rather pixelated. The soundtrack is generic, which seems rather poor compared to the classic.The vast majority of chapters (that I've played thusfar) I enjoyed less than in the original, barring Blast Chamber, Power Up, and Questionable Ethics (lobby fight excluded), which I feel exceeded it. I'm interested to see what the Lambda Complex or Xen plays like, but I've heard some bad news about the latter.

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa is a game that I have been following ever since I got into Half-Life. I would check up on it whenever it released a trailer or a gameplay video, I played the original 2012 mod, and yes, I purchased it the day it got put into Steam Early Access. Looking back, I couldn't have imagined how long it would be until this thing reached its proper conclusion. That said, having just now finished the public beta with all the Xen chapters, I am very pleased to say that it was worth the wait. No memes, just the hard truth. Now, before I touch on the Xen chapters, it's only sensible that I touch on the chapters featured in the original mod and the early access build, that being the chapters taking place in Black Mesa. Crowbar Collective did an excellent job reinterpreting the setpieces of the original Half-Life, whilst still remaining faithful to the general layouts of each area. Some places haven't changed much since the original mod if my memory serves me well, but in spite of that, they hold up very well in spite of being at least eight years old. Now, if you're someone who has played the original Half-Life to death and aren't sure if it's worth laying down $20 for what appears to be simply a prettied-up version of the game, worry not. This game is in many ways a beast of its own entirely, especially with the Xen chapters taken into account which I'll be getting to shortly. For starters, the combat feels quite different from both Half-Life and Half-Life 2. This is by no means a bad thing, but if you go into this game with the lessons regarding combat you learned in those games (like I did), expect plenty of booboos. The enemies are ruthless and they pack a punch even on normal difficulty, so you'll have to act smart in order to get the upper-hand in situations. On top of that, many puzzles are totally revamped in order to take full advantage of the Source engine. They take heavy inspiration to the type of physics-based puzzles, found in Half-Life 2, but in spite of this they manage to find their own identity with each having an interesting solution. It is an experience quite unlike any Half-Life game, but still manages to feel like a proper Half-Life experience overall nonetheless. Now for what really spurred me to write this review. As some of you may know, Xen is now fully playable via the public beta in order to help squash bugs and polish up some spots. Having waited so long, I decided I would take my chances and try it now, and boy was I in for a treat. To put in plainly, Black Mesa's Xen chapters blew my expectations right out of the water. Crowbar Collective took the original Xen chapters, which were a bit underwhelming in the original, and cranked them all up to a hundred, effectively making Xen the highlight of the entire game rather than a tedious and clumsy rushjob. I cannot understate how breathtaking it all is. Each chapter is beautiful, engaging, and quite lengthy to boot! While I could get through Xen in the original in as little as an hour, Xen in Black Mesa is about the length of a Half-Life expansion or episode. Playing through it all finally put things into perspective; it made perfect sense why the Xen chapters took so long, and why the team was so secretive for the longest time. Overall, Black Mesa is the Half-Life experience I have been desperately craving, and I can't wait to pick this up again once Xen goes out of beta.

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe it's just the fact that I'm turning 20 next month and I'm just looking back at the years I spent goofing off in high school, but all of a sudden 2012 really does seem like it was just yesterday. I remember waiting ferverously at my laptop, staring down the timer that was ticking down to the release of the Initial mod edition of Black Mesa. I remember eating the sandwich I brought home from Sonic as I watched the gorgeous new and improved tram sequence, thinking back to the first time I ever played half life back in 2009. For the uninitiated, Half-Life is a legendary first person shooter developed by the industry novice Valve that took many of the cliches the burgeoning FPS genre and smashed them over it's knee, mostly with it's coherent, uninterupted narrative and realistic level design. Alot of the technique that went into Half-Life was later mimicked by many other studios and developers trying to grasp what made the new king of the FPS genre so great... It was also the first FPS game I had ever played as a young kid, I remember begging my mom to let me play it even though it was rated M.Black Mesa, however, was born out of a desire to improve upon the lackluster Half-Life Source, which was released by Valve shortly after the release of Half-Life 2. People were understandably underwhelmed by what was essentially a port of the game with no real updates to the gameplay other than some wonky looking lighting and ragdoll physics. Forunately for the rest of modder-dom, a group of developers got to work to bring the world of Black Mesa up to the graphical standards of Half-Life 2.Initially released in 2012 without the Xen levels, Black Mesa source really did bring the game into the modern era, accomplished by but not limited to, updating and adding character and weapon models, fleshing out animations and textures, giving us clearer voice work, improving and expanding the maps from Half-Life to make them even more believable than they already were, and also adding in it's own custom soundtrack. You can certainly tell from just watching the initial Tram sequence that the developers treated this as a passion project for the longest time.Graphics nonwithstanding, there were a few changes to the pacing of the game which do change up the pacing and balance from the initial half-life. For instance, you get the crowbar slightly later than you normally would, and you'll pick up a revolver in the room with the guard behind the gate where you'd normally find a shotgun. Even though this mostly works to the game's favor, it does have some questionable decisions. The sequence you play through before you get the crowbar consists of you scooping up flares and throwing them at zombies while you wait for your security guard buddy to very slowly kill them for you. You can tell it was made to show off the capabilites of the source engine, but it's a very annoying sequence to actually play through. Even though these experiences aren't frequent enough to make the mod a chore to play, they certainly do feel a degree less intuitive than the original half-life. Overall though, the current release of the mod really does make the combat feel more visceral and more satisfying, with the gunshots being suitably menacing and the overall feel of shooting does make the combat sequences of the game all the better. They absolutely nailed the firefights you'll get into with the marines and black ops, as well as the aliens still being fun to fight.That being said, I feel like the sound design is mixed in some places. The voice acting for the Guards and Scientists is cleaner and crisper than it was in the original, but I feel like the original Half life has more memorable quotes that still comes ahead over Black Mesa. The sound design for the Aliens and Zombies is for the most part great (especially for the vortigaunts!!!), but I feel like specifically the houndeyes feel much less menacing than the original counterparts. The HECU in the game sounds quite frankly horrible, you can kind of tell that they were taking a page from Opposing Force's friendly grunts, but the enemies having almost friendly sounding voices doesnt hold a candle to the menacing voice chatter of the HECU from the original games.  On the topic of the sound-track, Black Mesa has it's own OST. The ambience and mood is on point, and when the soundtrack wants to make Gordon's experiences feel all the more primal, it can with tracks like the one that plays during We've Got Hostiles. Joel Nielsen is a very competent composer, but there's mods for people like myself who prefer the original OST.The last topic that needs to be addressed is the game, despite having been in development for over a decade, is still unfinished. The Xen chapters have been being worked on for a very long time. Some people will say you should shy away from purchasing until it's finished, and while I think their anger is understandable, I don't think the absence of the weakest part of the game is too terribly detrimental. Normally, I'd end my review with a footnote explaining my views on the game I'm reviewing, but I feel like Black Mesa is a unique case, as it does very much improve upon the original in many ways, while also falling short of the original in others. I feel like before buying Black Mesa, you should consider whether or not to try the base game first.  If you've never played Half-Life 1, and have no interest in it's vast ammount of mods or expansions, I'd say pick up Black Mesa in a heart beat. If you've played Half-Life 1 but want one of the biggest nostalgia trips of your life, I'd pick BM up on sale. If you want a game with tons more content, I'd pick up Half-Life 1 and it's expansions as Half life 1 has some of the most legendary mods known to gaming. Overall though, Black Mesa is worthy of being compared to the original, and it's certainly worth your time if you do decide to pick it up.

_childDocuments_.review: So I can finally say I've played a Half Life game, well technically since it's a remake, but either way this was one of the best video game experiences I've had in a long time.  It was a ton of fun, and I really appreciated the fact that this game doesn't question your intelligence as a player. You'll have to use this thing that most modern games ignore called your brain. The story while simple has a lot of deep underlying layers to it. There's more not being told on a surface level, and if you pay attention, listen to the radio, and once again use that noggin of yours than you're left with a pretty good tale of a scientist making his way through a govt research facility with his trusty crowbar! Gordan Freeman was the perfect silent protagonist. He's not the doom guy and the game recognizes this by not throwing you straight into the thick of it, but rather by slowing introducing you to the world of half life through the lens of a scientist just doing his job while these catastrophic events unfold. This game has some of the best pacing in any video game I've played tbh, it takes it's time to tell the story it wants to tell and shows you everything you need to know in order to understand and have fun. All in all Black Mesa was an incredible game and has given me some new found appreciation for how games are made and how much influence Half Life has on modern gaming. Crowbar Collective really outdid themselves here and it's really cool that Valve recognised that and published what started out as a fan remake mod to a fully fledged remake on steam.  Black Mesa gets a 9.5/10 from me!

_childDocuments_.review: This game really does have a strong answer for the age old question: Are modern games no longer fun or am I just getting older? Obviously, there are some fantastic modern games out there and you cannot paint them all with the same brush. However, playing through Black Mesa, having never really experienced the original Half-life in my youth, regrettably! I didn't have any of the nostalgia bias going in. Just a fresh open mind. And I'm so glad I did, as not only has the team who worked on this project for so many years earned every bit of recognition, it's clear that nothing but love and passion went into this. There is a clear reason why that not only is the game deserving of being Overwhelmingly Positive on steam but that the Half-life series is considered some of the best in gaming history. Do yourself a favour and pick up the crowbar.

_childDocuments_.review: a lot of people don't find the original hl1 too exciting and if you are one of those, give black mesa a try. this game makes your emotions do such parkour youve never felt beforepros:- the game is completely redone from the bottom- extremely gorgeous visuals- the bad design decisions from the original half life have been rethinked- good sound design- good gameplay- good story- the setpieces and small details make the world engaging and jaw dropping every step- a very memorable experience that anyone should playcons- the grunts ai is good, but less fun- the violence is a bit overdone for a half life game- the weapons dont feel as good to use and switching between them takes way longer making the gunplay worse in fights- the tau cannon's area damage and wall penetration is way worse- the xen factoryif youre new to half life, try the original aswell, it's totally awesome even 20 years later, but dont miss out on black mesa, this is one hell of a great game.

_childDocuments_.review: Having played and loved the first Half Life I was blown away that the experience can be improved by this large of a margin! The characters are alive, well played, the levels at some parts slightly different, improving the overall mood. _childDocuments_.review: A fantastic modernization of the original Half-Life that not only captures the original feel, but adds new depth and life to the environment and characters. Each level is painstakingly crafted with great attention to detail, movement and combat is swift yet punchy, the original puzzles are present yet slightly improved upon (usually), and the whole thing is just a ton of fun.I have little nitpicky complaints but my only substantial one is that the AI is a little spotty from time to time, and of course the slow updates. Though for a team originally comprised of fans working without compensation, it's an astonishing feat and well worth your 20 bucks, even with the wait for Xen (which is scheduled for December 2017)If you want to see what all the rage is about Half-Life but can't deal with games from the 90s, get Black Mesa! If you're feeling nostalgic about Half-Life but still want to play something new, get Black Mesa! It's good!

_childDocuments_.review: I played several gruelling hours of this with my girlfriend. The sound effects they've handpicked as replacements suck, the gunplay sucks, and the final parts of xen they've added is a complete utter slog and a level design disaster. They added more content to it which makes it feel so artificial and it gave us both a damn headache. They don't know how to make good level design.The game doesn't look good due to the engine's limitations, other than some parts of Xen Which are well done, but anything with bloom and bright lights can be pretty.Which brings the question, why make a remake of a game in Source which doesn't look great in the first place?I'd rather play the original. I found it more fun and less repetitive, tiresome (cough xen) and it didn't give me a headache. This took years to leave beta. Not worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: As far as fan made remakes go, this is the best there is, so much that if you'd slap a "Half-Life : Source" label on this and tell me Valve made it I'd believe you. It stays faithful to Half-Life but still adds a few things to make the universe more cohesive. The Earth part is somewhat close to what was present in the original but Xen has been completely remade: it's visually amazing and plays completely differently (overall pretty good but still a couple of boring parts too).Whether you want to replay HL or are new to the series this is where I'd start. It still shows its age with it having been first released around 8 years ago and being an HL2 mod originally but it's worth it and definitely a great solo game.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa is a modernised and reimagined vision of the original Half Life game.everything here been refined , from the gameplay , the level design and the visuals this game offer a great way to either experience Half Life for the First time or revisit it again.the levels design been cleaned up and expanded on. the gameplay feel much more balanced , the human enemies feel much smarter and less predicable while being much less tanky and the whole experience feel like a geniune and fun challenge , the aliens can still sometime be a pain to deal with but nothing here ever feel unfair or unforgiving like the original game tend to feel like.visually this game look excelent while still not demading an extremely powerful machine , the atmosphere in the xen levels are also great.

name: MythForce
detailed_description: Inspired by beloved Saturday morning cartoons, MythForce unites swords & sorcery with gripping 1st-person combat in a new roguelike adventure. Brave the dungeon alone or join forces with friends to take on an ever-changing Castle of Evil! Become a cartoon hero in a Saturday morning cartoon fantasy world. Scratch that nostalgic itch with wholesome fun that's easy to pick up and play (but tough to master). In true roguelike fashion, each time you’re defeated, you’ll have to start over at the beginning — but every playthrough makes you a little stronger. Level up as you explore the dungeon, uncovering magical artifacts and upgrades to make you say “I HAVE THE POWER!” Wield legendary weapons and powerful magic to smite hordes of enemies in an immersive fantasy dungeon-crawl through a colorful cartoon castle. Fresh adventures await with each new attempt to storm the keep! Explore a replayable dungeon with treasure, traps, and terrors lurking around every corner. Brave the dungeon alone or join forces in co-op mode for up to 4 players. Choose your team wisely — each hero brings unique skills to the fight! Meet the Heroes of MythForce : Victoria the valiant Knight joins forces with Rico the charming Rogue, Maggie the wise Mage, and Hawkins the deadly Hunter. Together, they form the legendary team known as… MythForce! These courageous champions are all that stand between Eldryth and the tyranny of the vampire lord, Deadalus. Will our heroes prevail against the many malevolent minions, tricks, and traps in his ever-changing dungeon?

_childDocuments_.review: Man is this game not getting enough love, and it's a shame. Admittedly, when this initially launched I didn't like it. Combat was slow and clunky while there didn't seem to be much incentive to continue playing. I ended up refunding as a result. Fast forward to April 2024, a massive patch was released. You can view the patch notes (Update 1.0.5.0 Patch NotesThe Harder, Better, Faster, Story Update) to see all that was covered, but the mention of story content and speed fixes was enough to draw me back in. I picked this up with a friend, and we're not too far into the game just yet, but it's miles better than it was at launch. Unfortunately, this didn't launch in the state it's currently in, and reviews prior to April 4 2024 are still bubbling to the top, doing this a disservice. Had the game launched in the current state, it'd likely have received much more positive feedback and attention. The developers deserve a HUGE shout out for turning this back around. The animation style and gameplay are great if you enjoy cooperative rogue-likes. Characters play differently and offer multiple weapon sets to choose from. Abilities, Perks, and Equipment are all upgradable, giving the sense of progression as well as variety in how each player builds their characters up. This is like playing the cartoons I grew up on, and that's been wonderful. Co-Op is online and supports up to 3 players.

_childDocuments_.review: In spite of the prevalent negative feedback regarding game mechanics, bugs, and clunky controls, I approached MythForce with unwavering optimism. I'm pleased to report that it exceeded my expectations.Regarding Bugs:I did encounter occasional setbacks, such as getting stuck on the floor with skeletons descending upon me from elevated positions. There were instances when my primary attack button didn't respond unless I initiated special powers to "unstick" my attacks.While all games have their share of bugs, issues tend to be resolved over time. Admittedly, investing in a game with known bugs isn't an ideal gameplay experience. However, I haven't encountered any game-breaking bugs so far—fingers crossed for continued smooth gameplay.XP Leveling:The game's approach to XP leveling might deter some players since in-level XP doesn't persist. Although you progress through stages and episodes, your level doesn't carry over when revisiting earlier episodes. Yet, the game doesn't solely rely on in-level levels or XP. Strength is gained by collecting glyphs, gems, and gold, creating a prolonged and challenging grind.You advance through Armory/Sun Disc Tiers, acquiring weapons and enhancing stats with gems. The learning curve may initially suggest a straightforward Hack/Slash style, but it requires subtle strategy, especially when playing solo on higher difficulties. Environmental utilization and precise timing become crucial.Nostalgia:The game boasts beautiful graphics, fluid animations, and seamlessly integrated mechanics. Co-op mode adds a humorous touch to the experience, delivering on the promised Saturday Morning Cartoon vibe. Similar to classic 80s/90s games, restarting from the beginning upon death can be frustrating, but understanding the mechanics improves with progression.Replayability and Final Thoughts:Every playthrough or replay offers a unique experience as each stage is randomly generated. The increasing difficulty requires extensive grinding to prove your worth. In my first day of play, I dedicated a solid 10 hours to the game. Despite its initial toughness, the grind proves immensely fulfilling, with each hour spent feeling worthwhile. The absence of a paywall for cosmetics is a definite positive. Whether you team up with friends for added fun or embark on a solo grind to showcase your prowess, MythForce offers a compelling and rewarding gaming experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I like this 80s cartoon Joel Haver fever game, but it's got issues. Issues that ultimately prevent me from recommending the game as of its current state.Multiplayer suffers a bulk of the issues. The game is peer-to-peer, but this game’s P2P is unstable all the time. I play other P2P games with my friends and those games are nowhere near this game’s instability. Perk/Smith shrines bug out for non-host players, mobs stutter about making range attacks difficult to lead and land, you’re never sure how close a mob actually is before it's too late to evade, the lobby can just suddenly break down and you can only invite half of your group back for whatever reason. The roguelike aspect of the game is a bit too grindy. After every run you get these glyphs that can be used to upgrade your town’s facilities. Armory (makes your starter gear stronger), constellation (allows you to slot gems and increase your base stats), emporium (allows you to find higher tier versions of trinkets), and conclave (allows you the ability to acquire a higher tier version of perks.) The amount of glyphs you get on the available difficulty is chump change after that first upgrade. My point being; expect to only get tier 2 of glass cannon for the longest eternity from biome 1 to 3 and still waiting in ng+. Melee combat feels uncomfortable, weak, and risky . Range is just the best of all worlds, even with the latency issue. When trying to switch to your off-hand or vice versa the game will eat the input, and it does this often. There are not enough variant tile sets per biome. You could easily see the same long center staircase leading into a big rectangle room four times in the same 40 minute run. The mob variety basically comes to an end at biome 2 of 3. The bosses of each biome are set, meaning there is only one. Dollar tree He-man monster, Hextar the necromage, and Deadaless the vampire BBEG. That is it. I enjoy parts of the game but I just cannot recommend it in its current state. I might play a little more with my friends if they wish to dive back into this lumpy pool. I know some of you won't understand and would want to reply with “Well if you thought it was d**s*** why are you still playing, huh? HAHA GOTTEM!” I never said it was any type of poop, and the point of a review is; to help others make a better buying decision, to share my experiences, and to let the developer/publisher know how I as a paying customer of their product feel.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is honestly close to good, but there are numerous issues, some would be easy to address, others would require some time from devs. Nothing that is truly requiring a full rework from the ground up, but tiny things that gnaw away at the enjoyment of the game. Off the top of my head:Perk/Enchant balance is all over the place. Perks vary from incredibly helpful to completely useless or detrimental to a surprising degree. Defensive perks are incredibly weak compared to the damage that enemies do, and offensive perks scale so quickly that they outpace enemy health hilariously fast.Hit reg: The only things that hit you in this game are because of their absurdly misrepresented hitboxes, and Caster mobs that teleport on top of you and throw a huge AoE suddenly. This wouldn't be so frustrating if these attacks didn't empty 60% of your health bar in one hit, but as I mentioned earlier, building defensively in this game is simply too weak compared to enemy damage.Missions: Why is the method for unlocking the next difficulty of a mission to beat it on the lower difficulty, instead of beating the previous level on the given difficulty? Why do perks/enchants scale so high in level when the chapters end so quickly that you have no time to level them up? Why are perks/enchants not weighted towards helping upgrade ones you already have instead of offering every perk at equal %?Voicelines: Love the voice acting, hate hearing a character point out the exit door 3 times in 5 seconds. The game is riddled with tiny design choices that just make you wonder why? The game is like... 90% playable, but that last 10% really detracts from how much fun this game COULD be if it was really cared about. You can tell there is a lot of love that went into this game, but it feels like when it came time to clean it up and ship it out, someone else came in and said there wasn't time to do any of that.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is actually kinda enjoyable for the dozen or so hours (the playtime info is incorrect due to a bug I'll mention below) I have played WHEN it actually worked, but I can't recommend it due to many nasty bugs and the overall unpolished state it is currently in.Note that I mainly played solo, co-op gameplay is more fun but it's hard to complete a co-op session due to constant network disconnects.: Nice art-style, great cheesy 80's cartoon feel, and the combat is mostly fun, especially if you get to play co-op with friends.: While the characters and objects have nice cartoon-ish look, the level map structures have some cheaper 3D-ish look, so the whole thing doesn't really have much cartoon feel during the gameplay itself (I think maybe it will feel more cartoon if there can be a third person perspective mode? since the characters look clearly more cartoon-ish). Actually the levels feel unpolished in general, there are invisible map barriers where arrows just stuck in mid-air, steps leading to straight stone walls (not collapsed stones), and minor glitches where rooms are filled with some kind of dirt pile but you can "clip through" and open chests sitting "inside" the dirt pile. Also your character can "clip through" the level transition barrier "halfway" and shoot enemies with ranged attack without entering the level.Also it's hard to call the levels procedural generated, as there are maybe half a dozen or so level maps for each chapter with mostly the same loot/object and enemy placements, so each level is randomly chosen as one of those available maps with very limited randomization of shrines and entry/exit points. Considering each run has more than 15 levels, it's inevitable to encounter quite some level map repetition in a run.And the random skills/perks and items you can picked up in a run can feel quite unbalanced at times, a lot are clearly useless while a few are extremely powerful. The traps and stuff are also more annoying than fun most of the time. Overall level design and skill/perk/item systems feel unpolished.: somehow the game requires Epic Games client to play, which in itself is nothing unbearable for me (but it may drive off some others), however I believe this Epic Games client may be tied to some of the worse bugs the game currently has. First, at times the game status keeps showing "running" after exiting, that's why I have 50+ hours playtime shown here, sometimes I played for an hour and exited, and the game time just kept adding for hours as it's still "running" for steam, and I cannot start another game session without a system restart as it's never really exited. I found out that force killing some background Epic Games processes in Windows Task Manager can end the "running" status, but not sure if it would have some side-effects for new game sessions or not.The network connection is extremely unstable, not sure if it has something to do with the Epic Games client or not, but it keeps disconnecting and going "play offline" at times. Also it seems it will keep switching between "offline" and "online" mode automatically, which leads to another bug: when you are picking a perk/skill and getting a "network disconnected" message, it means you have automatically picked the "dismiss" option, AND it will automatically pick the "dismiss" option for the ENTIRE RUN afterwards. That means once you get a "network disconnected" while picking a skill/perk, you cannot get any new skills/perks/ability upgrades from shrines or shops, and when you try to buy a skill/perk/ability upgrade from a shop, you spend the gold but get nothing! I think maybe it'd be better to have a "permanent" offline mode option where there would be no more "network disconnected" popup, currently even when you chose to "play offline" it will keep switching online/offline in the background somehow, with the untimely popups ruining the run.And there are complete control freeze at times, which is happening a lot since I'm in chapter 2, so much so that I have not been able to finish episode 5 due to this nasty bug, as some levels into the run all controls would be suddenly lost at some random point, the character would stand still with animations still playing, but no keyboard or controller input would work, so the game still plays on with the character standing still, and there's no way to proceed or even exit the game except a force kill. : this is about parts/designs of the game that's neither good nor bad, but just feel strange. first the character level progression is completely fixed, meaning you will be at a certain fixed character level at a certain map in a certain episode. So you will start episode 1 at level 1, episode 2 at level 4, episode 3 at level 7, and then back to level 1 at episode 4 (as you are entering a new chapter). It's okay for a roguelite game, but still strange.And the game shares the same resource (gold) for shopping items in the run and upgrading the character outside the run, so you spend less in a run, you get more points to upgrade for future runs. This is kinda strange as it makes less incentive to spend gold in a run (at least before maxing out character upgrades), thus leading to a potentially less varied and less fun game run. Other roguelite games I have played mostly have different resources for in-run purchases and out-run upgrades, so you don't have your hands tied when purchasing items/upgrades during a run.Lastly the constellation system, not sure if it's because I'm still not grasping the whole system or not, but since it's "constellation" where there are "lines" connecting the "slots", I kinda expected when you place certain same-type or different-type gems in "connected" slots, there would be some extra effects, but so far it seems there no such effects? Which makes the whole "constellation" thing feel strange as it just functions the same as separate gem slots with a bundle of lines not having any meaning?, I think this is a nice and fun game, and I'd recommend it despite its unpolished state and some weirdness in its designs, but right now given the nasty bugs (which may or may not be related to the required Epic Games services running in the background), I cannot recommend this game until the devs can get all those game-stopper bugs fixed up.

_childDocuments_.review: I love randomized dungeons and rogue-likes, and while I don't recommend Mythforce, I did have some fun with my time with it. The game reveals it's shallow nature very early on, but if there was more content and randomization, this could be a game I'd recommend.Let me tell you about a game called MYTHFORCE(!!!):(A) There's hardly any randomization to the "randomly generated dungeons" (which are really just repeating rooms in a random set) -In any particular dungeon you encounter the same 3 or 4 rooms which loop repeatedly. About 9 stages are broken into 3 areas. There are 3 stages in each of these areas that are essentially exactly the same, with just 3 or 4 rooms repeating.(B) Disappointingly few options regarding the Rogue-like aspects of the game. By the time you've played a couple of hours you will have found almost every perk/ability/and aspect available. Some are essential to a painless run, and therefore you quite quickly find your "cookie cutter" build. There's no variation and loot drops are unrewarding.(C) Combat is dull and simple, each character has a light/heavy attack, a block, and 3 abilities. The abilities never change, not even when you change gear. I could have a bow and a 2 handed sword, but my abilities are still shield bash, shield throw, and a atk power+ roar. Very shallow.(D) And lastly, this game is REALLY cheesy, and not in a good way. It tries to emulate an 80's cartoon, but it's more a mockery with none of the charm. You'll find yourself wanting to skip every cutscene and line of dialogue.Now, just say it aloud in your head, "Mythforce!"
_childDocuments_.name: MythForce

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastically well designed game, especially with the latest patches. Most reviews complaining about this game are of the older version - do not regard. The developers clearly listened to feedback and this gem now runs as smooth as silk. It's clearly a labor of love. Combat is solid and precise, while still maintaining the art style. Speaking of which, it's unlike anything I've seen before. The art is cohesive and perfectly captures what they were intending. Character and playstyle customization is fantastic, with weapon loadout swaps akin to Vermintide 2. Every character can use some form of melee and ranged, with most also being able to wield magic so your team isn't locked to a playstyle per character.There's only more content to be added and from the updates it's clear the devs are listening. Great work team! Can't wait to play and advance further.

_childDocuments_.review: My interest was piqued just like everyone else's: the look and feel, and the promise of being able to play in a world just like the Dungeons and Dragons TV cartoon I loved as a kid.Unfortunately, this game turned out to be mostly look and feel covering up a mediocre, ho-hum game. It's not terrible by any means, but after during run #2 I wondered, "is this it? Is it just a glorified corridor hack n slash where I fight various skeletons over and over?" The skeletons hit you with swords from way, way farther away than their swords appear to swing, changing weapons in game is clunky, the action is repetitive even 15 minutes into the game.By run #3 is wanted to quit even when I was doing ok. I felt, if I got to keep my level progress to run #4 then I'd keep the game. Nope, you have to start all the way over at level 1 each time. I have uninstalled the game.
_childDocuments_.name: MythForce

_childDocuments_.review: One of those "I wish there was a neutral option" reviews.As a roguelike, this fails hard. - There's no between-character progression other than stages and overworld levels. If you don't like your character after farming for 10 hours, guess you have to farm another 10 hours for gems.- There's no between-stage progression. You start fresh every time, which makes sense because (next)- Balance is ALL OVER THE PLACE, as many others have mentioned.- It's nearly impossible to solo on harder difficulties, especially with curses like "if you get hit, lose 10 max hp". Like, WHAT?- The overarching progression is... not fun? 1. You give items a higher drop chance. 2. You slot gems, which you have to ceaselessly farm (here you have to choose between damage and defenses). 3. You level max perk totals, but you can't delevel them so you can't actually make a consistent build. 4. You upgrade weapons, for incrementally doubling damage.- If you decide you like a weapon and don't want to use/upgrade the other one, well then you're definitely going to get a bunch of weapon upgrades for the one you're not using! Hah!- Gold is shared within the map and is tied to overworld progress. If you decide you actually want to use the shop, you lose out on progression. As a multiplayer game, it succeeds somewhat. Though, there are caveats. - You can give build-specific items to your friends. But, if any ability upgrades drop, it's first come first serve. Chances are you won't even *see* them. - If one member is bugged, the run is over. "You must gather your party before venturing forth!"- Quickplay is fun sometimes, awful at other times. It commonly places you in matches that are nearly over. Most of the time, you don't get any perks. You don't get any starting items. Sometimes it'll place you in a match where the host is AFK, and you CAN NOT join any other games (it'll just keep sending you to that one). Additionally, you'll be placed in a game that is NOT the difficulty you selected.There are a lot of bugs and QOL problems.- Hitting skeletons with a bow is damn near impossible to the point that playing the archer is inadvisable.- There are holes you can fall down and never come back from. You're not dead, but the run is over for everyone in the party.- Some abilities are 'slippery' in that you might miss if you're slightly off of the hitbox even if your weapon actually hits them.- General bugs. Sometimes you might use your Mythforce ability and not be able to attack. Other times, there are floating wall textures.- Enemies will occasionally spawn right on top of you.- Enemies will get locked behind the black spawning walls (tldr: bad level design) where they can hit you but you can't hit them.As a massive fan of their BG2 port, I'm kind of disappointed by Beamdog's take on roguelikes.
_childDocuments_.name: MythForce

_childDocuments_.review: More of a neutral review, but given the full price, it isn't worth that.The theme and art style are executed very well - but that's about it..I beat the first 2 levels, so I'm not sure if I explored all the systems or not fully but there's not much making me want to yet..The combat feels unresponsive, you'll hit things and there's almost no feedback (until toward the end of a run when you're decked out, but..)Levels are over just as you feel you're getting somewhere, I almost feel like they should go for something more like gunfire reborn.And then there just doesn't feel like there's much of anything.. Rooms in a level repeat a lot, you'll see the same few upgrades and items and each character's 4 abilities are very basic and can't be customised/upgraded much at all.I'd understand if this was early access, but it isn't.I'm aware the dev's did update the combat once already (I shudder to think how bad it was before) so I'll keep an eye out for further updates but doubt I'll touch this again until then.

_childDocuments_.review: I was  really looking forward for this game, probably I'm probably one of the few people that got hyped from the trailer.Anyway...In summary ; Good idea, awful executed. The game feeeels waaay to lazyGood stuff - Graphics are nice , althought I kinda understand most people won't like it.That's about it.Bad Stuff.- Combat is broken, ranged weapons are waaay to OP while melee combat it's too punishing. I get it, Melee combat is more focused in block and parry but it's kinda hard to when you're surrounded by enemies, while I can just shoot arrows from a safe distance, heck arrows deal more damage than meelee weapons anyway since it's really easy to aim to the head and crit.- Loot system :  In Dungeons you only find money, which can be use to upgrade weapons, items, trinkets. Exploring a dungeon is meaningless when you're going to find only money. There's no new weapons armors or any new stuff to be excited for,-Equip system. Awful, you have a few options for weapons, there's no armor system or character customization option.-Lack of content : after two runs you probaly have seen every trinket and modifiers. _childDocuments_.review: Love the style and graphics! Everything else is... well to put it nicely, it needs more time.First problem, epic service dependency, I do not want to launch a game via one platform, only for it to open another platform and launch it from there, what's next in the future? A nest of platforms just to run a video game?Second, after finally able to get in the game from the long initialization of epic service, after starting a quickplay game the tutorial were just dumped to me explaining everything at once in the form of GUI highlights, in silence, that tells me that this game does not have a proper tutorial, which means, its not finished.Third, after I dismissed all of the tutorial slides, I was immediately teamed up with another player and immediately skeletons just appeared and started attacking us, we killed them and more appear, we killed them and more appear, we killed them and... nothing happened? We were wondering around until we found what seem to be a way forward, then skeletons appeared and we killed them, skeletons appeared and you would not guess what happens next! Rinse and repeat for pretty much the whole game.Only momentary excitement I felt was during the 1 and only mini-boss fight in that mission against the mushroom mage, and even then the tactic between me and the other player was to just gang up on it and spam attack until it's dead. Afterwards, rinse and repeat.Finally we made it to the last room, there was a dialogue with the antagonist, OK cool let's do this, we thought, nope the guy ran away and leaves his minions to deal with us which we just need to keep killing them for.. 2 minutes straight I think? Which then we opened up the big chest at the end and.. we don't know we just get stuff from it, pulled the lever and the level just ended.This game just feels unfinished, at certain times I can tell that it has the potential to be fun and engaging especially seeing the potential to mix and match certain perks and upgrades, maybe later on it's more fun going against tougher and smarter enemies that just doesn't waddle to you slowly and swings their weapon at you slowly and gets staggered on every strike. I'll follow the development of the game, still hopeful that this game could become a good game later on, just not at this moment.
