_childDocuments_.review: First of all, let me clarify- This is not a thumbs down, game bad thing, this is a "Steam needs a Middle option for reviews" thing. Because I'm not mad at it, and it's not really bad, my negative review is STRICTLY because I think the price is too high for what they're peddling.This game is "ok", but it's not really a $30+ game at ALL.This is my biggest gripe. This would be a really great option in the $19-$24.99 bracket, you know, where I expect Indie games that aren't quite up to AAA quality to sit. GET IT ON SALE, GET IT ON SALE, GET IT ON SALE. Wait for a sale, it will be worth it on sale. It's real arrogant of these guys to throw it up on EGS for a year, and then bring it to Steam STILL f*cking unfinished, and missing basic coop game options, like voice chat, or a text box, for example. BTW, this game has neither and wants you to use a sh*tty radial menu during combat. This is another example of "just ok".  Actual great games will generally let you talk to other players because they don't have a cucumber in charge of that department.These guys made a coop game where you can't talk to the people you randomly meet, that's not "good". I don't CARE about it, but it's not a "good" design. It's basic af, and only "ok" It's got a great art style and it has some cool features, and IS fun, BUT--it makes you install EOS, which heavily depends on you, because some people are like f*ck epic, and some people aren't, but the ones who ARE, will refund instantly if a game has it. -Sound design is weird and while it exists, it's like a bunch of times i kept thinking, "man, this sound design sure sucks, i can't tell where creatures are at, and there's like a ton of sliders for audio but you really don't need that many, you just need to do a good job at the default settings, which they did not. -hitting barrels and pots gives you money! this is generally cool, but in this game, it's really underwhelming. -there's an overall lack of visual and audio WOW factor. _childDocuments_.review: This game is in a solid spot in my opinion. But the gameplay and pacing has also seen significant improvements as previously mentioned. It all makes me eager to see where they go with this game in the future. If they can process this much feedback and actually implement significant changes like this once, I have no reason to think they won't be able to do it again. Which for me means the future of this game is likely bright.

_childDocuments_.review: I played several hours of the demo, enjoyed the experience at the time and thought it had lots of potential, but upon returning months later for the full game, and only minutes after getting back in to it, much of what I once enjoyed now feels tired, and many of the things I hoped were placeholders are still there, making the full experience fall flat.I really would've loved if this had more varied maps with proper enemy placement and a moody soundtrack instead of feeling like an endless survival mode in copy/pasted prefabs sections. It's just such a wasted potential. I don't know how to describe it, but it feels like the enemies don't occupy the same space as the location.The roguelite mechanic is easily the worst aspect for me, especially in the form of drawing cards between rounds. Stopping the game entirely to have me make a choice in a hallway between random perks and debuffs instead of designing and balancing the gameplay from the start is just frustrating.It just doesn't feel like it's ready for release, and tests my patience with every step which is a shame because the premise, art style and presentation of this game are everything that I should love. There are games like Hi-Fi Rush that have that 2d look in a 3D space, but this game takes it to a very unique place visually. I want to play it every time I see a screenshot or promo but then once I'm in it just feels so tedious.

_childDocuments_.review: Nice casual coop game with some simple yet interesting character progression mechanic. Quite short though: First co-op playthrough took 6 hours to complete, but there are 4 classes and some different builds to figure out. As long as you do not expect a AAA-title you will probably have a fun time with friends. There are some minor multiplayer replication issues (e.g. Victoria's split arrows do not replicate correctly on client side), but all in all the experience was top notch stable and fluent: No crash and no connection loss in any coop run. I mention this, because I read some other player's reviews about "bad servers" of this game, which just makes no sense: It appears to be a peer-to peer-hosting system using EOS, so there should be no connection problems unless the players themself have a bad internet connection. I recommend to play coop on hard to unlock the next difficulties.

_childDocuments_.review: Made by people in their 40s, for people in their 40s.Honestly please read this and more reviews before buying, I fell for the recent reviews. "Oh it was mixed but now its positive and the positive reviews seem to be fine, maybe people were just picky early on!"I cannot believe BEAMDOG, the people responsible for the Baldur's Gate remasters, are behind this one. Or maybe I can? They had a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ reputation from doing those remasters. And you know what if you look at their catalog of games, they dont have any that ARENT remasters of old dnd games or ports of board games. This is basically their first forray into the game making space, and it really shows. Not to mention they laid off 26 of their staff on Sept 19th, a week after this game "released".This game's entire marketing gimmick is that its reminicent of 80s cartoons. But it also plays like its for someone who's not much of a gamer, someone in their 40s or 50s. The game is just.... slow. The overwatch-styled hud will mislead you, its not ANYWHERE near as fast paced or responsive. The game is full of shambling enemies that are effectively walking health sponges. Moving around doesn't feel fluid and dynamic. The powerups are roguelike and kind of interesting but you're really just stuck with your 3 abilities and they arent all that interesting truth be told. The whole game is really just... good on paper poor in play. Almost as if the people making the game are good at... pen and paper games... and not dynamic action games....I played as Maggie the wizard, the only of the four characters marked at 3/3 difficulty. It was not hard, despite somehow at the very start I lit myself on fire and spent the rest of the 20 minutes at 30% hp. No, it was mundane and boring. You start with a fire book as your weapon, and the standard attack is a fire puff. When I say puff, I really mean it, you have to be right on top of someone for it to even hit them. Okay sure, I'll just use the strong attack, charging up a fireball to lob at people. That worked well, outside of the fact that doing this spends your "energy" aka mana aka stamina so the entire time I played, for 20 minutes, was me just slowly charging and lobbing a few fireballs and then needing to wait to restore my energy and lobbing more. The enemies whether skeletal or mushroom in nature, wordlessly appear and shamble forth. Of my three abilities, one was a teleport, a shield, and a summoned bird that acted as a peashooter turret. So basically the next twenty minutes was nothing but slowly lobbing fireballs at walking sponges. It just tells me that there's some clear issues in the game loop and weapon/skill design. When your core game loop feels like you're kind of just existing and swimming through molasses, you have to go back and tune it up.There are some other things that bothered me. I did die once, because a mushroom-person spawned behind me, wordlessly and without sound. Normally in a game there would be SOUND to help you there. Thankfully I was playing with a random who picked me back up. There's no indication on how long this takes for the person on the receiving end, which is kind of basic game design guys. The "tutorial" is just a bunch of popups on your screen with endless "dont show this tutorial again" checkboxes to check. All of which pops up when you first enter a game, so hopefully you share my experience in trying to matchmake and finally land a game only to be standing there for a minute reading and then disconnect from the host. Character selection is also a bit weird, its a neat concept to have all the characters sitting there, but the way they look up at you is super uncanny valley. The loading screen is the mythforce logo with the guy saying "MYTH FORCEEEE!", I am unsure if that plays every time but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ I can see that getting annoying.Again, its like the people who made this game are an era behind. It feels like they are too used to pen and paper rules, that they designed all of this in a box and translated that to a game while never sitting down to make it feel fluid and dynamic. It feels like they know how dnd works and how to make a custom campaign and character backstories, but then looked to modern games like overwatch to try to design their game around without understanding anything about gameplay. This is your dad's video game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games i do want to succeed , but every  part of it feels lacking , and i hope its economy lasts enought to make it right.  The Bad :- Wrong Roguelite : the approach of sequencing levels forming a campaign, being replayable with different difficulties is just not fun. Id rather redo one single run mutated and branched as i go to tell a story.Look at other modern roguelites (out of my head Hades/Knock On The Coffin/Lost Castle 2/Witchfire / etc)  if you want to know how story supposed to be injected into genre.- Replayability : this one come from a simple loop recepie: challenge -> fail/success -> reward -> meta progression ->loop;This game lacking each, challenge - easy and not leaving desire to repeat, reward - no neat unlocks/grinding stimulus, progression boring - not offering any kind of juicy character building.The Average : - Voiceovers : This one is great , but become annoying fast . It is simple repeating itself too much, and during wrong times. Ravenswatch comes to mind, they have similar feature , but its happening at correct time (i.e when partner making a kill streak/ or taking serios damage) , should revisit this part.The Good :- Visuals/Theme /Music : This is classic, great  and very well done. This and coop is why the game ended up in my libarary.- Coop : Game works fine, i have not encountered any significant bugs.No featuring suprises too : No DarkSouls Style matchmaking joke , no complete this 40 mission campaign before you can play with friends.P.S I dont regret buying, but unlikly will play it until anything would be done with The Bads.Period.

_childDocuments_.review: Ah, this is the best of the "Rogue-lite" games my friend and I have played over the last few months! Without a doubt.The campaign is more "on rails" than is Roboquest, but the gameplay itself is the most fun we've had with this game style.You play as one of several "heroes," each one of which has particular built-in perks. Nothing new there. But the various perks are quite intriguing, and, each "hero" has its own in-game dialog that runs and interacts with the other "heroes'" in-game dialog. The net effect is that the game just doesn't take itself seriously, which adds to the fun. 19-hours in, and the running dialog is still entertaining rather than monotonous.For example, the "Victoria" character hits a trip wire and gets herself all corroded. The "Maggie" character, in a deliciously snarky tone, says, "Victoria, did you not even SEE the trap?" And it goes on and on. Back and forth. So far it hasn't gotten old. It probably will, but then it's just background noise.The "lite" part of "Rogue-lite" in this game is a very detailed, intuitive, and fun-to-grind tech tree. There is a "constellation" of four-colors of gems that you acquire throughout each run. You can spend "shields" (another in-game drop) to expand the constellation, opening new drop-points for your gems to enhance weapon-power, crit-damage, lucky-shot, various defenses, power-cool-down reductions, and so on. Cleverly, you can get 10 of a particular gem color and then stack them into a single higher-power gem, so you replace a single gem with a stack. And you can combine stacks (in exponential) fashion three more times (if you have time in your life to gain the many hundreds of gems needed and the millions of in-game dollars). It's an intriguing approach that is satisfying to build out.Of course, you can also level your weapons, which (unlike most such games) this game lets you keep! So, find your preferred weapon combo (you can have a primary and secondary), and then grind to level them.You can also level "trinkets" for both power and drop-frequency, and you can level perks for power and frequency that are granted at drop-stations between each part of an "episode."In short, there's LOTS to motivate you to mine for in-game drops and perpetually level your character, weapons, and chances. It's by far the best of the "tech" approaches I've seen in a "Rogue-lite" game.The story line is about as meh as all of these games. It's a "story" to motivate your pass through a particular run, nothing more. It also motivates some of the running in-game dialog between the characters. Again, meh, but the in-game dialog has enough high-points to be worth having in the game.The weapons are fun to play and feel right. Again, this is something that many games can't seem to manage to get right, but this one does.The balancing and difficult scale "correctly" IMO. "Easy" mode is indeed manageable for even your initial low-level, low-tech characters. "Normal" is a for-real challenge, even with a half-leveled character. We haven't even tried harder difficulty-levels yet, because "normal" is plenty enough of a challenge for where we are in the grind path. So, there's a LOT of replayability here.Co-op works well, with a simple Steam invite. I will say that a couple of times the servers have seemed to have trouble getting us connected, but that's been rare. It IS something you should be aware of, though, because the MOMENT that it becomes more money that it's worth for them to keep the servers up, this game is insta-dead! Remember Loadout, which was great until the moment when it was insta-dead. You are definitely taking a risk with this sort of multiplayer/co-op support. But you'll almost certainly get your money's worth by the time the insta-death happens.This game gets it all right IMO. It's our go-to game at the moment, and that's saying something, given our limited game-time opportunities.

_childDocuments_.review: Notes:- Gameplay consists of procedurally generated room-to-room runs of approx. 30 mins with an upgrade perk after each one.- Combat is fun and distills much of the feel of Tiny Tina's Wonderlands into a tidy roguelike.- There's plenty to upgrade, and plenty to customize about your kit, with different weapon types and favored items.- Stat upgrades are handled by a 'constellation' system where you can slot different types of improvements into different slots. i.e., a combat slot could be fit with a gem to increase physical attack, defense, attack speed, or combat cooldown, while a utility slot could be fit for crit damage, health, total energy, or ult cooldown.- The graphics are kitschy and nostalgic, especially if you grew up watching cartoons from the late 80s.Let's address the feedback on the Steam page first of all. Most of that comes from before the most recent patch that corrected a lot of problems, but it's still a new game with very few reviews, so each individual review will swing the stats wildly. It's not going to win any awards, but it's a fun romp well worth the half-priced (maybe not full priced) admission. I've played with some randos, which went well, but I'll bet it's a blast with friends. It currently supports crossplay between Steam and Epic, though it is available for all consoles. There's definitely room for the game to grow. It feels a bit like a final-stage early access title, but the devs are taking tons of feedback and working to improve it more than it already has.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite being a full release, the game feels the same (or even a bit worse) as it was during the demo - decent base, but needs some work to get it to be fun. Core mechanics are in place, but content is very lackluster. The need to grind for metaprogression to get decent raw stats and unlock higher tier upgrades made me not want to continue after beating the first major boss. I started 4th level and seen that my character is back to lvl 1 and takes around 10 attacks to kill 1 basic skeleton even after dropping the difficulty to normal, so either I am missing raw stats or it's just normal that enemies become damage sponges, neither of which is fun. Maybe (big maybe) if all metaprogression was shared between characters it would be less painful to grind it out, but in the current state I can't make myself continue to at least finish the whole game on single difficulty. Luckily I received the game for free, because otherwise I'd be rather disappointed even at half a price for the experience compared to other similar games. I only played single player, so multi player experience might be slightly different.- Visuals are nice- Access to both melee and ranged combat with every class- Too repetitive due to lack of room layouts, interesting upgrades (you'll see almost the same perks, weapon upgrades, and items every run), and very little weapon changes- Items are quite rare to find outside of 2 shop rooms per run, and they give such small bonuses at low tier (in demo you could get any tier immediately and felt like they were dropped more frequently. Even then items felt only OK-ish, mostly few generic buffs that aren't too noticeable). Most chests and pots in the rooms just drop gold to be used in those shops that each contain 6 items in total- Higher tier upgrades (perks, weapon upgrades, gems, and items) are locked behind metaprogression which takes many runs to upgrade everything- Most metaprogression upgrades are not shared between characters, so you have to grind them with each character- Difficulty is severely gated behind metaprogression upgrades (I went into 3rd level on hard with "new" character and I did 11 critical damage to the first boss which had 6k HP despite having perk that makes me deal 75% more damage. It took me probably 10 minutes to kill it with the help of environmental fire trap because I had no raw stat upgrades from metaprogression; the run got much more tolerable few rooms after when I got some stat boosts)- Some ability upgrades have buffs only for allies which is disappointing for single player experience

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this game up to about the last tier of equipment and about two thirds the campaign, and I can say I mostly love this game. Probably closest in genre to games like Vermintide, but here you play a 80s comic character attempting to tackle the vampire lord Deadalus over nine levels of progressively harder room-by-room dungeon crawling.The graphics, the voice acting, and even the cartoon intro for the game are perfectly evocative of the era the developers lovingly draw from, while still maintaining a surprisingly deep combat system, with cooldowns, stamina management, ultimate abilities, and a soft rogue-like game loop that will have you revisiting some of the same levels for more gold, more upgrade gems, and more unlock glyphs.Which leads to the only real complaints one might have of the game - that you could easily want more episodes to play. Right now the path to a "full build" requires millions of gold and possibly hundreds of gems. While progression early on feels very good, the late game gets a little bit grindy. Hopefully the company is planning more episodes to come.For $30, I felt like I got exactly what I wanted - a love letter to my childhood coupled with a game I could sink a hundred hours into. As a bonus, the company seems particularly checked-in with responding to the game's playerbase and is rolling out patches quickly as bugs are discovered. If you're in the mood for a hack and slash game with rogue-like elements, and the idea of a villain cheesily hamming it up from a balcony before letting his minions take care of you fills you with delight, then this game is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not for everyone as it can be challenging and repetitive since you might have to grind a lot before you can progress. If you like playing co-op games like vermintide II, darksiders genesis, and risk of rain 2, this might be for you.Sample gameplay: I kind of agree to some sentiment that this does not feel like a full released game yet. It really feels there is a lot missing pieces, especially the reward with the progress. Still, it has a good gameplay and likable character designs. You can also always wait for steam sale if you think its not worth the price. For what its worth, I had fun. Giving this a thumbs up and hoping there will be more updates.
_childDocuments_.name: MythForce

_childDocuments_.review: I have been eagerly waiting the release for Steam. The art, music and animation are exactly what I always thought games to look like ever since I bought a copy of Might&Magic 6 as a kid. Yet they never did! - One of the reasons I became an artist!Though I have only player Chapter 1 as of this writing, everything works. Can you imagine that? Everything actually working in a game in early access? Simple done well is great.The only thing holding this game back is content. What the game thus far does, it does so flawlessly. The current rating of mixed are absurd.
_childDocuments_.name: MythForce

_childDocuments_.review: I love the premise and art style. If you grew up in the 80s, Mythforce conjures up Dungeons and Dragons, He-Man, and Dragon's Lair (technically a cartoon video game, but still). Comparisons to Gunfire Reborn are superficial at best. The physics and combat in Gunfire are far more polished and responsive. If you are expecting gameplay akin to Gunfire or Borderlands, you will be disappointed. If you are expecting it not to install Epic's Game Store launcher, you will be VERY disappointed (note to devs: you need to patch that out, ASAP). This game does not feel finished, but the potential here is huge. I hope the studio does the right thing and incrementally works at bringing this game into its own. It's poised, just on the strength of the art style, of being at the top of the rogue-like looter-shooter pyramid. In the future, if Mythforce wants to become legendary, it will channel a far-future setting (think Jack Vance's Dying Earth or M. John Harrison's Viriconium stories) and marry it to visuals that will evoke Thundarr the Barbarian without calling down the wrath of IP lawyers.
_childDocuments_.name: MythForce

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Brewdog has taken feedback seriously and fixed a lot of issues I had with the game at launch. Big respect :) MythForce looks stunning and perfectly encapsulates the look and feel of 80s action cartoons. Unfortunately, its repetitive gameplay loop, frustrating stamina mechanic, and unrewarding progression system spoil what could've been an exceptional game.There's a treasure chest of potential here and I think Beamdog has the talent to eventually make the game shine, but MythForce doesn't quite feel like a full release yet. I desperately want to love MyhForce, and I'm hopeful that future updates will remedy its flaws
_childDocuments_.name: MythForce

_childDocuments_.review:
Become a cartoon hero in a bodacious 80s fantasy world. Scratch that nostalgic itch with wholesome fun that's easy to pick up and play (but tough to master).

In true rogue-lite fashion, each time you're defeated, you'll have to start over at the beginning - but every playthrough makes you a little stronger.

Level up as you explore the dungeon, uncovering magical artifacts and upgrades to make you say "I HAVE THE POWER!"

detailed_description: Marvel's Midnight Suns Legendary Edition DARKNESS FALLS. RISE UP! Customize the look of the Midnight Suns team and extend your adventure with the Marvel’s Midnight Suns Legendary Edition! The Legendary Edition includes: - Marvel’s Midnight Suns base game - Marvel's Midnight Suns Season Pass, which includes 23 premium skins available at launch and four post-launch DLC packs The four playable post-launch DLC heroes included in the Season Pass are: - Deadpool - Venom - Morbius - Storm Season Pass Premium Skins available at launch: - Captain America (Future Soldier) - Captain America (Captain of the Guard) - Captain Marvel (Mar-Vell) - Captain Marvel (Medieval Marvel) - Magik (Phoenix Five) - Magik (New Mutants) - Nico Minoru (Sister Grimm) - Nico Minoru (Shadow Witch) - Wolverine (X-Force) - Wolverine (Logan) - Blade (Demon Hunter) - Blade (Blade 1602) - Iron Man (Iron Knight) - Iron Man (Bleeding Edge) - Ghost Rider (Spirit of Vengeance) - Ghost Rider (Death Knight) - Doctor Strange (Strange Future Supreme) - Scarlet Witch (Boss Witch) - Scarlet Witch (Fallen Scarlet Witch) - Spider-Man (Symbiote Suit) - Spider-Man (Demon Spider) - Hulk (Fallen Hulk) - Hulk (Maestro) With the inclusion of the Season Pass, the Legendary Edition lets you keep the pressure on Lilith and expand your roster of Marvel heroes. This extra dose of vengeance includes four post-launch DLC packs, each introducing a new fully playable hero, new missions, new enemies, and more. The Season Pass also includes 23 Premium Skins at launch so you can customize the look of the Midnight Suns team. Note: Premium skins must be used with the equivalent in-game character. Characters may require unlocking through gameplay. Post-launch Season Pass content and the premium skins will be automatically delivered in-game upon release. DLC release timing for post-launch DLC will be revealed at a future date. Terms apply. Marvel's Midnight Suns Digital+ Edition DARKNESS FALLS. RISE UP! Customize the look of your Midnight Sun team with the Marvel’s Midnight Suns Digital+ Edition! The Digital+ Edition includes: -Marvel’s Midnight Suns base game -11 Premium Skins Premium Skins include: -Captain America (Future Soldier) -Captain Marvel (Mar-Vell) -Magik (Phoenix Five) -Nico Minoru (Sister Grimm) -Wolverine (X-Force) -Blade (Demon Hunter) -Captain America (Captain of the Guard) -Iron Man (Iron Knight) -Nico Minoru (Shadow Witch) -Ghost Rider (Spirit of Vengeance) -Magik (New Mutants) Note: Premium skins must be used with the equivalent in-game character. Characters may require unlocking through gameplay. Premium skins will be automatically delivered in-game by 1 December 2022. Terms apply UNLEASH THE DARKER SIDE OF MARVEL When the demonic Lilith and her fearsome horde unite with the evil armies of Hydra, it’s time to unleash Marvel’s dark side. As The Hunter, your mission is to lead an unlikely team of seasoned Super Heroes and dangerous supernatural warriors to victory. Can legends such as Doctor Strange, Iron Man, and Blade put aside their differences in the face of a growing apocalyptic threat? If you’re going to save the world, you'll have to forge alliances and lead the team into battle as the legendary Midnight Suns. With an array of upgradeable characters and skills allowing you to build your own unique version of The Hunter, you will choose how to send Lilith’s army back to the underworld. About the Game Marvel’s Midnight Suns is the ultimate crossover event combining the rich story, character relationships, customization and progression of an RPG with the tactical strategy and combat mechanics of a revolutionary new card-based tactics game. Set in the darker side of the Marvel Universe, you will forge unbreakable bonds with legendary Marvel Super Heroes and dangerous supernatural warriors in the fight against the world’s greatest threat yet…the demonic forces of Lilith and the elder god Chthon. Your Marvel Adventure You are the Hunter, the first fully-customizable original hero in the Marvel Universe. Personalize your appearance, choose your reactions to situations, and build friendships with Marvel legends spanning The Avengers, X-Men, Runaways, and more. Decide who to take with you on missions, which missions to embark on, and a host of other options to make this a unique experience. Fight and Think like a Super Hero From the creators of the critically-acclaimed tactical XCOM series comes an engaging and deeply customizable card-based battle system that rewards clever thinking with Super Hero flair. Deploy a squad of Super Heroes on tactical turn-based missions to thwart the forces of evil. Use your environment, move around the battlefield lining up the perfect shot or combo, and then launch devastating hero abilities to gain the advantage in each epic encounter. The combat leverages the best elements from tactical games and card-based combat in a truly unique and thrilling experience. Live Among the Legends Spend time exploring what Super Heroes do in their off hours. Explore The Abbey—your very own mystical secret base—to discover powerful hidden items and secrets to aid you in the conflict against Lilith and her minions. Befriend and get to really know some of your favorite Marvel heroes as you interact with them in ways beyond the comics or the films.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a solid little tactical combat game with a decent story and writing.  If you enjoy Marvel characters and tactical games you'll likely enjoy this. My  least liked part is the card system, which is good for card systems, I just hate card games.   You can get over it though and it does make for more interesting game play than simply having access to a set of moves that didnt change with each card dealt. Its not really a xcom like game though if thats what you're looking for. Maps are much more limited in scope and complexity.   Think of this as more of a tabletop style map game thats more about the order you play your moves than the positioning of characters on a map etc.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: Well, I've played this game about two and a half hours and so far I have to say that I've had a blast.  I don't know anything about Marvel Superheroes but the game is fun and now my interest has been peaked.  I like the game play and the graphics and voice acting are great in my opinion.  The story so far is very good and the combat and deck building are unique and fun.  I have experienced no crashes or stutters or lag.  I wish I had seen the movies but now I guess I have something to look forward to.  So far, I would definitely recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Game itself is alright, however the negative review is due to the very unreliable buggy performance. It runs terribly, constantly freezing and lagging, long load times and crashing frequently. If you disable the 2K Launcher (look online or in comments) it makes a huge difference, however it is disappointing that that is required from the player. Game thereafter still lags, freezes and is prone to crashingIn terms of the gameplay itself, I enjoyed the MCU movies, this game is ok. Very much like XCOM which I really enjoy. Story isnt super-gripping, but the combat etc, is fun. If not for the above performance issues I would probably give a positive.

_childDocuments_.review: This game just gets better with each play-through. [Especially with some light QoL mods from Nexus] For this summer sale, its ABSOLUTELY worth it. I just transferred my save-file from my Epic account and the New-game+ on harder difficulty is proving to be just what I need when coming home from work. Especially because you can choose totally different conversation options on the second play-through without effecting the relationship mechanics of the game too much. They also give a lot of NG+ options which I expect I will be using on my next run. If you like the tactical deck-builders and you like Marvel the definitely get this game. Even if its full price!!
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game, fav game of 2022 after Elden Ring. It's a shame it did not sell well on launch. I think this game has long legs. The campaign alone is long and engaging, the combat is deep and super fun, there are tons of ways to level up and customize your characters. I actually find the writing endearing. Each marvel hero is very well captured mechanically with their deck of cards, and you really feel like a badass when you pull off an awesome turn. I am excited to see this game get more content in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I love it.Combat is awesome. It's not at all like X-com, even if a lot of elements are similar, and not like a classic grided tactical rpg. It remembers me more of a conventional turn-based jRPG with a party of three characters, but instead of being full static here position matters for Area of Effect skills and for pushing one enemy against other, but not the rest of the time. The cards are an extra factor that mostly works making you choose which 12 skills every character deck has, and has little randomness since you can keep or discard cards from one turn to other.Spending time between battles, it also takes a lot of X-com elements but again the result feels like something completely different and more elaborate. It feels so natural and coherent with the game story and Marvel universe. You can really feel part of the team and it's somethingh more akin of how you bond with teammates in Bioware games, adding some daily drama on top of the story.The only bad things: -While graphics are good, facial expressions could be more elaborated. -Optimization is not perfect. Even lowering graphic options it seems impossible to avoid some framerate drops, so in the end I just keep graphics on high because it will happen anyway and most of the time it runs fine enough.-Price is a little over the top if you consider the DLC Season Pass.Lastly, I'd LOVE a game like this in Xavier's Institute with a full X-men cast.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: The combat is fun and there's some nice meta progression between runs - BUT it is waaaay too drawn out imo.There's so much filler that doesn't matter. Started skipping it all after 40 hours of reading everything and watching everything. It just overstayed its welcome big time.It even forces you to do general missions (there are only so many variations...) before being able to further the campaign.I do recommend the combat, which was fun - even though it got repetitive 40 hours in.If you really love Marvel you'll probably appreciate the banter a lot more than me.I like(d) Marvel but really don't care that Nico wonders what Iron Man thinks of her pictures in her room.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: I am quite enjoying my time with Marvel Midnight Suns.Starting with the core gameplay loop, it is quite satisfying.Good strategy with accessible difficulties to ease you in. Good RPG deck building and progression with the card system. These two combine into a very fun loop. I find myself wanting to up the difficulty as I am getting stronger and more and more familiar, because it is fun, not because it is hard.Looking at the story, I am enjoying it. It isn't the best game story ever made, but it is enjoyable. At the end of the day that is what I come to a game for. To enjoy my time. The relationship building and team building reminds me of Fire Emblems: Three Houses, and enjoy my downtime between missions. Gathering resources, cultivating the relationships and doing the side activities just add to the package for me. I am normally someone that is lucky to get 10 hours into a game before the novelty wears off and I move on. This one is going to be several playthroughs.

_childDocuments_.review: My second favorite game of 2022, just behind Elden Ring. I loved almost everything about this and I'm not even a Marvel fan. The battles were great, along with the deck building. I loved the characters and banter. Some of the dialog was a little corny, but that's OK. I didn't have many technical issues. Early on I did have some crashes, but they were short lived. What I didn't like was having to collect plants on the grounds. I think once they were discovered, they should have just given you a plant income each day. Don't make me waste my time with busywork. I really hope some of the DLC contains a roguelike mode akin to Slay the Spire. I'd love to be able to play this again without wading through the Abbey stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: I had to come here to admit I was wrong. I was actually a little excited about this when I first heard about it. Then I heard it was a card game and my expectations fell through the floor. I had seen some early reviews that said it wasn't really that great of a game. But for some reason I always kept looking at it after it released. It went on sale quickly thereafter and more people bought it and I saw better and better reviews for it. Right before then end of the sale I gave in and bought it.I am glad I did. Its actually pretty fun. The card mechanics are decent. With a little bit of work it is great on the steam deck and quite a good game for it imo. No regrets buying this game and i was wrong to judge it before I even gave it a chance.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: An overall excellent game and I highly recommend it.  The combat is Xcom-like with cards to mix it up and it is outstanding.  The story is good, the voice acting is fantastic, game design systems and mechanics are great.  It's weak point is the writing but I found not a bad as its made out to be.  The humor is cheesy which I think fits the super hero setting.  There is A LOT of social interaction and conversation (too much actually) but it is mostly decent.  Sadly there is some woke nonsense slipped in but it is very minor with Captain Marvels butch haircut being the exception.  I bought a skin for her to deal with that and it was worth the $2.  Don't skip this like I almost did because you heard about EMO club which is not what you think it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent, complete game stocked with content.  I mainly play strategy games and was really satisfied with the primary game play mode.  I think I completed all main and side content as well as the Deadpool and Venom DLC and got about 150 hours out of it, so for me it was worth the price of the legendary edition.  Firaxis is, in my view, one of the best developers around these days and I trust them such that I am basically ready to spend on whatever products they put out.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: I’m a fan of Marvel comics and the MCU, which is why I bought the game initially. I was skeptical about the card game element of it, but I thought the game play was mostly satisfying. The resources and credits are not easy to farm. I guess the devs just want players to do more side missions. That makes upgrading cards and adding mods somewhat harder. I played it on the Steam Deck and I installed CryoUtilities for it. The game’s frame rate dropped a lot during part 3, especially during the final boss fight. Load time of the game is a bit long too. Otherwise, it runs pretty well on the deck.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: This game strikes me as a design child of XCOM 2 and The My Time at X franchise. The pacing player driven, so less frantic than XCOM, and a good portion of the game revolves around befriending the characters through conversation and gift a-la My Time at X. If you're an MCU nut like my wife, you'll definitely want to play for the inside jokes, returning and new/foreshadowed characters, and so on. If you're an XCOM fan, I would say this game is comparably enjoyable to the Chimera Squad installment: a good game, but without the polish that I expected from Firaxis. The voice talent is top notch, the customization limited, and the missions, at least at the time of this writing, modestly repetitive, with a frustratingly narrow range of enemies. I'd say, though I paid much more for it to have it on release and get the XPACs, this is a 34.99 to 39.99 game. I overpaid a little, hoping for more from Firaxis, but it is solid, engaging, and worth a little less.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't suggest this game at full price.  Especially since they really want to push for the DLC.  If there was no DLC, no "different versions" (it's just cosmetics), and it was just a complete game, I'd say it's worth full price.  But on discount, 100% a good buy.Game play loop is really good.  Nothing overstays its welcome.  You rotate between a few things and spend enough time at each stage it's works pretty good.  Not always exploration/story and not always combat.The dialog is also very good.  It's pretty easy to consume stuff so it's great for all ages.  But it's not like some really in-depth story with several layers.A few minor visual glitches here and there, but nothing to bad.  Haven't experienced any game breaking bugs as of yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying it so far - the combat is interesting, the customisation amusing: especially the post-mission comic covers. The dialogue is very 'comic book', and though occasionally irritating it's also sometimes genuinely funny. There's lots to do. I get the feeling it could be a big comfy time-sink.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, after a fair amount of hours, my personal opinion of the game is:- somewhat clunky- gameplay, especially outside of combat, could be improved- dialogues are ok at best, often boring and too long (it feels like a drawn out teenage drama sometimes)- graphics are not great; they are not bad, but not polished at all. Don't expect God of War level stuff.Would I recommend the game. Absolutely YES. It's a mix of Divinity 2, Marvel Strike Force (yeah the mobile game) and Marvel Champions (the board game) and it all works. I keep finishing a day to its fullest and eager to get to the next mission, whether be it story or side quest. The dynamics with the other heroes are nothing new (build relationships with them, get positive outcomes), but I also feel compelled and excited about leveling up those relationships. Overall, if you like strategic, turn based games and you like the Marvel universe, this game is an easy choice. Play a few hours to get accustomed to it and you won't regret it. The main story is actually interesting and it feels like a proper Marvel arc, with multiple enemies and story lines. Bonus perk, you get to listen to Matt Mercer if you play male Hunter, which is always great :)

_childDocuments_.review: Initially slept on this game, the marketing didn't do much for me. After seeing a clip or two on youtube I bought the game with its DLC on a whim during a sale and was hooked right away.There is a fun amount of depth to the deck building system, with each character having their own fun little spins. Out of all 17 characters, which includes the 4 dlc characters, there was only ever 1 character who I didn't find too enjoyable (that being Storm). Some characters are blatantly better than others, but I never found myself feeling outright screwed when forced to play as anyone. The story is rather basic too, but the characters and their interactions are fun enough to keep interest. I also personally found myself passing on exploring the abbey, your hub world, much due to it being a bit boring.I highly recommend this game, the card system is incredibly fun and if you enjoy Marvel in any aspect you'll have fun with the characters and their interactions. A shame it performed poorly, as this game absolutely deserves a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: 1. There's alot of stuff already said by alot of other reviews which i mostly agree with. Mainly being the horrible script writing and certain ingame-mechanics which have alot of negative impact on the overall game experience (at least for me and it seems many others).I still recommend it because:1. Combat is awesome.2. Ofc its marvel and there's plenty of awesome heroes to choose from besides the teenage twilight boy/girl -band characters being the "midnight suns"3. General story isnt that bad.  (excluding all the idiotic wicca/charmed/gothic/emo/buffy the vampire slayer/ "lets all wear leather pants" stuff and sidestories)  *hint when they tell you to collect ingredients, you can just ignore it and it wont make a difference.4. Since its a marvel "mainstream" game i would have expected it to be alot shorter. So overal length and playability is pretty good, you can easily get 40+ hours out of it and not having completed everything.5. Since people are comparing it with Xcom and the likes one thing i liked in contrary to Xcom games is that you aren't being pushed, you can just play at your own pace, in theory you can level up to max level with general missions before even defeating the first boss.  (at least combat in my opinion is not like Xcom at all and i wouldnt compare the 2 games with eachother; Xcom is much more strategic and about movement on a much bigger map. This game is arena-based fighting, you enter a ring basically and fight it out with different objectives/ enemies etc.)6. There's a NG+ option.7. In general theres plenty of things done right on a medium level, nothing amazing groundbreaking or things you haven't seen before but its enjoyable and sometimes suprising to see from this type of game. At the same time this leaves alot of improvement to be desired and missing mechanics.8. Lot of people saying performance issues, ive had little to none.Even though im recommending it due to the pros outweighing the cons, things i hated:1. Horrible cringy af character-design. Tbf im not familiar with the original lore of the midnight suns and its characters so if i mention stuff that's loyal to the original lore i guess that just sucks too then.- Apart from the Avengers that participate (which are obv so much more experienced and OP, not only in the actual story of the game but combat-wise as well) you're basically left with 1 awesome completely out of place daywalker (Blade) and a bunch of mentally unstable, selfish incredibly stupid teenagers with what i suspect is a combination of bipolar disorder and schizophrenia or Multiple personality disorder. _childDocuments_.review: It’s not XCOM. It was never supposed to be XCOM. The Good- Combat/card system. An exciting take on the deckbuilding combat system. There are plentiful ways to customize each character’s deck, which allows you the flexibility to build them how you want. Different passives, different class fantasies. There are certain characters that I feel are more powerful than others (i.e., cards that are overtuned). Spider-Man can be the ultimate minion killer (1 hp) OR spend his turns binding big baddies in place with his webs. Heck, you can even do a combination of the two with moderate success (IMO).-Mass Effect-y dynamic, true-to-comic dialog. Absolutely enormous array of conversations, plot points, +1/-1 friendships, etc etc. If you’re into the overall comics and lore, then this will be a great place for you to see how the characters navigate “mundane” life fishing (yes, fishing). That said, I feel relatively ambivalent about the fact that your level of friendship with the heroes impacts their bonuses in combat. The power of friendship directly impacts combat.- Mission Types. Lots of different mission types. Save the citizens, protect a laptop while enemies try to kill it, etc. Overall neat despite the fact that every map is confined to invisible walls with roughly the same amount of space.The Bad- Weird performance issues. Exclusively out of combat while you traverse the central area. Chugging and other annoyances. Well documented across different comments. - Currency/resource after currency/resource. See the comments below about the crafting system. It’s just a lot of different things to keep track of for little value. Missed Opportunities- Little customization for The Hunter. I would have loved the opportunity to customize the main character. I understand that your deckbuilding accomplishes most of this ask with the light/dark system (see below) giving your deck a specific purpose. It would be cool to be a caster with a staff or a “tank” with a sword and board. The dual-wielding permanence feels mediocre, especially considering your abilities/attacks are not aesthetically linked to having two weapons (i.e., you send a shockwave from your character’s chest while holding weapons).- The card crafting system needs to be reworked - for UX reasons, not balance. This is actually a blend of a few issues (see: currency/resource). It’s bizarre and completely counterintuitive to hop from one spot in the to craft a resource, then go to another spot to craft a blueprint, then another to disenchant your current cards in your inventory. Here is my video suggestion for improvements: Just not for me- Light/Dark system. Too binary in nature. It impacts your dialog and the potency of cards. Otherwise, it feels too predictable and bland. How do you want to defeat your mom? Want to be all angry (dark) or do you want to find hope in your friends (light)? That’s mostly hyperbolic but the sentiment is close enough.- Microtransactions for customization. Meh. It’s all cosmetic and has no impact on the gameplay itself. I can see why people want full customizability for immersion's sake. If you made me give it a rating: 8.25 / 10. If you’re in super hero stuff, you’ll probably bump it up to 8.5+.

_childDocuments_.review: So played for a while (after reading the reviews) and, I have to say, as i often do these days; "I dont know what people are crying about!" - with regards to the game itself, the microtransactions are another thing, we'll get to that.So, long story short: No, this is not a "dating sim", not even sure where that came from! Yes, you can raise/ lower affinity with your team but not sure what that has to do with dating, (there's a lot more to dating, kids!). Possibly because the friendship meter is represented by a heart? i dunno.Also, yes there is a lot of non-combat stuff to do, much of it is actually optional but definitely encouraged. (the abbey grounds are immense!)Not sure what people's issue is with the dialogue, they all seem pretty canonical in terms of their personality. Childish? no. I'd say sometimes puerile but then, I'm 40 and these are broody, mostly teenagers with the odd man-child thrown into a big brother house. I actually enjoy strange and stark bickering, i think they got it spot on with their personalities (particularly stark). And always good to see Cpn. Marvel, my fav character in the mix!All that aside, the game has grabbed me in a surprising way, (i don't play card games at all, usually avoid them tbh!)The battles can be truly cinematic and there is a lot more strategy possible than I initially expected, once you get the hang of the card system and the teams basics. _childDocuments_.review: This game is just fun. If you like having fun, you should give it a try. Midnight Suns is an RPG that mixes tactical card-based combat with some light exploration and a Persona-style daily social interaction system. Each in-game day, you'll talk with the superheroes around the Abbey, choose tasks like research and sparring, then go out on a mission -- a tactical battle with a variety of objectives. At night, you can do activities such as hanging out with a fellow hero or going to a club meeting. With nearly all of these activities, you'll increase your friendship level with the other heroes, unlocking passive abilities and eventually each one's legendary card.Combat is absolutely one of the highlights of the game, with the knockback feature alone leading to a lot of great tactical decisions (plus the experience of seeing an enemy get blasted into a wall, an ally or an explosive barrel never gets old). Each hero gets a fair variety of cards to play with cool superhero moves, though I wouldn't mind seeing some new cards added in the future. Importantly, Firaxis captured the feel of each hero really well with their abilities, giving each hero a distinct playstyle and aesthetic.The social interactions are pretty good, with quality voice acting. If you've played Persona 3/4/5, you'll be accustomed to the somewhat surreal sensation of being a character that everyone just seems to confide in and love to a somewhat weird degree. The conversations here aren't quite as good as that series, but they are still done well and I liked hanging out with the off-duty superheroes. (With that said, I haven't read a comic since the early 1990s X-Men, so I can't really vouch for how authentic any of the characters come across.) Fortunately, there is no romance between your character and the other characters, so you're spared the awkwardness that makes up most RPG romances.Exploring the Abbey was a lot more interesting than I expected it to be. I liked uncovering the mysteries of the place, and doing so greatly expanded on the game's story. The one thing that feels like it should have been left out of the game was the need to gather plants and mushrooms; it just doesn't really fit into this game (or most games that feature it, to be honest).It took me about 91 hours to play from the start to the credits. I played on the Heroic II difficulty setting for nearly the entire game (you need to unlock difficulty levels first), and that felt like a sweet spot for me. Pleasantly, the game feels complete right out of the box, and I expect that the season pass for four more characters will be an enjoyable reason to revisit to the game.A less enjoyable reason to revisit the game is the New Game+ mode, which allows you to play through the story again with all the characters unlocked. Unfortunately, this mode resets almost everything you would want to keep for your second playthrough. In particular, needing to do all the Abbey exploration and hero trials again feels like an absolute slog -- those activities are fun the first time around, but there's little joy in solving the same puzzles again.Performance-wise, the game ran fine on my PC, with two exceptions. First, the title screen stutters a little. Second, the very cool final mission brought my frame rate to its knees.I encountered one serious bug with the game that was fixed within a few days of release. The game would often crash to desktop when doing manual saves -- but you could still quicksave safely, so it didn't have much impact on the game. I also had a character glitch through the floor in combat once, which only had a brief visual impact. Aside from that, it was nice to have a nearly bug-free experience with a game I played right from launch day.Since I bought the legendary edition, there were no microtransactions in the game and the game seems to go out of its way to hide the existence of any such thing from you. That was definitely a plus. (The legendary edition gives the season pass and a bunch of additional costumes for the companion superheroes.) If new cosmetics are added for sale in the future, I hope the game will continue to avoid aggressively trying to sell them, because it's almost refreshing in a modern game to have an experience that felt like a full game right from the start without microtransactions.

_childDocuments_.review: Unique, clever, and super fun.The gameplay loop consists of three phases: grabbing upgrades and improving your friendships with the other heroes in the morning, then running a mission, and then triggering an event in the evening with one or multiple heroes.The missions are where the card game comes into play. The goal is typically to either eliminate all enemies or one beefy target by playing your cards smartly and making good use of the environmental interactions (mainly pushing enemies into things). It's a lot of fun, with many ways to manipulate the action economy and every hero feeling very strong without compromising the challenge.There is also an optional, but recommended, exploration side to the game: you can run around the abbey grounds and unlock chests for cosmetics while learning the backstory of the abbey and its residents. It's a bit of a shame no card-based mini-games or puzzles were included there, it feels like a missed opportunity.As for the story, it's... fine? I find the writing rather juvenile, but I'm having a good time watching the characters interact. I suspect that fans of the comics will enjoy the world-building a fair bit more. All the dialogue, which is most of the text, is very well voice-acted, although the characters' faces are unfortunately low-res (a couple of the heroes look like absolute goons at the abbey).While a lot of people have apparently run into pretty bad technical issues, I have not ran into a single one except for massive frame drops in the very last battle.

_childDocuments_.review: PERFORMANCE FIX BELOW:First I would like to say that this game is amazing, if I did not have to manually find a solution for the performance issues it would be a home run. That being said I have found some workarounds that essentially completely fixed the performance issues many people are experiencing. I have tested this on both my laptop which runs a GTX1070 and my PC which runs an RTX3080 and it improved both by a large margin. I recommend making all three of these adjustments:1. In the NVIDIA control panel set your VSINC to "on" instead of "let the app decide"2. In the NVIDIA control panel set your max frame rate to the refresh rate of your monitor. My laptop has a refresh rate of 120 so I set it to 120. Simple. 3. Disable the 2k launcher, this is a known issue with the 2k launcher. (Plenty of videos on youtube showing how to do this. Basically it just changes the file path to launch the game directly instead of through the launcherAfter implementing all three of these solutions I can play the game stutter free even on the much less powerful laptop. Hope this helps others because I really enjoy this game and it was a total bummer when it was running so poorly.

_childDocuments_.review: So, this game is sort of story-first, action-second? And the action is kind of a turn-based tactics thing that involves deck-building and careful use of available resources under complex conditions. The theme that unites these two aspects of the game, I think, is leadership.  But, be ready to spend some time building relationships, managing social crises, etc., in addition to the turn-based fighting.The characters (Midnight Suns, working with a few Avengers and a smattering of X-Men) are much closer to their traditional comic book versions than the film versions. The voice-acting is well done once you understand that, and also that the player character, "Hunter," is...simple? I mean this in the nicest way. At first the voice work seemed wooden, and then I was like...no wait, this character is kind of reserved and inhuman because (well, reasons. no spoilers.) The story is character driven and great.I love it. It's a great example of itself, and a great tribute to the comics. If you like these kinds of games, you will love it, too. If you were expecting a game focused mainly on fighting, without too much concern for managing relationships and decks, it may take some getting used to.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to start this review by saying I don't usually play a lot of games with a sense of story or progression anymore. My most played games are rogue-likes and MOBAs, so sinking time into a game can really feel like a chore, and maintaining investment is difficult for me.THAT BEING SAID, this game is amazing and had me hooked from an early point. Playing this game made me feel like I was playing an old Playstation 2 game where the developers almost seemed like they didn't hate their job, and just had a passion for making a good game.So when I originally seen the core gameplay (especially when I did the tutorial), I thought that a card battler is a dumb idea for an XCOM like game, along with limitations of 3 card plays a turn, movement system also seemingly shallow because you can traverse only one character only once wherever you choose in the whole area. All of this gave so much impression to me that this game is probably shallow in terms of mechanical depth. To say the least; I stand completely wrong for thinking that. 68 hours in at this time of review and I spend many minutes on end trying to think my turn out and maximize the most of my limited actions, while also preparing for the repercussions of what the choices of my actions will be, and even beyond that the deckbuilding system is so unique for each of the characters playstyles and is generally flavored to the characters powers themselves ie Spiderman throws people around, binds them, and benefits a lot more from environmental usage compared to Captain America who usually focuses more on building up block for your team and taunting enemies to be the frontline of defense. There's also The Hunter who is technically your main character and his/her deckbuilding is probably the most vast in the game based on if you went down a light path, dark path, or any other kind of builds you can make out of them.Continuing on beyond the core gameplay, the characters and interactions you have with them are very surprisingly true to all of their actual comic counterparts and interacting with them through socializing can actually lead to some interesting and meaningful conversations that go beyond the gimmicks of their characters. There are sooooo many lines of dialogue that even though I tend to be invested I skim through a lot of it, but the writing is still pretty good overall and I will stand by that any day.Comparable to XCOM you have a main base type of area called the Abbey. You can explore the Abbey island and find interesting things about the plot of land, but most of this is secondary content and you can pretty much completely ignore it if it's not your cup of tea. The Abbey itself allows you to do research, get more cards for characters, hang out with some of the heroes, and can be actually upgraded and customized more than you would think.For the record this game does have microtransactions apparently, but I actually only just found this fact out 68 hours in so I think that says enough about how irrelevant they are to the actual game.I will say bugs are slightly common, but not once did I have a single bug that actually hindered my progress or broke the game. At most my experience were just visual hiccups, one dialogue line overlapping another briefly, and other small things that weren't very notable.Overall I'd say if you like XCOM this game has a lot of depth and is definitely worth giving a shot. If you're a big Marvel fan this game is true to what you're seeking from that. If you're neither of those people, then I would still recommend this game if it's on sale, because there truly is a lot going for this game and it might be a good introduction into a different genre for you.

_childDocuments_.review: This is just a day one review as I haven't had too much time to play but just wanted to state my thoughts:Marvel's Midnight Suns was a game that I was very cautious of. I am, and always have been, a very big Marvel fan and was looking to explore into this stream of comic books. I was nervous at the start when I heard that this is would be considered a "card game", but after playing it for about an hour and a half, I really do love the basics of this game. The story itself isn't the greatest story of all time, but I feel like it's enough to keep me engaged, and give me more background to characters I haven't necessarily have known much about in the Marvel Universe. Of course, the fan favorites are in the game, Iron Man, Spider-Man, Captain America, Wolverine...etc, but there are so many other great heros in this game that never get much recognition in the mainstream. Nico and Magik are great, and I have loved to learn more about them. Robbie Reyes is the ghost rider in this game, and since I am a big AOS fan, I am very happy they decided to choose him over the ghost rider we've known all our lives. The combat in this game feels great. Cards feel like they do enough damage, and there is a wide variety that you can choose from within each character. For a card game, I really like how they emphasize moving your characters. For example, there are explosive abilities that some enemies have that results in harming people around it. Fortunately, the game allows you to respond to this by moving characters out of the zones, as well as knocking enemies into the blast radius (very satisfying at the end of your turn)The performance of this game is the biggest thing hurting it right now. There is constant stuttering in cutscenes, as well as massively long load times just to load into things like The Abbey. If you're mixed on buying this game, my recommendation is to wait a week or two and wait for fixes to come, otherwise, the game plays and feels great and highly recommend for any Marvel fan!

_childDocuments_.review: After a solid 128+ hours into this neat Firaxis title with main campaign finished, I can thumbs-up Marvel's Midnight Suns (not to be confused with Midnight Sons), but not by a lot. This is not your daddy's XCOM or your sister's Chimera Squad. This here is TCG strategy action with snippets of XCOM elements that kind of make you wish you were playing XCOM2 instead. The actual length of story is not long if you ignore the extra stuff. By "extra", I mean the extensive mind-numbingly long and sometimes awkwardly delivered dialogue in your magical home base called The Abbey. That is where you spend the bulk of this title (better get used to it).When you're not slinging RNG cards at bad guys in the shiny little flat faux-3D playpens the game throws you into, Midnight Suns becomes a character-driven relationship simulator game similar to XCOM: Chimera Squad, but with more fleshed out friendship mechanics and somewhat better writing (albeit with some very cringe moments...I'm looking at you, Nico). I'll let other better reviews talk about the boring technicals and interesting, yet sometimes enormously frustrating gameplay and just focus on the cast:Hunter = generic awkward fish out-of-water heroic avatar for the audience with major mommy issues (found the female to be a little more compelling than the male (Matt Mercer still did a good job tho), also Dark Hunter dialogue adds a bit more spice to the Abbey chit-chat)Blade = grumpy discount Wesley Snipes, also... "YOUR MOTHER!" (best combat line in the game)Captain America = surrogate dad, a walking love letter to classic wholesome golden age comic book mentality that is virtually extinct nowCaptain Marvel = better than Brie Larson (and that's not saying much)Doctor Strange = perfect foil for Tony Stark (their banter is some of the best writing in the game), not as charismatic as MCU Strange, but truer to the old comic book versionGhost Rider = he's alright, not as badass as the MCU version in Agents of Shield, but likableHulk = SMASH (also, Bruce Banner is a ♥♥♥♥)Iron Man = discount RDJ (but in a good way), perfect Dr. Spooky foilMagik = grumpy Russian stereotype, but weirdly likeable and her snarky lines are way more entertaining than...Nico Minoru = insufferable young millennial with annoying combat cards that have long AF repetitive animations (worst character in the game by far)Scarlet Witch = Wanda is decent, but in truth she is quite simply............WASTED POTENTIAL (I think Firaxis dropped the ball with her both in story and gameplay, but still better than MCU Wanda)Spider-Man = very fun and likable as Spidey should be, his friendship with Robbie should make Marvel consider doing live-action or animated crossovers with Spider-Man and Ghost RiderWolverine = iconic chill Canadian war veteran badass uncle-type, too tall (devs clearly preferred Jackman's height), also Steve Blum's voice is back (again...yay...)No thoughts on Deadpool since I won't try DLC content until the full season is released. When all the new stuff is complete, I'll try a New Game+ since I badly need a break from this (the replayabililty is not very strong due to the length and repetitiveness, and also the things NG+ takes away from you such as your cards and first 25 levels not counting the bonus champion levels).Closing thoughts:One thing I greatly appreciated (besides the awkward pauses between lines) was the dialogue tree system. This is not your usual Nice/Naughty/Neutral system like Mass Effect or Dragon Age. It's more like Alpha Protocol (bet you haven't heard that name in a long ass time) where nice or professional responses aren't always the best approach. The writers mixed things up by making each character react differently depending on the topic being discussed. For instance, Magik generally likes dark lines, but I found that often the neutral, and very rarely light choices actually went over well with her.Midnight Suns is worth a shot if you're a big Marvel fan (especially the pre-2010 comics), or just dig that old Sid Meier turn-based thinking-man's game with a little Magic the Gathering flair thrown in. Would NOT advise purchasing at full price, however. Get this one on sale, and for goodness sake, try to play more than two hours before passing judgment on it.Godspeed, Hunters.

_childDocuments_.review: The game play is a lovely mix of Slay the Spire and XCOM, with less probability to make someone with a 98% hit chance miss. Where things kind of fall apart for me are 2-fold. (1) Optimization is abysmal. I'm using a 3080ti, but RTX Ray Tracing will give me 3 frames a second, no lie. The game stutters if you try to use it at any capacity. The fact that some people (not all) are also reporting crashing is wild. _childDocuments_.review: I had been hyped for a long time about the Midnight Suns, and I was not disappointed.I'm a big fan of XCOM and was half expecting a Marvel XCOM in the Midnight Suns, but it's very unique. Each hero having their own mechanics and playstyle, you'll have fun figuring out which combos are your favourites, and what synergies you want to play with.I appreciated the Persona-like social aspect where you get to know superheros better in order to become better friends and get combat bonuses for them. The depictions of heroes are very successful; they feel very authentic, especially the midnight suns.The exploration aspect also had me very invested, you learn more about your character and get to see the story through a deeper perspective. _childDocuments_.review: First time leaving a review since I really got hooked on the game. And after reading some of the bad ones and positive, I think I reached a some consensus that people ought to check their system requirements, I am running on a GTX 1660 SUPER, hardly anything impressive and experience no lag or game-breaking bugs. Pros: - Absolutely addictive gameplay. Most of my hours were achieved over the weekend. The card system gets so much better once you get the upgrades going and start to build a solid team composition. The card system actually works amazing, and as a big XCOM fan, I think it is only an improvement as you no longer have to suffer the 95 % hit chance miss. No save-scum needed. - Variety of Heroes. No one feels like they play the same and contribute with a certain talent to the team. The replay-ability is amazing due to this. For instance I ran majorly with Hunter, Captain Marvel and Magik for my campaign, and then I switched it up with different heroes and it felt like a new game altogether. Cons: - Weak story & voice acting. - Friendship grind feels like a chore - Backstory dump on every friendship activity Conclusion: The combat system alone is one of the better I've seen in a while, there are a lot of problems with the game, but that is mostly down to the storytelling and Hunter's voice actor who feels more robotic than anything in their responses. At this point I would probably have preferred a mute protagonist. I have a stark feeling that this will be a much better game next year with more DLCs and story content added. Right now, story is as predictable as it gets. The heavy lore dump is a treat for Marvel Comic fans, but I can see how newer players won't get much excitement out of it and end up skipping most of the conversations. I can say that this is one of the rare games where the combat is the most exciting with it all, enemy types are unique and plenty new ones they didn't show in trailers.

_childDocuments_.review: New York styled Pizza:Pizza dough:14 g instant yeast617g water - 95F950g all-purpose flour19g fine sea salt25g granulated sugarAmerican Pizza Sauce and Toppings:1 tablespoon (14g) butter1 tablespoon (9g) extra virgin olive oil6 cloves garlic, rough chopped2 teaspoons (4g) red pepper flakes28 oz (794g) can of crushed tomato2 teaspoons (2g) dried oregano1.5 tablespoons (21g) granulated sugarsalt and pepper to tasteSplash of olive oil2 cups (227g) low moisture mozzarella, fresh grated2 cups (200g) Monterey jack cheese, fresh grated1/2 cup (26g) parmigiano reggiano, fresh gratedAmerican Pizza Dough:Preheat the oven and a baking steel or pizza stone at 500F for 45 minutes before utilizing it.Whisk yeast and sugar into your water, and allow it to sit for 5 minutes. In a separate bowl, add flour and salt and mix by hand to combine. Pour your water mixture into your flour and mix by hand until you get a rough dough, then transfer to a work surface and knead until it starts to pull away from the work surface and is relatively smooth.Place your dough in a greased bowl, then cover with plastic wrap and let rise for 1 - 2 hours at room temperature or until double in size.Punch down your dough and dive into 300g pieces. Form those pieces into balls and place them in a floured proofing pizza box, cover with a lid, and proof at room temperature for 3 - 4 hours. (If you do not have a proofing pizza box, you can use a floured baking sheet, cover it with an inverted baking sheet and wrap it in plastic wrap.)American Pizza Sauce and Toppings:In a medium sauce pot, add butter and olive oil. Set that over medium-high heat; once the butter melts add garlic, cook until fragrant, add pepper flakes, and cook, stirring occasionally, until the garlic begins to brown on the edges.Add crushed tomatoes, oregano, salt, and a splotch of olive oil, boil over medium-high, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 12 minutes, stirring occasionally or until thickened and viscous—season with salt to taste and let it cool down.Assembly.- Place one of your pizza doughs onto a floured pizza peel, and flour your dough generously.Punch your dough down in the center, working your way out to create a ¼” wide. Pick up your dough, place it over your closed fists, and rotate it around, gently stretching to 13” to 14”.Place a couple of spoons of your sauce, starting in the center, spreading in little circles, and working your way to the edge until it gets evenly spread out.In a medium-size mixing bowl, place mozzarella cheese, Monterey Jack, and Parmigiano; mix until combined. Sprinkle your cheese mixture to your desire and place in the oven onto your baking steel and bake for 5 - 7 minutes or until the edge gets golden brown and the cheese melts.Enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: 1. Many people mention the side activities taking too much time. It's a little frontloaded, but once you get a popup saying "Exploring the Abbey is optional", they mean it. You can do all the side activities at your own pace. There's enough stuff to be stretched out nearly over the entire campaign if you're just doing a little bit between missions. Let me put it like this: the bonuses from the roleplaying & exploration will make the game easier, which means you can bump up the difficulty, which means you'll spend longer in combat.2. You'll probably find the writing less awkward with a female protagonist. You see the "default" hunter in the artwork and promo material for this game, and it seems to be the perspective given the most consideration in the writing. Matthew Mercer gives a great performance as the male Hunter, but I think most comic book guys are going to feel weird being asked to get all up in their feelings with Blade if they created a self-insert.3. This is NOT a dating sim. The friendship mechanics might give people that impression, but you cannot ♥♥♥♥ Tony Stark OR his porno stache. You need to become friends with characters to unlock their passives, but you can get friendship slowly just from missions if the combat is all you care about.4. The Abbey mystery sidequest is 100% worth doing. On top of getting a new armor and passive for completing it, you will also have a much greater understanding of the story. I don't recommend doing the final mission before you at least finish this questline. If you get stuck, read Wanda's open book in the library for a new hint each day.5. Play with whatever characters you want. This isn't XCOM and you can't "fail" a campaign. Every hero will be at most 3 levels below your avatar. (Almost) every character has a story mission you  take them on, so I do recommend taking a character on a general mission at least once to learn their unique mechanics. But any character you don't like, you can safely bench for the most part.
