_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: A slower more story driven game. Wasn't what I was expecting, but am looking forward to completing this game. Take your time with this game, there is a lot to explore.I was expecting some sort of X-COM style game since it was the same development company. What I've received so far (~40 in and I think only 1/3 of the way done) was actually the game I wanted. This is not a fast paced game where you will be jumping into a new battle every ten minutes. Instead, it is more of a Dragon Age/X-COM hybrid, where you spend as much, if not more time on storytelling and conversation than battle. Each day/turn is broken into 3 phases. Morning, you upgrade items, research tech, send out heroes on side missions, get to know your team, train and explore the Abbey (your home base). Phase 2 you pick your mission, similar to X-COM but the combat is card based, similar to the new Marvel Snap. Phase 3 you can explore the Abbey some more, hangout with teammates and take part in club activities like EMO Kids, Shop Class or Book Club. You go to bed to end the day and repeat.The downsides I've come across are not preventing me from enjoying the game. I also don't know if it is the game or my laptop when it comes to the graphics issues. But on occasion my character will lose their hair in a cut scene and the lighting effects are inconsistent, leading to rock cliffs looking like multi-color static or the lighting in my bedroom looking like a rave was going on.My biggest complaint is the character's movement. I'm using keyboard and mouse and it feels like it was set up for a controller. When I press 'W' to move forward, I feel like my character is immediately moving into a full sprint. Trying to make a turn while 'jogging' can be disorienting and often leads to you looking behind you at the way you came. Being patient and using walk to look around and aim before moving has helped this issue. Overall I'm enjoying the game. There are tons of references to the comics, the characters are voiced amazingly, most of the dialog is great and has had me laughing as I continue my journey. There are a lot of characters in this game and you get to spend time with all of them. I'm looking forward to the next 40 hours.

Everything hits, no RNG other than random card draws. So combat entirely relies on who you hit first, an attack which you know will hit, no matter where your people are on the map, and the attacks you're allowed to make are randomized. Meh.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended when on sale for half off or better only.This is a very good and very simple 'puzzle combat' tactical game.... under layers of mobile and AAA-chasing dreck. The actual missions are quick and enjoyable, and the story is a fun and slightly lighter take on the Midnight Sons/Suns comic runs. The new hero/heroine fits right in in the spooky side of the Marvel universe, depending on how willing you are to retcon the villain Lilith.Sadly it's got frustrating time gating, tedious materials collection, and a rather pointless open world aspect that all feel like remnants of some other game. I'm probably glad it's not that game -- the open world portion has chests that drop randomized cosmetics and power-ups that were likely designed to have lootbox cash shop keys rather than the in-game key system we actually got -- but it's still mostly worse for their inclusion given the fairly simple lightweight nature of the underlying tactical game. The net feel is of a mobile game trying to parrot triple-A trends at the minimum possible depth.A tighter focus probably could have released this as an uncritically delightful double-A title for less development cost and at half the initial price... which is about where I'd recommend buying it.Given the open-world and collection elements a part of me wishes they'd made this as an attempt at an iso-hack-and-slash, a solo revival of Marvel Heroes. All that tedious real-time travel would make a lot more sense in that kind of game, and there's definitely a contingent of us who miss the brawler superhero genre. If you're listening, 2K/Firaxis and license-holders.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly was not expecting much, I'm a huge XCOM fan but with this being a big IP game with an OC and all the horrible Marvel games in recent years I was ready to give this a miss and just enjoy the nerd rage response from others on YouTube.I can't recommend it enough after playing through it non-stop: The story is really weirdly high quality, the positivity of the main cast balances nicely with the darkness of the backstory around the abbey and the main villain, all of it is especially fleshed out and nuanced; the combat is addictive, I hate card games normally but it's usage here is probably one of the best I've ever seen with how they represent the characters' abilities and modify each other and the battlefield; I at least like all the main cast and love the majority, they decided to focus on the animated and comic book incarnations of the characters which I feel works very well; the main character fits surprisingly well with the rest of the cast, and the dual morality system works quite well with providing new abilities, new dialogue and story changes based on your alignment.My biggest gripe with the game is perhaps the menus, it's kind of annoying to have to run between four different stations in the base before every mission; you have to manage ops missions from one console which can give items to the other 3, then there's the Forge to open the Coils (lootboxes essentially) and purchase additional abilities, then run to the training yard to further upgrade abilities, get daily modifiers and heal injured units, then pop into the card menu accessible anywhere to equip and swap abilities. Sometimes you have to sprint between stations multiple times to get everything sorted out. Then finally run to the mission table to start a mission. I can understand why it's been made this way I suppose, but I kinda wish I could either fast travel between each station or just have it all accessible from the character menu, since it can get tedious to flit between the same 3-4 areas every in game day. Only a minor gripe though, the rest of the game is top notch and absolutely recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: Marvel's Midnight Suns is an exciting and engaging tactical RPG game developed by Firaxis Games and published by 2K Games. The game takes place in the Marvel Universe and features a variety of iconic characters such as Wolverine, Captain America, and Iron Man. Players control the customisable character, The Hunter, and work alongside the Midnight Suns team to prevent Lilith, the Mother of Demons, from bringing about the end of the world.One of the strengths of the game is its immersive and well-crafted story. The game's narrative is captivating, and the characters are well-developed and intriguing. The game's cinematic cutscenes, voice acting, and sound design all contribute to a polished and professional production.The gameplay mechanics are also well-executed. The turn-based combat system is satisfying and rewards strategic thinking. Players can customize their character's abilities and playstyle to fit their preferences, and the game provides a satisfying challenge as the difficulty level ramps up.The game's graphics are also impressive. The character designs are faithful to the source material and are rendered beautifully in the game's 3D graphics engine. The environments are detailed and immersive, and the game's visual effects are top-notch.Overall, I highly recommend Marvel's Midnight Suns to any fan of tactical RPGs or the Marvel Universe. The game's engaging story, well-crafted gameplay mechanics, and impressive graphics make for an enjoyable and immersive gaming experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I originally gave this game a negative review and now I'm still on the fence. But I find myself wanting to play it enough that I think the goods outweigh the bads. I'm going to lay them out below:Goods:1.) Story - The story on this game is intriguing and has a ton of little side stories and relationships you get to build with Marvel heroes. I find myself actually really interested to see where some of them will go. 2.) Variety - This game is actually several games. It is a deck builder. It is an exploration secret finder scavenger. And it is a relationship based dialog RPG. All of which are executed extremely well independently.3.) Graphics - The game is actually really beautiful and well optimized. It plays well on either my steam deck at medium settings or on my PC at Ultra settings.Bads:1.) Pacing.... The game is setup into day night cycles with each cycle including a few short active storyline progressing activities(fun). A single Mission where you get to use the deck battle the game is structured around(fun). An opportunity to make relationship decisions with each character currently at the abby(fun). Any then a host of boring homework tasks required to progress in building your deck (Lame!!!!!). The biggest problem of this game is that the actual combat makes up only about 10% of the time you spend in game. 2.) Functionality and support - This game crashes like a madman if directX 12 is selected. Whatever they tried to do in dx12 is not working. Contacting support was very unhelpful as well. On top of that it forces the 2K launcher to run by default in steam which is really annoying and a resource hog strangely.3.) Lastly and most importantly, though most of the sub games in this title are actually a lot of fun, you feel obligated to do all of them in every day night cycle and they don't feel super interconnected. Which leaves me sometimes skipping through some dialog just wanting to get around to another mission (combat), which is unfortunate because the dialog is good.Again, all in all the voice acting and the story and how fun the combat when you actually get to do it in was enough to move this from a No to a Yes Hope this helps.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has several flaws to its core design. Such as how it actually gets easier when you have fewer heroes "alive" due to your hand not being watered down by three different "decks". (Since you can only draw cards for "active" heroes.)The abbey outside free-roam section is also completely disconnected from the main game-play loop. You can literally ignore the entire thing and miss basically nothing. Which is good, because the free roam section sucks. You have no mini-map. This makes it very easy to turned around/lost. The map you bring up is also heavily lacking in details on what things are located where. So it's barely of any use either.Balance is also heavily off, with both Hunter and Iron Man standing head and shoulders faaaarrr above any of the other heroes. Some cards are also badly designed/utterly useless. Which is a problem, because you only get EXP/cards for the heroes you use. So the less you use someone, the worse they become.Speaking of cards, the card upgrade system is also a slog once you arrive at the "mod" mechanic. Mods are randomly generated, and trying to re-roll them gets expensive *very* quickly. So you actually have to keep juggling multiple copies of the same card(s) as you attempt to RNG a "good" mod for them.There's also an enemy with a very poor design in the late game. Its gimmick is that it will duplicate itself every time it survives being hit. Ideally, you build up your "hero" meter, and hit it with a super powerful attack. The problem? If you *don't* attack it...it will duplicate itself anyways! And then the duplicate will start duplicating other enemies as well! On lower difficulties this isn't too huge a deal, but the highest difficulty sets all enemies to 225% HP. So not only is it much harder to kill in a single blow, but it has a lot more time, and damage, to start stealing your HP to heal itself back up.It's not a bad game, but it's one that you can stand to wait for a sale on.Just don't but the season pass. That thing is overpriced to a sickening degree.

I just had seen some much of it and it was no longer interesting to me.One big mechanical problem (I was playing on Heroic 1 level) was that other than Hunter, the other hero skills did not scale very well.  IE: Average trash enemies would have like 550hp and more advanced enemies could have 1k or more hp, sometimes even 2k or more if they had block.Yet Captain Marvel's knee kick still did only 64 points of damage, along with her power punches. All heroes had this issue. except for hunter.  Hunter's light mace attacks could get upwards of 800pts for a 'basic' attack.  His AoEs did like 400pts of damage, meanwhile another hero's uber legendary AoE did like 150 which was nothing.   I think Dr. Strange's uber AoE was the only one that was worth anything.Finally they should have unlocked all the heroes MUCH sooner before I was totally sick of the side missions.  You get the Hulk at the very end, where as the next story mission is the final mission. _childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying that I love Marvel and turn based tactics games. So, it's a great combination for me, in theory. In practice... Well, let's make a short list of pros and cons:Pros:- Each and every hero feels unique and has their own, very lore-friendly set of moves and attacks- Card based tactical battles are pure fun- Card crafting, upgrades, etc. is very easy to comprehend and upgrades actually do make a difference- A lot to do in-between the battles - clubs, training, hang outs, story cut scenes...- Interactions between most (but not all) characters- Cringe - yep, it can be a pro too if you're into it ;)Cons:- I haven't counted but the game crashed on me at least 30-40 times in the first 30 hours of play. Perhaps it's a mixture of AMD CPU and nVidia GPU but it shouldn't have happened anyway... It's just tiring, really.- Very few kinds of missions- Very little variety in enemies and special "bosses"- It's less XCom and more XCom Chimera Squad- Performance (or lack thereof) - my PC may not be the most powerful out there but it's not a weakling, and Midnight Sun's performance is just all over the place. Fortunately most if not all FPS drops happen outside of combat.- Cringe - sometimes it is what it is...OK, so what could be done to make it better? Apart from performance and crashes, which are obvious culprits to redo, I'd start with adding variety to missions and enemies. Seeing the same four or five hydra agents with an occasional "boss" enemy is not enough. Why not add some more Marvel villains, the lore is huge and it wouldn't be tough to find some extras (if not the more well known characters) to add as opponents. Missions and mission maps could be expanded too. Switching from current arena-style maps to more XCom-like multi-screen locations with various new objectives would be a God-send for Midnight Suns. There's a lot to fix and change and hopefully, Firaxis will get to it.My final score is...For a Marvel and turn-based lover: 8/10For a Marvel or turn-based lover: 7/10For everyone else: 6/10

Well, it only took me a few hours of play to decide that this was something I needed to own and play all the way through.  It's a good game. _childDocuments_.review: Where do I begin? The Good: The combat is so much fun and amazing. It feels good and it looks good and it satisfies that itch we xcom lovers have, but in a new different way. Its refreshing to see something different combat-wise and have it not feel so drool. I feel challenged when I enter a combat scenario and I have to spend some time thinking and plotting out my moves based on the cards I was dealt. The graphics look AAA tier and the animation is candy to my eyes as my laptop overheats. The music is also another plus in this game, it fits the game well. The Bad: Unfortunately there's a lot. Not enough to make me refund the game, but enough to question the direction this game MIGHT be heading and wither to justify the cost for the game. Like others have said.... The dialogue, my god the dialogue. It would be different if they had better things to say... but my god what a slog to get through. I skip it every chance I can get. The Marvel dad jokes are getting to me as well. its hard for me to stay immersed and take the characters seriously with all the impudent comments they make. "The homeowners association isn't going to like this" -D.r Strange in reference to his 19th century wizard house. The ultimate reason i'm giving this game a thumbs down and I will do this for every game that does this.... Yes, the monetization... In a single-player none the less. Who am I going to show off my cosmetics too, My cat? My girlfriend? Both would leave me if I ever bought any cosmetics in this game. Lastly, thank god they didn't make it to where you had to buy this... they have (Loot Box like feature in this). Thank you to which ever developer stood up and said no to this. because you know the suits at marvel wanted to have loot boxes in this game. If you are reading this review and you love gaming no matter what generation you grew up in. Have some self respect and put your foot down to this kinda of monetization. We all deserve better.

_childDocuments_.review: Midnight Suns is an odd game and I really struggle with recommending it at full price. I think a half price it's a definitely worth it, but I think most strategy vets will get bored of the combat very quickly. After beating the game, I reflected on my experience and wondered why it lacked the magic feel of X-Com 1 and 2. Heck I think I enjoyed Chroma Squad more as well. I'll list what I find to be pros and cons:  Pros: -Great animation overall -Marvel characters are well voice acted and sound like you think the characters should -Marvel characters act like you would expect if you watched the movies -Combat is fun at first -The story is a comic book story for those that like that -Some have reported lots of bugs and performance issues, but I have had few. I had a couple crashes on only 1 mission and the final mission had a severe frame rate drop for the whole mission. My brother has a 3080 and I have a 2080ti and we both had this issue on the final mission. Overall though, the game is snappy and responsive. I think a few abilities may not work correctly, but I am sure that will be ironed out and didn't affect my ability to complete any missions. -controller support is great -some may like the difficulty curve on normal is much easier than X-Com -there are some fun customization options for your main character (nothing special) -all characters are viable (but some are definitely better than others) Cons: -The combat is designed in small arenas and your characters can't perma-die. so, you lose all of the tension from fog of war and easy fights. I realize this isn't X-Com, but what they fill those holes with is...nothing. There's no added depth to compensate for the streamlining of combat. In fact, the game strongly incentivizes you to take out the enemy as quickly as possible. You get to a point where you can win a map in 1 turn before the enemy can even move. The other big part of combat is using the objects conveniently placed in the arena for extra damage (think explosive barrels) that don't require cards to use. Once you figure out how to maximize your turns, the game becomes trivial very quickly. Slay the spire this is not. As you play the game more, it just feels like it's missing something, as the game never ramps to anything cool, new abilities are just different versions of what you already have. The exception is legendary cards, which you can only use one of per deck. The legendary abilities are so laughably broken and so easily cheated out, that it takes away any cleverness you may have felt. They're more or less a win button. -There isn't very much depth to the combat, there isn't very many abilities (cards) per character, and most characters abilities overlap with each other quite a bit. There are 12 card abilities per character and you can play 8, so don't expect to be making some insane strategy or expect to have some cool unique build. You get to add modifiers to your cards at random, so expect to grind A LOT for currency if you want to try and make a perfect deck.  -There is a big lack of enemy variety. This one really shocked me because X-Com always kept introducing you to new enemies to keep you on your toes, but don't expect this here. Even the last mission you're fighting the same trash enemies you've fought a million times. It disappointed me. Of what enemies are here, X-Com 2 vets will notice Hydra enemies are ripped right out of X-Com 2. There are also some demon enemies that are very similar to their X-Com 2 counterparts. This lowers the difficulty bar further when you know exactly what to expect. -There is just too much dialog and most of it isn't interesting. You keep listening because there are Easter eggs and bits here and there that are great, but they get fewer as the game drifts more toward established characters. Firaxis really tried to make the characters their comic book counterparts and I think the Avengers roster really hurt the game's story. I would've preferred more new characters or characters that gave more creative freedom. Nico and Magik were my favorite characters and I didn't expect that going in. The other big issue is that characters are dealing with the issues they've already dealt with in the comics, so most of the character's problems you're not going to care about if you already know about that. Firaxis goes back to well several times for the same character and it's just incredibly boring. "Yes Robbie, we know you think we only value you and not Sparky (his demon power)" you'll think to yourself when dealing with Ghostrider. Most characters have the same recurring problem and there is A LOT of dialog. It definitely would have helped the game (maybe not sales) to pare down the character roster to improve individual stories. -The game is made in the x-com 2 engine and the visuals look dated. Since the game is zoomed in more the lack of detail is more noticeable. I think a cell shaded or comic book aesthetic would've really made the game pop, but that's just me. It's about PlayStation 3 level, with better texture smoothing. -There is a lot of filler. It feels like half the game was cut out and what is there was stretched. You are forced to do a generic mission after each main mission. You may decide that it's not needed because you're doing so well, but sorry, you have no choice. It's baked in. -Too much progression is locked behind friendship levels. I was only able to get 2 people to max friendship level by the end of the game, which you will want to do to earn their legendary card. There are also powerful passive abilities and upgrades lock behind friendship. Also, I was never able to figure out why I could or could not hang out with a hero after a mission. Sometimes you can, sometimes you can't. Doesn't matter if it's a story mission or not, it just seems to be random. It's just a poorly implemented system. Friendship hangout scenes are some of the worst in the game imo, with some of the worst dialog. It's just boring. -There is some very light puzzles and rewards for exploring the Abbey grounds which is mostly optional, but a big chunk of content. You learn about the Salem Witch Trials through many characters diary entries. This simply did not interest me. There weren't really any fun or interesting surprises, just a way to get the games many currencies. There are far too many currencies for no apparent reason, since they can all be gotten in the same channels. Anyway, I think the Abbey exploration kind of sucks, but it is a nice change of pace. Like a lot of this game, it feels designed to take up time rather than be fun. Was this game supposed to be a live service, but changed at some point? I wonder... -Some heroes, like Ghostrider, are straight up broken. Some characters, like your dog, are so bad you're better off leaving them dead so you only get cards for your main character. The frustrating thing is that for story reasons the game loves to decide who you get to bring to a mission for you. This is annoying because characters level slowly and they don't get experience by simply being in the mission. It seems that experience is given on a per card played basis. So, the rich tend to get richer. There is a grind mission you can do, but it is painfully slow, the same every time, very easy, and done on a single character basis. With 11-12 characters and 4 more coming in the season pass, this is a time sink, and a bad one at that. -There is a base building aspect, but unlike X-Com, there is no time restraint, so you will be able to get everything. Without any sacrifices to make, it makes this a superficial and pointless system. -There is a light vs. dark dialog choice system and I hate it. I usually love this type of thing, but I want to pick my responses based on role playing, not to go full dark/light so I can unlock things. character limit :(

_childDocuments_.review: "Marvel’s Midnight Suns” stands out as a strategic gem that may not cater to all gamers but certainly shines for those who appreciate depth. The game boasts a rich array of mechanics, allowing players to craft unique decks for their heroes that align with personal playstyles—be it defensive, offensive, or specialized roles like healer or tank. The strategic layer extends to environmental attacks and difficulty-based challenges, ensuring a dynamic gameplay experience.Initially, the game may seem monotonous, but as you delve deeper, it unfolds new adversaries, formidable bosses, and intricate layers that captivate your attention. After a month of play, I’ve completed just the first of three chapters, indicating a substantial content offering. As my skills improved, I found myself breezing through missions, thoroughly enjoying the immersive experience. Visually, the game is a marvel, especially when played on maximum settings.However, there are aspects that might deter some players, and I’d like to share these from my perspective:1) Excessive Dialogue: Post-mission, the protagonist, The Hunter, engages in extensive conversations with other heroes at the Abbey, the game’s headquarters. These dialogues influence the light and dark balance points, affecting friendship levels. While integral to the narrative, the sheer volume of dialogue can become tedious, even for a self-proclaimed nerd and Marvel enthusiast like myself.2) Mandatory Day and Night Cycles: The game enforces night-time activities at the Abbey following each mission. While these free-roam tasks add variety, they quickly lose their charm after several repetitions. The routine of sleeping, researching, and engaging in activities before embarking on the next mission feels unnecessarily drawn out, detracting from the game’s pacing.Despite these critiques, my overall experience with “Marvel’s Midnight Suns” has been positive. The game’s strategic depth and stunning visuals have provided me with many enjoyable hours. I rate it a solid 7 out of 10, acknowledging that while it has room for improvement, it remains a commendable addition to any gamer’s collection.

_childDocuments_.review: Allow me to preface by saying Marvel's Midnight Suns is not for everyone. There's a Venn Diagram at play here; Midnight Suns' target demographic is the middle point between Marvel fans (a relatively big circle, but if you're only familiar with the movies there's a good chance a few members of the cast will leave you cold), fans of card games, and fans of self-insert fanfiction.Having said that, I'm speaking from the viewpoint of somebody who resides squarely in the middle of that Venn Diagram. I grew up on Marvel Comics even before the movies came out, and mercifully knew who Magick and Sister Grimm were before encountering them here. I play a lot of Magic: the Gathering, so the card battler system wasn't too hard to grasp; and I've written myself into more preestablished IPs than I care to admit. Thus, MMS scratches my video game itch like few other titles, and I've sunk WAY more time into it than I would most other games of it's sort (Slay the Spire, Fire Emblem Three Houses, and XCOM come to mind, all of which are excellent in their own way, but none of which I've played nearly as often).Midnight Suns does a lot of stuff right. I could easily have seen this made into a shoddy live-service game like Marvel's last attempt at gracing the world of Triple-A gaming with their flagship team of superheroes, but fortunately, once you've paid for MMS, you own the whole thing (barring a few DLC characters, which I will discuss momentarily). You get the chance to have unique hangouts with basically every character; Magick has an entire side quest dedicated to her birthday, and the three extracurriculars you can participate in (EMO KIDS, Shop Class, and Book Club) give you a chance to get to know many characters.Having said that, it's clear some characters get more love than others. I'm not sure why the creators are so obsessed with Magick; I don't dislike her, it's just obvious that she gets way more development in this game than some others I could Wolverine-I-mean-mention. Maybe it's because her relatively few appearances have made her character more malleable? ...But come on, it's clear Midnight Suns is working off it's own canon here. No reason to force every character to act like themselves. I'm pretty sure Blade and Captain Marvel have never even met in Marvel canon, and a minor plot point is hooking the two of them up in this game!Or perhaps the issue is the heavy focus on our main protagonist. Not that I'm against characterizing your protagonist; far from it. I find Hunter far more compelling than most of those silent-protagonist-types you see in video games, where the player is meant to project themselves onto them. That said, the characterization we do get comes off as somewhat Mary-Sue-y at times; Hunter's struggle with their inner light and darkness feels somewhat forced when I can't really think of a compelling reason they would be tempted to the dark side. And a lot of their stuff can get in the way of other characters; I would've loved for the EMO KIDS to have an internal conflict a la Shop Class, but all their meetings are focused around flashbacks of Hunter's last experience fighting their mom, leaving little room for interpersonal drama. The most we get is Magick snarking at Dr. Strange once or twice. And Book Club is just... so boring. Feels like an afterthought. Shouldn't Blade, Captain Marvel, Wolverine, and Captain America have started, I dunno, a bodybuilding club? Those guys are all RIPPED in this game!As for the gameplay, it's a lot of fun, for the most part. I don't SUPER love the card system, just because it puts a notable limit on our heroes' capabilities, especially when many key powers are locked off until postgame; why Blade's most reliable way of inflicting Bleed (the status effect all his other cards rely on) must be locked until you reach Relationship Level 5 with him, I have no idea, nor why the same must be said for Ghost Rider's Penance Stare. Either way, you're limited in what you can do by what cards you draw, which is fine, but it can be somewhat prohibitive at times if you only draw Hero cards but don't have any Heroism to fuel their use.Some cards feel better than others, which is frustrating; the pool is limited enough as-is, we don't need to further dilute it with suboptimal decisions! One I especially have trouble with is Scarlet Witch's No More, her capstone Legendary card that kills her whenever she uses it. There's no way that I've found to circumvent it, it's just "Immediately Kill Self: the Card." A few others I don't love are Dr. Strange's power that replenishes used items (potentially good on harder levels when items are actually necessary) and Deadpool's "Party Pinata" that deals a hilariously piddly amount of damage.Which might as well transition us to the DLC characters. At time of writing, there are two DLC characters out: Deadpool and Venom. Two more are promised, Storm and Morbius, both of which I expect to finish the "vampyres" subplot our first two players introduced. I'm enjoying playing with Wade Wilson and Eddie Brock (although Wade's kit seems eclectic and disjointed, with multiple dead cards that I don't much care for), but they're tangibly... well, tangential. Feels like the devs didn't really do enough to integrate them into the world, and seeing them awkwardly standing around and saying nothing during cutscenes kind of takes me out of the experience. Just add a few more cutscenes where Wade hangs out with somebody other than Blade, and Eddy talks to someone who isn't Peter, and I'll forgive it.Finally, I'd like to reiterate that these are mostly minor points, coming from a place of love, and I do LOVE this game. Like, a LOT. Should the devs happen upon this review, know that I really appreciate all your hard work, and had more fun with this game than I've had with any game since XCOM 2! I also have a list of characters I'd like to see in the sequel, if the sunk cost fallacy will keep you reading until the end: The Black Knight, Polaris, Quicksilver, Jean Grey, Dr. Doom, and Emma Frost.

_childDocuments_.review: Big fan of both Firaxis and strategy/tactics games, casual Marvel fan.A fun and novel mix of deck-building and turn-based combat. Each hero has some unique traits and cards that allow for some satisfying plays when comboed correctly. Hero decks are a mixture of basic attacks, buffing or debuffing, and heroic abilities. Heroes and their decks are fairly balanced though a few heroes are a bit stronger overall (ex. Spiderman and Magik) while others are underwhelming at times (ex. Captain Marvel and Nico). Still no hero is useless and it can be fun to try out different team compositions & decks as you continually hone your strategies. New cards and combos are unlocked as you progress through the game which has you revising each hero’s deck. Cards can also be enhanced and altered to an extent to customize each hero’s deck further.Missions alternate between story missions with cutscenes and standard missions that jump right into battle with a singular objective; the latter being the more grindy part of the game, but this can be kept to a minimum if you do not want to unlock all cosmetics. Non-story missions are varied enough that they do feel overly repetitive unless you have exhausted all story missions. The grid system found in most tactical strategy games is abandoned for a more open field allowing for more fluid positioning when making your plays. Difficulty can be easily adjusted if you are having trouble or if you want a greater challenge without having to start a new game. Additionally, each turn allows a movement and items as free actions as well as a number of redraws to even out bad luck with your hand for the turn.Down-time between mission activities is a mix of resource management, exploration, research, and socializing with your team members to further your character’s relationship with them. This is a nice breath of fresh air at first but can become quite tedious at times and requires an above average amount of tutorials. Exploring the abbey and doing a host of side fetch quest feels largely like padding. The hero relationship & conversation pieces are very light and wholly plutonic so do not expect any romance scenes or Bioware-esque dialogue trees.Fairly engaging narrative despite the generic “big bad has returned to destroy/enslave the world” plot with some surprise twists. There is witty dialogue in both the game and from the characters that will likely make you chuckle. Characters all have some endearing traits though there are few times they can come off as annoying. Dramatic moments are appropriately spaced and add tension without overwhelming the plot. There is sometimes a bit of a mood whiplash though when the high stakes moments are proceeded by the routine downtime activities.It should be noted that this game does not take place within the Marvel Cinematic Universe.The game hosts a variety of different environments for field missions which all have some unique flavor. Battle animations and effects are colorful and engaging. Character designs are a mixed bag with some interesting takes and some very dull ones, but you can purchase other options to suit your tastes and will likely find a look for each character you can enjoy.  Remarkable soundtrack in most cases especially the battle themes, ‘A Night at the Carnival’ was my personal favorite. Voice acting and sound effects are well done overall with no glaring weaknesses.A bit light on the content for what you get which is a new character and 3 two-part story missions for each DLC plus a final mission if you have all 4 DLC characters. Recommended if you get it discounted.Fairly mild, most of the replay value comes from trying out a different voiced version of the player character, dialogue options, and deck strategy for your character assuming you did not try all the possible combinations in your first playthrough.Heroes that are just 3rd wheels to other characters’ plot missions all use generic battle posing (ex. Standing with fists clenched) during cutscenes instead of displaying their powers which is a bit jarring in some cases. = Strongly Recommend

_childDocuments_.review: Midnight Suns is a great game if you are a Marvel fan. I originally played it for Dr Strange and Scarlet Witch, but I started to learn more and grow fond of the Midnight Suns as well. It's fun to hang out with your favourite superheroes, and not to mention, to fight with them. As an avid fan of card games, I really enjoyed building the decks and seeing how I could play out the cards in my hand and build great combos. The story started to draw me in in the middle-ish of the story (explore the grounds! The lore is so interesting), but the combat is what makes this game good. I think it's a must play for Marvel fans. Also, if you like XCOM there are some similarities, but don't expect to get the same sense of urgency that you did in XCOM.

Still, highly iconic characters such as Iron Man, Dr. Stranger or Spider-man are available in the early phases of the game so that you will feel at home.This game is a win if you like RPG, spend time running here and there to improve your characters and if you love the Marvel universe as much as I do.

_childDocuments_.review: 2.5 hours in (initial impressions)Game itself is amazing, especially if you're a marvel comics fan with all the nods and references to the characters and happenings in the universe that's never or barely brought up in the MCU.A few of the downsides:-MTX sucks for those that want the skins, but at the end of the day they're optional and don't really have any sort of impact on the core game.-Launcher within a launcher because 2K (there's a workaround)-Denuvo82 hours in and finished the main campaignFavorite Marvel game of all time. Firaxis did not disappoint. Gameplay is very fun, hub world and characters are also very enjoyable. There are a few bugs here and there, cutscenes can also feel like a whiplash during transitions.Overall you can tell the team put some heart into this title, and it may be one of the most underrated Marvel title.If you like entertaining though not necessarily deep writing that features Marvel characters along with RPG, Deck, and Team building gameplay then this is 100% a must buy.Highly recommended to turn RTX off for stable FPS.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a good, solid B. 4 stars. 8/10.The strategy card game, the meat, is a lot of fun, but it's a bit rough and unbalanced. This game would be so much better if they expanded, tuned, and polished the cards and the combat instead of spending all the development resources they did on the other two major parts.Exploring the Abbey is enjoyable enough, but the rewards are lackluster and once you get all the words, there's not a lot of incentive to keep exploring. The best use for the arcane chests is just to search them out when you dip beneath 50 credits to find enough to do daily sparring. Exploration isn't bad, but it's unnecessary given that they could have spent the time and resources on the meat of the game to make it better.The dating sim part of the game is the bad part. Midnight Suns unironically does what South Park: Fractured but Whole did satirically (and better). The dialogue trees are rudimentary. The dialogue is bland and repetitive, and there's way too much of it. It wouldn't be so bad, but the "social" system is both the method for upgrading the PC's stats and unlocking the Legendary card for all of the heroes. It's not skippable.I hope this game gets a sequel, and I hope it focuses on the card variety, the deck building, and the combat. Midnight Suns has the potential to be as big as XCOM if they focus it up.

_childDocuments_.review: Some time in, I am REALLY liking this game. The story is neat, the writing is clever (I think it's pretty funny and there is some subtle humor on top of the constant quips), the card combat system is engaging, combat is fun, the animations are good, and the mix of combat and get-to-know-the-team encounters is pretty good.Some negatives would be, so far, the game stutters quite a bit. It doesn't hold a constant framerate. It dips from 60 down to 25 at times. Several hitches. It's not a dealbreaker, and I am sure it'll be patched or cease once Denuvo is taken away, but it is annoying. Lots of characters to get to know. Lots of unique ways to pass through combat. Cool environmental interactions in combat. So far, just a really fun time.

_childDocuments_.review: Buy this game if you want a simple yet high budget turn based tactics with meta progression, or if you really like the Marvel stuff.Do not buy it if you hate the late Marvel with its cheesy jokes and overall silliness. Also do not buy if you’re looking for XCOM with superheroes – even though the gameplay loop is a bit similar, the Midnight Suns contains so many dialogues and side activities that they usually take more time than the combat. And the tactical combat itself has nothing in common with XCOM - if you need a comparison it’s more like a SteamWorld Quest with emphasis on arena positioning.The game is not simple to love. The dialogues sometimes are pure cringe. There’s not a single drop of blood even from Wolverine's or Deadpool's cuts. The story sometimes tries to be serious, but then in a minute a villain start to throw phrases like “You came for your doom, heroes!” or “I eat heroes like you for breakfast!” and it all starting to feel like I'm watching a morning cartoon for kids.And yet the amount of content is big, the characters are mostly likable, the presentation is very high level for this genre, and the gameplay loop is satisfying. Considering how it already has good discounts on sale it might be worth to pick it up along with all the DLCs.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a Marvel fan this is a must buy. Loved my time with it!Pros:- The Marvel characters are done really well in combat and feel true to the hero (the same cant be said out of combat unfortunately). With Wolverine for example you make use of his intense bloodthirsty rampaging style and healing factor. All characters for the most part feel authentic, the only one who sadly was underwhelming was Scarlet Witch as she should be a real badass chaos queen but she's really terrible in battle in this game. Every other hero were great in their own right. - The idea of a card based strategy system at first was off putting for me but I gave it a go nonetheless and its actually really fun and satisfying. If you're hesitant on the combat side of things of this game, don't be! Its executed perfectly and gives a good sense of variety in every battle and you never feel like you are out of options. In short, the combat, amazing!Cons:- Everything else outside the combat/battles is bearable at best. I ended up skim/skip reading the dialogue. The characters sadly are so dumbed down and there are some terrible cringy lines. The entire side of the game where you are not in combat feels like an absolute chore! Building relationships can get tedious but you feel compelled to push through it to be stronger in battle.- Beware of stability. The game crashed on me multiple times and was very frustrating. At times I couldn't even load up where I left off and I was blocked out of playing the game. Luckily loading a slightly earlier save would resolve this but I really shouldn't have to be doing this. The frames also were a joke. I've been a PlayStation user most of my life and so only recently made the switch to PC. The crashes and performance of this game honestly made me wish at times I had just played this on console instead. First game on PC that made me feel that (granted I haven't played too many as of yet).Overall I WOULD recommend this if you're a Marvel fan, if not it's still worth a try for the combat alone. Despite the cons the gameplay was really fun and had me hooked.7/10 game for me. Way better than the trash that was Marvel's Avengers lol

_childDocuments_.review: I had no interest in this game because I thought it was another "AAA" game. Assuming it had the usual glamour of a pig with makeup on. Waited a few years bought it on sale with all the dlc for really cheap. First AAA game ive bought in years and got what I expected. The anti cheat system the game has causes the game to run poorly in some instances in your home base (even with a 4080/i7) and at low. The anti cheat system causes your pc to work extra hard so make sure your cooling is at least decent. Even at medium settings your pc will blast an oven of air out trying to keep up. That is the only complain. Its a shame too, because the game is extremely fun and engaging. The little side stories with the heroes are a neat little touch too. This is a prime example of a AAA publisher sticking their hands in the cookie jar in their race to the bottom. Get the game on sale, and enjoy the game for what it is. Full price though, please go support an indie dev.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really surprised by how much I enjoyed this game. I wasn't expecting to like it so much, but it was tailored to my interests in Marvel characters, card games, and turn-based tactical gameplay. However, this game isn't for everyone. A significant portion of it involves poorly written dialogue and interactions with characters that can be tedious, even for someone like me who generally enjoys these characters and has a sense of nostalgia for them.You can skip the social aspect of the game, but it's important to note that making friends with other characters is crucial for combat purposes. If you choose to do this, you'll likely find yourself frequently hitting the escape key to skip dialogue. It's also possible to mostly skip the talking and just focus on missions.I suspect that the New Game+ mode will be more enjoyable once DLC is released, but it's difficult to say at this time. My 100% playthrough took 84 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this title on sale on the strength of the positive reviews (especially on RPS) and the Firaxis name. I am very glad I did. Gameplay-wise, while it can legitimately be described as having bits of XCOM, Monster Train, and Stardew Valley in it that gives exactly the wrong impression - this is not a pastiche of other games' systems with a big IP name pasted on. It's an original. Also worthy of mention is that it's completely non-twitchy; while it uses the current video versions of the classic heroes, it is much more like reading than watching a movie.

_childDocuments_.review: Huge fan of this game. The combat's really fun and the story elements are great. If you like X-COM, Marvel and keen on a game with some chunky narrative, this ones for you. There's an old school BioWare-esque style that flows through the story-telling.  It's not always perfect and there are areas the story is shallow (the relationship with your team elements can sometimes feel a bit gamified), but it's a genuinely fun romp, with some great moments and characters, as well as a pretty decent narrative overall.. I honestly feel this game is criminally under-rated. It really deserves a sequel. It's nice to play a game that does take a few risks, it doesn't always land, but I love how unique it feels, the ideas and story are a real nice change from a lot of modern games, reminds me of how games used to be 5 or 10 years ago, when there was somewhat of a soul to game creation and story crafting, which is often lacking in 'most' (not all) triple A game studios.Would love to see the developers return to this series.

_childDocuments_.review: This game takes the best mechanics from some of my favorite games and ties them together quite well. Xcom (obviously - same company) - research perks, bosses that move on your turnChimera Squad - immediate battle. Small arena. Enemy intentionsStardew Valley - Meaningful relationships. gift givingSlay the Spire - Altering cardsDragon age - Hero and home customization (I know they aren't the first to do this but it feels similar)They stay true to the characters. Voice acting is top notch. I usually find skin changes pointless but they feel so satisfying in this game with all their animations and cut scenes. Story is interesting so far. I like the grind.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't go into this game expecting a heavy focus on combat. That is, while combat is a significant part of the game, it's maaaaaaybe 35-40% of the whole experience. _childDocuments_.review: The TL/DR is simple. Play this game. It's excellent and well WELL worth your time.For more depth buckle up.I'll start by saying that  Firaxis as developer seem  incapable of doing the same thing. Each game brings something different. It's iteration but not just layering on mechanics. It's trying different things and I really respect that. Chimera Squad is different to XCOM2 and Midnight Suns )MS) is quite different from both of the others.Things I liked (or loved!)Story:Many of the reviews have said that the gameplay for MS is excellent but the stuff at the Abbey gets tedious and is uninteresting. This is more subjective, but I enjoyed the story and the social systems. The story is pretty cheesy but it's a comic book game. I feel like cheese is what they needed here. And not every game has to be deep like Last of Us.I like all the MS characters and enjoyed spending time with them and I enjoyed the conversations on Superlink, I laughed at more than a few of the comments. The game has a great sense of humour. Also I think it pays off in a very satisfying manner at the end.Music:The best compliment I can pay the soundtrack is to say that you could swap out the music here into any of Marvel's movies and it would work. Swap out the main theme from MS into that scene in The Avengers where they finally 'assemble' it would work just as well.Visual Style: I love the way this game looks. The environments are interesting. The costume character models are great the super powers feel appropriately powerful. It works well together.Special mention for the designs of the Lilin. They are quite striking. I also really love the animations for the enemy that splits itself or other Lilin. Those animations are really cool.Combat:The meat of the game, and it is well prepared. The card system is interesting and well-balanced. The interplay of generating heroism and spending it is compelling.What I find particularly interesting is how the game makes you feel like you are controlling super heroes by playing well. Let me explain. On the surface playing 3 cards per turn doesn't really feel satisfying. But when you start using quick abilities, the environmental hazards etc you get a lot more out of those 3 card plays, and you start to feel like your team of heroes are....well super heroes.Beyond that is how well the game balances that satisfaction to do better and improve with making it faijrly easy to get into. We need to bear in mind that this a Marvel game. People are going to find MS who haven't played an XCOM game before.I think they did a good job with that.Dislikes/Issues (heh, issues!)All that said, it's not all sunshine and roses. There are a few things I'd like to see improved/worked on.Performance/Bugs:I did come across a few bugs during my time. One where in a mission I'd set up a hero with 'counter' but it wasn't triggering. I had the game crash on me once and had to restart my PC.Also the game looks good but it shouldn't perform as badly as it does. I shouldn't be getting the frame drops I got here and there. All in all the performance was less stable than I prefer.Quality of Life:In MS you can edit the decks for you heroes, forge cards, upgrade cards and apply mods to cards. Most of which are done on different screens and in different sections of the Abbey.I'd had to walk back and forth a few times to different zones to fully construct a deck. It got frustrating.Everything really should be accessible from one screen. And with a better UI, the deck editing screen isn't all that great. In spite of those minor flaws I obviously strongly recommend MS. I had a great time with it and if I had played it in 2022 it would have been neck-and-neck with GoW Ragnarok for my game of the year. (I didn't play enough of Elden Ring to consider it, don't 'at' me.)

_childDocuments_.review: Purchased the game for $40. In today's market I'll rarely pay more than $40 for a game and  when trying to balance gaming gold versus computer crap, I usually wait until I read some reviews before purchasing. The game does have some similarity to X-COM, made by the same company, looks like a similar graphics engine.What I like: - Marvel heroes.- Card deck developing combos and strategies.- Decently written scripts with the ability to bypass dialogue.- Variety of heroes and when some new heroes are added.What I dislike- Combat gets repetitive.- The pre and post sleep cut scenes.- Running around to the same four rooms everyday.- Some of the heroes abilities seem similar enough to not warrant using some heroes.- Not being able to access the game after an update for 3+ days.Game is around a 7 or 8 out 10 depending on how much you like marvel.Currently I'm unsure if new purchasers can play the game as the installation since the newest dlc uses a desktop exe path that doesn't work (at least on my computer). _childDocuments_.review: If you want to be the Superhero in an epic story, then this is the game for you! This turn-based card battler and strategy game is engaging, rewarding and beautiful. Being a strategy game, every move you make could be the one that wins you the game or the one that seals your defeat. You must manage enemy attacks and your own skills and abilities if you hope to survive. Utilize your environment and your heroes strengths and cover their weaknesses with the heroes your choose to bring to each fight. Discover the history of the Abbey, the home base of the heroes. Save the planet from the mystic Lilith and her hordes of the damned! Hero choice determines playstyle and you are under no real obligation to play all of the characters if you dont like them. Having said that, I found a place for everyone on my team and enjoyed what they brought to the table.  This was my first true strategy game (I've played card battlers) so I didn't know what to expect but I found myself satisfied at every turn. I give this game a 9.0Pros:Mind over RNG (your choices will make the game's mechanics work in your favor)Hero selection matters and each feels differentArtwork/Graphics/Animations all made each ability feel goodStoryline is engagingMusic is on pointCustomization options for those unsatisfied with the base modelsVoice Acting made every character come to lifeCons:Glitches and hangs... My Radeon program and AMD 6600 had issues with certain scenes in the game, sometimes repeatedly. But no lost saves, so thats good!

_childDocuments_.review: Marvel farming simulator.The Bad:Starting off, this game has a very rough and unenjoyable tutorial that last for hours. Only 27.8% of people who own this game have finished Chapter 1 and that implies a huge underlying issue with the overall pacing. Story-wise its nothing you haven't seen before, worsened by dull and boring dialogue deliveries outside missions that take up at least half of the game. The weird and out-of-place world-exploring part serves two purposes: 1. through character and world interactions, you get extra lore contents that only further confuses and complicates the general plot.2. getting materials for upgrades and crafting. When I said this game is a farming simulator, it literally makes you walk around in a country collecting mushrooms and plants for crafting heal consumables. There are items which take 20+ ingredients that you can only pick up 2 per spot.And not to mention this game has micro-transactions for buying cosmetics. In a single-player card game. Unreal.-------------------The Fun (?):This game is made for a very specific group of target audiences, that is at least somewhat interested in the Marvel IP, and a fan of the tactical/strategy layers found in similar games like XCOM and Fights in Tight Spaces. You won't be here for long if you are lacking in any of those two aspects. Gameplay-wise for the card system, mechanics, and missions, they are somewhat solid, not much to complain about. You need to do little grindings for upgrades but its acceptable. One interesting feature is the difficulty system that if you perform well-enough or eventually completed set amounts of missions, you can freely choose to increase the difficulty or stay at where it is. With higher difficulty, apart from stronger enemies, you also get more experiences and rewards so the incentive is appreciated. Then again, at the start of game you can only go for the preset normal or lower difficulties, so it might feel underwhelming at first, but it quickly scales up fast.Oh and last word, I gotta emphasize again don't get this simply because you enjoyed Marvel or XCOM, it has no power here.

_childDocuments_.review: It isn't Marvel XCOM at all, but it's still Firaxis. I'd say it's a beefy, story driven adaptation of the CCG tabletop game Marvel Champions, if you're familiar with that. You have a team, you play cards, and you have to maximize synergy and positioning to win. There's a very satisfying flow and rhythm to it once you learn each hero. The story is more comic book than MCU movie, the conversation/friendship mechanic makes you feel invested, and the drip of customization and upgrade systems being introduced to you feels a bit slow but fine if you just let the story play out. I kinda feel like customizing your hero could have gone a bit deeper, and maybe that will change the further I get into the game but being locked into generic dual wield sword person feels kinda cheap. Final thoughts, it's as addictive as XCOM which is really all that matters but now I kinda do want a video game adaptation of Marvel Champions.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game. I love Marvel. I love Xcom. I hate Card games. I love Persona. I love this game. Despite not being a big fan of card games or deck building, and being very suspicious of the whole random cards per turn thing, I quickly fell in love with this game. There are flaws, some of which I hope will be fixed in patches, others that are disappointing but not gameplay relevant. - Gameplay: fun and easy to understand. Exciting battles, fast paced, and so far challenging on Normal difficulty. - Story: your typical marvel comics story. Good villains, good teammates. Decent but not earth shattering. - Dialogue: I love it, I laugh a lot at it in a positive way. It reminds me of comic book writing. This is a bunch of super heroes having fun and making fun of each other. - Graphics: hit and miss. Some characters are decent, others are quite poor. Main character for example has a much nicer model than Iron Man who really does look like an average Sims character. In game abilities and animations are great though and you really feel the impact of your powers.- Voice acting: good overall. I would say that those that I dislike the most are characters that are very present in the MCU. When you compare this Iron Man to Robert Downey Jr, it is a negative. On the other hand, Blade and Nico are quite good IMO- Sound effects: satisfying, good.- DLC/Microtransactions: you can get in game currency for some of them. You can ignore the rest. Not even slightly annoying in my mind. Plenty of in game stuff to unlock through gameplay. This is not pay to win. Comments about the game being SJW or woke: sorry, I do not see it at all. This is just normal every day Marvel comics stuff since the 1960s.

_childDocuments_.review: As a lover of the XCOM series, and Marvel Comics, I was excited to see how this played out.I'm just a bit in, 3rd mission past the tutorial but I like it  a lot. Even on a SSD and powerful PC, there is slowdowns on loading and sync issues with mouths/dialogues.2-There is a LOT of dialogue. It's great stuff but wow, so far, I've spent far more time listening to and talking to people then anything else.  I hope it starts to pick up.  I'll still enjoy it if not but I want to have some more action.Overall though, a really fun game.Update; I've completed the game several times now and still really enjoy it.  Yes, the weaknesses I mentioned before are there but it's not enough to detract from the enjoyable gameplay. _childDocuments_.review: I actually really liked this game, it does have its flaws but overall, it's a really quality XCOM-esque game with a card battle system and heavy cinematic cutscenes. However I did end up finding myself growing a little tired and antsy after a while due to how long some of the dialogue could drag on with talking to the heroes after every mission. Which is strange because I'm usually the type of guy who really loves to enjoy the story in games and strive to take my time talking to every NPC and whatnot.I think it's because the actual gameplay is super fun, like seriously, it's really satisfying having to balance your heroes card deck and then deciding what to do in any given encounter with the luck of the draw.But the cutscenes, while decent, can feel quite robotic and clunky at times, and the third person segment of being able to walk around your headquarters was interesting and fun at first, it quickly became quite tedious and boring in comparison. Especially since it felt very half-baked with the way the character moved through the environment, something just didn't quite feel right during those exploration segments to me.I'm sad the game didn't do as well as it deserved and apparently ended up being a commercial failure. But honestly, I can kinda' see why, like it must have cost a lot of money developing all of these fully voiced cinematic cutscenes, and they had a lot of high profile voice actors in the industry.I personally think it would'be been fine to have created a more visual-novel method for all of the hanging out with the heroes in-bewteen missions and keeping the cinematics for the heavy story segments.After playing this game, and I would love more of this type, it was really, really fun, despite still having some performance issues and the flaws I've mentioned and more.I would love an X-Men themed game like this, personally.

_childDocuments_.review: Free weekend review: I actually really enjoy this game, but I gotta be honest that it's definitely not for everyone, which is why I'm not recommending this game. The gameplay seems so niche, like a weird mix between XCOM Chimera Squad and Slay the Spire with more than a bit of Persona 5 social links added into the mix. If that sounds like something you'd like then I'd say give it a go, but wait for a sale because even though I like it I wouldn't pay full price for it. There's just too many things that are "off" for it to be worth 60 euro. I'll try to get into some of it.The combat is interesting, but kind of outstays its welcome by adding a wave or two too many enemies into every battle. I feel like they could have added a more interesting way of balancing out combat than to just add 2 or 3 weak enemies every turn.The "good stuff" in this game is the heroes interacting with one another and most of this happens back at the abbey that serves as your base. While most of the dialogue and friendship boosting seems like it'd work better for an X-Men game taking place at the X Mansion it's still fun here, even if it seems like it's not really in style with many of the characters. The writing is well done though, which means that the characters themselves will often point out that normally they'd probably not go painting in the woods with you.The voice acting is.... Decent, I guess. There's some characters that maybe could have used a better actor or a couple more takes for their lines at the very least. Just as an example I started the game out with the Male Hunter as my main character, but decided I'd rather start over with the Female Hunter since the male version was just Matt Mercer speaking with his normal voice and that broke immersion a bit for me when I know that it's him I guess.After playing a good chunk of the game as female though I wish I had stuck with Mercer, since the directing they gave the female voice actor must have been "Can you sound bored and confused at the same time?"She honestly sounds like she could do just fine if they let her go with a more natural voice, which is a shame.Now for the thing I hate the most in the game: Currencies! There's like at least a dozen different currencies you have to keep track of and the game does a poor job of explaining how you earn some of it (Knowledge for example), what it'll do and how much you have, while other currencies can be found in your inventory with a tooltip for where to earn it and spend it. Mix this with a Mortal Kombat Krypt-like island that you are meant to go and explore now and then and you'll likely be very confused about what you are meant to be gathering for the game and what you are just gathering for the sake of a lore dump. I'll admit that they do have some good lore in here, but the way it is presented could definitely have been handled better.Now to wrap back around, there's enough of this that I can tolerate and enjoy, so this is a great game for me. Others however, might find it very niche and intimidating to get started on, especially if they only know marvel from the MCU.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is quite addicting! I have personally never been able to enjoy turn-based combat, it just never clicked for me. Midnight Suns' combat is very accessible and the attack animations look amazing, plus you can use the environment by slamming enemies into objects for extra damage. There is a LOT of extra exploring, talking with teammates, leveling up abilities, crafting. etc. and I LOVE every bit of it. I am the kind of player who talks to every single crew mate in Mass Effect between missions, so this side of the gameplay suits me well. I can understand how some players may be put off by it, but for me it's perfect.There is a lot to learn, but I feel the game gives you new things at a good pace. It has a fantastic "day" mechanic where you sleep to start the next day, then each day you can explore, visit your craft stations, and run a mission when you feel like it. After a mission, it's usually evening and other social activities may trigger, then that's about it until the next day. What I like about this system is that, unlike something like AC: Valhalla, you never feel overwhelmed by the amount of stuff to do. There's only so much you CAN do, until you yourself decide to sleep and advance the clock. The RPG elements are fun, working on the card decks for each hero is fun, it's just an excellent package. You can choose the combat costumes and the off-duty costumes for your character and for each hero, and you unlock a ton of them during gameplay. There is even a light/dark mechanic for the player character, that changes the abilities available to you. I am very glad I decided to try this game, I'm looking forward to playing for many more hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Innovative Combat: It's not your typical turn-based game. The card system adds a layer of strategy and surprise, keeping things fresh with each hero's unique deck. Plus, the environment itself becomes a tactical tool.Compelling Characters: From iconic heroes to intriguing newcomers, the cast boasts distinct combat styles and engaging personalities. You'll find yourself attached to your squad.Underrated Mechanics: Don't be fooled by the cards! The system is surprisingly deep and rewarding, offering strategic decisions and satisfying combos.Overly Long Campaign: The story stretches a bit thin, and some potentially interesting plot points fall flat. Be prepared for a marathon, not a sprint.Midnight Suns might take a while to complete, but the innovative combat and well-developed characters make it a gem for strategy RPG fans.  The card-based system is surprisingly deep, adding a layer of strategy you won't find in typical turn-based games. So, if you're looking for a unique and rewarding experience, don't let the cards deter you -  Midnight Suns is definitely worth checking out.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm amazed at the effort they did for the dialogue and the voice acting. The VA for Spidey and Iron Man are awesome. I like Spidey a lot and was happy he gets to shine in this game. I like the gameplay. Even though I know it is not for everyone. Know which heroes to bring each mission, strategize and you will enjoy this game. You spend a lot talking to other marvel characters and upgrading cards. It is a plus for me since I'm a Marvel fan. Lastly the story was well crafted. It could really be made into an animated series and it could work. I can feel the love and time spent making this game and I hope fans would try it.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: It's good, it's fun. Playing this makes me imagine the developers coming up with ideas for this game and whoever was in charge just said yes to every one of them. There's XCOM elements but not quite, there's an RPG 3rd person exploratory story slice complete with jedi power wheel abilities and light/dark system, there's card game dynamics in the combat and a 'passing of each day' system like in XCOM, complete with a bedroom you can upgrade and adorn. The spaghetti they were throwing at the wall was very sticky that day and everything made it into the pot. All that said, its a very fun game and it runs fairly easily on my low to mid grade laptop. Also, there's a full metric ton of actual comic book references and lore drops to the great Marvel universe. Sometimes there is too much cut-scene dialogue, story shoveling but you can skip it easily and its not necessary, as the NPCs tell you frequently. The characters don't seem overly concerned with what's going on in the story, so you shouldn't either. It's a very satisfying Marvel game. Not a good turn based combat game like I was expecting at all. This is NOT Marvel XCOM. But maybe one fine day...
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: Under it's own merit, this game is definitely worth buying as a (in my opinion) superior and much more beginner friendly take on the XCom style of strategy game, though I'd wait for a sale to get the legendary edition for normal price to get all the skins without being price gouged. That said I can't in good conscience recommend the Steam version specifically. Between Denuvo (which is useless aside from them wanting to milk people for the skins) and the 2K Launcher tanking the performance randomly it can be unplayable at times. If you do buy the Steam version I recommend going into properties and bypassing the 2k Launcher entirely though you unfortunately still have to suffer from the Denuvo performance hits until they decide to patch it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: Another Revision:  If you do purchase, make sure to look up on the internet how to disable the 2K launcher.  Getting rid of that albatross has almost fixed all of the headaches.  What a boneheaded disaster.  This is the only game I've ever given serious consideration to refunding-- simply because of performance issues.  And to see that it is entirely because of some manky, publisher-demanded garbage, is just ridiculous.=======Original Review:  Almost unplayable.  Wait until they patch the performance issues, or wait until it's on a steep discount.Revision:   Now that there's been a patch, it performs better.  Still, needs more tuning, I suspect, but if you're a hardcore marvel or xcom fan, it'll scratch your itch.  Good writing, good voice acting, and once you catch on to how the cards work, that becomes smooth sailing as well.Enjoy.  But, realize, you may find technical trouble trying to play this one.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best game I have played in the past handful of years.  The strategy element is fluid.  It feels kind of easy once you get the hang of it but I thinks that's just a reward for spending the time mastering it.  The RPG elements running around the abbey grounds is an enjoyable small RPG.  The pacing is pretty good, I ended up getting my final levels of friendship about the same time as I hit the final mission.  The challenges for the special costumes were great.  I loved them.  If you are a new player my best advice is don't worry about upgrading cards and currency farming.  It all comes pretty naturally if you just play the game!

_childDocuments_.review: Update after 35 hours: every criticism I levied at the game bellow the dashed line after 7 hours of play is still true. That said, the game does get better, the ability crafting and upgrade system is quite complex and varied, and the encounters become addictive. Plus the game is long, I still don't have the end in sight, another play area opened just recently, and new enemy types. I expected to fight hydra soldiers all the way to the end, this changes things up, and makes combat more varied, especially since the new and old enemy types can mix. Even the writing gets better, not great still, but at least I no longer cringe at every spoken line. Maybe I just got used to it? No, it's definitely better.I really hate that steam only has positive and negative reviews with  zero granuality, I don't want to outright change my review from negative to positive, but I no longer hate the game as much as I initially did.---------------------------------------I don't understand how this game gets positive reviews. It is unacceptable by any standards.1. The graphics is straight up XCOM Chimera Squad, it is patently obvious they simply re-purposed the engine with barely any improvements. The RTX effects kill FPS while managing to not show any noticeable graphical difference.2. The story and dialogue writing is gibberish. It's the, high school fantasy of the uncool kids who were never invited to parties, so they wrote this game to live out their unfulfilled college/HS dreams of being in the cool kids club. But their idea of the cool kids club is callled "The EMO kids club" and I wish I was joking. The story and dialogue is written by people who do not understand or respect the material. It is gibberish to them, and so they think if they write their own gibberish, nobody would notice the difference.3. The game hates legacy Marvel characters but especially Tony Stark, they are nerfed and treated like dirt, except for captain marvel and blade. I bet the writers didn't see 1998 "toxic" blade, otherwise they'd hate him too. 4. The game is saddled with a TPS RPG like exploration area, that you must participate in. And socialize with the characters. It is not optional. Many powerups and abilities are only gained by befriending these utterly unlikeable poorly written characters. 5. The only passable part of the game are the actual encounters, but even this plays like a mobile game rather than a proper PC strategy game. Your options are limited, even more so than in Chimera Squad. If this is the trend, Firaxis's next game will be as complex as pong. This game is worth $20 at best, after they  release the patch to completely turn off the socialization part. It FREAKING has a built in version of TWITTER for crying out loud.
