_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely love this game. The combat is very engaging to me the higher you start to take the difficulty.  I have always been a big fan of RTS, card games, persona style games etc. This feels like a perfect combination of the games all in one. Yes it does have it's bugs, to be fair. Minor glitching in my experience. The occasion crash, however that has only happened when i'm trying to do other things on my computer while playing the game. Graphics in combat are great. Cut scenes do look a little grainy but something I can easily overlook.  If you like games like xcom, slay the spire and persona, this game will be perfect for you as it is their love child. If you don't, I'd still suggest checking it out.Story line wise, it does play out like your typical MCU story as an overall. The different friendships you get to do with the characters and getting some more insight to them as a character is really nice. Has a lot of comic book reference. This game is also jam packed with an all start line up of voice actors.  You can tell there was a lot of time and care and love put into this game.The only aspect I do not enjoy doing is the abby exploration. The very first time you do it, if you care about lore, is wonderful. On other play through after, it feels more like a chore than anything.  Speaking of play through, there is NG+.  I very much enjoy the way they did it. All friendhships carry over and champion levels carry over as well. On NG+ you start back with just the base decks and do have to re-earn everything but it creates the chance for you to come up with your own challenges to test your skills plus the higher difficulties. Example being, doing a NG+ on Ultimate 3 with no quick play card use after the first 4 story missions (you ALMOST have to use them until you start to get cards). Gives you the freedom to have your own challenge.All in all, I 100% recommend playing this game. I've sunk I don't know how many hours into between PS5 and then switched to PC.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: I am a huge fan of this game. I really like the most of the characters chosen, and I think all are written to match their comic counterparts while also giving (at least most of them) a compelling individual narrative and story throughout the main campaign. The light social aspects of this game may not appeal to everyone, but if you're a Marvel fan you'll definitely find things to enjoy here. While the card based combat didn't sound initially appealing to me, I really came to love the way it worked and creating decks and improving them for each character as the game went on. It added a lot of strategy and nuance to what could have been a more generic action game. The enemy and encounter types add a decent bit of variety, but if you try to grind out maximum friendship and experience with all characters it will probably start to feel a little stale. This game is definitely worth playing all the way through and I really hope we get another game like this from Firaxis in the future, even if it's not a direct sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic strategy game. Has time management/visual novel elements in the base reminiscent of recent Fire Emblem and Persona games but less tedious, and well-tuned card based combat to boot. Fun for Marvel fans and normies alike-- the cast of characters in Midnight Suns are likable, varied, and unique. Highly recommended for strategy fans both expert and casual, this game is pretty easy to pick up but hard to master to its fullest.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: It's more like Dragon Age than XCom, with in-depth dialog options for all the characters. The lack of a romance option is a bit missed, but it would not work in the Marvel universe with the existing stories so it's understandable. The combat is excellent with many options every turn to optimize your strategy. On the more negative side, the exploration doesn't feel like it has a great payoff, and it's gosh darn long - so much character dialog to go through! I thoroughly enjoyed it as a fan of RPGs and Marvel (a little) and recommend it, but recognize it's not going to be for everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a comic book brought to life on the skeleton of XCOM. The storylines and acting are superb (though you could play a drinking game with the word "spooky"... ). Graphics are stupendous, and the action comic-booky. Love hat they brought the actor from the Runaways TV series to voice Nico (Lyrica Okano). You can see where XCOM inspired things, but this is an evolution. The appey is your base, fully upgradeable, yoursoldiers are the heroes you find along the way, all with so much more personality than the grunts you throw into the XCOM meat grinder.... more like the Chimera Squad folks than the XCOM 1 or 2 soldiers, I guess. You can play around with outfits, pet dogs and cats ("cats"), and complete missions on your own timeline.You feel overpowered at times, but if you aren't careful you can become overwhelmed in battles.  The tutorial is in-depth and the missions that ramp you up to the main gameplay are fun and informative. During the battles, you literally have to play your cards right. Card playing is the newest "big thing" in video games, and they pull it off here.The only problem, and it's a significant problem, is the 2K launcher on PC. If you launch the game from the launcher & don't use the workaround, the game is laggy, stuttering, and rubberbanding. I will link the thread that shows a workaround, but be warned: YOU WILL NEED TO COPY AND SAVE YOUR SAVE FILES ELSEWHERE, THEN PUT THEM BACK IN THE FOLDER AFTER FOLLOWING ALL THE STEPS. Otherwise, you may lose these files.

_childDocuments_.review: After purchasing the game I got through the tutorial mission without a hitch and even past the 1st mission. After that the game would not load into another mission, every time it would just freeze on the load screen. It allowed me to play just long enough not to get a refund for the game as the limit is 2 hours and I was at 4. So beware.The game itself I liked, the combat is fun and the animations were also fun. The character creator was pretty limited though and the characters themselves look like action figures. The story seemed fine from what I go to see of it. My issues with the game freezing happened on both my laptop and steam deck. Cannot recommend on the game not working but if it worked I'm pretty sure I would love it.

_childDocuments_.review: I am really loving this!As a huge Marvel fan, the humour and story is not on par with the films, but it does a pretty damn good job. The charters included are well VA'd and written, keeping true to what is portrayed in the comics and films.As other reviews have said there is a "left field" relationship system and exploration system when not in missions - personally I really like both of these elements, but possibly not for everyone.The actual meat of this game is the missions - which are very x-com meets card game. It's done really well and is a lot of fun. Enough variation in the  cards / moves to keep it interesting, really great visuals for the moves and a lot of underlying systems that enhance all of this and continue to keep the game-play interesting.Overall this has been a hidden gem for me - not expecting much from it but deciding to give it a go after an impulse purchase. I think this might be my favourite game of the year.

_childDocuments_.review: Waited to pick this up on sale and I'm glad I did. It's fun, but oh my god so many cutscenes and the whole concept of friendship and hangouts was such a bad idea. This is coming from a guy that loved XCOM 2 because cutscenes were minimal and gameplay was focused on strategy and tactics. The battles are fun and I do everything I can to get into those as quickly as possible by skipping all dialogue. Does the typical Marvel fan love all this friendship stuff?? It makes me feel physically ill when I listen to it...I'm upset because I know the potential of Firaxis and they could've taken the best parts of XCOM 2 and combined it with Marvel. This game is definitely easier than XCOM 2 so if that was a barrier to entry for you before that will not be an issue here.I think this game also went a little overboard with the loot and all that crap, everything you picked up in XCOM felt meaningful, this game can feel like an ARPG with how much loot it dishes out.Could've been so much better, but worth it for the fun card battles if the game is steeply discounted.

_childDocuments_.review: Looks like an early 2000 game and somehow performance is horrible, full of stuttering and fps drops. This is not a PC game, this is a mobile game and not a great one at that. It feels like Firaxis took a look at Raid Shadow Legends and decided to make a Marvel version of that, but with less things to do, bad graphics, even worse character design, and throw in cards because who doesn't like card games, right?I asked for my money back but I would gladly pay double if there was a way to punish whoever made the choice to build this steaming piece of ♥♥♥♥ instead of making an X-Com game with superheroes. _childDocuments_.review: What I expected: Marvel XcomWhat I got: Into The Slay Massrvel Effect Spire BreachReally satisfying combat, fun characters, oodles of optional lore, solid story and you can pet the demon dog.The downsides I have are mostly optimisation. My PC isn't brand new, but still, this game struggled sometimes. Also while I didn't mind the extensive "On the Normandy" segments, I can see all the dialogue becoming a bit of a drag for the more gameplay focused people. Also to touch on the elephant in the room. You don't need to watch the films or read the comics to know what's going on in this game. There's references to events that have happened in the comics, but they're all throwaway lines. Anything important (character relationships etc.) is usually summarised in optional dialogue. But honestly, you'll be fine even if your marvel knowledge amounts to "Iron man is that flying robot guy right?" All in all, for someone like me who loves turn based games and the golden age of Bioware, this was brilliant fun and I highly recommend it. It was an iffy start with the tone, but actually as it went, the game very quickly pulled me in and by the end I cared about everyone in my little superhero haunted house.(Also only the other day did I realise that they referenced that insane 50's or 60's comic, where Iron Man goes to ancient Egypt to fight some Romans and fall in love with Cleopatra. Why wasn't that the plot of Iron Man 3? Disney you cowards.)

_childDocuments_.review: I am a casual gamer with a high end gaming computer. About 30 hours into this game, I'm very impressed. This is my first game with a card / roll style combat system which took some getting used to. If you like turn based, role playing, highly strategic chess like combat, this game is going to check those boxes.The story and character sub-plots are written extremely well. Kudos to the team that must have spent hundreds of hours putting this together. Even if the combat system isn't completely living up to your expectations, I would recommend the game for the story alone.I bought the game on sale for about $20.00 and definitely getting my monies worth. Load times aren't bad but I'm running an Alien R15 with modifications. Honestly I thought the load times would be better. Game has only crashed once and with the frequent auto-save functionality, it wasn't an issue.Highly recommend this game, especially since it's on sale right now.Edit 1/27/2024: I'm updating my review now that I've finished the game. I did a tone of the optional missions and completed the game with 96.4 hours invested. My original review stays the same. Highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm at the 97+ hour mark for this game and am still enjoying it.  I initially put off purchasing the game due to the card based battle mechanics.  I then snagged it with the season pass bundle at a discount out of boredom and a fairly substantial addition to Steam sales and do not regret my purchase.  Surprisingly, I really enjoy the card based battle style and recommend giving it a shot.  Plus, there's a tons to do in the game beyond the battles including exploration, amusing and interesting character development, etc. I haven't had a single crash or issue on my gaming laptop even when hooked to an external curved display.  The game plays flawlessly and is gorgeous... except on Steam Deck, read below if this applies to you.Steam Deck Warning: I initially devoted over 30 hours on my Steam Deck and do not recommend it for Steam Deck at the time of this review.  The game crashes repeatedly when the main character goes to bed and randomly at other points during the game, particularly during load screens that accompany cut scenes. Keep in mind, the game is literally progressed by the main character going to bed after each battle.  This means dozens of crashes/soft resets on your Steam Deck each time you sit down to play it.  Character goes to bed, game crashes and reboots Steam Deck, slug through the game reloading and then the character successfully goes to sleep and you can play until you complete the next battle, go to sleep and repeat.  This sounds awful and it is, but it gets worse. Fairly late in the game there is a triple cut scene that causes a game breaking bug that the normal reboot does resolve.  I tried tons of different tricks listed in the forums without success including a lack of cloud saves.  The Steam Deck indicates cloud saves work, but you'll find nothing on your PC.  This is another known Steam Deck issue and none of the forum tricks worked for me.  The fact that I brute forced my way through 30+ hours on the Steam Deck while dealing with dozens if not hundreds of reboots and then finally had to completely restart my campaign on my laptop ramping up 97+ hours at the time of this review should prove how much I thoroughly enjoy the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Revised Review (post-patch)TLDR: I enjoyed the game, but it has flaws.Caveat: I am a big fan of Superheroes, Turn-Based and Firaxis.The Good- The writing for the story-line is very good.  Drama, twists-and-turns, humour and heart.- There is a lot of character dialogue.  Most of it is quite good.- The card mechanics for each hero is fairly unique and flavorful.- The combat and challenge missions were interesting tactical challenges.- Charlie is totes adorbs.The Bad- The game is not entirely stable.  I have experienced multiple crashes, freezes and graphical glitches.  Before the patch, the save game system was also unstable.  Future patches may rectify these problems.- Hunter should have been named Gatherer considering how many plants and mushrooms were picked during the game.  Yes, your character, a super hero, needs to run around gathering reagents like this is some sort of fantasy MMORPG.- Do you like searching your house for loose pocket change?  Then you will love the orb gathering mini-game.- At the time of this writing, the number of options for deck construction are very limited.  Hunter has *some* limited options.  All of the other heroes have next to none.- Linked in to the limited deck options is the absence of replay value.  Once you have experienced the story and fiddled with the available cards, there really isn't anything else to try.Final verdict: It is worth playing once just for the story and dialog.  If the price tag is too steep for a single play-through, wait for it to go on sale.  Or wait longer for the YouTube story compilation videos.

_childDocuments_.review: I really love marvel. I grew up between the stacks of magazines and consider myself a true marvel geek. That's why it pains me do much to write this. Pros:Gameplay is top tier from the creators of x-com. The card system works really well and the heroes feel and play different as they should. Hulk smashes and bashes, spider man is fast and agile, Dr strange feels like the sorcerer supreme he is. Story is good, like watching a new marvel animated series you can be a part of. No stupid marvel comedy club like Love and Thunder, but good ol' hero one liners. Hero customisation and deck building are vast and plentiful. You don't feel like you need to buy the extra ski s really.Cons:The game is optimiser really badly. With recommended setup, game stutters alot right after loading or when there's a huge bunch of enemies on the board. Almost made me quit the last mission out of frustration. Maybe after several performance patched they can fix it. DLC is not worth it. Venom and Deadpool are cool as hell, but only three Missions is not worth the price. As a principle, Microtransaction skins suck. It's a great game overall and had me entertained through the campaign, but I don't feel like it's worth the box price. Get it on discount, maybe 50% off so you don't feel ripped. Also I recommend waiting for all DLC to come out as a package and discounted. 6/10 good marvel smashing, bad publisher decisions and sub par performance.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, one of the more fun Marvel games I've played in quite a while, it brought back a bit of the fondness I had with X-Men Legends and Ultimate Alliance.It is not without it's faults, but it offered something new in terms of a Marvel property, and fun gameplay taking a novel mix of tactical turn-based combat, deck building and role-playing character interactions that impact gameplay; which you could consider a pseudo amalgamation of X-Com, Slay the Spire and Persona.Sadly, it didn't sell well enough and was abandoned very quickly a year into release, despite this it is still worth playing, but there are a few things to be noted and areas of lost potential.The PC port has issues, from the launcher to the two most notably being a potential game-breaking bug in a later mission making the mission unwinnable due to changes brought about by the DLC, that will not get fixed. While there is a work around with in-game items or by playing on a lower difficulty, there is no warning for this issue. Additionally, for those who want to 100% the game, one of the later game outfits is bugged out, and has a very high chance of just not appearing when unlocked, with no other way to obtain it without mods.These bugs will not be fixed as the game was abandoned post DLC, which brings another issue forward, the lost potential.The endgame credits and DLC all build to a future event, DLC story expansion or new game. Which sadly will never appear, with Dr Doom, Dracula and Mephisto playing a role in the build up and potential story, it is a very unfortunate loss.On a personal level, my main complaint comes from the character roster. Simply, too many characters don't fit and are obviously there as marketing elements. A fantasy/horror game that relies on the Avengers over Marvel's untapped horror characters is unfortunate.I understand they help to entice potential customers, especially as characters included are now well known via the MCU, alongside long standing fan favourites like Wolverine and Spider-Man, are at the forefront. They just feel out of place.An argument can be made for Hulk and Venom with their ties to the One-Below-All and the King In Black, but the others are an even greater stretch from Captain America's werewolf period and history with Dracula, Spider-Man with the Spider Totems, and maybe Deadpool and his history with Death (although Deadpool as a character is very oversaturated, much like Wolverine).This could have been resolved with other DLC characters, but losing slots to Captain America, Captain Marvel, Wolverine, Spider-Man, Deadpool, Iron Man, and Hulk was a bit boring.We got a nice bundle of magic and horror characters as playable with Storm, Magik, Blade, Ghost Rider (Robbie Reyes), Scarlet Witch, Dr Strange, Morbius, and Nico; alongside cameos, Easter eggs and references to others like Man-Thing, and Johnny Blaze's Ghost Rider.But it would have been great to see others join the lineup, give lesser know but fun magic and horror characters the chance to be seen and know, build their fan bases and open them to a new audience; with interesting styles of gameplay and designs, we could have seen Agatha Harkness, Kushala, Man-Thing, Juggernaut, Daimon Hellstrom, Jericho Drumm, Wiccan, the Ancient One, Shaman, Wong, Rintrah, Clea, Elsa Bloodstone, Werewolf by Night, Captain Britain, Pixie, N'Kantu, Simon Garth, Shiklah, Sleepwalker, and Manphibian, etc.Even additional antagonists like Baron Mordo, Enchantress, Morgan le Fey, Doctor Doom, Dormammu, Selene, Nightmare, D'Spayre, Malekith, Loki, Kulan Garth, Moridun, the Black Tide, Morlun, the Hand, Robert Hellsgaard, and the Hood, etc.Despite all this, it is still a solid game worth playing, but go in with the right expectations. If you don't like tactical turn-based combat and deck building, or the universe of Marvel Comics, then this isn't for you.It regularly goes on sale, making the complete edition affordable, and worth picking up.It is very much a fun game very few people played sadly.

_childDocuments_.review: While Midnight Suns is not going to be everyone's cup of tea, it is a very unique blend of gaming genres,  For myself anyway as an avid fan of Deckbuilders, Turn based tactics and (more recently) with games such as Lost Ediolons or Persona type "Friendship simulators" there is a lot to love here.  Look when I first saw some previews and reviews I thought it was gonna be worse than it is I thought I wouldn't enjoy exploring the abbey and doing superhero hangouts but honestly I find that I do enjoy those aspects of this game too.Firaxis has another long running franchise hit on their hands here if they can keep expanding on all the interesting crafting and leveling up systems and keep adding in more variance and more expansions with new characters, stories and enemies to the game anyhow.I'd say give it a try as for me I've been really pleasently surprised and keep finding myself just wanting more of pretty much everything they have got going on here.The Micro transactions are not needed  but they are not over priced either in my opinion and you will unlock enough skins in the game for most folks anyhow is my gut.  But for me I find the Legendary edition to be worth the money in this case and I really did not think I would be saying that going in.Hands down the most tactical super hero and immersive moments of  RPG type fun I've had in a super hero game since the good old days of Freedom Force.

_childDocuments_.review: I initially dismissed this game, due to day one technical problems, what felt like fan-fiction writing, a generic story and the fact that it was not X-com 3.   The battles were great, but everything else felt sub-par.  I'll get it on sale down the line, I told myself.  But something was nagging me and so the next morning I brought it again, and boy am I glad I did as this game is actually amazing.  It just doesn't leave a good first impression, but once you accept the game for what it is, you will find that it is actually great fun, beautiful to look at, huge, and challenging.  Its actually a lot like x-com too: you have your fun but challenging tactical battles and a base that you upgrade and grow alongside the battles.  There is so much to do and all of it is fun.  since i am not a huge superhero guy, I skip through most of the dialogue, but everything you do adds to the meta game of making a kick ass team (literally), so that you can go back out there to kick some more ass.  The battles are glorious, on brand and actually quite challenging.  There is a constant feeling of marvel (pun intended) as you explore more of the Abbey ground and discover yet another cool system.  The story is actually not bad, as such stories go, and you get used to the constant quips.  You can skip through anything that annoys you and customize your experience - in my case the battles and opening up the Abbey.  Also, most of the problems I had with bugs and stuttering on day one seem already fixed, unlike another recent cluster♥♥♥♥ release (cough Calisto Protocol cough).  I can't put this game down now, and I am a 53 year old man who stopped reading comics decades ago.

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to give this game a straight thumbs-up or -down review because there's a lot to like about it. The game captures the tone and feel of MCU media quite well. Production design is right on the money (literally). The writing's not great but not bad and better than usual. The voice acting provides surprisingly decent riffs on the more familiar voice casts without being outright imitations of those actors. The different characters largely strike a balance between their classic comic-book personalities and their Marvel media adaptations. The cut scenes and post-fight "comic book covers" nail the Marvel Comics style, the story is warts-and-all accurate to the "edgy eighties/ X-TREEME nineties" approach, and the strategy element is a welcome change from high-speed button-mashing. I like having a (vaguely) customizable protagonist as the central character, accompanied by iconic Marvel characters. The friendship and relationship elements provide an engaging hook for this otherwise combat-oriented game. Aside from the downright weird choice of matching rigid card-game mechanics with the notoriously freeform realm of comic-book brawls, the design team made a lot of the right choices here. It's just nowhere near worth the game's retail price. The downsides of this game are huge: stuttery graphics (blamed, in other reviews, on the 2K anti-cheat protocol); extremely limited character movement and agency both in and outside the fights (you can't, for example, jump up or down - IN A SUPERHERO GAME!!!); extremely linear "roleplaying" elements (understandable, given the boundaries of intellectual property licensing, but still frustrating); environmental attacks that are infuriatingly limited by their effect area. Missions are repetitive, and utterly void of player agency outside of choosing cards and watching their effects play out. There's no sense of clever tactics beyond choosing combat cards, and that's a criminal misuse of the characters involved. A light/ darkness polarity doesn't suit the moral ambiguity of the Marvel Universe, either; Deadpool, Wolverine, Blade, the Punisher, Namor, the Hulk, and many other Marvel heroes are mass murderers - where does THAT sit on a light/ darkness scale? And let's face it: The story - while accurate to Silver- and Iron-Age comic book sagas - is goofy AF. I feel churlish complaining about that element because it IS true to the MCU's roots. Thing is, the MCU itself surpassed those roots over 20 years ago. Modern superhero media runs much deeper, more subtle, and more culturally accurate than the classic Marvel Comics stories did. (Why is Lilith - correctly referred to as a Sumerian deity/ demon - WHITE and apparently BRITISH? Why have Pagan witches spent centuries hanging around A CONVERTED GOTHIC ABBY?) Aside from a handful of culturally diverse-ish characters, the game's storyline and settings remain stuck somewhere around maybe 1990.  (Also, I realize they're probably setting aside DLC after stripmining the more recognizable Marvel Media stable, but where are the Werewolf By Night, Damon Hellstrom, Brother Voodoo, the Moon Knight, Hannibal King, Topaz, Cloak & Dagger, Jennifer Kale, and other classic "Marvel macabres"? I can see why they'd steer clear of Satana, Simon Garth, the Man-Thing, and Frankenstein's Monster, but there are still plenty of potential Midnight Suns characters out there - some of whom were actual members of the comics' Midnight Sons.) The Batman Arkham series wipes the floor with Midnight Suns, and most of those games - despite their own limitations - are older than this one. For a AAA-type game with a hefty price tag and the most successful media franchise in history, this game should be much better than it is. And so while it IS an entertaining diversion for a few hours of free play, or for maybe a handful of dollars down the road when the price drops, it's nowhere near worth the current price tag, ESPECIALLY not before they fix whatever is causing the glitchy framerates outside of cutscenes and combat. That right there is a headache that should never have been allowed to reach market. For a game currently hosting a $40+ price tag, it's unforgivable. Honestly, Midnight Suns feels more like an early-access proof-of-concept trial run for a better and more complex game than it does a high-ticket game in its own right.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game! Reminiscient of some of my old favorites, the Marvel Ultimate Alliance series. It plays in 2 modes. First is Exploration mode, a third-person RPG on the game's home base, The Abbey. This is where you upgrade abilities, explore the grounds for lore and new powers and interact with other heroes through a pretty fun social sim. The base is endlessly upgrade-able and really fun to manage. The second mode is Combat. This is a turn-based fighting game with a card-draw system for attacks and abilities that's both challenging and rewarding to master.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've played X-Com, stay with X-Com.If you've not heard of X-Com, play X-Com instead.No spoilers and i've played the entire game at this point...The battles (missions) in Midnight Suns are very cool and a lot of fun. The card-play mechanic works surprisingly well, the action is fast-paced, and you truly feel like Cyclops commanding a load of superheroes in the field. You face some cool villains and each hero is completely unique in combat with thematic abilities, so having to decide which individuals to take on which missions makes for a nice challenge. Making a comic book cover for each mission is a fun touch, akin to how easily you can get lost in Gwent in Witcher III and wake up Sunday wondering where your weekend went.However, the non-battle stuff that takes up 2/3 of the game is dull, and does not impact the game at all. It's more 1st person than X-Com, and all you do is talk to other Superheroes and do childish stuff like planning surprise parties and mediating secret crushes. If you're picturing a school playground right now, that's spot on. That's exactly what it's like. This friendship-driven element has nice morals, but makes for dull game play.There is no real base-building that affects the game play. You can buy aesthetic things and discover new areas, but it has absolutely no impact on the game. It's also very unclear you can do this, and i didn't realise until the end of the game! So there's some proof pudding that it's all pointless. There's also a hell of a lot of resources, but you forget about them very quickly. There's no Age of Empires-style mechanic for acquiring them and having to think carefully about where you spend them: you just find them or you don't. And, as mentioned, the things they buy influence the game so little you stop caring.A slight annoyance is how all the heroes level up automatically very fast. You can work so hard to get one hero up a couple of levels, but when you hit a milestone, they all bump up to that level anyway. This is very unsatisfying and makes you forget that levels are even a thing.Glad i got it on sale.Now stop reading this and go play X-Com!

And the cards just feel so good to play with the awesome animations. It's also diverse enough and has enough content to keep it fresh and exciting throughout the game. 10/10 for combat.Not a fan of the RPG elements. They are not badly made, just not my cup of team. Also they are thematically very decoupled from the combat, but gameplay wise you still have to deal with them. Again, it's well made and all, so if you enjoy Marvel stuff you're probably gonna like it.Performance. I had awful stutters in all parts of the game. Not all the time, which makes it hard to pinpoint what caused it. Made certain parts annoying to play.It's a good game, get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm very sad that I hate this game. This is everything I've ever hoped for. A Marvel game, with tactics and deckbuilding. Alas, it is god-awful. I played it for so long just out of sheer obstinacy (and with the intention of making a review for my YT channel but I think no one cares about this game at all).**I'll start with the bad. Some spoilers ahead maybe, who cares.+It is built as if it was a mobile game. Maybe that was the original idea. What I mean by that: -You can only do 1 mission a ''day''.-Every day you must do small, repetitive tasks.-There are numerous types of currency to level up your cards.-There are seemingly unecessary roadblocks in the story, forcing you to grind basic, repetitive missions.+Speaking of story,  story is lame, the dialogues are lame, the friendship system is lame and just artificially inflates game time. I might need to replace my keyboard soon simply due to just smashing the ESC key to skip the inconsequential and stretched out dialogue. At least 10 ESK smesh with every character interaction, a few times a 'day'.Speaking of game time, I think around 50% of my game time was spent in unoriginal, grindy combat.What I mean by that:-Most monsters are repetitive, bland and boring.-Most monsters are designed to extend battle time without offering true or original challenge.-A lot of them just spawn mobs, duplicate themselves or each other, and leech life from you.+What is the point of the 'base'? Roaming around trying to solve puzzles that are completely unrelated to the story and ultimately, barely offer anything cool to the player.The game will make your computer overheat like mad, to the point where I had to have the AC on AND blast my fan on my PC or else the game would crash (and I don't want to think about the damage all that heat could do).Game was running smooth on Ultra settings but I had to tone it down because of the heat issue. Then, last battle for no reason, the game suffered from a huge frame drop.I QUIT AT THE LAST FIGHT BECAUSE THE MECHANICS LOCKED ME OUT OF A WIN AND THE FIGHT WAS SO ANNOYING / BORING THAT AFTER 37 HOURS OF REPETITIVE, GRINDY BATTLING, I JUST WANTED TO MOVE ON. FRAME RATE MADE IT AWFUL TO PLAY THAT LAST FIGHT ANYWAYS, AND THE STORY IS SO BAD THAT I DON'T CARE ABOUT SEEING THE ENDING. I can just go look it up on YT anyways, probably. I'm not angry, I'm disappointed.**Here is the good:+Graphics are great.+Voice acting is amazing.+Good cast of characters. I learned a bit from the characters I didn't know much about.-Good diversity of mechanics for the heroes. They don't have a 'class' per say, but some are clearly made for DPS, tanking, buff, battlefield management, offering different strategies.+Combat was fun for about 10 hours, until the monsters became lame.-There were a few missions that I had to restart and adapt to the battlefield correctly to win, which made it very interesting. However, that wasn't often enough or became repetitive quickly.+Tons of unlockable skins.-However, the special skins you can only unlock through specific challenges were all unlocked for the final fight. So why bother?+Card system is interesting and makes you think about your decisions.-You can customize each hero's deck.-You can add modifiers to each card, making customization pretty deep.That's all I want to say for now, I don't want to spend any more time on this game. Do not buy unless it's at 90% sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not for me. And that's OK. I'm sure the people who it is for are having a blast with it! I didn't read anything or watch anything about this game at all before going in. My brother absolutely LOVES it. Additionally, I was a HUGE fan of Ultimate Alliance and someone who is off the Christmas Card list now had mentioned it gave them very strong UA vibes (it does NOT at all, btw) so I bit on the digital+ sale. And while it's not a complete waste for me, I was definitely underwhelmed. The story elements are cheesy, but entertaining. The graphics, while a huge complaint for some folks, I think fit it very well. The voice acting ranges from competent to outstanding. What ruins it for me (and what will save it for the right person) is the combat mechanics. It feels very mobile-game. I do not like card/deck builders at all - again, not knowing what I was in for - but I gave it a go anyway. And I just absolutely hated the combat. You have a limited set of mixed offensive, defensive, and buff/skill cards which get drawn randomly, coupled with some very limited move/sacrifice/point based options in any battle. It honestly feels more like Ooblets than any other game I've ever played. Though Ooblets is mercifully much shorter in the battles department and has round limits. The battles in Midnight Suns drag on and on and you're clicking the same handful of cards over and over. I would have much rather had a set of skills with burnable 'mana' or even a non-card based opportunity system. But if you love card mechanics, this is probably very light weight and might even be TOO simple. I'm just one of those people who doesn't understand the need to shoehorn cards into systems. Looking at YOU, Back 4 Blood. The game also requests a lot of lore knowledge to *fully* take in. It's not required, but it certainly expands the experience if you're aware of some of the non-film Marvel storylines. That's one of the parts I loved, but could see it turning off a casual Marvel fan. Also, Tony Stark pulling a constant Shaggy Rogers re: g-g-g-g-GHOSTS got a little thick a little quick. Overall though, I can't recommend it for people like me, who aren't looking for card clickers. And I definitely don't love the mobile feel to everything, including monetization mechanics. Also, googling how to bypass the 2K launcher is ESSENTIAL if you don't want really awful stuttering. The game is jam packed with the horsemen of the PCocalypse. Denuvo being the biggest offender, but extra launchers absolutely not helping matters.

_childDocuments_.review: Half thumbs up atm (so I guess a 'nice job fist bump'?).  Wait until the next video driver update.  I updated everything & NVidia still wasn't showing it as an option in GeForce experience to optimize.  I have a ticket in to them (this happened with Fifa 23 as well).My card is above the median, and about 20%th percentiles under the recommended card, which should be well in performance range for Med-High settings (I'm ultra on every other game), and the video froze on high settings during a loading screen transition about 20 min in (music still playing, full black screen).Overall its feeling like their 1st dev meeting went like this: Question: "Which gamestyle should we use?  Cards, 4x, adventure...?"  Answer: "Yes."Quick ratings:Gameplay            A-Music                   BDialogue/Story     B+Art                        B-Graphics               C-Replay                  D+Bugs                     C+Expectations        B-Gameplay is a tough one.  Some weird camera stuff to get used to and they set the default mouse sensitivity on 'duper extra spinney' for some reason, so that's annoying to have to tweak.  This is NOT Xcom or anything close to it.  It's WAY more of a comic adventure story/dating mobile game than it is Xcom.  It's 4x light for sure.  There's plenty of strategy, there's plenty of base building, but there is a decent amount of grind and storyline in between all of that.  The story is good enough to hold it all together, and I don't mind the 'friendship' stuff because I like comics, and that's what glue's it all together in this game.  It's not the game I was hoping for, but it's a good game and is keeping me interested.  I'm sure I'll get at least 100-200 hours out of it.Dialogue is decent/good/chuckly.  I'd recommend being a Marvel fan for full effect, but there's plenty in there for everyone.Music is good, nothing to write home about but it sets the tone.Graphics feels a bit "kiddie" even with the High settings.  I'd expect a bit more, I dunno, dank? with this storyline instead of the shinie faux vampire Anime sort of vibe they've got going with the game art?  Bugs are there, just minor stuff like a single crash while I was saving the game.  It's mostly just related to the graphics issues.  But shouldn't be given the AAA title & extra like 9 months they had to launch the game.Edit2: I changed the replayability rating from a B to a D+ b/c there's no way I could go through that story line again.  It is full on heavy teenage angst + midlife crisis.  The entire thing is about listening to EVERY character tell you how worthless they are IN EVERY TRANSITION OF THE GAME.  So you are a full on therapist, and omg does it get old doing that over a dozen Heroes plus, multiple x multiple times.  There is close to zero replayibility b/c of how tied into game advancement/combat all of that hero counseling is.  I don't think I could ever play this again like I have with Xcom.  It's fairly clear that Disney had an iron grip on this thing and tried to make it a game that appeals to everyone, and as we look back on it it's not going to age well.  I'm thinking that thumbs down will be permanent at this point.  I'll grind through it b/c I love comics and strategy, but it's starting to feel like work to get to the parts of the game that I enjoy.Additionally, even after an update to the game they have not aligned their graphics with Nvidia.  Nvidia says my card should be on the highest settings, and the game says I should be on med/low settings.  The game is correct, b/c even after the update I'm getting the same stuttering graphics issues I was before.  I've gone through everything on my PC with a fine toothed comb to try and maximize performance and I don't think it's me.  My rig should be able to handle medium settings based on the provided game specs, Nvidia agrees, and for some reason it can't.Edit1: So I've got a 6gb 1060, just under the recommended 1070, and 16gb of RAM and it's still lagging a bit in some transitions as well as taking awhile to load new areas.  I used the in game optimization button (which did drop it down to med. settings), and restarted everything first.  So not much more I can do aside from drop to low settings I guess?  The game just needs some optimization I think b/c I play FIFA 23 fine, which has very similar/recommended range of vid cards and less general RAM issues as well.  I've got another 16gb RAM I've been too lazy to try and pop in (b/c I haven't needed it, just bought it on sale 6 mo. ago), so I can try that, but it seems to be pretty clearly a VRAM slowdown so dunno if that'll do much.  Maybe area transitions.  3-4yo rig, so dunno how much higher I can go with the Vid., and of course we just passed Cyber monday.  Dumb of me not to check I guess.  Userbenchmark says I'm at about 57%th percentile for gaming 3D performance.  1070's are running about $200-250 rn, so if you don't have a new rig or recently upgraded, you will see some occasional lag in this game even on med settings.  I'm 50 hrs into the game, so it's playable and predictable where you'll see performance issues, but they're mildly annoying and more than infrequent (I'd honestly recommend low settings for EVERYONE that doesn't have a 1070 or higher based on what I've seen, but I just can't do it personally).I'm enjoying the game, and it has some replayability, which is saying something b/c my standards are high for that.  But it will remain a thumbs down though until they fix the optimization issues.  I'm gonna keep ranting here b/c I just have never had a graphics issue with any game up to this point, not even close to this.  It feels like they've jumped a full 1-2 years ahead in graphics requirements in the span of 2mo. since the last AAA title release.  Don't give me a recommended range of cards, put mine in the average to above average range and then make me put it on low settings.  I just don't see a reason my card shouldn't be able to handle the graphics when there is definitely nothing special about them that I can see.  I've played games with better graphics than this, they're just HEAVILY shaded I think, which is 100% an optimizable thing.  I've got 3 relatives that do that sort of work, it feels lazy to me.  Cool stuff, not bad, but if I can max out heavily modded Skyrim and see individual leaves on trees I should be able to handle a "whoosh" fire blast from Cpt. Marvel on medium settings in this game.  That and we're getting to the point where the human eye really can't see the difference in a lot of these quick moving things, the still art is MUCH more important than the moving art.  I mean ffs my dude's feet are below the ground on the training steps sometimes and he does a full on Fat Joe 'Lean Back' when he stops (even my wife noticed just glancing at the game).  Who cares about the million pixilated whoosh magic when you've got stuff like that and getting hung up on scenery running around the grounds to pull you out of the immersion.  It feels like bad/rushed design decisions/PM goal issues from the graphics folks.

_childDocuments_.review: Midnight Suns is a terrific superhero game, in an over saturated market, plagued by a myriad of bugs (some of which are FINALLY fixed). There's really two games in one here: a card-based strategy action game, and a friendship simulator. I've gotten every achievement (there's one that I still haven't been able to trigger), and have done basically everything to do in the game.: MOST cards are interesting in some way. Even if they don't always work out the way you hope, there's generally only one or two cards (out of many, many options) per character that I would classify as total duds. The upgrading options for the cards allows things that you initially didn't think highly of to suddenly find a valuable role in your deck, and sometimes specific character combinations make otherwise mediocre cards really shine. There's TONS of room for customization to your own playstyle, while different mission leaders cause you to have to constantly adapt and try different characters. Thankfully, each character feels very unique, even when adding in all of the DLC (I'll get to that). 10/10, terrific gameplay loop that's satisfying with every character.: When you're not off on missions, you spend your time at The Abbey, a hidden sanctuary in a pocket dimension inside Salem, Massachusetts. You can explore the grounds, find and solve mysteries (usually to unlock chests with cosmetics), and follow a sub-plot to gain access to great combat bonuses, along with your good girl demon dog, Charlie. Inside the Abbey itself, you can talk to a huge cast of characters from throughout the Marvel Universe, and befriend them via conversation, group activities (I love Blade's Book Club), exchanging gifts, and doing other activities like bonding over a drink (of root beer, much to Wolverine's dismay), or playing video games. A lot of the dialogue here is pretty hit or miss. Some characters and their developments and subplots are GREAT, and some just fall really flat.8.5/10, some characters could have used a bit more work, and I would have liked to see a bit more steps in the process overall. A big note here is that some of these things are not exactly skippable, and you'll lose out of valuable combat bonuses if you skip the ones that are.: It's an interesting mix of comic heroes and villains, with a new story, rather than ripping something straight out of comics. The story itself is interesting, and the cast works well within it. It's not amazing, and definitely has some pacing issues, but is pretty good. There's too many instances of, "Well if this person that has been here the whole time had shared THAT piece of information, we could have done this way faster," and "If this person had only asked for help, this other problem would have never come up" as primary ways to keep the story chugging along, and add to it. The  story is just decent, in that regard, but the character to character interactions are often great. There's not much new in the character interactions if you've read a lot of comics, but they're presented extremely well, and many of them develop organically, rather than feeling like I'm just reading a wiki. 8.5/10: All four DLC characters weave a connected story, separate from the main one, to add basically an entire extra (much, much shorter) campaign revolving around a whole new cast of characters. I actually might like this storyline more than the main storyline, simply because it's more focused and lacks a lot of those pacing issues I mentioned above. Combat-wise, they continue to all feel very different than every other character in the game, which is remarkable at this point, given the size of the cast. For the friendship simulator aspect of the game, most of them are pretty dry; I think they rushed that part of development for the DLC, based on fast timelines. Venom's interactions with Peter, and Morbius's interactions with Blade are pretty good, though. And Deadpool adds a lot of needed humor to the game.9/10: It's serviceable. Nothing standout, positively or negatively.7/10Ok, on to the bugs. As mentioned at the top, I've gotten all achievements except one. I may need to wind up playing through the game a THIRD time in order to get the achievement to trigger. I'm hoping they just fix that one like they've fixed others, so that sometime down the line I can just load my save file, and it'll happen. I do like the game, so playing it a third time at some point isn't the end of the world.The BIGGEST problem though, is the constant performance issues. When finishing loading, things stutter for a little bit, but it smooths out pretty quickly; that's not really an issue to me. What is an issue is how frequently it  I've played 25 hours in the past two weeks. In that timeframe, this has happened six times. Thankfully, the game very frequently autosaves, so I don't typically lose much if any progress, but it's extremely annoying, and does mean I can't do anything else actually important on my computer while playing the game. It's a major, major issue.: As-is, 8/10. If they fix those other bugs, 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Initially super positive about the game. Started out pretty dope, but it was pretty much downhill after the first 20 hours. At this point I'm just trying to complete the game so I can say I've done it.It has some great elements, and story telling that can be very interesting if you're at all taken by the marvel universe.Sadly it's also marred by a bunch of technical issues, some of which don't start showing up until very deep into playthroughs. I had absolutely zero technical issues with this game in the first 40 hours played, but since crossing over that mark I've started experiencing repeated crashes to the point where I am struggling finishing the game. It's 50/50 if I even get to load my saves at this point without the game crashing, it's a hazard to try and save progress every time, and there's never any telling if loading an old save to change a choice or simply completing a mission is what will set off the next crash. I haven't been able to string together 3-4 hours without a crash more than twice since I cleared the 40 hour mark.It's sad, because this game does have some nice, if shallow, customization options and things that make it worth playing at least once. I'll have to see if I can get around to a second playthrough, and if any of the choices you make in the game actually have any real impact (doubt it, from how mine has played out so far).I'd recommend this game if you can find a good discount, but not at full price. Can't promise you'll complete your playthrough before your save is corrupted, and the game has very little replay value from the look of it. It's very much NOT like XCOM in that regard. In fact I find the concept of these games being similar to be woefully reductive of what makes XCOM a great game. This game has very few surprises, very shallow strategy outside of very high difficulty settings (which are also balanced in a wonky way) and choosing to do side missions appear to have zero impact whatsoever on the outcome of the main story, because you have no pressure to achieve anything in a given frame of time. XCOM is great because you have bad things looming in the horizon, and choosing to delay certain missions can have lasting consequences - something that isn't felt in this game at all. It also appears very non-mod friendly (which can be understood due to the high value IP), but it again leaves the game as is without any options to mod it up for a new playthrough.The game desperately needs more urgency in how it handles missions, because without urgency, everything becomes meaningless.

_childDocuments_.review: Actually good it turns out! Despite generally really enjoying Firaxis games I avoided this one for a combo of reasons (Chimera squad wasn't very good; I assumed this would be another XCOM clone; the marketing is god-awful (why is the colour image so yellow! Why is Wolverine grimacing like that!); I am generally sick of Marvel ♥♥♥♥; etc). I eventually picked it up on sale (it is a Firaxis game after all), and it massively surprised me. It's goth but light, funny, well-written (if sometimes way too Whedonesque), and wonderfully original.It's essentially a tactical/spacial deckbuilder, with cards that let you move around a 2D plane, interact with the environment and hit things. During the combat missions, everything comes together real well, and play feels satisfying. Between missions, there's a bunch of chatting with characters and performing activities which all either advance the plot or help build decks (one deck for each character, which combine into a 24 card deck when three characters go on a mission). Those downtime bits sometimes get a bit tedious, especially if you don't give a ♥♥♥♥ about marvel characters, but the missions stay interesting and challenging with the help of some really well-implemented (and optional) difficulty scaling.I got a few minor gripes, the biggest of which is it is maybe a bit long. I was hardly racing through, but my 62  hours of gameplay is a single playthrough. I took a looooong pause in the middle of the story, probably about 40 hours in, because I'd lost... Maybe not interest, but momentum. I came back to it a week days ago and raced through the rest of it, and it felt fresh enough to keep me interested to the end. The deckbuilding could also be a bit more interesting: there are mechanics that make you destroy old cards, which discourages flexibility and experimentation, and some cards are Simply Better than others, which leads towards making a certain kind of deck for each hero except the Protagonist.Anyway yeah cool play it imo

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: An absolutely outstanding deckbuilder / turn based tactics game with a lot of really hit-or-miss character interactions bolted on (that you can either ignore or click through quickly).(EDIT: I also have completely ignored the DLC. No idea if it is good value for money. And the 'premium currency' stuff bolted on by 2k is just silly. Ignore it.)The turn based combat part of the game is absolutely outstanding. I thought I wouldn't like the randomness of the card draw but it is a lot of fun, making you think up new strategies on the fly and not just relying on the same 'optimal' strategy every turn. In the 46 hours I've played so far, I think I've only been screwed by the RNG just not giving me usable cards once. (And I could have built the decks better.)One thing I like about Midnight Suns compared to XCOM is that it is a move at your own pace game and much less punishing. Don't get me wrong, that sort of feel is essential to XCOM, but here it makes the game feel more like a superhero movie and less 'stressful'. I don't have to be constantly thinking about how a risk might set me back hours in the campaign, possibly even wrecking the campaign.Unfortunately, the rest of the game varies between acceptable and not-so-good. The inability to save multiple decks per character is a bummer and something I really wish Firaxis would have added. The card pool available for characters also feels too small. For example, having different types of quick attacks available to each character so you can tailor their strategy would have been nice. You can do some of that with card mods, but it isn't the same.Hero balance is also a bit of a mess. Just about every guide to the game notes how Captain Marvel is just underpowered. Blade is also let down by how events are resolved; his unique thing is applying bleed modifiers to enemies. Unfortunately, Bleed damage applied *after* the enemy acts. The limited healing options means the overall strategy is not taking damage, but Blade's whole thing is accepting weaker cards/increased setup to in effect give the enemy more opportunities to attack you. The way the game is setup and self-balances means you aren't screwed by using weaker heroes, but then you have a mission where you bring out top-tier heroes and you are like "Oh, yeah, why am I using the other ones again?"The Abbey interactions is where the game really starts to struggle. The Bioware style of conversations and hanging out with characters is very hit or miss. Some are great, like just about anything with Ghost Rider; while some are just boring, like Magik. The quality is all over the place and it is obvious Firaxis was unsure how to approach the thing so they just threw everything at the wall. I'd say the character interactions are most similar in quality to Bioware around Dragon Age Origins or the original Mass Effect.Abbey exploration on the other hand is a combination of tedious exploration and fetch quests. The story is fine. I'm not a huge Marvel person, so I have no idea why people care about the Scarlet Witch so much and hearing her constantly brought up did get grating. The pacing of the plot also feels a bit off. I have no problems with the visuals. I'm running the game at medium on a 7 year old computer that was good when I made it. I have some massive but brief framerate drops when there is loading going on in the background, but nothing more than slightly irritating. The environment design is extremely boring, but thankfully the animations - particularly the superhero attack animations - are great and haven't yet gotten old.Soundtrack is surprisingly forgettable given how good the XCOM soundtrack was. Sound effects are also nice and meaty in combat.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game may have been my game of the year for 2022. I went into this game very much so not sure if I would really enjoy it. I never got into the XCOM games because of their output randomness so I was excited to see that this game revolved more around input randomness.I spent about 35 hours beating the main campaign, and I really enjoyed it. I would listen to and watch each cutscene but anything else I just skipped the dialogue. Most reviews you'll see will say that this game is broken into two parts, combat and life-sim. The combat is absolutely amazing. I played about 25 hours of endgame content just because the combat is so fun. The life-sim stuff wasn't for me though. I see a lot of people saying that if you like comics then the life-sim is amazing. I couldn't disagree more. I've been reading comics for about 7 years and have read close to 10,000 comics in that time. Close to 75% of those being exclusively Marvel comics. Still though, couldn't stand the life-sim part of the game. My reasoning is that it's just so damn long and I've never really cared for those types of games to begin with. The good news is though, you can just skip all the dialogue and never have to deal with it, which is what I did.For the DLC's we've gotten Venom and Deadpool so far. The Deadpool DLC dropped with a massive bug where you couldn't select him or change his cards which was lame. Though that has since been fixed. The Venom DLC is still new but is a good time. The DLC for each character is quite short but think of it more like the DLC being less about story content and more about a new playable character. With that in mind, Deadpool is pretty meh whereas Venom an absolute powerhouse.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately I had enough of a taste to request a refund of this game. I'm a fan of Marvel heroes and turn based games. But honestly you could have told me they just copied a middle schooler's fan fiction for this game's writing and I'd have believed you. It's just the most generic kind of story with the most generic versions you can imagine of Marvel heroes. The visuals look like this game was originally intended for a phone. Combat is a slog, having to sit through the same unskippable animation every single time you use an attack.There was a lot of stuttering as well. I am running great specs that run most games buttery smooth with no issues. This game lags on the MAIN MENU!It's also one of those games that won't LET you do basic stuff until the tutorial holds your hand through the process over a lengthy amount of time. Would you like to reposition yourself in combat? NO. We haven't shown you how to do that. You need an entire turn, text on your screen, and pictures telling you how to move first. THEN you are allowed. Rinse and repeat for every single aspect of a traditional turn based combat system. It treats you like an idiotic child. Which is exactly how I felt when listening to their dialogue, or watching characters do a flip in slow motion like it's supposed to be the coolest thing I've ever seen.If recognizing images of superheroes is all you need to enjoy a game, then this is the game for you. There's a huge roster. But don't expect them to say anything thought provoking. It's for Timmy Ten Year Old to point at the screen and freak out because he sees Iron Man.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is WAY under rated. Not a traditional deck builder and also not a traditional turn based combat game, but something fun and in between.  It's only real drawback is a pacing problem that makes the end of the game seem very grindy if you are trying to get most of the upgrades and best builds for characters. The easiest way to fix this is by playing 2 random missions between each story mission every time and doing the same for each DLC mission. That just makes the games timing and development feel better spent, instead of grinding missions at the end. I'd also recommend not opening any chests with Arcane keys until you can open white and blue chests for free. Even then, opening purple chests is kinda a waste of time.

_childDocuments_.review: WHAT A SLOGFEST! GOD. These superhero games are so annoying. Gotham Knights, Avengers, Guardians of the Galaxy. Can no one make a cohesive superhero game right now, except Spiderman (though Miles Morales was boring. Weak supervillain character.)?Like, this game is 80% narrative, friendship sim. WHO'S IDEA WAS THIS?! I want to slap them. It's torture to have such a fun gameplay system wrapped inside this hot, steaming garbage pile of a narrative. The story isn't good, the characters are soooo one dimensional, and the "choose your own adventure" makes NO DIFFERENCE in 20 hours of gameplay.This should be an XCOM game with an XCOM style pre-fight system. What we get is some Harry Potter meets Xmen meets Avengers knockoff written by people without an ounce of creative weight in their bones. Of the 20 hours I have in this game right now, maybe 5 of it was dedicated to actual gameplay. At least that's what it feels like.Before a fight (daytime) I have to:1. Chat with everybody.2. Scour the house for new drops.3. Chat with more people.4. Scour the grounds for stupid collectibles to unlock stupid "new gate blockage" remover spell.5. Chat with more people.6. Hangouts, havens, and stupid clubhouse meetings aka MORE CHATTING.7. Upgrade my base (finally something fun).After a fight (night time):Literally all the same stuff as above. Literally. Oh, except for the base building. So just the boring stuff!This game is so disrespectful to my time it's incredible. It's like having to sit through a timeshare presentation in order to get free tickets to a concert you really want to see. Like you really want these tickets, but you really don't want to have to deal with 4 hours of garbage to get them.I have gotten to the point where I spam through every message now. Blindly. I do not care what anyone has to say, except for the main storyline, and I'll tell you I've missed out on NOTHING.NEVER DO THIS AGAIN, DEVS. Fool me once, shame on you. Fool me twice, well, won't get fooled again, I'll tell you whaht.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely and mind-blowingly fun for Marvel fans.Addressing common negative reviews:For the comments referencing the 'cheesy' dialogue - I believe these players may be . The personalities, dialogue, and voice acting all perfectly portray these characters as they are in the comics. Firaxis did an amazing job at doing some of my favorites the justice they deserve. For the comments referencing how skins shouldn't cost real money- these are , so the people that have them already had to pay, you guessed it, real money for the higher game editions. It's  if you only want one or two. I don't think enough people that leave a bad review for this reason understand/know that these skins are part of premium, higher editions of the game.Some personal notes: I do think the female voice actress for Hunter is a bit... stiff. It's obvious she's not bad, but the direction isn't my favorite. Thankfully, her combat dialogue and model are awesome enough for me to overlook it. I'll be doing a Matt Mercer male Hunter run next. Great animations, engaging gameplay both in the Abbey and on the combat field. It's as difficult as you want it to be and as customizable as you want it to be, giving you a lot of freedom to make some crazy team combos. I for one really love to gather everyone up in one spot with Magik and let them taste Ghost Rider's sexy Charger or feel the power of the gd sun with Cpt. Marvel's line-beam-of-doom.

The characters are lovable, and people says that the script is cringe, but it's a comic-book-type vibe of cringe, which is great. But the game has SO MANY CRASHES. I've had it. It runs like garbage, loading screens take upwards of 3 actual factual minutes, and you have to sit in those loading screens for forever because it crashes all the time!The gameplay is mediocre, the traversal is only fun because the walking animation is bugged, so you look goofy sliding all over the map while standing completely still, the collection is so tedious, and it doesn't tell you what you're collecting all this garbage for until a substantial portion into the game, and the writing is more than corny.I'm gonna keep playing this, cause I spent $60 on this, and I'm too far deep in this, but god this game is frustrating. _childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: Everything I wanted this game to be. Amazing tactical combat mixed with deck-building mechanics and with some of my favorite heroes. I haven't had any issues with my game play or encountered any bugs so far. All of the complaints about stuttering and low frame rates are due to the 2K launcher. Very easy to bypass, just look it up. I did that very quickly and have had a smooth game the whole time.I can easily see myself putting in hundreds of hours into this game, especially with the upcoming DLC. I'm 60+ hrs in and only about 50% through the story because I've gotten so caught up on doing side missions and exploring the Abbey to build up my decks, complete research, and increase my relationships with heroes. I just find it so hilarious that I can go meditate with Blade or chill by the pool with Captain America. The interpersonal relationships with your character and between the other heroes is really entertaining. A bit goofy but it's supposed to be and that's what I like about it. All the characters are true to their comic-book origins.There are 8(?) difficulty settings that you can change at any time (once they're unlocked) so you can make the game as easy or as challenging as you want. I'm currently at Heroic II which makes it so I really have to think about my card plays but not so hard that my whole team will get wiped if I mess up.If you are a fan of any of these games then you will love Midnight Suns:Fire Emblem 3 HousesPersonaX-ComDivinitySlay the Spire or other deck-buildersany other Tactical strategy game like FF Tactics etc
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: Great concept. Good jokes. Strong characters I enjoy being around. Excellent gameplay loop. Could it be excellent? Absolutely! Is it? No, it's buggy as ♥♥♥♥. On one hand, there's a lot of clipping and sometimes dialogue lines will play over each other. There's an occasional bug where dead enemies are still standing up- they can't be targeted and the game recognizes that they're dead, they don't do anything or actually exist, but they look like they're alive. On the other hand, I have to undervolt my GPU to avoid the game randomly shutting down my entire computer. Even with that, junction temps reach 105 C in the pause menu- higher than actual gameplay. This thing is undercooked. It BADLY needs some patches. Unfortunately, the devs abandoned it after it tanked on release. Very unfortunate.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: Great game.  Some make the mistake of thinking it's a bit like XCOM, but it really isn't - there's some upgrades of your base, research etc. but it's  all pretty linear - I don't mean this in a bad way, it's just not distracting.  Equally the main gameplay, there's movement and attack. limited moves, and plays, but that's really it for similarities.However, onto the good stuff - it's great fun, almost puzzle like in the way you approach levels - move this guy here, bash this one into that one to hit this barrel etc. the grunt type minions are really meant to be squishy, so you feel like a real superhero.   I've played it 99% on my deck despite having a 3080 pc, and I think the graphics and performance are ace.  As for the fan service, I'm pretty into my comics but not over the top, so I am predisposed to this stuff, but yeah, it's very cool.  Loads of costumes (though most are colour swaps, there's still 3 or 4 distinct costume models for most characters if you have the DLC, and loads for the main character, who is extremely customisable aside from the face type, of which there are 4).All in all, I paid for the full DLC version, about £50 at the time, and don't regret it a jot, it's been my "killer app" for my Steam Deck and I'm 60 hours in and still going, not remotely bored.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

Users running at the lowest level (playstation 2 style) will enjoy the same, if not more, amounts of crashing as the users running at the max level (playstation 4 launch title with 7 FPS). Pretty good idea to let users save any time because the game will crash without warning in:      -combat mode     -crafting mode     -resource gather mode     -game-saving mode - useful if you are trying to increase internal panic and want to lose progress     -walking mode - SPOILER you get to walk as a marvel hero, in fact, mostly you get to walkSo some players don't care about crashing and that's fine. It literally feels like the game designers wanted to make sure users spent more time on ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and not the one fun thing they created. _childDocuments_.review: A few caveats to my review: (1) I only managed to make it 8 hours in before I couldn't stand it anymore (2) I came from playing XCOM2 and was hoping for another masterpiece by the company (3) From the trailers I didn't even realize that combat was played using "cards" you draw (perhaps a personal failing).In watching any of the trailers for the game, you get the impression this thing is fast paced, action packed, crazy awesome attack animations, etc. It has all that...sorta. They are the same moves every time, and you might repeat those same moves 20 times in an encounter. For me, the game started off looking freaking awesome. I loved how it was like watching an episode of a film series for the cut-scenes. I kinda wish they just took it in that direction. For me, every aspect of the game was an afterthought. You play day by day (in game days), and each day you get up, chose a team mate to spar with (you don't actually see any fights, just a comic style photo), chose a solo mission for a team mate, talk to anyone you can, do a mission, come back and "chill" with a team mate, sleep, rinse and repeat. Oh and the team mates ask these awkward "how should I handle this scenario?" questions that they as seasoned fighters would not really be asking. You also have to cozy up to your team mates, which was the most cringe thing about the game to me. It's incredibly scripted and cliche. They also over emphasize the polarity of everyone's attitudes, making everyone insanely 1D as characters. Between missions, when you are chilling at the abby, on an island that only one person can teleport anyone out of (seems like a really dumb idea in case she dies and everyone is just trapped there forever), they want you to explore the grounds/island. You assume the 3rd person POV for your character and try to explore around. The controls of it are clunky and you can't even jump, so a pebble on the path can stop you mid-run. Also the map controls are just terrible. You can't use the mouse to just drag it or pan, you have to use WASD and it just overshoots everything. While they want you to explore the island and perform some sort of side project for a dead lady, you're told it's not required for the main campaign, which I guess is nice but also adds to the whole "everything is an afterthought" vibe I kept getting. You get the game thinking your gunna be in combat most (at least half) of it, but nope, you gotta go help Nico set up a surprise birthday party and talk up your team mates to deepen your bonds with them, otherwise you can't upgrade them as well as you otherwise would. They also have an annoying loot-box aspect (why am I not surprised since so many games are doing this) reward from missions to get things for upgrading your cards. That alone is a mega turn-off. Also, the card aspect of the combat is just really not cutting it for me. I get that a lot of people seem to like it, and to each his own. View my review as a lamentation that I didn't watch a streamer playing it first so I knew that combat was a fraction of what the game's about. If I compared to mass effect series, I loved those games! They did a great job with the writing, and those characters really had some chemistry somehow, so by the 3rd game you really knew you'd miss them when it was over (after all the DLC was completed at least). So I do like the idea of bonding with your team, but the way it's done in this game is just so cringe (again, to me). I really wish I could refund, but there's no way to get a feel for how the game is going to be in only 2 hours. It took me about 4-5, and I kept going in the vain hope it'd get better. If you do wanna get this game, I just suggest watching a streamer for a few hours and you'll see what I mean. Maybe you'll like it, in which case absolutely support the company. It's a good company that made some great games. This just wasn't one of them imho.

_childDocuments_.review: Marvel's Midnight Suns is surprisingly fun, but I unfortunately cannot recommend it in good faith. It constantly crashes, is riddled with bugs, and stutters a ton, all while being a full priced AAA game with microtransactions. To be fair, if I did not look at the Steam page, I would not know it had microtransactions as they are very not in your face, but it still has them. The crashes are annoying and only made worse by an auto save system that saves very infrequently. The first crash made me lose 40 minutes of progress and since then I’ve been manually saving quite frequently to avoid losing much time again. The bugs are numerous and include things like small graphical issues, cards not doing what they say they’ll do, settings constantly resetting, camera randomly jerking around, seeing two of the same hero on your screen at once, not being able to interact with things you are supposed to be able to interact with, and not being able to move the camera on the battlefield. The game is also missing a ton of basic features, like an FOV slider and the ability to get a good top down view of the battlefield. The game’s tutorial told me about a tactical view, but it does not seem to work.Now that that is all out of the way, frustrations aside, I do enjoy my time in this game. The game is split into 2 parts. The first part is a surprisingly fun turn based combat system. I'm usually not the biggest fan of card games or turn based combat, but I do enjoy the combat in this game. It’s simple enough that I can just play without worrying about learning any complex systems, and its filled with satisfying sounds and animations. The second part of the game has you babysitting a bunch of adult children who all really want to be your friend and share all their problems with you. This is also surprisingly fun, mostly because I can laugh at it, but also because parts of the story are genuinely interesting. Besides, I don't think anyone buys Marvel products expecting great writing. During this second part of the game, you can also explore the hub map, but you cannot jump and there are many invisible walls, which just discourage exploration.Marvel's Midnight Suns is a fun game, but if it’s going to be charging AAA prices, it needs a lot more polish. Still, I got a cheap copy in a bundle, so I will continue to play it, even if I do not recommend spending your money on a product that is this poorly made.

_childDocuments_.review: I held off on getting this due to fear of it being a dumbed-down XCOM. In a way that is true, but now I am sorry I did not pick it up sooner. Combat is turn based and will remind XCOM fans of its combat. There are no & chance shots here so any strategy you use will actually work. I found this made the game much less frustrating to play than XCOM, though the tactics are less deep. I was greatly surprised by the graphics of this game - they are amazing. The textures and lighting look realkly good in 4K. The only complaint I have is that a few of the animations are stiff. This is more noticeable during 3rd person section of the game. Instead of an overview of the base, this time you control a character in 3rd person to explore around and have conversations. I found that this led to an increased sense of feeling part of the world. For someone who is tired of Marvel movies, this game is a major step in the right direction. Mature themes and jokes that are more than silly puns really add to the game.The customization and story have outpaced XCOM 2 for me so far and I would recommend anyone on the fence to pick this up.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game, bought the Legendary as a Pre-order. I have had ZERO issues so far. None. Not one. Hundreds.It's the best game I've bought or played this year. Period. Full stop.
