_childDocuments_.review: Marvel's Midnight Suns is a triumph, seamlessly blending compelling storytelling with a sincere focus on character narratives and the power of friendship. As a Marvel and gaming enthusiast, I found the experience deeply immersive.The narrative delves into the intricacies of each superhero's life, transcending typical tropes and enriching the overall gameplay. Midnight Suns stands out for its commitment to exploring personal connections and friendships, creating a more emotionally resonant story.Gameplay is a well-crafted mix of strategy and action, requiring thoughtful planning in tactical combat. Each character's unique abilities add depth to battles, while the polished graphics and authentic comic book aesthetics enhance the visual experience.Respecting the source material, Midnight Suns honors the legacies of its characters rather than relying solely on their popularity. Anticipation for a sequel is high, as the foundation laid in this installment promises an evolution of the narrative and new challenges for beloved superheroes.

_childDocuments_.review: Update after finishing the game. TLDR: Not a terrible game, but a disapointing one, so i'm leaving this as not recommended. Casual, if long, game for casual fans of marvel/superheroes, rather than tactical games.First impressions were mostly correct, with only minor changes. Game is split pretty much 50/50 between narrative portions of "walk and talk" and gameplay combat missions. The narrative portions suffer from mediocre to godawful dialogue and butchering some characters. There's way too much angst and fake drama in everything, the writers treat everyone like quirky teenagers in a soap opera, doing little more than talking aobut their feelings 24/7 while the world is ending. Not entirelly terrible, some characters are good, but major issues here. 6/10. Story narrative is mostly fine. Nothing special but cant complain.Combat gameplay is kinda fun, but in a super simplistic way. Its extremely easy, even pushing the difficulty as far as the game allows, its pretty basic, there's really not that much options or tactics variation. Heros mostly fall into basic categories of "multitarget damage/single target damage/support", with individual gimmicks doing very little to add options or variety. Difficulty also only makes the enemies spongier, the fights longer and more tedious, but not really more difficult. Enemy types are also pretty low for such a long game. You'll be fighting the same 5 hydra goons for 20-30h, though in lategame its a bit better.Some other random things:Visuals are good, especially on the in combat abilities.Game has a ton of cosmetic unlocks, but 99% of them are recolors of the same 2 shirts for most characters. Game is long, took me 60h, and with more sidemissions and other extra content could go to 100h. That's not a good thing imo, the pacing doesnt support that kind of lentgh, many gameplay aspects become really tedious by the end.A month after release technical issues are still there. Framrate sometimes drops 3-4x for no apperant reason. Extrely frequant crashes on going to bed/ending the day. ---Original first impressions:So far:The writting is atrocious, the dialogue is like a edgy "helo fellow kids" fanfic.The main character is unbelievaly boring, and with some of the worst voice acting in any game in years. Voice acting in general very sub par.Combat is a glorified puzzle game with minimal pretend-depth, that belongs on a mobile game. But with great attack animations. No mod support (the absolute best feature of xcom2) to sell the awful looking costumes in the mtx store.But if you're here, you probably dont care about most of that anyway, so here's the important part:Game stutters like crazy and crashes a ton. _childDocuments_.review: This game is okay. I wish there was a "neutral" rating, but alas here we are. There are more positives than negatives, so I'll "Yes" this game.If you ever asked yourself questions like, "What would Spider-Man post on Facebook and what would a comment from Blade in response look like?" this game will give you an idea. The game does fan service really well and large parts of it feel like it's (admittedly well-written) fan fiction. So if you're a Marvel fan boy, this will scratch that itch. I didn't like the main character of the Hunter as much because they're your typical "blank slate" character that comes off very shallow and bland to me. But YMMV.If you're looking for an X-Com clone, this might be what you want, but maybe not. The deck-building element is done really well, but there's less tactical depth overall. Most of the time you're fighting the same types of enemies with the same theme of maximizing your action economy, which is...not too different from X-Com. So maybe I'll take that back. Certain heroes have abilities that obviously synergize with each other better than others, and since they're all Marvel characters, there's no real opportunity to build a team of "Your Dudes", especially if you're min-maxing.There are certain minor inconveniences. It's not clear when I'm in a cutscene and have to sit through everything (otherwise I skip the whole thing) or if I'm having dialogue that I can skip through line-by-line. There are lot of fan service things you can check out; in my opinion they don't add much depth to the game but you feel compelled to do them because the HUD is always popping up all these notifications. Annoyingly, resting (which you do after each mission) triggers 3 cut scenes you need to skip.Overall, if you want an X-Com clone and you're a big Marvel fan, this will be what you're looking for. I'm admittedly not as into it as most people (much to the chagrin of my friends, who absolutely love this game and can't understand why I'm ambivalent to it), so it's a very "Meh" game to me at the end of the day.

_childDocuments_.review: THIS GAME HAS SOME OF THE WORST DIALOGUE/WRITING A VIDEO GAME HAS HAD IN MANY GENERATIONSWith that out of the way, holy moly is this game fun. I'm 30 hours in and still getting them. - Hub-world is really poorly designed. - Bizarre social/friendship system that probably could have been integrated much better. - Cutscene and facial animations don't hold up to the level detail you would normally see in a narrative-based game. Which this game isn't, making it all the weirder they tried pushing their models to do it this way.- Collecting resources is a very weird, unnecessary hassle.- The "Abbey Swimsuits." Some of the most fun I've had in a strategy game ever. + Each hero plays so differently and as you unlock new ones it keeps the gameplay feeling fresh.+ Similar to the above, trying various combinations of heroes in a team becomes an exercise in strategic theorycrafting that's super satisfying to watch play out. + Lots of choices to be made in regards to upgrading abilities, cards, technology around the hubworld, training certain characters. _childDocuments_.review: I'll try to answer the question that probably most interests you: Should you buy Midnight Suns? The game has two parts, which, without worrying exactly how much time you will spend in each part, we can just call halves. One half is the missions, which are almost entirely combat. The other half is spending time in the abbey and the surrounding grounds. This half involves: exploring the abbey grounds (finding lore, gathering crafting materials, some simple puzzle solving and the occasional combat encounter), hanging out with your companions (short interactive "banters"), base upgrading (similar to say Xcom), upgrading cards/tweaking decks and various crit path developments (cut scenes, acquiring new heroes etc). Almost everyone likes the combat in the game, so you will very likely like that. (It's turn based combat, but involves playing cards drawn at random, rather than having fixed abilities with cooldowns.) Thus whether or not will enjoy the game will very likely come down to whether or not you enjoy the Abbey half of the game. I loved the "banters", which are well written and well voice acted, but generally involve quite banal conversation or situations. You are (for example) watching a movie with Magik or drinking with Wolverine. This is definitely not for everyone. (Incidentally, the voice cast is a veritable who's who of famous VAs, if you care about that sort of thing. Also for you Dragon Age enjoyers, when Cap and Wolverine are talking it's the Varric/Oghren chat you never knew  you wanted!) Similarly, exploring the Abbey is not going to be for everyone. If you find MMOs boring you may not enjoy this, although unlike hanging out with your companions this is almost completely optional. I enjoyed wandering around the abbey, I found the lore interesting (roughly codices from Dragon Age) and hey, free crafting reagents! Hopefully that is enough information to allow you to make the purchasing decision that is right for you.A few other thoughts for those interested:1) The game is made with a lot of heart, which I appreciate.2) The game definitely has issues which I will group together as "polish issues". E.g. in my 200ish hours my game crashed say ten times? (An estimate by me). The crashed weren't too serious in that autosaves are frequent, but still - games shouldn't crash. The single use cards (essentially item cards, which you can craft) don't stack when you view them in your inventory. So if you have 3 of a card, the instances all show up separately in your inventory and not even grouped. You will have to go through every card you have to see how many of the same card you have. This just seems like something that the dev team didn't have time to fix, but it doesn't make a good impression. (It isn't a big problem for you the player, just a minor irritation, but  I'm just using it as an example.)3) Possibly somewhat at odds with 2) above, I think the dev team did make a lot of good design choices. I like the size of the Abbey grounds - big enough to feel substantial, and to let you explore for a good while (and to have new lore build on earlier lore, new gameplay build on previous gameplay), but not overwhelming. The grounds have fast travel points, and about the right number of them in the right places. The steady difficulty unlocking is excellent. I assumed you could only unlock one higher level of difficulty per playthrough (which would've been terrible) but in fact all the harder difficulty levels are unlocked, one by one, as you play. A lot of the personality choices for the heroes and voice actor choices feel good. Etcetera.I have a lot of more fine-grained comments I could make, but this review has gotten long enough, so I'll end it here. Hopefully it's helpful.

_childDocuments_.review: It takes a while to get going, because there is a LOT of dialog and the start, and not all of it is well written or easy to follow. But once you get into the game loop, you will be hooked in a "one more turn" way that Firaxis is famous for.The writing improves quite a bit as well, when it comes to the main story. Each character reacts to the story in a way that is authentic to the comic books, and for the most part their personalities seem very true to the comics. What doesn't really fit in are the "friendship" moments. Picking mushrooms with Wolverine or Blade starting a book club to hit on Captain Marvel is just.. bizarre. And if you're going to have a system like this, why not have romance?So the game loop of: wake up, get your new cards, start base upgrade, do card upgrades, character level, play actual mission, friendship build, world exploration for cosmetics, repeat, is quite addictive. You won't spend a lot of your time actually playing missions, and this makes the game LOOOOOOOONG. I am 70 hours in, and still haven't gotten my last character. The issue is I have spent a lot of time maxing out my cosmetics and friendships, and that means doing a lot of extra missions. Now I'm at the point where I kind of want to rush to the end and finish the game, because it's getting repetitive. That being said, the story is pretty compelling, and again the characters well interesting. Overall I'd quite highly recommend it for strategy fans and comic book fans.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a good game here, but also a lot of flaws. Be warned this is not your typical Firaxis strategy game. You'll spend about half your playtime in dialogue and lot of it can get pretty cringy. I'm not a fan of the typical Marvel-esque writing where characters are constantly spouting cliche one-liners and sarcastic quips and this game is filled to the brim with them. I've only watched a few films, but it feels like some of these character just aren't written very well. Half of them are childish, petulant, and annoying while the other half are the cliche stoic 1 dimensional do-gooders. They don't feel very heroic at all, it feels more like the cast belongs in a high school anime and are not a collection of the most powerful and heroic beings in the universe. Despite that, the actual tactical gameplay is pretty good and the only reason I'm still playing the game. The combat has its flaws as well though. 3 actions per turn feels very limiting. Many levels require you to activate an objective card within a certain turn, limiting you to even fewer actions. As a result, "free" actions are very powerful as well as cheesy ways to stall out the game.  There is a 'mod' system that adds random mods to your cards, some of which can be extremely powerful. After a certain point you'll feel like you're cheesing the game rather than winning it. The character level system seems utterly pointless. The game even automatically levels up your lowest level heroes and also scales enemies.And then there is a 3rd part of the game, where you explore the Abbey for resources, recipes and items. I'm also not a fan of this part of the game, but it's optional if you're okay with missing out on, you know, all of the cosmetic unlocks, recipes for powerful items, and a large amount of resources that make you more powerful. If I replayed this game I'd definitely skip the exploration part because it gets pretty tedious after a while and you just end up resorting to looking up wikis and forum posts.So why am I recommending this despite being so negative? The game is still fun despite the flaws. I just have high expectations from a high developer like Firaxis. It feels like 3 different games shoehorned into one and I really only like the tactical combat part. I kind of wish there was an alternate game mode after beating the game that just focused on the tactical combat, because rewatching/skipping hundreds of cutscenes in NG+ doesn't sound like fun at all.

_childDocuments_.review: As soon as I heard about this game, I was excited. I was a little hesitant when I found out it was card based, but I really like the system. It provides a different way to play a strategy game. The story is solid and feels like you're in a comic book. The interactions with your team mates for the most part feel natural. The game play is solid and the missions are fun. They do start to get repetitive if you're a completionist like me and want to be besties with everyone. Overall, It's a solid game that Marvel fans and turned-based strategy fans will enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: Memory leaks. Crashes. Random bugs. Yep, plenty of them. Grindy and repetative? At times, for sure. But still, somehow manages to be one of the best Marvel games around, featuring the most fun card-based combat systems I've ever toyed around with. Not only that, but Midnight Suns tells a heartfelt, well-written story that brings out the best of it's vibrant roster. Those of you familiar with these heroes from comic book pages will be pleasently surprised, as some of them are way better written than anything the House of M has done recently, but I digress.So, here's the gist of it: if you don't try hard and just enjoy the ride, without attempting to complete everything on your first run, this game is an absolute blast. Sure, you will hit a few bumps along the road, but the sights will be worth it. The core loop is almost addicting, while managing to offer plenty of lore for you to sink your teeth into. Not only that, but some of the plot elements are real heavy hitters, highlighting the human side of our favorite legends. Also, there's a dog and you can pet it and yes, it's a mechanic. There's no hiding the truth: even though this game offers tens of hours of content, it still feels unfinished at times. It's obvious that the scope of the project was planned to be way bigger than the existing product, with a sequel after-credits teaser to boot. Sadly, the outlook of that happening isn't that good as of today. But I hope I'm wrong. I hope that we do get that sequel some day. Because I'm 100% convinced that Moon Knight was planned to be a part of this game and there isn't a single force in the universe, capable of convincing me otherwise. But I'll have to wait out until we get a sequel in order to see my fav hero enjoy the fun stuff, donning gold. So, TL;DR, here we go: Midnight Suns is the best Marvel game since Ultimate Alliance 3 and one of the best tactical games of its year. And that's not "nuff said", but I emplore you to find out why yourself. Yes, it isn't perfect. But it deserves your attention and love. Mark my words: this will be a cult-classic a decade from now.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite having many good qualities, I'm going to give this a cautious thumbs-down for right now. The main problem is the pacing. Oddly enough, this game is billed as a tactical team-building TBS game akin to the XCOM franchise. While the best parts of this game do involve turn-based tactical battles, this is by far the smallest part of the game, and the rest of it bears no resemblance to XCOM at all. There is no "overworld" map you navigate and no tension between deploying teams for missions and map constraints. Instead, you will find you are spending the overwhelming majority of the game back at your "base", the abbey, interacting with the other NPCs in your team. This would be fine if it weren't for the fact that there is always only one -- one, and one only -- tactical mission you may select *per day*. The tactical missions are by far the best part of this game, and the interactions in the base area are simply not. The writing is not cringeworthy, but it is not fantastic either. It just feels off -- the character models look incredibly outdated, reminiscent of just slightly post-2000 Deus Ex models -- in stark contrast to the way the figures appear in the TBS section. It is hard to get as connected to them as the developers seem to imagine you would through the way they emphasize the interaction. Worse, they (the developers) seem to insist that the player be interested in customizing the outfits of the heroes -- it really feels like some sort of Japanese doll game. The "powerful" new upgrades you "earn" through completing the "challenges" (interacting with the other heroes) at the base are different colors for your doll suits. It feels quite puerile. The developers seem to have divined that there is not sufficient *intrinsic* reason to explore the base complex, as you are optionally tasked to do, and to spend all the time interacting with your teammates. This becomes evident in the way that extraneous bonuses in the way of floating blobs of resource-nodes are dispersed about the compound at various times, waiting for you to pick them up. You won't pick them up (and thus gather the resources) if you don't scurry about the compound, and thus a very small *extrinsic* incentive has been added to make up for the forced derailing of the game's pace. You gain "friendship" "bonuses" for interacting with your teammates, which frequently "award" you with new clothes and other customization options -- but the dialogue is not strong enough to engage you intrinsically. All of this makes Midnight Suns a fairly poor strategy game and turn-based tactics game. It's much more of a mediocre RPG (or JRPG) with an excellent, if underused, integrated TBS system.The concept is smart, but the implementation does not live up to the concept, and the pacing is ruined, lagging far behind the heroic claim.

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty good. The combat is a card and turn based tactical game that feels pretty puzzly. It's a lot of fun, the animations are great (though they might get boring in the long run), There is a large emphasis on using the environment, environmental elements can be used for attacks without cards and most card attacks throw enemies around and preferably into stuff (and each other). It's fun and requires some thinking and planning. Though it is a mixture of genres, it still feels new. There is the Abbey, where you spend most of your time between missions socializing, talking to people, training, researching, customizing the abbey and the characters, etc. IMHO this is a hit or miss thing. For me it's mostly a miss, I'm not a huge fan of running around and talking between missions. Fire emblem 3 houses, maybe persona 5 comes to mind. It's not bad, just not for me so much, but due to the characters I'm kinda ok with it, and you get a bunch of stuff this way. Now about the common complaints. 1, It's not xcom. It's not and it shouldn't be. It's also not Pokémon and not civilization 7, nor pirates! 2. This is Marvel's Midnight Sun and it has nothing to do with xcom besides the developer. Sure there might be some similarities in that you have a hub where you upgrade stuff between missions, but it's not xcom, it's a different game, and IMO it's ridiculous to even bring this up against a game that it's not some other game. For me, I'm happy that it's not xcom, I've played xcom a lot since 1994, and I'd rather play something different. I'll still play xcom 3 when/if it comes out, but I'm happier to see something else. 2, performance. Your millage may vary. For me, I had small stutters when I first started playing new cards, but they are gone now. There are conversations with characters that get unresponsive with low framerate for a few seconds sometimes, that can be annoying, but it goes away after a few seconds and it's fine after that.3, microtransactions. There is a premium currency and at the moment you can buy the premium skins available in the season pass with it. That's it, there isn't anything else at the moment in the in-game store. I was also against this trend when it started, but the reality is that microtransactions are part of the game now. And these are as mild as they come. If you get the legendary edition, you have everything. If you don't, you probably don't care about skins anyway, and these are just skins, nothing else, they don't make the game p2w, they don't add anything to it, just cosmetics. TBH at this point I couldn't care less. And if I look at it from a different direction, I always disliked Robbie Reyes' costume, but I don't give a flying * about skins, however if I don't want to see this Ghost Rider costume and I don't want to get the season pass, there is a way to change just that one suit for cheaper then buying them all. :) But yeah, I'm not a fan of microtransactions, but as long as they are just cosmetics, I don't see the point of complaining anymore. 4, no cloud save. This only seems to affect the steamdeck and can be solved by creating a symbolic link between the folders where it syncs and where it looks for the save game. 5, Denuvo. Now, this sucks. I don't care so much about Denuvo itself, but limited activations on a steam game suck. No excuse, especially as I don't remember seeing this on the game page when I bought it. It's there now... Still, IMHO the game is good enough to not miss.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game so much, I completed it twice. You don't have to be familiar with the Marvel universe to enjoy the game, but it probably helps. The story has nothing to do with the MCU, except for some characters and locations that were in the movies/shows.The game consists of three parts: There is a turn based deck builder strategy part. Then there is a team building/storytelling part, probably best described as Mass Effect with Marvel characters. And lastly there is also an exploration element for your base of operations and its immediate surroundings.How much time you spend in each of those parts depends on your preferences. While playing missions and some dialogue is necessary for game progression, the exploration part while benefitial is mostly optional.If you're not a big fan of running around and solving (easy) puzzles and/or listening to a lot of words, you should be okay with just doing the missions and the necessary research. The actual missions are 3d arenas where your heroes battle enemies by using abilities from their respective decks and hopefully some clever positioning. The rules and systems are easy to understand, but the fights get more and more complex as the game progresses. The game does a good job making you feel smart when you pick heroes that work well together and have their decks compliment each other.Excellent: music, character customization, voice acting, characters/playstyle variety, ability animations. Very good: Character and story progression, battle system, story, general animations. Good: Most of the dialogue, exploration and team building part.Not so good: Enemy types and mission variety outside of the story missions, some dialogue is just mundane filler, (rare) bugs during the missions.DLC is worth getting in my opinion, although I would recommend getting the whole season pass during a sale. It includes additional characters, with lots of new dialogue and a bunch of new missions/story with new enemy types.The second time around I played Game+ which was suitably challenging and engaging. The only weird part there was having all characters available right from the start, before I reached the parts where they actually joined the team according to the story.Get it if you like Marvel, Mass Effect and turn based strategy games.

_childDocuments_.review: So here's the deal with Midnight Suns, the game has some problems, maybe a ton of problems, It's still incredibly fun and easy to recommend if you like marvel and/or like strategy games. Even though it's the weakest part of the game I now wish the Abby was in Xcom 2. It's just so much more immersive being involved with your teammates and getting to see them as they would be during the times they don't have to be heroes.Bottom line, this game is excellent and has a lot of potential. _childDocuments_.review: I was intending to leave a negative review until around the 20 hour mark, in the end I really enjoyed the game, but would say it has two main faults.Firstly, the mechanics are very complicated. The time to proficiency is long, and running through all your daily tasks can feel like a bit of a chore by the end.Secondly, the pacing in the open-world Abbey portion of the game is wrong, as it allows you too much freedom at the start. You can get through around half of the exploration and questing within a few in-game days, which has two negative impacts:1.  It ruins the balance between the exploration and card battle aspects of the game. The card battling is by far the stronger portion, but you can spend so much time on the exploration in the early game, that it makes the card part feel like an after-thought.2. You do eventually hit a gate in the exploration part, and then have to wait several story missions to progress (without any indication of WHEN you'll be able to progress) and no longer have anything to do at nights.There is a tonne of content here, built around a really strong card game as the base. I would recommend the game, but caution you to pace yourself with the Abbey exploration, otherwise you may not find the first part of the game very enjoyable.Last thoughts - Magik is best girl.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm about 50/50 on this one.Pros: the mission loop is excellent. Deep strategy and team composition with unique tactical gameplay mechanics. I could honestly play battles over and over again and not get tired of it. It's also perfect in this regard for a portable device like the steam deck.Cons: The rest of the game. The whole Fire Emblem/Persona social systems for "getting to know heroes" and "hanging out" feels so tedious and lazy compared to the rest of the game. Where I gave praise for the combat being excellent, engaging, and even immersive with the amount of love and care put into heroes moves, this does not. Playing video games with wolverine, fishing with blade, or having a dance break with Dr. Strange totally takes you out of the experience and provides no real meaningful benefit to the story or gameplay loop. _childDocuments_.review: This is a fun card battler. I make the distinction not to say card game or deck-building game as there are very few cards for each hero (more than you can take into battle but not enough to "build" something around). I played on normal, and for the casual gamer in me this was a very fun experience. There are still tactics involved and some heroes work better together than others. Some play an obvious role, while others I had a hard time figuring out. The combat is solid. The "hub" part of the game is still very interesting to me since I like dialogue, narration, and lore. Plus, the mysteries around the Abbey were enticing enough to follow through on. The only real complaints I have are 1. This game does stutter here and there. It's not constant. They're in the same places and it's more like a loading stutter rather than an environment stutter (it'll stutter a couple times, and then be good from the rest of that "visit"). 2. The dialogue CAN drag on a little too long. Lots of conversations could have ended 5-10 lines prior and the result would have been the same. 3. The general mission grind. I'm not much for grinding for grinding's sake. So I modded that aspect after awhile where I get all general mission rewards in one general mission rather than having to keep grinding different general mission to get different resources. One thing people seem to have complained about but I literally never saw were microtransactions. I literally didn't see it in-game. And I was half-way through before I even realized there was a premium currency that literally never shows up or is brought to your attention. Maybe it's because I bought the version with the season pass, I don't know.Overall, if you're the type of person that can enjoy a game for what it has to offer, then this is a great game with lots of content 112 hours on my first playthrough (even though I don't like grinding, I am a completionist in some aspects: especially when it comes to reaching the highest level of things).

_childDocuments_.review: Jake Solomon suffers from the Sid Meyer disease alrightHe makes games that make players go "One more turn" and next thing you know, its 3 in the morning and you realize that your not in your 20's anymoreRemoving any bias of Comic book/Movie preference ,the core competency of the game is very entertaining to make it distinguishable enough from the XCOM franchise. The Deck Mechanic with the Heroism resource fueling bigger plays allows enough for casual players to get by and hardcore Trading card game players to build somewhat broken and full of synergy decks. Power creep is very real in this game. Early game, you feel a massive power disparity vs as you get higher level and unlock new cards. Combat offers enough variety in enemies and their tactics where you really will think about how to approach future missions.When your outside of combat, I'm going to be contrary to many of my peers on Steam, it often feels like a chore. Don't get me wrong, there is ALOT to do. Like Researching new things, upgrading your room, Upgrading ability cards, Sparing with other heroes, buy gifts. Etc. At first, it won't feel repetitive, but by Act 2, your sort of just trying to push through ANOTHER cut scene or another hangout or another reminder to do extra stuff in the abbey so you can get back to the tactical gameplay. So positive to people who do want a decent retelling of the Midnight Suns Comic run, but negative for people who don't have hours to dedicate to side stuff anymoreI've heard alot of people on youtube compare the Friend system to the Fire Emblem/JRPG Friend simulator approach, but there is  a very clear approach that every hero thinks you (The Hunter) is the BEST and they all want to be your friend. Sometimes it takes you out of the game when some of the more Gruffier characters are like "Let's hangout by the pool". I believe the intent is to build the sort of relationship attachments one might experience in Knights of the Old Republic or Mass effect, but it feels really forced and almost Fan Fiction style approach to the protagonist.Hero Selection is very diverse and will fill the need for most fan service or mild passive awareness of the Marvel IP. Some hero's clearly are well themed to their lore, and play well. Some however can end up being very situational and or a detriment to the end game.In my current play-through (Have not hit New Game Plus) I've had a multitude of Asset breaks, Frame drops, and even texture's disappearing. The Texture issues were the most prevalent and happens while traveling around the abbey, while in the GUI and even in combat. For the amount of attention to systems and subsystems the game dev's have attempted to provide, it suffers from the modern Triple A Approach of "Could use some more polish, but it's stable enough to push".The game is a good time despite my negative observations. The core of the game fills the need for Tactical Combat. I would agree with some of the other reviews, 60 dollars for this game is ALOT for release build. You can probably wait for it to drop to Sale price and or specials before giving it a proper play.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: A solid tactical core with a LOT of unpolished bits attached to it. And Marvel superheroes.Here's the thing: I don't know how to start this, because pretty much every aspect of the game can be summed as "it's alright, but...". There isn't *the* worst aspect of the game, but, by the same token, I'd be hard-pressed to come up with something that didn't have some frustrating bits to it.I suppose I can try to summarize what this game even is. It is, at its core, a turn-based tactical combat game combined with a card game. You enter (most) combats with three characters. You start with a number of cards randomly drawn from their combined pools and each turn you can play three cards. Normal cards give you heroism points; heroic cards and environmental attacks spend them. Then the enemies take their turn, but they instead each make an attack. Of course, in practice, this is a lot more complex, which gives a lot of tactical options, while still forcing you to rely at least a little bit on luck, but that's the main idea.And that system can be pretty satisfying when you execute a plan perfectly, especially when you manage to KO every enemy before they even had a chance to act. It's clear that a lot of thought went into it, with different victory conditions, different enemy abilities and properties, etc. The default difficulty seems fit even for people who aren't very good at tactical games, like me, and while you can't start on harder difficulties on your first playthrough, they get unlocked pretty fast and you can switch to them, should you so desire.Unfortunately, it seems that little else received even close to that amount of attention. There is no other real gameplay other than this, despite the combats being only half of the supposed game process: after each mission, you return to the "base" location, where you can talk to the other characters, explore the grounds, solve some puzzles, unlock some chests, get new costume options and color palettes for them, etc, etc, but I hesitate to call any of this actual "gameplay", at least it's no more gameplay than a walking simulator.The dialogue between the characters ranges from okay to "worst parts of Marvel movies", and it doesn't help that most of it takes place with them in generic idle animations, even in some supposedly manually-directed cutscenes. The characters have very little chance to shine and develop outside of you pestering them by hanging out with them and giving them gifts, which is a shame because when some attempt at developing them is made, it's usually pretty good.Of course, I also have to mention the main storyline. It exists. It's precisely as bland as you would expect. Bad evil person is destroying the world, we gotta stop that.There are, unfortunately, some performance issues and bugs, ranging from hilarious, like characters showing up in cutscenes in their swimwear, to annoying (saving the game can take several minutes sometimes for seemingly no reason), to "why the hell has this not been fixed", like the reward for finishing up the exploration of the main base just failing to appear where it should.The graphics are both pretty nice and outdated at the same time. The environments clearly had a lot of love poured into them, which is especially odd for a game where you spend most of the time hovering 5 meters above everything, but people look a bit... plastic-y. The lack of directed and individually animated cutscenes doesn't help. The parts I liked the most in terms of art direction were the hand-drawn effects, but they were so rare it almost seems like a relic from an earlier iteration of the development process.The voice performances were mostly alright, though I have to say, I really disliked the way the main protagonist is so blandly unemotional most of the time. This was probably the direction, so I don't blame the VAs, but, unfortunately, listening to their voice is kinda what you do for half of the game, so...Lastly, I enjoyed the DLC characters and their side storyline, though it didn't fit into the main story *entirely* well, with some characters ending up being introduced twice and such.

First off, i cant recommend this to everyone, but if you are wealthy enough to not care about essentially a double priced game and you like the idea of a superhero dating sim, then this is for you. First off, the greed is real here.  Game released with dlc already in the works and the game comes with pleeeenty of empty rooms to make you think theres gonna be a huge roster, or that there was initially going to be one before someone seems to have told them to save a bunch of characters for dlc. So they expect us to pay almost the full game over again for the last 4 characters bringing it to a $110 price tag(or 120 without the season pass). On top of that, they also included microtransactions on the EA feeling level of currencies in the game, and seemed to have purposely made things extremely time consuming for no good reason.  The roster seems to also be greed-driven, as with the midnight suns being more obscure and darker characters, it feels really strange that they also felt the need to jam in some avengers for popularity or something.  Of course they are still shoving captain marvel down our throats in every way possible, and they also tossed in captain america and iron man who both seem really out of place in the story, though their characters are pretty cool in combat at least.The gameplay itself is good, at least the turn based combat part, but honestly in all the time i played i feel like i was forced to spend more more time doing two other tedious things instead of playing the good parts. First, with the very drawn out dating mechanics that are not as optional as people say since they unlock very significant upgrades for the characters, its just weird.  Most of the voice acting and writing is good, it's just there is so much nothing in this game its crazy.  I never imagined id be spending more time taking Blade fishing or going painting with Dr Strange than actually playing the rpg combat, but i did, and not because it was fun, just because the entire game is tied into this kind of stupid friendship mechanic.  Why are these world saving superheroes suddenly needing to befriend one specific person in order to reach their true potential?  And when the world is literally at risk why do they still spend most of their time lounging around and talking about feelings?  Now I will say at least in these scenes, the voice acting is still mostly good apart from Iron man feeling like someone else, and the writing is consistently good as well, so its not that they're poorly done scenes, its just that there are far too many of them and they are far too important for the actual gameplay portions.The second part of the gameplay that also was strangely expanded to take up more time than combat was running around the hub.  That's kinda it, its not really gameplay, its just running around a building and the confusing winding paths in the surrounding forest picking up MMO style respawning ingredients and doing annoying scavenger hunts that sometimes completely hold up the game until you do.  Even though that's all there is to it, this part of the game is still so drawn out that after the bizarre dating mechanics this is the next most time consuming thing.  It honestly feels like at some point in development someone told the team to artificially inflate the gameplay duration as much as possible, and this is what they ended up with.  It's rare for a game to feel this much like it's just giving you busywork to kill time in between being able to actually play the game.Finally, the combat is pretty great, and could have been so amazing if they just focused on expanding it instead of all this weird stuff that seems to only serve the purpose of taking up more of your time. I can't comprehend why with such an obviously solid and fitting baseline for a combat system, who decided they should make two different facets of the game that overshadow it in terms of time spent.  I think I spent the most time talking to people in the endless dialogue that is only sometimes relevant to the actual story, and the second most time running around the same limited forest areas over and over again because for some reason the designers thought that should be also more focused on than the combat even though all you do is pick up plants or run back and forth a bunch of times collecting things to unlock new small sections of forest that ends up also just being the same kind of mostly useless after the first visit area and mostly serves to waste time after that when you go searching for something else.  It's very confusing how anyone could have played these 3 modes of gameplay and actually thought the combat should be the least focused one somehow, but it seems to have happened.It's weird though, this game did poorly and from what I've seen it deserved to, but not because of the core mechanics or it being a poorly made title, just because they had this massive focus on making you play tons of non combat stuff in a game where the combat could have been easily the entire thing combined with the game constantly seeming designed to make things just take as long as possible without feeling so torturous you just put it down.  Still since you can skip maybe about half of the talking and use google for the dumb scavenger hunt parts, if you don't mind dropping double price for a game, or just don't mind leaving out the last 4 overpriced characters, it could still be a worthy purchase maybe if you're on a loose budget or specifically like the idea of a marvel dating sim with some well done combat in the background.  Overall though, I feel like they really should have just focused on the combat entirely, and if they put a game out like that with expanded battle mechanics and functions, that game will probably be absolutely amazing.  I should also mention too for those who were following it before release, the "creating your own marvel hero" part is severely overplayed to the point of almost being misleading.  You can't choose powers apart from the usual picking cards from packs like everyone else, and while you can go dark or light powers, its not really much of a choice since the only thing it's based on is an alignment system that gives you a few perks here and there in place of where befriending people would be.   Also the appearance customization is extremely limited.  You have one body type per gender, no height changes or body type changes after that, not even face modification beyond picking one of 4 preset faces.  You're also nonsensically limited to realistic skin, hair, and eye colors for your ancient non human superhero, just so they can lock the other colors behind one of their purchasable currencies later(Which in a storyline based game is pretty wtf, like oh i woke up looking human but i somehow ended up with purple eyes and blue hair cause uh.. profit?).

_childDocuments_.review: I've decided to re-write my review of Midnight Suns after finishing the main story-line.  Overall, this was a very frustrating and negative experience for me.  Now, let me be honest.  I'm not the best strategy player in the world.  I'm not one of the super-stars of gaming.  Just an average old man who has more time on his hands than anything else.  Also, I play computer games for the "fun" factor.  And that is my biggest problem with this game.  It felt more like a chore than something fun.  All of the missions in the Abbey, while interesting, were really just time-sinks.  Just a way to pad the "time played" counter.  Yes you did get materials that helped you make up combat items and yes the combat items did enhance your gameplay, but in my opinion the same result could have been implemented with better loot drops from doing side missions.Some of the game mechanics were clunky and not very intuitive.  Take the "slide" maneuver, for example.  Your active Hero could use a movement point in combination with a hero point to slide into an opponent and knock them flying, giving you an extra attack in addition to your battle cards.  Sounds great, right?  Only it was totally inconsistent.  I cannot tell you the number of times that I was sitting on a movement point and at least one hero point and getting the "you cannot do that" error message.  Without any explanation as to why you could no longer do that.  Frustration at its best.Replayability is minimal.  Sure, you go through the main story and then you can do a "+" version, which allows you to keep your cosmetic unlocks, but starts you back at the beginning doing 5-10 points of damage with your attacks.  Whoopee.  And for $60, not much bang for your buck.Graphics were great and some of the interactions with the other heroes had me laughing out loud.  Way too many of them, however, had me wishing I had a switch so I could paddle their poor immature bottoms.  You can tell the writers for this game were of the current, "I exist therefore I deserve everything" generation.   For a group of "heroes", these idiots spent more time whining about how nobody liked them and how hard their life was.  You're a freaking Hero!!  You have skills and powers that normal people only dream about.  Boo Hoo...my mother was an evil person and didn't appreciate me.  It's like watching the Kardashians piss and moan about not being able to purchase an outfit from a specific designer.  Fake drama.  And boring as all hell.Not sure how to fix this game and given all the frustration and issues with the heroes, not sure I would bother.  Got it, played through the main story and that's all she wrote folks.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was my first exposure to turn- based card battlers. I didn't really know what to expect, but I thought "it's a Marvel game so there's gotta be some cool elements to it". I wasn't wrong.  This game has kept me captivated from the start. The gameplay and character development/ customizations are enjoyable, moreso than I thought they'd be. I enjoy the strategy involved in each battle and with several difficulty options to choose from, you'll likely find something that works for you too. There are many collectibles and side missions to keep you busy. The story line is typical of what you'd expect from a comic book series, but with way more emphasis on witchcraft, demonic possession and the occult (parents, it's a central theme of the game...you've been warned). An interesting, Sims-like focus is placed on developing friendships with your teammates. Fully upgrading a hero's abilities is dependent on the relationship the Hunter builds with them both in combat and around the Abbey. I will warn you, this game has crashed several times on my laptop, but not on my Steam Deck. I'm not sure why b/c the laptop meets all recommended specs and I use the same internet for both devices. The laptop loads via 2K while the Deck seems to load directly through steam. Maybe that's it?  Anyway, the point is the game is fun but over priced and the Season pass is DISGUSTINGLY overpriced. Definitely buy on steep discount. Overall I'm really enjoying the base game. User reviews and price have kept me away from the season pass for now. You can enjoy the game with or without the season pass, but you can't get all the achievements without it... weasel move, 2k. Base game 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: A Marvelous Fusion of Comics and Gaming: Midnight Suns Hits the Mark!As a die-hard fan of both comic books and video games, Marvel's Midnight Suns is a dream come true, seamlessly blending the rich narrative depth of Marvel's comic universe with engaging gameplay that had me hooked from the first moment.First and foremost, the narrative of Midnight Suns is an absolute triumph. The game weaves a compelling and immersive story, bringing iconic Marvel characters to life in a way that feels authentic and respectful to their comic book counterparts. The writing is sharp, the dialogue is witty, and the overarching plot is a rollercoaster of emotions that kept me on the edge of my seat throughout the entire journey.The inclusion of the Hunter, a customizable protagonist, adds a personal touch to the narrative, allowing players to feel like an integral part of the Marvel universe. The interactions with beloved characters like Wolverine, Iron Man, and Captain America are a fan's delight, capturing the essence of their comic book personas and adding layers of depth to the overall experience.Visually, Midnight Suns is a stunning spectacle. The vibrant colors, fluid animations, and attention to detail in character design pay homage to the iconic Marvel art style. From the fiery spells of Doctor Strange to the acrobatic prowess of Spider-Man, each hero's abilities are visually distinct and a joy to behold. The game's environments, inspired by iconic Marvel locations, further enhance the immersive experience.Gameplay-wise, Midnight Suns strikes a perfect balance between strategy and action. The card-based combat system is a fresh and innovative take on turn-based battles, providing a strategic layer that kept me engaged without sacrificing the fast-paced excitement expected from superhero games. Experimenting with different hero combinations and building synergies through the card system added a tactical depth that I found incredibly satisfying.The RPG elements, such as leveling up and unlocking new abilities, give a sense of progression and customization, allowing me to tailor my team to match my preferred playstyle. The variety of missions and challenges kept the gameplay diverse, preventing any hint of monotony throughout the campaign.The attention to detail in fan service is commendable. From the nods to classic comic storylines to the inclusion of lesser-known heroes like Magik and Nico Minoru, Midnight Suns caters to both casual Marvel enthusiasts and hardcore comic book aficionados, creating a tapestry that celebrates the vast and diverse Marvel universe.In conclusion, Marvel's Midnight Suns is a triumphant fusion of comic book lore and video game excellence. It's a love letter to Marvel fans, offering a compelling narrative, breathtaking visuals, and innovative gameplay that showcases the best of both worlds. As a comic book and video game lover, Midnight Suns has not only met but exceeded my expectations, earning its place as a must-play for anyone who shares a passion for the extraordinary.

_childDocuments_.review: What a game!Scratched that Slay the Spire/Three Houses itch I've been having for awhile. Plus, you can pet the dog every day and be rewarded for it. So, if that's not enough to warrant a purchase, not sure what is.Didn't see myself loving Midnight Suns as much as I did. Filled with fun battles, silly hangouts, an occasional groan-worthy line, and a whole lot of heart. Complaints regarding the writing are severely overblown, in my opinion. If you've seen, and enjoyed, anything Marvel in the last decade, you'll know what to expect. I will note, however, that on rare occasions I got struck with visual glitches on the map or a character falling through the map during a battle. Nothing too game breaking or an easy reset didn't fix. I forgot how much I enjoyed Marvel when it got "weird" and dealt with the occult. My favorite Marvel "thing"! Has rekindled my interest in comics and looking to collect a few involving the characters as soon as I can find em!

_childDocuments_.review: Not a fan of the $50 season pass, but man this game was great. The last time I grinded out a game like this was when XCOM 2 released. No, you won't have to worry about 99% chance of hitting and missing (for the most part). The combat is well developed and there are MANY levels (on higher difficulties) that require more than just using whatever card/heroes you want and still winning. The mechanics are smooth and well developed. There is an endless amount of replayability and everything is well animated. Although I experienced some stuttering issues, it didn't affect my gameplay at all. There is a lot of depth into this game and the Abbey environment that you explore is a humongous upgrade compared to XCOM 2's menu UI of research, upgrades, etc. I liked the pace and many of the challenges. There are a lot of surprises, references, and a lot of dialogue that I can appreciate because of how much time went into creating the depth of the characters and the environment. As a big Marvel fan, I can further appreciate the interactions they threw in between all of the other characters as well. Albeit parts of the story were kind of lacking, it's something that is easily looked past.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely blown away, the combat is fun and tactical with a dynamic scaling model (based on the highest level hero) so the fights always feel like a challenge and you have a bunch of different difficulties to choose from!The voice acting is excellent (shout out to Laura Bailey on Magick) and the interactions between the Marvel heroes are just brilliant, I found myself just stood listening to them chatting away!I'm 65 hours in and barely half way through Act 2 as far as I can tell (no idea on how many acts though!).If you like deck builders like Slay the Spire and you like tactical combat like in X-Com you should get this!

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent tactical game wrapped in a so-so team "hangout" layer.Let's be honest - FIraxis was never that good at writing.  It wasn't a problem with XCom because nobody cared about the story much.  In Midnight Suns, the story and characters take center stage, but the writers couldn't bring them to life.So, why the positive rating?  The combat is really well done - possibly as well as XCom2 + XPac.  Just treat the superheroes like you would Bradford - click through the chatter and enjoy a great tactics game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is seemingly two games in one.  First there is a terrific card/turn based combat game which I really enjoy.  I don't love the card based combat system but it works in this game enough that I don't mind it. Second there seems to be a friendship simulator written exclusively by people trying to revisit high school where apparently they did not actually talk to anyone.  It's sophomoric and frankly embarrassing to play.  I'm talking Captain America and a 300 year old demi-god/demon talking about high school drama.  It's ridiculously written and at times I honestly can't believe anyone okay'd it.  It also takes way more time to play the friend minigame than you spend actually doing combat.  There are few enough great games in this genre that I still count this as a thumbs up but if I could buy this whole game minus the entire friendship side, I would much rather have it that way.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: Ok there is a lot so in the likeness of this game let me tell you a long story.For anyone who wants the short version:+ Combat amazing+ Deckbuilding cool+ Superheroes!- A lot of Story! (like out of my 50 hours at least 60% of that was story)The long version:This game is no X-COM 3 and while yes I would love a new one instead I got another new game that build up on the ideas and weakness of our beloved franchise. No more missed shots, no more going step by step  overwatch passing the turn waiting for a enemy patrol. This is fast paced combat that you need to setup with deckbuilding your own heroes. Each and every single one with their unique playstyle. I love it!The story is ok nothing crazy interesting here. Most of the time is spent in the "dating sim" talking to heroes getting to know them and raising their friendship levels for those sweet combat bonuses. After a while this gets you in a nice rythm of prep mission, do mission, do story and repeat. I actually did enjoy the small spins on all the marvel heroes (not all of them are straight ripped from the comics or movies) but everyone got their own opinions on that.I should say sth about the cash shop but so far it is just skins and you don't even realize there is one. Like I got no clue where I could even buy the currency xD. There will be dlc characters but we'll have to see how much they cost. My conclusion:I love this game and hope we see more of this combat system in future games!

_childDocuments_.review: Long game is long. Too long. Should be like 40 hours at best. Useless DLCs that cost an arm and a leg. Horrible MC face animation that basically forces you to always use a full-face mask. Uninspired repetitive gameplay that forces you to use characters you don't want to use. Lazy writing. Boring bosses. Dull challenges. Repetitive crafting. Stupid collectibles. All it all, it just adds up to a jury-rigged mishmash of characters, mechanics and it's not good.Would have been ok if not for the overall length of this tedious endeavour.

_childDocuments_.review: I am very picky when it comes to turn based games. This is one that is on my favorites now. The combination of card decks and combat scenarios are where it really shines. I was constantly trying new decks and new character combos. The game has a lot of variety when it comes to the core gameplay loop. Personally I thought the story could have been deeper, but it takes a backseat so the gameplay can really shine. I found myself loving general missions more than story missions. Exploring the abbey is a fun puzzle, but lacks deeper lore than a couple collectibles. Would have really liked to see more universe building in the abbey. The character moments were very enjoyable and conversations always seemed fresh. The comedy in the dialogue I felt was charming and well done. I am a cheesy joke guy though, so warning if you don't like cheesy or goofy jokes.From stargazing with Spiderman to reading a book by the fire with Magik, this game has plenty of moments where characters shine. In summary, characters were done well and mechanics are fun and evolve nicely. Story was nice but would have loved some deeper moments.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's address a couple things first.  Starting with microtransactions.  If you though you were going to pick up a game that has 2K involved and not see microtransactions then you clearly are not paying attention to the gaming world of late.  That is what 2K does in villainous abundance in their NBA games.  However, I can say with confidence that the transactions in Midnight Suns are non-invasive and purely cosmetic.  You can 100% ignore them and you will never know that they are there.Secondly, the launcher.  I am not sure the complaints about the launcher, but it is not such a big deal.  Ok, yes, there are some that are having trouble with Denuvo, but in the long run the launcher is no different that ones that come up with games like Cities Skylines or Railway Empire.  It's just a small hassle on the way to playing the game.Now, the game.  Fantastic, intelligent, quick, and deep tactical game play.  The story is a bit boiler plate at the start, but it does get much deeper as you go.  It is a joy that some side quest missions will have super villains reappear throughout the course of the game.  No longer do the bad guys feel like one and done bumps in the road on the way to the end credits.  Bonding with your team matters, and makes you more powerful in general.  I love the relationships that form between the characters.  Sure, your character might seem a bit meh at times like saw dust, but the more you dive into a relationship the more detail you uncover into your character, and thus the more they feel like a true character.This game is excellent for strategy lovers and Marvel lovers alike!Also, edit the game to bypass the 2k Launcher:Steps to remove the 2k Launcher (from the article)Step 1: Start by right-clicking Marvel's Midnight Suns in your Steam library, selecting 'Properties', then the 'Local files' tab. Click 'Browse'.Step 2: In the Explorer window that appears, open up the 'MidnightSuns' folder, then the 'Binaries' folder, then finally the 'Win64' folder. You’ll see an .exe file named 'MidnightSuns-Win64-Shipping' – hold Shift, right-click on this file, and click 'Copy as path'.Step 3: Go back to the Steam Properties window and click the 'General' tab. Paste the path to that .exe into the Launch Options field; it should along the lines of "C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Marvel's Midnight Suns\MidnightSuns\Binaries\Win64\MidnightSuns-Win64-Shipping.exe", including the quote marks.Step 4: To the end of this path text, add a space, then "%command%" (not including the quote marks). Then simply close the Properties window, and the next time you launch Marvel’s Midnight Suns, it should do so straight from this executable, skipping the 2K Launcher.

_childDocuments_.review: Listen. This game is AMAZING. There's so much story, so much to do, so much to explore, that I'm about 20 hours in and I've only done a handful of the story missions. Lilith is an interesting villain, and I'm not familiar with much of the Cthon lore, so learning through this game has been very fun.Speaking of fun! Like with the media surrounding Guardians of the Galaxy, I love being introduced to characters I knew only a little about. Especieally when they're this well done. I knew a little about Ilyana, but all i knew about Robbie and Nico were their hero names (and that Robbie has a SOV kinda sorta). Now I love them all, I feel attached to them the same way I do the Guardians and I'm excited to see their stories unfold! More Blade is always a good thing, I've been a fan since the films and this Eric is infinitely approachable and a powerhouse on the battlefield. I love him slowly opening up to your Hunter and the others, I can't believe how real these friendships feel. They're so well-written, and I'm actually drawn more to the Suns than the familiar Avengers (with the exception of Carol). Combat is a blast, especially once you've gotten the hang of each character's unique playstyle. My favorites to have on a team with my Hunter are Robbie and Carol, but Magik's portal usage comes incredibly in handy and each team member plays in such a way that you can't go wrong with any of them! I love upgrading abilities and using the environment to help thin the numbers of enemies, combat never gets boring or feels slow. Sometimes it feels overwhelming, but as you level up abilities and upgrade your training area you get little actions that make the action economy feel more expansive. I'm addicted to this game, and I'm so, so glad I was able to get it. I'm looking forward to more DLC characters to expand my friendships and more zones of the abbey to explore! 10/10, this is the most fun I've had with a single player game since GOTG!

_childDocuments_.review: I liked playing this game. Being a fan of Marvel, it's always enjoyable to interact with characters from this franchise.But in all honesty, Midnight Suns is full of defaults. They may not break the game (although...) but they still destroy a big part of the fun.Let's start with the least important(in my opinion): graphics.I played this game on the highest quality possible. And yet, there were quite a few ugly things: Peter and Tony's haircuts that look like hair from a Playmobil, Hunter's was barely better, Logan's body hair that made me think he got assaulted with a sharpie, the whole cast's faces, the cat Ebony's body and several others.Next, we have the two main parts of the game: the interactions mechanics and the fights mecanics. While the later can be considered correct, if a bit weak on several aspects, the former feels rushed. Every character sings the praises of Hunter very quickly and lots of characters appear obnoxious in their behaviour. And that, when they're not downright contradictory: one day saying this, the next one saying the opposite (looking at you Robbie).Then the bugs. Sweet baby Jesus, the bugs. I'm not sure even an early access has that many. It goes from texture bugs(dissapearing map, Abbaye's walls looking like they're covered in colored postits,...) to models bugs( dissapearing bodies, frozen ennemies, heros hitting the air yet still reaching the ennemies, Wanda's energy still stuck to her hands in the Abbaye,...) along with sound bugs(out of sync with attacks, game stuttering during each and every Limbo transition when Hunter replies,...) or simply crashing, multiple times. I even think the latest update worsened them.And finally, what utterly destroyed my love for this game. I could have ignored everything mentionned above. Just, not giving my opinion on this game, good or bad. But there is cosmetics. Cosmetics you can only buy with real money. That, along with the fact you need to litterally pay the same price as the game to have all the DLCs, is simply unacceptable. I know Disney, and so Marvel too, are losing money nowadays but that's no excuse to give us an unpolished, expensive product.There is still a lot of things I could mention. The lack of character's animation in the Abbaye, the 'dancing' clothes when the camera angle changes, the attitude of some characters that made me want to slap them. But that would be overkill.At least, you can pet the doggy. I guess it's something.

_childDocuments_.review: It's very difficult for me to recommend this.On one hand the combat is very fund and I totally loved it (apparent from the hours spent on side missions). I also loved unlocking hero cards and upgrading them. The Abbey gameplay (running around, talking to heroes, hangouts, collecting stuff) is okay, although a huge amount of cosmetics can seem intimidating. By the end I had unlocked the ability to purchase them with ingame currency and I could equip almost anything I wanted, so it's not that bad. Only ones that remained locked were bought with real money, but I don't really care that much. Writing is not the best (comparing to Guardians of the Galaxy at least), but it is fair and you can skip most of the dialog.But, and this is a big BUT, I've never had a game crash this much. Maybe you will be blessed by the Unreal 5 gods and it will run OK on your machine, but I wasn't so lucky. I can honestly say that 80% of the time I haven't closed the game properly (hitting exit), it just crashed to desktop. I tried all sorts of fixes I saw online, I also bought the game months after relase, so there were a few patches. Stability was improved, but I still get a ton of crashes and I consider myself lucky if I can finish a mission without a crash. You can save after each turn and continue, but not on every mission. Some are 'challenges' and the challenge is actually for the game to run for 4 turns. There are also parts where the game seeming decides that this particular mission is not for you and crashes after every action. I've had to restart and reload the game 5-6 times until I give up and try the next day.The DLC is also extremely expensive. I had interest in the extra heroes, but it costs as much as the game, so no thanks. If it was around 20 euro, maybe I would give it a shot.Anyway, as you can see from game time I've endured the game for quite a while and there is a lot of fun to be had, but the stability issues can be extremely frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: Midnight Suns is a bizarre mix of a dorm living simulator and a tactical, card-based RPG. The graphics and optimization leave something to be desired, but the love the team behind it has for the source material, and their commitment to their weird Mystical Marvel X-Com shine through, innovating on established formulas enough to keep the game challenging, while still letting players access the explosive power these characters are known for. It's not at all what I expected, but I loved it anyway, and I encourage anyone growing increasingly weary of Marvel to give this taste-breaker a try, as it really does show a different side of the franchise rarely represented outside of comic books, with the all-star voice cast from other Marvel projects (Steve Blum as Wolverine, Yuri Lowenthal as Spider-Man, Nolan North as Deadpool, etc) only adding to it's uncanny appeal.It's as weird, uncompromising, and dark as any Midnight Sons comic run. And I wouldn't have it any other way.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm coming at this game from a seemingly different angle than most reviews I've looked at.My interest in Midnight Suns stemmed from games like Across the Obelisk, Gordian Quest, and others of the same ilk. I consider myself to be fairly hardcore when it comes to card games, strategy games, and party battlers.I need my games of these genres to have real meat on their bones, layers upon layers of systems, real (but fair) challenge, and good reason to delve deep.To put it simply, Marvel Midnight Suns is checking all of the boxes for me.Let's get some of the hogwash out of the way. Performance is supreme on a 3070 + i9-10850k. I've played 12-15 games with Denuvo and I've NEVER had an issue or saw poor performance. And just to throw it in, using google is just as invasive as having some anti-tampering software attached to a game. Furthermore, this dev team deserves every last penny. Lastly, if you're living such a fast life that having to press one extra play button on a launcher is what ruins your day, then you need to take a giant step back and reassess your time management.Now, on to the good stuff.The game is gorgeous, the audio is delightful, the full voice acting is pretty damn good, and the writers definitely had a fantastic time with the script, lore, and dialogue. Give these writers a raise, but if you don't spend the extra money on the animations behind the voice acting.The story is the umpteenth iteration of save the world from the big bad evil, but who cares about the over-arching premise. The real draw here is the characters, their desires, motivations, quirks, and the interactions between them all. Some of the A to B from mission to mission is ham-fisted, but again... who cares. It's a FUN superhero ROMP. Heck, I've laughed out loud at more of the humor in this game alone than in every other title I've bought this year combined. I'll say it again, it's FUN.Systems are plentiful, able to be accessed and progressed at a good pace. There's a lot of stuff to do. Some might see certain things as fluff, but if you really throw yourself into each system, they build upon each other quite nicely.There is also a pseudo-persona/life-sim element wherein you have different sections (re: times) of the day that you play through. Basically upkeep/socializing in the morning, combat in the afternoon, and tying up loose ends in the evening. Now, don't read that too literally. It's more dynamic than that, but you get the idea.Now, the stuff that I originally was drawn to this game for:Deck-building and progression is pretty freaking great. There is a lot of room for creativity, theorycrafting, planning, and so forth. I've been deck-building since I first picked up Magic The Gathering in the late 90's. Homebrew or bust in Hearthstone, Legends of Runeterra, and others. At first, Midnight Suns will seem lacking, but trust me, the systems get deeper as you go, and eventually you'll be coming up with all sorts of decks.Decks for combat are an amalgamation of three 8-card decks. These 8-card decks are particular to each character, and each character eventually will also contribute to your stratagems with passives, stat growth, and other boons unlocked via social systems.All-in-all, it's dope and I still have some features to unlock that will really send the deck-building into the stratosphere.Combat is equally dope. Tight, fresh, fluid, dynamic, and fun. Strategy is important, having a proper team is important, preparation is important, and it all culminates in thrilling, challenging, and engaging magic, bullets, and fisticuffs.Each round you are able to play three cards*, with a drawn hand of five*. The hand draws from your total deck at once, so 24 cards* (8 contributed from each character brought into a mission). There is also a free Redraw of two* cards per turn, a free Movement action once* a round, and the ability to use consumables.You'll notice many asterisks above because there are ways to manipulate and bolster nearly every aspect of the "rules" to combat.In addition to using your own cards, you'll also be using the environment, and even the enemies themselves to conquer your foes. I won't spoil every last detail here. Just know that there are A LOT of ways to accomplish your goals, and you'll definitely feel like you're playing the way that YOU want to.My buddy who has also been no-lifing this game today and yesterday has a COMPLETELY different "main" party compared to me, and the character that we both use (outside of the protagonist) is built to perform a totally different role than my version.From what I can tell, there are 2-4 ways to tailor each of the available characters for battles.Before closing this out, I'd like to say that there are SO MANY aspects to this game that I didn't think would be a part of a game like this. At the same time, it feels right, rather than everything but the kitchen sink.I would say that anyone who's even remotely interested in card games, party battlers, or strategy games should give this a whirl. If you fancy all of those things then you need to stop reading these reviews and start playing straight away. You will not be disappointed. You'll be doing yourself and your free time a service.I hope you enjoy the game as much as I do!F*** Hydra.

_childDocuments_.review: A great tactical game with some fun social sim elements as well. If you like Marvel and the characters in the picture, and you like XCom or Fire Emblem, you'll probably enjoy this. The gameplay is a little bit different--it's card-based, which I know turns some people off, and it's not based around things like hit chance (hitting is automatic when you use an attack card). But while the general missions can get a little bit repetitive, they're always introducing new twists in the story missions (that will then get recycled into the filler general missions) and it keeps the gameplay fresh. The social simulation is also great, letting you form bonds with Marvel characters that feel organic and sincere. There's no romance, which is a little bit of a bummer for me personally, but there's very much a sense of found family which I love. Also a surprising open-world side-quest area that's unexpectedly robust and satisfying. All in all, a unique and extremely fun experience. I know it didn't do very well so my hopes for a sequel aren't high, but maybe they'll adapt the systems and do an X-Men or Avengers game. Well worth your while if you enjoy tactical games or social sims!
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game, with fun card-based tactical RPG combat and a lot of great character writing.  It is, unfortunately, frontloaded with a LOT of talking- but once you get past the tutorialized stuff and the introductions, the gameplay follows a really satisfying and fun loop.  Building individual character 'decks' out and then seeing how they play off of one another in combat is really interesting, and with a roster as strong as this game has (a great mix of prominent and semi-obscure characters) there's a ton of interesting combinations to find.There's a lot of love put into this game and it's characters, and a lot of fantastic design put into the gameplay.  If you like Marvel stuff you're going to really enjoy this, especially if you love seeing superheroes in a casual setting getting to know one another.  It honestly offers an experience that's completely different from any other Marvel game, focused on the characters and who they are instead of just showing off cool superpower moments.
