_childDocuments_.review: I have not played Castlevania 2 so I'll refrain from calling this "castlevania 2 but good" but either way this is an amazing non-linear 2D sidescroller.The best feature is the morality system, it's not a nuanced morality system, just righteously good actions and dastardly evil ones, but every choice has practical outcomes. Only did a good playthrough but even good actions with immediate rewards have bad outcomes later.So glad I bought this on a whim.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game, which instantly takes the top spot of the genre.A few years ago weirdly enough the Hentai game "Midnight Castle Succubus" was game of the year for me as it was basically a really good spiritual successor to the NES sidescrolling RPGs (Adventues of Link, Faxanadu, Battle of Olympus, Simon's Quest) with some arbitrarily tagged on erotic content to market it as an adult game.Now Infernax doesn't go the hentai route (except for one picture with bare breasts), however it also does incorporate some of the hentai platformers ideas, such as every death giving you a unique death animation.The platforming in Infernax is the perfect mix of challanging and not too mean spirited, riding the perfect spot between frustration and motivation. Of course you get a bit angry if you die, but you're mostly angry on yourself for not having nailed that jump, instead of blaming the game too much. And for those who are blaming the game still, there is an easy mode and cheats.So, it's a very good Simon-esque Metroidvania-ish platformer, but I want to highlight a couple of things that usually fly under the radar of other devs.- There is a photosensitivity option, toning down flashes and such. It works very well, without ruining the immersive moments.- Dialogues are kept short and too the point. It doesn't devolve into reading a visual novel to progress through the game. Those dialogues happen with NPCs in town, your game doesn't get interrupted by misplaced "cutscenes". There is an art to the less-is-more approach and Infernax nailed it.- It's one of the rare horror games, which doesn't devolve into animal-cruelty or other offputting triggers. Now it is gory, yes. But it's a game that provides escapism rather than showcasing every mundane cruelty. The enemies are all creatively designed demons, there are no cheap shots, where you go kill the fauna, because the designers couldn't come up with an enemy design. There's the occasional crow pecking, but it flies away and is not subject to attacks.What is admittingly a bit weird of the game is that you only ever have one weapon (the mace and shield) and you only get stronger versions of it which don't do anything special. And you also can upgrade your damage with XP. This is weird for two reasons. For one, when you buy better armor, you take less damage and XP upgrades your health pool. But what the interaction between better weapons and XP damage boost is, isn't really clear.And then again, there are other weapons in the game - but these are restricted to subsequent playthroughs with other "classes" or an in-game event, which effectively change your class midgame. Contrast that with Battle of Olympus, where you had your basic club, then got a fire shooting staff, then got a sword which does not shoot, but overcomes resistances and finally you get a lightning shooting sword, which is strong, but the shot isn't as usefull as the firestaff. So, you have a reason to switch to another weapon thoughout the game. In Infernax you are stuck with better versions of one weapon, yet weirdly can switch back to less good ones.However, these other classes with their respective weaponry are very well integrated into the game. So, they do this giant efford, which is worth of a standalone game, yet is just put in as a gimmick. Imagine an icecream truck, who just sells vanilla icecream, you look in the back see all the delicious other variants and the truck driver tells you that those are secrets, you only get once you finished your vanilla icecream. That being said, it's still a damn awesome vanilla.Any complaints about the game I might have are really minor. Like "oh that animation when you get a new item is 3 seconds too long".This game is absoultely awesome, takes the top spot of the genre, gives me enough and leaves me looking forward to a sequel or even some endless rogue-dungeon dlc thing or something. Unless you are put off by the gore, this is an abusolute recommendation, even if you're not usually into the genre, this is such a good entry that you might just wanna try it anyway.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: A brilliant hybrid of Castlevania 2 and Zelda 2.  You have the world design, music, and gameplay of Simon's Quest, but with the exp and leveling system found in The Adventures of Link.  A run through the game is not terribly long, expect to spend probably 7 hours on your first time around and maybe 5 on subsequent laps through the game.  It is important to note that this game is designed to be replayed as there are choices made during the game that change not only aspects of the gameplay, but the ending and even the final boss.  Aside from this, there are a lot of extra unlockables and easter eggs along the way.  If you loved Castlevania 2, you will love this for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: This game brings me back to the NES days of gaming and felt like a spiritual successor to games like Battle of Olympus, Castlevainia 2: Simon's Quest, and Faxanadu. If you enjoyed these types of games in the 80's and 90's you will not be disappointed in Infernax! Well worth the price even if it is a fairly short game.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: while many people, myself included, have compared this game to a simons quest (castlevania) type experience, i would argue this game's flow is more like a darker Zelda 2 sort of play. the experience is pretty highly refined, and the game itself has many accessibility options for difficulty and play adjustment so its up to the player to really decide on their difficulty experience. the additional (secret) character options all give good refreshes to the game, with varying style and in some cases even new music for certain areas. this was an incredibly enjoyable experience for me, and if you enjoy games like zelda 2/castlevania simons quest then pick this up. but know that there are some metroid-esque elements, but i would argue the game itself is not actually a metroidvaniaalso as an additional note, when playing with the cheats, do NOT enable/disable the jetpack with other cheats at the same time (do jetpack first and leave the menu, then go back in and do whatever other cheats you want), as it appears to cause a softlock as of current build (hangs on black screen) observed on windows desktop and steam deck
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute treat of a game. Not only is it entertaining in terms of mechanics (like everything is very tight and polished to the point that you can totally abuse the game if pay attention to how things work), the variety of magic, skills, and the way the story unfolds makes it interesting for a number of playthroughs. I mean, there's a total of 9 endings to this game. And you get SOMETHING in return for each and every one of them: be it a new character with a unique weapon or a different set of mechanics altogether, or a secret code that adds some whacky but cool feature that you can turn on and off at will. Like in the good old days of gaming.Oh and the pixel art and music in this game are absolutely superb. Check them both on the internet if you fancy, because the screenshots don't do justice to the awesome boss screens and cut-scene elements of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Well done. I'm not a huge fan of pre-SOTN Castlevania games, but I enjoy this because even on classic mode there are regular save points. I would recommend this if you like Shovel Knight (except Infernax is a metroidvania, not level based) but also are into the Berserk anime/manga; it's a weird blend of those two things that manages to be fairly effective in it's world building.I would have maybe liked to have seen additional weapons, but with all the spells and abilities it's not too bad.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of the best games I played this year. 10/10. The game is challenging and does not tell you where to go. You get so familiar with the villages and characters that you know exactly what to do whenever they mention a person or a place.  The game takes you for what you are, and it can be as challenging as you wanted to be. I cannot express enough how good is this game, so do yourself a favor a get this game right now my lord.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Play through this Castlevania type game and see if you can bring home that 80's nostalgia! This game is good on so many levels, because one, you could just play it and have tons of fun and not really care what you doing other then bashing monsters in the face, but you could play as a super good or evil person, or find a way to get an ax or a sword (heck even a gun!)Overall I was super impressed by the game, since most of the time I finish it and thats it but I am already going through my 2nd play through with it!
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the top RPG metroidvanias I've played in some time. I wish more games like this would release more often, cause I can't get enough of them. It's quite hard, but not unfair hard. I've finished it multiple times and it didn't get old yet.If I have something to criticize, that would be that the game is on the short side of the genre, but for how short it is, what we get is high quality, and it has some replay value to it with its multiple endings.9/10.It's short, but it's a very good retro metroidvania from beginning to end.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: I'll preface that Faxanadu was my favorite game growing up and I've played through it several times over the years when I get that itch and I've been looking for something new to scratch that itch most of my adult life. This game is that game.Overall I'd highly recommend this game. I've played through it several times now and will probably revisit this game in the future. To avoid spoilers I won't tell you why you should play through it several times but I will tell you that after playing through it you will find new ways to play that change the game and make it a different enough of an experience that I didn't get bored.The only thing I wish this game had that it didn't would be more gear and weapons. While the main character wields a mace it would have been nice to choose a sword, axe, etc as well as different types of gear that would change my combat style or appearance and offer different benefits.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: It's not bad, but has issues.First is that there should be checkpoints before the bosses, or at least a little closer to them. If we game over to them we have to slog our way through half the dungeon, which on most dungeons isn't too bad, but on later ones it is hell, literally.Second is enemies only drop gold, but with the health/magic system, they definitely should occasionally drop health and mana. The only ways to recover these as it is are limited potions and checkpoints, which only appear halfway through the dungeons and certain spots on the overworld.Last is the weird enemy balance when it comes to your arsenal vs enemies. Basically all the bosses are designed so you can reliably beat them with just your basic weapon if you're patient enough to dodge their attacks, the magic just makes them a bit easier. On the other hand many of the later non-boss enemies are next to impossible to fight without using magic, either they teleport or fly out of your reach, or they have such insane reach of their own actually dodging their attacks after smacking them is hilariously difficult.Downsides out of the way, the different endings and interactions are rad, no spoilers.Being able to just turn on godmode and fly if you're not enjoying a segment was also thoughtful, though I wish we could turn them on and off at will rather than just at overworld saves, as I wanted to fight a certain boss legit after skipping passed the annoying enemies in the way.Enemy variety is very satisfying, the many different ways enemies attack you and the different methods to counter them feels very rewarding, especially since we have a whole book to fill up. I think this is my favorite part about the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Started out strong, but quickly began relying on mediocre platforming with constant instant death as a consequence.  I could have dealt with the ultra-specific and awkward enemy hitboxes and their  ever-increasing spammy attacks, but the bad platforming and ultra-sparse save points don't do this game any favors.  I won't ask for a refund but this goes onto the uninstall bonfire.The art and music were pretty great, at least.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Decent enough game that takes more than just some inspiration from older NES games.I'm down one playthrough so far, i'll see if the novelty of the game stays fresh after multiple playthroughs. Would i recommend it ? Sure, but do expect the game to be flawed on many aspects. Pros - Seems the studio is from Quebec, that's always a plus - Graphics work great for the game, it is very reminiscent of the NES / early SNES- Music is enjoyable and does remind me of stuff like Shovel Knight- Short enough to be done in about 2 sittings. Took me almost 9 hours, and i,d say at least an hour and a half to two hours were mostly cheap platforming deaths ( See Cons)- Many easter eggs that made me laugh out as i found them.- Multiple "paths" adds to replayability- Magic being used for some puzzles is a lovely touch. it's not just about combat- Seems there are unlockables after each playthrough, including secret characters, that might add to the lifespan of the game. Cons- Janky controls. I suppose they wanted to emulate the older castlevania games, but there's a reason they stopped making those games back then. The game seems to have problems with quick controller movements, often sending me into the sky and / or ending a jump attack abruptly by doing the ground pound attack. Add to that the fact that you never entirely know if you're gonna undershoot or overshoot a charge since you don't see far enough ahead on some maps. - Lack of "long range options". The main character is very limited combat wise, especially when tricky enemy placement  complicates jumps and such. There's a reason why the old Castlevania games gave you secondary weapons. The closest you get are a few spells that just cost too much mana to be worth it, especially since during a good portion of the game you cannot replenish your mana "on the fly". As a whole, the magic system didnt feel right to fill that spot- The armor system. Does it even work below the 4th one ? I cannot say i saw any tangible difference between the rusty, chainmail and silver armor. Same with the shield spell. I did notice a sudden increase in defence with the last armor though. - Hit boxes feel off. Hard to describe it, but often felt like attacks i did should've hit, yet i end up being damaged by some enemies that seems out of reach. - Lack of enemy variety. Sure, there's a lot of "reskinned" enemy, but it usually boils down to the same enemy with the same attack pattern, only with more HP. How many time can you fight a Giant Skeleton with a sword and not get bored ? - Bosses are mostly a joke. Final boss on my run i litterally stood there and spammed attack and it was over before i knew it. - Insta Death Pits / Hazards. At this point i feel it's a staple, and a crutch, for indie platformers. Coupled with the jank of the controls, it's just gets overly frustrating to mess up a jump because an enemy was in a slightly bad spot or because you sometimes stop dead in your track during a jump hitting sometimes, yet sometimes you slide on the "side" of the block you'd have hit.

_childDocuments_.review: this is one has a very mixed feelling for me. I have followed Berzerk Studio for years, played a lot of their games, and as a fan of the genre was really looking forward for their rendition of a metroidvania game, more Castlevania 2 than anything else. I like the setting a lot, I love the music, I love the animations, it's super fluidy, I enjoy the gore and bizarre choices thoroughly of the blood and visceras and stuff. It's really nice to hit things with a mace and the animation is very good, it feels 'heavy' when you swing.  I love the difficulty of it, the mobs and bosses patterns and tricks that you have to learn etc, but the controls are not adequate for the tasks of platforming/precision jumping they propose. The game is hard on purpose, of course, to make you die a lot and expend time repeating the same dungeons a lot, falling from places etc, but at the same time it clearly is made more difficult by poor polishing/programming. There are a lot of times that the combinations of key pressed to do some movements (air dashes, 'super' jumps, stuff like that) are simply not recognized by the game in the time window you have to execute them. I play on the keyboard and I play a lot of hard metroidvanias with precision platforming and never had a problem that couldn't be bested with a 'I'LL GIT GUD ò.ó' attitude, but this time it didn't work. Most of the times I overcome those areas in the game it feels like luck and not skill and it's not readly repeatable. I bought this game at launch, played a lot and waited for a few months before writing this review because I thought they would release a patch or new version that would address it, but they didn't. I thought it was a problem for keyboards, but reading reviews from people that played with controllers saying the same thing I cannot recommend the game, unfortunately.

_childDocuments_.review: Ahh, the days of games like Castlevania 2, Zelda 2, Metroid.....all those old classics that left us with a feeling of having a huge world to explore and no hand-holding, just you trying to figure out where to go, what to do, and using your brain as well as your skills to figure it out and conquer it.Infernax is like all those. It doesn't hold your hand, even though you do get clues and hints on where to go. It's hard but in such a fair way that you don't feel like the game is trying to destroy you and make you cry.You play as Alcedor (or whoever you want his name to be) and you're a weary duke returning home from the crusades to your duchy, which is now overrun by horrific abominations and undead. What you choose to do from then on is in your hands. Wanna be the good guy duke and help your subjects, saving them from the darkness? You can do that. Wanna be a royal jackass and cheat, steal, and even kill those under you? You can do that. Wanna be an evil jerk who realizes he's been wrong and seek redemption at the very end? You can do that too! There's loads of ways to play and many different endings to seek out. Everything you do has consequences in some form....and it all works.In many ways, Infernax feels like a love-letter to those old games we used to love growing up (well, if you're at least as old as I am, being in my nearly mid-30's), but features enough modern complexity to let you choose from numerous paths and develop your own story. It's a merging of old-style gaming and modern gaming, and the fusion works.+ Pros +-Gameplay is smooth and easy to learn. Inspiration from retro games thankfully didn't include that old janky style that felt stiff and cumbersome.-THE MUSIC. I LOVE the soundtrack.-Varied moral paths for the player to take during the game, letting you explore what you want your character to be, and those choices affect the storyline.-Length. Several times, I felt like I was about to finish this game in 1-2 days, but it's actually longer than that, especially if you take time to explore everything. It took me about 9hrs to beat my first playthrough, so there was plenty of gameplay for a first run and yet it didn't noodle on too long.-Replayability. The in-game library contains special books you acquire for beating the game with different endings, which contain different things, such as artwork and shout-outs to backers, so collecting more of the various endings gives you more to check out. But also, some of them contain codes to input at the Name Select, allowing you to play a totally different character type (one makes you a wizard, for example), allowing for a new gameplay style altogether.-Cons--You do learn quite a few spells, but many of them see very VERY situational use. I played the Ultimate Good path and only truly ever used three spells....the Shield, Healing, and Fast Travel spells....of the 8 total you're given. Might be different as the wizard, but even then, I hardly used magic except to stay alive or travel.-Most of the skills are useful, but the down-smash had a habit of wanting to activate when I didn't want it to. Might have been my controller, and SOMETIMES this wasn't an issue....unless I was having to make jumps across water, acid, lava, or pits....-The final dungeon is BRUTAL if you follow the Ultimate paths. It's a very long level with many boss fights, loads of hazards, the game's toughest enemies, and the only way to save and regain HP, MP, and lives is to hike through it all back to the beginning. Even if your stats are maxed, it's still very rough.-Unfortunately, part of the retro-experience is also a con as there are a few obscure things that may not be obvious at all on a first playthrough. Most of the choices make sense in some form how they affect Alcedor's alignment (killing people willy-nilly is USUALLY a no-no), but sometimes the choices aren't clear what they do exactly (the one about the Caged Demon in particular stands out). There's also a LOT of endings, and some are specific in the steps required or would require the player to do things they may not know they CAN do.Overall, Infernax was an AMAZING game, one I sorta watched for a while, and I'm glad I did. If you're a retro gamer who appreciates the classics, PICK THIS UP. If you want to play something with a retro-feel cause you didn't have the chance to play those old games, I'd recommend the same. It's fun times and worth the amount, cause there's a LOT of game here.

_childDocuments_.review: [Introduction]Infernax is a game that takes a lot from old NES games like Mega Man, Castlevania and Faxanadu.However, what sets this apart from regular retro games is the story and ... wicked sense of humor.[Graphics]The GFX are crisp, clean and detailed. Animations are pretty good too, bit on the sparse side for some enemies though.However, dying in this game is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ treat where a lot of enemies and of course the bosses have custom animations where they kill you in extremely graphic and gruesome ways. The screen goes all red as it happens, adding an artistic flair to it as well. Beautiful to the extreme.[Sound] The SFX and music are on point and there's absolutely nothing to complain about here. Some of the themes in this game though make your skin crawl with how devious they sound. And of course the gory sound effects really help too! [Gameplay]The game difficulty comes in levels which is always appreciated and with some incentives to try and play the game again in a different way or two, or maybe change some choices, you've got replay value too if you want it. However, there are a few design decisions with quest references that sometimes are so obtuse that you end up wasting half an hour before you relent and search online for the answer. Also, there's some things that you're just simply not told, as in how jumping works. (protip to players: Learn what coyote jumps are, they come up in one dungeon or two)[Story/World]The world of Infernax is lovely, it's a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ treat for all the senses. It's raw, it's brutal, it's like you put the original id guys in a room and told them to make a NES era game. And, my absolutely favourite part of this is the fact that your choices you make matter in the game. And no, it's not always obvious what your choices will result in even though it might be seemingly simple ones. My tip to players is to go through the game and remember which choices you made. Then, on the next playthrough, do the exact opposite. The story is pretty standard fare, but the NPCs in the towns and especially in the oh so nice bars are fun to talk to. But overall, the thing that stands out and makes this game excellent is the very special attitude of it. There's a sort of undercurrent of grim humour and slapstick connected to a lot of the things in the game. It successfully straddles the divide between silly and too serious and gives the world a very special odd feel to it. I have a feeling that this is one of those games that I'll just keep coming back to every few years or so, because it's just so damn unique. [Summary]This is an absolutely amazing game that captures that old mysterious feeling that Faxanadu gave you back in the day. It has a few minor issues, but overall it's a really nice adventure!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is more about law and chaos than about good and evil. Combined with the disturbingly detailed art, the writing does not pull any punch to portray the torment and agony of our MC, the Duke of Upel. Being worn out by previous crusades, the Duke is already at his limit from the beginning. Yet, his responsibilities as a leader bind him to confront ever more appalling horrors incarnated on his homeland. One small crack in his sense of discipline might start a chain reaction that leads him to complete corruption, or his sense of generosity and benevolence might backfire at him with unexpected failure of his duty. Some may find this type of story as plain disturbing and unnecessarily stressful, but I found it rather thought-provoking and inspirational. If you are also sick and tired of the "good guys are destined for success and happiness" type of stories, I recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Some slight spoilers:After completing my first playthrough of this game (did an ultimate good playthrough), i can safely recommend this game to anyone who like games like Castlevania II Simon's Quest, Zelda II, Faxanadu, and any other side scrolling adventure game that falls under the same type of gameplay.Although the game isn't too hard if you're a seasoned platforming gamer, the game does have a couple hard platforming segments that might irritate you at first. Or just irritate you completely if you die on the same room. The way you level up is almost exactly the same as zelda II. Where you kill enemies to get exp and then choose which stat to upgrade. Though only on save points. Even the spells might be familiar to those who have played and mastered zelda II.One major difference between the games its similar too though is a karma system. Where depending on the type of quests you complete and actions you take will determing both your ending and alignment.  For example, deciding to kill a ruffian instead of taking his bribe is considered good. While drinking with some vagabonds is apparently evil (you'll see why when you try it). One other interesting tidbit is doing enough evil deeds will change your appearance and choice of weapon.If there is one thing i have to say about this game in terms of cons is some of the rooms in some dungeons. Eapecially dungeon 4 which for some reason has way more instadeath traps than dungeon 5. As i stated before, the game has some difficult segments. But some of them are just brutal. Just hope by the time you get to these parts of the game that you're actually ready. Otherwise expect to lose all your lives and restart back to a savepoint.Overall, the game is pretty solid. I like the ye olde game feel the game has and the cryptic moments, and the challenge is right up my ally. Its a pretty cool metroidvania game with quite alot of gore. As said, I'd recommend it to anyone who likes these kind of games and can stomach some pixelated gore (and boobs).

_childDocuments_.review: Probably Berzerk's best game so far. I love JSB like everyone else, but Infernax is an incredibly well-realized vision from start-to-finish that clearly had lots of thought and care put into its design. It's an excellent homage to a style of game that doesn't really get made anymore, and it pulls it off with boatloads of style and grace. And difficulty. It gave me some heart palpitations at one point. However, the juice is worth the squeeze and I found the experience to be very rewarding once I understood how to clear some of these extremely difficult screens.My only con is the difficulty curve in some dungeons is a little absurd compared to others. That and the solution to a couple puzzles / difficult jumps aren't as obvious as they could be.9/10, fantastic video game and another big win for Berzerk!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hyper violent little Metroidvania that's definitely worth the price of admission.You're a duke who has been away from his country fighting in the crusades. You eventually return home only to find that its been overrun by demons.  A mysterious cult has also appeared, though their intentions aren't immediately clear.  Will you banish the demons using your own strength, or will you side with the cult and pursue a different path to power?  Pros:- Multiple endings, including good and evil routes and multiple joke endings- Oodles of nightmare fuel, cenobite looking bosses with different attack patterns- Side quests that are actually worth your time (none are fetch quests, and several of them have great rewards or hidden bosses)- Several villages to explore with their own host of problems and politics- A slightly more relaxed difficulty mode option that gives you an extra life and more save points- A moral choice system that leads to some great animated sequences- Fun, nostaglic art styleCons:- There's a bit too much backtracking before you get your warp spell- Some of the moral choices are a little too ambiguous . . . so it's easy to lock yourself out of the pure good and pure evil endings- It could have been a few hours longer for a single playthrough (clocking in at 5 or 6 hours), though it's designed to be replayedIf you're a Metroidvania fan or a Castelevania 2 fan, this is a game that's worth checking out.

Different actions lead to story paths for different endings and replayability. All around I found it fun and very enjoyable. Starting my 2nd playthrough as I type this.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, but flawed.A pleasing jaunt that pays homage to the oft-maligned second entries in the Zelda and Castlevania series, Infernax also adds its own unique twist in the form of dozens of small quests with good and evil outcomes, allowing you to choose to be a benevolent crusader or a corrupted lord. Not just a narrative element, each path has several unique upgrades that can change how you approach its six dungeons.  Clean pixel art and a punchy soundtrack round out the best of the the package.Infernax also has some aspirations at being a Metroid-like title, and that's where it stumbles.  The abilities you get are serviceable, but the strange choice to freeze you in place before performing any of the movement tech leads to a clunky feeling.  The power fantasy of careening through rooms maintaining momentum doesn't manifest here.  The other major fault is the lack of a scrollable camera.  Whereas many 2D platformers allow you a limited degree of looking up or down to see if the jump you're about to attempt could be a disaster, here Infernax locks your view to around the character.  Several times I fell into a deadly pit I knew was there, but couldn't remember the exact location, or I took a challenging upper platforming section when I could've dropped down and simply walked if I'd only known the ground was safe.Ultimately, Infernax is a solid five or so hours of retro-inspired gaming; however, don't be fooled by "only five hours."  On top of the alternate paths, there are several secret characters that make repeat plays fun again.  If you can deal with controlling a character who's more Simon Belmont than Samus Aran, it's worth checking out.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Freaking awesome game. Picked it up after seeing them at pax last year. Their set up was a recreation of a 90s family room with a CRT, your parents old sofa, and OG gamer snacks. The game is awesome. It's obviously a labor of love from the developers and it shows in the game play and details of the game. The game is meant to be played through multiple times. You can play through helping the good guys, or the cult in the game, and you can also play through with a number of different job classes. Yes, buy this game. It's worth it!
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Infernax is an authentic retro action-platformer that harkens back to the old days, blemishes and all. That said, it does have several features to make the game less harsh than those older titles. Difficulty and accessibility options (not to mention a good ol' cheat menu) makes the game much easier to get into compared to old games.For me personally what really stands out is the unique presentation, from the over-the-top pixelated gore to excellent music and witty writing. I also appreciate how the game lets you get lost sometimes, and you may have to find your own way to where you're supposed to go or what to do.In short, if you're into retro games, this is easily worth full price! Otherwise, it's still worth a look!
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent metroidvania that is clearly a love letter to several games of the NES era, most obviously Castlevania 2 and Zelda 2, but with plenty of nods to others.  Gameplay is excellent and the provision of two difficulty modes makes it approachable for pretty much anyone.Most importantly, the game provides some of the best couch coop I've ever seen in such a title.  The second player is a first class citizen with an entirely separate set of skills and upgrade paths from the main character.  The game also provides instant drop-in/drop-out support.Plenty of replayability definitely seems to be there, as well, though I've only completed the game once so far (Couch Coop on Classic Difficulty).  Worth noting that my hours played is skewed (because it was played primarily offline), but I'd say it took us somewhere in the realm of 8-12 hours to beat.  Probably one of the best games I've played this year, I honestly cannot recommend it enough.To the devs:  Please make more of this and inject it directly into my veins!
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Just beat the first two bosses so far, but I must say to all fans of the older Castlevanias:The graphics, music, and gameplay are all an open love-letter to that series, only further improving on the tried-and-true formula that has made them nostalgic must plays. Everything in this title is on point, and there's even a few direct references to Castlevania within ( - I'm willing to bet there are ).So again, to fans of the genre:You certainly won't be disappointed, and can thank me later; I'm off to hunt down the rest of the bosses...
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: +++ Stunning enemy and boss design.+++ Catchy, memorable soundtrack.+++ Two difficulty settings with no penalty for choosing the easier one.+++ Precise controls in the basics...--- ...Floaty controls when the going gets tough.--- An excess of instant-death platforming.--- Alternate endings demand senseless grinding.This is an uncompromising title that wears its own design decisions openly, and is 100% aimed at those who entertain a die-hard fondness for the 8-bit and 16-bit eras.  Compensating the lack of creature comforts is a wonderfully sordid story featuring blood and guts galore, and satisfying combat where every crunch of the mace feels well-earned.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Zelda II + Castlevania II. Hard but fair. Multiple difficulty modes. Multiple accessibility options. Baller soundtrack. My one gripe is that most of the platforming skill jumps do not fit with the aesthetics of the somewhat awkward jump mechanics.  Also a minor annoyance in classic mode: falling into a pit of lava means exiting to the Title Screen no matter how many lives you have left. Otherwise it's a great game. (I haven't run into an ice level yet though. Slippery ice platform mechanics get an auto-thumbs down.)
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: I went into Infernax almost fully blind. I've heard good things here and there, but didn't know much of the game. I am glad that was the case. Infernax is one of the most fun games I've played in quite a bit. It's a beautifully crafted love-letter to Castlevania 2 and Zelda 2, but written by a person with the fanciest calligraphy you can think of. It takes what made those games great, replicated, and at the same time got rid of the frustrating and annoying. Infernax controls smoothly and feels snappy. The soundtrack is incredibly well done and fits the adventure. The script is clever and funny. The powerups feel very rewarding.If you are a nostalgic gamer, if you like indies, if you enjoy adventure games, if you wanna hear some bangers, and see some monster blood, grab this game, you won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: I'll say that the game is generally solid and will fill an itch for those whom enjoyed NES era games, notably Castlevania and Zelda 2. It also attempts to have replay value with multiple endings, and having a good/evil side play through, however it wasn't enough to entice me to play again, notably since it's missing NG+ options to carry over some of the grinder elements.There are also some frustrations carried over from the NES era that I wasn't pleased with, notably death pits with enemy placement made to make certain areas more aggravating then needed, dungeons that have locked door dead ends after a few rooms, to force you to back track into rooms where enemies have respawn, and just a generally lack of direction. I won't say the game is bad, but these elements also tied to multiple ending on completely different playthroughs, with nothing carrying over really sours the experience for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: As a person who grew up in the late 80's and 90's I have played many games like this. If you didn't I still feel that the younger generation could get entertainment out of this solid game. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished my first playthrough at about 7 hours, and I had a really awesome experience.If you ever wanted to play a modern retro take on Castlevania 2: Simon's Quest with many quality of life improvements, then I highly recommend this game.The Good:- Controls feel very responsive.  Extra Spells and abilities you can buy or unlock really match well with overall feel of the experience.- Main and side quests give you extra things to do and secrets to unlock.- You can play the game in casual mode instead of classic if you want to avoid losing some of your gold and experience when you die.  (I played through the entire game on Classic.  Not sure if it impacts achievements to play on the casual setting, etc.)- After 1 playthrough, I only unlocked a little more than 50% of the bestiary, so there's a lot of content.- Replayability:  I got the good ending the first time, but it seems like there's additional Bad, Perfect Good, and Perfect bad endings to play towards.The Bad:- The Jump arc feels a little weird and floaty at first.  Once you start to unlock the other mechanics to navigate the level design, it makes a lot more sense, and you get used to it eventually.- There's about 4-5 points in the game where the platforming might seem a little cheap, but you just need to power through it.- There's a few puzzles I had to lookup online because none of the dialogue (I found) in the game seemed to clue me in.  Some might find this a little cheap, but I didn't mind.- You have to play the game a certain way to min / max your decisions to get the Perfect Good / Perfect Bad endings.Overall:  8 / 10  (I hope they make a sequel.  This game is really well made!)

_childDocuments_.review: There is not a single thing about this game that I don't love!I also played this on XBox so have more hours than listed here. I loved it so much on Game Pass that I went ahead and bought it here on Steam.It's all a perfect time capsule of and sums up perfectly an era of gaming that I miss dearly.The aesthetic is spot on, the music is fantastic, and the over-the-top gore is an unexpected bonus that I find hilarious.  The easter eggs are superb!This game evokes the same sort of excitement that I felt the first time I saw my cousin playing a Nintendo. Where I knew that was something I had to have and sink an exorbitant amount of time into.Despite loving the many generations of video games styles that came after, the Nintendo era is the one i remember most fondly and still to this day love the most. It was nice back then being able to turn on a complete game that required zero logins and with zero fuss just play the game.  The games themselves were also simpler in structure.  There was a simple goal and just focus on the goal. The difficulty made completion feel worthwhile. Infernax has this essence built into its DNA but adds modern touches that the adult me can appreciate like altering the narrative based off of key decisions, the upgrades, the map and the easter eggs. Balancing the difficult with a sense of progression. I feel like they did these parts right as they just feel like interesting aspects of the game instead of the entire point of the game itself.The bigger point of this game to me is in the action, the platforming, and the mystery. It brings these elements together very nicely while also keeping the actions aspects of the game exciting to me. The music along with the colorful stills during the cut-scenes make the experience complete for me.Honestly this game feels like a cross between Contra, Symphony of the Night and Master Blaster. Three of my favorite games.I'm happy to add this one to that list!

_childDocuments_.review: I finished the game once playing fully in classic mode (the difficulty that emulates NES games) before reviewing. I've 100%-completed the game since then and my summary is in the comments below the review.There are some things I hate about the general design in this game, but overall it’s a very worthwhile experience.A single playthrough took me 7.5h and I did every optional content I could find while not looking for any hints online. Considering there are multiple choices that change the outcome of the story, you can maybe squeeze about twice as much out of this game for a total of about 15hIf you like 2D platform games or metroidvanias then you will most likely enjoy this.The best way to describe this is to point out what this game ISN'T.This is NOT a Classic Castlevania clone. Unlike games like Curse of The Moon, this does not have commit-heavy controls that require anticipation and lots of repetition to get good at. This can be played almost like a modern 2D metroidvania, like Hollow Knight.Point is - don't expect a Castlevania 1-3 experience.You play as a lord (and a knight), who returns home only to find it overrun by monsters. His subjects ask him to sort sht out, so you set forth to whack everything in your path with your mace.Aside from attacking with your mace, you also get a jump - direction of which you can freely control mid-air, but you can't control how high you jump. You also get potions to heal up and spells to cast (eventually).Sometimes a nighttime will come similar to Simon's Quest - enemies will be tougher and more plentiful at night and some NPCs will not talk to you until morning.You will also encounter optional quests and binary choices during your mission. These will have consequences, sometimes immediate, sometimes later down the line. In general you can try to be good and stand on the side of justice, or you can be a massive ass to everyone and everything.Very responsive with quick attack animations and ability to control direction of a jump mid-air.Enemies die in a satisfying way and if you die yourself – there’s usually a simple animation showing the enemy beating you to a bloody pulp. Unfortunately those death anmimations are monochrome, probably to save time on animations.Main level theme sounds a lot like Strike the Earth from Shovel Knight in the beginning, but quickly finds it’s own style. Other than that all music is great to listen to and remind me a lot of NES Ninja Turtles and Castlevania games.Looks nice and clear. Exactly what I like in pixel art.It’s not just a gimmick – choices really matter and can change a lot of things in the game, most notably – the ending.The only way you will die in this game is due to instant-death pits or pools of lava/acid/water. I died maybe 3 times during my entire time playing due to my HP depleting from enemy/trap attacks. I died a whole 2 times on bosses, and 1 of those was me being pushed down to a water pit, so it actually shouldn’t be counted.I never liked that part of Castlevania games. I would dare to say that it’s objectively a bad game-design decision. Why even have an HP bar if most of the time you die by being instantly killed?Especially early on some checkpoints seem to be spread too far apart and with your weapons being relatively weak – you will have to long sections and grind through enemies, especially at night.... or rather lack of control. Especially an ability to propel yourself forwards give you no control over the distance and maps seems to be designed in a way where you don't really know if rushing forward will put you on a platform you need to reach, or will it overshoot you into a pit of acid.I like it. It's not fully mechanical-focused like The Messenger, not overly simplistic like Seven Sirens and not as punishing as Curse of The moon. If you like 2D platformers or metroidvania games and like retro-style graphics - you will like this one.I'd give this game a low-endCloser to a 6 than an 8. I’ve had fun and will continue on to finish this game, but will probably forget about it in a year.

_childDocuments_.review: Would I recommend this? Yes.The art (particularly the cutscene art) is some of the best pixel art I've seen. I at one point in the game needed the double jump but could not for the life of me figure out how to get it. The secret had to do with casting a specific spell at a specific spot, and the only hint was an NPC vaguely commenting about it.Also, the fast travel is locked behind the double jump, and I unfortunately was unable to find it until near the end of the game. _childDocuments_.review: 9/10Absolutely wonderful game. It brings out all the classic tropes and game play values with none of the BS or things that you hated back in the day, like password systems and no saving, as well as having a god-forsaken timer over your head. I had an absolute blast playing it and I was really stoked that it didn't have crazy exploration or some super in depth skill tree. You have to get good at this game to get through. Many metroidvania's overwhelm me with the RPG-like options for character growth or exploration that's too unlinear. I tend to like linear and this game fits the bill, with satisfying, to the point combat that you will instinctively grab if you've played classic games. Still, it has the good parts of the genre. Ability gating and steady upgrades. It never feels overwhelming. The difficulty level is quite enjoyable and satisfying, never becoming too hard. The bosses are fairly easy but fun, the hardest part may be the platforming areas in the dungeons. All around, very fun game and I plan on playing it again someday to experience the contra mode and some of the endings I missed. The moral system was awesome and reminded me slightly of Undertale, but that's where the comparison ends. This was truly a classic game wrapped up in a nostalgic shell and covered in some sense of modernity. Wonderful work to the team who made this game, they clearly put in a lot of thought and work into making this.

_childDocuments_.review: Here's the thing: I like this game. Mostly. But after a while I started realizing there are parts of it that are frustrating on purpose.There's a lot of homage here. And I get that. I understand. Everybody likes nostalgia. But just because something is a trope doesn't mean it's good. Doesn't mean it's worth repeating.When the platforming was frustrating in Castlevania, it's because they didn't know what they were doing over three decades ago when they were making that game. They were still figuring it out. The formula had some kinks in it.When the platforming is frustrating in Infernax, it's because the developers want it to be frustrating. Why? Do you think people enjoy rolling the dice to determine whether they make a jump or start over from a checkpoint? Do you think people enjoy putting 10, 20 minutes of effort into something only to lose to some cheap garbage like an enemy with an unpredictable movement pattern showing up during a series of precarious rapid jumps? And being subjected to the HA HA YOU'RE DEAD LOOK AT YOU DYING HA HA scenes do not improve the experience.It's not as though that's the entire game, but at least two of the game's five primary dungeons seem to be wholly dedicated to 'don't make any mistakes or you're dead' platforming, and both heavily feature stupid nonsense like floating enemies that move erratically, enemies that jump up at you or teleport onto you out of nowhere, and enemies that camp the edges of platforms so that you can't even do anything. Getting a game over because you need practice is one thing, getting a game over because the level design is unfair is another.They tried to give us an 'out' in the form of magic - except that's not an option, because you will only (predictably) have one spell that will clear enemies from the screen, and you get to use it one time before you run out of MP. Unless you decide to use up one of your limited potion slots on a 'give me more MP' potion. Then maybe you'll luck out and get another shot. Unless you've used up all of your MP on healing instead, since just about everything in the game can kill you in three or four hits. Maybe even two.Overall, the game is pretty good. It just feels like they put too much effort into making parts of it intentionally annoying, which takes the fun out of it in a big way. I don't want to thumbs down it, and I don't really want to thumbs up it either, but since there is no 'Meh' option I'll lean towards the upvote instead of the downvote.

_childDocuments_.review: Objectively a good to very good game.Subjectively, finishing it was just a massive boring slog. And I grew up on Genesis and NES.The game was made with all the nonsense bs purposely kept intact from ye olde times including knockbacks, pitfalls, instant water deaths, enemies spawning on top of you, unskippable day night transitions, damage on touching an enemy, etcetera.This could be forgiven if the game was generally, just, FUN, but it wasn't in my opinion.The world just wasn't interesting to explore, especially not in any balance to the excessive amount of boring sidequests, relentless backtracking and trial and error gameplay that the game throws at you.Quests are often very ambiguous or vague, forcing you into choices that you cannot foresee the outcome for until much later in the game. By the time you realize you accidentally made a good or evil choice where you wanted to do the other, you're locked out of ultimate good / evil playthrough because it's been 5 hours since you initiated the quest and you have a single save slot for a playthrough.In the end the game felt like a massive waste of my time.

_childDocuments_.review: Another indie game that clearly focused too much of its development on graphics and music, and not enough on game design. It seems like the whole game was planned in an afternoon. The dungeons, which are obviously a huge part of a Zelda and Castlevania "tribute"(more on that later) game are unimaginative and lazy. They aren't really difficult, just tedious, which of course is not only bad in itself but also ruins what could've been a strong point of the game: the branching paths/endings. Achieving certain endings hinge on making decisions early in the game, (and you cannot have multiple save files for the same playthrough) which means you have to do completely new playthroughs to get each ending. This isn't necessarily bad in itself, but because the dungeons are tedious and boring, there is absolutely zero motivation for more than one playthrough. In regards to the "tribute" aspect of the game, (and many indie games that have come out in the last few years): enough with the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love letters to the NES era. What does being influenced by a game (or anything that matter) have to do with simply ripping things from that work? Take the influence/love and create something original. If you can't, then why the ♥♥♥♥ are you making and publishing works? And enough with "cute"(lazy) references to NES games. Yep, we got it, you also played incredibly famous works of this medium that sold millions of units. What a unique and special bond we share. A "It's dangerous to go alone" reference and a joke about wall chicken? Really, in 2022?Anyways, it's not a horrible game, just not a game I would recommend, lol.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sure this is a good game.But I hate it.I'm in my thirties, and I can tell you what this game is. It is an homage to the NES ultrahard unfair difficulty games. Buyer beware. This game is NOT for anyone that lacks the patience to deal with 30 year old dead tropes, like fixed jump height, insta-death pits, water and lava (in almost every area,) and very, very, very repetitive gameplay.If you want a game that is basically nostalgia porn for Simon's Quest, this game is for you.If you want a game that respects your time, is well balanced, and has smooth progression, with fair difficulty, smooth controls, and good and fair level design, pass on this one. This is basically a game that is designed to hurt you inside for playing it, in the old arcade style. I got stuck in an area and had no method of getting back, between, literally, an area I couldn't get through and an area I couldn't get through, because of the day/night cycle (game is 9 time harder at night, with high-health high damage leaping enemies.) So...yeah. Not fun. I have better things to do. This should never happen. My only options where to restart, and redo an hour of (mediocre) gameplay, or wait (the day/night cycle seems to be about half an hour, so yeah, no to that.) In other words.....this game wasted my time. So I can't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the "good ending" on classic mode. It was tedious with things like having to backtrack through castles to the very start where the save points are each time you get an item or else you inevitably die and lose all progress. So yes, that often means backtracking 3x for castles (it even recommends you do this in the wiki, go see for yourself). Also things like frequent insta-deaths due to awkwardly placed enemies when platforming, and touch damage that knocks you back 6 feet. Of course you can only swing in front of you not vertical. Bosses were incredibly simple and easy, so getting to the end of castles felt anticlimactic. Quick travel came way too late in the game.The visual style and art were pretty decent. But yeah, I wasn't huge on this one. If you want to switch to casual mode it might be a better time, but if you're stubborn like me prepare for a slog.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a hybrid of Castlevania II: Simon's Quest and Zelda II: The Adventure of Link, (plus the map structure of Super Metroid). It is more narrowly linear than either of the two originals, and ends up being less fun. To be fair, Metroidvania's are not my home genre, so I'm a little more critical of this type of game. I had hoped for something more expansive, exciting, dynamic, but instead I felt this game was fairly tight, inflexible, without interesting choices. The game has this morality system, allowing you to get 4 different endings. This didn't deepen the game or make it more fun, instead it feels like a lure to repeat beating the game. I'd honestly say go beat Zelda II and Castlevania II instead of this game. They were wildly original games and super fun, and I don't know that I've encountered their superior version yet.

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of writing I'm working through the only the 3rd castle, but I gotta give my recommendation anyway while the game is still new because it's pretty dern good.This game is a major homage to the classics done really well. From the start it's a very simple game, and on "classic" mode it's challenging and rewarding. Like a more graphic shovel knight in many ways, but more like Castlevania II and LoZ2.My only hang-up is I can't tell if the difficulty settings are a sincere accessibility for babies or a commentary on how sacrificing unilateral difficulty cheapens the overall experience. It's what a dark souls level difficulty game looks like with an easy mode. I'm still enjoying it under there classic mode restrictions, but the everpresent option to lower the difficulty upon every death (or a certain cheat code that's actually really bfun too) feels like a temptation to sin, which seems fitting for a game about fighting demons. Since I've not made it very far I can't say for sure how intentional this paradigm is, but I look forward to the rest of it!!----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------('bout a week and a half later)Ok, so I've beaten the game twice now and I'm at the end of my third. This game is really fun to replay after you beat it once because you kinda know what most of the game is like, but exploring other quest paths, finding secrets, and feeling like you know what you're doing this time is super satisfying. If you only ever play and beat this game once and take the ending you get you'll have definitely gotten a fun, quirky, homage to the classics romp that is well worth its asking price. If you play and beat the game twice, you'll have fun trying some new things, making new discoveries, have a second chance to be a better badass on another go around, and there's plenty of charm throughout the whole game. But there are so many reasons to play this game a third time like I currently am that you'll just have to give it a fair first shot. I mean, why would I play a game 3 times if I didn't think it was fun?

_childDocuments_.review: Update: With the quality of life update, the game is in a better place now to recommend it despite the criticism from before. These accessibility options are helpful in mediating the more painful instant death platforming sections for those of you interested in checking all the other good stuff in the game.Old review: This is the kind of game I would've loved and wholeheartedly recommended, but the platforming is just too much for the kind of mobility restrictions that this game is going for. I would still recommend it to people willing to put up with its platforming tricks, because they sure are tedious and frustrating, but outside of those parts the rest of the game is really good.I'll start with the positives because the game has a couple good ones, the art and theme this game goes for are great, maybe minus some portraits, there is also a fairly good deal of questing and involvement in it too, the upgrading structure is also fairly nice and consequential to how you'll play the next sections, the game boasts great replay value with multiple playthroughs and endings attached to them.Lastly, this game is the kind that has the best kind of Codes, something that I'm seeing few indie games bother with and wish more did, because past developers look like they had the most fun with these and provided a good deal of fun value to their players.With all that said this all sounds like a slam dunk especially for the price, but unfortunately, the bad NES platforming trope rears its ugly head and ruins everyone's fun.For old action games like these, platforming like this never provided good replay value or a first playthrough experience for that matter, it's obvious this was used to stretch out the length of those old games.The problems with the platforming I think are best to start at the section before entering Combbleton Necropolis, with the infamous 3 screens worth of falling chandeliers / platforms with spikes under them, that you need to jump from one to the next and to the next.First of all this didn't need to be 3 screens long, I believe even 1 screen would've sufficed here and second, a very questionable design choice was made here of giving you an extremely tight window for the waiting between the next platform to drop down again.. I seriously can't believe something this demanding was put so early on in the game and I say this, because I've beaten the game and very few sections later on come close to how stupidly tight this section is..This is a textbook example of a difficulty spike happening very early into the game. You can get through it obviously, but this is a very poor impression of the game to set for any new players, because in this is exemplified that platforming in this game exists solely to waste your time by undoing a lot of your progress.The second big problem that the emphasis on platforming presents? The combat is pretty damn easy..For my take, I would much rather have traded off every challenging platforming in this game in favor of a more challenging Combat and despite how many potions this game gave me, even on the final boss I hadn't used even one.Anytime that a boss ever felt challenging had little to do with the bosses and more with the threat of falling into an instant death because of the knockback, or, the threat of having to redo large sections of a dungeon again.The third big problem, is how it runs counter to almost every single upgrade the game provides.The only upgrade that holds any meaningful benefits for platforming are the Hearts / 1ups and even then I would argue it shouldn't because it is much more interesting to use as a health resource counter to potions, meanwhile, everything else either doesn't work or provides subpar platforming experiences that other games have done a better job at than this one.You might think Skycall (the upwards thrust attack) is a benefit for platforming, but accelerated fall velocity makes it impossible to use it outside of its intended uses, because there is virtually no time to react by the time your screen is scrolled down enough to see the bottomless pit / water / lava.Other special mentions here goes to Holy Charge (the dash move) which is borderline unusable outside its intended use, due to how freakishly long the distance it covers and the added momentum after the landing, this move also meshes so badly with the rest of the upgrades that you cannot perform anything else after you do a charge.The last problem that platforming presents the game, is that it diminishes the replay value of those choices and different endings, as well as cool codes we were talking about earlier, because it's not like if I switch to casual mode the platforming is gone and I'm playing a better game, right?. Well, no, the game is obviously designed more around the platforming and honestly, that's just a damn shame, because I don't think the game benefits from them that much and only suffered more because of them.. even if some might argue that it makes the gameplay more intense, I don't disagree with that, but I'll counter that by saying, it's the wrong kind of intensity that turns into annoyance and tedium if you fail and that more emphasis on making the Combat more challenging would've done that far better.A few words on some other mixed aspects in the game.1. Upgrades feel limited by their restrictions. Guided Strike (the downwards attack) locks you in place too long and despite being locked into place, you don't knockback enemies of any kind, which would make it useful for initiating combat with something bellow you, but the way it works is very limited and more often than not will cause you to take damage. Holy Charge often times puts you in more danger than if you didn't use it, since enemies don't commit to an attack direction until after their windup animation ends and even if you time it, the enemy will swap at the last nanosecond of the windup and you get hit for "mistiming" it or, you either might end up not clearing enough distance.2. Many spells just take too much mana and because of that, become borderline unusable. This might be different depending on the playthrough, but even then, I know you have healing in each type of playthrough and getting back to full health is always preferable to dealing a bit of damage to an enemy/boss at a massive mana cost.3. Health is very unclear in this game and I don't just blame this on the lines representing health, I blame this on the outdated notion that a bar of health cannot be half full if you take 0.5 points of damage, because while this wasn't possible to do back then due to both limitations and limited space / lower resolutions, this isn't those NES days, we can have this nowadays and being able to See a half full bar left or taking 1.5, 2.5 and so on kind of damage, would make this a lot more clear.To be clear, I mostly enjoyed the game despite these problems, but these are I think this game's shortcomings and worth reiterating, because they certainly didn't do it any favors the way I see it.If this game gets a sequel, I hope it gets better with time, because I feel this style of platforming is a crutch that retro indie developers need to get rid of and fast, especially when making games like these that aren't primarily platformers, because these infamous tropes might well be the death of retro indie games for many players, myself included.. I could get through it, but honestly, I'm feeling the burnout and I seriously don't care to have more games that opt in for platforming like this that wastes my time.Please leave platforming like this to platforming games.. Instead, if you're gonna have some then use it for the same purposes that Metroid games have it, reaching previously unreachable sections.

here's wot I like and dislike about it, in bullet points.+ terrific pixel art, and very impressive blood physics.+ the demon designs are wonderful creepy.+ nice chiptunes OST.+ combat is diabolically satisfying. melds Castlevania with Zelda 2 to craft something tactical, but much too in your face to have the pacing become plodding. you feel like a god when successfully mowing down foes.+ tight controls (though I personally needed to rebind them on keyboard to suit my preferences, and do wish that dual bindings were available with regards to movement (IE, having WASD and arrow keys doing the same things respectively)--these obviously aren't major gripes, however, and are just "it'd be nice" preferential or QOL things).+ the writing is pretty damn mean, lol. in a good way.+ I really like the implementation of the first optional boss. it catches you by surprise (well, you kinda know something's up going into it, so not completely) and can rip into you in short order. but when you step back and learn the patterns even slightly, it is INCREDIBLY EASY. in other words, that's a great and memorable tutorial!+ successfully completing dungeons is impeccably cathartic.+ I like the openness of it. first thing I have done in both playthroughs has been to run to a slightly later dungeon and grind there against the tougher mobs.- I wish you could speed past the shrine stuff more. the animations and text take a dog's age.- you can either have the boss runs or you can have the boss cutscenes every time you run into their arena. having both becomes absurdly tedious, even when skipping the cutscenes as it still takes like another 3 seconds to skip (a window that naturally becomes increasingly obnoxious the longer you find yourself rematching with a given boss). considering how hilariously trivial the boss runs are (at least as far as I have gotten in), and how little they assist in grinding, you could so easily cut them and not lose much.- I wish that the double spear trap telegraphed more which pipe it is shooting from (at least the first shot, as I get that it alternates from there). just would give a better idea of what to expect, and it's not like the challenge posed as is, is so significant or compelling.all in all, I do love Infernax a lot. it does retro revivalism right. I have a few minor gripes that can add up to make the game a tad frustrating, but it is otherwise phenomenal.for more thoughtful recommendations of the best games on Steam, check out my curator, .

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game, it's full of charm, nostalgia and great gameplay.  BUT, even on the easy setting, it's "Nintendo Hard".  Which for some is part of its charm.  But for a busy Dad like me that can't waste 30 minutes redoing an area, it's just not practical.  The easy mode adds extra save points, grants an extra life, and let's you keep half your resources on death.  But compared to other metroidvanias with save points, these seemed few and far between.  I would routinely travel room after room hoping to stumble into one.  All the while, the enemies would become harder and harder; only to end up dying and losing most my progress.  It seemed the only solution to this would be to farm the lower level areas, but having to do that at the very beginning of the game doesn't seem fun to me.  For those longing for the good ol' days of difficulty, or the 'git-gud' crowd, this game has a LOT to offer you.  But for those of us who lived on the Game Genie... well... we'll have to pass.

_childDocuments_.review: Everyone seems to be comparing Infernax to Castlevania 2, which I've never played so I can't comment on. But personally, I would compare this game to Zelda II: The Adventure of Link, and it's not a favorable comparison. The game feels like a spiritual successor to Zelda II that is simultaneously easier, but also more unfair with way more cheap deaths. Let me explain what I mean.In many ways, Infernax's difficulty has been nerfed relative to Zelda II. The biggest example of this is the insanely OP heal spell, which fully restores your health and can be cast 3 times with a full magic bar, combined with being able to carry up to 5 potions at a time, which can each fully heal both health and magic. If we do the math, this means that starting with full magic and 5 potions, you will be able to fully recover your health bar up to 23 times. Now, this is with endgame stats/equipment, but it doesn't take too long to get so OP that you will never fully run out of heals. What this functionally means is that most of your deaths will happen for one of two reasons - you fell in an instant death pit, or you weren't paying attention to your health bar and forgot to heal. Both of these feel pretty cheap and are not fun ways to die. By comparison, in Zelda II, when you die, it's usually because the game got the better of you and you genuinely messed up or ran out of resources. Infernax also has a bunch of other cheap "features" that make it more frustrating to play than Zelda II. Remember how I talked about instant death pits? Well, there are a TON of them, especially in dungeons. Way more than Zelda II. And the game loves to combine enemies that shoot projectiles with instant death pits, so you'll frequently get hit and knocked back into a pit. Another bad thing is instant enemy respawning. If you leave the room you're in and return, all enemies will respawn, which is a major annoyance if you have to backtrack. This is not the case in Zelda II, where most enemies in a dungeon do not respawn unless you leave the dungeon. Probably the worst thing of all about Infernax is the saving system. If you get game over, you lose all progress since your last save. In Zelda II, on the other hand, the only things you lose when you get game over are your experience points and physical location in the game. You keep any any stat upgrades, items/equipment upgrades, and dungeon keys. This goes a long way to reduce frustration because you rarely feel like a run was "wasted". Even if you die while attempting a dungeon, maybe you found the upgrade item, some of the keys, or leveled up during your attempt. All of this carries over to your next attempt. In Infernax, if you die, everything you did since you entered the dungeon is wiped and it was all for nothing. This is made worse by the fact that there's no way to safely exit a dungeon or save your progress mid-dungeon without beating the dungeon or walking all the way back to the entrance. This means that if you have made substantial progress (maybe found the main upgrade and some keys) and don't want to lose it if you fail the final boss, you will have to replay the entire dungeon in reverse. Remember how I said enemies instantly respawn if you leave a room? Yup, they'll all be back and trying to knock you into instant death pits all over again as you make your way back out of the dungeon to save your progress. It really is the worst feeling when you get halfway through a dungeon, try to escape and save, then die on your way back through first room of the dungeon. This happened to me. Multiple times. Additionally, Infernax's overall balance is worse than Zelda II's. In Zelda II, you have a wide variety of spells that are useful in different situations. Shield is good for rooms with a lot of combat, jump is good for rooms with a lot of platforming, heal is good to restore your health, fairy is good for skipping a difficult room, reflect lets you block normally unblockable attacks, and spell lets you make a room easier by turning enemies into bots (an easy enemy). The only "bad" spells are thunder and fire. By contrast, in Infernax, there is little reason to use anything other than the overpowered heal spell, at least in dungeons. The fast travel and day/night spell are useful, but are more utility-like and not really something you would use to help you get through a difficult section of the game. Infernax's combat is also way simpler and less fun than Zelda II's. There's no directional blocking (or blocking at all), and most enemies can be beat by button mashing and playing aggressively, even if you get hit, then using your plentiful magic and potions to heal any damage you take. Anyway, all things considered, the game isn't totally awful, but it was very disappointing. I was hoping for a modern successor to Zelda II, but instead, it just reminded me of how much better Zelda II is and made me want to play it again. If you're considering this game, definitely play Zelda II instead if you haven't already. Or, if you're looking for a modern nes-style game, try The Messenger. It's far better in pretty much every way.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like some indie game developers have this psychosis that stops them from realizing that old games had ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ instant deaths, offscreen hazards, and enemies that can approach you from angles you cannot attack, just so they force you to insert another quarter.This whole game only exists to capture the essence of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fake difficulty from games of the era. Save points are few and far between, and enemies respawn on every screen so you cannot even backtrack safely. Dungeons have one save point at the very beginning, and if you die to the final boss well get ♥♥♥♥♥♥ you do the whole damn thing over again, boring enemies and all. There are offscreen spear hazards in the very first dungeon!Games design has come a long way in the last 40 years, and while not all the strides have been great, stuff like this is a relic of the past for a good reason.Yes, there is a second casual mode to get around these flaws. Instead of making an easy mode, perhaps you should design the game around not being intentionally frustrating, so players can get satisfying difficulty. Playing on the casual mode doesn't even make the game good, since the difficulty is one of the only selling points and the game is otherwise mechanically shallow and uninteresting.

_childDocuments_.review: [★☆☆] - This one will sound contradictory, because the truth is that Infernax is a perfectly competent 8-bit tribute. The controls are tight and functional, the presentation is stylish with a thrust of authenticity, there's some genuine creativity and love on display here...  So how come I'm not having any fun?There's an infamous review of  (1987, Konami) where Arin Hanson explains that even if Konami tightened up the gameplay and fixed annoyances, the level design is ultimately lifeless with generic enemy placement and long walks through very dull 'hallways'. Infernax has some really great moments in it, and when it works the combat is fun, but the designers just didn't successfully string the elements together in a way that made me feel like I going anywhere. (like Faxanadu, Links Adventure & Battle of Olympus) . Though if any of those names gave you nostalgia, you might dig it or you might reel at what used to pass for top-tier gameplay. (Also, you're probably due for a mammogram or prostate exam.)

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR: Great love letter to classic Castlevania. Fantastic game that's well worth full price. Edit: Decided to come back to it. I'm through 2 castles and at the 2nd village. Good difficulty, upgrades happen at a good pace and has great callbacks to some classic games which are great fun if/when you find them (don't spoil yourself). The music has been really good. Unfortunately I got other games I'm working on so this has to wait a bit to get around to. But wanted to show some support anyways because these are the kinds of games I want to see more of (and not the plethora of roguelike/lites). It's classic Castlevania but with some more modern touches. The controls are simple but well done. Jumping has a single height (so no tapping for little hops or holding for big jumps) but isn't stiff and you're not locked into your jump (meaning you can change direction). There's a limited inventory of items you can buy/obtain such as potions, magic and weapons and armor. You can also upgrade your attack, health and magic using xp at save points. There's no quest markers so you gotta talk to everyone but you do have a quest log with the details. "Flea men" are still annoying ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.  Just from the bit I played I'm loving the game and can't wait to return and give it a proper play through (or more). I hope it does well because it's obviously made with lots of love and reverence for classic Castlevania.

_childDocuments_.review: I really didn't want to give Infernax a negative review...
