_childDocuments_.review: I've never actually played either Zelda 2 or the pre-Symphony of the Night Castlevanias, but I've seen enough of them to know the kind of gameplay Infernax is referencing. The best way I can describe it is a platform-heavy metroidvania with RPG elements and various ways the story can play out based on your choices. I HAVE however played a much earler game from developer Berzerk Studio: A humble flash game called Homerun in Berzerk Land, back in my Kongregate days.In Infernax, the player takes the role of a war-weary crusader knight named Alcedor, who has returned to his home and fiefdom in the Duchy of Upel, only to find it in the throes of a demonic curse. Beginning with little more then a suit of rusty mail and a stud-less mace, through the lands of Upel and a series of five major dungeons, Alcedor must battle cultists, undead, demons and more in an attempt to cleanse his lands, along the way acquiring new gear and spells, performing quests for the citizenry and being presented with a series of moral decisions that steer the player towards one of a surprising number of endings. Slain enemies award XP and gold. XP can be spent at the Souls-esque save shrines to permanently increase your damage, health or mana, and gold can be spent at various vendors for new equipment, spells and other items. The game uses a unique version of a lives system wherein you can purchase additional maximum lives from some vendors, and they are restored any time you touch a save shrine. Losing a life merely kicks you to the last screen transition you crossed, while losing them all kicks you back the last time you saved, with all progress since lost- including things like major equipment acquisitions and boss fights, so watch yourself. There is an optional "Casual" difficulty that lets you keep some of your XP and gold gains, but that won't help you with the platforming.Which brings me to my biggest complaint about the game. Some of the platforming sections in Infernax are rather more obnoxious then I would like, especially in the fourth dungeon, Kastka Palace, and one extremely annoying acid room in the fifth, Kadjanto Stronghold. Mercifully, it's always possible to leave a dungeon and save outside, say, after collecting a key or upgrade, and save yourself some time and effort if you run out of lives later on. As my playtime would attest, it's doable, and not as frustrating as say, the Plague of Shadows DLC for Shovel Knight, and certainly not like the bonus dungeons in Guacamelee or some ridiculous romhack kaizo game.It's worth exploring as much of Infernax's map as you can, though I could say that about most given metroidvanias. There are a handful of bonus dungeons and out-of-the-way NPCs with additional gear you wouldn't obtain otherwise. This is also necessary to obtain some of the more involved endings. Infernax is a fun 2D action game and certainly more respectful of the player's time then its spiritual forebears, or even other recent retro-platformers. It's technically on the shorter side but feels content-dense regardless- there is no wasted space on the map and you're always doing something towards a specific end. I enjoyed its dark atmosphere, audio design and boss fights. However, the annoying jumps may preclude me from further playthroughs, at least for a while.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Infernax is a solid and unique retro offering for the fans of Castlevania-style games. It can be described as a cousin of Simon's Quest if it was actually a good game.In a nutshell:Pros:- Solid gameplay- Surprisingly deep story and choices- Perfect game length- Many endings- Useful difficulty choices- Satisfyingly gory pixel art- Great boss fights- Amazing OSTCons:- Classic difficulty can be way too challenging, especially in dungeons. The game is plenty challenging in Casual mode, make yourself a favor and switch to Casual if you find the game frustrating. - The game makes a fairly bad job at explaining that the choices you make have a deep impact. I recommend you first play the game blindly, but consider doing many runs to get to the different endings. They're worth it.- Fighting monsters can get daunting, but nothing worst that classic 8-bit Castlevania offerings.Awesome game, I'm on my third playthrough and never thought I'd get THIS enamored with Infernax. Can only recommend. Great job Berzerk !
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: A very well done retro game that has its roots from castlevania. Amazing gameplay and setting. Only problem is I want even more content with how much I enjoyed it! Its replayability is very particular as the core gameplay is the same but with new characters and different endings. Would wholly recommend this game at full price!
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: I am probably not going to say anything that others have not.  This game is what the games I grew up with should have been.  Of course, it is made for an adult audience with all of the gore and occasional nudity.  It's full of humor, especially in the form of Easter eggs and inside jokes for the target audience.The team that made this game knew exactly what they were doing and did it well.The only real negative for me was the instant death platforming.  While the game itself isn't truly hard, especially in casual mode, it does have some moments involving spear launchers knocking you into pits of instant death that might result in a gray hair or two.All in all though, it is worth the buy.  It also includes a set of alternate characters which give it some real replay value.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Prepare for a splatterfest as you are asked to save the retched people of a land you abandoned for the Crusades. Upon returning home you find that everyone you encounter is asking you to make decisions with minimal context and maximum consequences. However, if you are up for the platforming challenge that only Mario Maker mixed with a Souls game can bring then jump right on into Infernax a pseudo Castlevania 2 clone.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: I was not expecting to enjoy this game as much as I did.  At the time of writing this, I have clocked in nearly 39 hours.  I've beaten it 7-8 times in the span of days and gotten all achievements.  A lot of developers who try to do a retro-themed, "difficult" game usually just add nonsensical design choices meant more for twitchy, precision platforming.  Infernax can be tough... but seldom ever is it unfair.Imagine Zelda II, but darker, more responsive and even more fun.  Imagine Simon's Quest without the obtuse puzzles, no visual restraint, and the ability to control yourself mid-air.  There's just a lot to like about this game, and, honestly, I can't recommend it enough to someone who wants a solid, action-adventure type with RPG elements, exploration, and multiple ways to play.I only have two complaints.  1st: The game has a morality system that can be tough to figure out, and you have to be all the way good or all the way evil to get the best weapon for your playthrough.  Not entirely a deal breaker, but can be a bit rough when you want to see all the content.  Though that does make the "Free Will Sacrifice" achievement a little tricky.  (Tip: start "good" quests before turning evil so you don't get locked out)  2nd: to hell with the Kastka Palace with its teleporting mages and a myriad of ways to fall down a pit.  Great music though.Also, the soundtrack's pretty stellar.  All right, that's enough praise.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Infernax does what Simon's Quest wishes it did. Solid platforming and combat with a “mostly” fair difficulty. This game is great in every department. Sound, music, gameplay and control. It also has a karma system which admittedly isn't too deep, however it is better than most because it changes the world around you. You can help a farmer's barn then actually see it get repaired or push out cultists to have access to a new spell. Things like that help in feeling your decisions have an impact on the world around you. I won’t spoil the quest lines but I would highly recommend picking a path and sticking with it. The non ultimate endings are very underwhelming. Thankfully the game is quite short with probably a 3-5 hour play time, plus with the inclusion of cheats allow for a make your own way to play. You also can play 5 different types of characters depending on your name or cheat which won’t drastically change the game play but is welcomed when you want to play it again.The only criticisms I have is I wish you could actually make multiple saves on the same playthrough and not one master save. The game could have had more overworld secrets. There are a few, but more would of added to exploring areas. Another dungeon would be great. And lastly, would've been helpful to get a slight nudge to the player to assist when things are unclear. One of the last dungeons has a very unclear way of using the double jump that I thought I was doing it wrong.All in all, a stellar game worth your time if you like 2D adventure games.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Classically styled metroidvania with modern controls and gameplay. What's not to like?The pixel art (especially the 'high-res' cutscene artwork) is masterful. Enemies require unique strategies to dispatch effectively. Tons of spells, abilities and equipment to find, and multiple endings.If you like Metroid, Castlevania, Shovel Knight, etc., then this game is for you.5/5. A masterpiece in retro gaming.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: A modern day mix of games of old makes for a pixel art bloody good time. Infernax hits on all of the nostalgia strings while managing to incorporate modern elements to make this game feel like it belongs in this era. Good length and multiple endings gives this game some good longevity to give you enough blood for your buck. Check out my full review here:
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Castlevania 2 but godlike. Infernax is a beautiful little game where you go around breaking magic seals in castles in order to take down the big bad demon evil at the end. The absolute designs of devil's and being able to thwack skeletons and mob monsters in the open world is a classic exploration style joy. Shhhh don't forget your game wizard codes to for later playthroughs as they make the game even more fun and no I won't spoil the funny antics that come from unlocking things like chainsaw mode. Lastly just remember Up, Up, Down, Down, Left, Right, Left, Right, B, A on the title screen. If you know you know.Absolute treat of a game that I'll be coming back to from time to time to grind out the remaining endings so do yourselves a favor and play Infernax!!!!!!!10/10 game
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: There are a LOT of interesting gameplay mechanics, and when you've uncovered the various characters and means of playing the game, it's entertaining to say the least. This game has had a lot of love, almost fell away from the eyes of most people ever since the loss of access to Flash games. Sure, there were some workarounds, but this game fell that much deeper behind the veil of legend. And now, here it is!Easy to get into, easy to accidentally into self-destruction, but it's still its own challenge for each playthrough. Normally I don't do evil runs (and I haven't as of yet), but I can be convinced to see every aspect of the game, and all of the means of seeing the 'grey area' ending arcs. The extra lives can be useful, but if you can keep from dropping yourself into pits of spikes/acid/lava/water/youalreadyknow/etc., you can complete it real damn well!I will spoil one single thing in this game, by means of a hint. *Facing towards a cliff looming over a dead cropfield, one may crouch down and observe it, in order to soar into the skies with no fear of falling.* Those of you that know the reference (lookin' at you, Arcade Crew 'n Berzerkers), I think you'll enjoy the end-result.It -can- be distracting or confusing with going in various directions, and not knowing where to go. There was -one- point in the game that I didn't quite know where to go, in order to get further into the game, until I started the basic gaming-troubleshooting, and it pays to LISTEN TO THE NPCs, as the hints aren't exactly telling, but they do help you figure things out, unless you're one of those smert gamers that'll catch on quicker than I do.Absolutely, get this game, absolutely play it as much as you can. Classic mode is the way to go, but sometimes you can do casual, if you wanna throw in some extra challenge for yourself. Also, go do an ultimate casual run with no extra lives, and comment if you manage to do it! :D
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Game is amazing. A real callback to when I was a kid. It's like a mix of castlevania and faxanadu. There's a morality system that generates several different endings, fun easter eggs and references to old classic games, and even a built-in cheat mode so you can skip grinding for money and exp or even go full invincible without tanking your achievements. I saw a friend playing it and I wanted in. I would suggest getting as many endings legitimately as you can stand before you start messing with the cheats and extra characters. Pay attention to the books you get after each ending and they will give you information and cheat codes without having to look them up immediately.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Back in the late 80's to early 90's, when I was in elementary school, video games were naturally the talk of the playground (or the Simpsons if it was Monday morning), and we always bragged about which video games we beat, which video games we loved, and which video games were cool. Among my favorites were Castlevania III and the Legend of Zelda, I could never get enough of either game. Does that mean I despised Castlevania II or Zelda II: The Adventure of Link? Absolutely not, some of my fondest memories are of me screaming at my television screen when the inevitable game over screen popped up, and my father yelling "TURN THE NINTENDO OFF!" at the top of his lungs. I didn't turn off the Nintendo then, and boy am I glad I didn't because lo and behold, here is Infernax, that offers the best call-back to my childhood possible. It also invokes elements of Contra, though to be honest, I may have spoiled too much.Multiple enemies? Check. Two different difficulties? Check. Awesome weapons like a mace, sword, axe, gun, chainsaw? Check. Cheat Codes that remind me of the Game Genie? Check. A wonderful soundtrack that you'll invariably want to buy? Checkmate.If you enjoy cheap shots and getting knocked into bottomless pits and raging at the heavens, this is absolutely the game for you. It's not exceedingly difficult in my opinion, but you'll want to think twice before jumping once in certain portions of the game, lest you have a Deep One knock you off a wheel unexpectedly. The game is rich in exploration, gore, amazing tunes, spells, and much much more. Buy this game, you won't regret it!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty awesome throwback you can toss on one monitor while watching stuff on the other monitor. For a single-character playthrough, it'll take 10-12 hours to complete with all items not using any cheats. If you want some pretty cool character unlocks or abilities, go ahead and look up the cheat codes online. Don't feel guilty, either. If you owned an NES or SNES, you'd be reading Nintendo Power for the latest guides, and you'd be rocking a Game Genie to smash that fourth wall.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: What a fun little platformer metroidvania. One of the highlights of the games I have played recently. Let's open it up a bit.Graphically, it's basically a pixelart game the closely resembles Castlevania 2: Simon's Quest the most. It's nice and colorful and the character design is nicely morbid and bodyhorrorish.The story is simple but it has some branching paths that really surprises you along the way. It's an engaging way to get more playability to the game. There are also secret characters to unlock that vastly differ from the gameplay you were used to so that's fresh also. The sounds and music are awesome. Meaty tunes and nice EXPLOSIONS. Just awesome. This game would be NES hard if the controls weren't so tight. The controlling of the character is easy and responsive. There are few places that are super hard platforming but you'll manage in the end with practice. People were complaining about the map and there is lots of backtracking but if you played the game a bit further I think there would be something to make the backtracking trivial...perhaps. :) I have no huge complains about the game. It's a bit of a short side but high replay value keeps it engaging. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED. 5/5.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: If you like castlevania 2, zelda 2, with some shove a knife up your @$$ music(shovel knight). You'll love this game.It's a really fun metroidvania game that plays like those retro games with decent gameplay, loving care, nice quests, and fun references.It is brutal but in the typical nintendo hard kind of way, and us old retro guys. we liked it.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: If you like 8-bit and castlevania then you can't go wrong with this game.It's addicting, fun, has some fun references to older games and it's beautiful to look at.It also has multiple endings for replayability and it's really worth checking out,especially if you're into retro games.I honestly liked it more than shovel knight
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: I loved every minute of it.its simple but detailed at the same time, the bosses are great and look amazing.the abilities and upgrades are a pleasure to play with.the Easter eggs are cute and funny.the story is badass.the soundtrack is ROCKIN!Its quite challanging as well so that kept me interested No doubt.The Cheats are really fun too! (Try the Konama Code on the title screen *wink*  *wink*)
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Lite spoilers in this game (just in what content is included but nothing game breaking)This game is solid. Not too long and designed to be played multiple times. (3~4). I beat the game as a Good/ult good knight, evil wiz, non-aligned warrior, repentant knight, and Konami mode for the future run.I would recommend this:1. First playthrough: Knight, Evil/ult evil (mace isn't great as a weapon)2. Warrior: Good/ult good3. Wizard for short playthroughs4. Konami for the future ending and for lols.I found the wizard extremely unrewarding to play. It's the hardest class to survive with and does poor damage. The allure of range attack is lost when it does low damage and requires mana. It was more effective to use Thunder than to spam basic attack. I didn't get to max attack b/c I chose to max mana... it just doesn't work. I spent most of a boss fight waiting for mana to regen before unlocking mana potions which will drain much needed gold from you. I think the wizard needs a higher mana regen rate as you either level up mana or when you get a better weapon. It just sucks... period. Konami dude just washes any reason why the mage exists.I wish profile graphics for non-default player characters were included in all of the story scenes and reactions. Seeing the normal or evil knight when you aren't plaything that sucks. Plus, the other characters don't even get a reaction. Just a static photo much like the npcs. That was a missed opportunity. The cutscene graphic changes would have been nice, but I'm just talking about having a good and evil face change that you get playing the default.Gold gain is frighteningly slow if you don't do quests. For certain runs, it makes sense to wait on doing quests until you understand when to do them or what to do. The extra life is a god send while potions are cool, early game they aren't as valuable as a whole other life.  Lives get replenished at save shrines while pots have to be acquired elsewhere. Speaking of early game, there are areas in the 2 and 3 dungeons that if you aren't playing perfectly are very difficult to try and backtrack to the outside shrine. As the wiz and warrior, I had a few death loops where I was just trying to get a key or key item and get back to the shrine so I wouldn't have to do it all over again or 1-life the entire dungeon (which I couldn't do until much later). There would be the cheap floating eye or axe thrower or something else located strategically by a pit that no matter how well I battled, I would inevitably die there. I get that it's nostagic, but some characters don't have a solid ranged option to deal with that and you have to hope your timing is flawless.The bosses are easy (most people are saying this). The boss that you have to attack the tongue, that was needlessly drown out... I think the most interesting bits were the ult good/evil raids. I wanted more of that. The Ult Evil raid was the most challenging aspect of the game. The ult good version really needs a bump in difficulty, especially given what the cult can do.I'm satisfied with my purchase. This peeled me away from Elden Ring. I've recommended it to my friends. Definitely a good amount of time spent.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: A whole lot of fun. One of those rare games that sucked me in to the point I felt I needed to get all the achievements just to see the story beats; don't regret the time spent for a second. Even after seeing everything, the combat is tightly built enough that doing further runs has been possible, just playing around, sequence breaking, etc.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Infernax plays like an old school metroidvania style game.  When I say old school I mean things like experiencing knock back when getting hit, dying when falling in water/lava, etc..  I've completed my first play through on classic mode and really enjoyed it.  Since beating it I've looked online and there are multiple endings and more things for me to unlock.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Got recommend this game by Lythero and extremely glad they did! Usually I am not interested in these sort of brutal old school platformers, but the charm of this one really hooked me, especially after completing the game for the first time, leaving me with only very minor gripes with the game. This is also the first game I have ever played that actually made me want to 100% complete the game! After my first completion I wanted to learn more about the story and after 50 hours I managed to achieve that. I enjoyed it so much I am now working on the 100% speedrun for the game haha :DThank you devs for all the little attention to details in the game, as well as your show of interest in the speedrun community for the game. Has been a great experience overall so far and I highly recommend <3
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: This game answers the question of "What if Zelda2/Cvania2 had been refined?" and then slams a demons face against the corner of a table exploding in blood. Infernax wears it's inspiration like a badge of honor and adds in a morality system, multi endings, multiple playable characters and great sprite work to be a contender for best indie game. Very challenging with lots of quick (sometimes unfair) deaths and very speed-runner friendly set ups to rooms that will drive you to get all the endings. I cannot stress any more that this is a must play game of 2022.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: A *really* good metroidvania in general even if you don't like the retro themes, but if you do theres a handful of easter eggs and references to Simon's Quest and other games in the genre from that era, the art is fantastic and the controls are smooth. My only real complaint is that some enemies should not have contact damage (flying enemies that just shoot stuff) and other enemies can spam a ranged attack so fast you cant really do anything about it without leaving agro range and hope the reset changed their pattern
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this nostlagic trip back to Simons Quest, but done good. The Easter Eggs and secrets really add a lot to the game and it was a really pleasant experience.But fair warning, it has some tough platforming sections and really hard Boss fights, especially if you take alternate routes.Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: I loved every detail of this game. It's like a blend between Castlevania and Zelda 2. The story is fine, the gameplay feels pretty good, the progression and game balance are just perfect for this game and the art is beautiful. You can tell when something is made with love and passion, and this game is one of those.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the game buuuuut there were problems. If you want to see all the bosses in this game will take at least 2 full runs, if not 3. The game has multiple choices where if you don't choose right every. single. time. you lock your save file from being able to see the true ending.I hate this so much, and it ruined wanting to play again. That said I enjoyed what time I did spend on it.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Notes: It may not look like it from the trailers, but the last three dungeons require a good bit of parkour. It is certainly possible, just know that ahead of time. As for the combat difficulty, every boss is very fair and can often be beaten first try if you take your time. There are spells to use as well but you don't get a ton of mana, so you won't be spamming spells. I mostly used spells for utility and healing instead of offense.Also, the game is only 7-10 hours long, but there are multiple endings that give a unique narrative so the game is very much replayable. There are a lot of "Choose A or B, but if you choose A you can't get B until another playthrough" decisionsThings I liked:The music, map design, the villages/npcs are charming, progression (enemies don't get OP super fast), bosses, and the branching narrative paths for each endingThings I disliked: When you hit water/lava/acid, you immediately die. Life lost, go back to the start of the room. This can be infuriating in some cases because if an enemy or projectile hits you while midair, you go into free fall. This makes some parkour sections feel very tedious.As for bugs? Didn't encounter any
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Play Infernax. Just do it. They took the graphics and sound of an NES Castlevania, made it a Metroidvania, and combined it with the leveling of LOZ II. Quests, sidequests and the option for good or bad playthroughs don't hurt either. It's the best parts of Castlevania and LOZ II combined in the best ways, with some modern flavor added in as well. Good combat, fulfilling progression, multiple endings and good music. And  all of the achievements are named after heavy metal songs. Great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun mix between Castlevania 2 and Zelda 2. Overall worth your time if you enjoy casually brutal games and Castlevania gameplay. The gameplay is reasonably fun but be warned that you will be going through the same rooms many times with little changing.The difficulty is both a nice challenge and an unfortunate aspect of the game. As you progress through dungeons you may find yourself wanting to exit the dungeon and save just to keep the key or ability you spent time and health getting so an unfortunate death doesn't make you replay that section yet another time. Ultimately there are an unfortunate number of instant deaths in this game that just eat at your progress.This game is still worth your time if you aren't terribly put off by the difficulty.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game, combines tight action platforming in a light metroidvania with a simple but rewarding combat system tying it all together. Although short, Infernax really makes the most of it's tight (yet still engaging) environment, gritty 8 bit graphics, and simple but dynamic story to create an incredibly rich and immersive experience. Can play a good guy or a bad guy, and watch the world flourish, or recoil in accordance to your actions and decisions. This game really makes me wonder at the possibilities if other games from the 80s and 90s had the level of freedom and immersion this does. Truly a masterpiece, I really want to continue to explore the world of infernax, slaying demons, time traveling, and uncovering all the incredibly well thought out design of this game. PLEASE, make a DLC, this is fast becoming my favorite game, and would love to see it expanded on! Cannot recommend this game enough!
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Yet anoher neo-retro metroidvania, this time with a big dose of Simon's Quest, a whiff of Zelda 2 and, as an additional twist, real choices to be made, impacting your environment to varying degree and leading you to one of the four possible endings.Add-in some inventive boss design, acidic humor and built-in cheats to enrich subsequent playthroughs, and you've got a winner, well worth of the ~8 hours you'll need to see it to the end the first time around.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Great little Castlevania 2 / Zelda 2 / Faxandu hommage with good controls and enjoyable gameplay. Nice soundtrack! Also, the game doesn't overstay its welcome, something I always like! But you can get some more playtime out of it by playing the multiple paths/endings (if you want to). I'd say the casula mode is doable even for people who don't usually enjoy "NES-hard" games. I enjoyed this game very much. 8/10!
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely worth the premium over other Simon's Quest-likes. Trust me, I've tried several other, cheaper ones, including one or two that aren't much cheaper, and they're all far from great at best. This one, though, has great dialogue, great graphics, great music, and some of the best gameplay in this type of game though some attacks can be finicky.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game.  This game is basically a love letter to the old school Castlevania (More the Metroidvania type) games but with some modern conveniences.  It's hard but not "Nintendo Hard".  There are so many easter eggs and details put into the game you can tell the developers really love this style of game and it shows.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Worth every penny.   Wife and I loved the Castlevania references such as "wall chicken"  I laughed out loud for a good minute with that one.The only complaints I really had: Enemies with ranged attacks will spam them continously  "Axe throwers" as example.Teleport mobs can go outside the room your in and still shoot in..  The platforming in the almost end dungeons ramps up, but the LAST true dungeon gets ruthless between platforming and enemies.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Slight spoilersIt's a really, really solid game! The game play is very satisfying plays like Castlevania and Zelda II in many ways. The only slight gripe I have is with getting the ""true ending"" but even then it just depends on if you are OK with replaying the game multiple times or not. If so I would easily recommend the game as the reward is so good.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Great game in the vein of Castlevania II, Zelda II, and Faxanadu.  This game is a love letter to those classic games.  A lot of tricky platforming with falls to your death.  Combat gets fairly easy by the end, platforming is more likely to kill you further in.  A lot of people complain about the up-jump attack being janky, I had no issues with it, playing on keyboard.  I rarely failed to pull it off, I was more likely to die from failing a jump in some other way than not having that attack go off.  If all else fails, there are cheats you can use to make certain things easier.  Or some just for fun, like over-the-top gore mode.  Certain things about the game may not be to everyones tastes, but this game nails what it set out to be.  It is exactly what I expected it to be and I loved every minute of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game with a great dark humor theme around it.What else could you asked for in a great retro metroidvania like this one :) !Yes some platforming gets a bit tedious but then you get good and then its no biggy.Great soundtrack!Loved the world! Sad its so small :(:( I want more lore !:DReplay value (hell ya!) I cant say how many times I said .. ah man if only I would ove chosen differently.Will definitely play around the world once more for sure!Thx for making this awesome gem Berzerk Studio and hope you will make many more entry! :D:D:DCheers!
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: I cautiously recommend this game. First impressions are great as you're introduced to this brutal world with choices that have meaningful outcomes and they mostly due, dialogue reacts to you different based on choices you make, and your actions have consequences, something not common for this genre. For me where it falls flat is subsequent playthroughs as the game ask you to beat it multiple times to get all the endings, and honestly, after 1 and a half playthroughs im kinda burnt out on it. Especially since there's no new game + to speak off where you can mostly breeze through enemies to rush through the game, there are cheats invincibility and infinite jumping, but it doesn't change the fact that you have to grind EXP and go through all the dungeons to get each power up and defeat each of the 5 bosses AGAIN to get an ending. For the first playthrough the game is great, every playthrough after that, idk, pace yourself ig.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Music 10/10.Difficulty starts out decent at 6/10 but you quickly become overpowered and the difficulty goes to 2/10.Combat is very simplistic, you swing your mace left or right, block with your shield, jump, duck and cast a spell every 3 minutes or so. :PThe RP element is a bit light for my taste, but it does increase replayability.Fairly small map, tiny dungeons, inconsistent hitboxes and a fairly linear progression.Overall i still enjoyed this game alot more than i expected :DTotal 6/10
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Might be the best NES style metroidvania game (and certainly the best Valentine's Day gift for myself) I have played so far. Bosses are easy, platforms are deadly, but still managed to clear almost all endings in Classic mode.  The more you discovered, the more fun the game will be, unless you suck at platformer part and rage quit.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: What a little gem of a game!  A great revisit to what was great about games like Castlevania 2 and Faxanadu without all the frustrating issues and poor play control. The game has several endings, and you'll want to unlock them to find them all.  If you like a challenge, still play on casual mode.  Casual mode just includes more save points.  Trust me, there is nothing fun about redoing progress.  You'll still have a blast!
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: This brings back child hood memories, literally reminds me as  if its a cross between Castlevania II Simons Quest and Zelda II Adventures of Link. Even some of the mobs remind me of that, not to mention the Day and Night Mobs -.-;  If you like old school  I would recommend it. What I really disliked is that I feel like this game took same ideas , just different weapon and slight different approach.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: This game has so much soul in it.I know that the game just launched but holy crap this is seriously underrated. I really hope and pray this game explodes because from the three hours I have played thus far it has proven more than worthy being a 20-ish dollar game. Its so simple yet I feel like this game bleeds nostalgia for the NES and I love that about this game. The art and music are very well done and mechanically it keeps it simple but also keeps it interesting by building on the existing combat and what not by unlocking new spells and skills like deflecting projectiles instead of only shielding.I am leaving this review in hopes that it will help this game skyrocket. 12/10 would walk across the entire map for potions again.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Zeldamania 2 The Adventure of Good and Evil.This game is fantastic. Really well done with a lot of nods to retro games of past. The sound track is banging, the levels are well designed, the controls are tight and it's gotten me quite worked up quite a few times on the classic difficulty so far.Really good stuff. Can't recommend this enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot believe that this game, a developer must have liked Simon's Quest a lot and I'm glad for that cause we got this game out of that and I feel like there's a hint of Spider-Man Return of the Sinister Six from the NES in it (and probably more)!The music is a banger it's so damn good, the game play is smooth and satisfying but also just a tad bit difficult (on classic mode) to give you a tad bit of pain just like in the old Castlevania games!Highly recommend this game if you like retro style games!
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Infernax is an outstanding game that pays great homage to the games of yesteryear, such as Castlevania 2: Simon's Quest and Zelda 2: The Adventure of Link. The graphics look great, the soundtrack is fantastic, the controls are sharp and responsive and the difficulty (while high) is fair. 10/10, I would highly reccomend this game to anyone who's in the mood for a retro-styled monster-slaying romp.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Good retro platformer action, I appreciate all the small touches that pay tribute to Zelda 2 and Simon's Quest. Some of the platforming can be pretty challenging (learned much later about the R-stick shortcuts, they really help) but that's also fitting with retro experience.The story lines are great. I suggest trying to do all of them. Neat game.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game. Zelda 2-esque style game with the same leveling system. Open world like simon's quest with eventua fast travel. Multiple endings, good vs evil playthrough, secret ending etc. Music is good, controls are responsive, monster variety is okay, dungeons are similar to Zelda 2. Saving can be obnoxious as it forces you to backtrack heavily if you want to save progress during dungeon. One shot pit are meh but it's very nes/snes era like so be aware. I recommend to people who like old platformers, with no checkpoints, progress loss and the whole package. It is a nostalgia trip.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid level design and platforming. Enjoyable exploration and progression.  The art is very good as well.  Difficulty of platforming and normal enemies is moderately high.  Expect to game over numerous times.  Bosses are actually quite easy.  I never died to one until the very final boss (Who killed me in two hits). Has several routes determined by the choices you make through the game. I got a mediocre "good" ending by not choosing absolutely every obvious "good" choice, which seems like it just has less content than going pure good or pure evil.  So there's replayability there, but I recommend just focusing on one side or the other per run.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished my ultimate good run.  Really like this game, highly reccomend it if youre looking for an old retro style castlevania 2 like game.  There is enough differences to make me want to play my ultimate evil tomorrow night!  EDIT:  Took me just over 17 hours to 100%, and I think a few extra hours are on there because you can miss one particular trophy on your ultimate good run, which made me do another whole run.  I love the game wizard codes, and the fact that they dont stop you from getting achievements,  I was able to tackle most of the game on classic mode, once I decided I wanted the achievements I just turned on a couple codes and ran through it hella fast.  I suppose if I had one gripe about it, it would be that I thought it was going to be a bit harder.  I even made it far more difficult for myself, as I wanted to keep my "lives" so anytime I died I would do a save reload to keep my life.  Until I found out the save statues just replenish them anyways.  Music and gameplay are awesome, graphics are the style I like, almost a good 20 hours from an indie game is pretty solid, could have been harder. 9/10 would play the sequel, and will follow this developer for more gems like this!

_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, yes, yes.  LOVE this game.  I've been watching and waiting for this game to drop for some time now, and I'm happy to say I'm not disappointed in the least.  It has the NES look, feel and difficulty that I was really hoping it would have.  Basically, you take Castlevania 2 and Zelda 2, squash them together and you get Infernax.  Day/night cycle and vibe of CV2, leveling/RPG and combat mechanics of Z2, exploration aspect of both and other misc parts of those games thrown in for good measure.  Movement and combat feel very good and the difficulty is at a good level (not easy, but also not unfair)The decisions you have to make are really quite interesting.  It's not the typical "be good and all the good stuff will happen".  There are serious and sometimes negative consequences (increase in difficulty or missing out on something) for choosing the good path (like real life).  I won't say anything beyond that, but I really like the mechanic, even though it hurts sometimes.I only have a little time on Steam so far, but I've played quite a bit more already on Xbox via Game Pass.  Love it so much I had to support the devs and actually buy the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Imagen if Castlevania 2: Simons Quest and Legend of Zelda 2: Links Adventure were combined and made using modern day design principles. A challenging, straight forward 2d action platformer that wear its influences on it sleeves while adding new features to the mix. Highly recommended to support a one man dev team making his fun dream game.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not leaving a negative review because the game has a lot going on for it , but I felt like the most important aspect - combat - was rather underwhelming. I'm used to classic Castlevanias and other retro games, and no matter how simple the core gameplay is, they compensate for it with creative enemy attack patterns and challenging AI behavior. Infernax didn't give me the feel of being challenged when walking through the levels or even fighting bosses.

Something to really test your reactions. But besides that, this game is just solid through and through.

name: Borderlands 3
detailed_description: Borderlands Collection: Pandora's Box This title is included in Borderlands Collection: Pandora's Box! Borderlands 3 Ultimate Edition Borderlands 3 Ultimate Edition is the quintessential Borderlands 3 experience, featuring the base game plus all 6 content add-ons and the full collection of bonus cosmetic packs! Borderlands 3 Super Deluxe Edition Continue your Borderlands 3 adventure with the Season Pass! This content is included with purchase of the Borderlands 3 Super Deluxe Edition, Borderlands 3 Ultimate Edition, and Borderlands 3 Collector's Edition. The Season Pass includes: Moxxi’s Heist of the Handsome Jackpot campaign add-on. Guns, Love, and Tentacles campaign add-on. Bounty of Blood campaign add-on. Psycho Krieg and the Fantastic Fustercluck campaign add-on. All 4 Multiverse Final Form Cosmetic Packs. A Butt Stallion weapon skin, weapon trinket and grenade mod. About the Game The original shooter-looter returns, packing bazillions of guns and an all-new mayhem-fueled adventure! Blast through new worlds and enemies as one of four brand new Vault Hunters – the ultimate treasure-seeking badasses of the Borderlands, each with deep skill trees, abilities, and customization. Play solo or join with friends to take on insane enemies, score loads of loot and save your home from the most ruthless cult leaders in the galaxy. A MAYHEM-FUELED THRILL RIDE Stop the fanatical Calypso Twins from uniting the bandit clans and claiming the galaxy’s ultimate power. Only you, a thrill-seeking Vault Hunter, have the arsenal and allies to take them down. YOUR VAULT HUNTER, YOUR PLAYSTYLE Become one of four extraordinary Vault Hunters, each with unique abilities, playstyles, deep skill trees, and tons of personalization options. All Vault Hunters are capable of awesome mayhem alone, but together they are unstoppable. LOCK, LOAD, AND LOOT With bazillions of guns and gadgets, every fight is an opportunity to score new gear. Firearms with self-propelling bullet shields? Check. Rifles that spawn fire-spewing volcanoes? Obviously. Guns that grow legs and chase down enemies while hurling verbal insults? Yeah, got that too. NEW BORDERLANDS Discover new worlds beyond Pandora, each featuring unique environments to explore and enemies to destroy. Tear through hostile deserts, battle your way across war-torn cityscapes, navigate deadly bayous, and more! QUICK & SEAMLESS CO-OP ACTION Play with anyone at any time with online co-op, regardless of your level or mission progress.

_childDocuments_.review: Times have changed, and it seems the game has changed for the better. When i first wrote my review i was very harsh, i was upset with the lag/stutter. It was horrendous. I am not just saying that, even on my missus PS4, and my PS4 Pro the lag was awful, even loading the map was a massive strain and caused the game to freeze. At the time of the review though it was in January of 2020, and at that time, they was a program at work within Borderlands, called Denuvo. I do not know if it caused the lag and the stutter i was having but it was safe to say that i tested the game on 3 different Computers i had at my disposal at the time, fairly high end as well for the time and all 3 suffered the same problem. Since then though Denuvo has been removed, somewhere in January 2021, a full year later after i had reviewed the game originally. I was still upset with the game and i did not even bother to check if it had improved. The year is now February 2022, and Dying light 2 has just been released. And i had to refund it in the first 2 hours because the FPS drops was awful, and turns out the game is using Denuvo as well, i do not know if it causes the FPS drops and i don't care the game plays awful, but i decided to come and check borderlands 3 with my missus after looking up Denuvo and seeing it was removed from Borderlands.It is like finding a Diamond in the Rough. This game is just what i needed right now. It plays fantastic in it's highest settings (yes that setting past ultra called badass). The game is colourful , vibrant , funny, engaging, fast paced, hectic fun. It is a perfect Co-op game.  Yes the game had a rocky start with FPS issues and it did ruin the game, but it seems to have been sorted. Since playing this time around i have not had no serious issues, nothing game breaking, nothing that has hindered my fun. I have enjoyed my self so much with my partner that last night we bought all the content, all of it, we do not regret it and i can see me coming back to this game every couple of years just like i do with halo,dead island and other co-op games,to have a blast. It truly is a great game now.  Oh and the DLC, My god so much content, it just keeps on giving, well thought out story content for the dlc's i am not disappointed.Previous review :Take is game off the store and start again. I am serious, re-write the bloody game. i am fortunate to have 3 PCs at my disposal, and all 3 had massive fps drops. From shooting my first bullet can drop from 210 fps ( had to take vsync off as i thought maybe just maybe that could of been the culprit)  to 40 fps, or going to loot a chest can drop to low as 30, or opening the map dropping my fps. My fps will then immediately go back to normal, but these damn fps drops make it impossible for me to play, the worst bit, i wanted to like it on here as i have it on ps4 pro as well, and it runs terrible on that as well, but consoles are crap in general i at least thought it would run butter smooth on here, and it don't. This was the same across 3 of my PCs. i also tried lowering the detail and it still did the same thing. Even at this point i can tell it is poorly optimised. People claim its that denuvo anti cheat thing that runs at a kernal level , god knows what it is but what i do know is i can not handle a game dropping so many frames so often. Looked at the reviews they is over 7k negative reviews and alot of people are having stuttering/fps drops. Sort your ♥♥♥♥. otherwise if you ever do a borderlands 4, or any other type of game, i will be keeping the hell away, just like bethesda, wont touch their games either anymore.FF Online, they made a hash of things, they pulled it off , they fixed it from the ground up,now its fantastic. Be like FF, and fix your stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: While Borderlands 3 has seen some of the best combat, the game itself won't stack up to other games such as Doom Eternal, Far Cry 5, Shadow Warrior 2, and other games, especially considering that there are crashing issues that can ruin the experience with your friend(s) and now we got a Season Pass 2 which is commonplace in fighters nowadays and which I believe could have been resources used to develop Borderlands 4 or better yet, reboot the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ franchise in some way because at this point, the story is unsalvageable even if the DLCs themselves were good and offered good character development in comparison to the main quest.This game has good moments sure but if you are like me and play video games for the story, you will be disappointed unless you find some way to ignore the story and I will say this, when Claptrap is no longer the most hated character, you know you ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up and even better, the worst part of the story isn't just Ava, it's that for some reason, the story takes the focus off nearly every ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ male character to put focus on the female characters probably because of some political agenda or something and worse yet, they decided to turn Tannis into a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Siren and thus, ended up turning her into a borderline Mary-Sue (Ava's Mary-Sue status is worse) and a sad part? If you were hoping for an epic battle that was being teased in Borderlands 2 and Pre-Sequel's endings, you will be disappointed, because I am. Was the TPS ending non-canon? Are we just going to ignore Hyperion? Apparently so, because it feels like they don't care about the story anymore.Additionally, I find the limited-time events to be BS and think they do not belong in video games. Animal Crossing did it right, sure but the way other developers are executing it in the MMO fashion is absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cancer and it worse yet, feeds on people's FOMO. Thank god I can cheat my way to obtain the collectibles.Now for some positive parts, the soundtrack is great, I already said the combat is good and going through the levels was great, hell I even enjoyed part of the story until Ava came along (loved the Maliwan Arc, should have replaced Children of the Vault with that entirely), and the first Season Pass offered enjoyable DLCs that didn't feel too in-your-face. Unfortunately however, this game is marred by a poorly constructed and executed storyline, poor business model that is sure to increase the game's overall price especially to double dippers, crashing issues that can ruin the co-op experience (hell, crossplay between Steam and Epic was near-impossible), and well, Randy Pitchford.Overall, wait for a good sale, because this game is great but it's not really worth buying at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Take my positive review with a grain of salt; more just because I rate it on a personal 0-10 scale just above midpoint.Borderlands 3 is a fitting sequel in a trilogy of games that are, overall, bland to the point of unsalted fries seeming exciting. It's chock full of loot, shoot, move and more action than you could ever hope to manage - no, really, when they said there would be tons of loot in the ad spot, they weren't kidding. Carrying all the shiny stuff you find can be a hassle early game, and even late into the main story. Not only that, but the frequency of the loot drops degrades the satisfaction of it very fast. You can easily end up in the mindset of, "well, looks like I'll not check that chest yet", or other cardinal sins of looter-shooters.Questionable story choices abound, though I won't go into those out of interest of preserving spoilers; the game gets better toward the end, and not just because the credits are so close you can taste them. That said, to critique the Borderlands franchise on its plot is like doing the same to the Doom franchise; the story is there, it can be enjoyed, but you're here to fire lead into the hordes of savages.Just like the story being overall bland in previous titles of Borderlands, 3 also maintains the trend of the DLC being the best, and most satisfying, part of the experience. I highly recommend getting the full copy of the game, so when/if you begin to burn out like I did slogging through the lettuce and sour cream burrito that is the main story, you can flip it around and get into the delicious meaty other half.Some of the DLC is rather short, especially if you're coming in at the later levels. That said, also unlike the story, the DLC stories and main body of missions doesn't overstay their welcome, and are pretty satisfying to finish.In closing, the time I played is how long it took me to beat the DLC and main game in one playthrough, After finishing the main game, I quit, uninstalled, and I don't intend to reinstall until the new DLC comes out. Take that for what you will.

_childDocuments_.review: Soooo...over the course of playing this from start to finish I've ended up being saddled with one burning question searing into my brain - WHY AM I STILL PLAYING THIS PIECE OF ♥♥♥♥?!The story starts out entertaining, but quickly becomes both annoying and insulting; the antagonists are tedious, lacking any of the wit or charisma that Handsome Jack had. To use wrestling terms, they don't have heel heat, they just have "go away heat" (in other words, it's not fun to boo them, you just want them off the screen); It tries to replicate the shock of what happened in 2 with Roland's death, which ultimately falls flat both because we've barely got to know the character from an NPC to player perspective, and because it's just setting a bad precedent for expectations; None of the plot twists are interesting or unexpected, you can see them coming a mile off. Claptrap and Tiny Tina BOTH take up more prominent roles, a concept which just baffles as they are like red hot pokers in my ears every time they open their mouths; it does a horribly obnoxious fake-out ending, made all the worse by the fact your character isn't present in the cutscene; to expand on that you're not present in any of the cutscenes, which is especially insulting when it comes to the post-final bossfight cutscene! One of the characters has essentially been setup to fail in a lot of fans' eyes because those fans will only ever associate them with being the cause of the aforementioned character death. And the storymode's ending isn't simply insulting, but outright offensive to anyone who ever had any investment in the series and characters, especially as it ultimately denies the player the ability to be the one to save the world.And then there's the technical side of things, some are actual observed problems, others are just personal gripes: We STILL can't abandon or reset quests, which is especially irritating if you happen to misinterpret the sentence "talk to me before you go" as "you can talk to these people in whatever order you want, but the quest won't be available before you've spoken to me", silly me *eyeroll*; inventory is still a mess, I don't know if this is because it's optimised for console or what, but that's not an excuse, get your ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ alignments sorted; getting quick travel to work is a chore as even when you're clicking on the right spot, it won't initiate until you click on the correct side-menu; one manufacturer of weapons is, in my opinion, almost completely useless with the exception of the SMG's, and I don't know if that's an intentional bad joke on the part of the devs, or if they're just badly designed, but either way Maliwan weapons are mostly only useful for pocket money; Eridium has been relegated to only being used for buying cosmetic upgrades, making the farming of it next to pointless, whilst in Borderlands 2, it was needed to get those all important inventory and weapon clip upgrades. But now those are all paid for with standard cash, meaning that you're desperately having to penny-pinch to make it possible to expand inventory to a size worth a ♥♥♥♥; Reload times are absolutely horrendous with some weapons, with some of them taking so long that I was sometimes thinking "Shall I just get myself killed, it'll probably be faster?"; Cutscene text can end up constantly appearing on-screen for hours after the cutscene happened. This can also happen if you go out of bounds and die, with the alert continuing to flash after you revive. In both cases fixed by quitting to menu and starting again, but THIS SHOULDN'T NEED TO BE DONE.And then there's the fact that Gearbox/2K are gouging for so much DLC it's unreal. Here's a great idea - how about you make a decent game first, then I might consider getting the DLC (In case anyone is wondering, what DLC I do have I won in a giveaway)I'm likely forgetting a whole host of things that annoy me about this game, but overall I just hate this and the only reason I completed it was because I'd already gotten as far as I had.I would say the game is in desperate need of patching, but no amount of patching can rescue it from the utterly garbage story. And of course, it's not like that patching will happen anyway now that Borderlands 4 has been announced, which will undoubtedly perpetuate all of the technical and logistical problems mentioned above, because why fix what has been broken since 2009?

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of fun to play in single player, I had some troubles with the shift network when the game first released on steam.  So I dropped the game for a few months, came back and it seems most of the issues have been worked out or patched.   Borderlands 3 stays true to the original formula in a lot of ways which I think is good and bad.   The worlds are amazing and everything looks fantastic. The game plays about the same, shoot everything, loot and upgrade.  The humor isnt a lot better than the pre sequel though..  I dont think it compares to BL2 when it comes to this.  A lot of the character dialogue just doesnt have the same impact as it did.. maybe its nostalgia for me? but it feels like its cheesing out on the fart jokes and I didnt find anything substantial that made me legit laugh out loud.   The game still checks a lot of boxes for me, it was fun overall.. just wasnt unique in anyway I guess.Great game overall, at the very least its worth a playthrough for anybody that is a fan of the franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: Now, this is a complicated case to crack. The Borderlands series is a well-known one, with a certain style of graphics, guns and comedy. This game follows all of these characteristics, yet fails in one, major one, that I did not yet mention.The writing for this game is... not good, to say the least. The story's filled with holes, insufferable characters, has no logic and breaks its own roles a few times. Does that mean the game's awful?I'm sorry,  it doesn't. Yes, no doubt, it can drain some of the fun sometimes, but the quality of the combat, graphics and side missions is probably the best in the whole series.TL:DRWhile suffering from a (very) bad story, Borderlands 3 is an awesome game, with amazing gun-play and nice comedy writing, and it has its qualities. I would advise to buy it when on discountRating: 7

_childDocuments_.review: There are some good points to this game, the gun play is the best of the series, the loot drop rate feels more rewarding than before, but there is a lot more that I take issue with this game. The story is... pretty bad. The story destroys the characters, there isn't a single character I like in the game, apart from maybe the main 4 vault hunters, all of which have pretty boring base game focus trees IMO, they're really bland. The story, in combination with the level design, are just so bad that I really don't want to play this game, To put it in perspective, I still did multiple playthroughs of The Pre-sequel FFS, and yet I don't want to play through the story of this game for even a 2nd time.Then there is the DLC, none of it is worth it, at best it's only as good as the base game, but most of it is worse. There's also the "2 season passes" that I COMPLETELY disapprove of, that is scummy and deceitful and Gearbox should be ashamed of that. For the price of what they are too, you get shockingly little content from the DLCs, they feel shorter than Borderlands 2s DLCs.Don't buy this game, if you want a co-op looter-shooter, go buy any other Borderlands game (Except for Tales, it's not a looter shooter, but it's still damn good) and you will not only have a better time, but they're better value as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Borderlands 3 is arguably the best looter shooter out there right now. Shooting feels great, gameplay loop is spot on and to cap it all, the endgame is strong with only the potential to get bigger and better. The game itself doesn't do anything particularly new or inventive, but what's there is entertaining and engaging. Not without it's downsides though. The writing is pretty poor generally, especially when compared with its predecessor Borderlands 2. The humour from back then which was fairly solid at the time seems immature and gaudy now, though there are occasional moments that shine. Inventory management is also a minor pain. It works okay and the stats are clear, but I can't help but think there could have been a better way of implementing this system.Overall, very enjoyable game that does a brilliant job of making you feel powerful while providing a challenge, and there are a nice number of improvements on the previous games as well. Just has some bumps along the road.

_childDocuments_.review: If you love Borderlands then you'll love this.  There's very little original in mechanics aside that my untrained eye can tell.  I'm running it smoothly on an old Intel Core 7 with 16GB RAM and a 980ti GeForce card.  I am not running it at Ultra settings, mostly because i don't like some settings like atmospheric fog.  Also despite early reports that the game runs better in DirectX 11 i am running it fine with DirectX 12.The story is interesting enough to keep me engaged.  I typically only play co-op games and this one is no exception.  It's very enjoyable with a friend or two or three.  I've tried two different characters now,  The voice acting is top notch.  The puzzles are fun and the scenarios and side quests are unique enough to make me want to do every single one of them.My friends are not as excited about the game but they play a lot of PUBG and other FPS.  I did find some guns can get in the way of targeting.  Some weapons are just pure fun!  Get this title on sale and you probably won't be disappointed;  I wasn't!

This game suffers an issue with alot of modern RPGs where as you gain levels and abilities, you become more and more weak until you're unfathomably weak unless you play their stupid item game where you use weapons and armor you don't like that bar off half of what you want to do just to not die.and the drop off is bad too, there is no "Challenging but possible" middle ground. You are either mowing through everything or dying every 5 seconds and it all due to the level of your items and nothing to do with your build or your skill at the game. I even tested this and didn't put any points in any ability at level 30 and was still as unreasonably strong as before, it's like levels give you 10% of your strength and items do the other 90%, and when items are obtain solely based on the luck of the draw, that's not a good way of doing things. and this isn't end game stuff, this is still doing the story. I can understand an End game where you have to grtind for better equipment and carefully pick and choose how to play your character, but that isn't the bulk of the game. It's like the game designers were so proud of their items that they balanced the game solely around the items and made huge gulfs of power between each level so your "+15% gun damage" that you spent 5 levels getting means nothing when in those 5 levels gun damage has increased by nearly 200% from just better equipment. Even the very 1st Borderlands knew how to balance higher level drops

_childDocuments_.review: I pre-ordered the game on Epic, put in all my hours there before getting the edition here on Steam later on. It was on sale, it had all the DLCs, and was cheaper than buying them all for the Epic version. Win-win!Game is fun, it has nice mechanics, fun worlds to explore. I love the vehicles. The characters are fun, with interesting enough skill trees. Interesting enough stories. I loved seeing some of the old cast and helping them out with quests. Loved Hammerlock's whole quest line! Loved that we got more lore here and there on the previous cast and new cast. Not sure how I feel about what happened with the cast from Tales from the Borderlands, personally. They felt very shoe-horned in to me, like it was a last minute choice because of how popular that game got. I loved the cast from that game, but they felt very out of character in this one. Also there's some, uh, plot holes. But I digress.The story as a whole felt a little underwhelming, but that honestly could have just been the case of me setting my hopes so high for it. It's not a bad story, really. I did enjoy it for the most part. I enjoyed the new cast of characters for the most part. I noticed a few people also felt underwhelmed by it, the hype for it was pretty wild after all. But I still think it's partially due to that hype that so many people felt disappointed. Could it have been better? Yes. But it really could have been a lot worse, too. I enjoyed it. I still think it's worth picking up if you enjoy the series. Though I will say, it doesn't quite feel as much like a Borderlands game as the other games did. Story wise or gameplay wise. But that's not necessarily a bad thing. I'm sure some people enjoy the chances, the new feel. I don't hate them, but it certainly feels different. I'm not sure I'd recommend this as an introduction to the series for new players, however. I'd probably go for Borderlands 2 for that, as it feels like the friendliest intro for people who are new to games and the franchise. Borderlands 1 is where it starts, of course, but I've seen people turned off from the series due to the dated style and mechanics in that one. But ultimately, this game isn't a bad entry to the franchise in my opinion. Just not what a lot of us were hoping for, I guess!

_childDocuments_.review: This is what happens when you take a solid core game and start welding bad design to it.  There are positives to Borderlands 3, and I can say good things about it, but they tend to be undercut in a way that spoils them.Characters have interesting skills and foci to play with, so building them up is more interesting.  That's good!  But they're also hilariously unbalanced, with some options brutally gear-dependent, some classes leagues below the others in power, and some skills mathematically inferior.  This makes multiplayer frustrating - when one member of the team is slaying gods and another is struggling to compete with mooks, neither one is having fun.Equipment (and skills) are complex, with things you can equip to try out strange functions and master odd abilities.  That's good!  However, your options are often 'Use intricate combo to deal slightly increased damage,' or 'Click button to obliterate everything.'  Gimmicks are only worth it if they pay off, and Borderlands 3 has a habit of making the option that just blows everyone up 100x more efficient than the one that's challenging to use.There are in-game events, with seasonal changes and gameplay mutators that alter the game on the fly.  That's good!  They're also invasive, unbalancing, and out of your control.  This feeds into equipment issues - time-limited weapons stronger than anything you can find outside events are a balance problem, and once those events end they make every new, cool drop that can't compete disappointing.But really the trouble lies in the characters and storyline.  The villains in the base campaign are obnoxious, but not as people; I don't want to destroy them, I just want them to not be in a game I'm playing.  Meanwhile I do dislike one of the "good" NPCs, but the narrative clearly wants me to be enchanted by her and she doesn't grow and learn so much as be patted on the head by the writers.  This is also not a plot that respects your character - you're here to witness, not participate.  I spent a whole cutscene in which a fan-favorite character is slowly executed wondering "Why can't I do anything to stop this?" and the only answer was "Because the player isn't part of this story beat," which brought me to the Eight Deadly Words - I don't care what happens to these people.  I was already bored and frustrated by the gameplay, so that pretty much tore it for me.I have really enjoyed this series, but Borderlands 3 is where I get off.  Thumbs down.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has never been  enamored with the Borderlands series - and given this game's generally apathetic-to-negative response online - I have been overall, pleasantly surprised. This is the first Borderlands title that I found truly enjoyable when playing solo.The movement and gun-play are both far more fluid and 'modern' for lack of a better descriptor; the previous Borderlands games have all felt just a little clunky and old fashioned to me.Loot is more numerous and the guns are, on average, much more use-able and don't become useless after only a couple of level ups. This fixes a real issue I had with the previous games, where you could hit a bad run of RNG and after a few levels, you had no decent weapons and the game became a painful chore to progress.Co-op now gives you the option of either individual loot and level scaling, or the old system of everyone fighting over the same drops and no scaling. This is a nice quality of life improvement.Borderlands 3 has gotten a lot of criticism for it's 'bad story', but its the exact same story that every Borderlands game has. The characters and writing are a slightly different matter though... While I consider Handsome Jack to be unironically annoying and wildly over-rated as an antagonist, the Calypso Twins (a caricature of streamers/influencers) are a grating misstep by the new writers, whose attempts at humour usually fall flat too.Beating the main story (which is too lengthy) unlocks both the new Mayhem Mode and True Vault Hunter Mode. This is frankly a chore on more than one character, and the implementation of Mayhem Mode has made TVHM completely irrelevant which is a shame.Mayhem Mode has 10 levels, each of which vastly increases enemy HP and the odds of getting rare loot drops, as well as adding an annoying combination of positive and negative game modifiers. Higher levels means better quality and quantity of loot though, so you will want to work up to Mayhem 10 ASAP.I can recommend Borderlands 3 to loot shooter fans, but depending on your tolerance for having to regrind all your gear or dealing with hard earned gear getting nerfed, you might be better off waiting until all the DLC is out and the level cap is finalised (Mid Sept 2020).The DLC is all pretty good (peoples opinions vary wildly on which is good and which is bad), and includes some really strong gear, so I would recommend picking up the Season Pass as well.Randy Pitchford is a douchebag, and I have no great love for Gearbox, but it's a thumbs up for BL3.

_childDocuments_.review: As somebody who grew up in the Borderlands, with 1 being my first ever fps game and the series itself my favorite of all time, I've probably clocked in about a thousand hours of gameplay across all systems. I've spent a lot of time running, gunning, and looting, and I can say without a doubt that 3 has the best gameplay, core mechanics, and weapons out of the four mainline games. Unfortunately, every other aspect is worse. Of all things to notice first, the music sucks. It doesn't have the twangy, desolate desert vibe that it used to. Or any vibe really. It's not a part of the overall experience, and that sucks. When you fought Jack, you were always happy when he showed up in the upper right, talking about one insane thing or other. You fight the Calypsos, you feel like actively tearing your ears off while desperately searching for something to do that isn't stand in a locked room, *waiting*, and being mocked by children. Whereas before, the Claptraps were little asides, defects of happiness and idiocy in a world of angry screaming and bloodshed. Now, everybody is Claptrap. And since everybody acts that way, when Claptrap does it's also frustrating, which is more frustrating in of itself because I freaking love Claptrap. This girl's got a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Claptrap figurine that she high fives as she walks past it; it's an issue. The plot for this game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ nonexistent. They ruin the canon of the other games by making all of their events mean nothing. When they made tension between Troy and Tyreen, where we thought 'oh man they're annoying, but it could be worth it if they killed each other', nothing happens. They do *nothing* with that story beat, and it's the only decent one. The only good characters are the ones not originally from this game, and Waynewrite Jakobs and Clay. The game is buggy as hell, and if you don't want it to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ crash on open you have to wait a full minute after you load in for the game to load in even more ♥♥♥♥ so you can't open your inventory. Mantling flat out sucks; you can grab stuff that is ungrabbable and the stuff that seems close is a million miles away. There's no way to actually farm car parts (even though the vehicle system is kinda cool), so god ♥♥♥♥ knows if you'll ever get all the unique parts. The few times I actually see new things I'm in a scripted sequence and they randomly spawned in. To even be able to play the game, I have to mute all sound, turn on music, and skip every cutscene (which by the way, wasn't in the game at launch, so it sucked even more!), and dutifully ignore most of the subtitles. The game just isn't worth it. You can get fun out of it, but it's so hard. You shouldn't have to work to have fun in a game who's only two premises are 'shoot' and 'loot'. You would be so much better off playing The Presequel or Two. Both of those games have ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing stories and great characters. Tales From The Borderlands (where Rhys and Vaughn are from) is a great game, and even though the same characters in 3 are the worst, in Tales they're much more unique and interesting. Hell, go play One. That game still holds up to this day, and I think the remaster is like 20 bucks. I couldn't tell you how much they changed because all that mattered to me was Autopickup of health and ammo. One is aged and shows it, but hey.Anything is better than Borderlands 3.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know really if to recommend this game or not. It's really hard to say, because I like the gameplay but extremely dislike the story. And it makes me unable to appreciate the game completely.For a Borderlands game the gameplay, gunplay and movement is on point, having improved movement with a handy sliding and returning with the slam attack from Borderlands Pre-Sequel. The weapons has further diversified since Borderlands 2, with each company weapon having an even more unique thing that makes them special. It's very meme-internet culture and grounded extremely within the weird odd ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ land the internet has become today. I and my friend never got further than the second 'world,' before we quit because there was nothing captivating me. The villains are bland, Lilith returns and continue to be a nail in my eye, everyone continues down the rabbithole of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ insane logic and weirdness. _childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of the Borderland franchise.  Do I recommend this for any Borderlands fan, yes of course.But how do you compare this to the moderlode of looter-shooters, Borderlands 2?  You just can't. Borderlands 2, It's too grand, too perfect.  It is the ultimate experience in the franchise.  From the dark humor to the incomparable Handsome Jack as your grand protagonist.  There's just nothing to compare.  The content, the story, the engagement, the characters in 2 was the peak experience.  In Borderland 3, there is a desperate reach to keep Handsome Jack in the players mind, but who can blame them?  There'll never be another Jack.  And let's face it, after Jack, we need a truly worthy adversary to feel that initial excitement again.  In the successive entries, Pre-Sequel and Borderlands 3, you lose a lot of the excitement that came with Borderlands 2.  A game I invested  1300+ hours in.  A game I'd easily go back to.  Here in Borderlands 3, it of course carries forth the world and gameplay with some tweaks here and there.  And I'd happily recommend it to the BL fans.  I would recommend playing the Telltale Borderlands for character continuity between 2 and 3, it will give you a more complete story that segues into where BL3 begins.  And have fun with the game, temper your expectations from BL2, it lacks the scale, grandiosity, storytelling and complexity for the genre, that we had in BL2.  BL3 feels very old hat without that many ingenuous additions.  I also found access to legendary gear so generous that farming was rarely needed.  Hit up the mayhem levels for a challenge.  This review is less about the technicals and more about how it makes me feel, you're already familiar with those I am sure at this point.  I want a sequel that made me feel how I felt playing BL2.  BL3 simply doesn't hit that note.
