_childDocuments_.review: Borderlands 3 is a big step up in the franchise and is definitely the best game in the series. POSITIVES:-Has AMAZING game/gunplay. Everything feels smooth and polished-Side quests and crew challenges are great. I found myself enjoying almost all the side quests and crew challenges added another great layer of completion.-Drops are much more frequent, but the addition of anointments separate those who want to grind and want a casual playthrough.-Mayhem modes are a great substitute for UVHM, and add great difficulty adjustments-DLC stories are amazing and consistently great. They feel way more polished compared to the main story.-CO-OP has never been better. No problems connecting, staying in game and joining other people.-Game has never crashed apart from day 1 and modding.-Every character is good and balanced. No character is bad solo or in co-op, and multiple play styles make for plenty of replay-Consistent gun buffs; the devs are focused on buffing bad guns compared to nerfing powerful guns which is making gameplay much healthier-Consistent events for solo and co-op play; ranging from boosted drop-rates, events with exclusive equipmentMIXED:-Arms race is fun and a great idea, but needs more added onto it. More maps and enemies would make it worth the price.-Raid bosses aren't in the game but are substituted with Takedowns. Takedowns are where you fight multiple difficult areas of enemies before getting to a final boss. This adds more strategy to getting to a boss, but means less endgame bosses (compared to BL2). This is more of a personal issue for me.-Older hardware can cause some crashes and slowdowns. I'm currently using a 2060 with no problems at all.NEGATIVES:-Main story is a letdown. Main characters are a let down and the lore becomes complicated. The plot doesn't make sense majority of the time. Dialog can come off as cringe and empty. However, at least it does a great job of making you hate the main villain. Story is improved on the DLC.-Cutscenes and in game story is way to long and kills some of the flow. Listening to characters talk in front of you while you sit there and do nothing is annoying. -There are some bugs and glitches still in the game, mainly to do with quest objectives and bosses. Some characters don't move to continue the objective. However, they've all been fixed with a simple save-quit and rejoin.If you're purely looking to play this game for its story, solo, and without any dlc, this is not the game for you. Borderlands 3 builds and excels on everything else the previous games in the series have to offer, and is the definitive looter shooter game out there today.  Also, you will have much more fun playing the game co-op with friends no matter what. I still have so much to explore in the game and I'm almost 200 hours in. Don't sleep on this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Borderlands 3... was a disappointment. And that's hard to say. I played through the game twice, with two different friends on two different characters. I would say I enjoyed the first 2/5, was neutral for the second 2/5, and actively disliked the last fifth of the game. The second play through was neutral to dislike all the way through, with some exceptions - and ultimately, having beaten it once, made the game feel like a chore.The story is largely nonsense and the ending is rediculous, almost to the point I feel insulted for having been subjected to it. The siblings aren't nearly as memorable or interesting as Handsome Jack - though I suppose they have their own charm, I don't hate them. Bringing back old characters is nice. That little girl I'm glad I've already forgotten the name of can leave for good, though, but unfortunately she's a key part of the story so if ever there's a 4 you know she's coming back and I hope they REALLY overhaul her character.The best part of the game for me was Lorelai - I don't know why but I just really love her character and every time she was around I was happy. Second best, ... it's taking me a long time to think of a second best, I guess the hub ship is pretty neat, but easy to get a little lost or turned around in. Overall, unless you're going through the whole series or really are a Borderlands fanatic, I strongly recommend playing through 2 instead. It's far more memorable and fun even all these years later.

_childDocuments_.review: I decided to finish the game and some of the DLC before writing this review so I could have a fair judgement of the game. I'm also going to exclude anything about the handling of the exclusivity deals and the general state of the everybodys favourite gearbox employee, you know the one I'm talking about. Borderlands 3 is actually a very good game that suffers from a bit of misinterpretation. A lot of people criticise the writing of the game, while not really understanding the reasons for it. A good example of this are the main villains. The main villains are childish and obnoxious throughout the entire story, they act like little kids on a power trip, because that's essentially what they are; children who haven't really had the growth to become adults. It's also why a lot of the jokes fall flat, which to be fair is the same problem borderlands 2 had.The gameplay has had a large number of improvements that greatly benefit the series, from new player actions, better enemy AI, more enemy visual variety, better character customisation, significantly more bosses/minibosses, more vehicle customisation, etc. Also a lot of characters which were degraded to stereotypes in borderlands 2, have been redeemed by given a decent amount of character growth.However there are a few parts that have degraded from these new systems; for starters they implemented a number system to give you an idea of how good a weapon/piece of equipment is. Unfortunately because the number accounts for all the bonuses a weapon has it often gives you an idea that the equipment is better than it actually is in practise. A good example of that system failing is; I had a weapon that was over 100 points higher than another in the same class for the level, but because it had a number of add ons for the weapon, the damage stat was so garbage, the gun was practically useless.And speaking of weapon problems, the rarity of legendary weapons is absurd. It's nice that there are a lot more legendaries in the game than the previous game, but before I even got to the 3/4 mark of the game I had so many legendary weapons in my inventory and bank, I was having to decide which ones to throw away, and that was even with pooling all my money into buying storage deck upgrades (inventory space upgrades for non borderlands people). Legendary weapons are far too common in my opinion which makes them feel less worthy.Now I played as Moze for my first playthrough, so difficulty may vary for others. But as my choice of character was ridiculously tanky, I found the difficulty to be quite easy for the majority of the game. The vast majority of my respawns were due to DoT effects that lasted a long time, and falling out of bounds. However the main problem I have with difficulty were from the bosses. There was one particular boss I fought that I only beat because my passive healing, action skill and general tankiness, which lead me to a turtle off that I came out on top of. However that was the only boss I had any trouble with. I was actually genuinely disappointed in how easy both of the main villains boss fights were, sure they had some interesting mechanics, and Tyrene did an absurd amount of damage IF she hit you, but in general I thought they'd be a lot harder than they were. But then again I was fully decked out in legendary gear by the final boss fight so maybe that had something to do with it. I defeated Troy by using a sniper rifle that left behind floating shock orbs, and IIRC he didn't even manage to break my shield.Despite the few problems I had with the game, which also included the occasional trigger point (button/switch/item drop) not working properly, and falling through solid items in the map (which was fixed by a quick quit to main menu, and reload of the game). I thoroughly enjoyed BL3. The ending is a bit cheesy, but still pretty nice. I don't think the game deserves a lot of the hate it receives, and I think the developers should be proud of what they've achieved. I fully recommend this game to fans of the borderlands franchise, and other looter shooters.

_childDocuments_.review: Borderlands 3. The sequel to one of my favorite games I've ever played: Borderlands 2. This game is an insult to the story that has been built up around the universe that Gearbox has built. The gameplay is good. Fun, even. I find all the Vault Hunters a bit bland, but maybe I'm just too attached to Krieg and Sal's gamebreaking antics. That's not what I'm talking about though. The main campaign of Borderlands 3 is an absolute DUMPSTER FIRE. The way they treat established characters is downright insulting, and the way they treat new characters (except Wainwright, he's the only decent character they made) is a crime. Lilith has been downgraded into a child with no intelligence, emotional or otherwise.  Ava. Don't get me started, this character right here is one of the worst written excuses for drama I've ever seen. Characters (good ones anyways) grow and change throughout the story. Ava is the same character at the end as she was when you first met her. She's an entitled brat who blames everyone but herself for things that go wrong, then goes and mopes about it like a child. She's not a child, she's a student of a badass Vault Hunter. Maya must have been on CRACK when she took in Ava, because she is a miserable excuse for a character. There is no growth. There is no change. She  The Calypso twins, Tyreen and Troy, are almost interesting. Well, Troy is. Tyreen is a completely static character, never changing her views, treating you differently,  or ever treating you with respect. I hate to bring up a GOOD game in this review, but remember Jack? What happened to the writers for him? Did they get thrown into the Overlook grinder for not  working enough crunch time? Did Randy Pitchford fire them all? Jack was fantastically written, and I refuse to believe it was on accident. He changed, grew, and AT LEAST GAVE A ♥♥♥♥ WHEN YOU DID THINGS. Speaking of that, cutscenes. In previous titles, your character wasn't in the cutscenes, but characters acknowledged that you were there, and worked around the player. There is approximately one cutscene in this game that acknowledges the player, and that's when Troy actually gets character development.  In a LOT of cutscenes, events play out in front of you, and you are essentially in limbo. Nobody knows you're even there, and you're powerless to stop what is happening. If you've played through the game, you know what I'm talking about.  They have straight up IGNORED loose ends, without a single mention. Fiona? Who's that? Where's Axton and Salvador? Who cares, they're not AVA, our lovable lil' scamp of a character, you'll love her, I promise. Let's talk about Troy. He was so close to being a good villain, maybe even a great one, but they didn't do ANYTHING with his character development. He feels like he's always overshadowed by his sister, and when he gets the ability to stand up for himself, he starts to talk back to Tyreen. That's something! Anything! And then? Nothing. They don't flesh him out into a better villain. They don't go anywhere with his story. They just drop him and don't look back, because I guess Tyreen IS better than him after all. Whoopsie! Almost had a decent story for a second there. Beloved characters like Brick, Mordecai and Tina are put on the backburner and are used for a couple of quests, then are trashed like they were never there to begin with. Krieg gets a whopping FEW ECHO logs of information as to what he's been up to. Gaige is mentioned ONCE in the base game in an ECHO log, but she doesn't actually say anything, because it's just people talking about her. Zer0 gets a couple of moments in the spotlight, but once you're done with Promethea, count him out of the story. This is a theme with this game. Characters that are used on a planet typically get used for a few missions and then are left to rot. Lorelei? I never really liked her, but she was tossed aside. Rhys? Love him or hate him, he's not coming back. Wainwright and Hammerlock? Gone until their DLC. The list drags on and on and on without looking back. I didn't like what they did with Vaughn in Fight for Sanctuary, but don't worry, he's even worse now and is only in the game for the first and last acts. Finally, there is not a strong male character in this game that isn't a playable character, and that just means Zane (and Fl4k, depending on who you ask.) Zer0 isn't really a big part of the story, and we don't even know what he is, or if he's a he at all. Marcus has 0 impact, and Wainwright and Hammerlock are shoved aside to have other people take over. All of the male leads are bumbling idiots, evil, or both. I wish so very badly that I could love this game, that it was worth waiting 7 years for. It isn't. I don't have the motivation to play the DLCs, because my one and only playthrough got me to level 47, and took all the love I had for Borderlands and killed it. Maybe I can go play BL2 to cheer myself up. Maybe I can lose these bad memories in the Marrowfields.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a damn good shooter and a really good sequel in many, but not all ways.  Combat is much improved, less floaty and the inclusion of Slide and Mantle mechanics adds wonders to the flow of combat. A.I is smarter and more diverse. Grinding is less central to the experience. Performance is good and highly customizable, it runs and looks good even on low end P.C's like mine, though it helps the art direction on this game is fantastic and much cleaner than BL2. Pop-in textures still happen though, but that's a Unreal Engine thing that's never really been fixed. Story fine, its not the worse; despite what some "gamers" say. Bl's humor is always going to be hit or miss, but the story suffers from under-development, and antagonists that are conceptually clever and relevent; but never land the way Handsome Jack did for 2; thus making them one note. The annoying BL problem of player characters not being a part of/or in cuts causes a lot of problems, but that's always been a BL problem. Also as a Tales fan, the inclusion of Rhys & Company is a mixed bag; and the lack of Fiona as a playeable Vault Hunter is bizzare.Those gripes aside, This a damn fun game, and one of the better Co-op experiences around. 7.5/10A-

_childDocuments_.review: Would i recommend? Hell no. 100s of hours on this game, so i can tell you iv'e done everything. I don't recommend, because the devs are lazy pieces of sh*t that don't deserve your money. They bring out half baked dlcs that take less than 4 hours to complete with forgettable story's. NO END GAME WHSTSOEVER. So you know all those guns and items you farm for? Guess what; you only get to use them in the same run down, boring places. Minos prime? Done it 100s of times, midnight cairn same, slaughter shaft? Of course, done it all. There is nothing to do with end game with all of the items your grind for. We have been asking for end game content for months, but the lazy devs only tweak underused or never used guns. That's it, they change a value in the guns coding to do more damage... That's our update. Yup lets go take these new updated guns to the same BORING places we have done over and over again. Multiplayer. Forget about it. If you aren't the host, you're going to SUFFER with ping, not being able to switch weapons for some reason, and if you're a Zane main, your cannon getting stuck in animation an unusable until you switch out skills, which in a boss fight will get you killed. Looking back on my 600 hours i have to say... Why, why did i play so long? Because i had hope that a game couldn't stay a piece of sh%t for this long, that the devs surely would create more endgame, but alas, they never did. DO NOT buy this game until they actually put work into the endgame. This game isn't cheap, and they don't deserve your money. Rating 0/10 Fix your ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game you lazy ♥♥♥♥♥. I'm over paying for over priced season passes.In all seriousness, the games a mess and there is nothing new for you to come to. The game is dying, and it's online numbers are ghost town levels of quiet. Save your money, i repeat, SAVE YOUR MONEY.Edit. The modding community has somewhat breathed new life into this game. Redux mod, and a few others have made the game more enjoyable. Redux actually adds in pearlescent, and contraband rarities. Which are more powerful and much harder to attain, giving you something to grind for, and actually happy to see a very rare pearl drop.Now Borderlands 3 devs have REALLY dropped the ball here. We were given Diamond keys right? Basically being able to open  up a room of legendary items and choose from them. Sounds cool right? Well.. Not really, not when the items in this room can be found easily enough from world drops or dedicated sources. SO, essentially the diamond keys really have no worth. Now. If the devs had some foresight, they would of added in Pearl rarity into the game, they would of made those pearls a small chance from the diamond armory room, thus giving the players something exciting to open every time you get a key, wondering if THIS TIME you will get a super powerful Pearl. They could be new guns entirely, or could of been Pearl upgrades of Legendary items already in the game. (Think a superpowered Hellwalker) This would of given this game a form of endgame that is much needed, and would of made the obtaining of Diamond keys exciting.My original review stands: The devs are lazy, and you can feel there is no passion in what is being made. In saying that: If you have a PC, and don't mind adding mods to the game such as Redux mod, then the game might be worth the buy, but tbh that money should go to the Modding community, not Gearbox.

I do not believe the story should be that much of a deciding factor in a game unless it is specifically focused on story (like walking dead or something), however when it gets to the point that it becomes actively hostile to repeated playthroughs of the game then you know you have an issue especially when it comes to borderlands a series which has historically always had very strong replay value. Instead of being enjoyable the story is an annoying chore to get through and only made worse by lengthy unskippable dialogue that almost seems like the writers enjoyed making you suffer through. So ya... it's a bundle, but I did have fun with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall Borderlands 3 is a fun game, but suffers due to a developers that does everything except listen to the players. I thoroughly enjoyed playing through the game because of the fun play style and variety. But once the main content from the game was cleared the games flaws became very apparent. The main storyline is lacking and makes many questionable story decisions. The endgame of farming specific guns with special features falls short when the developers decide to arbitrarily lower the stats on the best guns in the game. The online play becomes a disappointment when the servers crash leaving you and your party frozen and losing all progress. Ultimately attempts to fix the game have been the equivalent of putting a bandaid over a bullet hole. I do not recommend spending $60 for this game, but if it's on sale and you can tolerate the headaches that come with it you might want to give it a shot.

And the gameplay here is fantastic! Kills feel more satisfying than ever, and skill trees have become more powerful and super customizable. (Super excited for the 4th skill tree coming soon!)While piloting a mech suit, having a drone-clone combo fighting with you, and Amara are all cool, I find the most enjoyment with FL4K and their pet. Having a little buddy to follow me around, be able to command, and ultimately become attached to is such a fantastic feeling!On top of this, there are many quality of life changes. For example: you can fast travel to any station across any region  to your vehicle  Plus you can sell all your junk items in just one button press. While one may argue new movement options like wall-mounting or sliding aren't necessarily game-changers, I think they're a very nice change of pace from the previous Borderlands games.I've yet to play the fourth DLC campaign or finish the third, but I love the first two campaigns. And of course the base game is great as I've already said. I'm very excited for Season 2! I definitely recommend this.

But most of the time it's very obvious, they're reading of a script, which just breaks the immersion.- UI is too cluttered. Too many colours. It's clunky, slow and bad at handling a lot of items. I also miss being able to see yourself in the inventory, where you could turn around your char. - Old characters are either completely rewritten or missing entirely from the game.- Great characters are being tossed aside after 2 missions, while new shallow, annoying and utterly dumb written ones get all the highlight.- The sound mixing in this game is just bad. Got a 5.1 system but had to set it to stereo, since I could not hear anything as soon as I looked away from talking NPC's.- Players voice is so overpowering loud in contrast to everything else, it's so annoying. Sound options don't help at all.- Gearbox thought it was a good idea to let the player talk.. ALL THE TIME. And since each character has only 10 lines to say, every 15 seconds you hear a really ret*rded, cringy clichee line, that only cheesy kids cartoon villains would say. It's so bad with Amara. And her jump sound is so overexaggerated, she's as annoyng as the "villains" themselfes. But more to that later.- Leveldesign is extremely underwhelming. So many copy-pasted assets everywhere. Nekrotafeyo was the only place where it felt like, it was truly a different world.- Eden 6 is the biggest area in the whole game and it's just a big swamp.. with more... swamp. It's design is extremely bland and boring. Just awful. BL3 goes interstellar and they make swamp worlds.. wow.- The Vaults are so disappointing.. again! This is the 5th entry and they still f*cked the vaults up so hard. They are all  They just didn't care. Very questionable..- Loot-system is broken beyond measurement. Legendaries drop as often as blues in BL2 UVHM. There is not a single point in picking up anything below Legendary, since the game gives you 20+ in less than 2 hours. I got 9 Legendaries from one mission, which renders them completely unimpressive. Because of this, I don't even look at purples anymore. In just a few hours of playtime, my entire inventory was full of gold gear. I can't for the love of everything make sense of this. Why have over a billion guns when only maybe 100 are actually interesting? Marketing, I guess. And the saddest part is, that most legendaries are complete trash too. - The Vault Hunters are so uninspired, boring and annoying characters, it's so sad. They constantly yell and scream full-ret*rd-mode. I'd rather have quiet characters again, than having these constantly sh*t talking gremlins, that give you cringe goosebumps every few seconds.- All the animations in this game are not motion captured, which means they are just garbage. Even an untrained eye can spot how stiff and clunky they are. A triple A 2019 game with that budget should have mo-cap. - The cutscenes look like someone from Deviantart made an amateur fanvideo. They are so unbelievably bad, It's the only time the game made me laugh. From awkward camera angles to extremely bad amateur animations. The pacing is so off, they weren't even trying. So, so unbelievably awful. And what the flying f*ck happened with their faces? Everyone is so ugly now. Art direction? Hello?! Where are you at?- And to the final act of this clownshow: The "story". I actually still can't find proper words for this ungodly monstrosity they call a "story". It's easily the single worst piece of awful BS that I've ever encountered so far. _childDocuments_.review: I've thought about this for a while, whether to recommend it or not. I eventually came to the conclusion, that it's a good game, but it's not what I had hoped for in a Borderlands 3. I want Gearbox to know that, while I appreciate the work that went into this, it's not the right direction. Sacrificing storytelling and character building to chase the latest trends is not what I would call good game design. The main story is weak. There's no other way to say it. The baddies are bland, annoying and I hate them for all the wrong reasons. Characters that were built up over the last two games are killed off in what feels like a whim and for no effect other than to build a character that's not terribly likable to begin with. Some don't even show up at all which is a bit unfair towards them. The gameplay is great, and it improved a lot from the predecessor. Guns feel even better, look amazing and are more varied than before. Although the new Atlas guns strike me as very niche weapons, the thought that went into specialising the weapons manufacturers is admirable. Sliding and climbing are a thing now too so navigating while on foot is a whole lot easier and less frustrating. Loot feels balanced enough, although legendaries drop almost hilariously easy. Perhaps that's by design but I feel that it devalues them somewhat. Then again, most of the leg's are gimmick weapons at most and not practical in combat. Graphics have been turned up a notch as well, with textures looking crisp as they can and weapons shining as they should where there is metal, less so where there is plastic. It just looks real, no two ways about it. Reloading animations have been given some love too. What I'm not a big fan of is how there seem to be all of maybe 30 quests in the whole game, spread over 5 planets. It feels like alot of wasted space and opportunity. Where BL2 had lots of memorable and funny/quirky quests in all different areas, the ones in 3 seem a bit few and far between. I don't think we needed repeatable quests either, it just gives you the illusion of something to do. All in all, I do think my purchase was worth it at 50% off, and I will definitely play more of it. But I implore Gearbox, please think about what made BL2 great and learn from this. We don't need annoying wannabe streamers as antagonists if all they do is wallow in how much better they are and have no significant character arcs or motivations.

_childDocuments_.review: I was beyond excited for this game when it was first announced, as bl2 is one of my all time favorite games, however I cannot in good consciousness recommend this game. Let's start with the good, what little there is.1) Gameplay. The gameplay is the best in the series, and one of the most fun shooters I've ever played, as long as you turn the dialogue off. Or if you don't count the bossfights which are all so underwhelming I can't remember a single one from the entire game. The guns all feel & look great & the variety in character skill trees has never been so worthwhile.2) Soundtrack. The soundtrack is surprisingly good, I often find myself just taking a second to actually Enjoy the music while i'm shooting & looting. Hell even the weird radio songs in a few areas are fun! However the end credits song feels... out of place & in poor taste considering what happens right before it. 3) Visuals. Guns, characters, enemies, & Pandora itself has never looked as good as they do in this game. Picking a vault hunter was harder than usual since each of them has a fun design. I didn't just automatically gravitate towards one character in particular like I did with the previous games. Unfortunately good gameplay, designs, & music won't save this game from piss poor writing. The writing in this game is so bad it's almost insulting. Old character's feel like parodies of their previous selves, two of which in particular are reduced to one Very Minor personality trait. Some of them make decisions that make them look like the dumbest people in the universe, all in order to progress the nonsensical & barely there plot. New npc's are forgettable & uninteresting with hardly any depth or personality to them, despite the voice actor's & character designer's best efforts. Only 2 new npc's felt like valuable additions to this series with the other 2 possible one's having high potential that's wasted on this mess of a "story", if you can call it that. The vault hunters each have no real bearing on the story whatsoever, with them phasing out of existence whenever the plot needs to progress & a cutscene needs to happen. Despite the fact all 4 of them are canonically there. I will say that the dlc's are each Slightly better written than the main game but.... not enough to make me care. I still sat through the entire game relatively bored with a blank expression throughout the whole game. The only dlc where I Wasn't mostly disinterested was the second one, but that's pretty much only because of it's pseudo-horror setting & the fact it was about 2 of of my favorite characters from this series. The rest of the dlc had the same effect as the main story but with less groaning due to how awful the writing was. In conclusion, If you don't care about the story or characters & just want a fun mindless shooter you can play with friends or zone out to while listening to a podcast or something, yeah this game's pretty decent as long as you turn the dialogue off & skip every cutscene. Don't pay more than $15 for it though. If you want a good game or care about these characters? Yeah don't buy this game. Although, I'm guessing if you do care about that, then you probably already bought it & was just as disappointed as the rest of us.

_childDocuments_.review: Way better than I thought this game would be.PART 1 - THE BADA bunch of  negative reviews convey thinly-veiled personal insecurities, such as the game being "too woke" because it has strong female characters or embraces the LGBT community. Just watching the snowflake outrage is a win in itself. Maybe avoid this game if you're a fragile male who can't stand seeing minorities share the spotlight in a video game for once ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ Now that this is out of the way, I reckon the game still has a major flaw: The overall lazy/bland/shallow writing. I think the writing team for this entry in the franchise was a bunch of parrots on cocaine.> Your character is absolutely inconsequential, you're basically a badass all game except when a cut-scene happens. Then you're just fodder standing there while sh*t goes down around you. The writers didn't even bother making excuses for the fact you let people literally get murdered in front of you and whatnot. This is very frustrating, and takes away one major thing that made BL2 such a great game. > The villains are mediocre: Poorly scripted. Lacking motivation. Obnoxious without an ounce of charisma. I guess the general idea of  wasn't bad, but it's so poorly used. It lacks subtlety. We didn't reach the perfect balance of funny-yet-very-punchable-yet-awesome villain we found in Handsome Jack. The thing is, on each play-through, these villain wannabes with no depth are still chattering in your ECHO, and that can get real annoying. >> Major spoiler: > There are moments that throw the buildup from previous entries out the window. Some of the events in that game were VERY poorly built-up. Sometimes the story is also lacking follow-up to dramatic events. > Even past characters suffer from lazy writing, and only find their salvation in the amazing work of their voice actors. For instance .I felt the OST has lost some of its quality compared to the previous Borderlands, but I guess that one boils down to personal taste.PART 2 - THE GOODLooking at the game as a whole, I'd say it's alright - at least in my eyes. Most of the game dialogues are about farts, killing things, punching things, and overstating the obvious - just like in BL2. Not as beautifully executed? For sure. But the tone remains.There are so many Quality-of-Life improvements from BL2 (honestly ALL I wanted to change from BL2 has been improved) that I will forgive a (very) forgettable script.I'll throw some random things I liked at ya now:- I still got a few laughs out of some characters' lines- Fan service: The game pays its respects to previous entries, including Tales from the Borderlands- Digging deeper into the game you will actually get some interesting pieces of lore and answers to questions you've likely asked yourself- The money is useful now! - Guns from the same weapon class do different things! (And do it well)- Skill trees are highly-customizable:> You can choose your action skill > Some characters have several at once. Each class is different> Your select action skill can be micro-managed / customized- You can climb up any ledges/boxes/big furniture- You'll get into a good amount of Weapon Manufacturers' background and home planet! - Oh yeah, space travel! - Also, fast travel!- Quick ammo refill- Awesome vending machines- Neat story collectibles- Gunplay never felt so good- Customizable rides- The rare loot you missed is repatriated to Sanctuary- Mayhem Mode (Custom NG+) is amazing- Similar lifetime to Borderlands 2- Great graphics- Beautiful landscapes- Good performancePART 3 - THE UGLYAll in all this game is aight, however two things to note:1 - Get it at a significant discount, especially if you go for the complete edition. _childDocuments_.review: Borderlands 2 is my favourite game of all time. The characters were charming and unique, the art style is beautiful, the guns were all unique and interesting, the jokes were hilarious, the easter eggs were genuinely fun to find, and overall the gameplay and story were incredibly enjoyable. Borderlands 3, however, feels more like an attempt to profit off of Borderlands fans by trying so hard to create something that looks like Borderlands 2, but is not even close. Borderlands 3 has what seems to be a cheesy, lazy, story so far. The characters are mostly annoying and the idea to bring back vault hunters from Borderlands 2 is poorly done. They try to play off of the end of Borderlands 2 where they find the vault map that leads to a bunch of other planets, cool concept, right? Well, it would be if they did it properly. What they ended up creating is what feels like an endless, repetitive shoot enemies, walk a few steps, shoot enemies, walk, shoot, walk, shoot, OH look a vault key piece! Next planet please! It gets annoying, not to mention the increased drop rate for legendaries makes them drop like candy. By level 5 I had about 6 legendaries in my inventory, which totally defeats the excitement of seeing that orange drop. On top of the gameplay and story issues, this game is very poorly optimized. I have a Ryzen 5 2600 with a Radeon RX 580 and this game crashes every 10-20 minutes on the lowest settings. I have tried uninstalling and reinstalling, verifying game files, and changing the launch options, and yet no fixes. It seems as though I'm not the only one experiencing crashes, so just be wary of this if you plan on playing this game.What Borderlands 3 does do right is the side quests. The side quests in this game seem to be the only entertainment that I've really been able to pull. Maurice and the cartel is a fun quest line, most of Claptrap's quests are fun, same with anything Marcus wants from you. Overall, I think that Borderlands 3 was a big miss and seems to have simply been a rushed, poorly optimized, cash grab mostly due in part to the devs partnering with Epic Games. it simply feels like it's missing the love that was put into Borderlands 2. Pros: -classic Borderlands art style -Vault hunters brought back from Borderlands 2 -Gameplay and enemies are challengingCons: -poorly optimized -Dry story -Repetitive walking and shooting -Boring boss fights

_childDocuments_.review: Steam's limited review options don't give you much of a choice on how you review. I like a lot of this game and the base game has a decent amount of content. If you've played previous releases, you'll probably like this one as well.What the thumbs down? Business practices. I had to wait over 2 years to purchase the game. First, the exclusive release because I didn't need yet another game launcher service. Then, ridiculous pricing. I don't spend my hard earned funds for these silly prices at release. I waited till a Christmas sale. Looking at the DLC, which they now simply use as cash grabs from unwitting gamers. There was a time when the DLC for Borderlands was really exciting. Now, it's just an excuse to either withhold content or trick people into buying worthless junk. I loved the first two releases of Borderlands, thought the 2.5 release sucked and had to see if this one was good, regardless of how Gearbox/2k operates.On the plus side, the only real issue I've had in game is the occasional stutter ever so often when entering a new zone and mobs start to appear. It only sticks for a split second - just long enough to notice that it froze up a bit. During the overall gameplay though, I've not had any issues, crashes or anything different than any of the other games. It looks about the same as the first release, so I'm guessing they still use the same game engine.One of the biggest issues I've had with this whole series is how they love to claim they have 2 billion guns or whatever. Sadly, when roughly 98% of that amount is just trash, it doesn't really matter what that upper count is. I did find a few more things along the way in B3, although generally speaking, by the time some legendary or at least upgrade dropped, it was below my level. It takes a good deal of enjoyment out of the game and I think the art of having fun with loot is still completely lost on Gearbox.This isn't the worst game I've played. Unfortunately it also isn't a big step over B2 and with how they have DLC quest flags popping up and considering how the reviews of the DLC indicate they almost all suck, this is a bit of a let down. They could have released a big DLC for B2 and probably been just as well off.

_childDocuments_.review: I put 50 or so hours into this game before unexpected circumstances forced me to reinstall Windows 10. After the reinstall, the game refused to launch. After a few hours of troubleshooting, I was able to narrow down the problem. If a certain Nvidia setting is on, the game will not launch. On my system, having literally anything enabled in Nvidia Control Panel for BL3 causes a crash on launch. This is ridiculous. I don't know if this is on Nvidia or Gearbox, but it needs to be fixed. To turn in some missions, I have had to exit to menu. Not entirely game breaking, but very annoying when I have an audience. I would guess that the most recent DLC broke something, but it also could have been a patch as well.The main villains could have been good, but they turned out like Twitch streamer caricatures. The jokes get worse and worse as the game progresses. Half of the villain dialogue could be salvaged, but the other half is absolute trash. After a villain like Handsome Jack, Karen and her brother Tom are extraordinarily annoying. Loot drops baffle me. I receive orange items very, very often. In BL1, orange drops were very rare. In BL2, orange drops were still rare but dropped a little more frequently. In BL3, killing any Badass or Boss enemy has a very good chance of dropping an orange item. My vault has 300 spaces, and a good 200 of those are taken up by Anointed orange weapons. Based on my experiences with BL1 and 2, I am a bit of an orange hoarder. The problem with that is sheer lack of variety. After my first playthrough no new orange items seemed to be dropping. The same oranges drop 98% of the time. When the other 2% of oranges come out, they're extremely powerful. I have a rifle that shoots out what seem to be low blast radius seeker grenades, but I have never found another. There seems to be a sheer lack of balance in the weapons. The Hellshock is a Maliwan orange that usually has a good rate of fire, and shoots two shots for the price of one. I have killed bosses in seconds with the Hellshock. Attempting to do the same with the other orange weapons has gotten me killed on multiple occasions. The Hellshock can change between fire and shock, making it literally the most perfect gun in the game. The other orange weapons are not even close to that powerful. I would give this game a 4/10 just for the villains. Absolutely awful. I often turn audio and subtitles off when they monologue. Handsome Jack was hilarious and driven. These two memes are not even alright villains. I would expect villains like this in a low budget indie, not a AAA from a respected company.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge Borderlands fan since I picked up the first one when XBOX kindly gave away the games as part of its Games with Gold membership.  I've since picked up all but the first game for PC through Steam.  I have played and beat the game on XBOX One but wanted to add it to my Steam collection and the price was right.My main gripe with the game is the sole reason why I purchased it (Feb 2020); Cross Play.  I was under the impression that Borderlands 3 on PC could "cross play" with other SHiFT members regardless of what platform they were playing on.  This is not the case.  Currently the Steam version is only Cross Play able with SHiFT members/friends who bought the game through Epic Games.  I am encouraging the developers to please make Cross Play what it really means...to play with other Borderlands gamers regardless if they are on another computer and console.  Modern PCs, XBOX, and PlayStation consoles all contain pretty much the same hardware.  There is no excuse why Cross Play couldn't handle the capabilities required to allow for cross platform gaming. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Prettier than the previously title; worse in every other aspect. Play Borderlands 2 instead.A looter-shooter to be sure, but an ultimately inferior version compared to it's predecessors. The writing has lost it's wit, and has instead become trite with no shortage of callbacks to Borderlands 2's better writing and characters. For the main quest antagonist, there isn't much motivation for them to try and accomplish their goals beyond simply needing one to have a quest marker for the protagonist to travel to in order to progress the "story." Character development is shoddy at best, and half of the characters are either bumbling idiots (usually the male characters) or they're self-proclaimed badasses (usually the female characters). I wouldn't care if there were any sort of development on either side, but what you get instead is a "badass" character because the game told you so and that's it. Nothing denoting a person living in a world. The unnamed NPCs you'll find around the main hubs are far more interesting than most of the named characters you find along your questing travels. The Skinner Box aspect of this game leaves something to be desired, namely a reason to pick things up beyond the idea of collecting trash to throw at a vending machine for upgrades which, after only a short while, become redundant. The art design is beautiful. I found myself staring at several lighting fixtures and admiring the landscape while shooting my way through areas filled with painstaking detail. It was a shame that what I was shooting at was little more than reskinned enemies from previously conquered zones. Most fights felt mundane and like little more than filler despite the mechanics being phenomenal. I wanted to complete all main quests for the vanilla game and the DLC, but what a slog it turned out to be. My favorite was Krieg's Mind, and I'll be open about my bias for him as a character being carried over from playing him in the previously title for hours, but even that DLC wasn't fulfilling. Everything felt either like a chore, or it was simply a way to check off a box. There wasn't anything else here, which is a damn shame because you can tell just how much love went into it. This game is littered with sections where the 100s of man hours are visible, but you'll have a hard time enjoying them for lack of meaningful loot or reward.

_childDocuments_.review: Borderlands 3 is a worthy successor of Borderlands 2. It is a tad bit more serious than the Pre-sequel. Gunplay is improved, rare loot is more fun, bossfights are way better. It is less grindy.The story is mainly uninspired, but if you liked Handsome Jack so much that you will take a weaker Version of him as a villain, you will be fine. Jokes are ♥♥♥♥ as always in borderlands games.To be honest, you don't play Borderlands for the story. And the story has been consistently the worst part about these games, so i will talk about that last. There are some changes in this game and they are fun. They removed the gliding mechanic from the pre-sequel and but kept the stomp. Additionally you can now mantle (?) over obstacles and slide under obstacles. Both give you more to do in combat and change how you approach encounters. Gunplay has also been improved, so that the guns feel even more responsive compared to the second part. Atlas is back as a gun manufactorer and provides basically aimbot on all its guns. Every other maunfactorer got additional gimmicks and a lot of them additionally have alternate firing modes. This, again, gives you more to do in combat and more flexibility in your encounters. Drops also seem to be more frequent with every single boss dropping at least one legendary in my first playthrough and some worlddrops in between.There are only 4 characters so far which might still change if gearboxes DLC policy is consistant. Each character has 3 skill trees which are less diverse than the previous ones. One example is fl4k's Jabber skill tree where every single level contains a selfheal node. However these skill trees each come with an actionskill, that is comparable to bl2's. Speccing into a skill tree unlocks action skill modificators which improve or alter your action skill, you can even get new action skills entirely. Again, lots of choices, lots of fun.Progressing in the game is tedious. The game puts a lot of roadblocks in your way which are usually doors which are unlocked by your acompanying npc. But only after they finished their ten years of dialogue. Whenever that is done and you can explore on your own the game becomes fun, until you want to progress the story again. There are a lot of solutions for that, so this pacing issue is inexcusable. It's just the game forcing you to listen to its dialogue and watch the characters.Cutscenes are now a more important part of the game than before which will annoy you in no time if you don't have any summons around which still appear in the cutscenes, and make these far more entertaining.The Bossfights are great, in this game you finally get bosses which have mechanics. The first real bossfight is against a sound based bandit with a shield. He has speakers in stalled in the arena. If the cables leading up to the specific speakers light up, you have to leave that part of the room, he also turns invulnerable under certain conditions but i wont spoil too much. This is a huge step up from bl2's captain flynt or later bosses, which mostly were big versions of common enemies or huge monsters with glowing weak spots.The base game contains no raid boss though which is dissappointing to say the least.This contains spoilersImagine you typical adventure game of tough guys who are all badasses in their own way and basically beautiful women who lay down at their feet. This is the story for the first 8 hours of the game, but it's gender swapped. While technically it think it is an interesting idea it seems like they didn't go past this in their planning so now the game starts with you meeting this badass magic fighter that tasks you with defeating some bandits. Afterwards you save an almost naked fit dude who only talks about his muscles, dangling from the ceiling and return him to her to be sent of to another badass woman who despite being quite fat gets complimented by the player character for her appearance. Afterwards you meet the geek type scientist woman, who as you will soon fight out is also quite the badass. After that you first meet the villains who, you guessed it badass woman with dependent weak male sidekick, but again half naked with a six pack. Next character you meet is again a badass fighter woman, and in case you missed that from her cutscene, it is in her title card. I'm guessing this is some outrage bait for sexists and a way to score more positive talking points about the game, but the dialogue and story in general is really barren. Find vault key, kill bad guy. There are no sudden changes of allegiance, no surprising twists if you played the previous games. And for all the flexibility in your skilltrees and weapons the most impactful decisions in the story are things like consoling little girl after her maternal figure died. There is a lot of DLC for this game, half of which should have been in the base game. If you don't have the DLC the main hub of the game is full of yellow quest markers. Interacting with these objects opens a window asking you to buy the DLC which is interestingly the only way to get rid of these and there are a lot of these. They block the minimap in some parts. 10€ for skins and there are 8 of these.You can of course always buy the season pass which is worth the 50€ or rather would be if it contained the raid boss that they removed from the base game and the additional skill trees. It doesn't though so get this and the second season pass on discount if you decide to buy the game, because without the DLC the game is quite annoying in the main hub where the main part of the story takes place.The game is somewhat badly optimized, my fps often dropped to 60 and my PC is well above the recommended settings.

_childDocuments_.review: The fourth entry in the Borderlands series, replete with everything you've come to know and love from Gearbox's figurative baby of a series.You get plopped into the story in a very similar way to Borderlands 1, and out the gate it feels a lot closer to the initial experience than BL2 ever did. It's a first person shooter with some semblance of RPG spliced in via skill trees and unique abilities.It's the definitive 'looter shooter'.Another title that ranges from easy all the way to ludicrously hard. With the addition of the new modifier levels you can make this game an utter nightmare for yourself.It takes the series' art style up a notch honestly, with some sharper lines and richer art direction than previous entries' had. Each planet definitely feels unique, but expect to have a tank of a system to run ultra during a firefight.As with all the BL titles, I cannot fault the audio itself. Each clip is clean and well formatted to sound exactly as it should. Through comms, in front of you, recorded on an old device. It's all super well done. Creature sounds and ambient noise is great. I would say the only thing I still don't care for is the boost noises for the vehicles. Still hate those.Tons. There is a huge story, DLC, and you have multiple classes to play with.This game was a breath of fresh air compared to BL2 and BLPS for me. I didn't much care for anything in those two games. The humor, the guns, the anything. But this game...oh this does it right again. Now you have to understand I was a die-hard BL1 fan. So BL2 and BLPS were NOT enough for me. I didn't think either lived up to what the first did.The characters feel less derivative, even the old ones that were brought back have a new passion and unique nature to them that was not there in BL2. They say quirky things, and I caught myself laughing a lot more with this game because the dialogue was written much better this time around.The story is, well... it's actually pretty interesting. I really don't want to spoil it too much, as I found it to be pretty good just hitting those key points in the writing. It's hard to sum up all the ups and downs of it, it has some lackluster parts but it certainly isn't bad because of that. In addition, the DLC is all super great. Feels way less phoned in than previous series DLC entries (looking at you, character packs for BL2). It, combined with the new scaling system you can activate, lets you make every mission feel like a challenge and a reward.I had an IMMENSE amount of fun with this game, to the point I wouldn't mind playing it again with another class (something I couldn't even fathom doing in BL2/PS). You can break pretty much every class to a point of goofy entertainment, and if you prefer a real challenge there are now raid mechanics in the game (not exactly a raid, but extremely high level content that has good rewards, whatever), and oh man the guns.Some of the new characters are more annoying than they are memorable. Certain story elements you see coming from a mile away. A few too many back and forth quests but that's every RPG almost.I also don't actually care as much for some of the enemy designs in this one. I feel like they could have pushed them further to be a bit more unique.

_childDocuments_.review: Borderlands 3 is a very satisfying game mechanically, at least most of the time, but is difficult to recommend without caveats due to abysmal writing and some odd mechanical foibles. The game does not scale appropriately, and true vault hunter mode cannot be played without completing the game's story. It is guaranteed to be laughably easy the first time around. This kind of skews the other way with high mayhem levels, where mayhem on true vault hunter mode can result in impossible bosses without relying entirely on character skills. In addition, the plot and characters are so terrible that on my second playthrough I muted the game audio. There are good lines sprinkled throughout the game, but there is a lot of humor that fails to land as well as just insufferable characters. If your intention is to only play the base game, I don't recommend it.The game is redeemed by its DLC. I read somewhere that the DLC cost more to develop than the base game, and I can almost believe it given the amount of different assets, tracks, and the improvement in writing. All of the DLCs are at least average (handsome jack), with some being exceptional (krieg, guns). As a result all of the DLCs blow the base game out of the water in terms of narrative and presentation. Unfortunately, the second season pass includes an additional class tree for all classes, and two pieces of lackluster content. I recommend getting the season passes on sale. You do need both season passes to get 100% achievements.The absolute best thing about the game that I have not mentioned up to this point is the phenomenal soundtrack. There are real bangers present, especially in the DLCs (Arms Race excepted; somebody liked Aphex Twin a little too much and decided to put their tribute in a misguided battle royale pastiche). I still listen to the soundtrack in the car. One DLC has over an hour of music. Think about that.I would like to close by emphasizing that the game is fun, but probably not worth full price. After 100 hours I am still ok with playing more of the game, especially as other classes, provided the characters are muted. There are some odd mechanical issues like the overreliance on pistol weapons, the inclination towards elemental weapons etc, but it's a fun experience. The problem is the writing, which is so godawful it brings the entire experience down. If you could buy the DLCs without the base game I would recommend that, but sadly that's not the case. You really need the whole package, but I recommend waiting for heavy discount.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so a lot of people have addressed the gameplay overall is better and the story is meh to craptastic and the characters just fall flat for the most part. Another issue I want to address is that the story of the games is no longer the vaults or the player characters and their interactions with the villains.In BL2 the chief driving point is the player is a vault hunter and is targeted for being such because Handsome Jack is a bit of a ♥♥♥♥ to put it mildly and wants the players out of the way so he can obtain his prize from the vaults. Good story the characters are relevant to the plot and are essential to the story because they are Jack's competition for the vault. Moving on to BL3 the player characters reaaaaalllly don't matter all that much in the grand scheme of things. The chief actors with any real interest from the villains of this story are not the player characters, Where before the Vault Hunters were the Legendary Badasses of the universe they are now the supporting cast for Lilith and her Siren abilities. Normally I wouldn't have a problem with an RPG having the character as a more minor part of the overall plot i.e. Geralt in the Witcher. Geralt is basically the person who goes to save the really important character Ciri and really has very limited influence on the universe of the witcher by comparison to Ciri's title of the Lady of Time and Space. But I digress, in Borderlands it was always the PC who had the importance because that is part of Borderlands conceit that the player is the toughest SOB to see the sun on Pandora. Hell the difference in the post game even kind of highlights this between borderland 2 and 3. Badass ranks vs Guardian ranks. Badass infinitely scaling to the point the characters can become hilariously overpowered should players choose to play with badass ranks on to Guardian ranks where characters spin up a bit then hit a hard wall in the power trip fantasy in a coop only game despite promises of "infinite scaling" . In this game you only get a Zeno's paradox  to a roughly 15% across the board cap. Yeah you might continue to advance that half a percent and half of a half of a percent after that but its all fundamentally moot.

_childDocuments_.review: I just can't. This game is filled to the brim with ♥♥♥♥ ups. From an outsider perspective it looks great, amazing graphics and a decent backing track. But once you sink in you find a literal hodgepodge of poor writing techniques that weren't given any thought, a loot system that compared to BL2 feels like sifting through porridge with the sheer quantity but lack of quality items. Urggggggggggh.The characters almost all feel the same. Except for a few notable exceptions lots of the enemies and friendly npc have a similar speaking pattern, even some of the returning characters such as Maya or Rhys feel washed out of their individuality. Gun rarity and the parts system feels, for lack of a better term, mucky with how the new gun rating system, randomly assigned parts, and rarity make guns feel either incredibly similar despite being found levels apart or completely polarising. Seriously, I feel like I get 2 guaranteed legendary drops on killing a boss which already makes them feel less special compared to BL2 and most of the time they just aren't even effective making gun rarity and level feel arbitrary. I wanted to like this game so let's end on some of the few high notes.Like I said the graphics are great and the soundtrack is ok. I like how the brands have evolved with time to become more distinct like how Jakobs the stereotypical western brand now has a ricochet mechanic or how Maliwan the element brand can have 2 elements and more sci-fi designs.  In conclusion. Not particularly enjoyable. Play BL2 instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, absolutely yes without a single doubt. This is one of the most fun games I have played in the last few years. The variety of weapons is vast, and the new Vault Hunters all seem interesting and fun compared to the previous games where only 1 or 2 characters seemed interesting to play. Only downside is the story. It isn't for everyone and people will say that the main antagonists are cringey and annoying, don't expect them to be on par or better than Handsome Jack, I think that can't be beaten. Overall the story is definitely aimed at a younger audience that enjoys spending time on YouTube and Twitch, but can still be enjoyed. The writing's all right besides a few plot holes here and there. Where the game shines the most is with it's loot. Every gun feels different and is unique in some sort of way. _childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is simply the best of the series, everything polished, the guns and equipment are all interesting, the action is solid, the enemies are interesting and will challenge you to figure out ways around each type....While the story is simply terrible. Borderlands 2 had charm and one of the best villains in a video game ever, but this game has too many moments where it really thinks its funny but the writing and the timing of the comedy is just cringe. In Borderlands 2 you could really feel the menace of Handsome Jack from the moment you began the game, and the ever present Helios station in the sky constantly reinforced this, especially when it could moonshot reinforcements at any time. The game was goofy but the plot remembered to keep itself together and stay just serious enough to have an emotional impact.In Borderlands 3 the villains are not more than annoying talking heads in your echo device, they are ahead of you at every turn only because the plot needs them to be. None of the lead protagonists deserve anything they get, good or bad. You don't feel like a lead protagonist, you're just sort of there to shoot the game's plot forward. Aurelia was kind of good though, why couldn't she have been the main villain? She was the only antagonist in this whole game I was actually intimidated by.No, the game is still awesome and you'll get a chuckle here and there. If you weren't too too invested in Borderlands 2 / Pre Sequel's story to begin with, you can easily? ignore the annoying characters and have fun with the gameplay. If you did care deeply, you'll feel like everything you accomplish in the game is pointless. Maybe bring some friends with you so you can riff on the bad writing.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: If you liked the *combat* of BL1/BL2 and didn't care at all about the story, writing, characters, world, or anything else, then you might like this one. If you are interested in anything other than combat for combat's sake, give this one a pass.I'll illustrate my annoyance with one particular pair of scenes from about three-quarters through the game. As part of the previous planet, you picked up the mentor-figure (Maya) and a tagalong kid (Ava). On the current planet, in the vault you open, the kid (despite everyone telling her to stay put) sneaks in (somehow, despite all the monsters). Because of this, Maya hangs back to watch her while you go into the vault. When you come out, cutscene-incompetence engages and you, Maya, and the kid all stand around gormlessly while the villains drain the vault guardian's power. The kid stupidly yells about how Maya is going to beat them up, causing a distraction which allows one of the villains to drain the power/life from Maya. Despite the obvious fear this should cause in the kid, she continues taunting them until the villain force-pushes her across the room and they flee.Back on the ship, everyone is having a sad remembrance of the fallen mentor (at least I think it was sad; I was just bored). The kid gets angry at the messiah-figure (Lilith), yelling that Lilith was at fault for Maya's death because Lilith allowed her to go on that mission. Not a single person corrects the kid, or consoles Lilith. Everyone acts as if the kid has just spouted the truth. *facepalm*After that cutscene, I did some digging and discovered the cause of this stupidity: BL3 has 4 writers. Only one of them has any writing experience prior to this (another bad game) and only one has any significant experience... in visual effects. Was Gearbox so strapped for cash that they literally couldn't hire a single writer with any skill? Did they care so little about anything in this game that they thought hiring 4 no-names was a good idea? There are so many starving writers out there with the right chops for worldbuilding, but apparently Gearbox hates anything that isn't guns. Rather fitting, that.Gameplay's fun, I guess, but I lost interest near the end because I hated the dialog so much that I ended up turning off voices and music and listened to a podcast in the background. Oh, and there's tons of jank everywhere. Reproducible jank that would have been easy to catch. But, again, Gearbox doesn't care.

_childDocuments_.review: A decent borderlands game but buggy as hell and we probably wont get any real patches till community patch comes out in a decade. Definitely not worth the money at all, wait for a sale of at LEAST 40%.Eg: One boss entirely breaks and makes the fight unbeatable in the cartel event if you kill it in the wrong phase. This is extremely easy to do and the phase lasts more than long enough for even sub-par weapons to kill him. Host lag also directly affects the entire game for some reason, so if your host has bad specs and lags, all enemies will lag with him making coop play much less fun. Laggy coop will also break a few choice sidequests and you must fast travel back to sanctuary and back to fix them.With all of this said, the game itself including DLC is fairly enjoyable in singleplayer and can be fun in coop if players aren't lagging a whole bunch. Overall, broken as hell game with loads of content and fun gameplay when it is not breaking.

_childDocuments_.review: (This review is mostly spoiler-free, though I could go into GREAT detail as to WHY I loathe the story, such would spoil it, and I won't do such for those who may play it nonetheless)Would not recommend, personally, for the base game at least.The gameplay is better and the music is much better than prior entries in the series, too. But the story... oh god the story.To put it simply, the campaign is so terrible and slow that it makes the base game quite un-fun to play through, and it's much harder to rush through it due to so many instances where you have to follow NPCs around or constantly go and talk to specific NPCs to progress rather than the scene just continuing like it would have in BL2.There is also the issue of M10 being a clusterf*ck that destroys the build diversity that this game did so right just before the M10 update. Simply put, Mayhem 10 adds such high HP multipliers that it makes any build not based around gun damage and not using an EXTREMELY limited pool of weapons with an EXTREMELY specific annoints (bonus effects that are randomly chosen) completely unviable unless you like taking MINUTES to kill basic enemies.Gearbox also has decided to take a political stance and "show solidarity" with a group of domestic terroists, and use such as an excuse to delay an update that they'll probably still release in a horribly buggy and unbalanced state, just like Mayhem 10 was. Combined with the rather ever-present political and modern social themes in this game in particular... another reason I don't like such as much.HOWEVER, I must give gearbox credit for doing what I consider to be one of the best depiction of a homosexual couple in a video game, which, surprises me really, with how ham-fisted most of the political and ideological stances in this game are, I'm quite surprised Hammerlock & Wainwright are done so well. They're just, treated like any other romantic couple, and that's the best way to depict such I feel, so, I will give them credit for that.The DLCs might end up being this game's saving grace, however, and when they're all said and done, or when I feel like it, I'll go review each in turn, as these two major DLCs are LEAGUES better written and have much better mission structure than the base game.Of course this is just scratching the surface of things, really, but I think this explains my grievances with the game well enough, though, perhaps they'll improve, perhaps not, for now I'm shelving the game into the "only do it for multiplayer with friends so you can riff on the story together and keep sane that way" category.TL;DR : good gameplay/gunplay and good music, but such is NOT good enough as to salvage the awful mess that is the story and the HORRID mess that is the endgame. And credit where credit is due for doing one of the best depictions of a homosexual relationship I've seen from most modern media, though that does little to salvage the game.

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay in Borderlands 3 is the best in the series yet. Guns are even better, with alternate firing modes adding a little mix-up and variation. If you're looking to turn off your brain for a fun action packed shooter, this game is for you. If you're a long time borderlands fan however, this game might disappoint with its lackluster story. The antagonists are obnoxious, boring streamers that constantly yell at you. They have no real motivations for their goal of world domination besides doing it just because they can. The best missions are the side quests where beloved characters return. Their interactions with one another result in hilarious banter that remind you this is why you fell in love with the borderlands universe. Other main characters from previous entries are seemingly forgotten and you're left wondering what even happened to them... did they just... disappear? Ultimately, the potential of these characters you've come to know and love feels wasted in an empty story.

_childDocuments_.review: The game was fun to play with friends, obviously, but in the end, the game was disappointing.Half the game felt well done, the guns, the sound design, the gameplay. But then you are assaulted by the lazily written main story, only supported by a few characters and side quests. It seems like a silly thing to complain about as well but the cutscenes were just not well animated, nothing I saw felt impactful and I wasn't satisfied with how they played out. Then I encountered quite a few bugs that prevented me from continuing play, this game has been out for quite some time before I bought it but it seems like money still can't buy you enough QA to cover the story missions.Overall, if you are a Borderlands fan, it's worth playing but ONLY buy it on sale. I expected so much more from a AAA game after how well they did on BL2.

_childDocuments_.review: Borderlands 3 feels like the best borderlands experience so for.  It's more of what you expect from a borderlands title.+Each gun manufacturer's gun functions differently now instead of having slightly different numbers.  Hyperion guns create shields when aiming, vladovs have grenade launchers, maliwans have to heat up before firing an elemental death laser and so on.  +Exploring the galaxy.  We've heard of these other worlds belonging to the mega-corporations.  We've even visited a few before, but now it's the whole galaxy tour.   I do kind of miss the comedic overkill of Pandora, but fortunately(?) most of the galaxy seems to be only slightly better off than Pandora.+Character skills have been made even more versatile with the ability to choose out of 3 starter choices to how it behaves and unlock more as you invest in different skill trees.+Production value is at its highest for the series here.  Guns sound good and enemies react to being shot, which gives shotguns a much needed niche.  Enemies will flinch, trip and fall face first on the ground, or even ragdoll as they're sent hurtling through the air by an explosion or shotgun blast.=I just can't enjoy the main villains in the story.  They do a good job of making the player want to kill them, but they're pretty irritating with no redeeming values I've seen so far.  Sometimes I get the feeling the story in Borderlands 3 is trying to make fun of the millennial generation and the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ meme factory in the internet.

_childDocuments_.review: I think the game is great. It's a far better play than BL2, and I really want to forget about the Presequel so this does the trick. The amount of effort in this game is insane so hats off to them for giving a AAA game worth it's price.The story is meh, but ALL of Borderland's story has been meh. The people thumbs downing this game because of it's story are really ridiculous when the story has been mediocre at best. Borderlands parodies FPS and RPGs best, but if you're after a good campaign, f***ing play COD you dum-dum. Seriously, wake up Samurai - you're playing the wrong game.You, yeah, YOU - you came here for the GUNS, the EPIC BOSS FIGHTS, the CHALLENGING quests and sidequests, and the COMPANIONSHIP as well as being able to flaunt your own unique playstyle. Well... that's what I'm here for, and oh boy does it not disappoint so far.Edit: been playing it more and more and it just keeps getting better. Look at the negative reviews and tell me that they're not biased. Sure, Handsome Jack was a stroke of genius, but that's all - the rest of BL2 (and especially TPS) had an awful storyline - the developer's have done even worst stories with their other games, or are we forgetting battleborn? BL3 improves on so much that it's a legit win, no questions about it - it's a great direction for the series.

_childDocuments_.review: Borderlands 3 is a game I’ve been meaning to play for a while now but had to wait a bit to enjoy it on Steam as I refused to buy it in the Epic Games store. I figured to wait until a deluxe edition came out with all the DLC, bugs fixed, etc. before jumping in. I’m glad I waited since it was well worth it for the most part as I loved the original and its sequel and this one wasn’t so bad. It’s nowhere near as good as the original two but it’s a decent experience.All the usual Borderlands style of things is here from the great graphics, amazing weapons, and the beyond satisfying gunplay. It’s a lot of fun to get all sorts of unique and different types of weapons and plow through enemies. Even the boss encounters were awesome as it’s a tried-and-true formula that has defined this franchise for over 15 years now.It was great to see the return of many beloved characters in the series from Lilith, Ellie, Tiny Tina, Moxxi, and many others. Besides that, the graphics, soundtrack, and overall loot are all fantastic. I had some incredible weapons while playing which made it even more fun to go through the entire game. Now, the biggest issue I have with this game is its main story in the campaign and all the boring side quests.The entire story from the campaign is the WORST I’ve ever seen in a Borderlands video game. It’s so terrible, cringe, immature, and flat-out dumb that it took me away from the overall gaming experience. I knew going into this game I wasn’t expecting an amazing or super serious story but this just sucked. The main villains are trash and the entire story is a weird, hot mess.It wasn’t as funny or as good as Borderlands 2 and yeah, I get that this wouldn’t have Handsome Jack who is a legend in his own right but common now, the main villains could have been a lot better. It feels as if it was written by a bunch of teenagers who looked up #Borderlands on Twitter and used the most immature tweets they could find to write a story around them. The main story gets boring from the halfway point on as I just wanted to finish it already, collect my Steam Achievements, and be done with this hoping the DLC is better.There’s just way too many fart jokes, characters in underwear, pictures of butts, and a high degree of immaturity and not of the funny kind. Besides that, this game also has a good amount of bugs and issues while playing. Loot will disappear into the ground and it froze a few times. It also crashed numerous times while playing out of nowhere and luckily, everything was saved so I didn’t lose my gear, character, or progress. If that happened, I would have given this a negative review, uninstalled it, and never played it again but thankfully, that wasn’t the case.I will say though, after completing that abysmal main campaign, the four unique DLCs were a lot of fun to play. I enjoyed “Moxxi's Heist of the Handsome Jackpot” the most since we got to see the return of Handsome Jack. “Guns, Love and Tentacles: The Marriage of Wainwright & Hammerlock” was awesome since it was Lovecraftian-themed and I love horror so that resonated well with me. Both “Bounty of Blood” and “Psycho Krieg and the Fantastic Fustercluck” were fantastic and again, the graphics, new DLC weapons, and bosses were all a ton of fun. The storylines here were a lot better.I didn’t waste any time trying out the mini-game of “Borderlands Science” as it didn’t interest me at all and the same with 2K Games trying to tap into the battle royale scene with their “Arms Race” mode. I tried it and it’s okay but when it comes to the co-op and multiplayer aspect of Borderlands 3, you’ll find some people playing but not a ton so expect queue times.Crossplay and cross-platform are possible in Borderlands 3 so if you use its matchmaking you should be fine during optimal days and times depending on where you live. I was able to get into matches pretty quickly for the campaign but nobody was playing the other modes so keep that in mind.I give Borderlands 3 a 3/5 for being a decent experience and still being one of the best looter shooters ever made. I am hoping 2K Games learns from their mistakes here since if this had a great story as the original and sequel did, this would be a perfect game. Unfortunately, the storyline is terrible and the bugs, glitches, and crashes were a shame. Aside from that, the DLC balances things out, the graphics are great, and the multiplayer works well during primetime. Here’s to hoping Borderlands 4 brings this incredible franchise back to its roots since this one was very close to being a dud and a negative review.

_childDocuments_.review: I was always a huge fan of BL2, and was really hoping for a new addition to the franchise I could really get into again since I personally never enjoyed the Prequal.Thankfully, I found BL3 to be enjoyable and really fun. The classes and skill trees are really unique and stand on their own, I chose Zayne as my main and have loved getting to equip 2 action skills! It's closer to BL2 than the Prequal was in terms of gameplay (I hated the oxygen meter) but doesn't reach the same level of a well written story. Thankfully, this isn't too detrimental, as BL3 doesn't need a crazy compelling story to be fun. However, the main villains were far too cringe in their dialogue for my liking and underwhelming, and the side characters weren't as enticing or engaging as BL2. That being said, I really appreciated the fact that the main character you play has more of a 'role' in the story, with unique character lines and frequently interacting with other NPCs. It definitely adds a missing dynamic I never realized I wanted in the game.Overall, this is definitely a solid entry to the franchise. I'd give it a strong 8/10.
