_childDocuments_.review: "Borderlands 3" is a first person view shooting game with a focus on killing enemies and getting better weapons. This is confirmed by the fact that the work contains more than a billion weapons. For the first time in the history of the series, activities take place on several planets, which makes the size and variation of the locations much more noticeable than in previous entries. It is possible to discover different planets and repel the evils there, either alone or in groups of up to four. It is certainly no coincidence that there are exactly four Vault Hunters as the main characters - Moze, who can call himself a mecha named Iron Bear; FL4K, which specializes in animal testing; Amara, who is the obligatory Siren or magician of the work; and Zane, who can use digital clones, drones, and set up a digital barricade. All the characters play very differently, making it fun to hang out with friends.The story of the work takes place immediately after the second game, in which the map showing different Vaults disappeared. Upon receiving it, it will be stolen by this time's villains, the Calypso twins, and a galactic hunt over the Vaults will begin. This journey is filled with many old and new faces from previous games, including Telltale's "Tales from the Borderlands" and 2K Australia's "Borderlands: The Pre-Sequel". Unfortunately, the Calypso twins are nowhere near Handsome Jack and are terribly annoying, which is why they are sometimes even more evil, because I couldn't really wait until I was able to knock them down.In terms of playability, this is the best entry in the series. Shooting is so damn good and everything that comes in is extremely smooth, such as slipping or grabbing from higher edges. Freedom of movement, combined with different abilities, constant hail and loot, is reminiscent of the old days when, after school, "Borderlands 2" was opened with friends and we wandered there for hours. Now all these good things are turned to ten and the player never gets a moment of boredom. Various weapons also contribute to this, such as guns with legs, firing burgers or even spraying faeces.In addition to the main story, the work has many side activities - in addition to the usual side missions, the previous work also targets the assassin Zer0; decomposed CL4P-TP models from which pieces can be picked; ancient Special Arid texts that provide information about the past of the planets and more. Side missions are stories filled with the idiotic and childish humor of the series, which is a good pastime and leveling/weapons acquisition activity. Zer0 targets are, for the most part, references to pop culture figures, such as the ability for a player to hunt a dinosaur with a phone ringing in their stomach. For fans of "Jurassic Park", it is a familiar creature.Audiovisually, the work is fantastic. The game is colorful, especially in the middle of a battle. All this mix of colors is accompanied by great music, especially during boss fights like Killavolt or Mouthpiece. However, there are some problems with the frame rate, and the game sometimes even stops when you open the menus.Pros.+ Pleasant shooting system developed over the years+ Larger, more open and diverse locations+ Great boss fights+ Lots of minor improvements to the gameplay compared to its predecessors+ Mass of the content+ Nice graphics, with many improvements compared to predecessors...Cons.- The whole game is basically the same- At one point the landscape becomes indifferent"Borderlands 3" is a very worthy episode in the long-running series. The years long break has only benefited the series, as everything that was good in previous works is now great. Although the game is plagued by technical errors, it is still a good pastime both alone and with friends.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those times when Steam needs to add a "not really" button in the box that asks if you would recommend this game to other players.  Honestly, this game's rating really depends on how hard of a fan of Borderlands you are and how much money you're willing to spend on overpriced mediocrity.Are you a diehard Borderlands fan that spent countless hours on the previous games learning the story, lore, and falling in love with the characters?  Then no, this game is not for you.  The story is absolute garbage and unashamedly butchers the lore of the franchise up to this point.  Half the newly introduced characters are pure walking avatars of cringe, and several of the old characters you loved from the previous games got changed so hard that they are not the characters that they were except in name only.  You'll probably have more fun playing The Pre-Sequel or Tales From The Borderlands.Are you a casual who doesn't care about the story and characters at all?  Then yes, this game is for you.  Admittedly, the only redeeming quality this game has is that it honestly does have the best gameplay of the entire franchise.  If you can get past all the cringe from the terrible story, characters and dialogue, then you're sure to have a blast.  I would recommend silencing the voice acting and skipping all cutscenes and just go straight to the gameplay.  That will be your best bet.Another thing to consider is money.  The method in which DLCs are released in this game are predatory.  There's no other way to put it.  They hype the community up with promises, break those promises, replace it with things nobody asked for instead, and then charge outrageous prices out the a**.  This game should cost no more than 50 dollars tops, but at the rate they're going, it will cost over 200 dollars for all DLC included by the time they're done.So if you're a hardcore Borderlands fan: with bad story, good gameplay and dirty business practices, this game will probably feel like a 3.5/10 for you.If you're a casual: with outstanding gameplay but with dirty business practices, this game will probably feel like a 7 or 8 out of 10 for you.Use caution and consider these factors before puchasing this game.  If you somehow get it for free, even better.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: I'm leaving the original review below and updating as my perspective on the game changed pretty drastically as I neared the end of the main campaign: there was a story reveal that changed my feelings of the game, the story is still pretty full of holes but the reveal got me to the point where I just ignore the holes and enjoy the experience more. As I finished the campaign and found out that you don't have to replay the main story 2-3 times to hit max level, I got a lot more interested in continuing to play the game. As I started a new vault hunter and found out that I don't really have to do any side missions to keep pace on the game as the game, for the most part, scales to you as you go, I had a lot of fun and I ended up maxing all 4 vault hunters; in previous games I usually burned out on having to replay the campaign that many times to finish more than 1 vault hunter.I really enjoy the gameplay, the balance is much better than previous games and the way the vault hunters have 3 different action skills really adds to the build variety. The DLC is really good but the Krieg DLC is a bit short to be a main dlc for Borderlands, I still really enjoyed the experience but it just felt lacking compared to most main dlc in the franchise.Overall, I went from a sort of grudging recommendation to a more full recommendation. The only real issue I have with the game is that Gearbox doesn't seem to care about optimization the game post release but, maybe that will change as they did do some optimization for the new console releases, hopefully they put some of that effort into the PC release.Original Review:I've played for a bit over the free weekend and I've been trying to decide how I feel about the game, I played something like 6 hours before I just decided to buy it, I don't feel like it was a "must buy" decision but I figure I'm going to get enough playtime out of it and I kind of just want to see where the series is going. I just feel kind of meh about this game, it's not really bad enough that I want to quit, but it's not really good enough that I really feel that "one more mission" sort of drive to finish. It's just sort of meh. There seems to be a lot to do, the gameplay is solid and the graphics are great considering I didn't know if I'd be able to run the game--it auto-set to low and I'm fine with that, the game looks better than bl2 or pre-sequel. Overall it's more Borderlands, which is good and bad. Good in that Borderlands is fairly fun, bad in that it doesn't really feel that new. There are new things to do and there are differences but, idk, just doesn't feel enough like a sequel in the main series, especially considering how long the wait for this entry was.Story is kind of mediocre, The humor doesn't seem as strong as 2 or even presequel--I've laughed out loud once that I remember, so far, most of the time the best the jokes get is a bit of smile. Some of the voice actor choices I don't really like, but I don't know how much of that is from script, direction, or performance.Many of the previous issues in the series are back, a few have been improved but many are still there. One of the core issues of the series is even more present: billions of guns but you have a very small inventory and the vast majority of them are not worth picking up unless you can immediately vendor them. Fast Travel is a bit better. The UI is still really bad, maybe it works better with a controller though.I don't know, I'm sure I'll finish the game and DLC on at least one vault hunter, but I'm not sure I'm going to really spend as much time on this as I did 2. I think it will highly depend on if some of my friends end up picking this up. In the end, I recommend the game as it's fairly solid gameplay-wise and there is quite a bit of content in it, but, I probably pick a neutral rating if I had the option to do so. The game is ok, I had hoped it would be great but so far, it just feels ok.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been a veteran of the Borderlands franchise for 4-6 years. As of writing this review, I have clocked in about 1270 hours into the franchise. I can say with a high degree of certainty that Borderlands 3 delivers on the defining elements that make it a Borderlands games. While this game is not as iconic as Borderlands 2, this game continues to deliver the iconic elements that make it a Borderlands games. Core characters such as Claptrap returns as well as bringing in characters such as Rhys from Tales from the Borderlands. The game is certainly better than its predecessor (Borderlands: The Pre-Sequel) as the weapons appear to be more uniquely designed and not lazy reskins/renames. My only gripe with the game mainly was with the Epic Games Store exclusivity at launch in September and the slightly weaker story than its 2 recent predecessors. I absolutely praise the location variety, weapons system, and the balance of the game which is miles better than Borderlands 2's endgame balance. While I still think that the 6 month wait to play it on Steam was absolutely ridiculous, I think it was well worth it given how much it delivers compared to its predecessor. While it is no Borderlands 2, it is still no slouch and it is deserving of the 3 that it comes with.EDIT (April 2020): Since I put out this review, I put more time into the game and bought the Season Pass as well. The DLCs so far as of Guns, Love, and Tentacles (released 3/26/2020) have been decent but Moxxi's Heist of the Handsome Jackpot proved to be one of my favorite Borderlands DLCs in the franchise only to be surpassed by Borderlands 2's Dragon Keep and Borderlands: The Pre Sequel's Claptastic Voyage DLCs. I also highly praise Moxxi's Heist of the Handsome Jackpot DLC for tying up a plot hole that is connected to one of my favorite vault hunters from Borderlands: The Pre Sequel (spoilers withheld). My only gripes so far are the ones I said in my initial review as well as the balance of Zane compared to the other vault hunters. Zane is shown to be on the weaker end of the playable characters but definitely not as distinctly weak like Axton compared to Salvador from Borderlands 2. Despite this, Zane is my favorite of the playable characters this time around and he is definitely still playable while being able to hold his own at endgame.

_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion, the gameplay mechanics has definitely improved in comparison to previous installations (such as the addition of sliding, mantling/grabbing ledges, slamming and variants of an action skill); but the story and general narrative is definitely a downgrade from past games.The story is predictable and stale (and it feels very forced or unnatural in some moments), and the humor code leaves much to be desired. In my opinion, Borderlands 3 has lost a considerable amount of the comedy that was characteristic to the franchise. Some deaths of major characters from previous installations felt redundant and needless. Despite all that, there definitely were enjoyable moments in the main storyline, as well as in the DLCs. Although I wish some of the characters appeared more frequently or had a more significant role, I believe there to be much potential for their use in future expansions. I have loved many (if not most) of the new characters introduced.The gameplay itself is, in my opinion, a clear upgrade from previous games. The addition of the ability to slide and mantle is a major QoL upgrade. The game also provides more versatility with character abilities and skills, which makes repetition of playthroughs fresh and enjoyable. Although legendary items do appear more frequently than in previous games, I don't find it detrimental to the experience. On the contrary, I like that aspect of the game because it lets me test some experimental builds without having to pour hours into it (although I wouldn't mind a slight nerf on the droprates, although it is perfectly fine as it is). The gunplay itself feels like a faster paced Destiny 2 (another game I greatly enjoy). The game pretty much preserves the general atmosphere of the franchise, with tons of enemies and tons of loot.The game, in my opinion, can be summarized to the following sentence: Great FPS (or looter-shooter, specifically), but a mediocre Borderlands game.

_childDocuments_.review: I just bought the game a few days ago because I was bored at home with nothing to play.  Honestly I didn't like that some of the reviews we saying it was a bad story and whatnot.  But they have for the most part said it is just like 2 and still fun.  This is true, but I will counter argue that the story is actually a lot of fun.  I didn't really pay attention a ton to the story is 2, now in 3, I actually enjoy the story much more.  I haven't noticed what others are saying about how they switch the story up.  It has flowed very well and I am interested in where it is going.  The game play is great.  The gun fighting seems more fluid and a lot more fun with a better variety in the guns.  I love the new sanctuary even thought it is a lot more confusing to find places.  The enemies are a lot of fun.  The locations are even better with much more variety.  Also, I feel like you are rewarded much more kindly for exploring more.  I have gone off and explored and always found something neat and lots of loot.  I will say I wish loot management was much better.  There are so many dropped purple weapons that it makes the blue and white one's almost feel worthless completely.  Like there is no ease from white to blue to purple as you progress.  Like I was getting purple and gold in the first 10 minutes of the game.  So its like, what good are white and blue weapons.  In past games you wouldn't see blue until a good bit into the game.  And then same for purple and gold.  Like you might have your first gold weapon after many hours of constant play. Now I think I had purple and gold in like the first 30mins.  I'm not complaining, I just feel like they could have spaced it out more to make finding a gold weapon seem monumental.  Also, some blue or purple weapons are much better than gold.  But there are so many weapons that drop and so little space in your inventory that you can't possibly test every gun that drops.  I would love it that a dropped gun never goes to waste.  I could pick up all the guns and they would be put in folders for each type and I could sort by damage and type of fire etc.  Some guns seem real nice in their description and then you equip and fire it and you got some weird shot that needs to be charged up or something.  I have one sniper gun that has a charge up...but the thing does a crap ton of damage.  Like its a lvl 19 gun and at lvl 30 I still use it because it melts enemies.  I got an assault rifle that does the same, melts enemies and its level 21...I just can't find a better weapon.  The sniper gun is purple.  I've gotten oh so many gold sniper guns that don't even come close to the same effectiveness and they are level 29/30.  So the loot is wacky but fun. The whole game has been a ton of fun.  Highly recommend especially now while its on sale.  I bought ultimate bundle thing for like $50 and so far I love it.

_childDocuments_.review: Would recommend, BUTThis ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game. I don’t know what possessed me to want to 100% this. Well, I embarked on a journey with my friends and it took so ridiculously long to get all the achievements.Please do to ask me about anything story related, despite putting 186 hours into this game, I know literally nothing about that. What I do, however, know about is all the damn glitches in this game and I will need to rant about them *right now*.Some of these glitches are minor and wouldn’t bother you much unless you try to get 100%. Others are a bigger problem. For example, we were playing one of the DLCs when we couldn’t go on. We tried a bunch of stuff, nothing worked, so we figured we’re missing something and took to Google. Turns out this is a known game breaking glitch. We literally couldn’t complete the DLC. We had to wait for another friend who hadn’t done this yet to start the DLC and then we could load in. Otherwise, we would have been ♥♥♥♥♥♥. Many of the achievements are extremely buggy. For example, there is one for discovering each location. Well, I had all maps at 100% and the game told me I had everything discovered, yet no achievement. Since the game doesn’t give you a convenient list or *anything* that might help you in this case to figure out what you are missing, I had to go traipsing across all maps and all areas to find the one damn pixel I apparently hadn’t stood on. Similarly, there is an achievement that triggers after you complete all side missions. I triggered for me but not for my friend even though we played the entire game together. Oh, and another thing that pissed me off majorly – one of the DLCs has you in this weird game mode where you have no abilities, and you grab a few random starting weapons and battle your way through. So, along your run you pick up items and at certain spots on the map you can extract 3 of those items if you want to preserve them after your run. One achievement is for extracting 100 items. Grinded through that, didn’t get the achievement, but my friend did. Turns out, the extraction (although you do this separately for each player) only tracks for the person who hosts the game. Mind you, this is the only time this was the case in the game, so it’s not like this is something you can know in advance. In fact, that DLC in general was really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ annoying.Speaking of annoying, there are several characters in this game that were just grinding my gears. Tiny Tina for example. Or Ava with her eyebrows that look like she drew them on with a sharpie. The game was very grindy at times, very frustrating (how many times can one person say “hold on a sec, my inventory is full”?), especially with glitch after glitch. You know, if this had been a new release I would feel more forgiving about these glitches as I would expect future updates to patch them out. But apparently all of these were known problems that just never got fixed. And that is not okay. By the way, let’s talk about RNG for a moment. There is an achievement for beating the Debt Collector. This is an enemy that spawns in randomly. I cannot even tell you how many times (for sure over 100) we kept going back there hoping that thing would spawn. I get that RNG is RNG but ♥♥♥♥ me that really puts a damper on things.All of these negative points aside, I enjoyed the game overall despite it making me mad as ♥♥♥♥. It’s a lot of fun to play with friends. I like the style and the variety in weapons. I enjoy the different ways to tweak your build. I think my favorite thing in the whole game was the unicorn grenade that chucks out rainbows and unicorns after you throw it (btw, RNG ♥♥♥♥♥♥ me here again. I got that at the beginning of the game, soon couldn’t use it anymore because of the low level and then just never saw another one for the entire rest of the game). I like that there are so many customizable options for your outfit and especially for the weapon skins. I know that this is probably of the least concern to most people but it allowed me to make the game look more appealing which definitely bumped up my enthusiasm for playing. All that being said, I think had I started playing this alone, I would have binned it off at some point. While the game is fun and I enjoy all the mechanics of it, there are just too many game breaking elements that will cause you nothing but frustration. Some of the DLCs (yes, of course you don’t have to play them) are very much an afterthought and not particularly fun to play. With friends this is a nice game to pass some shooty-looty time. So, if you decide to embark on a BL3 journey, I can guarantee you will have fun but also that you will end up super pissed off. There really is no excuse for this many game breaking things to never have been patched. Keep that in mind when deciding whether to spend your money on this. I would definitely recommend only getting this when it’s on sale…

_childDocuments_.review: So, let's just get this out of the way. The Story... is not good. Especially when compared to  and even  (to a lesser extent).Putting the missing characters (Gaige*, Axton, Salvador, Krieg, etc.) aside, a lot of the characters that are in the game seriously missed the mark. The Calypso Twins, Troy in particular, have a ton of untapped potential that could've at least made for a decent follow-up to Handsome Jack. Vaughn has completely devolved as a character, and is a shadow of the intelligent pseudo-bandit he was at the end of Ava is quite possibly one of the worst characters in this franchise, and that's got a lot of competition. A certain character's  death is completely pointless in the story. . Rhys and Fiona's opening of the Vault of the Traveller is left completely unexplained, and Fiona herself is nowhere to be found. The Vaults of the Rampager and Graveward are extremely anti-climactic for something hyped up over 11 years, holding only standard chests with standard loot.But aside from that and the bulls**t Epic Games Store exclusivity, the game is honestly pretty good. While I prefer the Ultimate Vault Hunter Mode and OverPower Levels as opposed to the Mayhem levels, the Legendary Grind is a lot less strenuous than that of it's predecessors, so building a good enough build for the nonsense at Mayhem 4 is not terrible. The gunplay is still top shelf, and the manufacturer differences make finding your own playstyle much easier. The Auto-pickup makes Cash, Eridium and Ammo much easier to collect and maintain, especially ammunition from loot containers.I wouldn't call it the best game ever, the best looter-shooter, or even the best in the franchise, but I am having fun with it, and I hope that the DLC will show improvements in the writing department for the inevitable Borderlands 4.7/10 if you care about the Story and lore of the franchise,8/10 if you don't.*Gaige has yet to appear as of the writing of this review (2020-03-14), but is set to appear as a part of the second DLC expansion

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Good game, it's more Borderlands, if you like Borderlands you'll like Borderlands 3. The playable characters/classes of BL3 are all awesome, skill trees are the best they've ever been (apart from MAYBE The Pre Sequel which I would say BL3 is easily on par with) you have multiple action skills to choose from for each class and multiple augments for each to improve or change their function, AND you can freely swap between the action skills and augments whenever you feel like, you can only have one action skill and 2 augments equipped to use at a time (unless you're playing Zane who can have 2 action skills and 2 augments for each equipped if you want, in exchange for not being able to manually throw your grenade) but you're able to swap between and try the others without penalty.From a gameplay standpoint BL3 is a straight upgrade in every way from BL2, as great as BL2 is, BL3 is better GAMEPLAY-WISE. Writing-wise, If the Borderlands style of "humor" really bothers you then you're really not gonna like the humor in BL3, the story itself is pretty forgettable but it's okay, BL2 also had a fairly forgettable story but Handsome Jack hard carried the entire game by being such an incredibly interesting villain.. so people like to act like the story itself is a masterpiece.Unfortunately the main villain(s) of BL3 are just sorta there, they antagonize you and make you dislike them because that's their job but for the most part they're pretty vanilla, despite having an interesting enough gimmick within the confines of the Borderlands universe.. (they're twins that are "Echo Net Streamers") I feel like the writers could've done more with it to make them more interesting and try to give that similar 'villain you love to hate' energy that Handsome Jack had.. BUT I will say there are some good moments in side quests and here and there throughout the main story that you get to see more of their personalities shine through and these little flashes of greatness are so good, the VA's did a really good job, Tyreen specifically was SO incredibly well done.The other characters range from great to okay overall, with one big exception, but the problem character isn't nearly as bad as the internet would like you to believe, insufferable 50% of the time? Yes, but they don't "ruin" the game like alot of people would like you to believe.The main selling point of Borderlands FOR ME is the shooting and looting, the game "starts" once you've finished the story and start farming unique enemies and bosses for that specifically rolled gun or piece of gear you want/need to make your build really sing.. and that's all here and better than it's ever been, farming has been improved so much with the ability to now load in from the closest respawner/checkpoint after save+quitting, you will still have to run to the boss/enemy upon starting a new farm, but once you get there you can kill the boss, save+quit, continue, and it will spawn you in at the last checkpoint instead of at the start of the zone or at one of the designated fast travel stations, you can also now fast travel to any of the designated fast travel stations or your vehicle AT ANY TIME. This cuts down on alot of the extra time spent traversing the map while farming and it's a very welcome QoL change. There is also alot of quality DLC to purchase now and free seasonal events that you can activate and deactivate whenever you want.If you put hundreds of hours into BL2's endgame and it's DLC's like I did you will absolutely love BL3 despite it's short comings in the MAIN story, so far the DLC's i've played through have had amazing stories and super cool aesthetics (looking at you Guns, Love and Tentacles). I definitely recommend Borderlands 3 to anyone who is a fan of the series.EDIT: So far I've played 3 of the major DLC's, "The Handsome Jackpot" , "Guns, Love and Tentacles" , and "Bounty of Blood" and they've all been amazing expansions both thematically and story wise, as well as introducing some awesome new guns and characters. So if you're still enjoying Borderlands 3 but haven't tried them I definitely recommend picking them up.

_childDocuments_.review: After years of "development" I came back to see if the game was finally tolerable and while I'd admit it is (ON SALE), most of the bugs I experienced are still present... The enemies finally seem competent now on Normal difficulty! I guess my difficulty was bugged when I first played. I never did try Easy mode since I couldn't imagine it being any easier, the first time I played.This one improvement does make the gameplay engaging enough but I have spent more time troubleshooting hardcoded keybinds than playing the game since I bought it... There doesn't appear to be a keybinds file to modify either, so now I'm going to go in game to reset my keybinds to default and put them back in one-by-one except this time I won't assign F to the Exit Vehicle action, so I can continue to Activate/Use things in the world while also in a vehicle - If you assign your Activate key (F) to any vehicle action, it erases the Activate keybind without giving you a way to re-bind it in or out of game...Dumbest, most exploitable A.I. I've seen in a AAA game in years. I stood still 4ft from an enemy and 5 of 6 shots would miss me. How is BL3 A.I. worse than its predecessors? I can't even imagine what the easy difficulty must be... The only threat to my health in level-appropriate battles are my own explosions. Almost none of the bosses I've fought so far have hurt me and one of them wasn't even aware we were fighting while I shot him in the back repeatedly.So many obnoxious bugs on PC, this feels like a beta version.How does a world map get created without any cardinal directions on it? And WHY would you make it freely rotate as well????The fast travel points are hilariously difficult to use.There's no where to see a numerical XP value you possess or required to level... You have no idea how much 2,000xp from a quest means to you unless you notice the xp bar on the bottom of the screen move.Again, there's no numerical counter for how many talent points you have invested into each tree - essentially just another fillable bar.Equipment tooltips frequently break, disappear, or worse appear over the wrong item. Half the time I visit the vendor, the buy menu appears with my inventory's tooltips on the purchasable items until I sell or change pages.Some UI elements stick on the screen permanently, frequently subtitles get stuck, even while others are talking.The only thing propping up this experience is the gorgeous visceral combat using the most awesomely powerful and ridiculously fun guns and equipment ever created. You'll be overflowing with purple power by level 4 and probably a legendary or two at the very least. _childDocuments_.review: My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you

The story is Ok, a lot of people harp on it for not being as good as BL2, but there is only so much you can match with the slow insanity you put Handsome Jack through. If they did the same, it would have just been the same story with a different skin. Characters, Oh my the characters. If you want pure comedy your first play through, pick Zane, hands down. The other characters have their very funny quips, but he is a powerhouse of hilarity. Speaking of the comedy in the game, it is slow at first with a bit more of a serious tone, but ramps up over time, so don't worry if you feel disappointed in the first part of the game not finding the small jokes funny. They are good for a 'Ha' moment, but not much more, but gets better later on, especially if you go for the full completionist lore play through. DLCs. _childDocuments_.review: I don't like to write reviews, but I felt I needed to this time. Borderlands 3 is a game with solid gameplay, and okayish story, and somewhat meh characters. This is kind of par for the course for Borderlands games. However, this game is crippled by a number of technical issues. The first is matchmaking. It is dependent on the Shift servers, which seem to go down constantly. This often prevents any kind of online play. The second is its extreme lack of optimization. Certain zones lag, some specific areas in zones lag, lag spikes in combat, etc. No amount of changing the gfx settings has done anything to alleviate any of this. On top of this, their attempt at DX12 was very, very bad and often makes these problems worse. I can play games like Monster Hunter World with no problem, but BL3, even on lowest, will stutter and lag. As far as I can tell, its some sort of issue with how they handle texture streaming. And the final issue...the bugs. There are a lot of them, ranging from minor all the way up to disruptive/crashing. In light of these issues, I just cannot recommend the game until they are fixed.tl;dr - It has good gameplay, but a plethora of technical problems. Would advise waiting until they are fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing game whether solo or with a handful of friends, and with the semi-recent crossplay update, if your friends got it before you on consoles, you can play with them with no issues. The gore is very satisfying and cathartic to some extent when you need your dose of carnage. The DLCs are worth getting for some extra great stories as well as some returning vault hunters (sadly, no new playable vault hunters...). Cosmetics are plentiful (you can recolour skins now!) and will allow you to enact your inner fashionista. Loot is plentiful and varied, although the frequency you'll drop legendary items might make some people a little upset that they're not rare anymore. The game is sold at AAA price but comes on sale relatively often, same thing with the DLCs, allowing for those with tighter budgets to grab it. All in all, a great classic looter-shooter that is a must-have for Borderlands fans and shooter fans alike.

_childDocuments_.review: Borderlands 3 is a great game. I have probably 500 collective hours over multiple platforms. If you love the borderlands game series, you will have a lot of fun with this game.Gameplay 10/10 - A huge upgrade from borderlands 2. With a handful of new mechanics such as sliding and mounting aswell as smaller quality of life changes. Along with each weapon manufacturer having a unique feel to each of them, the gunplay is better than ever before.Guns. Yes/10 - The guns are even crazier in this game! Wild bullet effects, cool and ridiculous reload animations. I feel like there is a way larger amount of viable options in the end game compaired to borderlands 2 now that slag isn't a factor. I also found myself enjoying lower rarity and using them more often, which made the early stages of the game more enjoyable in my opinion.Story 7/10 - The main story is pretty much the only area where borderlands 3 is slightly lacking. Without spoiling, ill say that rather than the story being bad, it feels almost like there was too much happening for gearbox to handle. I personally enjoyed the story alot, but the journey to the end of the story is just as important if not more than every big event that is bringing the games main campaign to a close. It was hard for me to love the ending as much as i could have if a little more time was taken on gearbox's end. If certain relationships with characters are not fleshed out, then how are we as the player able to care for the story or what is to come next? Lets just hope the fix this with dlc in the future.TLDR: If you loved shooting in borderlands 2, you'll still love it in borderlands 3. If you love borderlands lore, there are a huge amount of echo logs and secrets to be found in the main story and in side missions that add to what we already know and reveal new things that are just as great. The story may not be as great as borderlands 2, but i don't think that is any easy task to accomplish for most studios.

I've bought over 8 copies of Borderlands 2 between Xbox 360/PS4 and PC to play with my friends because I loved it so damn much.The fallout with David Eddings as Claptrap really put an awful taste in my mouth, especially after playing the BL2 DLC Fight for Sanctuary(don't use your game story to slam the previous voice actor due to your stupid ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Pitchford) I really was not on board with BL3 at release.In time, I finally picked it up with my Buddy who we played BL2 and we MET on countless hours of Battleborn, and we both were incredibly disappointed. Even the main bad guys were streamers. Seriously the most obnoxious thing you could have done. Actually Kudos you really made me hate those two and yearn for their deaths just so they can shut their dumbass social circle jerkin' face holes.All in all I really do want to love Borderlands, and I do recognize my distaste for Gearbox and Randy Pitchford likely does give me a negative bias(but the studio still has many talented people), but this game didn't quite hit the mark. My first time through I played as zane whom is an operative, and my second time through I am playing as Moze who is a gunner.  The overall action in the game is completely different because of what each vault hunter is good at and what types of skills they have are vastly different. _childDocuments_.review: A case-study on how developers who grow in size/scope start to make decisions opposite to what made them so successful. Buy this game on sale or third-party and play the game without paying attention to the awful story and shoe-horned characters focused more on their intersectionality within identity politics instead of actual character development.Disclaimer: I have been to several Gearbox community days and have interactions with Gearbox employees and Randy Pitchford (albeit for a short amount of time.) The employees were all chill and even drew me a sketch of Claptrap. Pitchford was more interested in hitting on women rather than acting like a CEO; you could mistake him for a guest.Where should I start with this game? Maybe it should be how the CEO assaulted the original voice actor for Claptrap in a hotel lobby full of witnesses and then would replace him? Or maybe how the same CEO funneled 10 million dollars away from employee bonuses to a company solely owned by himself? Or maybe how the CEO left a usb drive full of softcore porn at a public venue? Or how his own lawyer is suing him for the shady things he's done?No, those are just sprinkles on top of what would be known as a colossal abomination that is Borderlands 3. It should be no shock that Gearbox Software is operating with limited resources due to the shady management. After all, management was so worried about leaks instead of game quality they targeted low level youtubers instead of optimizing the game. This review will look at some key aspects that impact why this game deserves a negative rating with a small concession at the end.A friend and I both worked on Borderlands 1 beta testing and one of the biggest concerns during QA was how easy/comfortable the UI and menus worked during gameplay. After looking back at all the games I can say that Borderlands 1&2 really put in an effort to make the UI something that doesn't break the the joy of gameplay. However Borderlands 3 does the exact opposite. Everything from the map's ever-changing scroll speeds, cluttered icons stacking over each other, and inability to zoom in/out, or change quests on the map page completely ruin what could be a good time grinding an open world area. Furthermore, this error will repeat itself by recycles designs and icons that can allow you to mistake a skill or location for something else. All around sloppy UI and HUD which leads me to believe that Gearbox had to make sacrifices in areas they normally wouldn't have...especially when you consider how they made so much money going Epic exclusive for a year. I believed that the writing from Gearbox couldn't be any worse than Battleborn...I was horribly wrong. I'm a big fan of story and typically will play the game immersed as the character the developer wants me to play. However in Borderlands 3 I despised just about every character and arc they introduced in this game to the point where I was skipping conversations and cutscenes because I was more annoyed at the dialogue than what little immersion it provided. In fact, they did the exact opposite of what they intend to accomplish. At one point, a character warns the player about how the new character they will meet will be incredibly annoying. This new character (Lorelei) was nowhere close to irritating as the first character warned about and the writing crew has been trying their damnedest to make the new character as likeable as possible but failed to an up-speaking barista bot...how, just how?! Props to the voice actor who played the Barista bot because I never thought I'd wish to hear up-speak over Lorelei's voice/personality. This is the only saving grace of Borderlands 3. As somebody who helped with BL1 beta testing and was asked to help with BL3 beta testing as well as going to Gearbox community days to hang out with dev leads at their afterparties; I knew there were some amazing people at Gearbox who put their heart and soul into the franchise, but many of which would leave before, during, or shortly after the BL3. So when the game started up and I enjoyed the gun mechanics, it gave me a false impressions that Gearbox was doing things right. However as I played more of the game I realized what happened to the game. All effort was put into the gun mechanics at the sacrifice for everything else including their port optimizations. I don't mind and in fact endorse developers taking this approach but this shouldn't have been the actions that a Triple-A studio should be taking on their third major installment especially after getting a huge cash injection by going Epic-exclusive. Probably the greatest of all sins from Gearbox is the fact that Hideo Kojima was able to port a Playstation exclusive game to PC almost flawlessly as well as add more content for Steam users at no additional charge or backroom dealings. What does Gearbox do? Greedily take Epic's offer without even thinking twice about it and they can't even make an optimized version for PC let alone Steam. Just more evidence to show that Gearbox was not using the money to make Borderlands 3 better which was the very excuse rabid fanatics of Gearbox were saying to defend Gearbox's sellout. this game is very cringe-worthy in everything except gunplay. However the gunplay doesn't make it worth a buy when you could get a more enjoyable experience from Borderlands 1 or 2. Borderlands 3 should only be picked up through a bundle or when the GOTY edition is no more than $5. Gearbox shouldn't be rewarded for their scummy behavior as well as poorly executed development.

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10Borderlands 3 is a great entry in the Borderlands franchise that, albeit not having a story as good as Borderlands 2 did, takes some steps in the right direction in terms of gameplay.The story in Borderlands 3 has some interesting moments and brings more of the Borderlands lore into the game, like including more about Maliwan other than just their guns, but for the most part it just tries, without succeeding, to recreate the feelings from the story in Borderlands 2. The new villains aren't horrible, but they often just feel annoying rather than actually evil. Certain moments in the game that are meant to feel emotional and impactful just... Don't feel like either of those at all. And one new character introduced in the game that is important to the story often just feels like they were forced into the story and also often feel more annoying than anything else. Plus, Borderlands 3 still leaves a lot of questions from previous games open without answers, leaving players to have to wait for the next entry in the franchise before we can maybe find these answers. Plus it also has a major issue of making the player's character feel nonexistant during cutscenes, even when it's the player's character that is actually doing most of the work in the games.That being said, the story is not entirely bad and it has its good moments. Though, story-wise, the DLCs are much better than the main campaign.The gameplay is where it's at for BL3. It feels fluid, gunplay is great and, compared to other games, there is a much better balance between characters, where all characters are playable without feeling too OP or too underpowered and there are multiple viable builds for each character, too. Action skills feel great to use, guns (in special legendaries) are incredibly creative in their different special effects and hunting for the best gear in the game goes way beyond just getting legendaries, as the game also now includes anointments, adding special effects for guns, grenades and shields.There is also a lot more customization in the game, both for the characters and for vehicles. For characters, it's not just changing skins and heads but also completely different bodies, changing color setups for each skin, adding emotes, gun customization with gun skins, trinkets... There is a lot to play with.For vehicles, there are some considerable improvements to vehicle handling and combat as turbos, tires, armor and weapons can now be changed for each vehicle, besides also including a new one-character vehicle. Special mention goes to hover wheels for vehicles which makes vehicle combat way more viable. (there are, however, still some issues with vehicle combat balancing during late game, where vehicles become too fragile against enemies, which has been a recurring issue in the franchise)It is also worth noting that the dialogue and voice acting for the playable characters is great - with a special note for Zane, who sounds fantastic and has some of the best and funniest lines in the whole franchise.Mayhem modes also add some extra difficulty to the game, though I'm not a fan of all the special effects they include - in a game where there is already a lot going on during the game whenever combat is ongoing, adding more special effects just make things way too confusing. Fortunately, the addition to Mayhem 11 helps with that by removing all Mayhem modifiers.The DLCs add a lot to the game, both in terms of more story and with new gear to be obtained, and the Arms Race mode in special is a really fun addition to the game, a PVE battle royale mode with some really great rewards, and I hope that they keep this mode in future new entries to the franchise.Overall, an easy recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: For the purposes of this review, I'll let you know up front I am giving it a recommendation solely from the perspective of it being a very enjoyable game for what it is intended to be, a looter shooter. The gameplay has a lot of variety with weapon types and effects, as well as various ways to build your selected character, so much so that two people could approach the same situation with the same character with wildly different results. The secondary firing modes is a good addition as well, it was kind of nice to have an assault rifle that could pull double duty as a shotgun, a sniper rifle that pulled double duty as an RPG, an RPG that pulled double duty as a mortar, you get the idea. There was a lot going right with the actual gameplay in this, and I had a lot of fun playing the game.I'm not exactly somebody who follows this series religiously, but even from a more casual perspective I could see that the story this game had to offer was, in my opinion (again, a casual one), one of the weakest things this series has seen. Tyreen felt like the stitched together pieces of Handsome Jack's personality that were left on the cutting room floor (and were better left there, to be frank), Troy felt like nothing but missed opportunity in the second half, and at least half the jokes presented in this game just left me with this dull, vacant expression while I thought "Can you just shut up and tell me who to shoot? I really don't care who it is, I just don't want to hear you talk anymore..."I can go on about the shortcomings of the story for a while, but the underlying point here is that the gameplay is very strong and very enjoyable, and the story is kind of the opposite. If you want a fun looter shooter to occupy your time, this is one I recommend. If you want a solid story with engaging characters and a compelling plot, you have my sympathy if you pick this game to fill that role for you.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a free-weekend, so I played a story playthrough, and I have to say, I'm done with this game. I'm not interested in grabbing another toon or engage in any of the higher difficulties or "end-game", in large part to the mediocre story, the unlikeable or annoying characters and the clunky UI. I also don't feel like thowing money at epig or denuvo. So, if you only care for shooting stuff in style and nothing else, pick up this game, you will not be disappointed. If you are undecided and haven't played any of the Borderlands, pick up BL2 instead. Maybe throw some of the community patches on there, "gib" your toon if you want to skip some of the egregious grindwalls and you'll have a far better experience.Shooting stuff is stupid fun, weapons are wacky with lots of BEWMS and EXPLOSIONS and wonderfully designed gore and mayhem! Audio and atmosphere are awesome. Maps are ok and the fighting-areas are awesome and well designed to minimise backtracking. (that does not apply to the quest design however, you're often sent around the large maps with lots of backtracking)To preface, loot'n'shoot games rarely have a compelling story, they don't need to, but what it has to do, is give the player enough motivation and understandging to invest just enough emotions to continue playing. For me, this game fails at this "simple" premise. The story is ok for a 'maniac of the week' and I'm surprised by how tame it is in regards to the anti-SJW outrage that has surrounded this game. I didn't particularly empathise or care for the new characters or their struggles and how they are presented. Plot-holes, lore retcons and reveals are frustrating. Some sidequests are fun and flesh out story archs others are fun allusions to literature or pop culture, but those are too few and far between. Then there are these selfaware meta quests that devolve into meaningless posturing, especially when the game and developers are engaging in the same tactics. I might have cared a little more if this game was the first in a franchise and I weren't a gullible and naive consumer i.e meatsack throwing money. The Tales from the Borderlands transplants in particular were annoying.The actually likeable characters are cast aside to be one-line questgivers, and expendable comic relief are main actors in the story. That's like 16 layers of irony, "Pot Thoughts" sums up what I think of the story overall really well. I was surprised at the science-minigame voiceover and I respect what gearbox are going for.UI and menus are beyond bad, it spans through the weapon selection, to stats, to map, to quest & markers and selection over to "social" features, to the various cosmetic options. What might have been ok in 2009, mildly inconvenient in 2012 is now an utter ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Basically I've reduced interacting whith menus to a bare minimum, adding abilities and upgrading when weapons didn't deal high enough numbers. For quests and finding my way through the maps I've had mapgenie.io up on a second screen, I just don't give a damn for these types of deliberate obfuscation anymore.I've had no technical issues, game always stayed at 72 fps (manually capped). No screen tearing or fps drops (on my ryzen2700 rx1080 32gb ram and NVME-storage). I've only had considerable stutter, on explosions, entering new areas or opening UI or selecting weapons, basically anything that demanded adhoc asset loading. Sometimes Audio crashed in intensive fights and could oly be fixed on restart, but that was only twice in my playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: I've gone back and forth with my recommendation a few times, but ultimately I can't recommend this game.  This is a strange game; 10% or less have achieved certain achievements, a lot of people seem to dislike the game in the comments, but give this a very positive rating.  I guess you have to be a fanboy to stick around, but if you're not more than likely this game won't be found enjoyable. Having sold 68% more than Borderlands two doesn't make this game good, it just means 68% more people expected something comparable to Borderlands two.Personally, I hate this game, and am only trying to beat the other two DLCs.  I have finished the main campaign and casino story, and am about 50% of the way done with the eldritch and western stories.  I'm not going for 100% and don't really bother for challenges either unless they are right front of me.  Yes the Borderlands franchise is a looter shooter, but others do it better.  Destiny 2 comes to mind and yes, while that is an MMO Gearbox is trying to do something similar with multiplayer here.The cons, because I don't have a lot of pros (for you non fanboys that are looking for a game to play):Story is bad; trite, contrived, one step behind always, no one worth getting attached to, you'll want to kill the NPCs you're working with because they're super annoying. (Gearbox should allow this or choices matter scenarios)  None of the DLCs either make me feel something except hurry up and get this done.  Although, the eldritch dlc is kind of mediocre.Game is way too long.  There are way too many good games out there to bother with a 70 hour base campaign.  I'm nearing 100 hours and still have the western and eldritch DLCs to wrap up.  Definitely not buying the supposed Krieg DLC.Game forces you into Mayhem one mode once you beat the main campaign.  Yes you can easily change it, but I shouldn't have to.  Not everyone is a BL fanboy, not everyone wants to grind for random loot roles, some of us just want to play and get the game over with.Speaking of random loot, there are too many boxes everywhere further lengthening the time to complete this extremely long game, if you choose to open them all.  And, the loot is bad too, just like in Destiny, the random rolls are too random requiring grinding in something that shouldn't have grinding.  (Destiny it might be ok)  This is not an MMO and there isn't really any kind of end game.Gunplay isn't all that enticing unless you like mindless firing.  Not a single gun feels special or deadly in your hand.  Not even a 9000dps Lob, or a rocket launcher that's for 25,000*4 rockets.  So, I don't find combat to be fun, but an extensive chore coinciding with an extremely long game.  A previous complaint of mine was the forced respawns of enemies everywhere that gave no XP; shouldn't be any at all.  Make all enemies reward XP or stop the respawn since they just get in the way.  Now, this no longer applies to Mayhem mode, but still, not everyone will beat the game.Lastly, FPS platforming is bull, cut that crap out, not just Borderlands but others (looking at you Destiny and Doom)  The movement is too rigid, you want jumping and high scaling it needs to be like Titanfall or don't bother. Having to smash the jump button to grab a platform is ridiculous.If you're not a BL fanboy and don't really like looter shooters definitely skip this game.  There are far better games out there.  Not to mention the game runs suboptimally and stutters constantly.  I wouldn't mind if the graphics were great.On edit: Took 115 hours to finish the main game and all DLCs.  This unoptimized game is a slog and runs like trash.  Also, a raid is something that consists of a large group of combatants assaulting a location.  Fighting your way solo into a base to kill a boss is hardly a raid.  Takedown is a nice name but you're only looking stupid calling it a raid.On edit 2:  Finally decided to come back to this game and give Psycho Krieg a try; same rinse and repeat bologna with the same poor optimization, bad drops, crap rng, annoying NPCs, and stupid story lines.  At this point I think Gearbox just wants to annoy the people that play this game.  Of all the things BL3 has to offer the vault card system is probably the best, except that even getting keys to unlock rewards are too random and RNG based.  If you've never purchased this and looking to do so avoid at all costs.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a Borderlands game, what can I say?You shoot bandits with your gun. You shoot some more bandits. You get a better gun that straight-up explodifies bandits or turns them into volcanoes or freezes them into ice statues. And then you achieve everyone's dream of killing Jake Paul.Gunplay and platforming are the best they've ever been; the addition of sliding and mantling really make the levels feel more fun and easier to move around in, and the variety of weapons available can't be beat. The story is good, but not quite as good as BL2. (I mean, Handsome Jack is a tough act to follow, but the douchiest streamers in the universe make a decent attempt.) There's a hefty helping of memes and callbacks in the game (I was BLOWN AWAY to see a Mr. Cool Ice reference) but it's not intrusive. And the DLCs thus far are loads of fun, with actual engaging stories and fun bosses and good loot, and I can't wait for Bounty of Blood and whatever Krieg-related thing is coming afterwards.8.5/10, buy it when it goes on sale and play it with your friends.

_childDocuments_.review: Very bad. Not a shooter Looter.Do you like unskippable dialogue? Do you like it when the dialogue, which cannot be skipped, is equal to or possibly greater than the time you spend shooting and looting? Do you like it when the characters that talk are half-baked and kept alive only by the fact that they can monetized? If so, this is the game for you!This game is advertised to be a looter-shooter but it will do everything in it's power to stop you from looting and shooting in a way that cannot be skipped. Even Skyrim had the skip option and it was a game made ten years ago that has a hyper-focus on story elements. With this game being advertised as a looter shooter, I'm surprised that I have to sit through more dialogue than I did in an elder scrolls title. There is hours and hours of dialogue that you will have to sit through instead of shooting and looting. Also, if you are playing in single player, opening up a menu pauses the dialogue of NPC's. This means that you can't sit through the unskippable dialogue while sifting through your loot and progression menu's, you cannot physically do anything other than sit there. Just so you know, there are more than three sequences of dialogue that are longer than 15 minutes and if you walk too far away from some of the NPC's while they are talking then they stop talking and will restart their dialogue from the beginning once you are close enough again to hear it. Idk if it was intentional to take hours of time and force players into sitting through it while not looting or shooting, but me and many others bought this game so we could loot and shoot, not listen to Tina or any other the other characters for hours on end while being FORCED into doing absolutely nothing else. How this game has "VERY POSITIVE" reviews while not giving a single ♥♥♥♥ about my time or letting me loot and shoot is totally beyond me. Me and my brother had to stop playing this game because there were so many pauses in fighting and shooting that last longer than 10 minutes due to dialogue that we spent more time listening to the game NPC's than we did actually playing the game. EVERY SINGLE PLAY-THROUGH REQUIRES YOU TO LISTEN TO THE SAME DIALOGUE, it cannot be skipped just because it is your second or third play-through. It's a shame too, because the gameplay and looting are excellent, there's just very little of it compared to whatever Lilith or Claptrap have to say. If you like looter shooters, don't get this game. It's not a looter shooter. It's a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ story game with no choices and unskippable dialogue/cinematics where you get teased with fun before being forced to sit COMPLETELY still for another twenty minutes.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, but with HUGE caveat! The teen character Ava in this story is super annoying, to the point of me just muting the in game voices. There really isn't a more unlikable character in the story, and to make it worse, even the voice actor puts an annoying whine into everything she says. If you deal with teenagers at all, this game becomes less of a reprieve and more like a living nightmare as Ava drones on with her whiny, entitled, selfish antics, and because it's written into the story, you have no choice but to comply and do her bidding. A really messed up creative decision that takes a 9/10 game and makes it a 6/10. Don't just take my word for it, go read about the universal hatred for Ava online. If Gearbox wanted to make some more money on DLC, a mod that removes her, or makes her less prevalent in the game would quickly be the #1 DLC.Compared to BL2, the gameplay is improved quite a bit. I especially like the ability to mantle onto objects and that ALL consumables now auto-collect (looking at you, Eridium). Speaking of Eridium, its role has been greatly diminished to just cosmetic purchases as all SDU's are cash based, so make sure you are collecting weapons to sell!I would recommend this game to people who liked the play style of BL2. I would not recommend it to people new to the franchise (because Ava will sour you on the whole series). I also don't see this game supporting many play-throughs the way BL2 did, simply because I can't keep putting up with that annoying little sht over and over.

_childDocuments_.review: BL3 respects the traditions of earlier games, but isn't just a boring repeat of earlier titles. It's a lot bigger, for one thing, but also has creative new leveling up options, side missions, equipment and, especially, guns. The background music and other sound effects are inventive, and enhance the game play. The characters voices are done by consummate professionals, and are really outstanding. I've seen the criticisms about the "wokeness" of the game. However, my impression was that features such as the two old gay guys and the many female characters simply reflect, for better or worse, the culture we live in. I never had the feeling I was being preached to. I found it a very entertaining game to play, and definitely not anywhere near as buggy as reviews of the earlier releases imply. In short, it's worth the price of admission.

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't Borderlands anymore, having pre-ordered both BL1 and BL2 way back in the it pains me to see what this franchise has become.The positives:- When looking at a technical standpoint it's great, it runs buttery smooth, no screen-tearing, all the video options you need and overall it's very optimized.- Lots of build variety with the skill trees.- Some nice QoL's got added which are nice when coming from the older games.- The new character models look excellent, Lilith and Maya for example look great.The negatives:good god where to begin- Probably the biggest issue for me personally is the extreme amount of visual pollution, apparently it got reduced but it's still beyond insane how much clutter there is, from the texture work to the light flashes to the insane amount of explosions, it's a nightmare when trying to look for the enemy or anything really at times.- The horrendous writing and the awful story deserve an award for being the worst I've experienced in the 100+ games I've played, it's laughably bad and whoever is in charge should be ashamed. The characters are unbelievably cringe and just blurt out random XD voicelines half of the time talking about bagels or some ♥♥♥♥.- The audio/mixing is terrible, 90% of the time you got voicelines playing which reduce the sound making you barely hear the music or anything else.- Visually it looks incredibly cluttered, Eden-6 for example just looks terrible with the amount of clutter it has.- The absurd amount of loot you get even when just starting a new character, you don't have to do much and you get showered in legendary loot making you never feel rewarded. There are now pearls or anything to get excited about, when getting loot you won't feel anything.- It's laughably easy, you'll be fine by just playing through the game without doing and side content, check the vendors every now and then for legendaries that are cheap as piss and you're good to go.- The maps overall are bland, some good like Athenas which you visit for maybe 1 hour.- I could go on but this last one kills all the fun, you have to wait every single ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ TIME FOR SOMEONE TO STOP TALKING BEFORE YOU CAN PROGRESS, it's infuriating how often you have to wait for a character to stop yapping before you can progress in the game. Also having to return to Lilith or any character really for basically nothing doesn't make any sense and slows things down.I can name a lot more but what stood out to me is I got little to no positives because there isn't much if anything it does better than the predecessors, Borderlands 2 still is the peak of the franchise and Borderlands 3 doesn't come close.At best this is a 5/10, just painfully average.

_childDocuments_.review: Game play is phenomenal, gun play feels amazing. _childDocuments_.review: As of this review I have spent about 50 hours to complete every main and side quest in the game, I also want to note there is a lot of endgame content to be enjoyed, and if you are dedicated to more than the story players could easily find at least 10 or more hours of fun here.The Visuals are fantastic, Borderlands 3 continues the art-styles of its predecessors while improving on it greatly, the game is stunning, and I found myself using the photo mode all the time to capture its beauty (Screenshots are on my profile If anyone is interested). The visuals are stunning, and it runs fairly well at all ultra I got roughly 120-150 FPS on my 3070 and 2700x Build.The Gameplay is where borderlands really shines, the unique gunplay and fast-paced environments make it incredibly fun to bounce around using your different abilities and unique weapons that are constantly evolving and changing. It's not perfect, and it can be fairly repetitive, but It's just pure borderlands, and if you liked any of the others, your going to love this.The story is fantastic this time around, it's heartfelt and interesting, I'm not really gonna get into it because I think it should be enjoyed on its own. The characters are where borderlands has always shined to me, and borderlands 3 is no different, the characters are amazing and interesting, and it makes you actually care about their fate, its not perfect, but it's done well enough to where the ending actually makes you feel.Overall I think borderlands 3 is a fantastic installment into the franchise and I am very excited to see what Gearbox does next with Tiny Tina's Wonderland, and I am very happy that I spent the time to play all the sidequests, as they are all quirky and interesting in their own way.Gameplay: 8/10Story: 8/10Overall: 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: At the hard edge of the galaxy lies a group of planets ruthlessly exploited by militarized corporations. Brimming with loot and violence, this is your home – the Borderlands. Answering the call of the Siren champion Lilith, four Vault Hunters charge head-first into a spray of bullets, blood, and bandits to recover a map to ancient Vaults and prevent a universe-destroying power from falling into the wrong hands. The rest is history. Fearless renegade mercenaries on the wildest interplanetary treasure hunt of all time. FL4K is a wandering robotic tracker whose cold steel heart warms only for their pet beasts. Amara beats bad guys into pancakes with her psychic fists. Moze’s best friend is a 10-ton walking killing machine. And Zane, the semi-retired corporate hitman... well, he’s Zane.  Hunting Alone? No problem! Shoot and loot your way through the Borderlands, discovering the region’s untold stories and piling high your increasingly deadly cache of goodies and weapons. [2K Games]

name: Metro Exodus
detailed_description: Owners of Metro Exodus are also entitled to the Metro Exodus PC Enhanced Edition - a stunning visual upgrade that REQUIRES a Ray-Tracing Capable GPU as part of the minimum spec. The DLC for Metro Exodus is also Enhanced – purchasing the Metro Exodus Expansion Pass, or The Two Colonels / Sam’s Story individually, entitles you to the Enhanced version of that content, accessible via the Metro Exodus PC Enhanced Edition. Metro Exodus The year is 2036. A quarter-century after nuclear war devastated the earth, a few thousand survivors still cling to existence beneath the ruins of Moscow, in the tunnels of the Metro. They have struggled against the poisoned elements, fought mutated beasts and paranormal horrors, and suffered the flames of civil war. But now, as Artyom, you must flee the Metro and lead a band of Spartan Rangers on an incredible, continent-spanning journey across post-apocalyptic Russia in search of a new life in the East. Metro Exodus is an epic, story-driven first person shooter from 4A Games that blends deadly combat and stealth with exploration and survival horror in one of the most immersive game worlds ever created. Explore the Russian wilderness across vast, non-linear levels and follow a thrilling story-line that spans an entire year through spring, summer and autumn to the depths of nuclear winter. Inspired by the novels of Dmitry Glukhovsky, Metro Exodus continues Artyom’s story in the greatest Metro adventure yet. Features Embark on an incredible journey - board the Aurora, a heavily modified steam locomotive, and join a handful of survivors as they search for a new life in the East Experience Sandbox Survival - a gripping story links together classic Metro gameplay with new huge, non-linear levels A beautiful, hostile world - discover the post-apocalyptic Russian wilderness, brought to life with stunning day / night cycles and dynamic weather Deadly combat and stealth - scavenge and craft in the field to customize your arsenal of hand-made weaponry, and engage human and mutant foes in thrilling tactical combat Your choices determine your comrades’ fate - not all your companions will survive the journey; your decisions have consequence in a gripping storyline that offers massive re-playability The ultimate in atmosphere and immersion - a flickering candle in the darkness; a ragged gasp as your gasmask frosts over; the howl of a mutant on the night wind - Metro will immerse and terrify you like no other game…

_childDocuments_.review: This was a very good game. The game brings in friends from 2033 and Last Light rewarding long time players of the series. That being said, it is still a complete game even if you haven't played any Metro before.The game was surprisingly jam packed with content. Easily over 10 hours by just focusing on main missions and omitting side quests. But way more if you explore the maps to the fullest (which is pretty rewarding in this game). The story is rich and full of character; there are lots of times where you can simply listen in to characters having full dialogues. The game feels so alive and like you are actually part of it so it's very immersive. The combat is pretty fun and if you wanted, you can go full stealth except for a couple of scenarios. There are lots of cool guns, attachments, and upgrades you can receive just by exploring the maps which made combat feel fresh even towards the end of the game. There are 2 endings based on basically being a better person (good ending) or a bad ending in which you don't respect others etc. It was easy to get the good ending without a walkthrough so just pay attention and be smart and you can get it.Anyways, the game certainly is worth it and I was totally immersed and invested in the story. There are a lot of challenges you face and have to overcome and it gets pretty emotional at times. I think this is the best Metro released to date and it feels like all the work from Metro 2033 and Last Light has paid off and you complete the dreams of the characters you have come to know and appreciate. Now besides the story, the game was very heavy to run at times and I'll admit it was a low fps slideshow during some encounters and I have an above average pc granted I am playing at 1440p. I also crashed probably 10 times from start to finish, maybe more. Make sure you are running dx11 in settings and try to save often so you don't lose progress.
