_childDocuments_.review: OverviewMetro Exodus is the third installment of the acclaimed series, inspired to the books of Dmitry Glukhovsky, and set after the events of Metro last Light. Once again impersonating Artyom, players will soon leave the cryptic tunnels of the Moscow Metro to journey on through the entirety of Russia, ending up in a variety of places ranging from deserts to lush forests - accompanied by Colonel Miller and his elite Spartan team. What initially begins as a daring escape soon turns out to be a journey for survival, as unexpected turns of events one after another come crashing down on the squad.🟩 ProsIncredible visuals with excellent art direction.Realistic, satisfying and unforgiving combat system on higher difficulties.Meaningful exploration with many secondary locations.Excellent narrative and character building.Overall good variety of content, situations, enemies and tools.🟥 ConsKarma system, which determines the ending, was reworked in a bad way.In Ranger Hardcore mode, Autosave frequency is inconsistent and can lead to significant progress loss.Rating: ExcellentClick here for the complete Rating ChartExodus' visuals are amazing, possibly the best available on PC to this day. Each environment is recreated with masterful art direction. A Screenshot of Metro ExodusBy: TamasterStarting with the good points, the strongest feature of Exodus as it was with the prequels, is the atmosphere and world-building, which deliver an uncompromisingly realistic take on the nuclear post-apocalypse. This time it's not confined to the cramped Metro tunnels, but shows in full the entirety of Russia's wastelands, and does so flawlessly. Fighting any kind of enemy on the higher difficulties is a tense and unforgiving affair, where all but the weakest attacks mean certain death for both yourself and most enemies.This realism is complemented by accurate gunplay and good variety of murder tools to use. Exploring the wastelands is not only spectacular but also worthwhile, as every map contains a bounty of secondary locations often hiding unique upgrades for Artyom's suit and weapon mods. They will make your life easier once acquired. The narrative and characters stay true to the excellent book series and do not disappoint in the slightest.There are however a few dents to an otherwise flawless execution. The Karma system has been reworked and forces players to take on the majority of situations with complete stealth, without also killing anyone in order to get the good ending. This goes as far as penalizing you for killing someone that shot first and is openly hostile, while the consequences will influence your companions' very lives as if some "higher power" was there to punish you - which makes no sense.Overall, Metro Exodus remains an excellent open-world FPS that delivers the quality already made famous from the previous chapters, at the same time enhances the gameplay in new ways bringing it to a new level that surpasses the previous ones in almost every department. It took me around 25 hours to finish the game on Ranger Hardcore, while exploring thoroughly every map and completing all side content. For the price of 40€ and excellent quality, I can recommend buying at full price.Liked this review, and want to see more of the same quality? Check out Tamaster's Review Archive to see all my Reviews in a single, convenient location.Weapons make up the lack of variety with extensive modding possibilities. Most parts will be found while exploring secondary areas. A Screenshot of Metro ExodusBy: TamasterIn-Depth Breakdown🎮 Gameplay AnalysisGameplay is divided into Exploration, Character Management, Quests and Combat.ExplorationIs performed on foot most of the time, except in a particular map where there will be a truck at your disposal. Ziplines and boats are also used sparingly to traverse otherwise impossible paths. While exploring, keeping an eye out for mechanical and chemical components - both used in crafting - is one of the primary goals, as you'll need them to craft supplies. Of course you can also find already made ammo, medkits and filters, but that's a more rare occurrence.Certain specific places hold unique modifications more or less hidden, and this is what makes exploring every corner worthwhile. A global map will display your position and all the discovered points of interest, highlighted on the map by using the Binoculars on a high place. Safehouses are sparingly set around the world and they can offer a safe refuge to wait night or day, craft at the workbench and more importantly save the game if you play Hardcore. There is no fast travel.Character ManagementCan be done on the fly with the portable workshop in your backpack, or in a more complete manner at a stationary workbench in a Safehouse. You will be able to modify any of your weapons with previously acquired mods at any time, as well craft simple ammo types such as arrows or steel balls, medkits and filters. More complex crafting requires a full bench and that includes changing your suit upgrades, crafting bullets and as well throwables like grenades, cleaning weapons to prevent malfunction.QuestsAre not numerous in the game and usually are about retrieving a specific item for one of your travel companions or another character. They do not always award anything other than achievements or Karma, but still they are worth doing for the sake of storyline and to explore new places.CombatIs one of the most consistent elements of the experience and at least on the higher difficulties, is a brutal and unforgiving affair where even just one shot can instantly kill you, as well as enemies. Ammunition is fairly limited, while grenades and throwables are powerful bit very expensive to create - using all your resources, stealth as well, is key to prevail against overwhelming numbers. Nothing prevents you from going in guns blazing but on higher difficulties it's a good idea to take out at least some enemies silently before doing so.Foes range from your average bandit with a shotgun to nine feet tall abominations with the strength of twenty men, passing from mutated shrimps and venomous giant worms. Each foe has strengths and weaknesses for you to exploit, for example most animals will be scared by fire or your vehicle. Human enemies are definitely smart and use tactics such as flaking, cover and grenades to overpower you, other than having swift reflexes and excellent aim - on Hardcore at least. Being accurate, fast and conservative are the pillars of Metro's combat.Not only humans, but also all kinds of beasts mutated by radiation will be your enemies. Some of them will act as powerful bosses. A Screenshot of Metro ExodusBy: TamasterTechnicalPC Specs: RTX2080Ti, Ryzen 3900X, 32GB RAM DDR4Critical Problems: None.Optimization: Resource usage is within expected parameters for the quality, no problems to report.Performance: The game runs without issues in 1440p, 85Hz on Ultra settings.Bugs: Key rebinds do not work properly for certain keyboard configurations.Other issues: Save system on Hardcore difficulty has frequency issues, might be a bug, unconfirmed.Final ThoughtsMetro Exodus is definitely a worthy successor that expands the prequels' gameplay, taking it to new heights, but not without some drawbacks. Fans of the series and those who like atmospheric games will not be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: It starts off as a bit clunky and slow for a modern game and takes its sweet time setting up the premise, but when you're let loose into the postapocalyptic wasteland, there's no going  back - the atmosphere sucks you right in and doesn't let go.It's not the extreme open world I was let to believe in advertising, but it's actually better for it. It's the perfect blend of open and linear. There are several quite big open maps with each it's own postapocalyptic style and within these maps there are more closed off linear levels with more horror elements. They even put normal action levels between the open levels.The looting is a little half done for a postapoc game, with only two crafting elements to make everything, but scavenging for these everywhere might also get you better gear and weapon upgrades. The weapon system is very cool and extremely wastelandish: You can for instance take a simple thing as a revolver and build it into a sniper rifle with the right mods.And then there's that constant fear of not having enough filters for the gas mask or that your weapons get so dirty they won't shoot properly. Not to mention your headlight running out of battery as a mutant jumps you in a dark corridor.What this games lacks in size and quality to games like Fallout 4, it makes up in sheer atmosphere. At the moment I can't think of another game with better Mad Max/Wasteland feel than this one.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tough one to review. There's a good game,under the grime,and the problems. I adored Last Light,I loved 2033,so much so I bought the books. But Exodus? For some reason,I just,can't get my vibe on with it. I really wish steam had a middle ground button more so than a thumbs up,or a thumbs down. I'm not finished with the game yet,and I plan to rewrite this once I complete the story(I'm currently in Taiga)Lets start with the good!The game looks so great.The weapons feel good mostly. They're punchy,they feel solid,the Ashot feels like a proper handcannon even if it's not my trusty Duplet. The maps are fun to explore.There's lots of neat little things to find. The crew is interesting,the Aurora is rather nice to just hang out on and listen to the various people chat.And that so far,is about where my praise stops.Metro Exodus feels like it was taken out of the oven far too soon. It reminds me so much so of Cyberpunk 2077. If you watch your shadows you have the goofiest animations.  I observed plenty of odd animation and texture bugs or issues(I.e Katya has a habit of..teleporting around for me,or oddly sped up animations). Plenty of animations look choppy in the Aurora. Especially if you observe certain characters. I have noticed in combat,the enemy humans play sort of strange animations when running and ducking into cover. This wasn't something that I noticed in Redux. The weapons that Artyom uses,have excellent animations,it's just odd that you can see your shadows,and the way the character moves,is so rigid,and clumsy.  The animation problems are often jarring I find because so many look plain unnatural.The enemy AI,I've noticed,has,weird problems. Between pathfinding to cover,to detection. There's times I shouldn't have been discovered (I.e hiding in a sandstorm in the dark) and I still get found,even though the bandits flashlights can't see me. Theres many,many bugs. The worst offender has been in Caspian Desert where I was unable to open my inventory. Especially near the end,where you are fighting in the Rig. It would've saved much aggravation and ammo had my backpack been functional. I find it especially odd,to see the weapon diversity enjoyed by Last Light,is suddenly gone.  The Mongrel is terrible as it uses Pistol ammo instead of assault rifle ammo.  There's no VSK,and nothing really to take it's place. There's many holes in the weapon library now,and it's sad to see them now gone. Especially now that your 3rd weapon slot,is restricted to the Tikhar or other Ranger weapons.While my PC surpasses the specs required for Enhanced Edition,I couldn't get it to run properly without CTD'ing. So I gave up and uninstalled it,and just played the standard edition. Mind you I did attempt the Windows update and it still failed to work for me. Even new GFX drivers as well. I'm not sure what the problem could be.Enemies are..hit and miss.Normal human enemies are generally fine(even if they blend in a little *too* well. The armored enemies can go burn in a hole,because they are the worst thing ever I've fought in a Metro game so far. Yes it's good to have them be strong,but it's annoying how they can sometimes shoot you through walls or cover you think is solid due to awkward hitboxes. They are horribly spongy,and you should always have a couple of molotovs ready for them. Storywise,it's fine. Nothing really too stand out,nothing bad either.  Buy it on sale,beware the bugs,the game is fun when it's not twitching out or freaking out in some manner.  But it's not worth full price,and I'm glad I waited a year before I bought it. If anything it showed that it needed more time in the cooker. This will be updated upon story completion.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely love this game!!! Just completed for the 2nd time a few moments ago... what an absolute masterpiece!!!One of the best story driven FPS ever made!!!Other game developers could learn a thing or ten about game design and depth of lore from this game!!!!!!!Brilliantly crafted characters, deep emotional story and dialogue, beautiful and dramatic landscapes, a huge, exciting and emotional rollercoaster of a journey, I would recommend to anyone that loves gritty post-apocalyptic adventures!!!So much detail everywhere, everything feels logical, real life, organic and decayed, wild and desolate, with isolated moments of beauty and tranquillity, so many different biomes the graphics can be outstanding if you catch the sunlight in the right way while crawling out of a dark hole into the world above...A decent mix of linear and semi-open exploring with scripted action and random encounters, but its the story and world itself here that really excels, the shear amount of detail and lore in this game is incredible, you can sometimes spend hours just exploring the world see what you stumble across, or relax just listening to the stories of the various survivors in your group between each mission, go smoke a cigarette with your friend at the front of the train as it chugs across the land, or discuss the plan with another, it really helps set the stage as your group slowly grows in size!! Missions involving team mates actually feel worthwhile, the team plays a genuine part in the mission, covering you, or assisting you with enemy scouting or info on your objectives, You can customise and service you weapon loadout in a ton of different ways to suit your playstyle, stealthy or guns blazing, long range or close quarters,Choose to kill anything that moves and suffer the judgement and dislike of your group, or go the humanitarian route and try to avoid unnecessary bloodshed...its a really cool game!!!!A few negatives... I got a bit of stuttering as the game autosaves and sometime loads areas, which is a little annoying, I've had two crashes on but who knows whether its the game or my PC..hahaAlso some of the initial loading times are inhumane!!!!Overall a fantastic, in-depth, gritty post-apocalyptic experience with some very minor forgivable quirks, well worth it!!!!I give METRO: EXODUS a solid: 9.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Metro Exodus is an immersive single-player story-driven first-person survival shooter. Visuals are stunning, post-apocalyptic (and also post-soviet) atmosphere delivered very well. As usual for Metro game, a fascinating story is the most significant part of the game. That's all for pros. Now let's talk about the bad stuff, and unfortunately, there's a lot of it.Artyom is put on mute. He doesn't talk, although he participates in almost every dialogue. It feels like those cartoons for small kids where characters pretend they are talking to the kid behind the TV. For instance, Dora the Explorer. She asks a question, then acts she's waiting for your answer. Same with our "Artyom the Explorer." People are asking questions, and Artyom's feedback is vital for the story most of the time. However, you, as a player, have no way to choose the answer; neither you hear the answer. It is so incredibly stupid that my limited English skills don't allow fully expressing it.Moreover, Artyom DOES talk during the loading screens. Also, he writes a diary, revealing all his toughs. So it is not even a case where the protagonist doesn't talk to allow the player to make his/her own decision. Metro's superior immersion level makes the player feel as Artyom. Feel dumb. And since the story and immersion are vital aspects for a Metro game, Artyom's dumbness ruins it. I could forgive the developers for the rest of the issues (and there are plenty of them), but this one is unacceptable.Gunplay is "Metroish." It is not an arcade shooting we've used to in other games, but it's also far from realism. I believe the developers wanted to show the lousy quality of hand-crafted weaponry. I admit that; still, I don't like it. Stealth dumbed down even more. More-or-less challenging stealth mode was in the very first (non-redux) Metro 2033. In Last Light, the level designers put all enemies to look away from you, revealing their backs for easy stealth-kill (or knockdown). But that was in the metro (underground), where guards had only two directions to watch in the tunnel, and apparently, they were always choosing the wrong one. In Exodus, there are wide-open areas. To guard the building, four guards should watch into four different directions. That's it - the entire area is covered. To avoid that and make accessible stealth for players, the developers turned some enemies facing a corner - "protecting against rats and roaches."Metro teaches you that shooting people is terrible: crappy guns, weird mechanics, low ammo, and eventually leading to the bad ending. Most enemies are looking aways from you like asking: "I'm standing in a dark area looking into a corner to make sure I see nothing. Please don't kill me, just come closer and make sure you press the right button to know me down instead of killing." I regret choosing a high difficulty. The extra challenge didn't pay off: less ammo, deadlier monsters, but the same, ridiculously easy stealth. Looting didn't make sense anymore: what's the point of reaching a super-secret area, where you find only seven bullets! And I've spent two magazines on clearing my way to the secret. The high difficulty didn't leave me a choice: I had to do stealth on human enemies to save ammo for monsters.Last but not least: BUGS. A lot of them. I waited an extra year for Steam release and hoping that during that year, bugs will get fixed. NOPE. It didn't happen. Bugs are still there. Game is crashing a lot, at least in DX12 mode. It was especially painful on the Caspian level, where I was supposed to downgrade to DX11 renderer. Otherwise, the game was crashing every 5-10 minutes. P.S. To be honest, the game isn't that terrible, and I enjoyed playing it. However, I'm pissed off because of:a) screwed up Steam release (extra year of waiting);b) bugs (that devs haven't bothered to fix during that year);c) voiceless Artyom.

THE EPIC GAMES STORE >:( !!! by no means am i saying that you shouldn't download the Epic Games Store for this game, as that is your choice completely, but I am am gonna suggest that you don't for various well reported security issues and Tencent *shivers* being majority share holder in epic. I myself was lucky enough to pre-order this game on steam when i heard about Epic poaching it off of Steam, i normal don't endorse pre-ordering games due to how games have been releasing over the past couple of years, but i was not sorry or disappointed when this game was released as it was released finished with only minor glitches. The developers 4A Games do amazing work both story and graphics wise and i highly recommend that you purchase this game when the Epic 1 year exclusivity deal is over, and it is back on Steam (probably 20% off just out of spite XD)But now to the game, and my opinions and gripes  on different aspects of the game.(AVOIDING SPOILERS as much as possible BUT SOME MIGHT SLIP THROUGH)Story: Overall the story is good and enjoyable, worthy of multiple playthroughs to see things that you may have missed on your first playthrough. While the story is well written and has good ups and downs, it doesn't consistently flow through different chapters with the very first chapter seeming to speed along a bit to quickly for me to catch everything on my first time playing, and the final chapter seeming to just be very very drawn out with multiple different section setup in a linear layout (which isn't a problem for me as i have played the other metro games ((which is how both of those games where from start to finish)) but may be a bit strange for newcomers to the series.) Overall a great story with pretty good voice acting with each character having their own personality even if some kinda fall flat *cough cough* Katya and Stepan *cough cough*. Gameplay: While the core gameplay is a bit clunky and a bit dated in 2019 (with "press E to" prompts everywhere) it is something that you get used to pretty quickly, and the slow intentional movements works great with the survival horror aspects of the game and with the majority of HUD elements such as a geiger counter, detection light, and filter timer (along with other upgrades you can find through out the game) being displayed on Artyoms wrist watch .         - Gunplay; while on the lower difficulties the combat becomes quite at bit easier and less of a risk to supplies as on easier difficulties supplies or much more plentiful, where as on harder difficulties the every bullet counts and stealth mentality becomes your best friend. There is also a weapon cleaning aspect in this game as the dirtier your weapons become the less reliable and more likely to jam up in combat.        - Gear Progression: Metro Exodus does not have a leveling system as it is trying to be "realistic" in the way that people don't gain more health and stamina by doing random ♥♥♥♥, instead to improve Artyom's kit you need to explore and look for upgrades for both Artyom's weapons and equipment. The weapon upgrade and hot swap mechanic is pretty cool but a bit shallow as once you find certain upgrades there is no point in using any other upgrades, i wish that it was more of a this or that sort of thing like a trade off         - Supply Management: As i said before on lower difficulties this a much less of an issue but on higher difficulties your gonna want to avoid large scale gun fights and mutants of any kind as much as possible/ other than when it is the only choice depending on the chapter. you will want to scavenge for supplies but will need to learn to make it quick, best spots for supplies seem to be in red zones, mutant nests, and bandit camps making planning and/or stealth a necessity for every situation.         - Enemies: same as before on lower difficulties human enemies aren't as big of a threat as the accuracy and range seem to drop off on difficulties lower than normal. On higher difficulties human enemies are much more accurate and deadly. Mutant enemies seem to be a hassle on all difficulties as fighting mutants just wastes supplies as mutants (other than the purple leech things in the putrid tunnel) don't drop anything, avoid mutants when ever possible.Graphics: Just like both of the previous games the graphics are truly a benchmark for pc performance with there being a special extreme graphic option ment for future hardware. while to graphics are extremely good you can still get good preformance by lowering graphics( i have a laptop with a 1060 and play on a mix between medium and low graphics to hit the 60-80 fps range, but the graphics are still amazing)Sound design/ Atmosphere: with all of the sounds in the game tied to one volume slider it makes a very atmospheric and immersive experience as when your around loud things in will overpower quiet things like voices and movement in a very realistic way, only downside is that you really have to listen to what people say which can be hard with there is alot of different sounds going on. Some of the most creepy and atmospheric moments in this game is when your alone in a dark dreary tunnel as there is usually no music in these sections making every little noise very audible and creepy (HEADPHONES HIGHLY RECOMMEND) Weapons sound awesome and powerful, and hit with alot of force. Final overview: Overall Metro Exodus is an amazing game with great graphics, fun gameplay, and a good story. Its only fault is that it is a Epic Games Store exclusive. This is my favorite game in the series so far and the "semi open world" gives the best of both worlds in terms of both linear story driven gameplay and open world exploration. I highly recommend that you purchase when it makes its return to Steam. I give this game a 9/10. i hope you found this review informative, thanks for reading :)

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: An interesting experiment that pushes the franchise into new ground, while stubbornly repeating old mistakes.Exodus is an ambitious game. Whatever else I say about it below, I want to put that out there first for  context. The first two games were ambitious too, of course. What they managed to achieve with their limited budgets was, quite frankly, astonishing. However Exodus is ambitious without that caveat. They have taken the leap in moving from a pretty corridor shooter of 7 hours duration, to a somewhat prettier corridor shooter of 15 hours, to full AAA level Odyssey adventure of 30 hours spanning multiple unique semi-open environments, with boats, vehicles, and several dozen different enemy types. So, whatever else you might have to say about Exodus, nobody can accuse the team of failing to deliver enough content, or enough play time. And nobody could say that they weren't brave enough in trying out new ideas. The developers should also be commended for sticking with the immersive, simple UI of the original games. In moving into the realm of the semi-open world genre with crafting they did not simply unthinkingly adopt the tropes of that genre, but made their own version of it. The in-game backpack and craft table UI is excellently done. The weapon attachments and choices are also well balanced. The scarcity of resources in hard core mode was really appreciated. Although a larger budgeted, more mainstream product, Exodus is still willing to make its hard mode actually reasonably hard for the most part. One of the gripes I had with Metro II was that it was so common to find you had more ammunition than you could actually carry, especially when fighting other humans. In Exodus I actually found myself counting my bullets. The paucity of supplies works well with re-usable weapons such as the knife and the crossbow, rewarding you for patient play by giving you more leeway for those sections when you really need some reckless firepower. There are also some really nice simple improvements that I appreciated after coming from Metro I and II. Some of the gripes I had, such as the simplified UI being -too- simple, so that you could not even see how many bullets you had by holding tab, have been dialed back. Something else I really appreciated was the environments. The first open area, the Volga, in particular, is my favorite. There was a point early on, maybe after I had spent an hour wondering the Volga, where I felt that Exodus was -the- grim apocalypse survival game I had been waiting for. Something to rival a nicely modded Stalker game, or a heavily modded Fallout 4. There were multiple places of interest to explore. The flow of looting, sneaking, shooting, and scouting all flowed so nicely. The atmosphere was cautious. A little grim, but a little relaxed. While in the first Metro games you often find yourself overwhelmed by the stress of 30 minute sections of terror, here we had that pleasant interchange of tension and relief, that I love about open world games. It was executed perfectly. I was in love. If you would have asked me for a score, 4 hours into Exodus, I would have said 9/10.Then it all began to fall apart. (Warning, some mild spoilers about the main plot follow.) Firstly, the story... Things got concerning when I realized my beloved.... I honestly forget her name and I have just completed the game... had developed a cough after exposure to a toxic gas. It was immediately obvious that the game was going to turn into a McGuffin search to save our darling. I felt very disappointed. The stakes were laid bare. The mystery shattered. We are going to save the damsel in distress. And this will supposedly be the emotional core of the game. Going forward that turned out to be entirely correct. Unfortunately, if anything the story of Metro III is therefore the weakest of the Metro games. While the first two have some interesting ideas to explore about the Dark Ones, the third is literally just "rescue the girl." If, and this is a big if, the game succeeded in making you actually care for that character... (now I remember, her name is Ana...) Unfortunately you don't really have a reason. The game takes you through all these sequences that are supposed to be emotional, especially towards the end, but for me at least they failed to resonate. The Metro series has always been fairly juvenile in part because of its source material, and unfortunately Exodus is no exception.The second area where the game falls flat is the world / level design. The early Volga map is excellent. It is perfectly balanced. However the subsequent maps have major flaws. The Caspian desert map is simply too large. They wanted a car, so they made a map big enough to require a car. But driving itself simply takes you out of that nice loop of tension, between exploring, fighting, looting, and instead gives you "drive to A." The Taiga map is really a wide corridor, with some very frustrating sneaking sections. It has a nice ending, and I do appreciate the overall concept, but the execution is just not very good. Dead City is... well... a return to the original Metro Games, but with perhaps even less player autonomy. It opens with what feels like 20 minutes of simply following a guy and hearing dialogue. This is not good. Taking away freedom from the player has always been an issue with this series. Unfortunately Exodus seems committed to repeating these mistakes for the sake of doing something a little fancy looking. Sometimes it works. Usually it doesn't. The final ten minutes of Exodus... well... it is an excellent negative example of what game developers should never do. Similarly, in order to get the good ending, there are sections where the game requires that you kill nobody. At the same time, stealthing some of these sections is a challenge. Two sections in particular I had to repeat dozens of times. Simply because I was not "supposed" to hurt any of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ who were willing to kill me on sight. Write it on your liver guys. Depriving players of autonomy is always bad design. Punishing them for failure by making them reload is bad design. Thirdly, there are some little AAA tricks that I did not appreciate. The original game was quite brutal, and I understand if the edges needed smoothing off for a bigger release that would reach a larger audience. But I certainly noticed when, after dying to a large beast in a certain section and re-loading, those same beasts were now mysteriously all dead. The game had decided that it needed to do some behind-the-scenes lowering of the difficulty level, so that I wouldnt feel frustrated. Given I was playing on "hard core" difficulty I was not impressed by this decision. The whole point is that I -want- to be challenged. If I die, then that is an opportunity for me to learn from my mistakes and try again. I'm far more interested in that aspect of the game than in getting to the next spoon fed story segment.It is a shame to begin a game with such strongly positive impressions and end it on such a low point. I want to emphasize again that, overall, it is a good game, and it is am ambitious game. If it has some very glaring issues, it is in part because it tries to do so much, and this left some key weaknesses exposed. They wanted to have both a very strong, linear, narrative arc, and also an open world exploration game. A better choice, I think, would have been to commit more to the latter, and to try and allow the interesting world to do more of the talking. There is talk of a fourth Metro game on the way. I hope that in hindsight Exodus turns out to have been a bridge to wherever they are ultimately heading. A bit like AC Origins was a bridge for AC Odyssey. There are elements here in this game which are simply superb, and I would love to see them integrated into a more refined package. But that may be difficult when there are some ingrained design habits that still seem to need unlearning. We shall see!

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics: ★★★★★ Metro Exodus showcases a significant leap in graphical fidelity compared to its predecessors. The game's environments are breathtaking, ranging from the hauntingly beautiful post-apocalyptic landscapes to the detailed interiors of makeshift settlements. Dynamic weather, day-night cycles, and realistic lighting contribute to an immersive visual experience that elevates the Metro series to new heights.Gameplay: ★★★★☆ Metro Exodus maintains the series' signature blend of first-person shooting, survival horror, and atmospheric exploration. The addition of semi-open world environments introduces a new level of freedom, allowing players to tackle objectives in a more non-linear fashion. The variety of weapons and the emphasis on resource management contribute to a tense and strategic gameplay experience.  Story: ★★★★★ The narrative in Metro Exodus continues the compelling story of Artyom and his companions as they journey across the post-apocalyptic Russian landscape. The well-developed characters, moral choices, and the exploration of the Metro's rich lore create a narrative that is both engaging and emotionally resonant. The evolving relationships among the characters add depth to the storytelling.  Soundtrack: ★★★★★ The atmospheric and evocative soundtrack of Metro Exodus complements the desolate beauty of its world. The music, combined with ambient sounds and the haunting cries of mutated creatures, enhances the immersive experience. The attention to detail in the audio design contributes to the overall sense of isolation and tension.  Level Design: ★★★★☆ The semi-open world design introduces a refreshing change to the Metro series. Each environment feels distinct, featuring a mix of urban ruins, frozen landscapes, and desolate wilderness. The level design encourages exploration, and the dynamic nature of the world, including day-night cycles and weather changes, adds depth to the gameplay.  Replayability: ★★★☆☆ While Metro Exodus offers multiple endings based on player choices, the linear narrative and scripted events may limit replayability for some. However, the variety in approaches to missions and the moral decisions throughout the game may motivate players to experience different outcomes.  Overall: ★★★★☆Metro Exodus successfully evolves the Metro series, delivering a visually stunning and emotionally charged experience. With its engaging narrative, atmospheric world design, and strategic gameplay mechanics, it stands as a worthy addition to the post-apocalyptic saga. While some series purists may miss the confined spaces of the metro tunnels, the expansion into a more open world proves to be a welcome and refreshing change for the franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished Metro Exodus, so time for a review!I didn't know what to expect here as it is the first Metro game I ever played. But I bought this game based on the overwhelming positive reviews. I can only add one more to that...Metro Exodus is a single player FPS in a post apocalyptic Russia. Do NOT expect a fallout game though! The game is linear with an insinuation of freedom but that's only because the maps are relatively big. However the base is like a book: each new chapter has a new map. The reference with a book is just, as as far as I understand the games are based on books. And if the books are similar to the game, then they must be very good. The core of this game is the superb story. Also it was very refreshing to play in a russian setting, the scenery, the atmosphere of the characters, the voices, all in this typical russian setting. I loved it!Let's start with the bad, so we can end with the good.-linear. This makes the game not replayable. Even though there is a game mode plus, I don't see why you would do that. True, there are several different endings but I for one will not start the same story driven game all over because I know the story already.-Pretty machine intensive. The first game where I had to put my graphics to medium to get rid (mostly) of stuttering screens.-maps and directions. The ingame map system could be more clear. Also the compass only points towards the main objective. Which makes it utterly useless when you want to do one of the few side quests. I have been stuck in levels a lot and had to google a few missions several times to get to the objective.-A few bugs where NPC's where stuck/bugged out so i had to reload previous saves. Not much though.-Content: I found the game a bit on the short side. But then again we're probably spoiled by so many other games with 100+ gametime.+graphics are stunning! All characters are extremely well made.+sounds. Voice overs are perfect. And that russian accent is awesome!+combat is very good. Challenging when needed but never too hard. Headshots are oneshots, but everything else can lead to bullet sponges so you learn very fast to aim for the head.+Crafting system is well done. Even though the options are limited, (you can only hold 3 guns) it always feels like you are one gun short. You can mod your gear to however you want to play but you need to think wisely as you must calculate ammo. sooner or later you will run out of ammo for your primary weapon so you need to switch weapons and depending on how you modified that, you may well be stuck between 5 monsters with only a sniper rifle with night scope... These situations really teach you to chose wisely when you craft your guns for the next missions :)+Story is stellar. Literally the atmosphere of a good book. You can connect and relate to most NPC's. Although the game is linear, there are sidequests that will reward you with background information of the world and extra mods for your gear.+My first Metro game but it's so good I will buy the next one plus all dlc without a second hesitation. A very refreshing experience this was.Total: 8/10Graphics: 9.5/10Difficulty: medium to learn, easy to masterstory: 8/10 (I didn't like the end and I had the good one...)Content: 7/10 Could be more content, but what's there is excellentprice/quality: 8/10 I can highly recommend for people that are looking for a story driven FPS. I'm sold to the franchise, that's for sure!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm punching the "Recommend" button so hard I think it's gonna be stuck and cannot be undone (and I didn't  just do that because I'm listening to Jerry Cantrell's new song [Vilify] while writing this review — I promise). In any case, I'm pretty sure everyone in my contact list heard the noise I just made. One of them, by the way, told me to go to bed yesterday when spotted me out of bed playing "Metro: Exodus". What am I supposed to say? You, mere mortals, don't understand me — I mean, anyone in this review section giving thumbs up. I have new missions in life: save Anna, my beautiful wife, defend my train, sneak past ghouls and rescue teddybears for Russian kids. (Hear that, Soldy?).Ok, so what's in the game that's making me as zombified at night as the ghouls I had to sneak away from in this vast snowy wasteland? Listen to Little Bran and take notes:- Tons of games are known for magnificent gameplays or graphics, but few satisfy you by just letting you BE there. Yeah, just be. Just exist. Feeling the environment, the noises, the snow, the ambience. Up to this point the game already deserves a thumbs up, and I'm not even talking about gameplay and graphics. YET! The devs wanted to make you believe and FEEL you ARE there, left behind, hopeless, walking, crawling or just allowing your senses to do the work for you.- Graphics? What can I say? I forgot how many times I dropped my keyboard, left my mouse and just stood there, drolling. One thing is for sure, if Neo was fooled by Matrix, this is another level even for him. - Gameplay? If doing nothing wasn't immersive enough, the devs took a good look at the mechanics. If Metro: Last Light was amazing as f00ck already, they perfected the moves even more. - Difficulty? THE MORE YOU DIE, THE BETTER YOU GET. Mark Little Bran's words: the game WILL NOT give you a moment of breath, for every moment, event, is gonna lift you outta your chair. Playing in hardest difficulty is simply outstanding, with a total of zero seconds of boredom. Every time a freakin' monster shows up is a WHOOOOOAAAA moment, where you scream of excitement. Even the bureaucracy of fixing/cleaning your weapon, counting ammo to go through a bandit camp, or radioactive pond monster pack, etc are sufficiently catchy to make you keep playing.- Overall, by far, one of the most immersive games I've ever played in my life! You fall in love with every character, hero, enemy, monster, whatever.  - Soundtrack? I couldn't forget about that one. A Masterpiece, no doubts! ps: DO NOT PLAY THE ENHANCED EDITION. It's tons of gigabytes containing bugs. This review goes for the original edition. 10/10 easily.

_childDocuments_.review: Making a new part of the Metro is a difficult task. Making a new part such that it was more successful than the previous two is an almost impossible task. In this part of the trilogy, players will leave the dark world of the Moscow metro and get to the surface in order to board the Aurora train and explore the regions of the nuclear post-apocalypse of Russia, and together complete the adventure of Artyom, Anya and his friends.Graphics and sound have improved significantly compared to the previous two parts. The linear level design is mixed with a small open world, and a more advanced weapon and equipment modification system has been introduced.The story is short, but it makes you think about life. Namely, about the horrors of nuclear war and all the consequences that follow from it. When every day survivors worry about how to live on. People go crazy not knowing where to find water, food, medicine and even some temporary habitat. When there is almost no living place left in the world and everything is covered with some creatures, and radiation exceeding the norm several times on the surface.I also recommend you to take DLC Two Colonels. It tells the whole ins and outs of the history of Novosibirsk in a concise manner. The turning point is very exciting, and the ending will not leave you indifferent either.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge Fan of 2033 and LL and beat them both multiple times. I had my problems with Exodus. It tries to be more of a Open World Shooter and does fail at that. I liked the more linear Levels way more and the Desert Level was by far the worst Level of the Game. It has a Vehicle to drive around and overall feels more like Mad Max than Metro. Overall I liked the Story even though I saw some Plot-Twists coming hours before they were revealed. If you haven't played 2033 and LL before you will probably be less invested in the Characters because you don't know Anna and Miller. I also wish the Dark Ones were present in Exodus, they were the Main Plotpoint in 2033 and LL and saved your life at the end of LL. I beat the Game on Ranger Hardcore, like I did with all previous Games and the Stealthsystem was way more fun in LL. The AI in Exodus has Eyesight like a Eagle and during Day they can spot you, and then One-Shot you, from far away. I really had to trial&error a few levels. The Game also completely removed Trading or Military Bullets as currency. You can't trade anymore and you have a Backpack where you can craft stuff everywhere. That really killed a lot of the Survival aspect. If you were out of Filters in 2033 or LL you were ♥♥♥♥♥♥ and had to scavenge to find some. In Exodus you just open your Backpack and craft some, same for Medkits.Took me 23hrs to beat the Game and I had to replay a lot because there are no Manual-Saves in Ranger-Hardcore you only get a Save when entering a Story-Area. So if you roam around in the Open World scavenging Stuff and then die you can lose up to 60 Minutes. I lost at least 2hrs in the Desert-Level because there were no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Auto-Saves and I got one-shot twice. I played the Game in 1440p everything maxed out with a 1080 Ti and I got anything between 60-144FPS. On Average around 75-85 I think. So its definitely a solid PC-Version, even though the Options are super limited. TLDR; The Game is not bad, but the changes to make it more Open World really didn't work that well. The 55€ I paid at Release, were definitely too much for it. If you liked 2033 and LL I would pick it up during a Deep Sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Metro 2033/Last Light meets open areas you've seen in games like Deus Ex, Dishonored, etc. Big areas that you can wander around in or do the main stuff and continue at a brisk pace. I find the new weapon customization to be a breath of fresh air, as it allows you to play around with guns beyond just what you use, alongside being able to carry a tertiary weapon now. Only issue I have so far is that if you wander around the open areas before doing the main stuff, you'll end up running into a lot of trouble. The trouble being enemies that overwhelm you and the potential lack of resources to fight all of them off. It adds a lot of tension, and I like it. However, it does feel a little wacky. Enemies respawning for instance...nah. I don't like that. Not for me in a game like this. So far I'm liking it more than the first two games, perhaps because of the gameplay improvements. People have said that the setting and flow are different but that's all subjective on whether you enjoy it or not. Many people will loathe this game because of how unforgiving the combat can be. Many people will love it. I mostly like the unforgiving combat, because it's not Dark Souls. It's not about memorizing enemy and boss patterns. It's about picking your fights, and taking advantage of situations where you can use less resources, or none at all, and by extension preparing for the next encounter. It's great. The crafting system lends well to it. Gives the player choice on what they want.

_childDocuments_.review: What I'm going to write in this review is purely my opinion I have of METRO Exodus, after I played and finished the base game story and many optional things. It is very likely that you won't agree with the things I'll say, since it's been proved I have a different conception of the entire METRO series from most of the videogamers out there. I also have read the books: METRO 2033, 2034, 2035, if you have questions, please leave a comment below.In Metro Exodus we have a complete innovation of the entire franchise.Guys at "4A Games" decided to go ALL IN, changing almost completely the setup of the previous METRO games, offering a few semi-open world maps combined with some new graphic features, including the all new nVidia RayTracing technology, which is absolutely stunning on ULTRA Quality.The game feels so immersive, which is the main positive thing of the entire game, and combined with the  (great musician), makes the entire experience really something else, especially for fans of the METRO franchise.Characters are so well made, giving options to the player to know more about them, or simply know the basics to follow and enjoy the story line. Enemies are also different in each map and location, and some of them will really offer you a good challenge and killing them isn't always the best option, this because Metro Exodus is not really a shooter, but a Survival Game, that will force you to take care of your ammunition, weapons, and your armor. You will need to craft your ammo if necessary, clean your weapon if it starts to get a bit rusty, and craft your own medikits and mask filters. All these items are not available in large quantity across the maps, and in most cases you're forced to loot around to gather the essential items to survive, which can give you a sense of frustration if you prefer action games like Rage 2, for example.The customization of each weapon is really well made, giving the change to the player to create tons of different combination, starting just from a selection of almost 10 different base weapons. Another important aspect of the game, is that your choices will change the progression of the game.A bad action during your gameplay can cause the death of one of your crew members, for example, and the majority of your actions can lead to two different endings.Tons of collectibles are available accross the map, that will give you some extra lore, and sometimes some extra items useful to proceed in the game.The graphic isn't exceptional or perfect, but it is very good indeed and very well enjoyable especially if you are lucky to have the possibility to turn on the Ray Tracing on ULTRA. If you love to explore and you're a fan of the post apocalyptic environment, you will have TONS of chances to make some great screenshots, that's guaranteed.A "New Game+" option is available at the end of the game, and new dlcs are coming thanks to the expansion pass.A new chapter of Metro will arrive in the next years with new stories to come.METRO Exodus isn't a game for everyone. But instead, for quite a few I would say.It wasn't even nominated to most of the game awards of 2019, and imho it was very bad damaged thanks to EPIC GAMES, since it was the first title to have this kind of "exclusiveness" of their platform.But it is indeed one of my favourite games I've ever played, for the immersion and the feelings I had playing it, the fun I had to listen their conversations (which most of them are optional), and the excitement I had to proceed towards each single side and main quest, and in each location of the maps.""(Fyodor Dostoyevsky)

_childDocuments_.review: Metro Exodus : By Triple F"Metro Exodus", the 2019 first-person shooter by 4A Games, marks a significant departure from the series’ roots in the claustrophobic tunnels of the Moscow Metro. Exodus takes Artyom, the series’ protagonist, and a band of Spartan Rangers on a sprawling journey across post-apocalyptic Russia, venturing above ground into a vast, irradiated wasteland. This shift in environment is accompanied by a newfound emphasis on exploration and resource management, crafting a unique experience that both expands upon and challenges the established formula.The most striking aspect of Exodus is undoubtedly its open-world environments. Gone are the strictly linear levels of previous Metro titles; instead, players are presented with expansive sandbox areas that encourage exploration and discovery. These sandbox environments, ranging from the sun-baked Caspian Desert to the lush Volga River Valley, are teeming with hidden secrets, enemy outposts, and optional objectives. Whether you’re scavenging for crafting materials, hunting for mutants, or simply taking in the desolate beauty of the post-apocalyptic world, there’s a constant sense of discovery that keeps you engaged.The world itself feels wonderfully alive. Weather systems dynamically change, with sandstorms rolling through the Caspian Desert and blizzards blanketing the Volga River Valley. Day and night cycles alter not just the lighting but also enemy behavior, with mutants becoming more aggressive at night. These environmental factors add a layer of complexity and challenge, forcing players to adapt their strategies on the fly.Exodus’ crafting system is another significant addition. Players can scavenge for materials in the environment or from fallen enemies to craft a variety of weapons, ammunition, and equipment. This newfound ability to customize your arsenal adds a layer of depth and strategy to the combat encounters. Do you prioritize crafting silent weapons for stealthy takedowns, or do you stockpile high-powered ammo for explosive encounters? The choice is yours.Combat in Exodus retains the series’ signature blend of tense firefights and strategic resource management.  Ammunition remains scarce, forcing players to carefully consider every shot. The human AI has been significantly improved, with enemies flanking, taking cover, and coordinating attacks. The returning mutant menagerie is as formidable as ever, each requiring specific tactics to overcome. Whether it’s the hulking Nosalises that can tear through cover or the skittering Watchmen that lurk in the shadows, each enemy encounter is a thrilling test of your reflexes and survival skills.While the open world environments offer a wealth of possibilities, they can occasionally feel a bit empty.  Certain areas lack the density of encounters and storytelling moments found in the Metro’s more linear levels.  The narrative itself, while compelling, doesn’t quite reach the same heights as the previous Metro titles.  However, the core themes of survival, hope, and the enduring human spirit are still present, carried by a cast of well-developed characters and hauntingly beautiful environments.In conclusion, "Metro Exodus" is a bold and ambitious evolution for the Metro franchise. The expansive open worlds, dynamic weather systems, and deep crafting system offer a wealth of new experiences for players.  While the story and world density don’t quite match the intense atmosphere of the Metro’s underground sections, Exodus remains a thrilling and atmospheric journey through a post-apocalyptic Russia. Whether you’re a seasoned Metro veteran or a newcomer to the series, Exodus offers a unique and unforgettable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely LOVE the Metro games- theyre excellent delivering characters, story, dialogue, setting, tension and atmosphere, and thankfully this one delivers on everything. While its not as good as 2033 and Last Light theres still a ton to like about this game, and while the open world setting doesnt  work here, its not nearly as open world as you may think. First, the positives...Like I mentioned, the Metro series nails just about everything from a human perspective- not a supersoilder doing cliche after cliche in tons of other modern FPS games nowadays. Metro really makes you feel like YOU are Artyom, and builds upon that with an excellent cast of supporting characters. Like the other games, theres lots of dialogue to stick around for if you want, but its all up to you. And its not just filler dialogue either. It really makes you feel like it actually means something- a trait that has carried over from game to game wonderfully. It looks great, sounds great and has a nice variation of places to go. The environments are incredibly detailed and diverse. You get a train too (trains are awesome!). The story moves along well and the tasks you need to do make sense. The weapons and shooting all feel great and satisfying. The crafting system is back as well and you need to be mindful of your ammo and supplies as well as keeping your guns clean so they work properly and dont jam.So now the negatives...First is the so-called "open world" aspect. I can see where 4A Games were going with it- and yes it DOES make sense storywise- but to me it came up a little lacking. Basically, youll visit a spot on your map via train as the main story progresses, and the game plops you into a decent size area, or "map" I guess you can say. While your main objective is always there for you to accomplish, youre free to look around and do what you like. Problem is, there just isnt a substantial amount of stuff and things to do out there. Yes, you can discover a bandit camp, kill em all and you may get a small reward in the form of a new part for your gun, but that seemed to be about it. I wanted more. I wanted side quests meeting new npcs/survivors with their own branching storylines. I also wanted more types of loot...but the game doesnt really have loot- its just chemicals and spare parts to clean your guns and/or craft ammo for the most part. Maybe I was just wanting a Fallout NV experience in Metro's shoes, I dunno. The second negative is performance. While I experienced zero crashes and zero corrupted save games, Ive read others have had this issue. Also, the FPS drops a lot into the high 40's and 50's for apparently no reason. Im playing at 1080/60 on high with no ray tracing or other resource hungry effects on so Im not sure whats going on there, but it can a little annoying at times. I eventually just dealt with it, but only because I was so into everything I mentioned before. So is it worth it if youve played the other Metro games? Oh hell yes, absolutely. They did an excellent job here once again and I cant wait to see what 4A does with the next game!

_childDocuments_.review: An FPS that tasks you with surviving the war ravaged remnants of Russia. It has a fairly strong focus on narrative, and a number of segments are more or less you watching an event unfold from your player character Artyom's eyes, the opening segment being a notable one. Some of these can feel somewhat lengthy but you spend more playtime in control in the end. Related to all this, I'm not sure if Artyom is supposed to be mute and the other characters are aware of this, but throughout the game he never says a single word, even in situations where you would really expect him to, like letting his teammates know he's alive over the radio, or saying something back to his loving wife when she pours her heart out to him. I don't know what the reason for having him never speak during gameplay is (I think it was like this in Metro 2033 too at least) but the result is baffling in every instance.As for the other characters, the antagonists you'll usually meet felt generic. You get more info about them and the factions they lead from conversations and documents in the world (which I never found all of), but they didn't feel all that interesting beyond their gimmick and are still hard to like for obvious reasons. Even though the factions you encounter aren't exactly as silly as something you'd see in a Fallout game, there is something darkly humorous about encountering a different flavour each chapter to impede your progress, and the portrayal of some is over the top enough to overrule how terrifying their concept is in practice. Intentional or not, I don't think I disliked it. The friendly characters fare better definitely, some have more characterisation than others.The plot is interesting even though the inciting incident can feel bizarre. There's instances of narrative contrivance to be found here and there. In the end in spite of questionable choices in some places it's easy to get swept up in the emotional journey these characters undergo. The world also has an interesting story to tell through the notes you can find and conversations you can overhear, and being able to witness these makes exploring it more worth it.As for the gameplay (I was playing on Hardcore rather than the highest difficulty), careful shooting and stealth is a must if you want to avoid dying. Headshots are instantly fatal to all but the most powerful enemies, so landing them is satisfying and very much encouraged. All out firefights can break out and these can be intense and enjoyable ordeals, though some weirdness can occur. One instance that thankfully didn't repeat had a group of enemies able to hit me through walls, also had a few instances of enemies managing to hit me when they shouldn't have had line of sight. Ammo can be limited, but you should have enough if you loot everything you kill and avoid firing with reckless abandon. The stealth is mostly what you'd expect, lots of tense moments await. The game's day and night cycle plays a part in this, some enemies might be asleep during nighttime and the darkness means they'll all be wearing flashlights on their helmets to act as indicators for their cone of vision. Despite enemies noticing corpses and unconscious enemies, you unfortunately can't move them as far as I'm aware. Some weirdness was also encountered here with enemies seeming to spot me as soon as I took one out when I shouldn't have been visible to any of them, may or may not be intentional. Overall in spite of some annoyances here and there this part of the game was really enjoyable too. When it comes to human enemies anyway. I've never liked fighting the monsters in Metro, but I disliked it less in this game and it seems just sneaking or running past is a viable option too, so that's nice. They can at least give you another reason to stay alert, and things like hearing the airborne monster roar above you without knowing whether or not you're about to get demoned away somewhere can be legitimately terrifying.Exploration is an important part of the experience too, and just stalking through the ruined world for whatever reason can be engaging on its own, it really does look amazing a lot of the time. The areas in the game can be large, although getting through them didn't feel like a hassle. Except for the first area that needs you to use a slow moving boat to move around, that also makes you a nice, big target for the aquatic monstrosities of the area. The game has sidequests, though they don't get tracked visibly like your immediate main objective. You usually become aware of them as a result of something characters say, though I'm not sure what performing the necessary actions without hearing about it first does. When talking to characters, you don't really prompt them for more info or ask about particular topics, I suppose they just talk as long as you stay nearby. They can sure go on for a long time, but it is usually interesting so worth listening to.Overall very engaging, I'd strongly recommend to someone looking for an often stealthy shooter with a narrative focus.

_childDocuments_.review: If you find this review to be helpful, my curators page is here: This is the third game in the Metro series, and is an easy sell for previous fans. It's the same mixture of environmental hazards, scavenging, melee and ranged combat, tense set-pieces, and boisterous OTT story-telling that the series has consistently delivered. The open world setting does make levels freer to explore, and allows for the game to expand in a pleasant way that doesn't dilute it's best qualities. It's not fundamentally all that different to play, but it does freshen up those aspects that were perhaps in danger of getting stale, and without sacrificing their talents at making intense or scary directed moments.For those who are unfamiliar with the Metro games: They take place in Russia, after a nuclear war has left the landscape uninhabitable and the survivors have fled underground into the train tunnels. Life is tough, and above ground has radiation and mutants, but there are relatively comfortable communities making it from day to day. You play as Artyom, an optimistic every-man who gets drawn into the fight for survival against foes that range from men to monsters, to advanced beings with control of time and space. Y'know...the usual post-apocalyptic USSR stuff, which is solidly constructed rather than anything ground-breaking.It's voice-acting is usually overdone, and the characterisation can be a tad iffy (most Russians are apparently a bit loud and blustery?) so it has never been totally convincing on the narrative front. However, it has also never failed  to deliver an engaging mixture of FPS combat, survival elements, and exciting sequences of tension and terror. You're not a cyborg super soldier, or roided up bad-ass military guy, and this is a world where your gun is powered by a bicycle pump, and whether or not you have any ammo for it will depend on if you want to eat your last potato for health, or use it as a projectile to try and brain someone with it.I'm kidding about the potato, but bullets are both your money, and...uh...well, things you shoot with. The most potent weapons will be guns, and so are costly to actually fire, or you can have air-powered weapons that are cheaper to produce ammo for, but don't pack as much punch. It's a game where lots of little touches add up to a fairly unique flavour: some areas require using a gas mask, and finding top-ups for it's filters. You can get dirt and blood splattered over the visor, and will have to wipe it off. Your torch is powered by cranking the handle, and bringing up the map is an actual "physical" object Artyom retrieves and looks at.This isn't Fallout, or Dying Light, when it comes to it's crafting mechanics. You don't just get some wires, a few Duracell batteries, some double-sided sticky tape, and a gun, then slap it all together A-Team style to make a rail-gun that shoots beams of energy. It's not Call Of Duty where you're firing off a gun so powerful that it takes bionic arms just to carry it, and then you call in a death-beam strike from an outer-space satellite. Generally you'll probably be going down the stealth route, and are shooting them with a cobbled together air-rifle that sounds like a duck politely farting, or getting up close for some stabbing / neck-breaking.Fire-fights are for bourgeoisie capitalist pig-dogs, with money to almost literally burn, as it goes up in smoke with every bullet fired. It's a balancing act trying to get by with the cheaper, less effective weapons, so you can eventually afford to purchase upgrades to improve them, or save up for something better, but that is also more costly to use. On the higher difficulty levels it's a tough enough challenge that in the first game of the series, I couldn't ever afford to buy a new weapon throughout the entire campaign. On this third game they've softened that challenge a little bit (in some ways, at least) and searching every nook and cranny will yield all the items, or all the bits and pieces for crafting useful additions. It's smoother to progress, but limits to your inventory, relatively scarce resources, and the levels of enemy opposition, mean it's still not easy.It can be played as a run-and-gunner, and the combat is slick enough to satisfy. Though stealth is a viable option too, and enemies have varying states of alertness and responsiveness to threats. Mechanically this is very polished across all of its elements, and by now is super-slick with it's set-pieces. With plenty of capacity for tension, scares, and thrills, these nicely break up the "loose" action for more tightly controlled sequences.Story-wise it's engaging enough, but I'd be lying if I said this was ever it's strongest suit. This is about immersion in it's world, the sense of place and atmosphere that the excellent graphics and soundscape help to convey, and all those things that ground you in it. The involvement with your weapons and utilities, as you pump them up in the heat of battle, or furiously wind up your torch to see in pitch-black locations. Hearing your character desperately sucking in handfuls of corrupt air as your last filter runs out, and you're stumbling around searching for another before suffocating. Around you there's weird phantoms of long-dead people going about their business in an echo of the distant past, and there's no time to pay this bizarre anomaly much mind when there's the somewhat more pressing matter of ensuring you can breathe.The adrenaline rush of hard-fought encounters, or nervously creeping through the shadows unseen. That huge sigh of relief as you make it to a quiet moment after all that tension. There's a stretch where mutants aren't trying to tear your face off, and people aren't shooting at you, and the only thing you have to pay any mind to is the hum of a geiger counter. Just as you get comfortable, something bursts out of a nearby lake, or out of the ground, or from the sky, and you are reminded that you can never be truly at ease in this world. It is possible to appreciate this without playing the previous games, as it doesn't riff particularly heavily on events from the first two. Though some familiarity, and connection to the characters, will make it's twists and turns that extra bit more poignant or involving. For the most part this release is a very enjoyable final to the trilogy (the voice-work, whilst not bad, isn't great either, but that's it's main flaw), and I highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: We all know what happened with EPIC and that greedy nonsense but the Devs deserve praise for this game.I had my reservations about Exodus at first. Metro on the surface? There is no way it's going to have that Metro feel. But I was wrong, this is probably the most Immersive and well done Metro game yet. The weapons all feel and sound great, every shot has impact and with the plethora of mods for each weapon that you can find that offer slight bonuses right up to complete overhauls of the weapons function every weapon can be 5 and with the crafting system that lets you change up the parts on the fly you can adapt to any situation quickly.The story is fantastic and excellently paced, you get to know and become attached to the train crew as after each chapter you have downtime on the train to wander around and listen to the crews thoughts, stories and interactions with you and each other. You can scan the radio to listen in on other peoples conversations out in the Russian wasteland which really helps to make the whole world feel alive. Your actions have consequences, slaughtering your way through a group of hostile people may seem justified at first, but later on you may learn that you didn't have the whole story and will end up facing repercussions for your short-sightedness.The open-world is less open and more of a large level that you are free to explore on your way between the main story beats. This works well as the Devs took a quality-over-quantity approach to the level design. It may not be packed with side-missions and content, but what is there is meaningful and really helps to flesh out the people and the factions you encounter.The Ranger mode feels like it was rushed and poorly implemented, giving you two options for HUD when choosing it, Minimal and Deep Dive. Deep Dive is only for those who have already completed the game as it strips out almost the entirety of the HUD including action prompts, which means you will never guess that certain doors can be opened or containers checked unless you go up to everything and hold the action button and just leads to more frustration than immersion, Minimal strips the HUD down to the bare essentials but leaves the action prompts (though they are more transparent). As for gameplay it's not the Ranger mode fans would recognize, everything kills Artyom in 1 or 2 hits but mutants and enemies can soak just as much damage as other difficulties, combine this with the fact that you will find almost no ammo and will probably use most of your crafting resources making medkits to survive the sequences where taking a lot of hits is unavoidable and it just becomes more frustrating than a real immersive challenge like it was in 2033 and Last Light. I would recommend just playing on Hardcore and turning off whatever HUD elements you can in the options. The crafting system is nice, but often leaves much to be desired. Why would I spend precious resources crafting a molotov or grenade when I could make 3 clips of ammo and 2 medkits for the same cost? The cleaning mechanic was a nice idea but poorly implemented, basically your weapons get dirty and you need to spend crafting resources to clean them or they will suffer massive debuffs and jam every other shot. Problem is, you don't have a lot of control over them getting dirty. Accidentally step into deeper water than you were expecting? Well now your rifle is useless and you need to trek all the way back to the nearest workbench and spend 2 medkits worth of supplies to clean it. This resulted in me cheesing the system by having my least used weapon out while I explored so that it would take all the damage and I didn't have to waste resources cleaning my other two weapons when I tripped and fell in a puddle.Overall Metro Exodus is frankly the most Metro experience to date. it is a fantastic game from start to finish and if it wasn't for the EPIC nonsense it would have been lauded as one of the best games of the year and easily the best in the series.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10 Good game but not a great "Metro" experience. BUY IT WHILE IT'S ON SALE, not worth full $60-90.Glad I bought this at a discount and waited for a year. Exodus was hyped for its open world approach and for leaving the Metro! You can expect the open world experience to be like The Witcher 3, with smaller open world area and some linear stages in between. So... is this game good? Yeah nah.....SPOILER STARTS HERE....TLDR; Too easy, not many monsters, small (20hrs-ish) and coolish ending.First the gun! In Metro LL & 2033, the game forces you to learn and use lower tier guns (because that's all you have) and this makes you approach the earlier stages differently. In Exodus, EVERYTHING is available from the start and lots of ammo (except the highest difficulty). This basically feels like New Game+ without actually finishing the game. So if you're a rambo style player, you'll have fun here.  Ammo currency is also removed, so I didn't get the feel of "shooting my money away".Monsters are easy and predictable. You still have the usual enemies from previous instalment, Watchmen, Shrimp, Spiders and a bear (boss fight). And the very first new monster you'll see in game a zombie. This zombie creature basically fills in two major open world stages. They are boring, predictable and honestly over used. Don't get me wrong, many of the monsters are still entertaining but the good ones don't really get the spotlight it deserves. There's only one real monster boss fight, the bear. But it's less engaging than Metro LL's bear. Battle sequence goes like this, Aim  n'shoot, wait for the bear to charge, run to the side, repeat step one until bear is dead. Nothing inspiring, very predictable. The other monster boss consist of QTE events and cheap animation scare.Compare to Metro LL, from the top of my head, Shrimp boss fight, nosalis brood mother the epic bear fight.....Even the human boss fight is down right bad, is it even a boss fight? Cramp you into a room and pump it full of enemies. Compare to Metro LL Pavel's boss fight... BUT WHY THE POSITIVE? Put simply, I enjoyed it. The gunplay is fun, the animation is cool, the graphic is beautiful, no crashes, no FRAME DROPS despite looking really good!!! And I got it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, the review will be exclusively about the game «Metro Exodus» and  not about any other aspects and scandals associated with it. It seems to me that if the developers screwed up at least in something, gave the slightest reason to bury their game (at least in optimization, at least in the plot, at least in technical aspects), then many people after the recent events would gladly do it in their reviews. But the rating of the game is steadily high, they play it. That is why I want to evaluate only what the developers have done, what has already taken away several sleepless nights and will take many more.«Exodus” - this is the torch that illuminates the bright future of single-player games, which took the best things from the previous parts and has changed with the help of many innovations. The conventionally open world gives the player a sigh of uninfused air outside the Metro, see what the torn Earth has become without the harmful influence of mankind, meet people returning to simple life, living next to monstrous creatures, but seeing the Sun every day. The player is given to visit various climatic zones with different nature, different living conditions, and each locality has its own interesting features.The game still skillfully deals with the plot, replacing the dizzying action scenes moments of peace, intimate conversations with members of their team, each of which as a family member for Artem. All the secondary characters are incredibly worked out, Anna is the best girl Artem could meet and marry, and is incredibly human, each of the team members has her own character, I want to worry about them in every difficult situation. Graphics and optimization at the highest level, the game flies like a feather and feels like delicate silk. The system of crafting weapons and components is implemented perfectly, it feels necessary, but not so much as to turn the game into a blunt grind of resources for crafting, but only encouraging the player to thoroughly research locations. The weapon feels realistic in all that relates to the physics of the shot and the system of damage to enemies. You really see how much damage is caused by shots from one or another weapon to different parts of the body, how distance, your position, etc. affect the shot. Monsters are much harder to kill and fighting with them requires serious planning and tactics, understanding their weak points. It's easier with people, even though I try to solve problems with non-violent methods and stealth.If we talk about moments that are not performed at such a high level, here we can say about the not always perfect facial animation of the characters (although most of the time it is quite good), several times I caught non-critical bugs, a mini-map could be more convenient, Artyom's silence is a bit depressing, enemies sometimes see you from an incredible distance.Metro Exodus is a great project that worthily completes the game series. A game in which it is equally interesting to shoot monsters with a shotgun at close range, and sit with your beloved girl in a reserved seat and listen to the AuktYon and Viktor Tsoi on the radio, looking out the window at the running life, thinking about the eternal.

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of the Metro franchise, I am in love. I'm extremely happy to say that it exceeded all of my expectations and delivered an unforgettable experience. The level of detail put into the environments is absolutely mental; each location felt like a living, breathing world with its own unique set of challenges I had to come across. I found myself constantly in awe of the beautifully rendered landscapes and dynamic weather effects, which in itself made the game so much immersing. The storyline was equally impressive, with well-developed characters and an engaging plot that kept me invested from start to finish. The game's blend of action and stealth mechanics kept things fresh and exciting, and I was constantly on the edge of my seat as I navigated through dangerous parts of the levels. What really set Metro Exodus apart for me was its emotional impact. The game tackled some heavy themes, and I found myself genuinely caring about the fate of the characters and their struggle for survival and the eternal "freedom" from all the post-war chaos. Though I got the bad ending, I am still happy with how the whole experience turned out. Overall, Exodus was an unforgettable experience that I will never forget. Thank you Metro, what a ride it was!

_childDocuments_.review: Metro returns with Exodus and continues to be one of the best single player story driven FPS experiences in gaming.
