_childDocuments_.review: The main reason for the negative review are the frequent crashes, especially when you attempt higher difficulty levels. A few too many particles or certain objects in the frame and the game just crashes on a loop. One example was a terminal I had to interact with. A dozen crashes in a row until I managed to get past it after loading the game in safe mode in 720p. Many negative reviews focus on the same problem, so I know I am not alone and this should not be acceptable from a high profile developer.Other than that, the game is a bit of a hit and miss. There's a lot of beautiful stuff, but the gameplay is kinda boring and the story predictable and dull. Developers tried to take the storytelling off the rails (pun intended) and let you explore an open world, but didn't know how to make the open world interesting. There is technically stuff to explore, but you should really just head towards the main objective. Most of the places you can visit are reserved for a future objective and feel broken and empty until it's triggered. Plan to mop up the stuff you missed as you prepare to leave for the next map, not the other way around.I think the writing is one of the things that put me off the most. The main character doesn't speak, but constantly interacts with people who deliver forced exposition via long, cheesy and unnatural monologues. You can tell the writer is the sort of person who really likes listening to their own voice.I think the DLCs are actually where the game was most fun. They are shorter experiences that are more linear and have much better pacing.

_childDocuments_.review: Metro Exodus is the third entry to the post-apocalyptic Metro game series, following Artyom's footsteps and his companions’ journey across the continent of Russia. Exodus features an atmospheric survival-horror gameplay with its own mixture of non-linear, gorgeous and deadly environments to explore. Exodus features an improved weapon system with more in-depth customization options and a few newly introduced features to the series: crafting system and a day/night cycle coupled with a dynamic weather system.Highly recommend playing the previous titles  before Exodus as I think Exodus doesn’t truly introduce series’ newcomers to the world of Metro and the metro environments itself as Exodus focuses more on non-linear open levels.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the first Metro and absolutely adored Metro Last Light. They had bad voice-acting but made up for it with an OK story, an incredible atmosphere and tight and intense gunplay. It seemed like a no-brainer to get a hold of Metro Exodus, even though I wasn't exactly thrilled about the game going open-world and abandoning the creepy metro setting.The game's obviously had a way bigger budget than the previous two, but I cannot for the life of me see where all that money went. The story's terrible and full of clichés and had me cringing for the most part, especially when you leave the first 'open' area. I'll keep it spoiler free, but I cannot imagine anyone getting shocked or even remotely impressed by whatever happened at that . The voice-acting this time around somehow got even worse. I have no idea if the script / producer told them to speak incredibly slow and with an even thicker accent, but everything's just. so. slow. No believable delivery at all from any of them. The gunplay's fine. I mean you point, shoot and reload. There's some good variety in the arsenal like in the first two games.In case you couldn't tell, I'm pretty disappointed. I expected and hoped for a better game.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, I've "played" about 6 hours so far. I deliberately played in "" because the game crashed or got stuck 3 times during this time and I was more busy listening to Anna and the others. But I'll get to that in a moment. Since I read a little before buying, I already knew that the game is now more open world and actually doesn't play in the metro like the other two parts. That doesn't have to be bad, does it?Nothing has changed in the controls. To play I still need what feels like 20 fingers to be able to somehow operate all functions. I didn't like that in the other parts, but  I don't know what it's like with the controller, I've never tried it, but I am of the opinion that it could have been solved differently or the inventory that you carry around with you could have been divided up or put together differently.The NPCs in this part look much better and more realistic than the ones in the previous parts. There are also new mutants like the beastmen, which at least has convinced me.From the other two parts it was actually clear to me in advance that there would be some speech scenes, cutscenes, stories and conversations, but: Either I watch a scene or I have to run after someone or listen somewhere.Even when I am supposed to fulfill a task / mission, I always have someone in my ear who has to tell me something.I just want to play, nothing more ...Speaking of which, I think it was a huge mistake to get involved in such an apocalyptic drama with a woman.Anna !To be honest, it really gets on my nerves and provokes slight aggression. Apart from the fact that she definitely has the say in the relationship with Artyom and he only seems to do what she says or wants, she just keeps talking, giving commands or having something to whine or complain about.Furthermore, I have the feeling that the game has mutated even more into a sneak game. Even if I run it doesn't last forever because I'm out of breath so quickly, puff and have to run slowly again. In the open world it's kind of tiring and exhausting. Since I don't just have to get from a to b, but in between I always have to go somewhere else, on foot or in a boat that feels as fast as you walk, it all somehow drags on so unnecessarily.At least now I definitely know that we are not alone and that there are other factions and peoples on earth.That was actually foreseeable, only why there was no contact so far was not clear. But we've already solved that. I suspect that in the next few hours I will meet one or the other faction and probably eliminate them. There are still too many people on earth after such an apocalyptic event...Well, almost 4 hours and a few more falls, I've left winter and the cannibals behind and I'm here, hm, well, I think it's summer, but the desert is more likely to hit it, I think. Apart from the fact that everyone else always has a lot to say, she annoys me mostly and extremely ...Somehow I'm bored of the game right now.There are phases in which you are challenged for a moment, be it with the fight against other factions or against mutants, but most of the time I run or drive around slowly to reach my next goal.Before I can do that, however, I'll be sent on side missions with more stories. If it could go a little faster it probably wouldn't be that bad after all.In principle and for the sake of the story, these are also good and expand the gaming experience. Because of the slow flow of the game and the speed, it's really difficult for me at the moment.So, actually I wanted to  today. Unfortunately, I had to find out that due to the last gamecrash yesterday, there are no more save states in the cloud so that I should / have to start from the beginning. Great game, honestly ... Fortunately, the saved games were still in the Steam Cloud, so that I could download them by hand and now can "continue playing" where I left off. Then let's wait for the next one to crash ... I have now returned to the metro. Since Anna is terminally ill in the meantime, she has been shut up for a long time. That's why Miller, her father, speaks all the more now. Worse still, I have to tour with him and no matter what he sees, he knows exactly what happened and has to tell me immediately. Apart from the fact that I am not absolutely not interested in what happened somewhere, at least 20 years ago, I thought, you are quiet when you are on a mission where mutants or other opponents can appear all the time? Miller was really cool in the first two parts, now he's a complete disaster. I wish he was only a third as cool as Miller from "the Expanse" ... honestly.So my friends, I finally managed to finish the game and paid the ultimate price and saved Anna.The whole time I thought about whether I should rate the game positively or negatively. Despite everything that annoys me so much, I decided to rate the game positively.Basically it's a good game and (almost) ties in with the other two and I just think who played the other parts should still play that because of the whole story.It's a shame that the game often crashes on DX12. There is some information and help on the various game crashes on the net (if necessary).For my part, I would have been happy if it had been possible to skip the cutscenes and all that I didn't want to know, see and above all hear. Well, I've got it and think about whether I will still do all the other things like collecting postcards, etc.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like they combined Fallout 4 and Wolfenstein and kept the worst of both and added a few jump scares. The crafting is unnecessary, boring, and only there because crafting is 'in.' Metro's never had great cover mechanics or been a great FPS but in the Metro it was less of an issue. Being suddenly swarmed by zombies (yeah there's zombies now) and watchmen in an open field, it'd be nice to be able to actually take cover. And of course the open world adds nothing to the game. In fact it detracts from the charm that the first two had. The open world is pretty, but empty except for a few packs of animals, the occasional surprise demon, and the areas that are populated with people. It may as well have been a metro system with a few branching lines. Overall 6/10. There's better horror games, better fps games, and better open world post apocalypse games. _childDocuments_.review: Metro exodus is a good game overall and worth the price for about 20+ hours of game play if you familiar to the series. Starting with the positives, Exodus adds on a lot compared to the previous series, it adds: a couple sandbox areas, several linear sandbox maps like last light, a crafting tree for all items (weapons, ammo, armor, attachments), two paths for bad and good ending plus dialogue trees through out the game based on killing or sparing(weapon holstering on some events), day and night cycle, bandit bases, mutant nests, a LOT of dialogue from your teammates and characters, boat and car driving, weapon degradation, enemy surrendering, and way more. The sandbox areas really shine for me like: what time of day makes certain enemies more active, bandits on guard in day, mutants roaming the night, safe houses to sleep and resupply, side events like the main enemy of the area setting traps, and points of interest (bandit camps and mutant lairs) for weapon/gear addons. The crafting system replaces trading system and gives better flexibility instead of going to a shop to remove components (and hope it works for this area), and its simply two materials that are used for making ammo and items. The story is about above average but makes up with a lot of side quests for your crew and the other characters who join you. The side characters who "join you" in missions usually take a back seat as supporting fire which is preferred over "tour guiding" as the first metro did quite a bit. The side characters are tied with the karma system on whether you went full bloodthirsty mode or mercy/stealth and can die based on that decision, along with a change in attitude/tone especially for Miller. Graphics are good when I played on minimum but on ultra pretty good if you have a high end PC. Voice acting great, sounds great, cutscenes are superb, small details just awesome (like weapons getting dirtier, small animal wildlife, and enemies talking about your actions).For the Neutrals well there's a decent amount of written lore that I don't bother too much with it. There's no real new enemy types as their reskins of previous (games) mutants with slightly different mechanics. I'm not fond of collectables regardless of what game. Stealth is harder as enemies are more aware of their comrades, see in the dark, and have bigger field of view in general especially in day. I have no idea how to switch ammo types for certain weapons so that annoys me. Certain weapons aren't available till later on, which shortens the amount of use you have with them which I guess is expected in survival games.The negatives rise a bit from the PC end so consoles may fair better. I played on minimal settings(gtx1060, i7 3770, 8 gb ram, windows 8.1 pro) and my pc was huffing and puffing so this is a demanding game, so take it with a pinch of salt to buy on PC. The custom keybindings aren't solid as it messes with cleaning guns, disassembling and silent killing binded with the use medkit button! Quickloading seems to glitch out the game the more you do it and leads to some weird bugs (my favorite is being launched out of the moving train to the sky box and dying on the way down). Hit detection is a problem it reminds of stalker clearsky, freaking bullets dancing around the enemies head. Of course Artyom remains a mute, really annoying me as why have him voice over the mission loading screens? The dark ones are hardly mentioned(I say this as its too subtle) and don't make an appearance, pity. This is just a general overview of the game so not everything is greatly explained in detail or I might of missed (especially in the negatives department and reviews have a character limit) but the positives outweigh the negatives and gets my recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: For starters this is one of the only games i feel i need to give a review of unlike most of the garbage i review also i tend to ramble but will do my best to keep it concise.First and foremost I should point out that i bought the game on sale but after playing it it would have been worth full price.Secondly I should say that I didn't have many gamebreaking bugs happen to me. Not to say there was none but nothing where i needed to restart my game or stopped me from progressing. Third i got the game on Steam so i had no issues with my copy being removed or something that i see some of the negative reviews mention. Last but not least I have not played any of the previous metro games so there is probably some story aspects that went over my head, but i didn't feel like i was missing any plot points or that things wern't clearly explained to me in the story. I played the game on all ultra and put motion blur on low i didn't notice it very frequently but some people had an issue with that, u can turn it off in your game files regardless. Also I play on a 1080ti i7 7800 and had no fps drops.The areas have this amazing charm to them and it really got me immersed into the world and character i was playing. Nothing ever really breaks that immersion nothing too much or too stupid. There are quite a few different areas and they are very diverse from each other making them all very memorable. All of the weapons also fit into this charm as they are all things that you could have possibly existed or shambled together.I will give the game alot of credit there haven't been many games that can do so many different settings and also keep me immersed in the fact im playing as a Russian Special Soldier.Guns have this weight to them that makes them feel powerful but are also not unresponsive. Reloading is slow, guns can jam, sights can get dirty, all things that can happen that i think are less tedious but play more into the immersion. There not tons of ammo to find depending on the area, so more likely you will have to craft ammo. Trying to maintain having enough ammunition for any fight you might have to take and conserving it and using it at the right times felt true to the situation. I will also use this section to talk about the AI. { For reference i played on Hardcore } You die from 2-4 bullets on average but you can down most enemy humans in a simple head-shot making aiming carefully and saving ammo really rewarding as you will usually get more back than u spent. The AI isn't completely unfair either they can miss but most of the time they are very accurate so stealth is recommended. Not to say that you cant just outgun everyone and everything and still survive but it is alot harder. There are quite a few different monsters that you will encounter over your time playing Exodus. Ranging anywhere from Flying Bat Demons to spiders afraid of light and a Giant mutated bear. They all have different weaknesses and different strategies you want to use accordingly. They force you to adapt to using different guns and ways of fighting them changing up the gameplay mechanics from fighting regular humans. I will cover this briefly cover this as i mentioned reasons to use it above. It is very useful vs both humans and mutant enemies, and plays in very well with the games day and night cycle. During the day the human guards at compounds are alot more alert and can u see you from much farther ranges, but if you decide to sleep till nighttime they will have a much harder time seeing you even when relatively close to them allowing you to take them out stealthily. I will not go into depth here as to not ruin things but rather focus on more of my opinion. I thoroughly enjoyed the story the character development between all the characters seeing how they all end up after following their journey. Its a very atmospheric game where you can do simple stuff like go out for a smoke drink some tea play the guitar. It all adds to this sense of realism, the developers did an amazing job making ever character feel real and not just some background guy that does nothing. They all make sacrifices for each other and there is just some great satisfaction and enjoyment in being a part of it. These are some characters i will never forget. Also i did Russian voice acting with english subtitles to make it feel more real. There is a few things to mention here such as cleaning your guns, workbenches / backpack and sleeping. Firstly your guns as you use them in different environments will become dirty and less reliable. They will jam more frequently and your weapon sights will get dirty making it harder to aim (especially with scopes). To counter act this you must take them to a workbench to clean them and it will cost a resource that you can find throughout the game. I personally never found this very bothersome but you can be cutting it close because you need that same resource to craft medkits and filters. The more you explore the more you are rewarded with resources and smaller things like notes to read or tapes that play. The other main mechanic is using your backpack that you can use anywhere unlike the workbenches only at select locations. The backpack dosen't allow you to clean your guns but to simply change the mods or craft the bare essentials.You will rely on the backpack very frequently through out your playthrough. The last thing i want to touch on is radiated areas, you need filters for your gas mask that you can change with 3 minutes of time each. You can tell how much time is left in total on that filter by looking at your watch on your left arm. When you don't have your gas mask on it tell you the time of day. There are only a few criticisms that i can make that really bothered me. 1. The saving feature is really bad it only allows you to quicksave rather than making a normal save and whenever u save again it over right the last one so if u happen to save after u did something you want to undo you could have to restart the whole area again. ( Only happened to me once) \2. In the Desert area 3. The Taiga level 4. The one boss fight in the game is very cool but very unfun to actually play its just an big ammo sink that runs at you and its very boring the play due to the amount of health points it had (it could be because of the difficulty i was playing so take that with a grain of salt). 5. Terrain and physics, if you run down a flight of stairs on a crane you can overshoot the tiny guardrails and fall right off. Or if you sprint at a tiny incline it can send you flying into the sky and you will fall back and die. ( only happened once ) 6. Fall damage is really annoying in this game and should probably be tuned down, you take substantial damage from 6-7 foot falls its only of the only things that broke my immersion. ♥♥♥♥ you im not some ign smuck that gives a game a arbitrary score of 1 - 10 i think its idiotic and dosen't tell you anything at all. I personally loved this game and it will forever hold a place in my heart. As for you i guess you will have to play it to find out : )

_childDocuments_.review: I have completed my first play through in 30-40 hours.  I tried to complete as much as possible and wanted to get all of the gear.  I ended up getting the good ending.  The good/bad ending system I enjoyed a lot more than the previous games.  In past ones you had to avoid killing creatures or animals.  In this one it is based on your decisions interacting with the societies you encounter and how much you help the companions you travel with.  This was much more engaging since I didn't have to worry about a random creature/human attacking me as much.  It also felt more justified with this.Visually everything looked amazing.  I am running this on a 8th gen core i-5 and a geforce rtx 2070.  It all ran smoothly and I never had issues with the lag or jittering.  The lighting from my head lamp & lighter were amazing.  There were definitely moments where I watched the lighter burn the spider webs away and particles and light blazed across the screen.  The textures and models also looked incredible.  After killing creatures for the first time I actually crouched down and just studied the beautiful models in the spectacular lighting.  The environments are also great.  They are interesting to look at and feel like a real place in the world.The dynamic weather system was beautiful and dramatically changed the way I interacted with hostile creatures/humans.  This also helped blend the world together.  The open world aspect of the game is incredible since I could go anywhere in the map and explore at my own desired pace.  The game also had the metro tunnel feel in multiple areas and integrated well with the open world.  The new factions were interesting and were a fresh breath of air when compared with the typical nazi & communist bad guys.  New creatures were also added to many of the old list of creatures.  They also integrated those creatures into the different environments & seasons.  The entire time I played the game I felt engaged and had a desire to continue forward.  I was initially upset that I didn't get to go and collect bullets and buy the new guns.  It was exciting to save up and get the new gun.  After an hour or two I was completely on board with the new system.  In the previous games I avoided using the pistol.  The shotgun and a long barrel rifle were always my favourite choice.  In exodus I used it all the time.  Being able to have a silenced sniper rifle with a massive clip & a short range pistol was amazing.  With the new system it made all of the guns feel valuable and versatile.This is a great game.  The mechanics are amazing and work well in this universe.  The combination of open world and closed tunnels are great and offer a new experience this universe has never had.  It has also allowed the story to expand in new ways that staying in Moscow would never have.  This has allowed the developers to tell an incredible & engaging story.  All that being said, a lot of the negative reviews are about the game being released first on Epic and later on steam.  It is fair to be upset, but the game is solid and should not be punished for this.  The developers clearly found it was in their best interest to go this route.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy oh boy. This is where it gets interesting.This is something different from it's two predecessors. Even the desert chapter of the game was amazing and I didn't expect it to be good because its different from the previous games where it snows all the time. A lot of times I just stop going to the objectives of the game and keep looking at my surroundings. The enemies you fight in the game even surrender when you kill most of them and have a hard time catching up to you when its night time because they cant see you in the dark. There's a day and night cycle in the game and you can check your watch ingame and completely changes your playstyle depending if you move around the map on what which time of the day. They have these perfect breaks in the game where you can relax after finishing a map and just be on the train where you can interact with other characters and prepare you for the next setting of the game. Without a doubt the graphics and gameplay in metro exodus is perfect just like the previous metro games but I still have problems with the soundtrack. _childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying I recommend this game only when on sale, and only bundled with it's DLC.That said...I do recommend Metro Exodus, but it is a very flawed game.Not in gameplay from moment to moment, or in story or characters.More it's in how it's laid out overall. For a game that prides itself on exploration and it's vast world this time, it honestly feels like it runs out of open world steam quickly. Not to say that their can't be linear sections or that the open world is bad. But thought the game tye two beat parts are the vast open world sections.Then the rest is linear and one semi linear section. It's a shame, because it really shines when it opens up. The closed in sections are interesting, especially the one after the first open area. That one is the right one gtg for an inbetween section. And the last area is really solid too. But then you have the semi area, and it just feels clunky.Frankly each part is good in its own way, except the semi open section which has cool ideas but feels like a half assed watered down attempt to fit more open world but still be railroady. It's a shame cause I thought it would be an interesting new vast open zone, but it ends up being just a way wider corridor. It's just kinda a bummer.Really it needed another major open world section to lead into the last area. It just feels like it's rather abruptly short. Like the best portions ended to soon.I recommend it, but man, I still feel bummed by the lack of more vastness to explore. Go into it knowing your only getting 2 open world maps, and then corridors, some wider then others. The DLC are interesting though, especially Sam's. The DLC are solid expansions of the worlds story. Overall not a perfect game but solid enough, with some disappointing failures that will bug ya till the end and leave ya wishing they'd expanded the world just a bit more.

_childDocuments_.review: After powering through  and , I have finally hopped aboard the Aurora for the latest title in the  series. While the game looked pretty good, most discussion of this game really vanished after its controversial PC release back in 2019. So to those of you out there that were like me up until playing this game and have no idea how good this game is supposed to be, allow me to answer that question: It's pretty damn good.I don't this really needs to be mentioned, but obviously the graphics are absolutely gorgeous. The outdoor areas in the open world levels in particular aren't as up to par, but this is alleviated by the linear outdoor levels, one of which has some of the best graphics I've seen in a video game. It never felt too bright or dark, building interiors absolutely nail that claustrophobic, spooky feel that these games are known for, and it generally retains the classic atmosphere. The character models also look very good, and the game maintains its immersion throughout. One thing I also liked was the variety in the environments. It's cool to play the game in seasons outside of nuclear winter, and it really shows off how capable these games can be visually. Overall, this game is  at its best visually, and while there's some smaller hiccups, but overall this game lives up to the series standard in terms of graphical fidelity.Now the gameplay is where things start getting interesting. Stealth is generally hit and miss, but it's not as awful as some other games I've played. The game doesn't offer as much variety in the weapon selection, but I personally don't mind because I liked the upgrade system. The combat is fine, too. It's still got the  jank, but it's nowhere near the same frequency as . Where the game loses a bit of its edge, though, is its open world segments. I had no issue with the idea of an open world, but I think  messed this up. There's a fair amount of things to do and there's some pretty neat rewards for exploring the areas, but my GOD, it's so tedious actually traversing through them. The first open world area has a boat, which is easily the more annoying one of the two. You're juggling a bunch of enemies that may try to leap onto your boat, a giant fish that will attack you, and floaty mechanics that just got increasingly frustrating. The second open world wasn't as bad because you didn't have to juggle all these things, but for some reason I kept having a problem where the game's camera would be stuck in a higher position if I pulled out my map and put it away, and while it was easily fixable, it was so annoying having to constantly do it because it slowed me down just enough to where it became a nuisance. Because this series is slower-paced, it works in a linear environment because levels are small and cramped, and when you expand the levels to a massive size, only to not increase the pacing, it makes exploring a worthwhile, but incredibly tedious task. Speaking of which, the linear segments are easily the highlight here, especially the last level, which might be my favorite level in the series. This game can absolutely nail the classic  feel in these linear levels, but I just wish there were more of them. I think, if there is another game and they intend to keep the open level approach, they can keep the level size but increase the pacing a little bit and have more small, cramped buildings to explore to strike that perfect balance. Other things I'd mention would be that I miss the bullet economy system, but it's not too much of a big deal. The game absolutely nails the immersion, and I love all of the little details that make the game feel a lot more realistic. I also love this game's morality system. It doesn't force you to play fully non-lethal, and ultimately just boils your actions down to "Pay attention to who you're killing", and the game does a good job of hinting at when you should try to avoid violence. But, while the game is pretty fun to play, there's a lot of technical issues which did make things a lot more frustrating, outright freezing in some cases. It took me out of the game just enough to be an issue to me. Ultimately, while the gameplay still retains some jank and the open world stumbled a bit, the rest of the game is fine and I had fun playing it.In general, the story is solid. It was entertaining enough and I didn't think the writing was too bad. It just didn't blow me away either, for a big reason I will get into later. I like the more grounded take, placing a far greater emphasis on a small group of people struggling to survive in a nuclear wasteland, and there were some really interesting ideas being presented with some of the factions, like a cult that despises electricity and one group that into two clashing sides because they interpreted their leader's (well-intended) teachings differently, mirroring the many religious feuds humanity has had throughout history. It's a nice change of pace from the Nazis vs. Reds and whatnot. While some may not like the lack of a "supernatural" element, it's still there. It's not as obvious, but there's some subtle details that raise some questions about the story that I won't spoil. The world building is excellent, and having a lot more variety in the locations helps make the post-war world a lot more fascinating as people take on the new world in different ways. However, while the main story was just fine, the ending was amazing. It concluded the trilogy incredibly well, and while it was bittersweet, it was still immensely satisfying. Overall though, the game's story isn't too bad. What holds it back, then? Well, that can be found in the audio department.While the story and characters are fine, the voice acting is not. My expectations weren't high because the voice acting has always been fairly cheesy, but it just does NOT work in this game. For one, Artyom is still a silent protagonist, and considering how much he interacts with other characters, keeping him silent in-game just breaks the immersion and totally bothered me. And because of how much human interaction is in this game, the poor voice acting kills some of the emotional weight that this story absolutely should have. The kid voices in general were pretty horrible, but everything was just so  to listen to. Anna and Miller are okay, and that's part of the reason why I like the ending so much, but the rest is just unbearable. The audio design isn't too bad, though. Everything sounds loud and crisp compared to how muffled everything was in  Overall, make Artyom talk in-game. Please.You'll definitely get your money's worth here. It's the longest game in the series, and the DLC content is supposedly very good. The side content is enjoyable, but the slog of getting to it brings it down a little. The ending will definitely stick with you, though. Not much else to say. is really just more of what you'd expect. I think it didn't fully achieve what it set out to do, but it's still an incredibly entertaining game anyway and I'd easily recommend it if you liked the other games. It's both a great conclusion and a solid blueprint for the future. I'm excited to see where these games go next, because even if it wasn't amazing,  is still a strong step in the right direction. - 9.5/10 - 8.0/10 - 7.5/10 - 6.0/10 - 8.0/10+ Strong world building+ Great linear levels+ Solid sound design+ Gorgeous graphics+ Good morality system- Tedious open worlds- Lots of technical issues- Horrible voice acting

_childDocuments_.review: ### Review of Metro Exodus:Metro Exodus is one of those games that stays with you long after you've finished playing. Developed by 4A Games and published by Deep Silver, this game offers a unique experience set in a post-apocalyptic world.#### Graphics and Design:The first thing that strikes you is the stunning graphics. Metro Exodus transports players to a variety of beautifully rendered locations—from snow-covered cities to irradiated wastelands and forests. The attention to detail is astounding; every nook and cranny of the world is intricately designed, fully immersing you in the survival atmosphere.#### Story and Characters:The game's narrative continues the story of Artyom, the protagonist from the previous entries in the series. The storytelling is impressive both in depth and emotional impact, touching on themes of hope, survival, and humanity in the face of total destruction. The characters are vivid and memorable, each with their own unique personalities and motivations. Interaction with your companions on the "Aurora" train adds another layer of depth and emotional attachment.#### Gameplay:Metro Exodus offers excellent gameplay that strikes a balance between action and stealth. The game allows players to choose how they want to approach each level—whether through intense firefights or sneaky maneuvers in the shadows. Weapons can be modified and customized, adding a strategic layer to combat. Additionally, survival elements like crafting and resource management make the overall experience even more engaging.#### Open World and Exploration:The game takes a step away from the linear structure of previous titles, offering more open and expansive environments to explore. This allows players to delve deeper into the game world, uncovering secrets and side missions. The freedom of choice and multiple paths to achieve objectives make each playthrough unique.### Cons:The only drawbacks worth mentioning might be occasional bugs or technical issues, but these are not critical and are likely fixed through patches.### Conclusion:Metro Exodus is an outstanding game with a deep story, complex characters, and captivating gameplay. It is a must-play for fans of post-apocalyptic shooters and followers of the series. Artyom's journey and the stories of his companions will stay in players' hearts for a long time.Rating: 9.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: As i grow older, i tend to lose motivation to play games since alot of them aren't even fun anymore and i usually have to force myself to play them. But THIS game is an absolute must play, i absolutely loved every second of it. Some people may be scared off because of the change from linear gameplay to a more open-world type gameplay unlike it's predecessors. But i think they executed this change of pace perfectly.The gameplay is basically the same as the previous games, they added a cool crafting system (that somehow magically turns some random chemicals and metal into gas mask filters and ammo). Your guns can get jammed if you don't clean them often and you have to manually unjam them, sand, snow, and even falling in water affects how fast your gun gets dirty. Your gas mask can get damaged too, and if it cracks you can repair it with duck tape (it's only temporary though), and unlike the previous games you can't pick up a new mask, you will have to repair this one at a workbench.The morality system makes a comeback, but there's not alot of moral points to be earned in each chapter, most of it is straight forward unlike the previous games (also as a tip, listening to dialogues won't give you morality points, but it can give you sidequests and cool marks on the map).The locations are really cool, there's a chapter for each season of the year, and you get to experience quite some interesting landscapes, ranging from snowy landscapes to desert places. I'd say the first chapter (The Volga) is probably the Highlight of the game, but that does NOT mean the other chapters are boring.I haven't encountered any major bugs, most of the bugs i've encountered were physic bugs, and those were extremely rare, there are some game breaking softlock bugs supposedly, so make sure to back up your saves as you progress (i made a special folder where i kept all my saves from the beginning of the game to the end)The best aspect of the game for me is probably how immersive it is, i haven't been immersed in a game like this in a really long time, in my opinion, i'd say it even takes the spotlight away from the first game.And it's not only the "horror" elements of immersion, it's the family and friends aspect as well, drinking and playing the guitar with your friends on the train was one of the most real scenes i've ever seen in a video game, and i am so glad that a video game could capture that beautiful feeling.Okay i'm getting quite stupidly philosophical there, to wrap it up, this game is AMAZING. It absolutely blew my mind, i thought it would kinda disappoint me after the first two amazing games, but it's quite the contrary. I think this is my favourite metro game, and i absolutely recommend it even at full price.P.S. I highly recommend playing this game on the Ranger Hardcore difficulty as with all the metro games, not only does it help you immerse better, but i think it's the best way to experience this masterpiece of a game.R.I.P. Андрей Корзинкин

_childDocuments_.review: The final journey in the Metro series comes to an all-powerful conclusion in Metro Exodus.Artyom is a grownup man now, no longer the young boy who lived all his life under the surface, on the tunnels of the Russian metro. No longer a newly accepted soldier of the Spartan order either. He's experienced now, respected by his peers, loved by his wife and also saved the world (at least, what's left of it). And yet, he’s still restless. He continues to venture outside of the metro looking for some signal, some possibility of going away from Moscow. Until one day, he finds something.This sets the stage for a year-long travel adventure, across Russia to the east. The journey is real, you start on Moscow on the classic Metro nuclear winter (snow and radiation everywhere outside, and under the surface enemies hiding in the darkness) and soon you'll find yourself hijacking a real train (steam locomotive kind) in a very movie like action scene. This presented the first kind of level that you will encounter in Metro Exodus:  The Classic Levels. These levels have a very strong narrative and focused path, which of course are the type of levels that you encountered in the old Metros. These paths are narrow because their intention is to tell a story unfolding before you (while you are in fact playing the game mind you, not just watching a cutscene) without losing rhythm and also because they can be very action heavy at some parts.These levels are not here because of nostalgia, or pleasing the metro fans only, they are here because they are needed to tell a certain part of the story in the game.Now, after escaping Moscow you start travelling, and here comes the second type of levels: transitional levels. These levels see you on the train on your journey, to the east, across seasons. You just start with the steam locomotive, but soon you will be incorporating new places to your train, new cars and spaces for the people you'll meet along your journey, some of these people will continue the journey with you. You will talk with them, listen to their stories, also what they say to you will reflect recent events in the story. And most of it, it's optional. You can also listen to the radio, looking for voices in the wasteland, or even a music station (there's a good amount of tunes to listen to) You will also write your personal diary, with a very neat database of every character you meet, every creature you find, as well as the places you travel to, even with some nice drawings. It's like having your own art book in the game. The amazing thing about all of this, is that you can spend in each one of these levels as much as two hours full of content. The attention to detail when building the game world was truly a work of passion here.But after that level, comes Volga, and this is new to Metro, the third type of stage, the semi-open world. This level plays very different from the classic ones. And yet it makes sense.It has its own story and the way it unfolds, makes a perfect playground for a non linear approach. You begin at the starting point, along with the main story objectives but you can go exploring on different directions. And this is really the main thing about it, exploration. Almost every way you go there will be something for you to find. Aside from the usual few collectibles you will find a few side missions, you will get also equipment and weapon upgrades. Some of these will change significantly how you play the game. But all of this doesn't take anything away from the main game experience. You can just do the main mission if you want. The metro experience is still there, even in open spaces, but there's just more variety. Different types of experiences. This is not just a new type of level to be fashionable with the times. This type of level is needed to tell the story on those specific moments. Because on a level like this, I wanted to explore, I wanted to take the time to go a little further, to be outside of my usual tunnel vision. The kind of narrative that you get from this level is completely different from the other ones. In this Metro you are travelling on the surface, through the wasteland. You have to see what's left of the world, and to do that, you have to feel the desolation and vastness of space and that takes time and a lot of exploring.This goes perfectly well with the classic levels, even the transitional ones. There's nothing out of place here. Everything goes together for a reason. The very last level of this game goes back to the roots of Metro and has quite possibly one of the most emotional moments in gaming this year and absolutely the most emotional moment in all of the Metro saga. In this game I found myself caring deeply for each and every one of the characters more so than in any other recent game. Playing Metro Exodus was a complete experience. It goes through all emotions the same way as it goes through all seasons across the continent. It’s charged with action, drama and love.  It holds nothing back and risks everything. It has a diverse set of characters and environments you’ll meet, many world stories to learn… but after all is said and done, the journey for Artyom, will finally reach the end.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a bad game but it's really average. It could have been so much better.I preferred the 2 previous ones that were more focused. In Metro Exodus, you can feel they tried to do too much and the result is mixed.The graphics are great with some nice lighting effects and it runs smoothly (at least some levels... more on that later). The game takes a long time to kick in, with some endless cut scenes (go grab a coffee because you can't even skip them). Once you reach Volga, it's quite good. There's some large areas to explore and it feels like you can have some real fun (and you do in some parts) but after visiting a few optional side areas you start to notice that all they offer is more ammo that you wouldn't have lost if you didn't visit the area in the first place.That kind of "open" world reminds me of... Half-Life 2 back in 2004!The guns *seem* great but they're confusing. You only have 3 slots and when you kill someone, you never know if his gun is worth it because all the info available is just a 2D drawing of the gun. So you just press 'R' to collect its ammo/add-ons and move on.The next part plays like a fast FPS. Quite a change of pace, but the corridors are too small which is annoying.The next stage, the Caspian sea is like they tried to do a Rage. What is a desert doing in a Metro game? It looks completely out of place. Also it suffers from a lot of performance problems. You also can drive a bus which likes to get stuck for some reasons.The next area is even worse. It also has performance problems and, while it looks open world, it's not. Just allows you to select a slightly different path at best.Then back again in a metro. At least the performance is back and the area is better. Except the end where you literally have to sprint past enemies otherwise they just make you waste your ammo or die.The story is lame and the characters are way too talkative and say unimportant things. In the end you just ignore them.I don't know. It seems like they ran out of money mid way during development by wasting it all on endless cut scenes, put it all together and hoped for the best.Don't pick it up at full price. Wait for a 40-60% sale and then you should have maybe 5 hours of fun out of the 19 necessary to complete it.

Sure, it doesn't break much new ground (although its weapon-customisation system will surely be copied), and there are those who will argue that, format-wise, it's a throwback.But if you like your shooters to tell the sort of story you would enjoy in a movie, and to ooze distinctive personality, you should find it very satisfying. _childDocuments_.review: Before I address my dislike, this game is  in terms of graphics, gun play and post-apocalyptic feels. Metro Exodus is not exactly open world like the Fallout franchise, but an area is usually large enough to  like it is. The gun play is highly detailed. A weapon can be modded very differently to your liking - CQC, long-range or stealth. The added difficulty of weapon jamming and cleaning (similar to Far Cry 2) is a nice touch, makes the game feel a lot more realistic. I  take the dialogue. They are cringey, unsynced and unnatural. Dialogues in the Fallout franchise actually flows nicely - no weird gestures, no odd or unnecessary redundant words and no pauses between each character's line. I like the idea of post-apocalypse and ME's story in general, but they really could put more work into dialogues since immersion is of high requirement in this kind of games.The control is a little janky. Running down a slope or stairs may fling you outwards unrealistically and cause fall damage, or climbing a ledge may sometimes be very difficult despite a perfectly acceptable height. Good post-apocalypse game with nice gun play and high realism. But otherwise lacks immersion and/or details contributing to immersion. Since immersion is highly sought after, I cannot recommend this game as it breaks every time a character line is spoken.

_childDocuments_.review: Metro exodus by 4A games  is the last in the 3 games based off Dmitry Glukhovsky’s best-selling metro series. The series is set in the Moscow metro tunnels in the aftermath of a devastating world war with the participants never directly mentioned. As befitting a game that is based on a world created by a best-selling author it is fully realised and very evocative. It's a living, breathing world with many different factions of humanity, and monsters and mutants that have evolved and adapted to their environment.In earlier games the game mostly take place in the dark and claustrophobic Metro tunnels with some outside activity whereas in this game it’s the opposite; the action mainly takes place above ground in one of its themed by season areas, with some underground/metro areas. It also differs in that the three main outside areas have somewhat of an open world feeling, there are upgrades to be found, secrets, and areas can be marked on the map. You are still playing Artyom, a Ranger hardened by metro life.The metro levels and the mini-areas have more of a traditional metro feeling, with a much more linear feel.Metro exodus is a first-person shooter with survival/horror aspects. Ammunition, Medi kits and filters for your gas mask are limited and need to be scavenged and/or crafted with one of the 2 findable crafting materials. On normal difficulty I never found crafting supplies to be that much of a worry, and I could be fairly well stocked on ammunition, filters and medikits with enough supplies to refill myself up if needed. I imagine it’s a different story on harder difficulties but on normal difficulty its less of a survival horror than a shooter with item management. You can’t go too crazy but it’s definitely a thing to make note of if you care one way or the other about the survival aspect. I quite liked experiencing the world and not worrying too much about every bullet, or ball bearing but if you want to struggle for resources try hard.It has a definite horror aspect. Without going too deep into philosophy of the horrors of war and how some elements of humanity are worse than the mutants and monsters there is literal horror. There are enemies both human and mutant alike who are depraved and murderous. There are many monsters who lurk and stalk you including a type who is blind but not deaf creating for some interesting moments where sneaking about is encouraged.There are a lot of dark, poorly lit areas and jump scares in the game. A lot of monsters who appear suddenly and imperil Artyom. There’s a awfully high amount of skulls, skeletons and strange monsters and horrifying scenes. I didn’t find it too bad but its something to note, for good or bad depending on your preference.As I mentioned in the introduction a lot of Exodus takes place outside and its an opportunity to show off the beautiful and diverse post-apocalyptic world of Dmitry Glukhovsky. The three main outdoor areas each have a very different feel and theme loosely based around on the seasons with a very icey watery first ‘level’ giving way into a summer desert, dried up one. It’s a very pretty world and Exodus really allows the developer to show that. The underground levels are dark and involving too, but the outdoor lands really allow 4Agames to show off.The mutants and monsters are all interesting and there are a few unique ones. The world tells a story even when none one is speaking with the ruined vehicles, structures and lands painting a picture of the catastrophe that befell it. The only weakness is that the characters voice acting in English is pretty bad, a tip if appropriate is to set it to Russian dialogue with English subtitles. The voice acting is a little immersion breaking in English with the comedy Russian accents of some of the characters. Think Chekov's Nuclear Wessels from Star Trek Couple of quick thought on the beginning and ending because they can often be make or break, at least for me. With a lot of games out there now a bad beginning can have me shelve a game and play others, and a bad ending can spoil a good game. I did not like the beginning its pretty much a glorified tutorial, in a very dark level with lots of use crouch here, use stealth here bits. It’s a bit out of place in a game like Metro in my opinion and if it wasn’t for me wanting to finish it off before the holidays then I may have left it, so uninspiring (and a little frustrating was the start). But stick with it!I really liked the ending, whilst the game itself is good the (good) ending is a fitting farewell to the series. I’m not going to spoil it but suffice to say it finishes off the game well, has important characters each with their own brief bit and offers hope and promise. There’s a bad ending too which I’m not going to spoil but may be less fulfilling. Hint be nice in the game!This is a game I have no difficulty in recommending. It’s not perfect and I felt like I persevered through the start, but there are some very interesting landscapes, diverse groups of survivors and the search for home plot is a welcome change for the Metro series. Get it, especially on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Metro Exodus (ME) is a first-person shooter game with survival horror and stealth elements. It has been developed by the company 4A Games and published by the company Deep Silver.++ Journey across the post-apocalyptic Russia on a train with your heavily armed friends. Revisit the claustrophobic tunnels of Moscow, shake hands with cultists on Volga's frozen tundra, liberate slaves in the desert of the Caspian, play hide and seek with the tribes in Taiga's lush forests, and sneak around blind gorillas within the irradiated ruins of a dead city.+ I like most of the characters because they are well written, and the game gives you enough opportunities to support them. My favourites are Stepan and little Nastya; I could not refuse her plea for the heroic rescue of a teddy bear.   + Solid addons. Both of them illuminate the events around side characters that you will encounter during the main storyline. - The depiction of Colonel Miller, a hardened veteran and military leader, as a naive and irrational commander lacks credibility. And believe me, thoughts of mutiny crossed my mind several times.- Occasional FPS drops, irregular crashes, and corrupted save games. I have experienced all of it, and it boils down to... *switches to a Russian accent* completely normal phenomenons.-- Taking the game out of the Steam store, two weeks before its release, is referred to as a d*ck move in the gamer scene.I consider ME to be a great continuation of the series, and the strongest part of the franchise. It has surprised me with its open world aspects and gripping storyline. Alas, the overall impression is tarnished by technical issues, and the rushed cooperation with the EPIC Games Store for temporary exclusivity. You can do better 4A Games and Deep Silver.Recommended for fans of the post-apocalypse and gas mask fetishists. Estimated time for 100% completion: +50 hoursSingleplayer achievements: 68Multiplayer achievements: none

_childDocuments_.review: Metro Exodus is A fantastic game, Despite me reading some reviews that say its glitchy and doesn't run well; after completing the game on hardcore I can tell you that it is a masterpiece. To sum up some of the things I loved about this game I would have to say that the world design is great along with the sounds in it, from the guns to the creatures the sound has to be one of my favorite things in the game because it makes guns loud, Like how they are suppose to be which some games fall short on.To address the glitches in the game, which every game has, the glitches I had mainly game from alt tabbing which is a pain to deal with when I want to check discord or something but I'm usually so engaged in the game I don't even check other apps. Other than alt tabbing I only had a few visual bugs which are hard to notice unless you really try to spot them.In most games I play that have story I don't normally pay attention to it and rather speed run through the game; But with the game play fully revolving around the story unlike some open world survival games (far cry). to not spoil, it was a very captivating story with a emotional ending. I noticed that some people in other reviews complained about the resource management and stealth system, While the stealth could get annoying at times I really didn't mind it and actually had fun trying to do that one challenging stealth move without being caught although I could see how its not for all people. The ammo/resource management for me was easy, that's mainly because I took my time searching every nook and cranny (which I do enjoy doing), but at times it especially near the beginning when I needed 10 more chemicals to fix up my weapons it did feel tedious, but that feeling goes away later on in the game. Ammo management is easy, just hit your shots and avoid targets that can be avoided.This Game is made for those who like Medium-High amounts of resource management, Fantastic Gun-play, Open world stories, good Character/story/sound/and world design. Overall I would rate this game a 9/10 Because some of the stealth was unpleasant and because I couldn't alt tab without the game crashing.

_childDocuments_.review: Metro is one of my favourite franchises, so I was really excited when this game got announced. I had a good time playing this, and I do recommend it. Still, it was not exactly what I was hoping for. Compared to the last games, that actually took place in the metro, this game mostly takes place on the surface. They do advertise it as that, so it wasn't surprising. Trying something new doesn't have to be a bad thing.While the surface experience is still cool I personally prefer Metro to take place mainly in the metro. The other Metro games give an unique experience down in the metro (And a little bit outside of it), which they do so well that no other game compares. But this game taking place mainly on the surface, it doesn't do as many things that makes it stand out from other games. It just feels like another post-apocalyptic shooter when you're shooting at these raider-like bandits and humanoid ghouls. It advertises the open surface areas as non-linear sandbox levels, but they are actually quite limited at times, with a clear line to where you need to go. You get a few different paths to the place you need to get to and the freedom to reach it, but calling it "non-linear sandbox" is a bit of a stretch. There's two levels that actually feel open and invite some exploration, but one limits you with a lot of water, and the other is just pretty empty. Trying to complete parts stealthily can also be extremely frustrating because that system does not always seem to work fairly.The game still did a lot of things really well, which is why I do recommend it.Atmosphere is still top notch, and the main reason I love these games so much. The sound, the lighting, the world, they're all really good and immersive and really draw you into the game.Metro's graphics have always been really great, and that did not change in this game. The gunplay still feels good, and weapon modding is bigger and better than ever. Like the other games the story is well done, and there is plenty of lore to be found in your diary, collectibles and by listening to conversations.Having the Aurora (train) and its crew to come back to after the lonely and sometimes claustrophobic missions is really cool. There's a lot of dialogue with your crew, and they're all fun characters. There's some things you can interact with that add to the immersion, without actually doing anything for the gameplay (Shoveling coal, taking a sip from your canteen, smoking, checking different frequencies on the radio, etc.). Like the other Metro games, this game features a similar morality system and multiple endings. I personally like both of the endings, and enjoy the ending in general. The final mission was probably my favourite one.Also the game gives you a wife for the lonely under us.There's also a well received DLC that actually takes you back to the metro, and another DLC releasing in the upcoming months.

_childDocuments_.review: I am thoroughly unimpressed by this game. I wouldn't say it's "bad" but there's so many stupid little quirks and crappy design decisions stacked on top of each other that make it feel like a chore to play.1. Fake jumping puzzles. Parts of the map that clearly look like jumping puzzles, so much that a 5 year old from Mars who never played video games, would recognize them as such. Spend 15-20 minutes trying to make it, finally do and there's nothing there.2. There's a few sub groups of AI behaviors in gaming that are common and really kill the immersion. This game has a bad case of "Blowing somebodies head off right next to their friend who doesn't notice, then casually walks away."3. Dirty weapons/crafting is not thought out at all. Basically in the beginning of the game your choices will be: Make medikits, which you will burn through real quick since some enemies can just phase through doors and walls or hit you from out of nowhere with no indication. Keep your guns clean to avoid jamming and play flawlessly so you don't get hit at all. Make ammo, run out of medkits, filters, crafting mats.4. Water is dumb. Fall in an it's basically 50/50 live or die. You can't control your movement so if you manage to not get killed immediately, it will just throw you back out of the water wherever it decides it wants to, regardless of distance. Meaning I was like 10 feet away from a platform in the middle of the water, fell in and it put me back on the shore at the beginning of the jumping puzzle despite the fact that it was much more than 10 feet away.I'll leave it at that because I got ♥♥♥♥ to do, but I could keep going. Not a terrible game, but nothing special either.

_childDocuments_.review: What it's not:Fallout. Here's what it is:A very visual and cinematic game that follows a man and his struggle for a better, less dystopian way of living. Tired of being in underground Moscow, after Soviet Russia faced nuclear destruction, our main character, Artyom, sets out in search for an oasis among the radiated, post apocalypse Russia. With a very good story and many options to approach different scenarios, I highly recommend this game for those who enjoy a good post-apocalypse RPG.  While the game is some-what linear, it plays very much like a movie and breaks from the cinema enough for you to feel as though you have the freedom to roam and create your own story.

_childDocuments_.review: As ever with the Metro series this is a very story driven game, but this time with wide open spaces. It has a rather different feel to it considering the different map style and the fact that most of it happens overground, but the core elements are the same: cool bodge guns, moral choices, rich backstory, mutants, thick Russian accents and a secret "good" ending which you have to be REALLY morally good (and a little completionist) in order to obtain.I would have liked the game to be longer (I would say its about 30h per play through of the main story atm) but mainly because I didn't want it to end, and considering the already massive game size (77GB with the expansions) I suppose I'm just being greedy.If I had one REAL criticism, it would have to be that there are a lot of what is essentially cut scenes, but they are scripted in-game interactions meaning they can't be skipped, so I spent some time playing on my phone waiting for the touching guitar jam session between buddies to be over so I can play again, or that painful 2 minute scripted fight scene with a mutant where I just have to mash "E" and died 3 times because I apparently wasn't doing it enthusiastically enough.All told this is a great game, I got halfway through then started again from the beginning because I decided to do a "good ending" playthrough, and I just finished the game, and Im already considering doing it again on Ranger Hardcore and New Game+ (which gives all kinds of options to make it harder) so it doesnt get old.Though its a bit of a departure from the other 2, its a great 3rd game I would highly recommend to lovers of RPG driven FPS games and fans of the Metro.
_childDocuments_.name: Metro Exodus

_childDocuments_.review: I love the Metro games, and I can say that in my opinion, every Metro game improved upon the previous one, which is very rare for a game series. The mix of smaller open world maps and very linear maps is perfect. I am fed up by giant open worlds with a million of questionmark icons that you have to collect. The atmosphere of every single Metro game is what makes these games to outstanding.Only remark: For players that want to go achievement hunting, unskippable cutscenes and dialogues can be frustrating.I am looking forward to the next Metro game! (Please release the game on multiple platforms, not as an exclusive to a specific store)

_childDocuments_.review: I think this is a great game if one is ok with powering through entire regions that are bad.It's a great atmosphere worth experiencing, but from chapter one onward the game just gets worse and worse. I think the lowest of low was by far the Taiga region (forest) as well as the Caspian region (desert). More to the end of the game Metro redeems itself again and gets considerably better with a great ending. So in summary it starts great get's worse, stays bad for quite a long time and then gets better again. My favorite area besides the starting region and a more later region, was actually inside of the Caspian area. Without spoilering, there's a certain bunker in this region (story related) that together with some other areas, could actually make this game count as a horror game.It's also worth mentioning,  that this game does a great job of incorporating everything into the world, from opening maps, crafting medkits/ ammo to seeing if your gas mask is damaged or needs a refill.

_childDocuments_.review: 6.5/10well, not sure what to say about this. I have tried 2x now to get into this game and it's just not doing it for me. Then when they released the enhanced edition ( and seeing as I had just bought a 3080 ti) I thought what the hell I will give it another go.3rd time is the charm, I'm actually enjoying the game this go around, and not because of the enhanced edition, but because I knew what to expect. _childDocuments_.name: Metro Exodus

_childDocuments_.review: Story.Everything you would ever expect from a Metro game, Loads of dwindling Russian pride among the surviving civilians of an ever fading civilization, still fighting each other to extinction. Storywise the game may seem predictable at times with its deus ex machinas saving you at the very last second when you seem like you're about to die. Though there's plenty of overall events one may not expect and want to unravel more as they go further down the linear railway story that is metro hoping to see how it will all end. It is filled with many characters you may or may not forget along the way, always ready to help you out and spill the tragic stories of their life to you. Tragedy builds character for most of these characters and suprisingly it works well, you can see the kind of people they turned out after loads of disasters they encountered in their lifes. The games message about the greater good still feels a bit black and white but you may enjoy it if you don't care for that as much as adbout the action and the overall mood of the game.Gameplay.Combat in itself is pretty advanced for a shooter yet can feel slow at times. Lots of customization and lack of ammo will make you care for your guns and the dangers ahead. Sneaking still feels like it could use more work but it was never the main focus of the series anyways. There are some quick time events scattered here and there but metro luckily doesn't abuse these as much as previous games of early 2010s. Overall Gameplay is fun and a bit strategic, if you're into that i highly recommend you shooting through this semi open world wasteland of Russia for heaps amount of fun.Visuals.Certainly a lot more detail than in the previous titles, you can feel that most of the development was put into the atmosphere of the game and its bigger than ever. It perfectly pulls you into this world especially when you're out in the wasteland by yourself. Now i'm not saying NPCs are poorly made but they do seem to have Animation issues such as their unexpresive movements, especially on the side characters you'd see pushed further away from the main story. They close and open their mouths like fish as a recorded audio comes out. You can see this right on the first room where a child is talking to his mother. Of course you can still get quite immersed in the characters as i find what they're saying is a bit more important than how they're saying it. As for other Visual problems i must inform you that 2k is its highest resolution and there is no borderless mode.Bugs.The Game has a few barely noticable bugs here and there such as hearing a clanking of metal tank if you step on a kitchen tile near the corner of a table. Nothing ground breaking reallyMusic.Like i said the atmosphere of this game will suck most of the people in and music does that job no worse than the visuals. It goes from gloomy, sneaky and action packed just at the right times and excels in all of them.Overall.I highly advice you to buy this game and finish it at least once. Especially if you're a fan of singleplayer shooter games such as Bioshock or Stalker

_childDocuments_.review: Read the book and played on hardcore. WHAT I LIKED: 1. Great game visually, one of the best for sure. 2. It can look really nice even on a mid-tier laptop gaming machine. 3. Main story was great. 4. Monster design was great.  WHAT I DIDN'T LIKE/WHAT KILLED IT FOR ME: 1. Its one of those shooters where when you're in combat the enemies have extremely annoying animations. During every moment of combat you're forced to shoot-then-wait until they're finished their flinching animation from your last round that made contact. And don't bother shooting at them while they're climbing a ladder or ducking into cover, nope they're in an animation and your bullets can't touch them. That REALLY kills a gaming experience for me. 2. Secondly was the conversations; What should take one minute to spit out takes three because there's a two and a half second pause at the end of every sentence. It's like nails on a chalk board. THATS really annoying for me because I'm generally the type to choose a more detailed game by opting for the 'hear-more' option in story conversations.  3. During those lengthy conversations was the lack of care the devs put into the atmosphere of audio. All of the talking was spoken into a mic and pasted straight into the game. If we're talking in a small quiet room with nothing but a small crackling fire, it should sound like that. If we're talking in a train carriage, it should sound like talking in a train carriage. If we're talking in a room with hard walls and nothing in it, it should sound and project/reverb like that.  In summary, it was great to look and the art was exceptional but the rest was painstaking and very poorly executed. Out of every hour you play, half of it will be spent waiting (jokingly).
_childDocuments_.name: Metro Exodus

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately the very good setting of Metro:Exodus was ruined for me, due to a couple of factors.1. To get the "good" ending, the game requires you to use stealth in a way that is often bugged and works horribly in combination with...2. The ranger difficulty seems like the obvious choice for a "realistic" setting. I didn't mind that you can get two-shotted from any distance. Heck, if someone hits you in the head, it is over - fair is fair. But something that is really annoying is the fact that you cannot save on your own. And the game often only saves when you pass certain passages (no walking from a different direction allowed) or hit certain story checkpoints. This leads to the frustrating experience of losing 30 mins of progress, because the game didn't autosave. This is especially annoying in combination with...3. The stealth mechanics. Granted, I only know about the stealth mechanics on "Ranger", but they are so very poorly implemented, it is an audacity. As I have mentioned before, you need to stealth a lot in order to get the good ending. However, not only do all enemies get eagle eyes on Ranger difficulty, it is also downright insulting how one is supposed to sneak in some passages. The icing on the cake is then to get spotted in the last moment just to be sent back 15 minutes ago.4. The non-lethal takedown option is bugged at times, which leads you to standing behind an enemy without being able to do something. Also, melee-attacking someone with a gun kills people, needlessly complicating getting the good ending.5. Although the setting is very interesting, the dialog fails to deliver. Lines often sound cheesy or out of place. Emotions are either not present or overly dramatic and not fitting at all. At times, I was just waiting for a soundclip like in Oblivion ("lets do another take").To be fair, I did not encounter too many bugs (if you don't count the lasersight of the enemies) so there's that.All in all, I think this game could have been a lot better. Game developers, please stop forcing stealth in games which are definitely not designed for stealth. And no, a little light that indicates how visible I am is not an indicator for a stealth game.EDIT: Now that I have finished the game I am even more furious. The story is really good, but the execution of the steps to get to the good ending is just bothersome. In conclusion: good setting, good storyline, good soundtrack and graphics but poor gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright where do I start?Let's begin with the graphics: In dark areas, Metro Exodus is not too impressive, but in well lit spaces, the game shines with amazing textures, effects, lighting, it looks absolutely incredible.Sound design is also great, especially since it is an important tool to figure out whether enemies are nearby.The story of the game continues after the second part of the series, but most of the characters in your team are new additions. If you are one of those people who enjoy a game which adds a lot of story and simple ambience, you're gonna love this one. There's a lot of that here. As it is tradition with the Metro series, you can constantly choose between "good" and "bad" options, which this time actually have a more significant impact on how the story progresses before the ending.For the gameplay, let's compare it with the previous parts of the series. Instead of rather linear areas, you now operate mostly inside of a half open world. There is now a day / night cycle, which has a significant impact on the environment and on your options to approach a situation. You can still upgrade and change your equipment, but this time it is less centered on gearing up between missions. Instead, the whole equipment system has been turned upside down compared to Metro 1 and 2: There is no more military ammo and no more shop owners, but instead you now constantly scavenge two main components for crafting and utilize them at a workbench or in the field. This allows for regular weapon / equipment maintenance (yes, there is weapon decay now) and changes, and you can also craft new ammo and other equipment with it. To unlock new weapons and equipment, you take them from enemies or find them hidden within the world, instead of buying them from vendors. As with the other parts of the series, you always have the option to choose a more aggressive or stealthy approach, with stealth mostly being the better option. The gas mask, which was almost a permanent companion before, has now become less important and is only used in a few "critical areas". Stealth works the same as before, but can be a bit weird at rare times (such as not being able to knock out an enemy because he's standing 10 centimeters above you). If you enjoyed the feeling of dread and general darkness of the first two games, you will find a significant change from that here. However, the game definitely deserves all the praise it has received and I strongly recommend it to everyone who enjoys (half) open world shooters with some equipment management.
