_childDocuments_.review: - Miller doing probably the best roundup of Artyom's misadventuresAfter many years of waiting I finally came around to play , the third part of the  trilogy. Prior to this, I already read all of the novels and spin-offs released in the west, played all the games plus the pre-4A stuff like the  franchise. So it's no wonder I was very excited when a few years ago 4A announced a sequel to the events of , vaguely based on parts of the  novel.Before the release I made sure to look up no footage, content or whatsoever about . What made me kinda skeptical though during the period of its development was the hype this game stirred up in the mainstream media. Let's be frank, the original  started as an genre underdog to a first quite unknown, though highly acclaimed Sci-Fi novel from Russia. Today, now almost 10 years later,  grew to a AAA franchise that doesn't need to hide itself from the big players of the industry.But eventually I'm happy that my worries turned out quite unfounded - in the end 4A Games delivered a solid singleplayer experience that stands true to its roots and predecessors. The doubts of other players who expected a lazy open-world clone of  or a Bethesda   also didn't come true. Metro Exodus is still a linear, classic-to-the-core FPS experience in the likes of  but with several small quirks and well-implemented ideas from open-world games.The story is quickly explained: After the events of , Artyom desperately searches for signs and ways to escape his miserable existence in post-apocalyptical Moscow of the year 2035. Together with his wife Anna he soon reveals a major conspiracy that changes his whole perspective about his life in the Moscovite Metro. Thereafter he embarks on an adventure that takes him thousands of kilometers across the Russian landmass...Of course the game puts you again in the shoes of our hero Artyom. As in the predessecors the game lets you use several pieces of firearms like the iconic Bastard submachinegun, the trusty AK or, the all-time fan favorite, the pneumatic Tikhar rifle. Unfortunately, I was dissapointed to see that some weapons from the first two games didn't make it to third game, like the Saiga-12 or the Abzats. Looking at it objectively, it can even be assessed that  has the lowest number of featured weapons in the whole trilogy.But interestingly the game makes that up by introducing the new backpack feature to the franchise. At any part of the game you can open up your backpack and modify your guns with scavenged parts. Weapons now also can get dirty which causes them to jam in critical situations. On workbenches, which are scattered on some parts of the levels, you can maintain your weapons and craft new ammunition and equipment.But still, don't expect a mindblowing plethora of micromanagement and gun-geekiness - the whole inventory and upgrade mechanics are pretty simple, straightforward and a far cry from  or similar games.Where  ultimately shines is in its level design and atmosphere. The outdoor maps are beautifully crafted and brim over with details, life, hazards and wonders. 4A Games made a great decision to move away from the dark tunnels of the Moscovite Metro to the green of the Russian taiga or the dust of the Caspian Sea, all while still keeping true to the post-apocalyptic vibe and stereotypes. Some sections of the game will also remind you of 's driving sections, with many places to stop by and to explore. And for all of you who missed the creepy and dark tunnels from the first two games, rest assured: The designers made sure to build in classic tunnel sections into each of the big maps as well, so  old-timers should feel at home just as well as newcomers.Combat is pretty much the same as in the first two games - you can either go in guns blazing or you can take the stealth route and knock out enemies from the shadows. As in the predecessors,  borrows the iconic light meter from the  series that helps you hiding in the dark. But then again, I thought that not all stealth sections of  were that well designed. Often you get detected without even knowing who could have possibly seen you and other times you laugh at the stupidity and blindness of the AI enemies. For me, this was a bit a hit-or-miss.Shooting common mutants and monstrosities is also quite straightforward and true to the franchise - nothing much to complain if you already liked  and .The story and character development on the other hand is really well written, and I go as far to say that it is the best of the whole trilogy. You will certainly empathize to Artyom's friends and their stories, and once more it's possible to achieve either a good and bad ending. This of course makes a second playthrough all the more tempting, all along with the legendary Ranger Hardcore difficulty, which also makes a comeback in .The only drop of bitterness was the terrible and sudden decision of Deep Silver to release the game exclusively on the Epic Store and therefore ♥♥♥♥ over all players who wanted to buy the game on Steam on the day of release. Their excuse to release the game a whole year later on Steam doesn't justify anything, nor does it help to cultivate fair competition among PC gaming launchers and platforms. Personally I don't think it's correct either to review bomb this actually excellent game, but what Deep Silver and Tencent did was way beyond dirty and is putting a lot bad light on 4A Games and their bright minds. As long as this trend takes place, I would recommend to boycott platforms or launchers that do ♥♥♥♥ like that until they learn to respect an equal and fair market. I know Steam / Valve is not an angel as well, but that was just terrible.Apart from that I experienced a polished, intense sequel to one of my favorite FPS franchises ever made. Personally, I still rate the original  a bit higher for a lot of nostalgic reasons, but  surely delivered what it promised. pump-ups on the Tikhar rifle

_childDocuments_.review: Metro Exodus is the third installment in the Metro series and it is the first one to have an open world setting.  This open world setting does have its negative experience such as:- You are encouraged to explore the many place of interests BUT do take note that most of the time, the amount of effort taken to kill the enemies surpassed the reward that you will potentially get. In other words, if you don't mind this and just loves to explore/immerse into it then that is fine.- Some of the chapters may feel like a slog (it'll get worse if you plan to explore as many place of interest as possible)There are also some mechanics in the game that can be annoying for example:- The car feature in the desert is good but can be a pain to use it, it is quite clunky to be honest - Too many animation when changing, reloading, pumping weapons, getting into/out the car etc etc. Animation does helps with the immersion but in some of the chapters these behaviors is downright frustrating as the enemies just keep popping out of nowhere to deliver surprise cheap shotThere are some things that are done right but I've got to say that overall the general feeling for the entire play through is quite a slog and there are still a number of not so satisfying things that could be listed down. Some sections are nice and reminds us of the previous two Metro settings that we love for example the linear subway environment. Perhaps Artyom and company should have just stay underground.Metro Exodus is definitely the weaker one among the three but still, I'll recommend this game though because it still can be enjoyable but stick to the following tips and you'll be fine:- Focus on main objective- Do not go out of your way to explore the places - Some map or areas can be very confusing, in this case just slog through I guess

_childDocuments_.review: Metro Exodus is overall a positive experience, but not without flaws.The biggest selling points are still here, the lore, the narrative, the characters and the story. It all clicks and it's the core foundation of Metro for me, as it's what keeps the game in shape despite its flaws.I didn't enjoy a lot of new aspects which differ Exodus from previous games. The "open world" looks more like the one we got from Mafia 1 - sure, you can divert a little from the path and explore, but that's it, the linear progress is still here and will close behind you almost all the exits, you can't just "go back" and collect missing stuff or finish open cases. Speaking of those, there are no side quests of any kind, the "best" you can have are a few small activities which all look the same - go kill/knock out everybody around and retrieve an item or pull a lever, that's it.The open world on the other hand is completely empty, the only thing that exists are enemy encounters, you can't get rid of them even on the easiest difficulties where they just spawn and you have to kill or sneak past them, there is very little opportunity to explore, it feels more like a chore of the main quest that makes you visit almost all of the point of interests that are interesting, because everything else is not. I think I found literally ONE location at caspian sea which looked interesting yet the main quest didn't make me go there, and I explored whole map on each level.Personally I enjoyed the linear story of the first metros more, the "affair" with the open world didn't end well in my eyes, yes, the game is indeed located mostly in open areas as opposed to claustrophobic metro tunnels, but that's pretty much everything the game has to offer - the locations are indeed designed well and unique as the places you find yourself in, but the moment you start exploring you notice that it's all empty world that tells no story at all, even Fallout 4 did better job here by having a lot of locations that were simply interesting to explore without any quest forcing you to go inside.I'm still leaving Exodus a positive note, because it's still the Metro universe I love and it'd be unfair to put equality sign between badly designed "open world" or underwhelming crafting mechanics and the excellent narrative, story and the lore. It's still a very good game to play, but personally I enjoyed the claustrophobic prequels far more, where you could feel the struggle of living and explored locations were polished to perfection, as opposed to the "open world" we got that feels rushed and boring.If you've enjoyed previous Metro games and you're into the lore, you certainly won't be disappointed. As a starting point, I discourage, you'll get thrown into the middle of action with characters you don't know, and the mechanics won't keep you for much longer alone.---If you liked my review, you can find more of them on  and on my .

_childDocuments_.review: > METRO EXODUS <One of the best narrative story driven shooters I've ever played. The story really makes you feel a part of Artyom's family. Over the course of the series you bond with Artyom's mates in a way that feels closer than family. You care about everyone's well being and you want to play through the story to make sure everyone remains safe. Not only that, but the development of each and every individual character is wonderful. There's a lot of depth to them and you hear it in random conversations when you stumble upon them or smoke with them on the train ride. Hearing every word that everyone has to say any time really does mean a lot. The Soundtrack. I can not justify verbally how incredible the soundtrack is for this game. The emotion, the feeling, the atmosphere, the intensity is something that sounds like it was composed by a supernatural deity who knew music better than any human composer. The soundtrack perfectly harmonizes with the atmosphere of the game and setting that you find yourself in. The story is incredibly immersive as you encounter real problems you would expect to see in a post nuclear wasteland for example radiation, drought, and lack of supplies. The PC version of Metro Exodus is a genuine game-changer for graphics technology - a vision of the way in which developers can take real-time rendering to the next level. > THE TWO COLONELS <So heart touching… A Masterpiece !!! cried so many times at the end..... two stories, two different times, through metro they bend together and it will twist your emotion so hard...a must buy DLC to complete Metro Exodus main story line, a perfect classic Metro experience. Around 2 hours at it was all over. Game lean heavily into the horror aspect of the survival horror experience found in the Metro series. The excellent sound design and clever gameplay balance choices made with the inclusion of the flamethrower create some genuinely tense sections. Your flashlight is removed, instead replaced by the flickering yellow flame of your weapons pilot light. The reduced visibility and arsenal, coupled with the slower aiming and reload times force a more cautious pace. Hats off to the writer of The Two Colonels DLC.> SAM'S STORY <The final DLC for Metro Exodus brings players a brand new open-world level to explore, filled with intense gameplay opportunities and stories to tell. a next level experience, it's 10 times scarier than Metro Exodus. The character of Sam is a lot more upbeat and feisty than the perpetually silent Artyom, so following him as the leading man of the story proves to be a much more engaging experience. Some of his lightheartedness occasionally feels like the situations call for it, while a few story developments feel somewhat rushed, but by and large, this DLC tells a solid narrative.Beyond narrative strengths, Vladivostok impresses in other areas as well. For starters, it is perhaps the single most visually impressive location I’ve ever seen in a Metro game. The city is half sunken and fallen into ruins, with water flooding the streets and seeping into the buildings, while an overgrowth of plants on structures and roads and layers of moss in the water give sections of the city a bright, green aesthetic. Design-wise, too, Vladivostok feels fresh and exciting. Traversing through the city in a boat and finding new areas to explore or points of interest to check out is constantly engaging. The unique properties of the environment also pave the way for some excellent encounters, like wading through waist-deep waters in the corridors of a dark and half-sunken building, while underwater enemies camouflage themselves in the moss and suddenly jump out at you. The trademark tight, claustrophobic corridors of Metro feel even more oppressive in Sam’s Story. A great mix of linear and open-ended missions.

_childDocuments_.review: Metro Exodus is the last game in the Metro Trilogy and is based on -and inspired- by the Novel Metro 2035 from Dmitri Gluchowski.   You once again slip into the boots of Artyom, who is married by now and a well-established Soldier, with a desire to find out if anything outside of Moscow survived the great War. And to most people’s surprise, there still exists life outside the Metro.After a, more or less, successful rescue attempt of his wife Anna, Artyom and a handful of his comrades escape Moscow with an old train. Will they survive? Will they find a place to live in the wastelands of Russia? And what is still out there?   Metro Exodus has pretty much the same gameplay loop as the two previous games. You explore the world, gather resources, craft ammunition, other necessaries, like health packs and filters for your gas mask and improve your weapons.Exodus has one massive difference thou from 2033 and Last Light. You spend most of your playtime on the surface and in three big semi-open world levels, you are free to explore and tackle objectives to some degree in an order of your choosing.  The levels are well made, and fun to play through, but they do not have the claustrophobic spooky atmosphere of the Metro obviously, which I really missed. But of course, the devs stuck to the source material, and they did a good job. But it is something to be aware of, since Exodus has a way different feeling through this.    The game looks and sounds absolutely gorgeous. The world feels and looks good, the underground levels have the classic Metro atmosphere and design we all love.  The weapon and background sounds are great, and the English Voice actors doing an amazing job in my opinion.   This is only for the Enhanced Version which I played, and I regret that I did.Thanks to the Raytracing which can’t be disabled in his version, since it is build around it, I had to play most of the open world areas with around 30-35 fps, which wasn’t exactly fun. I had Raytracing on the lowest levels and graphics on normal, but apparently a GeForce 3070TI + an Intel i7-12770k and installing it on a M2 SSD clearly wasn’t enough to handle the game. So be aware of that. If I would play it again, I would definitely choose the Normal version of the game.     Exodus has 2 DLC’s :  This DLC’s is maybe my favorite part of the entire game. It plays a long the final Chapter of Exodus to go deeper into what happened and explore the other side of the story. The entire DLC has the beloved Metro atmosphere. Loved it.     This DLC’s Story begins after the ending of the main game and follows one of your comrades who leaves the group in his dream to travel do San Diego in the hopes to see this dad again.  Also, a great DLC with a nice story a lot to explore, but it is set in an open world environment again. Can definitely recommend playing through it.   Metro Exodus is a great and well deserved round up of the Trilogy. I liked what everything leads to, and it feels like a good conclusion to the entire Story. The gameplay feels great, the characters are well written once again, and you feel satisfied to end your Metro experience with this game. If you can’t warm yourself up to the open world levels thou, I can’t recommend Exodus.  Personally, I prefer 2033 and Last Light but Exodus still deserves a recommendation.  (Since the review playtime apparently only displays the playtime of the non Enhanced Edition, my playtime as of wrting this review is 62h)

_childDocuments_.review: As of writing this Im planning on doing a second playthrough some time in the future       If you're like me and only heard about metro through the Metro Exodus E3 announcement, so you bought both games and played them for context, you're going to love this one.        Compared to the last two games this is really the most "open world" I've seen in  a linear shooter before, at some times it felt like I was in a better Fallout environment wise, the graphics aren't on the level of the Frostbite engine but they have gotten a massive over-haul, especially in a section where you spend time in "the valley", however its not just there , the game is beautiful at times and each map has its moments, especially at night, ill also add the day and night cycle is a much needed improvement, combine that with the random packs of mutants that spawn on the map really helps to keep this world alive in its own way, this helps them later on in the game really hammer home that an area is "dead" in one of the later levels     A Complaint I had in the last game was how Anna felt sort of forced,although I'm not sure if that's just a limit of the technology of the time, here her character is fleshed out much better since there's just more room for it and she feels more natural.       I loved the level of weapon variety and customization I found myself restarting levels just so I could get every kill as a stealth kill, similar to Batman Arkham.     My playthrough was on the normal difficulty level and the Survival mechanic has been vastly improved, vs the last game where you could potentially have 60 minutes worth of filters, they also introduced a crafting system to create your own med-packs instead of just hoping you find some which i really do like.Everything they did here feels like a massive improvement, the game is a 9/10 for me, it would be a 10/10 if i had not encountered some rather annoying bugs, it is definitely worth the 60$, its such a shame a great game like this has to be out-shined by a poor publisher decision

_childDocuments_.review: Metro Exodus: Choo-choo to Sunshine, Shoot Mutants, Sing with Artyom (Metro in a Nutshell)Sun-bleached Moscow? Nah, we're chugging across irradiated Russia in a train the size of your hopes! Metro Exodus throws Artyom and his trusty guitar (seriously, he never leaves it) into a post-apocalyptic road trip, trading claustrophobic tunnels for mutant-infested wastelands.Story? Twists like a radioactive vine. Think bandits, cannibals, and mutated beasties bigger than your bad decisions. You'll navigate political intrigue, make choices that'd leave a moral compass dizzy, and maybe even find some post-apocalyptic romance (just don't get caught singing with Artyom, dude's voice is rougher than the Caspian Sea).Gameplay? A post-apocalyptic buffet. Stealth shank mutants, blast bandits, or craft traps so intricate they'll make MacGyver weep. Scavenge, barter, upgrade your arsenal – duct tape and scrap metal are your new best friends. And then there's exploration: from sand dunes to jungles, this irradiated world begs to be unraveled.The world? Gorgeous, even with the radioactive glow. Sunsets over ruins, sandstorms that'll hold your breath, and an environment so alive you can practically smell the irradiated dust. Just be careful of the giant mutated shrimp…seriously, devs, what's up with that?So, perfect? Nah. Bugs the size of the Tsar Bomba, wonky AI, and fetch quests that'd make a postman cry. But here's the truth: Metro Exodus is a masterpiece. It's immersive, emotional, and reminds you that even in the darkest corners, there's hope, humanity, and maybe a decent cup of noodles aboard the Aurora.Grab your gas mask, tune up your Kalash, and climb aboard. Just remember, comrade, in the Metro, the only constant is Artyakov's bad jokes (and maybe the radioactive glow, but that's not as funny).Sincerely,M***o ♡P.S. _childDocuments_.review: Edited:Finished the game. This is my first full review of a game. First off, this game is marvelous! Thanks 4A team for delivering this masterpiece.( - ) Let me talk about the negative things of this game first:Metro Exodus is a great story-driven game. Graphic is top notch. However, there are few minor problems with character animations and audio bugs. People talk over each other sometimes and if you're going to play without subtitles, it's kind of hard to follow the dialogue. Facial animation was not that great, some of the cutscenes were a bit off for me but most of the time they were good. I guess it's not originally for the English version, playing this game in Russian version could be better but I would never know for sure. Still, these are some minor issues that didn't really affect too much of my experience playing this game.( + ) Let's get to the good part:This is definitely the best single player first person shooter with a great story for me! It's been so long since I really enjoyed a game like this. The character development is one of my favorite things about this game. The game does a great job of making you feel connected with the NPCs. Everyone in your Aurora squad has their unique personality and you can easily tell the difference.The new crafting and modding system is interesting. I love how you can change the mods on your guns while you're doing quests because it affects the gameplay a lot. You have options to choose your loadout before and during the missions. However, if you decide to play this game on Ranger Hardcore mode, the resources are pretty scarce which forces you to play this game on stealth most of the time.  Cleaning your guns is very important because the dirtiness affects your weapon's stats (accuracy and fire rate). Your guns could be jammed many times if they are too dirty.New quest-finding system is great too. The game doesn't show you where the quests are, you'll have to discover those points of interest on your own using your binocular. Those high grounds are the goldmines of intelligence if you take your time and look for places. It will be shown as a question mark on your map after you stared at a specific location for about 3 seconds.I love the day-night cycle in this game. The game gives you options to select day or night time. There are many safe houses around the map and you can use them to heal yourself, use the workbenches or sleep. It changes the whole game of how you choose to approach your next mission. Day time means less monsters and the human AIs are quite harder. They can easily see you from afar and alert the other guards so for example, if you want to take down a bandit camp, night time is much more effective. However, night time in this game is horrifying (more monsters to deal with). There are also anomalies in this game and it gives me S.T.A.L.K.E.R vibes. It only happens at night and will hurt you if you get too close.The atmosphere is one of the best about this game. It's breathtaking with 4 different seasons and environments that the game offers you to explore. Different biome has its unique feeling into it. Just take your time to explore every corner you go through, there are many surprises that won't let you down.Just like the old Metro games, your playstyle and your decisions dictates the outcome of the game. In my opinion, the karma system in this game is one of the best I've seen so far in all of the games I've ever played. You will see the consequence of your decisions during mid game and at the end as well.There's no need to say about the soundtracks. They're insanely good and fits the theme well.I got the bad ending even though I tried hard to get the good one. There are things that the game won't tell you but you have to think carefully before you act. Therefore, I'm still working on my second playthough because I missed so many things on my first playthrough and I'm trying to get the good ending this time.Thank you 4A! Solid 9/10.Edit 2:I just uploaded a GMV that I made for Metro Exodus.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, this game is riddled with bugs.To start with, there's a persistent post-processing filter that's laid over the game at different moments. It's unfortunately not possible to turn this off, and the filter makes the night scenes far too light, and the daytime scenes far too dark. I don't think this has anything to do with the new ray tracing features, because the filter sometimes disappears during cutscenes, when waking up, etc. Very weird. Wish they included an option to turn it off.There are a number of other bugs which damage the experience, too. For example, my subtitles got completely stuck very early in the game. The same two lines are stuck on the screen permanently, and no other dialogue will display. Very annoying...Despite the beauty of added ray tracing and the fantastic impact of DLSS 2.1 in the new Enhanced Edition, the graphical options are so bare bones it's almost laughable. All you can really change is texture quality. No anti-aliasing or other options.The big kicker for me, though, was that I am now at the end of Caspian, and the game crashes whenever I try to load my save. I've tried to load older saves, I've tried starting the game in safe mode. No dice, it's broken. I'm not sure what caused this, but it's pretty disappointing. I can put up with the graphical weirdness but this is obviously a dealbreaker.Since my save file was now effectively bricked, I decided I would play the DLC. A few moments into starting up Sam's Story and, guess what? Yup, can't progress due to another abundance of crashes, this time in-game. So I ended up giving up and just uninstalled this. Not going to waste my time any further by putting hours into a game that will randomly hard lock me.In any case, if you were waiting to buy this for Enhanced Edition, you'll probably be disappointed. It's a very unstable game, even now, two years after its original release. I like this game a lot but unfortunately I can't recommend it considering how unstable it is.If you liked this review and would like to hear my opinion on other games, please feel free to follow !

_childDocuments_.review: First, I am surprised that the game is at a very positive right now with an 82 Metacritic score, and I would check twice before buying. I primarily see EPIC store drama being discussed, not flaws and strengths. Review below.The Metro skin is here, but without any of the charm. The claustrophobic and fantastical elements of being in the Moscow metro are just completely lost, which was the biggest downer for me. The story is utter trash as your girlfriend holds your hand through a story you do not really believe is happening. Story excluded, the open world design change adds some new satisfying elements, but just barely makes up for what was lost. The graphical fidelity cannot really cover up these issues.The graphical quality is impeccable, but the art design adds almost nothing new and lost its Metro charm. The original truly distinguished itself from other FPS-apocalyptic-horror-gopnik games like Stalker. Not much was added to make up for the fact you left the Metro, with the one exception, a mfn Soviet train. The soviet steam train is quite interesting... but... that's it...? The train does not makeup for the metro tunnel charm and immersive world that so engrossed me into the previous games. I loved going into the narrow tunnels, not knowing what could be in the dark or around the corner. Maybe the game creators pulled a GoT DandD when they pulled away from the book, I do not know. But now the game is essentially a disappointing Stalker clone, and it is kind of sad.The game is an open world game, and has been compared to STALKER, and I think that is an apt comparison. BUT Metro was special, not because it was a Stalker clone, but because it was ya know... Set in a metro... It then expands out into this open world game, but still tries to be Metro, creating obvious design conflicts. The game-play loop is aided in some ways by these choices however. For example, there are many new ways to approach enemy encampments due to being in an open world. The crafting system has also got a nice "upgrade" (laughs to self), and things feel more satisfying when you feel each victory builds you up so well, encouraging exploration. But, here is an excellent example of a huge flaw. I played on ranger mode (hardest difficulty) because obviously, I am a bada$$. However, resource scarcity never seems to be a problem on that difficulty, at leasthow it is supposed to, at least not currently in six hours of playing. I almost always have enough ammo, and if I do run out, I am stranded in the open world with no escape. Refining how much ammo a player gets is easy in a linear or semi-linear game, but that refinement was lost here. Sometimes open worlds get the right sauce for survival, but this game is not refined enough to keep me on the edge. Usually I am so comfortable, that I rarely check supplies, and THAT is the only way I run out, by accident. These kind of issues are frequent throughout, and just show the lack of refinement for the game experience. It shows that open world games often become quantity over quality.The story and dialogue show a complete lack of passion. The beginning two hrs of the game, your girlfriend... fk if I remember her name... holds your hand through it, yelling "Artyom!! Artyom!!" like she just came for the first time. The story hook is a really bad twist, and is conveniently at the very start (maybe to guilt reviewers into not talking about the story). Basically the trope of a plot of conspiracy, and everything you knew was a lie, plays out in the space of an hour. Every little thing that happens are all just painful and unconvincing plot devices to give you something to do. And do not even get me started on the dialogue. I am so glad to be free of the clownish characters as soon as I step out into the wasteland. The narrative is a far cry from the gripping characters and traumatizing horror of the original, making a "not even so bad it's good" level of storytelling.Speaking of the trash, is anyone tired of the corporate greed bs that has allowed these kind of games to stay in this buggy mess for so long? Seriously, half of the time I use a boat, it gets stuck on the goddang spawn point, ffs. The game has been out for a year, and on just this point alone, I would not recommend it. Fix your game , fixing boat spawns is not hard, we live in a society.I loved the original game so much that I picked up the book. So believe me when I say this game has the Metro skin, but is not really Metro anymore. The design choices lack the refinement that added so much tension to the original, but still added some good elements.  The story is so incredibly boring, it is hard to take any of it seriously. The dialogue is phoned in with crappy lines and forgettable characters. Metro: Exodus feels like a phoned in RTX showcase that sold out to the EPIC store because their game was just not as good this time round, but I can see why some people might like the open world design choices.I did however only get through 6hrs before I got bored, so take this review with a grain of salt.

_childDocuments_.review: Having already completing this multiple times, on steam and on Epic, I cannot suggest buyinh this game unless you are a die-hard fan or it is on sale. I would give this review a sideways thumb if I could. It is the weakest game in the trilogy in terms of game play and story. When I first heard this game would have open-world parts to it, I knew that was a bad sign. Instead of sticking to the claustrophobic atmosphere and enviroment that made the original games so good, it decided to go open-world in order to cash in on how popular is with the crowed. So now Metro is a loot and shoot game, making it no different to most games being spewed out these days. One of the uniquest ideas the Metro series came up with, was using military-grade ammo as a currency. This offered the player to use the military ammo on enemies (as it is more effective than regular ammo) at the cost of not being able to buy better/ more equipment, or save it up, at the cost of being weaker. Now it is good, it's just harvesting things you find on the floor, which is plentiful. In terms of level construct, the best chapters are the linear ones, with the final chapter "Dead city" being the best of, as it resembles what a Metro game should be like, with the worst chapter being Caspian, for the opposite reasons. The chapters follow a pattern of: Linear, open, linear, and open, with the 'Taiga' chapter being a mix of both, and the final being linear. Gunplay is alright. If you play it on hardcore, humans are as delicate as you, making it fun to fight them, But mutants are sponges, and will often take more than several rounds just to take them down, which is really cancerous. Another thing is, Artyom seems to have brittle bones, as falling from 1m in the air or running down the stairs can either kill him, or wound him quite badly.Story? It pretty much sucks. The story is that you're finding a new home after escaping Moscow. However, there are no real stakes outside of Anna. This would have been fine if you consider the fact Last Light had you blow up D6 (with you inside) in order to save it from the Red Line if you got the bad ending. You can't really top it. That being said, nearly all the characters in the game are boring and 2D. The Colonel is a grumpy old man, Anna is there because she has tits, and Artyom is a plank of wood that is too shy to speak, and has to write his inner thoughts in a diary. The side characters are forgettable. None of them hold a candle to the colourful personalities that both Khan and Ulman had, and they either died/ went missing after Last Light. So you're stuck with more planks of wood. Supposedly, Pavel from the last came was supposed to be apart of the crew. He would have been the only interesting character amongst the crew, especially considering his role in the last game.The DLCs are actually worth getting.Two Colonels is what you'd expect from a Metro game, and fills in gaps for the last chapter and offers a great mini story with a very touching ending-scene, which is just as good as the ending for Metro Exodus. Sam's story is a open-world expansion, with Sam as the protaganist. He's the only member of the crew to be fleshed out, and is unique in the fact he's American. What makes it rather funny is that if you play it in Russian, he speaks English in a Russian accent, and comes off as quite humourous when he starts insulting people. The expansion offers a interesting map worth exploring, new weapons, new creatures and an open-ending. The thing I liked about the expansions is that both characters talked. This actually gives them character, and helps the story move along, as opposed to being a mute. Please make this a feature for the future instalments that are being made.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, where to start?   I went in expecting something like Metro 2033, and kind of did get that.  However,  with that came a hell of a lot more.  Incredible graphics and story telling.   Cold, gritty, solemn and scary at times.   In my time of 18 years of playing First Person Shooters there have been a handful of stunners.   First was "Wolfenstein 1992.  Second  was the game "Marathon" for Macs in 1994, and it's multiplayer ability.   Third was Halflife from Valve (1998?).   Make this the Fourth in that lineup.Metro Exodus drags you into the game from the start and you stay there in depth the entire time.  The storytelling is superb.   The game action is outstanding and can be frustrating sometimes.  It's departure after two Chapters to a semi-sandbox atmosphere is a gloriously fun change.   I got a little shooting crazy and ended up the sad ending and I still think it is the best.  Completely emotional.   I went back and played again and was more friendly, because I just had to see the happy ending.  It was good but as expected.You will be tested.  If you play over the level of "Normal", I pity you.   Hell, you'll be tested at "Normal" too.   To be honest I found it necessary to go to the internet twice to help.  Yeah, I cheated, but I still loved it anyway.  I can't say enough for this game.  I went in expecting to be bored with a game completely like Metro 2033 and came away changed.  I know that sounds corny, but it's true!

_childDocuments_.review: I pre-ordered Exodus very early on so managed to avoid the Epic store kerfuffle that went on. I can see why it ♥♥♥♥ off a number of Steamvets, however.My main concern with the new direction Exodus was to head in was that there was the potential for it to lose too much of its "Soviet Soul". I really enjoyed the claustrophobic confines of the Metro of the previous 2 titles, as well as the games linear nature.  New open world format aside there was still enough metro spaces to get into, with Novosibirsk/Dead City in my opinion being the highlight of the entire game.Overall, the game managed to retain the magic of the previous titles for the most part, though as time goes along and replays are done, I still pine for the old metro. There is still so much story to tell back there that I hope somehow that we can return there in future. Granted many of the old characters from the previous titles remain back there so my fingers are crossed that we will see them again in some form. Perhaps the same emerging threat that has taken over Novosibirsk in such a slimy and disgusting manner since the civil war could be a good antagonist in the Mosco metro, requiring Artyom to return there.The new crafting system is quite good, though I think they should have retained military grade rounds and that currency in some format, it would have complimented the crafting system well.Graphics, as per usual, are AMAZING and you can spend much time wandering around appreciating such a well constructed world.All in all I highly recommend Exodus

_childDocuments_.review: THE GOOD-A crisp chill perturbs the leaves of the auburn trees. A single string of golden light caresses the bolt shaft, the usual shimmer muted by a delicate crust of dirt, invisible regardless, through the cracked scope. The target, a curious individual, covered tip to root in a motley of dried brush and bramble, stands as if to sniff the surroundings. You observe it's absentminded ambling with a stately gaze: it appears the target is as bemused by the forest as it is awed by the sunset. The cool, rough finish of the spring trigger glides pleasantly over your finger, beckoning you to commit the shot, to free the bolt from its tensioned cage.A deep throaty roar sends tremors through the very earth! The bolt flies wide and dives for the river as if dying of thirst. The forest dweller, abandoning all pretence of injury or innocence, starts and sprints into the nearest cave. You curse silently as a thunderous pack of wolves force you back into the tree hollow. Watching as they zealously rip and tear the virgin foliage asunder, you notice a flash of light atop the opposite cliff. A mirage? No, it repeats in a pattern. Could it be?The long-awaited third chapter in the Metro saga has arrived! It does indeed boast much larger worlds and vastly improved visuals (even over its predecessors), while sticking true to its brand of rich, driving, environmental storytelling. It feels as though the series has evolved to the next plane of narrative gaming. In many ways, it feels more engaging and genuine than the best AAA titles of today, and that is saying far more than something.The devs have outdone themselves in a big way, with a world that lives and breathes around you. Every character, human or beast, has a life and routine to follow and a story to tell. The story beats unfold themselves seamlessly around nearly every corner. The atmosphere is palpable and ripe with just the right mixture of fear, apprehension, dread, sorrow, rage,  mirth, hope and joy as each situation prescribes. This is one that you can lose yourself in without even realising it.Whether you choose to indulge in the modern Raytracing (Dare I say it?) paradigm or not, the worlds in Exodus are drop dead gorgeous. Filled with disarming weather effects, lifelike (albeit mutated) beasts, meticulous design details and far too many secret crevices, it cannot be played through only once, if you hope to experience it all. Every vista is bursting with visual splendour that both calls you forth with awe and demands that you trade haste for curiosity. Indeed, no matter how much you might pride yourself as a speedrunner, Metro Exodus, evermore than its progenitors, commands your explorer's spirit. Period.THE BAD-This is where things get serious. The game has been publicly available for two years now and it still suffers from some, not insignificant, freezes, crashes and heavy frame drops in places. It also occasionally fails to trigger story beats, which often requires you to reload a save in order to progress. Part of this may have been my eagerness to play on a new generation of hardware with drivers that may have literally been born yesterday, but these issues did persist (at a noticeably lower frequency) well into my binge - I... I mean playthrough!This one has been well documented, so I'll be brief: Metro Exodus was one of the original 3 games to utilise first-generation RTX tech, and while it certainly pushes the lighting fidelity to unprecedented heights, it failed to allow for DLSS at standard resolutions. This may have been a limitation of either the game, or possibly, the infamous Nvidia drivers themselves. Either way, it does diminish the experience of the technology to the player, without logical reasoning. At time of writing, an update to DLSS 2.0 and Raytraced reflections is on its way, so I'll definitely be taking a look when it drops for PC.THE VERDICT-Metro Exodus vastly outstrips its predecessors in every way: The levels are far larger and reach a level of detail and fidelity most games struggle to achieve even today. In true Metro fashion, it provides a compelling narrative, lifelike characters and living environments.While it does deliver on its promise of a rich, meticulously crafted world, the experience is inconsistent. Stability issues have slipped through the cracks which, if encountered, will break your immersion, if only briefly.All of this eye candy does demand a lot from your system, though, so many sporting older hardware will need to make some settings sacrifices that they didn’t have to on other titles of the day. Something to note before jumping in.With all of that in mind, Metro Exodus is a necessity if you've already played, or watched, the previous games. For those who haven't, you'll definitely get more from the game's lore and character development, if you go back to the older titles first. That said, it's still an excellent standalone experience that imparts what you need to know about the world as you go.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: 9/10Genre: First Person Shooter THE GOOD:+ Graphicly, each level features rich detailed environments with plenty of graphic and accessibility options. A photo mode can be toggled anytime to take beautiful pictures of the scenery or gameplay. + Every level has its own unique atmosphere. Some levels are more open world while others are more linear. Each level has some great cinematic story segments that highlight the dangers of living in the world  + The game has a sense of realism with its gameplay that you don’t find in many other FPS games. Weapons can get jammed if they get dirty, you have to wipe your gas mask for visibility, charge your battery for your flashlight or night goggles, some weapons need to be pumped for maximum efficiency, enemies surrender when they realize they’ve been beaten, etc. Non of these are overly obtrusive either so you don’t feel overburdened or frustrated by these mechanics but they do a good job of reminding you that you need to be a bit more aware of what is happening. In addition, there are no traditional menu screens or traditional HUD so your entire focus is always on the game. The game does a brilliant job of keeping you immersed in the world. + NPC’s act very realistically. They have conversations with each other about the situation or the world around them in between missions. The developers did a good job humanizing the NPC and in general I liked sitting down and talking to them.    + Like previous games there is a hidden morality system which does affect how the story unfolds. Killing people indiscriminately usually results in loss of morality while sparring people grants you good morality points. Each level is designed to encourage both action or stealth depending on your play style.   + Much of the gameplay revolves around scavenging for materials to upgrade and fix weapons. Being prepared prior to battle is important and adds to the tension of combat. Different weapons types and upgrade parts further facilitate different play styles. +Both story DLC”s are excellent further highlighting the world of Metro Exodus and add many more hours of enjoyment. THE AVERAGE:+/- The main character is a mute character during gameplay which is really odd and distracting given that he narrates the story during loading screens and given how many NPC characters interact and talk to him during gameplay segments having him stay silent feels like a very odd design choice which doesn’t really work in this case.  +/- In between missions you have to listen to many NPC characters talk and as realistic and cool as it is, non of this is un-skippable making subsequent playthroughs frustrating.  Conclusion: One of the most immersive games I have played all year. I loved exploring the world scavenging for items while trying to survive every combat encounter and seeing the story unfold. Highly recommended for any fans of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: This game follows on from the previous two Metro games and does not disappoint at all. The graphics are beautiful creating an amazing atmosphere on a post-apocalyptic Russia. The story is one of the best out there as it builds onto the characters from the previous two games until you reach the endings. which ending you get is based on how  your morals are across the game. To get the "good ending" complete most the side quests and also kill less people (knock people out when you are not detected or just sneak past them). To get the "bad ending" basically just kill most of the enemies you see. However in my opinion there is not a good or bad ending as they are both good.

_childDocuments_.review: Metro Exodus it's an incredible step up for the series making the game separated in 4 principal parts of which the first two are semi-open world.The world, like the games before this, is INCREDIBLY detailed! Every of the four main parts of the game are incredibly different from each other. From the textures, the lighting, the guns, the characters ecc... is all made with the most detail and cure as possible making this game for me the best game graphically ever made (at the time of this review), it also has high quality animations for every little motion you can do and this adds to the atmosferic and immersive feeling which is the best parte of the game. Differently from the other two games it has a very huge enphasis on the relationship with the characters you start the journey with, being all very well characterized and well written, sucking you into this beautiful post-apocaliptic world (expecially if you read all the additional stuff and listen to all the dialogue that unfortunally can be easly missed).The ending is emotional and somewhat satisfactory making this game the last chapther for the METRO series!There is some bad stuff like the jumping and running that constantly gets you stuck into the poligons of the terrain; the incredible hitbox that your character has, even behind an object you can easly get shot and possibly die; the stealth is at times well made and at times horrible with enemies that see you instantly even if you are in the dark and lastly some minor bugs.The bad stuff is almost nothing compared to what the game can give you and is definatly worth playing!---------------------------------------------  ---------------------------------------------

_childDocuments_.name: Metro Exodus

_childDocuments_.review: ★★★★✯The game is amazing, I really loved the first two Metro games due to their horror take on the post-apocalyptic genre, you were constantly afraid of what might happen because a monster could easily kill you or take almost half your ammo to kill it which should be avoided as they don’t drop anything. Anyways I’m talking about Metro Exodus now, it is a really cool game and the open world areas don’t feel like they were shoehorned in.The gameplay is still what we’ve come to expect from the Metro franchise, tight combat, immersive mechanics, weapon customization and now crafting as well :), the crafting is quite tame as there are very few item types in the game so you can easily horde up a lot and make what you need/want at the moment. The fact that upgrades are thrown/hid all around the open world segments is quite a nice way to encourage exploration so that’s also a positive. The driving mechanics are really good and I see no faults with that nor am I annoyed with it being there.The story while not amazing was fun and definitely kept my interest and made me want to play further to see the outcomes, anyways I don’t want to go to much into detail, the gameplay is bloody amazing, the set pieces are cool, the open world aspect is a welcome change, the crafting mechanic and unlock system is really fun so yeah. I would definitely recommend this game to just about everyone 4.5/5 !!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Metro Exodus

_childDocuments_.review: I won't be knocking the epic store here, only voicing my disappointment with the publisher of exodus for believing that exclusivity benefits anyone.  I do not wish for the epic store to fail, but I do hope that devs and publishers can see the flaws and downfalls of exclusivity for both the company and players alike.Metro is a fantastic game that deserves to be experienced by as many people as possible and exclusivity inhibits that.  The story and characters are engaging and you will doubtless care about them before you go very far.  The gameplay is refined to a knife edge and incredibly satisfying with fantastic weapons and sound design to boot.My primary disappointment was how exodus has moved away from the paranormal aspects present in previous games.  Otherwise, every minute of this game is enjoyable and engaging and you will not regret taking time to see everything and listen to what people have to say.
_childDocuments_.name: Metro Exodus

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing and soul-stirring game! I fell in love with the gripping story, soundtrack and brutal combat. The story is about human connection and sacrifice. Without giving too much away, the great lengths that Artyom goes for his wife Anna culminates in a very satisfying ending and is sure to tug at your heartstrings.I will say though, you will need a little patience with the game. It develops a little slowly in the beginning and the combat takes some getting used to but, given enough time, the storyline comes together really well and the characters end up being memorable.The combat is BRUTAL and stealth-driven. You will need to be on high alert every step of the way because ammo and work benches are limited. The horror element is very well done and lends itself to the gripping nature of the game.Oh and did I mention how incredibly good the graphics are? I played the PC enhanced version (highly recommend) which allows you to fully customize raytracing settings. I cranked those settings to "extreme" thanks to the powerful 6900 XT and boy do the environments really transform. Since this a post-apocalyptic game, the everything around you is almost always rusty, dilapidated and just plain dead or mutated. This is in my top 5 of the most graphically beautiful games I've ever played. If you're looking for a stealth-based post-apocalyptic game that you will have you at the edge of your seat throughout the entirety of the game, look no further! You will not be disappointed!

_childDocuments_.review: Exodus is a great addition to the Metro universe. It has both open and linear sections for both new and old fans. _childDocuments_.review: Worth £10 but no more.I don't think its worth £45 or an AAA title, very over hyped, graphics are ok but it just seems like a Fallout 4 mod, some of the animations are off and there are lots of glitches.Playing on maximum settings, some of the graphics in the desert seem a little bland and there are no footprints in the sand or snow when you walk, seems to kind of lack detail in places. The character graphics are good, and the forest is ok, I think its more the animations and graphical layout of some areas that seem a little last decade.I like the gas mask  feature the way you have to utilise it, and keep your gear up together, and there are some nice touches like emergency mask repair with sticky tape, wiping the grime off the mask and changing filters, getting the map out constantly is a bit tedious, even with the wrist compass.General game play is fine and combat is good, you can't blaze away finding and using cover is recommended. The different weapons are interesting the modding of the weapons and finding different parts is well thought out.The melee sound is hilariously ♥♥♥♥! The sound is the same awful crack no matter what you are hitting, it sounds like they ripped a nut cracker sound using a commodore 64. The rest of in game sounds are fine.I've seen some bad animations also, monsters attacking other monsters and not actually touching them, but seemingly lifting them up on invisible wires.Lots of floating objects.Creatures disappearing through walls.Shooting at ghouls and had them flat out vanish into thin air in front of me.Characters all speaking over each others dialog and not looking at you while talking (are you talking to me or him?)I had someone who's gun was constantly firing, even when on her back.Enemies stuck in walls.Enemies able to see you through walls.For some reason reading the map in a van makes you smash your head through the roof so you have to get out then back in to get the driver view back to normal.Controlling is also a bit old fashioned, having to jump over tiny ramps because he can't lift his leg over a small step.I've had less glitches in 300 hrs of Fallout 4 than 12 hours of Metro (which says a lot)Also it's not very open world like Fallout or Skyrim is with a giant map to explore. It has different zones that you can explore but it tries to push you where to go, and having done some exploring there isn't a lot to discover that isn't map marked.Some of the zones there is pretty much only one direction to go in which is slightly disappointing.Because of the lack of dialog boxes I have no idea if an NPC has finished talking, so I just get bored of their waffle and walk off, only then to have to come back.I got woken up by some thugs after a sleep, had a conversation. When I left they said 'oh going so soon?' So I came back presuming they had more to say, only to all stand around with nothing happening (have you finished?) Left again they said 'going so soon?' So presume that's how that conversation ends - It's not very clear when to leave and they do go on a bit.The story hasn't really grabbed me and the people need to say their ♥♥♥♥ quicker, there are some very boring or cheesy wank cut scenes that seem to go really slowly and on for a long time, and some interactive driving - hold W do a bit of steering, none of which adds to the game.Might be worth checking but don't pay more than £10 for it.65%

_childDocuments_.review: Before you start this game, you should definitely play Metro 2033 and Last Light. Both those games are good, really good, but Metro Exodus is Masterpiece. Great soundtrack.- Story is great, you spend a lot of time with the crew, which is new in metro series (in the first two games you change your companions in like every mission). You feel like you are part of the crew. - No major bugs, crashes, fps drops (there is one major fps issue in desert city, but you will be there like 5 mins and then it's ok, playing on rtx 3060ti)Cons- few minor bugs- one badly optimalized locationI definitely recommend this game (and 2033 + Last Light) for everybody who is thinking about buying this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite being a Diehard Metro Fan, I could not finish this game. Metro Exodus takes absolutely everything that was good about the series, and jettisons it. What's left is abject poverty. The writing is poor in all respects - from the dialogue, to the cookie-cutter story. The gameplay isn't much better - It's a stock standard shooter game. Gone are all the things that made the original special - the labyrinthine tunnel system filled with dark places, begging to be explored and hiding a dagger to the back. Instead, we have a variety of open-world maps with exactly the same gameplay loop as every other modern shooter released in the last decade, that comes off more as 'game design by checklist' than any kind of integration. Was this designed by a focus group comprised of the marketing team for modern warfare, battlefield, and fallout? I know this is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ review, but that's because I don't even really want to write it. I just want metro exodus to go away. Received the game as a Birthday present - sorry bros'.

_childDocuments_.review: It's still a fun experience, because it's still Metro. But, Metro Exodus is definitely the weakest entry in the series.Voice acting is horrible this time around, something the previous games were at least competent, or great (Pavel in Last Light) at. The story is very bare and the horrible direction and line delivery killed any possibility for it to be interesting. This is especially jarring since the intriguing stories are what originally helped the Metro franchise succeed.Every open world set piece is essentially exactly the same with a different coat of paint. You go to a zone, there are lunatics there, you do a small quest chain to allow the train to keep driving and move on. There is barely any side content, and what is there isn't meaningful. And don't get me wrong, I'm the last guy who wants side content in Metro, I hate that they opted for an open world game in the first place.Then, you have the bugs. New Game+ is still bugged to this day, where at a certain point in the game, there is a very good chance that you won't spawn with any weapons. DX12 crashes are as present as ever and sometimes the game just freezes to 1FPS for a minute or two and it just might catch itself again, but it also might not. Some of this is fixed by simply switching to DX11, but then you miss out on the beautiful raytracing. Oh well, better safe than sorry when you are doing an Iron Mode playthrough.The human AI also kinda sucks. You feel that the hardest when you are playing on any Hardcore difficulty and sniping an enemy position from a solid 100-150 meters away, only for them to have pinpoint accuracy on your head with their Bastard guns and killing you in an instant.Because the story is so mediocre, the endings aren't impactful either way. In the bad ending In the good ending, well, it's obvious how it will play out if you've seen the bad ending. It's similarly uninteresting, especially compared to Last Lights amazing ending(s).But, the game has its merits. When you're not in one of the open world levels, the story moves at a nice pace and things speed along. These areas are where the game shines and the most important and interesting plot developments happen. Gunplay is also quite interesting, you can modify your weapons on the fly and add/remove attachments at will. You can also craft some stuff in the open. More sophisticated crafting requires workbenches. The game is extremely gorgeous as well. Raytracing certainly helps but even without it, you can't deny that it's a beautiful game.All in all though, this game  qualifies for a positive review. I just hope that for the next entry, 4A Games decides to go back to a linear, more focused approach. And please, ditch Artyom for the next game since his story should effectively be over. And give the next protagonist a voice. It gets increasingly annoying how they work around Artyom being 'silent'.

_childDocuments_.review: An extraordinary game in terms of atmosphere and visuals. Absolutely crippled by an old-fashioned savegame system. Openworld games can be built on a checkpoint-only system. But never ones where the difficulty is intentionally so high. A single mistake can see 10 minutes of stealth ruined. It becomes impossible to track what was looted and crafted in the many minutes you lose to a crude checkpoint. I've never seen a game so good ruined by such an easily avoided flaw. A simplistic checkpoint system and single quicksave would be fine in a corridor shooter. Basic checkpoints can even work in openworld, if the punishment for death is low enough. Examples include Far Cry or Dying Light.By all means have a harsher save system at higher difficulty. But I have no interest in watching huge chunks of achievement disappear due to inconsistent stealth or spikes in difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: Metro Exodus Is the conclusion in the series and from playing them all first to last starting with Metro 2033. The story keeps you compelled, Exodus offers some great characters and new gameplay mechanics that are more advanced than just simply buying a weapon from a merchant. You can fully customise your weapons now just like in Crysis and your choices matter during gameplay as the story unfolds impacting on what ending you will get.If you've played games like S.T.A.L.K.E.R you'll probably enjoy this too for it's story, it's more linear than open world but that's not a bad thing. There is tons of variety in the weapons and customisation compared to the previous games. I've completed and beaten the game myself on Ranger Hardcore mode and it can be only slightly difficult at the beginning since this means less health and ammo is scarce, so be careful and pick your shots wisely overall adding more challenge. Though on your first playthrough I would recommend playing on Normal as you'll be able to ease in and get into the game better. You'll find yourself venturing out to new locations across post apocalyptic Russia and immerse yourself within it's world. For even more immersion i'd suggest setting the localisation to "Russian" and playing with Subtitles, though subtitles can only be a little distracting. My only complaint to the game really is that there is no "save game" feature at all. Which should be a standard for all PC games.. When also playing on the harder difficulties, you'll want to save your game at certain points which you won't be able to. The "Autosave" system can be frustrating as you'll find yourself lost in progress a few steps back and have to do certain things over again like re-organising your weapon upgrades or driving/walking from point A to point B again. I wouldn't say it's too game breaking on the normal difficulty but if you're playing on Ranger Hardcore mode, it can be a challenge of patience in certain areas. Overall if you liked the other games in the series or you're new to the Metro franchise. Exodus is worth a buy and you should pick up Last light and 2033 on sale if you want to know more about the story from start to finish!
_childDocuments_.name: Metro Exodus

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the original Stalker and the Metro games following it, I loved the Slavic take on the post apocalyptic world-building compared to that of the rest of Europe and America with it's mostly Happy-Go-Lucky games like Fallout, Borderlands (not in America but an American developer anyways). Something about the cold nuclear winters, frost kicking onto your visor as  you wipe it off with a dedicated hand button and the constant ticking of the Gieger counter firmly reminded you that the world with the now-deranged mother nature is far more dangerous foe than anything you will face. When it is shown that the new Metro game will take place mostly outside of Metro, fans were rightly skeptical as one of the core series strength was always the dark interconnected tunnels of the Metro stations of Moscow which drenched in atmosphere which other games in the genre could hardly come even close to. After having played this game in hardcore difficulty, which took me around 30 hours as I took my time as I usually do in these sort of games; I am happy to say that the new open environments are not detrimental to the series core, in fact the the claustrophobic metro sections are still there in the game and elevated up several notches in atmosphere.This game at its heart is probably the closest to Half-Life 3 and a true Crysis sequel we are ever going to it. The one year journey as the game takes you across the desolate Russia with your wife and the people of your ‘Order’ evoked me feels of Half-Life which I have not gotten for so many years, damn I missed that. The maps are not open world, but many are very large, giving you multiple ways to tackle problems, just like Crysis. Also debuting is a on-site attachment system, again similar to Crysis in many ways. That is not to say the game simply borrows everything and calls it a day, there is still the Metro atmosphere which really gels everything together. You have a mobile hub, a train called the Aurora. Here the game becomes a little bit like immersive sims like Deus Ex. Here you get to talk with your crew and play with the weapon modifications. I was surprised how lengthy dialogue can get with you or when the crew is talking amongst themselves. It is a non-issue as you are forced to listen to everything, but I like how the dialogs were often long and felt ‘real’ as opposed to a minute or two conversations. These Aurora sections bring the much needed downtime, especially when you consider how brutal the game can get at times. The thing which bothers me a lot unfortunately is the English voice acting, it is simply not good most the time, minus your wife Anna. It feels like an amatuer person reading off the script, also the voice writing is off for me as well. I heard it sounds a lot better in Russian and it does, however it hurts my gameplay as I constantly checking the subtitles will force you to the bottom third of the screen a lot of the time as you would be missing out a lot in front of you. You don’t want to miss out on that one as Metro Exodus, just like it’s peers, is gorgeous. It now has a dynamic day/night cycle and RTX users can enjoy true Global Illumination which makes the game look even more realistic. Even if you don’t have RTX GPU, the game is absolutely jaw dropping on my GTX 970. I get a good 45-60fps on high settings and the frame rate mostly stays high during combat so it doesn’t bother me. Although bear in mind that the frame rate can vary a lot depending on the location you are in and what you are looking in front of you. There are some off low resolution textures on certain objects here and there, which is a shame but not a deal breaker but overall though, this game is a stunner and easily one of the best looking games out there on the PC.I played it Hardcore difficulty and I suggest everyone to start playing from this difficulty as it tunes the game the way it is meant to be played. Ammo and crafting supplies will be scarce, I had to make difficult decisions like breaking down my ammo for some materials to craft a filter for my mask for example. On this difficulty, you will regularly making such decisions, although it never it felt like it is the focus like a disaster management game. It made me appreciate the gameplay systems even more. The gunfights can be very lethal on hardcore difficulty. 2-3 shots or a shotgun blast can kill you, same rule applies to the enemies. The enemies are challenging because of this, but unfortunately the AI isn’t that good. They take cover and aim pretty good but they never force you to fall back rethink your move. Careful planning and the right gear with the right modifications can make all the difference.Speaking of gear, the weapons and items in metro exodus looks and feels very real. It has that raw look which tech and junk strapped together to make it function which I love. Weapons will degrade overtime in the weather, and will cause it to jam or shoot off the mark when it happens. So it is always a good idea to take note of your gear before heading out. There are also crafting stations outside of the Aurora which will allow you to make ammo and clean the weapons.I did not feel much for the story but in the end it truly grabbed me. It shows the desperation of how far we will go for the people we love. As someone who lost the love of his life very recently, it teared me up. Rachaelle my love, if you read this, I am sorry I failed you.They simply do not make games like this anymore. It was longer than I expected as it took me around 30 hrs to beat in my own pace. It is very unfortunate the steam/epic thing blew to the point the game suffered in the public view. For those are waiting for the steam version of the game, trust me this game will be worth the wait. Make no mistake, this is a great game...one which I wish my girl friend watched me play from...wherever she is...=========My System=========Windows 10 proIntel Core i5 4570GTX 970 OCed16GB RAMSamsung 840 EVO SSDGame installed on a Western Digital Green HDD

_childDocuments_.review: You can consider me quite impressionable, but for me personally this game was so deeply remembered and caused a storm of emotions after passing (I mean the final scenes) that I was a little taken aback and did not start another game for 2 more days after completion, digesting the plot and events unfolding in it ... and also wanted to go through another - a bad ending, which I will soon do.Developers so professionally instill in the player an affection for (open and prescribed) characters that you can unwittingly listen to their conversations, which can sometimes last for 4-5 minutes !! (and I haven’t met this yet) and empathize, worry or support them in monologues (yes, Artyom’s voice has not yet been delivered, Gordon Freeman sends his regards).The developed and almost open world in some large locations is very impressive, accessible to the player to research, search for loot and improve equipment and weapons, random encounters and search for notes and tapes for understanding the plot as a whole, etc.It used to be fun to watch comparisons between STALKER and METRO.I always understood that the first is huge open locations, open lands and so on, and the second is linear corridors and tunnels and that it’s simply impossible to compare these games ...But with the release of Exodus, you realize that here is as spiritually Stalkera as possible. But not about that.+ I liked the customization of the weapon and its presentation itself. The body kit of trunks and the improvement of Artyom’s suit are elegantly presented and woven into the mechanics; almost all of them are clearly worth the time spent searching for them.+ Gorgeous traced locations. Very atmospheric. Winter on the Volga River, the dried Caspian Sea with rotting hulls of ships and shacks, rotting their age, autumn Taiga with beautiful forests and rivers and the Dead, abandoned winter city, which only drives you almost depresnyak, from its doom, "grayness" and hopelessness+ Excellently expanded bestiardia of monsters.+ Interaction with characters is simply incomparable. The game crashes pretty well into the brain and evokes emotions, I haven’t been so impressed with the history of people who often want to help ... and you do it over and over again.+ Graphics. Everything is on top for me. Weapons, landscapes, and room interiors are well designed: bunkers, abandoned huts, tunnels of abandoned metro, etc.+ I really liked how the navigation is presented in the form of a tablet with a map and current tasks.Compass on hand, Geiger counter, Artyom detection sensor in the dark, etc. All this is very well implemented and the main thing is not meaningless.+ Train Aurora. A wonderful and atmospheric hub for the player to take a break from long explorations of the world and dangerous zones. Get to know the characters better, get high from the interior of the equipped wagons, listen to music and talk on the radio waves of unfamiliar survivors among themselves, smoke a cigarette and have a little thump ...You can still write a lot about the pros of the game, I found a huge number of them, but I just recommend buying this wonderful product to every player.Despite the publisher’s idiotic policy, it wasn’t worth underestimating the ratings of the previous parts in this way - this is primarily stupid and stupid. They gave us a great series and maybe! already regretted the transfer of the game to EGS, but there was no turning back ... In the reviews of previous games, frat is a bad deed, I think.The game deserves the highest praise for me, and I recommend it to everyone for passing.

_childDocuments_.review: So, something about Metro Exodus.I rarely write reviews. It just usually goes like buy game, install, play, maybe finish if it is good and that's it. I own the other two games too, 2033 and last light but never played them much. I only have like maybe few hours on them both. Now i am ashamed that i did not give them a proper chance because that would have given me a lot more backstory to work with in Exodus. But still, every single character was so well made that i grew to like every one of them. They were so well made and had their own personalities. Sure there were some minor bugs here and there but nothing major. Had a little laugh with most of them and moved on. I'm not good with horror games. Not at all. I was a bit worried that i would not want to play this game if it was only jump scare after jump scare in dark metro tunnels but oh boy was i wrong. Sure, there are some situations which will get your heart rate rising but somehow they were actually enjoyable situations it this game. Exploration is very rewarding which is an important point in an open world game. I like to stroll around looking in every little shack and open house what i can and to be able to find better upgrades for weapons etc in there is very good game mechanic. If i had to come up with pros and cons, here are some:Pros -Big open world, which is not limited to just only one-Weapon customization and sounds -Characters and voice acting-Graphics. Shame i was not able to run it on extreme settings.-Variety of enemies-I would be sitting here the whole evening coming up with pros so lets move to cons if anyone is even still readingCons-Random crashing when the game is paused or loading. Might be just my PC or messed up files.-Character feels like it is sometimes gliding randomly-Sometimes i felt like the weapons got dirty instantly and started to jam but might be just me playing for 30 minutes which felt like 5 minutesI would highly recommend this game if you like first person shooters with a very good story line, looting, stealth and an open world filled with interesting places and npcs.And i played the Enhanced edition so i needed to download the original version and leave it running for a bit to post a review.
