_childDocuments_.review: Alright, so I originally gave this game a positive review because the opening is pretty stellar, but it falls off pretty quickly after that.If you're someone that really loved the last two Metro games, I would go ahead and give this one a miss. The design decisions they made to accommodate the large open maps absolutely destroy the foundation of the series as we've known it thus far. This could change in the later parts of the game, but I could not bring myself to play any more of it. So to preface this, I played the game on Ranger Hardcore, which is the difficulty I have played all of the Metro games on because it's the only difficulty that makes sense for these games. Ranger Hardcore is usually marked by extreme resource management, an emphasis on stealth and a "realistic" approach to weapon damage. Let me explain how Exodus destroys all three of these tenets. Resource management is non-existent in this game. In the previous games, military grade bullets were used as currency (which in and of itself was a commentary) to purchase things like new weapons, upgrades or even lower quality ammunition to keep you going, but they could also be loaded into your weapon if you needed more damage against certain foes. So there was a balance that you always had to maintain. In Exodus, they  for a couple of reasons. One, because you will never encounter anyone to trade with. Most humans you meet either shoot you on sight or are part of your little crew (or will join your little crew shortly). There is no trading and no reason to have a currency. Two, the entire in-game economy revolves around crafting everything  which removes resource management entirely. I didn't find myself with anything less than full ammo at any given time in the starting area of the game. That's a pretty big problem for a Metro game. This also affects the tone of the game, which is very far removed from the others in the series. Metro was always about braving the inhospitable depths of the tunnels or the irradiated surface of Moscow and arriving at the next bastion of human civilization. People were just trying to live their lives as best they could, and Artyom was fighting to save humanity, even from themselves. In Exodus, you couldn't give less of a ♥♥♥♥ about anyone except your small crew of outcasts. You don't even need to rescue anyone as you are completely self-sufficient and the relief of finally seeing a friendly station you used to get in Ranger Hardcore is absent entirely from this game. Also, Miller has a completely different character from the last two games as well and a sniveling coward, a far cry from the leader of the Rangers (and has no idea how to wear a beret).Alright, so how does this game screw up the emphasis on stealth? Well, to be honest, I think the problem is that the stealth mechanics they built into the series simply don't work in large, open-world maps. The line of sight combined with level of light works great in the tunnels under Moscow, where it's always dark and there's plenty of cover to sneak around, but when you find yourself in the middle of the desert at noon, enemies can see you from about a million miles away. And maybe that wouldn't be such a big deal, except that they screwed up the weapon damage.I want to stress that this is not an exaggeration. Every time I got spotted from 600 meters or farther away, I got shot at by some bandit novice with a pistol shotgun. That is to say, a shotgun with a 6-inch barrel or so. The spread on a 6-inch shotgun barrel at 600 yards would be such that hitting me should be an impossibility. Except that in this game, it is a certainty. Now you might think that since they hit me at such distance, it shouldn't do that much damage right? Well you'd be wrong, because I have consistently gotten one or two-shot by pistol shotguns at extreme range, often from enemies I can't even see. And to compound this problem, I often spent 30 minutes walking all the way across the map only to get spotted by one of these ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and killed only to find out the last time the game saved was back at the start of my journey, and in Ranger Hardcore, you can't manually save at all because they needed to pad the runtime of the game I guess. So basically these mechanics encourage you to sprint around like a madman so that you're harder to hit and get into giant firefights constantly since ammo is essentially unlimited. Which is a pretty big change from the Ranger mode of the last two games. Whereas Ranger Hardcore was previously tough but fair, an exercise in scavenging, knowing when to take a fight and trying to balance survival with saving bullets, in Exodus it's a run and gun shooting gallery where you never run out of ammo or medical supplies and might as well go in guns blazing every time. All of this is without addressing the story, which I'm not going to spoil but basically an event occurs very early on that immediately and obviously starts telegraphing exactly where the story is going to go that I didn't feel the need to play any more and find out what happens because the game had already given it away.So, in summary, if you liked the previous Metro games, I wouldn't really recommend this one. If you're looking for a Eastern European open-world post-apocalyptic shooter, try the STALKER series, which handles everything so much better and has an unmatched, oppressive atmosphere while retaining the glimmer of hope Exodus lost. If you're looking for the Slavic version of Fallout 4 (i.e. the weakest in the main series) then this is probably the closest equivalent, but I'd rather just play Metro 2033 again to be honest.

Whole point is with the backpack system you can change your attachments instead of in previous games where you would have to either use military grade bullets, or pick up enemy weapons, but maybe take some compromises, or do a mix of picking up weapons and spending bullets, you can do what you want alongside crafting some other small items like cans, and it mainly eliminates the need, dont get me started on how your gun can jam now and where at one point my gun was so dirty during a fire fight, it basically made my ak a burst gun where I had to pull the charging handle back after a few shots, stuff like this makes you consider your resources if you should clean or maybe craft more ammo for your next journey, knowing your gun might jam more often, alongside that you can pick up stuff like green mushrooms to use in crafting/ scavenge lockers, boxes, corpses for any craftablesOk, I wasnt always a stealth guy whatsoever always going in gun blazing but some missions stealth is full on required, or just recommended for the amount of enemies, but I never went stealth that much so I can't comment on it, but it seemed ok and kinda punishing if even one guard spots you, but that would be how it works if someone sees an enemy they are gonna scream and make sure all the guards know, you also have cans and throwing knives to assist you if you decide to go stealthThe story really isnt a mess, the total gameplay I found is around 15-20? hours and it depends on how you spend your time what you explore what you don't, which I also really like how you can explore the world and hows it a bit less linear than the previous games, although you don't have to do them if you want to and progress with the story, although if you do more content and all that, you also have to consider the fact that people speak/do stuff that you may wanna listen to as it adds to the world and makes you feel like your part of the world, and not just the whole word, people having normal convos a drink yata and some of it can be interacted with. If you decide to get the "Gold Edition" as well which you can play after because it spoils the main story, it adds about 10 hours as well, sams story being 7-8, and two colonels being 2-3? all these times obviously will vary on the personTHE BADOk, dont get me wrong there are obviously other things wrong or some things, like for example in some parts of the game as not to spoil it, is there are parts in the game where it can be hard to tell where to go, which is really the only issue besides bugs i've had, but these appeared on the previous games, 2033 and last light were there was at least one or a couple sections I had to look up because I genuinely had no idea to go and it ended up being something else then I thought or something that I just did not notice! Sure, this will be different for some people but as some people may have a more keen eye, some people may just investigate more, so you can take this with a grain of saltThe main thing is bugs oh oh, the bugs alright, so theres a few bugs ive known/experienced myself some may be rare and one that seems to be common from another friend, one is probably just launch issues, sometimes it takes a while to launch or may prompt you to launch in safe mode, which can be a pain making the resolution, I remember even when i had this game on xbox pc gamepass when that existed, and it just full on wouldn't launch, but this issue did not occur on steam version so I doubt its an issue, now my most prominent issue is not really big bugs, I had one where I bugged under the whole map in the first mission, but it wasn't that bad just reload yata, but theres one where you drive something and when you open the map you grow 1 foot suddenly, making your character taller and you see really high, what I found as well is to fix this I had to get out of the car, or use the map while or when not moving to get it to unbug, which was really annoying and pestering me especially because damn you kinda either had to barely use your map, or get out of the car if you do and it bugs or slow down, also I tab out a lot which I found is a terrible mistake, I had to reboot the whole game several times either after using discord overlay or tabbing in and out, because it would not let my character move or bug where it would basically be infinetly/for a bit selecting grenades/cans and I would have to listen to that for about 1 minutes, I now have the can noise stuck in my head, and it would also like show my weapons kinda in the tab menu, so maybe try not to tab out of this game too too muchWith all this considered should you get the game though? Yes! Sure there are issues, and bugs, but personally they didn't really break the experience too too much and some are only for a specific section, although these bugs obviously vary between person to person, it's just safe to address them. Besides the bugs and a few minor gripes of where to go, and sometimes some things tripping, its a great experience with a good story, good gameplay and you really feel immersed in the game, the environment shining around you and you can interact/listen into convosOverall, good game with some issues and bugs but if you can get past them the experience should be really fun with little issues, especially if you played the previous games. _childDocuments_.review: Rating: 10/10I've never been a fan of story-driven games, but the Metro series, and especially Metro Exodus, touched my heart in ways I never expected. It's not just another game; it's an emotional journey through the Moscow Metro and into the harsh Russian wilderness in search of a new home. that hooked me from the start.Metro Exodus offers a gripping narrative without feeling overwhelming. It strikes the perfect balance between storytelling and gameplay, making it accessible and engaging even for those like me who typically prefer action over plot.The characters are well developed, and their relationships evolve throughout the journey. The choices you make carry weight, making you genuinely care about the fate of Artyom and his companions.Lastly, the graphics and audio are top-notch. The game's visuals are stunning, and the sound design immerses you in the eerie and dangerous world of Metro.This game proves that even if you're not a fan of story-driven titles, Metro Exodus can convert you. It's a rare gem that transcends genres and offers an unforgettable gaming experience that touched my heart and will stay with me for a long time. Don't miss it.

_childDocuments_.review: So how do i start? This game is just absolutely beautiful.Putting aside the whole fiasco with the Epic Store (let's not even mention how bad it is), which was a publisher decision and not the developers. I am going to speak out only for the game itself and what an amazing job the dev's did with it.As we were familiar with earlier Metro titles, each action in the game has a consequence to a certain degree that will influence the game's story and ending. Thus we are able to go 2 main routes in the game, the bad karma route with a equally bad ending and the good karma route where the ending really hits our feelings deep. I have played the good karma route since the beginning. Back when i played Last Light i had went the bad ending route by mistake and had punished myself for it, yet i couldn't replay the game as whole again. So this time i had decided to make sure i do everything right. And boy did it pay, the amount of satisfaction you receive is worth every bit of effort.Having read the books, I had liked the spin of the story in Exodus. Leaving the Metro on the train with people i had not expected to follow was a nice start to the game. Traveling through Russia on the train was really a pleasant experience, every new chapter and place brought new flavors to the game. I especially really liked the Caspian Desert and Taiga, the beauty of those places in an apocalyptic desolated world in which we were too used to the sorrowful look of Moscow in it's nuclear winter state, made me feel like i wasn't playing metro anymore, but not it a bad way. Objective wise you could follow any path on the map, leaving you to explore places before hand and really go anywhere possible within the map, yet keeping the story line unaffected and linear.Combat and gameplay wise, the game is felt just like any other metro game. With the introduction of the backpack and the wholesome on the go customization and craft benches, i had easily embodied the stealth and ammo conserving play style. I fell in love with the pneumatic gun, with the backpack you can craft bullets for it anywhere as long as you got materials, dead accurate and pretty deadly too, especially against the humanoid mutants which died in one clear shot to the head. I had loved this style of playing, sneaking and making accurate shots without raising too much attention gave a really good immersion on how things should go in a real apocalyptic world.The UI of the game is really brilliant as there is almost none of it. Map wise, you take a physical map / journal in you hands which has a few marks and the current objective written there. Other than that, there are no navigation indicators other than a physical gadget on your wrist, as well as the geiger counter and other physical queues (breathing) that indicated when to put on the gas mask. To fully understand what you have to do and how to do it, you had to listen really careful to the dialog the other NPC's are having with you and follow accordingly.In conclusion, i believe that this game was beautifully executed and rewarded well the long time metro fans and newcomers alike. Perhaps we could get another iteration of the series where we go back to rescue the metro now that we know what's really going on in the world, but we will wait and see for that.

_childDocuments_.review: Metro Exodus is a first person shooter set in the aftermath of a nuclear war, where a small group of survivors live in Moscow’s underground rail network. This is the third game in the franchise, following Metro 2033 and Metro Last Light. The player once again controls Artyom, as he leads a squad of soldiers on a quest across the country.• Combat is enjoyable and fairly challenging on normal difficulty.• First 90 minutes feels very restrictive, with lots of lengthy dialogue scenes broken up by a few short combat sequences, during which you have an AI partner constantly saying “hey go over there, do this”. Thankfully, when you reach the open world sections, the game finally backs off and allows you to explore at your own pace.• The world is a dangerous place, inhabited by several different types of enemies including Human bandits, Humanoid mutants, dogs, Watchmen (large wolf-like creatures that hunt in packs), flying demons, giant shrimp that live in lakes, giant spiders hiding in dark tunnels, and some boss level creatures that I won’t spoil. Occasionally you’ll notice the bandits and monsters attacking each other.• Weapons feel great to fire, and include pistol, shotgun, assault rifle, sniper rifle, crossbow and the Tikhar, which uses air pressure to silently fire metal balls. Each weapon can be upgraded with mods to improve damage, accuracy, clip size, as well as changing how they function, such as different types of zoom sights or silencers. You can carry three weapons, which allows your loadout to have a nice mix of short range, long range and stealth.• Its often a good idea to use stealth if possible, take out enemies silently, or avoid them completely to conserve ammo. Going loud usually attracts more enemies, and you can’t recover ammo from looting monster corpses, so you could quickly run out of ammo. You can craft more ammo, but crafting resources are limited and probably better spent on medkits and gas mask filters.• Open world has a day/night cycle, and weather conditions like rain and sandstorms, which reduces visibility both for you and your enemies. Some areas are heavily irradiated, requiring you to wear a gas mask and change the filter periodically to avoid suffocating.• Main story took 19 hours to finish. There are two different endings depending on your actions during the game. (I got the good ending :D)• Main story is mostly well written.• Voice acting is fine, but I’ve heard better. • Your squadmates don’t just exist to shoot stuff, they’re living their own lives.• Artyom is a silent protagonist like Half-Life’s Gordon Freeman, which feels very weird because the other characters constantly talk to him during cutscenes. Its especially ridiculous every time they try to call him over a radio while on a mission. “Hey, Artyom, are you okay?”. Do they expect him to answer?• I suffered some frequent stuttering, even though my PC (i7 6700K @ 4ghz, 16GB ram, GTX 1080) is comfortably above the recommended spec shown on the store page. After adjusting some settings I had a constant 60 FPS, but occasionally it would freeze for half a second, which was very noticeable when turning my mouse sideways. Strangely, this was worse in the narrow underground tunnels at the start and end of the game, and it actually performed better in the open world areas. It never hurt me during combat, but it was annoying while exploring.• Controls are fully rebindable, however there is a quite annoying bug. I prefer to use arrow keys for movement (yes, we still exist), but there are some scenes where you sit down while listening to an NPC talk and you have to use WASD to interact with objects, or to leave the conversation, meaning that I had to change my keybindings back and forth several times.• When exiting back to main menu I frequently got a message suggesting that my saved games had been corrupted. I never actually lost any progress so I always just ignored the message, however you might want to research this further before purchasing. Maybe I just got lucky.• There are two DLC missions where the player controls different characters. The first takes place during the last mission of Artyom’s story, the second is set after the end of the main story.• Combat is the same high quality as the main story. The first mission adds a flamethrower to the player’s arsenal.• The stories are less detailed compared to the main story.• The first mission is quite linear and lasts around 2 hours, while the second mission contains a new open world area and took me around 7 hours to finish.Metro Exodus has enjoyable combat and a good story, but is let down by some technical problems. As the game has already been out for a year on the Fortnite Kids’ Anti Consumer Store, I doubt these problems will be fixed now.Still, its worth playing for fans of the FPS genre, and the Metro franchise. I bought the game plus DLC for 40% off, which feels like a fair price. If you’ve never played Metro before, I’d recommend picking up 2033 and Last Light, because they’re also really good.

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the first two games but I was really disappointed with this one. Shame... Pros: - Beautiful Cons: - Laggy movement (sometimes when I press A, it registers as W and moves forward and vice versa. Also delayed stops when I release a strafe key). - Bad voice and mouth movement synchronization which makes it difficult to feel immersed. - Bad surround sound. I tried using varations of spatial sound on/off, and 5.1/7.1 sound and no combo made the surrounding sounds feel spatially natural or accurate.  - Objects are often found stuck in the middle of the air. - Bad hit scan. I can stand still and aim at the middle of the enemy's torso from 10 meters and apparently miss my bullet. - Characters teleporting randomly like it doesn't know where it's supposed to be. - The finale left a lot of loose ends. I especially loved Last light and I really thought Exodus would be an even better game but now that I've finished it, I really can't say that it was. I've never written a review before and I'm sad that it had to be a negative one. 5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Metro Exodus is what I find a perfect ending to the Metro Trilogy, with you finally leaving the tunnels and venturing out into the rest of Russia and seeing how the Nuclear War effected it. Each area you visit feels unique from the last in more ways than one. I'm glad that the game follows a storyline that is Linear in nature and not just one giant open world, as those end up being overwhelming and too much, with a narrative dissonance that comes into play, but with the way Exodus handles its flow of Linear Section>Open Map>Linear Section>Open Map it perfectly breaks up each of the sections so you (probably) won't get burnt out on a section, and I wish more games would do this instead of just having one giant open world. Admittedly, I find the first open section on the Volga River a weak way to start the game after your first Linear section, as the main way of travel is incredibly tedious to do but you can (almost) completely ignore that.The game feels incredibly immersive with all the first person animations being well animated and thought out, world building for each area is great. The addition of the crafting system is a nice change, as you'll be scavenging for supplies rather than buying them with bullets, and being able to customize your guns on the fly ala Crysis. My biggest gripe with that is it lacks the amount of gun variety from previous games, especially from Last Light, thought you can make the Kalash into an RPK and somewhat into an AKSU, and the only shotguns that exist are the AShot you can turn into a Single, Double, or Quad Barrel shotgun but unfortunately because of that the Duplet is no longer a thing, and the Shambler can be upgraded in ways to where it fits the role of the Saiga 12.If you're going to play it, I highly recommend playing the game on Ranger or Ranger Hardcore for the best experience.The DLCs are both fantastic as well, with Two Colonels highlighting the more Linear gameplay as seen in earlier Metro games and Sam's Story highlighting Exodus' more open gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic, between the story and the different options you can take throughout, the sound that gives the game the perfect tone, and visuals to grab you by your collar and drag you into this world. Honestly a 10/10 game IMO. There's much more to it, but if anyone is on the edge about this, I can promise you it wont disappoint.

_childDocuments_.review: This game that vividly depicts the post-apocalyptic atmosphere. After a outbreak of war, people who lived underground due to the aftermath of the war describe the journey to find a new land. Communism that controls people, mutations caused by radiation, pirates living in the forest, and various regions and processes are detailed. Especially about game's details, it's perfect to the point of being a work of art.

_childDocuments_.review: after playing 10+ hours I thought it was time to write a brief review:Before, I couldn't recommend the game because of crashes, and yet I have to discover if it will still crash so now and then after validating game files in steam. (PC specs for the matter are: i7 7700K, 16GB RAM, GTX 1080)For now I can only say that you can see there's put much work in this game. The graphics and scenery are amazing, the story is compelling, the atmosphere and dynamic weather/day-night system with it's different playing-approaches and overall gameplay is one of the best I've had in the past few weeks or maybe months. To me, honestly, this game can be my number one game I played past year.I really hope the devs will patch the game against crashes or system-hangs.For now I will definitly recommend this game but keep in mind you might end up with the desktop view all of a sudden during an infiltration in a bandid camp. Not so pleasant as you may understand.
_childDocuments_.name: Metro Exodus

_childDocuments_.review: Metro Exodus is a good game but there are certainly places it could have been improved.The story is great and the graphics are amazing, but you've heard that before.The gameplay isn't half bad. There was tons to explore and loot. Once the game opens up it felt "fallout-ish", there were many points of interest and with many weapon & armour upgrades it was well worth checking them all out.Customising weapons was really fun, with multiple different ways to modify a weapon and certain modifications changing how the weapon played entirely. Managing equipment and keeping your gear clean was an interesting mechanic and forces you to keep track of how much gear you have & if it's a good idea to engage certain enemies.Stealth was a viable option in Metro with certain paths lead around & behind enemies so that you didn't have to engage at all. But if you play like me and want to takedown enemies then you can do so with enemies looking straight at the one you are taking down. The AI didn't seem to recognise that there mate just got clubbed and they would stand there and watch me do it with no reaction.I had a very few crashes but they were there. Couldn't figure out why. And I had a few game sessions where it didn't save so I played the same part twice.Apart from that, Exodus was pretty fun and I would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: In Metro Exodus, Artyom and a band of survivors must flee the shattered ruins of the Moscow Metro and embark on an epic, continent-spanning journey across the post-apocalyptic Russian wilderness. Explore vast, non-linear levels, lose yourself in an immersive, sandbox survival experience, and follow a story-line that spans an entire year in the greatest Metro adventure yet. [Deep Silver]

name: Spelunky 2
detailed_description: Spelunky returns in this greatly-expanded sequel to the original roguelike platformer! Meet the next generation of explorers as they find themselves on the Moon, searching for treasure and missing family. Spelunky 2 builds upon the unique, randomized challenges that made the original a classic, offering a huge adventure designed to satisfy players old and new. A Bigger and More Dynamic World, with So Much to See and Do Spelunky 2's world is even denser than the one in the original game, offering many more areas, characters, traps, and items, as well as new ways to interact with them (and for them to interact with each other). The world has expanded in other ways, too, with branching paths and multi-layered levels adding a third dimension to the classic 2d platforming. Animals can also be tamed and ridden. And dynamic liquid physics create new challenges and make the world feel extra reactive and alive. Build a Community, Make Friends Back in Base Camp, characters you unlock will mill about and relax between runs, offering encouragement and advice. As you explore, your camp will expand and develop into a thriving little community to welcome you whenever you need a break from exploring. While there, you can also access shortcuts and practice your moves in safety. The Game is Yours to Explore Spelunky 2 is not just about 'getting good and beating the game' - more than that, it's an endlessly replayable playground to experiment in and find your own way, creating stories against the backdrop of an expansive, deeply-interactive world filled with secrets. The more you play, the more the game becomes yours! Key Features, Summarized: A Bigger World with all new areas, monsters, traps, and items! An Extra Dimension is added by allowing players to access a second layer behind the normal playfield. The second layer might contain treasure rooms, hidden passages, and other special places. Multiple Routes Through the Game will add variety and give players more ways to personalize a run. Find and Ride Mounts (like turkeys!) that have special abilities. Enemies may ride mounts, as well! New NPCs that you can help, hurt, or ignore… to make each run feel even more like a unique story. Variations and Changes to Classic Spelunky Concepts like shops and ghosts that will make veteran players rethink their strategies. Improved Liquid Physics allow water and lava to move and pour realistically, which drastically affects the playfield (and looks cool) Deadly Poison and Curses can be inflicted on players and enemies alike. Build a Permanent Home at Base Camp as you do runs and explore the caves. Improved Lighting and Special Effects are paired with richer visual and audio design. Deeper Mysteries that may require a community effort to unravel. Possibly More Eggplants

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best platformer roguelike games of all time. I say platformer first for a reason as all the gameplay eventually boils down to that core genre. It rewards creativity and perseverance more than any other game out there in my opinion. I doubt I will see every consequence or outcome that this game has to offer. Every movement of every object and enemy is variable given context of your circumstance. Be prepared for anything and you'll still be surprised.

_childDocuments_.review: I sort of recommend this after a few hours of play, because I had an awesome time with it. But, putting it succinctly, here's what you can expect:If you loved Spelunky HD, you will probably like this game too. It's more of the same action, with some of the old stages, traps and enemies returning and a host of new ones as well. Plenty of new items and stage mechanics too, more keys and such. I enjoyed Spelunky a lot, even with its sometimes arbitrary moments of death.If you disliked Spelunky HD, you probably won't like this for the same reasons you disliked the first one. So, consider that if you have any experience with its predecessor and had a bad time with it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an amazing follow up to the original Spelunky. I recommend you play that game first, but it is your choice. There are many changes from the first game to this one. While there are some similarities, the game is wildly different from the original. (Mild Spoiler about areas) Spelunky 2 still has the Caves, the Jungle, the Ice Caves, and the Temple, but they also have new levels like Volcana and Tidepool. This game will offer more than the original Spelunky and will challenge everyone in new ways that the original never could. Bats are still just as deadly though.

_childDocuments_.review: There's something about this second entry that just didn't jive with me. Maybe it's the soundtrack, maybe it's the subtle change in overall tone, but this one, although shinier and new, felt more punishing, and not in a fun way. The joy of moving through the levels feels like it's an afterthought rather than a centerpiece for some reason. More was added, but it turns out Spelunky didn't need more, it was perfect the first time.

_childDocuments_.review: The design of the game, completely contradicts how it is meant to be played. Spelunky 1 you had to plan out your moves as you went, the enemies and traps were well thought out and well placed, designed to be difficult but be beaten and the game was good because of it. Spelunky 2 throws unfair ♥♥♥♥ at you just to do it, just a big screw you, there was literally nothing you could have done to save yourself. Enemies and traps are more abundant, not designed to be difficult, designed to be ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, but the same rules of Spelunky still apply. So if you get hit one time by any of the dozens of enemies crammed in a tight space then you are dead. Most times they don't give you an out, it's a "here we go I guess" type of situation that ends in you dying 90% of the time. That is bad design. I bought it, played it nearly 2 hours, then promptly refunded it months ago. Spelunky 1 does many things better and is leagues better than this.

_childDocuments_.review: As of Today I have officially gotten the true ending of the game and wow, was discovering all the secrets of the game easily the greatest gaming experience I have experienced in my entire life. Every secret I found would leave me gasping with a giant smile on my face as I discover a new area, NPC, or item. This game is HARD, but not unfair, even if it feels like it sometimes. Me calling the first area ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ 50 hours ago has transformed into me breezing through the first area with little trouble. The game only rewards you more and more the longer you play it. $20 is a steal for the amount of content, secrets, and time I will continue to sink into this game. You are doing yourself a genuine disservice if you hold off on purchasing because you aren't sure if it will be worth it. Going in blind was magical, and I hope other players will feel the exact same way I did when I sacrificed my first Present.Oh, and ♥♥♥♥ THE ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ MOLE ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ DUDE.

_childDocuments_.review: Busted controls, enemy hitboxes don't line up, multiple ways to break the very rudimentary boundaries between 'blocks'. Sure, I'll keep playing it, but I wouldn't recommend it to anyone due to the ability to loose all of your progress in a single hit from one of many overly broken enemies that you stand no chance against if you're even a little unlucky.So many additions and changes have been made to this game that it doesn't even feel like the classic spelunky anymore. Borrowing the Spelunky IP to create a 'Spelunky 2' was a horrible idea, the game would've worked just as well as a standalone under its own marketing and design scheme.
_childDocuments_.name: Spelunky 2

_childDocuments_.review: The first stage(Dwelling) is my problem with Spelunky 2. I enjoy most of the game greatly; the gameplay is as fantastic as ever(with maybe some questionable hitboxes) and while most of the areas are harder than stuff in the first Spelunky they feel good and manageable. Visuals and music are both fine though music especially doesn't really hold candle to the first game. The rest of the audio is great with various sound effects mixing perfectly.But yeah that Dwelling sure is a doozy. It's just too much in too small of a space and playing it I feel less like I'm powering up to face the meat of the game and more like I'm trying to endure past a massive speed bump(at the very start of the game!). There are just so many gotcha-style enemies and traps that the game keeps spamming. It takes too much effort and patience simply to get through let alone gain some advantage/actually building an interesting run that I'm exhausted getting out of it.And it's one thing to have this intense of a stage later in the game when the player can prepare for it; get some advantage to exploit against the worst stuff. Those stages are here(haven't explored the game at all fully; I have beaten it once in a full run) but as the first stage Dwelling is kinda miserable. There is so much variety and secrets in this game but I'm being slowly drained by the first area and it's such a shame.Now all that said I'll keep trying and maybe with more time I'll start to understand it better. But for now I don't see it and at 20 hours and with a pretty deep understanding of the core mechanics from the first game it sure feels like I should not have to be spending so much time and effort just starting a run. There is some other stuff in the late game I could praise/complain about but in short it is pretty good once you get there; way WAY better than the beginning.EDIT: Welp I gave myself up until 100 hours to beat the Yama equivalent of this game(so not the extra secret boss), didn't get it done and then gave myself more time. Got the kill at 121 hours and now am done with this game for a good long while if I ever play it again at all. Dwelling is still IMO by far the worst stage in the game even with the balance changes; largely because of how tedious it is; but it is more manageable now. On the whole I still greatly prefer Spelunky HD but I'm sure for people who wanted an even more hardcore instakill experience Spelunky 2 delivers that in spades. For me the added bs does sway the balance of the game to a point where it's just too much for me; even now that I've gotten decent at it. The gameplay/destruction is still fantastic though and carries the mediocre bits well enough which kept me going; but I never got past that frustration and as such am keeping this review negative.
_childDocuments_.name: Spelunky 2

_childDocuments_.review: wow, this is a phenomenal gameok, so after writing a few reviews i learned that it REALLY isn't for me but this game is so amazing that i'd feel like i'm doing it a disservice by not reviewing it.when i first played spelunky, i failed, i triumphed, i learned, but most importantly; i died, a lot. the thing about spelunky is that it does not hold anything back, and i was not dissapointed to learn that the sequel is very much the same, but even harder. this game can manage an incredible balance between being extremely difficult and yet fair. through my hours of playing and countless deaths, maybe once or twice i felt like a death wasnt entirely my fault. enough with the basic overview, let's see what's changedchanges for the worsei don't want to end this review on a sour note, so we'll get the things i didn't like about this game out of the way first.first of all, the music.spelunky 2 expands on nearly every single thing that spelunky 1 put on the table, more enemies, more areas, and many more ways to find yourself dead. the only thing that it didnt expand on was the music. the first game had maybe 4 tracks per area that would each have a random chance of playing so you dont have to listen to the same song every time you die. i think this is a great thing, and i was slightly dissapointed to see that it didn't appear in the sequel. the music is still wonderful, don't get me wrong, and maybe it's a little nitpicky, but i don't really know the reason for this change.second of all, the lag.this game is beautiful. the effects that appear are amazing and make for a great and immersive experience. however, if you have a low end pc they might be an issue for you. i dont run an amazing setup, i play most of my games on a laptop and i usually don't get lag or graphical issues. however, i noticed that in dark levels and levels with liquid the game would slow down to a crawl. a day or so later a patch came out that made the game feel much less _childDocuments_.review: Some would describe Spelunky HD as the perfect game, and I would agree. So then, how can you possibly improve upon perfection? The team found a way.Spelunky 2 features much of the same gameplay loop the previous entry had, yet adds variety and player agency by having options for the zones the player can head through. While Spelunky HD had a linear game from mines-jungle-ice caves-temple, Spelunky 2 has a split path from the Dwellings (zone 1) and the boss fight of zone 4. This isn't the only innovation however, as the area between the character select and core gameplay features a hub where you can interact with characters that have been unlocked, each with their own personalities. An improvement over the last game's characterisations (which had no interaction and they were all named after their predominate colours).These aren't the only improvements though, as much of the game has been refined, better balanced, and more variety to objectives, as there are mini stories one could progress through the game. For example, one can meet a vampire hunter locked in the lave area, and meet him later when you confront the vampire, and a few more times for a small arc.Every death in Spelunky still feels like it was a learning experience, and the same holds true for the most part in the sequel, although there is the occasional sky bombing mole that you couldn't possibly see.Ultimately though, Spelunky 2 shows what a great sequel can be, and definitely worthy of carrying on the Spelunky name.

_childDocuments_.review: Spelunky 2 is a masterpiece.The typically fair, but brutally challenging randomness of the generated maps, plus the endless interactions this game has, will provide you with endless goals to strive for. The difficulty is somewhat dynamic with multiple endings, and multiple zones to choose from along your way, each with their own unique enemies, traps, npcs, items, and even bosses! With it's ultra responsive controls, combined with smooth animations, navigating through the different environments feels perfect, and everything you do, purposeful.As you learn how enemies move, traps work, and most importantly: how to utilize your whip and items you find, you'll eventually find yourself at the victory screen feeling more accomplished than ever. The only thing that might steer you away is it's extreme difficulty. Don't let it's charming nature and sprite-work fool you; nearly everything in this game is designed to end your life if you aren't careful. Despite how much fun the game is, if you take it too seriously it'll piss you off. You'll call the developer things you have never even heard of before. Sometimes though, your death is so spectacular that it feels like a win, especially if you can use shadow play or something to record the moment to share with your friends later.  I highly recommend that if you are getting particularly frustrated to simply take a break. I often find that my best runs are the first one of the day, or after a long rest. The dwelling is also the most difficult zone in my opinion, so if you can get past 1-4, you can beat Tiamat. Also, don't be afraid to read guides and watch other players. There is no way any one player could figure out everything in this game. I even suspect as of the time of this review, that there may still be secrets left.So grab your hamter or grab your friends and journey into the forever shifting rabbit hole.Good Luck, and may Kali be pleased with you.

_childDocuments_.review: In a vacuum, this game is easily good enough to get a thumbs up. The problem is, that for newcomers and fans of the original alike, my advice is "Your better off sticking with the original."Basically, there are 2 things that differentiate this game from the original. One good, one bad. Sadly, the bad outweighs the good.The good is that there is a branching level path. At the end of World 1 and World 3, there is a split in the path, so you can proceed to worlds 2a, 2b, 4a or 4b to bring some variety to the table.The bad thing is that the game is predictable. The original gave you  a grab bag of different tools to gather from the shop, which made each run feel different from the last as you improvised your way forward.Those tools are still present, but there are new features you can consistently rely on. Every level has a dog and a ghost pot, which optimally you just carry to the end of the level for extra health, and extra money respectively. But you can only hold 1 item at a time, which makes this tedious. And even worse if you want to grad another holdable item to bring with you. Sometimes, there will be a golden idol in a trap, that you also want to bring to the exit or shopkeeper, which again, just makes the errand running back and forth worse.Levels 1-2 will have either the udjat eye, another carry item from A to B quest, or wild turkeys. 1-3 will have the other scenaria. Wild turkeys can be bombed or otherwise cooked for extra health, or ridden to enable a double jump and slow falling until they take too much damage and die. Then when they die, you bomb them for extra health. If you're feeling adventurous, you can kill turkey fetish man to grab an extra turkey and some extra treasure. You really shouldn't give him the turkeys though, as they're just more useful than his rewards.The really big problem with the turkeys is that they largely invalidate many of the items that you would ordinarily have to rely on. The double jump means you need to use far fewer ropes, or the climbing glove, and straight up don't need the spring shoes. The slow falling renders the cape redundant unless you switch mounts or your turkey dies. And since you have access to these every run, the items they invalidate rarely have time to shine. Oh, also, the spike shoes don't work while you're on a turkey.The game is still a tough as nails fun roguelike platformer. But the predictability really kills the strengths of the roguelike genre. The original did not have this particular issue. Both will kill you a lot though, in a mix of fair and unfair manners. I want to say Spelunky 2 is substantially harder, but it's been long enough since I played the original that I can't say for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say? This game is just about the best possible sequel to Spelunky we could've asked for. Spelunky 2 takes the formula from the the first game (Spelunky HD that is) and refines it down to the best possible version it can be. The movement is extremely fluid, The whip feels better than ever (especially backwhipping) and the game overall just feels so satisfying to play and learn. There's a real sense of reward as you get good enough to discover each subsequent area, and almost the entire roster of enemies and items all feel unique and fun to fight/use.I can't gush about this game enough, especially if you have friends to play it with, as it offers a different and hilarious experience. My first few hours in this game were with friends and I think that's the best possible thing you can do to get yourself into the game. Discovering all the game has to offer and laugh out loud at all the moments that you could have never predicted.The great thing about this series is 99% of all things that go wrong are the player's fault, no matter how ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ they may seem. This game is all about observing what's ahead, then planning out your approach. One mistimed jump or careless charge forward could lead to you getting combo'd to death. You'll experience various deaths and other happenings that you can just sum up as "getting spelunky'd" but despite all that, the vast majority of things in the game still have player-dependent outcomes. Which is why it feels so rewarding to play and progress.I also should talk about the music. Spelunky HD had some BANGIN tracks and this game is no different. Definitely more atmospheric than HD, but the thing is there is only one long track for each area that dips in and out of each level. In HD, there were multiple different songs that could play for each of the 4 levels in an area which gave some variety, but even without that, Spelunky 2 has some great music.Lastly, going for 100% achievements is certainly a grind. But despite the insane difficulty of it, it was actually one of my favorites to date. I got all my friends into this game at the same time so there was a very organic learning curve that we all went through at the same time which gave me more of a drive than normal to complete such a hard game. Definitely worth it if you're willing to put in the time, especially for some of the harder achievements where you're pretty much at the mercy of having good spawns and the right items in the shops.Overall this game is well worth full price and then some. Especially if you're going for completion, you'll learn the ins and outs of every area, enemy, item, and pretty much every interaction in the game. You'll master advanced tactics like bomb chucking and ledge whipping, and even get good at speedrunning just for good measure. Spelunky 2 is the full package and is a blast any way you look at it. 9.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Update 14/04/2021: Revised my review from Negative to Positive.Initially when I bought Spelunky 2, it had no Windows 7 compatibility. While I understood the decision by the developers not to support an old OS, I was bummed out not being able to play as a Windows 7 user. Luckily a patch was soon released by the community, and I was able to play the game. Still, as the devs pointed out, "any future patch may break Windows 7/8/8.1 compatibility". Therefore, I couldn't recommend Spelunky 2, as a warning to others still using an older OS.Having now played 80+ hours, I want to revise my review. The game never broke, and it is better than Spelunky 1 in almost every aspect. It's more dynamic, bigger, and a bit more difficult (which is a plus). There is a lot to explore, especially in terms of the end-game. While reaching and beating the main boss might be fairly difficult, it is nothing compared to some of the very specific achievements, such as entering the Sunken City. And even though this is a challenging, sometimes brutal game, it almost never feels unfair. With the rare exception, dying is always the result of a mistake you made, making it a truly rewarding experience to finally reach one of the several endings. If you enjoy easy-to-learn, difficult-to-master games, Spelunky 2 should be right on top of your list.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game, but don't play this if you're expecting a typical rogue-like.This game demands a ton of attention from the player, as practically anything can end your run.The strongest point of the game is its unique learning curve: there's so many interactions and techniques that can change the way you play, and learning all of them feels like you're really mastering the game. It's a feeling you'll find in very few non-competitive games. (unless you're a speedrunner, that is.)The sense of progression, however, isn't going to be everyone's cup of tea. Newer players (especially those new to the series as a whole,) will often find themselves dying repeatedly until they've gained their bearings, which can be an incredible mental-hurdle to overcome. I know that it's cliche at this point, but I'd actually compare this 'difficulty'/'learning'-curve to that of Dark Souls (provided you didn't power-level and cheese everything lololol) as, the majority of the challenge can be erased with clever planning, mechanical-familiarity, and skilled execution.Overall though, playing this game is an experience you'll find almost nowhere else. Especially not with the quality that these games provide. I highly recommend this game, so long as you're masochistic enough to survive the learning curve.

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about Spelunky 2.I played the original Spelunky a LOT back in the day and also played quite a bit of Spelunky HD. I'm definitely not someone who is new to the series and so I do have a certain understanding about what Spelunky offers. In my opinion, the previous games were really about risk management. Once you learned the various things the procedural generation would throw at you, runs became a game about weighing up risk and reward. It was inevitable you would make mistakes, so you were constantly preparing for the future. For instance, should I go for that gold in that risky area that I've learned is dangerous, or do I play it safe and continue on? etc etc.Spelunky 2 is frustrating and not in a good way and I think it's due to the fact that the fundamental risk/reward is unbalanced.Early on in a run mistakes are too easily punished. There are enemies that will effectively one hit kill you because they will stun lock you (lizard, rock dog). There are enemies who are just straight up not fun to engage with (mole). There are enemies that will give you status effects that will last forever and effectively end a run with 1 hit (scorpion). 3 of these enemies can appear in the first 4 levels.This makes me way more risk averse than in the previous games. Health, for instance, is really devalued. A lot of enemies will do 2-3 damage to me. You may as well not risk saving the dog or killing turkeys because it's not going to do much to help given you can get severely punished.Given the game is about WHEN you make mistakes and not IF you make mistakes, having mistakes so severely punished early, makes runs feel really inconsistent and it makes the latter levels not as nerve wracking like in the previous game. (which WAS fun).In my mind, the early game was about gathering money and items. But here, it really feels like a slog, trying to avoid all risk entirely so you can get to the fun bits of the game. The mounts and the cave system (you can enter door ways mid way through a level to reveal caves behind the map) are surface level at best and at worst take away from the game. In my opinion, mounts will just get you killed. They move too fast. You cannot grab rope or ledges. They will do moves that will just kill you (the axolytol teleporting into walls for example). I basically just avoid mounts which is a problem because it is one of the few things that makes this game different from Spelunky 1Entering caves midway through a level will just get you kill because enemies can spawn in door ways.  This brings me onto another big issue with the game.The beauty of these games is that when you die, it's your fault. But for some reason in this game, I feel a lot of the deaths are more to do with the game than me being bad.Hitboxes for enemies feel tiny. I have seen my characters sprite overlap a lizards sprite when jumping on it and it did not count as a kill.Cave doorways will sometimes have enemies spawn there. You cannot see this when entering a cave. This makes the new additional mechanic basically a lucky dip of whether you'll take damage or not.Stun locking enemies. Okay, I made a mistake, but do deserve to lose 4 -5 health?Aesthetic features hiding parts of the game. Okay I understand that traps should be hidden, but there are walls and background features where it's unclear what is part of the level and what is part of the background (ocean level in particular). When you are making split seconds decisions to jump on things, that is a bit of a problem, since your lizard brain doesn't register these as part of the level.The first 4 levels are frustrating and lack variation. Level variety is actually lacking quite a bit. Random modifiers to levels (like dark levels etc etc) seem really few and far between. Things are far more formulaic than they were before.The addition of branching paths is odd because some branches are far easier than others, so you tend to just take the easy branch and never visit half the content in the game. (unless you are actively searching for it (which you will do if you want to an exploratory run)).Later levels are easier than the earlier ones even without items.The inclusion of the olmec boss battle half way through the game is so bizarre. You effectively wait 2 - 3 minutes half way through a run to get to the next level. Very frustrating. I have got 15 hours out of this game. It's definitely good value for money. The core spelunky experience is still there, it's just not as refined as the previous incarnations. I (hopefully) imagine that this will be refined during the lifetime of the game. This is a game that doesn't do much to the Spelunky formula. I was expecting something a bit more revolutionary rather than evolutionary. Regardless of that, I would have still recommended it, but in it's current form I just find it so much more frustrating than the previous games.I want to be fair to the game because I do really like Spelunky and will always be excited to see what they do next, so maybe I am being too harsh!

_childDocuments_.review: Just like Spelunky HD, but with more content, improvements and deaths!Spelunky 2 is a roguelike platformer, a very challenging one at that.You make your way through different areas, each containing various deadly traps and enemies that can end your run in an instant if you're not careful or prepared. Every death can be frustrating, especially when it happens out of nowhere (Spelunky moment) but with knowledge and new discoveries comes confidence. What might have made you panic or anxious before, not knowing how to overcome it, is now only just a small problem in a bunch of other complications.The improvements are quite nice, like better graphics, more precise movement and local/online multiplayer (Co-op/PvP).Though if you're going for 100% completion you probably will be playing alone most of the time since a lot of the achievements require you to play non-seeded singleplayer runs.It is an unforgiving game that will actively try to kill and break you, but once you know everything and are confident enough it will become a rewarding experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Satisfying, tight fun. I can't stop, run after run. And I'm making progress at an absolutely glacial pace. I am horrible at this game. I feel like I spend too much time in the first area. It's not so much that this first area is overtuned, but that it really does wear you down unless you are pitch perfect. Sometimes you encounter few obstacles and sometimes it's harder than the second levels. The second levels, which in a surprising number of cases, do not allow a single mistake lest your goal was to be instantaneously one-shot. And I'm not angry. I am disheartened, because dying means, of course, you have to start from the beginning, which I'm not against, but I am never thrilled to do the same first-area chores over and over again. Chores like: juggling an ever-growing list of fragile luggage down through the winding tunnels, dropping these cats, and dogs, and ghostly jars, and keys every five steps to deal with the dirty, evil lizards and the hundreds of spiders and snakes that jump out of pots, and- OH the millions of bats that you must have the most patience with. And among all this, the path is so staggered that you get an intense weariness, claustrophobia even, repetitive strain, and then you die.It's okay. You die. That's the game. The game is to die. Maybe I will one day beat Spelunky 2.Update: Somehow ended up as my GOTY which is either really good for Spelunky or really bad for this year in video games.

_childDocuments_.review: Really wanted to like this game but there are so many quality of life and gameplay issues that make it near miserable to play at times. The Spelunky moments can be hilarious. When something blows up off screen and takes out enemies or triggers traps in fun "physics" ways is when Spelunky shines. The art style is great, music is fitting, enemies fit their respective biomes and are interesting as each has a different strategy to engage.The problems:The primary weapon being the whip is horrible. If you have online game articles talking about how "back-whipping" is how you should be playing then there's a problem.Speaking of whipping, why is attack and pickup the same key? In a game where NPC's are the most dangerous characters in their ability to kill your run and are so easily aggro'd, picking up an item from them shouldn't be a liability. This along with not killing your damsel or ghost jar.Speaking of the ghost : why does a game named after discovering and exploring caves hate exploration so much? A 3 minute timer before the ghost comes does nothing but rush new players and inhibits any exploration. Break the ghost jar? Sure, reward greed with risk. Attempt to explore and learn the game? Get rewarded with death. The concept, style, lore, secrets, variety of levels, "Spelunky Moments" = 10/10Gameplay: 2/10.

_childDocuments_.review: A good roguelike is harsh, but fair. You die a lot, but each death teaches you something you can use to do better next time.Spelunky 2 is not a good roguelike.Yes, your skill matters and you'll do better as you keep playing. But your success in any given run is far more dependent on luck than on anything you can do as a player. No matter how well you play, most of your runs will end because the level generator screwed you over.Some people enjoy that sort of thing. I don't. I kept playing because I'm a stubborn completionist who will pour hours into a task I don't enjoy just to say I "won".A few of the standout issues:- Wonky level generation. Impassable lava pits, self-destructing Kali altars, key items trapped behind multiple layers of walls, lethal traps that can hit from off-screen, "drought" runs that leave you without useful items or shops, etc.- Absurd stunlock that forces you to twiddle your thumbs while your character is slowly tortured to death.- Wonky collision detection, especially with falling objects. I've had multiple runs ended because my feet touched a falling object. Cue damage and stunlock.- A bizarre difficulty curve that places some of the toughest enemies and traps in the very first section of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: When reviews call Spelunky 2 "more Spelunky," they don't make it clear that this is really "more Spelunky." It expands in every way, including many more enemies and perils, many more tile sets and environments, but that's just the start. The secret areas require more effort to find and reach. The secrets go on much longer, making a "true" run far more perilous than the original game, as well as longer. Branching paths mean there are more settings with their own unique threats you have to choose from. You now will have to beat the equivalent of three bosses just to finish a normal campaign run, and more to get a "truer" run.It is like learning Spelunky 1 all over again, with a higher ceiling for what you'll have to absorb.It's a brilliant game where you'll die over and over.And it'll be your fault.And it'll still be fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun for a while, especially if you're familiar with the original, but you're also more likely to notice how much content is rehashed from the original (i.e. basically everything, making it feel more like a Spelunky 1 expansion pack). While the new content and plentiful secrets are generally pretty exciting and entertaining, the still-poor platforming physics and hitboxes will slowly erode away your enjoyment, as will the decision of the developers to focus more on funny death potential than quality of life (every throw of the dice in the gambling den threatening to either damage you when it falls on your head or get you murdered by the bouncer if they land one pixel outside the door, shopkeepers and NPCs becoming aggroed as soon as you enter the level by procedurally generated objects damaging them or their goods before you can take one step, teleporting enemies that can telefrag you no matter how much health you've stockpiled), the sad part being that many if not most of these problems were imported from Spelunky 1 and were intentionally left unfixed for the funny Twitch clips.Of course, the new content has plenty of its own problems, with enemies too fast to reliably hit with the floaty, momentum-lacking jumping controls, enemies that damage you as soon as they see you regardless of how far you run away, and progression-necessary rooms and items that are generated in locations unreachable without using all of your resources and simultaneously angering instakilling NPCs (or they might as well be, as taking most damage stuns you long enough for most enemies to stunlock you to death no matter your health) for the rest of the run. Overall not the worst roguelite on the platform by any means, but a very disappointing follow-up that doesn't improve on its predecessor in any meaningful way and seems more concerned with producing funny clips for streamers that it personally calls out in the hopes they will generate more buzz for the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Clunky controls, non-intuitive gameplay, false difficulty, extremely repetitive.  Controls are sketchy for picking things up + riding things.  Leads to multiple attempts for what should be very simple level navigations.  You can get a turkey mount - kinds fun?  But turns out double jumping on an turkey and trying to duck/enter a tunnel seems to work like 20% of the time for some reason.  Want to pick something up?  Better hope it isn't buggy or just hop off, pick it up, get back on.Difficulty... you can be doing extremely well (lots of health built up) and there are multiple ways the game will random you to death (essentially stunlocking you). _childDocuments_.review: While there are a lot of things that I do like about this game, there are just too many things that I don't like about this game to actually give it a thumbs up recommendation. For one thing there isn't a ton that differentiates it from its predecessor, the stuff that was added feels pretty inconsequential and are mostly in service of making the game harder than its predecessor, and while there's nothing inherently wrong with wanting to make the game harder, the way that Spelunky 2 was made harder wasn't an improvement in my eyes. The original Spelunky is a hard game, but it was hard in a way that made you feel like the fault of dying was your own and that you could overcome the game by learning more about it, cheap deaths were rare and the difficulty was more satisfying, but Spelunky 2 doesn't feel like that, there are a lot more cheap deaths and a lot more instances where you feel like you were put in a situation where there was nothing you could have done differently that wouldn't have resulted in your death, there were a lot more cheap deaths.Spelunky 2 is also missing some key usability features. In the original Spelunky upon start up you had a quick start option which would start the game using your last used setting, and allowed you to skip all the menus and other stuff and get playing right away. Spelunky 2 doesn't have this, so you are forced to go through the menus each time even if there is nothing you are changing from the last time you played it.To me, there just isn't enough of an improvement over Spelunky to really recommend Spelunky 2, and in some aspects it feels like a downgrade. If the only thing you were looking for was a more difficult Spelunky then you've got a new game, but for everyone else, just stick with Spelunky.

_childDocuments_.review: An intensely difficult sequel to an already difficult platformer, Spelunky 2 goes the way of Super Mario Bros: The Lost Levels by demanding the player implement every skillset they've learned in the previous title and then some. _childDocuments_.review: The local co-op experience is unplayable. The camera follows P1 and only P1, so other players can easily fall off camera and die. _childDocuments_.review: Spelunky 2 is interesting to talk about a few years later after 100%ing it. This is a sequel that does a lot right but adds a lot that just adds frustration in many scenarios, but is overall a great experience.To get things out of the way the "community" aspect in the trailer is literally just seeing all the playable characters you unlock walking around nothing more.This game is structured similarly to HD but adds a lot more shop variants, areas/alt paths, npc interactions, and different secret areas. a lot of these add way more gameplay variety and run choice but some choices are just straight up better than others. IE: Vlad's cape, going to Tidepool in many cases, etc etcThis game does give even more player choice via learning skips and exploits, such as being able to skip the entirety of the requirements for the hard mode ending if you're really good at jetpack movement.The biggest negatives I can give this game are how some items were changed + a late game area: Cosmic Ocean...Jetpacks and other backpacks that are electronic/ will ignite and explode dealing 10 damage to you, this wouldn't be that crazy if it weren't for the fact that lava as a fluid is very fickle and unpredictable in many scenarios. The real offender in this case is the hazards in Neo Babylon, but are entirely dodge-able. This is just a skill issue on my part but it can be quite annoying to acquire a great item for a heavy cost/risk just to instantly lose it. This sorta leads into Cosmic Ocean and a few other area caveats.Cosmic Ocean IS designed as the ultimate challenge, but being screwed over time via a single mistake, whether it be poison or curse status and NOT be able to remove it ever in this zone is poor design. You can often be boned without the Kapala (item that lets you heal via blood) and just have a slow agonizing trickle down.The only other area in the game that can often be straight up unfair is Volcana in a singular instance. When using the drill to reach the castle the lava flow the drill impacts can often leave you just... waiting.... sometimes you can't even get through and have to give up on going to the final area if you don't have enough bombs. This rarely happens thankfully due to some restructuring of level generation in patches.Despite these two area negatives this is a great game with so much depth, my only biased negative that isn't gameplay related is that HD's soundtrack, which included easter egg songs and multiple tracks per area really added to the run variety and general vibe.TLDR; Fantastic game but lacks in many areas compared to its precursor.
_childDocuments_.name: Spelunky 2

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the difficulty push you away. _childDocuments_.review: I tried to enjoy the game with my partner but just couldn't. The stun after being hit is so long that if you make a mistake you normally just die. You get hit because the attack range is weird, then you bounce like 10 ft., hit another enemy or trap, bounce again, get hit by the first enemy again and now you're dead. I can't tell you how many times I dropped down to a lower level to immediately get hit by 2 separate arrow traps and then die to some random enemy. Also being able to hit your partner is terrible since the hitboxes aren't great and you bounce like crazy and just end up dying over nothing. I enjoyed the first spelunky, I hate this one. Sorry not sorry.
_childDocuments_.name: Spelunky 2

_childDocuments_.review: If you thought the first one was fun, prepare to enjoy what simultaneously feels like the same game AND new experience at the exact same time. I mean this in the absolute best way possible. This game keeps everything that was amazing from the first game, while adding so much new content to keep you playing for hours. This game demonstrates how sequels should be made.
_childDocuments_.name: Spelunky 2

_childDocuments_.review: It handles like it's predecessor with some minor hitbox changes to enemies and the whip. The art style has been changed up a bit to be a bit more crisp. There's more variety to enemies and levels and there are a whole bunch of new characters to unlock. Controls feel smooth and responsive.I won't claim to be the best at the game but, this game wants to kill you with haste. It has a tendency of wanting to stunlock and kill you for a simple mistake. For certain hits, you stay down for a while and get knocked back a fair bit, which can trigger enemies that remove the remaining HP within seconds. There are also certain scenarios where the level generator decides to force you to use a bomb or force you to take damage.I'd still recommend it, just not for everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are coming from Spelunky HD, Spelunky 2 has not changed the mechanics or formula, but adds an overwhelming amount of new content. New items, mounts, places, and monsters. This results in plenty of refreshing fun if you are finding Spelunky HD stale. In my opinion, Spelunky 2 is the perfect predecessor, and a must-buy for any fan of Spelunky HD.For any player coming in blind to Spelunky 2, prepare to die a lot. And then die a lot more. Spelunky 2 is an amazing game with a great amount of depth (pun not intended) that might catch you off guard. As the hardest platformer I have played, plenty of deaths that will feel unfair at first. As you learn the game, you will realize it is your fault 90% of the time. Bottom Line: If you are looking for a roguelike platformer that has charm, original creativity, and is very difficult, you should get Spelunky 2.

_childDocuments_.review: I have about 250 hours in Spelunky (the first one).  It's an amazing game.  If you are an experienced Spelunky 1 player, you will be decent at Spelunky 2 right out of the gate.  However, the movement mechanics in Spelunky 2 feel gummy compared to the first game.  In the previous game, the mechanics felt tight and reliable.  Here, they feel like you're trying to hold a bar of wet soap.  Also, the first 4 levels are too hard.  Everything is so tight and compact, making it super easy to die.  And yea, maybe I should just "get good."  However I would imagine this level of difficulty is pretty frustrating for a new player.  If I am having trouble (even after 10 hours), new players might be turned away.Those are the only reasons for this negative review.  If Spelunky 2 is your first Spelunky experience, it's worth the buy--on sale or full price.  The devs at Mossmouth did a great job, and props to Derek for coming up with such a great series.  If you're interested, read other reviews to see what's great about this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Twice as hard, but only half the fun.I put in hundreds of hours into the first game and consider it a classic. It was difficult, but after a couple dozen hours of gameplay you got most of the game down and can enjoy the real fun, being able to relax and explore each level at your leisure.  The game was cruel, but fair.Spelunky 2 is not a game that offers that experience and sadly after 89 hours of playing I've had to come to terms with that fact. The game is overly difficult, the music isn't very good, the gameplay changes from the original are practically a detriment, you never feel like you're able to really accomplish anything because of how much easier it is to die, and most importantly its just not much fun.The game never allows you to really relax or explore like in the first one, The crackhead moles on the dwelling area who you pretty much have to spend the time to kill because it takes twice as much effort to run away from them at times. The ridiculously small hitboxes of the mosquitos from the Jungle area are almost as bad as the thorny walls that you're gonna bump into with your last one or two hit points.The lavamen and the lava liquid spread from the Volcano will randomly end an amazing run in an instant. Keep in mind these are JUST the first 2 levels of a run.If these weren't bad enough you also have to now deal with unreliable hitboxes on both enemies, lava, and traps that will end a run faster than a black out. You can be just out of range on several of these and the game will still say you take the hit. Sadly ladders, ropes, and platform edges can also be unreliable and at times, especially when they count.The level design now has removed a lot of the more open exploring feel the first game had and instead has everything whittled down to maybe two paths and a few dead ends and the game feels incredibly claustrophobic and lacks a more open feel. While the original had a lot of claustrophobic design in the level layout it still maintained some open areas, several settings lack this in the sequels randomly generated map layout and it lacks variety in a lot of the maps as a whole. The Dwelling is especially hit by this.The games soundtrack is hit or miss. I loved the music in the original and while this games soundtrack does have some really nice tunes, several of them feel flat and bland. Also I was surprised that each setting now only has 1 soundtrack, where as in the first game each setting had several ones which helped create a really unique feel and was always a pleasure to listen too. But with the same soundtrack just endlessly looping until you finish the setting and move onto the next it gets pretty monotonous. Shout out to the Tide Pool soundtrack actually making me want to go to sleep -_-But the real irritation is you cannot play this game the way you played the first one. Thats an instant death. You have to practically start over and if you spent a couple hundred hours on the first one you have that muscle memory kick in and get penalized for it. Thats not exactly an easy adjustment to make :/There was an lot of anarchistic to the first game which was a lot of fun and kept you on your toes, but unfortunately this game takes that concept and gives it a steady supply of crack. There are times when you'll find out its just easier to commit suicide in a run rather that continue on and thats honestly a very depressing thing to admit. It feels almost counter productive to try to learn how the game works as I did with the first one because no matter how hard you try, this games randomness will just keep you from ever really going anywhere.I'm no slouch to Spelunky and its not easy to say that a game is too hard, and I don't want to sound like a games journalist but Spelunky 2 is way too hard. There is an amazing game inside here, but the new design approach to trying to kill you every strep of the way combined with random elements that never allow you to really relax and have fun with the game, isn't fun at all. I'm saying this after the Mole enemy changes from a few days back too.This isn't a game you can sit down and really have fun with as I did with the first one, and despite all the things in this game I really love, the new Olmec fight, the Temple of Anubis, the hidden levels within each level and the side quests, the non stop difficulty keeps me from getting to savor these moments because you can't enjoy what happened if you die a quarter second later from a Mole, or Lava, or flying saucer that got blown up across the map and ended up launched at you.Spelunky 2 needs a lot more adjustments to it than just the mole issue on the Dwelling setting. If Jesus Christ was in a world made of video games then Spelunky 2 would be both the nails and his cross.5/10
