_childDocuments_.review: Your liquid physics are all cool until you get soft-locked in a corner of a level because of a lava flow that no amount of ropes or bombs will fix.The core of spelunkly is still there, and it's still good, but jesus christ this game needs a rebalance. level generation/design is worse, with more areas being way to claustrophobic, filled with traps and enemies, and areas requiring the use of bombs and ropes. More enemies lean towards instant or certain deaths (infinite stunlocks) than the first game.I really hope this gets some patches in the future to fix these issues, or at the very least fix the enemies being right on top of doorways. there's thoughtful hard and there's exercise in futile frustration hard, and spelunky 2 is the ladder whereas the first was not this way.Edit: The later levels such as Tide Pool are shockingly better than the first one, which feels imbalanced even when the level generation dosen't suck. some minor adjustments like forcing no lava to spawn under the drill's path in volcana would be welcome and make getting to vlad's castle much less rage-inducing since the aforementioned lava has a chance to make that path suicidal.

_childDocuments_.review: I do not consider myself a masochist, but after 100%ing this game, I would need to reconsider my previous statementAfter just over 100 hours of torturous runs, ranging from killing a god who is a giant egg, trying to reach a certain mass of water in the void, to getting brainless purple children back home, this game has drained 2 months worth of my free time and filled me with regret and sorrow.I would only recommend this game to people with no social life or those with a LOT of free time who have an abundance of patience. Alternatively, if you hate yourself and have £15.49 lying around, go ahead, be my guest.Don't get me wrong, the game is great and an amazing sequel to its predecessor, but it does not make me feel content after completing, and Derek Yu should know that he's created the equivalent of waterboarding yourself until you develop stockholm syndrome.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game last October and after playing around 20 hours I got bored and put it down for over a year. Just recently picked it up again out of boredom, and after 3 weeks and 40 hours I finally beat Tiamat.  This game is a treasure if you put in the correct work and effort into it. The joy you will feel when getting deeper than you ever had is great, but that is not to say that you won't want to rip your hair out. I don't think I've ever felt such polar emotions than in this game. 99% of the time I want to throw my computer out the window and that 1% of unadulterated joy is what makes it all worth it. This game is a game that you must be willing to figure out all of its ins and outs to get your true enjoyment. Spelunky will punish you in the most brutal and unforgiving ways, but it just makes beating  it that much more pleasing. There are loads of secrets to discover (unless you're like me and just looked them all up on Youtube) and there is way more content in this game than any regular person has the capacity to get through. In all, this is not a game for everyone, but those who are up for a souls-like cartoony dungeon crawler, then go right ahead. EDIT: Finally beat Hundun after what seems like a year. . I now feel I am truly done with the gam , but I cant recommend the game more to those who are up for a challenge

_childDocuments_.review: I grew from hating Spelunky 1 to liking it a lot. it was a game that will take you a lot of time to learn, and to understand that it's hard but it's fair. Spelunky 2 is actually not very different from 1, so do expect to spend quite some time if you want to really get to know the brilliance of the game. What's really good about Spelunky 2 is that it doesn't fix what's not broken. It doesn't add what's not needed just because some believe that a sequel must be bigger, nosier, crazier. Instead, it just continues doing what it is good at, and brings in more of the same, but also different.  It's still balanced, challenging, and fair.Bottom line, it's a well made rogue-like platformer. It rewards patience, dedication, and skill. It's not very fancy, but it has a lot of variations, so it takes time to learn. It's quick, responsive, and very satisfying when you overcome the challenges.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd recommend it to anyone that loved the previous entry. I understand that 10's the majority of the market now but everyone I know that uses it didn't actually want to)Game is highly addicting and full of optional stuff. Truly branching choices add a lot to the game, and they've been ironing out some of the issues (like the first area being the most annoying for some reason, soiling the far more interesting later areas with a lot of rng). _childDocuments_.review: As a person who spent quite a few hours with Spelunky 1, I find the difficulty of this one to be pretty fair, however, people who are new to spelunky should know that this game is extremely hard and  Don't just give up and assume you suck, practice a bit everyday and you will improve.The first area has some nasty new enemies but nothing you can't handle once you learn what they do. Some people are arguing that the first area feels overcrowded with enemies and traps now because the new enemies are added on top of the ones from the original game, but I disagree, there's no more enemies per level than in the original game, there's simply more variety of them, which is clearly a good thing.The new art style is brighter and more simplified, the environments feel a bit flat at times,  , however I think the characters and creatures look generally nicer now, a good example is the cavemen or the bats. They also added some pretty nice looking lighting effects which look awesome specially in dark levels.Hilariously enough, you can see your "win percentage" on your player profile, as if anyone is gonna have a win percentage above 0,01%.Overall I just feel excited to explore this game and find all the secrets and alternate paths and what not, so far this feels like a worthy successor to the first one.

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of posting I have 197 hours for this game and all of it's achievementsDo I recommend this game?NoRight off the bat I'm going to be very honest in saying that if you haven't played Spelunky HD, or if you're someone who looks to play games for a short while and have moderate success and put it down feeling happy - this is not the game for you and there is going to be plenty for you to complain about.That's not a slight either - this game is very hard, and you're going to have to play it for awhile for you to learn most of the crucial things the game is trying to teach you, as well as for you to get comfortable finding creative ways for you to deal with an innumerable amount of unique situations you will encounter. It will be unfun for you if you only plan to play for a short while and never get to see any of the zones that go beyond the starting area of the game, "dwellings". Beyond that I have to be honest to you and say that this game at the time of posting is being patched very frequently [multiple patches a week], because there are a lot of bugs being fixed and changes being made and as requested by a large part of the playerbase. Just to name a few that I've run into: Textures in the Super Super Secret Spoiler area tend to flash and appear in and out of the game: You can't see your own score on the daily challenge leaderboard even when you press the "Me" button: at one point a sticky bomb exploded almost as soon as I put it down in the dwellings without there being any cause for it in context of what I know about this game in 197 hours. Currently at the time of posting the feature of multiplayer is not a part of the game, which was a huge selling point to me - but if it is the "only" selling point to you and you wish to play it casually I would suggest waiting. In the games current state, I can say that I've enjoyed it but the numerous bugs I've had to endure in the line to actually posting this review is been more headache, and heartache than it has enjoyment. Some people believe it adds quote "depth" to the game that the forward swing of your whip has very little utility. A bat can be coming at you from above - and you can jump and time a swing you believe to be perfect but it literally has to be the tip of the front of your whip that makes contact with something - the swinging blur of the whip reaching that point has no hurt box. But that's not even the worst part: the back end of your whip - which is a startup animation and in theory shouldn't hurt anything at all because it's a wind-up is 1000% better and has a larger hitbox and greater consistency than the front of your whip. To fully explain what I'm saying here - you will have to train yourself to turn around in many instances to hit arrows/enemies/objects with the back end of your whip because the front end of your whip can't do much at all.In summary, the games difficulty and harsh learning curve will be a turn-off to a lot of casual players. But even for the "hard core" playerbase in the games current state with all the issues in the game being patched and reported on a daily basis, as well as the missing addition of multiplayer: I cannot in good faith recommend this game. The constant patching for bug fixes and changes is an indicator to me that this game is not yet finished. I will update my review in the future in things change but this is a present day review and my thoughts on the game. NOTE: I have other gripes with the game such as the graining dwellings song and the lack of variation in the music that was a feature in Spelunky HD: but the soundtrack is dynamic in Spelunky 2- meaning that the song changes or transitions while keeping many elements of the base song depending on whats happening in the game. So I can understand it would be difficult for the developer team to orchestrate numerous songs for every zone because of this. Again, I could just be nitpicking, but a lot of time will be spent in dwellings- especially at the start.

_childDocuments_.review: I was extremely excited for this game! The previous Spelunky HD is one of my all time favorites, and my gold standard for modern roguelike games. I can understand that Derek Yu wanted to make his sequel more challenging, but Spelunky 2 goes way too far with it, to the point that it isn't even close to fair anymore. But to be fair, the game does some things better than its predecessor, and I wanna list some stuff off, both good and bad.There's lots of new characters! Each character has a unique kind of rope that they use, which is a nice touch. I also really like the newer character designs and the big influx of new characters to unlock. I like the new golden idol altars in zone 1 more than in the original. The giant pillar is much more manageable than a giant wild card boulder of death that could easily ruin a run by crashing into a shop or a vault far off screen from you.There are many more zones to explore this time. Not only that, there are two different paths you can take at the end of zone 1! I love that! I love the turkeys and other mounts that you can use and even keep between floors. Those are cute and I love them.There are now mini game shops that let you enter a special challenge room where you can earn money and prizes. Sweet!As for the bad things....Moles are an obnoxious new enemy that can chase you through walls and floors. I've lost count of how many times they've dropped on me from seemingly out of nowhere because I can't see everywhere at once, or I ended up stuck between a gopher and another hazard and couldn't avoid taking damage because I can't watch the the whole screen.There is a now an equivalent to the tiki trap that shows up in zone 1, and that's pretty neat! But the arrow traps are now 2 or 3 times as frequent as before. Staying on alert for them means you basically can't ever stop being paranoid about them. The first one wasn't nearly this stressful about that. Enemies are far more frequent now, and avoiding one enemy very frequently leads you straight into something else.  The first zone has an actual boss enemy that will very easily instantly kill if you aren't extremely careful, and that got old really fast. Sometimes a level will just randomly be HUGE. That wouldn't necessarily be a big problem on its own, except...The ghost in this game is much more punishing for players who want to explore a bit. And the thing is, it already WAS punishing for players in the last game. It's just even more so now. It now splits into multiple faster ghosts if you aren't quick to get out when it arrives. The previous game already didn't really give you that much freedom to explore levels, so this change seems needlessly aggressive. I could see this being a feature in a version of the game meant to challenge speedrunners, but having it in normal runs seems cruel. This game feels a lot like one of those "insane brutal challenge designed to make children cry" challenge mods made for the most dedicated fans of a game. Except that's just the standard game here. And its just not that fun to me. This would be a whole other thing if the game had a difficulty option, and this were merely the hard mode. But there isn't an option to make any of this less of a chore.I gave it my best try! But I just can't justify playing it anymore. I sank over 600 hours of my life into the previous game, and I had a blast with it. I'm putting Spelunky 2 down after 30, because it's just not worth playing any more.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm still waiting on the multiplayer, but even so, I've had a blast both playing and watching this game. It's frustrating some moments, goofy in others, and everything in-between.Spelunky 2 is a skill-based roguelite platformer that is all about managing resources, tackling deadly situations quickly, and once in awhile, some silly Rube Goldberg death. Core gameplay revolves around exploring randomly generated levels with certain guaranteed setpieces and stage themes. Players learn through experimentation (and maybe through a wiki, because some stuff is pretty obscure) and death. It's a tough game- newbies to the genre will find it hard to make it past the first few stages. There is insta-death nearly everywhere, and there are few things that can completely take that part out. You need to be decisive, deliberate, and deadly.Good luck out there, fellow Spelunkers!

_childDocuments_.review: I have over 340 hours into Spelunky HD, and it is one of my favourite games. I REALLY wanted to love this game.Spelunky 2 is a consequence of the developers mistakenly thinking people liked Spelunky solely because of its difficulty. Early levels, especially those in the Dwelling, play like Frozlunky (for those unaware, it was a Spelunky mod that could drastically boost monster rates, among many other things) levels instead of an intro section. I don't think people want 6-10 arrow traps on every level, or extremely unfair levels of stunlocking. Many people in the community have said without any exaggeration that the hardest section of the game is the Dwelling. This really shouldn't be the case. I should also point that this is being written AFTER the first patch on the Dwelling. It was even worse before.This is coupled with the fact that it feels like you're doing the same exact thing every run. The lack of variety in the early levels (which you will be spending most of your time in because of the nature of the game) makes it feel like I'm doing my taxes before playing the game each time. It lends itself to being quickly frustrating and dull.Artwork and music is fantastic, and later levels look stunning. The initial items, branching paths, and (most) of the new enemies are great. The game suffers immensely from incredibly poor design in the first few sections. I'll happily return to the game if these issues are addressed.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely horrendous in terms of balance. The very first area in the game throws 2 of the toughest enemies at you immediately, and either floor you choose past this dreaded place contains its own gauntlet of badly designed horrors of traps, secrets and enemies. A boss blocks most players from enjoying the game past the first few areas, and one of the following zones contains the spammed hardest trap in the entire game as well as all 4 of the most irritating and strong enemies in the entire game all in the same area.The final zone for standard runs also contains the perfect weakness to those who were lucky enough to find a beneficial back item, and the final boss proves almost impossible to defeat without the assistance of sticky bombs.The final secret area contains a kind of block which will instantly kill you, as well as one final hurdle of a boss that always finds a way to kill you in the most unsuspecting way possible. _childDocuments_.review: This feels more like Spelunky 1.5 than 2. The good parts of the original Spelunky are all in here. Tight controls, fast entry into gameplay, and a lot of fun treasures to play around with. The art is more refined than in the original Spelunky, and the music is good, though there aren't many song tracks in this game. The game is also nice on my 144Hz display, where I believe the original Spelunky is capped to 60 FPS.Unfortunately, it feels like there's very little innovation going on here, and instead there are simply newer and more ways to game over. The one thing I had truly hoped to see was fewer ways to meet instant-death, or better ways to recover from situations where you effectively are punched to death without being able to regain control. That didn't happen. I don't think this is just me, either. I was able to get better at, and beat, the original Spelunky. It took some luck, sure, but I felt the progression. But I'm already familiar with the Spelunky brand, so I have a baseline experience to rely on. And yet somehow I feel like it doesn't matter how much I improve at Spelunky 2, there will be something which subverts my expectations and makes me feel not that I made a mistake, but that the game was eager to punish me.I haven't had a chance in seven hours of play to really explore the new weapons or secrets, since I lose so frequently. But now with the cursed ghost jars, damsels, and mounts, and weapons it feels like I'm doing a lot of Spelunky's version of inventory management rather than playing the game. It just gets tedious, and my own time isn't so worthless to keep at it.I'd been hoping for a Spelunky 2 for a long time. And since it's quick and easy to launch the game and start playing, I find myself doing so frequently these past few days. But I am just as quick to find the exit, because I'm not having fun. I suspected as much when I first started playing, but I thought I'd give the game time to slow burn its way in. I'm regretting not following my immediate instinct to issue a refund request after the first hour, because the experience didn't grow more enjoyable over time.

_childDocuments_.review: Spelunky 2 is a game that delivers more of the same, but instead of a familiar feeling of nostalgia and fun, it comes across as frustrating. I put over 170 hours into the first Spelunky (Spelunky HD) and while it is a wonderful game, it’s definitely flawed. The way levels are generated could result in cheap deaths or irritating setbacks. Enemies flying at you from offscreen traps, shopkeepers and deities getting angry for something you had no hand in doing, all that fun stuff. While this was annoying, it was rare enough that I could still enjoy playing it. So I was excited to get my hands on Spelunky 2 and see how it improved the explorer formula.And to be fair, it does improve quite a few things. The art style is much cleaner and nicer to look at, the music is lovely. The main game has been massively expanded, with many branching paths, secret levels and new characters. Despite the fact that many enemies and level templates return from the original, it feels like this is a whole new world to explore and fall in love with all over again.At least...it would be. But all of this leads to a much more ambitious game, with many more moving parts. And unfortunately it feels like those complaints about bad room generations and cheap deaths just slipped under the radar. Worse than that, it’s more common than ever. Enemies will get flung (or fling themselves) at you at high speeds. Important NPCs and items will spawn next to a trap that destroys them before you blink. Shopkeepers and gods will still get mad, and now there’s a lot more for them to be mad about. It all leads to an experience that causes many of my sessions to end with a death that I had no control over. Definitely not an experience that makes me want to come back.It’s incredibly frustrating because there they did address criticisms with Spelunky in this game, but it all crumbles under this oversight. For example, the final level has much more forgiving moving blocks, with Spelunky’s instant-kill blocks being relegated to an optional previous level. But then they decide to put in new traps that can hurl exploding enemies at you faster than you can react. Shopkeepers stop being angry at you after a certain number of floors? Well that’s great, but why not fix the fact they can get angry at you before you even take a step in the level? The game itself is longer, with many more optional secret areas? Cool, more chances for something to go horribly wrong and ruin my run.It’s possible that all of this is an intentional design decision, and that’s why it wasn’t touched. I’ve seen plenty of players get enjoyment out of the silly ways they can die and they just “laugh it off”. But in my opinion, this kind of chaos is only a detriment to the Spelunky series, where your success directly depends on your patience and navigation of deadly enemies and traps. If you agree, then I’d stay away from this one and play the original in its place. It can be annoying at times, but not nearly as bad as this.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of reviews out there praise Spelunky as the be-all, end-all of rogulikes, the perfect manifestation of the genre that solved all problems and deserves a golden throne as the king of games. That's an exaggeration, the game is far from perfect, but it is amazing, and everyone should at least give it a try.There are plenty of people out there explaining why the game is great, so I'd like to talk about a few things I didn't expect when I picked it up, so you can ask yourself if it suits your tastes.Firstly, it's less of an action platformer and more of a side-scrolling puzzle game. The game is made out of rooms, and each room is hand crafted, meaning that it already has at least one solution built into it. Your task is to figure that solution and perform it with perfect accuracy. It's a hell lot of fun to do that, but it's a bit different type of fun than many people expect.Due to that form of challenge, the game follows a somewhat realistic approach to its logic. The infamous dart trap is a great example: it triggers when something gets near it. Once you realize that something means anything, and you can throw pots and rocks you find around, the game clicks. This is the sort of challenge you'll be facing a lot of the time.Finally, it's not a perfectly balanced game. There's some RNG involved to the events that take place, mainly due to the dumb AI of creatures populating the dungeon. They can kamikaze into you and jump into spikes, they can fall on you from off screen, there's a lot to watch out for and many things you just won't see coming. I believe this AI behavior is the only reason why you have health points in this game, as everything that's not an enemy will always kill you in one hit. This being said, having extra health often makes little difference.The biggest offender among AI are shopkeepers. They will decide to kill you for dumbest reasons, like a rodent entering their store while you're inside. This is supposedly a remnant of the previous game, but I find this memetic behavior so frustrating I'd rather they fixed it already, even if the optimal play is to always kill the shopkeepers anyway.Oh, also, "always run" is turned on by default. If you haven't played the first game, change it to walk immediately.

_childDocuments_.review: This is another one of those games that I wish Steam had a bit more of a robust reviewing system in order to properly showcase what works and what doesn't work and even a tagging systemAlso for the OG Spelunky Fellas, I've never played the original. This was 100% fresh new to me. Keep that in mind when reading this perspectiveGenerally I'd give this game a Depends out of 10There's so many rogue-likes out there these days and Spelunky 2 does an incredible job at differentiating itself from the crowd. How it does that? Well not only it's unique art style but also by being one of the most punishing and unforgiving gaming experiences I've ever had. If you're easy to rage or even somewhat moderate to it, don't come anywhere near this game playing wise. There's been so many times I've been killed due to off screen shenanigans that eventually made its way over to me and insta-killed me. Or I'm at an absurd amount of health and I get stun locked to death.So often you get killed extremely early on, nearly a good 70-80% of the time by either dying to some dumb **** or because shop screws you over and even then those 20% runs can be destroyed 19.99% of the time. So why even play this game?Because it's those 0.01% runs which are pure adrenaline pumping. Fueled to know what is truly at the bottom of the caves. This is the furthest you've ever gotten. Sweat dripping from your forehead. I've never seen this level before. I've never seen these enemies before. How do I have this many bombs and ropes?? _childDocuments_.review: Spelunky 2 is an experience inferior in every way to its predecessor. Just play Spelunky 1; unless you are the sort of challenge-addict who does eggplant runs for fun, Spelunky 2 adds nothing of value for you.Spelunky 1 was charming for the minimalism of its design and the extremism of its gameplay. The experience of being struck from an arrow-trap at the far edge of the screen and sent flying into a row of run-ending spikes was novel at the time; the consequences of errors were severe and would heavily punish careless play, but nearly any foreseen and understood threat could be avoided with only moderate platforming ability. The combination of those two traits was important: if you got stunned and sent flying, the wacky exaggerated physics meant that the consequences could range from slightly-damaging to fatal, but threats were sufficiently noticeable and telegraphed that this result was generally due to a significant and understandable misplay on the player's part, or the punishment for a 'greedy' maneuver. This also meant that the game could get away with various little clumsinesses; because the game's challenges were only moderately mechanically demanding, it didn't matter so much that some parts of the execution were awkward.  Spelunky 2 treats the game of Spelunky as though it needs no basic improvements or updates, and only needs increased difficulty. Much content is shamelessly unchanged; for someone expecting the new game to be a *new game*, navigating the same old caves with the same old enemies and even collecting the same old Udjat Eye is a disillusioning experience. As for what content is new, it uniformly departs from the old design philosophy of predictability. New enemies move more chaotically, are harder to hit, have larger and less-avoidable methods of attack, inflict crippling and difficult to remove new status-effects. Additionally, they are more-densely packed into less-open spaces, multiplying the probability that any misstep results in a wacky chain-reaction of unpreventable fatal damage, especially given that old boons like the jetpack now often become explosive liabilities instead. The final region of the game's normal route embodies this chaotic premise wholeheartedly; a bullet-hell landscape of perpetually-circling fireballs not only turns normal enemies and their corpses into high-speed projectiles fully capable of stunlocking and juggling away whatever amount of health the player has managed to accumulate, but will make cheerful pinball-game sound-effects on each impact to emphasize the whimsical unpredictability of having an exploding UFO chucked at you from offscreen. In Spelunky 1, physics-driven instant death was always a possibility, but even near the end, it was the norm for most hazards to just deal a reasonably proportionate amount of damage and then allow you to act again. In many of Spelunky 2's areas, suffering a hit and 'just' taking damage cannot really be expected.Making matters worse, the game's chaotic new portfolio of threats is not matched by any improvements in controllability. The slightest variation in D-pad input will still arrest the player's movement on ledges or ladders they had no intention of stopping against or flipping over; the climbing glove in particular frequently spells death in the game's chaotic later areas, introducing deadly undesired pauses into the necessarily-rapid navigation of constantly crushing elevators and eternally-milling fireballs, because the game still insists upon a minimalist control scheme for increasingly demanding platforming challenges; overloading the 'move left or right' control with 'also cling to the wall' just doesn't cut it when you have to sprint through a series of narrow, twisting, moving horizontal-and-vertical passages. Sometimes this insistence on control-minimalism makes very basic actions impossible; suppose an item the player wishes to pick up is located on a 1-tile-wide platform which can be descended through, but there is a rope passing through the platform. The player *cannot* pick up the item, because they cannot crouch on the platform to do so, because the crouch-input navigates the rope instead. But Spelunky 2 wears these clumsinesses with pride; mechanical awkwardness is a proud feature with a long history, not a bug to correct. While not a control scheme issue, this proud embrace of pointless problems is best exemplified by the Hired Hand. 'Rescuing' one of these 'allied' NPCs and attempting to actually traverse the dungeon with their 'help' invariably means being killed shortly thereafter by their wild, reckless attacking and throwing of objects; one learns just to not bother rescuing them, or if they are accidentally released, to simply kill them before moving on rather than to suffer their 'help'. No gameplay function is served by having a 'benefit' that is actually a strict liability, but that's just what kind of punitive-for-its-own-sake gameplay Spelunky 2 thinks it's supposed to be about. The first Spelunky was fun. This one just feels tedious. There's little joy, after having one run end due to some offscreen lava-spewing explosion, in setting off again to discover what Kaizo-style configuration of hazards will be thrown together this time. In the first game, losses felt mostly deserved and victory felt achievable with attentiveness and a *little* luck; even the alternate Hell route was enjoyable enough to both discover and to conquer without outside spoilers. In this one it's hard enough to put up with the normal game, much less embrace the even-more-random conditions dictating whether following an alternate route is feasible on a given run. So if you're a punishment-craving veteran of unforgiving precision platformers who doesn't mind intentionally-awkward controls in a game willing to punish anything less than a perfect run, go for it. Otherwise, there are other better games for sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a big fan of the original Spelunky, and put in a good 50 hours or so which is a good chunk for a game of this sort. Of course I would want more Spelunky.Spelunky 2 feels like a mod level pack or a DLC add-on to Spelunky 1.It definitely brings in tons of changes and new things, but it re-uses so much from the first game that it hardly feels like there was any form of innovation and it feels more like a rehash.The game still plays well and is as addicting as the first, but there's a lot that feels off.Difficulty: They definitely ramped up the difficulty level, making it much cheaper than the first game. I also feel like, while increased difficulty can make the game be a huge challenge to returning players - it will alienate newer players. I think it'll be harder for new players to get the hang of this game, without having played the first one.Rehash: The zones from the original game, all the enemies, all the traps, all the items return to this one. I would have preferred a "sequel" to actually do everything new. Instead we got all the exact same ♥♥♥♥ with some minor adjustments and visual changes. It feels incredibly lazy and hardly like a sequel. For a price higher than the original, I was expecting the content to be more original.Music: Spelunky classic had some great music. It was super chill, very retro style and fit the game beautifully. Its only downfall was being somewhat repetitive as there weren't many tracks for the game. Spelunky HD completely redid the music into this funky jazz style that was forgettable, had awful instrument choices, and simply wasn't enjoyable.The music of Spelunky HD is one of the only things I didn't like about that game. I found myself modding it out to be my own custom music packs instead. Fortunately, the game was easy to mod so that I could do that.Spelunky 2's music isn't quite as bad as Spelunky HD's, but its somehow even more forgettable. The soundtrack is really as generic as they come. It sounds like they just went on a site with royalty-free background music and used tracks off of there. Why they don't go back to the original musician and have Spelunky have great music again is beyond me. A lot of us are just modding the OG music back inThe music was a huge letdown, though my expectations were low after Spelunky HD.Truly horrible soundtrack once again. What a shame.Visuals: Spelunky HD looked great. Its artstyle was very charming, it had tons of color, and the environments were nicely detailed.When I first saw Spelunky 2 in the trailers, my initial reaction was "wow that's hideous."This game's artstyle is much more clean, which isn't a bad thing. What is a bad thing, is how incredibly washed out and desaturated the visuals are. When Spelunky HD was so colorful, I don't know why they thought it was a good idea to make this game look as drab as it does. You can find comparisons online of the original game's maps versus this one's and its night and day. The jungle is the easiest example. That was my favorite zone from the first game because I found it very cozy and liked the art. On here, its just a gross washed out puke-green color. I really don't know what they were thinking with the visuals this time around.This game isn't one of those indie games where people are going to praise its visuals.Its actually a bit of an eyesore.Overall: I haven't given Spelunky 2 nearly enough time to actually give a verdict if I like the game or not.Its possible I'll end up loving it and praising it and I fully intend on playing it more.edit: Scratch that, I refunded it. I just didn't think it was good enough for the price. I'd rather play the OG again.I don't think a rehash product warrants its price point and I'd strongly suggest newcomers to buy the first one instead.I'll edit this if I change my mind, but right now the game feels like it rehashes way too much from the original and the awful music and visual art do not help its case at all.Only get this if you absolutely loved the original and want more of it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is brutal, painful, and makes me very depressed. And yet... I wouldn't trade it for anything.This game is stupidly difficult, if you are going in with no Spelunky experience it won't be easy. Your first runs will probably last less than a minute, maybe a couple minutes if you are lucky. But through each run, you will learn. It'll be the big things first, like how arrow traps work, or how the enemies function. Maybe you'll realize that if you bring that animal you found to the exit you'll gain more hp. After a little bit, you'll reach 1-2. You'll see the shop and realize the importance of money. This cycle will keep going, you making it further and further each and every time, getting better and smarter. Even if you die in a hilariously stupid manner, you'll improve. You could have the perfect run with great items and lose it, and it'll hurt. The pain never fades. Yet with every failure, you learn. You get further. And maybe, just maybe, you'll beat it. And every run, every loss, every heartbreaking failure will make the victory ever sweeter. It'll be a glorious moment in your life, but there's more. Secrets litter the game, with the primary secret being an expansive route leading to a whole new world, and a new, difficult, powerful boss. There is more secrets, and throughout the game you may see snippets of it. You can look it up, but going in blind is a very neat trip of discovery, with each step drawing you in further. This game is packed with content, with multiple different worlds hidden beneath the surface and many more challenges to find. This game is an absolute masterpiece. The controls are incredible with (most) deaths feeling like it was an error on your part. I'll be playing it for a long, long time.TL;DR: I got PTSD from playing this game, 10/10.Seriously though, this game is incredible, get it, you won't regret it, except you will regret it when you lose a great run, but regardless it'll be worth it in the end.

_childDocuments_.review: I remember when I bought the first Spelunky 3 years ago. I played the freeware Spelunky Classic, thought it was a blast, and was curious about the HD remake. I figured that I would return it after an hour and realize "Oh, it's not worth it." 150 hours later, I can say pretty confidently that it was. I'm not gonna say that it was some grand revelation, but it tweaked the near-perfect formula, while adding plenty of new features, and it came out as the truly definitive way to play the game. I'm barely an hour in Spelunky 2, and I can already feel that same process happening again. The differences between this and the original, compared to the original and Classic, are too numerous to count right now, but the heart of the core gameplay hasn't changed a bit. It still has that systemic, dynamic, risk vs. reward gameplay that the original nailed, but adding more features and tweaks to make it even better. Every single attempt so far taught me about some new interaction, new system, or new technique, and that's almost exclusively in the first area of the game. This doesn't reinvent Spelunky, but I feel like this is the new definitive way to play, just like Spelunky HD was before. I'll update the review after I've sunk more time into it, but if you're any sort of fan of the original, or just want a ball-crushingly hard roguelike to sink your teeth into, you can't go wrong with this.Edit 28 hours in: finally beat the game once with the last shortcut. can't wait to dive in for more torture tomorrow

Sad to say it's strictly worse than its predecessor, and not recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome new game, I loved the first one, love the second one too. (5h of playtime at review)I saw some people played 20 minutes and complained (with negative review) that the game is identical/should-be-a-mod of the first one: this is FAR FAR from the truth. If you liked Spelunky 1 you'll love Spelunky 2 (unless you suddenly became uninterested in challenge for some reason)I'm going to be honest it makes me sad to see negative review with ♥♥♥♥♥♥ arguments like "first one runs on my pc but not this one", "wip is smaller", or "doesn't add anything"Here is my response to those people, and to the people wondering if there is truth in it:Gameplay-wise: yes there are some differences with Spelunky 1, the wip feels a bit smaller, but it's hard to know for sure, I'm glad there are differences, it's not the same gameRequirement-wise: yes you need a better specs than spelunky 1 to run spelunky 2, but I mean 7 years between the two, of course requirement went up, it makes total sense. Would you complain that Skyrim needs better spec than Oblivion ? Content-wise: there are tons of things that have changed/have been added from spelunky 1, I haven't yet encovered everything, here is what I've seen so far : graphics (visually huge positive changes), multiple path to choose, new monster, new minibosses, new characters, gameplay changes, backrooms connecting parts of the same levels, lots of secret passage and worlds to uncover, level design is completely differentMusic-wise: completely new music, it fit the game, I don;'t know if I love it yet, I'll tell you when I reach 500h.

_childDocuments_.review: Spelunky 2 is a sequel to Spelunky which in of itself is the HD remake of Spelunky Classic. In Spelunky 2 your goal is to make it to the bottom of a perilous floor to get to the next. Each floor is procedurally generated and filled with many horrors that sometimes do 1 damage and sometimes kill you instantly. The satisfaction that comes from self-growth displayed through just a little bit more progress, or discovering a brand new thing you hadn't seen before is what makes this very challenging game special. You're going to die, over and over and over again, but more often than not you'll come away with new knowledge that will help you get to the next floor, or the next area. _childDocuments_.review: The most satisfying gameplay that, unless you can foresee the future, will still make you want to throw your controller."Spelunky 2" is a roguelike in its textbook definition: procedurally generated levels, restart fully every time you die, knowledge is the only power-up you can carry over to a new run.The story is a minor element of the game. There is enough lore to come up with a comprehensive world, but the universe is not fully explained outside of some retreads from the first game.What took me so long to consider the game "completed" is that there are multiple endings. The first two are quite straightforward and reward you with achievements, the other one is a long, LONG challenge for those who are willing to take on it. Don't let your inner completionist prevent you from having fun.The gameplay is the highlight of the game: the movement is extremely fluid, terraforming allows the player to manipulate levels in multiple ways… and there's also RNG. You will get frustrated from falling particles, bad events outside your control, and sometimes even unpleasant level generation with countless traps."Spelunky 2" offers cross-platform multiplayer and arena modes, but I haven't experimented with them much. If it sounds like your jam — prepare for co-op shenanigans.You will lose your patience with this game… and it's going to be glorious. Have fun in whatever way you'll choose.

_childDocuments_.review: Spelunky 2 is so much fun to play that the extreme difficulty almost doesn't matter. It really is one of the toughest games I have ever experienced, and normally that would be a huge barrier to my enjoyment, but the controls are responsive, smooth and satisfying, and the excellent procedural generation gives you almost infinite replayability, with a great variety of tactics and tricks that you pick up naturally as you play. Every death is a learning experience, and the game only gets better as your skills improve...while still keeping you on your toes at all times.Spelunky 2 is the best time I have had with a platformer since Sonic 2 on the Sega Mega Drive (you won't get much higher praise from me) and one of the easiest thumbs up I have ever given on Steam.

_childDocuments_.review: Spelunky 2:This game is about the rouguelike experience. Now what do I mean by that, well I believe this game has four main sections that I believe are worth discussing, Movement, Items, Level Design, and Difficulty.To start I will be discussing Movement. In terms of movement options, you have a walk, run, jump, clamber, and that's it. The movement is very simple, although this incentives the use of items, so that you will have more movement options or other various power tools at your disposal.Items: The items in Spelunky 2 have many utilities, and purposes, to start I will go over the basic items you start with bombs, and ropes. Bombs and Ropes are both items that are consumed over a gameplay session each providing different utilities, the bombs blow stuff up, whilst ropes let you climb up to higher locations. The next items are equipment, these items are applied to the player character similar to a backpack and each can provide different helpful tools to a player, for example a jetpack to fly, a cape to glide, or a power pack to power up your attacks. Speaking of attacks, the final item type is the weapons and items that you are able to pick up, these items consist of guns, weapons like boomerangs, and even magical weapons that have special properties.The level design is a short and simple discussion. The game is a roguelike and as such will have a nearly random generation for every level in the game even having special locations that will appear in certain locations if you know what to look out for, but new to the series is a choice between different locations, for example the jungle, or the volcano areas.Finally there is the difficulty, what I feel is the greatest part of this game. To be absolutely honest, this game loves to not through it's punches, and is absolutely brutal. The tutorial shows you the tools at your disposal, but the rest of the game you have to figure out how to do tasks, you have to learn so much about this game, and you are more than likely to die on your first run-through of the game, but if you stick with it, you will get good, and you will learn to overcome so many obstacles.To finish out this review, I hope you will join me on this adventure, by buying the game, as I believe this to be an excellent game, and the extra content that I chose to leave out as I believe it is a discovery when you learn how to do a lot of it, will be worth the purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: Derek Yu...You mad genius! Seriously one of my favourite roguelike platformers out there. Can't recommended it enough but with a few caveats: Firstly, if you're not that patient then there isn't much longevity for you to find solace here. Your incredible run of 20+ minutes can be wiped out just like that with one Thanos snap (or lapse of judgement) but the payout of progression and getting better with time hits the dopamine just right. Secondly, this incredible sequel is much more difficult than Spelunky HD, at least at first. However there is so much more to it.Most principles have stayed except for the order of progression is jumbled slightly, aaand there's generally a load more content. Personally I find this the perfect recipe and the balance is pretty much perfect.I strongly recommend you, dear reader, to give the first game a shot. If anything you'll like both and will have more Spelunking to do :D.I won't comment on visuals/music etc because it is obvious....10/10.Every moment is golden and every death is to blame on me. _childDocuments_.review: I really liked the first Spelunky, which I played when it was a free Gamemaker game. I actually own the Spelunky Wiki, though I haven't done much on it in years. The first remake was worth a buy even if it didn't appeal to a lot of people because it added quite a bit to the overall game. This one, however, doesn't really do enough to stand out as a separate game. It feels more like a mod.In general, Spelunky 2 feels like a game trapped in 2012, when roguelikes that were based on RNG screwovers were considered good. Thank god we (mostly) got over that. The first game had its share of issues, from the dark levels (which no one liked) to the fact that RNG played a huge part in how successful your run was. I was hoping that Spelunky 2 would fix that, but instead it doubles down on the difficulty while not doing anything to alleviate the issues the first game had.The first area of the game is now full of enemies that may as well be invincible unless you throw them into spikes. In the first game, this was more or less exclusive to one enemy (the caveman) who didn't always show up. Now you're guaranteed to have full hallways of them, and with Spelunky 2's more compact map design you're generally going to have to fight them in tighter quarters. It also seems like item drops have been severely cut from where they were in the first game, which kind of makes no sense as now everything that isn't on the direct path to the exit more or less requires bombs to access.Other than that though, this is more or less the exact same game the first one was. The whole "City of Gold" chain that starts in the first area is still in, the areas are set up exactly the same as the first game's were (Caves, Jungle, Ice, Lava) and it's just.. too much of the same thing. The only way I'd buy this is at a steep discount. Otherwise, just play the first one.

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible platformer that's extremely hard to master but immensely gratifying once you do. _childDocuments_.review: My point still stands, EVERYTHING CAN KILL YOU.My first review of this game I had made within my first 10 hours of playing it. I was very quick to make a review, but it didn't go into depth at all. And honestly, I'm still going to avoid going into depth about this game. Trust me, you'll want to experience EVERYTHING for yourself. DO NOT LOOK UP VIDEOS ON THIS GAME, PLEASE TRY TO FIGURE STUFF OUT FOR YOURSELF. It has so many secrets, and they're all incredibly rewarding to find out. This game will really try your patience though, as it is extremely unforgiving. Be constantly aware of the fact that stepping on the wrong tile can instantly kill you regardless of your health. If you don't like difficult games or having to lose all your progress in a run and being set back to square one, this game isn't for you.Alternatively, if you want a challenge that will last you hundreds of hours, hop in! I think even after putting in nearly 100 hours I still haven't seen much more than 50% of the content in this game. I can't wait to dig deeper!

Rescuing pets to increase your health goes a long way.

_childDocuments_.review: I have a lot of hours in this game because I guess it's still pretty fun? But I honestly can't recommend it. It's so frustrating and poorly designed. The health system seems so unnecessary because once you get mid to late game the only things that kill you do it in 1 hit no matter how much hp you have, and half the things in the early game one-hit you too. Every boss seems poorly designed because all of them, besides one, you just kill by throwing a few sticky bombs at them (so you're completely screwed if the game didn't randomly generate that item for you. And the random level generation consistently puts key quest items buried in walls so you have to use a number of resources just to get it them. It also spawns arrow traps off screen and on the same line you walk on so the only way to dodge the sudden arrow is if you play the entire game slowly inching forward. And whenever you manage to survive damage, you're stuck laying on the ground for like 5 seconds as a bat or a skeleton slowly approach to finish you off. But you also need to be willing to accept that you will die, a lot, often from completely out of the blue, and especially so when victory is just within your reach.

_childDocuments_.review: It's somehow the same, yet entirely different. I marvel at how close Derek Yu paid attention to all the things fans loved and did in the first game, then expanded and changed those things to give you a fresh experience all over again. I'll admit, having played so much of the original I went in a bit cocky thinking it won't take me too long to get a win. But holy ♥♥♥♥ just the first new area kicks my ass even now. All my muscle memory from the first game became immediately useless in the second game. The whip feels different, you run by default, all the little nuances in gameplay feel different requiring me to completely relearn and adapt.It gave me everything I was hoping for in this sequel. New areas, enemies, items, secrets, and endings. I just wanted more of the same but expanded and worked upon. Its delivered this is in spades. Brutal, relentless, and unforgiving, Spelunky 2 has to be the current pinnacle of roguelike games for me. The sense of progression, getting better, and overcoming odds to achieve that ultra feeling of gratification is second to none and only rivaled by something like Dark Souls. Yet this can all happen IN THE SPACE OF 30 MINUTES. Then you cry and do it all over again. I'm over 1000 games in as we speak, nearly 100 hours on the clock (on PS4), and am currently playing almost exclusively with friends on PC due to its new online coop mode.

_childDocuments_.review: Spelunky 2 is an amazing game. Difficult, but amazing. Whether you don't notice something, or you throw an object that ricochets and hits you, or you throw a pot too close and it has an enemy inside. The game is completely fair but sometimes really mean. For example when you barely have any health and the dog is generated in the sub-area or in a wall. So to get the dog... just use a bomb. Resources in this game are meant to be used. Don't just use them all willy-nilly, but use them. In my opinion, Spelunky 2 is an "objectively" perfect game.

_childDocuments_.review: I have around 300 hours and all achievements in Spelunky on pc alone. Prior to September 29, 2020, It stood as my favorite game of all time. I like games that reward learning various mechanics and games that have secrets and puzzles you have to dig for. Spelunky was a beautiful mix of the 2. Every time I reached a new milestone (i.e. killing Olmec, killing Yama, getting the no-gold run, getting the eggplant run), I got that feeling of progress, but I wasn't satisfied to the point where I could happily stop playing. That is, until Spelunky 2 dropped. In the dwelling, the differences felt fairly minute: cave drawings on the wall, a turkey here, a horned lizard there, updated arrow trap visuals, etc. It still felt more the same than different though. The same tight controls, meticulous platforming down to the end of each level, and the ridiculous/brutal rube goldburg machine that was dying in the first game. It felt familiar yet fresh. It wasn't until I dug deeper that I saw just how Spelunky 2 set itself apart from it's predecessor. And that's exactly how, it goes oh so much deeper. I won't spoil even a little bit of Spelunky 2 here, as I feel puzzling your way through  the treasure trove of secrets in the game holds a lot of it's charm. I've been blown away by said secrets thus far, and I don't believe I am even close to seeing the entire scope of this game. Derek Yu is an artist and has claimed the silver and gold medal on my podium of favorite games with this franchise alone. Thank you Mr. Yu.TLDR: 10/10 game. Guaranteed to have you scream with joy and agony in the same breath, and still say, "Just one more run"
_childDocuments_.name: Spelunky 2

_childDocuments_.review: Spelunky 2 overall is a pretty ok sequel to Spelunky 1. This includes many refinements to the original, such as what feels like slightly more responsive controls, more content and balancing which encourages you to use a larger variety of items than in the first game. However, some of it's additions weren't exactly good ones. While accessing the background of a stage appears to give another layer of depth to a level, it mostly isn't used in interesting way (although does have a few good uses). Also, there are a lot of levels that will always have a certain shop or miniboss area, which does make the game feel repetitive with how frequent these are. Overall, I feel like the charm of random level feelings from the original has been forgotten in this game, with the strength of the procedural generation of the levels being downplayed significantly in this sequel.  Another thing to note is that I would say that the music definitely does not live up to that of the first game, with many levels only having one track that plays rather than 3, making the level themes much more repetitive.Even though Spelunky 2 has more in terms of content than it's predecessor, I would recommend that you play the first game before this one. Otherwise, most things that made spelunky great are still here, while the increase in difficulty should be fun to tackle for more veteran players.

_childDocuments_.review: If you have never played Spelunky before, get this game.  It's fantastic.  Seamless movement and physics, with items/traps in the game that can impact each other- it can be chaotic or organised.  Entirely depending on how you approach it.  Procedurally generated levels so no one run will be the same as another, but not betraying itself in such a way that things seem unfamiliar.  Like Spelunky HD, this game is a masterpiece.If you're not a fan of solo games or find yourself in a setting where you have other people around, then that's perfect too.  This game has couch co-op, meaning you can play with someone on the same system and the same screen.  This will add a lot more chaos to your game, keeping it fresher for far longer than a solo experience.If you own SpelunkyHD and are unsure whether or not to make the leap to Spelunky 2, however, then allow me to assure you that this game is so much more than a HUGE texture change.  Alot of the older mechanics and enemies from SpelunkyHD still exist and some have even been shaken up to keep you on the back foot. In addition, there is SO MUCH more to discover and die to than HD.  If you thought HD had variety in it's game design then you will surprise yourself when you start playing this one.As a SpelunkyHD player myself moving over to Spelunky2 it was an incredible breath of fresh air in a familiar setting.  Personally I didn't like the graphical changes that were included with the sequel but i've warmed up to them and looking back, the graphical change is night vs day.  The grass is greener.With tonnes of new content and a journal that may well be a library as far as the critter/places sections are concerned, this game will hold my fervent interest for many months to come.As a matter of fact, I enjoyed this game so much that I purchased a 2nd copy for a friend and they are now trying their hand at it!

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted so desperately to enjoy this game, but every time I tried to play it I ended up getting pissed off. When I first played this game I thought it was just difficult like the first, but after playing it for a while, 90% of the challenge comes from pure ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, I honestly don't have a better way to phrase it. A run could be going perfectly, but no matter how perfect and careful you are one single wacky hitbox or miscalculated jump could throw that whole run out the window. It's very easy to get wombo-combo'd by almost any enemy since you get knocked down for about a second and a half after taking damage, if there's more than one enemy coming after you when you get hit, you're almost always just dead, even if you've stocked up on hearts and equipment, one wrong move and you're done. I consider myself decent, if not pretty good at games, one of my favourite genres is rougelike/rougelite so I'm used to having "bad runs" and "good runs", but almost every damage taken/death feels undeserved and stupid, over time it turns into anger and overall unhappiness. Although there are things that make Spelunky 2 fun and charming, besides the gameplay itself.The art style in this game is great, even if it is simple. The OST is also very good and really makes you feel like you're spelunking! There's also tons of characters to collect and play as, most have different ropes which is a nice attention to detail. The different areas that you can explore are really pretty and are much different than each other.The main problem I have with this game is the gameplay, as I've already stated. There are mechanics that I really like, for example the ghost and the ghost pot, but there are others that, in my opinion, make it frustrating to play. One quick example of that is how the dart traps work, when you dodge the arrows they will hit a wall and bounce off, yet even if they bounce off and just nick your bum you still take two hearts of damage, when this happens I have the urge to kill. It just feels unfair.OVERALL - If some gameplay mechanics are polished a bit, I think I would love this game, but how it is now it's just rage inducing. Everything other than the gameplay is great, but that doesn't excuse the gameplay (which is in my opinion the most important aspect of a game). A lot of time and effort obviously went into this game and I wanted to support it, but after about 10 hours of playing, all the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ just starts to come to a boil and it just got to a point to where I decided to write this review.Putting this into a score, I'd give Spelunky 2 overall, a 4/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Quite disappointing. Spelunky HD is & was such a great game, almost perfect. I had been anticpating the sequel since the announcement a few years ago. The sequel seems to try and cram so many new mechanics in that all the fun has been pushed out. In Spelunky HD, you always felt like a death was your fault & that made you eager to press on. In this sequel, there is so much to keep track of that the best way to move forward is to slow down to a crawl so nothing pops up and kills you cheaply. Some of the level 'chunk' designs are really confusing. You'll see these spots where there is a gem or pot placed in such a way that forces you to use resources to get to them. In Spelunky HD these situations were few & far between & were there as a 'bonus' in case you had some extra bombs & ropes. In Spelunky 2, the level design is constantly trying to milk you for your resources around every corner.Health is pretty irrelevant - because everything now reacts to everything else, getting hit once usually means stunlock-bouncing around until all of your health is depleted, & that feels really cheap. Maybe I just need to put more hours in, but unlike Spelunky HD, this game doesn't give me any motivation to press on, because I know it'll be more & more cheap deaths that are beyond my control. If you're a fan of Speluky HD, I unfortunately would have to say stick to that one and pass this one up. This game is suffering from sequelitis quite a bit, & that is a real shame.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I've thought about this a while, the review and all, and here's my heavily summarised sentence; I love this game, but I wouldn't recommend it unless you're either a content creator, or have friends to play with; though, The sole exception to this is if you've completed Spelunky 1 and want more. *Spoiler warning Below!* To Summarise: The Good-  There's a lot to do in this game, it's got a really good amount of secrets and discovery; it captures the theme of adventure incredibly well. - The animations are very smooth and the art is great, a clear and concise visual upgrade from the previous title and a game that's almost always nice on the eyes- The gameplay is still really enjoyable most of the time, with good controls and satisfying movement- The Multiplayer is simply incredible, and easily the best part of the game; It really is better with friends, The deaths become funny and the run isn't immediately over when one person makes a mistake. not to mention, outside of other players' movement, lag is nonexistant. It's really incredible how Mossmouth did it.The Bad - Dwellings is Incredibly, violently repetitive and if you do not have the drive or skill to constantly get past it, You won't enjoy the game. - In spelunky 1, most deaths were fair, and the few Rube's Machines to send you to 1-1 were at least, rare enough to be funny, but in spelunky 2 I often find myself not even reacting when one kills me.- Neo Babylon has the most, cheap and out of control deaths of any area in spelunky history with it's combination of UFOs, Reflecting shields and crushing Elevators. It's not fun; no sane person is arguing that a UFO going mach 9 to teleport you to 1-1 is Well designed and fair - While Discovering the secrets is great, Actually doing them is a different story. Spelunky 2 feels as if the Udjat eye spawns in resource-demanding locations so much more than 1, and Olmec's 3 phases still drag on way too long; for something essential to progression - I lose brain cells everytime a Shopkeeper outpost spawns with a ghost jar in it. Seriously; Why is that even possible, they always shoot it and it summons the ghost and forces you to speedrun an area with shopkeepers in it - I still don't understand why shops don't have a door, or some form of, Entry protection; Firemen, Lizards and Dart Traps can often spawn in front of shops, and if that shop has a bomb bag in it then it simply ceases to exist when the shopkeeper channels their Inner Mr. Sir, and uses a double barrel shotgun to take out a lizard. Seriously, the only reason I can assume this exists is because it generates those "Family Guy Funny Moments" compilations where a lizard rolls into a shop and proceeds to blow up the entire shop because of a powerpack and oneshot the player inside of it. It's funny the first 5 or 6 times but, it gets old fast- The Music, now, don't get me wrong, the Music is Incredible, an OST worth buying, however; each area has one track, unlike 1 where each level has 3. this contributes to the problem I mentioned above, where the dwellings are repetitive, as the music is always, Always identical. Overall, I can't recommend the game unless you have friends or an audience. A lot of the downsides are negated by that; The violently repetitive nature of it, the unfair deaths that stop being funny after a while, etc etc. It's a good game, but, Get spelunky 1 instead, and *then*, only then, if you really desire more, get spelunky 2.

_childDocuments_.review: Spelunky 2 is a overall fantastic game. It builds a lot after the already amazing game and adds or refines an insane amount of content. The game allows you to play in varying ways depending not only on what you want to achieve (as in score, time, distance), but also with your skill level. Levels are filled with various tasks that you can complete, that aren't directly instructed, but optional if you see them or wish to complete them. You can skip collecting certain items that are used for progression in the late game, items to temporarily help you, or items to permanently give you a boost. Spelunky 2 can be very difficult due to the need to manage your resources and evaluate risks. The game can be brutally difficult and does have a large learning curb because of this. The only form of permanent progress is shorcuts to areas farther in the game which do not allow you to go for hard endings or special endings. What you do gain from deaths and runs is experience on how the world that you are playing in functions, and how to evade or predict certain dangers.tldr: Overall, Spelunky 2 is an extremely fun and challenging game that allows you to play in many different ways. It's procedurally generated and you never play the same game twice. It's well rounded and allows you to learn and improve at the game. Online multiplayer is extremely fun w/ friends and hopefully deathmatch will be released soon

_childDocuments_.review: spelunky 2     :   I was excited to see a new spelunky 2 and bought it at full price!  it's on the moon apparently?  There are new elements and things you've seen before, if you played the first.  I enjoy the spelunky world but it is not for the faint of heart or sensitive souls who just want to have a nice gaming experience because it is very difficult, and often one wrong move will set off a chain of events leading to death.  I don't have a controller which makes it more difficult.    There's a lot to look at.  I enjoy the lil dun beetles and piles of bones that you can whip.   Plus now there is a second dimension to the map, where you can go behind the scenes in a way, or in lil holes to a second, darker area.  I love the lil ghost jar you need to carry around, not wanting to wake the ghost.  It does feel like more of the same, which is a good thing, in lots of ways.  In other ways it feels like an unfinished game, in the sense that there is only this extremly difficult speed run mode, when i want a more chill mining experience.  The AI is interesting but pretty dumb, it's trying to jump on the plants that eat you in one bit, or jump in lava that annoy me.  The insta deaths are pretty annoying, and there are times when its hard to wake up in time to prevent the same enemy from repeatedly getting me till death.   I don't want to be a complainer but it's way to hard for me.  Maybe it's better in co-op, probably more fun.  Most things are insta death anyway, so i feel like im wasting my time with the dogs and turkeys.  I do like the changes but it's still basically impossible to beat this game and that is why i find it... not as fun as it could be.

_childDocuments_.review: Spelunky's difficulty is like if you opened the door to a party you were invited into but it turned out that it was a kung fu party. But then you go back every single day and you make it a little further into the party. But the door guy still beats you sometimes. Finally, you get to the kung fu master at the end and she beats you senseless and she says "I hope you enjoyed the party" and you say "yes, I'll beat you next time and I'll truly know kung fu" and she smiles and one day you beat her and she says "You have done well, this party is truly rockin." _childDocuments_.review: Spelunky messed around with this design philosophy where the game is just a set of rules, and having cool and interesting interactions between stuff is more important than being super balanced or even fair. I think the first game was pretty careful about upsetting people with this since there was no way of knowing the game would be a hit. Spelunky 2 goes wild and adds obstacles not because of their difficulty, but because they add something new to the playground. Chain reactions of harmless objects will launch you into spikes, enemies will accidentally release the ghost at the start of the level, hired hands will pick up your weapon and kill you with it, and you will get softlocked by lava, but at the end of the day each death is a product of rules you already knew about and you learn to predict and defuse the BS before it happens. Sometimes, the chaotic nature of the game will cause something memorable and help you out, like a caveman picking up and throwing an item you can't reach or a shopkeeper shooting his own bombs and blowing himself up. Not everyone will enjoy this game and it's probably more frustrating than the first, but if you push through it's extremely fun and offers tons more depth and possibilities.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of people have already said this, but I feel the difficulty has passed the point of  "fun because it's hard" from the last game and is just "hard because it's supposed to be". It almost feels as though the developers forgot that they're really good at Spelunky now, and didn't realize they were making it too tough. As of this writing, only 23.5% of players have even cleared the first zone. My experience so far has been frustrating, constantly being caught in world generation dead-ends where there's no way to move forward without taking damage or using resources, and that's not including the un-dodgeable enemies in doorways.Beyond the difficulty though, I'm actually more disappointed in the music. I remember the original having multiple tracks for each area, or at the very least for the world 1 where we spend most of our time. Now each world only has one track, and in just over 3 hours I've already turned off the music and replaced it with my own playlist.I really want to like this game, and I'm going to keep trying at it, but so far it has felt like it attempts to pack more onto the original title, without realizing the space is way too tight. I feel I would enjoy this a lot more if the first world was nerfed some. Every zone after has felt easier, but because of the way the secrets work I can't just skip past the garbage part.

_childDocuments_.review: Spelunky 2 is an incredibly difficult game, much more difficult than its predecessor Spelunky HD. The game will make you rage, a lot, for hours. However, this game is still incredibly fun. With lots of content you'll probably never get to see!The visuals, levels, enemies, bosses, and almost everything else is an incredible improvement over Spelunky HD, apart from a few things.That mainly being the music, the music is still very good and is actually dynamic now which is great. There are many amazing tracks you will likely love... however, they all fall short when compared to Spelunky HD. This is likely because that game didn't need to focus on dynamic music and only needed to focus on happy jingles to nod along too.Another criticism about the game actually stems from 2 new features, that being the back layers and fluid physics. The back layers are a very interesting concept that just isn't used very effectively, with there not being much content or anything interesting to explore there. The other one is fluid physics, while being a great concept, the lava causes more annoyances that great times, blocking level paths and making the drill in volcano slightly more RNG heavy as well as making the game significantly more computer intensive.Despite this criticism, the game is still amazing and one I heavily implore you to try. While it doesn't have the exact same feel as Spelunky HD you will still have an incredibly, painfully fun time! (Especially, if you enjoyed Spelunky HD.)The new areas are great to venture through, and you can finally play with your friends online if you can manage the input delay. I have completed all achievements and it took me 61.9 hours, the achievements are varied and great and I am almost ready to hang up mining helmet, however I still crave to do one more challenge, that being the endless expanse of pain after those 22 levels of turmoil. You should play the game to understand what I mean, because there is a greater challenge hidden away from the achievements here, one you will likely never complete...I give this game a solid 9/10 - great gameplay, difficulty and challenges with good but not excellent music. The game is slightly more RNG dependent than the previous game, but this still leaves room for a lot of fun.Well done to Derek Yu! And remember always to "ransack those shopkeeper's pockets" while Kali watches!

_childDocuments_.review: A very great sequel to Spelunky HD. While the music isn't as catchy, I still find myself singing along to the right side second area song (can't say the name because of spoilers) and the dwellings song is hard to get annoyed of. I would appreciate some music variety, though. Smooth gameplay and highly addicting. My biggest problems are 1. Spiders can hide behind the little cloths on the ceiling that appear sometimes in the dwellings, 2. m o l e s, 3. how poison works. A run can be utterly destroyed because I accidentally had a scorpion lunge into my jugular because I couldn't see in the dark? Better rescue a pet or looks like the run is flushed straight down the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. In fact, the run is already in the pipes! Better fish it out from a sewer using a pet so you can finally stop being in constant pain. While those are the bad things of the game, I'd like to talk about the good to great to absolutely amazing. First off, it feels so good to be genuinely surprised when you find a secret. Having a game make me say "woahhhh" is pretty rare and its super fun seeing the red place (can't say the actual name because of spoilers) and then meeting the big but not bigest man. What I also love about this game is that it will break you. This game is really mean to its players. Not like a mean where it randomly restarts, more like a brutal mean. It is relentless, and you will never catch a break. You can have 99 bombs, be at the final level, and have 10 billion health, and somehow die to a regular spider. Anything can kill you. A n y t h i n g at a n y time. Thats why I love HD and this game. It will scream at you "No, you can't beat me!" but you keep trying. And when I finally beat this gem, the only thing I'll be able to do is play it again.In summary, buy this game or beg someone to gift it to you if you like a challenging, 2D, and brutal but fun experience with good music. Also, ♥♥♥♥ moles.

_childDocuments_.review: Having played the first one a lot, my review is gonna sound unfair at times but bear in mind despite all the cons I'm going about, I'm giving it a positive review since the game is obviously good and a great purchase choice, especially on sale.Spelunky 2 builds up on all the hard time you had before, making it incredibly hard to go through the game. It's still fun and addictive as hell, bringing a lot to discover and fresh ideas. Also great artwork and animation. And fantastic gameplay. Seriously the game's really good, let me just vent out a little:Where the problems start, at least for me: the game is somewhat obtuse every now and then. Some sections break the momentum and you're in the middle of something that's not that fun at all, like when the elevator goes through a lava pool, or those infuriating moles don't make up their minds, or having to search for the correct statue, and so on. The number of traps, plus the two ghosts mechanics, get in the way of wanting to search an area better. I get it's part of the difficulty, but it's still something that keeps someone from exploring the game, which I would debate is a good idea. And still the game finds other ways to punish you, like losing Qilin to the ceiling lasers and ruining your run.Spelunky 2, for me, unfortunately ended up being more frustrating than fun. If you're just playing for the regular ending and not touching it again, then I'd say the game is on point in terms of difficulty and punishment. It's said every death in Spelunky 1 is by your own fault. I'm not so sure about that, but that's definitely not the case here. The game will be upfront unfair now, expect that, and try to laugh in the process. A great game to play with some friends watching your pain.
