_childDocuments_.name: Spelunky 2

_childDocuments_.review: Programming failures and an anti-player development attitude make this an inferior version of the original freeware game. Bosses are programmed in ways that are frustrating and not fun and take more time than they should, torches if lit a second time after being used in a level do not do the appropriate level of damage, bosses have more health than is needed, speeding through the game is frustrated by skulls that hit the player for no real gameplay reason, controls that feel broken and 'floaty' like your inputs are getting duplicated (works better without dpad but why play without dpad), the length of the game feels padded out in ways that don't contribute to gameplay, and there are so few features compared to the original game it makes you wonder why they needed to release a sequel. I enjoy it but my nostalgia is VERY heavy, I could not and would not recommend this game to new players. Game is difficult to enjoy, multiplayer lacks really basic anti troll features and other basic gameplay features, and the "fun" of the game seems to have been abandoned in favor of making the player frustrated through poor game design. I might just go back to the freeware version.I tried to play this game every day but with the programming and game design flaws it is just not fun to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Spelunky 2

_childDocuments_.review: I dunno how this game both incredibly furiates me at every turn yet enthralls me to no end - so much so that I can get crushed by that god forsaken yellow cube man on a really promising run, put the game down for 10-20 minutes and then I’m right back playing it again.Absolutely wonderous, I adore this game
_childDocuments_.name: Spelunky 2

_childDocuments_.review: Four days before launch it was announced they would omit online multiplayer as a launch feature because it wasn't ready. Devs estimated it would be a few weeks at the most to get multiplayer working. Game has now been out for a month and still has no online support. Game should have the early access title.UPDATE: Multiplayer beta is now out three months later. The game is unplayable online with players teleporting everywhere only a two player session. Refunds should be given for this. I'll never support this company again, easily one of the worst game developers ever to have outsourced their multiplayer component, delay it and then release it in an unworking state.
_childDocuments_.name: Spelunky 2

_childDocuments_.review: The voice actors really make this game what it is. I also really love the gun-play because it is super realistic and allows for different approaches when it comes to devising tactics for conquering enemy bases. the story is really amazing and the character development throughout the course of the game really brings the experience together. P.S. We hate Clovis.
_childDocuments_.name: Spelunky 2

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best video game experiences I've ever had. Game feel is amazing and the way all of the objects, environments and mechanics interact with each other is amazing.This is also one of the hardest games I've ever played and has some deep, deep secrets. It's the kind of game that never gets old. It also has cross-play multiplayer on every modern platform so you can play with friends regardless of what they're playing the game on. An incredible sequel to Spelunky 1.
_childDocuments_.name: Spelunky 2

_childDocuments_.review: A well-designed, enthralling sequel to the well-known Spelunky, Spelunky 2 has a lot more to offer than its predecessor and certainly packs an incredible punch. Having played Spelunky Classic and Spleunky HD for hours, I still find myself challenged by this game, a testament to Derek Yu's game design and creativity.
_childDocuments_.name: Spelunky 2

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing and fantastic roguelite with an addicting gameplay loop that had be playing "just one more run" too many times. I'd say with all the hidden secrets throughout each level, you find something new almost every run. And did I mention the music was banging?The only downfall in my opinion was the extreme difficult and the RNG elements did contribute to that. But over each run eventually you start to see strategies and the game slowly becomes easier. I'd say this is definitely a 9/10. With mods or if you're someone who is more skillful at 2D side-scrollers, then it is a definite 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Spelunky 2

_childDocuments_.review: (but in a good way)The characters feels really nice to control while being hard to master at their full extent, the different objects scattered throught the world are usefull but dangerous at the same time, the enemies can easily end your run, but have paterns that will help you mastering them, and the world is filled with traps, items and more that will intrigue you during your whole playthrought.They require skill and thinking to get, while still hinting at their existence, so that you can more easily find them. A lot of items and places will feel out of place, almost useless, but in spelunky, NOTHING is useless. This makes the world feel alive and mysterious, there's always something that will make you say "". This leads to a lot of goals that you can set to yourself, which helps to get involved on the game. At the time of writing this, I have nearly 50 hours in the game, and I've discovered less than 25% of what the game as to offer, I always discover more and more to do...If you don't like hard games, you might not like spelunky, as the game is baased around dying, it is a core mechanic. However, spelunky might be a great start to learn how to enjoy hard game. Don't feel discouraged by the difficulty of spelunky, because every mechanic are well-tought to help you understand the game, it's traps and it's enemies. Every death is a lesson on how to survive next time, and feels fair, you harldy never feel cheated (well in the beginnings at least, it would be a lie to say that I never got killed unfairly, but it's stuff that happens...) Even if you find hard game not fun, Spelunky will help you to change this opinion, has it is made to make you learn and accept.If you don't know if you should get the game or not, ask you 2 questions :if not, then it might not be worth it to get spelunky, since it requiers time and patience to enjoy itLike I said, if you really hate dying, Spelunky might not be for you, but if you want to challenge yourself (even if you don't like hard games), this game is a great start, since it's fair and fun.Spelunky is a game about difficulty, mastering, secrets and bombs (a lot of bombs), and it's one of the best rogue-like I've ever seen, let alone one of the best GAMES I've ever seen, so hesitation doesn't have it's place here. If you like rogue likes, hard games, plateforming games, or just want to torture yourself a bit, this game is MADE for you. It's really good, like  good, so just get it, you won't regret it ;)Sry, that was a bit long, I just have LOTS to say about this masterpiece, which is and will always be one of my favorite games of all times... there are a lot of helpfull guide here and there on Steam, and some will help you enjoy the game even with all the frustration, so I'd recommend reading them. Thx for reading this, if you see spelling issues here and there, be sure to let me know (I'm not english so it's hard for me to write perfectly), and on that note, have a nice day ;)

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game AFTER the first area (the dwellings). Even after an entire year of the game being out and them making repeated changes to the dwelling to make it easier, I still find that after all these hours, the vast majority of my deaths happen in the starter area of the game, which makes no sense. After about 10 hours of starting this game I decided to purchase Spelunky HD to see if the starter area difficulty was the same, which of course it wasn't because lol. The mines of Spelunky HD are a lot more simple and open, meaning players have more time to learn and get a feel for how the game works. On the other hand the dwelling punishes you repeatedly for no reason, moles jumping out very quickly everywhere, the armadillos just rolling into random ♥♥♥♥ and throwing things everywhere getting you hit, they just front loaded the game with a bunch of nonsense to make the game appear more difficult than the first. To first time players trust me after the dwelling the difficulty drops for a few areas.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like playing the first level over and over, then this is the piece of crap game for you.  This is not a roguelike.  It's more like a random chaotic generator, thrown together with the first level being the worst of all levels to slow progression. This kind of crappy design does not endear people to the game, only makes them ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ frustrated, but it keeps the youtubers playing and the discussion boards going.  Making a game for the stupidass 1% is not a good strategy.  Play your first level over and over.  Go on.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to recommend this game, I really do. I had some fun with it but there are some serious level design and gameplay issues, some of which ported from the 1st game, some new, some not in the 1st game.Here's is the list of BS:#1 : Shopkeeps get pissed when a trap or enemy hits them or damages their shop. Derek, make them pissed but not at you!#2 : Arrow traps on ground-level that appear from off-screen horizontally and shoot you but you couldn't see them in time. This is a level design flaw. Make it so they're always positioned in visible range.#3 : Enemies covering exits or too close to entrances. #4 : Whipping while grabbing a ledge sends you flying. Da ♥♥♥? Remove this entirely please. When on ledge it should do nothing when pressing whip button.#5 : Gently dropping a bomb next to a dead turkey to cook it sends it flying to kingdom come.#6 : Moles dropping from ceiling is mostly unpredictable and frustrating. Make moles less dumb please. They should dig out up & sideways only. There's enough ♥♥♥♥ to deal with without having to check ceilings all the time.#7 : Why in god's name do jetpacks explode now? When you wear them you're one hit from being BBQ. Please no. Just NO. AT LEAST, AT THE VERY LEAST make them not explode instantly when you get hit.#8 : Poison is a ♥♥♥♥♥. It will keep ticking your health away until you get a doggy kiss. Considering how bloody hard it is to get one in most levels, and the time it takes, getting poisoned generally means your run is over. Make poison expire after 3 hearts so it's less OP please.There are some other issues too but these are the essential deal-breakers for me. They are all things that I think Derek and his team could fix in an update and I sincerely believe doing so would make the experience more enjoyable for everyone, while still being a very punishing game. It would at least feel less unfair.As it stands though, I cannot recommend it in it's current state unless you are masochistic.I will keep trying to beat it, though I fear I may send my monitor flying in anguish and rage.

_childDocuments_.review: Actually just the best game ever made.I've played Spelunky HD and Spelunky Classic for hours on end and I wanted to see if this game held up to it's predecessors.Great game, there's a lot of content here, and even though I only have 1 hour in the game, I've been having a good time.my god BUY THIS GAME

_childDocuments_.review: this game is an absolute ♥♥♥♥♥ of a challenge, i remember trying to play the first one with my brother when we were younger and we never made any progress whatsoever, i found out they made a second one and i just had to play it, this games ups everything from the first one including difficulty in my opinion but then again it's been a while so i may be wrong. if you're a fan of roguelikes this game is a pretty good choice, i'm not usually a fan of games that are meant to be incredibly difficult, but this game is 100% enjoyable even with death spouting from every oraface of this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Spelunky 2

_childDocuments_.review: Huge kudos to Mr. Yu for developing a great sequel to a great game that almost single-handedly brought about the genre of roguelike. You're going to die a lot. Like a lot a lot. You'll be gently brushed by bats, spiders, moles, lizards and cavemen before being crushed to death, exploded, burnt, eaten and more.Like the first game, each death is a lesson. If you mess up once it can all come to an abrupt end in an instant. But that's where the appeal comes from. There's secrets galore to uncover and mastering the game takes a lot of grit, focus and effort.Play solo, or with friends online in adventure or arena mode or try your luck at the daily challenge. Whichever you choose, you'll be tested.

_childDocuments_.review: It is almost a replica of Spelunky (1) but with some changes and upgrades. My favorite aspect of 2 is that they added the ability to play with friends online. It makes it a lot easier than being on one screen. It also makes it so much more fun because you have more of a chance of accidentally murdering the other.

_childDocuments_.review: Genius game design. Derek Yu is a god.Mad game, balls difficult. Everything is a "Spelunky moment" cuz of the way all elements of gameplay can interact with each other.You could easily spend thousands of hours learning and mastering this game, and it would still be fun (yes some people have played that much).Soundtrack slaps too.

_childDocuments_.review: Truly the sequel to Spelunky. Core gameplay hasn't changed at all, just a lot of new stuff. A lot larger game than the original (hd). The new stuff blends in nicely. Soundtrack is nice, however personally I prefer the HD and OG soundtracks. Multiplayer is a very nice addition. Really a must-have if you liked the original or HD.
_childDocuments_.name: Spelunky 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a ton of fun to play, especially with friends, yet very punishing. You can easily lose the best run you've ever had because of one mistake that takes you from 7 hp to 0 in a few seconds, yet can also have a ton of fun playing with friends (If you can still call them friends after they killed you for a shotgun last run). All in all, 10/10, challenging enough to keep one occupied for a while, while also still having enough replay-ability even after you beat the game, with the cave generation always being different between runs (unless you do seeded runs) so that no two expeditions will ever be the same.
_childDocuments_.name: Spelunky 2

_childDocuments_.review: You wrecked something I loved.  Tantalizing me with better graphics, more options then throwing the balance out of whack and making it both randomly unfair and too much harder.There's a phrase "the definition of insanity is doing the same thing over and over and expecting different results" - well the original Spelunky free classic and the Earlier version I could have played like mad till I did all the impossible runs if I'd had nothing better to do - and loved every minute, just relaxing, no biggie.THIS game I do regret wasting any time on - it is just frustrating.  All that art and options to make it nightmarishly difficult even for normal play then plenty of ways to get stuck even when careful and have gear, like floors of nothing but lava and no alternative route or easily trapped in caves without enough bombs.Plus - you removed the "Damsel" with pets, putting a playable character that looks like her but where few will reach.  I'm sure Anita Sarkesian approved of that...Just shows we'd better NEVER trust a sequel to ANYTHING even video games.

_childDocuments_.review: Spelunky 2 builds upon the unique, randomized challenges that made the original a roguelike classic, offering a huge adventure designed to satisfy players old and new. Meet the next generation of explorers as they find themselves on the Moon, searching for treasure and missing family.

name: Wolcen: Lords of Mayhem
detailed_description: You are one of the three survivors of the slaughter of Castagath. Rescued by Grand Inquisitor Heimlock, you were drafted into the Republic’s Army of the Purifiers at a very young age to be trained in the military academy and become perfect soldiers against the supernatural. You also had the chance to benefit from Heimlock’s occasional advice and training, which led you and your childhood friends, Valeria and Edric, to be called the “Children of Heimlock”. Recently, the Brotherhood of Dawn has infiltrated the Crimson Keep, a mysterious republican fortress lost among the northern deserts known as the Red wastes. While the purpose of the attack was unclear, the republican Senate voted a retaliation act against all known locations of the Brotherhood. Led by Grand Inquisitor Heimlock himself, troops are soon deployed on the Coast of wrecks, near the city state of Stormfall, to terminate a camp of Brothers. You are, with your two childhood friends, part of operation Dawnbane, under the supervision of Justicar Maëlys. Key features: Free character development Wield a great variety of weapons and find your own playstyle thanks to their unique stances and combos. In Wolcen, there is no class, only your weapons set the rules for your skills types. Three types of resources Rage and Willpower interact with each other, using the Resource Opposition System. Stamina allows you to use a dodge-roll to avoid danger or travel faster. Item diversity Gear up according to your offensive and defensive choices with common, magical, rare and legendary items. Break the rules and unlock new possibilities with Unique items and rare affixes. Rotative Passive Skill Tree Make your own path throughout the 21 sub-class sections available in the Gate of Fates to customize your passives and make them fit to your play style. Skill customization Level up your skills with your character or alternative resources to gain modifier points and create your own unique combination of skill modifiers. Change your damage type, add new functionalities, grant buffs or debuffs, change the skill’s mechanics completely. The options are limitless. Strategic fights Wolcen’s creatures have complex patterns including deadly skills. Pay attention to various markers and to animation anticipation to avoid lethal attacks using your dodge roll ability. Aspects of Apocalypse All characters can shapeshift into one of the 4 Celestial incarnations available, each of them offering 4 different skills, and one devastating ultimate. Endless replayability Improve your gear by looting or crafting, gather resources to unlock rare missions, face advanced challenges for special rewards, experiment new builds, become the greatest achiever. There is always something to do in Wolcen: LoM. A taste for beauty Using the Cryengine technology makes Wolcen an immersive and beautiful game with highly detailed armors and weapons. In addition, 8 hours of epic orchestral music will accompany you during your journey. Unleash your fashion sense Customize your appearance by switching the visuals of your armors and weapons. Loot more than 100 different dyes and tune up your armor to have your very own unique style. The asymmetric armor system will also allow you to change your appearance for left and right shoulder and glove. Difficulty modes Choose how you want to make the campaign with 2 different difficulty settings: the Story mode and the Normal mode. The endgame is shaped to allow a progressive increase in difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: I will start out by saying I am new to the Action RPG genre, and having little to no experience in the genre I rather enjoyed my time playing Wolcen: Lords of Mayhem. Before starting I saw the mixed reviews and was not sure what to expect, but right from the early going I was delightfully surprised to like and even be impressed with many aspects of the game. The game play was fun and I was kept mostly engaged throughout the story. Wolcen isn't the most challenging game even on the harder mode, but I didn't find this to be a drawback. The end game does become repetitive but still offers ways to up the challenge. The combat was solid and even in the end game it was still fun mowing down endless hordes of enemies. There are many enemy types and some have a really cool design to them which helps keep the game fresh. There are many types of weapons and spells to choose which all can be tweaked to your own liking to better suit your build. The perk tree is massive but doesn't feel overwhelming, you can even rotate the perk tree to allow even more customization to your character. You can make some really OP builds and there are a lot of possibilities. I enjoyed the story even if it was a little cliche and predictable, but it had some depth to it and was on the longer side. Some parts of the story were hard to follow but still in the end I was satisfied. The graphics were a strong point of the game. From the cinematic like cut scenes, to the detailed environments and enemies, its a pretty game. The music suited the game nicely and added to the medieval feel of the game. There were some parts of the game that reminded me of The Lord of the Rings which I thought was cool. That being said there were some aspects of the game that were inconsistent and held the game back. The game lacked polish in areas, there were some graphical glitches and audio glitches but nothing too severe. On occasions a piece of loot could not be picked up off the ground. I did experience infrequent crashing though the game did a good job of keeping your progress. Some parts of the game like the hub area and project map felt a tad bleak and lifeless. There is an online component to the game with an related achievement that allows you to play Co-op, but that feature will be removed September 17th, 2024. The price is fair for the quantity and quality of the product, though there are games in the genre that are free and many would argue better games. However these negatives weren't enough to deter me from liking the game and my time playing it. Wolcen might not be winning any awards for best in category but I still thought it was a good game and one I would recommend.

Bad: sluggish mechanics for melee, cursor gets lost in the battle--cannot scale, uninspiring skills, poor balance, skill tree/gem sockets feels like Paths Of Exile rip-off, uninspiring main story. You'll have to buy skills yet each skill costs 2k golds while each gear you pick up only sells like 5 golds in average. Respec also costs a ridiculous amount of currencies so it basically requires you to have a build on your mind before you get to know the mechanics. And I haven't even mentioned the fact that you may not get the skill you need for your build if you had bad merchant RNG.Skills also feel mediocre and lack identities. And character progression is extremely slow. 4 hours in and I'm still auto-attacking with basic skills that only do more damage, and there's no power spikes whatsoever. Each level only gives you about 3% chance increase which makes leveling like a chore. "Keystones" on the passive tree have very little impacts. _childDocuments_.review: In short: horribly optimized, a visual hard to read mess, frontline mechanics work against the flow of the game, and it's unfinished. A strong diablolike underneath the cruft, but this needs about 6-12mo more of early access.I finished the plot in 8 hours, what there is of it. It's not finished and as a result has a very disappointing end with no payoff. There's some wild bugs, and captions randomly break with the programmer's variant of "[put caption about X here]"The game is horribly optimized. My PC was screaming the entire time with everything on low. People say "It's the most beautiful Diablolike" and I wish they'd instead made it slightly less graphical and made it run better.Because of the effects and the detail, battles turn into a visual soup. Every time I died, I had absolutely no idea what hit me. Diablolikes need a clear, distinctive visual style so you can easily see dangers, this does not have that.The post-game is a mess of player time disrespect that descends into Farmville "Build a thing then time sink" mechanics where you pass time by doing what amounts to D3 rifts. Could be worse I guess, but there's no carrot at the end of the string to explain why I'm doing all of this. The rewards floated to you immediately are things like "You can choose another ultimate form"; sidegrades and choice swaps, no additional power.These "Rifts" are a bit of a mess too. Several of them are just ridiculous gimmicks to limit player choices and slow down the experience. Things like "An NPC slowly walks a static path on the map and if you move away from them you die". The skill system is neat, but Last Epoch did it much, much better. Leveling up skills is almost pointless; have a skill on your bar for a little bit and it'll rocket up to your level. Why bother at that point?The game boasts "no class system" but that's only true at the surface level. You're limited by what skills you can use based on what weapon you have. While you can change this at any time by swapping weapons, the difference between "I'm holding a staff so I can only use spells" and "I am a mage" is rather academic. Some people have made hybrid builds and there is gear that lets you use multiple skill sets, but this doesn't come in main game and doesn't come easily or naturally.I'm frustrated; this has the makings of a solid game but it needed more work and polish. It feels like they pulled it out of EA so they could just say "We launched" or they gave up. Can a game go back into EA? This needs to go back into EA.

_childDocuments_.review: Currently I have been trying out the different classes that this game has to offer. At the time I have not clocked so many hours into this game without needing to write this. First, I want to say that I enjoy the direction this game is taking. It looks very beautiful and I can tell there was some love and care put into it to make it feel more alive than most ARPGs around. I must commend them for what they are currently doing. According to notes they say that they will be making a huge patch they hope to have out by September, however, until then I cannot recommend this game.The way the current system works, it feels clearly unpolished. At the time of writing I am attempting to make a ranged fighter and I almost can't force myself to get past the point of the first boss. There is a problem where, if you're in the middle of a firing animation, your character will only continue to attack if you attempt to move them. This causes it to feel incredibly out of the player's control when you have no defenses(Besides the dodge roll that I still canNOT remember is even there) and enemies are slowly walking up to you while you can't move unless you allow your character to finish the animation. I do want to say a few things for the developers. I wholeheartedly am cheering you on for future updates, but there are a few things that kind ruin the experience for now. I have hope that something amazing can be made from this and will happily change my review when that time comes. Another thing, I need to suggest making it possible to kill brother leon. After playing through the beginning of the game several times and always having Leon dropped on me, I can't help but want to kill him. If you're melee he will end up on top of the one thing there is to attack and you can't click through him, so instead you get to watch him hit the zombie for 3 damage when it has 100 health. Or, when you're ranged, he BLOCKS YOUR SHOTS! I was amazed by that one, really, I was. I had never had an NPC follower that makes it impossible to shoot something if they are between you and your target. I do actually have anohter suggestion that I'm not sure everyone would agree on but I really want to suggest it. Make the games movement not controlled via clicking. I'd love if you could amp up the way the game plays by making it controled by WASD. I thought of this when I entered the graveyard at the beginning and found myself, yet again, unable to move because I could not find it possible to quickly click between the row after row of tombstones(Of which, all of them are targetable). TL:DR I do not currently recommend this game as is, unless you want to support the mostly small team. It is currently in patch limbo up until they come out with the large update that doesn't have a set release date, so none of the glaring problems in the game will be adressed until then. Still a cool game and a lot of thought was put into it, but the lack of polish really killed my experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This game makes me wish there was a third option for reviewing games on Steam. I don't think this game is BAD, but from what I've experienced so far the negatives tend to outweigh the positives.also tl;dr it's slow and there are too many cooldowns so don't buy it unless you're a filthy casualLet's start with the good:+ Graphics are great. Game looks good and runs well enough.+ Soundtrack is pretty good.+ Movement feels pretty fluid overall.+ Character customization is always great.+ The perspective and camera angles are all pleasing to the eye.+ The willpower/rage resources system is a welcome addition to ARPGs and a nice change over the plain mana system we see in most games like it.+ Big passive tree and the cool rotation mechanic coupled with how spells work allows for tons of (potential) customization.Now, the bad. Here I feel there are some glaring flaws that automatically disqualify the game for me:- You can't reassign LEFT CLICK. You're stuck with a BASIC ATTACK as left click for the ENTIRE GAME. The game basically forces you to play at a huge handicap after level 10, as you'll very quickly get enough good skills to completely ignore the basic attack. You can't rebind it either. This is an absolute embarrassment and would be reason enough to never touch this game.- Too many cooldowns. Cooldowns are just lazy game design, especially when what feels like two thirds of the skills have them. The game has a really cool resource system with plenty of potential, and the devs had to resort to putting cooldowns on almost every skill? Neither the resource costs nor the power of the spells couldn't be tweaked? Cooldowns immediately make the gameplay feel boring and bumpy, leaving giant valleys in the gameplay where it feels like the character I'm playing is doing nothing. This game's poor design is no exception. Are there any builds with no cooldown skills anyone recommends?- Popups, especially quest rewards. Sometimes you'll still be in the middle of combat and a big fat quest reward window or other prompt pops up that covers your entire character. Really?- Slow overall gameplay. Between some spells having long windup animations and others (or some of the same) also having long cooldowns, it feels like the game drags its feet. The best way I can describe it is that it almost feels like MMO style combat but in an ARPG package. Admittedly I'm not terribly far into the game, but looking at some other gameplay videos it seems like this doesn't radically change.If you like fast-paced ARPGs like Diablo II or Path of Exile, don't bother with this one. Between the huge number of cooldown spells and overall slow pacing you'll be bored stiff with this game. If you're looking for something to play casually I honestly think this would be a fun game to play with friends, though. You also might like this if you're a fan of the steaming turd that is Diablo III.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite some launch bugs, this game is a lot of fun.  It pulls a lot of elements from games such as Diablo and Path of Exile, and melds them very well. _childDocuments_.review: I played this game for hours when it released. I didn't dare touch the online mode because of all the Reddit/forum posts crying over it. It was a mess.I simply avoided those talents, abilities or whatever. I payed close attention so I wouldn't be a victim of a B.U.G.  Well the bugs and panic aside, the game was hard, like I rage-quit-for-the-first-time-in-my-life hard. The second boss simply broke me after the fifteenth attempt, many hours of grind for any extra exp or anything in my favour. However after repeatedly trying, I was done. I thought to myself why is this game so f-ing hard? Then people began posting and after some light reading I found out my abilities were literal ♥♥♥♥ and changed them up for a few others along with some skills and voila I beat the bastard in under a minute. I finished the game and played the end content. It was meh. Anyone who has played a hack and slash RPG similar to this one knows what I mean. It became an endless dungeon-running-for-nothing fiasco that gave me night terrors with the taunting ghost of Diablo 3 looming over head. However.. I decided to wait, see what happens. The game might after all make a huge profit and ''make it'' or just, you know make an expansion worthy of my time and return. They did just that and I did as well. I returned for the changes Bloodtrail brought and man was I pumped. That is, until I opened my character screen today and saw my level 3 character on the online mode. I switched the mode to offline. But wait, where is my character? I asked myself as the create character button was the only thing visible on there. For whatever reason the devs made an offline mode but nothing to back up the offline character you created? _childDocuments_.review: Wolcen: lords of Mayhem is a new entry into the ARPG genre that blends a little bit of Diablo 3's rune system with Path of Exiles web of passives when leveling.  I personally found the game enjoyable.  I finished the full 3 acts of the game, and have entered the end game mode that you arrive at when you finish your first full play through.  I did this with an offline character.Right now if your looking to play with others online, you may want to wait until the online issues are more thoroughly fixed.  But if you like to play solo offline then you can have a good time here if you like ARPG's.  There is enough here that warrants the price of entry.  I think the game would get a 7/10 if online play was in better shape.  But this is definitely a good base for this new ARPG, and if the developers iterate on what they have they can have a soild 8/10, 9/10 ARPG that would fit somewhere between a more casual Diablo 3 and the more indepth POE.  As it is right now though i think the game is a 6/10 ARPG that is new and has some roughness out of the gate but has a chance to be much better down the line.

_childDocuments_.review: This game seems so good until you get down to the finer details that makes an ARPG actually good. Even after fixing half the trees, their math and numbers are just downright depressing. You wanna dual wield guns? Bet you thought that was fast, but it's not. They have a slow animation and do half the damage a single pistol would give you. If you equip a catalyst with that pistol you do 3x the damage you would if you just used a pistol. In fact, dual wielding anything in this game cuts your damage by over half. It'd make sense if this actually sped up how often you attacked but it barely does for any amount of dual wielding weapons. Daggers are the only thing that seems to speed up if you dual wield them, and it still isn't as efficient as just wielding a single dagger?Then there's the buggy skill trees, much of the third tier wasn't working at all at launch. Many trees are still glitched out. The story is what you think it is, a hindrance and gate to the real meat of the game. The end game seems to be by far the best part of the game, as it should be, but this good point gets overshadowed by my next point.The game can be downright unplayable at times. Every time you launch the game your frames will be garbage. In dungeons, you'll just have a poor frame rate sometimes, period. Bosses in the story are some of the worst boss design I've ever seen when they're working properly, but you may have to restart them several times just to beat one because they glitched out. The poor frame rate and appalling glitches of the game make it not worth your time. And that's not even getting into the math passed the way they handled their weapons. I'll amend my review if this game gets fixed, but for now you'd do best to stray away from it until it is.

_childDocuments_.review: So, far after it's 1.0 release, Wolcen's finally gotten enough updates that it actually reminded me to update MY review.So first, yes, some bugs still remain, but considering the one I was concerned about-specifically the one that soft-locked the game- is no longer present, I'm happy.Second, with the new "Arise" update, the summon skills get a much need overhaul, coincidentally playing a summon class is my favorite and you can 100% do that here, now.One thing that still gripes me is the willpower/rage system, and the lack of dual-weapon diversifying. When you cast a spell type skill, willpower is consumed and you gain rage. When a physical type skill is used, rage drains, and you gain willpower. That's all well and good, but basic attacks ALSO accrue, and subsequently DETRACT, your rage/willpower. It feels like teetering on a seesaw a little too much, but I guess that's what potions are for?As for the weapons, it's fine, they're great, I STILL just wish I could hold a staff AND a sword or other one-handed weapon. The little rinky-dink catalysts just don't scream "all-powerful wielder of magic" enough for me, but this is more a personal problem.Bonus point: kinda wished there were diablo 2 druid-like skills that could turn me into a ravenous beast-like creature, but oh well, Grim Dawn didn't have it either.

i would love to switch my basic attack to another key. i often can't move out of a big group of enemies as a mage and i don't need my basic attack)- damage calculations of spells don't really make sense (spell x has 99-129 frost, 74-154 lightning, 0-20 aether and 20-26 sacred damage. switching lightning to sacred damage with a skill modifier makes the spell heavily occult damage biased but you get more damage when you go for elemental than occult damage. so sacred damage (occult) will get stronger if you're using elemental damage)suggestions:- npc who rerolls one stat of each item (like in diablo 3)- training dummies in the city would be awesome to test build changes- a search bar in the gate of fates (to find the bonuses you want to have)

_childDocuments_.review: This game is such a masterpiece of a wonderful mess. It is expected to have bugs in the game due to it being a beta, but it's like an  of them that can really make you mad. I still recommend this game for the finished product nonetheless, because I see the potential in it being a stable and complete game. I completed the first act of the beta and now going through the Soldier of Fortune (expedition) quests. It's just like Diablo's Adventure Mode.• Overall game play is like Diablo 3 and Path of Exile.• Storyline really captures your attention.• Graphics are great.• Expect bugs.• When playing Multiplayer, if you teleport to one of your friends, sometimes you will fall through the ground into blackness, and end up on another map.• Sometimes your character will show up with his feet underneath the ground.• Character will be completely naked to the other person in Multiplayer, until they take their armor off and put it back on.• You can travel outside of the border of the map (if you fall through the ground into another map) and you will be stuck there until you quit.• When you hover your pointer over an item in your inventory, sometimes it won't show the description or even have a selection of the item you're over, until you right click or left click.• When playing Soldier of Fortune mode, you can clear an entire map with no more enemies to fight, and sometimes the progress bar won't be maxed out. Keeping you from fighting the boss to either finish the level or go to the next one, ultimately forcing you to quit and lose your progress.• The passive skill tree needs an improvement.• There is no merchant to merge your gems to a better quality gem.• Legendary & Unique items are randomized and not really class specific.• Singleplayer works better than Multiplayer.• Definitely more issues with this game for me to even remember or mention.Enjoyed it, though.

_childDocuments_.review: I give this game a 5/10. This is a very Diablo-like game but doesn't really meet the bar for the genre. A lot of the abilities and movement are clunky. The pathing on some of the spells and warrior abilities is terrible. You can be facing and enemy and your character will randomly turn the opposite way and hit nothing. There is a glaring lack of fluidity between skill chaining. Its almost like their is a passive global cooldown that exists between all action whether it be combat abilities, healing, dodge rolling, or just moving. The boss fights are very unrewarding. I enjoy high difficulty games like Nioh, Soulsborne series, Sekiro where the fights are very high difficulty but also high reward. Wolcen fails hard in that area. It seems like the developers tried to hard to make a challenging game and just ended up making it frustrating and unrewarding. A lot of the fights are just unpredictable cluster$&#@s of endless waves of units while dodging 1 shot mechanics. Its just cluttered and there is no real enjoyment to the fights.The story is not that impressive either but that's not too big a deal since these types of game are normally combat focused.I don't really find there to be much in the way of viable customization for your character. When i first started the game and saw the talent point system and all the different abilities I was hopeful. But  as i progressed It seemed to me like there are a total of 15 abilities in the game. That's it. They are divided by weapon and class type which means that you are limited in the skills you can use depending on your playstyle. All in all i am very disappointed in this game. If you like games like this i recommend Path of Exile, Diablo, or Grimdawn. They do it much better.

_childDocuments_.review: Quite interesting endgame. Pretty good story as far as the genre goes. Enjoyable gameplay with quite abit of room for making interesting builds and min-maxing. A few things are very annoying. For one, you can't seemingly rebind keys in the settings, they keep resetting when attempting to do it. Like it's hard-coded even though. Furthermore, the female models are atrocious. They don't look human. 80% of the body is legs and the head is tiny. What the ♥♥♥♥ were they doing? It's lowkey offensive honestly but at the same time more ridiculous than insulting. Like the sexualisation of the female body originally blurted from the mind of a retarded 12year old. While I do like the warhammer-esque theme when it comes to architecture and rigid codes of the factions I find the enormous pauldrons almost as cringe as the female models. Floaty shoulder-guards about half the size of the human body... Yikes. Maybe it was "cool" in the late 90s early 00s and the developers simply never grew away from it? One more thing that annoys the hell out of me is that you can't rebind the useless basic attack or make it not trigger. You can try walking away from a boss but unless you click well beyond the model, you will remain, mindlessly wasting your time and your quickly diminishing health-bar while doing 0 damage with these useless attacks. This also seems to override your dodge-roll, making it exceedingly frustrating to move around. Movement is one of the most important parts of a game like this, which makes this particular design-choice a failure on every level in my opinion. No other game in the genre, that I've come across, has such disrespect for player QoL when it comes to moving around the battlefield. That said, I sunk 20 hours into the game because it's quite fun when you arn't hitting your head against the wall in sheer frustration over dumb mechanics or staring, dumbfounded, at the models. The voice acting is good, cutscenes semi-engaging (would be better if I didn't have to watch those bizarre leg-women), story interesting and gameplay mostly fun. So a reluctant thumbs up. Worth the 75% discount for sure but I've dodged this game for a few years, occasionally at 50% discount and in retrospect I think that was a good choice.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Skill tree, Gem system, easy to learn, easy to jump in and out of, cosmetics on armor, dodge mechanic is really nice, achievements Pro/Con: Graphics - They are nice looking graphics but absorb more out of my CPU & GPU than 'Control' & 'Doom External' ultra 4k (Control with Ray-tracing maxed and using reshade). I'm using a i9 9900k & Rtx2080ti with a 2nd dedicated samsung 970 evo plus...there doesn't even have to be action going on and it utilizes more resources than I feel is necessary.Con: Endgame is fun at first but then becomes a real slog. I don't remember the story. Development team communication is garbage.  It's not uncommon for you to lose progress from game crashing or you getting stuck on geometry. Stacking ailments is more or less your end-game build (many runes will go unused). Uniques are a joke, you can't even socket them and there is no set items. It reminds me of vanilla diablo 3 where you'd try to get the best RNG rare weapons. Quirky UI system. Buggy Multiplayer. Good luck finding your mouse-cursor in battle with 4k resolution, especially multi-player (check out Yolomouse, if having issues). Enemies are boring. I recently started playing the Last Epoch which is early access. It has not crashed on me once. I used my nvidia control panel with Reshade to improve the graphics. Wolcen has made me appreciate other ARPGs for their shortcomings. Wolcen is a game that still feels like it could have used another six months for Q&A (It honestly still feels like it should be in beta). Conclusion: I feel that there is a lot of potential for this game but it's going to take awhile to get there. This will be a game I check back on every now and again. Do I feel like I wasted my money? No.... but it left me yearning for other ARPGs.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, the game is fun. It looks great, and the customization for cosmetics is great, when they work.It's feasible to use both magic and weaponry at the same time without being rendered impotent. Most games will sort of force you to choose one or the other.However, there's not as much diversity as was advertised in a "class free" game. To begin with, there are maybe 40ish skills. And half of them aren't that great. Your ability to use each of them is locked based on what sort of weapon you're using - and in this, you're basically choosing a class anyway. You can't run around with two swords and also use magic. One of your hands need to hold a magic implement which itself isn't a weapon. Not to mention the gate of fates or whatsit - which is essentially a spider web of talent points that further shape you into a certain class archetype. You have to choose one to get another, so you can't just decide to be good at certain aspects of one thing without deeply investing in some things you probably don't really want along the way. And, as most other reviews will tell you, the game has a fair amount of bugs and glitches. The most recurrent of these for me is with the sound. There's a near constant interruption of atmospheric, effect or music based static interruption that pops up, and I'll have to fiddle with the sound volumes until it disappears. Sometimes some environmental objects like trees just sort of disappear, and all you can see is a floating base. Occasionally, when using a channeled skill, it'll continually cast until I'm out of willpower regardless of my efforts to stop it. The most egregious bug I've encountered was that, when my computer lost power, all of the cosmetics I had accumulated had simply disappeared. It didn't really affect my progress in the game, but it's disheartening nonetheless. And they don't seem to have a solution to it.Yet, overall, the game is basically fun. The combat is more dynamic than most ARPGs where you just stand and use skills, and are either so underpowered you'll just randomly die or are so overpowered you're basically a god. The dodge roll is a pretty interesting feature, and adds a lot in terms of combat mobility. Plus you can just use it to speed around when you're running somewhere far off. The skills run together smoothly, and everything you do has an impactful feeling, action wise. Story wise, it's just a linear little story that's as good as whatever other hack n' slash you're into. So I suppose it's a recommendation, as long as you can keep in mind that somewhere along the way, you'll probably lose something you've earned, and eventually you'll likely tire of using the same skills over and over again.

_childDocuments_.review: After spending years playing this game, I was disappointed to find that it ended up being a bad experience in the end. While it was fun to play with friends, creating an online character was required in order to do so. Unfortunately, the online and offline characters were completely different things, meaning that once I created an online character, I was restricted to playing online only.　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　This would have been fine if the online connection was stable, but it wasn't. Even after three years of development, the game's online functionality was still not in a good state to play with. As a result, my overall experience with the game was soured by the fact that I could not reliably play with my friends due to the poor online connectivity. I would not recommend this game to others unless significant improvements are made to the online functionality.　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　Update review in 23/03/26　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　------------------------------------------------------------------------------------　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　After taking a break from the game for a year, I was pleasantly surprised to find that the developers had released several patches and updates that made the game seem more promising. However, my optimism quickly turned to frustration when I started playing again after their first major update.　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　Creating a new character for Chronicle I resulted in numerous crashes, which was incredibly frustrating. Despite this, I do appreciate the game's character build system, which is well-designed and allows for a lot of flexibility.　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　However, the online lag experience is still a major issue that detracts from the overall gameplay experience. Additionally, there are still some small bugs here and there that can be quite frustrating. While I do believe that the game has potential, these issues are unforgivable and make it difficult to recommend to others.　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　Update review in 20/05/12

_childDocuments_.review: I am thoroughly impressed by this game so far. It has launch issues, but they seem to stem from the game being far more popular than they were prepared for and overloading the servers. Even their website was hard to get onto when I tried.The game takes the best parts of Path of Exile and Diablo 3, and blends them together in even more interesting ways than they were originally done. The attributes and way the game handles different mechanics like status effects are all very interesting and new, there's a good variety of very fun and customizable skills so far, and I've been engaged with the story and setting since the start. The appearance customization also seems amazing, though I haven't gotten far enough to really bother touching it yet.I hadn't heard of this game before today, and I usually try to keep more up to date on upcoming games than most, but this is by far my favorite ARPG. I love the ideas of ARPGs but I rarely get very far before making new characters and getting bored, and I don't see that happening here. This game brings me back to the feeling of playing Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance back when it wasn't dated and terrible. Play this game, support these developers.

_childDocuments_.review: I left this game on the shelf for a while and picked it up again with the new Chronicle, Bloodtrail. I started out with a new character, finished the campaign and I'm now in endgame and I gotta say: my opinion of this game has soured.While most of the things in my original review (see below) still stand, I discovered that this game doesn't offer much in the long term. The most egregious omission is proper itemization. I have played quite some Diablo 3, which I personally find quite a shallow game. But the one thing Diablo 3 has got going for it, are the multitudes of items that have build-defining properties. Compare this to Wolcen, where items do get better stat-wise, but do not offer any gameplay incentive compared to the items you already have. In short, items are uninspiring and dull.The item hunt is the most important part of what makes an ARPG good. Without it, the game gets boring pretty quickly.On top of this, the game still lacks a lot of polish. It feels like the team doesn't include a good user experience expert, because there are so many small irritation factors in the way the UI is presented and handled. Some small examples:- When assigning and confirming a passive skill point, the confirm button remains, even though there is nothing you can do with it anymore- When using the gem interface to remove gems or re-roll sockets, the item doesn't get returned to the slot it was in, but is instead put in your inventory- When clicking on a zone-transition, the game seems unresponsive. There is no visual feedback that you actually clicked. The game could for instance have your char walk in the direction of the glow to give you feedback that you click has registeredThere are many many more of these small omissions/faults/bugs that really show the lack of polish and care for this game.Lastly about the Chronicle, Bloodtrail: doing hunts is fine for the main campaign, but after that you've done it 5 times or so and it becomes super boring. On top of that, hunts are quite buggy, with strange and nonsensical modifiers being offered every now and then, or sometimes none at all so you can't finish the hunt.I know this is going to piss off a lot of Wolcen fans, but if you want to play an ARPG with a great skill system, great gameplay, good itemization and decent graphics (although not as good as Wolcen), I recommend Last Epoch.I bought Wolcen in Early Access more than a year ago, played it a bit back then but left it in my backlog after that until now. Wolcen has officially been released! Due to unforeseen server issues, I've only been able to play about 6 hours since the official release, but I can honestly say that I love what I've seen and experienced so far, and I'm totally willing to wait a couple of days to be able to play this gem in a stable state.Some Pros & Cons:- Beautiful graphics- Good voice acting- Meaty, satisfying combat. I really dig the movement in combat, being able to dodge, and the movement-based skills. It gives you a lot of options to approach fights.- Deep skill system that is easy to learn, hard to master. Despite what people say, I definitely not perceive it as "derivative" in any way- Lacks polish in some areas, including (so far for me) minor bugs. Examples:    * Background music cutting out after cut scenes sometimes    * Lack of UI feedback when performing certain actions    * Random freezes and lack of responsiveness sometimes. Example: sometimes I have to click an item multiple times to sell it to a vendor-  They're online again!Would I recommend this game? Definitely! But that's also because I trust the team will overcome the server crisis and we'll get an amazing game in return. I've seen glimpses of what that game looks like, and I love it!Would I recommend you buying it _right now_? Probably better to wait until the server issues are resolved so you're certain you'll get your moneys worth.Now, lastly some remarks for both the devs and the community on how the server crisis was handled:- You're did a great job communicating upfront what was happening- But you somehow slowed down in transparent communication over the last 18 hours or so. I have a feeling that you are drawing back because of the community backlash, but please don't feel discouraged. At moments like these, transparent and frequent communication is key!- Let us know in more detail what is going wrong. Even "We honestly don't know what is causing the networking issues, but we're looking into it" is totally ok! Honesty goes a long way.-  It seems unfair to coax people into buying a game that is currently not fully playable. It makes it harder for people like me to defend you, if you do unfair things like this.- Don't ever release a game close the weekend anymore. Do it on mondays.- Keep up the good work. I believe in you!- Get some perspective! This is not the first tumultuous launch, nor will it be the last. If you have a bit of patience, a lot of good will come out of it.-  Stop making the lives of everybody around you miserable, just because yours is. Yes it sucks that you took the weekend off to play the game, and now you can't. Let others have their fun nonetheless- Armchair devs: . If you claim to be a developer and at the same time claim that this could have been prevented by proper preparation, I don't believe you for a second. I'm an engineering manager and have been a software engineer for 10 years before that, and let me tell you: this could not have been predicted nor prevented. And this could also not have been solved by merely spinning up more servers. Scaling software is  and many problems in scaling software are magnitudes harder when you pass certain thresholds. For example: going from 1k concurrent users to 5k concurrent users: simple, just add more servers. Going from 9k concurrent users to 11k concurrent users? Now you're hitting the famous 10k problem. Adding more servers is not going to help you necessarily, you need to fundamentally alter your networking strategy.Building an online game is orders of magnitude more complex than building web apps, and your experience in launching"Enterprise applications" for 80k concurrent users, does not make you qualified to understand what the Wolcen devs should do, or how easy they have it.

_childDocuments_.review: I always wanted to play through an ARPG with gameplay similar to Diablo 3 and skill tree similar to Path of Exile. And Wolcen, seems to cure that itch quite well. Combat pace seems to be at a very good place. (Personally, I always found Path of Exile's combat gameplay to be quite boring and tedious past level 50-60.)- You get to build your own class from scratch.- Skill tree is not as big as Path of Exile's but, expansive enough to make a unique class and experiment- Beautiful environments- More character creation customization options compared to other ARPGsCons:- Storytelling is a bit weak and dialogs have been uninspiring.- Weird rubber banding effect with melee weapons. (I hope this is just a bug that will be fixed.)I haven't reached end game yet. I'll update this review once I do.

_childDocuments_.review: Been following the game from kickstarter, but sadly was only able to actually try it until a few days ago. The game pretty early in it's development, so expect the game to have numerous stability issues and not much in terms of content. With that said, even in this early form the game is brimming with potential. The aRPG genre is nothing new, however the game already doing a lot of things differently to set it apart from it's peers. For one thing, even at this early stage, the graphics are beautiful, definitely one of the best looking aRPGs out there. The game combat has a lot of weight, making every hit very satisfying. The multiplayer and coop aspects are very promsing, althought the moment it is not developed into the game yet. Early Access is always a gamble but bearing in mind that this stuidio is often highlighed by Crytek themselves and how active they are in the forums to g ather player feedback. One should not need to worry about the game's final outcome.So in the end, I can't recommend this game at the moment if you have low tolerance to bugs and want a good experience from the moment you buy a game. _childDocuments_.review: Wolcen isn't too bad at the moment, although it had a rocky start.STORY: A simple, serviceable family opera in a fantasy setting. I didn't mind it.COMBAT: I like it, and as far as these sort of games go it seems nice.VISUALS: No complaints from me.CHARACTER CUSTOMISATION: Limited options, but I'm not complaining.BUILD CUSTOMISATION: It helps if watch a youtube guide if you are still a bit new to the genre and skill trees, but you LORE AND WORLD: It is no Song of Fire and Ice or LOTR. It didn't seem deep, but I liked the perspective of the way that the in game organisations were run, including the city and the army.EASTER EGGS AND EXPLORATION: I don't know of many.SKILLS: Deceptively varied, you can modify skills to do things I didn't know they could do until I saw other pull of interesting things on youtube.MUSIC: Nice, more so in a new republic than original wow kind of way.COMPETITIVE BALANCE: I have no idea, I'm the wrong person to ask.MULTIPLAYER: I have no idea, I'm the wrong person to ask.OVERVIEW: If you enjoy hack and slash ARPGs without needing lore, well balanced competition, or exploration easter eggs, then this game seems fine. I got it on sale, and apart from its launch I don't regret it.Honestly, I think their studio is small and what they have accomplished is something to be proud of, and while I'd like to ask more from them I am surprised by how well they have done, all things considered. I wish I could code combat feel, animation and skill variety like they do. But I think that they should try and figure out which market they are trying to go for - is it for the competitive community, whimsical build makers, multiplayer parties, or whimsical world explorers? Because each type of gamer group has expectations, and at this stage I'd recommend the experience for the build makers because the others I mentioned are not really having their expectations met.

_childDocuments_.review: Wolcen is a game - not necessarily a good game, but it is a game. It is an experience, not one you should necessarily have, but one you may encounter. It is what happens when you take good and bad mechanics, merge them, and call the result perfect because good and bad balance out to neutral.TL;DR: I can not in good faith recommend the game.The Graphics are very average for the current time of gaming. Things try to look realistic and ultimately fail at it and end up looking like someone put color onto plastic and called it dirt. Animations are smooth, but uneventful and overall just feel like fillers. While the sound design of the game is pretty okay, the voice acting is average at best. Not exactly an award winner, but also not the worst. Just again, the exact balance between good and bad, neutral.It is as standard Hack and Slash as it could be. You have a Top-Down view on things slightly tilted to the side, have actions in addition to your primary attack, with various classes of actions. Actions can be offensive, defensive, or movement, and they can level up to be modified to do some different things. You also get your character stats to freely modify and your damage scales with whatever your Primary stat happens to be. Then there's the "skill" tree, with three freely rotate-able rings, so you can combine Melee-Ranged-Magic, Ranged-Melee-Ranged, and any kind of cobination you can think of. So far so standard.Investing anything into either of the two feels like nothing changes, as the biggest improvements come in the form of gear, which improves as you level up. Effectively the only actual improvement you can make is leveling up to get better gear, which allows you to level up again.Combat is pretty slow, but fair. There aren't many insta-kill attacks that I could encounter. If you don't have any destructible boxes nearby it's actually somewhat easy, but if you do your character will prioritize those boxes over any enemies nearby. Boss fights are pretty much just click, move, and hope that a cutscene doesn't interrupt the gameplay.The story is pretty bad and feels like it was added in post just to have a story. The backstory is next to nonexistent, character development was cut off with an axe, story progressing is pretty much "Hold my beer and watch this" and Cutscenes are just inserted into the middle of anything with no transition or warning at all. It is one of the most jarring experiences I've played in over 10 years. A rollercoaster has more of a story and character development than Wolcen does over an hour of gameplay.The game requires you to connect with a third-party server provided by them, despite the game being on Steam where Peer-To-Peer playing is a solved problem. The servers are super laggy and react delayed to everything, which makes the game even more jarring to play. The best comparison I have to this experience is Path of Exile with 2 seconds of server lag.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm about 35 - 40 hours into the game. If I had to rate it on a stars rating, it'd get 3.8. Here's a rough breakdown:PROS* Pretty good hack & slash * Making the skills for all classes simply droppable/purchaseable is amazing and I've waited for ages for a game to do this.* Class tree progression has depth and is pretty fascinating. That you can rotate the rings of the tree to make a more linear path for progression is fascinating and a great idea.* Graphics in general and those for skills and spells do a good job to make you feel pretty awesome* No issues with my save game getting messed up/corrupted/lost, but I am playing "online".* Story gets a 3 out of 5. It's not amazing, but it's enough to keep you moving.* All the components to make this a 5/5 star game are present, but the developers made choices that detracted from this potential.* Allowing the ability to reroll character points & class path points for a reasonable price is most welcome.* The interplay when your character and Valeria is well done and the only emotional lynch pin this game has, sadly. There is Hemlock, but his voice acting is flat so I just don't feel it.CONS* I don't know why hack & slash games, especially those trying so hard to be Diablo, make legendaries exceedingly rare or level blocked, but this game does. That greatly hampers the excitement of loot rather than building it up. Getting a legendary per session in Diablo is a pretty great cadence IMHO.* Dropping crafting components with no mention or hint of a crafting system is maddening* Having literally 1 NPC that sells gear is super annoying especially when there's no clear conveyance of when his loot changes. If you log off and log back on, he'll have the same stuff in both cases. That's incredibly underwhelming.* The lack of variety in NPC loot vendors lends to gold hoarding. Seriously...I have over 100K gold and nothing to spend it on.  A gamble NPC would be welcome, but only if you could get legendary from him...which you probably couldn't if one did exist.* I've come across 2 NPC's in the world that sell a single unique item. The first time I didn't have enough gold. The second time, it wasn't something I wanted. I have yet to see any such NPC again. That's maddening.* I found the equivalent of a treasure goblin...once. Just...why make that so rare?* The game really does need an ingame codex for some of the affixes you discover because it really hard to know what they do specifically. Adding +9 to my critical score....does what? By what percent does that actually increase my crit chance?* The only stat worth a damn IMHO is Ferocity. I've dumped all my character points into it for the most part. My crit chance is about 44% and crit damage around 250%. The over simplification of character stats is a detriment to the game.* The acting for Hemlock is sub-par. The voice is right, but his lack of emotion takes away from some moments that are supposed to be more impactful. He just comes off as flat.* In one scene early the game Eadric is all about "We'll do this together, sister. NO matter what." In the very next level, he's like, "well if they're going to execute you, that's your fate. Accept it." Wait, what? There's no good explaination for this.* Crafting is an end-game component that happens after you essentially beat the game...Yeah, this is trying to come off as the premium product but ending up like that My Pillow guy. So, like I said. The stuff to make the game amazing exists. In short do this:* Make legendaries drop at a cadence of once per session * Build crafting into the game from the start. Revamp crafting to whatever degree needed to make that possible.* Add a codex to explain affixes or quantify the pros/cons of equiping one piece of gear over another * Revamp the character stats and how they work. Take that back to the drawing board.

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of this review there are 99k players online with 20k mixed reviews.The reviews went from positive to mixed due to bugs, exploits and the online mode not being available for several days. I have experienced worse or similar launches for other games, some being AAA titles.     For background purposes some of the ARPGs I have played are Diablo, Diablo II, Diablo III, Titan Quest, Din's Curse, Grim Dawn, Torchlight I, Torchlight II, Hellgate London, Deathtrap, Sacred I, Sacred II, Victor Vran and Path of Exile. My top three favorites being Diablo II, Path of Exile and Grim Dawn.     I have beaten the game's story twice now, I used the same build, offline and online. I played offline initially to test my build while the servers were down but I kept going as I enjoyed the story and gameplay so much.     Though the story is not particularly long it is engaging and written significantly better than certain other ARPGS. Act 2 was my favorite, I found it quite charming. Also you are not met to repeat the story multiple times on different difficulty levels, there is a seperate endgame mode that you unlock of all of your characters once you complete the story.     The graphics, audio and gameplay are all very well done.The lighting and shadows, voice acting and textures are all top notch.Customization of your actual character is bare bones and the model for a female player is ... well her legs are 3x the length of her torso. Now the customization allowed by the transmog system is exceptional. Every item you pick up gets added to your list of possible transmog choices. You will also find many different dye colors over the course of playing. You can apply multiple dyes to various pieces of armor for an high level of armor visual customization.     This game plays closer to Diablo 3 than PoE but uses a PoE like skill tree; I personally enjoy the amount of depth in character build creation as there are no classes.     In combat you generally only auto attack to gain resources to use your active skills. You have two resources and they are polar opposites, one is willpower and the other is rage. As you use active skills that consume rage, you gain willpower; the reverse is true if you spend willpower you accumulate rage. By default your willpower regenerates over time however you can put a point into a passive skill not that reverses it, allowing you to generate rage over time instead. There are recharging potions and health globes that drop. Each active skill can be modified to suit a player's preferred play style.     This game includes a dodge mechanic, initially you start with 4 recharging dodge rolls that you will need to avoid devastating attacks as well as instant kill moves. Many players complain about the difficulty of the story, particularly the bosses for each act. While they are more complex than any other ARPG at this time you cannot simply fight them with a poor build and you do have to learn their patterns or you will lose; this is in spite of the fact that you have 3 revives per fight.     After you beat the story once, unlike other ARPGS, you enter a post game gamemode which consists of randomized dungeons similar to rifts and map dungeons similar to PoE. It also includes a town upgrade system that gives you bonuses as you complete the upgrades.     Right now the game has quite a few bugs and some issues lacking polish. The dev team, while small, is working around the clock to improve the game as fast as they can. Their level of communication (twitter) is very much appreciated. It appears online play is also stable now. Keep in mind offline characters are stored locally and cannot be taken online, this is to prevent cheating. Cheating/exploiting online, according to the EULA you accept, is punishable with a ban.     Overall I really enjoy the game, even over some AAA title ARPGS and I would highly recommend it.Its charming. So charming.

_childDocuments_.review: so i had bought this game late December and kinda found it lackluster and dropped it after about 6 hours, However over the past weekend i picked it back up and beat the game and have been running bounty dungeons and daily dungeons pretty much none stop since Friday, and now on top of fairly lackluster i also find it unbelievably disappointing. There are so many good ideas in this game and unfortunately none of them are implemented well, the back and forth of you UMBRA and RAGE is a really interesting idea and honestly could of carried me on this game by itself, BUT in my experience and from what most of my friends who play this have experienced is dual "class" builds do not really work so you end up going for a rage user or umbra user, stack skill points that allow  you gain as much of your resource back as fast as humanly possible and carry either a rage or umbra potion to help refill your meter then ignore the concept in its entirety, the next unbelievably disappointing feature is the neat way they made the skill tree which allows you to rotate each tier of the tree to path in different ways to allow you to get to certain parts that otherwise might be unassailable to the build you are going for, however if you disconnect any part of your tree in deeper tiers you do not gain benefits from those passives rendering the model useless. Lastly and i feel this is very prudent to this kind of game during each play session i had usually about 6-9 hours to play during wich  i was forced to leave the game usually 7-10 times, either due to bad collision getting me stuck, quests not completing, bosses not spawning, my character not spawning when going into or leaving dungeons, and a really annoying bug related to getting frozen by enemy's  that can leave you with the frozen status effect forever and you unable to do anything, yes i am aware that this is early access and that bugs happen i get that trust me but when you are forced to quite because someone cant get collision right or because someone left a stupid freeze effect bug in the game it  is aggravating and if you can still have fun at that point i am so happy for you i wish i could as well but all these issues considered i can not in good faith or conscious recommend this game , which feels bad there is so much potential here for an amazing wonderful classic of a game that could stick with you for years to come, but as it stands its an irritating disappointment that will leave you feeling bitter rather then happy to have spent your 20 dollars on.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Can be fun but depends on where you draw the line with all the downsides.The game is fun or rather it can be fun, but it has so many issues I just can't recommend it. I would understand if this was Alpha or Beta, but it's supposedly a finished product. We the consumers paid for something that isn't working - server issues aside (some people still have them though) - the game has a ton of bugs (even game breaking ones), severely lacks in informing user of what items, passives (a lot aren't even working) or ability modifications do. Regarding offline mode some people can't even play that.The only thing that was tested was ACT 1, and let me just say that I have no idea how the act boss got released in this buggy mess and I can't even imagine (since I couldn't beat the act 1 boss because apparently I need to L2P around the bugs) what Act 2 & 3 are like since those haven't been tested before the release.For some reason we also can't unbind the left mouse click which is the default for auto attack and moving - which means you'll find yourself attacking a mob when you wanted to move out of the harms way.Most of my "game play" was spent in the menu trying to play online and offline on a modified max lvl character killing some stuff to see what the endgame has to offer because I didn't want to ruin the starting experience for me and my friends, did I mention that co-op also has issues?REVISION: Since steam didn't grant me a refund because apparently being in the main menu and trying to log in to the game counts as "playing" I had no choice but to suck it up and play the game in offline and then online once the servers were fixed (worked for me at least). At a first glance the game is great, but it's really just a turd with nice looks but sadly you can't tell that until you get to the endgame because nothing is tested, and I just saw the steam banner shows the game is "Out of early access", yeah no this game is still in early access be it alpha or beta but definitely shouldn't be advertised as a full release, because that is quite frankly not true, false advertising and should NOT BE ALLOWED BY STEAM!
