_childDocuments_.review: Wolcens core mechanics are an entire mess, even the most basic ones. Gold drops rarely increase and you have to pickup and sell every sh*t you find, gems cannot be improved in quality, you just pile em up and when you reach the next quality level you sell the rest. But regarding the drops and the gold, you have to pick up every rare+ item anyway, because there is no way to tell if its a good or bad item before it isnt in your inventory.The item management is one of the worst aswell, you can right click items and put them into or remove them from the stash, but it only works like 30-40% of the time, the other times you just pick up the item.When you want to edit the item at the jeweler, you cannot just pick it up from the Gem Removal Tab and put it into the Socket Editing Tab without putting it into your inventory first.When you want to try out a different item and check how the stats change, the items dont swap at the cursor, they swap the inventory place they were in.The map system is trash and there are like 3 or 4 different area layouts with giant pre built tiles which never feel like you experience just a little variaty.When you are dont with your map series, dont forget to click the two interfaces because when you log out, all progress would be wasted because you dont automatically get the rewards.Skills are a bare minimum and can be reduced to 3-4 usefull attack skills which heavily favour 2h weapons, shields are useless garbage because any weapon can easily reach 100% block, but then block isnt really block because there is a percentual damage reduction on a successful block behind it.The passive tree looks more complicated than it actually is since you can skill like 2/3rd of it and everything pretty much comes down to the same nodes. In addition to that you cannt just respec 1 or a few nodes even though they have the PoE Orb system alsong with the ancient gold based one, instead you have to spend resources you get from finding duplicate skills to do a FULL RESET of the tree, even for 1 single node.While mages get automatic willpower regeneration, melee characters need to either build rage by basic attacking mobs or spend like 13 passive points to swap from willpower reg to rage regenaration.Uniques are a hot dump of useless crap because they cap out at level 40 of 90.The story stops right in the middle with a giant cliffhanger without even letting you know that you bought a half finished product. Even  better, the next 1 of 2 acts is released in around 8 months they say.If you are just a man of beautiful garbage and dont mind that everything else is badly "stolen", this game is for you. Otherwise just wait 1-2 years and check if it'll improve.Oh and btw, the interface might show you a ping of 15-20 but there is a lag the game doesnt show you, you can feel it clearly, sometimes projectiles pass an opponent and register a second later along with other indicators.There is so much wrong with it that you'll really appreciate PoE, apart from its 2000s engine and the really close camera maybe.

_childDocuments_.review: I recently picked up Wolcen: Lords of Mayhem on sale and decided to give it a try without any prior knowledge of the game. My review is based on playing through the story and a couple of missions, reaching level 65. As such, I have yet to experience the potential bugs or issues that may be present in high-level gameplay.So far, I haven't encountered any game-breaking bugs or crashes.The game's story is genuinely interesting and well-executed. The voice acting most of the time is top-notch, and the cutscenes throughout the game help to immerse the player in its world. I found myself becoming invested in the story, which is a testament to the game's writing and the performance of the voice actors.However, Wolcen is not without its issues. Loading times can be a significant problem on occasion, even on high-end PCs. This issue can be frustrating, especially when trying to maintain immersion in the game's world. Another problem is the secondary quest reward pop-ups, which can obscure a large portion of the screen during combat. A simple fix for this would be to delay the pop-up until the player is out of immediate danger.One major aspect of the game that could use improvement is the lack of a loot filter. As with many action RPGs, Wolcen has a vast array of items that can be found and used, but without an adequate filter, it can become tedious to sift through everything to find what you need.Additionally, there is a minor annoyance where minions can block portals, making it difficult to click on them. This issue could be quickly addressed by making the portals easier to click or giving the player an alternative way to interact with them.As a newcomer to the game, I found it to be an enjoyable experience with a captivating story and solid gameplay mechanics. I'm not sure if I will play this game long term, but I will definitely check back from time to time. Playing through the story was worth buying the game at a 75% discount for sure.In conclusion, Wolcen: Lords of Mayhem could be a diamond in the rough. While it has its flaws, the engaging story and gameplay make it worth trying out, especially if you can find it on sale. I found the concept of skills and skill tree to be quite interesting, and I was able to put together a build on my own that got me to 65 with no problems. With more tweaks and polish, this game might become a must-have in the ARPG genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Play fighter: have to deal with horrible melee attack animationsPlay archer: have to deal with horrible hit detection including enemies that straight up CANNOT be hit by your ranged attacks.Play mage: Game crashes over and over again.I don't think there's a way to win with this game. I finally bought it after it had been out for a couple years because I assumed that the glitches that people complained about in the negative reviews would have been addressed. If this is the state of the game after YEARS of bugfixing then I hate to imagine what it was like on release. I don't have high standards for ARPGs. _childDocuments_.review: This game has come a long way since its Early Access days. As reflected in the Steam user review ratings, it has been a rocky road for Wolcen Studio and their flagship title. I've played it off and on since very early in its development. I've seen it go through some major changes and overhauls. The game we have today resembles the original very little. At one point you could even build your own house to display your trophies. It seemed that Wolcen didn't know which direction to go.  They wanted a dark and grim fantasy world ARPG. Hardcore gamers themselves, they wanted to make what they thought Diablo 3 should have been, a lofty and admirable goal. It took them some time to figure out what the fans wanted, but they did, and now it finally shows. This is one of those titles that would have been better off waiting for full release rather than making it available in early access, since current ratings reflect earlier stages of the game. It's a win for players, but the devs take it by way of long-standing negative reviews that remain long after they become irrelevant.  What we ended up with here seems like a compromise between the dev's vision and what the fans wanted. The game is much more like D3 than the devs would probably like to admit, right down to the voice actors and their lines.  ,who apparently does all the female lines in every video game now, is still "unstoppable!"   A little history out of the way, the game is currently a solid ARPG experience that fans of the genre are sure to love. If you were disappointed by the early state of the game, now is a great time to dive in and start working a build. A big endgame update is on the way this month, offering 4 new game modes, and I'm excited for that.  What makes Wolcen different from D3, Grim Dawn and PoE? The classless build system. You choose a starting weapon and from there you can adapt your build however you like. Stats are determined by items, equipment and gear. You get your 10 attribute points per level, and passive skill points, to allocate however you like. Certain gear set-ups allow you to hybridize and optimize across different skill sets. You can use both magic and melee if you want. And you can switch it up at any time. This allows for an unprecedented level of freedom in your build. So far I've made a Void Witch, a Toxic Assassin, a Blood Baron, a Holy Crusader, a Pyromancer, and more, some of them from the same character. Skills and abilities have real impact, they feel nice and weighty, very satisfying to play. Certainly there is a difficulty curve between mobs and bosses. Clearing mobs is no indicator of your ability to take on a big boss. While I haven't had to grind over already tread paths, the option is there if you need it. If you falter at the bosses, it is 100% your build, which is easily remedied by grinding and/or trying something different. The latter is not easily achievable, if at all, in other games in this genre. In Wolcen, you can switch up gear and tweak stats a bit, and voila! a whole new class to try without starting a new character. The game looks amazing, built on CryEngine, it is more detailed than any top-down isometric I've ever played. It is truly stunning to explore the different environments. The gameworld is a work of art, and the 3D models for everything from gear to actors are no less aesthetic. This is a labor of love and it truly shows. If you tried it before and walked away with a bad taste, try it again, you will be pleasantly surprised. Wolcen is a must-play for any ARPG fan.*My ReShade preset

_childDocuments_.review: Stay away from this game, or give it a while. It's got issues and it really seems like the devs either have no idea what to do, or they don't care. This situation is exactly like the launch of "Hunt Showdown". In comparison, the Hunt devs released their game and left to have a launch party. The game was unplayable. Not a figure of speech, was literally unplayable. They ignored a server bug for all of beta, and it crashed the servers for the entire night almost instantly. Now on to Wolcen. The devs had 5 YEARS in EA to work things out, and the game was on the top sellers for days before launch. Either they are oblivious to their own purchase numbers, or they simply don't care. I'm inclined to believe it's option #2. The online aspect of this game has been down for days at this point, and there's no end in sight. They keep posting updates about the servers on their discord, but it's pointless. The updates have been "We'll tell you tomorrow at noon", leaving the servers down. All this put together tells me that they are simply not trying to fix the issue. The servers were taken down because of two bugs; Item stashes removing items after hotfixes, and players losing progress after hotfixes. There's basically no other reason the servers would go down for this long to fix two issues like that. My guess is the devs gave up and left for the weekend. They made 3 million USD off launch, so they just left the servers down and went home.TLDR: Wait on this game if you're interested. As of now, Online does not function at all. It's a shame because the game is decent.This was Wolcens' time in the spotlight, but instead of showing the world that it could be THE next ARPG, Wolcen just crapped it's pants on stage. One of, if not the worst launch in the last decade.

_childDocuments_.review: The hardest boss is the glitches.Wolcen offers flashy, engaging, visceral combat - but it falls on its face when poor hit-boxes and odd design choices make it seem like your actions don't "work". The rolling mechanic rarely seems to work as intended, and bosses often hit you despite you being behind them/outside the area they're attacking. This makes it quite frustrating.The story is largely predictable and generic - it's fairly pretty for the genre, and I would say it runs well, except that it seems like it's dependent upon connection to their servers for everything, and that connection failing abruptly kicks you out of the game. The leveling mechanic hearkens to PoE, but it doesn't feel as fleshed out and certainly not as balanced. Although I don't necessarily see this as a negative, the different "classes" you can choose to pursue don't seem very balanced. There are some obviously pushed abilities that will make most encounters feel the same.No drop-in co-op is a big miss. That's really one of the best things about this genre, and it just feels incomplete without it.Overall right now it really feels like a solid tech demo. If they can make it stable, tighten up the combat mechanics, and add drop-in co-op, it'd be a gem. As is, I can't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: ARPGs are meant to have fun combat, good customization, and fun grinds for loot. Overall, Wolcen is worth the $40 price tag for its fun combat and amazing customization alone.+ Combat is fun+ Vast amounts of customization to cater any playstyle you'd like+ Gorgeous graphics and VFX for spells/abilities+ Good content for its price+ Unique story, not a Diablo clone+ Interesting mix of fantasy, scifi, and other themes+ Pets can pick up loot; auto-pickup gold+ Boss fights feel unique and are fun. Later acts have more challenging bosses to make-up for the insanely easy act I and early act II "difficulty"+ Beautiful level design and badass or gruesome looking enemies.+ Awesome music+ You can take on the form of an apolocalyptic deity. Albeit, not that often. However, each one is unique and have some fun abilities.+/- Clunky movement (animation cancelling) compared to other ARPGs. Once you're used to it, you can manage around it.+/- The game is too easy for the majority of the campaign. Difficulty spikes suddenly happen when you start reaching act II bosses. There's only Story & Normal mode. The game needs higher difficulties. This may have been due to the initial playthrough is treated as a longtime tutorial, slowly introducing you to more game systems. Perhaps the devs want to avoid the typical artificial inflation of difficulty that plagues this genre. Still, my boredom from lack of challenge was forgoed by combat's sheer fun and my curiosity to experiment in different ways of obliterating enemies with combos of spells and abilities.+/- End-game systems revolve around city management as a mechanism for end-game systems for continued skill and gear grinding+/- The game apparently has crafting. I never used it and it was never explained to me by the game.- Bit rough to learn at first since there's so many stats and the game just throws you into it without much guidance. A lot of combat metrics/stats could benefit from more tooltip info. What's the difference between attack power and weapon attack power? Do they interact? Etc.- Campaign ends on a cliff hanger, leaving you unsatisfied with the story.- Movement bugs will sometimes trap you forcing you to teleport to the city hub. Or will make some mini-dungeons completely unplayable as you cannot move past invisible wall- Desync of mouse cursor, character, and your movement--- Always online required. You cannot interchangeably play your online character with offline mode. They are completely separate. Wtf??

_childDocuments_.review: I can't speak for those, who bought it at release or even backed it during development.What I can say however, is that it feels amazing to use skills in this game. Enemies are numerous and skills are varied. You can choose perks for every skill and even change the damagetype it does, allowing build variety. Sounddesign is great and possibly the enemy design too.Why "possibly"? Because it is not a very hard game (at least at the beginning of the endgame). Running a self made hybrid damage build I barely see the attack patterns from enemies / bosses because of the "break" mechanic. Big enemies are shielded but after breaking through they get stunned and get killed pretty fast.This leads sometimes to pretty much instant deaths for you, when getting hit, because most of the time you win unharmed. However this means most of the time you don't know how tanky you are...I think Wolcen's greatest problem is that there are little problems in most areas:1. Bugs: In the last area I moved like I was glued to the ground. Nothing gamebreaking but for the final area pretty anticlimactic. Then there are the game modes: Online or offline. One of my skills felt laggy, possibly because even while playing solo in online mode, you have to have a good internet connections, otherwise everything lags around. Also 2 times during campaign I was disconnected from server. Again: Nothing gamebreaking.2. Variety: I'd love to make a mage with a two handed weapon, but I can't. Skills are tied to equipped weapon. This means when you use a two handed weapon you limit your options significantly, so experimenting with all skills (the most fun for me) is only possible with the right type of main weapon and a cestus.3. The number of equippable skills is pretty limited: Until endgame you have 5 skills, in endgame you can equip one more. However I didn't feel too limited, but I'd wish there was a second bar available, so you could switch depending on the situation.4. While the campaign's story is solid and sometimes even great it wastes potential at critical points. For example your hub city gets destroyed more and more during campaign, but if you just move to the traders and port back into action, you wouldn't notice! There are voicelines and critical worldbuilding you won't notice if you just play the game. Oh, and the campaign isn't finished. The final act isn't released right now.That said overall it feels great to play and looks good. The endgame is grindy but what game of this type isn't grindy? And I like the idea of rebuilding the city in endgame.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Due to the prompt fixing of many of the games bugs I am returning my review back to positive.Wolcen takes a much appreciated horizontal approach to the evolution of the ARPG genre. Other game's of the genre tend to evolve it by adding more depth to some features, or streamlining others. The developers of Wolcen were brave when it comes to making changes to the typical ARPG formula and the game greatly benefits from this. The game still needs some bug squashing (one quite ridiculous bug had some weak mobs that I was unable to target via normal attacks) and some optimization in a few of the games areas. All in all this game is a major win and its improvements included in the launch patch are awe inspiring. Pros:-By far the best visuals the genre has to offer-Mostly superb optimization with the exception of a few areas-Systems that are just intricate enough without getting out of hand-interesting combat with a new take on resource management and an actually useful dodge mechanic-well telegraphed enemy attacks-beautiful cut scenes, story sequences and impressive voice acting from such a small studio-fantastic animations-challenging and sophisticated boss fights- Stunning environments - No item sets?cons:-Some bugs-Could use some general polish-Though loot is abundant the game does not appear to have gear with interesting affixes - Some frame drops and stutter may rarely occur

_childDocuments_.review: Old Alpha review below...So the game has been released. With a ton of bugs. With poor balance. I don't know man, isn't that what Early Acces was for? Small team or not. They took their time, revamped the  game twice and well, the latest version is kind of new with the same assets and hence full of bugs and exploitable stuff.===Those things aside. Is the core gameplay good? No, not really. The skill tree still feels kind of unfinished and uninspired. You can easily spot what came from Diablo 3 and what came from Path of Exile. This game is 75% D3 influence though. The engine looks goods. Performance is better than in Alpha for sure.But the killer is how sluggish  it all feels. How boring the visually lively areas are. But even if the graphics are good, the environments are all reskinned caves. Some stairs and ancient buildings here and there instead of cave rubble. And man, did they lean heavily on Diablo 3 environments...The skills are not that special, even if the rage / mana system is. But your character feels like it is playing very indirect. Targetting ranged skills is awkward at times. Sometimes you cannot name lock some enemies anymore. Sometimes your projectiles just don't connect. Melee has some dash to make it better which is a saving grace, but it is a patch for a flawed mechanic.Enemies have too much health. Or annoying regeneration. I hate those things in ARPGs. The occasional challenge, fine. But make it cool due to mechanics. Having to spam your attacks five times extra on enemies that are no treat to you at all is just boring and a grind.Items are kind of the same. The artwork is fine, but why call every single bow "bow"? Why not give them names so you see some progression there too. Give the items some more character.  Some pistols have it, but staves don't really, they fire the same projectile in a different color.And then there's the first Act boss. I do like some Dark Souls gameplay, but why... Eventhough I have a fiber connection, on 21ms latency, it feels like I'm playing behind. I can see the well telegraphed attacks coming, but is my character snapping out of his animation in time? Dark Souls works because the controls are thight enough. You can build and equip gear in certain ways. Here you are, 60% of your points invested in speed through agility and still you feel just a bit  too slow. Hitboxes of the attacks aren't true,  sometimes you see stuff flashing around and you just die. No hint to what happened. These servers need work. Dark Souls like Boss health pools and punishing attacks with a very strong focus on dodging isn't fun if the boss randomly lags out on you. Can you image having to rely on RNG to get through the last of a 3 stage fight  that drags on forever on the first two phases?Well, I have had enough, I'm not coming back any time soon,  what a waste of money and time.=== Beta review: Which sadly still holds true on a lot of accounts.Well, so the Alpha is over, and the game still feels generic and low on content.The new combat system leaves a lot of room for improvement, there's not much to do really, gameplay feels slow, slower than Diablo 2,3 or Path of Exile. They wanted to borrow from the more tactical Warhammer 4K ARPGs I guess, but there's still VERY little tactics here...The beta content right now is boring. It's a walking / attack spam fest till you hit lvl 15 on your class at which skills and gear start to scale.Looks best out of all ARPG titles, but stylewise and environmentally boring. If the story / missions of  the Alpha are  indication, I don't expect a strong plot or great story telling either.Hope the upcoming beta patches improve things, because right now, there's not much that warrants the price tag at all.This game is what Warlords or The Surge is to Dark Souls. Looks good, has potential, but overal isn't enjoyable and low in content.Oh and did I mention the new EULA that states ingame currency for BOTH cosmetics and ingame special items? Pay to win, while admittedly they strive to ban all cheaters, even in offline? Oh no...

_childDocuments_.review: Just want to preface this review with the fact that I recently played this again after a break for over a year.I played this at launch for quite a while. Seemed like a fairly solid game with good gameplay and graphics.  A year and a half in I cannot recommend this game at all  you plan to play offline 100% of the time, or have the patience of a saint.Game is pretty balanced and, like any other game in the same genre, some builds are better than others, There are some bugs, like other reviews have stated, but I feel like, from my experience, the story gives a decent experience.  Switching from one build to another, melee -> ranger/magic, are easily made during character development for the most part,  Find a sweet 2-hander while you're a mage and want to switch, not too hard of a transition.  That said, if you're a completionist do not buy this game, you will not be able to complete every part of the storyline unless you're willing to work around all the problems with the game.After coming back to the game after a decent amount of time I found that some of the new features seemed to be positive to the experience. Gameplay seemed smoother and the skills seemed fairly easy to understand, albiet with a veteran player they should be easy to understand.My biggest gripe of this game is that it is default always-online. Which is most likely a decision made by management due to investor BS to 'protect revenue'. There is no mixing of online/offline characters. This is understandable to an extent, but when you take into account that  they release will break online play, it becomes a problem.  Semi-related to this problem is that when there are discovered exploits, their tactic is to nerf everyone's online character.  After the first wave of exploits were removed, they decided to take everyone's wallets down to 100k gold, which may have just been those who took advantage of the expoits - I can accept that.  However I played for a few weeks after that, but when I came back to the game my wallet was nerfed back down to 100k again, even after having gone back to playing legit! I should note here, that the end-game gold grind is/was atrocious at the time. You have no control over your profiles/characters which you play with your friends; take that for what you will.TL;DR: Good game with a good story, lots of promise, becomes giant let-down because of what I can assume is management. In turn, management doesn't give the slightest of ♥♥♥♥♥ about the experience for end users.  When patches break the game, there is no communication to the community, just dead silence.  I don't want to misrepresent this as an isolated issue; when there's a patch you should expect to not be able to play online for a couple days, and this has been their  since launch. Even at launch patches frequently broke the game for online play.TL;DR;DR: Decent game, but only buy if you're playing offline single-player; they break every other online patch.

_childDocuments_.review: Even putting aside the server issues preventing online play, even putting aside game breaking bugs that wipe act progress and lock up your computer, the game itself just...isn't great.Abilities are locked to weapons rather than classes, which at first glance might sound freeing but it's frankly more restricting than a traditional class option. The balance is all over the place, a warrior with a two handed weapon will crush absolutely everything while mages or rangers struggle to out damage their auto attacks with abilities. There are far too few spells/abilities in the game as well, for spells there are essentially 1 damage spell for each element with occasional utility abilities that deal damage while warrior/ranger abilities are themselves just spells that summon phantom weapons rather than use your actual gear. And all of the skills available in the game are obtained by the end of act 1, there's nothing else to look forward to after that.The game is remarkably easy, only the act bosses really pose a challenge while the rest of the game barely seems to fight back against you. And this is on the 'difficult' mode rather than the story mode.Would recommend virtually any other diablo clone over this game at the moment, and this will take a lot of work to reach not just a playable but a recommendable state.

Also, there are numerous bugs that prevent you from advancing in the game, wiping your stash, giving you infinite gold, etc. This game was not ready for release, and to be frank I'm not sure what they spent the last 4 years in beta doing.

_childDocuments_.review: First off: bugs! Server issues! Technical issues! With that out of the way...this has got to be the blandest ARPG I have ever played. Most mechanics and design principles habe been copied from games that have done them better. Granted, the passives tree is not all that bad. But the rest is really mediocre. Yes, it looks good...but that's pretty much it.But the worst offender in this game has got to be the loot. That's what we grind for, right?  Wolcen, Legendaries are (with a few exceptions) just slightly upgraded versions of their rare counterparts, meaning that getting one (which doesn't happen all that often) does feel pretty bad. But there's a higher tier of items: uniques! And do they feel special in any way. For the most part not, no. Look, in other ARPGs, there are items that can either drastically enhance your build by bringing something to the table, that build didn't have access to before. Or it altered your build. Or it just made a skill really useful, that would otherwise haven been rather "meh" (I'm looking at you, Jekangboard!). None of those items can be found here. Okay, a handful of those can be found here. Maybe. Can it compete with Diablo 3 in terms of gear variance and options? Nope. What about Grim Dawn? Nope. 35€ will get you games that offer a lot more depth than Wolcen does.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit:Eh, I guess it really depends on what you're looking for in a game. Once you finish the story, which simply ends abruptly on a cliff hanger (F that), the negative aspects of this game really become clear.Lag and unresponsiveness is just a really big thing in this game. Often times the named enemies cancel their animations and blink on top of you; a fraction of a second later you go from 100% HP to dead (42 ms ping...). It feels like about 30 % of your auto attacks just don't register as hits to enemies or destructible objects; you can see the animation, the bullets just pass right through them. You often have to move around to get your ranged attacks to register at a different angle.I could go on about other aspects but other negative reviews cover them in great detail. _childDocuments_.review: I don't comment a lot but I wanted to input my statements here. For those who enjoyed playing Diablo III and Path of Exile, this is your game. So Basically, this game is Diablo III meets Path of Exile. You get the flasks like Path of Exile, the passive nodes, a few other things too (Which is freaking awesome), but the rest is just like Diablo III, literally a clone. The cool thing I really enjoy the most is that this game is based on Crytek Engine (Crysis and Far Cry), which graphics are amazing, very vivid colours while keeping the grim vibe from Diablo 2. This game reminds me of Devilian (MMO-A-RPG). You get a super power version of your character when fighting enemies (Just like a VAAL Skill in Path of Exile), but instead of being a skill, it's your whole character that goes in a trance mode, just like the Archon form or Wrath of the Berserker in Diablo 3. That's my reviews for Wolcen so far. 2020/02/27.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a mess, and complete false advertisement.  How the hell can they call this a full released game. Servers started out completely broken, characters being deleted, stashes being deleted, constant crashes, items missing after crashes. Game economy breaking exploits that from what i've read have been around since "beta".Severs being ♥♥♥♥ aside lets go into the broken game play.  I put 86 hours into this game TRYING to give it a fair chance.  Broken skill trees,  from over tuned abilities to abilities that just straight up DONT work.2h staff and bow seem like a joke but its what ever.   lets get into things that just BREAK the game.So im lvl 75 map level 121, tryin to progress.  Putting resources into ubers nets me zero reward *they since fixed this but how did they miss this to begin with?*Zoning into checkboard dead zone after spending resources on modiferes and untainted maps.  welp there goes your resources you wont get back.  Trying to upgrade reagents? if you put a stack of 20 in it spits out 1 and destroys your other 19.   Want to cancel a upgrade or quality upgrade? welp you can but you lose the item completely.  Quality upgrade doesnt even do any thing for stats.what was the complete LAST straw that made me NOT want to play this game any more is MULTIPLE occasions at least 1/4 of my runs end in some game breaking glitch that makes it so i cannot complete the level.you get one shot and you DONT get refunded after spending your gold and Primordial affinity.now that is fair if you fail.  but once you get into higher level maps they spawn 3 enemies in particular that will break your game.1.  Shield Champ that can put up a shield and reflect dmg.  He can charge you and knock you into a wall and go out of bounds which you CANNOT ROLL OUT OF or TELEPORT OUT OF!  so once that happens, alt+4 b/c you are stuck.2. Wizard champ that disapears makes a bone cage under you and teleports you to a random spot.Again so many runs ruined by being teleported into a wall that is out of bounds, or a peice of scenery that you cannot roll out of.  3. Untainted boss that spears you over and over again lifts you into the air and slams you into the ground.  AGAIN another mob that picks you up and drops you out of bounds.   on top of that these can spawn at the same time, and you have to PRAY you dont get lifted out of bounds.these literally break the game.  once you are put out of bounds you have no choice but to force shut down the game and start over.only to grind more resources to try again and hope you dont get bad RNG and pushed out of bounds.and if you are put into a Cathedral map you are pretty much screwd, you HAVE to run and avoid these mobs, because you WILL get pushed into a wall in a tight quarter map.and once you grind out a bunch of maps you'll start to realize, the maps arent randomly generated, its the same set up.    only "maps" are worth it is Omen maps for money,  bounty maps are worthless xp/loot and the treasure maps hardly spawn any treasure, not even worth doing. I dont normally write reviews but i feel cheated and robbed of my money putting time into this game. _childDocuments_.review: The game is fun at first, but needs rebalancing. I'm playing a caster (purple branch in the passive skills tree), and reached the end of act 1 at level 22.Towards the end of the first act, the enemies start to become a bit overpowered, capable of killing you in just 2-3 hits. I had probably 2100 health between my HP and shield.The act final boss is ridiculous. The boss spams enemies for potion/resource recharge, but this means that you can never hit the boss as a ranged class as they get in the way of your ranged attacks, making each phase really long.In phase 3, he can suddenly one-shot you through your shield and health if you don't dodge perfectly, and you have to keep this up this perfect dodging for a really long time, due to the mentioned enemy spam not letting you hit him. He also has you dodging some AoE from the sky here too as if it wasn't difficult enough.I'd point the developers to Grim Dawn, Torchlight 2, and Diablo 3 as examples of games that have good balance on normal difficulty.However, it could be that the developers have got themselves into a bit of a corner, since there is really nothing to tune around as your character can be anything. _childDocuments_.review: Really neat ideas for a hack and slash diablo style arpg. You can wear any armour, use any weapon and use any skill without having to make a new character. You level up the stats on your abilities and powers by having them equipped . Each skill you use is assigned specifically to any weapon you have equipped. In other words you can play however you want. You can play warrior class mixed with rouge if you hold a sword and a dagger as an example. The first act is available and took me about 6 hours to beat. After you beat the first act the after game unlocks which allows you to do random loot quests, and basically diablo III style rifts for loot. In the early access as is you can get to level 20. _childDocuments_.review: What's rather good: Yep, that graphics!What's not soo good: All the rest..First, the game is annoyingly buggy and unfinnished. Not only will triggers deny to execute, forcing you to reload the game several times. No, the whole "game" ends without any proper message. Having received the quest called "@ui_A1_Q5_S12_StepNameLabel", you will have to deduce on your own that you just experienced all available content and might want to close the application. Moreover, the minimap is buggy (does not save revealed areas, or turns completely black on a regular basis), enemies are stuck in stairs, checkpoints are not saved correctly (you sometimes must repeat a mission after quitting the game), and, and, and.. many minor bugs as well..But.. well.. I would still oversee such flaws and really look forward to the final version of Wolcen.. ..if the game itself would be fun to play. But unfortunatelly, Wolcen lacks the most important aspect of quality: A good game balance and game design.I actually LOVE to grinding creeps. I can collect items and compare stats for years. But there is nothing to love about in Wolcan! All the items barely vary in a meaningful way at all. There are 5 rarity levels, but rarity levels 3 and 4 seem not to exist at all. Unique items are super boring, especially compared to PoE or D3. You will definitely find a sh*tload of "rare" items (rarity level 2), but you will just have no fun digging through that garbage over and over again. I find that remarkable how the developers achieved to make the stat comparison of items a boring, nearly frustrating experience. Uh! Oh, and of course you can sell items for gold.. ..but you won't need gold for anything! All shop prices are completely imbalanced. And all shop offers are completely pointless. Let's put that in clear words: This is a grinding game, and I even had NO FUN finding unique items and upgrading my gear.But well, what's maybe even much worse than the lack of a nice item variety:There are NO real strategies for a possible character development and there is literally NOT A SINGLE tactical element while playing: It's just so super easy to pick ONE good skill and kill all the monster-filled floors with just that single skill. There is no real "skill" you can develop while playing the game: Just evade the enemy attacks (when they surround you, you are dead; when they do not surround you, you easily win..). Just keep button-smashing that one overpowered skill to clear every stage. In my case: I played as a hunter, and just setting up a single turret cleared the whole screen for me, INCLUDING BOSS ENEMIES! The game even to easier and easier over time! Not that there ever was a challenge at any given time. It's just that the game starts non-challenging, and then continues to get even easier with every single minute!But well, at least the skill tree looks nice.But, yeah, that's exactly it: It LOOKS nice.Having checked out the actual opportunities, even the skill tree turns out to be absolutely shallow and pointless. Yes, you can add some percentage of damage here and there. But again, there is barely any tactical and/or strategical impact. You just get stronger with ever level up. Simple as that. No increasing complexity. No meaningful decisions. No unique style of playing a character. Nothing of that at all.Plus, all the novel elements introduced by the game appear to make no sense at all. For example: In Wolcen, skills are gained by looting skill items that you will find occasionally from time to time (as normal loot from any creeps). But you will have found all five relevant skills for your class within an hour or so. And from then on, your inventory is just spammed with skills you already own. You can actually sell these skills for skill XP in order level up your skills. Nice idea. But here, again, there is NO BALANCING at all: You will have to gather and sell 30+ of these non-stackable skill items in order to successfully level up a single skill a single time.. ..but you won't do this, because all your skills already progress more than fast enough just by playing. The whole feature is implemented in a completely pointless and boring way. And the same goes for all the other features. Well.. "All the other features"? Sorry, I have to correct myself:There barely are any other features! The game has about 90% less features than PoE and/or D3, and it seems SO FAR AWAY from being finished. The release date of late January 2020 should hopefully be a joke!Currently, Wolcan is more a TECH DEMO than a proper game.It's a copycat that looks beautiful, but has nothing relevant to offer under the surface. The whole game design is boring and the game balance does not exist.Oh, and just a short word comprising the narrative design: Random. It's so random and boring I can not even tell. The dialogues are basically just a concatenation of stupid fantasy words and I never felt so disconnected to a game universe. Humm.. What else.. Boss fights are 10-20 seconds showdowns without any suspense or challenge. Winning fights in general is purely due to keeping up attention, not having any skill. There is never ever a moment where you actually have to use more than 10 of your brain cells. These are needed to match the creep allocation on the screen with your one good skill. Oh, did I mention that there is no challenge??!What else.. Dungeon generation is boring. Some sounds are just weird (VERY russian voice for african king, I actually had to laugh). Act 1 was super fast to play through (without bugs, it would have taken me 2.5 hours, I guess) - so even with Act 2, 3 and 4, there would not be enought relevant content. Yeah.. More does not come up to my mind, right now..Summed up:Wolcan is not challenging AND not rewarding at the same time.Do only buy if you'd like to see a tech demo for a hack'n'slay game made with the cryengine.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. One of the best storylines in the ARPG genre, hands down. Well written, emotive, excellent pacing. If you like stories, this is worth a try. But for us ARPG grunts who usually kek at the thought of stories being in our games, it's just great. And the ending! That's all I'll say about that.That said, people are down voting this because the company did not anticipate their game becoming this popular. they have a post saying that during beta, their peak player count was sub 2k. at launch it was over 60k. They were not prepared. Fortunately there was offline play, so you get to experience the story and learn about the game while they play catch up.Should we be angry at them for servers being down? Honestly, it's not that big a deal. Though some did lose characters, and that's rough. The game also has some glaringly (hilarious but should really not exist) bugs. Like bats that are untargetable by ranged weapon attacks and getting stuck on a ledge because you leapt at some monster that was too close and now you ant get down, so you tp and hit that waypoint. There's obvious things they gotta work out. Now, you'll probably also hear that some people are angry at the last boss of Act 1 being impossible. Spoiler, he's the easiest of the final boss fights but he can suck if you got bad loot drops and your dps or survivability is bunk. Solution? Grind a little, get your DPS to like 300 - 400, roll under his flame novas, and you'll make it through.The visuals are stunning. Not just because of the engine, but the zoomed out shots that help you imagine just how f****d up this world is. The back drops are so good. Many of the abilities are just really clean (though some are kind of jangky). Havoc orb.... LOL Anyway. This game is way better than the current 58% rating given on steam. If you like Diablo style ARPGs, if you like good character driven stories featuring characters that actually have different personalities, this game is for you. Get it.10/10 would buy again.

_childDocuments_.review: A game with plenty of potential and a seemingly dedicated dev team that was released too soon. Wolcen will definitely need some more time and tender loving care before it reaches a point where it can compete with the bigger titles in the looter ARPG market.Watch some gameplay steams or vods before buying. If it interests you, then go for it. Otherwise, hold off for a few more months.Powered by CryEngine, this game is quite easy on the eye. Environments have vibrant colours and spells look amazing. Enemies are both gorgeously designed and easily distinguished amidst the chaos. Combat information is conveyed quite well with champions and bosses having clearly marked aoe markers with *just* enough time to react.Character creation is a simple affair with only a handful of options. This is remedied by the extensive wardrobe system that includes all collected skins as well as extensive colouring options via dye drops. There is a wide variety of options, even if most of them boil down to different spikey bits with angled plates. The game foregoes a player controlled camera which can lead to situations where you may have reduced visibility or mild annoyance when casting abilities. For the most part this is not an issue, though it is a thought that would consistently reappear in my mind.Levels that are visually appealing soon become monotonous sequences of corridors. There is little variety in the actual stage layouts and the relatively limited number of stages is only exacerbated in the end-game grind. More on that later.The sound quality in Wolcen is meaty and distinct. Every ability is easily distinguished from the others, though this does not seem to apply to enemies. Key enemy abilities can become drowned out by the din of your own onslaught. The soundtrack is your general fantasy orchestra and choir. I personally find this bland and did not find it engaging enough to keep it on throughout the whole story, instead replacing it with my own playlist. After talking to others who like these types of soundtracks, I have been told that this is a very solid soundtrack that they enjoyed. For the most part, it handles like any other ARPG. Skills are LMouse for move/default attack, RMouse and 1-5 for abilities, two potion buttons, an ultimate and a dodge. Key binds are customisable, so adjust to your preferences. Inputs can feel sluggish: this is due to your character being locked into animations. Although this does not affect general gameplay, you will notice it clearly in circumstances that result in your death. Here we go. I had high hopes for this game: skill variety through a classless system, interesting attribute distribution, a customisable skill tree, slower paced yet smooth combat. What I got instead was bits of these and plenty of potential that I can only hope will become tapped. Skills are categorised into Attacks (split between warrior and rogue weapon choices) and Spells (requiring a staff or catalyst off-hander). You can access different skills with different weapons. For example, there is the core warrior, rogue (melee and ranged) and mage archetypes. But you can mix and match – you might have a dagger and a catalyst, or maybe a pistol and a sword. This allows you to juggle your two resources, Willpower (used for spells) and Rage (used for attacks). Using more of one increases the regeneration rate of the other. Skills can also be customised as they level up, increasing their core effectiveness or granting different effects (including changing their damage type). Unfortunately, you still find yourself with a distinct lack of variety.Loot is boring. You are simply chasing better stats in order to progress later into the endgame. Uniques seemed like a very cool way to challenge this by making distinct changes to the core mechanics. Unfortunately, these quickly fall behind the stats given by rares and legendaries. What was promised was that uniques would bring interesting changes to builds and skills. What was given was...mostly low-tier legendaries in a purple font.Crafting is currently undergoing some changes. There really isn’t much to say since the devs are looking to revamp parts of the system.The story gameplay is your standard A to B affair. End-game is divided into Mandates and Expeditions. Mandates are single instances where you have to kill either x enemies until a bar fills or y champions. Expeditions are multiple instances, each culminating in a boss fight. You can add some modifiers to increase your looting outcomes. Unfortunately, the levels and the bosses grow boring. The same handful of layouts and the same bosses are featured. Even then, the bosses are simply larger champions. What makes this worse is that there is no significant variety in the modifiers: there are a variety of +stat modifiers or extra ambient damage sources (explosions, circling blades, etc). Expeditions can be made more difficult by progressing through a variety of notches on a scale. That’s right, you simply grind for bigger numbers.There are enough of these that they deserve their own heading. Many of these have not been resolved since beta and many more are introduced with each patch. There are also core design issues, such as stat modifiers not applying correctly. One check on Reddit or Discord and you will see plenty of the current ones.There is a very vocal community that actively raises these bugs. The devs appear to be making attempts to address these, but it is very clear that they rushed the launch. I am sure that these will be ironed out in time, but at present I can only warn you to expect plenty. Thankfully I did not encounter any of the game-breaking bugs in my run of the story, only afterwards during my time with Mandates and Expeditions.The story is very shallow. In a nutshell: you manifest powers and daddy banishes you while he plays politics. Your siblings act like rash adolescents and you struggle with your newfound daddy issues. A plot twist! Another!? Credits. The characters have no substance and no time is spent on developing them. You are simply riding along as a series of events occur. At least the voices are enjoyable, even if the writing is not.Wolcen feels like it was released too soon. It needs more testing and development – maybe in six months it will be worth revisiting. Until then, approach this as an early-access title. It shows promise and the devs are actively working on it, however it just isn’t quite there yet.I hope that when I revisit Wolcen I will feel the need to change my review to a positive.Regarding to review bombing at launch: the game was released with an abundance of game-breaking bugs and the servers buckled under unexpected community interest. This resulted in the game being unplayable for many of the players, leading to the outrage still visible several weeks after launch. Unfortunately, many chose to vent their frustration with malice. Regardless, they were right in their underlying points: the game was not ready and the devs underestimated the number of interested players, leading to crushed servers that had to be taken offline.Communication has been an issue since launch, but the devs at least seem to be working long hours to make this game into what was promised at launch.

_childDocuments_.review: I've had enough. I bought this game at release, I gave it a lot of time because the team is new and small, but we're at patch 1.0.11 now and the game still throws me out at random so often it's effectively unplayable. I've patiently waited through bugs preventing total story progress, I've beaten the campaign, but the game is too broken to consistently have fun with and my patience has hit its limits. The game itself is actually fairly competently designed. Graphics aren't bad at all, the art style reminds me of Warhammer with its complete overdesign, gothic architecture influences and humongous pauldrons. Effects are good, attacks and spells feel weighty and satisfying and there is a bit of a story that, while convoluted and a bit amateurishly presented, is by no means bad. The character's abilities work on a system that's pretty much a simplified form of Path of Exile's, which while less complex also means the skill tree has a lot fewer filler nodes and the attributes' effects are calculated in such a way as to allow a variety of builds. Nonetheless, it's only good, not great and it's nowhere near as good as it would have needed to be to tolerate the amount of bugs - not just small, annoying bugs but gamebreaking bugs and crashes that make it hard if not impossible to satisfyingly play for any amount of time. Sorry. I tried.

_childDocuments_.review: My review for Wolcen: Lords of MayhemAs an ARPG enthusiast I can tell this game has great potential but the team has a lot of work left to be done.I've been playing since early access years ago and the game has changed a lot over the years.But really guys fix your game, fix the gamebreaking bugs. There's bosses with no animations, bosses that get stuck and invulnerable. People cannot finish their game. Thus they are enable to begin with the endgame.Once you beat the game you can start endgame with new characters: Prepare to get beat and beaten like there's no tomorrow with fresh start characters. While normal mobs will pose no threat, anything blue or yellow will absolutely crush you. Making this entire mode with fresh characters really not enjoyable but quite frustrating. So my advice; scale down the elite mobs for low lvl characters?Next is passive tree,The tree may look great and hold potential but everything is so damn cryptic. calculation of damage is hard to figure out. Strange wording of terms. I have the impression only half of the nodes really works and there's also really useless passives to that need to be increased. I think this entire thing needs to be redone.Epic and legendary equipment; I can't help but feel as if 90% of the things I find is complete trash. My rare gear with a fraction of the value of such said items outperform the shiny expensive gear by far. Finding epic and legendary equipment feels really underwhelming and it kinda dulls the grinding experience cause after a while you think, ah great more crappy loot.Stat attributes: 4 stats to lvl but really I don't see as why to lvl anything else besides toughness. All the other stats give worse damage increases while toughness adds more to my damage and my survivability. How does that make any sense?Been lvling toughness for 50 straight lvls now. The whole attribute thing should be entirely rewritten too for a more diverse and enjoyable progression system.Game difficulty. At a lot of times you'll feel like everything hits you like a wet noodle and then outta nowhere, BAM, BAM. Bro you died! This can be quite frustrating at times. I've memorized the mobs now so I know which ones to be careful for but still... some things need to be tuned way down.Attack skills.Well as in all the above while a lot of them look great. You'll soon realize there's a handful of Overpowered skills. Making other skill which may look cool but render them completely obsolete. I'm assuming this problem will cause everyone to roll the same damn build. In other words boring and bland. Rebalance skill damage and their corresponding passives.Also I feel like pathing and mob targetting is missing something it feels like it could be way smoother but it feels kinda really off at times.Now the good!!Really impressed with the graphic style and the design of some of the bosses and enemies.A lot of the gear really looks super, great gear cosmetic system with a lot of customization, I really commend it.Liking the variety of skills but these would be more enjoyable if not most of them sucked complete ass.I really believe the game holds potential and could grow into something big. But a lot of things need to be fixed and adjusted before that. Fix broken things before adding more content.Despite the negative I will still put this review as positive as I see it as a rough gem that could shine really bright one day.Not gonna rant about the speed things get fixed or broken. or the time the game has been in development. I'm an optimist sending positive vibes to the devs. Hold on and make this game great. There's no point in spewing toxic rants all over their product I doubt I could make something better. And who knows maybe my review will prove useful in order to make the game better.Buy the game if you want to see a game with potential and scratch the surface, just don't expect a finished game and make sure to be patient.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Wolcen is not worth the purchase price at this time. It needs a lot more polish before I can recommend it to others.PROS: Looks pretty, but that's all negated by terrible animation and laziness (see below).Passive skill tree is awesome, makes you want to keep playing to get those sweet, sweet points.CONS:The animations are so bad it distracts you from the game. Everything from your character's idle animation on the menu screen, to monsters in groups on cutscenes that look like they're on a carousel track. Your character moves like a wooden board no matter what type of weapon you have in your hand. The animation sequence doesn't match up with so many parts of cutscenes. Some of the cutscenes seem unfinished - your character model just gets dragged to where it's supposed to be. It's really unfortunate that the fantastic looking environments are ruined by abysmal animations.Bugs are proliferant throughout the game. There are far too many to list here. Some of the more annoying ones are not being able to click items in my inventory, sound going out at random times and the terribly inconsistent hit detection. On the hit detection issue (minor spoilers follow): On the multi-phase Edric fight he has some abilities that you pretty much have to dodge. The problem is that sometimes I'll get hit rolling out of them, which I might chalk up to me not timing the invul-frames correctly BUT, sometimes I can stand still and be invincible for the fight. This is just one example of terrible hit detection and hit boxes I found throughout my playtime.There are a decent amount of skills but the majority are worthless. Some of the damaging abilities you can completely max out damage on your gear and in the passive tree and they still barely scratch enemies. I found myself using one, maybe two abilities no matter if I specced warrior, rogue or a mage type character. The skills need a lot of balancing in my opinion.There are a lot of blatant ripoffs of Diablo 3 (note: I'm not saying ARPGs, specifically Diablo 3) and not in good ways. One of the areas is exactly like  ACT V of D3. Not like it, almost EXACTLY it. It looks the same. The enemies are the same (seriously, it looks like they ripped the models straight from D3). The Yuodai(sp?) fight even has the same attacks and patterns as the Malthael fight. Yikes. Another cringeworthy ripoff is the random chest events. Except these are generic and have no gameplay feedback during them or upon completion. Which leads me to my next point.A lot of stuff in the game feels generic and unfinished. Some of the stuff I thought was going to be a placeholder in the beta is still in the game. It detracts from the gameplay as a lot of elements clash with more their more polished counterparts. UI text, menus, popups, enemy names, events, area names, I could go on.The dialogue is some of the worst I've ever experienced in any form of media and entertainment. Some of the lines made me wince sitting in my gaming chair. I found myself trying to read fast to get a gist of what was going on in the story and hit the skip button to avoid hearing the dialogue. I think I said. "Oh no," several times throughout.I didn't get to play multiplayer as it was't working for me last night or today. I'm not too critical on this aspect as the game just released and I'm sure it'll be fixed soon.The itemization feels really generic. That's true for a lot of ARPG's in the early game, though.I'm going to stop there. This review went a little long and I still don't feel I adequately covered everything I found wrong during gameplay. I don't get my hopes up for games too much these days but this was still a disappointment as I'm a huge, lifelong fan of ARPG's. I'm going to let this one sit in my library for about a year and then revisit it. I wish the devs nothing but success.

_childDocuments_.review: I finally got to play this one as i was waiting for controller support and damn it's good!Totally worth the wait according to me.I had a couple of tiny bugs here and there but besides those everything else was awesome and entertaining as hell!The controls feels good, the visuals and design are great, combat feels heavy and powerfull, progression is satisfying and fast (i'm currently lvl 48, so i don't know after that but so far so good) and the story isn't finished (3 chapters so far) but i loved the campaign.I don't know why so many people seem to hate this game or complain so much about it.Yes a lot of things seem to have been promised and it may have taken longer than expected but the devs are working on this game, they improve, it's far from dead and i'm looking forward to see more of it soon.Endgame is pretty fun too, seem like it's gonna take ages to do all the activities but i guess that's the point of an endgame, right? to have some things to do and stuff to kill for a long time.I like this one, much more engaging than the Greater Rifts in D3 or just the "replay the story in harder difficulty" kinda endgame.Not dissapointed at all, i'm only 31 hours in and already know i'll play some more, way moreSo far i like Wolcen as much as PoE, D2, D3, Grim Dawn, Last Epoch and all those great ARPG's.Good job!

_childDocuments_.review: Servers down for about three days after release ? C'mon, cut them some slack. They are a small company after all and they got a huge influx of players. Story being mediocre ? Flat out broken talents ? Ok, getting a bit nervous here. Not being able to use your heal potions while in a cast or attack animation ? Ok, that is just plain stupid, but since there is no hardcore mode anyways, who really cares.EVERYTHING feeling finicky and laggy ? Yeah, you know what fam, maybe I should just wait for D4 or PoE 2, but since I already paid for it I am going to at least finish the story and see what the end game looks like. Well, I guess I am going to write my first ever steam review then. The voice acting was great though.

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly to discuss the games launch:Early access for 4 years,Beta testing for about 18 months.Sold around 150k copies.Released with almost all of the bugs from beta still in the game.Supposedly 'didn't expect' any more than 2000 players (1.3% of purchased copies) to play the game.Broke their own game with a hotfix and then went back to the didn't expect people to play excuse.Rallying around being not the only game to have a terrible launch - Just because others did it badly, it doesn't mean it's okayNaivety at it's purest regarding this games launch, cost-cutting to not allocate resource for at least half of purchase volume. Rushing fixes in a way that neglected proper testing, causing an accidental, almost complete, wipe of characters, stashes and progress.This is a huge disappointment to a game that has essentially been play tested endlessly for years.On to the game itself.PROS:Beautiful gameEngaging storyLikeable charactersRepeatable post story contentSkill and passive variety.CONS:Bugs galore, including but not limited to world clipping, untargetable enemies, invulnerable enemies, unresponsive npc's progression wipes, character wipes, stash wipes, item issues, crafting issues, crashes, freezes, online mode basically yet to exist.Some stretch goals from initial kickstarter not available at launch with no announced plans to implement.limited tilesets leading to quickly encountering repeated layoutslimited enemy pool with only 4-5 real 'types'only post-story boss fights are the phases of the story boss fightsimbalanced weapon typesanti climactic, poorly made 'cliffhanger' endingfemale character animations - the walk oh my. 78% legaspect of apocalypse system only serves as an oh ♥♥♥♥ button, lackluster.FINAL NOTEEven with all of the above, I am choose to recommend this game.The game is a very good start with a very high potential for growth and could be a massive hit. However, my exact recommendation as of now is to wait. Wait until the game is in a much better state than it is, better yet for the game to be on sale. Close to AAA price for what is obviously an unpolished, unfinished game.

_childDocuments_.review: Game has been in alpha/beta for years yet had a fail launch in many ways.  The online mode is down more often than not. Characters you level up offline can't be used online so there is no point for me to play offline. Targeting most enemies that are not huge is abhorrent in this game. It is the most frustrating thing in an aRPG where you both move and attack with your left click. Even in your inventory you have to hover multiple times on an item for the game to realize you want to select it.And from what I have seen, this game does not seem to offer anything substantial over other aRPGs; it seems to be a copy of Path of Exile.The game had mixed reviews until a few months back where it finally hit positive, and it just seems to be the dev's decided to quickly release it before it falls back to mixed/negative reviews. Until they fix the online thing and how unresponsive your cursor is, not much can be said about this game other than avoid it.

_childDocuments_.review: After putting more time into the game, got to level 60 which let me do a bit into the endgame I can confidently say my recommendation is still a "No". I understand its a small company and doesn't have the man-poiwer or financial backing as Diablo and PoE but in terms of an ARPG its just boring. Sure there is tons of loot to find and you're constantly finding better gear to make you guy stronger, but frankly the game is too easy overall. The game's difficulty scale endgame is just facing higher level monsters, which I'm only about +10 levels higher than my guy right now for expeditions but I feel like my character as is could do much higher. Grinding out 3 expedition levels at a time to progress just feels so tedious and aside from more exp it gives nothing as a reward. Watched a few higher level people in their 80s doing level 160 expeditions and it all just looked like more of the same.The city rebuilding part of the endgame was an interesting addition, and the story was pretty good to play through so I will give the game that. Outside of those two things, however, the game is the exact same as other ARPGs. If you've got $40 burning a hole in your pocket and are wanting something to do while waiting for diablo 4 then go ahead and grab the game, otherwise don't waste your money.

_childDocuments_.review: Only played offline and after the "Endgame" updateI have a lot of hours in other ARPGs and I think this one is fun and unique in a lot of good ways that makes it worth playing for any fan of these gamesPros:The story, voice acting, music, and set pieces are interesting and really good for this genre. Combat animations and effects feel good and the rage/willpower and dodge systems add a lot to the gameplay. The builds and customization are varied and easy enough to understand so you can make your own build as you play through the game, with very accessible respecs should you find some interesting gear or another skill set more fun. The endgame loop and systems are fun with some variety in activities and choices as you continue powering up a character. The boss fights were good and engaging. Cons:Itemization is tedious, with a lot of stat reading to know if something's an upgrade or not. Unique items are fun and impactful but you can spend a lot of time waiting for a drop for a build to even become viable. Balance feels off at times, and the difference in an efficient build and a useless one is sometimes hard to read - there's a lot of not obvious interactions due to the formulas which means some choices are worthless while others are absolutely necessary.

_childDocuments_.review: Great Game!  Story is pretty good for a ARPG.  The Classless system it runs on is pretty damn amazing, imo.  You're not bound to any one build, and the build variety is Insane.  There's Online and Offline.  Currently, Online play only has playing in groups going for it, along with a slap in trade system that is said/meant to be fixed later.  Servers were iffy at first, but keep in mind that the Devs didn't expect 100k players on this game.  Not all Indie devs can expect that many players, and these devs are no Exceptions, as they were counting on a lower (much lower) count.  So be patient with Online, if you go that route. They are indeed working on it.I must say, AND REALLY HOPE IT STAYS....  That Offline mode indeed has Mod Support, to a limitation of sorts.  So switching between the two is a good idea, imo.  Online for when they have massive events (if they hold them), or even Massive updates, as a way to play only Vanilla.  And then Offline as a way to change things up a little, as a sort of break from the Vanilla version. (which is needed, due to the Grind.  Remember, ARPGs are a REAL grindy genre.)I give this game a 9/10, overall.  COULD be a 10/10, if they added some quality of life features, and work out all the bugs and server related issues, as well.  Note:  Story Mode Bosses in this game are Difficult.  Especially if you don't dodge, or plan on a super tanky build.  You may rage, but in the end, it's worth getting through it all.  End Game looks pretty good so far, and they have already said/promised more content for End-Game.  So Def look forward to all that.HAPPY GAMING!!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: --- End Game finally Ended It ---So... Essentially they took the large scale city building bit, and hid it behind the boss fight I mentioned bellow. Giving you instead a hollow version of it until you complete, and win, a single loop of the new "rogue like" end game. This is difficult as you finish the game around level 40 and all the Lt's an big baddie himself are level 65. So... You get to grind your way through dozens of maps with 0 good loot and spend your money near pointlessly to TRY and down this boss that is 20ish levels above you... if you fail... you do it again. When you FINALLY KILL HIM. You then get the old city building back... and get to do the same thing again. I'm burrying the game after this. If it ever manages to hit 75% or above I'll give it another shot. Not counting on it though its about to be rolled on by D4 and PoE2. ---------------------------------------------UPDATE WITH THE NEW CHAPTERHoly ass batman... that end game I said you should have the whole game long? Well now even if you unlocked it they relock it behind another chapter grind.... the chapter is just corridoor levels that finalize in a painfully long and dull boss fight, after about 15 minutes of trading blows with this thing (Even with the dmg buff pickups) she was down to like 80%... and now that the end game is RE LOCKED the only thing to do is run this level until you beat it. Uninstalled-------The Isometric ARPG has been a favorite genre of mine since I booted up my first Diablo game back on the ps1. Wolcen sadly falls pretty flat compared to it's competitors. Overall 5/10, buy it on sale and play the campaign on easy just to get through it because its a slog. End game is the only semi redeeming feature and I feel if it was actually PART of the main game it would have made the game a bit more interesting. There are much better ARPGs out there. Visuals: 7/10Sub par character animations and beautiful spell effects make for an ok experience. The world itself looks decent enough but lacks it's own identity. Looks like diablo and warhammer had a baby, which wouldn't be bad if it had any depth beyond that. Story: 4/10Demons bad, save world blah blah. Nothing very creative here. But it was told with a lot of ... heart? fully VO'd and decently at that. Controls: 6/10Feels like everything has a .5 second global cool down. sluggish and unresponsive. Really makes the game a chore to enjoy especially during their "this isn't even my final form" boss fights. The roll was nice. Skills/Build freedom 3/10This game has a depressingly small selection of skills, 40 total, well under half of most ARPGs I've played. Skills are also gear locked. You wana play a 2h weapon user? you get 11 skills to choose from. However, the skills I enjoyed I THOROUGHLY enjoyed... lookin at you Juggernaut!Gimmicks 4/10Pets: You get two pets throughout the whole campaign and they pretty much do nothing and look wonky. Dual resources: just... eh. Rage and Mana, Spells cost Mana Attacks cost rage. However, used mana becomes rage and vice versa.End Game: The end game gimmick should have been what the game itself was all about. This was at least TRYING to be                    interesting. World: 1/10Non-existent, you have 1 quest node and 3 merchants that never really change much if at all throughout the campaign. End game may have some things you can do to tweak them a bit perhaps but yeah, there is no world beyond the maps you run. Getting into it:This is my more wordy personal experience with the game and some deeper insights, if you're the reading type. So this genre is mostly about how well builds and combat works and LOOT. Sadly gameplay is pretty lackluster due to some poor design choices. Skills for instance. On top of the weird input issues there are only 40 skills in game, With PoE sitting at over 200 and even Diablo 3 (a very lackluster ARPG imo) sitting at 25 per class (175 total ish) 40 seems like kiddy pool ♥♥♥♥. At least you can modify these skills with runes much like Diablo 3's skills. However, your skill choices are also weapon locked. Limiting you to as little as 11 skills to choose from depending on your weapon choice. -Sword and Board or 2h melee = Only fighter skills (11)-Bow =  Only ranger skills (11)-Staff = Only mage skills (18)-1h weapon + focus = Fighter + Mage skills (29)-Dagger + Focus = Ranger+ Mage skills (29)-Dagger or gun + 1h Melee = Fighter + Ranger (22)This struck a particularly personal cord with me as 2h Warrior Priests (SIGMAR BE PRAISED) as well as Sword and Shield clerics/crusaders are a personal favorite of mine in the ARPG genre. SO... with both the builds I WANTED to play not an option I chose to play about halfway through with 1h+Focus my rotation was to Light bringer in (think falling sword from d3), Juggernaut (a MASSIVE bubble) and pretty much Solarfall (Heavens Fury d3) everything to death while i stood still. I had a passive that slowed my movement but increased my defenses as long as I wasn't moving and it seemed to all stack pretty well. Got boring though and that slow combined with Juggernauts slow (I have it spec'd for maximum bubble power which slows you when it's active) just made for a very boring rotation and slow clear to boot. I decided to swap to a Warhammer build, you can get your block chance pretty damn high even without a shield in this game. With my warhammer I'm at 39% chance to block. So I worked in a counter attack node, block nodes, some crit nodes just to try and maximize my Anvils Woe (Hammer of the Ancients d3). Rotation then was to jump in and stun things (my juggernaut and my Warpath (shield bash d3) as well as my Sovereign Shout all stun) This boosts the crit chance for my Anvils woe massively and whenever it crits it chains to others on top of having a cone attack rune attached to it. Was a functional enough build to finish the game. The game does have a few very unique skills too though. Like psi blade lookin things and a sniper rifle lolYou also get to choose from 4 "ultimate form" skills which is pretty dope, love smashing a horde with those things. Boss Battles:Nothing was really "hard" to me.  Most mini bosses where pretty damn easy and the big bosses where just multi stage bullet sponges with ass loads of helper and poo to step in. All Praise Juggernaut. Loot:This was aight, there was nothing to do with your bad loot but sell it for gold though which was a very shallow experience. Legendary gear was generally just high stat gear where as unique gear offered interesting twists on game play. I have a glove that makes things explode when they die for instance. Overall you could combine different things to accomplish a lot of different stat boosts which was nice. There is also some PoE like items that will allow you to reroll items and give them bonuses based on the gems inside them which is interesting. But they don't come around often enough to experiment with atm. Armor TypesHeavy Armor = Massive Resistance bonusesBruiser Armor = Some Resistance and some HPRogue = HP and Spell ShieldSorcerer = Full Spell shieldWeapon Types1h: Swords, Maces, pistols, daggers2h: Warhammers, Great swords, Staves, BowsOh: Focus, Shield, Bugs I encountered in my playthrough-Quest Markers disapearing-Unlocked TP points becoming locked again, as a stay at home dad these points I relied on heavily as I need frequent breaks and don't want to lose my map progress. -Tons of Audio bugs (sounds that continue happening after the maker of said sound is gone)-The first fight in the Blood Trail content had an NPC helping you who randomly disapeared on me during the fight. -Transitioning between zones is odd and laggy, your clicks don't always register and entrances are generally just marked with big ass beams of light, no actual door or anything.

_childDocuments_.review: PSA: Anybody who wishes to play the game as a minion horde necromancer will surely be disappointed. They're new to 1.0.0 & absolutely garbage. There are older skills with objective, defined tooltip information like "+X damage & -Y Attack Speed" Then there's subjective tooltip information that's just "Increases damage."Bugs I've encountered:1. Very, very difficult to hit enemies. The starting zone bats, as mentioned in other reviews, are notoriously difficult to target and hit.2. Some maps generate with enemies in the floor.
