_childDocuments_.review: This is a very difficult review to write as I have been holding out hope for the first few patches. However after them I can not recommend this game in its current state or with the current priorities the dev team has demonstrated. They are by no means bad, however they need time and so does the game itself. Unfortunately all the people saying that this should still be in beta are not in the wrong saying so. The number of bugs present in almost every system the game has (UI, quests, map generation, item values and unfortunately more). The passive tree is definitely a good unique selling point though a good portion of the tree simply does not function as intended which is due to more than a single issue. Combined with an issue of them just not working or the stats system needing some refining. Though I would say the stat system is a rather minor issue.All in all the game is not ready for a full release. It adds to the growing problem of fixing a game after its officially released. I am more inclined to support a smaller studio doing it than another but the scale of issues here can not be understated. Perhaps they were forced to release it now for whatever reasons or perhaps they just believed it was ready. The latter would be extremely concerning if true.I truely hope that this game succeeds and it becomes a main stay in the ARPG genre. However it is still a few years away and I cant even say its at the state to be a distraction between POE leagues. Though it may well be worth the buy way before then since POE is an unfair match having run for many years and developers who have many years of experience.Nothing below here is important to buying decision but my two cents on current issues with the community.I am seeing a lot of extremes on both ends. People hating on the devs and people showering the devs with praise. Both of these things are harmful in their own ways and each get more extreme along with each other. My main issue is with all the "Good work devs" crowd. They are by no means bad developers however they have made a lot of mistakes here that need to be addressed and not minimized. There is no need to belittle or abuse, but encourage and hold them to mistakes so they are not repeated. They are a small studio that have made a visually appealing game but that is not cause alone to ignore every issue and simply sticking to "good work devs" in an attempt to counter the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ abusing the devs is only adding fuel to the fire.

Either very long times to connect with someone or not working at all in specific regions.* The loophole involving rising in level for no reason and doing the same thing over and over again, just to get stronger and bigger is so cheeky and ... disgraceful. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a great game.  Think of Diablo 2 with a hint of Path of exile.  Not overly intense like PoE but a tad more versatility/complexity than Diablo 2.  The launch has been rough with bugs but if you put those aside as im sure they will be fixed this is a great game.On top of the game, the community involvement that the developer  has is second to none.  They expose their trello boards for upcoming enhancements, bugs and even let you vote on and submit new ones.  Their discord community manager is active and willing to help where needed.  I've been really impressed overall with every aspect aside from losing out on some items due to glitches and the server stability at launch being non-existent.  I think if the launch had gone perfectly and less bugs this game would have gotten a LOT more positive exposure.  Since there have been issues everyone on the internet will attack those which is a distraction from the overall quality of the game.  I'd highly recommend this game.  That aside I'll speak to a few things about the game:There are "Super" moves when you build up kills that are unlockable and different stats depending on the need.There are the typical attributes  like what many refer to like strength/endurance/willpower/agility that apply to all the skillsThere are skills that you obtain via loot dropsSkills can level up as you have them equiped (up to 4 at a time until you unlock a 5th one)Skills can have all different types of modifies as you level them up to get skill points (im not sure at what level intervals you obtain points though so i would say there should be clarity there.Armor has 5 different levels of quality.  There are no "set" itemsThere are gems for sockets and at this time you cannot combine them to make better versions.  i think this makes sense as im almost done with the last chapter as it scales well with the gameThe best armor (unique) have cool stories and visuals to go along with themThe skill tree is customizable in that it looks overwhelming at first, but once you understand the 3 tiers and you can adjust them to accomodate your playing style its great! The game starts you on normal difficulty which in itself presents challenges however if you are just interested in the story they have a "story" difficulty.Thats it!  Theres more to it but over the years this developer has given their all to tailor this game to what the community has asked for.  This has been their only game and i would say it would be a shame if this game didnt get the justice it deserved due to unfortunate launch issues.  Give it a shot and support a small developer.  You wont be sorry if you give it a change and liked games like diablo/titan quest/PoE.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot to like and fits in well with other games like it. We have had a blast getting through the story and the end game is a lot of fun with a mostly unique way to progress your character.* Respeccing skills and attributes are "essentially" free late game. You only select a class to get starting equipment but you can change from a tanky melee to a glass cannon on a whim. It does cost gold and affinity, but the amount is negligible by the time you are likely to get into it. No need to worry your character is ruined at level 20. * The Skill Tree looks complex but is not so bad and finding what you want is straight forward, and again, if you make a mistake you can just undo it immediately or in the end game. * You can learn every skill quickly and they can be modified to fit your playstyle, including changing their elements to match your equipment in many cases.* Skins and dyes are free to change whenever you want and there are a large number of options. * We had heard the game was buggy as all hell but we had only experienced one bug early on in the story that was fixed by simply restarting the game.* The end game city building is a fun way to progress. * Playing with friends was fast and easy and you progress together in story mode and both players can even make their own city building choices in the end game while still playing together. You won't be losing story progress or stuck having to go back and forth between leaders to make sure you are both progressing* The story isn't incredible but it also isn't so over the top that it gets in the way of playing and it is fun enough.* Some of the skills can feel a little clunky at times. * It appears a lot of people got turned off from it so finding up to date builds is tough but, again, experimenting on your own is super cheap in-game so the cost of not having one at the start is nil.At the time of writing this, Chapter 4 isn't out yet and there is a planned reset down to level 40 to realign several gaming systems. I've played a little of endgame and can certainly understand how annoying losing progress can be. For a new player though, it will have negligible impact and from my understanding this reset and update is meant to help prevent the devs from feeling the need to do it again in the future as they want to add in a season system similar to PoE and Diablo.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend Wolcen in a couple months or when the first sale occurs.  It launched as an unplayable nightmare (online) and an unbalanced, exploit riddled mess (online and offline).  It is now functional and stable after its first major patch today, but leaves much to be desired in terms of balance and viable specs.  Beyond the time wasting bugs like losing items, currency, progress, etc. the visuals and story barrow extremely heavily from Blizzard's Diablo franchise.  And not because this is an isometric ARPG, the borrowed comparisons are obvious.  Go fight the 2nd boss in the D3 campaign then fight the 2nd boss in Wolcen's campaign.  You will audibly laugh its so blatant.  They borrow level design, monster design, ui design, etc. Even your character's ending of the wolcen story is very similar to D1.  There is so much to complain about yet, I have almost 85 hours into this very flawed game because it just happens to be out at the right time.  If I wasn't bored with D3, PoE, and Grim Dawn, I would be playing one of them instead, they are all far superior ARPGs in every way.  So yeah, get this game in the future, on sale, when it is balanced and patched.  It is pretty and should eventually be a solid entry into the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the time I played until the end. When I beat the game I was expecting to see the game in all of it's full endgame glory. However, upon learning that Bleeding Edge is basically as far as the melee meta goes, my enjoyment was over. I was having a blast just buffing myself up and being a tornado of fury and doing nice 30k crits, 60k on a double crits at level 50. Then suddenly 5 levels later I stopped being able to kill bosses and so I went to the trusty internet to look at builds. Most if not all the melee builds focus on Bleeding Edge. Having literally just thrown the skill on I realized why, I had to do nothing but click one button. All of a sudden the game was braindead easy a blade was swirling around me doing 160k crits, all my fun was gone, the only way for me to fight bosses was throw this overwhelmingly dull attack at the boss which on average took barely 3 seconds to die. I fought against the plethora of bugs and came out on top only to hit the disappointing rock bottom that is Bleeding Edge spam. When/If the game catches its stride and fixes its plentiful bugs, terrible skill balance, broken passives and gets some much needed quality of life improvements I will try it once more.Tldr; If you want to face roll everything just use Bleeding Edge and turn off your brain, its boring and nothing else does anywhere near as much damage.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has bugs and is amateurishly made. The levels are uninspired, linear and static. The combat system can be frustrating. There is a game mechanism where you trade rage for willpower and visa versa. You get the one you need by using the default attack.  The default attack is so weak, like a butterfly kiss, compared to the special skill attacks which are like lightning strikes.   This is a frustration at least most of the game (I haven't finished) much like the power up mode that is not particularly powerful and lasts a short amount of time.But, it is fun enough if you get to chapter two. It scratches an itch that is not being satisfied right now. This is a Diablo clone that gets enough right to be satisfying. The story is similarly convoluted and silly, but is no matter since you can skip most of it. The side quests are just offshoots of the map where you transport to a small dungeon to "cull all evil," or some such. The same monsters are standing around every corner or might just pop out of the ground. At least I don't have to perform any platforming puzzles. That is all i ask. This game is a good time sink on sale, and I encourage the devs to keep upping their game.

_childDocuments_.review: As of Patch 1.0.3.0_ER...The game in its current state is not worth the asking price, or any price, as you are simply paying to beta test a product that claims to be in a released state. At face value, it is a common ARPG that does nothing to reinvent the wheel while using the likeness of both models and abilities throughout the game play experience; however, in its core, this game is so buggy that you can accidentally duplicate items, duplicate gold, hard-lock your character ('brick') from being able to be played to even having entire inventories, stash pages or characters be deleted from your account. There are finicky ways of getting some things back, such as your stash pages, but if an item is gone from your inventory, it's most likely gone for good -- same with your character.The developers have expressed a desire to fix a lot of the issues plaguing the game, stemming from items not working properly to passive nodes not functioning as intended (or at all) to the easily exploitable systems that will actually force their hand into punishing you permanently for it... but when they can only 'hotfix' once per week (which isn't a hotfix... it's a patch), there is just too much for them to handle where I doubt even a month from now they will have half of the problems with this game even addressed.When I was ignorant of all the issues, it was a fun time wasting game that I did enjoy experimenting with. As more of the game opened up and all the problems started to flood in, it was merely a chore. This is without including all the server downtime that this game has suffered since launch.Summary: Do not buy. Do not wait for sale. If game is ever fixed, consider looking into; however, game is NOT in a state to be called a full release and will not for the foreseeable future.

_childDocuments_.review: Wolcen is a hidden gem:It’s got a bunch of unique mechanics that make it stand out. The story is solid, with engaging cinematics and lore that pull you in. Like the ailments system, which means damage over time for some types. The crafting system follows the basic recipe of unique loot and gem socketing.The late game in Wolcen is tied to the story in a unique and interesting way. It had a rough start with bugs in the early access and 1.0 release, but don’t let that fool you.One of the best things about Wolcen is the character customization. You can use any weapons and armor, which means you can create all sorts of builds. The skill tree is interesting, and you can reset everything as you play (for a cost). So, if you start playing one way and don’t like it, you can change it up. This level of freedom is really nice.Furthermore, the skill system in is also flexible and in some cases unique. You can take a skill and change its damage type or even how it works. For example sunstrike-like ability for a caster could be changed into cold damage and/or a targeted location instead on caster. You can even add to that the ability to move it around. This was probably one of the first arpgs where I played as an ailmentalist mixed up elementalist wearing a mixture of mage, rouge, berserk and heavy plate(s)...Finally, despite some initial challenges and b-rated aspects it's a good contender in the ARPG genre. Developers should take a page from Wolcen’s strong points and look at the customization and player freedom. It's probably a good time to give Wolcen a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: I've completed the story. I did one Portal at end game.There are multiple reasons why. What Ultimately sold me on Not recommending this game is: Unable to Cancel actions & Atk.spd, or cast.Spd Does not increase the Speed of the animation of an Attack. It does increase the frequency of your attacks or Spells cast. This needs proper explanation which will take a wile. And YOU will need to test it yourself. Easiest to do IF you can Record it or if you have a buddy that owns the game. a Short lived fix as eventually they become disjointed again.This is a list of reasons why I dislike the game. Its the same thing as a Hit Box. They are often Much larger then the Object. Some times they expand Double the Height of the object they are apart of. In the early game I first noticed it on the flying bat enemies in the Saviir Caves. their Click-Box I was unable to find. I got through it by Holding L-Shift and attacking causing me to hit them. Since their Hit-Box is Correct, I was able to have my attacks hit them. But I was unable to interact with Targetable Abilities and left click, Since their Click-Box was Disjointed. This I believe was a bug. as it didn't always occur in the area. a Restart of the game Seem to fix this. There are certain Destructable Objects that does not get highlighted as Destructables. This Often Causes you to Start attacking them when you don't intend to. Forced Movement is by Default bound to Lctrl. You are able to rebind it. But not to Left-Mouse Button.  This is more of a Culmination of all the Above. If you are trying to run away. The Click-Box is disjointed, this Causes you to dash into the enemy you are running away from. It is possible to turn off the dash-attack. However upon Closing the game & starting it again, it is reset. Forcing you to turn it off again... and again... and again. each new start of the game. If something Say Score, like "% Increased attack speed " Avoid it. as it does not do what you think it does. Any Bonuses to the Score of a Stat Increases the Flat Number called a Score in your character sheet. This score then in Turn Increases ur Attack.speed by a %.For Example: At lv 38 I had a Cast speed score of 828.8. This Equals a increase in atk.spd of 45.4% I also had a "50% increased Score." in it. so a minimum of 1 Third is increased. You gain less then 0.05% increased Cast speed per Cast speed . This increased Atk.spd is Also Effected if your Agility stat is a Primary, Secondary, Tertiary or Quaternary. Mine was Primary & as such the atk.spd score & Cast.spd Score Gains a grater bonus from any stat increases. compared to if it was secondary, tertiary or quaternary. It does increase the amount of attacks, or Casts, you can do over a duration. Example 30sec. However. If you time 2 Attacks at the exact same time, one with Increased Attack speed & one without. They will have the same animation length of the attack. Attack speed or Cast speed, instead changes the duration in-between each attack. The Time after a Attack, or Cast, were you are unable to do anything. to better portray the issue. Imagine you using a Ability. the Ability has no Cooldown & can be recast again as soon as it is done. Lets say the animation takes 1 full sec. Normally those 2 are bound as the same as the animation speed for each ability. Normally that would mean your atk.spd is 1 attack per second, or 1.  Also Imagine there is a seperate duration that blocks you from activating another ability while a ability animation is playing. However in Wolcen they are Separate & do not effect each other. So there is a small duration after a animation has ended that doesn't allow you to use another ability, Including Potions or Dodging. When you increase your Attack speed, or Cast speed, The Animation speed stays constant. But the seperate duration that blocks you from activating another ability is decreased by it. Because of that you will be able to activate more abilities Then a person with a lower . This time in-between is a very small duration. So any increase in atk.spd or cast speed is hard to notice. Increasing your atk.spd or cst.spd makes combat feel better to play. there is more fluidity to the combat. Best way to see the difference is to Either Record yourself doing the same attack, One with a major bonus in attack speed & one Without. Then placing them side by side to compare. Or Have a friend connect with you online and activating them at same time. I believe this is because it is unable to be activated while a ability is active & Extended by the In-Between time I talked about under "attack speed is a lie". Either it is that or it is a lag issue from when playing online with a 53ms ping connected to london from Sweden. a Boss prepares to do a big hit, you see the red marker. You Dodge. Mid roll, outside it's highlighted area you die. This occured multiple times as i was playing through the story. this could be a Ping issue from playing online. But when the game itself say you have a ping of 53ms, Then I doubt it. Unless it is a net code issue. but then it is a entirely separate issue that needs resolving. mid attack animation, you press dodge to avoid an attack. That started after your attack. That is Quicker then your attack. But because you are unable to dodge it. Even with a attack speed score of 828.8.  Example: "Avanger" Autoturret. I am only going capture a few bullet points here with the intent of writing a full review later.The GOOD:the most visually stunning aRPG to datecombat - dodge roll, right out of the box. Puts the "a" in aRPGskill progression via skill levelling and modifiers (no cookie-cutter builds)character attribute spending and respec (like how it's directly tied to dmg).Gates of Fate (passive skill tree) - well thought out to encourage build diversityBloodtrail - really nicely integrated into story campaign (love the modifiers)The BAD:The CRYENGINE will be very hard on systems more than a generation from today's hardwareBugs - while I have only encountered 2 (one really a QoL, one a defeated boss not recognized 1st time around)Long cut scenes, 1st time around you have to experience all the lore (and it is pretty good)Load times. I have a SSD, but new region loads can be lengthyCommunity Presence - since Bloodtrail, there has been a tremendous amount of hot fixes however you would not know it based on their forums as it appears there is not much sign of a community manager in several months

_childDocuments_.review: Since Steam only gives you 2 hours to make a decision on whether or not a game is worth your time, this is my short, sweet, fair, and completely transparent Wolcen: Lords of Mayhem review from a seasoned ARPG player. There are 2 major items that heavily influenced my thumbs down which will be covered at the end of this review.I had a tough start simply being able to get an online game created. It took roughly 30 seconds, multiple times, of me twiddling my thumbs waiting for the game to start just to be hit with an error. I scoured the internet in hopes of finding a solution. A solution was indeed (eventually) found. I needed to go into the game settings to change the server from auto to something, I don't know, closer than what the auto server selection chose for me? It was a really odd and massive waste of time that triggered a negative mindset before even starting what I was hoping to be an enjoyable grind. I'd like to point out as well that I 1. had to choose a number of different servers before one worked (it definitely wasn't the one closest to me) and 2. I saw multiple posts about this from 2 years ago -- people complaining or feeling defeated not being able to create an online game. It's clear that this fix is not a priority so hopefully this helps save someone some time in the future.I finally got into the game and I wasn't immediately disappointed. The graphics were pretty solid and the voice acting was really good from what I heard. However, the intro bit took a little too long and the characters following you around were really invasive to what I was trying to accomplish around me. The bright glowing outlines on them didn't make it any better. On the positive side though, the tutorials that show you around the different menus and systems were not bad at all. Keep in mind that I only made it to level 5 before writing this review, but for someone like me, that's plenty of time to identify if a game is for me or not.The overall movement and combat is just not good in my opinion. I tried on mouse as well as controller. Controller felt like a joke. Using the left analog stick to move your character for some reason made the character model lose frames or something. It wasn't natural movement and ruined the experience. Using the right stick to dodge was extremely inaccurate (when compared to other PC ARPGs using a controller). Using a mouse, clicking on enemies to attack made the character model "jitter" frequently and NPCs once again would constantly get in the way making everything feel really clunky. Holding shift ended up making the combat feel better, to an extent, but then dodging to avoid boss attacks would not place me where I wanted to roll and I ended up on another planet due to dodging so fast in any direction and typically more dodges than I wanted. Dodging is just extremely sensitive and unnatural feeling. I could press the spacebar once but I end up dodging twice to three times and at the speed of sound. It just didn't feel right.Fog of war. One of my favorite things about ARPGs is map completion, even if it's randomly generated. Knowing where I have already explored or have yet to explore is critical for me. Based on information I read up on online, the story missions do not have fog of war, but all of the other content does. What's the point of that? I see that people have been asking for it for years but it's nowhere to be found. There's absolutely no reason for some content to have it and not others, especially main story content.The reason why I felt the need to write this review for this game specifically is because this quite literally has pretty much everything I want in an ARPG: a diverse / classless combat system, loads of skills (that level up as you use them), stat attribution (combined with the classless combat system makes for some dope build opportunities), random boss encounters on the maps, cosmetic system with dyes and awesome glowing weapons, solid voice acting, good graphics, etc. However, because of the two main complaints above, I have decided to refund the game. I think this is a solid ARPG option for a lot of people, I am not saying the team behind this title did a bad job at all, but I am hyper critical + very picky when it comes to the games I play, especially when it costs $40.

_childDocuments_.review: I've deleted my old review for this new one since the new beta has arrived.Difficult to be brief as many elements have changed from the previous alpha.As a backer of the kickstarter campaign I have to say I am now impressed with this 1st act!positives: -the artworks looks amazing now, definitely an improvement over the past versions (definitely looking forward to the artbook!!).-the world looks a lot more refined aesthetically and has rich storytelling, very immersive too (up to par with what the devs plan to do with the game)-the music is definitely one of the highlights of this new version-in-game cutscenes (skipable for those who don't want to go through them)-voiceover: YES!-great story and engaging characters-good character progression and nice spells (although the spell modifier screen could use a bit of improvement in terms of presentation, I think it could be even more immersive to the game's universe)-very solid Act I (long yet engaging enough to keep us players wanting to go for more)-beautiful effects and amazing level art (lots of variety and solid world building)negatives: -lot of features removed from the previous version (housing, character creation, item crafting, etc.) that yet to be re-implemented-I would've expected more gameplay features to be implemented by now (like apocalyptic form and pets)-the plan on adding in-game currency purchasable with real money, that's a big NO for me.-the current player character model looks bad and there's no female character anymore-bugs, lags, etc. (clipping in walls, floors, etc.) which is normal for a beta-items/gear models look generic and not as cool as their 2D icons for the most part-character animations look a bit clunky still-some attack/spells feel a bit slow at timesWolcen team, if you're reading this I must admit you've surprised me with this Act I update (in a good way!). It's gone from a Diablo 3 clone to an experience that is unique and more engaging than Diablo 3. Keep doing this for the remaining acts as well as adding back features from the kickstarter and I swear this will be a hack n' slash game to be remembered for decades!To people that consider buying this game I won't recommend it at that current stage just yet. I'd say wait at least another 5 years until something tangible enough is released.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, finished the main campaign yesterday. I played as your typical sword and board tank warrior which was tanky enough for me to only die once, ever, and only to the end boss of act two of this game. My experience of this game is that of a dirty casual: i only played to complete the game. I did not experiment with the game's skill tree system, I did not grind for legendary end game loot and I did not use a single mage or rouge skill. Pure tank warrior which was super boring because it boiled down to out lasting all of my enemies. So yes, super casual.Game play: Solid, balanced and bog standard. I never felt anything was unfair and enemies equal to your level do provide a challenge. Even as a tank i could not allow a mob of mobs just wallop me, I had to use skills and remain decently mobile. Story: I'm on the fence between Bog Standard and Good story telling. All characters including the main character do have a reason to do what they are doing. Environmental story telling is great. voice acting is serviceable. I found the threat of the three cults a bit odd. Their motivation works: remove/bypass a dimensional barrier so that demons rule the planet. Their methods do not work in my mind but hey magic *shrugs*. last point is that the story ends on a cliff hanger "to be continued."Loot: numbers go up. I haven't seen anything exciting yet since i only have 2 legendary and 3 iconic pieces of equipment. The legendary pieces are so powerful that they lasted me the whole campaign while the iconic pieces became too weak to use in later levels. Pets are useless. Loot is bad in this game.bugs: the game crashed once in my 28 hours of playing, that's it.Verdict: A solid ARPG that is worth the purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: Where do I even begin. Firstly, for some odd reason, this game seems to chug. I see frequent FPS dips for no discernible reason. It's funny. There was a point in time, about a patch ago, where the game ran at a seamless 60-100 FPS no problem. That was after the patch before *that* causing me to chug worse than I do now. So I can say with certainty, it's not my rig.Secondly. The animations in this game for the boss fights are a *joke.* They often deal the damage long before the animation even completes, which *normally* isn't much of an issue. But then you get to some of the later boss fights. GIRL. It is with the utmost certainty I can say that nobody in their right mind tested these final chapters of content. The combat is meh. Most of the passive nodes at the time of my writing don't work. The loot is boring. The socketing system is much less complex than Path of Exile, and much more irritating to work with than Diablo 3. I applaud the dev team for trying something different, but it's largely just an irritating aspect of RNG. Which, of course, I expect from an ARPG game, so I'm not super bummed about that. All in all, I wish I'd waited to buy the game. I'm positive it'll be fantastic after a few patches. Which is really weird because the game has been in early access for how many years? By all accounts from the old heads, the game has actually gotten just plain ol' worse since 1.0. That surprises me immensely, because 1.0 releases are supposed to be... you know. Worthwhile. After 23 hours of playing the game mostly cooperatively, I can tell you to pass on Wolcen unless it's $10 in its current state, or it's massively patched. And I mean massively. If you want to get really sad, go look at all the content that was in the game prior to its 1.0. The character customization was BOMB, apparently. And now it's super not. Transmog is really cool, though, so I've got to give them props for that. The dye and transmog system are the only saving graces of this game right now. Once it's better optimized, perhaps I can overlook some of the other small issues I've got with the game. But when the content I'm playing isn't fun already, having ghostly performance issues arise is the icing on a particularly ♥♥♥♥♥♥ cake. I wish this game was released in a better state. I wish I liked it more, because it's gorgeous and the potential for it to be a really good time is there. I wish I'd waited to buy it, because I don't think I'm ever going to be able to look at it and say YES THAT IS MY FAVORITE ARPG because of the launch. This is a good example of why you don't add untested content to your 1.0 release. The final boss fight is so incredibly lame. The end of chapter two, also incredibly lame. The first act is the only act that really felt entirely fleshed out. After that? GIRL.

_childDocuments_.review: Wolcen is a weird one, and I feel weird giving a recomendation to a game that's held together entirely by prayer, has a self-contraditcoray class system, and loses steam shortly after level 5. It was an engaging game, a very interesting game, but maybe not a particularily good one. I've got no credibility higher than "I am a fan of ARPGs", and there's some structural problems here: A 'classless' system that still rigidly forces you into 1 or three actual classes (because your ability pool - limited as it is, is cut up into three basic groups: 2 Handers, Ranged Weapons, and Magic), a God of War wrath mechanic that doesn't really digest well in the ARPG system (because fights are, to some extent, balanced around the idea that you can be invincible for large segments of them, when they're balanced at all), and a weirdly unbalanced loot system. I'm not saying I want to constantly be swapping out gear bits for +1, but I went through the whole game upgrading my main weapon twice and I feel like that's a problem. The game is buggy too - which ranges from 'Oh that's nice, I'm playing a game made by humans (a lot of models T-Pose or Duplicate)' to 'Well, fustrating but not a problem (there's a second of lag for all health on hit effects, which means your HP bar is jumping all around the screen), to "Catastrophic" (at time of writing the final boss can, for lack of a better term, 'evade bug' during the second phase of a grueling three phase slog). The whole point of early access, to my understanding, is to make it so your 1.0 version doesn't teeter on the brink like this. All that said the act of combat is crunchy and satisfying. Spells and abilities feel good to use, though you'll find the power pool to be distressingly limited - a sacrifice to a Classless system that I don't feel exists -, and the whole game has great presentation and a top notch cast. I stopped enjoying the loop but kept playing to try and see how it ended. Then the final boss evade bugged on me and I've lost my sense of humor. I think $40.00 is hiddeously over priced for a game that's "Kind of fun" and "Mostly works". If you can pick it up for $15.00 (or, realistically, wait for it to end up as an Epic Free Deal or a Humble Bundle) then it's worth a look, but beyond that I'd say it's for enthusiasts alone who are willing to put up with a mountain of jank for a very interesting experiement.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: A more powerful and immersive story than any other ARPG you'll find.-indepth skill system that gives you a lot of customization with both skills and talent points to toy with-fun combat as long as you're mage class-You level skills up akin to PoE skill gems except they don't have a dumb gem system, the skills are also insanely customizable at higher levels.-really dynamic fights, and you do have warning with attacks so enemies don't end up steamrolling you without consent-Voiced side characters that actually fight well, too bad they can't come for end game-A very comprehensive end game that is both customizable and feels like "The End is a New Beginning" with custom map modifiers, talent-like speccing for end game challenges and very challenging combatCons:-Some skills are useless until higher tiers, and therefore a pain to level -Weapons aren't all equal-I haven't figured out a need to make a melee or rogueish build because they're so clearly inferior-despite having the system recommendations the game still chugs a bunch, especially in later acts and endgameOverall I can tell a lot of work and love went into Wolcen. While they still need optimization work, it's a ton of fun to play as is. Balance is the main issue they face though.The fact I completed all 3 Acts without dying makes me think the Staff is the most unbalanced weapon. I had trouble with this game playing with ranged and melee weapons. Gave up. Restarted character with the Annihilation Beam and the Staff and just face-rolled the entire game. Seeing as only 3.3% of players completed act 3 without dying says a lot, probably staff users, I'm not sure though obviously.Otherwise, a lot of effort went into endgame and if everything is addressed the end game could be better than anything else that's come along for ARPGs.

name: Factorio
detailed_description: Factorio is a game in which you build and maintain factories. You will be mining resources, researching technologies, building infrastructure, automating production and fighting enemies. In the beginning you will find yourself chopping trees, mining ores and crafting mechanical arms and transport belts by hand, but in short time you can become an industrial powerhouse, with huge solar fields, oil refining and cracking, manufacture and deployment of construction and logistic robots, all for your resource needs. However this heavy exploitation of the planet's resources does not sit nicely with the locals, so you will have to be prepared to defend yourself and your machine empire. Join forces with other players in cooperative Multiplayer , create huge factories, collaborate and delegate tasks between you and your friends. Add mods to increase your enjoyment, from small tweak and helper mods to complete game overhauls, Factorio's ground-up Modding support has allowed content creators from around the world to design interesting and innovative features. While the core gameplay is in the form of the freeplay scenario, there are a range of interesting challenges in the form of Scenarios . If you don't find any maps or scenarios you enjoy, you can create your own with the in-game Map Editor , place down entities, enemies, and terrain in any way you like, and even add your own custom script to make for interesting gameplay. Discount Disclaimer: We don't have any plans to take part in a sale or to reduce the price for the foreseeable future. What people say about Factorio No other game in the history of gaming handles the logistics side of management simulator so perfectly. - Reddit I see conveyor belts when I close my eyes. I may have been binging Factorio lately. - Notch, Mojang Factorio is a super duper awesome game where we use conveyor belts to shoot aliens. - Zisteau, Youtube

_childDocuments_.review: Diving into the mesmerizing world of Factorio has been an epic journey, spanning countless hours across both the Steam and  versions. This game isn't just a futuristic building factory; it's a symphony of creativity and strategy that resonates with every player.Factorio's brilliance reveals itself as you ascend the technological ladder, transcending relativly primitive burning machinery to embrace the awe-inspiring might of solar and nuclear power. The initial chaos, akin to navigating a spaghetti maze, gradually transforms into a harmonious dance of inserters, assamblers and belts, culminating in a factory that stands as a testament to your engineering prowess. But it's not just about conquering the industrial landscape; you'll find yourself fending off hostile natives who, with a hilarious disdain for your planet-polluting antics, add a delightful twist to the narrative.Cooperative play elevates Factorio to new heights, effortlessly accommodating a multitude of players with a multiplayer setup so seamless it feels like magic. The developers, the unsung heroes behind this digital masterpiece, have crafted policies that demonstrate an unwavering commitment to the player community. And let's not forget the mods—oh, the mods! A veritable playground of creativity awaits with an array of mods and bundles that transform Factorio into an ever-evolving universe.Visually, Factorio may adopt a 2D isometric style, but within its pixelated realms lies an intricate tapestry of details that captivates the imagination. If the mere mention of titles like Stronghold, Stronghold Crusader, Transport Tycoon Deluxe, or the Anno series sparks joy in your gamer heart, Factorio seamlessly weaves together the essence of these classics with its unique blend of complex building, resource management (let's call it what it is—economic genius), and extraterrestrial showdowns.A word of caution to the graphics connoisseurs out there: if your heart beats solely for cutting-edge visuals, perhaps your quest lies elsewhere (I'm looking at you, Satisfactory). But for those who revel in the sheer joy of intricate construction, resource ballet, and power orchestration, Factorio beckons, ready to unravel its intoxicating magic.In summary, Factorio may not boast the flashy graphics of the 2020s, but what it lacks in visual glamour, it compensates with an abundance of insane fun, depth, and untapped potential. So, if you're prepared to embark on a gaming adventure that is as challenging as it is rewarding, Factorio eagerly awaits your command. Prepare to be enchanted!

_childDocuments_.review: If you like problem-solving (puzzles, math, and logic), you'll like Factorio. Try to weave one more belt through a dense area of factory; Calculate how many machines you need to fill a belt; Use logic circuit networks to run things more efficiently, etc. There's also a side of combat against wildlife that thinks smog = food; They are an annoying and dangerous--but completely optional--distraction.Factorio is the best-developed game I've seen; The only bugs in sight are the wildlife, and with it's mod-friendliness and well-documented API, there is a wide array of mods ranging from quality of life to complete overhauls that can take hundreds of hours to finish!

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: RimWorld where you play as the only pawn who has to build, research, and defend a sprawling factory of your creation.Crash-landed on a randomly generated alien world, you have to build up your own personal factory to manufacture resources from raw materials in order to ascend research tiers and ultimately construct a rocket for your escape. This is Factorio, a top-down game of placing conveyors, resource management, and base defense from the aliens that don't like pollution from all your coal-burning furnaces. You have to find a suitable starting point, start gathering basic stone and iron, and work your way up to an automated jungle of steel. The game has had several graphics updates since when I first picked it up, and the controls take a little getting used to, but the game play is extremely solid and satisfying. All of the pieces of automation just work and the logic for how conveyor belts, inserters, and assemblers do their jobs is satisfying when you learn how everything is supposed to go together.Like many resource games, such as Minecraft, you are finding raw ore and smelting it into workable metal. You start with iron, copper, stone, and coal. Your early automation is fueled by coal, but one of the first things you do is set up electricity to power your inserters, assemblers, and research labs. As you develop more research, there unlocks more resources. Oil refining, uranium, steel plates, etc. Which in turn means more complexity to the middle and later games.There are aliens that dislike pollution and will attack in waves once a threshold is complete. You'll have to break away from laying conveyor belting to defend your base, and can divert research and resources into construction of automated defenses too. Eventually you will even need to strike out on your own to clear out nests, as the aliens have valuable artifacts necessary for research of later technologies.Most games nowadays don't have demos for you to try, they instead would rather you pay more for access to an incomplete mess. I have a feeling the developers really stand by their product, which is why it rarely goes on sale. Try Factorio out for free and see if you don't fall in love with it today. You'll get hundreds of hours of enjoyment for half the price of a "full" game that you'll be bored with in a fraction of the time.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is what you'd get if you take city builders like Anno or pre-5 Settlers games, strip all the fluff, leaving nothing but production chains, then make those production chains more numerous, complex and intertwined.At it's core, it's a real-time automation game where you manually build infrastructure to support ever-growing production chains that will ultimately turn your raw resources (coal, iron, copper, oil, uranium etc.) into research, which will unlock more resources, more production and more upgrades. You start with nothing but a pickax, an your ultimate goal is to build a space rocket, load it with rocked fuel and a satelite and launch it into space. The context to all this is that you're stranded on an alien planet and are trying to build a rocked in order to escape. Of course, you can always keep playing even after launching the rocket (I guess you decided that you were having too much fun polluting the planet and slaughtering the alien hordes that attack you in response) and there's even an incentive: there's a whole number of technologies that require "space research" resource that is produced only by a successful satellite launch.In addition to "building tall" (expanding your central factory), you'll also have to "build wide" (expand your resource gathering network). Basically, resource patches are limited and will get exhausted (with the exception of oil fields; they suffer massive drop in productivity, but they never completely dry out), so you're forced to move out, clear out the alien nests, build more resource gathering outpost and then use trains to bring those resources back to your factory.This agitates the aliens even more than the pollution, causing them to grow more violent and stronger over time, forcing you to build walls, turrets and other forms of static defenses. Of course, you can also turn yourself into an alien killing machine with various technologies, but you can only be in one place at the time, so static defenses really are a must.Also note that this review was written in November 2018 and the game is in constant development. Core gameplay loop is unlikely to change, but additional resources, production chains and technologies are guaranteed to have been added in the meantime.

_childDocuments_.review: I've watched Factorio from a safe distance, since I try to avoid early access games. I played the demo for a bit and got hooked to play it. The game starts very smoothly, you can either try the campaign, which serves as a tutorial, or go straight into "free mode", which gives you an objective to launch a rocket into space. Seems something simple, a single objective, this will be quick, right?Nope. And that is not a bad thing, at all.You will start with nothing and you'll think you're on your regular craft/survival game and think "let me grab here this iron ore to craft some goodies". The start seems to be familar, as you'll smelt this iron in a furnace. And that's where it all starts. You'll soon find out you need much more iron to smelt and make more items, so you might as well craft a drilling machine to help you out digging while you focus at other stuff.Then you decide you can just make some belts to move that iron to the furnaces, so you can further do other projects, maybe find some copper. The way you find these little automations are amazing and fulfilling. You'll start to make a huge mess with belts and inserters, but that is ok, you can always move stuff around to fit a better layout if you want. Or leave the mess as it is, it is functional after all.Without spoiling your fun, you'll find ways to automate everything in sight, because the game is so huge. And don't be scared from videos or screenshots with huge factories. Before you realize it, you'll zoom out your factory and see the huge spaghetti and you'll proudly say out loud: "I made this". Yes, you did. And you will do it again, or improve that design, adjust bad designs that you created when you didn't know better. And you'll know every corner of that giant base you have, be it a mess or a flawless design.Plus tip: If you like playing with trains, this game will make you smile.Don't be scared by the "early access" tag. The game is very polished in it's current state. I have not bumped into any bugs so far.And by the time I'm writting this review, with barely 100h in gametime, I'm about to launch that damn rocket. I'll just tweak my module production, which needs some more red circuits...EDIT: 400h+ in. 0.16+, my railroads are going so far that I can't believe it. I have come so far. Send help. Or maybe not, I'll automate it :D

_childDocuments_.review: It's a game about building a factory to escape a hostile planet. In the process, you make the planet even more hostile because it doesn't like how much pollution your factories spew out.I have never had a game simultaneously make me feel so stupid, and so smart moments later after I solve a problem [that I created because I wasn't forward-thinking enough in my design].It's great single player, but I feel like it really shines in multiplayer because it is a true cooperative experience, and it's great to have people to bounce your ideas off of. There is always something new to learn from your fellow engineers - tricks or shortcuts, or blueprints even that solve a problem you didn't even know existed.You start on a planet with nothing - just a few tools, and surrounded by resources. Of course early on you can do a few things by hand, but eventually the requirements for the next thing you want to do requires too much to do by hand. We must industrialize. To industrialize, you need to setup a manufacturing and resource base - machines can collect resources, machine can process the resources, machines *can make machines.* So the question then becomes: How can I do this faster, better, more efficiently, and make sure I do not run out of resources to feed this machine? You have to take inputs into considerations, ratios, power consumption, travel time. 16 hours ago I was chopping logs, but now I'm trying to understand how to meet the demand of hundreds of circuit boards per minute in order to build the required robots that restock my turrets with bullets.... Anyway. Don't be intimidated by what I'm saying here! This game is actually very approachable in how you can setup and design things with conveyors and the inputs/outputs on machines. Everything is very easy to pickup and fun to learn. Trial and error are the best teacher, and there are few things more satisfying than watching your factory grow from a few stone buildings to a sprawling megacomplex.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sure my review will get lost amongst the slew of others out there, but I wanted to add my humble opinion.There's something relaxing about factorio, something that allows you to whittle away your hours running your factory in abject oblivion to the world around you. It's refreshingly simple to get into, harvesting resources, then automating that process, then building a logistics network to carry to it. You find yourself looking forward, innovating, solving problems.It's one of those games that rewards your efforts and you'll find yourself thinking of ways to streamline the process... get more resources or more efficient even while away from your factory. There is joy here in every corner, from setting the mines and smelters in harmony, with a staggered curve that doesn't punish you for making poor decisions. When something isn't working... a pathway isn't ideal, it's just a simple matter of ripping it up and starting again.And as your technology develops, new and better ways of running your factory present itself.To give you some idea, i spent roughly 70 hours on one map... and I never felt rushed or pained by the individual acts, there was always some new technique or approach that draws you in.And if I may say, all those lovely pictures you'll see making the game seem very complicated and innaccessible, but the reality is far from it.

_childDocuments_.review: Factorio is an absolutely amazing game, and despite still being in early access it is very well put together with few flaws. The goal of the game is to construct a rocket on an alien world and launch it. To do this you have to research technologies, build factory structures, conveyor belts or other feeding mechanism, handle train lines and robotics, all while managing to keep an alien presence at bay.It's all incredibly intricate, and as you advance further down the games tech tree more advanced options for base management and more advanced building become available. Which allows you to build even larger constructs and designs. As you play, you will see your base start from little more than a single “burner drill” to a gargantuan power house of industry and production. The feeling of satisfaction at seeing your hard work create such a bastion of industry cannot be over stated.Eventually, you will get into the fun of min-maxing your designs, finding the most optimum paths to turn raw resources into technology or weapons. You will start to play with production “enhancements” to even further tweak your designs by speeding them up, growing your production, or limiting your consumption to get your supply lines running just right.Of course, there are some down sides. Some of the features of the games are quirky, such as your inability to rename rail station stops to something more descriptive, or seeing a hundred different stations when there’s only two actually available on your current line. Things like this make the train aspect cluttered and bit hard to use at times. Which is a shame given how powerful it is.Other minor disappoints would include the lack of advanced or complex enemies. Currently there are only two types, with four difficulty levels for each type. A close range "bitter" unit, which is  melee fighter and a long range “spitter” unit. Difficulty increases health, armor and attack values but little else, and their attack pattern is the typical "zerg swarm". Given the limited nature of your enemy, engaging with them tactically can get stale fairly quickly. But, being this game is early access I’m hopeful the developer will add more complexity to the aliens before full release.Overall, having played other factory simulators it’s hard to find one that quite compares to the depth and breadth that this beauty of a game delivers. At $20, I feel this game, even in its current early access phase, is a bargain that even more expensive games will fail to match.

_childDocuments_.review: Disappointing ... very disappointing game ... after tons of mods (bobs, angels, space, krastorio, and dozens more) it is still a disappointment.  And the people who love this game are even more disappointing ... I will explain why. Factorio is a very simple basic game that gives the illusion of depth.  Once you have put together your first automated science set up - you pretty much played the whole game.  You will add fluids, trains, nuclear power, etc. but in the end everything follows the same linear flat game play mechanics stuff goes in one way and other stuff comes out the other. You can spend a large amount of time puttering around with this but it requires no skill, is easy to understand, and unrewarding because of its simplicity.  So then you turn to mods ....You will spend your time constantly searching for mods that add more to this game because the vanilla game is very lacking.  Every mod you add, you will experience it once, then change some map settings, maybe do it again, but you will hit a point where you are just going through the motions of laying down the same conveyor belt systems, the same train systems, the same robots, the same assemblers set up.  It does not matter what mod you use since all mods only really impact the length it takes you get sick of the game. The game is completely sandbox but you will get to  a point where you are just done with your base and anymore would just be a waste of time.  The "MegaBases" you see on youtube make me immensely sad since I now know how time consuming they are to make but there is no challenge or difficulty in making them.  You just blob machines and stretch conveyors over and over and make the same defense set ups over and over once you figure it out.  Which does not take long ... The Enemies in this game consist of melee and ranged enemies that attack you if they sniff your pollution.  THey are simple to predict and simple to defend against.  With mods you can make them infinitely stronger but then you will have to modify your turrets to defeat them since the vanilla defenses are crap.  So you end up in this loop of constantly trying out new mods, changing settings, modding the mods, to get a small spurt of actual dynamic difficult gameplay but then you find a way to beat the biters and they become an annoyance.  Or you buff the biters to the point where you cannot beat them at all and then you have to go back and find something that will give you a chance .. then the cycle repeats again ending in an unrewarding win ... The game is very customizable and moddable but certain settings just do not work.  If you make the biters too strong you have to speed up research, if you add too many biters you might not be able to reach any oil source near you so then you need to add a mod that lets you make bio-oil.  So you have a lot of options but you end up back where you started because the gameplay loop in this game is too simple. Way too simple and it depresses me that people think this game is great when its repeated loop is so dumb. 1) you get resources2) You learn how to defend your base which no matter what mod you use is simple OR impossible.  It is not a challenge to defend your base it is just routine.  There are mods / settings where you get killed by hundreds of aliens in the first minute so you just regulate those settings until the challenge is controlled - but it is ALWAYS controlled.  No unpredictability. 2) Then you waste 90% of your resources into research and very little on weapons, tools, defenses, and cool stuff.  You can make this part as expensive as you want - make everything cost 10x as much or make everything 10x cheaper. THe game will be the same just for longer or shorter periods. The gameplay itself will be the same everytime - no unpredictability. 3) You keep eating resources which you can also set to be either quickly used up or last forever.  Then you reach a point where you are done with that factory.  Then you find a new mod and start the whole thing over again.  But it is NEVER that different or surprising ... This next part is kinda insensitive but I cannot find a nice way to say this : The people who like this game like it because of the psychological comfort it gives them in watching things move around.  It is basically like ASMR for gamers. There is no challenge here, there is no surprises, there is no emergent storytelling, no adventure, no mystery, no excitement - just repetitive actions that are comforting to certain mindsets.  It is an illusion of achievement.  No matter what base you build or how many rockets you launch per minute - there is no skill involved and no glorious thinking involved.  It is just placement after placement of the same systems repeated and scaled for as long a time as you need to comfort your brain.  I have logged hundreds of hours in this game but in the end I feel it is doing more harm than good for this genre and for gamers as a whole. It is pushing a type of game that requires no skill and provides no challenge but can suck immense amount of time.  This game is basically a clicker or idle game that gives CERTAIN people a feeling of accomplishment but requires no real skill or talent or divergent thinking.  It just requires time ... so much time ... This stupid "The factory must grow ..." crap is sad.  Growing your factory just requires time and a high tolerance for wasting it  .... No matter how many mods you use you will always end your factory the same way  ... staring at all the crap you placed thinking "Whats next .. ?" and then go looking for new mods/settings.  But you never stop to realize that you are never satisfied because the base gameplay loops and interactions in this game are MASSIVELY UNREWARDING AND SIMPLE. So you constantly search for something that will make it not end in emptiness ... you have no good memories of anything because there is no narrative, no events, no unpredictability, no interactive gameplay - just tile placement. The map generator is nice though ... I think sadly that Factorio has dominated this genre so much that the next games are just capitalizinf on the worst aspects of this game.  ... Dyson Sphere Protocol is just larger even more meaningless factorio  .... no enemies no challenge ... just machines ... and if that gets you excited  then i cry for you  .... sorry .. once again I am being insensitive.UPDATE : Main developer sounds like a douchebag .... typical inadequate male.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll keep it simple. Factorio is like life; Hard, unforgiving, and sometimes downright sadistic but also immensely satisfying. You will spend almost a month working out solutions to various problems. Some with oddly simple solutions, only to find a tech that solves the problem and obsoletes said solution. Others you will find yourselves building walls and entrenching yourself because you forgot about that nest on iron 20km away but now you need that iron, and have to slowly fight your way to it. Every time you fail you learn, and every time you succeed you get that rush of "Finally Did it, F*** yes!" Making the days spent working things out worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting game. Pretty much you accumulate capital and put together a base primarily to do research which you then use to research new techs which are then used to do more advanced research until you have both the capital and know-how to make a rocket silo and then you attach a satellite to the rocket you build, launch it, and that completes the game. You can keep playing to experiment with the mechanics of the game and get space age research but the game pretty much ends when you launch the rocket. There's modes where you have to defend your base from aliens which you can tweak but the fun is in building the base so I prefer to play without aggressive aliens. I'd recommend getting this game even if it will only get you a hundred hours or so of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR - Just take a a glance down the reviews, Overwhelmingly Positive is an understatement.If you don't like factory type games, this will likely not be for you. But if you do like logistical or factory games, this is THE game. Build amazing things, share those things, try things other people have made. Make your own insanely complex factory with a horrible spaghetti layout of belts and pipes. Or, take your time and make something of beauty.Hold back the zerg. Find new resources. Ship those ores around using belts, or, spend another 5 hours learning to make railways. Then learn that there's a better way to make railways, and redo your whole network.And through it all, even though your learning newer and better ways to improve on your really stupid implementations, you don't really mind reworking parts of your sprawling Rube Goldberg factory.If you  don't know if you like factory style games, this would be the one to try that itch out on. If you do, and don't own Factorio, what's wrong with you?!

_childDocuments_.review: A friend linked me this game a few days ago and I was intrigued. My initial thoughts after viewing the trailer was, "Trains? Aliens to defend yourself from? Largescale factories built within an infinite 2D world? Wow! I must buy it! Factorio has been out for years, which if I had've known it existed sooner I surely would have bought it.Your first thoughts when looking at Factorio might be, "Another Early Access game? Ugh!" or, "The price of this 2D Early Access game seems high.." - Let me clarify: It took my friends & I 103 hours to finish the game. That includes sleeping, regular breaks, playing everyday for hours, etc. Few days ago when I bought the game until now I have over 80+ hours with still much more I want to do in Factorio. Factorio has replay value and is well worth $20+, especially how much content it has in it already.Factorio has procedural generation (infinite random world to explore) and different biomes. With that in mind, that also includes an infinite amount of alien hives and aliens. Yes, aliens. They don't like you and you shouldn't like them. Build defenses to keep those buggers out or go out on foot on an adventure to conquer as many as you'd like! Either way, you'll have your hands tied in the process.The basics of the game is easy to learn - never hard. Mine and chop to gain resources and craft hundreds of items to build your factory. Make your factory automatically work by logistics and/or the circuit network, that way you won't have to lift a finger again when it comes to crafting.There's more to the game, I just summed up basic gist of the game and how great it is.Endless possibilities, endless world, endless factory, and endless gameplay all in one 2D package. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: 186 hours in about a month and I put in 44+ hours of RL work 6 days a week. My house is in shambles and the cats are starving.  Master of orion 2 achieved this, Xcom apocolypse achieved this, Minecraft achieved this, Fallout 2 achieved this. Also lets not forget the recent, Stardew Valley and now we have Factorio. "one more turn , more more build, 3 hours later,,, crap, I gotta be to work in 4 hours and I havnt slept yet.". The thought and execution of how this game works and how it is put together is astounding to todays standards.It has a balance and flow that doesnt force a player into a instant meta as in "you have to do this like this all the time" but instead says, "it is your game too, play on.".  , then again why would you want to? Some folks have over 500+ hours on one map! I have one that has 96 hours currently. , you can feel it by how the controls and overall game mechanics flow seamlessly together. A lot of thought and some pure old school genius is at work here.If you loved the games from the 90's that relied on game mechanics and getting the most depth out of a little space then here it is.Parts of this game remind me of, Roller coaster tycoon, Minecraft, Sim city, and oddly Commando from a over head view "old NES version". It even has the flavor of a train simulator. It also is a puzzle game and really makes you think in a good way. _how can I build this-how can I make this better-how much bigger can I make it.I gotta add the negitives as well but there are not much to add; At first the game can seem daunting or even overwhelming when it comes to figuring out how things go together and work but that soon passes.  Starting the tutorial campaign helps with this. I would give this game a easy 10/10 but I give it a 9/10 because it is not finished yet.I strongly reccomend this game for those who like a building sandbox game where you feel you are achieving somthing every step of the way.

_childDocuments_.review: Factorio is as much as a game as SimCity, Stronghold or Eve Online. If you find enjoyment in those types of games and charts, then you will like Factorio.Factorio is along the lines of an classical RTS, utilizing 3-4 base resources to process and construct new buildings. The entire process is a little more complex than your common RTS. The core of Factorio’s gameplay is to gather iron and copper ore, then smelt them into a plate with coal and begin processing them into more complex and refined materials. The deeper you go down the tech tree of Factorio; the more complex and time consuming the production of the required material becomes.It’s not just a vertical depth the game has. Quite soon after starting your world, you will need to start working on generating electricity, an entire system on its own that requires observation and maintenance. Shortly after that, oil adds another system and in most cases it won’t be close to your main base of operation, meaning you need to start working on ways like trains or drones to transport the larger amount of resources from the production centers to your main processing centers.This may sound like a lot at first and speaking from my own experience it was but you also have to consider that this is a very slow game which is the reason why I compared it to the previously mentioned games. Factorio may expand quiet into the viable options for you to focus on but it does so over a 2-5 hour time period for each new system, depending on how fast you are. Additionally, Factorio comes with great multiplayer support which eases up a lot of the complexity when you can figure it out with a friend.Although the multipliers help a lot and the time frame is well placed, Factorio is still a complex game and with that will be a niche. The game will ask you to either pick up on resource management and some other economic ideas quickly or bring them with you prior to play it, or you will end up clocking up your production system and the game will slow to a halt, forcing you to fix the problem before continuing. In addition, the base setting of a world is a hostile one, meaning as you expand your factory, hostile mobs will begin to attack more frequently and in larger numbers.Suggesting Factorio to a new player is a hard decision to make. Personally, I am a person who enjoys having the options of filling his screen with more graphs than gameplay and this is how I spend most of my time playing Factorio by fine tweaking production and transportation as my friend works on processing and research. My opinion is that Factorio is a great game which will consume hours without end from you due to its nature but if you’re thinking about getting it, I suggest asking yourself if you like graphs and if you enjoy optimizations.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: This game is for the kind of people that always have something on their mind, albeit getting a new outpost up or tweaking the production line. There's always something you need to micromanage in this game, and that is what makes it fun. It's a never ending loop of complexity.And even if you end up beating the game, there's always a challenge ahead, be it speedrunning the game as fast as possible, trying out a couple of complex and hard mods or just trying out one of the vanilla modes such as marathon or death world.It's all up to you how you progress: alone in singleplayer, planning out your base beforehand; trying out multiplayer with a couple of friends and spending the whole night trying to get that coal; or just playing at your own pace and derping around.You will always have a challenge with Factorio, there's always something that will bugger you for the whole playthrough. And that is what makes it so much fun!  :)

_childDocuments_.review: This game is in all seriousness, one of the most replayable, well-optimized games I have ever played.The vanilla game is about as perfect as can be, the core gameplay loop never really feels repetitive because there's always more to do, and different ways in which to do it. Everything I could say about it has already arguably been said by other reviews, so I'll refrain, but it's excellent.Not to mention the fact that the modding scene is expansive and well-developed, which means that even after a few hundred hours in the game, there's always some other horizon upon which to expand, whether it be more complex factories, or going far out into space.I would normally try to moderate a review with some criticism as well, but it's hard to do so for Factorio. One could argue that the only major "problem" with it is that it's incredibly addictive, largely due to that oh-so-effective core gameplay loop. The factory, as they say, must grow.I would wholeheartedly recommend this game as one of the, if not the best factory-building game that exists right now. There's a lot to love here.

_childDocuments_.review: 3550 hours says a lot about how much I love playing this game.TBS How to be sure it is for you? Try the demo edition for free.I play the sandbox mode exclusively, usually vanilla (unmodded). But play it anyway you want because of its strong modding community support. Play it solo or multiplayer. Need some nightmare tower defense gameplay? Select deathworld mode. Don't want to deal with enemies so you can focus on building? Select peaceful or no expansion mode instead.After trying the demo, if you don't like Factorio, then uninstall and move on.Don't buy it if you see building and automation as a chore. If you still doing stuff manually 10-15 hours in and hating it, then it is probably not for you. This game encourages automation to free your time to do other stuff. In my current game (80+ hours), I have launched over 200 rockets, its production fully automated. I am now going for city block expansion, where I would stamp my own crafted blueprints, and bots will do the rest. Give this game a try. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a neutral rating because Factorio is not terrible, the fact I put 40 hours in confirms I got  my money's worth but honestly the further I got into the game the more of a grind it felt. Fighting off Aliens is really annoying and not difficult at all. You can set Aliens to peaceful so they don't attack but if you do that you will soon realise there really isn't much else  to the game other than a grind, on my fourth save I decided to go peaceful, spent maybe 5 or 6 hours building a nice factory set for the third tier of science research and then spent about 6 minutes completing ALL third tier science research, I started preparing for fourth tier and my goodness messing around with the oil/chemical infrastructure became a long and mind-numbingly boring excercise especially given that the Factorio UI is far from great and TERRIBLE when it comes to oil. _childDocuments_.review: 188 hours in. I dont think I can stop! Factorio is a game in which you build on your knowledge with every playthrough. I started with the campaign but I don't think it helps you realize the meaning of true automation. The first time I played freeplay, my base got spaghettified so quickly that I couldn't make red circuitss without robots. Red circuits became my biggest bottleneck. I built another batch again, ground up, but it only added to my woes. I am a programmer. This not how you write code! This is not how you build a base! The second time around, I imported the good parts of my first base with blueprints. I didn't want to get blueprints from others. It has to be me who solves the puzzles. I planned it perfectly. Or so I thought. Further down the research tree, factories demanded fluids! Nuclear power is hard to build! There is no space! Infinite world, Railways, Robots, Defence against biters, Power spikes due to laser turrets! I some how managed to complete the game in the third play through. It took 36 hours of play time! And they challenge me to complete it in less than 15 hours! Less than 8 hours! Well challenge accepted. Oy but what about mods? Uhh. Yeah there are mods where its a completely different game with completely different logistic demands! OH MAN! This game is a work of art.
