_childDocuments_.review: Who doesn't love a good game of mini-golf?  If you don't, you are looking at the wrong product, friend.  Golf With Your Friends is exactly what it says on the tin.  An online mini-golf game, complete with Workshop and cross-platform support.  Going into this game, I was very excited, as it is 100% up my alley, and I even have friends to play it with!  Imagine that.  If you don't, there are open servers and the community is very active.  I can't judge the community in terms of play experience, due to only playing in private servers, but it's mini-golf so how bad can it be?With all of that said, this game isn't perfect.  My primary issue with the game is that it isn't very well optimized.  I tested this game on an HP Envy 17-1181 (Core i7 940XM, 8GB RAM, ATI Mobility Radeon HD 5850) and on a late 2012 MacBook Air (Core i5-3427U, 4GB RAM, Intel HD Graphics 4000).  Both run the game smoothly enough, but the game caused audio issues with Discord on the Mac, and caused the HP to shut down due to overheating.  Granted, the HP runs hot normally, but other Unity games don't cause the computer to shut down.  To be completely fair, the game is in Early Access, so this issue should be patched out once the game goes Gold.  Additionally, unlike a AAA development team, the devs of this game are probably limited on their testing hardware, so they can't possibly make the game run perfectly on every computer.  So while the poor optimization is an issue I ran into, I'm not as bothered by it as I would in another game.I'm normally rather critical of the Early Access model, as it can feel like a leap of faith to the consumer.  This game is very worth playing, if only to see just how high (or low, if you have skill) your score can get.  I ended Oasis with 100+.

_childDocuments_.review: for more eggcellent reviews like this.Golf With your Friends is a fun but at times jank mini golf simulator. It comes with a good selection of premade maps that have their own gimmicks and ideas, and are pretty fun to play through. These courses are all very well designed and creative. You can also play through every map in either online, offline, or in different modes such as a basketball and hockey mode. These are nice little distractions but aren't as good as the golf in my opinion. The game also gives you the ability to jump as the ball which brings in a whole new set of strategy for creative players. From what I've experienced, the community is very welcoming and fun to play through games with. You also have access to the selection of community made maps which is home to some fantastic maps which can also be played online with others which is really fun to do. This game also has drops which is always a plus. It does have it's own share of bugs though. On more than one occasion I've gotten completely stuck on maps that were premade. The amount of times this has happened honestly shocks me considering the developers have had more than enough time to fix these. I've also had the ball randomly launch itself off like a space shuttle and go waaaaay faster than it normally would and it can end up in god knows where but this one happens less often. Overall if you're a fan of minigolf, or just want a nice relaxing game to play with friends, I think you'll enjoy this.

_childDocuments_.review: Golf With Your Friends—the game where it’s totally not your fault when you miss a shot. No, seriously, every time I miss, it’s clearly the game glitching. But foreal, this game is pure chaos, where the rules of physics bend and Moto still finds a way to need more Aimlabs training. I mean, come on, Moto—this is golf, not a shooter, and yet somehow, you’re still missing!It’s all fun and games until the course turns into a battlefield of rage and laughs. You’re trying to hit a perfect shot while your friends sabotage your every move, and then when you land that epic putt, you wonder how you’re the only one holding it together. Meanwhile, Moto’s probably launching his ball into the stratosphere instead of the hole.This game is all about timing, finesse, and blaming the game when things go wrong (because, let’s be honest, it’s always the game). But despite the glitches (or my "glitches"), it’s a blast with friends, especially when you want to laugh at how wildly unpredictable it can be.Randy Rating: 4.3/5 — Great fun, but if you’re missing your shots, don’t worry—it’s just the game glitching. Right, Moto?

_childDocuments_.review: It was a regular Friday night for a group of friends who loved to play online games. Tonight, they had decided to play a round of golf with their friends. Alex, Adam, and their other friends were all excited to compete against each other in the virtual world.As the game progressed, Adam couldn't resist his mischievous nature and kept knocking Alex's ball away, causing him to lose points. Alex, usually a calm and friendly guy, started to get frustrated and angry with Adam's actions. But Adam just laughed it off, thinking it was all just a game.However, as the game went on, Alex's anger only grew. He became obsessed with beating Adam and winning the game. But each time he was about to make a good shot, Adam would interfere and ruin it for him.Finally, Alex had enough. In a fit of rage, he grabbed a golf club from his room and stormed over to Adam's house. Without warning, he swung the club and hit Adam on the head, knocking him to the ground.The other friends were shocked and horrified by Alex's sudden outburst. They quickly called for help, but it was too late. Adam was pronounced dead at the scene.Alex was arrested and charged with murder. As the investigation unfolded, it was revealed that Alex had been struggling with anger issues and had been seeking revenge against Adam for a long time. The online game was just the trigger that pushed him over the edge.The once friendly and fun-loving group of friends was now torn apart by this horrific event. The game that was meant to bring them together had only caused destruction and tragedy.From that day on, the game of golf was banned from their gaming sessions, a constant reminder of the terrible consequences of letting anger and competitiveness consume them. And Alex was left to live with the guilt and regret of his actions, a warning to all of us that even in the virtual world, our actions can have real-life consequences.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Golf With Your Friends is infuriating. It is rage-inducing simply because it is so fun. The basic gist here is simple,  it's golf. The controls are pretty solid, and the course design is clever. It is mini golf. That's basically it. It's really very good mini golf, but it is mini golf. So if you don't like one of the other implementations of this game on Steam, then you probably won't like this. But if you do, it's fun.It's hard to really make a case for these individual mini golf games, simply because mini golf isn't a very broad niche, meaning there is significant overlap between games in the genre. However, I think Golf With Your Friends is a very well-done example of a genre which is most certainly worth the price, especially on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Golf with your Friends is a casual game you can enjoy with others. I'm sure everyone is familiar with the base game of golf. Now combine this with different skins for your golfballs, trails, little hats and tons of maps that can be absolutely frustrating to finish. You can either properly play the map or use your ability to jump over shortcuts  and annoy your friends and make them wonder how you keep getting those low scores.I've recently played this game with friends of mine and once the bumping was turned on, it turned into a mess and it was more of a fight of who can hit who instead of actually getting the ball into the hole to win the game. It caused a lot of laughter and fun banter and that's enough for me to absolutely recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a 45 yo father, probably one of the oldest people playing this game. I am a single father to my Son, who is 14 now. My son got this game for his birthday from his uncle, so we installed it on his computer and he started playing. By the end of the week he had 300 hours on this game. This was horrible for me, as it was already hard for me to find ways to spend time with my son, as he is always out with his friends or just watching YouTube. So i decided to make a Steam account and get this game to see if I could maybe play alongside him. I loaded into the game, picked my golf color and started playing but I was stuck on what you where supposed to do. I asked my Son for help and he hosted a game for me to join. I loved it as it was the best time I had spent with my son since my wife had died. This game has ever since brought me and my son closer again and now we actually spend time together outside the house together as well. This game reminded me that there's fun to be had in everything, and it has brought both me and my Son many happy memories.

_childDocuments_.review: Was complete and utter crap in early access, and is still complete and utter crap after coming out of early access. I can't believe they're selling this for $15 when it used to be $5.If you're looking for a golf game on Steam, you're kind of out of luck. This is one of the best of the few golf games Steam has to offer, which should basically tell you that there are  good golf games on this platform. I have played other golf games that are available here, and I do not recommend them either.The only real pros of the game are that there's a lot of content that is otherwise well made. There's lots of official courses as well as user generated courses (though those tend to have even worse issues than official courses).Anyways, why is this trash? It has awful physics, lots of clipping issues on courses, horribly chosen pars, awfully designed courses that frequently make calculating the trajectory of your ball more difficult than it needs to be, and high CPU usage for no good reason. The graphics are dated and ugly, and the music is so repetitive and trite that I had to mute it to retain my sanity (it's not that the music is bad, it's just so incredibly cliché). The only reason I have any significant amount of hours in this game is because some of my friends either don't know what else to play or want to play different game.

_childDocuments_.review: A clock or a timepiece[1] is a device used to measure and indicate time. The clock is one of the oldest human inventions, meeting the need to measure intervals of time shorter than the natural units such as the day, the lunar month and the year. Devices operating on several physical processes have been used over the millennia.Some predecessors to the modern clock may be considered as "clocks" that are based on movement in nature: A sundial shows the time by displaying the position of a shadow on a flat surface. There is a range of duration timers, a well-known example being the hourglass. Water clocks, along with the sundials, are possibly the oldest time-measuring instruments. A major advance occurred with the invention of the verge escapement, which made possible the first mechanical clocks around 1300 in Europe, which kept time with oscillating timekeepers like balance wheels.[2][3][4][5]Traditionally, in horology (the study of timekeeping), the term clock was used for a striking clock, while a clock that did not strike the hours audibly was called a timepiece. This distinction is no longer made. Watches and other timepieces that can be carried on one's person are usually not referred to as clocks.[6] Spring-driven clocks appeared during the 15th century. During the 15th and 16th centuries, clockmaking flourished. The next development in accuracy occurred after 1656 with the invention of the pendulum clock by Christiaan Huygens. A major stimulus to improving the accuracy and reliability of clocks was the importance of precise time-keeping for navigation. The mechanism of a timepiece with a series of gears driven by a spring or weights is referred to as clockwork; the term is used by extension for a similar mechanism not used in a timepiece. The electric clock was patented in 1840, and electronic clocks were introduced in the 20th century, becoming widespread with the development of small battery-powered semiconductor devices.The timekeeping element in every modern clock is a harmonic oscillator, a physical object (resonator) that vibrates or oscillates at a particular frequency.[3] This object can be a pendulum, a tuning fork, a quartz crystal, or the vibration of electrons in atoms as they emit microwaves, the last method of which is so precise that it serves as the definition of the second.Clocks have different ways of displaying the time. Analog clocks indicate time with a traditional clock face, with moving hands. Digital clocks display a numeric representation of time. Two numbering systems are in use: 12-hour time notation and 24-hour notation. Most digital clocks use electronic mechanisms and LCD, LED, or VFD displays. For the blind and for use over telephones, speaking clocks state the time audibly in words. There are also clocks for the blind that have displays that can be read by touch.

_childDocuments_.review: My life was in shambles before I found Golf. I had a severe drinking problem, and was arrested and charged with multiple DUI's. While in prison, my wife of 15 years filed for divorce, taking our three children with her. I lost my job. I lost my family. I had nothing. _childDocuments_.review: This isn't your ordinary session of minigolf. Golf With Your Friends consists of numerous maps with special conditions and items that can be used. There's gravity wells, black holes, jet packs, and cannons, just to name a few. Fully customize the conditions of your game from the amount of holes to the shape of your ball. You even earn little fancy customizations the longer you play.I've always been curious about this game from watching several YouTubers play it. Eventually it went on sale for $5 and I was able to convince about four of my friends to get it. We usually only play over the weekend but it is pretty fun. I don't even mind losing, which I do most of the time.There are some frustrating bugs and other elements to the game. During the Worms course, I fell through the world multiple times. Expect to waste a stroke frequently because either the flagpole will bounce your ball away from the hole, or the hole will slide you over instead of right into it. There's also this frustrating lack of direction on some holes. The game has very elaborate shots and when it isn't clear where to go, you can run out of strokes fast.I've been through all of the default game courses (excluding the DLC ones) and I definitely have my favorites. Steer clear of Worms and Twilight if you don't want to yeet your computer out the nearest window. A map editing mode makes for endless possibilities but so far, the workshop doesn't seem that full of too many options.The game is three years old and still has some kinks that need to be worked out. I recommend getting it on sale, but either way, it can be a pretty fun time, especially if you have friends and voice chat.
_childDocuments_.name: Golf With Your Friends

_childDocuments_.review: Golf with your Friends is an incredibly fun game to play with friends or just chill out and play a round on your own. The default maps are re-playable and quite good. The physics is surprisingly good, assuming consideration for the elasticity of the objects (the ball goes where you think it will), though, Ive not played with bouncy ground - or the new bouncy house DLC. Playing with jumping turned on is my true life hack - it makes this game downright comical and can occasionally outsmart the hole - I have unlocked the secrets to quite a few maps. I don't play many video games, but I find myself coming back to this game and wanting to buy it for all of my friends - and at this price point, its hard to say no.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot has changed since I've posted my previous review in 2019 (see below), Team17 first seemingly cooperate with Blacklight to bring the game to other platforms and then bought the IP and Assets outright at the end of 2020 / beginning of 2021. A game that did receive regular updates and bug fixes from a team of 3 developers is now withering away under the ownership of a publicly traded company with 200-ish employees that couldn't even be bothered to post patch notes for the last update. I hope that £12 million buyout was worth it... well, it probably will be once they'll shove GWYF 2 out the door.If all you're after is a simple mini golf game and don't plan on anything other than playing it, this is still the version to get. When you're done with the official maps, the workshop has content for days which you'll not get on other platforms. I'd still recommend it, even with it's obvious faults that should be long gone with the resources that T17 could throw at it, as long as it's not at full price. Stay away from the editor though...Coming from someone who build 10 maps over the span of 2-ish years... no. Just no. It feels almost like they're purposely sabotage the editor. Whoever was given the job of working on it is either incompetent, doesn't give a ♥♥♥♥ or simply half-asses it. Known bugs (e.g. pieces will just jump outside the map when you look at them wrong, breaking the map) won't get fixed. Responses by their support on the Steam board are worthless copy/pasta. Formerly working stuff in the editor is now broken (can't rotate assets on more than one axis, manually entering values doesn't work, ...) and, this is the best IMHO, scaling/position values on existing assets were changed so much that already published maps on the workshop were unplayable. No QA, no patches, no ♥♥♥♥♥ given.--- Old review:A nice relaxing mini golf game... that is until you miss a shot that you should be able hit blindfolded. For the 3rd time. While your friends are laughing at, never with, you. Embrace the rage. It sure could use more work and polishing, specially the level editor, but it's already quite nice as it is.

_childDocuments_.review: **Title: A Hilarious and Entertaining Mini Golf Experience – Golf With Friends****Rating: ★★★★☆ (4/5)**Golf With Friends is a wonderfully chaotic mini-golf game that brings a fun twist to the classic sport. With its quirky courses, customizable gameplay, and multiplayer focus, it’s a perfect choice for casual gaming sessions with friends.**Gameplay Mechanics:**The gameplay is straightforward yet engaging. Players use a power meter to control their shots, and the physics are designed to allow for both precision and unpredictability. The inclusion of various power-ups and unique obstacles keeps the gameplay dynamic, leading to hilarious moments as players navigate through challenging and creative course designs.**Course Variety:**The game features a range of imaginative courses, each with its own theme and challenges. From whimsical settings like candy lands to more fantastical designs, the variety ensures that no two rounds feel the same. The vibrant graphics and attention to detail in each course make exploration enjoyable.**Multiplayer Fun:**Golf With Friends shines in its multiplayer mode. Whether you’re playing locally or online, the competitive spirit is infectious. Watching friends struggle with tricky holes or pull off incredible shots adds to the fun. The game supports various modes, including classic mini-golf and more chaotic variations like "hockey" or "basketball," keeping gameplay fresh and exciting.**Customization Options:**One of the standout features is the ability to customize your ball and game settings. Players can choose different ball types and even adjust gravity, ball size, and other parameters, adding a personal touch to each match. This customization enhances replayability and allows for creative variations in gameplay.**Graphics and Sound:**Visually, the game is colorful and charming, with a playful art style that matches its lighthearted tone. The sound design complements the experience well, featuring cheerful music and satisfying sound effects that enhance the overall enjoyment.**Final Thoughts:**Golf With Friends is a delightful and entertaining mini-golf experience that excels in its multiplayer gameplay and creative course design. With its easy-to-learn mechanics, varied game modes, and customization options, it provides endless fun for players of all ages. If you’re looking for a game that combines skill, laughter, and friendly competition, Golf With Friends is a fantastic choice that will keep you and your friends coming back for more!

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been in early access for at least four years now and has been changed and modified so many times I doubt the devs have any idea what they want the finished product to be like or will even realise when it's complete.Regardless, possibly as a result of the ridiculous development time this game has been the victim of a feedback loop from their beta testers. Since the only people playing are beta testers, many of whom have been with the game for years now...the bulk of the feedback has been coming from people who have been playing the game for hundreds and hundreds of hours...very little from newcomers and people who have less playtime.As a result, the entire game has been tweaked and modified in an attempt to please this base of hardcore fans, seemingly to the exclusion of anybody else. Case in point, the first couple of levels are pleasant enough, but the game quickly becomes INSANELY difficult very quickly, to the point at which it's virtually unplayable unless you already have mounds of experience with the peculiarities of the gameplay and somewhat odd physics engine. Not only do many holes REQUIRE you to complete incredibly complicated, precise moves (Rather than having them be optional shortcuts or bonuses, these are the STANDARD path)..but it's not often even clear which way you're supposed to be going. I get the impression that the long-term fans are wise to the devs way of thinking and can anticipate how they've mapped out the holes, but this is NOT obvious to most of us.This could be a good game, but the devs desperately need to take a step back and look at it more objectively, perhaps getting input from people who haven't been putting hundreds and hundreds of hours into the game already. After all, when a software house has completed the maps for a game they're developing, they don't base the difficulty curve solely on their in-house playtesters, do they? People who know every nook and cranny inside-out, the location of all the enemies, pick-ups, secrets and nuances....They need balance, something this game is sorely lacking.

_childDocuments_.review: "Golf With Your Friends" is an online multiplayer golf game, a golf game with your friends -- as the title states. This game is very straightforward. You can either play an online game with other random players or with your friends. An online room fits up to 12 people, and games will get crazy when you have more people playing! You can also choose to play alone, though playing with friends or with other people will offer you a much more amusing experience with the game. As of right now, there are six stages: Forest, Oasis, Twilight, Haunted, Candyland, and Ancient. There are 14 holes in each stage. I thoroughly enjoyed playing all of these stages. My favorite is definitely Candyland! One of my favorite features of "Golf With Your Friends" is that there are a plethora of settings that you can adjust, such as ball size, ball appearances, ball shape (dirty-minded people, hold your horsies), time and shots per round, jumping, gravity, and much much more!If you have lots of friends and if you love Mini-Golf, I'd recommend this game! It's very cheap and affordable. For funsies, I'd like to inform everyone that I made my friend rage-quit during a game because I continuously knocked him off the stage, since Collision Mode was on.Pros:Amazing online gameplayMay choose to play offlineFun stages!Customization optionsPlenty of game settingsCons:Can be boring if you have no friends.Needs more stagesMay ruin relationships.A level editing mode would be nice.

_childDocuments_.review: This is basically a copy/paste from my previous post (which went ignored) regarding my original post 6 months prior.Tried giving this a go since way back in March when I played. I had forgotten just about everything from my previous play through, but it all came rushing back pretty much immediately. So much seems exactly the same.Things that jumped out right away:o Camera (or lack of) to see an overview of the hole you are on. I'd say by far this is the biggest annoyance of this game. Maybe I'm in the minority, but I feel like 100% of the enjoyment is lost when you sink the ball into a hazard that you don't even know is there. This trial and error is extremely frustrating. There should be an overview (top-down) button that is always selectable at the very least A flythrough camera would also be nice at least for the start of the hole, but a birds-eye view would at least give you an idea where you are even shooting for. It is a fundamental of the game to be able to see the course/hole to know what you are aiming for. This is so much more important (in my opinion obviously) than additiona courses or ball shapes at the moment. It is the one thing that makes me not want to play the game again.o No sound for striking the ball. Not only should it make the sound of hitting the ball, but it should also be louder based on how hard it is hit. Without this sound, it just seems weird (especially since hitting the ball into an object makes a sound). Very sterile and like the game is muted. The sounds could be realistic (like a ball actually "pinging" off the putter).. or more arcade-like with the sound of a swoosh of air and the driver whacking the ball. Just something to give it a little "life".o No visual or audio cue that the turn is over and the ball is ready to be struck again.o The stroke counter resetting to 0 immediately after sinking the putt. While yes, the score card is shown at that time, it still would be nice to leave the current stroke count at the bottom right of the screen until the hole is advanced. Since that is where you normally are keeping track during the game, it always seems odd when you sink the putt and glance to see what you got (something that is just natural), but just see a big 0 instead of your actual stroke total.o Ball is routinely covered by world geometry. While you can still see your power indicator, it is very jarring (and just plain looks odd) to try and aim a ball you can't see.I know this is still EA and you guys have been working on it quite a bit. Just giving my opinion again for that very reason...

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite pastimes is playing miniature golf. I have decided to review the various places I have made the attempt to play at and set them up here. If you have a comment, please send it to me and I will add it. I will rate all of the locations on four options using a scale of one to ten. The facilities will be rated on:  Challenge, Variety, Fun and Overall Value.There will also be a brief description of the facility and the amenities offered as well as prices as remembered from past experience. Some prices may have changed since I was there. Challenge is a ranking of how difficult the course is to play. There may also be a factor for how much skill it takes vs how much luck is involved in playing the course. Try to view it as if you don't play often when using this rating.Variety is a ranking of how many other things are available to do at the facility. Does it have any extras like batting cages or go-carts. I generally will keep courses that have a good variety of holes but nothing else around a 5-6 range. The more amenities, the higher the score.Fun may be my most subjective item. Is the golf course too difficult to have a good time, or to easy. Is there a good balance between difficulty and challenge. How much do you enjoy this course vs. some others? Would you take a date there?Overall Value is based on the price to play vs the fun had. It should reflect some composite of the other factors.    Feel free to try them out and tell me if you agree or disagree with my ratings. I am, by no means, an expert. I just know what I like.    Also, a note for the owners of the locations: If you find I have made an error in reporting your location or prices, drop me an email and I will correct it at my first opportunity. My opinions are my own regarding value for dollar, but Idon't want to provide incorrect factual information.    Please note that, unless otherwise stated, all prices are for one round adult admission. Children's pricing and specials may vary.    I wanted to apologize, publicly, for not having updated the site for a while. I've been very busy and, frankly, the web site was not at the top of my priorities. Please check to make sure I have updated everything you sent.    There is one other thing. I have noticed that a lot of miniature golf owners lately have been sending me reviews of their own places, basically for free advertising. I have no problem with this, per se, but I would like to ask that any owners who do so also be sure to post at their facilities that they are shown on the Miniature Golf Review Page and encourage your customers to send me an objective review. (I know many of you try to be objective, but it is extremely difficult to be critical of your own work. Trust me, I know.) It seems like a fair deal for those looking to get themselves noticed.Mulligan MacDuffer Adventure GolfSubmitted by: Nancie Wilson Course Website: Price:            4-7 Challenge:        8 Variety:          8 Fun:              10 Overall Value:    10            Two 18 hole courses that climb mountains, go over waterfalls, and meander by streams and a pond.  They also have a nice "clubhouse" ice cream parlor.  Very challenging, very well maintained, and lots of fun.Location: 1360 Baltimore Pike, Gettysburg, PA 17325,  717-337-1518Woodland GolfSubmitted by: Mike J. Perry Personal Web Site:   Course Web Site:   Price:            Free to Locals Challenge:        10 Variety:          7 Fun:              10 Overall Value:    9            Woodland golf is located in a secluded town near Pittsburgh, PA called Jefferson Estates.  If you are a local, it's free to play.  If not, play anyways.  This is a very unique course, set, literally, in the woodlands.  It is played on the natural floor surface of the infamous First Woods in Jefferson Estates, PA!  So check out the site will ya?    Editors note: I tried to contact the individual for more information, but they never responded. I take their rankings with a grain of salt. If anyone has been to this course, I would appreciate an objective review. It sounds interesting to me and well worth a look for locals. The free to locals, in my opinion should make the value a 10, depending on the state of the course.Water's Edge Mini-GolfSubmitted by: Tom SweetPrice:            6.50 Challenge:        9 Variety:          10 Fun:              10 Overall Value:    10            Water's Edge Mini-Golf is located in Lancaster County, Pennsylvania, right in the middle of the Amish Country. The course is three years old and looks like the day it opened.  It is immaculately kept.  Landscaping, (in which I have a degree) surely cost a fortune as this course is built with varying degrees of topographical difference.  Three waterfalls two stream crossings and four ponds are inside this facility. This  must be one of the nicest in the U.S. Each time we visit from Atlanta, Georgia, we're sure to make this a stop.  People are so friendly, and where else can you park your car beside a horse and buggy and go play golf with an Amish couple!  The facility also has a clubhouse with an Ice Cream parlor, dipping some of the biggest cones I've ever seen!  I encourage anyone in the area to stop in and give it a try. The course is small, yet beautiful. It is only mildly challenging, yet tons of fun. Every year I spend a week on the island and find myself going to the course every day. There are weekly tournaments that are really fun. The course is great and the environment is friendly that is why Hartland Golf is my favorite mini golf course!Hole in One Miniature GolfSubmitted by: Brian O'ToolePrice:            6.50 Challenge:        7 Variety:          5 Fun:              8 Overall Value:    7    This course is challenging and fun to play. _childDocuments_.review: Now that it's out of early access, this still feels like a promising early access game. It needs a lot more polish -- for example, the camera angles often get annoyingly blocked by environment art, which in a professional and polished game you would expect to fade out to allow you to line up your shot. More thought also needs to go in to the speed and responsiveness of the game, as you often end up watching out of bounds balls rolling very slowly to a halt, with no apparent option to just skip the rest of the turn or immediately reset the ball.A level editor is always a very nice feature to have and could potentially give ongoing life to the game and community, but sadly it is broken and doesn't come with a tutorial or even any balloon tips, so it's unlikely that anybody but the most die-hard fan will use it. They should look at the Trackmania Forever level editor for inspiration if they want to improve on this.The frustrating thing is that all of the games problems are very obvious and shouldn't be too difficult to fix if Team17 had any interest in the title, so the fact that they've come out of early access without these fixes suggests to me that they've cut their losses and won't be providing much in the way of ongoing support or fixes. If that is the case they would be far better advised to release it as a F2P title to populate the servers and allow a community to form, which they could then monetise further down the road. It occurs to me that the game may have been designed whilst loot crates were still de-riguer, and now that that trend has thankfully passed they just don't know what to do with their product.It is still a fun game, the sort that could occupy an hour or so with friends at the end of the evening. It can be played in turns around one screen, but it really shines in its online mode where everybody can take their shots simultaneously. Sadly I've only been able to find a server with more than one or two people once. I would very much like to play Golf With Your Friends with my friends, but I can't in good conscience recommend that they all spend £6 on a copy. If it gets reduced to <£3 in a sale I'll buy it for them and we'll have a good laugh.

There is more content now, but the amount grows kind of slowly. There's now 7 maps, and more gamemodes, including Basketball and Hockey to change it up from just golf. They've also added microtransactions too, however, but it's not bad at all. The items in the game are earned by players from playing the game, so it's ridiculous, and it is purely cosmetic, and effects the game in no way. The steam market thrives like other games with items, and it's interesting to collect. All in all, still a good game, and it's much better than it used to be, despite still being considered "early access" currently.Other than these, it's a nice game, and it's very enjoyable. I love the concept and I hope to see new maps, bug fixes, and increased optimization. I still hope this game becomes more popular and gets more updates to make it better than it already is.November 2020:The visual style has taken off, and it's a much different game, for the better!

_childDocuments_.review: Look, I mean I've played this a lot, had a lot of laughs, even did a couple courses on par completely.That said, the reason im giving this a thumbs down is well deserved in its own right, let me tell you what bothers me.Clipping, Yes, sometimes at some levels its possible to clip through walls, and lose.Physics : Not always accurate as other play throughs (So I guess the game becomes more luck based).Pars : This is my biggest annoyance, whoever set the par rate in a LOT of courses, set it straight out on "If you're really lucky this should be right!"The game is actually pretty fun, but the creators (Team17) should've made the par chart a bit more on par with the course itself, like the barrel level in Forest should be a 3 par instead of a 2 par so that it's not completely luck based of hitting the hole in the barrel but more so for people that don't get that (Super lucky shot), btw this comes from someone who finished THAT COURSE on its par limit already.Beyond that, the physics are often wonkey, and in some levels (like space station and the haunted course) you can legitly get your ball in place where there's sadly no more saving it, since the level see's it as a "legit part of the course", while factually you shouldnt be able to get there.Lastly the camera can go completely wonky on you (especially close to walls) making shots or even looking at your screen a headache, and in levels with minecarts, or other moving objects, they sometimes just decide to go invisible, making it a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ playthrough.Also, more often than not you get disconnected from the "Rare already" Multiplayer sessions because of a "Network Error" which is just sad.Can't believe that we're now sold a singular DLC map for 3$ and it's a garbage map too.Lastly, Snowflakes for instance sells in marketplace for 1100$, but as far as I know its unobtainable, it's an effect from what 2019? or so and has since been unlocked since the game doesn't do "holiday events" or something.Still thumbs down for me.

_childDocuments_.review: During this global pandemic, I found myself often stranded in my room with a library of games that had gone untouched for times that had stretched up to two years. When I sat down in a discord call, my best friend Sam actually suggested that we play a game called "Golf With Your Friends" From that day forward my life had begun to change. When you first enter the game, the bliss and appeal of it isn't immediately apparent. You have heavily themed stages with goofy mechanics that at first can make the game seem more like a rage game that you play with your friends to make them angry. However, the more you play this game and look into in its programming, design, physics, and most importantly, yourself, you find that the game is more of a life lesson than a stupid rage game that you play with your friends. So after the call with Sam and my other friends ended, I kept playing. I grinded the first stage for maybe an hour before getting par on it. The moment that I did, the satisfaction of succeeding in that stage and finally beating it to completion washed over me and in that moment: The game's bliss had revealed itself for the first time. In fact, I was so happy and dazed that I actually fainted and collapsed on the ground. From that moment forward, this game became my new way of life, waking up, getting a breakfast sandwich and playing each of the games stages for hours and hours, trying to beat the pars of each level and continually building that gratification from achieving those goals in each and every stage. These moments eventually made me fall into a crescendo of endless happiness from playing this game. Looking at the graphics jump off the screen into my life made me feel enveloped in my childhood of going to mini-golf with my family. Getting a hole in one made me feel so enlightened, like I was getting blessed by God in the chapel. And I don't even know if God exists! Then the devs reveled that the game, after a long time in the "Early Release" oven, was finally coming out. With one more stage included. I fell into a coma after that, laying in my bed for days on end. And as the sands of time blew over and it came out, I continued to lay in bed, far away from my conscience. Then today I awoke, Thursday, May 28th, 2020. I finally rose from my bed and crawled to my chair, clawing my way to my seat and finally playing the fully released game. I turned it on... I played the new course on every mode... and then the game had made me realize something. Something brand new that I had never noticed before.This games sucks.Don't buy it unless you want your heart broken and your illusion of happiness shattered.

_childDocuments_.review: Golf With Your Friends is an elaborate tale of a tragic loss, and phyrric victories. Every shape has a story. Every hole has a gap needed filled. I myself experienced such experiences, and have decided to record my memoirs here to share my experiences with the public from the Great Golf Race.Myself and several others had gathered 'round the colorful and bountiful territory, known as Candyland. We prepped our colors; Green, Blue, White, more Blue, and Pink. We dashed off with ease, eventually landing at the terrifying chasm of the speedy gumdrops in a simple three swipes. Such irony, a tasty snack used against us as a weapon of mass destruction?An ally had gunned his speed, luckily travelling through the narrow path, missing the plump drops by hairlengths. Another soon followed, only to be met with sugary death. It was my time to challenge them. I braced myself, groaning into my microphone before closing my eyes, opening them to see that my boldness had paid off. I finished the coarse with only five gentle, yet firm putts.I turned back to watch the remaining two struggle to push through the gumdrops. Two, after at least eleven attempts, made it. We continued forth onto the next Course, accepting the lost of our eldest member.Upon arrival to a watery stop, the floor made of Hyrdogen Oxide had stopped us from approaching our destination. We had to design rafts for our spherical embodiments. Upon cross, our initial organized group had fallen apart, leading to every man for himself. I was thrown off against the wall, before gasping for air, feeling for any land that I dreamt of. My wish was granted, I dragged myself onto the shore, rolling away to the end of the horrid waterland.Several courses later, amidst the gurgling leaps of faiths and rummaging into each other's spherical forms, we encountered the final stage. The long anticipated finale was just ahead; we could see it's glimmering pole. There were two directions the group could of went in. Our initial ally, the common dim wit charged into one direction, only to reveal that he had no escape, that his final steps were already set in stone.As for the rest of us, we left in the other direction. Expecting a challenging journey to and fro was no surprise to us, we lost an additional sphere, the opposite Blue. "At least there'll be no competition." The second blue golf ball claimed. We all chuckled at that, pushing onwards. Seven putts in. My time was limited. Another ally, one who beared a street cone upon his head, had resorted to madness, coldly using his remaing putts to lash out anyone who attempted to gain entry and the end of the course. We moved in sync in parellel with each other, confusing our former friend. Unfortunately, it had overtook him.His last few breathes were spent wishing a horrible spell were upon us. The game at the usual level is played on a course with an arranged progression of 18 holes, though recreational courses can be smaller, often having nine holes. Each hole on the course must contain a teeing ground to start from, and a putting green containing the actual hole or cup 4+1⁄4 inches (11 cm) in diameter. There are other standard forms of terrain in between, such as the fairway, rough (long grass), bunkers (or "sand traps"), and various hazards (water, rocks) but each hole on a course is unique in its specific layout and arrangement.Golf is played for the lowest number of strokes by an individual, known as stroke play, or the lowest score on the most individual holes in a complete round by an individual or team, known as match play. Stroke play is the most commonly seen format at all levels, but most especially at the elite level.The modern game of golf originated in 15th century Scotland. The 18-hole round was created at the Old Course at St Andrews in 1764. Golf's first major, and the world's oldest tournament in existence, is The Open Championship, also known as the British Open, which was first played in 1860 at the Prestwick Golf Club in Ayrshire, Scotland. _childDocuments_.review: This is the greatest game of all time."Golf with Your Friends" is often heralded by its players as a truly unique and immersive multiplayer gaming experience. Though the idea of golf might bring to mind precision, patience, and perhaps solitude, this game turns traditional notions of the sport on their head, transforming it into a fun, chaotic, and dynamic competition. It might seem bold to claim "Golf with Your Friends" as the greatest game of all time, yet the game’s innovative approach to casual gaming, its accessibility, and the ways it fosters memorable shared experiences make a compelling case for the title.1. Fun and AccessibilityOne of the key strengths of "Golf with Your Friends" is its simple, intuitive gameplay. The rules are straightforward, with players aiming to get their ball into the hole in the fewest strokes possible—just like in traditional golf. However, it removes the typical barriers that might intimidate a casual player. There’s no need for extensive knowledge of golf terminology or mechanics, no expensive in-game purchases required to be competitive, and the controls are accessible even for those who are not familiar with gaming. The game welcomes players of all skill levels, bridging the gap between experienced gamers and newcomers.The variety of creative courses and obstacles makes each session unique and engaging. With courses themed around candy, space, haunted houses, and even forests, the game ensures that there is something new and exciting around every corner. The obstacles, like spinning logs, bumpers, and portals, introduce an arcade-like unpredictability that injects a sense of lighthearted fun and challenge.2. Emphasis on Multiplayer Engagement"Golf with Your Friends" shines in multiplayer mode. The game allows up to 12 players to join, fostering a true party-game experience. Whether players are teaming up or competing, the multiplayer mode is what gives the game its name and its charm. Unlike many games that pit players against each other in intense and highly competitive settings, "Golf with Your Friends" emphasizes fun and laughter over competition. The matches create an atmosphere where players are less concerned about winning and more focused on enjoying each other's company and the experience itself.The game offers additional customization, letting players add wild modifiers like increased ball size, zero-gravity settings, or the infamous collision mode, which lets players bump their friends’ balls around. These customizable rules encourage creativity and spontaneity, turning each game into a distinct experience. This level of customization ensures that every round can feel fresh and different, tailored to the mood and preferences of the players.3. Community and Social BondingOne reason "Golf with Your Friends" has gained such a dedicated following is its ability to create and strengthen social bonds. With its lighthearted, humorous take on golf, the game provides a low-stakes, high-fun environment that is ideal for friendly competition or just catching up with friends. People can play casually while talking, catching up, or even discussing serious topics, all without the need for intense focus. The game has become a staple for remote social gatherings, especially for friends or family who might live in different parts of the world.Additionally, the game is available on multiple platforms, making it easy for people to connect with friends who may use different consoles. This cross-platform compatibility allows for a more inclusive gaming experience, where the technical details don’t get in the way of the fun.4. A Game That Embraces ImperfectionAnother notable aspect of "Golf with Your Friends" is that it fully embraces its absurd and occasionally chaotic nature. In many games, players feel an urge to “win,” focusing on honing their skills and mastering every possible mechanic. However, "Golf with Your Friends" stands out because of its willingness to throw randomness into the mix. It is not a game about mastering controls or memorizing levels; instead, it’s about laughing at the unexpected outcomes. The physics can be unpredictable, and a single obstacle can send the ball wildly off course. These imperfections make every round a new adventure and give players stories to tell long after the game is over.The game’s unique blend of humor and randomness keeps players coming back, and it’s in these imperfections that players find its charm. By encouraging a sense of humor about the occasional mishaps, it sets itself apart from other games that rely heavily on precision and realism.5. Fostering Positive Gaming Culture"Golf with Your Friends" promotes a healthier, more inclusive form of gaming culture. There is no “elite” mentality because skill level does not strongly influence the experience; beginners are often just as capable of achieving fantastic (or hilariously bad) results as seasoned players. This spirit of inclusion helps players feel comfortable, regardless of skill level. There’s a sense of community among players who enjoy the game not for mastery but for the laughs and the memories created along the way.The game's lighthearted nature encourages positive interactions among players, reducing toxicity and promoting mutual enjoyment. It’s a game that shows competition doesn’t always have to be about skill or scoring; sometimes, it’s about sharing a good time and relishing the shared experiences of triumph and failure alike.ConclusionIn the realm of multiplayer gaming, where titles like first-person shooters or battle royales often dominate, "Golf with Your Friends" stands out for its simplicity, creativity, and its ability to make every match a memorable experience. It’s a game that values community over competition and invites people of all backgrounds to join in and share a laugh. By transforming golf into a whimsical adventure, it brings players together, letting them set aside their worries for a while and just have fun."Golf with Your Friends" may not have the polished graphics or complex mechanics of more mainstream games, but its charm, accessibility, and ability to foster genuine enjoyment and connection among players make it a true contender for the title of “greatest game of all time.”

_childDocuments_.review: My friend made it so every time you lose due to time expiration, it gave you plus sixty points.  I ended the game with something around five hundred eighty points.  10/10, would get 580 points again.This is just one example of various I have available.  As for a serious review, my friends and I play this game when we need to get away from serious strategy games that require intellectual thought and planning as a way to "unwind" of sorts and be stupid, and the beauty about it is, after a relatively short amount of time, you're ready to play whatever game you were playing initially again.  For example, a group of friends and I were playing Men of War: Assault Squadron.  After getting steamrolled by the Germans for the third time in a row, we were basically fed up and needed time away from it.  It was looking like we were just going to call it a night and get off till a friend decided this would be a good idea, and bought me a copy while it was on sale.  What followed was about fifty minutes of utter ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and cancer.  It turned from a game about golfing with friends, to a breeding ground of divsion where the main goal was to sabotage the other player's efforts to win by sacrificing yourself and wasting your own time to knock them away.  After those fifty minutes, we were ready to go back to Men of War.  It should be noted, fifty minutes is a comparatively short time period, whereas otherwise we would have gotten off and the time would be measured in hours, rather than minutes.  If you're looking for a "filler" game to play in between gaming sessions where you and your friends can cool off and have fun (or lose your ♥♥♥♥ and ragequit), this is an excellent option.  Binge-play hours in a major title, take a thirty to sixty minute break in Golf With Your Friends, and you're easily ready to go back.  Or, simply play the game on your own, or, as the title suggests, with your friends.  The game is well off enough that it can stand independently and not as simple in-between filler.  The oftentimes challenging level design will encourage you to stay up, similar to a game of Civ, where you must get in that one, last turn to succeed.  It's well worth it, but prepare to lose your friends.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a tough one.Picking it up is easy and if you start with friends, it's fun at first.Especially the first cup "forest" is pretty awesome.But if you play longer, the short comings of the game often destroy the fun in the competition with friends.- The physics are bad and often weird things happen, like your ball is jumping in a crazy direction.- The objects don't have proper collision. Sometimes your ball is colliding with an invisible barrier. This happens often, especially in other modes than classic.- The levels are quite unforgiving that if you don't get lucky on the first shot, sometimes you end up in a place where you need 3 to 6 shots to just recover the position.- The game features many uncalculatable objects. Example, right at the start is an acceleration field and a ramp. Now it's unpredictable how fast you have to shoot because you can't know how fast the acceleration field is pushing your ball off the ramp.- There are quite some bugs. On one map your ball just jumps around if you switch the camera. On another, you get reset to the start although you're on the track.- Many of the additional game modes just add further RNG to the already luck dependent game.The good things are the easy way to play with friends, the customization of the games and the minimalistic menus that are straight to the point.So all in all I cannot recommend the game.If they would have made simpler courses with simpler architecture, the game would have probably benefited.Also it feels like this game has never ever been tested.

_childDocuments_.review: Basketball is a limited contact sport played on a rectangular court. While most often played as a team sport with five players on each side, three-on-three, two-on-two, and one-on-one competitions are also common. The objective is to shoot a ball through a hoop 18 inches (46 cm) in diameter and 10 feet (3.048 m) high that is mounted to a backboard at each end of the court. The game was invented in 1891 by Dr. James Naismith.A team can score a field goal by shooting the ball through the basket being defended by the opposition team during regular play. A field goal scores three points for the shooting team if the player shoots from behind the three-point line, and two points if shot from in front of the line. A team can also score via free throws, which are worth one point, after the other team is assessed with certain fouls. The team with the most points at the end of the game wins, but additional time (overtime) is mandated when the score is tied at the end of regulation. The ball can be advanced on the court by passing it to a teammate, or by bouncing it while walking or running (dribbling). It is a violation to lift, or drag, one's pivot foot without dribbling the ball, to carry it, or to hold the ball with both hands then resume dribbling.The game has many individual techniques for displaying skill—ball-handling, shooting, passing, dribbling, dunking, shot-blocking, and rebounding. Basketball teams generally have player positions, the tallest and strongest members of a team are called a center or power forward, while slightly shorter and more agile players are called small forward, and the shortest players or those who possess the best ball handling skills are called a point guard or shooting guard. The point guard directs the on court action of the team, implementing the coach's game plan, and managing the execution of offensive and defensive plays (player positioning).Basketball is one of the world's most popular and widely viewed sports. The National Basketball Association (NBA) is the most popular and widely considered to be the highest level of professional basketball in the world and NBA players are the world's best paid athletes by average annual salary per player. Outside North America, the top clubs from national leagues qualify to continental championships such as the Euroleague and FIBA Americas League. The FIBA Basketball World Cup and Men's Olympic Basketball Tournament are the major international events of the sport and attract top national teams from around the world. Each continent hosts regional competitions for national teams, like EuroBasket and FIBA AmeriCup.The FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup and Women's Olympic Basketball Tournament feature top national teams from continental championships. The main North American league is the WNBA (NCAA Women's Division I Basketball Championship is also popular), whereas strongest European clubs participate in the EuroLeague Women.

_childDocuments_.review: The accuracy in calling Golf With Your Friends a 'game' is open to debate. There exist interactive controls, coming in the form of hitting your ball. The game measures your progress toward the end of the hole, saving your position should you find yourself going astray from the course (most of the time), and has an end goal, that being the elusive hole at the end that progresses you to a greater challenge; the next hole.These are traits that games have possessed since their inception, and Golf With Your Friends seems to follow this trend. There is no evidence to contradict the fact that Golf With Your Friends is a game.So why can't I shake the feeling that Golf With Your Friends is more than just a game? Why do I feel that Golf With Your Friends is a journey to be ventured, rather than just a game to be "played".It may be thanks to the stretches Golf With Your Friends takes to its mundane source material to make it a mini-golf experience you could only find through the medium of a video game. It's courses that take you through outer space, underwater, on a pirate voyage, or through a grotesquely sweet world of candy. It's absurd customization options that can make your ball jump on command, use power ups, or even make your presumably round ball into a cone, cube, hockey puck, egg, or even an "isosphere". It's course obstacles ranging from as simple as a rotating windmill to as complex and problematic as a black hole, if you could believe it.Although all of this is captivating enough by itself, with endless hours of replay value at its disposal as you try more and more to lower your scores on each course, there still seems to be something I'm missing from the equation that transcends "game" territory.If we want to find the answer as to how Golf With Your Friends is more than a game, we don't have to look too far than the game's title.The goal, intentional or not, is not to "beat" Golf With Your Friends. The Golf is merely a surface level medium to attract the primary demographic of this game; Friends. Any other video game about golfing would have you simply play golf without any ulterior motives. Because Golf With Your Friends keeps reminding you through its title and multiplayer functionality that this is not to be experienced alone. You can either start your journey playing with random strangers or through copies you may have bought for your closest friends, or copies they bought for you.My friends and I have played this game for about a week now, and to me, the fun has only begun. Our experience started out mundane, on the Forest course, no special settings, no crazy game altering mechanics, only mini-golf; or so we thought.Things quickly took a change for the weirder. We found ourselves messing around with more difficult courses, alternate game modes such as "hockey mode", or turning our golf balls into golf "isospheres". We found ourselves discovering flaws in the programming and physics engine through glitches, or seeing which odd ways we could complete a hole with obviously easier solutions.And I can say, without any doubt, that it was a blast.Our new discoveries, mostly accidental, stirred many conversations and made me laugh harder than I have in a long time. The courses we stumbled through, their dysfunctional, almost bull-♥♥♥♥♥♥ mechanics seemingly treating some more fairly than others being a running joke during our sessions were experiences I wouldn't trade for the world. It truly made me feel that Golf With Your Friends put these experiences in the forefront, and not the broken mini-golfing. It has brought us together in a way that not many other games have. We have had so much fun in this week, and yet there is still so much to do, the possibilities are endless. So in conclusion, when you buy Golf With Your Friends, the price tag is misleading. Buy 2 copies, one for you, and one for a friend, maybe a close one, or one you'd like to get back in touch with. The ultimate goal of the journey in Golf With Your Friends is not to "golf", but to appreciate the bonds you share when you golf with your friends.

_childDocuments_.review: Visually, "Golf With Your Friends" charms with its vibrant and whimsical design. The courses are a kaleidoscope of creativity, featuring fantastical themes such as candy lands, space stations, and ancient ruins. The attention to detail in the course design and the playful aesthetics contribute to the game's overall appeal, creating an inviting and enjoyable atmosphere.The gameplay mechanics of "Golf With Your Friends" strike a perfect balance between accessibility and skill. The controls are simple and intuitive, allowing players of all ages and skill levels to jump into the action effortlessly. The physics system, while offering a realistic feel, also incorporates a touch of whimsy, resulting in unpredictable ball behavior that adds an element of surprise to every stroke.The true strength of the game lies in its multiplayer focus. Supporting up to 12 players, the multiplayer experience is a chaotic symphony of simultaneous golfing endeavors. Whether you're competing for the lowest score, racing against the clock, or embracing the party-like atmosphere, "Golf With Your Friends" offers a variety of game modes that keep the experience fresh and engaging.The extensive customization options add an extra layer of fun. Players can modify their balls, trails, and even don quirky hats, injecting a sense of personality into the gameplay. The inclusion of power-ups and obstacles on certain courses further contributes to the game's unpredictable and entertaining nature."Golf With Your Friends" truly shines when played in the company of others. The built-in voice chat feature enhances the social aspect of the game, fostering camaraderie, friendly banter, and occasional rivalries. The game's ability to create moments of shared laughter and surprise makes it a fantastic choice for casual gaming sessions with friends or family.While "Golf With Your Friends" excels in delivering a casual and enjoyable multiplayer experience, some players might find that the lack of a robust single-player campaign or progression system limits its long-term appeal for solo play.In conclusion, "Golf With Your Friends" is a hole-in-one when it comes to delivering accessible, entertaining, and downright fun multiplayer experiences. Its charming visuals, easy-to-grasp mechanics, and focus on social interaction make it an ideal choice for gatherings or online sessions with friends. Whether you're a golf enthusiast or just looking for a good time, "Golf With Your Friends" delivers an engaging and whimsical take on the classic sport, making it a standout title in the realm of multiplayer mini-golf adventures.

_childDocuments_.review: The Bitter Par: How *Golf With Your Friends* Turned My Escape Into A NightmareI had always enjoyed playing games with friends, especially those that promised a lighthearted, casual experience. *Golf With Your Friends* seemed like the perfect choice. It was quirky, fun, and just the kind of game that would allow me to relax and laugh with my closest companions. I imagined spending hours in a virtual world, hitting colorful golf balls through wacky courses, laughing together, and escaping from the pressures of life. At the time, I didn’t know how wrong I was. Little did I realize that this seemingly innocent game would eventually deepen the anxiety and depression I’d been battling for years. And worse yet, it would come not just from strangers, but from my friends—people I trusted.When I first suggested *Golf With Your Friends* to my group, everyone seemed eager to dive in. The mechanics were simple, the humor light, and the idea of playing together in a relaxed setting seemed like exactly what we needed. We started playing in a private server, just the four of us. The first few rounds were fun—we joked around, made silly shots, and shared in the chaos of the wacky courses. I found myself laughing for the first time in what felt like weeks. It was a brief, fleeting moment of relief from the depression that had clung to me for months. For a while, the game was everything I’d hoped it would be.But soon, things began to take a turn. It started with little jabs—nothing overt, just small remarks when I missed a shot or took longer to finish a hole than the others. At first, I brushed them off. It was all in good fun, right? We were friends, after all. But as we played more, the comments became more frequent, and they began to sting. “Wow, you really suck at this game,” one of my friends said with a chuckle as I missed yet another shot. “It’s just a hole-in-one, how hard can it be?” Another friend teased, making exaggerated gestures of disappointment every time I failed.I told myself it was harmless—just friendly banter. But inside, I could feel the familiar feelings of shame creeping in. I had always struggled with self-esteem issues, and the constant mocking triggered something deep within me. I started to dread playing. Every time it was my turn, my heart would race, my palms would sweat. What if I messed up? What if they made fun of me again? The playful jabs were no longer funny—they were cutting, and I couldn’t shake the feeling that they were intentionally trying to make me feel inferior.It didn’t stop at the comments. My friends began actively sabotaging my attempts at the game. They would make sarcastic remarks when I lined up my shots, mocking me for taking too long or choosing the wrong angle. One friend, in particular, started messing with the in-game mechanics, intentionally hitting balls in my path or distracting me when it was my turn. The course, which had once been a source of laughter, now felt like a battleground—one where I was constantly fighting not just the game, but my own friends.The worst moment came during a match where I was already feeling particularly low. I had been having a difficult week, the weight of depression heavier than usual. I was struggling to concentrate, my mind clouded with negative thoughts. As I lined up for a crucial shot, one of my friends made an offhand comment about how I was “probably going to mess it up again” before I even took my swing. The words stung like a slap in the face, and despite my best efforts to keep it together, I missed the shot by a wide margin.The others erupted in laughter, but this time it wasn’t playful. It wasn’t the carefree laughter that we used to share. It was harsh, mocking, like they were enjoying my failure. “Wow, you’re really terrible at this,” one friend said, her voice dripping with sarcasm. “Maybe you should just give up and let us finish the game for you.” I froze. In that moment, I felt like I was sinking, the weight of their words pressing down on me. The laughter felt like an accusation, like I was somehow less than them. I could feel the tears welling up in my eyes, but I refused to let them see.I didn’t say anything. I didn’t want to cause drama, didn’t want to be the buzzkill. So I kept playing, silently, trying to force myself through it. But the laughter continued, and so did the teasing. With each round, the mockery grew, and I found myself shrinking more and more. It wasn’t just about missing shots anymore; it was about how my friends were treating me. The game, which had once been a fun escape, had become an arena of ridicule, where every failure felt like a confirmation of my worthlessness.As the days went on, I started avoiding the game. I’d come up with excuses not to play, telling them I was busy or tired, but the truth was, I couldn’t bear the thought of facing them again. Every time I saw a message or an invite, my stomach would twist in knots. I dreaded the idea of being ridiculed again, but I also hated the fact that I felt like I had no choice but to play. These were my friends, after all. What if I lost them if I refused? What if they thought I was being “sensitive” or “too serious”?But the longer I stayed away, the more I withdrew. The anxiety and depression grew, fed by the shame and the sense of isolation that *Golf With Your Friends* had left me with. I began to feel like a failure not just in the game, but in life. If I couldn’t handle a simple, silly game, how could I ever succeed at anything else? The feelings of inadequacy, of never measuring up, became overwhelming. I couldn’t shake the voices in my head—voices that told me I was a burden, a disappointment, and that I didn’t deserve to be part of anything good, whether it was a game or a friendship.The PTSD hit me in small waves. Every time I heard someone talk about *Golf With Your Friends* or saw the game in my library, I would freeze. My mind would immediately go back to that moment—the mocking, the laughter, the sting of betrayal from the people I thought I could trust. I couldn’t escape the feeling of being small, insignificant, and unwanted. I started avoiding my friends, feeling like I couldn’t be around them without being reminded of how they had treated me. The depression deepened. I became more withdrawn, more isolated, and the game, once a form of escape, had turned into a trigger for my deepest insecurities.Eventually, I stopped playing entirely. I couldn’t do it anymore. The game that had once been an opportunity to bond with my friends had shattered into something painful and toxic. But the emotional scars lingered. I lost my sense of self-worth, and I lost my ability to trust the people I had once considered close. Even now, I find it hard to play games with others, afraid that the same thing will happen again—that I will be ridiculed, belittled, and abandoned.Looking back, I realize that it wasn’t just the game that hurt me—it was how my friends’ behavior reflected the way I already saw myself. Their cruelty amplified the negative thoughts that I had always struggled with. And in that moment, I couldn’t tell where the game ended and my depression began. It wasn’t just about losing a match; it was about feeling like I was losing myself. And the worst part was, it came from the people who were supposed to have my back.*Golf With Your Friends* wasn’t just a game—it was a mirror. And what it showed me, was something I wasn’t ready to face.

_childDocuments_.review: A stroke is a medical condition in which poor blood flow to the brain causes cell death. There are two main types of stroke: ischemic, due to lack of blood flow, and hemorrhagic, due to bleeding. Both cause parts of the brain to stop functioning properly. Signs and symptoms of a stroke may include an inability to move or feel on one side of the body, problems understanding or speaking, dizziness, or loss of vision to one side. Signs and symptoms often appear soon after the stroke has occurred. If symptoms last less than one or two hours, the stroke is a transient ischemic attack (TIA), also called a mini-stroke. A hemorrhagic stroke may also be associated with a severe headache. The symptoms of a stroke can be permanent. Long-term complications may include pneumonia and loss of bladder control.The main risk factor for stroke is high blood pressure. Other risk factors include high blood cholesterol, tobacco smoking, obesity, diabetes mellitus, a previous TIA, end-stage kidney disease, and atrial fibrillation. An ischemic stroke is typically caused by blockage of a blood vessel, though there are also less common causes. A hemorrhagic stroke is caused by either bleeding directly into the brain or into the space between the brain's membranes. Bleeding may occur due to a ruptured brain aneurysm. Diagnosis is typically based on a physical exam and supported by medical imaging such as a CT scan or MRI scan. A CT scan can rule out bleeding, but may not necessarily rule out ischemia, which early on typically does not show up on a CT scan. Other tests such as an electrocardiogram (ECG) and blood tests are done to determine risk factors and rule out other possible causes. Low blood sugar may cause similar symptoms.Prevention includes decreasing risk factors, surgery to open up the arteries to the brain in those with problematic carotid narrowing, and warfarin in people with atrial fibrillation. Aspirin or statins may be recommended by physicians for prevention. A stroke or TIA often requires emergency care. An ischemic stroke, if detected within three to four and half hours, may be treatable with a medication that can break down the clot. Some hemorrhagic strokes benefit from surgery. Treatment to attempt recovery of lost function is called stroke rehabilitation, and ideally takes place in a stroke unit; however, these are not available in much of the world.In 2013, approximately 6.9 million people had an ischemic stroke and 3.4 million people had a hemorrhagic stroke. In 2015, there were about 42.4 million people who had previously had a stroke and were still alive. Between 1990 and 2010 the number of strokes which occurred each year decreased by approximately 10% in the developed world and increased by 10% in the developing world. In 2015, stroke was the second most frequent cause of death after coronary artery disease, accounting for 6.3 million deaths (11% of the total). About 3.0 million deaths resulted from ischemic stroke while 3.3 million deaths resulted from hemorrhagic stroke. About half of people who have had a stroke live less than one year. Overall, two thirds of strokes occurred in those over 65 years old.

_childDocuments_.review: It’s a great title to enjoy playing with family, friends, and co-workers. This is a great pick-me-up game to jump right in and play some golf and to see who the best golfer among peers is. The game is relaxing, fun, and even challenging at times with the maps at hand. This isn't your standard put-put golf at your local family fun center; this is golf on a whole new level. With crazy twists and turns it'll make your head spin with enjoyment and contemplate your golf skills.The game is so crazy fun that I'll bring some beers and shots with me and have a drunken golf session with good friends. Let me tell you... it becomes crazy fun playing drunken golf. Now, there is a map editor too, which means you can make your own maps and share it within the community. So, not only do you have the maps that Blacklight Interactive made for this fine community, but the community also made some crazy maps for us to enjoy. So, if one thought it would get stale playing the same maps over; try downloading some maps and enjoy endless amount of content.You also have custom content such as hats on the golf ball, the colors or animations of trails when the golf ball moves, floaties for when the golf ball meets the water, and the entire color grid for changing the color of your golf ball. You can change the custom settings for match of golf too. How much gravity do you want for the golf balls? Do you want another shape instead of a ball? How about power ups? How about jumping balls? Spinning balls? You get it. There are many options and modes for how the balls and maps operate. Easy graphics to run on today's PCs and not so demanding that it can be played on older PCs. The colors are vibrant, easy on the eyes and fun and dazzling to see for many hours. The noises are crisp, fun, and easy on the ears. There are options to host your own server and there’s even a single player option in case you want to tone up your skills before your friends log on. I recommend this game not only to play with your friends, but to beat your friends at it too. Enjoy, drink and golf responsibility and golf on! I recommend the game at its current pricing.

It is another one of those games that does not take itself seriously and does not expect you to either. It is a simple game revolving around blasting your golf ball towards the hole. There are like 2 controls, 3 if your friends are sweaties and play with jumping. The game is graphically simple, yet the cooked-in maps are visually interesting enough, especially the later ones. The game has memorable/memeable music with plenty of funny sound effects. The golf balls behave like you would expect. The game is very, very straight forward. The fun of the game really comes from turning on collision and colluding against your friends. GwyF is really just golf if you have no friends to play with and the game really cannot carry itself without you and your friends making your own fun from what the game offers. Don't think about it too much, don't be too sober when you play, and I guarantee that this will be a fun experience.
