_childDocuments_.review: Opinion is subject to change during development.I expect to get more play time with Badass Hero, but I feel confident recommending it in its current Early Access state after 4 hours.Badass Hero is a hard game, expect to die and restart plenty of times, but it does become easier little-by-little thanks to a permanent character progression system often found in other similar modern roguelikes.My first dozen runs of Badass Hero were about getting acquainted with the controls, enemy types, and character progression system, all the while "oohing and aahing" at the wonderful comic book graphic style. Once I was comfortable controlling my badass, it opened up advanced platforming techniques like air dashing while wall-bouncing grenades and shooting at baddies.After choosing a comic book (thematic set of levels) to play, each run had me discovering and equipping various weapons and armor pieces, found with both numerical random stats and special effects: rocket launchers that could freeze enemies, machine guns that could make enemies explode on death, and armor that made me invulnerable while air dashing, just to name a few. This item system aided in making each run feel fresh and surprising.There are moments where the random level generation went against me, creating what felt like unfair, near-impossible to beat rooms, but with the right items, health pool, and skill, I felt there was still a sliver of chance. But the game is made to play over and over again.Does the thought of finding a shotgun with piercing bullets and chance to ignite enemies excite you? Go on then, be a Badass Hero.

_childDocuments_.review: I am 32 years old.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: There is so much about this game that I like: the comic book style graphics, the sound, the music, the effects.But it is the game format that I dislike - the rougelike with grindy meta progression.Fury Unleashed is a game based on fast moving, bullet spraying, combo building gameplay.But this is a rougelike in which you have one life and then have to start over. You can't be as aggressive as you would like and play the way the game wants you too. The other problem with this game is the difficulty. It is way way too easy. I've beaten every boss I have found first try and the levels you can finish while barely getting hit. But then the second section hits and you feel a big wall. Your weapons are way underpowered and you need to grind lots and lots of meta progression. You don't feel like you need to get better at the bosses or practice, you just need better weapons and meta progress and the game is easy again. You can start at section 2 but you really need to play the boring first section to gain some power and weapons, it's annoying. The bosses themselves are very underwhelming. Most bosses you need to only move slightly to dodge all attacks or just run around them in a circle. I kept expecting there to be more phases of the boss in which it gets hard, but nope another flawless victory that feels empty.In conclusion, this game would be perfect if it was in the style of lets say My Friend Pedro but the rougelike style makes me bored and not wanting to play anymore, which is a shame as the developers did a great job and obviously put in a lot of time and effort. I'd give it a 6/10, buy on sale, play for a few hours and then get bored and move on.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played a lot of bullet hell and rogue-likes so this looked really good.  The controls are mostly nice and smooth aside from a little difficulty with the mouse now and then, or hitting the middle mouse to use melee and having it not do anything (haven't solved that one yet) probably a lot better with a controller but I haven't tested that.  The leveling system is well though out.  Most of the skills are pretty standard:  health, armor, crit chance, crit damage, etc...  It has a lot of fun moments but loses a ton of points with its drawbacks.  Examples of this include:  Too many animations, gibs, what have you on the screen sometimes to even see the projectiles so you'll take damage and not even know what hit you.  The randomization can be not so good.  Too many times of getting the "5 combo to enter" portal of the "10 combo without it breaking" box in the last or second to last room with less than 5 enemies left.  Don't make the mistake of triggering the box with an existing combo if it's near ending because that will count as breaking it.  A lot of rooms that are either just halls or start out as a narrow kill-box with enemies that will start shooting before you can reach anywhere with room to dodge.  Going back to the last room doesn't work.  The projectiles will often magically "pause" until you step back in the room so they're point blank when you come back.   But don't worry, all the ink and gold orbs that had dropped before you left instantly erase.  Some of these issues can be mitigated with skills but that's more of a crutch for a bad design.  Your run can be ridiculously easy or insanely hard based purely on luck of the draw.  Good weapons/items, room spawns, and enemy placements are completely out of your hands and with the rng often  being complete crap it takes a potentially fun game and makes it feel as frustrating as a bad slot machine at a casino.  I'm more into skill based games than gambling so it just feels stupid to keep playing this.

_childDocuments_.review: In short, the gameplay is really great, but the current version has only one world out of three fully finished (took me ~3.5 hours to complete twice), so for that price I'd probably wait at least until the second world is fully introduced.Badass Hero is a roguelite platformer where the action hero under your control goes through the comic book universe. The game is well styled: each level is shaped like comics which you traverse, „picture by picture”. There’s a lot of action going on and the game rewards you being fast: as you kill enemies, your combo meter goes up. The death is inevitable, but as you die, you get a chance to improve your character, making further walkthroughs much easier. During each playthrough, you have a chance to find armor / weapons. You lose them when you die, but they greatly affect how far can you go.-	Action packed gameplay-	Plenty of items like armor / potions-	Very-well polished/juiced: even basic weapons feel awesome to shoot, lots of effects on hits, gore, explosions-	Responsive character controls, which is very important for the genre-	World is generated randomly, but there are good room variety so the room layouts do not feel boring-	Not much weapon variety so far (yes, stats are generated randomly (I think), but shooting patterns do not differ much: gun, smg, shotgun, bazooka, grenades)-	Only 3 worlds planned, with 2 first ones available (they have plenty of enemies, but backgrounds get repetitive pretty quickly)One of the biggest achievements of the game, in my opinion, is the way that authors dealt with random element. In roguelites, you often feel cheated when the random is against you. Since initial weapon is not bad and killing enemies is pretty much skill based, there’s no feeling that you are getting dealt a bad hand, which is really commendable.I think that’s a great game for anyone who’s into Roguelite Platformers. Definitely grab it if you liked Rogue Legacy.

_childDocuments_.review: 09.05.2020 — Finally Fury Unleashed reached release state (renamed from Badass Hero)Developers asked me to give it another chance (fourth? fifth? i lost count long ago), so let's see what have changed and how game growed over course of five years. This time i'll write in english so everyone can better understand, cheers!So, first impression is what you get from first hour of playing. This is where customer decides to keep it or simply return money. I have erased game saves to make it fair. After playing for 10 minutes, electricity in da house sudenly went down for a minute (this is very rare occasion, but still). Surprisingly, there is no autosave feature, so everyting i farmed and reached just dissapeared. Bad omen...Grapchics are great, weapon varietty expanded incredibly, there are lot's of different creatures with rarities and types. I like that, trully. This is exactly the quality you expect from a game in 2020. But as a gamer, i play all the time and want to see mostly gameplay features, not some shiny stuff. Does Fury capable providing it? As a hardcore player who beated majority of hard games ever created, i expected Fury to provide challange, but there was none. You can only reduce difficulty and it will increase after winning whole game (which makes no sence).So, there are three game types overall: rogueliKes where it's hard and you lose everything on death, rogueliTe where you upgrade something between runs and simple arcades. Sadly, Fury has no rogue mechanics. While you do gain skillpoints for upgrades tree, it mostly grants basic stuff (extra hp, shields and +score). You can absolutely win without it. The most benefical are crit chance mechanic and grenades drop.Looking behind i can see lots of games released in 2015-2020, like Dead Cells, Salt and Sanctuary, Hollow Knight, Sundered and list can go on and on, and on. All of them having depth, upgrade system, unique style and are indies as well. What can Fury Unleached offer to rival them? Nothing! This is mostly because we got a game in 2020 which was created in 2015 and copied some 2005 games. Back then, trully, was era of simple arcade platformers. PC was spammed with projects like Gun Girls 2 and Captain Claw. But time changes and player demand changes. Fury simply ignores everything that happened to genre over last decade.So, the core gameplay loop is mindless killing of enemies with guns, melee weapons, grenades and stomping. You will see everything it has to offer in 2-3 runs (30-60 minutes) and there is nothing to keep you interested. This is the biggest sin of gaming — lack of immersion. No story, no character development, no quests. For some reasons devs injected backstory about development INSIDE game. So you will find sketches and twits during runs, describing how it was created. Just imagine: you shoot and kill, blood and monsters everywhere, combo meter has to keep going, but suddenly there is black'n'white monitor about dev talking to someone while drinking cofee. What is this???What was a point of creating bosses and mini-bosses with a single attack? Is this a joke? They are using predictable movement manner and slow attack animation.So, what do i get for clearing whole zone (100%)? No idea. Why do i get weapons in chests weaker than my current one? No idea. What is a point of armor if it breaks in a few hits? It feels like developers zoned out during balancing stage. Some weapons also feel inccredibly weak and may even ruin your run.Alright, there are some errors in translation, like "Boss throws # V1 more balls" etc. So it is not about lack of proper translator, but about quality of release. Such issues were there in past as well and i posted about them. Why are they still present?As you probably checked already Fury has 90% positive score, so my vote will change nothing. But it will remain negative. Not becuase i hate game itself or developers, but just because there are so many other much better projects. Besides, they chose very bad time for release, since we have too many giants coming right away (or already out). Like Terraria Journey, Lobotomy Corporation 2, Gears Tactics, Dread Nautical, Help Will Come Tomorrow, Before We Live etc. Right now there is simply no time window for little arcade like Fury Unleashed with it's mediocre gameplay....Sorry, but it is very hard to please me. I do like arcades tho and will definitely play Fury some more with pleasure, it is mostly worth the price and overall fine project. But that gonna probably happen in a half year and scedule is really thick. The problem is, in a half year there gonna be way too many GIANTS of GIANTS, like Binding of Isaac Repeatence, Spelunky 2, Rogue Legacy 2, Hollow Knight Silk Song. You have to dish out something really outstanding in order to interest gamer in 2020 with basic platformer. Cheers!

_childDocuments_.review: Now before I get into the negatives of this game, I do like to point out that I had a good time with it. Y'know, it has good gameplay, amazing art style, and not only is the music really good but, it also changes depending on how high your combo is. Which I think is pretty neat. Now, even though this game has its pros, it also has its cons. Like for starters, it has some performance issues. I don't know if it's just me but, my PC be FUMING when it's running this game. And mind you, my PC is very strong. Like, it has 16GB of RAM, a 6GB graphics card, all of that. But it be having hard time running this. And that's crazy considering that this game only requires 1GB to download and all of these graphics are hand-drawn. So what the heck?I think the reason why this game requires a lot of power to run is because there are a lot of objects in each level. Yeah, these levels may load up very fast but, when you have so many objects for your PC to run, it can make it sound like a jet engine. What they should've done is like split the levels. Like, you're in one section of the level but when you enter the next section, that one section you were in is gone. So your system won't have to run it in the background. Take Batman: Arkham Asylum for example. When you open a door, the game commands you to walk into the next room. And once you do, the other room you were just in is gone. So your system won't have to run it in the background. But in this game, they just plop down a huge level for you and say, "have fun". So yeah, that is a problem. I do like how these levels represent 2 pages from a comic book but, you gotta optimize your game, man. Gotta optimize it.P.S. You can turn off blood & gore in this game but at the same time, the devs would mock you saying, "If there are young children around, turn this off." You could say that is for young children but, shouldn't they know that not all adults want to see that nasty bull-bull? Well, either way, you can turn off blood & gore in this. Just thought I point that out.P.P.S There's a comic book with an issue #69 on it's cover. Shameful.

_childDocuments_.review: Of all the roguelites, metroidvanias, and side-scrolling games I own, this is hands down the worst quality of the genre. It has all the traits of the top games, even done up in Comix Zone classic style. So one would THINK it would be awesome, because that certainly checked all my happy boxes. Then it happened; I played the game as much as I could, before I realized it was a cheap, frustrating mess of a game. The talent tree is so difficult to ramp up, you'll spend most of your time dying from cheap enemy fire with very little upgrades to show for it. Even when it's all said and done, there's little replay value, a thrown together story with unimportant characters, and the main protagonist has no identity. TL;DR - There are SOOOOOOOO MANY (emphasis on that) games that do everything Fury Unleashed does, just 10x better; go buy the Rogue Legacy series, Metal Unit for guns, Hades because it's Hades, so many other games out there, shining out this steaming turd. Avoid it, unless you like that cheap Android feeling on your steam account.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start by saying I can't stand rouge-like or very hard games. To old to deal with it. I did try Spelunky when it came out and stopped playing. Gave up. Well I happen to see Fury Unleashed on Steam and it started the video of it automatically. I thought it looked great from its style to its gameplay.And seeing you can level up, even after you die, I was impressed. But of course I wasn't sure still. Then I got a chance to play it and I was blown away! But it NOT on sale. Something I never do really. Obviously on the harder modes it is difficult, but you get used to what to do after awhile and can move through the levels with ease. I recommend a keyboard/Mouse personaly.You may be saying "Leveling up? Kind of ruins the rouge genre!". Well in the very hard modes being leveled up is taken away. You earn points to unlock 1-2 skills as you go on. If you die, it's over. Your skills reset. So with that its very much rouge like (soft rouge like as they say). But on the first two difficulties your leveled up skills continue over to each run through.Content-wise there are three comic books to go through. They may seem small but its random every time. And depending on how hard the mode is, it can be bonkers to beat. Especially since each comic has its own enemies and methods you have to get used too. For example when I got to the second comic, I had to learn all new strategies to deal with the levels.There are alot of mini-bosses and end level bosses. And the levels they are in seem to be random. Some are bullet hell like, others are just a matter of figuring out a good attack.There are a ton of weapons and characters to unlock. You can even download user made heads in the Workshop.And from what I have seen there will be online in the future with maybe more added content. For $20 you can't beat the price. It's a great game and you can see the worked hard on it. You won't be let down!

_childDocuments_.review: So freaking good. Seriously, if you like run n gun games of any sort, Contra, Megaman X, 20/30XX, other inferior versions of run n gun, get this game. It is a little bit short, but the replayability is high enough that doesn't matter much. A run takes anywhere from 25min to an hour and a half (if you are playing on hard mode with no upgrades like I tried one run, oof!), averaging about an hour for me. There is enough in the tech tree to make different "builds", there are many little quests to unlock weapons, get extra ink (currency and exp), that kind of stuff like a good rogue-lite should have. And the story, despite being tiny (it is basically like 14 total still-frames with story on them and some pieces here and there from characters) is actually phenomenal. It is clear this is a work of passion, from the art to the weapons, but the story really brings home what the developers put into this game. I don't want to spoil even the first part of it, but suffice it to say I was incredibly pleasantly surprised. To the point I've been telling my friends and family about the story!

_childDocuments_.review: Fury Unleashed is a mobile app that's been dumped on Steam as if it was a real PC game (it's not)... it's a cash grab from greedy mobile devs.  The game is a simple console-like platformer/twin stick shooter hybrid with cartoony artwork and a comic book theme.  Blast your way through enemies and platformer traps using dash abilities and grenades as well as normal twin stick style shooting, adapted from the mobile phone screen controls the mobile app was designed to use.From a technical perspective, the game doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.The game features simple, cartoony 2D graphics, of the type you normally expect to see in low effort mobile apps.  While some work went into them, this still looks bad compared to any contemporary game designed for PC.  3D graphics programming does require a degree of skill and competence and unfortunately not all developers have the budget or talent to deliver this, despite 3D graphics cards hitting the mainstream in the 1990's.  Considering this is being evaluated as a PC game, having the graphics phoned in like this isn't going to result in a high quality, visually impressive game that PC gamers are used to seeing.Because this is a mobile app, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the iPhones that the game was designed for.  These are unfortunate handicaps and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was an afterthought for the iPhone developers who are to blame for this.  The game is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for mobile phones forces upon a game.  Once more, mobile devs have made gaming worse for everyone.  I didn't spend thousands on building a gaming rig just so I could pretend it's an iPhone.Once more we see greedy mobile devs trying to scam PC gamers. On Steam, this is an eye watering $20 USD, on app stores, it's only $5. Mobile devs must learn PC gamers are not here to be gouged, and can't be expected to pay a FOUR TIMES AS MUCH for a cheap mobile game just because it's been lazily dumped on Steam.  This is unacceptable disrespect for PC gamers.  Because this is a mobile app, is priced to insult and gouge PC gamers, and because of the other defects, it's impossible to recommend.  Just who do they think we are?The developer has weighed in to inform everyone they didn't read the  for Steam "partners", or they deliberately ignored the part where Valve says:The developer makes the absurd and immediately disproven claim that my review is factually incorrect, in a bizarre, pointless, and self incriminating response.The developer both acknowledges that this is a mobile app (and even provides the launch date, confirming without any doubt this is a mobile app), but seems angry about me pointing that out already.  See, it doesn't matter what order the developer launched this mobile app on which platform, the fact is that it's a mobile app, has all the qualities of a mobile app, was designed for the lowest common denominator of gaming platforms, and thus compares poorly to games designed for PC.  This is useful for gamers to know, which is why I include this important information in my reviews whenever I catch a mobile phone app developer dumping mobile trash on Steam.  But we must ask why this mobile app developer is so angry about being confronted with facts they themselves confirm.  Guilty conscience perhaps?The developer also confesses they don't have adequate staff and budget to produce video games of acceptable quality for PC.  This  the poor quality of this mobile app, but .My review stands unaltered and now that the developer admitted they're trying to scam PC gamers FOUR TIMES AS MUCH for a mobile app dumped on PC, gamers should have a pretty easy time deciding whether or not to buy games from developers who behave so unethically.  And they have the gall to question my morality.  I guess it's easier as a failed mobile app developer to attack gamers than face the facts. I'd like to thank the mobile developer for confirming they dumped a mobile app on Steam and providing the date they did so.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun little game, that can be played solo or with a friend which makes it even more fun.Not an easy game by any means though, but very rewarding if you're fast and good at dodging. You can play on easy difficulty, and even then it's not that easy, there are modifiers you can adjust to make the game even easier, which is always a nice touch, having the ability to make it as difficult or easy as you like. Having a partner also helps, but might also get in the way of you and make you lose track of yourself, also additional projectiles and more clutter on the screen.  Leveling up is a bit of a grind, and the game isn't that big or long, the enemies, mini bosses and regular bosses make up for it's length, they are all very different both visually and gameplay wise. Different comic books are also very distinct. The game it self is pretty damn fun, lot's of jumping, dashing, shooting, stomping and killing enemies with melee weapons. Dying does not feel that bad. After killing 3 different bosses in a comic book, you can start from the second comic book, which helps with the repetitiveness.   All in all, a fun little game with co-op and ability to choose how difficult it gets. A beautiful, fast-paced roguelike, that might be worth trying especially on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: You know, I am not fond of rogue-lite games anymore. At the moment, I believe the market is overrun with rogue-lites that are very similar in terms of their gameplay. Very few games try to add something different to their gameplay formula, and I do not have an exact reason for that.That was why I was pleasantly surprised by Fury Unleashed. On the surface, it's just another rogue-lite that tries to mix various genres together. But it also introduces a gameplay mechanic that makes it very different from others, in exchange for it not appealing to everyone.Fury Unleashed is about a comic artist who has lost their creativity and contemplates about what to do with the creations they hold dear. You appear in-game as the action hero of that artist's comics, named Fury, and have to find a way to prove yourself and rekindle their flames in order to be able to avoid being forgotten.And such story has directly affected the visual presentation of the game, although not as detailed as examples like Comix Zone. Each stage is presented to you in forms of different issues of Fury Unleashed comic series, containing three chapters and a final boss fight. Each of the chapters/levels are presented as pages of a comic book, with each randomized tile inside them presented as frames with torn sides to indicate where you can exit them and go to the next one. I do believe the devs could have done more with the presentation, but we have is enough for the game.In terms of gameplay, the game feels really fun to play and I dare say it becomes addicting. The movement options are incredibly well-done and Fury feels good to control as a result. The game retains the classic control method of twin stick shooters, using the left analog stick/WASD to move and right analog stick/mouse for manual aiming, then places the other buttons in locations that create the least amount of hassle for the players who decide to use the default keybindings. The dash button can also be held down, which makes Fury run faster on the ground and auto-climb small ledges in front of them to allow for fast movement.Then we have the stomp attack. This attack is initiated by pressing down while in the air, causing fury to slam to the ground and crush whatever that is underneath them. Since this attack is able to kill every enemy in one hit with the exception of powered up ones and bosses, it become a really fun and also risky method to dispatch enemies; as you now have the option of damaging the enemies from afar to play it safe, or get in close and personal when you get the chance to finish them off in one hit. This becomes very fun to do when you take a specific gameplay feature into account, which I will explain very soon.So far, everything feels good. Then come the gameplay features that make Fury Unleashed not suitable for everyone.Fury Unleashed is a rogue-lite, and that means RNG decides how hard your runs are going to be. The game utilizes RNG in various ways: The tiles that make the chapters, the weapons, the shops, the challenges, boss arena layouts, and even the number of bosses and their types are going to be decided by random. And on top of these, we have the chaos events.Every once in a while, you might run into roooms that are covered in black and white, replicating a sketchbook aesthetic, with enemies already in them or gradually spawning in. These are known as chaos events, with some of them awarding you with a weapon blueprint to unlock new weapons, and others offering nothing in return. Contrary to other rooms, there is no way to get out of these and you need to kill every enemy in order to be able to proceed, making these events a primary cause of failed runs.However, these randomizations are quite limited and not always well-done. The number of tiles and layouts are enough for a first playthrough, but not for hours of gameplay; which is a curse for the casual player and a blessing for a speedrunner. As for the enemy/object randomization, you can sometimes run into enemy placements with no way out of taking damage, get targeted by specific types of enemies who are outside of your field of view, constantly get guns with pitiful DPS, or may find a challenge in a place that you have no chance of completing it. All of these are not game breaking, but are very frustrating.Depending on the RNG and which weapons, bosses and enemy placements you get, you're either gonna have a fun time or the game kicks your ass very hard. And the ass kicking is going to be even more brutal if you cannot perform the one thing the gameplay is built around.Fury Unleashed is a game that is  reliant on doing kill combos and maintaining them as the main gameplay mechanic. If you honestly can't reliably keep a kill combo going, you better refund the game immediately because you won't get much out of the game and will probably never make it to the end.By killing an enemy, the game starts a kill combo meter at the upper left side of the screen, just below the health bar. Each kill increases your combo by one and upon getting to certain combo levels, the soundtrack suddenly changes to more dramatic themes to notify you of how well you are doing. The combo ends if you either get hit by the enemies or the combo meter runs out. Coupled with the smooth movement system, this makes for an incredibly fun and even addicting gameplay, with your desire to maintaining your combo growing more and more.And doing combos is absolutely needed, as helpful mechanics (like shields or faster reloads) and even healing are directly tied to the kill combo. Fury Unleashed has no reliable system for health recovery. You can only heal yourself by finding an RNG-driven doctor NPC, beating a boss, or maintaining a combo level of over 3 so each enemy has a chance of dropping health items after unlocking a certain skill. On one hand, this is a good way to make players want to master the game and learn the enemies' attack patterns to keep their combo going. And on the other hand, this makes for a lot of frustration if you are not good enough or when you desperately need healing before facing the bosses.Fury Unleashed also has two extra modes, with gameplay based on other indie games: SUPERHOT and Crypt of the Necrodancer. And both of these modes have problems.SUPERHOT game mode uses a predefined set of skills for the playable character, then applies SUPERHOT's ruleset to the gameplay by slowing down the action while being completely still and returning to full speed on movement, and also your character dies in one hit. To be honest, this type of gameplay doesn't fit Fury Unleashed's encounters. This game is about moving fast, baiting enemy attacks and using a variety of attacks to dispose of them. In SUPERHOT mode, melee attacks and fast movement become very dangerous (the latter because of environmental hazards), and that just takes the fun out of the game.Crypt of the Necrodancer mode is even worse. The game claims that in this mode, you will run and attack to the beat of the music and that's not true. In terms of movement, the gameplay slows down and briefly returns the speed to normal on each music beat, resulting in a headache inducing movement. As for the attacks, they really never feel like they are in-sync with the music either, resulting in a horrible experience.A very fun and even addicting twin-stick rogue-lite game, despite some shortcomings when it comes to RNG features. Although the gameplay's reliance on kill combos can turn many away from it.

_childDocuments_.review: Fury Unleashed is a roguelite platformer shooter, with a meta story backing it up.The movement and gameplay is solid, and reminds me a lot of the frantic yet precise feel to games like Spelunky. I only played through the first 2 chapters (twice, it is a roguelite after all!) and the story had some intriguing meta elements to it, with a comic book style without. This manifests itself in “ink” as currency, the occasional “sketched” levels, and a narrator describing each chapter.The levels can get a bit bullet-hell at times, with enemy movement and various projectiles all over the place. Because of this, I found it tricky to get through a level perfectly, something that is usually possible in games like Spelunky. Due to this, there’s more of a reliance on accepting damage, but then healing from it moving forward.Definitely looking forward to a few more runs through this!

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game, but unfortunately the online co-op was rather buggy, just be aware of that.Had soft locks a few times, one at end of a level couldn't press A to continue, and one where we tried to claim a quest reward while characters was on top of a doctor, and the game got confused. The bosses near the end of the game seemed to have issues with network desync and lag.Also, it's not particularly well designed for co-op in general. The game puts a lot of importance on the need to maintain a combo, even for healing, but in co-op the combo counters are seperate, which makes it pretty hard for an individual player to maintain a combo, and therefore hard to get health back, and other bonuses.Still had fun though.

If you like Contra style games, including a high difficulty level, this will be right up your alley. However, the controls have some issues. _childDocuments_.review: This game is so excellent!! The upgrades you can purchase with skill points as you play, die, and play agian are at just the perfect pace, and the variety of weapons in the game is superb. The theme that the game takes place in a comic and to unlock new weapon types, the character Inkmaster has to "receive sketches" from the "creator" and then "bring them into existence" for you to start finding them in the world as you play is just so imaginitive and cool. _childDocuments_.review: Good game, but some suggestions for a less frustrating experience:Remove the frequency of ink-related items, or at least allow players to remove them from the item pool. As of now, ink is basically experience point, with which you can gain levels, and  for each level gained do you get a skill point for a permanent upgrade. This is currently ink's only use, which makes ink-related items very boring to find, as they have no material impact on gameplay.  They also don't matter nearly as much as the combo counter when it comes to total score, not to mention being totally useless for players who unlocked everything like me.The same applies to health and damage-reduction stuff. I mean "damage taken reduced by 50% when air dashing"? Really? Who's going to find that kind of bonus useful when combos determine your scores  gives you invincibility. They also clash directly with the health and armor shops - countless times I've wished to get a weapon shop or Inkmaster instead. In short, the core system of the game incentivizes reflex and hit & run tactics, while the items create safety nets for taking DMG - 2 diametrically opposite direction. I was going to recommend reworking the useless items, but I think allowing players to remove certain items and weapons from the pool is more feasible. The game is great otherwise!

_childDocuments_.review: I'd recommend it if it were cheaper. No way it's worth 20€.It's fun at first, but it gets boring and grindy very quickly. There's 4 areas and you gotta beat the first area 3 times if you wanna start from area 2 instead of starting from the beginning. I got more stuff to do with my time.It also has some performance issues - it stutters randomly for a couple seconds once in a while and I know it's not my hardware's fault because this has never happened with any other game I've played, many of which are way more demanding.Normal mode is way too hard (I had to change to easy) because there's not a lot of space to dodge bullets coming from all over the place at the same time, and you can't avoid getting hit sometimes. I changed room/screen and when I entered the same room those bullets were still there and killed me while I entered the room (I don't think this is good design).The combo duration (main feature of this game) goes down way too fast and you lose your combo every time you get hit. I never kept my combo score for a long time.Despite all this you can see a lot of work was put into this game and these devs do listen to people. It's too bad that they decided to price this so high. If I'm paying such a high price then I expect more. If it were cheaper then my review would have been positive. As it is, I couldn't even be bothered to finish the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is really cool. A slick, single or co-op (I play in local co-op) side scrolling shooter almost, sort of, perhaps similar to the Metal Slug games in terms of feel. It's quite challenging and fast, if you've seen the trailer, the game isn't quite *that* hard or crazy and the "hard" mode will probably be fine for most people.I think it looks really good. I wasn't initially sold on the art style but after some hours I honestly don't know what my misgivings were as most of the environments and characters are really well drawn and animated in the same chunky (and kinda Metal Slug-y) style. The sound effects and music are pretty spot on too. It's a nice thing. The way the levels are put together can be a little samey sometimes as they're basically a procedurally generated grid, but this serves up the nice, room by room, kill everything and move on beat that makes up the game.I'd recommend this to anyone after a fast and slick co-op side scrolling shooter.

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly we don't have a "meh" rating here, I can't give it a negative review, but being honest, I don't recommend either.The game has a lot of potential, it has a nice world, I loved the idea of the comics. Nice art, the gameplay is good, nice weapons, cool bosses.But the "roguelike" aspect of it is really the downside, you will replay a lot the first comic until receive some levels to not die so fast, them you start to notice that the levels in some point will not make much difference and the upgrades isn't that interesting.The biggest problem with this repetition is that the map is randomly generated, and every single game that have this "randomness", in the end this feature made the game a lot less memorable, you enter generic rooms after generic rooms. Another issue with this is that when you explore the map you find hidden portals and chests with challenges, for example: need X combos to enter the portal, or increase the combo meter to X times, but a lot of times you find those bonus in a moment that there's no more enemies on the level. So yeah, you'll fail.I tried a lot to enjoy, but roguelikes isn't for me. If this game was "Contra-like" it will be perfect.If you enjoy roguelikes, that's a really nice game!

_childDocuments_.review: Nice fast paced action but do not buy this for multiplayer alone. It's not "really" online multiplayer. It's the remote play multiplayer kind. So every time any player decides to look at the mini map, open a store, start a quest, enter a challenge, or sneeze, the other player will be taken with them into those things.In a fast paced action game like this, being interrupted out of nowhere because another player enters a store is really not a well functioning multiplayer mode. You take so much unnecessary damage from enemy fire you were intending to dodge but suddenly time stopped mid-fight. Or you fell into a pit because being taken out of the action made you forget you had already used up your double jump.Besides that the game is a good time waster, so if you're looking for some single player fun, then this will probably do it for you if you like action platforming.
_childDocuments_.name: Fury Unleashed

_childDocuments_.review: The best roguelike I've played this year (or maybe ever), and I didn't think it would be coming into it. The game starts out fast, they throw every button on your controller on you and I felt a bit overwhelmed at first so I basically just jumped around meleeing every enemy and it actually works. Only a bit later on I started using the gun but was still mostly meleeing every enemy because it was fast and easy. Grenades came in much later in my arsenal and I still forget to use them on any other enemy than the bosses, same thing with the superpower. This game has provided a constant new content feeling through out all the 20 hours I've put into it (and I'm still not finished the last sketchbook). There are lots of interesting new weapons to discover and the enemies are different enough to keep the fights interesting too. And once you get the hang of it and become a killing machine, then chasing that big combo is what keeps your interest (current record 104). I think this game surpasses the games it takes inspiration from. A must buy if you like action packed roguelikes.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is definitely a fun game for couch co-op.  Similar vibes to original Contra, with rougelike elements added in. _childDocuments_.name: Fury Unleashed

_childDocuments_.review: I don't understand why this game keeps getting called a run-n-gun. I mean, you use guns and you do a whole lot of running around, but whenever the term run-n-gun gets mentioned, memories of Metal Slug and Contra tend to come to mind. Traditionally, a run-n-gun meant you ran and jumped your way to the right, shooting anything that moves, blowing up anything that doesn't move, and desperately trying to avoid all the shots coming your way in the process. Fury Unleashed should be thought of more as a twin-stick shooter with some platforming elements. Take off the rose-tinted nostalgia goggles...if you think that Fury Unleashed is going to be an extension of those running-and-gunning good times we got to enjoy mainly in the 8 and 16-bit eras, you'll only find the inspiration from those classic franchises here.But that's not a bad thing...quite the contrary! Fury Unleashed proudly displays such divine levels of video game inspiration, and becomes a great and solid title all on it's own! The graphics make me think that the Metal Slug games and the Steamworld games were thrown into a blender, and Fury Unleashed popped out...so in other words, the visuals are off the flippin' hook! If you're a fan of excellent artwork, you can't go wrong here. In particular, some of the enemy and boss designs are so cool I'd like to meet the artists and shake their hands for cramming so many jaw-dropping and stunning visuals into one game.The music is definitely appropriate for the settings and the action, pumping up and intensifying as you rack up the body counts. Your blood lust pumps up the music, and the music feeds into your blood lust, to the point to where you're zoned in on the action and will love every second of it. I don't know that I'd listen to the soundtrack outside of the game, but muting the soundtrack while playing this game should be a crime.The sound design brings it all home with some of the gun shots and explosions making all so satisfying that you just want to dive back in for more after the game is over.Admittedly, the controls (for me anyway) took a little bit of getting used to. A small, ever-so slight learning curve at first. But now, controls mastered for the most part, it's so comfortable zipping Fury around while laying waste to all that oppose him (or her, if you so choose) that his movements are second nature.This game is tons of fun. I'm almost 50 and have been playing video games since I was six years old...I've seen so much of what this industry has to offer...so you can imagine that a person could get jaded with this hobby over all of those years. Not with games like Fury Unleashed coming out! This game does so many things so right that I can't stop recommending it to my friends and co-workers. And if you're the type of person who likes to have fun, you have come to the right place.Now excuse me while I go beat a Nazi tank to pieces with a baseball bat...
_childDocuments_.name: Fury Unleashed

_childDocuments_.review: First off Id like to say you could ignore the majority of the negative reviews on this game. IT IS DIFFICULT and its meant to be this way, which makes it so much better once you finally beat that stage you couldnt do before. There is no such thing as "slipping some damage in during a fight hoping you wont notice" every point of damage you take can be easily avoided if you are paying attention, the traps make for harder gameplay but not impossible.As for the flow of the game, it has a fast travel feature which keeps you fighting to keep your combo up and every 5 combo you get a combo shield (up to 3 max at a time with skill points) which negate a hit entirely and doesnt reset the combo.Ive seen some people saying that the second comic enemies have too much HP and therefore making the game feel longer, get good and this isnt a problem. within 3 runs I reached the 2nd chapter of the 3rd comic and got enough skill points to get all the "necessary" points on the skill tree (extra combo time, extra combo shields, extra fast travels) and you can unlock new weapons to find throughout the runs by doing special missions that randomly appear. It is also 100% possible to full combo the entire game if you learn the attack patterns of the enemies and bosses there is nothing unfair about it that I was able to find.As for the games story, it is a 4th wall breaker of a story that tells you bits and bobs about the history of "Fury" the comic book. If you actually read all the story lines then it makes sense and the game has an actual objective other than "SHOOT ALL THE THINGS" and all the bits of info are interesting to read. It is fully possible to just skip all the story and still enjoy the game but from what ive seen of this game the 4th stage will make little sense for its existence if you ignore it.Default controls atleast for me felt really weird but after changing some keybinds in the options it felt completely natural and honestly quite smooth. All the guns have their unique aspect to them and sometimes DPS is not the only stat that matters depending how you like your weapons. on my 3rd run I used the same gun I got from chap 3 all the way until comic 3 chap 2 where I met my demise to enemies I didnt yet know.Overall Id rate it a 10/10 I cannot find any bad aspect about it. Its difficult, but not unfair. Its not too repetitive since after you beat all 3 different final bosses for each comic, you can start the run from the next comic. It has an aspect of randomness, but you can always find the weapons and gear you like best within a reasonable time (unless RNGesus has something against you) and the weapons are mostly balanced so even if you dont get that 1 gun you really like you can still do just as good with the others. The skill tree needs alot of levels to complete, but it isnt too difficult to level up quite a few times if you go for the combo related skills first and rack up huge combos which increase your ink (exp) multiplier, and also to note hitting destructibles like pots and boxes refreshes your combo timer and standing on portals (the shops, chests, quests ect) keeps your combo timer at maximum. also using fast travel refreshes the combo timer and opening the map pauses it so its harder to lose the combo to time if you plan your fast travels than it is to lose it to damage.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. I played on the most difficult settings first and died a lot but eventually got use to it. _childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game but I truly feel that the bump in difficulty once you get to the 3rd comic is ridiculous.  This is a tough but fair game up until this, as you now have to deal with a LOT enemies that can do things you haven't seen yet such as;Can fire homing bullets at you that pass through all obstaclesHave shieldsCan target you with a physic blast from anywhereReflecting lasersLasers that connect openings that do a LOT of damage, making avoiding the above extremely difficultElite enemies that are bullet spongesRooms with a 'mothership' shield that can protect multiple enemies that almost always does serious damage when you destroy it ... but you have to engage it ASAP or several of the aforementioned enemies will pound the crap out of you and can't get rid of until you kill itYou start the comic with weak weapons so if you don't get a decent replacement in the first couple of rooms you might as well start overI would still recommend this game but don't be surprised if you give up at the 3rd comic, which is a shame as it's a great level with beautiful graphics.  Better starting weapons (even just a much better melee weapon) would go a long way to leveling this out.

_childDocuments_.review: A generally fun game with really nice environments and amazing feeling weapons. Enemies also feel fresh with interesting abilities.The main problem I had with the game was the huge focus on combos. Having combos is fine. Lots of games do it. But having to keep up combos requires a lot of focus and the game has to let up the pressure a bit after a while. Here that doesn't happen. The entire playthrough is a crunch where every second matters and I feel like this severely hurt the experience after the first 20 minutes. I managed to somewhat fix it by not specing into the combo part of the skilltree and focusing on other things instead. Level selection was a bit too confusing, especially after finishing the third book.

_childDocuments_.review: Having played this game now for nearly 20 hours, I do highly recommend it, in particular to those who are fans of 2D side"scrolling" platformers. The thing is, in this game you move from frame to frame through "portals" rather than play in one big side-scrolling map, and though I'd like the teleport function playing its part in your combo meter, the game can sometimes feel very zoomed in, and I've felt unable to really prepare for what's to come. Some of the stuff your ink on in the game can also feel very under-powered for such a short experience, like getting 5% extra reload speed / bullet damage or what have you. I for one would like to see stronger upgrades as you progress through the levels. All in all, very glad I bought this (on sale I think) and I have loads of fun with it, but can't wait until it's completely ready in the hope it will improve further.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a little hard to be fair to this game; my gamer-snob came out when trying to write this, wanting me to pan it for being so simplistic and just not bringing much to the table that we haven't seen before.However, there's another side to this- it's perfectly adequate for what it is.  It doesn't suck, everything worked, and the graphics were cute.If you enjoy Metroidvanias with guns, and enjoy cartoony graphics, it might float your boat.  Normal difficulty is pretty darn hard, but there's a persistent upgrade system that takes most of the sting out of death, and Easy is actually very easy, so it's enjoyable if you just want to jump around cutting up your enemies with an overgrown machete without trying very hard.None of the mechanics are terrible, although I really wish there was a bit more real variety in weapons choices- there were clear Right Answers.  The game a better way to select the right tool for the job, when having multiple weapons; the lack of the traditional number-key quick-selection system in most FPS's was an issue while playing.  The camera is kept a little too close to give the player a lot of options with long-range weapons, and overall, it felt a bit like a Flash game from 2003.  The weapons balance, overall, is  OK, if imperfect.  For example, the shotgun is terrible, even up close... but the other starting unlocks are functional and players will quickly discover which other weapons to ignore / avoid.The story, unfortunately, is a bit of a letdown; it's given out in multiple unskippable areas and cutscenes, but it never really made a lot of sense, due to how it's presented, and it just got in the way of the gameplay, rather than adding interest and context.  It was something about a frustrated, failing comic-book artist... but frankly, it was too wordy and unconnected to the actual gameplay for me to care.The boss fights are perfectly adequate, borrowing heavily from the Contra series and some other classic bullet-hells.  The AI is basic, but it works.  Honestly, it's one of those games where I feel like I've already played it a few times, frequently worse and sometimes better than this.  But none of the bad stuff is so awful that I started frothing at the mouth... it's all little goof-ups here and there.Honestly, this is maybe the hardest game to give a final up / down on, of the dozens of games I've reviewed on Steam.  My initial feeling was Thumbs Down, because it just doesn't bring anything new to the table and it's only moderately interesting, and the story's bad.  However, it's not terrible; it's just not quite where one would hope.  I really want a "meh" button for this one; I probably wouldn't have picked it up if I hadn't gotten it through Humble, but then we wouldn't have this review, would we?  When deciding a "meh", I think I need to be optimistic, and say that some players, who really enjoy this kind of game, will probably find it perfectly satisfactory, so it'll be a thumbs-up.
_childDocuments_.name: Fury Unleashed

_childDocuments_.review: Fury unleashed is a beautiful 2d rougelike shooter. Your character movement is snappy, the weapons are fun and varied, and the story is nice and also not really in the way of shooting things.  Luckily the rougelike elements aren't the main impediment to progression, you don't have to wish for lucky armor/gun rolls just so you can win. But there's one big problem that seems to get in the way of my full enjoyment of it: the level design.Since Fury is a procedural game, they used the template of small metroid like rooms with traps to create their dungeons. Sounds ok sofar, right? The big problem is that the levels get cluttered fast and your characters hitbox is rather large, causing you to bonk into traps while trying to avoid shots often. Also, the enemies can be a bit tanky, so you might have to dodge 3/4 times before wining. However, whenever the game opens up its arenas in the boss levels, you can see the potential in the game. The bosses are all excellent and have more thought out engagements, making pattern memorization and thinking necessary to defeat them. I think it shows how much better it is when the levels wide open.One last nitpick is the last level of the game. It locks out of the previous 3 levels and halts your progression in the tech tree unless you replay the old levels. The problem is that you can only play one of the previous 3 levels, and if you try clearing the hardest one of the three, good luck, you only have a starter weapon and the simplest enemies needs like 4 rockets to kill. And for the last level itself, its rendered in a admittedly awessome black and white sketch style, however this covers up most of the traps. If only some of the traps (looking at you holes for spike floors) had some small red highlight, I wouldn't die to trying to butt-stomp an enemy directly to getting a spike up my bum. Still, after all the setbacks I think fury is fun enough to try, it's just a small bit further before it becomes something great.
_childDocuments_.name: Fury Unleashed

_childDocuments_.review: This Mega Man and Comix Zone-inspired rogue-lite starts strong with some fun progression system, not overly long runs and highly responsive, fast-paced gameplay. I personally think that it gets a bit too hard towards the third world and the risk-reward system is not very worthwhile. Once you get a decent weapon there is not much sense in exploring the levels rather than rushing to the exit because the rewards are rarely worth the trouble and health you might lose in the tough encounters. An diminishing returns hit faster than you'd like. First, you get a lot of skill points during your runs, but later you only get like one for 30 minutes of gameplay and upgrading a skill costs several skill points. And then there is the last world that throws all progression overboard. You don't get any skill points for playing the last world and it's also easily the hardest of the four worlds. The final boss is a total pain in the ass and for reaching him you have to replay the whole last world which always consists of rooms that you have to fully clear and three bosses that need to be beaten first. It was frustrating and I don't know why the devs decided to change the core gameplay that much for the final world. Well, you can lower the difficulty to an absurd degree to just put it behind you, but that doesn't feel rewarding. I still recommend this game for the first three worlds alone.
_childDocuments_.name: Fury Unleashed

_childDocuments_.review: If you like rogue lites and shooting and whacking stuff while dodging traps and bullets in a 2D plattformer, give this a try.Gameplay is fun and smooth, feels very polished, great cartoony comic book style artwork. and it is challenging, but has difficulty settings so you can adjust it to your liking.
_childDocuments_.name: Fury Unleashed

_childDocuments_.review: Great and fun rogue-lite with amazing comic-book inspired look. There's a steady progression so even a botched run doesn't feel like a waste of time. Controller is heavily recommended.The only complaint is that there's no Warhammer 40k-inspired comic book or sequel, seems like match made in heaven. :)Can recommend, even for full price (20 EUR).

_childDocuments_.review: The art style and comic like environment reminds me of the old school game Comix Zone and this game is cool, just wish it was progress based to another stage rather than having to start from the beginning all the time. _childDocuments_.review: Can't stop playing this game. _childDocuments_.review: Oh absolutely recommended! Visually this is nice and clean. Plays well too. Kind of an interesting take on platformers with the comic book feel. A little bit Dead Cells too I'd guess. Pretty fun from what I've played although staying alive into the second section seems to be my new favorite challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: Fury Unleashed

_childDocuments_.review: I was looking for a side scroller / platformer / shooter game with procedural generation maps. Fury Unleashed perfectly answers all these points and adds on top character customization and very cool graphics as well as dynamic soundtrack. It is a really addictive RogueLite which even manage to bring a cool story behind the action. Quite challenging but progression helps and at some points it is possible to start back at a given chapter and not from very beginning: very appreciable.
_childDocuments_.name: Fury Unleashed

_childDocuments_.review: If you want a chill relaxing roguelike game that's fun and simple to burn sometime on here and there without too much thought process then this is a great game for that. I do enjoy it a lot when I don't want something too serious even compared to other roguelike games, But definitely one of the best of it's genre.Request: Please add online Co-Op rather than just local Co-Op, it will make this game so much better by adding just that to it.
_childDocuments_.name: Fury Unleashed

_childDocuments_.review: Satisfying and engaging gameplay with beautiful comic-inspired art all around. The combo system creates a dynamic risk-reward mechanic where you can choose how "fast" you want to play, with all of the added benefits. Co-op was implemented well, but does present unique challenges on its own like split drops and combos. Difficulty is mostly linear, like all roguelikes, so be prepared to get stonewalled. Thankfully, the grind is particularly enjoyable. Highly recommended, especially if you nab it on sale!
_childDocuments_.name: Fury Unleashed

_childDocuments_.review: Admittedly, I wasn't sure how much enjoyment I would get from this roguelike shooter after the first hour.  I genuinely loved it comic book art style and frantic gameplay, but getting used to it's unique control scheme seemed to be my biggest challenge.  After getting a better feel for running, gunning, and bad guy shunning, all those initial worries vanished.  Fury Unleashed is as satisfying as it gets.  Plus, the workshop allows you to create your own custom player skins.  Fun stuff all around.
_childDocuments_.name: Fury Unleashed

_childDocuments_.review: I was generally surprised by how much fun I've had with Fury Unleashed so far (I've played on my own profile as well as via someone else)A fun, fast-paced shooter that also contains an interesting backstory surrounding the mental health of creators behind the scenes, it's a joy to play.You're welcome to check out the full review below too:
_childDocuments_.name: Fury Unleashed

_childDocuments_.review: PROS:- The gameplay has fantastic aspects considering the graphic- You must do every chapter over several times but the chapters change their bosses and this is coolCONS:- The game is a little frustrating because, from my perspective, the chances to finish the chapter depend on the amount of luck you had and the type of guns that spawned through the game- There were some articles way too long to read for a FPS game; we just want to have fun!- Maybe It would be better to have more different chapters than having to do the old ones over and over(?)
_childDocuments_.name: Fury Unleashed

_childDocuments_.review: I love Roguelike games, but there are SO MANY - Fury Unleashed is one of the first that compares to Dead Cells in terms of how fast the game moves and how quickly you can build up your character...It's actually faster to build up your character in Fury Unleashed than Dead Cells. Otherwise Fury Unleashed plays a bit more like a run and gun where you're constantly getting new weapons of all types and balancing between melee, air stomping, grenades, and 2 guns at a time.Presentation-wise, the game is told through a living comic-book and the aesthetic is extremely well done and very unique, I haven't seen anything like it since Comix Zone on the Genesis.It's been a long time since a game has grabbed me like Fury Unleashed, it's actually the first Steam game I've written a review for. I did receive the game for free from the publisher because I wanted to capture some footage for the Switch version, but I would buy this game in a heartbeat, and actually HAVE on Switch because now I just want to play it everywhere.
_childDocuments_.name: Fury Unleashed

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed it, and while it is not a great roguelite, it is definitely a good one worth trying for those that would enjoy its jump and gun gameplay.The main positive point of this game is likely its combo system, in which every 5 kills (as long as you don't spent too long without hitting anything), you get a shield that fully block one hit, up to a maximum of 3. While this is only an optional upgrade, it is one everyone should get. This system allow a gameplay where mistakes are pardoned if you take enough risk to move fast enough. And when you reach a 30 kills combo, the music goes from OK to awesome (while that one track could have gotten old if played non-stop, I always enjoyed it when I got to it).
_childDocuments_.name: Fury Unleashed

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. I'm a huge fan of action roguelike platformers. I just can't get behind the pacing and reward system. This feels like a less thought out version of rogue legacy. It's not fun to play, feels off and you can't find a good rhythm. Price seems high as most folks seem to burn out around 10 hours. _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR  Buy this game.Holy. Cow. Just holy cow. Where to begin. Art style. Game oozes art direction. Just the right amount of detail in ever way. Enemies look great, one frame I'm fighting a giant flying Aztec skeleton god to end the first chapter, next I'm dropped into WW2 fighting Nazis that have future tech. In addition to them looking great, they are all distinct. You look at a skeleton in the first chapter, at a glance you know exactly what that thing is going to throw at you (as long as you have seen it before). There has been no problem with things looking unclear or muddled, no question about what was and wasn't an enemy or where they were. It looks good. Chef kiss level of good. Animation is clear and precise, I love the way this looks. One run I'm a guy in warpaint murdering things with assault rifles, smg, sniper rifles and a katana. 90 mins later I have unlocked a skeleton guy and a set of soul weapons and another set of acid weapons, all the starting melee weapons. From military man to skeleton warrior with a mace and a bone cannon shooting flaming skulls.Gameplay. This game is tight. The controls are all well thought out, and after two runs in the game I was controlling it like it was the beating of my own heart. Responsive, no friction, just the right amount of 'wiggle' in terms of hit boxes. Barely graze the sawblade, won't count it. Mistime your dash and yea, you took damage. Speaking of dash, Fury (Name of your character) controls like you wish your game characters control. You want to jump, move a little to the left, jump again in air, move to the right, activate your air dash, overshoot and move back left then stomp straight down on your enemy and dash off to begin murdering the next thing? You got it. Your ground dash is unlimited, close the distance and break some skulls.Unlocks. You start each run with a basic firearm and a basic melee. This isn't Enter the Gungeon, these weapons will murder everything on their own, but don't worry, you'll only have those for maybe 2 rooms anyway. Heavily sprinkled though out the levels you will pick up new weapons, new armor, and many of them bring with them a new way to play. Suddenly you have a pair of boots that makes enemies explode? Hell yes I'm going to stomp on them. I'm gonna go out of my way to stomp on them. A shotgun, close range with lots of damage. Picked up a 'legendary' shotgun with bouncing bullets. Now I've got a spread shot murdering things behind me. Die a horrible death? You have leveled up your character, head right to the page and toss some points in, make your guy just a bit better for the next run and every run after that.Pace of the game. Fury is as fast as you want to be. I first started I was cautious, taking my time, aiming my shots and trying to avoid any damage. Within an hour I was holding down the dash button, double jumping to stomp a guy while shooting a man-eating plant, chucking a grenade just as far as I could. Couldn't see an enemy there, but there was a high chance there would be one. That leads us into the COMBO! The combo is, more or less, your 'kicking ass and taking names' meter. Do damage, it goes up, kill things, it goes up, break a pot or box it goes up. As it goes up the drop chance of health goes up, currency-ink goes up, and regular ink goes up. You see it starting to run out, you are looking for anything to hit, anywhere to go, keep those numbers climbing. Level Layout. Have you seen a comic book? This is a comic book. When you start a level you get the general layout of the chapter, but you don't know exactly how the rooms connect. At any time you can press your map button and see it. Here's the beauty of it. Say you ran into a dead end, murdered everything and have a combo going. 'Oh no, I have to run back through these empty rooms, I'll lose my combo.' Wrong. Pull the map up, and select any doorway you have seen and you can go right there. Need to revisit a room really quick to buy an item, bam, done. One room way off in the corner you missed, bam, there. The genius of it is that, while you are limited to have many you can do, I've abused the hell out of it and haven't run out. You can even unlock more as you level up. Oh, and did I mention that your combo meter refills when you do this? Because it does. Music. It is perfect. It is there, you are feeling it as you play the game, it is telling you to move, move fast, kill, kill faster. But it isn't assaulting you. Sound design is one of those things when done perfectly you barely notice, but done badly, you know. Every gun sounds like it should, every hit sounds like it should. Again, a chef's kiss.Am I rambling? Yes. Should you buy this? Yes. I don't know how I hadn't heard of this game until today with as long as it was in Early Access. This game deserves more people playing it. I love some Metal Slug and Contra, I love the roguelite progression. Marry the two and, well, the third chef's kiss.

_childDocuments_.review: I give this one 100% The art style is amazing and the attention to detail is beautiful. It is like Rogue Legacy but beefed up for the modern game era where faster playstyle, combos and all around better polish. _childDocuments_.review: Fun, tight, crazy re-playable and beautiful. Twin-stick controls that play like butter. There are only 2 games I can compare this to. Hades and Dead Cells. For sheer replayability and kick ass controls, this game can certainly hang with both of the former.  Can't wait for the full release!  Release has happened...get this gem!
_childDocuments_.name: Fury Unleashed

_childDocuments_.review: I'm huge fan of rogue-lite/rogue-like games and I played lot of them during last few years. Fury Unleashed is very dynamic platformer rogue-lite game developed by polish dev studio. Game is made in very cool looking comic graphical style and I really love it.Fury Unleashed has everything that I want to see in this type of game: lot of character upgrades that you can get for special ingame currency "ink", so it's perfect for players that love grind (if you are good and don't want to unlock everything then you don't need to do it), it also has many monsters, mini-bosses and main bosses to beat. Game is also full of quests and interesting events that can occur during gameplay in random places. Game is very dynamic and you will get more rewards for doing combos so it's very action based game.What can I say more... if you are looking for really good rogue-lite game with great progress system and interesting graphical style then you should give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Fury Unleashed

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent run n' gun iteration of the roguelite genre. The controls are very tight and the gunplay highly satisfying. The permanent upgrades generally mesh with each other and typically require a good deal of skill to use properly, nudging the player in the right direction to improving at the game. The combo system is spectacular for rewarding precision and maneuverability and ads a whole nother tactical layer to the game. As of April 2nd when I'm writing this, there are still some relatively major bugs, such as one of the superpowers (the stationary turret) won't deploy at all, taking a lot of potential away from your run. Full release is due in just over a month, so hopefully bugs like that are resolved by then. Other minor graphical glitches as well.  The worst part of the game though might just be the marketing. It's been in early access since 2017 and I only just heard of it on a random Youtube video. I think if this game got more exposure it has a great shot at being a large commercial success.Bugs aside, I would absolutely and emphatically recommend Fury Unleashed to fans of roguelites, and gamers in general.
_childDocuments_.name: Fury Unleashed

_childDocuments_.review: In the beginning the game was was okay, and I kind of regretted getting the early access, but the devs have done a terrific job of updating and improving it.  It is total a good rogue-like now.  The weapons are enjoyable and the progress is good and the art style is fantastic.  Totally pick this up now!
_childDocuments_.name: Fury Unleashed

_childDocuments_.review: In less than an hour, you'll shoot at Aztec zombies in the face with your shotgun, crush-stomp acid-spitting bugs, lob freezing grenades at cyber-Nazis, blow giant, fire-peeing robots to smithereens, and laser-blast the behinds of alien invaders. You lost? Fury is now stronger, so enter the fray once again - and again, and again, and again. If a fan of over-the-top action,  is an easy recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Fury Unleashed

_childDocuments_.review: Beautifully presented rogue-lite action platformer. Great graphics, fun weapons with good sounds, unique enemies and bosses. It follows a similar design layout as other games in the genre so there is nothing too unique about it but I found it to be very fun. I couldn't get a good flow going with the default keyboard/mouse controls so some rebinding is necessary. Excited to play more of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Fury Unleashed

_childDocuments_.review: The game is loads of fun, and reminds me of playing old shooter platformers on NES as a kid.  The mechanics are simple to grasp, but the skill ceiling is high enough that you can't just button mash through the game.  The story is also pretty interesting, even though it doesn't really have much effect on the gameplay.The story is currently unfinished, but 3/4 of the "levels" are available, and can be beaten pretty quickly.  It only took me ~3 hours on the higher difficulty setting to beat all the levels from start to finish, it'll probably take even less time if you play on the easier difficulty setting and take advantage of the shortcuts that allow you to skip levels.  There is some replayability though, with character cosmetics, and a higher difficulty to unlock.  There are also 3 bosses per level, so you can replay the game until you beat all 9 off the current bosses.There are only two complaints I have about the game.* The control method you use changes how easy parts of the game are.  Playing with a controller, melee feels very smooth, but shooting is more difficult (like all shooters played with a controller).  Playing with a mouse and keyboard makes shooting much easier, but melee is more difficult because of the default bindings for attack and dash/run.* Some bosses are much harder than others, particularly the bosses in the 2nd level were much harder to beat than the bosses in the 1st and 3rd level.Overall, I'm happy with my purchase.  It's simple and fun, and I could see myself picking it up periodically to play 20-30 minutes.  There is also a multiplayer mode, but I didn't get a chance to try it.
_childDocuments_.name: Fury Unleashed

_childDocuments_.review: i guess i'm a fan of rogue-ish games, so i keep playing badbutt hero to try to be able to last long enough to kill a boss or two, but it is terribly frustrating at times. there's hidden enemies that pop up out from underneath you with little warning and you can easily just fall down into a pit of enemies that attack you instantly; most games i play i can blame myself for getting killed, but there have been several times in this game where i yelled aloud, "oh come on!!!"otherwise, controls are tight, graphics are a fun comic book style with a tiny bit of character customization where you can change the skin, hair, and accessories. leveling up is slow, especially as the game progresses. i've yet to see any other environment other than the jungle, but this just might be the fact that i haven't progressed long enough....there must be other enivronments, right?! cuz i'm not seeing any others in the screenshots.there's still some bugs too. there's times where i can't get to the next "screen" at the bottom and have to re-jump up and down again to continue. 3440x1440 displays, but the vingette is set at 16:10, so you see dead ends where rooms are supposed to connect...strange. w/e, it's still fun, so: get it on sale for a quick fix here and there.
