_childDocuments_.name: Fury Unleashed

name: The Pedestrian
detailed_description: The Pedestrian is a 2.5D side scrolling puzzle platformer. You are The Pedestrian! Enter into a dynamic 3D world with stunning graphics and challenging puzzles. You play by rearranging and reconnecting public signs in order to explore and advance through each engaging environment.
about_the_game: The Pedestrian is a 2.5D side scrolling puzzle platformer. You are The Pedestrian! Enter into a dynamic 3D world with stunning graphics and challenging puzzles. You play by rearranging and reconnecting public signs in order to explore and advance through each engaging environment.
short_description: I can see the signs in my sleep now, always guiding me closer. Will this really work? Have we almost achieved the impossible?

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles are good and broadly have a smooth progression of difficulty. There are a few places where new mechanics are introduced where the lack of explaining the does makes things un-intuitive for a bit, but they make sense after more familiarity.Recommend playing "couch co-op" with a second person to help think problems through, even while only one person can have hands to keys/controller at a time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This is a nice little puzzle game with a great aesthetic. The final few puzzles really surprised me and kind of made me wish there was a little bit more.The only sticking point is whether you think € 16,79 is worth a (honestly rather simple) game that will last about 2,5 hours. Though to be fair, most people do spend more on things that will entertain them for less time than that.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: By no means a horrible game but I never really got a rush out of it. I don't think I'd recommend this to anyone who likes the more hardcore puzzle games. It is a short cute casual puzzle game that most people will be able to finish if they play it long enough. I think you're enjoyment will depend on your expectations. I do like the mechanics however the only reason I put the time in to finish it is because I saw it wasn't a long game. I guess in that way it doesn't out stay it's welcome. This is much more a "I wouldn't recommend it" rather than a "I disliked it"
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually write reviews, but this game really stood out to me. Its a wonderful puzzle game and for it being a puzzle game, its immersion into the world is great. Don't even get me started with the music, it is so good. I had times during this game where, I just paused and had to listen because the song that was playing hit just right. I highly recommend this game, it was very enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely amazing puzzle gamePlayed the demo awhile back and it left a very nice impression on me since, been waiting to get this game for a good deal, until when a friend of mine read my mind and bought it for me as a giftHave been endlessly thankful since, I would just lay down in bed and enjoy this masterpiece. It is a great game to play during a lecture or while somewhere noisy as the games audio isn't too important.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10i wanna preface this review by just saying that i suck at puzzles and don't play puzzle games too often but i do enjoy them from time to time.-for me all the puzzles were enjoyable and somewhat challenging. i didn't come across one that i felt like i couldn't solve. i didn't need any guides except for the very last one at the end and when i saw for a split second how this puzzle was different from every other in the game i just had an "OHHHHHHHH!!!!" moment and immediately turned off the guide to solve it myself and was able to.-visually this game makes me nut. it's beautiful-music is great and relaxing and i plan on purchasing the soundtrack.-just the idea of this game. that you're one of those little man or woman figures from a restroom and you just go around town solving puzzles going from one area to the next is awesome to me. when i saw the trailer for this game a while back it just blew my mind how simple the idea was but just hadn't been done before. at least from my knowledge.this is honestly just nitpicking. i think this game is great and recommend it if there's any doubts.-game is kinda short but i guess the length will depend on how long it takes you to solve the puzzles. i beat it in 4.4 hours according to steam. which wouldn't be too much of an issue but the price they're asking for is 20 dollars. so i recommend waiting for a sale-i would have loved a longer section of puzzles that were like the very last puzzle, but like i said this is nitpicking. i try to judge a game by what it offers not what it doesn't. i guess this is one is more of a "What I Wish It Had".If you love puzzle games I think this is worth your time. If you don't play them often I think this is a great one to start with. If the asking price is too much for you then I 100% recommend picking it up on sale. Got nothing else to say other than I love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Stunning in both visuals and audio with great puzzles ramping up as mechanics are introduced at a steady pace.No real replay value beyond experiencing the beauty all over again and nothing but the main objective to strive towards.Highly recommended if you enjoy puzzles and a fair share of wonderment.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably already one of my favorite puzzle games of all time. The puzzles, at least to me, felt like they were built in such a way to make you think, but not completely stump you. Not sure how exactly the developers did it, but it made for a wonderful gameplay experience.If it was just that, I'd still like it, but what made me like it so much as to actually write out a review was the fact that it looks and sounds SO GOOD. The aesthetics and soundtrack elevate it from a great game to an absolute must-play. There's an astounding amount of detail, and the soundtrack feels like it just KNOWS when to start and and when to stop.Basically, it's so well-constructed in every conceivable way that it was like I was playing a Pixar short. That may sound cheesy, but it's honestly true.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game, gorgeous aesthetic, novel puzzles with a nice gentle difficulty level. Really a beautiful exemplar.Took me about two and a half hours, with essentially no replayability, so if value-for-money in terms of time is a factor, maybe hold off until it's on sale, but personally I would've felt well-served at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The Pedestrian is a game developed and published by Skokum ArtsThe game offers some really nice graphics and a nice yet simplistic aesthetic which is pleasant all the same and has some amazing attention to detail even though it is a little rough around the edgesThe game does suffer with some repetitiveness at certain areas of the game but a fun game nonetheless and ends just at the right timeAnodyne overall, however, is an okay game to play, yet sometimes repetitive and it does get boring if being played for a long time, but is an okay puzzle adventure platformer game to play in short bursts!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The length of the game is going to be highly dependent on how quickly you can solve the puzzles. I've seen people mention anywhere from 3-7 hours. I enjoyed the ending section the most, and I wish the game featured a little more of the mechanic used at the end which I won't specifically reveal as it is spoilers.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game, with an extremely creative yet simple and easy to understand premise, taken to perfect lengths. About 4 hours from start to finish, so not a massive game, but I'd much rather have this than something bloated that overstay its welcome. Potential for workshop levels? The only thing I would add, developers, please loop the music during the levels... It gets... so quiet. Over all, this is on par with Portal in terms of quality and brilliance, if you're at all into puzzle-platformers, get it!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice game, with different and rewarding puzzles, they are also very hard but not hard enough to have you looking online to solve them, which I really like. When you solve a big puzzle, as you feel better for having solved it, so does the Music, which also celebrates your victory. It is a nice little detail that made the game 100% more rewarding for me
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Didn't rush at all, still finished the game in 5 hours. If you like puzzle games and just outside the box storytelling and problem solving or puzzle platformers, this game is for you. Strongly recommend. If it's on sale, don't even hesitate, get it immediately! Almost worth the full non-sale price of admission, but the game is rather short, so YMMV.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: I love almost everything abou this game. It really amazed me that puzzles can be designed this way. after hours of binge-solving puzzles , you finally get the ending which means after years of work,developers finally got this work done. and also means a lot to the players.If you like solving puzzles , you definately should play this game. Pros:  beautiful background graphics. almost like you are visiting the city.Very complex puzzles with short learning curve. Some puzzles are quite challenging.Very amazing background music appears just in the right time. beautiful like a poem.Great ending. I can tell developers put a lot of thoughts on it.Everytime you replay this game. it is like a new game. You can never remember how you solved this puzzle last time. because there are so many puzzles.cons:No chapter selection. if your save file correpted or something happens with your disk. You can only start over.I learned that in hard way. My video of last scene was correpted, to make this video again, i have to replay the whole game.----If you get stuck somewhere, you can check my walkthrough video, hope it can help you :
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: I had a great time playing The Pedestrian, good and clever puzzles.The setting and the soundtrack of the game are incredible, the city feels really alive.For most of the game, each new mechanic is introduced and developed appropriately. Generally, you always have the necessary knowledge to solve each puzzle. The game does a good job teaching you to play by increasing the difficulty at a good pace. My only conflict was in the last puzzle in the game when you can control a human. This section presents confusing and non-intuitive mechanics that go against what has been taught throughout the game, perhaps to fit the narrative of the game.Overall, The Pedestrian is a great game, I'm glad I played it. Totally recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Already hooked, and I'm only 1/2 hour in.The game is simply complex. The design and artwork make you feel completely immersed in the world. The simply controls lead you on a journey that gets only more interesting as it gets more complex. Everything about this game from the sound to the controls is well thought out and leaves you comfortably in control. If you enjoy puzzle games this is sure to become your new favorite. If you haven't tried similar games this is a great one to start with.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Aie Aie Aie... I recommend to play this game BUUUUT!! Although i bought this game in 2020, i played a short time then stopped, I continued in 2021, 2022 and then stopped again, because of the boring mechanisms. This year, after seen so many recommendations, I decided to 100% it to really understand what this game has so special and I am sorry to say but getting to the end was a pain, not because of the difficulty of the puzzle but because of the boring repetitivity of the puzzle mechanics, some of them were twistedly over-designed, which was breaking the rythm when playing. Moving the character in one window, interrupting his progression to move the window, generate the connections between the windows...The concept is original but for 20-30mins, not hours. The last part of the game is original and interesting but comes too late. The artistic design is very good, but again if the player does not have fun, the player stops playing... The words that come to my mind when finishing the game were: "over-designed puzzles", "exagerately entangled connection possibilities". Now, don't make me wrong it is not a bad game, it is the dosing and ryhtm management that did not convince me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The visualization of this world and the way it's embedded in the game play is really creative. The puzzles and concepts to solve them are introduced well, and the levels of the puzzles scale in a great way too - challenging enough that it takes time to solve (and sometimes a break away from the game is needed to get a fresh perspective) but never tedious or repetitive enough that you get sick from routine. Soundtrack is great too!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: It's short, unique, and a ton of fun. The puzzles never get too tough, instead introducing different mechanics to keep the gameplay fresh while the difficulty stays pretty level. My only "complaint" is more of a personal preference, I really was hoping for a little more of a story. What is there exists to give life to the puzzles, and that's perfectly okay, I just maybe came in with the wrong expectations as far as that's concerned. I definitely recommend it, playtime was ~4 hours but I'd still say what's there justifies its price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: A short, but sweet experience. The music was beautiful and the backgrounds hold so much detail that the puzzles nearly pale in comparison. I do wish that the mechanics towards the end had been used more, because I would have loved more puzzles like the last big one, but I understand why it was only used this late and sparingly. It certainly holds a nice surprise as it is. I was stunned.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The Pedestrian is a great game, albeit short and over too soon. The pedestrian has you operating a figure commonly seen on a variety of signs as you navigate around the world through differing signs which act as platforms and puzzle areas. The game is quite simplistic in its actual game play which has you pushing buttons or levers, jumping, moving and picking up objects. The game definitely excels in its presentation however as you navigate the world. I will say that one of the better mechanics implemented early into the game is the ability to move and connect signs. This creates some quite mind bending puzzles, especially as new elements are introduced as you progress from area to area. There's not much story to the game outside of interpretations and the game doesn't really have much to speak of other than its core mechanics which may make the game feel a bit light on content. Additionally, (spoiler ahead) as you progress you collect parts for a device. The last part is just kind of given to you and after that point there's only a couple of puzzles. I really loved the last puzzle but it felt as though the game had just introduced something incredibly interesting without it being earned and then it barely utilised it. I really wish the game did more with it as it seemingly ended a bit too quick. Perhaps that's just me however as it seems the average time to beat the game is 4 hours yet it only took me 2 and a half. I'd definitely opt to wait for a sale if you're looking to pick the game up. Don't get me wrong, there's some fantastic puzzles here, I just don't think that the content overall however holds up to the price. I really wish there were more.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: lovely puzzle game, just falls short on some areasfor starters, i think the ideas and mechanics involved in this game are really really promising but i dont really think it was ever fleshed out. it feels lacking, especially the end game which i think couldve been an entire chapter on its own but instead was just limited to one puzzleit also has a very weird difficulty spike, where for the most part the puzzles are easy but then it suddenly just turns really "hard" in the context of the game. i think the game just lacks a bit more substance to flatten the spikelastly,  the fact that this game still has no chapter select after four years is a crime. this game really needs one, especially when theres hidden levels which just makes them a pain to find and exploreoverall, its a 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: What starts of being simplistic puzzles using simple movements of tiles, turns into a impressively complex but not taxing array of different unique puzzle mechanisms not seen anywhere else. The final puzzle completely changes the perspective. If you like a puzzle game, spend 30 minutes getting into the meat of this.

_childDocuments_.review: A short yet pretty nice puzzle game. Really beautiful art style and music.Took only a short time to finish it (5,3 hours for me because a few puzzles are "very different" from the rest and took a few times of to enjoy the atmosphere of the game).Pretty expensive but I got this game and a bunch other from Humble Bundle so definately worth it.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This Kickstarter title has had an interesting development and is now finally out for everybody to try. It's a fun little game with 2d mixed with 3d environments all leading to a unique climax. In the 2d puzzles you affect the real world and it makes for some interesting situations. There's quite a few puzzles for this cheap title and with that its basically a no-brainer that will keep you occupied for about 6 hours. Some are fascinating and for others you might need a timeout to take another look after you've walked your dog or whatever. Its never really that hard but its also easy to overlook the solution to a more complicated puzzle. So take the time (or timeout) to finish it.It's a neat journey that is well worth the wait and I hope the devs will continue to give us such beautiful and unique content in the future. I'm just very happy to have been part of the process that enabled these nice devs to bring their brainchild to life.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: I beat the game at a leisurely, experiential pace in approximately 5 hours. What a beautiful game it is.- The puzzles balance difficulty and accessibility extremely well. Each challenge required time and mental effort, but I did not find them to be excruciating. I failed plenty of times, but by the time I exhausted my options, the puzzle was solved. You don't need to stumble upon secrets in order to progress. New and innovative mechanisms are introduced every level. My jaw dropped out of sheer gratified surprise so many different times, I'd sound like a liar were I to number them. I was totally riveted from start to finish.- The Pedestrian's rolling backgrounds and scenery depict city life - messy and occasionally chaotic, but colorful and lived-in. The developers' attention to homely detail was astounding; they clearly have a love for the city. Simply gorgeous.- The score is breathtaking. I thought it was delicate, whimsical, and even a little sad a times, but ultimately uplifting. It left me teary. Very charming.If you like puzzle games and haven't picked up The Pedestrian, your collection is incomplete. I can't recommend it enough. I bought it on sale, but it's worth the full price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: So much charm. A 2D puzzler with barely any platforming. It's a great concept as you need to arrange tiles in a specific order to progress. The preview video does it proper justice but the puzzles are really good and challenging at times. They really take the last gimmick and work on that to provide a good curve. However, the game is a bit short and despite it’s fantastic art style, doesn’t take advantage of the 3D portions. I REALLY hope they use this as a launching pad to make a bigger and better sequel that really incorporates it. That being said, it’s still a fantastic game with  music and I really enjoyed it!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: It isn't often that I encounter such a beautifully designed and executed puzzle game. Without any words or instructions, they were able to teach and reinforce the game mechanics while introducing new twists on the rules. Although some of the puzzles were very challenging, there isn't a single puzzle that was too difficult to solve without researching the answer online.  The  combination of the setting, design style, animations, music and sound effects made this game an absolute joy to play. Thank you for making it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Frequently surprising and somewhat simple to learn and understand, the game never fails to keep things interesting.First learned about it in 2016, wishlisted at launch and let it sit there until the time was right.Incredible game, absurdly creative, really one-of-a-kind.Finished in one sitting, got stuck only twice.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most unique puzzle games I've ever played. And the most beautiful. The music comes in as you solve screens, acting like fanfare, and dies down while you're trying to think, allowing the atmospheric sounds take over. The graphics of the real world background are lacking, but not so much that it takes away from the experience.If you enjoy out of the box thinking, buy this game. I beat it in about 2.5-ish hours, but I'm very experienced with puzzle games, and had little trouble with the puzzles. Not to say they're not hard or clever, the game is heaps of both. But it is still fairly short
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: brilliant little game, absolutely wonderful concept, beautiful art, excellently thought out puzzles, and a twist ending that made me gasp and say "wait... oh my god!" out loud with my human voice. 10/10 started recommending it to everyone i know before I even finished it, well done and thank you to the devs! <3 <3 <3
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't had this much fun with a puzzle game in a long time... a long time!The presentation is top notch, the game is beautiful and it plays incredibly well. I don't recall ever having struggled with the controls, which is quite an achievement in itself. I played with mouse and keyboard, which I think is the best way to play, since you are frequently switching between directly controlling the player character and rearranging panels and connections.My only gripe is that I'm finished already (took me a little more than 5 hours). But for all the great puzzles in a truly innovative game and the fun I've had, I consider the price very fair.Verdict: Awesome game. Haven't seen anything like it before. Fun. Buy!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This is a neat little puzzle game, which felt like the right amount of challenging. Two or three times I didn't see what I needed to do (not a puzzle, I just didn't realise I could connect two things, for example), but it's mostly self-explanatory. Definitely worth a play and try not to read too much about it before playing, because I think that would make it even more enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a breath of fresh air when it comes to gameplay. The puzzles are incredibly satisfying, and the visuals are beautiful. The ending puzzle is quite surprising and doesn't drag on. The sound design is perfectly relaxing. In a nutshell, it's a short but incredibly creative game that will leave you feeling satisfied.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute 100% recommendation for any puzzle fan! The levels are quite extraordinary, on a much different level from most puzzle games. The surroundings are a beauty to look at and the soundtrack gives it an overall chill vibe. I'd say this game is not for a beginning player, the levels can get pretty difficult.I wouldn't say this game has a lot of "story," but every new gaming element is introduced by a sort of tutorial level so you can get used to its principles. At no moment does the game become boring, as it keeps introducing new elements. Throughout the game you collect certain items. On full price it is pretty pricey since it is a relative short game. In my humble opinion: it is worth every penny. If it is a bit too high for liking, wait for a good sale. The game needs to be played and discussed! Officially, the game can be completed in about 4 hours. It took me a while longing because of some dumb mistakes and certain areas  being the bane of my existence.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This was a fun twist on a 2d puzzle platformer game. It's really notable how much detail was put into the mostly-decorative 3d world surrounding the panels holding the actual play areas. There are a lot of neat little story elements. It's definitely worth sticking through it until the end, which presents a nice surprise. My only disappointment was that the game start to get really clever and interesting for the last few sections, and that ended too quickly.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful game in every sense of the word. Everything (and I mean ) from the basic puzzle mechanics, music, even the menu screen coheres together in to a wonderful and complete whole.Of particular note are the puzzle designs, which I think are complex enough to feel rewarding but easy enough that you won't ever get stuck for long. I recommend this game for anybody who likes video games - even if you don't ordinarily gravitate towards the Puzzle genre. At least give the demo a shot, it easily swayed me to pay full price for this excellent title.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: I must say. Even though I played on the lowest graphic setting, it was still beautiful. I enjoyed all of it. Now, I may not have a lot of things to say about it, but Ive recommended this game to so many people. Regardless. This game is a gem that will hopefully become a nostalgic boost for me in 10 years! Whenever choose to play it again after said boost, I can have another terrific experience. 10/10!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The pedestrian is one of these games where I wish Steam would have a "neutral" review option, rather than just recommend/not recommend. I mostly enjoyed playing it, but there are quite a few flaws or just things I wish were different with the game:The good:+ All but the last mechanic () are fun. The green paint (?) mechanic was one of my favorites, but sadly it was introduced way too late and I only got to use it for 20 minutes or so.+ It looks great! The environment in the game is well made and actually contributes a lot to the game, despite only being a background visual. The meh:- It's short. Super short. It took me less than 4 hours to beat the entire game and get all achievements. Short games are fun too, but considering that the game is €20 I can't recommend anyone to buy this at full price. - The music is nice, but it doesn't loop. I was playing in complete silence for most of my playthrough which was a bit boring. - The last mechanic and ending to the game were quite confusing. - The last chapter has a bug when you're using multiple monitors that makes your mouse go outside of the screen, making me click on other windows and remove focus from the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a short adventure, to say the least. I feel for the full price of it it isn't worth it as much. I spent about 4 hours to complete this and while I loved my time with it I didn't feel I got my money's worth from the amount of time invested. That being said the game is beautiful and atmospheric. The puzzles are really challenging and make you need to think out of the box a lot. I really enjoyed the style overall!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Decent puzzle platformer that should provide enough challenge and good feelings for most players who like puzzle games. Story is minimal but effective enough and pacing is good as new mechanics are introduced through out the game, and doesn't make the mistake of dropping mechanics out the moment you completed an easy puzzle, which something that some puzzle games do unfortunately. Not that many flaws but if I had to name a few; there are secret rooms but accessing them doesn't seem provide achievements for some reason (didn't spend my time on them) and game could've used more music during the puzzle rooms, as it's good music but it only played between puzzle rooms, which I found odd.Considering it's base price, The Pedestrian could've been longer but I would check this game out whenever there is a discount.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: At the start of this year, i broke up with a girlfriend who i thought really cared. i was torn really bad. one day scrolling through instagram, i found this on the GeForce Instagram page, a post about a 2D platformer that was also 3D. This had reminisced me back to an old toy, Rattica's Cube world toys. They were really enjoyable and they were so cool to me as a kid. This game while not quite the same, gave me HUGE of nostalgia. _childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Very beautiful puzzle game. The gameplay is very simple and very polished. _childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The graphics are, quite frankly, amazing. Yes, you may say they aren't perfect, but they create ambience and thy add a cozy feeling to the game. The individual puzzles (while may throw you for a loop once in a while) are manageable. There were a couple instances where it was unclear how to proceed, but that is the nature of puzzles. The key take-away is that none of the puzzles are frustrating to the point where you may want to stop playing.Best puzzle game I've played (I've played lots outside of this steam account :P ). I would recommed to anyone who wants to have a whole experience, rather than brain-breaking puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Simple in its design and mechanics The Pedestrian is such a joy to play, it is one of those puzzle games where you feel great after figuring out how to solve each stage.Such crafty design is always welcome in these type of games where difficulty gets often misinterpreted making things obtuse and convoluted.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

The only thing I don't like it is very easy puzzles. If you want 100% achievements just beat the game(I think max time is about 5h)
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very fun puzzle game. Challenging, but not too terribly hard. Got a little stuck on a couple puzzles, but not for too long. It's a little short. I would've loved another hour of gameplay. But at the same time, the game's length meant nothing felt played out or stale.I bought the game on sale. Now that I've played it, I would've played full price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This is an accessible puzzle game that will have you scratching your head, but pleased with yourself when you figure out a solution. The world around you is rich and great eye candy, and the concept of the puzzles themselves is quite fresh.It wasn't the most fun I've had though. This isn't a criticism, because being a clever AND fun game is exceptionally hard to do, with only a game like portal and a few others achieving this imo.. and if you're playing a puzzle game, the chances are you just want to stretch your brain a bit and not exactly outright have fun.. but all I'm saying is, I was happy when it ended.The paint mechanic particularly was really quite jarring and difficult to get my head around.For these reasons, and it's short length, I probably wouldn't recommend it at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Nice night for a walk, eh? Welcome to the game of Skookum Arts presents Fun With Signs!So far, this is has been a nice break from the games I usually play, with the most clever use of street, machine shop, etc signs that I've seen and played! The music is upbeat and helps the mood, on top of the addictive 'whoa, I just did that' gameplay, for keeping on going!All I know, otherwise, is that seeing this game in the Store surprised me and then playing the game itself surprised me even more... and that this is either already my Puzzler of the Year, or at least 'The Best Use of' objects game of 2020!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Be warned the game is quite short. I have 6-7 hours, and some of that was idle time and getting stuck on a few puzzles for awhile. I would expect some people finishing the game in 3-4 hours.That said, I enjoyed it quite a lot. There were quite a few head-scratchers, the mechanics were interesting, the background environments were quite a treat, and I liked the way they taught the controls and mechanics through gameplay and the environment.I think there's supposed to be a story, but if so I had no idea what was going on. The ending gameplay was a surprise, and the ending itself was pretty but if there was supposed to be story/meaning in it - it went over my head.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very unique and clever puzzle game. However, it is incredibly challenging. Particularly from about mid-point in the game. It becomes very confusing and if you don't have the best of memories (like me), you may find yourself quickly overwhelmed. This is well worth playing for the puzzle lovers out there. For people who are on the fence about puzzle games, I would avoid this one. I had to use a guide myself in the end and even with a guide it took several hours to 100%. All achievements are unlocked after certain levels and cannot be missed.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: What a refreshing game!  While the puzzles are not entirely unique, the atmosphere, the graphics, the music, and everything put together so perfectly make this a very unique experience.Overall, this is a puzzle platformer.  You control a stick figure, such as ones you would see on road signs.  Some puzzles are simply one panel which means solving the puzzle to access the exit to the panel.  Some puzzles are made up of multiple panels.  On panels are doors and ladders.  You must draw lines between the panels to decide which door opens to what door and which ladders connect.  This can be as simple as possible, or sometimes as complex as possible.As you progress, the difficulty ramps up.  You start to have electricity involved, where you panels are more like circuit chips where you must connect wires in order to activate barriers to be lifted and the likes.  Later on, you will get to an even more difficult gimmick of the game, but I'll let you get to it so as to not ruin the latter half of the game as not only is it difficult, but the very last level is stunning.The world is 3D, but you play on the panels.  So you will still see a living and breathing world around you.  The graphics are beautiful.  The panels are like white board, though that can change from time to time in beautiful fashion.  The animation of your character, and the objects you can manipulate all looks and feels great.  Never once was I frustrated with movement, it was always the puzzle that was the central focus of why I couldn't move forward.While the 3D world around you is mostly just a graphic background to the real game, there are times where you can manipulate the 3D world.  Such as when you entire the front of a train, enter a specific code, and hit the button to activate, you will actually see the train move and when you exit you are in an entirely new area.  This gives you the feeling the 3D world around you is not entirely just a backdrop for you to play the game.The music was amazing throughout.  Very mellow and soothing to keep the nerves calm as you dig into your brain to solve each and every puzzle.  The game is intuitive, beautiful, and.....again....just refreshing.This was a surprise hit for me.  I saw that people loved it when I first saw on the Steam store page, though I had never put it on my radar.  The videos looked intriguing, I bit the bullet and bought it during the sale, and I couldn't be happier.  Don't miss out on this great indie hit, kudos to the developers....you just hit a home run with this one.

_childDocuments_.review: All puzzle games exist in the shadow of giants. Games like Portal, the Witness and Myst tower in the memories of gamers. These are experiences that subverted expectations of what a puzzle game could be, what it should be. Portal showed us that a game could deliver an engaging narrative whilst pushing a unique mechanic to its very limits. Myst proved that puzzle games could be pretty and compelling as well as teeth grindingly difficult. And the Witness proved that gamers will pay for any old ♥♥♥♥ if it's pretentious enough.So oftentimes, a new puzzle game will try to ape one of these giants. Portal has perhaps the highest number of imitators, with QUBE, Quantum Conunudrum, Turing Test and more, and Myst has had its fair share of successors too. But the Pedestrian has its sights on the Witness, but not just to blandly imitate, rather, it intends to evolve the concept. How can you better blend the 2D and 3D than Jonathan Blow did? Seemingly, the Pedestrian comes to the conclusion it's better not to.Almost all of the gameplay takes place in the second dimension: a fairly rudimentary puzzle platformer that takes place on street signs, blueprints and all sorts of other flat planes that you would expect to see a stick figure on. The 3D rendering is reduced to background work, enhancing the sense of a journey being undertaken by the player character as you travel from a factory through sewers and backalleys to eventually neon lit rooftops. It's quite pretty and while it doesn't add much to the gameplay, I find it hard to argue its pressence isn't an immense benefit to the game.Now if you've played a few puzzle games before, you can probably guess the twist already. Why design and create all these 3D assets just to have them serve as digital wallpaper? The twist is so obvious and almost inevitable that I think I'd respect the Pedestrian more if it hadn't gone for it. Rather than be happy with its position as an exceptionally pretty and well crafted evolution of a flash game, instead it reaches for the lofty pedestal of the Witness. In its final moments it delivers its thesis, a proof of concept that goes nowhere and is so poorly explained that it kills all momentum. As well as breaking its own gameplay loop, the final puzzle suddenly crowbars in a trite, wordless narrative that hadn't even been slightly hinted at before then and completely undermines the rest of the game. It's like if the final boss of Dark Souls had been a DDR level and tells you that it's all been a dream.This is to be expected though. Aspiring to be like the Witness is a fool's errand. I maintain to this day that the Witness is a meta-narrative, about the desire to see hidden meanings in that which is intentionally hollow, about a player's need for something so hard to have "meant something", and how easy it is to fool people with insincere, faux-emotional imagery. Trying to be the Witness is like trying to do an impression of an impressionist, it ultimately takes away more than it could ever have added.Perhaps I'm being too harsh and what is, at the end of the day, a mostly cute and fun little puzzle game. I think I'm disappointed that the Pedestrian wasn't brave enough to stand by what it is. That it could have delivered a little wordless narrative about a stick figure on a journey and been happy with that narrative, but instead reaches for loftier heights at the cost of its own achievements. It's still worth playing if you love puzzle games, it's not the most inventive or challenging game, but it's generally quite cute and well paced. The Pedestrian could have been more if it had been brave enough to just be less.

_childDocuments_.review: The Pedestrian is a puzzle game with a unique art style. The game takes place inside various 2D panels located in a 3D world, with lots of cool transitions between puzzles.The puzzles play in 2D, where you navigate a character between panels that you can move around and connect. The objective most of the time is to retrieve an item, and there’s also some light platforming involved.The game gradually introduces new mechanics, but it doesn’t get overwhelming. Also, for a puzzle game, it’s on the easier side; I never got stuck for too long. It’s a bit on the shorter side, but I felt it didn’t need to be longer.Overall, I found this game enjoyable. I loved its unique style and puzzle design. The ending is also something you have to experience for yourself. It’s an easy recommendation on sale, even if you’re not the biggest fan of puzzle games.

_childDocuments_.review: As a kid, you might remember car rides not being the most exciting. You generally had to make your fun and let your imagination run wild to be preoccupied. I, for one, would imagine someone running across rooftops or the little guys on street signs coming alive. It worked for me back then, and I still think back to it now and again. I find it strange, though, that no one had attempted to recreate that fantasy since I’m not the only one who thought of it. That is until I discovered The Pedestrian.If you haven’t already heard of The Pedestrian, it’s an indie 2.5D puzzle platformer from Skookum Arts (that’s also their first game). You play as the Pedestrian, a small character on a street sign left on a road. You move between different signs, moving around and connecting different signs at will to solve the puzzles. Move on to bigger and more complex areas in your quest for freedom. The game is available exclusively for PC on Steam, and you can learn more here.Now, if there’s one thing I think everyone will agree on with this game, it’s that it’s filled with an incredible amount of passion and charm. The backdrops, despite you never playing on them, are designed as a living breathing world. I often found myself admiring the backdrops before doing the puzzles, which is something I very rarely do in games. Even the play area and the different signs are designed with such thought that I wouldn’t normally expect, and serves to enhance the experience. On top of all that, your menu is an old TV screen. What more could you ask for?But of course, that isn’t entirely why you’re playing the game. You likely want some solid puzzle platforming too, and Pedestrian serves not only to meet that but also excel at it. The game introduces a lot of new mechanics and does so phenomenally, which is something most puzzle games don’t do. They start the mechanic out simply, having you get the hang of the idea and slowly ramping up the difficulty. Then eventually, you take on complex puzzles that make you think about it extensively. I have to commend the development team behind The Pedestrian. I haven’t seen this level of polish since playing Portal many years ago, so it was quite refreshing. Overall, the gameplay had a lot of thought put into it, which paid off.This is combined with the emphasis on thinking outside of the box literally and figuratively. You have to move around a lot of your play area if you want to solve certain puzzles that require a lot of outside thinking. You’ll also push the entire piece of the backdrop around in some parts to access different areas. This thinking out of the box goes to big lengths for the final puzzle of the game, but I won’t go into that to avoid spoilers. There isn’t a lot that I can say wrong here.And of course, everything is wrapped together with some excellent sound design. The entire score of the game is the right level of calm that you’d want from a puzzle game of this sort. There are also different songs depending on which area of the game you’re in that fits the setting. Logan Hayes, the composer for The Pedestrian, deserves every bit of praise he gets. The soundtrack’s Steam page says the soundtrack is “carefully crafted to evoke a myriad of pleasant emotions,” and that’s not exaggerating.Despite all these great things I have to say about the game, there are admittedly two issues I have with it. The most notable of those is the length of the game. My entire playthrough took about four hours to complete, with only a few extra things you can do. A puzzle game like this needs a bit more content, especially at a $20 price point. Not to mention there isn’t any replayability for the average player, meaning many likely won’t be going on a second playthrough. What’s there is incredibly solid, but it was just a shame not to see more.The other issue was with the options available. There isn’t a whole lot you can change within the settings menu, and the ability to change keybinds is missing.  It isn’t the worst since the control scheme is alright, but it would be nice. The options you have already will likely be fine, though.Verdict: The Pedestrian is an incredibly solid experience, filled with a lot of passion and charm. The art of the game is beautiful, and will likely hold up for years to come. The gameplay feels consistently fresh, with many new things being introduced all the way through. To wrap it all together, there’s a beautiful soundtrack that makes you feel pleasant while playing the game. The game may be rather short and lack some options, but it’s an experience that any puzzle fan needs to play.You can find this review and more at . Thank you to Skookum Arts for providing a review copy.

Then it got delayed once, twice, and ultimately got their release date removed completely. I was sure it will end up in a production hell until I checked the Steam page for it in the late 2019.Needless to say, I was not gonna keep my hopes up again, but as the day approached, I started checking the store page on daily, and yesterday on the hourly basis. It's finally here!The simple mechanics and awarding "Aha!" moment every here and now, wrapped in the wonderful surrounding that is, in contrast to simple "game area" rich and detailed is a real grip this game holds you with. _childDocuments_.review: From a first glance, the game already didn't look like anything else I've seen. It looked like a clever game, making use of one of the things we see every day, all around us. Signs. And that is the setting of the whole game. As you travel, you remain in the signs.And that alone already makes the game feel so much more unique in a world that keeps getting sequels, remakes, or games that just attempt to copy others.The puzzles are smart and enjoyable, with each part giving room to more creativity in how you should solve the puzzle, by giving room to another small part. Accompanied by calm music and a background that, even without seeing anyone, feels alive, the game honestly drew me into it.As you can see, I don't have many hours in the game. _childDocuments_.review: I've a few hours of this game (received as a gift), but this game is really obviously something special from the get-go. I think the way they presented the game mechanics in such an intuitive and engaging way--having the player explore the mechanics as they are introduced, with no tutorials or the like. It seems to be a pretty accessible puzzle game anyone could play (whether its at gaming cafes, one's own home, etc.), almost akin to those flash games that were once so popular back in the day. The soundtrack too is a huge strong point for the game. It's really relaxing and not at all distracting from the gameplay. All moving parts of this game, in themselves, are pretty strong, and the sum of these parts do not just form a whole in their union, but something that is even greater than the sum. Highly recommend this game. And this game would make a pretty great gift for a friend or relative (as it was for me)!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The best part about the game is it introduces new puzzle solving elements before you get bored of the old ones, and the transitions between levels introduce the new elements perfectly, Love the art in this game with the 3D and 2D sets. Awesome Game worth every penny to support these awesome devs if you can afford it but if not just wait for a sale like I did.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: I do not mind short games. But if your game is 2 and a half hours long, it's pretty inexcusable for 45 minutes of that to feel like padding, which is my main criticism of the game. Unlike any many other games in the puzzle genre, which aim to have low times between figuring out the puzzle and having the game realize you've bested it in cerebral combat, Pedestrian puzzles have a comparatively long time between that. This is made worse by there being deaths in the game - and each time you die, the level completely resets with no way of undoing. There is no way to undo. (This is utilized for a mechanic later on, but that doesn't excuse it.)In between each puzzle area you have a long while running through signs. The game often likes to do a "hub" puzzle area with signs connecting the disconnected levels to the hubs, leading to you running through many non-level signs twice (or more). This walking can be quite long too. I suppose the intention is to allow you to drink in the (admittedly often quite excellent) backgrounds and pace the game, but to me it felt purely tedious. The end-of-game twist panel also has inexcusable amounts of walking back and forth especially while you realize what's going on.As a puzzle game, the puzzles were... fine. Too many suffered from the issue of being able to look at what tools they gave you and being able to find the answer simply from the path that used all of the tools. Besides the aforementioned pacing problems, they were decently inventive with the main gimmick, although none ever made me gasp in the clevererness. I did not leave the game wishing for more puzzles of this type.  The twist puzzle at the end surprised me. Besides again the tedium of doing a lot of walking, it was a nice gameplay capstone. I think if that were to be expanded upon more, though, a lot would need to be done to avoid those issues (that puzzle had the longest time to realize the solve to actually solve of any puzzle in the game for me)The "story" ending frustrated me. The diabetic explanation came out of seemingly nowhere. That's usually a sign (hehe) to look at it from a metaphorical level, but I couldn't get any clear grasp of what The Pedestrian was actually trying to say. Even ignoring any discussions of price to game-length, there's plenty of puzzle games on the market (Like Baba is You, Lingo, The Witness, etc...) that I would recommend you play first before The Pedestrian, unless you like the aesthetic *That Much*. Unfortunately, I can't say I recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually enjoy puzzle games, but this one is simply phenomenal. I personally felt as if the difficulty for the puzzles is well balanced, no need for a guide on this one. For anyone wishing to 100% it, all you need to do is complete the game. This puzzle game relies heavily on its perspectives, especially for the last puzzle which makes it stand out.TLDR: Sweet, Simple, Fair, Unique, and most importantly fun.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Cool little puzzle game. Takes around 3 hours to complete, each area comes with each own unique twist to puzzles introducing new elements along the way. Doesn't overstay it's welcomeGame makes you feel smart for thinking "outside the box" and puzzles are not that hard that you have to look up the solution.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: A nice little puzzle game that has a unique twist, with a nice take on the same concept toward the end. Definitely a few tricky puzzles mixed with some easy ones, so not all that taxing. Love how it gradually breaks you into new ideas as the game progresses, so no two puzzles feel too similar. The graphics are also really nice to look at and the sound design is really quite mellow. Feel like I didn't do everything either, as I'm sure I saw a lot of doors I couldn't get to as I went through it, almost made it look like I could do the whole game in reverse (? Or I'm going mad *shrug*)If you like puzzle games, pick this up. It is totally worth the $15 I spent on it!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, but where are the puzzles, though?I enjoyed the art style, smooth controls, pretty environments, but for a puzzle game, there is a distinct lack of puzzles. I'm disappointed to have 100%d the game in just three hours, merely by following the 'do the only available move that is not completely dumb' strategy. I hoped for a challenge!There is a neat TheWitness-like perspective altering moment, but it's very brief, and so this gameplay mechanic feels like it could have been utilized much more.The art style is quite polished, but in terms of gameplay there is as much content as I would expect from a free flash game. Feels more like a tech demo, a tutorial, or a teaser for an upcoming actual game.The concept of moving a character between sign-shaped areas looks cool, but maybe, just maybe, perhaps it doesn't actually offer any opportunities for good puzzle design. Maybe.Not worth the full price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: A neat, small, amazing puzzle game which has a unique mechanic. It's very relaxing, the environment in-game is wonderful and the soundtrack. _childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This was a very fun puzzle game to play through. The game wasn't all puzzles, it has a cool storyline heightened by the achievements, and a terrific background in between puzzles.Pros: Incredible graphics, sufficiently difficult puzzles, great ending.Cons: A little expensive for being on the short side, but worth it, especially if on sale.Overall, worth it. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Ambiance is great, music is relaxing and its simplicity at the start is easy as it rewards you with new challenges giving the experience a refresh at each 'stage'. Puzzles are never impossibly difficult or require expertly fast reflexes, and are very manageable if you tried games like chip's challenge. However, its rather difficult to recommend the game because its very forgettable; mechanics and art drew me to buy the game but was not the most impressed with it.I don't normally play puzzlers and the last one i did was Helltaker; with its music and wacky theme (and its free) seemed more remarkable with a fun conclusion - not the pedestrian's ending though... honestly i get it yet i don't get the why. Yeah i guess  it is kinda cool having 2d concepts play out in 3d. Would i pay for this..? probably if there was a better/more memorable soundtrack and at a price of a cheap lunch maybe.. i paid more than a cheap lunch for this and the soundtrack while adds to the atmosphere/relaxing, is not definitive unlike say, undertale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The Pedestrian is a relatively short, but fun puzzle platformer. You are a character from one of those flashing 'walk' signs. You connect signs, and use your little pedestrian to solve various puzzles. The puzzles are quite unique. As for difficulty level, I've played lots of puzzle games, and I'd say this is a medium difficulty puzzle game overall. I found the puzzles satisfying and there were a couple of times I really had to stop and think about things to solve them. The game rewards you for patience in the puzzle solving not rushing. The learning curve on the puzzles is not bad, although there was one concept/mechanic that took me a bit to grasp and felt significantly more difficult than the others. As you complete the puzzles you move across different areas of a city. The game shines aesthetically as the surroundings as you travel the city the surroundings are nothing short of beautiful. There are different tracks of music as you go through the city, and they evoke a sort of peaceful feeling. There is a story inside the game, but I am not sure I understood the whole thing, and after talking with one of the developers the story is left up to some interpretation of the player. Without spoiling anything I will simply say the last half hour or so of the game is a culmination of your work throughout the game and really is something special that tells you a lot about the story.I have only a couple of drawbacks with the game. One is the music. The music is good, but it appeared to me to not be playing at certain times, and I'm not sure every area had some. The other thing with the music is the volume either goes down or off when you are moving signs in the game to solve the puzzle, but I found myself wanting the music all the time at the same volume. My second drawback is length. The game took me seven hours to beat, which is not really that long. Of course one wants good games to last pretty much forever, so this is more of a nitpick. The third thing is not really a drawback but is worth noting. It gets to be kind of a hassle trying to move the signs with a controller, which is how I started playing, so I would definitely recommend keyboard and mouse, which is how I finished playing, but you can play with a controller just fine if you want to.I was a kickstarter backer of The Pedestrian. From the beginning I guessed this game was going to be a gem and I was right! The developers were really responsive throughout the development process and took feedback seriously as they made the game. I am willing to bet this has made the game even better than it initially was and as a backer and a gamer, knowing they took feedback seriously is a big deal. At a price point of $20, I think it is a fair buy just a little high in my opinion for 6-8 hours of gameplay. On sale, it would definitely be worth picking up. If you want a peaceful, satisfying, beautiful puzzle game then I definitely recommend that you pick up this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Took me around 4 hours.  Solid, well paced puzzles, with good progression and interesting new paradigm shifting mechanics introduced at several key points along the way.  The visual presentation is delightful, with the mix of 2D and 3D presentation really paying off in the end.  The 'story', if you can call it that, is mostly ambiguous and dreamlike metaphor decorating the edges of the experience, but the focus is really on the puzzles.  Don't expect some kind of big twist ending that makes a coherent narrative out of it all, but there is still a fitting and cathartic ending that feels like it ties everything together thematically, if not logically.There were also a number of points where I noticed additional paths that I could not quite reach.  I got the impression that solving certain puzzles in a different way might leave me access to a box or a key that would lead me to some kind of secret area... should at least provide something to look out for on future playthroughs.Overall, I would recommend it to anyone who enjoys puzzle games, and doesn't mind things getting a little whimsical.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been keeping my eye on this game ever since it fell into my radar and now that I've managed to put in at least an hour plus into the game, I can say that my hype over this game is very well justified!Part 1:Part 2: (Got stumped here. Once I find the solution, I'll do a part 3)The first thing that caught my attention right off the bat is the signs-based theme and the gorgeous graphics - yes, funnily enough, I'm also a "visual" person despite loving the written word. In my opinion, it really takes a creative person to see something as mundane as a sign and think, "What if the signs can be turned into a platformer?" The screenshots you see in this store page are exactly what you'd get to enjoy in-game... and boy! What a feast it is for your eyes! It is for mine :)Of course, a game isn't just defined by its theme and graphics, the gameplay is very important too. For someone who's moderately good at puzzle games, I love that the game starts me off slow, introducing each new gameplay mechanism to me without rushing through them all and giving me the time to familiarize myself with every new element. I also like that the game isn't just levels after levels of puzzles - there's a sort of continuity in this game since you'll basically be running from sign to sign while solving puzzles along the way. The Pedestrian doesn't just give you increasingly difficult puzzles as well. You'll encounter some difficult ones in between easier puzzles, essentially giving you a nice breather in between brain workouts. + Challenging 2D puzzles interspersed with some easier/simpler puzzles.+ Visually gorgeous - a feast for your eyes!+ Uniquely creative theme+ The price is right!- None so far! No bugs or glitches that I've found so kudos to the devs for releasing a proper game! The Pedestrian is definitely one of the most entertaining puzzle games that I've had the honour of playing. The game is not only will put your brain on a treadmill; it's fun; it's refreshingly unique; it's well-made; and it's just a... *chef's kiss* ...masterful piece of art! If you're a fan of puzzle games, I would highly recommend getting this game - you'll fall in love with it as much as I did, I'm sure!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: I was excited to play this game months ago when i saw it on reddit, unfortunately i forgot about it over the holidays. i found it again today and to my suprise it was released a few months ago. _childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The Pedestrian is simply put, a wonderful puzzle game.  It's such a breath of fresh air after some less enjoyable puzzle games I have played recently.  What I like in a puzzle game is a game that doesn't require expansive tutorials, but rather through simple trial and error things start to make sense.  The game introduced some clever variety to its simple concept of traveling from sign to sign.  The graphics and art are beautiful too.  I loved the soundtrack and the fantastic backgrounds as I shifted around the world.  Oh and the ending is phenomenal.  I got the very end and got initially frustrated, but once I figured out what was going on I was blown away by how clever they ended that game.  A+ effort to the developers.  I simply cannot find any faults in this game.  Added to my list of all time greatest puzzle games ever.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: An inventive and unique puzzle-platformer that has a lot going for it. My favorite thing about it, and the most readily apparent, is the unique mechanic that serves as the basis for the game itself -- you are a small pedestrian sign silhouette that jumps from sign to sign across a large cityscape in order to navigate the levels. It is a new and super interesting take on the genre that I most definitely have not seen before. The way that this game incorporates the environment and everyday objects into its' gameplay is brilliant. At a running length of about 3 hours, featuring an amazing Disney-like soundtrack, buying this game on sale made it feel more than worth it.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: NOTE: I ENJOYED MY TIME WITH THE GAME, THE MAIN ISSUE IS THE PRICE TO CONTENT RATIO*While the game is very well crafted and uses some solid mechanics, it only begins to get truly challenging at the end. throughout the first portion of the game, you will steamroll rooms with the simple mechanics being explained to you through stickynotes. It's only when lots of mechanics intertwine that we end up with the hard level of gameplay that you would expect of a puzzle game. The dificulty does slowly ramp up, meaning that this game is more accessible to people new to puzzlers, but I myself found that my playtime was less than 3 and a half hours, even given that I took a ♥♥♥♥ and ate dinner with my family durring that time. The game is less than 3 hours for someone who's moderately ok at puzzlers, and only durring the final buildingtop puzzle did I once again struggle to understand how to go about completing the tasks. If there was one level higher in terms of dificulty, I would have felt that I got my moneys worth. It would be interesting if the devs made a campaign crafting option, where someone can make either levels or sets of levels, but as the game is currently, there is no way to make your own levels. As it stands, the game is too barebones and there isn't enough content to justify purchasing it at its full price. It's an experience like the witness but without nearly as much of the content. Wait for a sale on this one.edit: for the steam autumn GOTY awards badge
