_childDocuments_.review: Great puzzle game, the visual atmosphere hits just right and is half the reason you should play this game. The closest I can think of with a similar visual and artistic vibe is the Unravel series. I played this with a friend and we both found ourselves admiring the environment quite often.The puzzles themselves are refreshing, have good freedom on how you want to solve them and pick up on difficulty at a normal pace, although a handful of puzzles in the second half of the game were really difficult to the point where on finishing I wasn't sure if I had found a valid solution or some cheap rule-breaking exploit. I found myself throwing random ideas that sounded out of the box to see what would stick and I wonder if there might have been a puzzle or two that I solved in some weird manner that was not an intended solution. This game isn't long enough for this to be a real problem though and it poses a challenge only if you're new to puzzle games that require you to step back and take some time to think things though.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Charming puzzle game where you play as a stick figure. The screenshots might be confusing because the world is 3D but you are not and you only move on 2D planes within the 3D world. 3D world is just a beautiful background. Something to look at while trying to work on the puzzle. The 3D is not static, it lives and moves on its own. I have not seen any humans though. The 3D environment changes as you progress through the levels.The puzzles start slow but the game introduces new mechanics as you progress. The stick figure can move between 2D planes if they are connected somehow. The stick figure can move,jump and carry 1 item at a time. There are teleporting mechanics, ladders, jumping platforms, lasers,walls, jump-through floors,doors,locked doors,keys, cables and other things. Some 2D planes can be moved some are locked in place.The game has a lovely soundtrack that keeps you company while thinking. It has no words, but it also isnt low tempo so its not going to make you sleepy but it also isnt high tempo which would break your concentration. Definitely worth a listen on its own.The only issue I have is that sometimes the music stops playing and theres silence unless you go to the next level.Overall a very beautiful game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent puzzle game, with beautiful graphics and just the right level of challenge. Similar to the Talos Principle, in that progression is derived directly from the mechanics, with no tricks or edge solutions. There are a few timed jumps, but the controls are responsive and these should present no issue. Slightly reminiscent of the Swapper in some sections, in that players will need to "kill" their character from time to time, but the conceit of the player being made of paint, chalk or marker pen makes this more amusing than dark. The game does not outstay its welcome, and is worth playing twice in order to study the details during level transitions, which players can take at their own pace. The music is somewhat overbearing in the early sections, but blends better in later sections, so do not be put off. It would be nice to have a level select, as there are some sections I'd like to return to without playing through the whole game. In terms of narrative, endings are hard, and it's not ultimately clear what the game is "about", but this is preferable to undermining it all with some tiresome metaphor or allegorical message. The Pedestrian is worth your time for the gameplay and scenery alone.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game to anyone who likes puzzle platformers. It is a masterpiece in my eyes, the only thing I could wish for is a workshop map creator or something to prolong the life of this game. It is not very long and you can easily complete it in one sitting. To some this is a turnoff but honestly I wasn't looking for another 100 hour+ game that I would give up on completing because I got distracted by something else, hands down best game I have played in a long time. Devs all I can say is thank you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first game I ever backed on Kickstarter and I am happy to say The Pedestrian deserves every bit of your attention.  The gameplay exceeded my expectations and quickly became everything I would want in a unique indie game experience.The overall feel is very whimsical, with a welcoming art style and relaxing music. Exploring the city high and low presents a creative diegetic atmosphere of adventure that draws you from one puzzle to the next. The puzzles feel natural in their progression of new mechanics to challenge you. Some puzzles will make you feeling accomplished after a hard fought tinkering, while a few will leave you wondering why such an easy solution wasn't apparent 10 minutes ago. Either way, they are a lot of fun.This is one of those games that when put down to go live life, you will be thinking about solving The Pedestrian's puzzles in the back of your head. It is easy to see a lot of love went into this title from the developers.I strongly suggest trying to not spoil the ending for yourself or for others as it was a pleasant ribbon on this present of a game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say about it game, its amazing.Journey through a beautifully crafted world solving puzzles in signs as a stickman/woman. The music is perfect, keeps you calm while trying to solve the puzzles. There is an amazing attention to detail crafting a wonderful world around you and not just focusing on the puzzles. Puzzle mechanics are clever and evenly pace throughout the game allowing you to get used to them.Simply a joy from start to finish. I am not much of a purely puzzle game fan but I can not recommend this game enough you need to play it.10/10 in my books couldn't fault it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Pedestrian is a really cool puzzle game where you explore signs in the environment. You go from sign to sign - those often have to be connected or otherwise altered with props in the environment. You have to activate switches, move crates and dodge lasers. It is a really neat idea and, while the game is a little short (about 3 hours give or take, I was afk for at least 30 minutes once while playing this game), it is a lot of fun and interesting, but also generally pretty easy. The game also looks great and sports a cool aesthetic with lots going on in the background - it is amazing what you can get out of Unity with a little bit of effort.What does leave a bit of a "sour" taste in my mouth is that the game throws a really cool twist to you at the end - no spoilers, but it is a really good idea, one that should have been expanded on much more and could even be its own game. Instead, it only gets used for one puzzle and then the game is over, clearly setting up for a sequel or a DLC. While I do hope that will come and continue to use this cool idea, it feels a bit weird to use it for only one puzzle and then end the game. I wanted to see much more of it.Still, The Pedestrian is a clear recommendation and I hope we will see a sequel or DLC that plays with the ideas presented in this game even more, as it was just a bit too short to really encapsulate its full potential.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: In general, I can recommend this game. However, if you're not a puzzler or don't like to play the same puzzle (with some variations) for an extended period of time, you're not going to like this. I also may be a bit late to the party on this, but I still want to get my feelings out there. Overall, I liked it, but I did get tired of it about 3 hours in.THE GOOD:+ The simple graphics of the playing area and the style sticking so close to the familiar look of signage is done excellently. It also contrasts pretty nicely with the surrounding “real life” environments around it.+ The interplay of a 2D field focus with the surrounding 3D world is very unique and well implemented. It makes you keep your eyes on the active areas, but also anything that might be interactable in the surroundings.+ The mechanics added to the puzzles as you go are very inventive and a bit more mind-bending than I expected from a smaller game. Simplicity is probably a key factor since they could focus more on the puzzles over graphics.THE OKAY: > While the sign style is well done, it caused me some issues when I would play for an extended period of time. I’d find my eyes starting to have trouble focusing or even hurting. This can be a problem when you stare at a screen too long, of course, but it seemed oddly exacerbated by this game.> The reset mechanic is integral to the game. However, it is an absolute PAIN in the longer puzzles, where a mistake can set you back more than just a couple minutes. When I’m already getting a bit tired of a puzzle, a setback like that leads me to checking a guide instead of more trial and error. An undo button may have helped that, but I’m sure it would also have its own issues.> The ending is a bit underwhelming for what potential it had. I came into it very intrigued, but at the very end I was like, “Uh… okay?” The achievement name only makes me curious in the way you would be when you’re questioning someone’s decision, not in the intrigued way.THE BAD:- I like puzzle games, but I started feeling worn out a while in. By the end, I was following a video guide because while the puzzles were still well done, I was tired of the same sort of puzzles for so long and how long they can take if you’re not sure of the solution (and don’t want a guide). - Achievements are super disappointing. They’re only connected to the chapters and are unlocked as you go. It would have been nice to have one or two for the secret hats or something. This is just lazy. :/- If you drop the game for a while, good luck coming back because you’ve forgotten the controls, the mechanics, and the point. I did this to myself twice, which did not help my engagement.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: While it's on sale, I'd say 100% worth it, even not on sale it depends if you really enjoy puzzle games and/or lots of environmental eye candy. My first play-through I probably had a solid 5-6 hours of time solving the puzzles, and they are very interesting and somewhat different from other puzzle games. The unique gameplay/art style in the game makes it always a treat to see the next environment. It was a very fun experience, and It reminds me of The Witness with it's "simplistic" puzzles and pleasing eye-candy of a world you explore. I'd say for a Indie game of the puzzle genre, 9/10. It would be a full 10 for me is it was another 2-3 hours long, I really hope there is a sequel some day, if not, something of this caliber again, as it was very enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Very clever little puzzle game, albeit a bit short. Beautiful visuals and great sound design. The final puzzle definitely surprised me! I've been reading about a story in other reviews, which I didn't understand at all. But that didn't matter to me at all, since the gameplay is great and speaks for itself.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and unique but also fairly short puzzle game!+ Beautiful artstyle, such a unique concept for a game!+ Relaxing ambience (both music and visually) and gameplay+ Very fun transitions between the puzzles and levels+ Fairly hard puzzles but never anything crazy+ Very unique puzzles, each level bringing new and interesting mechanics Without spoiling anything, I wish we had more puzzles with the last level. The mechanic it introduced was the most unique of them all and it was only used for two puzzles before the game ended- Fairly short. Took me 6.5 hours to finish which includes a couple of times being stuck on some puzzles for a while- No separate volume sliders for gameplay and audio. Although music is great but still would've been nice- Mouse sensitivity while playing on controller is a bit awkward sometimes (played with a Steam controller)If you love puzzle games, I definitely recommend this one. A bit short but I think the base price is appropriate for it.Could definitely benefit from having workshop support so we could play custom levels.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: I often get frustrated by level-based puzzle games, but The Pedestrian is just the right mix of complexity to make it challenging but still doable. Most impressive is the cinematic style of the game which makes it feel like the game is one continuous shot. So charming. Clocking in at around 4-5 hours, its' a perfect short game experience that respects your time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely excellent mind-bending puzzles.  The amount of detail put into the environments is frankly absurd, and each new mechanic that gets introduced just keeps upping the ante, but without ever stepping into too-hard-to-beat territory.  Game is a bit short for its price (roughly 4 hours), but absolutely great if you enjoy unique mechanics with a great sense of style.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The Pedestrian is a puzzle platformer that involves rearranging signs to progress through the levels. The increase in puzzle difficulty as time went on felt appropriate and the overall design of the game is very smooth. The soundtrack is also great. My only real complaints are that it's not clearly shown what some of the features you learn as you progress actually do, so I felt like I had to play around with some of the signs for quite awhile just to figure out the mechanics when it didn't need to be that complicated, and the game is relatively short for the price (it took me about 5.5 hours to complete). I also didn't really get the ending, though I don't mind not completely understanding it.With that in mind, if you enjoy solving puzzles, can get this game on sale, and the trailer looks interesting to you, I recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: When I went into The Pedestrian, I was expecting a fun yet simple 2D puzzle platformer, however the game design and frequent head scratching moments were an amazing surprise. I was able to finish the game in about 3 hours, and it left me wanting more and yet I believe it might have been the perfect length, as if the game was longer if might start to over stay it's welcome.Without spoiling anything, throughout the game you are collecting little gadgets to attach to a Gameboy like device and once you have collected all of the gadgets the game takes a major turn and reveals an interesting twist that made the world in which the game is based in intriguing to say the least.I would recommend this game to fans of all puzzlers and fans of 2D platformers even if they have never played a puzzler before.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This game reminds me heavily of Portal, and no, not for the portals. For the portal-like mechanics it provides, way it keeps screwing with your head, and the fact it keeps throwing curve balls like it revels in your constant confusion. That keeps it fresh all the way through* to the end where they very much surprised me...twice.*Which really kept my mind on edge because I had to constantly think about how I am mechanically supposed to solve *this* room vs the previous area.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: My scores/reviews are almost always based on having bought the game at close to the "lowest historical price" on steam at time of purchase.Quick score: 5/5Notes: Great Soundtrack and probably the most unique aesthetic I've ever seen in a game. I would have liked to see a bit more of an emphasis on the platforming and a slight increase in the games difficulty, but otherwise the game is great. _childDocuments_.review: Overall** — 9/10 : A puzzle platformer with amazing visuals that provides challenges requiring out-of-the-box thinking without ever being frustrating! If you are looking for something to twist your brain while also providing a relaxing and unique environment, this game is a must have.Graphics** — 8/10 : It blurs the lines between 2D and 3D gaming in a gorgeous and seamless manner.Gameplay** — 10/10 : A twist on 2D platforming that gives a truly unique experience for puzzle enthusiasts. Audio** — 9/10 : Beautiful music that provides an extremely relaxing feeling as you focus on what the game has to offer.Price** — I found it is well worth the money. _childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: It was such a simple but good experience!!!From the simplest of features like the game loading up and you being immediately in it w/o any bs menus or anything else and it staying true till the literal end of it! Everything was  done in such a nice and pretty way!So happy to have chosen to play it! 100% worth it just for the background scenes and the puzzle n chill! :D

_childDocuments_.review: is a quirky little puzzle game where you get to re-arrange signs on walls and allow the animated stick figure to navigate around and escape, moving onto the next set of signs.You can tell pretty easily from the trailer whether you'd be interested in what it does. I think it's worth your time and has some unique aspects to it,  at the ending of the game, so I would recommend giving it a shot.Length-wise, it's decent but takes just a few hours to get through, so you can decide from that whether you'd pay full price or wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This is a puzzle game where you play as the little cross-walk dude, navigating an increasingly complicated series of street signage in order to.........well, here's the problem, there's no dialogue, so other than progressing for the sake of progressing, you really have no purpose (see below for negatives) until the very end when you sorta figure out what the whole point was (a little too late...).**-Graphics-  The environments are really awesome (even if the puzzles themselves are pretty minimalist) truly giving you  a sense of progression through an urban landscape (nightclubs, construction sites, etc.).-Sound Design-  The music may be all but non-existent, but the soundscape and in-game effects are top notch.-Fun-  This is a truly enjoyable puzzle game.......up to a point.........see below**  -End Stage Gameplay and Narrative-  While for the most part the game is quite enjoyable and you will pat yourself on the back for your big brain, eventually more and more gameplay wrinkles are added, and the lack of any talking or instruction kinda cripples the fun factor at that point because not only do you really have no clue as to why you're ultimately solving all these puzzles, you will eventually have more and more multi-step puzzles with new mechanics that are completely unexplained!  I'm not ashamed to say that I looked up a walkthrough to figure out what the heck was the deal with the paint spray canister, because there is not really a good, thorough explanation given in the game, and the tutorial is super weak.So we've got a mostly enjoyable, pleasing to look at  puzzle game whose lack of dialogue hurts it from a narrative perspective (why am I doing these things?!?!?) and whose end levels are rendered frustratingly obtuse because of mechanisms and objectives that are simply not explained.I'm ultimately recommending The Pedestrian, but mostly because of the first 3/4 or so of the game......the last quarter is just plain frustrating and opaque.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: A bit on the short side, and I would have loved more puzzles like the final  segment, but all in all it's a good time. An original puzzle game that's a breath of fresh air. . A few added features would be nice seeing as there's zero replay value, like players being able to make their own puzzles to share with the community, and allow the player to select the music. Or a time trial mode for bragging rights. I could actually see this having a sprawling, interconnected map like a Metroidvania. I actually thought I was going to do some backtracking as a few times I saw multiple exits but could only take one. My biggest request though is to please add an option so the music never stops. Doing the puzzles in silence breaks the immersion. The music is absolutely beautiful. Easily my favourite thing about this great game. Reminds me of Child of Light. The segment when it's raining with thunder lightly rumbling and a soft piano was fantastic. More of that, please! I am definitely going to buy the soundtrack. Thanks for a great experience!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The Pedestrian. Both extremely unique and extremely rewarding. A complex puzzle game that is one of the most most interesting concepts that I have ever seen, a visually stunning experience that takes effort to work through each level. This is amazingly accompanied by a wonderful soundtrack by Logan Hayes and a compelling story that keeps the player guessing and marvelling as it expands beyond their initial imagination. I think the phrase that best describes The Pedestrian is that is "Short but  sweet". The gameplay itself combines loads of puzzle-solving elements that you learn as the story progresses to create imaginative and individually different, logical problems. Despite the short time it took me to complete the story (between 3 and 4 hours) which of course may differ based on skill level, this game is remarkably replayable as every puzzle, though not forgettable, takes time to cognate the solution. And once you have solved it after trying and trying, you get that sense of effort rewarded as everything clicks into place (both mentally and in-game) and you can continue your journey. To sum up, I would highly, highly recommend this game to any fans of the puzzle game genre or those who are new to such games, in which circumstance, this would make a perfect introduction. Skookum Arts did an amazing job.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best puzzle games I have played in a long time. It nails that balance between challenging and frustrating. It make take a bit to work through some of the puzzles, but you always feel you can find the solution and it feels good when you solve some of the trickier ones. _childDocuments_.review: The Pedestrian stands out in the puzzle-platformer genre as a true gem. I highly recommend this game to anyone that enjoys puzzles, and think it is absolutely worth the price despite its short length.Games in the puzzle-platformer genre are best evaluated by two criteria: the core concept and the progression.The core concept is that you play as a stick man (or woman) that lives on the 2D planes within our 3D world. This concept resonates with me, as I have often daydreamed of similar ideas during my daily commutes. The concept also has plenty of room to expand, as new interactions with the 3D world are plentiful.The progression in The Pedestrian is very quick. Just as soon as you are comfortable with the current set of mechanics, the game moves on. New mechanics are typically easy to pick up, and hints in the environment behind the puzzle are readily available. The Pedestrian never overstays its welcome, and concisely explores each new idea before introducing another.The Pedestrian, however, is not done once it has explored the world it has built. The last portion of this game throws an M. Night Shyamalan-esque twist, opening an entirely new dimension of gameplay, and turning the entire game on its head. Unfortunately, the twist on gameplay is not quite as seamlessly crafted as the rest of the game, both changing your goal in the puzzles, and providing significantly less guidance than before. Still, this twist in gameplay is extremely interesting and unique. As for the story, The Pedestrian ends with a new take on  in a rare, refreshing, and thought provoking manner among and about video games.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great little palate cleanser kind of game like Flower or ABZU. After beating a long or stressful game you can fall into a rut where you don't know what to do/play next. The Pedestrian provides a charming five or so hour puzzle game that lets you chill out and move on from the previous experience. The puzzles aren't too hard or have abstract gimmicks that are difficult to understand, just relax and take your time playing through it. The Pedestrian is a great experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This is a delightful little puzzle game. It has a nice supporting soundtrack, a good handful of puzzles with a steady, well-paced introduction of new mechanics, and the aesthetic of this game is rather charming. Difficulty-wise, the last puzzle was the only one to really give me trouble but even then I spent maybe 5-7 minutes on it max. Other than that, each puzzle is satisfying, makes you think, but shouldn't stump you for more than a few minutes if you really think it out. My only warning is that I managed to beat the entire game in one sitting, clocking in at just under 3 hours. I strongly recommend picking this up if you like puzzle games, but please do yourself the favor of getting it on sale like I did.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is specially made for those who like to get all the achievements in games.Some gameplay spoilers ahead. The Pedestrian is a 2D/2.5D  puzzle platformer where you control a stick figure like the ones used in traffic signs (hence the name of the game) across several different zones. Each puzzle has different boards and there are different objects to use and interact with.The game doesn’t have a story in its traditional sense, only a sequence of different chapters where you go through different areas of a city, until you reach the end.The graphics are very simple in the foreground, only two colors are used in the boards  where you solve the puzzles, but the backgrounds are 2.5D and very detailed, realistic  and dynamic, with greeting lighting, effects like rain and objects moving. I think this contrast works very well and gives a sense of depth that a simple 2D game wouldn’t have.The music is excellent but different from what we usually see in puzzle games. It varies from a jazz or lounge band music to something more orchestral depending on the chapter and the mood, that varies from melancholic to hopeful. Something else I noticed is how the music stops when you’re solving a puzzle and starts playing again after you solve, acting as a sort of reward and encouraging you to continue.The puzzle design is very well done and enough new mechanics are added on each chapter to avoid repetition and keep the gameplay fresh and exciting. Overall, to solve the puzzles you need to link the boards correctly and use the switches and objects in a specific way and in the right sequence. Some took more time than others and got stuck in a few because I missed one detail. In the final level things get a bit more meta and you’ll probably struggle to figure out what’s happening, but once you do you’ll realize how cleverly it was designed.    10 Achievements. Around 4,5 hours, without help. Easy, in general, but has some harder puzzles. Easy, one achievement for each chapter, no missables.   The Pedestrian is a great 2.5D puzzle platformer, with amazing graphics and an OST that is a delight to listen to. The game’s puzzles are very well designed and very original, something that isn’t easy to pull off nowadays.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Nice, simple, but challenging puzzle game. Unlike many other "puzzle" games, the challenge isn't in figuring out complex mechanics *before* actually solving the puzzle. Here the puzzle is the challenge, which should be obvious but I find many puzzle games fall into that trap. It's very atmospheric and tranquil, and provides a relaxing experience. If you're looking for a real ball buster this isn't it.The puzzle concept, the pacing, and the tranquil atmosphere the game portrays are really solid, and the score adds to that as well. Because of these, it was a very pleasant overall experience!The main two things I didn't like so much were the length of the game, and the background score presence. I felt the game was too short, which was a little disappointing. I felt that I spent a little over what I got (bought at full price). As far as the music, if you spend too much time on a puzzle, the score will just stop playing completely, like the orchestra is just waiting on your dumb ass to finish the puzzle. Like "Man I'm not playing until this guy solves this thing". it felt somewhat comedic but also a little awkward when that would happen. This one didn't ruin the game for me per se but I did find it a little annoying.I loved the fun puzzles, the unique concept, and the pleasant, mellow overall experience, but what hurts the game is the length. I personally wouldn't recommend full price, but I do very strongly encourage everyone to eventually give this a go.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely amazing game, the puzzles were simple enough that you can solve them just by thinking about the puzzles while not pulling your hair out. The platforming, while simple, was still thought of deeply and was designed immaculately. Very much so recommend, also absolutely avoid spoilers for the final area of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not sure why this game gets such positive reviews on Steam. It is a reasonable puzzle game, but I wouldn't rush to buy another game from the same developer.My biggest issue with the game is the it is very flaky. You can get stuck, placing a movable item in the wrong location, and you can't pick it up. You can't reset the level, because there are no levels, just areas. Sometimes to restart an area you have to pull apart your work. Worse, a few times I had to exit the game to reset the area - sloppy coding.Sometimes, when I got stuck it was because an new game play element wasn't properly explained. Not the kind of puzzle solving I enjoy. The final area was annoying - up until that point I solved everything on my own. However the final area was so annoying I just consulted a walkthrough so I could watch the ending, which was boring.I'll recommend it because it is a reasonable puzzle game, possibly worth buying on sale (but not for me).

_childDocuments_.review: I love puzzle games, and this was top tier. So much so, a week or 2 after playing I still felt the need to give them a good review.Art style is amazing.The level designs and transitions are beautiful.The Puzzles are tricky but satisfactory.All the puzzle features are introduced in such a clean tutorial I didn't even realize it was a tutorial until I was finished with it. By far my favorite puzzle is the last one. Moving bridges and boxes to get access to them in the "real" plane was very cool.10/10 would play blind again
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: If The Pedestrian's puzzles were by themselves it would be an ok puzzle game. One that isn't too challenging but still fun to play. The Pedestrian is so much more than just it's puzzles. The environments that the puzzles reside in are beautiful and detailed. The way you move throughout the game is so creative and unique (at least as far as I've seen). The progression of puzzles is also pretty good a lot of puzzle games introduce a few concepts at the beginning of the game and nothing else, but each section of the game introduces something new.What sold this game for me though was the ending. I don't think I've experienced an ending as unexpected, satisfying, and impressive as the ending of The Pedestrian. I would explain it but I don't want to ruin the experience for others.Some might disagree, but for the experience three hours is worth it in my opinion, if you think that 20 dollars is too much for three hours then just wait for a sale.Either way I 100% recommend this to anyone who enjoys puzzle games or if you're looking for a unique experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I played a fair share of puzzle games, and the Pedestrian is one of the best "2D" platform puzzle games added to my list of memorable ones. To describe this is as "2D" puzzle is kind of misleading; it is set in a beautifully sculpted 3D environment that adds to the visual ambience. Its 2D platform style isn't exactly new, but the unique mechanics it gradually introduces kept it interesting and had me hooked all the way. It's fairly challenging but never overstays in a a level mechanic for too long, nor it does not feel overly convoluted or cumbersome that you'll have difficulty remembering how all the mechanics coming together (unlike ). But the real payoff is  I haven't had a puzzle game stunned me in a while like Portal, The Talos Principle, The Witness, and that's saying something. All in all, it deserves 10/10. It's a well thought and planned unique puzzle game that everyone should buy and support the devs.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Short, but full of ideas, this puzzle game manages to use almost ever possible aspect of its mechanics to its fullest. Some riddles are a bit hard to solve due to their reflex-orrientated aspect (meaning more depending on quick fingers than logical thinking), but overall this is a very good entry for the puzzle genre. A hauntingly peaceful soundtrack and some vague hints of a story rounden up this experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: A fun puzzle game that finely executes its concept, taking the idea of a living pedestrian sign and building upon it with clever arrangement puzzles and well-placed interactions with the surrounding environment. The lovely soundtrack helps inspire the feeling of having a good time. The game itself takes about 2-3 hours to complete, depending on your puzzle skills.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - This game is fantastic for every reason imaginable. Buy it and play it. Please. It deserves more attention than it has. When I first laid my eyes upon The Pedestrian, I was certain that it was going to be a hit; the core concept was simply too endearing for it to not be one of the most hotly discussed releases of the year, and it was a Kickstarter project even! Surely, this had to find a considerable audience upon release, right? Imagine my shock when I saw that it was receiving relatively little attention compared to other games out there, even including some other fellow indie titles. I haven't encountered much discussion about this game at all, and it didn't even release during a particularly busy period.The worst part of this obscurity is that The Pedestrian deserves to be a hit. Every little inch of this game oozes charm, creativity, and quality. This game had me smiling from ear to ear, even when I was stuck scratching my head and wondering what to do next in a room. Let's start with the most pivotal part, in my opinion: the core gameplay. The Pedestrian is a puzzle game where you travel between street signs in a realistic 3D world. You connect doors, hook up wires, and do all sorts of other things that range from the expected to the fantastical. New mechanics are introduced at specific periods to shake things up, and all of them are introduced incredibly well. I was never confused on how a new mechanic worked or how it functioned, all the way up to the end. Every puzzle is designed wonderfully. All of them use the established mechanics in ways that test your understanding and knowledge of them in a way that feels appropriate, and there is never a point where I was asking "How was I supposed to figure THAT out?" The logic behind all the solutions is incredibly clear, even during the most challenging brain teasers. The puzzles get incredibly creative with the core mechanics as well, especially towards the later parts where some of the more unusual mechanics are introduced. Now, let's tackle one of the most blatant subjects here; the visual design in this game is STELLAR, both in the puzzles and the world they inhabit.The 3D world that these signs are plastered all over doesn't just feel like a playground for the player; it feels like a living, breathing world that people actually inhabit, and it feels like you're walking through a real place when you transition from one area to another. Cars drive by, the weather changes throughout the game, and you'll even see things like graffiti and stray personal items. The environments meet the level of detail that makes the world feel real, and all without it being overly distracting during puzzle solving. Textures are also great, and the game makes an excellent use of lighting and color. The most incredible thing about the high fidelity visuals, however, is that they don't make the game unplayable on lower end hardware; this game is incredibly well optimized. I played this on a relatively low end laptop that isn't even made for gaming, yet I was able to play this game just fine by simply adjusting the visual quality... and the game still looks great! The puzzles have great visual design as well. Every little icon is clear and distinct, and the game keeps track of what doors you've moved through and which ones you can move through eloquently with hardly any clutter. There's even visual variety; different locations have appropriately colored signs, and the game plays around with what counts as a street sign in some very fun ways. I can't leave out possibly the best part of this game's presentation: the soundtrack. The Pedestrian's soundtrack feels like a film score in the best way possible. Every track is sensational and sets a distinct tone when it plays; the entirety of the game's music is brimming with emotion and charming melodies. Honestly, I have no flaws to point out for this game; everything that it does is done incredibly well. This is an incredibly high quality game that's fun and delightful to boot. If you like a good puzzle game, a good platformer game, or a good game that's just all around creative and fun, I implore you to buy this game. At least try the demo.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a simple puzzler for the most part; however the last level completely changes the premise of the game and could have been better explained.  In general The Pedestrian is a 2D puzzle game with a nice background and some spasmodic but relaxing music.  It's a bit short and easy for it's price tag but in general worth getting for a mildly challenging few hours.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Not a particularly exciting game - it sets more of a contemplative mood with its slow meditative music and lonely backdrops. There is no undo button implemented, but the little tedium this entailed was generally bearable. Took around five hours to play through, and all achievements got unlocked along the way.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game, very pleasing to look at. The puzzles are unique and shows new game mechanics as you progress. But the game is not very long and it took me less than 5 hours to complete it. I think you could allow everyone to create and share their own levels so we can all continue to enjoy this great game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very cool, not very long, and also not very hard, but very cool indeed. It's not just a journey forward, solving some puzzles, but it really shines in introducing new game mechanics step by step without revealing the solution too quickly. I also very much enjoyed the puzzles that require you to solve a bunch of subpuzzles and retrieve items from them, not to mention the final puzzle, which blew me away once I figured out how that final game mechanic worked. I absolutely recommend this unique puzzle game and I would certainly love to see more of this kind, or even an editor to create your own mind-twisting puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This is a neat little puzzle-platformer that boasts a pretty interesting mechanic that takes some getting used to, but doesn't take long to master.The game takes place across various "signs" laid out in a variety of 3D areas -- where you're basically trying to connect a path for your character from the start to the finish. Some of the puzzles are fairly simple to figure out, just connect one or two entry/exit points and you're there -- while others take a little bit of planning/thought.The game does a pretty good job of introducing you to any new mechanics/controls, but is otherwise pretty hands-off.The rules are pretty simple -- if the sign can be moved (some signs are stationary), you're free to adjust the layout to make connections, etc., even after you "begin" the puzzle, but you're not allowed to disconnect anything you've already used, without resetting the puzzle state (later in the game, you will be introduced to something that bends this rule).Some of the puzzles are all single-screen, while some of the later ones are "fetch" missions where you go to other puzzle areas to retrieve items to solve a larger puzzle.For the most part, the game is pretty easy -- you can probably beat it in ~2-4 hours depending on your skill level, but nothing super crazy.Without spoiling anything, I think the way the material is weaved together to create a very interesting puzzle experience at the end helps bring everything together.Pros:+Easy to learn+Good for casual gamers+Innovative puzzle dynamic+Pulls off simple very well (not a ton of controls to remember/master)+Doesn't hold your handCons:-Pretty short (~3 hours of gameplay)-Achievements are 100% handed to you as you play-Not a lot of easter eggs or secrets to find (there's one that I found about midway through the game, but it's cosmetic only)-Puzzles could probably have been a little harder, background clues could have been spread out/broken up-Not a ton of replay value once you finish-Price is a little steep for what you getBottom line: If you're into puzzle games that don't take a ton out of you and want something fresh/new that'll be good to kill a few hours, check this one out.If game-for-your-money is more important to you, then pass on this one until it goes on a bigger sale
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: - Graphically, it looks outstanding for an indie. The city in which the game takes place is a visual feast from the dank sewers to the scenic college campus- I loved the variation in the signboard person motif. Your little man or woman will change appearance depending on the sign you're standing on, so the visuals stay fresh despite the simplistic design choice- The music stays thematically appropriate but tends lighthearted throughout- It's pretty much a straight up puzzle game. If there's a story, it flew well below my radar- The vibes more or less follow the visuals and music. When you're moving along the streets, the music is cheery to match the sunny visuals. When you're traversing the subways, the lighting and soundtrack take on a more serious, gritty tone- I did not expect the "twist" at the end of the game. I won't spoil it here, but it's a pretty cool surprise that comes out of nowhere- As far as puzzle platformers go, this one leans far more heavily into the puzzles than the platforming. Contrary to the deviousness of some of the puzzle design, you're not going to have to dodge too many obstacles or make difficult jumps very often- Although the puzzles begin easy and become pretty tricky by the end of the game, what lies between is a little uneven in its difficulty. Some of the puzzles preceding the penultimate chapter are surprisingly simple- Although it'll probably be a while, I wouldn't mind playing this one again. Sure, you'll almost certainly get all your achievements on the first playthrough, but the game is interesting enough visually and mechanically to warrant a second look down the road- All in all, this game was a pleasant surprise. The trailer and reviews definitely made me optimistic, but my expectations were still exceeded- In spite of the good times, it's a little on the pricey side for a game you can 100% in 4-6 hours- The game won't tax your system too badly and ran very well- . The price is a touch steep and would benefit from a more natural progression in difficulty, but there's enough fresh ideas here to make it stand out in a crowded genre. Definitely worth picking up for the right price

_childDocuments_.review: A short but quality puzzle gameIt's quite a clever concept, and the design is great as well.The game doesn't tell you what or how to do anything, you have to figure it all out on your own. However, thanks to the learning curve and intuitive design, you're never thrown anything insurmountable. A lot of the puzzles were satisfying, leading to many ah-hah! moments, and small bursts of triumphant joy.That being said, I had put the game down for quite a while. I bought the game alongside a bunch of other games during a steam sale, played a bit, probably got bored/wanted to get to some of the other games I bought, and put the game down. I finally came back almost a year later (and although I forgot some of the mechanics) got back into it, and enjoyed the game up to the satisfying end.I found the puzzles to be satisfying, although I never found myself stuck (gameplay time includes time I paused the game and went to eat, etc.) Which leads to one of the problems... The game is short. But perhaps that's not a bad thing, because as much as I enjoyed the puzzles, I had gotten bored enough to put the game down for a year. I think if you just sit down and try to marathon the game, you'll get tired like I did. Which is a shame, since the game really is pretty good in smaller doses (maybe don't leave the game so long that you forget all the mechanics though). But that leads to the other problem: it's expensive. I'm not saying the game creators don't deserve to get paid, it's not a reflection on them. But as a consumer, I think the price is a bit steep for something that is fun, yet short and doesn't have a lot of replay value. It has nice graphics, but 99% of the gameplay has nothing to do with the beautiful graphics and everything to do with 2D Game&Watch graphics. There is only one save slot, which is not a huge problem if you play by yourself, but midway through I thought: "This would be a good puzzler for my kids to try."So overall, the game is great for what it is. It's worth buying, especially if you wait for a sale. Don't play too much all at once, and if you do put the game down, make sure to come back to it someday. It's not perfect, but it's worth playing to the end.8/10Positives:+ A lot of good puzzles+ Clever and intuitive design that doesn't require tutorials and long exposition.+ Nice presentation, good background graphics, clean puzzlesNegatives:- Short- No replay value- Expensive at full price considering the length
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: If I were to break up my thoughts into segments, I would just be repeating myself. Everything about this game is so incredibly crafted from the gameplay and controls to the aesthetic to the puzzles to the plot. Yes, this game has somewhat of a plot! Every element of the puzzles is communicated efficiently and clearly and the gameplay is perfectly suited to it too. Put simply, this is a side-scrolling 2D platformer featuring a number of signs you have to link up, move objects between and progress to the next area. The art style is wonderful as most of the focus is on the signs you are platforming in, but the detail in the backgrounds and 3D environments has just as much care and detail as the signs! I don't want to spoil anything in the game as many elements are introduced so smoothly and logically but there is never a dull moment where a puzzle is just a repeat of a previous one. This is how you make a puzzle game! This is such a charming little platforming game! The art style and overall concept of the game is beautiful and at each and every turn, something new and innovative is introduced. The puzzles are at just the right difficulty to make it challenging but not frustrating and

_childDocuments_.review: So I want to start out by saying that, without a doubt, this is a well made game. The music and visuals and game-feel are absolutely excellent and I have nothing bad to say about them. I also think that the gameplay on offer here will be appealing for a lot of people (clearly it must be, given the Overwhelmingly Positive review average). The problem is, it just wasn't for me.I think my problem with The Pedestrian comes down to the basic mechanics. The act of connecting signs with other signs just doesn't require a lot of lateral thinking - most puzzles can be solved by correctly identifying the solution condition and then working backwards from there procedurally. Over time, the game adds more mechanics, like bouncy platforms and lasers and wires the change the state of the external world, but these elements usually don't combine dynamically in ways that force you to reconsider how you solve puzzles. They just become additional steps between you and the solution.Over time, these additional steps wore on me. Early in the game when I was still solving learning the mechanics and solving puzzles quickly I really enjoyed the game. But the joy I got out of the game at that point wasn't about puzzle solving, it was the joy of completion, the kind of joy you get from untangling a knot. By the halfway point, however, the knot was so tangled that the process of unraveling it became frustrating, even though it wasn't "hard" per-se.So yeah, The Pedestrian is definitely a well made game. But it isn't the kind of puzzle game that I like.

_childDocuments_.review: A puzzle game where you connect different "rooms" of the level and solve puzzles to traverse an urban environment. You do this by connecting different exit points on each tile and then go through them with the stick figure avatar. Connections can’t usually go through other tiles. The game proceeds to layer more mechanics and tile interactions as you go through the game. The game is a bit on the shorter side, although the length can vary depending on how much you struggle with the puzzles. I was done in about three hours. If you’re using the old formula of 1 dollar = 1 hour, then this game is probably not worth it to you. So, is the game worth the price?I bought the game with the 25 % discount and I’d say that was money well spent. It bought me an evening with pleasantly difficult brain teasers, a soothing soundtrack and gorgeous transitions, backgrounds, and set pieces. However, the game inevitably feels short. Many times throughout the game I thought to myself “hmph, that’s a really interesting idea, I’m curious where’ll they go with this”. They never went anywhere. The last level of the game (potential SPOILER:) uses this interesting fresh idea that could easily be its own game but does so only once and then the game is over,I guess that’s it. I was left wanting more. I’d be hard-pressed to recommend this game at the full price. At a discount though, for the price of roughly two movie tickets, I got a three-hour-long session of intellectual masturbation. Worth it.And if you're still on the fence, download the free demo and see for yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: The Pedestrian is a wonderful, albeit short puzzle platformer.-The core puzzle design is incredibly well done and enjoyable throughout. Everything is wordlessly explained seamlessly. Some of the puzzles are rather ingenious, and it does a good job of slowly introducing new mechanics. I particularly liked the "paint" near the end of the game; that was quite clever and it took my brain a little time to adjust.-You play as the little gendered icons you see on bathroom signs and you travel from puzzle piece to puzzle piece by physically traversing a city (New York? Looks like New York?). If that sounded a bit confusing, just look at a trailer, it's quite neat. I enjoyed this quite a bit and was always looking forward to seeing what new environment it'd send me to. You'd think the environments would be nothing but neat little background graphics, but the game actually uses them within the puzzles a lot. Loved this aspect of the game.-I had the game idle for a bit, so expect about 4-4.5 hrs of total playtime. It's quality the whole way, but it's a tad bit of an underwhelming package. There isn't a "finale" which puts together all the mechanics in one maniacal set of puzzles; it just sort of gets slightly more difficult then ends. -Overall, the game is quite easy. The first ~2.5 hours I didn't even have to stop and think for any of the puzzles. I just kind of solved them right away. So, you take that out and there's about 2 hours worth of quality, challenging puzzling here. Even those 2 hours aren't all that difficult either, which is a shame because I think puzzle games in particular really need to hit a certain level of challenge to ascend to the next level. It's all well designed and clever, but never fiendish. And I like fiendish.-There's a story somewhere in here, but I couldn't parse it. I googled it once I beat the game, and it seems like no one else really understood it (or cared to understand it?) either. It doesn't really matter, the puzzles are the core of the game, but it didn't help make the ending less underwhelming. There are weird sticky notes that allude to ... stuff? ... but none of it forms a cohesive whole.-Maybe the worst thing about the game is the music. It doesn't loop! You play in silence for the majority of the game. The music that's there isn't all that great (pretty generic..) but I'd at least liked to have heard it over nothing. C'mon.-No saveslots, no way to jump and replay a particular puzzle (once you beat the game it just restarts you at the beginning), no bonus/challenge puzzles, no hidden puzzles / easter eggs, etc. It's a linear one-shot that expects you to beat it in a sitting or two and never touch it again. Which I suppose is fine. Just not going to make me love it as much as the all-time great puzzle games. Still very good though.The time you spend with The Pedestrian is great, and definitely worth it. What it does right greatly outweighs what it does wrong, and in the end, it's impossible not to recommend. Great puzzle game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very charming and stylistic puzzle game. The interactions are platformer-esque but you don't need any platforming skills to get through it. Each area has a sort of theme and usually a new mechanic, some are re-used periodically and some are layered but for the most part you never get overwhelmed with a puzzle that uses 800 different systems or anything. I did have to refer to a guide for one of the very last puzzles, because while it was technically very similar to previous ones, I missed some fundamentals about it early on that made me not realize what was going on. It's short and $20 is a hard sell to people but that's still cheaper than 2 movies in many areas and you get roughly that time here, and I would absolutely recommend it on sale for any puzzle fans. The art and design and sound are top notch and I loved playing through it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The game is beautifully made. Awesome job. I bought this partly because of the sale and partly because of the Steam rating.  The Steam rating is way out of balance.  It should be positive but not overwhelmingly.The puzzles are fine but just aren't that interesting. And the ending is twist but not in a good way and left me just saying "what?" Then I felt conflicted because I was glad it was over but was also annoyed that it was so short.Edit: I guess I should have played the demo (I didn't notice it had one until after posting this review)
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This game was absolutely gorgeous. The controls were smooth and the platforming felt very natural.The puzzles felt very creative and slowly introduced a ton of interesting mechanics. I definitely liked some of the puzzles more than others (the ones where you have to connect a bunch of the puzzle pieces in the right order were a bit tiring for me) but on the whole I thoroughly enjoyed the whole game.It only took me 2-3 hours to complete though, and at a $20 price tag, that's just not worth it (at least on my student budget). I would highly recommend buying it on sale!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This is the whole package.Interesting, but intuitive and logical puzzle design.Simple and naturally intuitive controls, despite the mind-bending world presentation (and that is saying something, honestly).Brilliantly executed aesthetic.Non-verbal narrative that does seem to say something interesting about how we view the world around us.And not a single bug encountered in my entire playthrough and I can't remember the last time I could say that.It's not a long play through but, to paraphrase Yahtzee Crosshaw talking about Portal, that's not necessarily a bad thing as it doesn't try to overstay its welcome.  The pacing and playthrough feels right on point to me overall and I was able to play through in about 4 hours.Simply excellent.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: I took my time with this game and admittedly left it running when I was away from my PC by accident a few times. LOL So my true playtime is probably about 10 hours maybe 11. However, I really enjoyed so much of this game! Some of the puzzles had me super confused because I kept forgetting that you can pause your character and make some adjustments but mostly because my brain tried to over complicate the puzzles more often then I'd like to admit. There's moments one has to remind themselves that the simplest answer just might be the answer or work backwards if you can. The backgrounds were so beautiful too and the music was awesome! I wish there was even more to this game! Great job and fun puzzle game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good puzzle game. The visual presentation is the highlight here. There are some good puzzle ideas, not super challenging. Implementation of the mechanics is really solid, and I admire that even the rare physics/timing based ones avoided being fiddly. The final part was needlessly irritating because the controls can't be configured, but that be my only real criticism.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: I lovee the pedestrian. If you love puzzle game, i think you will also love this game. I think there is little to no story in this game, just a simple puzzle grinding game but I have no problem with it. It's fun to see the stickman interacting with the puzzle while the actual thing in 3D world also change. Towards the finale,  thus I can't continue finishing the game. Decided to take a rest for a bit but for sure I will come back to finish it!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Think game is a great relaxing platform puzzler with intriguing mechanics. Several points in the game challenge me to think outside of the box. The scenery is interesting and has nice ambient music. The math puzzle felt repetitive. These could be made harder but those were few and far between.Haven't played a puzzle game this unique since the portal series & manifold gardens. If you likes these game then I think you will enjoy it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: "The Pedestrian" was a delightful combination of side-scroller + puzzle game which relied far more on logic than quick reflexes. The puzzles built on one another well and each completion gave a satisfying moment of "ah ha!" upon completion. I felt like each solve was "earned" and never felt I'd been given a "gimmie," or a puzzle that was arbitrary and reliant on luck to solve. I took about 11 hours to complete, though to be fair I was also enjoying playing through the game with my 8 year-old, so YMMV. :-) Well done to the team at Skookum Arts... I look forward to seeing what you come up with next!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The game's background looks nice and the basic idea is fine I guess, but ... for 95 % of the game that's it.Most of the time it's just quite easy, repeating 2D platformer puzzle without any story, comedy, or whatever you'd might like. The "beautiful" 3D background is just that - background without any meaning for the player at all (or I haven't seen any; I think it might be of some inside importance to the developer, but it gives nothing to the player). You don't have any option to look around, zoom, focus, etc. to explore it.I expected something similar to the ending twist from the beginning, and yes, it happened (predictable, but at least something fun). It's a shame though that it didn't come earlier, since it made the game much better, but just for like the last 10 minutes - I saw the potential, but it wasn't used fully, because the game ended right when it became interesting.Good puzzle games have something more in them - they are either hard or inovative (Baba is you), have story (Portal 1+2), have humor (Portal 2), are cute (Cats organized neatly), or if it's easy, it's non-repeating, or whatever. This game achieved it only in the last 10 minutes - if the whole game was like that, it would be great (finally some challenge, something new), or it could have had some story happening in the background (imagine seeing people doing something, maybe even interacting with the signs, might be fun), the work spent on the background was in fact pointless.I finished the game fully in 3 hours, the only thing I'll remember about it is that it was underwhelming, I had higher expectations of it.Oh yeah, and the price: 3 hour ok-ish game for 20 euros/dollars? Or for 6 when it's on sale? If I knew how short it was, I'd expect less than half that price (less than 10 normally and less than 3 in sale). I know that it's hard, time- and money-consuming to develop a game, but I would place it among 1-5 bucks worth games, sorry.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Well deserving of its acclaim. A very refreshing take on the puzzle genre that, instead of getting more difficult as the game progresses, it just gets more . Sure it builds on earlier lessons, but in new ways. You don't "first locate the corner pieces" for every new puzzle but stop to think, which puts  ahead of other modern puzzlers that become tedious without a revolving door of gimmicks.I particularly liked the game ending naturally with 100% achievements and that there weren't any trick tiles in the course of the game. With a free demo to try before you buy, this title's $20 list price is right on.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: A unique puzzle platformer, where the platforming takes place on signs or papers hanging in the real world.  The puzzles come from drawing lines from one exit to another on different signs, as well as interacting with objects such as keys and boxes.  Once your character uses a line though, erasing it resets the level.  Exiting a level means moving to a new real world area, and as you go on your actions can have interactions in the real world as well, such as moving an elevator.  As with all puzzle games, new concepts are added as you go through keeping your brain working and removing tedium.  Things such as being able to move the signs around, freezing the contents of a sign, etc.  It starts easy, and gets harder but never anything too brain-twisting, except for a couple that had me scratching my head for a while.  As the journey is as much of the experience as the puzzles, I won't go into more detail than that.Positives are good puzzle design, very unique experience, and by the end just kind of blowing up your expectations.  For negatives?  Nothing really to be honest, some of the later puzzles maybe were a bit convoluted or minorly tedious I guess.  Some levels were a bit dark or used drawing mechanics that were not as legible (chalk for instance).  The stick figure graphics might be a turn off for some, but not for me.  It fits the game.  And game length is short, but felt about right.  All minor things at most.Overall, a great game.  Due to the length I wouldn't buy it at full price personally but otherwise highly recommended for puzzle game lovers.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: A short but fulfilling puzzle game, with a focused concept, thought-out difficulty curve, and a calming atmosphere. Expertly designed, and it hit the sweet spot for me of bending my brain (especially in the second half of the game) in a super satisfying way, but never being obtuse, seemingly impossible, or headache-inducing like other puzzle games I've played recently can become (*ahem* Baba Is You  *cough cough* The Witness). Loved it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Since Portal 2 and the Talos Principle, I was looking for a good 3D puzzle game. The moment I saw the trailer of The Pedestrian, I was shocked by how interesting  its game design was. It is a puzzle platform game that proceeds with a 3D background. Puzzles themselves are really good and even gets more interesting with the new tools you have to use within them. If you loved Portal and Talos I think you will love the Pedestrian too. I'm really excited about the next game developers will make.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The Pedestrian is a unique and interesting blend of 2D puzzle-platforming with 3D navigation and interactions. The puzzle mechanics are well introduced and taught, and the 3D component of puzzles are concise and easy to grasp. The difficulty curve and puzzle progression are well balanced and give the player time to get used to each mechanic or behavior before introducing the next one. There were times where I felt a given puzzle was a bit overwhelming (as in, too many panels/possible connections), so I'd leave it for the day and return the following day with a fresh mind, thus allowing me to solve them more quickly.The graphics are very fancy, and I love how seamlessly the 2D and 3D components merge together. The UI is interesting and innovative, and the scenery is very detailed/high polished. The signs have a very simplistic design, but that actually helps gauge the puzzle more easily. Some more clarity between some elements would have helped. Namely, distinguishing between . Some wall details also seem superfluous/decorative, so it can be a bit confusing at first.The controls are smooth and easy to grasp and get used to, and there's enough wiggle room to make some platforming sections relatively effortless. Some player-object interactions are a bit fiddly at times, but never in a way that hampers your progress. The only time I had a bit of a struggle with controls was nearing the end of the game, when , as it involves keys/buttons that were already established for other purposes.Late game puzzles, with the newly established paradigm, feel like a missed opportunity for further exploration, as that type of gameplay lasts very shortly in comparison to the rest of the game. In fact,  introduces a neat mechanic that is only introduced in a large-scale puzzle with no tutorialization.Overall, it's a fantastic game with clever ideas, excellent execution and great graphics. However, as many noted, it is far too short of a campaign, and although I recommended this game to some friends, I advised them to wait for a sale. One way I think would make this game's price more adequate would be by introducing a level editor/workshop support, which I've heard is in the plans. That way, the game has more replay value than its 2-5 hours campaign, and more ideas can be explored by the community. I for sure would love to design some puzzles!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Been following this game's development for 3-4 years now.  It's come a long way, and I had to play it on release day.  Took me a bit under 4 hours to beat, and overall enjoyable.Pros:-Great art, both the 2D and 3D backgrounds-Good puzzles-Challenging but not smash your face into a wall hard-Nice progression of new tricks and gimmicks throughout-Atmospheric music, when there is musicCons:-Not my favorite control scheme and no ability to change the layout-Lack of puzzles from the 3-digit codes throughout the game-No secrets (except for 1 hat), easter eggs, post-game content, or other forms of replayability-The transition from 2D to 3D didn't seem needed at the end-Some fluff puzzle screens with trivial difficulty between the actual meaty ones.Solid 7/10 for a few hours, but no reason to ever boot it up again.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Neat little puzzler! I was able to finish in around 4 hours, but I play these types of games a lot. Some of the later puzzles, and especially the last one, could definitely stump someone for hours. But when I see the answer, it becomes obvious.I wish there was more to it, the concept and the story are very intriguing!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Wasted Premise: The Game.This review is from the perspective of somebody who loves pure puzzle games and platformers. I played The Pedestrian for around an hour, and judging from the way the game appears to be tracking my progress, I'm about 2/3 of the way through the game. The game is competent enough, it's just boring. You'll go through these rote puzzle exercises with mildly novel mechanics sprinkled throughout, but it wasn't enough to actually interest me. I eventually stopped playing when I reached a new puzzle area and, for the 4th time in a row, was faced with the exact same "go to 4 sub areas and bring back 4 objects" pattern. I could see the solution right in front of me, but since actually  solutions in this game is so bland, I just... didn't care.The core issue is that the major conceit of the game - that you're a 2d figure projected onto 2d signs in a 3d city environment - is . It's all just window dressing that has zero impact on the puzzles or gameplay. Every area I visited, I kept waiting for the game to actually involve the backgrounds in the puzzles in a meaningful way. Will they allow me, the player, to interact with 3d objects, like the buttons and levers that are on almost every screen, to open paths? Maybe draw on the signs, or rotate them? Unscrew signs so they can be moved? Open and close doors to cause new signs to come into frame and add to the puzzle? The answer to all of these questions, as far as I can tell, is "No." Your cursor exists just to drag signs around and connect doors and ladders. They might as well just be monochrome boxes on a pure white plane.Whatever cool puzzle ideas you might be EXPECTING the game to have, based on its premise, you'll probably be disappointed. It's incredibly bare-bones and simplistic. It's possible that something mindblowing happens at the end of the game (apparently it's very short,) but I doubt it. I'm too bored to bother getting there.-----------------------Edit: So, after reading some other reviews I decided to watch the ending on youtube, and now I'm just kind of annoyed.Yes, this game EVENTUALLY manages to explore an interesting 2d/3d freedom mechanic. This section of the game is about 15 minutes long and is the very last thing you do before the credits.I have no idea why the developers decided to make an interesting 15-minute game with 2 hours of boring padding at the beginning. The ending mechanics should have been the majority of the game. As-is, it's like the game FINALLY gets interesting, and then abruptly ends.Save yourself the money and watch a youtube playthrough on 2x speed.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: A very pretty puzzle game with unique mechanics and ideas.The puzzles are well designed and varied. But while it certainly has quality, I feel it lacks in quantity. I finished the game in 3 hours. While I know there are some secrets I missed and could've back-tracked for, 3 hours is still a very short game, especially for one with little re-play value. While exploration of the city is an integral aspect of the game, I cant help but feel if theyd spent less time crafting detailed environments that you cant actually walk in (but merely see in the background), they could've expanded the scope of the game.Nevertheless, it's a fun and extremely well-made game with an unprecedented mechanical twist at the end, so I give this game 8 / 10 pedestrians
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Supported this game on kick starter and can't say as I'm impressed by it.The gameplay is simple yet annoying, figure out the puzzle then walk your character through, got old really quick.The worst part for me was the first 5 minutes when you launch the game, you have to sit through a stupidly long intro scene there are no instructions to press the arrow keys to actually start anything, I thought my game just crashed but no, I had to randomly press keys to figure it out.Overall if I'd paid the steam price it might not be too bad but as a kick starter I feel totally ripped off by this developer.Just remember it took these guys 3 years past their delivery date to actually deliver the game, hopefully no bugs pop up or we'll be waiting another year for them to fix it.

_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian
