_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The good- Beautiful visuals. Nice, realistic graphics with various lighting and weather conditions and attention to detail even on small objects' design at extreme close ups. Although the 3d environments have actually nothing to do with the gameplay, they give it a strong atmosphere and a sense of exploration. Also, it's nice that the signs have a lot of different styles and colors, that alternate the aesthetics of each level.- Fantastically designed, creative puzzles. Well balanced difficulty level. They're challenging, but not too hard. The game introduces constantly new mechanics or ideas and the puzzles are evolving so they never feel repetitive. Each time a new mechanic is added, it does a great job to help you learn it with easier levels that get more difficult gradually. Great pace.- Good, responsive controls. Nice, smooth animations of the stickman.- Fantastic, relaxing music to accompany you while solving puzzles.- Great direction and cinematography. I didn't expect to say that for a puzzle platformer but the locations and the camera movement while moving from sign to sign are amazing.- There are some points that connects awesomely the 3d world with the 2d signs with a little bit of interactivity between them.- It has a few small levels that are almost pure platforming without puzzles. They're simplistic, but give you a nice break between the puzzles.- That trick at the very end is so cool.The bad- There is no plot at all (not counting the very last part). With all this great work at the environments you could easily imagine a storyline evolving inside the 3d background. That would give you a purpose and a whole new meaning to your actions. Now you just solve puzzles casually and the concept of a stickman teleporting from sign to sign doesn't even make sense.- Small duration. Each time that you have truly mastered a new mechanic, the puzzles' section ends. Maybe I just wanted more, but there is so much potential here. It feels like a lot more puzzles could have been added.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: it's good for what it is. Weird that they clearly spent so much effort on the 3D environments, even though it is actually just a very simple 2D puzzle platformer. The environments and concepts are cool, but the core puzzle gameplay is very repetitive. Essentially just arrange the rooms in a way that gets you to the objective. I guess you could say that about any puzzle game but this one felt very formulaic for some reason. The mechanics it introduces just feel like more steps between you and the goal instead of a puzzle.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun, creative puzzle game with pretty environments. Not too difficult, though it's a bit on the short side considering the price. You can expect to finish it within a few hours. I can't complain too much because I got it in a bundle but I do wish there were more puzzles, especially involving the late game mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The game is an absolute masterpiece, there is nothing in the genre (trust me! I played tons of puzzle indies) that requires you to configure your way out. The main game that you played is just a simple black and white drawing, what really satisfying about this game is that you progress along the city street, into the restaurant, into the subway, into the school, the game turns into an exploration adventure that you have no idea what is the next in line. Even if you are just pushing buttons or pulling a lever, you are actually interacting with the detailed, beautiful and vibrant world behind. While progressing through the story, the various relaxing background musics blend in so well with the game and environment. The main puzzle part of the game is brilliant, as mentioned briefly in the beginning, you have to move the map pieces around and connect the paths to make your way to reach the quest items or exits. It is a simple idea and the game is easy to understand in the start, but things get much more challenging when the game introduces the player to tiggers, laser beams, lifts, portals, keys to unlock doors etc. The puzzles may keep you stuck for 5 minutes, 10 minutes or even half an hour depends on your solving skills, the game however rewards you with a seamless journey across familiar city streets, but we often missed out the small things how lively it actually is in a different perspective. The Pedestrain is one of the best puzzle games in 2020, thank you Skookum Arts. It will be better if there is steam trading cards for the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The game was really good at making me use all my brain cells.The chapters are a good length and I liked the different mechanics. The game definitely has good graphics and I think that's where the price comes from a bit. As for the game length, I expected it to be a bit longer, but that may just be my personal impression. Still, it's a good game that delivers what it promises. If you are unsure, you can definitely buy it on sale or try the demo first.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: It's a relatively short but very unique game. During the entire game, you will constantly encounter new and interesting mechanics, The graphics are simply stunning - there's so much detail! If you look at my playtime, you may wonder: "Only 7 hours for a game THAT expensive?". Yes. All of those seven hours were filled with enjoyable gameplay, something you rarely see nowadays. If you prefer quality over quantity, this is the perfect game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The Pedestrian is a pure work of love. In puzzle-logic games what most people seek are the mind bending challenges & the reserved consecutive thoughts that will lead in solving X brain melter. The pedestrian offers a great deal of those with evolving mechanics that are satisfying to the core but it doesn't stop there !It holds an amazing presentation from beginning to the end with truly breathtaking sceneries, the graphics , lighting effects and camera movement are eye-candilicious  while the not-less-than-amazing lounge soundtrack accompanies ya in almost every part.8.5/10 for sure
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The pedestrain is a chill little puzzle game where you control a stick figure with the ability to jump from one map to another. Your primary goal is to help this little stick figure collect some unique parts for a device he's trying to build. Overall the game's very relaxing with only a few tedious sections. The game has no proper toturial and when new mechanics are introduced you'll 100% need to figure out how they work. This is fine for the majority of the game but there was 2 new mechanics that I didn't feel like were all that easy to figure out. It's quite a solid puzzle game but it takes about 3-5 hours to fully complete this game and there's no replayability so a second playthrough is very unlikely. The game's currently prized at 16,79€, this is way too much for what you get so I can't recommend it simply due to it's prize. However if it's on sale for 5€ I would definitely pick it up.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Fun lil puzzle game, starts off pretty easy and light, last few levels made me sit there and think, but not in an annoying way. Really cool aesthetic and mechanics complement the puzzles. Definitely worth picking up when on sale, those with experience with puzzles can prob bang this out in 5 hours or less.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: It's a cool game with a really cool concept, but if you happen to have a history of getting motion sick at all from games, you may want to take that into consideration before purchasing.I rarely get motion sick from games but the way that the camera floats around I had to stop after 2 hours of play because I was starting to feel queasy. I don't think I'll be able to complete the game because of this. There isnt anything in the settings that I could find to change this either.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This was one of the most unique puzzle games I've ever come across. It mixes simple platforming mechanics with an interesting room connection system that increases in both complexity and difficulty as you progress. It never feels too challenging but the highly detailed 3D backgrounds you traverse through gives you the experience of traveling through a real world. Though the minimal story isn't immediately obvious to the player, it's purpose is delineated through your progression towards the ending location. This entire 3 hour experience is more about the journey than the destination itself. Artistically speaking, there's a lot to enjoy here but if you're looking for really challenging brain-twister, this isn't what you'll find. Instead, just sit back and relax to the calming soundtrack while you decipher what this game is all about.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: I've been watching this game for awhile, waiting for it to release. I've been through the demo probably ten times, and never stopped enjoying it.The final game has exceeded all of my expectations, and I've only been through perhaps 15 or so levels. I cannot wait to see what more is in store.Thank you for producing such an excellent game! Well worth the wait.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, quite a good puzzle game.  Other than a couple of bits that really caught me up, the puzzles tended to be just the right level of challenge to make you think but not hold-up progress.  The game gradually introduces more complex puzzles, ensuring you are entirely familiar with previous elements before introducing others.  I was also particularly happy about how the challenge-level waxes and wanes.  The puzzles gradually build-up in complexity until you get the big puzzle for the 'level,' then you get a series of easy puzzles to wind-down with.The final minutes were a little weird.  It suddenly shifted from pure puzzle to something that implied the whole game had a larger narrative.  I probably missed something, as this made absolutely no sense to me.  I have no idea what this narrative was supposed to be, or what was happening in the final section of the game.  This did not hinder my enjoyment of the game, however!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a neat little puzzle game! Even though the basic concept is simple, it is explored thoroughly with new challenges and gameplay mechanics around every corner. I had a lot of fun playing this since the difficulty of the levels was pretty balanced. You can tell that quite a lot of work went into making this game, even just by looking at the beautiful background and listening to the pleasant music. On top of all that, the creativity of the last level had me in awe.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This game can be summed up with a single word: Amazing. Everything from the gameplay to the art is perfect in this game. It was like a 4 hour long movie and I enjoyed every bit of it, taking my time to admire the scenery and enjoy the music, while challenging me with some puzzles that can all be overcomed (even though some took me quite a bit of time). Anyway the pedestrian was a refreshing little game, and one that I'll probably play again !
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The primary flaws: The Pedestrian is very short (like 3-6 hours for most), and is inconsistent in both quality and difficulty.  As a puzzle concept the game is satisfying and well-implemented, but not thoroughly explored. Especially at the end it feels like new mechanics are introduced at a much faster rate than they are actually being used, such as the  for example, which adds a mind-bendingly awesome mechanic but then uses it exactly once. On top of that, many of the puzzles are often simple "tied knot" puzzles (essentially just re-ordering the few available actions until one works), or "remember to bring the box" puzzles (where a long series of steps is meant to make you forget that the box at the beginning of the level is still available when you get to the last ledge). There are a few times when it's clear the designers got extra lazy, such as the repeated detail between major sections where a three-digit numpad sits adjacent to a note with three handwritten numbers as if that were a puzzle. The point I suppose is to make interactions thematic, but in such a short game having that specific interaction and others like it over a dozen times feels more like padding.The games strongest features is the fantastic environments. Despite the low polygon counts and texture resolutions that reveal its low-budget nature, the detail and design of the world still brings everything to life. There's palpable energy as you travel between different kinds of signs, each one shaking or swinging slightly from the traffic below. On the other hand, probably the weakest aesthetic aspect of the game is the oddly-incongruous music, which despite demonstrating impressive technical composition skill, waffles aimlessly between epic like a fantasy adventure and brooding like a mystery. It doesn't help that the music punctuates the levels obnoxiously by starting and stopping in between puzzles.All in all, worth picking up on sale, but probably not at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: A cute 2D puzzle game with beautiful backgrounds that integrate with your puzzling. The puzzles escalate nicely with your understanding and it's enjoyable to do so.+ Simple, beautiful graphics.+ Resonsive controls, decent puzzles.- No support for 21:9.- Short-ish. About 2.5 hours with little replay value.It's alright. Glad I got it on a discount, though.

I know it is too early to review a game but I have serious HIGH hopes for it.Finally found the time to finish it and I was not disappointed. I loved this game 10/10. melted my brain cells.

_childDocuments_.review: Been playing this too much with a tired brain lol, it gets pretty mindbending near the end. _childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: For me, this is close to the "perfect" puzzler. I never got hopelessly stuck and resetting a puzzle is very simple. But it remained challenging enough that I didn't breeze through it. The music is solid and the story has a bit of intrigue (why are these signs here? what's the goal?).My only nitpick is that I wish the layout/camera for some puzzles was different so I could view more puzzle pieces.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The Pedestrian is a challenging puzzle/platformer that requires moving signs around that a stick figure will run across. You will need to position and connect them appropriately to solve each puzzle. The game has some great background visuals but you never really interact with them much. Overall, it's still a fun, short puzzle game that will likely take about 2-3 hours to complete.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Very interesting concept for a puzzle game. For $13 (Discounted) it is well worth.The difficulty isn't too hard, but rewarding for those who think through it. The last part of the puzzle was very amazing.Really like the little details of the environment, and I learned that the developers had to manually set camera angles and movements for each stage, which just showed how much work they put into.Chill music, and I wish there will be more!Will probably play again when I forget the solutions.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: A solid puzzle adventure. Players take on the role of a pedestrian sign protagonist and venture through well-designed puzzles through varying environments. The soundtrack was quite relaxing and an enjoyable listen, the puzzle difficulty felt just right, and the game was visually appealing and engaging.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

The last puzzle combines both the 2d and 3d world and I think that would have been cool to see a bit more of.As I have an ultrawide monitor running at 3840x1080 resolution, there is an issue with the game not displaying in ultrawide. _childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Great puzzle game with the exception of the last puzzle. Would have like this game more if it wasn't included it all instead of ending on a low note. The other parts of the game are a delightful puzzle platformer with low consequences for failure. The last puzzle introduces a new mechanic which is kind of neat, but the gameplay includes a new nauseating first person perspective in a 3D world, definitely not what I signed up for.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: I so, so, so, sooooo love the game mechanics in this game. It's great and I refuse to spoil any of it. The game also looks great, plays great, sounds...well, okay sometimes the music stops playing in maybe a not intended way but its okay I was thinking too hard to notice most of the time. My only complaints are:1. There doesn't seem to be separate volume controls for the Sound effects and Music.2. The mechanics for the last level messed with the motion sickness a bit. I had to take long breaks to handle it and even then definitely didn't enjoy it as much as the rest of the game despite still loving the mechanics introduced for that part. (And there was no FOV setting I could adjust to make the motion sickness go away.)Other than that, I have no complaints. This is a great game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The Pedestrian is an interesting and charming puzzle game that reminds itself to have a story by the end. I believe the ending is open to interpretation and for that reason and possible (honestly irrelevant) spoilers I won't share mine and leave you to reach your own conclusions.I wouldn't say that's the main focus though, this is really just a relaxing puzzle game in which you play as a street sign stick figure and go through multiple levels presented, among other things, on signs. The game succeeds at challenging the player as every time you get the hang of a puzzle mechanic, it introduces a new one.Pros:-Good graphics (outside the simplistic focused part of the game).-Creative style and approach to the environment.-Brain teasing puzzles.-No monotony as new mechanics are frequently introduced.-Right balance in terms of difficulty. Easy enough to be entertaining rather than frustrating, hard enough to get you to stop and think.Neutral:-Multiple branching puzzles. Certain puzzles require you to go through other puzzles which sometimes require you to go through yet more puzzles just so that in the end you can solve the main one. I don't think it's either a Pro or Con, but I still feel like it should be pointed out as some people find that annoying.Cons:-No chapter select.-No puzzle quick reset option. I often found myself wasting some time having to manually undo my solving on specific puzzles in order to rethink my approach. A quick reset would have made that easier.-The last three'ish puzzles present a totally new gameplay style. It's an interesting change of pace, but it also makes the puzzles (mainly one) really confusing to solve as at first there isn't much of an indication of how they work. Note that this isn't a comment on their difficulty, but rather on how confusing they are.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely brilliant. Not terribly difficult; only a handful of puzzles really made me think for a bit. But boy was this fun to play and it's way more beautiful than it has any right to be. The developers could have done way less with the scenic design and still had a fun game on their hands but they really went the extra mile and the game is that much better for it. At 4 hours, it felt a bit short, but on the plus side, I never felt like it was dragging on for too long.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Game is fun.Puzzle are sometimes ok sometimes on the weird side because it's a mechanic that hasn't been taught yet.That is the negative point for me, I looked up 2 or 3 times solution on a guide because I was stump on some mechanics.I had fun, after finishing it, the price may be a bit high for the content but it was fine by me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This game is excellent! A must buy for puzzle fans. The puzzles could have been a bit more difficult at times, but there were plenty of times I had to bend my mind. Once you understand how the puzzle works, however, things tend to fall into place. Still, the visuals, the music, and the gameplay are top notch.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: I loved The Pedestrian's concept from the moment I saw the trailer, and the actual game did not disappoint. The puzzles would be fun without the theming, but the experience really is heightened by their impact on the surrounding world. Occasionally I'd feel stumped by a puzzle at first glance... but after taking a break and returning with fresh eyes, the "light bulb" moment always arrived.I did wish for an easier way to reset puzzles in the game's first half: I ended up quitting and restarting a few times rather than backtrack. And my brain stutters a bit while switching between character control and cursor-based puzzle manipulation (in this or any game that combines the two). Small complaints aside, The Pedestrian was everything I'd hope for in a short and sweet, dimension-hopping puzzle experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The pedestrian is  what it says it is. A short puzzle game with a twist. You play as, what seems to be, a sentient stick figure. You play by rearranging and reconnecting public signs in order to explore the city and advance through the game. You start out on a white board in an office and make your way through several different environments by connecting signs with lines, moving the signs around, platforming, unlocking doors, collecting objects, and sometimes even stopping time to reset only certain things, all to solve puzzles to get to an unknown destination. Whether it’s safety signs in a warehouse, a chalkboard sign outside a coffee shop, or a street sign hanging high above a freeway with cars driving past, The Pedestrian manages to keep things simple and stick to it’s goal to be a side scrolling puzzle platformer. If you watch the trailer or even look at the screenshots of the game you will get exactly that if you purchase. I imagine if you’re already interested in buying this game, as long as puzzle games are your jam, then you will absolutely love this game. If you think for any reason that it may not be something you’ll enjoy, well, then move along, because this game is not trying to be anything else. The puzzles are mostly towards the easy side with a few headscratchers. I think I got stuck for maybe 10 minutes total between two puzzles in the entire game and one of them was the final one, which was absolutely excellent. Trying to figure out some of the more difficult ones was fun and challenging without feeling obnoxious, and each of the sections are so well designed and add new ways to interact that the game doesn’t overstay its welcome. In fact, about the only negative thing I have to say, and even then it’s being slightly nitpicky, the game is a bit short for the non-sale price. It feels like a good length for a game of this style, but if you’re paying $20 for it then you’re basically paying $10 an hour for this game, as it does not have any additional side content or challenges added to it to extend play time. Once you finish it you are , much like this review is now! Unique puzzle game that is gorgeous and engrossing: Length and no additional challenges/level creator/ side content.Thanks for reading  and please let me know if you found this review helpful at all!Cheers!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: is a puzzle-platformer with an emphasis on its heavily logic-based puzzles over the jumping and dodging. The protagonist traverses various street signs, progressing to the next section by completing a set of challenges. Solving the game’s main puzzles often requires collecting a number of items from other areas which in-turn involve puzzles and platformer style obstacles.The game takes place on simple street signs against a mix of detailed, industrial and metropolitan backdrops ranging from grubby to colourful and bright creating an interesting contrast. Overall, the art style is clean with polished models and atmospheric lighting.Overall, The Pedestrian is aesthetically pleasing and will provide around 6-7 hours of satisfying gameplay. It has a surface level simplicity that, along with the gradual introduction of puzzle elements make it very accessible whilst also providing a real challenge, especially toward the end of the game. It is clearly a labour of love and I’d definitely recommend it to fans of puzzle and puzzle-platformer games, however, it definitely places emphasis on problem-solving and might not be for anyone looking for a more fast-paced platformer focused experience.For a more detailed review of The Pedestrian, complete with a second set of opinions, please visit .

_childDocuments_.review: I came across the demo of  quite coincidentally and was instantly stunned by the combination of a 2D puzzle game put into a nice looking 3D world that's connected from the beginning until the end. So I couldn't resist getting the full game to see what more it has to offer...There are quite a few mechanics and objects being introduced while playing the game to combine and to reach the next part of the game. That way it alwas keeps requiring you to think in different ways so the "levels" don't feel repetitive and sometimes you even seem to have a "puzzle in a puzzle". You can notice sometimes that they took some inspiration by 's famous  games. Also the  made by Logan Hayes just adds so much to the game.I finished  in  and I can't say I rushed. _childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This was an amazing puzzle game. The graphics looked stunning and it was so fun to go on the journey through the city. _childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Really cool game. It's short but to me the length is just right.It's not those difficult and complex puzzle games that makes you scratch your head, and the platforming doesn't require any precise timing. Just relaxing and satisfying.The background seems irrelevant to the puzzle at first but later they will get involved, and probably you'll have one or two wow moments. Oh and by the way the graphics are beautiful.If you really value money vs playtime, you can buy it on sale. But it's always worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The Pedestrian is cozy, clever, and tight. If you're looking for a 4ish hour puzzle game, this is quite nice. Puzzle solutions don't often ask you to make jumps of logic that haven't been clued by prior puzzles, but you'll still feel a little proud by conquering the harder puzzles. The music is great for thinking or relaxing to, too.The environments and implied plot, while lovingly created, are more window dressings though, so don't expect answers to questions beyond "how can I solve this puzzle". There are also a couple of concepts (both lateish in the game) that could have been presented slightly better. But overall, these are minor complaints. Well worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: I'd recommend it, but when on sale as it's quite short. But what there is is good. It's mainly a 2D puzzle game where you have to use logic to work out which order to do things and how to connect up rooms based on a small number of rules and constraints, which expand a little as the game progresses.There were only a couple of parts I found hard enough that it took me a few minutes to work out what to do, but it also wasn't so easy that I was bored or didn't need to think at all. Not the greatest puzzles I've ever played, but far from the worst either.I think my main criticism would be that most of the difficulty ramp came from adding lots of options and potential paths for you to consider and eliminate until you found the correct connections and path through them, rather than making you think of something genuinely novel or clever to solve a level (although that does happen in a couple of places, to the game's credit). But the puzzles never got so complex that they were overwhelming, at least once you started attacking them, and my mind was engaged throughout. It's a good puzzle game, but with a bit more it could've been up there with the very best. That still makes it worth a play.There are some quite interesting ideas at the end of the game which I wish it had explored further. Maybe if there is a sequel?Graphics are good, although textures and geometry could have had a bit more detail in places (at least playing on a huge TV). But the graphics are mainly a background thing, and are generally very good and go well above and beyond what was needed for what is mainly a 2D puzzle game, so I think they struck a good balance there, for a small team. It's also a neat combination of visual styles which I don't think I've seen before.Controls work fine, and I never struggled to do anything; the time was spent working out what to do, not convincing the game to do it, which is how it should be in a puzzle game. Well done there.No technical troubles to speak of.In summary, a short but sweat puzzle game. If they make another that expands on the ideas, I'll definitely pick it up.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The best six hours I wasted on a game!...and I took my time solving these awesome little puzzles!Sometimes one can get lost in the details of its background.Which puts a 2.5 dimensional puzzle game in a three dimensional environment and it seems to tell a wordless story of a journey through a city in the background.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Nice puzzle, game, for sure challenging enough. The graphics around the puzzle are nice and the game has a relaxed atmosphere. All puzzles are doable to solve by yourself if you take your time. For me it is a refreshing take on the puzzle genre that, instead of getting more difficult as you make progress, it just gets more different. Minus is that it's not clearly shown what some of the features you can use as you progress, actually do. I felt I had to play around with some of the signs just to figure out the mechanics exactly (for example the overlay-sign). Also the music cuts out occasionally. A good thing is that the variation keeps the game from becoming stale. Having said that, I can recommend this game for those who are looking for a challenging, relaxing puzzle game that can be all solved by yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The universe decided I am not smart enough to handle truly intellectual and brain smashing puzzle games like Stephen's Sausage Roll and The Witness and Baba Is You.  They are all great on their own but each one has a point (different for each player of course) where things are no longer fun and you just feel like an idiot.  Maybe it's in the first 15 minutes.  Maybe it's in the last hour.  But each time ended up with a cold unloving screen staring at me in disappointment while I realized that nothing is more pathetic than looking up a walkthrough for a puzzle game. And then enters The Pedestrian which solves this problem.  The game doesn't necessarily get harder, it simply...changes.  The mechanics change, the setting changes, but the game is never just simply hard for the sake of being hard.   And the world it exists in is so alive, I realized just how dead every other puzzle game is.  You just jump from stencils to street signs to blueprints to paper while traffic flows underneath and each puzzle is sharply crafted to make you think (but not punish you for not having an IQ of 150).  The music is beautiful too, I honestly can't think of a better puzzle game than this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. It starts off relatively simple but doesn't take long to become challenging.  I also loved the unique soundtrack and clever product placements.  Wow.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This game was really amazing. The difficulty of puzzles is well balanced, the "story" is great, and those *** graphics, they're absolutely awesome. _childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Great, unique puzzle game with beautiful music and interesting, varied environments. The puzzles never get stale, and despite finding some parts a bit tricky, it never reached any level of annoyance. The game doesn't stretch itself too thin either, it lasts the perfect amount of time (around 5 hours). In terms of issues, I suppose the only thing I could point to is the lack of replay appeal. That said, you'll still have that first memorable experience if you only end up playing it once, especially considering the ending, which I was pleasantly surprised by. Overall, I believe this game is absolutely worth it, so this is an easy recommend to anyone. There's a demo too, so you can try that out.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The Pedestrian is a quaint little puzzle-platformer, that leans more to the puzzle side of that term. The concept and art style as well as the music are all exceptional and the way the game plays out was surprisingly unexpected. You could say that its pretty short runtime is a negative but in my opinion, that just means it's the perfect game for an afternoon gaming session. Overall, The Pedestrian was a fun puzzle game with a ton of charm and I recommend it to anyone who enjoys the genre. Also shout out to Columbus game devs!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: 100% a great game that blew my expectations out of the water and is without a doubt almost a must play game only thing holding me back from being a must play is its playtime mine ending at 6 hours which is steep for the price and would love to see the developers make a sequel or a secsessor to this game and loved the additions found the further into the game. _childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This game was great! Wow. I enjoyed the puzzles, the artwork, the music. Absolutely fantastic. _childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: I've never seen puzzles that were so well designed to be challenging, but not frustrating.  At first glance they seem impossible, but within a few minutes you've solved them.  This game is amazingly well polished, from the control to the esthetic to the story telling.  It really kept you guessing, right to the end.  It's amazing this wasn't designed by a triple A studio.  The platforming is easy, which was the right choice for this type of game.  If you're looking for an enjoyable puzzler to use different parts of your brain, you can't go wrong with The Pedestrian.  I found it randomly because I liked the title, and I'm so glad I did.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: What did I like? All of it, all of the little 4-5 hours of gameplay. Puzzles are great, the idea is completly new and I had a lot of fun. But for 23$CA+tx, I find that 4 to 5 hours of puzzle is not that much if you compare to other games like We were here 1-2-3 and The Room 1-2-3 which are also from independant devs and cost approximatly the same for 3 times the gametime. Don't get me wrong, the game is awesome, but for the time I played, I'm glad I got it on summer sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: I don't have a lot of time in the game,  at the time of writing about 10-15 minutes.  However it is a puzzle game,  I have a good grasp on how it is going to play since the rules, while increasing in complexity,  are intuitive and have a sensible progression as you move through the game.  The premise is simple, you're a 2d guy who travels through from sign to sign.  Weird right?  Not a concept that makes much since on the surface,  but it isn't supposed to make sense.   The signs placed throughout the world interconnect via passages which are sometimes hard linked,  which cannot be changed,  and sometimes you have to link point to point,  the points are designated with a direction component,  so a left facing door can only connect to another right facing door a ladder at the top of the sign can only connect to a ladder at the bottom of another.   The signs can be moved around within each local puzzle and to continue onward one must create a path to the next off screen exit.   Watch the trailer, that's all you need to understand.   It is a simple game at its core,  but I feel the puzzles will become much more challenging as the door is open for a whole lot of complexity in this design.  That's pretty much the how of it all.   Now what I haven't yet mentioned are the visuals.  I mean you're a lackluster little stickman,  stickmen aren't pretty,  they're sticks, well or stickwoman as you can select your character,  there's much more to it than this,  the ambience of the world outside of the signs where your character resides,  a visual representation of his travel in 2 dimensional space through a 3 dimensional world which feels alive and dynamic which adds a nice bit of presentation to the game.  Overall,  I like it.   10 minutes in I can't say whether I have any complaints yet,  but I am enjoying it.   If you don't hear back from me and my time played has increased,  then I still have no complaints.   Give it a go,  this is a novel concept for a puzzle game and looks to be a single indy dev,   While the price tag feels a bit high, I don't feel faulted for paying it,  since I'm supporting an obviously talented and creative dev.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: A cool puzzle platformer with a nice difficulty curve. Doesn't get too hard and flows nicely. The puzzles introduce concepts regularly, keeping them fresh and interesting, with a last-act twist that I really wish more of the game had been built around. Moving around the environment seems to suggest a story, but I didn't really understand what it was supposed to be.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely beautiful game - the entire experience is well crafted, the puzzles are challenging without being too difficult yet no cakewalk.  The visuals and soundtrack left me in awe - can't recommend it enough and as a AAA game dev, I love seeing these Cinderella stories of indie devs who make a masterpiece.  Bravo.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The Pedestrian is a really neat idea, that is very well executed. It flows very smoothly, and the visuals and ambiance are really satisfying. That said, there just isn't anything here to make me want to go back to it after an hour of playtime. A nice concept, but just way too shallow to justify a £15 price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: I first saw the game on Reddit a few years ago. The game seemed to have an interesting premise, and I was intrigued. After playing through the entire game, I can say, I was not disappointed. Although the game is short, it is totally worth it, especially if you like puzzle games. There are definitely a few head scratchers. I won't spoil anything, but it had a great and unexpected twist in the end. For me this is definitely a must play.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: I had the good fortune of finding this game while it was still on KS and loved the demo and concept enough to back. I am glad I did or I might have not found it in the pile of games that launch every month. My backing money was well placed, as the game is everything promised and more. The tutorial is nicely integrated and builds smoothly to teach you how to interact and solve each area. I enjoyed every minute, and can't wait to see what's next for them.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: A Really enjoyable puzzle game. Looks really nice, far nicer than it needs to be to play but it adds a lot to the feeling of calm and relaxing nature of the game.The music is very nice.Both combined makes it feel like playing a Pixar movie.Game play is in nice chunks so I can play a little each night and save a regular point and start into a new set of puzzles the next time.It is really nice as well that the game just loads directly into the gameplay, no menus just loading and playing, absolutely how it should be.Runs great on Integrated Graphics (Intel Iris Pro 580).The progression of puzzle additions is nice, each new puzzle feature is added in a way that playing is its own tutorial and intuitive what you should be doing, so no  "annoying" tutorials or taking you out of the gameplay to explain new features.Skookum as Frig!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The Pedestrian is artistically a very well crafted game - the transitions between puzzles, the 3D background and foreground, and the soundtrack all show that clearly quite a lot of development and creativity went into designing this game. However, unfortunately, I am leaving a negative review due to the lack of emphasis on the core game mechanic and the surprisingly short play time.From the trailers, it would appear there is a strong emphasis on solving the puzzle of connecting the signs together in order to construct a path through a level, as well as some interaction with the surrounding 3D environment. However, this novelty quickly wears off as there is rarely more than a single obvious route and the environment does little more than showing progress through 2D levels. So, if you're looking for a stock puzzle platformer with boxes to climb, switches to open doors, and lasers to dodge, then this fits the bill.However, this leads to the second issue - the price. At $20, this is certainly a no-go due to the short 2-3 hours it takes to complete, none of which is particularly memorable. I purchased this game for $14 during the Summer Sale, and don't believe even that is a fair price. Unless the visual aesthetics are enough to win a prospective buyer over, I cannot justify recommending this over other puzzle games due to the lackluster attempt at a new mechanic and simplistic puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely amazing! It's so gorgeous and it's so fun! Most puzzle games are kinda the same but this is so different! It's so much fun and it's just challenging enough to still be fun and not tedious! I will definatly be playing again! And again and again! The only downside I can see is that I'd like a bit more of the type of gamplay you have in the end (trying not to spoil anything) but it's absolutely not a big downside! Amazing game and the people who've made it are so talented! Absolutely worth the money! (even though my boyfriend bought it for me haha)
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This game is simply charming. The soundtrack is light and fun, reminiscent of a Pixar short film. The puzzles are clever and the visual style this game is presented in is very pleasing. I'm not finished with The Pedestrian yet but that's okay as I'm enjoying taking my time with it! Big recommendation for puzzle fans!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Very charming puzzle platformer. Not terribly difficult overall, but it does well to provide some harder sections that you need to think through. The difficulty ramping is gradual, so pretty much anyone could pick up this game and have a good time while enjoying the beautiful background scenery and music. As with many of the other reviews I have read, I would have loved to see more of the mechanic at the end. It felt like a last minute addition that got no depth whatsoever, introducing as many new questions about the premise of the game as it resolved. Overall, The Pedestrian is a great game, and I would love to see these mechanics expanded on in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the top puzzle games I have ever played. It may seem like an eternity for the game to come out, but the wait is worth it! The music just makes your head bobs and the graphic is pretty spectacular. I love how the puzzles started out small and easy to give you a preset of what is coming and then it gets progressively harder as you move forward. It would be too boring if the puzzles didn't make your brain hurt and The Pedestrian definitely made me scratch (ok, pull) my hair a few times. I like how the developers implanted a little something extra for the players to find and makes you want to go back and play it all over again just so you don't miss anything. Love the twist in the end and I definitely wish it was longer! Perhaps an upcoming sequel soon? Definitely recommending this game to all my friends and family and to anyone who love a good puzzle game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This is a "short but sweet" puzzle-platformer that does not overstay it's welcome.  True to form, it unveils new mechanics and increasing challenges over the course of the gameplay; each new mechanic is rather intuitive, with perhaps the exception of "Paint" and the final true puzzle at the game's conclusion.Despite this small speed bumps, I had a terrific time-- the animation is crisp, the game stable, and the music hummable and appropriate in each new setting.I purchased this at 50% off and I think that's the "sweet spot"-- it's a bit brief for full price but it leaves a pleasant memory in its wake.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fairly short but very pleasant and cleverly designed puzzle platformer which has you travelling through signs while solving numerous puzzles along the way. The Pedestrian has a very gentle learning curve, as the game constantly introduces new mechanics to the player without becoming too overwhelming. It's also good on a technical standpoint, with detailed graphics and a relaxing soundtrack which suits the action well. My only complaint is that I wish there were more puzzles and more challenges, since I feel that some gameplay mechanics in the ending areas, while intriguing and well implemented, are underused. Still, as it stands, The Pedestrian is still a very good game and it's definitely worth buying if you love puzzle games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: What a great little puzzle game! Relatively short but expertly crafted and highly polished. Found myself thinking "that's so clever" over, and over, and over again. Story is surprisingly engaging given the complete absence of dialogue.Visuals are really stunning for such a small team as well, it's very impressive and immersive that every single game element exists within the world, from tutorials to the pause menu. The genius is in the details, after all.Perfect for the steam deck as well!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: I won't say that the puzzles are difficult. Like... you have to do a lot of guessing? No. Not at all.You just need to be as creative as the game creators ;)Try to see the levels with a few different perspectives. You will most certainly find clues around you.Sometimes you see a nonsensical mechanic when completing a level, but that's how the game works. An example, pressing the "F" key is not only useful for planning, but is also useful for pausing the character movements, like when you jump of a trampoline, press "F" to pause and change the state of the room to avoid the laser guns.There are so many surprises throughout the game because of the extraordinary interactivity between the sign world and the outside world.And the last level makes me smile even bigger :Dbecause of the completely nonsensical mechanic, where you need to switch between a platformer sign character and a first-person human who brings a handheld device. It makes me think, "am I now a ghostbuster?" hahaaaa XD
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Puzzles aren't for me, but this is a creative and very interesting game. The lore is a mystery, the entire game shows you, not telling you. The different locations as you travel through signs, lights, paper, chalkboard and more, are great. It's nice to see a game like this despite it not being a game I wouldn't go for normally. But I'm happy I did. There's heart put into this game and I always appreciate something like that.Please Play The Pedestrian as it's a lovely game to pass the time and put your brain to the test.It's a game for a peaceful travel through a city, and the final parts of the game is what really sold it for me. I do say again, please play The Pedestrian.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: is a good puzzle 2D platformer that is 3 to 6 hours long. Buy it if it looks interesting at all to you. It is frequently on sale for 50%+ off.The game's key mechanic is that the 2D platforming is split up into separated sections. You must determine how (and when) to arrange and connect these sections as you guide your character through them.* Difficulty: Comfortable? It is neither trivially easy nor terribly difficult. That said, the game does have a bit too much filler, where you are simply traversing empty space or the difficulty is too low. Overall, I think the game would be better if it had been slightly more difficult.* Graphics:  Lofi 2D platforming that moves you through a nice looking 3D city.* Variety:  The game stays reasonably fresh for its duration by introducing new items, effects, and restrictions. New concepts are introduced in a way that is easy for players to grasp.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine a jigsaw puzzle, except you're inside the puzzle pieces and putting the puzzle together sets your path. That is the core mechanic of the Pedestrian, and the whole game is built around it. Each new mechanic brings a clever twist to the basal concept, and I'd dare compare the cleverness to Portal.From beginning to end, the game's visuals are filled with lots of passionately crafted detail, and the way the environment occasionally interacts with the puzzles makes interesting solutions. The game may be short, but its qualities more than make up for it.Pick this up if you want a creative short & sweet puzzler.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This game is genius! The mechanic of solving puzzles with a 3D background on a 2D platform is well implemented. In the end there will be a special "plottwist" where I found myself thinking "This game is SOOOO great!".Also the music was very nice. There was not constantly music in the background but by solving puzzles or changing levels there would be some music playing. I liked this concept a lot, because while solving puzzles I liked the silence, so I could concentrate better.I had so much fun playing the game and can't wait for another game from the developers, maybe "the pedestrian 2"? I would definitely recommend playing it if you like short, not too challenging puzzles with great graphics.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: How the hell has this game been out for a year without my knowing about it?  While the concept is not completely novel, the execution is flawless.  Stunning graphics, smooth-as-silk gameplay.  And based on what I've seen so far, the puzzles are clever, with no reliance on "pixel-perfect" accuracy.  And best of all, there's a free demo if you're on the fence about purchasing.  I did something that I very rarely do:  I bought this game at full price.  And I have zero, repeat ZERO regrets.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: A new take on puzzle platforming. The atmosphere and soundtrack of the entire game immersed me completely. It is short enough to make me want to keep playing, and long enough to not get tedious and repetitive with its puzzles. The final puzzle has a small twist in game play that surprised me completely. The entire feel of this game is amazing. It is simple, fun, and has an amazing set of music to it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a while since I've played a puzzle game  well designed. It's a short, sweet, and pretty easy little experience you can beat in an afternoon. While it's probably a bit too pricey for $20, it's absolutely worth your time just for the cleverness and thought put into it. The core concept is very creative, moving around between street signs is fun and feels satisfying. What's here is a series of extremely well designed (if pretty easy) puzzles with consistency and clear direction. I was never really stumped or too challenged. My only complaint is that it stops just as it's starting to get really good, and only takes maybe 3 hours to beat. There's tons of creative potential for more puzzles and environmental storytelling, but it doesn't really expand much beyond pretty simple 2D puzzles and a handful of same-y signs and layouts. It would've been neat to see more ideas, and expansion of the core concept. Still, it's fun to play even if there's not a lot to it. Visuals are well crafted, easy to look at, and the backgrounds are unique. Pacing is great, there's no loading screens which means the game transitions between sections smoothly and feels very cohesive. The soundtrack is stellar too. Not much of a story, but that's alright! It isn't that kind of game. Even though it's probably a little too short and a bit pricey, The Pedestrian is 100% worth playing if you like puzzle games (especially if you find it on sale).
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: It's no "The Witness", but, it's really good. I just wish it was longer. I beat it in under 4 hours. On the bright side, it doesn't wear out its welcome. It isn't overly hard, and the graphics and music are vibrant and calm and relaxing. It slowly adds new mechanics over the game that don't take too long to figure out, and by the end of the game the puzzles all come together in a very neat way. It is overall a great little experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: nice little puzzle game. the puzzles are neither too easy nor too hard. well, except for the very last one (the one on the 4 skyscrapers), you probably will consult a walkthrough for that one.overall the game feels like someone who really likes to design everyday buildings/scenery slapped some platformer puzzles onto his work so it can be sold as a game. and it worked very well.some people complained about the controls; the menu has no mouse control and is a bit awkward to use but otherwise i had no complaints in 2d or 3d mode.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Been following this game for about a year and have been excited for it since I first saw it. And luckily it fully delivers! The puzzles are fun and make you think without making you feel like and idiot. Solving a puzzle that you've been stuck on is very satisfying. Pros:Puzzle are well thought out.difficulty curve is pretty good.Background scenes are cool to look at.controls are very simple.Variety of mechanics to keep it interesting.The atmospheric music is nice.Cons:Fairly short(4ish hours)If you like puzzle games you will probably like this game. solid 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Quite a charming but refreshing puzzle game. The puzzles are unlike much I have seen before which is nice. The art style is cool and some of the environments are beautifully made. This is a chill puzzle game to play. I haven't finished it yet but I no doubt will. There is also a decent challenge involved unlike some other puzzle games. Considering that it is pretty cheap I would say this is an easy buy
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an incredible and engaging feat of art and science.  A logic puzzle-adventure game to warm any Portal fan's heart - with button and cube puzzles (and even a little portal transport action) served up in an incredibly clever concept - a blend of a 2D platformer with 3D elements and interaction between game objects and "real world" objects.  The game is very intuitive with minimal controls - you are introduced to the world and the boundaries of the game, and then the boundaries are pushed - again, again and yet again for very satisfying puzzles.  I have to mention that each added element of complexity was pitch perfect - just challenging enough but not too challenging.  I do admit it took a few experiments for me to fully figure out the "yellow paint" but once done, I really enjoyed the new twist on the puzzles it provided.  The final set of puzzles was just superb, and the endgame quite satisfying - and leaving you wanting the next adventure.  Highest recommendation if you like logic puzzle and adventure games - and a hearty Bravo Zulu (well done!) to the developers .
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing and very beautiful! It does give a Pixar-esque kind of vibe to it, which I find very cool. For the price, I would highly recommend it as the puzzles do get more and more challenging. I think the only downside is that the music sometimes stops if you're stuck at a certain level for some time, so it then just becomes an awkward silence when I was really enjoying the video game soundtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The Pedestrian might be one of the most challenging yet fun games I've ever played.  Excellent graphics, innovative puzzle designs, and the finale levels that really surprised me. Best of all, no annoying timed puzzles that make you want to tear your hair out, you can take all the time you need to think about your next action. Buy this game, it's really worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Well done puzzle-platformer (very much puzzle, almost no platform skill needed and you can always pause to think). Took me 4 hours to complete; I only once got stuck for more than ~20 minutes on the same puzzle. Doesn't try to have much of a story, but the end level did a new and different thing that felt like a satisfying conclusion.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a fine, but it's something I would expect to pay $5 for, not $20.It baffles me how short the game is because the last puzzle is where it finally starts to get interesting. Prior to that point, the game consists of simple 2D puzzles without any innovative mechanics or story. Then for the last puzzle, it combines operating in 2D and 3D simultaneously to create a truly interesting challenge. It also introduces the story for the first time when you arrive at the protagonist's apartment.I was excited for the game to branch off in this new direction (similar to how Portal changes tone as you escape Glados), and I expected it to continue for another 3-4 hours as we use the new gameplay mechanics and resolve the story. But...it just ends.I even searched online to see if there was something I was missing, but that's it. It's so bizarre. It feels like I paid full price for a game but only got chapter 1.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely wonderful little puzzle game. The puzzles throughout the game were very well designed, and they kept constantly expanding on the base puzzle mechanics in new and interesting ways that I did not expect. The puzzles can be difficult and take some thought, but unlike most puzzle games, I never found myself frustrated and stuck, even without a single tutorial message to explain the mechanics to me. In addition, the graphics in this game are absolutely beautiful, and the music is nice, with an enjoyable piano theme that I kept finding myself humming along with as I played. Overall, great game. 6/7
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting puzzle game, none too complicated. Its a good lazy afternoon game. Graphics are good, no real complaints. I wouldn't say it's short because if it was any longer it would get repetitive and boring. Definitely recommend it if you can get it on sale for around $10 or less. _childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The Pedestrian is a cute little puzzle game where you move signs around to make paths for the man on the designs to run around and collect pieces of a device. The gimmick is quite cool because you see detailed 3D backgrounds as you manipulate a 2D surface. The game is also quite short (I beat it in less than 3 hours), but honestly that's preferable since it was close to getting repetitive. It was also nearly the perfect difficult aside from the last gimmick -- not too easy as to be unengaging but not too difficult as to be frustrating. I am a bit disappointed in the overall lack of depth, though, as from the trailer I thought it would be a little more interactive.

_childDocuments_.review: ~3 hours game time, constantly changing up mechanics while still developing the main concept. solid pacing and great ending, just when you think it's finally run dry it hits you with the finale. i think i just played a short film and i'm ok with that. prob wait for sale unless you're financially inept like me

_childDocuments_.review: A cool, clever and innovative puzzle platform game controlling a stick figure through a multitude of road signs.  Very polished and no bugs.  Don't be put off by the opening credits.Puzzles start easy and by the end, you will be head scratching to work out how to get the pedestrian to the exit.  Challenging, but moderately so. Takes 4-7 hours depending on your IQ.There are a few hidden ladders which lead you to secret rooms where you achieve new headgear.  There is no achievement for that.An engaging game with relaxing music in the background.  Clever interaction between normal life and the 3D boards.  Highly recommend for puzzle lovers. _childDocuments_.review: This is quite the unique little game. Although the puzzles aren't particularly complex, the visuals are a true treat, way more than you'd expect to find in a 3-4 hour puzzle adventure like this. I wouldn't come into this expecting something that'll challenge you, but I can imagine coming home after work and relaxing with this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: When I think about 'hobby games' like Destiny 2 or bottomless time sinks like AC Odyssey,  It's a privileged take, granted. People want value per hour out of economic pressures on top of a melange of other reasons. You already know - your attention piqued from vids/screenshots as it is -  The Pedestrian is the king of the background. As you shift from sign to sign, the camera dramatically sweeps through these massive, detailed (if a little low-res at times) 3D environments and near every puzzle/platforming scene is perfectly framed for impact. The intro, in particular, bursts forth with intoxicating momentum. With its energetic backing track, it's a triumphant sequence I thought had simply set the bar beyond reach before settling into a comfortable groove. I was wrong! It's true that The Pedestrian gets comfortable - playing as it does with its wealth of mechanics. Every time I thought a puzzle might end up being the standout going forward, its representation in my mind would be veritably extirpated by the next. Every time I thought the remainder of my time would be a reshuffling of the mechanical cards, a new pack was thrown my way. Unlike many games that introduce new mechanics too quickly, everything felt iterated on to its logical end. When one particular new set of mechanics was introduced I responded with such unrestrained glee that they'd read my mind. But that's even before the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ending sequence.Its bread and butter is definitely its puzzle piece-like mechanics. Given a selection of signs in a scene, you need to link up ladders and doors in an unbroken way such that you can progress. Sounds simple, but it's added upon and subverted in enough ways that it never loses its lustre. Although initially overwhelming and even demotivating occasionally, I appreciated how little hub sections wherein you go on 'quests' for items let you disengage with certain puzzles and still have somewhere to go. It also helps ground the locations as these 3D areas to explore rather than something to power through. If that means anything to you, you might now be excited. I can't say anything more except to avoid the user screenshots or YouTube vids. It's a small slice and leaves you wanting more, but it was such a powerful move of flipping everything on its head that I couldn't have been more impressed. If a short, indie experience such as this can avoid being a homogeneous experience, why can't we expect such boldness industry-wide?
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a lot of fun to play through. Some of the puzzles were really challenging, but nothing that I felt was too difficult. The highlight of this game is easily the aesthetic and how creatively the game is presented. The soundtrack is fantastic as well. Highly recommend a play through of this game, it's short and easy to get through in a couple days, or even one sitting.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: An enjoyable puzzle game, there's a steady stream of new mechanics that get introduced so there's a nice learning curve and an even level of challenge. Some of the mechanics could have stayed around a bit longer or be developed a bit further, but overall it is entertaining and does not get too repetitive. Definitely recommended if you like this sort of game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Straight out, this is an awesome game. The concept in itself is facinating but the execution easily makes this one of my favourite puzzle games ever. The music, colours, levels and level difficulty are all in this amazing harmony. Not to mention the ending, the twist really makes this game worth playing through. I would actually love to see another puzzle game based on the same mechanics (Spoiler alert->) just in 3D, as you did in the end there. That would be a fantastic followup to this game. Then ending still has me just baffled. Its really beautiful, and i love the "open ending" theme its going for.All in all, great game. Really worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: It is a very good game, with decent puzzle mechanics, some nice twists and turns, really beautiful backgrounds, some small hidden things to satisfy the explorer, BUT it is very short.It took me 4.7 hours to finish the game and I really wasn't racing it. _childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Oh My Gosh! I loved playing this.While I read reviews I did not look at any game play videos. I went in knowing very little.It's a very good puzzle game. I found it very challenging. I will admit I had to look up hints for 2 sections, but when I saw the solutions it my brain simple forgot I could do certain things.The graphics are sweet to look at. Very realistic. Everything made sense.This was a joy to play! And the ending!!!!! Oh my! it threw me for such a loop! I had to go get my husband to play that last section with me. He loved it too!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: A 2D puzzle platformer in a 3D environment. You sometimes have to switch modes and move the modularized 2D sections around within the 3D world.Honestly, if you're like me, you'll be too focused on playing the game and traversing the 2D boards to notice the 3D environment around them that has been built with much effort. More interesting for a watch-along person, or pass-the-gamepad couch co-op, compared to solo play maybe? It happens frequently that the background music just stops. Not abruptly … the song is just over and it doesn't loop. Then the music picks up again once you solve a puzzle. Maybe the tracks aren't made to loop? It's an odd design choice. They should have looked at what iMuse and modern Zelda games do.The controls are simple with just a D-pad and three buttons. And yet, having to move the movable boards with the gamepad is not made convenient. I ended up switching between gamepad and mouse controls whenever I switched modes – and that in itself feels clunky.There seem to be some extra boards hidden along the journey, granting minimally alternative outfits … But the game offers no sense of tracking them. No progress listing or menu section or "inventory" page in the pause screen; no "home base" to return to and see a gradually growing collection, as some games provide; not even an achievement for getting them all. You just stop at a new secret board to choose between merely two new options. You can't even revert to any past outfit, let alone the default. It would have been cool if players could select unlocked costumes at will via such a pause screen, rather than being stuck with the last choice until the next secret board.I think the game could have been longer, overall. Especially, the game mechanics introduced later fall a bit flat.It's an interesting idea that is sadly lacking polish.[played on Steam] 6.0/10.0
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most unique puzzle games I've ever played. The concept is simple at the start and they keep adding on new mechanics without really making it feel overwhelming. You can play this game at your own pace or straight through in 4-6 hours. Also, the soundtrack is actually incredible! I love this game and hope this team continues to make more in the future! Highly, highly recommend buying this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Such a great game, not overbearing or too difficult, but hard enough that it can stump you every now and then, I loved the sound and visuals, pausing while crossing over between signs was delightful. _childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: It's good but not as good as the overwhelming might suggest. I'd say the last 25% of the game are great. Also there is great gameplay twist at the end but sadly right after this new concept is introduced the game is over. The first 75% of the game are basically an overly long tutorial. The frist time I played I thought how great detaching rooms from one another would be for complex puzzles. But this mechanic only happens at the end of the game. Before you need to figure out one route that works and stick to it. As for the visuals, again except for the end of the game they don't matter. _childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: If you like puzzle games, it's certainly worth trying this one - it's quite short (I finished in a bit under 7 hours of playtime), but the puzzles are nicely designed and new  mechanics are introduced in ways that makes how they work readily apparent just through playing the game.Due to the type of game it is, the replay value is obviously not that great - but based on the price/entertainment value it's fine.  There is also a nice little twist near the end which can confuse you a bit until you figure out what's happening.

The concept is great and is well executed, a bit repetive certain times despite some variation in gameplay mechanics and I found it annoying that when you "die" you go back to scratch in the puzzles so you have to "edit" everything again, well since you died your current setup in the puzzle is wrong.
