_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game. Its a good combination of jump n run and a puzzle game. The soundtrack and the visuals are supreme. The only issue i kind of have is, that sometimes new mechanics, that get introduced to the gameplay are a little poorly explained, so you have to play around with it some time to fully understand how it works.Definetly a must play
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The Pedestrian is a fantastic puzzle game that consistently mixes in new mechanics to keep you on your toes. The backgrounds are lovingly crafted and pleasant to look at while you pick your way through each puzzle. It's a little on the short side but a definite pick up for anyone who enjoys the puzzle genre.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game, it was challenging but not impossible and the game implemented new features gradually which I loved. The environment was beautiful, had fun features and great sound without being over the top.If you like a good puzzle game with lots of little twists and turns I recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This game is beautiful in every single way. The visuals are calming and stunning, the music is very relaxing, and the gameplay is absolutely amazing. Every single puzzle brings something new to the table and you always feel smart after completing each one. After beating this game, I can say it is without a doubt my favorite game of 2020 so far, and it is well worth the 20 bucks!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: A short little puzzle game where you play as a little man on street signs who is tasked with traversing his environment by rearranging the signs and using items within them to carve a path forward. It is almost reminiscent of a 2-D Portal game while still feeling like its own thing, so if you enjoy puzzle games (specifically the Portal games), you'll definitely enjoy this one. However, it is a very short game, clocking in at just over three hours for me, so maybe wait for a sale to pick it up.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: **Neutral rating** The Pedestrian: the game’s gimmick is that you have to build the puzzle before you can solve it. Connecting the right doors, arranging the tiles in the proper order, etc. This means the game stops every couple of screens so you can run through each puzzle in your mind first before actually running through it. This has appeal, I know, but I didn’t like how the game comes to a complete halt like this so often. The bulk of the game is you standing in one place and preparing to solve each puzzle. I’d rather solve by taking action rather than stopping for ten minutes to trace potential routes first. I didn't want to spend all my time preparing to do things. Please just let me move. Still, I can understand how people would enjoy this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Love the aesthetics of the game, which was a huge deciding factor for me when I bought it. The mechanics of the game was also quite a novelty for me. The puzzle solving was satisfying and the change from 2D "sign" world to 3D real world towards the end was literally mind-blowing for me because I didn't refer to any guide until that point (felt like my brain was fried trying to think of the solution myself). Overall it was very memorable experience and hopefully we will see more games from the dev in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This game's a quite unique and interesting puzzle game. I enjoyed it the whole way through, as the game slowly kept adding more aspects to the gameplay.The difficulty of the puzzles increase over time, but don't take insanely long to solve.I can definitely recommend the game, especially if you can get it in a sale for a bit less.But honestly, if you enjoy puzzles, this should be worth the full price too.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Portal but wished it was 2D, a quarter as complicated and one-tenth as long, you might be interested in this game.An interesting puzzle-platformer with cool but shallow puzzles and awful but mercifully little platforming. Suffers greatly from lack of content and UX polish. The puzzle concept is interesting but doesn't go very deep on any of its gimmicks, and suffers severely from lack of quality-of-life features, especially an "undo" button. I beat every puzzle in under 3 hours - JUST long enough to not be able to get a refund. I'd say it's worth it at <$5 but no way at >$20.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The pedestrian is a short, casual puzzle platformer with an emphasis on visual presentation. The puzzles are alright, I like that you don’t have to solve the entire puzzle all at once, you can start out with an idea and then test it out. If it doesn’t work you can make adjustments to your solution until you solve it. The game rarely reuses the same puzzle idea so most puzzles feel fresh.The worst part about the game is the controls. Moving the boxes around and changing the connections is annoying.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game for an hour and a half, getting 6/10 achievements and 5 of the 7 MacGuffin.  If I'm being generous, 10 minutes of that was spend solving puzzles.  The rest was walking down empty or trivial corridors, Watching screen transitions, getting back to where I died, and most of all, pausing, dragging things around, unpausing, moving a bit, pausing, dragging things around, unpausing, moving a bit, pausing ... the game is just slow and tedious and repetitive and repetitive and repetitive.  Based on how far I got and how long that took me, a more cynical person might say that all the screen transitions and empty hallways and cutscenes and repetition and repetition are to get the game to clock in at over 2 hours so people would refund it.  I'm not going to say that, because this game feels like it was developed to be the kind of style-over-substance experience that thinks that's actually what players want.  If that is what you want, just go play gorogoa instead.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: A short and unique puzzle game. It has a really laid-back ambiance and the puzzles all feel well crafted and never overstaying their welcome. Some of the puzzles will require some careful thought but they all felt extremely reasonable and never leaving you completely stumped as to what to do next. Strong recommendation for anyone with even a mild interest in puzzle games (like myself)!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one hell of an idea!Puzzle and platforming are wonderfully combined, as well as the 2D signs (where the game actually takes pasce) and the 3D environment (which gets sometimes involved in the puzzles).By the way, I've seen proper 3D games with a less polished and detailed world than this one! I wonder if it wasn't too much work for what is mostly background, but I'm glad the developers spent time on it like they did!New mechanics are introduced every now and then, which is always good, and the final puzzle is just brilliant. If you're ever going to do a sequel, you could make a whole game out of the last puzzles (please do it, you'll have my back, I promise!)The only thing I would have changed is the transition between sets of signs: instead of putting it under player's control, I would have just made it automatic. This is just because sometimes you don't know if your character is already "arrived" or not and it feels a bit weird to stop mid-transition. But it's a minor complaint, really.I went for it full price and I don't regret it, even if it lasted three hours only.Good job! We want more of it!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Cool game. I've afked for about 1h or something, so you could think that it's a bit short, but imho puzzle games with 1 billion levels tend to become boring and uninspired.The Pedestrian has a good amount of puzzles with enough variety.I grabbed it while it was discounted and I feel like it was good purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Everything. Puzzles were mixed. Some easy, some medium (and you feel good for solving them), some hard (and you feel really good for solving them), some incredibly difficult (and you don't even feel bad looking up a tiny hint because that's all you need to get back on the track). I really hope there is a Pedestrian 2
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed it thoroughly despite its brevity (I have about 3 hours of play time logged). I think it's greatest crime is its failure to really engage with its "final mechanic" (which I won't spoil), giving you one real, actual puzzle that utilizes it. I think this is a shame because the game shuts itself down just as you feel you've entered the last real stage of it. Every other mechanic gets multiple puzzles that explore its use, but the final mechanic (and I assume it's because of its complexity and the dev time it took) is essentially a one-off. This is compounded by the fact that this mechanic feels the most interesting by far, and would provide a fantastic framework to show off its interactions with some of the game's other mechanics to that point (the fact that it never once even plays with the very first ability to move panels around is a huge letdown) to sort of tie the game up, but instead they give you an appetizer of this thing and then shunt you off to the end credits.Pedestrian 2, I guess.Though it's not mechanically too similar, it reminds me in a good way of Perspective (from DigiPen), and if you enjoyed that then you'll enjoy this. Definitely a must for fans of puzzle platformers generally, even if the ratio of price to playtime is a bit steep.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The may game be short (I completed it in ~4 hours) but everything the game has to offer is so worth it. Everything, the forefront and the background, is amazing to just stare at. The soundtrack is so relaxing to just listen to. And the puzzles presented are challenging, but satisfying once you solve them and are always changing with new mechanics to work with. If you're ever looking for a puzzle game and have a free afternoon of relaxing, this is what you should be playing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: A fun and challenging platformer with increasingly complex puzzles and a few twists that will keep you entranced up until the game ends. I really enjoyed this game and definitely recommend it. The music was nice and charming throughout the game and definitely helps set the tone. There were at least 4 or 5 times where I had to really think about what I had to do to solve the puzzle and a bit of trial and error before it finally clicks and you get introduced to new ways of thinking about the puzzles/signs. The puzzle's challenge/reward gave me similar feelings I had when playing Portal for the first time. There's some secrets that I didn't end up getting so there's a bit of replay value to find all of those. I wish the game let you do more with the finale mechanics but maybe they'll make a sequel? Hope so at least.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The summary here is that although this game is good, it is not great and it is very VERY short (2-4 hours I'd guess). I'd recommend buying it for $5, since it feels more like a very pretty flash game than a full-fledged indie title. 6/10 if 5 is meh.This game is visually great and brings a unique set of mechanics to the table, but ultimately fails to do much of anything exciting with either its world or gameplay.  There are very few moments in which the game takes the familiar set of rules you have been working with and twists them in some genius way that you never saw coming (like in Portal, The Witness or Baba is You) although it does often introduce new ideas that make you think it probably will soon. This in large part is due to the fact that the game is so short, it feels like it barely has time to introduce new ideas before moving on. In my case, the game took only 117 minutes (steam says 3 hours but that includes menus) and there are 8 major 'chapters' to the game. 15 minuets of gameplay is obviously not enough time to build expectations and then subvert them. The one saving grace here is that the mechanics add up over the course of the game, so some early game ideas can be toyed with towards the end. The game leaves you with the feeling that a lot of cool puzzles could have existed, but were not fully realized.As a small tangent, this game also suffers very much from the problem a lot of puzzle platformers have where you can solve some of the easier puzzles faster then the character can complete them, so you wind up waiting around, bored and annoyed constantly.I don't want to spoil anything as far as the story goes but I will say it disappointed me. If you played The Witness and hated its ending, this game somehow manages to limbo under that low bar. Funnily enough, you get the impression the devs must have thought The Witness' ending was a masterpiece and wanted to emulate its feeling as much as possible.In conclusion, wait for a sale or maybe just pass altogether. You aren't missing out on much and you'll probably regret it if you buy it for $20.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: An incredibly *ahem*  puzzle game, saved by its gorgeous and unique presentation. The puzzles here won't be much of a challenge for anyone who plays puzzle games with any regularity, but it's a cozy way to while away an evening. The final puzzle is a particularly clever touch that left a huge smile on my face once I realized what was happening.Even for a newcomer to puzzle games, The Pedestrian is going to feel really short. It would be well served by some additional challenge content or workshop support, but I also respect the devs sticking to their vision.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a fan of puzzlers then this is a good one. While the art style is simple it doesn't take away from the game at all, and the unique street sign aesthetic ends up making this really stand out. The puzzles are good too; challenging at times but not so much so that you start hating the game. Honestly, I would love it if they came out with a second one of these.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This game is beautiful!The  downside I can think of is the length, it left me wanting more (which is a good thing?)A pure 2D puzzle platformer with some interesting gimmicks and a mindblowing ending puzzleThe graphics and soundtrack are stellar aswell, you can tell there was a lot of love put into this by the devs!8.5/10, must buy if its on sale!cant wait for a sequel
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The Pedestrian is a very short game but a fun puzzle platformer that makes you think a lot. I had a lot of fun playing this game and the puzzles get more and more creative the further along you get but it isn't long enough to warrant a high price. Anything under 10$ I'd say is worth. I just wish there were more levels that build off some of the mechanics that were implemented at the end.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely little puzzle game, but sadly a bit too short to warrant the price. I got it at 50% and I think that's a fair price (only took me about 5 hours to finish).I was very impressed by the design and the "gimmick" of the protagonist moving trough different environments and interacting with them while staying only in 2D. _childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely side scroller with great atmosphere and engaging puzzles, the Pedestrian is equal parts relaxing and challenging. With its simple and unique creative vision, the Pedestrian is also a no frills game. It is one more example of the prowess of the Indie game scene and the wonderful imagination of certain individuals.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most creative puzzle games I've ever played. Short, sadly, you can finish the game in about 7 hours if you take your sweet time. Nonetheless, the gameplay is fluid and fun to play, the soundtrack is amazing, and the attention to detail to the background is a highlight as well.Totally recommend to people who wants a mind bending puzzle game with a chill time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Very interesting puzzle game with various mechanics in each area. It is quite short, my dumb ass brain finished it in 6 hours (1.5 hours of which I had my game run in the background while I was doing something else), so actual run was even shorter. But game is worth its price, at least its current price on sale, looks good (sometimes reminds me good old Pixar animations), sounds good and it is one of those puzzle games you play while relaxing, cause puzzles arent that hard.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This game gave me the same feeling of playing Portal 1 and 2 so many years ago. Incredibly clever puzzles that's bursting with charm. Every time I found a solution, I felt elated. There's not much in the way of a story, per se, but the final moments of the game are pretty incredible. Highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The Pedestrian is shockingly good for its simplistic exterior! I would compare it to Portal's thoughtful gameplay except instead of Chell and GLaDOS you have a bathroom sign character and a suped-up Gameboy! Great game and a satisfying ending as well! Shout out to GTLive for piquing my interest in this gem!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Oh wow. The finale is an unexpected meta level, somewhat better than Portal. Not going to talk about  introduced in the whole finale part, but I'm blown away, loved it so much!Also the attention to details is amazing.Yet I must note that this kinda feels like an another unoptimized unity game (framedrops here and there), but this didn't bothered me - core gameplay stayed smooth. A bit disappointed that there are no optional achievements and the level design is very linear, with a very limited room for a multiple solutions.And, sadly, it felt short. I know, it took me about 5 hours to beat the game (durr), but this time passed by so fast with this game, I barely noticed :) Yet I seriously wish it could be at least twice longer. If there will be any DLCs, I'll definitely get them all. Great game and worth its price.Thank you, Skookum Arts ♥️
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The good:- The game looks absolutely fabulous. The front is slick and polished, while the backdrops are dynamic, colourful, and lively.- The main mechanic is quite original.- The game does not get stale, constantly dropping something new on you, in terms of both game mechanics and environments.The bad:- The puzzles are frustratingly easy for the most part, to the point where they can hardly be called puzzles. The difficulty is revved up to the decent level closer towards the end, but it feels too little too late.- Just like anyone else has mentioned, the game is shockingly short, sitting at about 3 hours. It does offer a complete experience, but I just cannot recommend it at full price ($20 as of this review).
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Very difficult to rate.It's a great game. Like really great, one of the best games I've played in a long time. And it's really, really clever, like insanely clever. I kept being amazed by it and the last level was so unbelievably clever, I can hardly describe it. The graphics are nice and the music is great too, all in all a really solid experience.BUT: I finished it in 3 hours. That is extremly short, even though the puzzles and everything are great, 3 hours is nothing. This does not mean the game is bad, but I don't quite feel as if I got my 16€ worth of content. I know there are some more secrets to find, but the game is over and that after only 3 hours. I'm really torn, I would love to give it a "yes" but I can't because of how short it is. I'll wait and see, maybe they'll release some new content and maybe all the secret stuff is worth doing, then I'll reconsider. But right now I wouldn't buy it again, maybe at a lower cost.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Bought the game here to support the devs.Smart think-out-of-the-box (literally) puzzles, there are a handful memorable ones (especially the 3-pistons one, and the 4-tall-buildings one).Fantastic design of interface.You can see the devs' soul and the fact that they put a lot of love and time in it.Amazing scenes even though to most players they probably don't matter.Wish there was a sequel!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The Pedestrian is a really nice puzzle game that I would recommend for anybody who likes games such as Portal, The Talos Principle, or The Witness. The only thing I could complain about is that the game felt too short, but it was a good experience, so I can't even complain about that. The soundtrack is stellar, and helps to keep you calm while you rack your brain for a solution to a puzzle. And the graphics look amazing. It may be 2D for the majority of game time, but the glimpses of the world you get between puzzles really showcase the talent of Skookum Arts.TL;DR: Top tier puzzle game with an amazing sound track and stunning visuals. 9.5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: + Good-looking and unique art design+ Fun yet challenging puzzles+ Lots of variation keeps the game from becoming stale- Music cuts out occasionally, developed and published by Skookum Arts, is a 2.5D puzzle platformer with a unique art design based entirely on signs that released on January 29th, 2020.In , you play as a stick figure traversing a 3D world through signs which you must manipulate to your benefit. The gameplay itself is hard to explain, as you unlock many different mechanics the farther along you progress. At the core, you must rearrange and connect signs in a logical order to complete the task of that particular level, say, opening a door.I would sometimes find myself breezing through levels, while other times finding myself stuck for many minutes on the rearranging screen, deep in thought, trying to figure out how to continue. But this isn't necessarily a bad thing. The sense of self-improvement and progression in this game is strangely profound. After a new mechanic is introduced,  gives you a few levels to get the hang of the mechanic, possibly master it, then throws you a new bone. follows your journey as a two-dimensional icon of a man or woman (think of washroom gender signs) making its way through a three-dimensional busy city's signs. Along the way, you'll explore many different environments, such as sewers, buildings of all shapes and sizes, subway systems, etcetera. While there isn't a real "plot", I actually found the lack of exposition to be calming and befitting of the game's minimalist aesthetic.The art design in  is very unique, and the game itself is incredibly good-looking. While the main gameplay takes place on signs, the environments provide a great backdrop, are nice to look at, and make the world feel lived in. The soundtrack is nice on the ears and relaxing, but I found that the music would sometimes cut out entirely until I moved on to the next level, leaving me in silence. was originally successfully Kickstarted and has a price tag of $20. The length of the game depends on your puzzle game affinity, but most can expect to beat it within a few hours. I'd suggest purchasing when on sale.The only bug/issue I ran into was the aforementioned music cutting out, which fixed itself when I advanced to the next level. ran well without issues on my computer, but its 3D backgrounds could potentially affect performance on older computers. Modern computers should have no problem running this game at 60 FPS. is a very enjoyable and relaxing 2.5 puzzle platformer with a very unique art design. If you're looking for a good puzzle game to put your brain to the test, I would highly recommend checking out this title.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: A very lovely, peaceful little game. The puzzles aren't too hard - there were only a couple of times when I felt frustrated in a "ugh, what am I even supposed to do" sort of way. But at no point did it get so bad that I needed to look up the answer. The backgrounds are so gorgeous - the whole game is just a pleasure to play. Very much enjoyed it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR :- A must have puzzle gamePedestrian, a puzzle game that starts out as a 2D platformer with mind blowing graphics unnecessary for a stick figure game, keeps surprising you with its endless props that forces you to think differently never allowing you to slack off, takes a sudden turn after 9 hours of straight gameplay to become the 3D game it always was 😊Only now !! you find that your gameplay is haunted, and like all supernatural movies, the logic is bent and broken at arbitrary places leaving you with a puzzle that forces you to make sense out of the nonsense.Where all the learning you have had for the past 9 hours goes down the toilet forcing you to unlearn common sense to relearn a haunted universe, that reduces you to the level of a toddler who requires hours of experimenting to figure out simple things like moving a box 😳#HorrorPuzzle #PedestrianGame
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The Pedestrian is an almost perfectly executed casual puzzle game.It starts out extremely simply, then drip-feeds the player a handful of increasingly advanced mechanics while not wearing any of them out.The mix of the ultra-simplistic 2d signs with the photorealistic surroundings is great, and all the visuals are very well done.My only real complaint is that I want  time with some of the late-game mechanics, but I suppose not enough is better than too much.If you have any interest at all in puzzle games, go play The Pedestrian!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Day 1 backer on Kickstarter just due to the art style and the impressive puzzle types.  Took awhile to get out into the wild but I have enjoy playing the demo and early betas.  Now the final version is even better than I could have hoped.  I recommend this to all.  Even tough puzzles are solvable and have a real rewarding feel when done.  Now I find myself trying to organize the various "signs" to have a nice look with all the connecting lines.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Nice little Puzzle Game to play when multitasking.Allthough the ending puzzle needed all my attention to solve xDI played it while waiting for friends and it's perfect for that.Graphics are great and the puzzles get more complicated over time.I would have loved more 3D / Multidimensional Puzzles like the ending one.9/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Great puzzle/platformer, never too hard to get stuck but challenging enough to give you that satisfying feeling when you complete most of the levels. Aesthetically gorgeous and diverse, and the soundtrack is pleasing but during some quiet moments where there's only ambient sound, you feel like something's missing.Try the demo if you're not convinced, the game is very solid overall and gets better while you progress.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Outstaning creative take on a "basic" puzzle concept. Love the music and art direction as well.  and in particular the end puzzle "endgame" just blew my mind. My only complaint would be that they should have explored the 3rd person puzzle concept even more throughout the game. One of the very best game experiences i had this decade! highly recommended, if you love to think and tinker. This game had me smiling all the way through. SO rewarding! :D
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: An overall relaxing and enjoyable experience. The game isn't long, but that's because you don't spend a ton of time stuck on puzzles. I only had to look up a guide in two places, once when  and once when . Would definitely recommend if you feel stressed out by your current games and need a palate cleanser.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This was a very fun and addicting puzzle/platformer with heavy emphasis on the puzzling.  For those who steer away from platformers, no problem here--not even a handful of places where you need quickness and/or dexterity.You make your way through a background of different "city" scenarios but the puzzles are all done on groups of "signs."  Most of the puzzles are very challenging but also  intuitive if you put your thinking cap on.  The complexity of the puzzles and introduction of new mechanics ramp up nicely as you progress.Very unique form of game playing and a nice twist in the game mechanics at the end.  Definitely replayable.Highly recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Lost my save after a PC crash, asked for help and in less 24 hours. The Devs sent me a way to recover my save file.Very grateful and Developers that cares about its community.It is a very nice and atmospheric game. Challenging puzzles and new ways to solve them after each level.If you want a nice, relaxing and a little brainwork, this is the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: It's a case of style over substance, but that style is really good so it may be worth it.  I didn't like some of the puzzles where lots of enter/exit door tiles needed to be moved around trial & error style, and I almost quit after a few hours, but then I started finding some clever puzzles too.  The game ended up hooking me and I'd say it's very good overall.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This game is beautiful, and the puzzles are presented in a very clever way, but the whole experience feels shallow. I completed the first three of the game's seven zones, and watched a video of the seventh zone to see where the whole thing was heading, but there just doesn't seem to be any substance beneath the pretty surface.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Mindbending.The Pedestrian blends 2D and 3D surfaces\objects with brilliant puzzles (having occasional difficulty spikes). For some might be a bit short. For me – it’s just enough.The game conveys great sense of scale and unique perspective thanks to richly detailed backgrounds bustling with life and beautiful soundtrack.You can see the devs playing their own game

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliant, short, little puzzle game Never over-stays its welcome and while the puzzles aren't overly difficult/frustrating, they aren't brain-dead either and definitely makes you feel pretty damn good for figuring them out. _childDocuments_.review: It's a very interesting puzzle in term of presentation, and the final puzzle is a surprise to me. There are many nice backgrounds to look at when you're solving the puzzles, and there are quite a few new mechanics added to the game while you're making progress. My only complain is that it seems a little bit overpriced for a 3~5 hours gameplay, and I do understand some of the development cost went into the background. Therefore, if you're looking for a long enough puzzle game for you to enjoy your 20 USD, this is probably not your choice.For achievement hunters: When you finish the game, you'll get all the achievements. The length is about 3~5 hours, depending on your smartness about puzzle games :P
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The game starts off a bit slow for people that play a lot of puzzles, without much challenge. But the visuals and aesthetics really pull you through, and soon enough the game introduces new area interesting mechanics, and things get harder and really fun, with some well thought puzzles.Each new surprise is really cool, and the visuals are incredibly eye-catching.But then, when you are completely hooked, the game ends with a cliff hanger, which is a pity.Overall, a pretty good puzzle game, maybe a bit too pricy for the duration, but the different ideas and feel compensate for that matter. Definitely recommend it for any puzzle enthusiastic, more so on a big sale given its ~3h30 duration.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: It looks nice, the puzzles were fine, runs well enough, but I can't recommend it.It's not cheap even at half price considering you only get about 3 hours of gameplay: of which at most 1 hour was spent on problem solving.You can extend your playtime by searching for some hidden levels that reward you with cosmetic hats... Not that it makes completing the game more satisfying.Felt like I spent more time trudging through a walking simulator to get from one puzzle to the next than actually solving puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This is quite possibly one of the best games I've ever played. The music is phenomenal, the cinematography is astonishing, the puzzle platforming itself is appropriately challenging and shakes up gameplay just enough to keep it fresh without feeling like you're suddenly playing a different game. All the transitions are smooth and there is a story that is told without any dialogue, and quite frankly it is just awesome. It might be a bit early, but I unironically think this may be in the running for game of the year.If you like puzzle platforming, play this game.If you like Minecraft-esque music while you work on figuring out a difficult problem, play this game.And if you want to experience one of the most mind-blowing ending sequences this side of the Stanley Parable, play this game.Stop reading Steam reviews. Play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic, original puzzle game. I've never played anything else quite like this: the most reasonable comparison I can give is that its a bit like a (mostly) 2D version of the Portal games, or The Talos Principle. The mechanics are very different, but somehow the process to solving the puzzles feels very similar.The game is a bit short, but otherwise basically perfect.Definitely recommended if you like spacial puzzles with a smidgeon of platforming tossed in.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles are very interesting and there are a lot of original mechanics. It seems to be just a fun theme, but there comes a moment near the end of the game that completely blows your mind and the entire world explodes in your head as you realize what's really going on. Similar to  in The Witness.I highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Great puzzle game which is quite challenging at times.This isn't just a mindless puzzle game with levels upon levels. There's a goal you work towards (even if it ins't so apparent at the beginning).This game really goes above and beyond with an amazing breakage of the fourth wall by the end.Can't recommend it more - really relaxing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The Pedestrian is a puzzle solving game that bring you along a ride through beautiful scenery as you attempt to solve mind boggling puzzles.Truly a game that needs so much praise for the countless hours the developers put into this. It's mechanics were challenging but they still gave you a sense or direction before they smack you with a hard puzzle. Being one of the Beta testers on this game, seeing the progress from what i've saw in the alpha and into the final form. Man It's ending was a masterpiece that left me wanting more. Can't wait to see what else they have in store for the future!- Williepoo
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: What an atmospheric and charming puzzler The Pedestrian was! You play as a familiar stick figure hopping from street sign to street sign solving puzzles left and right while enjoying a scenic tour through the city. The puzzles aren't too hard and are built up well. Especially the last major puzzle of the game is a treat. All in all it took me about 4 hours to beat the game, a decent length for a concept puzzle game like this. I would've liked a chapter selection screen after beating it, alas it starts a new game automatically. I'm looking forward to finding all the secret hats in my second playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: - Creative, fun puzzles, which I found perfectly balanced on the difficulty/entertainment scale- Transition between levels/puzzles is done in a unique way instead of just selecting them from a menu- Visuals while not the highest resolution, are clearly delivered with care and with attention paid to details- Great ambient sound-work, paired with charming, relaxing music- Well priced- Lack of a level reset button- Due to how the transition between each major puzzle is done, you can’t just go back to previous puzzles, adding a level select feature at least after completion of the game would’ve been neat- Short- Just a minor annoyance, but I’m not sure why you can’t cross transitions between the signsI’m a ‘bit’ late to the release party of The Pedestrian, I only just stumbled across this title a few days ago through a speedrun of it, but this doesn’t by the least diminish  For more detail on the above points and a look at gameplay, please join me as I elaborate on my thoughts in this video:.We also have a complete walkthrough on The Pedestrian, if you’re interested, !- Don’t rush, there’s no time pressure- Re-organize the tiles you’ll need to use to gain a better view on the puzzle- Traversing archways you’ll keep your momentum and direction, just remember they’re one-way only- Mechanical arms only need to be powered once, you don’t need to keep them powered after they de-active - Spray paint grants immunity to objects, switches and your character against the reset that would come from manipulating connections- You don’t need to keep holding the interact button to push boxes
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: A short but really beautiful game. This puzzle-exploration game has really fun puzzles and beautiful environment that changes based on the way you interact with the puzzles. It has non-stop amazed me with it's creativity!Playing through the puzzles wasn't stressful nor too uninteresting/easy/monotonous. The idea behind being able to move the very level itself has opened up extremely interesting puzzle mechanics that makes this game feel fun and interesting. I also love how there were some interval - "cooldown zones", before reaching the next big puzzle that will open up the next area. The intervals made the game feel less intense and stressful all the while flowering my eyes with the beautiful asmr of the amazing background.Finally, I absolutely love how playing within the levels can change the background objects. This makes the game that much more immersive!The beautiful background has only improved the game and made it that much more enjoyable to play! The atmosphere was also nailed and feels very natural; From the  to  and , the lively/untidy parts of the world makes me feel as if I'm in the game.My dense ass didn't get what was the story going on behind this game. Maybe there isn't one at all but I highly doubt that since the end showcased some really interesting Sci-Fi logic (exposing some hidden story detail?), before ending off with a hilariously cliche ending.I really enjoyed every second spent playing this game whether it is to solve puzzles or to view the amazing background scenery. Moreover, the lack of focus on the story aspect didn't really matter to me as I was having lots of fun and already overly immersed in the beautiful and interactive background objects. Even though it is a really short game to complete(finished under under 3 hours), it is definitely worth to get for how fun and creative it is!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed Portal, then you will enjoy this relaxing puzzle platformer with beautiful background graphics and an incredible symphonic soundtrack. Price is steep but it is very much worth it. The twist is that your character is a pictogram on a pedestrian sign, and each sign is a mini-maze with entrances and items that you need. Each segment of the game is a set of usually more than one sign, and you have to move around and connect the signs in specific ways to navigate your way out and collect the items. There are probably 100+ different puzzles in total (again, many are very simple but it gets more challenging later in the game). The best introduction is by watching a few minutes of the gameplay video on the store page. The maze graphics are functional but very clear (like you expect with city pictograms). The background music is reminiscent of James Horner's movie themes from the 1980s onward (look him up on imdb) and give this a larger-than-life feel. This game unfolds like Portal (although you don't have a "helpful" AI to guide you through the puzzles). There are no verbal or text clues, much of the fun is figuring out what you need to do to navigate the game world. The early puzzles are easy and teach you aspects of game mechanics that you will need to solve later levels. Puzzles range from very easy to challenging that you get later in the game. You can expect anywhere from about 3 hours to 15+ hours of game play to finish the game with extra some secret stuff hinted at (longer times if you want to savor the puzzles or end up staring blankly at the screen at a puzzle you can't figure out, I'm not sure how people can finish this in 3 hours). People have reported speedruns of about an hour.Just when you think the next door leads you to the end, you see a whole new game world with new types of puzzles in front of you. If you are in doubt about buying this (the price is a bit steep), try the demo. Well worth it!EDIT: Ever watch a movie so detailed, with so many character nuances, that you just want to stop part way through and rewind to the beginning to make sure you got everything? I did this with this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful and imaginative little game, that feels cozy and comfortable too. The puzzles are worthwhile and never veer into frustrating or 'BS' territory. It finds a good balance of complexity and leisure. Overall this was a great and well crafted experience.If I had any criticism, and I'm digging deep here, I'd recommend not trying to knock out the game in a single sitting. Two sittings was a good dosage for me. The game does NOT feel repetitive, it consistently finds new ways to add elements and keep its gameplay and puzzles fresh. The slight fatigue comes from the gameplay not being broken up very much, with constant puzzle solving simply being rewarded with another puzzle. That's my only complaint, and it's hardly an issue (just take a small break, which the game allows at any time)Otherwise, almost every other element was positive for me. Loved this game, and would definitely recommend The Pedestrian to people who like inventive puzzles, cool aesthetics, and/or charming games
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Only 2h on record at this time but since this game is done with much love and very entertaining to play I'd like to throw in my positive review already. No crashes, solid logic in puzzles and the 3D-environment that solely serves as puzzle-decoration is a nice touch.Also there's a native Linux version which I appreciate greatly. Hopefully it also generates additional sales once the steam deck goes live.Only oddity I thought was a bug is that you have no mouse cursor in the first minute of the game and in the menus. I though it was a problem with the Linux version and tried the windows version too, but it's intended.Hope to see a DLC or second game some day.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The Pedestrian is a detailed platform-puzzler that starts small, adds garnishes, twists, and dimensions. It's at times cute, playful, patient, challenging, and even sentimental. Rarely, if ever, does it feel punishing.Well worth the price of admission. I would purchase a sequel, especially one that expanded its framework & universe in the manner that the brilliant Portal 2 elevated the groundwork laid in Portal 1.I suggest thinking through the puzzles that may stump you at first instead of looking up the solution; discovering how it all fits together is so satisfying.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a creative, mind-bending puzzle game! There is a little platforming, but not much so don't let that scare you off. The background and transition art is amazing and the little details around are fantastic to look at. (As a former pedestrian during college, the little touches to the background art really makes me happy, like stickers put random places, haha.) I'm an experienced puzzler, and it's taken me about 2 hours to complete 3/7 stages. The music is pleasant too - usually I turn the music off very shortly into games because it drives me crazy and I can't manage to listen to it very long, but this game I haven't felt the need to do that yet. Which is saying alot, imo.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Only a couple of hours in and I can already imagine the amount of time I'll lose in this one. Beautifully done with a great soundtrack. _childDocuments_.review: This was such a lovely game. For only about 4-5 hours of play I will say that the price is pretty large, but overall the game is very fun and engaging. The puzzle mechanics are very interesting and unlike what I've seen in a lot of other puzzle games I have played. The atmosphere of the game was also very good. The soundtrack for this game is amazing and the art is lovely too. I highly recommend it as a late night vibe session kind of game. Also the achievements are unlocked just by playing through it, so its a good game if you are a completionist.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was an experience, and one that I enjoyed taking.The game follows a stick figure like you see on Bathroom signs as it moves across various signs, platforming through the signs into different signs. All the while, the player is able to see the areas around these signs, showing the world outside of the signs as well, which can make for some nice scenic screenshots if you're into those.The game does also throw in a few interesting challenges as well, having the player make their path through different sign panels in order to solve puzzles and progress further through the game, all with a very calming and enjoyable music within the background. My favorite moment of the game was a manic that comes near the end of the game, which I will not spoil for those interested in getting the game yourself.Overall, the game can be an easy 2-4 hour experience, but one that is well worth the time and effort to put in. While $20 might be a bit expensive for such a short amount of time, it is well worth getting when you are able to, especially during a Steam sale.

_childDocuments_.review: The Pedestrian has a cool idea and aesthetic, but it falls back on just pretty typical puzzle-platformer and one-hit-death platformer tropes that prevent it from being very interesting beyond the nifty premise.The core aesthetic of this game is rad. You play as a little person icon that adventures through various signage through a dreamlike city. When you reach the exit of one sign, you’ll pan the camera through the environment to a new sign. This part of the game is its shining achievement. It works well as transitions between levels, but the best is when the surfaces the levels are drawn on have some physicality in the greater world. Example, there’s a point where a level is on the side of a large crate that’s suspended from a crane. The crate rocks back and forth as it moves and stops with the crane. It’s a cool conceit done well. The main mechanical gimmick involves you arranging the signs and connecting the exits. There are some clever variations of this throughout the game, but it’s never as interesting as I hoped. One the reasons it falls short of its potential is reliance on very ordinary puzzle-platformer conventions. If you’ve played a puzzle-platformer in the last 15 years then you’ve already experienced a lot of what this game does. The addition of moving rooms around and altering which rooms they connect to tends to make things feel more tedious than clever. This is especially expressed when you fail. For most of the game, if you touch an obstacle (like a buzzsaw or laser beam) you die and the level resets. Occasionally you have to intentionally die to reset the world, but often death means you have redo the puzzle you just did from the beginning. This wouldn’t be so bad but the game doesn’t have the sort of precise control of a more Meatboy-like game. The platforming is never so demanding, but sometimes the lack of precision will cause an annoying death or you’ll end up putting an item in a place you didn't intend. Then you have to do the last 5 minutes over when you already solved the puzzle in your head 10 minutes ago. The actual puzzle design is also rather uninspiring. They have some real clever ideas, but never quite put them together to make fun puzzles. Many of them devolve into situations where you know exactly what to do and you just need to execute it in the correct order. On the occasions where I did find myself stuck, it was mostly because of some fiddly solutions that almost always involved the game’s equivalent of backtracking. Overall I find it to be a mediocre game that has a really cool premise. I almost wish it was more about exploration than puzzle solving. Like if this game was mostly a 2D walking simulator I think I would have had a better time with it, especially considering it’s end game mechanics. As of now though, I don’t really think I could recommend it. It’s not terrible and I suspect it’ll win some awards, but it doesn’t reach its potential. I will say that I watched the current world record speedrun and it makes for a good speedrun game.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a backer for this game.I think it's very good, with a fair amount of great ideas.The overall look is nice, all environments look good and there's a ton of small details. The concept is awesome, the puzzles are fun and clever and if that's your kind of games, you should definetly get it!Even though the experience is pleasant, I was feeling peckish at the end. I would have liked super hardcore secret stuff.The ending is cool but Overall, recommended 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: A whimsical puzzle platformer which is a bit too vapid and pedestrian.  It’s an odd style choice having the backgrounds contain so much detail and 3D graphics yet the game area itself is relatively basic 2D line drawings, but it makes the presentation different and adds to the setting.  The puzzles are well designed and offer a good and varied level of challenge, but they aren’t really that remarkable and can be fiddly at times.  I was expecting a lot more variety in the signs and for them to be actual sign designs as opposed to just compartments of a level.  The number codes are pointless, the instant death parts feel out of place and just as the game offers something potentially interesting, it ends.  The music is cheery but when it stops, the silence is noticeable and the game isn’t that long and has no replay value.  Conveying instructions through pictures instead of words fits nicely with the setting, but is a bit too obscure at times and overall, I didn’t really enjoy it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this a lot.  A nice progression of difficulty, and I like how they structure it so figure out the new functionality seemingly on your own.   The puzzles could seem a little overwhelming at start, but they were all doable without outside hints. And the ending puzzle had me laughing in surprise several times when figuring out how it worked.

_childDocuments_.review: Cleared the game, didn't really use a walkthrough (I had seen a lets play of the easier levels like 3 years ago, I don't think I retained THAT MUCH)This game is very good at making you feel smart. As the puzzles progress so long as you take it step by step you don't have to worry too hard about losing progress. Some fun secrets for those with a good memory/good observational skills.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: With 4.5 hours to 100% this Indie Puzzle Platformer game, it was an interesting experience. If you are looking for a short game but enjoyable (assuming you like the genre) then this makes for a quick adventure compared to games like The Talos Principle or Infinifactory. The game mechanic that the platforms themselves are the puzzle pieces can make your head spin at first but you can catch on pretty quickly - which is good because then they become switches, circuits, etc.Pros:- Visually it almost feels like you are running through comic strip panels as you move from one sign to the next- Moving through the real world as you move from one panel to the next is also visually stimulating- Music is nice but I wouldn't pay to listen to outside of the gameCons:- Price seems a bit steep for a game that is short and there isn't really that much of a learning curve- Steam achievements are a joke and really just show your progression in the game with no real challengeOverall, a good game but not enough to leave installed on my computer between play throughs.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Challenging puzzles, soothing music, and atmospheric environments await! My only problem is a puzzle in the alley where you have to get the coil/cable item. The puzzle introduces a one-time gimmick that isn't explained or ever used again which made it frustrating. The solution is to use the spring to shoot the figure through the portal/gate onto a different plate which carries over the inertia from the mirrored L-shaped plate. Aside from that one puzzle, everything is introduced nicely and gets progressively more challenging and manages to subvert your expectations beautifully! The ending feels like a nice little conclusion and while the very last moment in the game is a bit out of place, it doesn't ruin the otherwise down-to earth environment. The game runs smoothly and is very optimised. Kudos!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The Pedestrian is a fantastic (mostly) side scrolling puzzle-platform game with an interesting gameplay idea, mixing the 2D world of a little figure (pedestrian) and the 3D outside world, that both have to interact with each other to find your way through the story.It's been great fun, has got some nice, not too hard, puzzles and it's certainly a recommendation ...
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: I loved every second of it. The puzzles are challenging but very rewarding, as you get that sense of accomplishment. You really feel proud of advancing through the game, especially during the ending part. My only problem is how short the game is, considering how I beat it in 4 hours. But besides that, I loved every second of it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Damn, that's one of the few games that made me write a review about it! I just finished it (FYI 4.4h, taking my time between puzzles but trying to solve them fast).And that one is a gem, I consider it the little brother of Portal. There was so much effort put into tiny details, most of them are not even playable but add much to the game, helping others that are playable to blend in perfectly.That's one of those rare games where you have no HUD, everyhing you see is part of the game itself, even the menu which is displayed on an old green CRT screen.The difficulty progression is amazing, going from super-easy to quite hard at the end. I had to think quite a lot on the last puzzles. Also, when new mechanics are added, they are often included in simple puzzles before getting more complex, so there is no need for an explanation text, you just understand what you have to do.I wouldn't want to spoil you the end, but wow, I wasn't expecting such puzzles!! You NEED to try it!My only regret about this game is that I bought it on sales, not at the full price!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game....with a surprise at the end. The puzzles keep evolving and are never too hard. If you are good at puzzle games it will be actually very relaxing and easy. The atmosphere is great and the idea of the 2D platforming through signs is perfectly executed.The ending was just pure heartache.Good job !
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this, except for a small caveat which I'll get to later. This game is not a difficult puzzle games, even the hardest puzzles here is unlikely to keep the scratching your head for more than maybe 10-15 minutes, but the game is an experience with remarkable environmental storytelling, environments, situations etc. which was HIGHLY enjoyable. I recommend playing the demo to give that out. Now to the caveat I cannot sufficiently put into words how much I hated and was aggravated by the finale. It isn't anything they do wrong narratively, just a mechanical change, but it did effect me a lot, yes. I'm not one of those people who will say that a bad finale completely ruins the experience, because I feel that's disingenuous. I had enjoyed the game immensely up until that point. But it did very much aggravate me and was a terrible closing to a game that I very much had enjoyed. That said, my overall feelings of the game are definitely positive.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: A complete playthrough doesn't take long (4-5 hours), but the puzzles are very cleverly designed. The overall difficulty is medium and it does require some deep thinking sometimes (and can get quite tricky a few times). The visuals and soundtracks are very atmospheric, especially the camera movements - they're like birds flying through seeing different parts of the city. The finale part is interesting and can be exploited more. No language barrier at all (cuz there're no words). The only con is that you cannot choose or locate a particular level easily (cuz there's no menu or level selection either).
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent puzzle game that takes a surprisingly large amount of 2D thinking. i.e. "If my character is here then will this happen? What about over here?" Not terribly long which is truly a shame. I await DLC with bated breath. However the real star here is the presentation; how the camera moves between puzzles is innovative and the soundtrack is beautiful, only coming through as you complete a puzzle and giving you a sense of accomplishment. As I type I am reminded that I can only play this for the first time once. The sense of adventure and satisfaction I felt upon completing a puzzle, the excitement at what comes next; I will never feel that in the same way again. The most I can hope for is a reflection of that as I introduce this game to others. Which, believe you me, I *will* be doing. However, the completion remains a tad bittersweet.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: A very good puzzle game. Despite the lack of a standard tutorial, it is very quick to understand the principles of the represented world. All elements of the game (music, graphics, gameplay) are refined and very harmonious with each other.The only drawback is that the game is relatively short.It basically ends when the best part begins.I got the impression that the developers wanted to take the game further, but they ran out of funds.Especially since there were elements in the game that looked like we were going to return to them (e.g. after unlocking the second stickfigure)."Or maybe I'm wrong and these are secrets? Hmm ... I have to play again to find out."However, I recommend purchasing this game, not just for the game itself.But also in order to support authors who publish high-quality content.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Buy this game. No, seriously. Buy it. Show the devs some love and play this wonderfully short but expertly crafted game. Everything's intuitive and if a complete brickhead like me can make it through these puzzles, you can too. This game has the same feel on first play like Portal 1. You think you understand it...and then it goes and proves you wrong. Save the money you'd use to buy big overblown, overhyped 'next-gen graphical fidelity'-style games and buy this one. Seriously, why haven't you yet? Go. Shoo. Stop reading this and go buy this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start off by saying I do like this game and feel it's worth the price tag IF you like puzzle games. But it felt like there were a lot of missed opportunities here, I feel bad for saying this because I know this game took 5 years to make but the consumer has a right to know all the good and bad since it costs money after all. I'll make this relatively quick by listing pros and cons of this game. It personally took me about 3-4 hours to beat this game (I spent a lot of time AFK). (SOME SPOILERS, YOU'VE BEEN WARNED)!Pros:-Passion project, refreshing as it's not just another corporate cash-grab designed to siphon a fortune out of your wallet-Background had a LOT of effort put into it, looks especially nice at the last third of the game-Has a really good prologue that gets you hyped on what you're about to play.-Soothing music that helps build the atmosphere-The ending looks amazing, showing that there's an even bigger and better project coming from this studio in the future.Cons:-This is when the "missed opportunity" comes into play as the background had all of this effort put into it but does almost nothing creative to interact with the gameplay, which felt neglected at times-The last section of the game introduced a completely different mechanic which felt rushed through, doing something unique at the end of your game doesn't always go well, and this is no exception.-Game gets repetitive, 80% of it is just "here is the main area, go to these 3-4 sub-areas to get through," which got old fast.-There could have been a narrative added to the game in order to engage the player in what was going on, lack of a story further made it feel like style over substance at times.Conclusion: A good passion project that felt like it had so much more potential that it could have lived up to but ended up falling a little short. However, this game nudges closer to being good despite some shortcomings, most puzzle game fans will end up liking the game rather than hating it.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a fantastic game as a light brain tease.  It was never so rudimentary that i didn't have to think about it, and never so convoluted that I had to study.  It is the rare game that can be light without also being simple or empty, this is one of those rare games. I certainly recommended it to any gamer (like parents of small children) that loves video game puzzles but lacks the time to dig into a massive title.

_childDocuments_.review: Exceptional puzzle game that follows in the footsteps of others by blocking your progress until you've overcome simple puzzles, then uses your newfound understanding to pose more and more ruthless puzzles as you progress.The trailer is representative of the game. You navigate 2d platforms, pushing boxes, throwing switches and the like, then head for the exit. Many of the puzzle involve dropping out to the real world to alter the route for your stickman. There are a few timing based challenges which are thankfully very simple to execute; nothing more stressful than jumping and pressing a button - a good thing for those not seeking a game that requires practice and precision.You will spend the majority of your time planning, visualising all or part of the solution and conducting a little experimentation, until you figure out what should happen and in what order to get out of the room and on your way with whatever gadget you need next. Later on, you'll need to incorporate new mechanics and relearn where all the boundaries lie.Puzzle games can suffer from tutorial syndrome, but The Pedestrian never comes close to this. Every time I learnt a new mechanic, the game followed up with half a dozen unique puzzles that went beyond the scope of the dedicated tutorial areas, and each incorporated things from previous areas - just how you want it.All tolled, the game should take around 4 hours give or take a bit, but that all depends on how much time you spend solving problems. A better indication might be that there are roughly 50 puzzles that can halt up your progress.This was a Kickstarter game; there's been plenty of eyes on it. I can't speak to the update history but found no bugs as of summer '21. There isn't anything to do after finishing, no bonus levels or extras, no achievements to track down or alternative routes to exploit, and the credits read like graffiti on a passing freight train. Hold LMB to skip... you're welcome.On the plus side, it appears the game's levels were also crowd-sourced, which is a great choice and explains why the difficulty curve was so smooth and the challenges so varied. I'm guessing here, but I'd wager the backers were offered a level design tool and the producer then cherry-picked from submitted levels to build out the game.If you like puzzle games, this is a must own. It'll give you a good challenge and make you feel justifiably smart.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: At the end, all I wanted was more.  Not in a bad way, not by any means, this game was so great that I wish there was more.  The Pedestrian is a puzzle-platformer where you can rearrange and connect street signs to solve puzzles and get to the next area.  Set in many gorgeous, loving-rendered 3D environments with a great soundtrack, you’re left wanting to continue exploring and solving.  The game effortlessly teaches you its mechanics, with its puzzles so cleverly designed you’ll get the rush of success every time you manage to solve one.  I want to say more, but I feel that the game is best described by playing it yourself.  As with many puzzle games, to say any more about it would be a disservice to what they have created.  Some may believe the game is too short given its cost, as many of the other reviews point out.  If you strongly believe that a game’s worth is dependent on its hours per dollar you get out of it, then this game would probably only interest you during a sale.  I used to be that way as well, and for some games, that’s a fine metric to measure by.  However, if you’re willing to put that aside, I promise you that the game is worth every dollar, if not in time, then in everything else it has to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: The Pedestrian is a very good example of a well-made puzzle game. I'm not going to spoil, but nearly all the mechanics make logical sense, and they're designed in a way that makes them recognizable in an instant. Said mechanics seem simple at first glance, but as the game progresses they're mixed with old mechanics and played with in such a way that it never feels like you're doing the same solution (keep an eye out for those big doors you see in the trailers!). The final mechanic the game shows you is purely awesome. I wish there were more puzzles like that, but again, maybe less was more.I like the world building, too. Each area has a feel to it, and despite the fact that you technically only see one person (you!) the world is still alive, from the hustle and bustle of the city to the eeriness of the subways to the sleepiness of the alleys. If you keep your eyes peeled, there's even some measurable activity. For example, in one part, there's a burrito that has a bite taken out of it each time you return. When you're about to finally leave that part, the burrito is gone, with only some beans left for proof.Would I recommend buying it for full price? Not really, no. My playtime was just short of 3 hours, and considering I carried over my save from the demo, the game SHOULD be about 3 and a half hours long. I got it for 60% off ($8.00 USD). As with anything on Steam, just snag it when it's on sale. If you feel generous, though, there's nothing wrong with paying the whole 20 bucks (USD).

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely incredible. The Pedestrian combines old flash puzzle platformers with The Witness. It's one of the few games that I found myself completely unable to pull myself away from until it was over. I did happen to encounter one soft-lock, but it was quickly fixed by saving & quitting and loading back in.

_childDocuments_.review: The Pedestrian is a fantastic puzzle game with light platforming elements. I absolutely love the aesthetic and theme of the game. The Pedestrian perfectly implements the concept of a stick figure roaming through the world via street signs and digital screens. The music fits the journey well, but it eventually fades out instead of looping. This is a minor complaint, but it is especially noticeable during more difficult puzzles where the awkward silence becomes oddly distracting. The best part of the game is of course the puzzles which are creative and satisfying to complete. The puzzles are constantly adding new mechanics to test your problem solving skills. My only regret is that I finished the game hungry for more.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: My all-time favorite puzzle games off the top of my head are Talos Principle, The Witness, Antichamber, Gorogoa, and of course Portal 2. And I am not exaggerating when I say The Pedestrian is up there with all of them in my book.The puzzles were inventive and always had me guessing, The difficulty was a literal perfect balance across the board. Got frustrated a couple times, but it was never the games fault. Visually it was always fun to look at and the perspective was so unique and charming. The actual quality of the 3D graphics at points could have been better i guess, but it never detracted from the experience. Maybe my biggest critique is that i wish it would have lasted just a bit longer. Maybe 30 min to 1 hour longer as (no spoilers) the ending was satisfying, but I could have definitely spent just a little more time in the world and been just as happy.As it stands though, it's difficult to think of negatives with this one. I'm so impressed. I saw the trailer for this game and was sold, but I still did not expect something this wonderful. Highly recommended, honestly a must-play imo, for anybody who likes platformers and puzzle games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: Quick Description:-The Pedestrian is a puzzle platformer w/ a gorgeous visual style, a very fun story that will make you smile, and a very unique premise.  This is a game I've been excited to play for quite some time.  However, I was a little disappointed w/ the actual puzzles themselves, which makes up a majority of the game.  The puzzles actually remind me of the puzzles from Cocoon quite a bit.  Most of the puzzles felt either too easy or tedious due to the long list of steps that they required.  I also found the paint mechanic confusing at times, b/c I only really learned the rules through lots of trial and error (do the objects go back to original location or do I go back to start or both?).  At the end of the day, this is such a charming and like-able game, but I'd recommend picking it up on a hefty sale.Consensus:-Middle of the Road Game (Tier 4 and makes up 25% of my reviews).  I really want to give this game a higher score, but I just didn't have nearly as much fun during my 6 hr playthrough as I was expecting.  I think the game length is fine (4-6 hrs for most fans of the genre), but I realize that others may expect far more content from a game w/ a $20 price tag.  I do think that this game may be a good choice for those looking for a more beginner friendly logic puzzle game as this game is far more forgiving than most of the other games in this genre.  Wait for a 50-75% sale and see for yourself if The Pedestrian is a worthy addition to your library.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: The Pedestrian is quite the mind-bending, but very fun adventure! The core mechanics of the game sort of remind me of the old flash game Continuity, but The Pedestrian builds off of that and expands that idea to a world of fun and unique possibilities. Every area you explore comes with new mechanics, beautiful scenery, and a true sense of immersion that really makes you feel like you're apart of the adventure.Now with everything I love about the game I will say the performance has had some hiccups all throughout. As a life long Mac user I've come to expect there to be small issues here and there, but I've found this game to run really badly on higher graphics settings, which I find a bit unusual because the specs of my Mac more than meet the recommended requirements. I suspect this is likely an issue of the game's optimization and if the devs were to consider looking into this I think it would be very beneficial, because I would LOVE to experience this game in its intended higher definition.Overall though this is a really good game. If you enjoy games like The Witness or the aforementioned Continuity then you will feel right at home here!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a complete delight on all fronts. It is a shining example of "more than a sum of it's parts".The puzzles themselves are pretty good honestly. Quite a few made me scratch my head wondering how they could be solved. Every area introduces a new mechanic and a new way of interacting with the environments which is always neat. The game is also a bit open ended in that you can choose which puzzles to solve in an area. My one problem with the puzzles is that the difficulty curve is a pretty wild graph where certain puzzles will make your ears blow smoke but the next one you would breeze through.The visuals are absolutely gorgeous. The world around the signs is vibrant, colorful and beautifully realised. You definitely feel like you're moving through the various places in the game rather than simply being limited to the signs and papers and stickers. The very pause menu itself is made of actual CRT TV screens placed discreetly in various places. You even control the motion of real world objects in a limited fashion which affects the puzzles themselves which gives me the fuzzies every time I trigger it.The music is fantastic and a neat mix of jazz and a melodious orchestral arrangement and is a very gentle accompaniment to the experienceMy one hang-up would be the the length compared to the price. I bought it at the launch discount and felt like I got every penny's worth out of it but it may not be as attractive at full price. Nevertheless, I highly recommend you pick this up if only to appreciate a really well made polished, fantastic little romp
_childDocuments_.name: The Pedestrian

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing game! the puzzles are not easy, but not so hard that i ever had to look up a guide to finish the game. The environments in the game look awesome, and the music is beautiful. I plan on buying the soundtrack when it gets released for sure. You may see the other reviews that say that the music "cuts out" or something similar. The music fades out if you are taking a while to finish a puzzle. I think that having any song going the entire time you were struggling with a puzzle would get annoying or frustrating fairly quickly. The music does come back when you finish a puzzle and move to another area though, so it feels a bit like an additional reward on top of making progress. The music waits for you :)Overall I'd say that this game is worth every one of the $20 it's listed for - zero bugs, great puzzles, and great polish.The only thing I could really ask for is a level select after the game is over, since I'd like to look at some of the environments again  , but you can play through the game again after you're done.
