_childDocuments_.review: ------------Gameplay-------------- ☐ Magnificent☑ Amazing ☐ Great ☐ Could be better ☐ No thanksManifold Garden is a game where you traverse non-euclidean spaces and infinitely repeating rooms to solve puzzles. The game play loop feels very similar to the first portal where you would solve a puzzle and move to the next room, but unlike portal the main feature of the game is changing the direction of gravity. It seems simple enough but the insane amount of stuff that you can do kind of suprising.------------Graphics--------------☑ Magnificent ☐ Amazing ☐ Great ☐ Could be better ☐ No thanksThe graphics of the game are the main reason I picked up the game myself, and I was not disappointed. The graphics themselves are just like any modern game and I would expect that the average computer could run it, but the artistic style of the game itself is outstanding. There were points in this game that absolutely amazed me. If you like Escher or geometry this is a perfect example of a game that got it right.------------Sound----------------- ☐ Magnificent☑ Amazing ☐ Great ☐ Could be better ☐ No thanksThe music is good, but is very atmospheric and dynamic which is very nice to hear. The main reason the sound score is so high is because of the effects. Wow. It's best to experience it for yourself but all I have to say is its a treat.------------Story----------------- ☐ Magnificent ☐ Amazing☑ Great ☐ Could be better ☐ No thanksThe game doesn't have an outright story or narrative, but certain things in the game write the story for you. Without spoiling much all I can say is you need to read in between the lines on this one, but once it clicks its an enjoyable story.------------Difficulty------------ ☐ Absolutely insane ☐ A good challenge☑ Fairly difficult ☐ Casual gameplay ☐ My grandma could beat thisThe main difficulty is puzzles, and oh man are they good. I got stuck plenty but I never really got stuck for long. Thinking outside the box and being creative rewards you as most of the solutions, just like the game itself, are a bit wild. Despite the difficulty, I never felt frustrated or annoyed with a puzzle and after every one I had a smile of satisfaction on my face. It was just the right difficulty for a game like this.------------Game Length----------- ☐ Single Session☑ A couple days of gameplay ☐ Average game length ☐ Longer than most ☐ Infinitely replayableI beat it fairly quickly, taking under four hours, but it felt much longer during the play sessions. I did spread it out over a couple days but if your someone who likes to spend more time on a game all at once, you might be able to beat it in a single session. Of course being a puzzle game, completion time will vary between people depending on if they get stuck on puzzles and whatnot.------------Should you buy--------☑ Yes ☐ Wait for a sale ☐ If theres nothing else to get ☐ No ☐ Absolutely notFor anyone who likes a spectacle, puzzles, or having your mind blown this is the game for you. Should you buy it? Yes. Should you wait for a sale? Maybe. If you don't like games that take a shorter amount of time to complete, maybe wait for a sale. I myself got it during a sale and had I known what the game was like, I would have easily gotten it full price. If your not someone who enjoys puzzle games, wait for a sale or for a rainy day when you have nothing to do, but try it out, it really puts a twist on the genre and I think anyone can enjoy it. In conclusion, Manifold Garden is a game that, in my opinion, rivals portal as one of the best puzzle games I've ever played and my only complaint is that I couldn't have played more of it. 9.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: This one kind of hurts to vote down. _childDocuments_.review: A friend once described FLCL to me as 'Excel Saga on Excel Saga'. In much the same way, this game is Antichamber on Antichamber.A bit more seriously, this game is quite impressive. Unlike Antichamber, this game operates heavily around a sense of scale. A lot of the places in which puzzles are solved are literally infinitely large with huge structures floating in an endlessly repeating void that loops at the edges, often with some of Antichamber and Portal's signature non-Euclidean doors thrown in. Unlike Antichamber, none of the mechanics ever really feel oddly hacky. In Antichamber, especially later in the game, I'd often find myself wondering if that was really how I was supposed to do something, but never really had that in here.Unfortunately, the game is not perfect. None of the puzzles are particularly difficult, and basically every single one can be done with little effort past figuring out where and what all of the pieces involved are. Still, they are fun to do. The bigger problem, by far, is that the game is  short. I beat the entire thing in slightly over 4 and a half hours,  Edit: Never mind. There is extra content.The bottom line is that the game is very fun but extremely short. It's not too expensive, though. If you've been looking for another non-Euclidean puzzle game that'll have some neat woahs in it like Antichamber, or maybe'll even surpass it a few times, this is it.

_childDocuments_.review: Visually fantastic game, great sense of non-euclidian space. The puzzles were never frustratingly difficult, except one spot for me, and that was because of a bug. For anyone else who might encounter this: in the red area, a yellow tree fruit didn't spawn, and I spent an hour or so thinking I was doing it wrong. Restarting the game caused the fruit to spawn and I could continue without problem. If the devs see this: sorry, I don't have any repro steps, I had just been playing from the beginning for 2-3 hours.The music was great, but it was a bit disappointing that for most of the game it was overly subdued. I think if the majority of the game's music followed the style of the last bit of the game and the end credits, it would have made for a fantastically groovy experience. As it is now, though, the bulk of the game's music is too low-key and chill for my tastes. A Groove Mode where the soundtrack tone is closer to the credits song, but for the whole game, would be amazing.All in all, a great puzzle game. 10/10 (11/10 if there was a Groove Mode).

_childDocuments_.review: ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥! Get ready for some pretty unreserved gushing. This game is AMAZING!The most obvious feature is the infinitely looping space. This core mechanic makes for some interesting (and beautiful!) environments. It's like exploring the inside of a kaleidoscope!This game is billed as a puzzler which of course it is, but I also loved the exploration aspect. You have to understand the space and resources in it before you can go about solving anything. This initial portion of discovery in an abstract world was very compelling!What got me as I played through the game was the no-so-obvious cosmetic or UI elements that really showed some lovely attention to detail: The informative use of colour to indicate orientation; the tesseracts; the 4D➜1D before the credits... All just beautifully done.It's hard to find criticism of this game. But, if I could change anything it would be to make the latter levels a tad more challenging.While I acknowledge that this is of course very subjective, personally I found the pacing for the early parts of the game (as you're getting familiar with the mechanics) very good. But, once you grasp how things work, there were times where I just flew through a level and was almost surprised that there wasn't more to do in order to complete it.Admittedly, this is a nightmare to "balance". I did get lost once and it took me a while to find my way back to where I'd wandered off from. Depending on how much you like the exploration aspect, this could get frustrating.My biggest wish is simply for MORE! I don't want this game to be over! I'll likely play through it again at least once. What I'd really love is procedurally generated levels! That's a tall order I know. But, I think it would suit this game perfectly. If offered with a few user selectable complexity options to ideally accommodate a wide variety of players, I'd likely never uninstall.Hope the devs see that last bit. I'd definitely pony-up for a procedural generation DLC :-)TL;DR If you like clever puzzlers with unique mechanics and gorgeous minimalist graphics with great attention to detail: BUY IT!
_childDocuments_.name: Manifold Garden

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a TRIP! I first got it on Switch and finished it, but I wanted to experience it with no hardware limitations so I bought it again here. That's right, folks - this is a game so good I bought it twice!The broad gameplay loop is that you'll enter a hub room with a puzzle that can only be solved by solving other puzzles in the rooms adjacent to the hubs. Some of those adjacent rooms are hubs themselves. The world is navigated on flat planes at 90-degree angles, but you can't jump. You can only turn the world... or are you just turning gravity?The puzzles are based on getting a cube to the goal point, but the cubes don't move unless you're aligned with their parent plane. Manifold Garden is kind enough to ease you into it with a wordless tutorial that teaches you the basics on how to solve puzzles, but after a couple of hours I hit some puzzles that I had to sleep on.The visual design is... well, William Chyr *is* an architect. Sometimes when I traverse the levels, I feel like I walk from a modern skyscraper office building, through a doorway, and on to the steps of a Mayan pyramid or into an Indian well. Almost all of the levels repeat in all directions, and if you're "outside" you can traverse the level infinitely. With the repetition of cream-coloured geometric structures with purple outlines, Manifold Garden achieves a kind of psychedelic experience.The music helps too, with a chill atmosphere and synth effects right out of the movies Blade Runner and Annihilation.I cannot recommend this game enough.However, I must note that if you have trouble with visual-spatial awareness, you might struggle to navigate Manifold Garden. On the other hand, what a marvellous challenge it would be to overcome your troubles and finish the game!

_childDocuments_.review: An enthralling Mobius/Tesseract inspired exercise in walking simulation. From the simple idea of gravity manipulation comes something truly exquisite, and the sound design undoubtedly plays a major part in the experience. Aside from the initial task of moving cubes/keys around, the extended mechanics are a grab bag. The particular mechanics may seem annoying, but the level, or rather, the room you're in, never does.The kaleidoscopic psychedelia is a bit gratuitous, and the levels could arguably stand to be better organized in sequence, but every moment of this game looked and felt incredible, even and  when I didn't know where to go next.

name: System Shock
detailed_description: System Shock is the fully fledged remake of the ground breaking original from 1994, combining cult gameplay with all-new HD visuals, updated controls, an overhauled interface and all-new sounds & music; it even has the original voice actor of SHODAN, one of gaming’s most iconic villains. Witness the rebirth of one of the greatest and most influential games ever created. SHE IS SELF-AWARE AND AWARE OF YOU Meet SHODAN. The psychotic AI has taken control of Citadel Station and turned the crew into an army of cyborgs and mutants; She now plans to do the same to Earth. You must explore and battle your way through the depths of a space station gone to hell. Stop SHODAN and avert humanity’s destruction. HER TERMINATION IS OUR SALVATION FEATURES - Fight to death in the depths of space - Face off against the forces of a rogue AI gone mad - Improve your skills and adapt to take on your foes - Discover a non-linear story unfolding at your own pace - Jack into cyberspace to hack the system and open other routes - Innovative art style combines retro future design with modern technology Become fully immersed: shoot, brawl, crawl, climb, leap and think your way through Citadel Station.

_childDocuments_.review: Take an amazing classic game, make it a little more approachable for a modern audience, and most importantly do no harm.  They did a great job of modernizing a classic while keeping the feel right.  Anyone who played the original, anybody that tried and failed over the years, and anyone that wants to experience one of the first and one of the best immersive sims should pick this up.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Game has a major bug where it will delete your savegame and you lose all of your effort and have to start again. Seems it has happened to quite a few people. This is NOT the sort of game where you can "Speedrun" what you've done - it's very much a grind, so I really have to wonder what kind of idiot thought it was OK to botch the save system such that the autosave, over which you have no control, completely destroys your efforts... And yeah, this fault is pretty much by intentional design. Until this serious fault is acknowledged and fixed and you can make a few savegames I suggest avoiding this game altogether. Prior to that, it was nice to go back, but seriously, I don't want to play the whole game all over again and go through that grind just so I can see the ending. There are a few victims of this bug.

_childDocuments_.review: I really don't understand the positive reviews, 2 with the graphics update mod is a MUCH better game.The graphics are I suppose loyal to the first but are still really ordinary, the whole game is bright light city inside a space station which makes it very hard to select or see the buttons which open things and so on. The combat is meh, a lot of things make it annoying, hitting things in melee doesn't make enemies stagger or interrupt their attacks which leads to a lot of getting beaten up, even on lower difficulty there is a lot of enemy spawns all over the place which just becomes tedious. Example in 2 Medbay you might expect to encounter 1-2 enemies spawning when you enter a level, in this a previously cleared area had 12 in mobs of 4 so you get to play do I use all my ammo or lose a lot of health.The inventory system is 1. annoying 2. Even more annoying, you can vaporize pretty much all the junk you find which is a lot and then turn it into credits in a recycler when you find one you have to vaporize each item one at a time there's no automation to this. The need to complicate this from the nanite system of 2 is just baffling. It makes it an enormous chore to collect vaporize and then credit things. There are corpses everywhere, aliens, human robots, almost all of them have nothing, at all, but you gotta search em all and generally can't remember what you've searched or what you haven't.The puzzles were designed by someone who hates you and hates fun. They're irritating, poorly explained and really difficult with multiple options to fail and spend 20-30 minutes figuring just the right combo for each one. The cyberspace is some huge shoots things with magic lasers and get through a gigantic maze with no idea what exactly you're supposed to be doing, also with no navigation to objectives you're just supposed to figure it out while getting progressively more irritated and lost. I was expecting something more, as it is it's really tedious and for me not very fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I am disappointed. Not utterly disappointed, but still. I was not expecting so many flaws and cheesy stuff in this game. Some game design decisions are completely horrible and ruin the impression from the game big time. Luckily, I didn't pay the full price for the game, but for 20 Euro I had enough fun. However, I don't recommend anyone to pay the full price for the game because of the following:- Disabled and blocked game console (had to use Cheat Engine to enable it) - I want to be in control of my game- Inability to change difficulty settings during the game - really, how hard could it be to allow this?- Some areas are completely impassable even with easy difficulty setting, they are just eating up your resources and you die so many times that it gets you really angry- Inability to skip death cutscenes and the end credits - I have to wait for 30 or more seconds to just quickload, the credits ran for over 5 minutes!- Inability to save game in cyberspace - it kicks you out when you die and you have to start everything from the very beginning- General lack of direction throughout the game, no waypoints - it's very easy to get stuck or get lost, I had to periodically go online in order to figure out what to do next or where to find necessary items- No pointers to key locations on each station's level - it's very easy to get lost and finding your way to the necessary point may take a while- Very questionable level design - doors that are locked by default with nothing behind them, very vivid wall textures that make you color-sick sometimes- Reactor overload code is random, so you have to remember some numbers shown on small screens on 6 levels, but the game doesn't even give a hint about that, so you have to go back to every level and write down those numbers - that is a total waste of time- Very limited selection of enemies - I was expecting to see more variety- Very limited inventory space - you have to sacrifice loot in order to carry weapons, weapon upgrades reduce the carrying space even more and there are not many options to expand it- No highlighting of important stuff like implants and gear - it's very easy to miss them with those colorful textures and that makes the gameplay more difficult in irradiated or infected areas later- Very disappointing ending cutscrene, one of the worst I've ever seen so far - even the original game could do better than that- Really lousy song in the end, completely stupid and unrelated to the System Shock's universe - I mean couldn't you really get a proper System Shock alike song or track?- Lousy in-game music that doesn't resemble the original soundtrack - the game doesn't feel like a REMAKE at all- No "New game +" option - obviously no one bothered to make the game interesting enough for a rerun- No saving of changes when switching between tabs in the Settings menu - you should remember to always click "Apply" before selecting the new tab, otherwise settings are just silently lostNormally, I play each good game twice, but not this time... Comparing to Dead Space's remake this game is a lousy parody...

_childDocuments_.review: A good, fun game that kinda starts to struggle the further you get in it. while i didn't play the original game for long from what i played, and saw, this is a great remake. the cyber space is fun and the final boss is much better, i never played 1.0 version of the final boss so i don't know how that was, but almost anything is better than the original's. the inventory being taken from 2's instead of the original is also a huge improvement though i will say i think all items take too much space, most if not all weapons take 2x2 to 2x8 spaces and some items too. some items stack while others don't, you can't tell me you can't stack trays and pans into each other, and that scissors will take up all that space. the cargo lift is way too small, it is the same as a small storage container. the item stack is also very small i can only stack 10 batteries and patches, 3 first aid kits, which takes 2 slots, as such mods to increase the cargo lift and shrink the items feel necessary and i'll have those for future play throughs. you do get inventory upgrades but they don't upgrade enough, they give you half a row at the bottom of the inventory each, i could accept a full row each but half feels so little. another problem is enemy respawn, i had a case where i opened a door killed a mobile turret took like 3 steps before hearing something lift right behind me and it was another turret as it had respawned right behind me, it's also these respawning enemies that will take all your ammo. another problem with respawning enemies is that i had died in a spot and respawned to walk out directly into that virus thing in maintenance and i had no healing items so it would kill me fast and after finally killing it another 2 came by and i had to do the same thing all over again but against 2 and every time i dead my respawn health was lower and lower causing me to die faster, i was able to finally kill them and the game decided to randomly stop spawning enemies, this left this respawn point worthless and i'd have to go down to reactor to heal if i ever respawned there. the game has a habit of giving too much ammo when you don't need it and not enough when you do. i think that having to go from elevator to elevator gets tedious and really should have been just 1 elevator, or an elevator room that multiple people would be using for such things, that goes all the way up to security with the only second elevator in security as it would make sense that you need to pass through security to reach the bridge, kinda like shock 2 does, and you just need to get some sort of key to unlock going higher. while i understand having some codes set up so you can't skip bits of the game like the reactor, laser or the executive code it also makes it very annoying to have to search for them. some deaths felt very cheap and while i'll admit that i would forget to apply the shield, there were times where i had the shield on and would still get one shot by enemies, the final deigo fight did that multiple times, and in these instances along with the 2 times i was spawn camped made me feel like it wasn't a death by my fault, but just through shear cheapness and i know your fighting the ai of the space station but no matter what a cheap death is still a cheap death and can cause frustration, and once i had a moment where i felt like a heal point here would be nice not because it would add comfort but because it was right before deigo and i wanted one just to be able to continue moving forward, i still went to beat him with just a berserk and the saber thinking that would give me the achievement. i also am a firm beliver that there should be no permanent missables, i can understand post security, but i still think that due to how beta grove is designed it makes you want to rush through it, easily done with the rocket boots, especially if you don't have healing or any detox on you, but doing so can lock you out of the achievement for lowering security to 0 on all levels and a weapon mod. in cyberspace i had occasions where the enemies just stopped following me, this was more noticeable with the blue ones, they would just stop and stare at a wall sometimes notice me again and start attacking again, i don't know if that was intentional or not but it did save me in times. dying when you either don't have a respawn point or in boss fights force you to go through the first part of the respawn before showing you the game over screen makes it just annoying and i had to get used to reloading before the death animation finished just so i wouldn't have to deal with waiting through that to skip the game over,  i do need to remember of quick saving in games that have it i just forget to. finally the worst part of the game is the bridge, the robo mine section sucked and i remember hearing people saying it was worse in the original as they infinity respawned until you got out, luckily they don't do that in this, but it's still not fun and that last gauntlet of enemies before the last cortex reaver was just plain awful. i do hope for a shock 2 remake from nightdive though i doubt it'll happen any time soon if at all.

_childDocuments_.review: As one of the original backers of System Shock (Remake), I'm very happy that this exists at all. *Update* NVM, it finally arrived, this Collector's Edition just makes me so happy!! Honestly, the main thing I was thinking while playing this is that I wish this wasn't going to be the last entry in the System Shock series. But, SS3 continues to be non-existent and Nightdive probably won't want to return to SS any time soon. Minus the upcoming SS2 update. Which, I can't blame the studio if they never came back. I hope they do, I think they have the right idea here. But well, alas. Continually creepy, a little bit moon-logic puzzly, and ever nerve wracking combat, System Shock does a great job of updating the game to modern standards while keeping its original soul. It is frightening, it is frustrating, but it is oh so satisfying when you do accomplish your goals.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, good job Nightdive!Even though System Shock 2 gameplay was not very standard, I really loved the game ( since I loved Bioshock, deus ex and Prey 2017, I had to try the source) and since the remake to the original was already announced, I preferred to wait for it and worth it.Amazing job to improve the original game while preserving the essence of the original instead of reimaginating.Really enjoyed the retro graphics, gameplay, puzzles, story.I have some minor complains about the game, and some of those I think Nightdive could fix in a update for future buyers ( I already finished the game):URGENT Problems (these ones to me NEEDS to be fixed):- Before you go to the Bridge, It needs to appear a popup saying you would not be able to go back. What happened to me is, I didn't save a lot and got a problem with ammo, since I only was carrying the submachine gun and the railgun(no melee rapier). This lead me to not be able to continue, forcing me to use a cheat to get more 9mm ammo to be able to complete the game(I don't like to use cheats, so at least I only used the railgun ammo that I had/found). THIS IS BY FAR THE WORST PROBLEM OF THE GAME.- The death scene needs to have a skip button, dying is already the punishment( the scene is very good, but I don't need to see it everytime).Minor Problems:- Enemies barely feel any shot or hit, this could be improved.- Enemy AI doesn't behave very well when you are on a different height, making it easy to kill enemies bellow.- To make it easier for everyone, have an option to show your objectives. I've been stuck two times in the game where I didn't knew what to do, no matter what I red in the emails. It could be something to add a checklist when you open an email that contains some information to at least point you where you should go. Making it optional to enable/disable in the gameplay options would be great, could be shown in when you start a new game, something like: "Would you like a enable an Objective List? ( This is not the original experience of System Shock, but also can be disable in gameplay menu during game at anytime ).That's it, thank you Nightdive, I would really like you to actually re-imagine what a system shock 3 would be, since this one was more of a modernization of the classic and you guys already announced an enhanced version of the 2. You guys did really well! Thank you!

_childDocuments_.review: This was a triumph!I am making a note here, huge success!It's hard to overstate my satisfaction!To borrow the words of Shodan's little sister.SS1 has kept its spot in my top 10 for 30 years or so. But it really showed its age, being in particular the 3rd immersive sim and the last one without mouse look. For a long time, I had dreamt of a modern remake, and what a remake we got. As I am running throughout Citadel station's corridors, I am panting and sweating, and also making a lot of happy noises as I appreciate how good the original game was, and how lucky I am to play this masterfully executed remake.All the right choices were made (or nearly so). It's faithful to the original where it matters: the story, the game design, the chilling atmosphere. And it improves really well where it was needed: UX, graphics, sound design, and so on.Bravo to the dev team, it was absolutely worth the wait.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic remake that is both faithful to the original, while improving upon some areas with quality of life changes, additions and gameplay mechanics. Recycle stations are a new feature added in the remake, where you exchange scrap for credits. You collect scrap by vaporizing junk items throughout the levels. The credits are then used on vending machines and other item stations scattered throughout the levels. Also new to the remake are weapon upgrade mods placed throughout the game that can be used to make certain weapons better. There are a few new enemy types and some minor level section redesigns here and there, but nothing is significantly changed. They mostly add to the immersion and atmosphere.Graphics are faithful to the original, while also looking very modern as well. The music in the remake is not as good as the original and is more ambient in design. I would have preferred an option to switch between the remake and original music. Overall, it is a very fun remake and was definitely worth the wait.Highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly my experience was not enjoyable. At first it was fine but two major issues arose for me (Mind you I was playing on normal difficulty).1.  I never know where I'm going. Without spoilers, story wise this makes sense, and that is fine, I'll explore but the next problem then connects to this. 2. Enemies endlessly spawn. I would of thought once I clear an area...that area would remain clear but it does not. This becomes frustrating when I have to backtrack (as you will be doing that alot in this game) to figure out what to do next. I only have so much (and they get limited) health packs (you have a health bar in this game), ammo, energy to deal with these enemies. I can't make progress and then I become stuck. And I don't feel like going back 20 minutes to find a spot where I wasn't struggling. Thus, it's way to hard (on Normal difficulty!), becomes a pain as you have nothing left but melee to use and that's WEAK most of the time. Ammo being scarce.....ok fine.....but I can't find health often enough! It's not for me. I don't think it's a bad game, I quite enjoyed it at first, but it being so hard I gave up on it.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, a game that doesn't hold you hand. So much so that you will backtrack just to find a single digit for a code. This is a guarantee, and you will LOVE it. My only complaint is the final encounter and the hacking sections. But honestly with how much this game does right these issues don't amount to much of an issue for me.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: System Shock can be clunky, it can be weird, but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ does it succeed where it wants to. Right when you think you are getting equipped for Shodan's cyborg and mutant horrors, it throws something new at you and you realize you are always outmatched. This remake took a strange, strange game from the early 90's and made it playable. A wonderful game well worth a purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: A great reworking of a classic game. Some minor changes to the levels compared to the original but nothing that causes problems and for the most part improves things greatly.A minor ♥♥♥♥♥♥ would be graphical detailing on some signs and lettering.  Some of it looks garbled from a relatively short distance
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic game. It's a bit crazy when you play this to see how little games have advanced aside from graphics. This game still holds up wonderfully in the current generation. It's like playing the progenitor of Prey and you can see all the game-changing ideas the team had back in the day. Props to Nightdive for recreating the game faithfully. I was worried it'd be like the Gothic 2 remake but no, it holds up and I loved it. The only downsides are a few crashes (especially around the chess game and the cyber levels), and I felt like the music was a big downgrade from the original. Aside from those small points, I loved it.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty cool game. However, I was not ready for how "90s shooter" it is.If you get into it, which you should, brace for insaneo maze levels, wandering around wondering why you cant progress only to realise you missed an access card 3 floors back, endlessly re spawning enemies, etc, etc..If you are cool with all of that, you will be right at home here. If not, then I suggest checking out someone streaming it on twitch. A lot of love went into the game, and its worth experiencing however you can!
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: From what I remember of my System Shock playthrough from a few years back, this game seems pretty close to the original, at least in realspace (I read somewhere that the new cyberspace is quite different from the original, but I barely remember it). This is the update that this game really needed, the new, state of the art UI and mechanics make it much more accessible than the original. Took 42 hours with all four settings on Normal difficulty. Remake rating: 10/10Standalone game rating: 9/10 - The same few nitpicks that I had with the original design are still present here, a testament to accuracy- There were several crashes and stutters, and some UI bugs (none of these were game breaking).Highly recommend, especially if you enjoyed its successors System Shock 2 and the BioShocks. Well done, Nightdive!
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: This is how it's done.If you loved games like PREY (2017), Dishonored or the first two Bioshock games, you'll very much enjoy this as this game was the one that helped create those games all from 1994.Even without those, I'd still recommend it to anyone.Great atmosphere, intriguing plot and banger soundtrack and a lovely customisable difficulty system.The melee combat lacks impact but the shooting is just good enough for the type of game SS is.One of the nicest surprises is that this game is only 8GB and has wonderful optimization which is outstanding considering the majority of games are unnecessarily 100GB+ nowadays and run doo doo.Yet nightdive, a small studio with their first game, have managed to completely trump all the issues that plague modern gaming when it comes to optimisation.I've been having a blast.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game, and highly recommend it.PROS:The shooting mechanics were solid and enjoyableDiverse selection of weaponsGood storyPuzzles were challenging and different from other games. There was no basic lockpicking, it was similar to bioshock tube puzzles. I played on puzzle difficulty 3, which from what i can tell is the highest. Art style is unique in that from a distance is looks high quality, but up close it has a pixlated/retro view.Cyber space has been vastly improved over the original game.CONS:The dead bodies of enemies will stand back up when you leave and re-enter a level, providing a few minor jump scares.I could not find specific details for the cybernetic enhancements after i picked them up, for example, I never figured out how to use the target ID software.Some of my cyber space abilities like decoy, sprint, etc will not carry over cyber space terminals, not sure if this is intentional or a bug. The main attack never glitched though, so I could always beat them.I think some of the achievements aren't working properly.Final boss fight was very underwhelming, I know it's a remake so I understand if they wanted to incorporate some of that cyberspace feeling into it, but i really wish it was done differently. It seems like an improvement over the original boss fight though.If you can afford the price and are looking for something a different from all the modern games being released, I think you should try this game. If you are unsure, there is a free demo that covers the entire first level.3 June 2023
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: A mix of retro and modern twists... The OG System Shock shines best in its own habitat but this is just perfection, even in modern times of gaming, and graphics.And its not even that power hungry when it comes to perfomance.. My RTX 2060 Super / Ryzen 5600X config runs this on 1440p with high graphic settings... Compared to other modern titles and graphical standards, I was just really happy to see that the dev team managed to create this to be so immersive and compatible at the same time.Can't recommend enough!
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: You did it, Nightdive. You managed to recreate the feel of the original, meanwhile streamlining all the UI bits that made it hard to play and somehow managed to retain that special feeling. The station feels more alive, things make sense, the enemy models are nicely creepy while retaining the same profiles as the original sprites.You have my respect, you didn't disappoint. I'll be spending some time on Citadel Station, once again.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: *I WILL UPDATE THE REVIEW ONCE I'M DONE WITH THE GAME"So far so good, solid remake. It gave me major RE1 Remake vibes, which is a good thing. Instead of completely reinterpreting and modernising the game, Nightdive has kept the core design and philosophy with improved gameplay (mainly shooting). They left the exploration untouched, which made me quite happy. Being in complete isolation and fear as you try to figure out where to go and what to do in the labyrinthine sectors is a fun way to spend your evening.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic.  I've never played the original but this really caught me off guard and I thoroughly enjoyed it.  If you've ever played Prey or Deus Ex, this is a remake of the original game that gameplay came from.  Lots of clearing area by area, gathering clues and items to resolve issues to progress further.  The new Steam overlay notepad feature is super helpful for this game.  My thorough playthrough took around 20 hours and only had one crash.  Highly recommend (if you enjoy games that don't hold your hand)
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent Remake, and an excellent first game from a studio that so far has only done remasters. some bugs can be annoying but nothing truly gamebreaking so far. do not expect 2020' style gameplay design. this is a 90's game at heart, where there was wild experimentation and nobody quite knew what they were doing.but there's nothing quite like rocketing down a industrial corridor on plasma skates, throwing grenades and whacking cyborgs with a energy rapier.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: They don't make games like this any more, we need to get back.I just finished it and loved the need to pay attention, to figure things out, to browse all logs in search for clues. Have to recognize it was hard though, modern games with infinite hand holding and markers made me lazy. Feel smarter now.Great remake, the style visual design is so good, so retro yet technically sophisticated, interesting and different. Loved every bit.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Not for everyone but if it is for you it's pretty great. A few things to note, though. The game's gunplay isn't great. It has the scrap economy from Prey but done worse and you'll spend a lot of time picking up every toothbrush on the floor (I wasn't a fan). And You'll be doing a ton of backtracking. So why is it so good?Hands down, the exploration is top notch. The game has no interest in holding your hand so it's on you to figure out where to go and what to do (there is a difficulty option that changes this, but I didn't try it so I can't comment). You'll be scouring the map for audiologs just to find hints as to what you're supposed to do. And there's tons of great secrets and gear to find. It's more of a metroidvania than an Immersive sim, tbh. The atmosphere is great, the villain is excellent, and if you enjoy resource management this is the game for you.A few helpful tips that I think might make the game a little easier to get into:Ration your resources. You might have a lot of something right now but that doesn't mean you'll have a lot of it later. Every bullet counts. Your inventory is also tiny, so don't be afraid to leave something somewhere and put a marker on the map to come back to it.As much as I dislike the junk economy, it is kinda important. So vaporize those hats and jars and run to the nearest recycler. I encourage you to take notes on things. If you see a number on a screen, WRITE. IT. DOWN. With a little note explaining where you saw it. You will thank me later.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly well polished and optimised game. What a lovely surprise from small dev. Everything works so smooth. It was definitely worth the wait and it will be a proof that remakes of classic games can be done with passion while not compromising source material. 9/10Couple non-essential problems which could be patched later on:1. When changing V-Sync ON/OFF you need to restart the game2. Corpses convuls a little when entering the room with them insideSo nothing game breaking, but would be great if they get them fixed to achieve perfection.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I'd been waiting years to get into playing this, and I can't say it's worked out well after all the wait. The original is one of my favourite games of all time, and the first PC game I ever sunk a real lot of time into. The remake is .. almost a demake? It actually has fewer quality of life features than the original game in a few ways, and some of them are really quite impactful on gameplay - particularly the removal of nameable map markers. Many things they've just flat out removed, like the pose selector and being able to freely aim weapons, remove a lot of the fundamental character and charm of the original game. What has been removed was interesting, what replaces it is just boring tripe that makes it feel like a generic 2000s shooter.It's like someone remaking Doom, removing all the 2d art, all the original sound effects, all the original lighting scheme of the levels, and replacing them with some unity assetflip game quality placeholders, and going - "here's your remake". No it isn't, buddy. You messed it up. This is some cheap feeling crap.Ed - just from curiosity, I booted up the old SS1 Enhanced for a bit. Two things immediately stand out:1:  literally, from the very first room you're in, the changes in Remake are inferior, pointless, and remove a half dozen interesting pieces of content from the game. I knew remake was worse, but I didn't remember it being bad to quite that extent!2: Nightdive have left everyone who wants to play SS1EE with a choice of two delicious game breaking / experience ruining bugs (broken enemy movement OR inability to play above 30fps) since 2021. I simply can't believe these people get work - HOW can they be so bad at this? Architecting out the movement system vs viewport update frequency is ... really somewhere around the top 3 things you would need to do to rebuild the game? And in all seriousness, they've simply left it busted and told people "turns out that's a real pickle" years after finishing the work. More or less instantly explains a great deal about how the remake has turned out, I think.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Let me just put it this way, I had a cracked version of this game and ended up playing through it three different times. So I decided they deserved my money and I plan on 100% the game. If that doesn't convince you this game is amazing and they deserve your money then I don't know what will. Side note I did not play the original system shock so I'm not just some fan boy still living in 1994. (Though there is nothing wrong with that mind you)
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I never really got into SS-1 (I have played it), but I loved SS-2 when it came out.I love the feel of the game, and got to love SHODAN, thought she's a real pain in the...Then here I am, waddling around the space station minding my own business, then I get a jump scare.  I do wish we can toggle the run button, we can do it for crouch but not for run.  Other than that, for me it's a great game.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely faithful remake that modernizes the original without losing sight of what made it special. _childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing System Shock, I actually felt like a hero. I don't know why, but in the 16 years of gaming this is the first time I actually feel genuinely satisfied for defeating the villain. Bare in mind, this is my first time with System Shock.SHODAN is such a good villain, genuinely despicable and scary, so destroying her plans and seeing her getting mad at you till the very end was one hell of a joy. Combat is decent, the weapons feel very nice and have a lot of cool varieties, with all of them being useful. The levels are like a maze, but you get used to it and learn them, and the story, while told only via audio logs, mails and environmental storytelling, is exciting to follow. And the game looks gorgeous, it has this modern retro style, and it runs very well on my PC.Amazing game. Everyone who is into horror or first person shooters is obliged to play this game, seriously.87/100
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: What a wonderfully crafted experience. Hard as nails, terrifying atmosphere, and a well-observed reverence to the source material. You play as the Hacker, who has just woken up on a space station with a rogue GAI named SHODAN in control. It is up to you to find a way back home to Earth and deal with SHODAN's forces. The game plays a lot like Bioshock meets Rainbow Six: Siege; tons of audio logs to reveal the story of what has happened to the station, along with the slow, methodical corner clearing and quick leaning from R6. There is something of an augmentation system in the game, but expect nothing as deep as a modern game. You can acquire different shields for different damage sources, an upgradable radar, some boost boots, and a headlamp. Most of the weapons you get will have multiple ammo types and upgrades available, but the number of guns you can carry will be limited by an old school inventory system that you will have to manage yourself. There is a customizable difficulty system that allows you to tailor the game to your preferences. That being said the higher up you go, the less the game holds your hand (.) You can adjust the difficulty of the Combat, Mission, Cyber, and Puzzles. I finished the game on 3/2/2/3 a couple days ago and I'm already considering trying a 3/3/3/3. The last time I wanted to do that was when I played DX:HR the first time almost 10 years ago. The only gripe I have with the game has to do with the final section of the game, which I will detail in spoilers for obvious reasons.  Other than those small things mentioned in the spoiler section, this game is an absolute win compared to today's live-service infested, money farming, awfully unfinished AAA games. I went from playing Diablo 4 to this and felt so much more joy in my time playing this game than I did grinding to 100+ content in D4.10/10 Buy now, why are you still reading this? GOTY
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: SYSTEM SHOCK. goThere are only a few Video Games that compel me to take written notes while playing...I woke up on a space station - with no ideas of how far I have to go just to survive.I had to determine (for myself) what actions to take.There, on Citadel Station, I was the patient detective and the intense weapon chooser; sometimes charging, sometimes hiding near a recycle station.If I like the idea of running within a science-fiction maze, and also there is the 4D Cyber terminals: (there is an entirely additional game inside SYSTEM SHOCK during which one or multiple junctions have to be eliminated), and some weapons and ammunition management, then I LIKE this !Also, it is scary, surprising, frustrating, relieving and thought-provoking.This game is really really good!I will play through it again when it is released in VR (Virtual Reality).          (VR should be an obvious way to export this game.  what is going on?)

_childDocuments_.review: This is a remake, and a love letter to the original 1994 System Shock.Aggravating at times, the game relies heavily on player intuition to figure out your own objectives, routes, and generally just "What's going on" and "How stuff works"; this could have worked well by including a few additional audio logs, but being true to the original makes the game hard to love at times.The art, audio and story of the game are exceptionally well put together, but the game-play has a few missteps that I'm sure will mean a number of players never complete the game.Overall, it's a solid game that's held back by staying too close to the original; but I hope we see Nightdive doing a remaster of the second game.

_childDocuments_.review: Man... Where do I start. I love this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game! I never played the original due to it's primitive controls and happy I didn't. Playing this game for the first time with a new fresh coat of paint was truly magickal. This was definitely a 1:1 remake of a retro cyberpunk dungeon crawler. System Shock does not hold your ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hand and It's all up to you, the player to figure it out. On what to do and to weave the story all together. This game may be hard but it's also fun and rewarding and requires you sometimes to think outside the box and to really pay attention all of your surroundings and the logs... and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ refreshing. _childDocuments_.review: Honestly this game is a real master piece. _childDocuments_.review: Oh boy this is gunna be a long one so buckle up insect.Nightdive Studios is known for porting classic games to PC and making older PC work on modern systems, and overall they do a petty good job. The games they've worked on are includes, Wizardry 6, 7, and 8 the Tex Murphy games, Turok 1 and 2, Doom 64, Quake 1 as well as the original System shock 1 and 2 as well as an enhanced edition to System shock 1 witch has some quality of life improvements. A studio that actually takes care in porting games to PC is rare nowadays and they have a good track record. This however is the first actual game they've made, even though its a remake it was built from the ground up from a passionate team some even getting some of the veterans from the original game to work on the remake.  If Doom 1993 set the groundwork for gaming, system shock was the first to build a house on it, Well a full apartment block really. Many people, including me believe this is the first truly modern game. With many options on how to deal with the challenges the game throws at you. I think the main reason it diddn't get anywhere close to the amount of commercial success that Doom got is probably the controls, it gained a reputation of playing like a motherboard bios and needlessly complex and confusing UI. Witch is a shame but understandable.First things first lets talk about the obvious, the updated graphics and controls. The controls are now pretty standard for a FPS not much to say here but the art style balances a lot of different styles perfectly. Its colourful and cartoony yet metallic  and realistic, hell there even a sprinkle of pixel art thrown in as a nod to the original, it's 90's yet cyberpunk it's tries to do so much visually yet it doesn't feel confused or overwhelming. The cyberspace parts were the worst part of the original, boring, tedious and frustrating, while the remake improves this its not by much. It goes from garbage to mediocre at best i get they're trying to stay true to the original but i feel they could have done something else but at least it looks better. The rest of the game is pretty much 1:1 with the original i'm talking every light switch the location of key items, everything down to even the most minor of minor things witch you have to give Nightdive credit for as they seem to care. But you know what that means be prepared to get lost and have no clue on what your suppose to be doing, and make sure you write stuff down. This is a must you will not survive without taking notes. On top of that the levels are mazes stacked on top of mazes. Luckily i didn't find myself getting lost too often as each place is distinct with landmarks that stand out. Also have fun searching for audio logs and text entries, yep these aren't just lore stuff you can skip no no no these are mandatory and you better be paying close attention to each of them as these will tell you your next step, This game fu*king hates you, and that brings us to the star of the show. SHODAN. She is one of the best antagonists in videos games. Her presence alone can be unnerving. You really get the feeling of being trapped on a space station that she controls and she wants you dead. Its a cat and mouse game and your the mouse and once you start making progress and breaking all her stuff she comes up with new plans. Just as you think your safe she will lock you in a room with tough enemies, turn off the lights and fill the room with toxic gas. She will bend you over and spank you until you cry. Okay i made that last one up but you get the point. Also if you aren't paying attention and just touching every switch you will accidentally blow up earth, just another way for SHODAN to laugh at you for trying to fu*k with her. Y'know playing through the game i don't really have any major complaints. The cyberspace parts can get pretty samey but i wouldn't say they were bad. That is until the last 5 minutes of the game witch is another cyberspace level but this time instead of flying around in an enclosed environment shooting stuff with your pink Shuriken gun. instead you are given a single shot rifle and you walk around, push a button, fight a few wave of enemies and shoot SHODAN, repeat 3 times. Also i have a feeling they didn't program the AI to work with you just walking around. If you stand halfway behind a corner and shoot the edge of the enemies this breaks the AI and they just don't move and wait for you to kill them. Sigh* and it was going so well. This is like dancer putting on the best performance of their life just to trip and fall off the stage as the judges are given the scores. It's a fantastic remake that brings a classic game to a new generation while still keeping retro styled. With that being said its definitely not for everyone if you don't like being lost and not knowing what to do for half the game you should probably give this one a skip. Lastly the fact that they could pretty much copy identically the original and it still be good today show show ahead of the time the original was and i hope Nightdive will be brave enough to do another remake similar to this one or maybe even the new title but we will just have to see.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah, as a huge fan of the original, this remake is great.  It definitely goes for a different tonal vibe than the original, and part of me still misses the crazier soundtrack of the original, but it's obvious this was made with a lot of love.  I'd happily still play through both versions depending on what experience I am looking for, but I do think this version is drastically more approachable to modern audiences.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who never played System Shock 1, and only a couple hours of System Shock 2 before losing interest due to the clunkiness, this modernizes the aesthetic behind those that I enjoy so much. This has made me excited for the System Shock 2: Enhanced Edition release, despite any clunkiness that might remain in it.Love Bioshock, love this even more.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I was an original Kickstarter supporter for the original funding campaign. So I didn't receive this game for free I did get it at a significant discount.The original System Shock was one of my favorite video games growing up. This remake is an amazing update on a foundational video game. I have played through the original game more times than I can count. They did an amazing job on updating the station to take advantage of the new technology. The new station felt extremely familiar to the point where "I remember a secret door being there..." and boom still there. And yet there were a lot of times that I got thrown for a loop when they had updated the formula to keep you on your toes. For instance the Cortex Reapers in the original game weren't very intimidating. A single concussion bomb and they were done. In the remake they represent a serious threat on the station and in cyberspace. Because of how the cyborg works it doesn't matter if you have turned off the cyborg conversion system. If you die fighting a reaver you lose. Which brings up my only real gripe, an unskippable cutscene plays when you die. When doing some of the more difficult fights it can be really annoying.I really love what they did with cyberspace. It plays pretty much like the original but it is a lot more fast paced and tactical. Also the visuals are stellar. It feels exactly like how William Gibson describes cyberspace in Neuromancer.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: This is everything I wanted Prey to be, but it wasn't. I never got much into System Shock 2, but this works fabulously for me. It's dense, it's intricate, it's oldschool in all the right ways while feeling sleek and modern in terms of UX. The audio and visual design are stellar, far batter than I expected from an AA studio and Teri Brosius is back voicing Shodan, what more could you ask for?
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Perfect remake of the old classic. Great atmosphere of the Citadel station, which unfortunatelly lost a bit of horror, but is still tense. Terri Brosius returned with nhanced SHODAN voice and did an excelent job. Her taunts and threats are one of the best features of this game and without her, the atmosphere would be greatly diminished.Graphic design is unique combination of modern and oldschool pixel graphics, which creates great visual experience. Gameplay is greatly improved from the original, which is almost unplayable for moder audinces. Remake plays like a modern fps shooter with survival mechanics, which can be harder or easier depending on your hoarding minset. Every item can be collected and recycled for credits and exchanged for ammo. This can make the game significantly easier, but with it comes inventory management, which will make your stay on the station a true horror, expecially in the later stages.Soundtrack is also imported from the original with slight improvements. As a negative, people without processor with AVX won´t be able to play because of constant crashes. On some levels there is visible stuttering which can make the game unplayable, especially on Security level where I had a lot of problems staying alive because of this. In the conclusion System Shock Remake is a great experience for both new players and connoisseurs of the original.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Truly amazing!There isn't much i can really complain about. Much better and more enjoyable than the original. My only real gripes would be the difficulty curve, "sponginess" of some enemies and how easy it is to get lost, but it doesn't take away from how great this game is.My shooter of the year and had BG3 not come out this year this would be my GOTY no contest.

I highly recommend it for me it's game of the year. Great job nightdive.

_childDocuments_.review: yes yes a thousand times yes! this is the remake that the mother of a all fps games deserves .graphics update looks  amazing game play almost 1 for 1 like the original 10 out of 10 . but don't be fooled this game will not hold your hand it is tough and will require a lot of thinking from you . play well hacker .

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game. It was a great remake, and one of the better things was the skill selection screen, where you can customize each part of the game to your liking. I played on skill 1213 since I love puzzles and missions (but not combat and shooting, and not time limits either).Positives:* A GREAT remake, that makes it also easier to follow the story.* Skill selection made it pretty good.* Good story* Loved all the hacking and finding keycards, mission items, and the "open world" travelling.Negatives:* Even on skill 1 combat is extremely hard. Would wish some "skill 0" in combat, both cyberspace and normal combat. Maybe with health and energy regen? And having skill 0 should also, maybe make the stacks for health, patches and ammo 4x bigger, meaning more room for items, and maybe make every weapon 2 slots smaller in inventory size.* For puzzles, a skill 4 would be nice. The circuit boxes were wayy to easy even on the most difficult setting.* I found it kinda unfair that some cameras were in hidden areas. Personally I think 0% security should be part of story, and I think the reactor code should not stop scrambling unless you have 0% security. (This could be bound to the "puzzle" skill, so selecting skill 3 or 4 in puzzle difficulty will require 0% security to gain a a reactor digit)

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliant remake of a brilliant game.9/10What would make it 10/10:1. Add more space to lift and inventory. The little amount of space doesn't make the game more difficult, it just brings frustration and discomfort. Becasue of no space I had to throw weapon on the floor. I didn't use 2 weapons. Not a single shot. Did it make the game more challenging? No. It just, for no apparent reason, reduced some fun from the game.2. A lot of people mention this, the final boss. I actually really like it, it's a huge improvement compare to the original game. I also understand why we can't save there. But why the intro is unskippable?  By the time I beat this part, I knew the intro by heart and switched off sound to not hear it again. What value does it bring? Please make it either skippable or restart from the beginning in case of death, but after the intro.

_childDocuments_.review: Concept is great, implementation not in my opinion. Too much walking, excessive walking. No shortcuts, easy to miss things. I think this ramake could have solved many things from the original version (and probably it did it, never played the original one). _childDocuments_.review: I played the Enhanced Edition of System Shock not that long ago and this is a very faithful and enjoyable remake.  The HUD, which is a lot less confusing in this game, still captures some of the look of the original, while the inventory system is more similar to System Shock 2.  Space is limited, but there are a couple of upgrades you can get and also a storage dumb waiter for extra items.  The weapons all feel great and I especially love the new shotgun that replaces the riot gun from the original that I never used.  While I think the Mag-Pulse Rifle was nerfed a bit compared to the original game, it was still useful for many of the levels.  The Laser Rapier still cuts down enemies quickly, especially while using the Berserk patch, though my one complaint about it is that there are not enough audio cues and damage visuals so it sometimes felt like I wasn't hitting an enemy.  The colorful pixelated look is a matter of personal taste but I love it because it captures that 80s cyberpunk look very well.  The Executive level is especially good looking.  However, I wish they would have gotten weird with the Bridge level like the original game.  The gameplay is very satisfying and level design is so close to the original that you can still use the old maps as a guide.  I especially like the new hacking puzzles and the cyberspace levels.  Cyberspace was my least favorite part of the original because it was so confusing to navigate, but in this game it felt like I was playing a mini version of Descent.  I did experience a few issues while playing like crashing during the Maintenance level Cyberspace game, but these will be addressed in the upcoming patch.  Compared to a lot of other games I've played recently, System Shock Remake runs quite well. The music is the weakest part of this game.  The more ambient soundtrack is okay but not very memorable.  They could have added some punchier tunes to it.  Fortunately, the sound effects and voice acting are great and it's a joy to get some extra dialogue from SHODAN.  If you were intimidated by System Shock, you should definitely check out this game because it captures the spirit of the original, including the variable difficulty settings that give both games excellent replay value.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I'm consistently blown away by how games like this seem to always let you have just enough resources to get by while continuously getting more and more ridiculous in the difficulty.I did not play the original, like many, I played system shock 2 only, but I did enjoy the experience enough to want to play the remake. I was absolutely not disappointed. Tons of things to interact with, garbage loot that is actually worth collecting, and audio logs that are actually meaningful and not just essays of nonsense with the only purpose describing lore that has nothing to do with what's going on. I imagine the quality of life improvements were substantial, but it does make me want to give the original a try.The map is humongous and quite overwhelming at times, but the exploration is very satisfying. The fact that similar upgrades are spread on multiple floors and multiple locations because of how open ended it is makes it even more satisfying.The last few stretches are very overwhelming, requiring lots of use of saves and quick saves to get through, but I really liked this game. Huge recommend for anyone who likes the survival and immersive sim genres.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: The game's alright. Would I recommend it as a new game? Yeah, probably.Would I recommend it as a remake - Probably not.I played and LOVED System Shock. It's easily in my Top 3 of games. So probably my review is biased by nostalgia and comparisons between the versions. Then, however, it is a remake, so that may be fair game. I even still play the Enhanced Version of System Shock from time to time, and enjoy it very much. Yeah, so the graphics is blocky and dated - who cares? Its fun! And while I could always go for another round of the Original, I fear I will have to force myself to keep playing and finishing this. Keep in mind - I'm only almost through the second level. Lets start with something positive:They certainly could reproduce the atmosphere of the Original. You feel right at home on Citadel.Now some things that annoy me:- Recycling: If you're a loot hoarder like me, you'll hate it. You can recycle junk stuff at a machine for credits. Or you can 'vaporise' it for junk, roughly worth half the credit value of the machine. So you're either running around with an inventory full of junk, going to the recycler and back, or you always have the feeling of wasting money. It's especially bad if you're on a new level and havent run across the recycler yet .That's a personal thing, granted, but it takes away from the fun for me. What's NOT personal is that you can recycle and vaporise broken weapons - but not working ones. I don't need a third Mini-Pistol, thank you. But I can't t recycle it unless its broken? Bollocks. - The station design. It's somewhat more realistic, maybe. Useful? No. In the original, you could spot at a glance if there was a button or a useable object, since the background was rather uniform. In this, there are lights and screens all over the place. Can I press this lighted button? No. This one here? Yes. This one over there? No.Once again, a matter of personal choice, but I think a bit more clarity would have been good.- The puzzles: I like puzzles. But if you randomize your puzzles, and if the first puzzle I run across on my second game I get stuck on for 15 minutes and still can't solve it - it kinda stops me from playing further. In the original, I believe the puzzles were set. The first one was easy, a couple of clicks - even on the hardest puzzle setting. (Later ones were tougher, but you get logic probes later on that will let you bypass them, if you felt it necessary.) Also, I said it during development, but still: I hate that the puzzles, keypads etc. have to be used in your usual viewscreen. Press those buttons with your crosshairs, don't even think about having an enlarged HUD window version for easier access!And last, and most certainly the biggest issue: - Cyberspace.Yes, I'm one of the thousands of people complaining about cyberspace. Sorry. As others said, it's empty. Big empty halls, spawning enemies in an arena-shooter way. Thats about it. And if you fail the CS level, you will have to redo it from the beginning.Now, in the original, there was a lot of stuff in there. Keys, notes, software upgrades, data files...  and if you were beaten halfway through, you could reconnect, and the enemies you had already finished were still finished. Which means, even in tough CS levels, you could grind your way through if you healed up in between. Now? Succeed - or retry.And, seriously, who thought that Shock needed an arena shooter part? "We're remaking an atmospheric survival adventure game - so of course, we need a part where you tape down the fire button and strafe around with lots of enemies"Then there are a couple of little annoyances for me: No quick-heal button. No button to play the last unplayed audio log.  No auto-junk, junk all or whatever. The ever repeating annoying animations (using a medbed, using a keycard, grabbing keycards, audio logs, etc) which you WILL at some point wish to be able to just skip. If you want to quickly grab three things, but the first one is an audio log, and you will have to wait for the animation to finish before you can pick up the keycard, and wait for that animation to finish before you can pick up the third thing - you'll know what I mean.Also, the occasional lack of info: Like many, it took me some time to notice that on the puzzles the plugs had different power. And you don't know what setting your weapon is on or what ammo you loaded - if you don't already know it. For example: The pistol has normal and Teflon rounds. Loading one you see the ammo count. Loading the other, you see a circle around the ammo count. Thats it. Would it have been so hard to put a little "Teflon" below it, or a "T"? You know, like the Original did?All in all: This certainly isn't bad, but I recommend you play System Shock Enhanced Version, if the graphics dont bother you. I find it much more fun and actually even somewhat easier to get around in.Edit: Almost through now. Not feeling better, rather worse.There are so many QOL things that just weren't added, it baffles me.- You can't split stacks. Recycler gives 1 credit for each 10 scrap. You have 57. Well, get ready to waste 7, or don't recycle.  You want to stash half your ammo pile? Tough luck.- No quick-heal button, I think I already mentioned that, but it still bugs me.- You can't add notes to the map. Like in, for example, you know... SYSTEM SHOCK!?!There's a door you can only open after level security has been dropped? Just search for it again! You need one digit from the CPU cores on each level for a code. Better write it down on a piece of paper, because you certainly won't in your high-tech Computer hacker gear! Text editors are dead, man, dead!!- The inventory. Dear Lord, it's small. In the Original, you could keep 7 weapons, with all the ammo you got, 7 types of grenades, 7 healing and boosting salves, and 7  misc items (batteries, severed heads, c4, etc.) In this? Well, everything takes space. I have like 5 weapons, ammo for them and other weapons, a couple of healing items, some batteries, emp grenades, some quest items and credits, and my inventory is full. Get a new weapon? One you (yet) only have 3 shots for? Well, either skip it or drop one of your "old" weapons. Oh, and your ammo stack for guns x and y has reached max capacity, so either use it up or skip the rounds you just found.- The recycler. Ohh, the bane of my existence. The bigger, more valuable broken weapons are 2x4. The recycler is 3x3. Yes, you're right - you can't recycle them directly. It's nice that it says recycling will give you 5 credits, but in fact you are just not able to recycle it. Ever.- I feel better about the recycler and scrapping mechanics now, though - mainly because I am now able to ignore them. You get credits, but there's not a lot you can spend those on, so recycling is just a basic thing and not really worth it. Mostly you'll need it for weapon upgrades you can find 1-2 on every level, I think. Then you can buy some healing and aid patches. And ammo, which is really, really sparse (each vendor has two ammo items, and there are like 2-3 of them  per level). You don't really need to buy ammo, though, IMO - and if you do, the little there is to buy likely won't make much difference.Besides that, all you can spend your credits on is... snacks. Great.Edit 2: Done, finally. And let me just say... ugggggghh. The last level, beating SHODAN.I feel like now I owe an apology to Shock 2 for what I thopught about its last level. Its just...bad.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Great story and game play for the most part, but this game desperately needs some quality of life updates to reduce the high amount of tedious backtracking you'll need to do.Your character's inventory space is not big enough to hold all the weapons and quest items you'll pick up along the way and you'll pick up some quest items hours before needing them. The secondary inventory is the cargo lift which is on some levels but only holds a pathetically small amount of items. This means you'll need to resort to throwing items and weapons onto the floor or in a random crate somewhere you'll remember to come back to later? The problem is you have no idea of what items and weapons you'll need on specific levels, and not every level has a cargo lift (that I've been able to find). Combined with levels are intentionally maze-like, it's frustrating as now I need to backtrack 10-15 minutes to a previous lower floor to pick up some quest items I now need, and because the character's inventory is small, I'll have to drop a weapon or other items to make space for these quest items, meaning I'll need to do yet ANOTHER backtrack run after this to pick these up again. This inadequate inventory space also means you are not encouraged to regularly try all the weapons in your arsenal as you'll always have a good 3+ weapons that you can't fit in your inventory at any given time.I also think the cyberspace levels could be re-imagined, as these are pretty tedious too.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: While I mostly enjoyed the game, I cannot in good conscience recommend it due to it's poor performance during certain levels of the game. I was able to upgrade my computer to overcome this (not exclusively for this game  obviously), but most people are not so fortunate. However, provided your specs are , rather than the listed minimum, then I do think this game is indeed worth playing.That being said, a review of the actual game. I also want to make clear this is a review of the game as it is now, not a comparison of remake to original. Overall the game is highly enjoyable despite all its flaws. Its fun to run around and explore the station, resolve the various complications, shoot stuff and loot everything not nailed down. I have special praise for the aesthetics of the game, not only supplying great design that's reminiscent of the early 90s sci-fi, but also the idea to make all textures intentionally pixellated rather than going for pointlessly high resolutions. The music is great, voice acting is good, sound design is solid. Some might find the level design to be a bit obtuse but I think the maze-like structure works out in its favour, giving the player a feeling of being trapped while exploring.I would say my biggest issues with the game was easily the puzzles and cyberspace segments. (By "puzzles" I refer to the hacking mini-games mostly, rather than the actual mission objectives, as that's what the game means when it says puzzles). The cyberspace segments are a cute idea, but very quickly became tiresome and are frankly completely disconnected to the actual game. The hacking or wiring puzzles are similar, feeling like a time-wasting barrier between you and getting on with the fun parts of System Shock. Puzzles at least provide a (limited) item you can find that bypasses them, so you can save those up for the puzzles that you get sick of. Some more minor complaints involve how combat feels a bit shallow sometimes, there's a lack of menu QoL and hotkeys, and the game displays a lot of info to you via a tiny text box at the top of the screen which is fine for names of things but not events that happen briefly.

_childDocuments_.review: 9.4/10Wow.. what a game.. I absolutely love this game. The only downfall is the somewhat boring cyberspace and some sections that didn't seem well test played. beyond that, I think it's absolutely amazing. I love the aesthetics of this game and despite loving bioshock's aesthetics, I think these are more my style. 80s inspired cyberpunk for the win. Shodan is also a great antagonist.
