_childDocuments_.review: Deep-Dive did a very good job remaking the game with modern hardware. It is basically the same game as the original. To some that is a good thing, to others that is a bad thing.Pros:-Melee combat is the most fun form of combat-Lore of the game is interesting-puzzles are somewhat interesting.Cons:-NO CLOUD SAVES, It is 2023, how do you not have cloud saves???-Extremely claustrophobic, confusing, boring, and frustrating map designs.-No guidance or sense of direction to progress the story. Unless you've played the original or have all day to read/listen to every single audio log/book you will have no clue where to go or what to do next. In my opinion this is the biggest downside to this game. At least provide an option where you can toggle on/off quest markers or an assistant of some sort.-Constant back-tracking. This ties into the lack of a quest guide/objective markers. Also needing to re-arrange my inventory every 30 seconds and running halfway back across the map to the lift storage or recycler every 10 minutes is mind-numbingly annoying.-This remake is nearly a copy and paste of the original which has not aged well and does not hold up to modern titles.For these reasons I cannot recommend the game to a "massive audience."This game is a prime example of "appeals to a niche audience."I pre-ordered this game over 3 years ago. I was super excited for it and was hyping it up to all my gamer buddies. unfortunately I got bored with it after 6 hours on day 2 of release and was extremely disappointed. I wanted to like the game, but the cons just outweigh the pros too heavily for me to continue wanting to drag myself through the game.I pre-ordered this when deep-dive was offering system shock 2 remake for free if you pre-ordered this so hopefully that game is worth the $40 I spent on this.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: This has been one of the most thrilling and immersive narrative gameplay experiences I've ever had. Impeccable world-building pulls the player into it's unique, compelling aesthetic from the start. Tension is balanced with dark and occasionally twisted humor.  Shodan has a playful streak.  It is terrifying.I didn't play the original release so I don't have a yardstick, but the gunplay is fun.  The exploration is really old-school, and suited me down to the ground.  I *loved* Half-Life - if you actually *enjoy* getting lost and having to learn where you're going and why you're going there - quids in.  I can see where the subsequent Prey gets a lot of its DNA, but this is an entirely different story with an entirely different vibe.Shodan, the antagonist AI draws the obvious comparisons to GLaDOS, but apart from being artificial and homicidal, that's where the similarities end. Shodan's cold contempt, delivered in Max Headroomesque glitches and stutters by a superb voice actor is the best part of an already fantastic game.I loved it.  Even while I was swearing at it.  Perhaps, especially then.I'm really looking forward to more from this developer.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start out by saying that I completed this game on normal difficulty and I appreciate that the devs of this game clearly had a lot of passion for the source material. But this game is just not fun and is very dated. Bad level design, annoying combat, confusing objectives, I could go on. Before anyone says "its a remake of a really old game its suppose to be like the original" if you compare this game to a good remake like resident evil 4 there were very clear improvements to make it more playable for a modern audience compared to the original unlike this one which tried to be very faithful almost to its detriment. The only people who I could see actually enjoying this game are boomers who played the original and just want some nostalgia. Everyone else will just have a unfun time with this very terribly aged game. A good metaphor for this remake is a Turd cover with gold and diamonds. You can put all of the prettiest stuff on it but at the end of the day its still a turd.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, I fully enjoyed it, the theme, the sound design and gameplay.I recommend playing the game on the highest difficulty otherwise normal feels too easy, bar the 10 hour limit difficulty if you like me, like to explore and take your time.Wish I played the original back then, looks like they were truthful to the old game and it's visible with the inventory management and maze like levels, but there's a charm in that.I recommend this gem.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: It's everything a game needs in a remake. There is no filler, no cutting corners, and no nonsense. This is the original game improved while retaining all of its charm, even including the actual voice of Shodan, Terri. Among all of the fantastic dialogue and world immersion, I noticed a bunch of goofy, messed-up stuff that raised the game even further, not because the bugs were awful. They are what made classic games amazing, a randomly placed NPC swinging from the ceiling to greet me on a return trip through an area I had entered multiple times and had never seen him before as if the game was mocking me but in a classic way like "welcome home."It goes by old school means. You pick p a key item and drop it somewhere? Good luck finding it unless you're recording your gameplay for streams or content. There needs to be a quest item map locator or something. I've spent so many hours backtracking very important key items. Thank god you can return to the groves once jettisoned if you have dropped key items there.I intend to finish this game once I have some free time and am not suffocated by all the games I have to go through, but my god has this been entertaining and nostalgic, maybe a little bit exhausting but that's due to the long session and games getting to me, the games great!
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I consider System Shock 2 as one of the best games ever made - finished it many times with different builds. Even though I haven't played the first one, I was so happy when the remake of the original System Shock was announced. I bought it on the first day, actually hitting the refresh button on steam until it would finally unlock. Unfortunately I must say that this game is not even remotely as perfect as System Shock 2 was. I was surprised how inferior the game- and especially level design is. Don't get me wrong, I respect Nightdive Studios for making a faithful remake, and I am sure for some people this is a dream come true - unfortunately not for me. My personal review would be a "mixed".I am constantly lost, progression is painfully slow, and I don't like the hacking-cyberspace levels. After 20 hours or so, I found myself spending more time in forums or youtube to shorten the hours of clueless walking around. I even struggled though the chess game - although I don't know how to play chess. Today I decided that playing this game feels more like work to me - so I quit. I tried so hard to like this game, but it just does not work for me. There is a lot of good stuff in this game though. I like the graphics, I like the exploration (before it turns into a desperate pixelhunt) and of course Shodan is great. The music is a bit on the weaker side - compared to System Shock 2. Anyways... I usually don't write many reviews (as you can probably tell). I am just disappointed I guess. Many people seem to enjoy this game - and that is good. However, if you have only played SS2 back in the days and think about buying this one - I'd wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I've always felt nostalgic about this game. I didn't play it properly when it came out ages ago but I knew it was something very special. Now, thanks to this remake, I'm finally enjoying this masterpiece. Yes, a absolute masterpiece and the first true immersive sim.VISUALS: Amazing style mixes some retro vibes with modern technology. I love it. I'd give it a 10/10 for merging the old with the new. Easy on the hardware too - RazerBlade RTX 3070Ti on a 4k TV (4k maxed out and 60fps DLSS QUALITY).SOUND: Very good. Does a great job, It didn't stand out to me, but maybe I didn't pay enough attention.GAMEPLAY: Very good to great, an easy 8.5-9I definitely recommend it. It's a great way to familiarise yourself with a timeless classic.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: An outstanding reimagining of one of the most influential games ever made.It is an old-fashioned, difficult, tough and unforgiving experience.The setting is incredibly atmospheric and SHODAN reconfirms herself as one of the most iconic antagonists ever. The original was an immersive-sim, survival horror, maze-like first-person game like no other, and this nearly 1.1 remake is to be commended for giving new life to such a video game classic.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: So personal tidbit of information... My uncle was a release engineer for looking glass studio and basically compiled/programmed the installers for system shock 2. Its good to see this was a remake of the original but my concern is, its not really as scary as the original was. Its a good game, but doesn't have the same atmosphere.No tutorial, just throws you into it, tons of things to collect, keypads to find, puzzles to complete, and some messed up cyborg/backstory, reminds me of quake 2/4 in its cyborg storyline. The cyborgs remind me of the borg from startrek, just consider it a copycat in their design. The mutants keep some of their humanity, or at least it shows when they try to access vending machines, etc. Its a nice little touch, allows for some instant stealth melee kills, but otherwise nothing noteworthy.I feel like the gunplay is pretty lackluster, they dont feel good when firing. If I am at the head I am not entirely sure I do more damage than the body. If it does its not by much. The game feels massive, took me 2.3 hr to complete the first level, doing everything I could. I would rate it a 7 out of 10, I would wait for a sale, worth about $25 to $30 from my experience with the first level.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: really good UNTIL the third halfI really enjoyed this game at first, despite a few difficulty spikes here and there, but then you get to the point where you feel like you stop getting more powerful but the enemies don't. All the late game guns are either too slow, uses too much ammo, or just don't compare to the guns you get within a few hours of starting.The final boss consists of you finding a safe corner and popping out to kill some enemies, then fighting another spider cyborg, the getting a weak gun and dying over and over to the digital enemies as a normal dude.Very underwhelming
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: If you've played the original, you've played this game.  That can be a negative or a positive.  To me, it's a positive as, besides the tech, the original design holds up quite well all these years later.  I love exploring a dense, intricate, interconnected level based station and discovering all its secrets.My 2 gripes are that I wish combat was better and the retro style wasn't so... pixel heavy.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: High quality remake of a classic game, with modernized UI/UX for, well, actual playability in the modern age without changing core systems and gameplay for the sake of it. The art style is a bit special, some might hate it, but it does work well to make the game look pixellated / retro in a unique way. Some of the enemies / bosses were... odd or clunky, but afaik that's basically because of how they were in the original game.Well worth the purchase, and if you're unsure, try the demo, which is the first level and fairly representative of the game as a whole.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: While I do personally wish they wouldve kept the first, more realistic, artsyle they originally showcased years ago, the newer retro one has grown on me. That being said, this game is not for everyone. This is the OG immersive sim and Nightdive staying so true to the original does mean somethings are still painful o play through. Chief among them is the level design, my god can constantly navigating a maze be mentally exhausting. Still, they did a good job of making the levels feel lived in (though not to the degree as say bioshock, but thats intentional). Combat is much closer to a tactical shooter suprisingly enough and the game (and SHODAN) isnt afraid to blow your bhole in. Same goes for handholding, there is zero, which i perosnally enjoy becuase I miss the days where all games didnt start with a 1 hour+ tutorial and constant quips and hints from companions. That being said, some things maybe shouldve been highlighted a bit more to the player (like the damn circuitry/power reroute puzzles). They did their best with cyberspace which also sucked in the original but my god do they really need to be so long?? The boss fights are ridiculous as well and required save scumming but w.e. Anyway, good game but not for everyone and it may take a bit for you to understand it. Still, this OG imsim got me hooked way better than that overrated "Prey" game did....god that game sucked
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: What a wonderful game. You know those games that just feel so "Game-y"? That scratch that nostalgic and FUN itch? Games that do not try to be super high resolution polished miracles, but focus on the essentials, on the "play", rather than the presentation? This is one of them, and I love it for that.I never played System Shock 1 or 2. But I did love the Deus Ex Games, Bioshock, Prey, etc., and was looking for a game that is similar.Now, this remake feels very oldschool in a modernised, awesome way. Kinda like synthwave pretends to be 80ies sound, and feels like 80ies sound, but clearly fits modern sounddesign.This is a game that does not hold your hand, forces you to do a lot of trial and error, but it is fair in doing so, and only punishes you when you are careless, or did not listen or read well enough. And sometimes, in rare occasions the game messes with you in an unfair, but intentionally unfair way, to perfectly portray what it means to be locked in a station with an evil AI. And all of those "unfair" and rare occasions actually made me laugh, because they were cynically funny.The whole story is told by audiologs, textlogs and the environment and things you discover. And sometimes by Shodan itself. That creates a surprisingly good immersion feeling, because there is no overlaying narration, only you, yourself, experiencing a story. No storyteller. All mechanics are fun, and some ideas for the weapons feel fresh and unique. Explosives are satisfying AF, because they actually do a ton of damage, so I find myself using grenades way more often than in other games. Combat is rather "Basic", not very dynamic, but for me it has this polished oldschool flair, and is still fun enough.The atmosphere, environments, levels and the sounddesign are wonderful. It has a very unique charme to it, a lot of character. It is not just "another game", it tries and succeeds to have a memorable, enjoyable style to it.The map design itself may be frustrating for some, and some maps can be a bit confusing at first, until you "get used to the station" and even start to not need the map anymore. Some might consider that a flaw, but considering that System Shock 1 was a puzzle (the overall story and station) inside a puzzle (the maps/levels), inside other puzzles (level areas and access) that have their own smaller puzzles (access panels, tasks, etc.) , I consider that good design. It is part of the gameplay and storyline to get to know the levels and to find orientation. To find out how to get where, and where to get what.And once you secured a level, the walkways always get shorter because of better access, so even IF you have to backtrack because you missed something, the game makes it easier and quicker the longer you play.Inventory management can be a bit of a hassle, if you, like me, have a tendency to pick up everything. (Which can be rewarding, because you can vaporize clutter for credits, which can buy upgrades etc.) But since I do not HAVE to pick up everything... Can I really blame the game? What is unusual, but fits the retro-gameplay, is how much space your weapons take up in the inventory, and that you sometimes have to intentionally leave weapons and items at certain areas of the station, because you simply don't have the space to carry them around. Bit "meh", because I'm spoiled from other, easier games, but it also forces me to think ahead more, and enhances the feeling of "living on that station" - because everything stays exactly where you left it. I really like my "Elevator shotgun", and my reactor consumable-archive. :DSo overall, it is just a really fun game that focuses on the essentials, and is a worthy, lovingly crafted remake of the original. I'm having fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Great remake of a classic. Graphics are absolutely amazing, the environment and the illustration of the textures fit in perfectly. _childDocuments_.review: For my tastes this updated version of System Shock updates to something more contemporary without going overboard, and was exactly what I was hoping for. Playing the original System Shock in the mid 90s was a special experience. I don't know if what was amazing about it will come through anymore just because of how many advances in video game design we can take for granted now. But for anyone playing this for the first time should know that this game (along with the Ultima Underworld series, which I didn't come to until much later) was the computer game experience that felt closest to playing a tabletop roleplaying game at the time. Hopefully some of that magic carries through for people playing this game for the first time.

_childDocuments_.review: I never got to play the original System Shock before it was painful to attempt, though I played SS2 to death - so I went into this with pretty rosy glasses.Overall an excellent remake. It feels very faithful or a lot of the design choices feel like they were done over 20 years ago. The maps are crazy clustered in a way you just don't see. For me it was refreshing, like coming home - but it has to be said game design wasn't all that so long ago, they make a lot of choices because of the limitations of the hardware.So long as you don't die, there's not a single loading screen for the whole game, which is impressive.Unskippable cutscenes which is the awfulBalance is all over the place, especially boss battles.I have mixed feelings about sticking so close to what I assume is the source material.It lacks System Shock 2's "Play next unplayed audio log" button which to be fair *no other game in the last 20 years to my knowledge has*The Beta garden was pure pain. I nearly quit during that thanks to unskippable death cutscenes.I think the people who would like this most are those who felt like the missed SS, but also people who did play it and wanted to again without gouging out their eyes on a 320x240 dosbox window and slicing off their fingers with an ancient and terrible UI.

_childDocuments_.review: Nightdive Studios has brought this legendary immersive sim classic to modern audiences with a new new coat of paint that truly compliments and respects the original art, as well as game design. Graphically, it's a sight to behold for old school fans! The art style can at times mislead you into feeling like this is what it truly looked like decades ago, in a very good way. It's a remarkably stylized look that truly suits the remake.In terms of optimization, it couldn't be better and those saying that it's not optimized are definitely experiencing a serious PEBCAK moment. This is one of the first releases in quite some time which utilized the Unreal engine without any serious issues at launch. So, optimization wise, it's virtually a flawless release. If you have a relatively modern system, there's nothing to worry about, it will run extremely well. Nightdive Studios should truly be applauded for their efforts here.In terms of game play changes found within the System Shock Remake, there are countless gameplay mechanics and systems which received much needed quality of life improvements from Nightdive, removing or updating many of the older archaic systems found in the original, bringing the game as a whole closer to the modern era without removing its original identity. If anything else, it brings clarity to the original vision, making it a much more enjoyable experience overall. That being said, considering these changes, this is in my opinion the definitive System Shock experience that all immersive sim fans deserve!Now onto the main issues I have with the this release. There aren't many but...Nightdive has truly done themselves and their community a disservice by releasing the System Shock Remake with issues in terms of re-mappable keys for both Keyboard & mouse. The feature exists within the menu, but at times it functions, but more times than not it simply doesn't and considering this near flawless release, seeing an issue like this at launch was disappointing. Nightdive knew of this issue during the beta builds, but it was never resolved. For me personally, I wasn't affected by this, as my keyboard and mouse have configurable software, so I simply created profiles for both keyboard and mouse and moved on with my life. Yet, many don't have this available and they shouldn't have to. This has been a function feature for decades.Then in terms of the controller experience, it's just not where it needed to be. Although yes, it is listed as partial controller support but, there's simply no reason that Nightdive couldn't have had full controller support ready for launch. The partial controller support available is generic and doesn't suit the game. It's quite clear to see they didn't put enough time into it. I wouldn't go as far as saying it's unplayable with a controller, but it certainly isn't a satisfactory experience and anyone saying it is must be delusional. All one has to do is try to navigate the inventory to see how insufficient it is. Nightdive should have ensured that inventory management was navigated using a D-Pad, not emulated mouse using the right stick, because there's never been a time where that form of navigation was acceptable, let alone in 2023.So overall, those are my primary issues. Input device support is lacking and Nightdive needs to provide an update soon, so those affected by the above mentioned issues can enjoy the experience the way it was intended.Now that those negatives are out of the way, I 100% recommend System Shock Remake! It's a magnificent remake of a legendary game that truly must be experienced by the entirety of the pc gaming community. If you enjoyed Bioshock, Prey, Thief or other immersive sims, but never had a chance to play the original, there's never been a better time to do so. It's superior to the original in every way.It's everything I was hoping it would be and more! Once those issues I mentioned are remedied, I'd go as far as saying it's flawless! A definite must have for your Steam account!

_childDocuments_.review: I have been playing this updated version since alpha and, as part of the backer beta group, I have watched it just get better and better. Nightdive did NOT make the same mistakes that several of the other remake producers have made in the past. _childDocuments_.review: It looks ok, but the gameplay gets tiring after a while. You run around and get attacked. That's it. You have to scavenge, a lot, or you will run out of ammo and health. There are puzzles, fine, but they don't really fit. The "cyber space" tasks are downright weird. But the worst is that there's no feeling of progress, not after the first, nor after the 2nd, 3rd or 4th level: everything is more or less the same everywhere, the puzzles become a chore, only the enemies get tougher. _childDocuments_.review: I've never played the original, but as a fan of the many, many games it inspired, this is a great way of getting a taste of what all the fuss was about. The atmosphere and level design is on point. I found myself annoyed by the labyrinthine maps and obtuse objectives until I realized that that lack of hand-holding was half the fun. Being dropped into the station and having to figure things out was refreshing compared to the typical linear "follow the glowing arrow" gameplay  I've become used to. Each level is a little puzzle with delightful little details and quirks hidden about; I never felt bored traversing the map (even if I got lost sometimes).Combat is enjoyable and the weapons are delightfully hefty, from a gigantic wrench to a plasma rifle. Enemies can take you down very quickly, but you also pack enough punch to make things feel fair and strategic.  I also <3 the grid based inventory management and recycling mechanics (I spent far too long hauling random junk across maps just to amass credits that I never spent). The only downsides for me are the cyberspace sections; I found them to be an annoying interruption to the otherwise superb exploration and combat.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hard one for me. I recommend it, that being said, I don't think that I will ever finish the game. I think it comes down to personal tastes really. I really liked games like Bioshock and Deus Ex where I have been told this game these games takes inspiration from and I think that the game in itself is pretty good. It is challenging, gameplay mostly feel smooth (even though I have a though time dodging enemies attacks), puzzles are good and you really get the feeling that you are fighting a station with Shodan lurking around and not just some ragtag enemies all over the place. HOWEVER, I mostly play games because I want to reset my brain from work. Thus what I really look in a game is short levels ranging from a few minutes to an 1h-1h30 nowadays. This game as many people have pointed out will require you to take notes (by yourself, since the game does not babysit you. I think it is a good thing in life in general, but since I have become more busy in my life and want to improve on multiple spheres , I now prefer in game more straightforward in their progressions), to backtrack and complete certain sections as it was intended by the creators. All of this unfortunately makes the game for a modern audience hard to get in. It is rather unique in itself as since it is a living station, you really feel that everything is interconnected and that is where I applaud the effort of Nightdive that they have conveyed this feeling in me. I think they did a fantastic job at that. On the other hand, since everything is interconnected, you have to reread everything, backtrack, ask yourself how to do it strategically, explore the station in a very secure manner and take your time and take copious notes of where you left item number 4 that you thought was useless, but in fact was key to finish the game. Things that unfortunately I don't want to do anymore in a video game. For the record I have played (and finished) all dark souls games and found it easier (even with a wiki open) than this game. If you want to immerse yourself in a game and are ready to put in a lot of hours, this is the game to go. If you want something where the action is quick and require less brainpower, this is definitely not a game for you. I hope you may find this useful. In the end, I do recommend it for people where what I saw as a downside is for them a huge plus. As I mentioned, I won't finish it because of personal preferences, but I do see a huge appeal for certain people who want to take on this challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven’t played the original System Shock and only played System Shock 2 for a few hours, so I can’t talk about the differences between this and the source material. This means that I will only review this game for what it is and not make any comparisons to its previous titles. But with that out of the way, I have to say that this System Shock game has been an absolute blast to play through.Beginning with something I enjoyed the most playing this game and that is its visual design.The game has a beautiful retro/cyberpunk art style, and it’s executed to near perfection. Each floor has a unique look and feel to it because of the way color and geometry are being used, not only for gameplay purposes but also for world building. The enemies do not really have that that much going on in the design department, since you will be shooting at zombies or robots the majority of time, and some can even feel a bit out of place. This is not to say that theenemies look/are bad, I just think they look fairly basic or a bit over the top in some other cases . On top of that, I think it’s just extremely hard to compete with the main antagonist of this System Shocks story.Talking about Story, this section is going to contain mild spoilers elaborating the first few minutes of the game, so just in case, skip this section if you plan on playing it yourself.Basically, you are playing as some hacker guy, that was kidnap to a space station in order to remove the ethical constraints from an AI called Shodan. Afterward you get put into a coma for six months on that space station, only to find out afterward, that the entire place got taken over by said AI and that all humans on board have been killed/mutated or fused with machines. Now it is your job to stop Shodan’s plan to take over the world and get back home as well. Shodan is such an interesting and fun villain because she is always around, just like in portal 1 with Glados, trying to make your life as hard as possible.Spoilers overYou can not only read, but also LISTEN to audio logs to figure out more about the story and the world you’re living in. The addition of audio logs is fantastic, and I really hope more games finally pick up on this, because it makes me consume the lore and story during gametime and doesn’t force me to go out of my way to read something that may or may not be of use to me. I can look around for secrets, sort my inventory, might as well grab myself a drink irl while listening to a guy talking how scared he is of dying and getting his brain and organs replaced with machinery. But with that said, the game suffers, at least for me, with bad gameplay direction. Foremost, I want to state that I don’t have anything against the combat when saying gameplay direction. If you ignore the very lackluster bossfights, the combat in this game feels very satisfying. Blowing some poor zombie's head off with a clean pistol shot or blasting robots with grenades while trying to cover yourself from incoming gunfire is something I really enjoy, and that’s how I dealt with most combat situations. No, what I meant by gameplay direction is the progression system and the hacking minigame. At some point in the game, you are forced to backtrack to previous floors, and I for the life of me could not figure out how to progress with the “main quest”. I was checking guide after guide, but I simply couldn’t figure out how to continue the game’s story. In the end I finally managed to figure it out, but I have surely spent hours running in circles trying to find any indications, clues or missed rooms just to end up nowhere again and again. The other major problem for me was the “hacking” minigame. It’s nothing too difficult but mostly just annoying and unnecessary, but for some reason almost every single floor, if not all of them, have one.Would I still recommend this game? Yes! I did present quite a lot of negativities in this review, and they are very very noticeable while playing the game, I still have to say that System Shock has been a breath of fresh air compared to the rest of the games on Steam. The goods do outweigh the bad and the atmosphere, environment, combat and story this game offers, works out so well together which makes it such a unique experience and an absolute joy to play and experience.

_childDocuments_.review: yeah its goodoverall had two crashes and very little bugs with a minor visual one on respawn tht was fixed by crouching briefly.especially fond of the user interface here, as its very intuitive, fast, and looks slick as hell. the crosshair swapping to your cursor when you press tab, its a neat lil thing.this game is extremely faithful to the original, seeing some rooms that i remember from playing it a few years back is so neat in this games really well done art style. the music is fantastic, the weapons feel significantly better in the final release than the demos i played, its a really good time, besides two main gripes for me:- some of the large enemy fights are just annoying. a lot of weapons feel borderline useless, and you pretty much have to completely avoid using energy weapons to save your shields to reduce damage. i wish fights felt less limited in options in a game about having options. felt this way about the original too, so i expected it, but i mean its still annoying- the final gameplay section of the game is so sick in concept, but TOTALLY flops on making it feel intense, like genuinely one of the least exciting moments of the whole experience. which is a bummer.all things considered though, system shock is very much about the little decisions, the exploration, revealing the stories of those who were on the station. the final bit be kinda lame, but they did great on the rest of tha game.

_childDocuments_.review: I really love og Deus Ex, and this game actually gave me the feel of it. Something new Deus Exes didn't manage to do. To me they all just felt secondary comparing to the original, like they had nothing new to say. And this to me felt like if Deus Ex devs made a new game. Which is funny, because histrically it goes the athor way around.Very nice visuals, good sound, great variety of very distinct enemies. Liked the puzzles, they actually made sense. For me game has a couple of issues, but both regarding interface. The first one is the game doesn't save codes you find in a separate tab, so you have to search through the logs manually each time you want to check something, it is just too unecessary and doesn't make sense in term of immersion. Surely protagonist would note those somewhere.The second one is mapping - you realy have to hug the wall to be sure that all of the side corridors are displayed on the minimap. The game has some metroidvania elements, and you'll visit most of the locations several times, it's really crucial to see everything you haven't visited yet on the minimap. And I've spent like an hour searching a level, because the first time I didn't walk close enough to the wall, so instead of displaying the side corridor it was showing the solid wall on the minimap.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't play the original System Shock, this is my first experience, and what a game! I just couldn't put it down, finished it in about 18 hours in just a few days because all my free time went to it. The game is supposedly a faithful remake of the original and it reminded me of how hand-holdy games are today. There are some things they could have modernized, mainly how the inventory system works. It would be nice if they had buttons to rotate inventory or auto-sort even instead of having to right click on something and then click rotate. Well, that was my only complaint so let's get on to why I loved this game!The story, while minimal, is done through world building and exploration. There are no real cut scenes. You don't have objective markers. You explore every nook and cranny, looking for audio logs and emails. For those who don't like to go reading through lore, don't worry, maybe 15% of the story/lore items you find in the game are emails, they're almost all audio logs. The audio logs are what you need to listen to to find out where to go next. Occasionally, you'll get a call with some guidance but the majority of your story guidance will be from audio logs. As a result, you'll have to listen to them carefully! You'll probably even go back and re-listen to them to be reminded of something like a pass code. Shodan is a terrific villain. She is the AI in control of the entire space station, always watching you, always sending robots out to kill you. You can limit the enemies she'll spawn in the level by destroying surveillance cameras. After all, if she doesn't know where you are, how is she going to know where to send enemies to kill you? The dialogue with her is phenomenal. Every corner you turn, you'll find dead humans. You'll find skulls. You know, the way she talks about not only you, but the entire human race, that she's out for total annihilation. The combat is about what you'd expect. There are plenty of useful grenades, a range of guns to find that you can upgrade, and even an awesome melee weapon you can find rather early in the game. You can even unlock it very early in a second play through after you know where it is and can make a B-line straight for it. And that's what's great about the game! The space station is open to your disposal. After you get most of the way through the second floor, you can go practically anywhere next! There's an order you'll approach each floors when listening to audio logs and as a result, you'll be facing enemies that scale appropriately, but there's nothing stopping you from doing things in the order you want. This game has some of the best exploration. I heard complaints about "maze-like" levels but these aren't a maze. Maze like implies that you'll constantly be getting lost but I never felt lost. There are a lot of winding corridors but referring to the map and just paying general attention to your sense of direction, you won't ever really feel lost. Towards the end, I felt like I could confidently speed run any floor of the space station because the floors really aren't that confusing, they're just big. System Shock is a phenomenal title and I'm so glad this made it through development hell for me to experience if for the first time. I've always heard about how Shodan is one of the best, most underrated villains of all time, and I finally got to experience why. If you like games like Deus Ex, Prey, etc, and want to see what inspired those games, give this game a go! It's definitely worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Never played the original game so I've got no nostalgia, but this remake still holds up in 2023, it's just a great game; highly recommend playing if you like any of the games that this inspired. There are definitely some places where the game shows its age and the design decisions seem a bit rough in a modern context though.If you decide to play: Level 3 difficulty on everything except cyberspace.  Set that ♥♥♥♥ to 1 and thank me later, unless you like painfully bad 6DOF shooters.

_childDocuments_.review: First off I want to say that I really appreciate this game. It seems the devs really took their time in recreating a retro yet advanced graphical world. But my god is it boring. The same vibrant colorful corridors over and over and over. It's like prey lite. I can DEFINITELY see why this game WAS so popular, but in this day and age it feels like playing the classic wolfenstein. Same corridors, same doodads, same wall panels, over and over. And its so freaking monotonous. My second major issue with it is that I found it impossible at times to tell just what a certain flipped switch or pressed button had actually done. So get ready to flip a switch then run back through those corridors over and over going "Wait, was that door unlocked before? Is THAT what that switch was for? No, I think that was already open I just didnt go into it at the time. So is it that way back there from the beginning of the level?" 'Switches galore' could be another name for this game. or 'find what the switch did' and so youre just retracing and retracking through the same corridors over and over and over and it all looks the same. I'd say watch a video of gameplay of the first level to decide whether you will like it or not. I really wish I had. Lastly, theres about ten bajillion junk items strewn across the ship and I don't know if you eventually unlock a way to do this faster but you have to individually click on one in your inventory then scroll down in the dropdown menu that appears to 'vaporize' which destroys the item and gives you scrap. Prepare to spend literally forty percent or so of your time vaporizing things in your inventory to free up space, and after the first hour you will most likely stop bothering to pick up anything. It's a hassle and a headache and utterly destroys the flow of the game. But I can definitely see that prey was made by people that loved this game growing up.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: A faithful reproduction of an old classic with improved graphics and gameplay, System Shock is a thrilling science fiction adventure that challenges the mind. I would recommend this to the old fans of the series as well as those like me, who wanted to play the original but had too much trouble adjusting to the dated 90s style to truly appreciate it.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: The 90s was a great decade for video games. Technology of that decade was still developing and originality in game design and concept was fresh and very creative. I remember playing System Shock for the first time in the mid-90s and remember how amazing it was. I loved the idea of the game world being set on a space station that had been taken over by a psychotic computer AI that was converting the human inhabitants into twisted cyborgs to do it's bidding. It was absolutely creepy and intense. And the gameplay was amazing! I enjoyed the way you had to explore every part of each level in order to advance through the game. This immersive style of exploration really poured over into every other game I've ever played, teaching me that secrets could and would be hiding in any dark corner. And the logic puzzles always had a way of keeping you thinking. I love a good challenge, and that aspect really brought something big to the table. When I found out that they remade it, I simply had to play it. One of the biggest draws for me about the remake really has been the way they recreated a feeling of playing an old-school style game with the graphics being pixelated but in an up-to-date way that gives it a whole new life. And the voice acting with the recorded voice logs and especially Shodan's periodic announcements as you explore deeper into the space station are chillingly creepy. This game really satisfies me in a way I've been missing in gaming for a really long time now, and I couldn't be more pleased. I definitely recommend System Shock to anyone who wants an incredible gaming experience!
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Being a complete newbie to System Shock, I liked this. On one hand I liked the way the game throws you in with very little in the way of tutorials and knowing what you're supposed to do aside from some initial hints but  on the other hand, I was stuck... a lot. I'd push a button with no indication of what that did. You're not clearly told what the objectives are and it's up to you to piece together from audio logs and notes, some of which I had to reread to work out what the hell to do. I do appreciate this lack of hand-holding though, it makes us use our brain more. Towards the last half of the game, I did wish there was an elevator that went to all levels as backtracking was a common trend and it took ages to get from level 6 to level 1. The art style is not for everyone but I actually love the blend of old and new - I think it works well! The guns are exciting, my fave being the magnum. I did ditch the melee weapons after while, apart from the rapier to free up inventory space which I really had to keep an eye on. Maybe I'm a noob in this game but I did find the bosses frustrating. It's not that they're so tanky, it's more that they are fast and deal so much damage. I often found little cover that didn't explode and kill me immediately (last fight with Diego for ex.).  I died a lot and shouted expletives at my screen. So much for having time to patch up. Towards the end I did want it to finish as I think it the game dragged and had outstayed it's welcome a little. I especially didn't enjoy the last cyberspace chapter which felt bland to me. It's a shame to end an otherwise great game like this. With few the negatives I have though, it's a good game.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: After spending 48 hours on Citadel Station, this is one of the best games I ever played. I never played the original because I missed it in the 90's and later on I was drawed back by the graphics, controls and music. This remake made it possible for me to experience the System Shock world with updated graphics, controls and music. Firstly, do not expect tutorials or hints. You have to find out everything on your own. This is the type of games which were made back then. As you progress through the Citadel space station and slowly make your way to Shodan, you feel more and more attached to the story. I especially enjoyed the design of the space station and how each level has its own purpose in your journey with completely different architecture, monsters and music. This is just genius.The combination of updated graphics, story and ambient music creates addiction to play more. Personally I prefer this ambient music much more than original which I think does not suit the game well. The grim atmosphere of you being alone in the space station full of dead bodies, mutans and cyborgs with Shodan which is tring to kill you on every step is one of the core aspects of the game. You learn what happened to the crew through audio logs which are scattered on every level. One by one, you complete the full story of what happened on the station. And it wasn't exactly pleasant for the crew...Pros: - Story - Graphics - Level design - Game mechanics - Music - AtmosphereCons: - Cyberspace missions can be sometimes a bit annoying - The game ending could have been done better, but I understand they wanted to stay true to the original - Some may find lack of any tutorial or guide frustrating (but this is done on purpose)If you like sci-fi, puzzles, blade runner, cyborgs, horror and challenging games with original story, then go for it!10/10
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: A faithful remake of the original that sands down the rough edges, while fleshing out the later floors with more logs and taunts from SHODAN. Be aware, this game is  oldshcool in it's mindset, only the easiest story difficulty has waypoints. Keep a pen and paper handy to jot down codes and directions to save yourself the hassle of sifting through your log archive.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: For those who are huge fans of the original release, I am sure that this will be highly regarded as a fantastic remake. But this is more than that: for those new to the franchise, this is also a great point to step in at. Nightdive’s System Shock remake is one that will appeal to both audiences. The core gameplay mechanics may not the best or most polished, but it’s the world design, atmosphere and engaging plot that make for an experience that is still very much unique, and well worth the gigantic wait. I had a blast playing it bit to long and kinda sucks sometimes duel to the clunky gameplay. but overall nice special game. Oh and btw Shodan is 1 of the best video game  villians ever!
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: What a fun game it is! It doesn't hold your hand, doesn't tell you "go there! do this!", you have to figure everything out yourself. You get a code? Write it down! You have no log for such information. One of the later areas has a bit of a confusing layout I might say and in the final part of the game you get swarmed by strong enemies but with a bit thinking you can get through. While the original System Shock didn't age well, I think Night Dive Studios made an excellent Remake and actually managed to keep the thrilling atmosphere.IMO it is as good as System Shock 2 and that is really high praise. For me the remake is up there with System Shock 2, Deus Ex and Dishonored 2.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game! Atmospherics, level design, hidden stashes. Sometimes it's hard to follow what you need to do from the audio logs, but it's a rewarding way of playing a game in a contrary to the current "do that and that to finish the game". Only thing which was a massive disappointed was the final "boss fight" I won't spoil, but the very ending is a little bit disappointing. Other than that, it is a master pierce. I would love to see other classics remade like this!
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of System Shock 2 and Immersive Sims in general, I was quite looking forward to the original System Shock being remade, since I never played it. Having looked around in various places the general consensus for the game seemed to be that it was great but very much a product of its time, with all the limitations that entails. My hopes were that the remake would bring the best ideas of the original to the modern day, while leaving the uglier parts behind. While I can't speak to its faithfulness to the original, I can evaluate it as its own game. With that said, how did it fair?Visually, I think System Shock is quite appealing! The textures all have this pixelated look that gives the game a fake oldschool feel, reminiscent of slightly younger PC games such as Quake (A modern example that also emulates this aesthetic is the VR game Compound.). The lo-fi models and textures have been combined with some more modern lighting and VFX technology. Some areas really benefit from this, as the blocky walls cast hard and striking shadows, or beams of sunlight crest across the floor of a lounge in real-time as Citadel Station slowly rotates in real-time. It's pretty cool! That said, I have a major complaint: Bloom is unbelievable in this game. There is no setting to disable it, which means that any time you put the Sparqbeam on max power, you're getting periodic flashbangs in your eyes. Puzzle cabinets are also really bad for this, when you need to see little details on some elements, but the bloom is engulfing a good portion of your view. It's bad and it ought to have a toggle.This is the most important part for my evaluation, and unfortunately I think that the gameplay is pretty mediocre. Melee combat feels floaty, and in a game with limited healing supplies and plenty of ammo, putting yourself at risk feels unnecessary. Ranged combat is a bit better, but you will quickly find that even with improved ammo types, a good portion of the enemies are major bullet sponges. The bane of my existence early in the playthrough were the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Hopper Robots and Laser Robots, that inexplicably tank multiple magazines from your pistol. The AI isn't great, but they're unbelievable crackshots, and once you've been seen, they will find you no matter where you go. They will also stun themselves with their own EMP grenades, or gib themselves with their own mines, so they are selectively competent, I guess you could say. Additionally, they don't always make noise, so sometimes when you're walking down a corridor, SHODAN decides to open one of her monster closets behind you and you end up getting mauled for half of your health with no warning.This game also has one of the most embarrassing excuses for an inventory system I've seen. The Hacker can only carry a pitiful amount of things at a given time, meaning that you'll probably never pick up any of the Stim Patches outside of Health and Detox in your playthrough, and collecting junk for salvage to get credits is a huge chore. Fear not, however, because Nightdive has thought of this, and in their great wisdom they put in a dumbwaiter for the player to store spare items in! It holds a whopping 16 slots worth of items, which means you get to put two whole weapons in storage! This alleviates maybe 15% of your inventory problems, but it's something, I guess? You can just drop weapons in a level because they're persistent, but this is problematic for another reason.The backtracking in this game is obscene. The station consists of ten levels, all of which are large and labyrinthian, and you constantly have to return to previously explored levels to pick up a mcguffin or input some kind of code. This wouldn't be that bad, if not for the fact that the elevator layout makes no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sense whatsoever. There is no main elevator to connect all the floors, instead they're spread out helter skelter across the levels. Going from Systems Engineering to Medical requires you to stop at like five floors, and that's too ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ much. Audiologs are also a huge prank. 95% of them are just inane babble from the station denizens talking about how much things suck, but the remaining 5% are really important! Missed a tiny datachip that blends in perfectly with the motherboard-patterned floor? Whoops, you dumb idiot, that's got CRITICAL information on how to progress the game! Also, if your game's going to commit to the idea of not telling the player jack and ♥♥♥♥ and making them rely on taking notes, then put in a functional journal system so I can log where I've been and what I'm supposed to do next. Don't make me have to alt-tab out of the game to do that, come on.The puzzles in the game are a bit of a mixed bag. Any quest related puzzle is probably going to suck, especially , but I found that the little puzzle cabinets where you have to reroute power were actually pretty fun! The plug puzzles were too easy but the pipe puzzles genuinely stumped me at times, which is what I was hoping for when I picked "Puzzle Difficulty 3" when I started the game. I think that a couple more puzzle types like this and a bunch more cabinets could've done this game wonders.The game drags its heels by making you do arbitrary busywork with very little obstacles in your way (Enemies stop respawning after a certain point.), and by the time I was done with the Executive suite, I was checked out and ready for the game to be over with. I'm not even gonna talk about the Cyberspace segments, because there's nothing to say other than they're just really generic 6DOF-shooter minigames.In conclusion, I'm disappointed with System Shock. There are good elements that I haven't gone into much detail over (SHODAN is excellent as expected.), but with a stringent character limit for the review, I felt that I should focus more on the negatives and why I don't recommend it. I'd love to go into more detail about the sounds & music, plot, and so on, but it's just not feasible to do on Steam. It isn't  per se, it's just not able to compete with the immersive sims that succeeded it.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game and incredibly faithful recreation of the original, but two things: 1. it would be great if there were an option to skip the game over sequence of SHODAN possessing you, and 2. a strange glitch happened where upon my respawning in a reconstruction machine my legs kept clipping above my weapon. Not so bad when I was facing toward but most other times they would kick up like a military march on steroids and block my field of view, the worst part is this won't go away when I tried reloading! The second problem is worse than the first but when these are fixed this game will be, and still is, highly recommendable!
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great remake full of contextual 90s goodness you'll want to play thru multiple times. Hard mode requires you to beat the game in 10 hours or less. When was the last time a game had 10 hours of content? TBH the retail price for such an old title is high, but it's a genuinely good price for someone who's never played System Shock series. You're getting an honest-to-god fully fleshed out retail title with no microtransaction or loot chest bulls$$t. $40 for the whole enchilada. An easy choice if you're into Sci-fi horror.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: When a rehash of a nearly 30 year old game is the best release in 2023, yeah, that. I can't recommend this enough. My only prior complaint was the dreadful final battle.This has been significantly reworked for the 1.2 update; so that it's possible to lose. The puzzle takes a few moments to figure out, but once you understand the mechanics it's still largely a case of going through the motions. Objectively, it's a better finale. It cannot get away from being an anticlimax unfortunately. The very same problem that Deus Ex has - going from an incredibly strong gameplay loop to a necessary stop.The audio log achievement is "broken" in the sense that not all logs necessarily appear - or might be blown out of the world by explosions. Nuisance, because the story is very much the point of this game. A player could expect to be very frustrated if a critical game progress log were knocked out of bounds.Nitpick aside, this game is well worth a play through or two whether you know the original or not.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Never played the original and would never care to with how archaic it is. I definitely respect it though, especially for giving us the immersive sim genre as we know it and being SO unfathomably ahead of its time. But DAMN, this remake is something else. Can't describe the level of satisfaction I get from every little part of this game, be it the puzzles, the exploration or combat. This game is definitely NOT for everyone, but patient people who get high off those dopamine hits from solving things will ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love this.Edit: Going further and further into it, this game is bar none one of my favorites of all time. I can't believe how good this is. Edit 2: Scratch that. This  my favorite game of all time. Don't get me wrong, I can still see the flaws in some of the bugs and technical issues here and there, but that's inconsequential to just how masterful of a game this is. Imagine every genre of a game put into one, but with all of the soul and integrity of each genre somehow still intact. Dungeon crawler, immersive sim, sci-fi cyberpunk RPG, FPS, puzzler, survival horror, Metroidvania. This game literally has it all, and hits on everything it does with so much competence. I've always been jealous of those people who love certain games like Skyrim so much that they can replay it over and over again and feel at home, feel at peace, because they found a game, a thing, that can be their comfort food or warm blanket when life gets tough and an escape is needed. I finally found that game for me. I beg of you, check out this game and surprise yourself with something a little bit different.

_childDocuments_.review: Just bought it cuz I was a huge fan of System Shock 2 and the original System Shock was one of those games that the mechanics felt "too old for me" to try and get completely invested in it. (Also I was busy back then) And in the end, I ended hooked up on the story, the environments and the exploration, a marvelous remake of a marvelous game!I also appreciate that the game runs pretty smoothly on my sad Laptop that can barely hold something new like Elden Ring or Black Myth: Wukong, wished more games were this optimized! Congratulations to Nightdive studios, you guys are doing an incredible job! _childDocuments_.review: As a kid i saw pictures of this game in monthly gaming magazines (no internet reviews back then).The computer at home could not run this game.Now with this remaster i was so exicted!For me one of the best games of  2023.+ Great style of graphics+ Sound & Music+ The game does not hold your hand+ Recycling is fun+ Atmosphere of this game is mindblowingThank you developers for creating such a unique experience, looking forward to the System Shock 2 Remaster.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I have really enjoyed this game so far (cleared the first two levels and progressing further now). I played the original System Shock back in the day, then System Shock 2 a few years later. Every few years I tend to replay the second game, but I never went back to the first game even after it got better mouse controls. This remake made me finally experience the original story line again.Nostalgia plays a part of course, but I can easily recommend this game. I personally like the retro style graphics. Some people don't, so maybe check the demo or Youtube videos to see how you like it before purchasing. Better controls and some quality of life improvements make the game feel mostly like a somewhat modern FPS.Item handling is maybe the least improved part. You have rather limited inventory space that you have to arrange manually, and the game is littered with junk items that you can scrap for a bit of extra cash. While resource management is definitely an intended feature and you should feel the pressure not to waste ammo/consumables, this leads to quite a bit of clicking that could have been streamlined more.In my opinion, this remake succeeds in the most critical part: creating a great atmosphere. I've really felt the same mix of excitement and anxiety as when playing the original games. SHODAN's voice is as creepy as ever, and experiencing the story mostly through voice logs works as well as three decades ago.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Do I like this game? Yes. Did I enjoy this game? For the most part, yes. Do I recommend this game? Yes. However, would I pick it up again and replay it? No. For the simple reason of the Boss fight, which really is one of the two points of criticism. The Boss fight, as it is now, is doable but so so difficult. You cannot skip Shodans monologue and sequence, no healing - feels kind of wonky if you ask me - no checkpoint there. Oh, and you have to "alt + f4" out of the end credits since they are non-skip, which feels like a odd note to end a game on.Apart from those two points, i had hellofafun playing it. For the most part: Good job, Nightdive! But please add a checkpoint after that mentioned part of the boss fight, it would really add to the game experience.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I never played the original back in the day (Too young for all that and going back looks painful) BUT, from my understanding this as faithful a recreation you can have. I have finished this game twice, both times I played on the Hard mission difficulty with the 10 hour timer but my second playthrough I maxed out the difficulty. LET ME TELL YOU I made it to the final fight with just 13 minutes to spare on my SECOND playthrough only a few months after the first. This game is hard, this game is confusing and this game, much like SHODAN, doesn't give a ♥♥♥♥ about you. It does not care that you are lost and out of ammo SHODAN is sending more Cyborgs, it does not care that you haven't been taking notes, good luck finding your next objective.System Shock refuses to hold your hand and is a cold-hearted ♥♥♥♥♥ at times. SHODAN is the perfect villian to encapsulate this as she gets more and more frustrated at your continued existence. The threat level changes as time goes on and more objectives get completed, to the point that when most of the game is complete she says "♥♥♥♥ it, NO MATTER WHAT, you die" and I vibe with that. This game is very very obviously a game from the 90s so take that with a grain of salt. It is tough and it is very easy to not know what to do next. The hints are all there, the documentation is everywhere, you just need to find the pieces and put together what is happening and more importantly, how to stop it. PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE buy this game as I want a system shock 2 remake from NightDive. Normally I will say "eh maybe wait for a sale, or I'd say $20 is the max for this" whatever they want to charge for this game I will happily pay. $40 is a great price point but it recently went on sale for %55. Thx
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Games like these aren't made anymore. There is something about it when there is no dialogue, no conventional story, no waypoints, no levels or skill trees. Just you and the game.A pretty bad game.Contrary to what people say, this is not an immersive sim. Once you get past the early game, you'll be zooming past everything, exhaustively checking every corner, hoovering up random items, occasionally stopping to heal and recharge.People pride that this game "doesn't hold your hand" except you're given explicit instructions on what to do, but since some of them aren't  told to  and are instead located in audio/text logs, that are all conveniently scattered on your path, it then counts as "not holding your hand", I guess.The instructions themselves are not something you can think your way through. If someone says "go to storage bay 8" you have no clue where it is unless you walk around the map randomly. There are no signs with directions, there are no maps in the world you could consult, the architecture and layout make 0 sense, it's never about searching and finding something, you can only stumble upon things. Which again takes away from the loose "immersive sim" description.Combat is, well, the old style combat where you can't dodge anything. The combat consists of either A) you stunlocking the enemy for the duration it takes you to kill it or B) peeking, shooting, hiding, waiting for enemy to stop shooting, repeat.The visuals are extremely noisy, so many lights glowing in the same colors as buttons and doors, so many places having great visual prominence, to just be empty rooms. I quickly resorted to exhaustively hugging walls just to not accidentally miss a door or something.The technical aspect of the game is a big mess, but that's a given for modern games today, so who cares.The remake had a chance to alleviate some of these issues, enough that I would recommend the game, but it hasn't, it is a failure in every way, except for one that made me buy it in the first place: I can actually play it, unlike the original with it's archaic controls.If you want to experience "The Olden Ways" you're probably better of playing SS2, though I can't speak for it without having played it myself yet.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: AFTER SEVEN YEARS IN DEVELOPMENT, I CAN SAY IT WAS WORTH THE WAIT!I backed this on kickstarter seven years ago, and hoo boy, it was a wild ride for development from what I could see. I'm very grateful it came out. It's everything I ever expected from the remake, except for one thing, the final boss. Without spoiling anything, I feel the final fight against SHODAN could've been implemented better, but other than that, totally recommend playing this. Buy it. You (mostly) won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played 1994 the original System Shock 1 as a child (got some spooky nights then), some months later the CD-ROM version of System Shock 1 with language support. Things like this today are normal. Retroperspective, the game in the past played like excel with graphics. Nevertheless, I played through both games. However, I was wary of how the developers would handle the System Shock 1 brand. But they did it - one word: respectful. The changes to the game especially in the controls and QoL are excellent. The mood is captured pretty darn well; the immersion is fantastic. The improvements are also reflected in the puzzles, which have been brought in at the right place. It's still a bit early to tell how consistently on the further levels of Citadel Station the developers respectfully implemented the attention to detail. But if it stays that way I am very happy and look forward to the hours yet to come. Definite buy recommendation and many thanks to the developers of Nightdive Studios!btw: the cyberspace is also a good ride back in the 90s ;-)
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I played on release so there were some technical issues, including a few softlocks, getting stuck on geometry, and other odd bugs, but they may be patched out by the time you play.Visually, the studio has designed to make the game look appropriately retro, being a one-to-one remake, this includes purely rasteurised lighting, and textures with a pixel shader applied.The music and sound design/scape is stellar, which is no surprise considering its origins in Looking Glass Studios.Gameplay mainly consists of solid FP shooting, with breaks between consisting of exploration, puzzles, a flying hacking secondary mode, a frankly ungodly and unwelcome amount of inventory management, and running up and around and back and forth through the levels completing various objective tasks you can discern from the audio logs.Generally these audio logs provide enough direction, but one could easily get lost if you don't find them all, and further, they can be quite obtuse at times, which actually forced me to consult a guide on one occasion.Despite its obvious flaws, the remake has made System Shock generally accessible and for me was compellingly immersive through my 40 Hour playthrough on medium difficulty. I fully intend to play it again on hard eventually.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this game blind, I've seen videos before vaguely about this game and I've heard great things about it but never got around to playing the original. I was eagerly awaiting this remake to be released after keeping an eye on the kickstarter and watching all the teasers and trailers.After putting in around 30 hours or so and completing the game I can say that this is an instant classic. The game play and overall game design is well thought out and I've heard it's extremely similar to the original also so that just proves that old game design can still work in a modern game. The level design was fantastic but mainly corridor based with some variation in openness. One drawback which annoyed me quite a bit was the amount of backtracking needed and a lot of linear corridors/crouch spaces which you had to go through multiple times. Things like this could have easily been fixed and improved upon. Apart from these small issues the overall design of the station was amazing and it really made you feel like wanted to explore every single nook and cranny of each area. The puzzle design was also quite cool. I felt like it wasn't too tedious and actually took a few tries to complete them and they actually made you think. The combat was also fantastic and there is a wide variety of weapons and gadgets you can use as well as skill/equipment that you can upgrade by finding the higher tier version throughout the station. I did find that the key binds for these were missing so if you don't check you won't know how to use them so make sure to bind these. I'm eagerly awaiting the Enhanced edition of System Shock 2 and I really hope they do a similar remake of that in the style of this one. Overall, I'd recommend to buy this If you're a fan of old school RPGs and great game/level design and you're fans of games like Prey or Arx Fatalis.
