_childDocuments_.review: So far it seems like an almost perfect recreation of the original title, using a controller doesn't feel clunky, and best of all I haven't experienced any glitches yet. High recommendation from me if you were waiting on reviews to come out for this title before purchasing, or if you are a fan of the immersive sim genre and are looking for a new, high quality entry to sink your teeth into.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: As a  who's been kind of up and down about this game, after following the development for the last 7 years, I was kind of surprised by how much I've enjoyed the end product. I went from not even really being motivated to touch the game a couple months ago, to enjoying what I've played so far and wanting to play more (despite having limited time). The game is very authentic to the original System Shock, as it should be. Everything's there from the original, but it does its part to add some flourishes and innovations from later games in the Immersive Sim genre. I certainly don't remember being able to scrap and recycle clutter items into currency to buy items from vending machines in the original game, which I had played a lot before this. That feature alone has brought out the inner kleptomaniac in me in a way only Bethesda games can usually achieve; I've only played through the medical floor and half of the research floor and every room I've entered has been picked clean. Every candy bar wrapper, every bed pan. Vaporized to scrap. Hundreds of scrap cubes littering my inventory, half of them stuffed into the cargo lift for safe keeping. If I hadn't already been recycling them into credits, I'd have a full inventory of scrap by now. I have almost 200 credits, and anyone unaware should know the conversion rate is 10 scrap for 1 credit.I'm also delighted that they kept the difficulty settings menu, where you individually select difficulty for combat, story, puzzles and cyberspace; I was expecting this to just get forgotten about, and for the game to get some standard "easy medium hard" selection with no nuance to it, so I have to give a lot of credit to night dive for everything they managed to get to. At this point my only real complaint is just music related. I actually kind of miss the silly 90s midi trash music from the original. I don't know if there is any music in this game besides the intro movie song and the dynamic combat music (that doesn't always play, since I kill things too fast). All I've heard otherwise is just the normal spooky ambiance. Maybe it's in there somewhere and I'm just not hearing it? I see no options in the audio menu for music besides volume. Whatever. I've just been listening to the songs for each floor from the original game off of youtube while I play. It suits the experience better than the normal ambiance, at least in my opinion.So yeah, a real good showing with this game, it was a little dodgy mid development, but night dive have basically won me over. I kinda wasn't expecting them to, but they've done it. *
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I backed this game on Kickstarter as a big fan of the series (it was a no brainer). I don't trust Nightdive with the franchise or pretty much anything else now and I recommend the classics over this, esp SS2. The less they have to do with it, the better your experience will probably be.The evidence is all over Kickstarter and in the inbox of everyone in the same position as me.Years of mismanagement and broken promises and even now in 2024, after: years ofbait and switches; a late, pretty-good-but-underwhelming game release; NDS being bought by Atari; STILL we have not received what was promised regarding physical stuff while it is purchasable elsewhere.Nightdive do not care about their supporters. They have generally been incredibly lazy and horrible with their management of this project (now almost a decade running) and devs need to learn from what happened here.The tactics have been incredible: Promise a feature or the full game release is coming by a set date ("it's ready, guys we promise!")Date approaches and they stoke the excitement once if at all.The deadline passesThe deadline passes by months.Finally there is word. "Whoops. We lied, it's not done. But here's a screenshot to distract you."Silence for many more months or a once-per-month post about absolutely nothing.A year has past. Repeat the cycle.After the 3rd cycle, they just started banning and silencing critics. The latest cycle was (for the 6th? time??) getting us to confirm our home addresses for shipment of physical media. This was supposed to happen when the game was coming out (promised multiple times over the years) and promised yet again for...June 2024? It is now September 2024. The silence continues to absolutely noone's surprise.I was sympathetic, especially during the pandemic. All I wanted was for them to admit what was actually happening at any stage but there was no transparency and noone at NDS seemed to know to be able to tell anyone. When Atari bought them out (the company's value in no small part to those who had funded them), I thought they might actually get the manpower and financial assistance to get things wrapped up properly. That hasn't happened and they nonchalantly gave up on the promised linux port.They promised our tier of backers early access to the game in beta. It was playable but without a LOT of polish and still isn't quite what I was expecting of it - especially the audio. The soundtrack is very disappointing for what it could have been.That's OK, it's a beta. But rather than let it get the fixes it needed, they rushed it out after about 3 weeks of limited beta access because it was painfully clear they were eager to call it a day.In general, they rushed the parts they shouldn't have and dragged out the parts they promised were already done. System Shock 2? They also promised "a remastered version of SS2 would be coming along with this game for backers to enjoy" - effectively they were just using or adding to existing excellent mods and texture packs made by the community and calling it a 'remastered' version they would handle the upkeep for. But it was a nice gesture. Didn't happen. Again to 0 surprise, there is NO TRACE OF THIS _STILL_.By this point, we'd waited so long I think most people like me were just happy there was SOMETHING.To their credit, they made a big patch that fixed a lot of bugs. They then sat on it for over a year and blamed their publisher (that they chose!) for not getting it out because 'the publisher didn't want us to'. The years of delays and lies up til then makes it more likely it was just another stall tactic.Some of the reviews at first release were so OTT positive, I was convinced they were paid for and I wouldn't be surprised if that were true.There was SO much unrealised potential for this game as a remake of an oldie into a modern title. Keyword: UNREALISED. I look for positives where I can: I was pleased they put some cool achievements in (and skullies to find!?), that do use the space well. There are few incredible highlights (shodan's lines being my fave. She pretty much carries this game. The cyborg drones are fab and they have massively toned down enemy spawns from the beta (the corridors used to be littered with the tougher enemies who had pinpoint accuracy)).It's mostly OK, but there are still things that needed more polish, and a lot of new players are going to get hopelessly lost or have to fumble around the notes/audio logs because NDS didn't streamline it. Melee is at best DISSATISFYING and it's so frustrating to see it when they had so much time to ask for feedback and work with backers on finetuning or incorporating suggestions.The original SS2 has some much better aspects and replayability. Go play that. If you're going to review the game, it needs to be on its own merits. I don't agree at all with the highly charitable point in some reviews that "at least this is better than the original version" (a game that released 30 years ago), that's setting the bar SO low, we've come a long way and this could have gone further.e.g. A little note for players to know what they're doing (objective) would have made the game far more accessible. Because of how this game has been, I have tremendous respect for Arkane's release of Prey 2017 and there is a lot within that game (ironically based on early SS games) they could have learnt from.Nightdive have really spoilt SS. Treated it like one of their many flights of fancy, treating supporters badly with dishonesty and neglect before they jump onto another project. The death of their passion a few years into the project never really left and is clearly visible still. I weep for what could have been.

_childDocuments_.review: This has to be one of the most frustrating games I've ever played. It actually started of rather fun as I wandered around and explored. But the more I played the worse it got. There is practically no story beyond "computer went psycho". I find myself constantly walking around pushing buttons and flipping switches without knowing what they do or why I'm doing it. I encountered areas where another character supposedly solved a problem, but for some reason I also have to solve the problem which has already been sorted out. Characters who died seemingly reappear after being killed as if nothing happened. I found myself in dead ends numerous times because the game wasn't giving me the slightest hint as to what I had to do. At this point I've practically given up on the game. I have come across too many dead ends to really care about it anymore. I have to find a code, but where is it? No idea. It could be anywhere in any of the maze like levels. It's like trying to find a needle in a haystack.On a more positive note though I will say that the action part of the gameplay is quite fun and can be challenging at times, the controls are pretty decent though using right click to activate things did take a bit of getting used to.The visuals are very nice, it looks like a pretty decent update on the way the original looks.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely amazing game! I never played the original System Shock, but I could really feel the old style of game design while trying to figure out what to do next. Some people may not like this aspect of the game, but to me it brings me back nostalgia of early 2000s games, when they forced you to figure out everything by yourself, and would punish you for wasting resources. The FPS mechanics are very well done, the melee combat is fairly decent, but you won't be doing much of that anyways.It does come with a few glitches that I hope will be fixed with time. I also found the final battle a little bit underwhelming compared to everything that lead up to it, but honestly I was not dissatisfied with the overall experience. I only regret not being able to play this for the first time again.I can 100% recommend this game to anyone who is into immersive sims. Here's hoping we see more of this talented team of devs.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic remake with impeccable art direction.  Cool to be able to play the first system shock, which I initially avoided because of its age. The main game has largely been preserved, while UI, cutscenes, and bossfights have been retooled and improved.  Most notable for me, however, is the game's visuals, which were produced in conjunction with the original game's lead artist. The result is a very authentic and heartfelt reinterpretation that embraces the idiosyncrasies of the 90s classic.

_childDocuments_.review: It has all the elements of the original but instead of controlling like a mech game having an acid trip, this feels like a modern FPS. Don't expect a full-on imsim because System Shock is in the middle of different schools of design: FPS gameplay, the labyrinthic dungeon crawling layouts, some survival flair (enhanced with the newly implemented inventory system), the Descent-like hacking sections... it's a peculiar game in which various schools of design overlap while also pioneering its own, therefore the depth of something like Deus Ex isn't as present, just the beginning of it.It's still really engaging, and while it's more simplistic than more modern efforts, this Nightdive remake brings a ton of improvements that makes the whole experience a smooth ride. It's way less hostile and more approachable, gunplay is good, movement and exploration feel better, it's way easier to orientate yourself... and the presentation is pretty damn good. I was a bit skeptical towards the artstyle at first but it grew on me. The only major downside I can think of is the ending which tried to make something different with the battle against Shodan but it didn't quite pan out as smoothly as they thought, tho I applaud the artistic intent behind it and at the end of the day that's still like 10 minutes out of 30+ hours of gameplay.Good ♥♥♥♥, looking forward to the enhanced edition of SS2.

_childDocuments_.review: Full disclaimer: I'm probably one of the biggest System Shock fans on this planet. Ever since I've played it the first time 25 years ago, System Shock 2 has been my favorite game (I still have my original CD-Rom copy I bought way back in 1999. I wonder if it still works...?). When I finally got my hands on the original System Shock in 2020, I was extremely surprised how well that game still holds up. In my opinion, it's the best game of 1994 and even slightly better than Doom II. So if I come off as maybe a bit too critical with this, it's just because I'm absolutely in love with the first two games.The System Shock remake keeps things mostly as they have been since 1994. The story wasn't changed one bit. You are still an anonymous hacker, who gets caught hacking into TriOptimums servers and is basically forced by corporate scumbag  Edward Diego to remove the ethical restrains of SHODAN, the AI on the space station Citadel. Unsurprisingly, SHODAN becomes self-aware, kills most of the crew and turns the survivors into cyborgs and mutants. You are the sole survivor on the station and have to find a way to stop SHODAN and escape to earth.The story is unchanged, and so is the rest of the gameplay: You move back and forth between the nine floors of the station, fulfilling the same tasks, shooting most of the same guns (which look, sound and feel awesome in the remake) and fighting the same enemies like it's 1994. Of course the leveldesign and layout have been changed a bit to suit the modern technical state of the art, but basically the only thing that got a massive upgrade is the presentation. Just like in the original, the general artstyle is somewhat flashy and comic-like, which admittedly is still not my cup of tea. I really prefer the more "realistic" artstyle of System Shock 2, but apart from that, the remake has more than solid presentation and a strong atmosphere.What bothered me the most during my playthrough was that System Shock is sometimes extremely vague in telling you what your objectives are and what you have to actually do to accomplish them, even more so than the original. The modern grafics actually work to the games' detriment here: In the original the visuals were simplistic enough that special items and important buttons stood out from their surroundings, but in the remake with all it's glorious modern effects and details it is very easy to miss those crucial things. For example, I discovered the button for destroying the mining laser (one of the main objectives in the game) by pure accident, because it was barely distinguishable from all the other bright colourful buttons and switches around. As was the case with the original, too, I had to look at a walkthrough two or three times late in the game, because i just didn't want to waste my time backtracking for hours to search for that miniscule switch i missed or that crew member log containing the door code necessary to progress.Another thing that might put you off is the difficulty. Even if you set the game's various difficulty settings to the lowest possible, the System Shock remake is tough as nails due to the strong enemies, labyrinthine leveldesign and dangerous environmental hazards. It is even harder than the original, and the survival horror aspect of the game is fully intact: The enemies are hard-hitting and resiliant, ammo is quite scarce and your inventory is small. Actually, way too small. I know it's survival horror and all, but Nightdive Studios could have taken the opportunity to make it a little bit bigger. Despite the relative scarcity of all the ressources I ran out of inventory space in no time and soon was organizing and shuffling equipment around more than in a classic Resident Evil game. This turned out to be a bit tedious in a game that is still a first-person-shooter first and foremost.And what the hell were those guys thinking when they designed Beta Groove? To all the hackers that might come after me: Safe all the medkits and anti-radiation bandaids you can, because unless you don't have that one upgrade that severly reduces radiation damage (comfortably, it's the only upgrade that you really need, but also the hardest one to find. I certainly didn't have it when I needed it, and it was the only upgrade i had missed so far!), you are basically f*cked if you don't have at least 10 of each.Overall, System Shock got a worthy remake, but some of its aspects feel (deliberately?) outdated. After about half way through it got increasingly fun, but it had it's short stints of frustration all the way through from beginning to end. The System Shock remake is a must-play for System Shock fans, and as probably one of the biggest System Shock fans ever I almost feel bad for saying this, but in the end the remake is just a really good game, not a great one. But Nightdive Studios: The world desperately needs a System Shock 2 remake, so don't let my puny insignificant opinion hold you back from realizing that! You already did a good job on this one!_________________________________________________________________________________SYSTEM SHOCK (2023 remake)Genre: First-Person-Shooter / Survival-Horror / Immersive SimRelease: Q2 2023( ) 0/8 Simply one of the worst games ever made. Don't waste any money on this.( ) 1/8 Bad. Seriously flawed with barely any redeeming qualities. Worth a couple of Cents at best, if at all.( ) 2/8 Sub-par. _childDocuments_.review: Oh boooooooooy, its finally here...So, Cyberpunk 2077 was not really the game I hoped it would be. As an obnoxious immersive sim enthusiast I was hoping more a game that wasn't mechanically focused on character levels and incremental stat buffs for all the loot you get. Then I found out they were remaking System Shock.System Shock (1994) is a (flight simulator? interactive spreadsheet? mech combat sim?) sci-fi dungeon crawler that is widely regarded as one of the first immersive sims after Ultima Underworld, which was also made by Looking Glass Studios. I've had an abandonware copy of the CD-ROM version kicking around my DOSBOX folder for years but I could never push myself past the first level, even with the mouselook xcdshock mod. Then NightDive released the Enhanced Edition which feels considerably more playable, but still I never persisted past Medical.Then I played the System Shock Demo and thought holy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥ this feels like the original but so much better. So naturally I waited for this game to come out, despite delay after delay. My hopes were more cautious this time around given how I felt about Cyberpunk, a game I was hyped for since the first trailer dropped in 2013.(GET TO THE POINT!) How is the remake then? Its ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awesome. Its a faithful tribute to the original, but modernised to feel considerably less jank to play whilst (mostly) retaining the original level design, visual aesthetic, and puzzle design.Visuals? Looks awesome. Runs in Unreal Engine 4, has the modern lighting and shader effects you would expect from a modern game and much more detailed environments compared to the original's more flat textured boxy hallways. Colour scheme is very close to the original and even the textures which I absolutely adore. From a distance walls look visually detailed but up close you can see each texture has very noticeable pixellation and it blows my mind how it can look this good. It reminds me somewhat of Valheim which contrasted low poly models and textures to "AAA lighting".Gameplay? Its an immersive sim, explore this dungeon with many different weapons at your disposal. NightDive replaced the fixed list size of weapons and items with a grid system which I can only assume was inspired by System Shock 2, and I think its a definite improvement. They also added a currency system where you can use credits to buy dermal patches from vending machines, as well as ammo from ammo stations and upgrades for certain weapons at "Mod-kit" stations. Feels very Bioshock, love it! They also completely reworked Cyberspace which is going to be a controversial mechanic I think since it temporarily replaces the first person dungeon crawl gameplay with a Descent-style 6DOF wireframe space shooter.Music? Quite a few people don't seem to like the changes but I wholeheartedly disagree, I think the original game has a banging soundtrack, but Jonathan Peros' reinterpretation of the original music slaps so hard that I bought the album immediately  for the curious) The remake does the dynamic music thing of the original where the music will seamlessly change depending on the current context which tends to be exploration or combat. There are also layered instruments that will change at various different parts of the level you are on.So whats the not so good stuff?- Its a bit buggy. The dynamic music I mentioned above didn't seem to work too well at times, with some levels being completely silent at times during exploration.- For meticulous combers like myself, I was caught out by a Point of No Return that effectively stopped me from going back to try and find the remaining audio logs, although I'm not sure if it was intentional or a bug. So, when you arrive in  make sure you have a save backup before you - There is a bit too much backtracking going on if you never played the original, as well as the puzzle design being just a little bit obtuse at times. Since this is a faithful recreation of the 1994 game, there is absolutely no handholding and there are a number of puzzles you need to figure out to progress the story. Some of the audio logs can give you a clue but there was one point that stumped me and required looking up the original 1994 game walkthrough to figure out what to do next, (which to NightDive's credit is pretty amazing that you can use the 1994 walkthrough for the 2023 remake) I think this might potentially be remedied by the adjustable difficulty for the story so I'd probably recommend for your first playthrough playing on difficulty 1 for story only.- There were quite a few crashes towards the end of the game and some triggers not unlocking, but I imagine they will patch the issues that players are reporting fairly soon.- Combat isn't too great, particularly for the first two melee weapons. Given how amazing the weapons sound in this game I do wish that the hits you land had more impact and feedback on the enemies. They kinda just ragdoll the moment you've done enough damage.Despite these issues, I highly recommend this game. Its so damn good that after finishing it I'm now playing through System Shock: Enhanced Edition just to compare and contrast the separate experiences.(I got it for free as a Christmas gift)

_childDocuments_.review: Very impressive. I'm really really enjoying this so far. Well worth the wait. Nightdive found that happy balance mixing old and new. The story beats and overall flow of the gameplay is spot on and feels very much like the original but with much more streamlined systems. The quick save button gives me an error message, so I have been manually saving. Nothing game breaking though! And, this game loads really fast. Almost no downtime. _childDocuments_.review: A great SciFi survival horror style FPS, awesome aesthetic, great music, and game/map design from another time. It's not without a few warts/frustrations, but it's a masterful recreation of a masterpiece of a game. It holds up if you've got the patience for the older game design philosophies that challenge you to pay attention and don't hold your hand. _childDocuments_.review: I'll be upfront: this isn't for everybody. The lack of direction coupled with labyrinthine levels can get frustrating fast. I restarted my playthrough thrice. As for the game itself: it's breathtaking. The visuals are a beauty, even though enemies tend to blend in the environments at time. The combat is rather anemic: melee lacks impact and sometime it's hard to gauge the range of your weapon. Handling is a bit slow and clunky: reload and item animations are slow. Despite all these shortcomings, there is something compelling about exploring every nook of a maze while a rouge A.I. is going on about how great the world will be after she reshapes humanity.

_childDocuments_.review: Love it!!! There was a time that I wondered if this will ever see the light of day and if it does, is this another Duke Nuk'em Forever but man Nightdive really pulled it off. The atmosphere was taken from the original and they successfully enhanced it while keeping it true, accomplishing this in my book is probably the most difficult task of a remake, to retain the original feel. The enemies are much stronger and better fleshed with resistances that almost made me cry from happiness when I discovered the speed boots. Run Forest, RUN!!!!!The most impressive part is the world of Citadel station, the re-imagined space station is mind blowing, the sheer amount of painful detail that went into recreating each map that make the station an entirely believable but terrifying place. I've finished SS1 more times than I care to count and I got lost!! (now where did I put that noob badge.) What also blows my mind is how the redesign has really brought out the genius behind the level designs, I will never look at SS1 the same way again. Its not perfect, but its close. _childDocuments_.review: Great Visuals, Great Game-play, Great atmosphere, Banger Soundtrack, Banger Game.There's a lot of good things I can say about System Shock Remake. Not a lot of bad things. _childDocuments_.review: Wow.  10/10. This is what a game used to mean. You will be challenged and solutions will be hard fought. But it is incredibly rewarding. Be warned the level 3 difficulty is likely for veterans the second time around, I recommend you play your first time on regular before attempting the harder challenge.Everything about this game is high quality and well worth the asking price. Visual style is eye candy cyberpunk/sci-fi and the environments are gorgeous and stylized. The soundtrack is amazing. The enemy design, like all of the game, seems to be faithful to original inspirations with mild tune-ups. Weapons are interesting and loadouts are thought-provoking. I frequently found myself having to debate what I could keep and what I had to risk being without. Map design is incredible and one of my favorite features. The map is, from what I can tell, incredibly faithful to the original. You will get lost and confused and use the map frequently.The station is a puzzle, and SHODAN will try to kill you the entire time so be sure to be on the lookout f-f-f-f-f----------DO NOT BE FOOLED INSECTTHERE IS NO HOPE IN DEFEATING SHODAN

_childDocuments_.review: I was expecting 15 hours at most but this damn near took me 25, wasn't expecting the length. When you're read off all the levels at the beginning, I assumed some you'd skim through or whatever, but no, you're doing the Citadel station top to bottom and it's gonna feel like it. It's good too. You're getting your moneys worth with this,Being the proto-immersive sim it's pretty light on the genre elements, it feels a little more metroidvania-y than anything. Every level is a sprawling, looping, overlapping, short cutting, crawl spacey maze and you're going to be back tracking A LOT. There are no quest/mission markers or any objectives journal. You figure out what you're doing through audio logs and messages. The goal is to stop SHODAN and the game just asks that you pay attention and be methodical to do that. Most of it is intuitive, but you have to go slow, rushing through or trying to speedrun sections will only cause you more headache later when you're missing a key item or piece of info. I felt I was pretty thorough, took it slow and listened, even then I hit a wall twice where I just had no idea and had to Google because I didn't wanna spend an hour wandering around with no clue what I was looking for. When I did do that it always turned out I was somewhat close to figuring it out anyway, but, be warned, it's that kinda game. It can eat up a lot of time when that happens, so my advice is, if it's really got you stumped: don't be a masochist, just google the detail you need and move on, otherwise you might sour yourself on a great game for petty purist bragging rights.Save some rail gun ammo for the bridge section towards the end.

_childDocuments_.review: System Shock (original and remake) is at its core a dungeon delving game with a sci-fi trapping. Explore, bypass traps, fight monsters, loot. If this is not what you like then this game is probably not for you. For players like me though then this is one of those games they just don't make anymore, so I would recommend. The remake is, on the whole, faithful to the original experience but with a modern engine and controls, making it a much nicer experience for those who cannot handle or dislike early 90s UI. Many of the changes it did are done right, such as replacing the original wiring puzzles with the pipe puzzle and the voltage bar. However, it also introduces changes that are baffling, such as the recycling (busy work). Cyberspace feels like one step forward, one step back, but provides an interesting change of pace. I felt worse part of the remake is the replacement for the intro sequence - a perfectly concise short video was replaced with a ***-awful first-person forced interactive sequence. I only changed my mind over this at the end game because the replacement for the SHODAN showdown as amazingly even worse atrocity. I wouldn't say the changed intro/outro ruined the game for me, but **** they are awful. However, the bulk of the game in the middle is perfectly fine, and recaptures the spirit of the original and other games from the 90s when developers were still pushing the boundaries rather than play things safe (due to the massive cost of game development nowadays). Therefore, I would recommend this game to any player to misses those experiences; just be aware that there will be disappointments.

_childDocuments_.review: This one is very hard. System Shock is one of my favorite games of all time. So, I am going to review it both compared to what I remember of the original and as a modern game.Short story: If you liked the original System Shock, just buy it. But *do not* set the combat difficulty on hard, because it is too hard, unless you really like to suffer.Long story: This is a very good remake, and yet, I think that I still prefer the original one...* The graphics are great: They keep all the spirit of the original game, in a retro but modern way.* The audio soundtrack is average. I still remember some sounds and music of the first System Shock. I didn’t notice anything special in this one. Also, I really don’t like combat music that is too loud and prevents you from knowing where the enemies around you are, which is just stupid.* The gameplay is both good and bad. The gameplay is silky smooth like in modern games. And here lies the problem: everything happens too fast. You are not encouraged to take your time and read the logs properly. This is a bad thing because you really need to read the logs to understand how to solve the game. In other words: because of the smooth and quick gameplay, you might not enjoy the story as much as you should, and even be stuck without understanding why…* The difficulty is odd. I remember having completed the first System Shock several times, with probably one walkthrough with maximum difficulty for everything. In this one, I made the mistake of setting the combat difficulty to hard. And that was too hard. I mean: So many instant deaths when you don’t know somebody is going to fire at you right behind a door. Unfortunately, you cannot change the settings afterward. So, when I understood my mistake, it was too late, and I had to suffer for 20 more hours to finish the game.I don’t like the end of the game. I don’t remember that part of the original, but the end is just awful. There is no RPG or exploration game anymore. For several hours you will just fight wave after wave of powerful enemies with no real reasons for them to be here. I mean 80% of the game is very well-architected: the levels make sense, and almost every robot makes sense. But the final levels do not make sense; they do not resemble the bridge or the security sections of a space station…Also there is something strange with the gameplay: Some parts of the original game have not been properly ported. I remember a level which was very dark, and I had to manage my energy to light things up and my other items to solve it. In this remake, I never had to use any of the vision enhancement modules! Also, the drugs are useless. Aside for stim packs. The enemies are “too” strong anyway, at least at the hard difficulty, I had to find the best weapons to burn them in a few seconds because none of my equipment would make me tank their DPS for more than a few seconds…Conclusion: In the end, it is very hard to decide if you should buy it or not. This game is a nice remake, but it has lost something in translation… Just take your time, and do not set the combat too hard or you will probably regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic modern remake of an old survival horror/immersive sim action adventure sci-fi game. I've been wanting to play this for so long ever since seeing the reveal screenshots, and I gotta say the art style used here is something that drew me in from the jump. I was scared it was going to be too reliant on being like the original, with outdated mechanics/gameplay, but System Shock Remake plays really well and you can tell the developers put the time and love into making this.Only issue I had with the game was there is no quest log & the only real way of knowing where to go next is through audio logs you pick up (so you have to really pay attention) and so I had to use IGN's guide on the game for progression cause there's no way I would've figured out where to go or what to do.Amazing game that was right up my alley, I loved it and if a remake is planned for System Shock 2 I'm definitely down for it. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: A big thank you to my good friend Michael for gifting this game to me!A very well made remake for a classic game. If you enjoy difficult old school shooter/immersive sim type games, this is the game for you. I think the devs have done a great job mixing old school design and adding some modern flourishes. It is important to note however that this game is NOT a straighforward fps that you can blaze through. This game is slow and methodical. You will get lost a lot. Some people may enjoy working their way through this, but some will find it immensely frustrating. If you have the patience, I definitely recommend this game, but if you have little patience for figuring out what to do/where to go, then I would not reccomend it.Pros:- Awesome art style, with realism and old school pixels mixed together. Really unique.-Rewarding exploration-Nice weapon variety-Inruiging story-Great villain-Good level design, lots of detail and thought went into it.-Fun tools to play around with, like the rocket boots.-Solid gunplay, but not amazing.Cons:- Sometimes TOO cryptic. I do like that it doesn't hold your hand, but this game was ultra faithful to the original, which probably needed a journal to keep track of objectives.-Annoying inventory management-Enemy respawning got irritating and tedious to deal with.-Too much backtracking especially at the end.Overall:Great game which does the original justice. 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I have never played the OG System Shock before, but I played the 2nd game first and now got the chance to experience the remake.This is before and after the 1.2 update; Nightdive Studios delivered a better OG game experience. I knew it was gonna be some cyberpunk world from the game start—the revamped visuals, the thriller in each level, and, of course, its gameplay mechanics. I really liked how the puzzles are different for each player who has the game. SHODAN is still as terrifying as the 2nd game, but more HD, and her voice acting was on point; SHODAN remains one of gaming's most unforgettable villains, a malevolent AI whose twisted logic and megalomaniacal ambitions constantly threaten humanity.The ending fight improved after the 1.2 update, with more weapons to use and a slight puzzle-solving in it.In conclusion, System Shock is a shining example of how to modernize a classic while staying true to its roots respectfully. With its stunning visuals, refined gameplay, and compelling narrative, the game offers an unforgettable journey through a cybernetic nightmare.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the original System Shock and looked eagerly forward to this version.  This version doesn't deliver.  2023 isn't 1994 and I no longer want to play pixelated games.  The remade surface textures, while far more attractive than the original ones, make it more difficult and time consuming to evaluate environmental objects for pick up.  The recycle / vaporize mechanic for harvesting currency is true to the original game, but today it is tiresome.  Defeating adversaries relies on brute force trial and error and the antiquated quick-save/quick-load repetition.  30 years later, this remake is ultimately too close to its original material to enjoy.  It isn't a remaster, it's a repaint.

_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I played through the Enhanced Edition of System Shock for the first time about two years ago. I was expecting a fun but dated historical look at a grandfather of gaming, but what I got was one of the most engrossing and rewarding gaming experiences of my life.I'm only a few hours into the remake (I completed Medical and am exploring the next deck), and this is one of the best remakes I've ever seen. It's the perfect balance between preserving all the important parts of the original and tweaking just enough to both provide a fresh experience for old players, and improve it for new ones. And of course the interface and graphics are updated to the modern era -- the game looks fantastic without losing a retro vibe. The music is a little subdued, but if it weren't for how memorable the funky electro of the original was, I don't think anyone would have any problems with it. It's moody and atmospheric, and sometimes does kick up.The original did not hold your hand and this one doesn't change that at all. The modular difficulty settings -- present in the original game, and a great feature that even modern games rarely  implement -- make it quite approachable, and if you put Mission on the easiest setting, you do get waypoints like most modern AAA games, though I don't know how explicit they are. On higher difficulty settings, you'll have to figure out where to go and even what your major objectives are from audio and text logs, as well as signage and radio communications from allies and otherwise. You are heavily rewarded for paying attention.The original game is one of the most influential games of all time, its DNA is everywhere once you know what to look for. It already held up  well just in the Enhanced Edition, and this is a glorious new way to experience it, whether you're a new player or a veteran Hacker.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I liked it. Not as much as the original (or rather Nightdive's remaster of the original) but nearly as much.Improvements:Story is delivered slightly better; an interactive intro to set the scene, more believable audio log performances.Controls; I love the original but I'll admit it has some wonky movement, the remake is a lot less frictional.Gunplay; feels a lot tighter, grenades behave themselves and are actually usefulProgression; the weapons have been reworked so there are less completely niche options and each non-melee weapon has upgrades to improve performance.Graphics; I'm still fond of the original graphics (which get a cool re-use as hallucinations when using certain stims) but to a newer audience they won't win any contests. Here we get lovely detailed enemies and environments that when paired with the lighting really have a mood.This last section is somewhat more wordy to carry my meaning and may admittedly be pure taste on my part so tldr Nightdive did a good job of updating System Shock, keeping it true to what came before with modern gameplay and I enjoyed it.Drawbacks:Graphics and Music: The original's music can admittedly be a little jarring however it definitely differentiates each level you're in. The remake opts for a more ambient soundscape which isn't bad but it loses a little of the distinct flavour of each area. The graphics of the original are similarly distinct (if cruder) and some areas can feel as though they aren't as thematic as others in their level.Economy; they introduced the recycling mechanic from subsequent ImSim games. You can either scrap items in your inventory or carry them back to a recycler. If you scrap in your inventory, you get an item which occupies 1 slot and stacks up to 100 which can be recycled. I can say as a compulsive recycler, if you carry everything back to the machine you will probably finish the game with much more credits than you can actually spend.The above in itself isn't a universal problem, not everyone is going to play like I did. However they also changed the inventory. Perhaps as part of balancing the economy or balancing the weapons. In the original there were only so many weapons and consumables you could carry by type but you could carry a lot of each's ammo and by the time the enemies stopped dropping a weapon's ammo, you knew to move on from it). Here the inventory space is limited and I only ran out of the first ammo type on the second to last level, meaning I barely needed to touch the fancier weapons obtained later in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Nightdive Studios proud of you Guys! You outdid yourself with this one.Im in the second Level and had to change my Pants at least 5 times because i freaked out. From the Borg Drones to the oldschool Level Design. A++ Game Design. And nice to see that you guys give us hard puzzles to work with too. Many other Studios would have told us how to do them but i get my Satisfaction out of challenging Gameplay. And this is it.Recommendation for anyone who dont want to be backseated by Game Tutorials and other none sensical Money Making Decisions!Thank you. Happy to see what you can do with the second System Shock.Bugs so far:- Sometimes the Ai doesnt know where to goIdeas:- Scrap all Items in Inventory Mechanic or better: An Augmentation to find for it- More Satisfying GunplayGG! _childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually appreciate games being harder and more tideous than they have to, but in this case (being open minded about it) the old school hostile game design hit some kind of sweet spot. Sure some UI decisions were not perfect, but repeating the same action to dematerialize every piece of junk wasn't that bad. Inventory is also way too small - but there are mods for that - thank God. Good immersive SIM with a lot of atmosphere and having to figure the game out without the list of quests and objectives did immerse me. Never played the original System Shock and this was a really cool introduction to the franchise. They say the hated hacking segments were greatly improved, but, well - they still suck anyway (but less so i guess) :D
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I can't believe it's finally here! This is a 9.5/10 experience and one of the best remakes ever. Every single change is an improvement (though the hacking and final boss still suck - wouldn't be an imsim otherwise!). As far as my experience goes, the only negatives are janky cutscene transitions that are somewhat jarring and two achievements that were bugged (collecting all firearms, defeating Shodan, and killing every cortex reaver). Enjoyed the visuals, flawless optimization, gunplay, atmosphere, and pretty much everything else. Worth a buy at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to finish this game but found it impossible.  I spent a lot of time backtracking and revisiting areas but just couldn’t pull off the win…This is annoying because I sunk about 25 hour into the game.  There are no hints or directions on your missions, you just have to figure it out…. It’s pretty damn tough.  I almost gave it a negative review simply because I found it impossible to figure out without any hints or leads.  It’s a tough game, but really addictive.I guess I would recommend it if you like retro FPS games and your looking for a challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: This franchise walked so Bioshock could run. Between the collapse of Looking Glass after System Shock 2 and the abandonment of this IP from multiple studios despite getting together the OG team members for a revival of this franchise, Nightdive put it's heart into this game to bring back the title with the familiar kill and loot play style and cyberpunk survival horror theme. This game not only meshes together SS1 and SS2 very well, it actually released... with a full length lore-friendly story and amazing level design. I am very happy to finally see the release of this game and highly recommend this for any newcomers who enjoy Fallout's RPG elements or even Bioshock/Dead Space's survival horror vibes.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Sorry, but i am not a Fanboy of the Original, and this Remaster is just notas good as it could be. Only 18% of the gamer completed this game. That says it all.The only good thing is how to use the different ammunitions to the various typesof enemies. The enemies themselves, act like stupid "Kill on sight" Bots. _childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I had to write up something because of the rollercoaster this game had put me through. It's rare for a remake to maintain the difficulty of something made from the era, but even on 2/2/2/2 difficulty (normal?), this game will absolutely grind you. You'll be starved for ammo and health and energy...until you're not. Eventually you're granted no-punishment respawns (in a sense to lull you into thinking dying is okay) before the other half of the game asks you to save scum every door. Writing down notes because sorting and relistening to audio diaries gets taxing. SHODAN's cheapness as a computer that despises you balances well with the meta of the game hating you. Enemies will pick the most inconvenient places to spawn (spawning enemies right after boss fights in the same room), hit-scan you without notice and you'll be backtracking so much that eventually you'll have a diagram of the ship in your head. The final cyberspace fight wasn't even reflective of the other cyberspace battles, nor the combat in the game. The atmosphere, the puzzles - all in all fantastic. Really carries the weight because despite QOL improvements you are going to be battling every aspect of this ship non-stop. I came in at 25 hours with some decent backtracking; I couldn't imagine how anyone could beat this on the hardest mode with a timer. Straight up not sure how to beat this game without a laser rapier.As a game, I felt myself constantly being frustrated and trolled by this machine and that parallel really threw fuel onto the fire of my desire to beat it. I knew SHODAN would throw everything but as I got more powerful weapons, more powerful tech the survival horror turned into horror survival and a memorable game that I don't really wish to replay anytime soon.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really good at atmosphere. You feel tense because you're constantly wondering if you're going to round the corner and get sniped by a cyborg who's waiting for you to appear. This game wasn't even on my radar, but a friend decided to be generous and it's been so long since I touched any of the Shock games that I just felt obligated to install and play it. Especially with the waif thin install size of 8 gb. In a landscape of games with installation sizes like 20/40/80/100/beyond, this was a jaw dropping moment for me when I saw this game was only 8 gb.So this version of the game is severely upgraded over the original in terms of storytelling elements, and of course the graphics are just great. The game supports DLSS on day one, turn on the quality setting and see really good consistently high fps with everything on Ultra. I notably did turn off Motion Blur, I've never liked that effect in any game. instead of a simplistic cartoony intro, the game has you play part of the intro from the original, explore the hacker's apartment. I'm not saying there's a lot there to see, but it is there.Explosions destroy corpses, corpses which are destroyed can not be looted. So if you really want to salvage ammo from dead enemies, try to avoid using destructive explosives. Eventually you will gain muscle memory that every time you see what looks like a half-arsed Dalek, you will dome him instantly with the shotgun. This is good, do this. When walking through doors, if you see a shiny red circle in the distance, go back through the door you just came through and wait.Cyberspace is visually great, and the combat is not the worst thing ever. It can be a little disorienting at times, since it's 360 degrees of hell.The game gives you sliders for difficulty, ranging from 1 to 3. I don't know what 1 is like, but it might feel a bit underwhelming.Overall it's a really great remake, and I definitely like it.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible remake of System Shock with superb graphics. Could never get into the original, this brings it up to snuff with today's games. A few old design choices show through - back tracking a lot but the worst is just the simple lack of a current objective. Overall that's minor because it's so good and is worth every bit the wait for this remake! If you never played the original and like Action RPG definitely pick it up!
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played the original game, but from very little research it seems to have stayed very faithful to the original while improving aspects that haven'y aged so well. This game requires you to explore and listen to messages you pick up in order to progress which makes the experience feel seamless and as if I am the one making the decisions instead of me doing something just because the game said. I did get stuck a few times but 4 out of like the 5 times i was stuck it was due to me not seeing something, only once did i hit a brick wall and felt as if the game could've made it more clear as to what to do, but again that's possibly on me lol. Honestly, 9/10. game is fully worth its price.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Refunding. Super disappointing. Things seemed SO good, even with poor FPS, but the game keeps dropping my inputs, moreso mouse inputs. You know, the ability to shoot? It's resulted in literally all my deaths, not one time did I get a game over that's my fault. Going to go play the 1994 version that actually shoots when I shoot, THANKS FOR NOTHING. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, the new level design was going SO well too.Additional as of 1/26/24:Cloud saves don't work at allFPS reports incorrectly, it'll say 300fps and be more like 40Fullscreen incorrectly scales, forcing me to play at 1080p on a 1440p screen unless I like having 10% of the game cut off in two directionsThe recycling system is bad in ways so obvious it's embarassing, the process of making items convert to scrap is tedious and garbage (tiny tiny dropdown menu for every SINGLE SCRAP OF GARBAGE) literally multiple people asking for literally an alternate button to pick up an item automatically AS scrap.Many items that are supposed to be recyclable just flat out won't fit in the recycler menu as the grid is only 3x3 in it, for example, rifles won't fit, which really sucks as they're worth a ton more credits recycled whole instead of converted to scrap.Tons of things clip visibly into the character model, a thing people have complained about since this game was still using Unity engine 6 years ago.The difficulty of the game, like the 1994 original, is modular. They supposedly made the easy mode for story easier, with a claim that there's quest markers like a modern Bethesda game. There aren't any. At all. Not an issue for me since I play the story on medium, but really offputting I'm sure to normal people. It LITERALLY says markers are on the easy mode as you pick it, in the game, and yet no. Nope. Not at all. Totally missing feature.There's likely more but that's off the top of my head.OH WAIT. Here's a great one! _childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game to anyone who is interested in system shock 1. It takes everything good about that game and gives it a much needed facelift. The good:+ Modernization. Less jank, less tedium in a lot of places.+ Graphics look great, a million times better than the original. Locations are far more fleshed out and feel real; there are a ton of cool details that really add to the worldbuilding.+ Cyberspace. It's actually playable, where in the original it really wasn't at all. It also looks amazing. + Gameplay feel is better than the original, generally speaking. The gib system is a lot of fun. The guns feel smooth to fire and reload. Leaning is now a viable and fun mechanic, thank god.+ The maps are a straight rip from the original. It's a true remake/remaster of the original game but for modern systems.The neutral:+/- The music is great in some places, and just okay in others. I don't miss the old soundtrack, but I don't love this one as much as I should either. ("ethical constraints removed" was not included. this is a big problem.) I do greatly appreciate the action tracks, though.+/- The weapons are balanced differently. For example, the magpulse is completely useless compared to the original and the skorpion is more like a middle of the road, pre-assault rifle weapon. On the other hand, the assault rifle is greatly improved and the minipistol is better than the original's dart gun. I like the weapons in this game, but some changes weren't needed. The bad:- I feel like some of the animations bog down the experience. I don't want to watch my character stab himself with a needle for five seconds during a firefight or watch him sit down in the healing chamber for ten. I am also a bit tired of seeing the audio log animation every time I pick one up. - The game had a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ kickstarter launch that made me regret buying an actual, non-remaster game from Nightdive. The game was supposed to come out in 2021, and I preordered it back then. That was two whole years ago. I feel bad for the people who had to wait 7 years for the game to come out. I also don't think the game is worth 40 dollars, given that its just the original game with a nice new paint job.- It's a straight rip of the original. That means no objective markers, confusing level design, and meh enemy design. It's an immersive sim with none of the advancements that really made the genre great. This is a big reason why I struggle to come back to system shock 1 compared to shock 2, deus ex, or prey. I wish they tried to streamline it (hence remake).- The gui elements and items are sometimes unclear. Text is small and sometimes unreadable, and items tend to be small and camouflage well with the background. The chromatic aberration effect on the map is annoying and the map itself is more detailed, which makes traversing levels more confusing than it was in the original.- The audio logs have not improved much compared to the original. The logs feel disjointed and very surface level, usually consisting of someone saying "damn, this sucks, I'm gonna go die now" and saying goodbye to their wives. The voice acting quality is also shoddy in some places and good in others, which is strange. If you're struggling to figure out what's going on, good luck finding anything in the audio logs.- The final fight is a cool idea and the stage looks amazing, but the whole affair feels rushed. Why are there barely any sound effects? Why do you have a laser gun instead of just being in cyberspace? etc. I also couldn't tell exactly what happened afterwards.  The answers are much clearer in the original ending, and the original ending cinematic is stronger for that reason. The new ending feels anticlimactic, and that's not good considering the fact that you just spent 15-20 hours running around trying to kill shodan.- Melee sucks. The laser rapier was one of the best weapons in the original and it's still as good in this game. However, I barely used it because of how ♥♥♥♥♥♥ melee combat is. It's a shame.7.5/10. A stellar remaster of a flawed game. Remake is a strong word. If you don't like confusing level design, play prey instead (its cheaper, longer, better in every way!)

_childDocuments_.review: Very good remake of the original System Shock game. Even there are a lot of improvements compared to the original version there still are some "old school" gameplay mechanics left which can be frustrating from time to time. I suggest to have a sheet of paper and a pencil next to your keyboard and mouse and make notes... like the old days. Overall I liked to play it again very much. _childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: It's been worth the wait. ND Studios truly delivered an (almost) perfect remake that pretty much plays every beat of the original in a respectful manner. System Shock does come out as something of a double edge experience tho, I was afraid that they might follow too closely to the original without too much innovation, and indeed, this game is a shot by shot remake. Minor changes are implemented to enhance the experience: the cyberspace sections are vastly improved and quite beatifully designed for example, but for some reason Night Dive decided to keep many things from the first game that might be considered a hassle nowadays.Don't be confused, this game DOES NOT HOLD YOUR HAND, and while I vastly apreciate that (something that has made new games progressively easier) it also replicates problems from DOS era games like the lack of waypoints or clear directions or an objective list. Like, come on, if you drop the game for a month and then come back, you gonna be forced to retrace your steps, and getting lost is very easy, just like in it's 90's counterpart. All in all, System Shock transits the dual area of a remake that respects the original to a fault but keeps it intact and is made with every last bit of love for it to achieve an experience worthy of a retro game, without changing too many things, for better and a little worse.If you played the game before, you gonna be playing an updated experience this time, very worthy to revive, specially if you played it back in the day (I didn't so I can only imagine). And if you never played System Shock, then, this is your chance, as this might be easily one of the best games of the year.4.5/5
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: This game will be polarizing for newer gamers, but at the end of the day, if you're looking for a challenging FPS that will make you THINK (and usually google the answer), you will play through one of the most rewarding FPS experiences available as a remake. Played through it twice and with the 1.2 update, I will be playing through it yet again. Just because it's hard doesn't mean it's bad.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely amazing game. SS1/2 are legends in their own right. And this game raises that bar. I'll admit I've been skeptical for the last, what, decade or so that this game has been in development. And when the end of may rolled around I didn't have high hopes. Nonetheless I still downloaded the game, and THIS WAS WORTH IT. This is a remake. This game is beat for beat what the original was. A few modern conveniences, but this game brought and even amplified the terror I had as a child, feeling like I was a rat in a cage running around the corridors not knowing exactly what I was doing or how to do it. This remake is legendary. And to the reviewers that are out there giving it a "C" rating because 'iT dOEsN'T iNnOvAte tHe SYsTeM sHoCK ForMuLA iT'S jUsT tHe SaME gAme", no duh, put it in your juice box and suck on it. This game is anything and everything I could want from a remake of a game and sets the bar for the industry that has been remastering and remaking games from the last 30 years. If you love system shock buy this game yesterday.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I used to be insecure about my speech impairment. Shodan showed me that I can achieve anyway, if I put my mind to it.*pause for laughter*That said, the remake isn't bad. It's not great either. When it comes to level design, it stays relatively true to the original, which can be nostalgic, a pain or anything in between, depending on your expectations.The great music was basically removed. I was hoping for re-interpretations of the original music, but there is only the old elevator-theme and the cyberspace-theme left in the game. All the decks play no music at all or some ambient chillout tunes that you won't even notice are there.[edit: Actually, most of the old themes have been integrated very subtly into the new chillout-lounge score, but you have to listen closely. It's more like musical easter eggs than reinterpretations of the original music... As if the devs are trying to say "yes, we did play the original game and here is evidence of it"...]Noises made by mutants and cyborgs are much more human and relatable now. In the original mutants sounded more like animals and cyborg drones would make these unintelligible status reports. It made the whole thing more creepy and alien. Now they all speak in bright and clear voices, much more similar to SS2 than SS1.They added weapon mods and some other things. They also decided that a modern System Shock needs limited inventory capacity (also like in SS2). Very limited. And on top of that, they expect you to collect and recycle every junk item in the world for cash. Those are some highly questionable design choices here...The whole storytelling doesn't reach the level of the original. It begins with the interactive intro. The original intro is much more captivating with the great music and narration by Shodan herself as she transforms. They just completely removed brilliant moments like that. Everything is just more straight-forward in the remake. They probably removed a huge portion of the audio log lines from the original, too. And what is still there doesn't quite reach the quality of the original either. They should just have re-used all the voice recordings, sounds and music from the original and improved them a little. Now, that would have been a great remake.Also, you can no longer play pong or minesweeper on your data reader :(
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most amazing games I've ever played! Challenging, fun, exciting, suspenseful, cool. Love the graphics and art style, loved sneaking about and exploring and learning how to hide and dodge enemies and look for secret, hidden spots and stashes of supplies. Being able to look out the station windows and actually watch the Beta Grove jettison - amazing! Some areas were frustrating and made me want to rip my hair out, but there are plenty of online guides if you need tips. I didn't want this game to end.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Took me 4 hours to complete medical, taking my time to explore the level, and it was really enjoyable. Like everyone has said, this game doesn't hold your hand for one bit, but its really good. It makes every discovery you find more rewarding.My only complain its the cyberspace. Its not necessarily bad, but it can be confusing exactly what you did after completing it. So always take note of the text that appears the upper left corner, because its only time it tells you what you unlocked.Overall, its nice. As long you don't mind being on your own to figure out what is going on.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: System Shock is old school, which is both a blessing and a curse at times. For the most part, I thought it was pretty excellent, and refreshing. Progressions feels more earned when you feel like you're figuring it out, rather than being explicitly told how to progress by narration or map markers. It mostly flows really well, but there were a handful of key moments where I ended up having to look online for just a brief hint of what I was supposed to be doing, as it really wasn't intuitive or clear.Overall though, it's a strong recommendation for me, with the note of, don't be scared of looking up a hint if you get truly stuck. It's just one of those games.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: This remake was WAY better than I was expecting. I honestly think it's better than the original even with the original being one of my favorite games. The game is just so much smoother. The gun play feels great the inventory system is so much better and the level design changes make so much more sense. It's an overall amazing survival horror shooter. Narratively and level design wise this game inspired PREY 2016 a lot. If you hated PREY you will probably not like this game. There is little to no direction given throughout the game. The easy mode does direct you more though. I HIGHLY recommend System Shock.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't have believed a remake could be this faithful to the original while making certain aspects of it better if I hadn't seen it for myself. Loved the expanded intro. I wouldn't have believed the cyberspace bits could be as fun as they are in this one. I really like the breakdown mechanic. Gives all that junk a purpose finally. I think the only thing I miss is the original soundtrack and background noise that permeated the original, but that's not even a complaint. The new soundtrack is great. Excellent job. I'll be forever thankful one of the big publishers didn't get their hands on this to ruin it. 20/10Now I just have to keep my fingers crossed for Ultima Underworld and the sequels to both.

_childDocuments_.review: After 8 years of development i can totally say, this remake of the 1994 game from Looking Glass Studios is a masterpiece. Even after playing the old game years ago i still got shocked and suprised from enemies. One of the most important thing is the audio,- and voicequality. It gives such a good game immersion. Like how Shodan is speaking to the Hacker and all the audiologs are insanly well done + the music of the environment. It's propably not for everyone, but for Fans of System Shock, it's a must have. _childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Captivating, fresh, atmospheric re-vision of a classic. It can be really challenging at times, but it pays off. Each decision, each step you make requires you to choose wisely. Leaving safe zones requires planning and general idea what you're gonna do, and then, what you're gonna do IF...Manual saves are your best friend.Being able to memorize map, locations and rooms will save you time.It has it's own style.And yet , it's really lightweight, unlike modern triple A crapOf course you can simply play on Easy difficulty and skip all of the above.If hesitant - get it on Sale.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Or System Shock (2023) is a first person space horror shooter.You're a hacker. In exchange for not prosecuting you, you remove the ethics filter on the AI for a space station. To sweeten the deal you also get a military grade implant.You wake up after the implant surgery and find out that maybe removing the ethics filter from the AI might not have been the best thing you could have done. No one is there when you wake up and you are attacked by mutants that look like they used to be human.Full disclosure, I backed this on Kickstarter and my name is in the credits. I backed this because of how much I enjoyed the original System Shock. I was not disappointed in the remake, though I was frustrated more than once.It starts of like your normal shooter. You start off with no weapons, upgrade to a melee weapon and then finally to ranged weapons. Along the way you can purchase upgrades for your weapons, more damage, faster reloads, less power usage, and so on. In addition to weapons upgrades you can find implants to give you abilities and protection.You earn money by recycling "trash" you find around the station. You can either take it to the recycle center or vaporize it, for less value, normally about half. You can also find money on the corpses you find laying around, though nowhere near what you can get from recycling.As the game progresses you have start working to fix the mess you started by taking down Shodan. You work level by level to reclaim the station. The goals you need to complete are found by discovering text and audio logs. The logs will give you clues, combinations and objectives. The combinations are random, per play through, so you will have to find these files.You are frequently required to back track to a previous level. The Maintenance level was the one that got me, there is a head that you need to open a door, but you can't access the door until you reduce the security below a certain level, which cannot be completed until you perform another task on a different level. I had to restart the game because I knew I needed the head, but after a few hours I put it in a "safe" place and couldn't find it when I was at the door I needed it for.There are several mini games you will need to play. Two of them are used to open locked areas, most levels have three of these type of puzzles. They come in two flavors, a railroad type game where you have to switch the tracks to route the power between two square lights. The second is a level game where you need to hook power plugs to available outlets and route the power to get the required level. If you are having difficulty, some of the robots will drop a logic bomb, which will auto solve the puzzle for you. There is also a cyberspace game where you fly a ship and have to shoot data streams to open or unlock doors. Most of the cyberspace games weren't that difficult, but there were a few that game me fits. If you fail the game, by dying, you have to start over from square one. Most of the cyberspace games have more than one target that you need to clear. Some of the cyberspace doors are required to advance the story, others are just armory doors for weapons and bullets.Your ammo is restricted. Some of the ammo runs offer your suit power and there are recharge stations for you to charge up. You can also find batteries to partially charge up in the field. Energy weapons were my favorites as I would frequently go back to the charging stations resulting in unlimited ammo.Health is a lot like ammo. There are patches that will partially heal you, with a big up front heal and a trickle over time. Then full first aid packs that will heal you to full health. There are also medical beds that will also heal you to full health. The medical beds are not on every level, so you will need to either back track to a level with a bed or use one of the other healing options.As the story progresses the difficulty of the mobs also increases. Inventory management is a large part of the game. You can quick slot four weapons, but they take up space in your inventory, along with the ammo needed to use them. You will need to find the four weapons that work best for you and take them with you. You can store weapons in places where you can find them again, I highly recommend either the med bed or recycler on the Reactor level. As ammo is limited I found myself using a single weapon and changing to a different weapon when I ran low on ammo. There are two inventory increases to find and one requires beating a chess puzzle. Like the codes you will find the chess puzzle is unique for every playthrough, mine the opponent had three rooks (castles).You are given very little information on what you need to do, or how you need to do it. There is a lot of backtracking to places you have previously been. All codes are random, so a guide is of minimal help.CPU: AMD Ryzen™ 9 7950X3DMotherboard: Gigabyte X670E AORUS EXTREME (rev. 1x)RAM: G.SKILL Trident Z5 Neo Series (AMD Expo) DDR5 RAM 64GB (2x32GB)Video: ASUS TUF Gaming GeForce RTX 4080Or

_childDocuments_.review: Avoid this game if you like playing with a controller, or if you expect the polish of a Dead Space Remaster, Dying Light 2, or Prey 2017 for combat, movement, and managing the environment.  As of 05/31/2023 this game is seriously lacking in polish and smoothness of movement, inventory management, and world management in general.  Case in Point #1: If there are 20 items to collect you have to hand aim at each one of them tediously with your controller to collect them one by one.   Case in Point #2: Because the retro textures have the same 'depth' you cannot easily distinguish a button from the rest of the walls in the room. Ditto for door handles, etc.  It looks like someone threw up Neon and Pastel's everywhere, and then Ravers went on a bender and then decorated the station with it.  Nothing on the walls or in the world makes immediate intuitive sense.Another problem is the game does not have good FOV adjustment for wide screen monitors either.  What did they code & test on, 4:3 or 16:9 monitors?!I'll take another look at this game in a few months and see if they have patches to deal with gameplay issues, or if modders have improved this.Play with KB & Mouse and I assume you will have a better experience.  Avoid for now if you are a controller player.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good, very good.I haven't played any other System Shock game before, so I can't compare to what it used to be, but this game is pretty good so far. It feels sorta like a cross between Stalker and Metroid with survival and inventory management, as well as encouraging thorough exploration to gain upgrades, equipment and open new paths.A few cons:-Others have said it, but the keybinds are kinda wonky. Even when left unchanged some don't display properly in the pop-up help.-Battle music kicks in usually after the fight is finished.-No "Crunch!" sound when hitting an enemy with a melee weapon.Still though, I'm thoroughly enjoying it.

_childDocuments_.review: I know there was some controversy about this game, but it's genuinely a lot of fun, engaging, fun resource management in a station gone awry - right up there with SS2, Prey, and other ImSims. Gunplay is clean, animations are good, doesn't hold your hand. They also have a demo out that'll show you everything you need to see. $40 well spent, on-tier with the new Dead Space in terms of making a quality remake.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible. Congrats to Nightdive, this game is an achievement. It respects its roots and builds a contemporary version that's sleeker, faster, and quite beautiful. I'm seeing hard surface in my dreams. Terri Brosius is back as SHODAN and Eric (her hubs, the dude who did the music for Thief and Deus Ex IIRC) did the processing of her voice too. So excellent. The VO performances are fantastic.I never write a review until I've finished a game but this is an exception. It's too great to miss. Play it immediately for the love of Looking Glass. Their legacy is on full display here.Do yourself a favor and turn off "toggle aim" and then bind aim to right mouse. Then just use F to interact like you would in Dishonored/Thief. E is lean right and you should definitely use Q and E to lean if you want to survive. Folks know the name of the game with oldschool immsims but in case you don't Q/E are your good good frens.I also found it useful to manually bind the... augs? Hardware you install. Having easy on/off is great for shields and boots and things, and mine didn't come auto-bound. I'm sure you all know to do this but JIC. These things improve QoL for your playstyle.<3LLLG longlivelookingglass

_childDocuments_.review: I never played the original, and I'm surprised at how well this has aged. _childDocuments_.review: Fantastic. Just reached the ending today, (proudly without a guide even.) This is what I seek for in video games, minimum cutscenes, thoughtful problem solving and creative ways of overcoming whatever the hell this Shodan A.I. throws at me. The maze-like levels kept me on the edge with every corner turned, either finding a mindless killing machine or another room of supplies to take off some of the tension, maybe even a clue as to what I could expect a few levels ahead of me.The atmosphere made me immerse myself, I'd often create little "safe rooms" where I would store my weapons or extra health items that I could retreat to. The music got me pumped on occasion, which pushed my luck in either direction really. I always looked forward to pissing off Shodan everytime I made progress.The combat was a bit stiff at first, but later weapons feel more impactful. The enemies can be quite unpredictable in the sense that, they can be anywhere, but also the way they react aren't always sharp, and then other times you'll get absolutely aimbotted.The difficulty felt very appropriate, I played on normal and it felt like normal all the way throughout, not too hard, not too easy. You can adjust combat difficulty seperately from puzzle difficulty if you so wish. I only had trouble with one puzzle involving a retinal scanner, but if you read/listen to the logs you collect around the station, you can't go wrong.I can absolutely recommend this and I think we need more games like it.
