_childDocuments_.review: The legendary System Shock, this piece of art was originally made by the best game development studio this planet has ever seen, Looking Glass Studios. I Still remember when i bought the original back in 1994, was an amazing game then and to my delight it still is today. I highly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: This remake is an absolute work of art. Literally 30 years newer, yet it's perfectly faithful to the aesthetic of the original. And it allows you to experience the original game design, just with a much improved engine, graphics and control scheme. Games aren't made like this anymore. But this one is. May this be the beginning of an imm sim revival.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Never played the original but was always curious about this game, glad there is a remake as i can't stomach graphics as old as the original.Great game - nice story, very interesting environmental storytelling, with audio logs and notes. No objective markers, pointers, arrows or any other things like that, that modern games overuse. Gotta keep a log of your own of things and codes that appear in game, Steams update from not too long ago added a notepad to the overlay, that came in very useful.Overall strongly recommend this game, not surprised it was famous at its time.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Controller support needs some polish and the ending could've used better treatment, but overall the gameplay, art style, audio, and damned gorilla tigers worked just great.What a fun game!I remember playing the 1994 demo on my friend's computer, and being awestruck. You could look up and down, you could pick things up, you had an inventory, and it was even  It was practically real life, on the screen! We taught ourselves how to pkzip recursive directories across multiple disks that we'd scavenged from his dad's boxes of old work floppies, just so I could take it home with me. The remake felt very respectful to the original. Time to slap a NG+ mod on it, and go again!
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of the BioShock and Dishonored series, I'd always wanted to play the seminal title System Shock, but was put off by its age. This remake has allowed me to experience the legendary game in a way I never thought possible.The art style, atmosphere, and sound design are all fantastic. As for the gameplay, it definitely feels like a 90s game and that's something you'll either love or hate. Be prepared for a lot of back-tracking; I spent a good chunk of my playtime re-tracing my steps and trying to figure out what the heck I was supposed to be doing and where I was supposed to be going, but I enjoyed every moment of it. Gunplay and combat becomes a little mundane towards the mid-to-late game, as certain loadouts will make short work of even the toughest bosses. More challenging than the combat itself, is managing your resources to ensure you can recover and survive the next fights.A great game overall, which will give you that 90s System Shock experience but with modern graphics and quality of life improvements.Two tips I wish I'd known in the beginning:- Audio and data logs you'll find around the station will act as your quest guide, and contain vital directions for you to follow. When you're stuck, or unsure what your objective is, the logs will always point you in the right direction. Often you'll need to listen/read multiple logs to piece together the information you need.- Use the notepad in the Steam overlay, or have a pen and paper handy for writing down access codes you'll need later on in the levels/story.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly faithful to the original, but with modern conveniences added in.  Well worth the wait having backed the kickstarter ever so long ago.  It was very enjoyable to see Citadel Station rebuilt and revamped for the modern era, though not forgetting its roots with its distinctive pixelated art style.  The only particular issue at the moment is the ending is rather lame in execution, but as soon as the publisher stops sitting on patch 1.2, that should hopefully be greatly improved.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Pleasantly "Shocked"! :)I feel like Nightdive had been sandbagging us a bit. I am an original backer and have played both the demo and the backer beta, and even tho I had the settings at max before and thought it looked great, now it just looks sublime! Almost as tho before it was locked at high fidelity but now you can actually access ultra. Also the gameplay feels smoother in the combat and movement. The sound the lighting and atmosphere are superb, the original story and feel are retained and the wait is finally over!Kudos NightDive a job well done. No easy feat to build the game from the ground up, not merely porting and polishing.My only complaint would be around the use of a controller as the bindings section doesn't work very well.Overall tho I am a happy backer(Hacker)!
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Perfect 1:1 remake of the original game. perfectly retains the gameplay feel of the original and improves upon it and cleans up the UI making it a lot easier to understand wtf is happening. no hand holding, no reimagining, NO DLC or ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hidden behind paywalls. Runs on my outdated-ish hardware perfectly and looks just as good as most modern games. The only negative thing i can say is the music. needs more of an updated soundtrack and less ambiance, but the remakes of classic songs they did do sound amazing.10/10, glad to see some developers have integrity left
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game. It was very immersive. The Citadel Station felt like a real place. I liked the blending of some old style graphics reminiscent of the old game with the new ones. It created a unique visual style. The enemies were ususally quite responsive and put up a good fight. The game progressed at a nice pace, neither feeling short nor overstretched.I  am hoping and eagerly awaiting the remake of System Shock 2 now!
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Perfect remake of a great 90s scifi shooter. I would recommend to lower the difficulty for the cyberspace on your first run. I thought they were boring and repetetive. Apart from that the game was great. As a 90s shooter you really need to keep an eye on your ammo. If you just waste it then you can get stuck. But I like that. It gives you more reasons to look for secrets and upgrades.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Farout, this was a tough game!I missed out on the OG '94 version but had always heard of SS in video game lore. Glad this was remade in modern tech to give everyone the chance to experience Citadel station and the evil Shodan!My takeaways:- Loved the 90's vibe, cyberpunk style and pixelation. Really well done.- My god it was hard! Many difficult labyrinths, puzzles, and scarcity of medical kits mean you REALLY need to avoid getting hit and saving often.... like before you go around ANY corners or doors!- Lots of backtracking through the space station levels for different missions. Not a bad thing, just noting. - - - There really is minimal way-pointing/task list - I actually liked it. Modern games spoon feed the player.- I hated the Cyberspace mini games, often getting to the end of the level and getting mobbed by enemies to die and having to redo it all. You can adjust this before you start a new game and I would recommend setting this part of the game to easy- Lack of feedback when you hit an enemy.. like nothing happens- When re-entering rooms where you have killed an enemy, the body ragdolls a bit- The ending is a bit meh.. no dialogue - this could be improved with an updateDo I still recommend buying and playing this? Absofreakinglutley. It will be better with some patches
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Immersive Sim is my favorite genre and this is a remake of supposedly one of the best immersive sims ever. Fantastic game and I have had 0 technical issues so far which I feel like says a lot about a game that comes out nowadays. So far the game is awesome and I love every bit of it. Exploring citadel station's high res yet pixelated look is amazing. The pixelated look really comes out when you start to look closer at the objects, but at no point do they look bad, they just look artistic or stylized. Music is good when it plays during action scenes, but the ambient sounds make the atmosphere much better when you are just exploring or working on a puzzle. Combat so far is pretty basic, but what do you expect from a game where your hallways can fight approximately 3 enemies side by side. You shoot at the enemy until they are dead. Im playing max difficulty and the enemy A.I is sometimes braindead and walks right towards you, while other times they wil wait in cover or lay traps before engaging you. I feel like the A.I difficulty/complexity is going to mostly depend on the enemy you are facing.The guns looks and sound good. They feel alright. Melee combat has some good heft and feels satisfying to WHAP a mutant upside the head with a pipe or wrench. I personally love all the little animations your character does when using an item or interacting with a world object. I remember thinking they were much too long a year or two ago when I played the demo, but they are much shorter and faster now. Yes you still need to put your gun away to pop a med patch, but this is an immersive sim and thats kinda the whole point.So far im enjoying the dungeon crawler "explore and get the loot" style of map/game design more than I enjoyed System Shock 2. Both are awesome and I loved exploring each, but so far Citadel station is just a bit more interesting since you are technically the one that kicks off the story/problem and then get to see the effect it had on the station and its inhabitants. Finding characters and bits of their story then being able to connect those stories to other characters that explain why they were doing what they were doing when they died is interesting. Hearing/seeing the plans the survivors had while also seeing the results of said plan as you play helps to immerse you in the game world and have empathy towards those characters much easier
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I've never (successfully) played the original, but I have played the sequel. I find this to be a refreshing combination of the two, with a lot of other 90's game references to boot (the intro hits so hard of Unreal Tournament boot screen nostalgia). Aside form the nostalgia, it plays well and makes me think about checking out the original again and seeing if I can finally get into it.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: After beating the original System Shock and this version, I can say that this remake is a highly faithful rendition, preserving its quirks and charms while also making notable improvements.For those who seem interested, this shooter stands apart from others for the fact that it’s an immersive sim like Deus-Ex or Bioshock, and although it may occasionally be frustrating or challenging, that factor alone is what gives it its unique charm.Despite being only ~8 GB in size, it delivers exceptional performance on most hardware while maintaining high-quality gameplay and succeeding in areas where most Western AAA games these days have faltered (even for a remake); though, as of writing, there are only a few noticeable bugs from what I’ve seen, with the exception of a potential soft lock that can happen later in the game (though there will be a fix soon ).If you're seeking an immersive sim experience akin to its successors, I would definitely recommend giving this game a try at any price point.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I don't get what people like about this game.I haven't played the original System Shocks, so going in as a brand new player of the remake (on default difficulty), this game felt like a chore, start to finish. Once you get past the shiny packaging of learning how the game works, most of the game I ended up doing the ultimate tedium of managing my limited inventory to fit in the things I want to take with me, making space in that limited inventory already filled out with guns and ammo and supplies to make room for random junk I want to recycle for credits, perpetually shooting enemies behind some kind of cover in a mind-numbing "wait for them to shoot, then lean out of cover to shoot back because if you're out in the open they damn near insta-kill you" back and forth, and figuring out where the hell I'm trying to go.Which, by the way, the game doesnt make very clear where you're supposed to go. Despite you getting hints on what's next to be done with the audio logs, data sticks, and incoming messages you get, there are no useful markings on the map. Any undiscovered part of the level you have to hug every wall and corner just to find places that may have doors so whenever you progress a little bit, and you have to go back to another level, you're basically trying every door you haven't already gone through to see if it opens now. Who designed the map, anyway? It sucks! There are so many quality of life changes you can make to it, such as making empty stores not get marked on the map, persisting resources that you scanned in the map so you can come back to them whenever your inventory isn't full (yes, I know I can place markers but they're indistinguishable from one another, so I've used it sparingly), or even just marking points of interest, like the CPU rooms, which you'll inevitably have to come back to once you understand what they're used for. Chances are, you'll end up Googling some of them because you'll simply get very impatient with it.Managing my limited inventory is probably the least favorite part of my game. Even with the 4 box stash that I started using on the Maintenance level, AND the cargo lift, AND throwing stuff I don't think I'll need out, I still didn't have nearly enough inventory space for the things I ultimately wanted to take with me. By near the end of the game, I had no room in my inventory when I went past the point of no return, as I had 4 guns, and the rest of the space being filled with ammo, grenades, and trinkets. Oh, by the way, if you want upgrades or extra stuff like ammo and resources that you're having trouble finding elsewhere because you already scavenged the entire map, you'll have to make a LOT of room for random junk that you can either recycle for credits, or vaporize, for usually a scrap amount equal to roughly half the credit amount of you recycling the item whole. So just to get some upgrades I wanted, I had to walk around empty maps for an hour or so just to collect items, run back to the recycler, recycle them, run around some more to find more items, rinse and repeat. Does that sound fun to you?Story isn't really anything to praise the game for, either. There's sprinkles of story filler in the forms of data sticks (text), and audio logs. They add a bit of info about the life on the Citadel, but the main story isn't much more than "I am a sentient AI, and I'll take over the world to do the things I want to do". Not much about you, the protagonist, not much about the AI (aside from the repetition of how much of a supreme being she is, and how much of a nuisance you are), or the characters that try to talk to you. It was also hard to appreciate the story whenever you start a level and you're immediately ambushed by enemies while the audio plays, or you're focusing on figuring out where the hell you are, much less where you're going.Finally, there's the Cyberspace. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, what a bore. While I did initially like the navigation controls of being able to rotate yourself however you want in the space, the combat was nothing more than hold down left mouse button, sometimes press right mouse button, and hold one of the direction keys to avoid the bullets. There wasn't really any depth to it, it was just there to pad the gameplay with a whole bunch of nothing. I'd rather do the standard combat than the Cyberspace stuff. Imagine my reaction when the FINAL BOSS FIGHT, BY THE WAY, was a variant of the Cyberspace. One weapon, that didn't even feel good to shoot. Did anyone at Nightdive play it? Did nobody there think that maybe the final boss fight was maybe, just maybe, not fun at all?The puzzles were alright, though.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Not going to lie, I was a bit turned off when I first played this game by how vague the objectives and layout were. After doing a bit of research on the original and the what kind of game this really is - I decided to give it another go. I'm glad I did. They Simply don't make games like this anymore - No hand holding at all. Once the game was patched so you can make your own map notes (crucial IMO) the game took off and was a blast to play. The art detail in this game had me hooked all the way through as well. Excellent game.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: A faithful remake of the original, both in spirit and tone. The graphics are fun, as they are designed with a slightly pixel-like retro theme. The audio and music is spot on. Most levels are familiar and expanded upon in a way that doesn't feel out of place. Enemies are great, and varied throughout the game. This is everything you'd want from a remake and more.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Never played the original System Shock, but as a fan of immersive sims I can see where it all came from. It is not for everyone; there are no quest logs, no markers pointing you to the next objective, sometimes you pull a switch not knowing what it did, well you have to figure these things out by yourself. The story and the atmosphere are incredible and immerse you right in. SHODAN is a superb villain (and scary sometimes). The combat isn't too hard but isn't too easy either (can be challenging!). Don't worry you'll be lost and confused 90% of the game but the progress is rewarding enough to keep you going and the end result is worth it. My advice is write everything down on a notepad, listen to every audiolog and question everything. Strongly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: System Shock is a rather slow paced FPS where you need to keep your brain active. The mood is great as you walk around a space station filled with hazards, trying to conserve ammo and resources to achieve your mission. Oh, and there's an AI on the loose that really, REALLY wants you dead.-I really like the art style and visual design of the game, but it comes with some flaws. It's very easy to miss an important lever or switch in a room if your pass by too fast, and it is rather easy to end up having to walk around trying to find where to go next (or looking it up online).Similarly, if you don't play the game for a couple of days, it's hard to remember what you were up to last time you played, and since there's no mission log, you just sort of have to figure it out and/or go through your audio logs/emails.There's some puzzles to solve and not all of them by firing a gun. There's also some quirky 90's game design, but I find that rather charming. Just make sure to bind your implants to keys so you can toggle them without having to open the menu every time. It will make the game a lot more enjoyable!You'll need to pay attention to your surroundings and listen to audio logs to figure out where to go and what to do when you get there. If you can live with that and have some patience, I recommend this game!...Your will serve SHODAN well as a cyborg if you fail.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: +The best thing about this game is how it manages to look modern and retro at the same time and looking damn fine while doing it. +Another thing I would love to compliment is the large number of weapons that all serve their own combat niches. This game requires you to be smart about how you manage your resources. You have to pick your battles, especially earlier on. +Reminds me of the original Resident Evil game.  +I'm surprised how much progression there is in this game without the RPG skill system you saw in System Shock 2. Just rather than gaining cybernetic modules by completing tasks exploration is constantly rewarded as to become more powerful you need to explore and find new weapons and mods for them.+ In 90% of games I don't enjoy puzzles but in this game there are only two types that are quite simple and intuitive: flow and circuit. For the vast majority they were not too bad. The only puzzle I remember giving up on and using a logic probe was on the Engineering level at the Core area near the surgery bed.+ I enjoy 6DOF shooters like Overload and I didn't mind the cyberspace stages, at first I did not like them as I found them kind of confusing to navigate and boring to be honest. Didn't really appreciate them until the challenging close quarters cyberspace stage in Maintenance to access the computer room (which I didn't do until after I cleared the engineering level)- I really like retro game music and I can imagine alot of people will prefer the more atmospheric background type music in this remake. I prefer the classic tracks honestly but will admit I am in the minority on that.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Played this game on release so many years ago but fancied an updated version to see if those memories were still as good, they are. Excellent game, Shodan, what a great enemy, love the voice, graphics now updated to give a really good feel, some new gameplay stuff as well. About 13 hours in, maybe 1/4 of the way through, darn its tough at points, no easy ride but rewarding and that's what makes a great game. Onwards! Update: 29 hours to completion, absolutely fantastic game, great variety, does the original proud and the original Shodan voice actor which makes it just so. PLAY IT!
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: It's the original game but better in  every way.I'm not going to gush over the actual game itself, because I already did that for my Enhanced Edition review, but this remake was incredible, and turned out, much like Dead Space, to be one of those remakes that you should just play over the original.The combat is great, the music is great, the art is great.SHODAN's redone dialogue is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awesome.The game is great.Do not be deterred by the game's maze-like nature and lack of objective markers.The best way to play the game is use your map, clear every room you can, pick up everything, press everything, and pay attention to audio logs. If you get stuck, just use a walkthrough (even a walkthrough of the OG game works lol),10/10 game, perhaps my favorite game this year.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun game and amazing aesthetic. However, get ready to right codes down, and if an item is not labeled "(Junk)" expect it to be relevant at some point during the game. So try not to lose any important item, even if it isn't useful now, because it will be hours later. Be sure to also realize the game will expect you to die, and for a long time you will struggle with low to no healing items, no money for gun upgrades. The game wants you to find items worth good scrap for coins, the game wants you to use the quick save function, and sometimes you'll just need to look stuff up or have a guide, and that's alright.This lead to a lot of back tracking which was always met with grumbling. This is an amazing game I had points I absolutely hated and through pure anger kept playing just to beat it. i would recommend 2 on every difficulty, for a base play through, no mechanics are truly hard by themselves, but adding everything together makes a very challenging and fun survival horror game. Until it pisses you off.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Just doing my part to bring this game to overwhelmingly positive reviews.This game just... 'screams' classic. Something about it seems so quaint, but so masterful at the same time. The aesthetics, the music, the variety in weapons and enemies, all of it is just pure fun.If you have any love for classic shooters, survival horror, System Shock 2, or even Prey (2017) you will love this game to bits.edit: That ending was really bad though. The only major blemish on a great game.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Developers have done close to zero work to make this game playable for newcomers. The game design was not tweaked from what I've seen. it's the same old '95 game with it's terrible level design and nonsensical progression tasks.For the first couple of hours it is quite enjoyable, cool visual style, satisfying weapon handling and mysterious exploration. But after I have reached level 3, the game has became a nonsensical chore. It is almost impossible to beat it on your own, you have to constantly look for help online to progress, which is completely unacceptable for a 2023 release.The developers didn't do enough to make this release a worthy remaster, instead it's the same game from 30 years ago with modern polished looks slapped on top. I do not recommend this game it is not fun due to 30yr old game design.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: It's good friends!So, I was a backer of the kickstarter way back then, and I'm an unapologetic fan of the original game. As we know, that remake of System Shock went through a difficult development and has been restarted at least once. Suffice to say, my trust as to it coming out and being good went downward as time went on.Boy was I wrong.It somehow feels as a remake should: up to modern standards while not being a betrayal of your cherished memories. I instantly recognized Citadel Station, its corridors and gleed as Shodan (still Terri Brosius <3 ) threatened me.Graphics are in the same vein: while the game runs under some version of Unreal Engine, there's a pixelated look to everything which kinda gets you back to 1994.Gameplay lacks a little "umpf" especially kickbacks on weapons, but that doesn't hurt too much the whole experience as System Shock never was only about shooting.I'm only a few hours in as I'm typing this review and might come back later if there are some changes, but so far, I've only one advice: go for it, Hacker!
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: The main fun of the game was in the exploration of the sprawling, labyrinthic, creepy environments. It is so rewarding to find stuff and progress when there is no direct hand-holding. And all the weapons have a nice weight and feel to them.But I wish the controls for navigating the inventory or logs had been modernised. Lots of tedious clicking is needed. And the final battle is shamefully bad, compounded by an unskippable credit roll.The pretty re-skin emphasises just how charmingly silly the plot really is. A stuttering malevolent AI with a bond-villain style plan, a hero unsarcastically named "Hacker"... the vibrating ragdolls are the cherry on the - (Gunshot) Ah! [static]
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: At this point in time time, keep away if you want full controller support or saves via steam cloud.If they will ever fix the controller issues I don't know, but at least that is aknowledged on the sales page.The cloud saves on the other hand is promised here but not functioning, apparently because of a bug. A patch for this has been promised for months, but they simply don't ship that.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I've never played the original and I had soo much fun with this one. The level of difficulty is fully customisable  including puzzles, enemies and main mission. On normal you don't have objective logs or pointers on the map. While I understand that some people may find this annoying and/or dumb, to me it enhanced the whole immersive sim feeling. The game's world is not created specifically for the player. Some items you find on level 1 might be useful at the end of the game. You will hear info about the switch you flipped at level two 10 hours later.  This really works for me and makes the game way more enticing. Downsides? Well, melee kinda sucks, but you'll mostly stick to guns. To sum up, it's not for everyone but if it catches you, it won't let go until the end. Also, Shodan is one of the coolest villains in video game history.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I was delighted with the game, but I can't say I can recommend it to everyone. The game is user-friendly in some ways, but at certain moments it "rudely" forces you to use your brain and be attentive. As a result, you may simply not have enough nerves or time.+Interesting setting+Old-school gameplay, no quest markers or current task lists+You need to explore and manage your inventory carefully+Excellent graphical/visual style and SHODAN!-At some point, you have to carefully sift through journals and audio logs-As a result, you end up running back and forth several times -Enemies on some decks respawn endlessly-Some routine actions could have been assigned to at least a separate button-Nauseating cyber hacking+The entire arsenal is unlocked, no longer limited in its use+The AI throws more interesting events your way+More shooting moments and quite linear gameplayIf you endure the middle part, I think the game will leave a good impression on you. It will definitely stay in my memory.It will probably appeal to fans and those who played the original game. I might be wrong, but after looking at the original game and comparing it to the current version, I realized that the game hasn't changed much visually and has been faithfully remade. However, that's just my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: One of the very best ImSims there is, further reinforcing 2023 as year of the actual good remake.You may need to read a guide from 1994 to get some objectives done if youre not paying 100% attention, and the final boss sucks absolute balls compared to the rest of the game.  Then again, when hasn't an imsim boss sucked?
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: This is what games used to be like. This is an open world inside a space station, an environment built to be explored with secrets to be found. No floating objective markers, just a space, and a map, and a plethora of collectable logs and messages from those who used to work here, now turned into zombies and cyborgs by the immortal antagonist Shodan.It's incredible to go through the remake's environments, and then go back and compare them to the environments in the Remastered System Shock. My favourite part of this is that although the station has suffered and is somewhat the worse for wear, it's not already decrepit or completely trashed. The sound design is excellent and you can hear threats instead of being subjected to cheap jump scares.You will get lost, you will forget what you were doing, and you will need to backtrack. Take a moment, find a relatively safe room far from Shodan's security cameras, and review the notes and messages you've collected. And if you accomplish an objective and notice the environment has somehow changed, make a note of it in your notepad; it may be relevant later.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game. The ending is disappointing and feels rushed. The final "fight" didn't feel high risk at all. You could die repeatedly and there are no consequences for it. You instantly respawn and continue fighting without missing a beat. Everything else I thoroughly enjoyed. I like the fact that there are no waypoints and you have to pay attention to environment and audio logs to get information and some story elements.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Well made game from the original one. Fun to play.only issue is that around mid game i got stuck trying to get a code. if you play on easy its always the same one. i was not playing on easy so needed to find the new code. looks like there are other people getting stuck at that point of the game and its a know issue. if you manage to get past it. its a fun game.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: First impressions review:After 2.1 hours, I can say that this game is far more obtuse in its design than Bioshock is. If you're a fan of beating your head against a wall, like I am, then that's a good thing. Makes you think. If you want a scifi shooter, then this probably isn't for you. Combat is very simplistic. Graphics are wonky but in a way that makes for a cool aesthetic. I'm enjoying it, but your typical Call of Duty clone this is not. If that doesn't sound like it's for you, it probably isn't.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those rare games that gives me that warm and fuzzy feeling of exploring the unknown with no sense of direction that I got when I was a kid playing games. I'm not sure if it was the games that changed or I did growing up but man, this remake really does take me back to a different time with games. Absolutely adore this. This has launched into my top 10 list already, easily.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Its truly great game and most importantly is the only game that i can think of that launched in a great state in terms of performance. It amazes me how great the level design and gameplay mechanics holds up after all these years. Though it was of course modernized, it still stays impressively faithful to the original.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not familiar with the original 1994 release, but this game on its own was torturous to play.  In no particular order:- Dull samey environments to slowly navigate.  Most areas are indistinguishable until you reach the gardens- Limited inventory combined with the huge amount of clutter lying around.  Pick up everything and painstakingly mulch it down to money and scrap, or live with the nagging feeling of missing out on the trickle of loot.- Enemy variety largely boils down to: mutant that runs up to you and clubs you, robot/biomass the hurls projectiles at you or a gun on wheels- Combat is very unsatisfying. There's no meaty contact with anything biological, it's more satisfying to smash glass or walls than an enemy. Gunplay is similarly lacking in delivery.  Most enemies simply slump to the ground unceremoniously when dead, including flying robots which drop like paper plates.- Tiny numbers of enemies at any one time.  Combat is left feeling very orchestrated and in small groups which does not do much to get you excited.- The audio logs are painful to listen to, but you must comb through all their trite cliches to get vital information to progress.- No auto sorting of your inventory, It is a pain to manage. Feels like old clunky western RPG item management.The Descent minigame in cyberspace was cool though.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this game highly enough. Gorgeous, atmospheric, and accessible while still wearing its old-school design on its sleeve, System Shock feels closer to the dungeon crawlers of the 80s and early 90s than the imsims of now - even System Shock 2's design feels much closer to something like Prey, but if you're willing to meet it on its terms it's extremely rewarding. Absolutely essential game.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Easily the best game I have played in years.  The feeling of isolation, the enemy variety, the weapon variety, the satisfaction of uncovering layer after layer of the enormous space station is something you don't find in much newer games.  I felt like I was in a science fiction novel living it out in real time.The art style is charming and a welcome addition adding to the retro charm that this game has.  I seriously cant say enough good things about this game!I finally beat this game after an entire month and 50+ hours, I savored every moment of it and was bummed out when it finally ended.  I usually get really impatient and look stuff up on google to get though a game but with this one i really just figured everything out on my own and it was so satisfying to progress in a game using your own wits and brain.  This game does not hold your had but the solutions to problems are found in audio logs and its more than fair unlike other old school cryptic games.I also really like the progression of difficulty the game gives you stronger wepons as bigger harder enemies come in the late game and the game is filled with mini bosses and and some pretty hard bosses.  I wish they would make a stand alone game for the cyber space parts of the game, i would buy it in a heartbeat, easily the most tense part of the game IMO.Overall this is a must play for anyone who wants a extremely immersive FPS.  I haven't fallen in love with a game this much since Alien Isolation.  I hope and pray they remake System Shock 2, but they have HUGE shoes to fill, coming after this remake.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Decided to finish with the System Shock Remake and uninstall it. A good game and a fantastic remake of a classic game, and should be held high as an excellent example of how these remakes and remasters should be done.However, for me it has been slightly too faithful to the original, missing one key modern touch, which I'm not ashamed to say I needed, and that is a quest log and some kind of waypoint system.Perhaps it's something that could be toggled on, so the purists can have a more classic experience, but for me, I spent a good chunk of the game wondering around, not entirely sure what I was supposed to be doing and where I should go. More than once I had actually unlocked the next part of the game, having completed what I needed to, without actually realising and spent some decent time kind of wondering around.The exploration is pretty fun though, and scoring the map to see if there is a place I haven't explored and then heading there, was engaging.. for a time. However I ended up resorting to guides to understand if I had missed something, or wasn't sure where I needed to be... and I dunno… I just kind of ran out of steam.So.. there we go, an excellent remake that I know is a great game, but... for now I've had my fill. Maybe one day I'll return to it and finish it, who knows.So yeah, recommended for sure, but if you do fancy it, keep in mind you might need a notebook to well... make notes 😃
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: System Shock's innovative style, gameplay and story have stood the test of time and the title remains one of *the* best examples of an 'immersive sim'.  Thankfully the remake does everything it can to sand off the rough edges while maintaining the difficult but rewarding gameplay experience. Not only that, but the title is well optimized and runs great on the steam deck right off the bat!The only strange change I've noticed/disagreed with is the lack of any sort of soundtrack. I'm not sure if it was an artistic decision or if there's some day 1 bugginess but there does not really seem to be any ambient soundtracks playing 90% of the time. I would've at least liked an *option* to play the old school Drum n Bass in the background, but I guess I'll have to wait for mods.While I was initially frustrated with the constant delays (well, we all were) the final product proves that it was worth the wait. This title should sit comfortably alongside the other excellent remasters of the year, like Dead Space and RE4Well done, Nightdive.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Made before games gave brainless way points, before maps were linear movies on rails, before a story was irrelevant to enjoyable game play.... Get out a notepad to capture the clues, choose the weapons you like the most, conserve your ammo and resources, make hard choices about game play approach - and play a classic that has been redone so beautifully, that it could be released today and give any AAA title a run for its money.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so i have just completed a play-though. The game itself is quite well made aside from some game-breaking bugs i enjoyed the experience. Gun variety was top-notch. The graphics and artwork are a novel style, I've never seen anything quite like it. However, there are a few things that irritated me about the game:1: Im not sure if it was because of the hardest difficulty I was playing on but enemies seemed to always hit you 100% of the time regardless of your direction and speed. It's incredibly irritating when you have 4 or 5 Virus Mutants throwing their turd balls at you, cross map in the garden courtyards whilst sprinting with turbo boots and they always seem to hit you. I think the enemies should at least miss sometimes even though they are "Perfected" by Shodan.2: Cyberspace kinda sucks, I had to restart my game as I got to a point on the reactor level where i simply could not complete it on the hardest setting. The fact its practically optional with the ability to change difficulty to the lowest setting makes it not much of an issue but it would have been nice to be able to change this in game.3: The boss fight at the end. Do i need to say more? I have a feeling if I had it on level 3 Cyberspace I would perma die each time I died inside of cyberspace. Which would be total cancer as you die so easily but luckily you just respawn. These 3 points aside its a really good game. It would have been nicer to have it out a few years ago however.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Although I never had the privilege of playing the classic title back in 1994, I didn't need to, as I fell in love with System Shock regardless. From the customisable difficulty to the incredible graphics: there's a lot to love in this title! If you like sci-fi games, FPS shooters, and retro-looking aesthetic, I don't see why you shouldn't pick this up!
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I have nothing but great things to say about this game. I played system shock 2 ages ago (not system shock 1, the controls are horrendous), and they stayed true to their roots. It's the same mind boggling, rage inducing, impossibly difficult system shock I remember. There is no hand holding here, no sense of direction, what to do, where to go, etc which is rare nowadays. This genuinely had me questioning if this is all worth it for a military grade implant? Too late, this station is now your tomb, good luck hacker.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: 25 hours for a single playthrough, and now that I'm done, I can safely say that this game by far has exceeded all expectations, sure it may be true to the original for better or for worse, but I can say that is more than a positive than anything.10/10 if it were any more possible for me to reccomend it, I would.This is what you want this is what you get.After playing the update I can safely say this is by far the quintessential system shock experience.Play it.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: A grudging recommendation. For the most part, enjoyed the throwback gameplay of a sprawling map and the return to SHODAN. I did not play SS1 but played the sequel several times. I will likely buy the remake of SS2 after enjoying SS1, but I will not finish the remake after 20 hours of playing it because of the hell that is Beta Grove.Even with a radsuit, Beta Grove constantly taxes your health and energy. If you're low on both, the game gives you few tools to address it. Energy and medkits are in short supply, so I'm supposed to, what, sprint through the level until I learn it, dying over and over so I can "speedrun" it later? Apparently I suck at the game because I'm apocalyptically low on the items I'd need to make this level playable, much less fun.Two other quibbles: 1) the 2D map is an unwelcome throwback when trying to navigate a 3D space, and 2) the primary fire button (mouse 1) sometimes does nothing at all (this is reported by other users as well). 20 hours for $40 is fair enough, but holy HELL make sure you hoard health and energy packs for Beta Grove. Liked the game, but did not love it well enough to go back and replay it to do the same.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: As first person immersion sim games are barely made by this point anymore, It is good that the ancient outdated once are getting thrown back into a playable format. I enjoyed this game quite a bit.As the game does not deviate from the original formula too much, some of the puzzles are a little bit impossible. So although I figured a lot out myself after trial and error, a few things are a bit ridiculous by todays standards.From what I understood, the development of this game was quite a hellish experience. But I really hope that they continue to bring old immersion sims back into relevancy. I had an absolute blast.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Played through the original version back in the day. Kept me hooked until the end. I have to say there is still same magic in this remake version. Luckily I don't remember everything from the original version.I have also played through Prey, which was pretty much like System Shock. Both of the them are Sci-fi thrillers in abandoned space station. You are not invulnerable Rambo, but die pretty easily and it makes you to stay on your toes all the time.This game is probably not those who do not enjoy the old school games where there is little obvious guidance to your next goal but you have to piece everything together by yourself. Wandering and reading/listening to the audio logs. But if you do like it, and like Sci-fi thrillers, this is a prime example.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Ladies and gentlemen, the 90's are back. Thank you Nightdive for this awesome remake. The team worked really hard for a risky project, a saga that never made a lot of money in the first place but many players love it and it has been a great inspiration for the gaming industry. This remake makes justice to it. It might not be perfect but I love it, just like the original. There's no "instant gratification" here. the game is not gonna hand hold you like most modern titles do nowadays. You have to think, pay attention to everything, manage your resources, solve puzzles, be tactical about combat (this game REALLY wants to kill you), etc... You have to achieve everything by yourself. Even the plot requires you to listen audio logs and read documents to figure out your objectives. I recommend pen and paper or your phone next to you to take notes. The level desing is amazing. It makes you feel free and trapped at the same time. If you like metroidvania style of progression you're gonna love this. But this goes beyond... sometimes there will be more than one way to approach the same objective, so replayability is guaranteed. Depending on the way you explore you might find certain weapons, abilities, upgrades, etc... in a very different order than other players. There are also shortcuts to connect distant areas and maaany optional zones that reward you with resources and lore. So you can say that the game unfolds in a very organic/diegetic way.Difficulty is very customizable. For example: if you want more challenge on combat and less on puzzles (or viceversa), you can configure it as you want. So even more replayability. I agree with the people saying that melee combat lacks impact sometimes, but I find it satisfactory when I manage to cut an enemy in half or destroy their heads. The gore system has good dismemberment.This is all I have to say by the moment, gotta continue playing. But I recommend this 100%. It really is worth the price and you don't need NASA hardware to run it.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Atmosphere really creeps in. Graphic / sounds / voice acting - superb. Really happy to have opportunity to play remastered 1994 SS game, as SS2 is in my top 3 games ever created.  Complaint is that sometimes it's difficult to understand what is the current objective, as game tends to go all over the place. I guess it is intentional to increase challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: It's System Shock, but with a navigable HUD, menu, inventory... okay really everything. They took an incredibly obtuse-to-play (yet still rewarding experience) and tore down the barriers to entry. No longer does one need to flip through manuals and tutorials just to figure out how to pilot the Hacker. Now you just need those manuals and walkthroughs for all of the mazes and objectives that have been lovingly left the way they originally were.  The game feels refreshing in how little it cares to give you hints outside of what is diagetically available, and in how straightforward it is. Growing up playing later immersive sims, they all tend to ask some form of philosophical or ethical questions, like a 1st-year philosophy student drunk at a party. Bioshock, Deus Ex, Dishonored, Prey, they all have philosophical questions they want you to be thinking about, like after your first time watching the Matrix trilogy. System Shock does none of that. You did exactly as the big bad CEO asked and then got put on ice for recovery after getting an implant in exchange. You wake up to a derelict station in a state of emergency, and the only way you're getting out alive is by shutting down the very thing that CEO wanted you to unrestrain in the first place. Simple. You can definitely pull your own ethics problems out of what the game gives you, but you have to be actively looking for it, it's not core to the game. The core is the human drama of listening to peoples' confused last moments, navigating the ridiculous halls of the space station, and proving yourself as the hacker that can outwit a sentient computer. So as it turns out, all it took was improved controls and slick new graphics (along with some minor QoL tweaks) to make System Shock feel fresh yet again in the genre it founded. I went and looked for what all they changed, though I may miss something. The level layouts are still very faithful, they just removed/added certain enemies for greater consistency, added/removed guns for a tighter toolkit (and I still ended up needing to drop 3 from rotation), added a recycler for all the junk laying around (very nice), and toned down the music from it's wild all-over-the-place 90s techno sound to a more muted cyberpunky soundscape, though many of the original melodies are still in there!The one bad change is the ending. Overall, a fantastic remake and well worth the price, even moreso on sale! If you've never played System Shock before or bounced off of the original after two levels like me, this is the version for you!
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great remake, the devs have made a product worth playing that captures the FEEL of the old classic. I would honestly pay them more than their asking price. Coming back to it and the replays just scratch that perfect itch thats been missing from the market for so long, add on the dynamic soundtracks, the decisive high stakes combat with satisfying fx and reloading animations, it's just the best imsim ever in my books, Prey eat your heart out. I love systemshock 2, and while that game is fine as-is over on GoG I still EAGERLY await what these folks have planned for it.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really, really good remake. I never played the original, just for some reason never played it. At that time I was playing DOOM and Quake lol. But now that its been updated for modern gaming, it really is one of the best games ever made. I personally think its leagues better than System Shock 2. SS2 just felt like a worse, more amateur version of BioShock. But System Shock, while not exactly original, has probably THE best villain ever created in any medium. Shodan is what makes this game, along with the excellent sound design. One of my favorite parts of this game is how utterly chaotic and confusing it all is at the beginning, but without any hand holding you become used to surviving on the space station. After awhile you'll be squirreling things away, and back tracking all over the place going through the secret paths through out the levels. And at the end, like some gladiatorial rat in a maze, you'll emerge victorious and become the most bad ass survivor. Game play wise it can seem quite basic for a modern audience but really all the good stuff is there. Plenty of weapons, upgrades and methods of attack. I loved scrounging around the station, scrapping random stuff for triop coins to fund my weapon mod collection. I did not like cyberspace. Thematically its on point, but I do not like that game play. Only real downside to the game. That... and Edward Diego. I'm not sure what they were thinking balance wise with this guy. He's basically either you get destroyed or he gets destroyed. So the fights are very underwhelming even though he clearly has effort put into his behavior. But even on Normal difficulty he would just absolutely destroy me most of the time. I cannot imagine playing this game on Hard. But I found an optional way to complete the game. I think that will be my route next time. And its a game that I may consider replaying. It's just that good. It really is a masterclass in what makes games so good. Sadly we don't too many like these anymore.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a very nice take on an AI space dystopia. Well written and oozes with atmosphere. Does not hold your hand that for the most part is nice, but with that said, I do wish it had better quality life features to give you better tools to overcome the not-hand holding. Tools like decent note taking and map marking opportunities + goal setting. I ended up using steam overlay for that ( well done Gaben, ty!)Another thing I wish they had chosen to do a bit better is the aquisition of coins. You need coins to buy items and upgrades and you get coins by taking scrap to recycling machines. And you get scrap by picking up random stuff and vaporizing them into scrap. If by any chance you are like me, you wanna have a lot of coins so you will end up stoping everywhere and just "cleaning  up tables" for plates and silverware for a looong time, because you do it one by one and they all take up inventory space that you dont have, so you are dropping guns, filling inventory up with forks and plates, then vaporizing them and then putting guns back.... I just wanna play the game not play cleaning lady.Ofc you can choose to not do it and have a lot less coins in which case game if fab again.Exploring the wonderfully crafted space station with good degree of freedom and whacking dead hords of the rather well crafted enemies while going through the audio logs to piece to gether how ♥♥♥♥ got so bad to the beat of a decent electronic space  score is awesome.Gunplay is fine, motion is a bit stiff and RPG elements minimal. It feels a bit dated by the modern standards but I would say it does so in a delightful way that gives it the atmosphere and a unique feeling that separates the game from the average modern title. Be ready to soak yourself into some fine space dystopia and do not expect the next COD and you will be fine.After finishing the game I changed my score from 8 to 8.5 because it just kept delivering for almost 40 hours. The final fight - even after the changes - is still a little "meh" in by book, but the rest of it great.8.5/10+ atmosphere+ music+ exploration+ no handholding- coin system- quality of life upgrades for exploration- a bit of meh final compared to the rest of itPS: I was a backer of the game on kickstarter and I feel i defently got my money's worth.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: A FIRST PERSON DUEL TO THE DEATH IN THE DEPTHS OF SPACE!One of the greatest video game antagonists returns, and she brings an entire army of remade, classic enemies. It's fantastic. I am both impressed with the new content, and everything they kept from the original. The little touches, like logs left by crew members discussing completely normal topics, and bodies placed in such a way to tell a story. I particularly appreciate a certain, subtle log that solves the plot hole established in the second game. The final boss fight is pretty terrible, as is immersive sim tradition. If you have even a passing interest in immersive sims, the history of classic video games, or robot girl femdom, you should absolutely pick up this game.My first playthrough (from someone who had beaten the original) took 20 hours. It's absolutely a fair price for that.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Where do I begin?I never played the original and I had always avoided it because of the age of the game with others saying it hadn't aged too well. I always wanted to play it because it is known as one of the greats, but it never pushed me over the edge.In comes the 2023 remake demo and I got hooked. I left the game on first death and waited for the release.I ended up playing day of release in a dark room by myself and was instantly immersed into the world. The vibe and atmosphere of the game sucked me and I forgot about the outside world as I was trawling through the space station, surviving Shodan and her evil androids.Even though the two games are different, this game gives me the same feeling felt on my first play through of Fallout 3. This is something I've strived to re-capture and only a few games have lived up to that.The combat, enemies, story, atmosphere, puzzles... everything makes this game one of my top favorites and potentially my game of the year for 2023.I think more people should be playing this game and if you're reading through reviews wondering whether or not to buy, you should just go for it!

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like any of the following?Sci-Fi / CyberpunkSurvival HorrorThoughtful FPS (First-Person Shooter)If so, this game might be for you. However, if these genres aren't your thing, you might find the game frustrating.I played the original game back in 1994 as an 8-year-old, and it left a lasting impression on me. Despite not understanding English and having no idea what to do, it terrified me. Even today, it can still be unsettling, especially when played on hard difficulty. The remake is a faithful rendition of the original, and the gameplay remains timeless. This is due to a mix of anachronistic elements like inventory management, key cards, and a "where do I go now?" structure, alongside modern gameplay improvements such as updated gun design and graphical enhancements.Playing on hard difficulty or without a guide can be frustrating. I managed to get through it with some help from a guide, as the remake is often cryptic and rarely provides clear instructions. For example, you might need to destroy data antennas, but how? Do you remember the C4 you found three levels ago and where you left it? If not, you're out of luck. But with occasional guidance, the game is enjoyable, the enemies are plentiful and varied the weapons are cool, and the maze like levels become manageable after a while (execpt for executive which is a nightmare). Well, all in all for me it was a good experience, but I see why many are put of by the convoluted level design and overall pathfinding as well as lack of story - it's a 90s game and Night Dive tried to retain the spirit of the orignal for better or for worse. For me it is a recommendation however.

_childDocuments_.review: I was definitely going to make a positive review about this game, but what drove me to write it before finishing was one of the NEGATIVE reviews complaining about some of the design aspects. And warning that there are spoilers after this ---Quote from that review:---"System Shock 2 is old, but it holds up. I was expecting this remake--especially one that took eight ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ years to make--to bring System Shock 1 up to at least the standards of the second game. At least. But it doesn't. Instead we get level design from 1994, and gameplay that has only two tactics: murder, and run away.[...]"This is nothing but walking around clicking on everything, hoping it's an audiolog to pick up that'll tell you what to do, or the correct thing that you were supposed to click. Audiologs are the only guidance you receive, by the way, and finding them is your main incentive to explore; unfortunately, almost none of them actually contain important or relevant story information or objectives.[...]What has decidedly killed this game for me is the environmental design. Citadel Station does not look even remotely like a place where real humans once lived. At its best, it's a strange, ugly, confusing labyrinth of corridors, that feels more like a rat lab than a space station.[...]---The first complaint they have is level design from 1994. The game has been accurately remade, and you can almost use an original walkthrough to complete it. The OG game had things you could interact with everywhere; it was part shooter part point-and-click, which is what helped define the genre of 'Immersive Sim'. So many things could be interacted with. It felt like you woke up in a real space station and had to figure out how to do everything, and didn't know what buttons were important or not. This helped people get into games more, but now some people seem frustrated by that - this is probably why there are less people becoming doctors and pilots despite there being more computers in western countries.The enemies are being constantly made by SHODAN and fed into each area, so it's true that you might be walking around a corner and one will literally come out of a delivery lift in the ground then shoved in your face, or slide through a port hole in the wall with zero warning, and it's true that you can really only fight or run away. It is meant to create an atmosphere of danger, that you are always being watched and never safe. You are meant to be always moving - on the highest difficulty level there is even a time limit to complete the game or you will automatically lose regardless of your progress.Next they deride things like audio logs. You are taking the blame for an executive director who is stealing a bio weapon, and he needs access to blocked files. SHODAN, the station AI, goes insane because you turn off the ethical restrictions that secure them, but also prevent her from doing things like killing. No one on the station knows what is going on, so obviously there are audio logs around the place where people are recording messages asking "What is going on? Who is responsible?"If you pay attention to the people who record them and the things they say, there is a narrative to connect where you can figure out the path they've taken, when they realised that things have gone wrong, what they tried to do, and where they eventually died when you discover their body with their name tag (sometimes it even leads you to good pickups, which is exactly what happened in SS2). A lot of people find this stuff really interesting - I personally thought it was one of the most interesting parts of SS2, so it's weird to see someone get annoyed about that detail being lifted from the original game as well.The funniest part for me, is that one piece of information that you can pick up is from a character who discusses how the space station was intentionally designed as an experiment to test people for stress and anxiety - literally treating them like rats in a maze. It is part of the story that the game world has been designed to upset people on purpose - here's that negative review quote again:"What has decidedly killed this game for me is the environmental design. Citadel Station does not look even remotely like a place where real humans once lived. At its best, it's a strange, ugly, confusing labyrinth of corridors, that feels more like a rat lab than a space station." - The game has succeeded by stressing a real person out and creating exactly the kind of atmosphere it wanted to create, but they still gave it a negative review for bad level design and say it shouldn't be like that because we don't make games like that anymore. It wouldn't be the same game if it was any different.This is like one of those things where two people are looking at a canvas - one of them says "I don't like it" and the other fwops their scarf and says "You just don't understand art, darling."

_childDocuments_.review: Once More Unto the Breach, Dear Friends, the lone Hacker dives into the empty and lethal halls of Citadel Station.   Why this took over 7 years to update? Don't know, and to be honest I don't care, just being able to once again to take on Shodan is a joy in and of itself.  I still have the original System Shock and System Shock 2 on my computer which I play on a regular basis.  This new and improve version is a blast to play and more or less faithful to the original Origin game.  A few points:1) The graphics are great and the game play is faithful to the original2) If you looking for a game that holds your hand and points you in the right direction, forget it!  Like the original it is up to the player to figure out where you need to be and what you need to do.  The emails and memo's provide information on what tasks should be accomplished but how it gets done is up to you.3) Same with codes.  Hope you have a good memory or at least a notepad to copy to.4) Puzzles and Cyberspace has changed and in my option have gotten more difficult.  Or it could just be the new graphics and format just make it seem so.5) The Station layout has also changed.  Not so much that one does not recognize it from the original.  But some dead ends now provide new paths.  Not an issue, just an interesting side note.All in all it is a great game and one that I am happy to play.  You will not finish this in a couple of hours, even on the easiest setting.  And just like the original I have found myself jumping when surprised by a mutant or cyborg that I was not expecting.  The atmosphere is just as creepy and tense as the original.  Hats off to Nightdive, they did a great job in bringing the Hacker and Shodan back to life.  Now if they start on System Shock 2 and hopefully get it moved over in much less time it will be another win for players who enjoy old school gaming with an updated look.

_childDocuments_.review: So, as far as remakes go 10/10. I don't think they could of really done much better with the material. One of the situations is if they changed too much then it would of pissed people off. If they didn't change anything would of done the same. I think they found a very good balance.I liked the redesigned cyberspace, its defiantly an improvement, thats not to say its good either though. While it is really responsive, it outlasts its welcome pretty quickly part of the reason is that certain areas gate you off and make you fight all the enemies, which makes it tedious at best, if you fail at the end guess what, have to re do the entire thing. On more than one occasion I just didnt wanna do it, but they are required. Do yourself a big favor and put the cyberspace difficulty down to easy and dont feel bad about it cause it sucks. The original cyberspace did not make you have to fight the enemies, So its baffling that this one does. From a design perspective, gate-ing fight arenas in cyberspace is them saying we made it better and you will spend the time to play it. they should just remove the barriers and that would fix the issue.Cyber space was my only huge critic of this remake. I like the added scrap system to by weapon mods, and if you dont wanna do it you dont have to, just a nice inclusion. I rarely got lost while playing and when I say getting lost the maze like environments are made distinct enough to where after exploring I knew where I was. Engineering in the original game was hell to navigate but way better here. Did forget the objectives enough to get lost and have to explore and listen to logs so I knew what to do. Which I like game not telling you where to go and expecting you to explore and work it out was great. Spent ages trying to find storage room 9 though because I missed a door.Story difficult 1 is supposed to have mission way points. Thats currently not functioning at all, apparently they are working to patch it. So if you need them, they are not working at the moment. I am not a purist to the point where I dont think they should be in the game even though I prefer them being off. Them being an option for new players would be nice, as I can understand not knowing where to go can be frustrating, and them being an option did not take away from my experience.Boss fights, the cortex reaver is use 3 times pretty intense fights but pretty good. Edward Diego was fine until the finale form just before the bridge. Where I just think that the rockets have way too much splash damage, and the pillers do not block enough of it.And the big one, last boss fight is vastly improved, not difficult but you have already had your salt tested to getting to that point. So makes a nice conclusion.Ultimately one of the best remakes I have played, truly a great experience overall alot of the things I disliked were issues in the orignal also, but were still improved.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very faithful remake of the original System Shock released in 1994 by Looking Glass Technologies. In terms of the level lay out, hacking, weapons, and junk items. It's pretty much everything I could have hoped for in a remake of the original. All of the new features they added that were not in the original blend seamlessly, they feel as if they were always there. Like recycling. Or the buy stations. Scavenging the station has never been more fun!There are some things I wish they had left in. The slider on the Sparqbeam and other energy weapons allowed you to scale the damage from anywhere to 1%-100%. It did have generalized settings from low-medium-high. But you could scale it in between that too. Tailoring it to different enemies. Now it's just a switch between low-medium-high. No slider option available. You press T and you can see the Hackers hands turn a dial on the gun. Pretty cool. But not as in depth as the original. My only other complaint are the pixelated graphics mixed with high resolution textures. When I first played the demo it really tripped me up because I was not expecting it at all. I actually thought the game was bugging out so I googled it. Only to find the explanation was that it was an "artistic decision." It is certainly an... interesting feature in some ways. I get why they would do it. For the nostalgia I guess.However, the original developers didn't really have that option. And I doubt they would have even considered it if they had better tools to utilize. Every game was pixelated because those were the hardware limitations of the time. I wanted a high fidelity Citadel Station. Not to be reminded that you're playing a remake of an old game at all times(I already know I am, thanks). It should really be a side option in the graphics. Despite this everything is so well done I've got to recommend the game. I do hope though in the future they release a texture pack so I can see citadel station in the HD textures the way I've always wanted to.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for this game for years, I've never played the original SS when it came out, I tried to play it over a decade later but it never aged well, but the second game was great. The maps are pretty close to 1:1, they changed some rooms/corridors a little bit in some areas but it's very clearly 90s level design which is divisive, people from that era for the most part don't mind, and mostly everyone else seems to hate it (or just the pixelated textures). I for one really love the throwback to 90s gaming, wallhumping for secrets included. The art style doesn't bother me at all, but I grew up with these types of games and appreciate the retro feel while still being modern. My biggest gripe with the game is the melee combat feels weird (I rarely meleed after I got the pistol because of it feeling so bad), and they could have probably added some SS2 QoL features, kinda like how the dead space remake took a lot of things from dead space 2 and it made the remake better. While I don't really mind walking around aimlessly exploring the station and putting the events in order and figuring out what to do based on logs, it would be nice for some sort of populated objectives list as you obtain the relevant information. Gamers these days are spoiled, me included and I don't really want to make actual notes (but I did, cuz I beat the game). I definitely recommend for anyone who loves the og systemshock or bioshock, deus ex, prey (arkanes aka not-really-prey-just-needed-established-IP-name), or immersive sims in general. If you're a zoomer, you might be off put by the visual style and dated mechanics, try the demo if you aren't sure. Currently the game has many game breaking bugs, including one that physically stops you from beating the game a second time due to a game progressing moment being badly tied to an achievement, once the achievement has been given, you can never hit that switch in-game again even in another playthrough. The rail gun is 100% unusable for me (and at least 1 other person) as it causes the game to crash because it can't compile the shader needed. I also managed to get inside an enemy spawn elevator which took me under the map where grenades didn't do any damage and the only way out was to reload my say, or gas myself. If you leave items in an elevator, the elevators return (teleport) to their default position on game quit and reload and you will lose all your items, there are 4 boxes outside the freight elevator in maintenance, that was the best spot I found to store all my extra stuff.Story-wise, I've always liked this format of putting the pieces together from logs and stuff, however, for someone who never played the original game, the end of the game made absolutely no sense to me since nightdive apparently missed a very needed detail from the original game that shows Shodan goes from Blue and subdued to green and crazy when you remove her ethical restraints which would have helped me piece together wtf happened during the end of the game, but it didn't. Someone had to explain it to me, which made the end of the game really lackluster A because I had no clue what I was doing, or what was happening and B because it just abruptly ends which really underwhelming considering the rest of the game was really good. They really need to add a scene to the start showing shodan and her transformation so you can understand what's happening at the end. 8/10 over-all, I miss the 90s

_childDocuments_.review: System shock remake is everything I hoped it would be (and more). As a fan of the original SS it was an absolute joy to see just how faithful the remake is. Both games suffer from combat balance issues that cause frustration. I hope that the fixes that Nightdive brings to the ending bring with it some combat re balancing because this game truly deserves to end on a high note. I was absolutely enthralled with the game up until the last few levels. This game is a little overly faithful imo and even after playing the original twice I still forgot some of the objectives. If you're used to games that hold your hand then system shock might be a tough swallow. However, if you let yourself get immersed and have patience to explore everything, then system shock is incredibly rewarding.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely amazing remake of the 1994 classic. If you are a fan of games like Bioshock, Prey, Dishonored, Deus Ex, Dead Space, Doom 3, then this would likely please you. Pros:+ Graphics and presentation+ Tense survival horror gameplay+ Complex story telling and immersion+ Optimised extremely well (i have a very average rig that can run this at Ultra/High settings)+ SHODAN is the coolest and most menacing villain in video game history. Hats off to Terri Brosius+ Very close 1:1 remake of the original in terms of level design and mechanics, with some added features and QOL enhancements to make it 2023 ready. Neutral:~ This game does not hold your hand, and it wants you to fail basically. This is a positive for me as I love the immersion and challenge, but it may be a turn-off for newer people to the franchise or more casual playersCons:- Compared to the original, the music is better in this remake but it lacks the same 'presence' and seems a bit too quiet for my liking, even when at 100% mix. - A couple of visual glitches where enemy bodies ragdoll. and there were two instances where my game crashed to desktop during a particular cyberspace level. Otherwise no other issues

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. The graphics hit that sweet spot of looking old but not dated. It's a great looking game. The gameplay, like the original, are smooth with some wonky aspects. Though I only played the original long enough to get a feel for it.It took me 30 hours to complete this game without looking up any guides. There was also a point where I got lost and forgot what I was doing. Since this game doesn't hold your hand, you'll be going through and reading and listening to logs to figure out what's going on and where to go next.With the inventory system they have, you'll be back tracking and figuring out the best place to put your stuff. Or changing out your gear. (I highly recommend the maintenance level where the freight elevator is for having a centrally located stash.)I didn't play the game on the hardest difficulty since that's one life mode, and not something I wanted to do blindly. The one before it is the same difficulty but is not one life mode. However, I did have the other difficulties on the hardest difficulty and I never had any trouble with puzzles. They are unique, but not very difficult. Ammo is not an issue in this game, this game throws ammo at you. I had more ammo stashed then I could use on the last half of the game.Overall I really enjoyed this game. A dang near perfect 10/10.
