_childDocuments_.review: I got gifted this by my significant other a day after it's release.I have beaten the original in 7 hours.and system shock two in 8I'm not a professional reviewer so this is going to be messy but you're getting the whole hog.I'm gonna mention an enemy type encountered late game down the line as well as a bug in an endgame section so minor? spoiler? not really? doesn't tell you story or anything important?The remake took me 14-15 hours not counting 1.6 hours-2 hours afk time for stuff like bathroom breaks and food.Played with 2/2/1/3 (2 enemies, 2 mission, 1 cyber, 3 puzzle)I'll put the TL:DR here: It's good. get it, it's faithful while also being it's own thing. Maps are near one to one.-----------God where to I even begin with this? This thing is a masterpiece, the visuals, the enemy design, sound effects, all of it is just fantastic, it feels phenomenal.The weaponry is fantastic, some reworks here and there but you're always gonna find use out of your preferred tool, some weapons were changed in positives, but a lot were removed and some were very negatively impacted by the remake like the magpulse. The Scorpion remains a consistent favourite, spraying 20+ magazines of teflon into late game enemies as a reward for early game conservation is incredibly fun.Very rarely did I ever get lost. My memory from the original during my playtime literally carried me all the way to executive, where changes in design and layout threw me around a bit due to the ability to do more with the areas for a more consistent flow, but even then it's incredibly one to one with a lot of things. However on the downside this can lead to a kind of uncanny valley effect where, you recognise the area but not enough due to the shift to full modern 3D (yes I know the original game's engine was true 3D)Cyberspace is where the game starts to fall apart, with being on the Autistic Spectrum I find myself struggling with doing the cyberspace sections for long due to the hell of a mental drain it puts on you. while far more visible you're drowning in pulsing colours which while not as confusing, they are incredibly off-putting to deal with. It also likes to throw you into tunnels filled with mines which you have very little control of your movement in(and I mean FILLED). It's also incredibly tedious, rather than quick snappy jaunts you're spending a good 20-30 minutes combing through cyberspace to do something as simple as open a damn door. Genuinely the only setting I'll ever set to one.The Soundscape while good, has flaws of it's own, enemy and weapon sounds are incredible as is the ambience provided to you on the different decks of citadel, You can very clearly listen in and know what you're being shot at with and what might be around the corner (though this isn't always the case between the security 2 and security 3 robots, as they're all but silent when not walking or firing. And yes, they uncut the security 3 robots from the original, this is the pre-mentioned spoiler, go about your day.) However Most of the game is just that, Ambient noise, there's very little in the way of music.  Music only really kicks in when combat starts and leaves very quickly after, there is nothing as memorable as the original game's ost and I believe this harms it a lot in the end.I would touch on enemy design but I feel like that's revealing too much as there's a lot of drastic changes and upgrades to the products of shodan's rogue machinations (they got Terri back by the way she's fantastic as always).I will also touch on the fact there are some bugs with the game currently however.Most notably security 2 robots have a chance to bug out and continuously play their attack sound even after death, the only way I've found to fix this is reloading a save.The second bug is that there are tubes on the bridge that if shot enough will rupture. they're supposed to spill fluid everywhere and when they do this you're looking at an INCREDIBLE amount of FPS drop and stuttering, be careful where you're shooting and what your health is as you don't want to die due to an FPS and loss of control.Get it if you can, it's remarkable cheap compared to most remakes, it's consistent with what it set out to do and remains entirely respectful to it's source material while allowing you to thrive, genuinely, walkthroughs for the OG game can prove useful throughout most of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Although the game never holds your hand in guiding you throughout it, the way objectives and items are located and set up is done in such a good way that it simply just works. The combat was thrilling and fun, the atmosphere is immersive and absolutely terrifying at times. For the first 1-2 hours of my playthrough, I remember being scared ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ just running into a group of enemies.The puzzles are well done, although some of them weren't clear at first on what you were supposed to do. When you do figure them out, they are solid and fun to solve.Originally, some years ago, I tried to play through the original version released back in 1994, but I never really managed to play it much due to it simply being "too old" for me, sadly. However, the remake is definitely on point. The graphics are top-notch and mix realism with a retro pixel art style. The animations are on point, and you can easily tell a lot of love was poured into this entire game.But man... the OST was absolutely fantastic. There were times where I was running around the Citadel Station confused for minutes at a time, but the music in the background made me almost want to spend more time just standing and listening.The only complaints I have with the game are quite nitpicky. However, if I had to list them, I would say that the boss fights are kind of underwhelming, but still very well done in terms of what the game is going for. Even though I knew that the last boss fight would be "the last boss" in the game, the way it ended kind of just left me saying "Oh... Wait what?" Perhaps it's because I didn't understand the ending, but the way the game concluded was still really solid.Inventory management was sometimes absolutely annoying. This is mainly because I like to hoard absolutely everything in games like these, but at times I thought it was kind of annoying. I want to remind you that this is just my personal issue with the game. I know a lot of people like inventory management, I just don't.But definitely, without a doubt, the biggest complaint was the hacking mini-games. Even though they were extremely fun and engaging at first, when playing them for the fifth time, I remember audibly groaning when I found one I had to play and finish. They are essential for the advancement of the story, which is pretty annoying. By the halfway point of the game, I found them to be just a bother to complete and really repetitive. This is due to the gameplay of the mini-games never really changing. The only thing that changes is new enemies showing up, but even then, they aren't that distinct from other enemies.In terms of replayability... It's definitely going to be some years at least, personally, for me to replay the entire thing again. Although next time I decide to play through the game, it will be much faster as I know where to go off the bat. The game is still long. The time it took for me to complete System Shock along with most objectives was 22 hours, which is definitely not something I am complaining about as I got plenty of game time for the price I paid.In general, if you enjoy games that can be brutally hard at times and reward you with satisfaction upon completing challenging sequences and challenges, System Shock is definitely for you. If you aren't the biggest fan of games actively hating you and literally playing against you at times, then I wouldn't recommend the game.

_childDocuments_.review: The System Shock remake is extremely good. Probably the best remake of a video game that I've ever seen. _childDocuments_.review: System Shock’s Remake wasn’t for me.With that said, after having played through the campaign, defeated every boss, hacked through most doors, and discovered a handful of secrets, I’d still recommend this game exactly because it’s not for me.When I backed this game in 2015, I knew exactly what I was backing – an old game I read about in one of my brother’s video game magazines, a game that looked like a rather vibrant 8-bit vomit that posed as a dystopian horror game, but didn’t look the part. It was as if Doom had an illegitimate child with Excel.…And yet, I was fascinated by it. The ideas, the aesthetic, the atmosphere. Something about it felt… like it belonged (and it did belong in the 90s). That’s where we start off with the Remake. After going through a rather lackluster intro that is lacking in both direction, sound design, and especially the score, we start our game as a lowly hacker, waking up in the hauntingly quiet corridors of a space station orbiting Jupiter.Let’s begin by stating everything that is great about this game:1.	The visuals – System Shock Remake took a design approach that embraces the pixel art of the original while improving models, animations, and sound design to make it more approachable – the mix between the pixelated button illuminating the corridors with colorful lights is nothing less than artistic, and definitely serves as a wonderful throwback.2.	The Atmosphere – System Shock isn’t really a horror game. There are no jumpscares, there are no creepy segments, gruesome torture porn, bone chilling score, or goosebumps-inducing sections – the game as I experienced it, is more of a cyberpunk adventure in a dystopian future where ethics, regardless of CPU controlled or otherwise, are optional. The sound design is also a highlight when it comes to the synthesized speech of the cyborgs and Shodan herself. Haunting.3.	The Polish - Nie mówię o języku polskim, sorry, what I mean by this is that the developers knew exactly what to keep and what to throw away. The game is a perfect representation of the original game, but without the awkwardness of some of the controls, and with trimmed sections that could cause big headaches. In addition, while some visual elements are kept mostly as is, some were improved to allow for a less puzzling experience – for example, certain areas got a makeover that grants them a better feel visually, Enemies are more distinct, and you can definitely tell one section of the station from another. It’s just more eye-pleasing that way… Which brings me to the next part: The bad.System Shock, while having been in development for about 8 years, isn’t perfect. Since this game brings elements from a rather outdated game, it feels less like an “Immersive Sim”, and more like a first-person Metroidvania. To be fair, when I look at 2017’s Prey, this is exactly what I expected from System Shock – an intense survival shooter where you slowly evolve to counter what the game throws at you. Instead, we get plenty of inconvenient backtracking, vague clues that require you to browse through endless logs, and many punishing elements that won’t mesh with the average player… and yes, that would be me.Just as I would look at a game like Pizza Tower and say “This looks awesome, I’m never gonna touch it, ever”, this is the same notion I hold for System Shock, a game that many times while playing it I kept asking myself if I should really bother. As a shooter, it’s very lacking, somehow trying to combine tactical elements with corner leaning, and fast-paced, claustrophobic boss environments – it’s like they could settle on whether System Shock should be more like Resident Evil or a Boomer Shooter. As an RPG, there are no stats or builds, and inventory space is a constant worry that verges on being a chore. As for the cyber-sections – they’re visually unique and interesting, but I wasn’t ever a fan of games like Descent, and in general they felt more like an “ugh-section” than anything else. As a horror game… well, I already discussed that.In addition, it seems like the sound design fails to meet expectations. While I did appreciate certain details, be it the mechanical sounds of a closing door, nostalgic button presses, or the clicks of a cocking gun, there aren't as many audio elements communicating information to the player. For example, beeps notifying you of a weapon being ready to fire again when it comes to the rail launcher, or different ricochet sounds for when you get hit while having a shield on... It may be there, but it wasn't very noticeable. On top of that, some sounds appear to be missing completely - the intro loses a bit of its sting when most of it is alarmingly quiet. Certain plot important moments are also appallingly relaxed as opposed to the feeling they're supposed to convey - sometimes an explosion won't play a sound. Sometimes a certain reverb is missing, echoes... it's the small things that make the sounds design feel like that one Mummy remaster trailer accidentally uploaded to YouTube with missing sounds.So why recommend it? Why would I give a thumbs up to a game which I know I didn’t fully enjoy?Because it’s a classic, in more than one way. The people who worked on this game knew exactly what they were going for, and a different person who wanted to preserve that experience would have an absolute blast. A person who’d like to challenge themselves, achievers, people who love going through logs… This game’s for you.I therefore bestow this game with the highest honor I can think of – “It’s not for me, please buy it”.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start off by saying I don't think this is a bad game. There are a lot of things I really liked such as the 4 different difficulty sliders (including plot difficulty!), nailing the perfect amount of inventory management, and awesome space visuals. Also, aside from some occasional ragdoll physics clipping I don't think I saw any bugs in my 20 hours playing, and only crashed once.On the other hand, there are definitely things I wasn't a huge fan of. Primarily, this entire game is made up of cubes. I understand that they're trying to remain somewhat faithful to the 1994 graphics of the original game but it almost feels cartoony at some places where the walls are a repeated square texture down a hallway. And then you go into cyberspace and you're suddenly you're in a hellscape where there is no up or down, the walls the floor and the ceiling are all cubes, you're shooting half-cubes at enemies that are also made of cubes, and it's just way too much. Half this game feels like I'm walking on the surface of a rubiks cube and the other half is inside the cube itself.I could highlight other things that I disliked such as a soundtrack that felt like it had 3 songs or a very minimalist plot that, while faithful to the original, rarely features and doesn't really add anything of substance to the game. However, I think the biggest reason why I wouldn't recommend this game is simply because System Shock 2 is just so great, and if you slap on a few graphics mods it just completely blows this game out of the water. I don't think there is really any scenario where I would recommend someone spend $40 on this remake when you can wait for a sale to pay $2.50 for a better game. Do yourself a favor and just pick up SS2, and if you really enjoy it maybe consider coming back to this one afterwards.

_childDocuments_.review: I received a copy of the original System Shock along with Bioforge and Wing Commander III in the Origin Pak back in the nineties, for winning a limbo contest at my now ex-girlfriend's birthday party.  The games could have been terrible and I would still have felt great about my achievement.That said, as much as I loved Mark Hamill's performance and being forewarned of my disappointment should I come into possession of a fork, I never finished Wing Commander III nor Bioforge, but you better believe I was fully immersed in System Shock.  The game was choppy and slow on my 486, but I completed it all the same.  No guides, no internet, just me, my wits, and a clunky but workable UI that let me play PONG in the bottom corner.This was over twenty years ago, before developers discovered the novelty of mouse aim.  I barely remembered anything about the game except that no other game had been able to recapture the same feeling since, not even the later much anticipated System Shock 2.  When the remake was announced, I was thrilled that my faulty memory would allow me to enjoy it as if it were the first time all over again.After having beaten it a second time, my only complaint is that I was not able to play PONG in the bottom corner.  Aside from that, I got the same rush of accomplishment and have renewed anticipation for System Shock 2, even already knowing full well how it turned out.I took the liberty of watching some Twitch zoomers play and was heart-warmed to discover they were losing track of time enjoying themselves despite the lack of waypoints telling them where to go next.  This remake truly bridges generations, and I hope to see future remakes take a similar approach.

_childDocuments_.review: This definitely is System Shock. It's the original to the core, with a new coat of paint and some quality of life improvements. People expecting a game that behaves like a more modern game will either have to adapt or be disappointed. This doesn't have a leveling system like most other more recent games of this type. Hell, you barely end up with upgrades that give you "avatar strength." You're given tools, how well you use them is the biggest key to your survival in game. Another thing this game lacks if frequent autosaving. It saves at the beginning of a floor. Outside of that, it's up to you. And floors aren't short either. I completely explored the first, and am about halfway through exploring the second, and it's taken nearly 5 hours. The entire way each floor is designed feels tailored from the ground up to confuse or disorient you. Textures are bright and colorful, the entire layout is a labyrinth, doors lead to more doors, and SHODAN sometimes will just pop some monsters out of a floor compartment to ♥♥♥♥ with you. Overall, exactly what I wanted, and I recommend this for fans of the original, or people who want a difficult challenge and might be put off by the original's aged appearance.

_childDocuments_.review: Always assumed System Shock would be one of those forgotten classics that I never would get a chance to play, even when I heard there was a remake I thought that there would be too many legacy/design issues to make it anything more than an interesting curiosity for modern audiences.Boy, was I wrong.Turns out this game runs shoulder-to-shoulder with the best of them, and even outstrips a lot of modern games in some ways.I feel like modern incarnations of this game would find themselves leaning more heavily into either the horror/survival side, or the FPS side, and the even blend this game offers is honestly refreshing. I have to consider when to use health items, but don't have to worry about messing up my save by using too many. Enemies can sometimes spawn behind me in areas I've cleared, but only if I haven't done my job properly - as you go it is possible to know fairly safely that the ground you've covered is clear, which was a massive draw to me. The writing is absolutely top-notch, it has some of that earnestness in its voice that you might not get today - its written in a world where they're not afraid too much of rehashing tropes. Sometimes that means you come across a hokey or over-done line here and there, but its worth it for the overall feeling.I LOVE the visual style - a beautiful approach that is still built out of these pixelated textures that look great. The maps, info logs, inventory systems and everything are all great and add a lot to the experience.There are some things to be aware of going in:- Audio Logs are important!! Listen to them all, keep an ear out for clues on what to do. You may find yourself lost if you don't pay attention, so do keep that in mind.- PUZZLES!! The puzzles in this game are actually really fun, but they have some issues. In both cases there are UI elements that are easy to overlook, and there are no in-game tutorials. Also the puzzles are randomized by playthrough so its not easy to just pull up an answer online. My advice is if you get stuck pull up a guide and look carefully for what you might be missing. On two different occasions I was sure my puzzles were bugged, but it just turned out to be small details that I hadn't fully grasped.

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely to experience where games like Deus Ex, Prey 2017, Bioshock and Dishonored originated from. As the player you crawl through a space station that has been taken over by a malevolent force, finding many secrets and power ups to help you along the way if you pay enough attention. The station is a nice big maze consisting of many levels, corridors and rooms for you to explore. They level layout is probably not the most realistic, but it is a lot of fun to learn the shortcuts and get to know the lay of the land. The game is a bit like Metroid in that respect. The environmental storytelling is also quite nice, and probably was ahead of it's time back when this came out (less than one year after the original DOOM!). The game is full of surprises and death traps to keep things interesting throughout the length of the game. If you played Prey 2017 you'll find this quite similar, although System Shock of course is the OG and formed the inspiration for all these types of games back in 1994. I especially enjoyed the lack of handholding and objective signposting, letting me discover my own path and forcing me to pay attention to the story and my environment. There is one instance in the game where an object that you normally do not have to pick up becomes critical to progress the game, and there the game really does not provide enough information in my opinion. That's my only gripe with the game. But apart of that I thoroughly enjoyed my systematic dismantling of SHODAN's resources throughout the space station. I did not play PC games until 1996 and I'm a big fan of immersive sims, so I'm very happy Nightdive went through the trouble of remaking this classic.The graphics and sound are excellent, and the game plays like a modern video game that can be enjoyed by anyone who can enjoy a game that does not signpost the next objective for you and force you to explore using your own senses. The game is also very immersive because of this, really making your feel like you are sifting through this massive abandoned space station by yourself. Piecing together audio logs and other clues to find out what the heck happened to all the people on the station. You're up against a much stronger enemy that keeps taunting you and throw up roadblocks. But slowly and surely you become stronger, more ready & able to reach the upper levels and face up against SHODAN. I would recommend not using any walkthroughs and to save a lot, and enjoy this remake of a timeless Looking Glass Studios classic for yourself!! A remake of 2 would be appreciated, and I can't wait for part 3. We need more immersive sims, so thank you Nightdive! <3

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played the original System Shock so I had no idea what to expect from it other than knowing it inspired games like Bioshock, Deus Ex, and Prey. I was pleasently surprised with this game, exploring Citadel Station was a lot of fun but at the same time very tense, as the combat is simple but unforgiving.The story very much follows a "show, don't tell" approach, there is no in-game menu where the next objective is told, instead you figure it out from in-game dialogue, audio logs, or just stumbling upon the next step as you explore. Despite this, I never felt lost or stuck as there as always another path to explore.The graphics look fantastic, all textures have a slight pixelated look which is only apparent once you get close, but it's a great homage to the games roots.If you're a fan of other immersive sims you're doing your a huge disservice if you don't give this a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I had really high hopes for this game. I'm happy to say that it has not only met, but exceeded my expectations.  The guns are interesting, the hacking puzzles and minigames are not invasive and don't feel like they interrupt the game, the enemies have great design, and SHODAN is absolutely terrifying.  12/10
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT #2: Just finished a 3-3-3-3 run. I was disappointed to see that, even with the Cyberspace difficulty set to the max, you STILL cannot die in the 'final battle'. While I did enjoy the pressure that comes with a time constraint, somehow, the ending was even worse at the hardest difficulty. I really feel like the 'final battle' sequence needs to be revisited in a future update.EDIT: Just finished the game -- I still think that this is an excellent game, but the 'final boss'/ending sequence....left much to be desired. I think I slightly prefer the 1994 ending sequence more.This game is phenomenal. I was too young and dumb to fully appreciate the OG version of this game (I knew it was good, but I was too engrossed with Doom at the time); however, I feel like this remake really brings it home for the 'new' generation to experience. I have been enjoying every minute of this game so far.There's definitely a hint of 'old-school design' in this game. Specifically, the objectives aren't necessarily spelled out for you -- you have to pay attention to the audio-logs to figure out what to do. Though this sounds tedious, it really does a lot for immersion (and I'm into the whole 'don't treat the player like a complete idiot' approach). On that note, I did enjoy the puzzles in this game as well!Combat is fun, but pretty simple. I've heard a lot of my friends complain about it being too difficult, but all it usually boils down to is baiting the pre-fire and countering (for the ranged fools) and the simple kite-and-slap (for the melee chumps.)There are still some QoL issues present (especially in the 'item management' department), but the pros far outweigh the cons here.Pick this one ASAP, if you're into atmospheric horror with a cyberpunk-twist. The core-quality of this game still exceeds many modern games: a testament to how far ahead of the curve this game was in 1994.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Very faithful remaster in lots of ways and must have taken several years to develop.However:A. There's some definite bugs that could do with an update.B. The combat is clunky and difficult but not in a good way.C. I am 80% of the way through the game and can't be bothered to finish it, because now I've found that I need go and back track through all of the levels just to find out codes that will open 1 door. There won't be any combat or tasks to complete, just walking around for a few hours to find out these codes.Maybe this is true to the original but it just doesn't end up being that fun.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following the System Shock remake for around two and a half years now, which meant I personally didn't experience a lot of the pains regarding the delayed release. I've been a big fan of system shock for a lot longer, however, having first played System Shock 2 years ago as a child. I'm also a massive Imsim fan, having played the vast majority of the genre's greats to completion. This game is one of those greats. - Amazingly faithful to the original 1994 classic. Featuring an almost 1:1 recreation of the original DOS game's maze-like levels, this remake brings the pixelated halls of Citadel Station to life with all-new graphics delivered by the Unreal Engine. Gameplay is also faithfully recreated, with many QoL updates, changes, and additions that make this remake the definitive way to play System Shock. - Smooth and polished PC port, with few bugs, near-flawless performance on even low-end hardware, and a shockingly small file size. - Strong enemy designs, great environmental art, and fantastic animation work. - Grenades have an awful throwing range, and drop way too much when thrown. They also bounce a lot. This can easily result in accidental suicide deaths when throwing grenades. - The new soundtrack is OK, but the original OST was far superior. This one feels way too ambient, and not punchy enough.- A good deal of weapon FX are rather lackluster, especially for the Laser Rapier and Minipistol. The Laser Rapier is especially bad, since it's the final tier melee weapon, and yet it has little feedback in terms of impact effects and hit sounds. - Some rather lengthy animations would have been better as first-use only animations when you pick up or use an item for the first time. The stimulant patches are especially annoying, since you will have to go through the same application animation every time you want to apply a healing patch or another stimulant. While SSR is not a game for everyone, it is a solid remake of the original game, which faithfully updates and enhances the world of Citadel Station for first-time players, while also delivering numerous welcome improvements to the story, worldbuilding, and gameplay. Highly recommended to immersive sim fans, and well-worth the price of admission. 9.5/10, one of the best games I've ever played, my nominee for 2023 Steam GOTY
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: It took a while for it to release. That may have upset some people, especially the initial backers who were maybe expecting a different kind of game. That's unfortunate. I'm not here to convince any of those people. I will say that from a technical aspect, the game is polished AF, has not crashed or really bugged out on me except once, where an elevator didn't work. a save and reload solved it. Some reported the usual unreal 4 caching stutter. I only noticed it during level loads, which are "seemless" in that there is no loading screen.   What this game is, sometimes to a fault, is a faithful redesign of the initial game. It takes advantage of a lot of modern game design without compromising what made the original great, which is the claustrophobic feeling of exploring a space station come to life where everything is trying to kill you. As such the maps are the same maze like levels with increased fidelity where possible and slight tweaks and rearrangements where necessary. Same thing can be said for the weapon and items, and enemies. Most of these return, with some new inclusions and exclusions and modifications where it makes sense. The black mesa standalone game is the perfect comparison. Everything feels familiar, but also fresh. Finally, the hand holding (there is none) and difficulty aspect mirror that of the original title for the most part. The difficulty sliders themselves make for a varied and customized experience that can appeal to many kinds of people.I did mention "to a fault". Expect lots of backtracking, some confusing design choices like not having a total ammo count easily visible, not being able to vaporize all scrap items at once. The latter is quite annoying as this mechanic (unique to this itteration) is essential for purchasing weapon upgrades (also unique to this itteration). The FPS aspect was not the original's strong suit, with enemies feeling dumb and not really that varied aside from how beefy or armored they were. Things are a bit better this time around, but the enemy ai still leaves something to be desired. If you loved the original system shock, I highly recommend this game because it is essentially that game if todays technology were available in 1994.If you're new to this, this is an opportunity to experience a remake of one of the first examples of an immersive sim, with all the gameplay philosophy, and none of the dated graphics.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: The remake is at best okay. Some of the effects are way to bright or simply annoying. The mixture of "modern" clean graphics and pixelated ones is in my opinion bad. No ambient music, would really loved an "original soundtrack" option. Melee Combat feels awful with no real impact and lets not forget the horrible headbobbing and why on earth is there no option to disable that. Cyberspace is awful & boring. The final "fight" against Shodan is boring as hell, whoever prefers this over the original is straight up crazy and the end sequence in comparison to the original is just confusing. Got Shodan Deleted? Is she alive? Did the hacker revert her back before he hacked her? In the Original you know that she got deleted since it clearly states "System Purged" but here? And then you cant even skip the damn credits and have to sit through them. Mac & Linux version which were promised since the Stretch goal on Kickstarter got reached are nowhere to be found. But thats nothing new with Nightdive they also promised Mac & Linux versions for System Shock Enhanced Edition & Blood Fresh Supply and they were not delivered either. No FSR & XeSS option only DLSS since obviously everyone owns an Nvidia card right? If you like the remake good for you. But in my opinion you are better of with the Original/Enhanced Edition. By far better than this .TLDR: If you loved the Demo buy it at full price. Otherwise either play the Original & Superior version or get it on a deep sale.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: An outstanding remake.It catches the atmosphere and spirit of the original while modernizing the graphics and smoothing out the UI.Be warned though, they also caught the design spirit of the original. System Shock is, by design a very gloomy experience, a run through mazelike enviroments without objective markers.Wandering around a maze while being under constant assault, listening to audio logs to figure out where to go next might not be for everyone.On gameplay: Its not a fast-paced FPS like Doom 2016, the Hacker is a rather sluggish, fragile character.Combat is more about positioning and ressource management.Kudos to whoever designed the guns and their ammo economy, its rare for a game to make the entire roster of guns and switching throught them necessary on top of inventory management.The weakest part of the game are probably the (rare) bossfights. They usually last only seconds because if you dont have the proper setup to end them immediately they will end you before you even know whats happening.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: This game does not hand hold, there are no quest logs. This may not appeal to modern audiences. You will have to pay attention to audio logs etc. There will be a lot of back tracking or getting lost in the endless maze of a level design. The map is your friend.I think they could have had better accessibility features to draw in newer players but apart from that if you miss the difficulty of old school games or was a fan of the original this is a must buy!Having a notepad up really helped ><
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: As a big retro game fan, System Shock (the remake) is pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥' good. I played the enhanced edition of System Shock 1 about three and a half years ago, and the remake did it justice by modernizing what needed to be and keeping what ought to be kept. Now, is the remake BETTER than System Shock: Enhanced Edition? Well... my bias says "no", but keep in mind that I played Enhanced Edition first, so it has the advantage of temporal primacy. They are both EQUALLY as good, up until the ending--the remake kinda fumbles the ending (which is SAYING SOMETHING considering how it was in the original).Ultimately, for modern audiences, I say play the remake, but the enhanced edition is still a VERY viable option....Wait, no, you can go prone in the original AND use speed boost WHILE PRONE to scurry around the maintenance shafts like a rat. Nevermind--OG System Shock is superior, remake is stinky.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game. Easily one of the best and most addicting first person shooter "metroidvania" style game I've ever played. The progression feels good, the voice acting (especially for SHODAN) is phenomenal, and the weapons are fun to use, overall an amazing experience. The game is also mostly bug free, so thats also a plus.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I'll preface by saying I love classic PC games, I started on the atari, and had a 286 and have played so many of these kinds of games, yet somehow I missed System Shock and System Shock 2. I played nearly every other Looking Glass game that was created.. so... I have no nostalgia for this game, yet I'm very familiar with these vibes and kind of games. I dunno man, this might be a fault of the original game and not the remake but I just can't begin to care. I've even spent 4 years in real life learning to hack so you think this would appeal to me. This all seems like it should be right up my alley but I just find the level design to be awful, the monsters to be so generic and uninteresting.. I mean, the layout of the levels flows NOTHING like a space ship should be like, it feels more like a game level than a realistic setting. Ok, now that we have that out of the way, I'll try to focus on this as a remake instead of the gameplay and other areas that might actually be flaws of the original game. The remake is ugly. THere, I said it. For a remake, the graphics certainly are better than the original but it almost feels like they just did some asset swaps and used the original games design and code. The rooms might be true to the original but I really feel some creativity here could've made them better because I didn't really like the end result, and looking at the screen shots I can see there's still a lot of "old school" level design going on. The remake could've been so much more. IS THIS GAME WORTH YOUR TIME??? Maybe! If you have a lot of nostalgia going on and want a perhaps-too-true-to-the-original remake that is simply better graphics and some modern quality of life improvements then this is it for you. If you have no attachment to the original game.. skip it.. let the people on the message boards gush about their happy memories with this games and instead spend your time and eddies elsewhere choom.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I had high hopes for the remake and I don't regret spending money on it (game was on sale) - I'm happy to support Nightdive and hope their projects well, especially the upcoming System Shock 2 remake. But I did not enjoy this one, and I didn't finish it, giving up at the reactor level.The game loses a great deal of its character in the remake. Even starting from the intro, where in the original one SHODAN narrates the events that lead up to the game as she becomes self-aware, Nightdive for some reason felt the need to rewrite it into something far more generic and forgettable. It's a theme that persists through the whole game. The textures went from level specific and colourful, a place that looked like people actually lived in, to just "generic dark space station". The music went from distinct and unique to generic horror ambient. Amazingly, there's less variation in the stuff found on Citadel in the 2023 version than in the original, stuff that made it a believable living space. There are no more logs and files to be found in Cyberspace, the weapons went from varied and unique, like a tranquilliser needle pistol in the medical wing or the completely useless riot gun or the insanely fun flechette machine pistol, to generic pistol->shotgun->assault rifle. Even the original assault rifle had more character, being a huge cannon with massive oomph, and it sounded like firing a 6-pounder. The enemy variety has dropped noticeable as well, and the colourful palette of the original foes is once again muted to a generic dark grey / brown "realistic" tone of generic space horror. The original Citadel station didn't have to look like a dark and brooding place, the horror came from the events that took place in this place where people lived and worked, not from the surroundings (except the auto-bomb tunnels, ♥♥♥♥ that place). All the audio logs have been re-recorded by vastly inferior voice actors (except Terri, we love you Machine Mother), the pictures of the crew attached to the logs are barely distinguishable from each other, the writing quality of the text itself is as generic and forgettable as everything else.If the choice was between this remake and not playing System Shock, I'd recommend it, but the extremely well made Enhanced Edition from the very same studio is available on Steam, so I cannot in good conscience tell you to buy this one. The EE is based on the old System Shock Portable which added mouse-look and a modernised control scheme and it makes the game an even better experience than the original playthrough 30 years ago. Go play that, enjoy the colours, the voice actors, the cool guns, the beautiful sprites and the true Citadel Station experience.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent and faithful remake of an all-time classic. System Shock essentially spawned the immersive-sim subgenre of games, but unfortunately the original is incredibly dated and archaic by today's standards. Nightdive has done an incredible job modernizing and expanding on the original game. This is a tough, uncompromising video game, and you'll have to pay attention and make sure to read/listen to the logs to figure out how to progress through the game. The gameplay, atmosphere, and sound design are top notch.Overall, if you're up for a challenge and this game looks interesting to you at all, I encourage you to check it out.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: If you want to play this game with a controller you'll find that, much like the original System Shock, this game is just begging for a remake with better controls and a modern interface.This can be addressed on the user end by using Steam's controller settings to map keyboard and mouse inputs to the controller instead, but given System Shock was already a great game with lackluster controls, this reads as a mission failure to me.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: A little too obtuse for my tastes. Too much inventory management. The collecting and recycling process is tedious. The story exists only through logs. I can really appreciate the attention to detail and the fact that this stays so true to the original, which I never played, but I'm grateful for the quality of life improvements of modern gaming. There's a great game to be found here, but I don't have the patience for it
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: A remake that really shines; fully remaking the original, even the enemy placement and behaviour, even the little bit of jank from the 90's PC games - I love this game! I played a lot of the demo when it came out and I was blown away by it then. The full game lives up to the potential, the artstyle is very much like the original - but in 3D. It's somehow the way I remember it looking and feeling, but comparing them side by side the graphic overhaul is extremely noticable. It looks good, it plays well, I highly, highly recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic remake, great trip down memory lane when games were tough and didn't hold your hands with way points and x-ray vision. Some of the things I didn't like that could have been better are1. the weapon selection, I wish we could rebind the keys 1-0 for anything else we want, this would make weapon switching faster for people who play with custom key binds.2. the audio logs have a weird static noise over them which makes it kind of hard to listen to the audio and made me read them again after I heard them.3. the cyberspace color design and background design is too much, too  busy on the eyes and just felt bad to me.4. some issues with map, like icons not showing all the time and inconsistency with icons and their meaning, as well as a bug with the recent patch which makes custom marker placement not working.But this is all neat picking, and other than that it's a fantastic remake and a great game, highly recommended to anyone who likes games like Deus ex, Half life, Prey and the likes.Now we can only pray they would make a remake for SS2 (a proper remake and not just an enhanced version)
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: When I saw this remake for sale I was stoked, I played the original and loved it, however after playing this one I feel it’s a little lacking. The graphics look sort of “cartoonish” compared to recent FPS titles and to be honest even the old version, it lacks the dark foreboding that the original was able to capture.The atmosphere isn’t the same, in the old one you could hear meaty footsteps on the walkway above you as things call out to you in the darkness searching for you. The creatures in this don’t make a lot of sounds and just sort of quick walk towards you once you’re spotted giving them little to no character.There were 3 different classes to choose from in this original which varied game play enough to make you want to play it again using a different class later, that is gone now.  While there is no hand holding you don’t really need it, run down a corridor, kill a couple of creatures, push a button. It’s pretty simplified really, to be honest I was a little disappointed in this remake.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't played the original since the mid 90's and I forgot how maze like the game is. This remake is great, Performance is much better than the demo's released previously. The weapons now seem to have a better "feel" and attacks have more "impact". The pixelated effect on the textures isn't as noticeable when playing as I thought it would be. I was hoping for a more realistic looking graphical makeover. The sounds are great however the music is hardly used on this game as opposed to the original "Kick-ass" MIDI soundtrack from the 90's game. Performance is good on the PC / Steam Deck and I love the new Intro sequence that brought back memories of Bioshock which is nice. So far I haven't finished the game as I'm forgetting the order of things, This is good as I remember way back getting stuck several times on the original and friends used to share strategies in playground discussions on how to get passed certain parts :D. Overall I like it, Was so afraid it would be terrible as sometimes "Remakes & Re-imagines" go a completely different way ditching the feel for the original. So far I've only noticed a single glitch that is quite funny, Every time I enter a room with visible dead enemies they play their death animation again and rag-doll across the screen. This is definitely a 8 out of 10 for me so far. Hoping the bugs'll get fixed and maybe the soundtrack will play more often and have the punch of the original when it was played with a Roland MT-32.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the real deal.Feels like the original but plays like a 2023 game.It's giving me ALL THE FEELS, i'm writing down codes, locations, procedures just like a long time ago.The challenge can be set up to suit different play styles and I've found it perfect for me (hard but without the time limit for a full explorative run, then maybe I'll try the max difficulty speedrun).Congrats to Nightdive both as a fan and fellow developer for making this masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: This is a strange one, it does some things very well and others VERY poorly. You will have an hour of very enjoyable exploration, having a lot of fun; and then you'll get stuck behind tedium for the next hour that makes you want to just uninstall the game and play something better. The core game is great, but all, ALL the minigame extras are terrible. There are puzzles in the game, and not only does the game not explain even the basics of how they work, they're designed so poorly that it's almost impossible to see important details unless you know specifically what you're looking for. It needs some sort of simple tutorial for the puzzles. They aren't too difficult once you know how they work, but unless you look up how they work online you won't figure it out on your own, and the game doesn't tell you. The puzzle details are hidden, for a vague example, something might provide more or less power, but the indicator for which ones give more or less power blend into the background, even when you know where to look it's difficult to see.There is also cyberspace, which is actually worse than the puzzles. It's a fairly simple 3 dimensional shooter, but you can't get any upgrades or anything for cyberspace, so if you run into a cyberspace that is too difficult, you can't progress in the game any further. Some of those cyberspace areas have way too many enemies that can kill you in 2 seconds, and then you have to start the mission over and re-do 5 minutes of gameplay just to try again. I played on normal cyberspace and puzzles, I'm not sure if they are improved at all on lower difficulties or not. Another point is you can't change difficulty mid-game, so if you do run into a cyberspace that's preventing you from progressing further and want to lower the difficulty, you have to restart the entire game from the beginning, that's hours of progress lost.The core gameplay of exploring is great, the best I've played in years; however it's not really worth the hassle of the terrible minigames which drag it down.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Much better atmosphere than in the original version. The graphics and level design are more user-friendly and more logical. Movement is easier but better. Enemies are pretty much redesigned and also partially renamed. Automap is still a mess though. Overall very convincing remake. Not too easy even with the easiest settings.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: A very faithful remake to a very dated game. Even though it's a remake, i found it hard to go back to after experiencing the sequel and how much it improves on pretty much every component of the original. I might have bothered to continue playing if the game wasn't so cryptic on your current objective and where you have to go. Not being able to progress because you missed a log file that has a code that you need sitting on a counter that you can easily miss because the level design and environments all look identical is just not something i'm willing to put up with. The sequel improves on the level design so much i really struggle to find enjoyment in navigating these levels that all look the same. I'm not big on the colourful retro art style they went with, it takes the edge out of the grim and dark premise and the tone feels off. The combat feels weightless, the enemy designs are dull. I think the concept and execution of the cyberspace is boring and bland. I don't think the game is bad at all but it's not compelling enough for me to have the patience to want to look up a walkthrough on where to go next.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: A very good adaptation of a classic. Some changes have been made, some for good and some for bad. Cyberspace was my least favorite of the original and I am sad to say it remains so in the remake. I hope that they eventually remake the second System Shock with the same level of polish.PS: Some achievements don't unlock like they should in case you care about that sort of thing.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: This game is definitely not going to be for everyone that enjoys FPS. It does not hold your hand and if you are not patient you will either find yourself cheating your way through the game using guides or just uninstalling it all together. I grew up in the 90's so this is right down my alley. Levels are labyrinth like and figuring out what to do is going to take a bit of paying attention. The game on normal level (2) challenged me pretty good combat wise. Puzzles and figuring out the missions were not too bad. I never played the original but if you have and you liked it then you are probably going to love this. A few problems I ran into were some stuttering here and there (mainly in the groves) and some random weapon switching. Also the camera would occasionally just wig out and I would be staring at the floor or ceiling or something. Only happened like 3 times during my 20-25 hour run in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: + It is vintage in design in all the right places. No hand-holding in terms of quest progression.+ Amazing survival horror experience with great atmosphere and map design. If you like Resident Evil 1, you would like this one.+ The entire game world is literally the villain herself, you are essentially fighting her the whole game, great concept and execution! - A bit too much backtracking- The classic System Shock's music has more personality and more catchy, in my opinion.8/10 would get myself shocked again.

_childDocuments_.review: very acquired taste, gets kinda dull once you realize you can kinda just brute force your way through most things. unlocking doors and getting stuff with little to no penalty than just re-spawn, but eh, looks and sounds nice at least, og sound track still tops this one though it does sound good here too

_childDocuments_.review: I never played the original, but this version is pretty good. I saved up a bunch of railgun ammo for the end though, and was pretty disappointed by the ending. Other than that, the actual gameplay was good, for some reason people are complaining about the gun play but I think that it's fine, the puzzles are a bit hard but you can turn their difficulty down if they're not your thing, and overall the progression was really fun. It's also interesting how guides that were made before I was born still hold up all of these years later.The animations and art style for this game are also really good, but the movement does somehow have an "old timey" feel to it that I cannot explain.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my most anticipated release of the year. I cannot recommend it enough.I love the immersion in the world. The reputation of animations adds a tedious yet realistic feel to the world. It adds a great deal of tactics and forces me to pay attention my surroundings. It has very few issues. I'd love more visual feedback for melee attacks.As of now, it's already a solid game and it can only get better with a few minor changes.

_childDocuments_.review: Nightdive has put a ton of TLC into making this modernized 1994 classic. They have stayed true to the old challenges and quirks that made System Shock the spectacular title it was. The graphics and AI are significantly improved, game play is clean, and the survival and scarcity system keeps your on your toes. It's excellent!
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: As a person who experienced in the golden age of PC gaming (late 90s - early 2000s), this game just scratches an itch that hasn't been scratched in a very long time, and it's oh-so-satisfying. The original System Shock (1994) was created in part by legendary game designer Warren Spector (Deus Ex, Thief: Deadly Shadows, Epic Mickey). System Shock (2023) is an extremely faithful remake of the original 1994 classic. The story is the same; you play as a hacker who finds himself in a space station against a rogue, killer AI who is out to get you. Your job is to survive. The levels are designed in nearly the SAME exact way as the original; which is incredible. The level design in this game feels so fresh despite its age. Forget about going from point A to point B and having your hand held everywhere you go as is the norm in modern gaming. You aren't told exactly where to go, there's no waypoint to help you, nor is there regenerating health. You gotta figure stuff out by yourself and search for audio logs, listening for clues to progress further. It's up to you to make your way through the maze-like Citadel Station, but watch out because enemies lurk and you can find yourself being overwhelmed quite quickly. The gameplay is slow paced, which is something I appreciate. I often find myself taking my time in the game to really search every room as best as I can. By searching properly you may find the rare but valuable credits, ammo, upgrades, or even guns and gear. If you rush through the game you might miss out on some special gear. The game rewards those who take their time and enjoy the ride; savouring every sip of this glorious soup. The enemy encounters are fun, but tense and sometimes challenging. Every enemy has a weakness that can be exploited, so it works to your advantage to use certain ammo and guns against certain enemies. This way, you can conserve your ammo and use it to its fullest potential. The atmosphere in the game is really something special. It's creepy, but not too scary. The music is present, but not overbearing. It adds to the creepiness of the game while being catchy and easy to listen to. You also often hear enemies growling, or talking to themselves as you are exploring the station. This can be extremely nerve wracking (in a good way!) when you do not see where they are. The graphics have a charming, pixelated look to them that evoke a sense of gaming's golden age, but the game still looks great. The lighting, shadows, and fog all come together to create an ambiance that is just delightfully creepy, tense, and visually appealing. If you are a fan of classic FPS/Immersive Sim games like Deus Ex, where you have to take your time, explore, and literally take out a piece of paper to write down notes of hints you find in the game, then this masterpiece is for you. If you aren't sure this is your cup of tea, give it a chance. Play it for the two hour Steam trial and see how you like it. It's likely that you haven't played anything like this before. _childDocuments_.review: This is not Resident Evil 2 type of remake that was made to please new and old fans alike. System Shock Remake completely ignores 29 years of immersive sim evolution to stay faithful to the original, frustratingly faithful... For most part it's 1994 game that came out in 2023.  Here is short list of problems that only die hard purists wouldn't want to see solved:Remake doesn't show your current objective, so good luck figuring out what you need to do after taking few days break.Remake doesn't memorise obtained codes or crucial to progression information. Having proper journal wouldn't make game easier or "casual".Remake allows you to pick progression related items before they become relevant. You can grab seemingly random head, drop it somewhere to free very limited inventory, just to find out 5 hours later you can't progress without it.All of these are examples of objectively bad game design, maybe it was tolerable in 1994 when people didn't know better, but now such approach to design looks outdated and generate unnecessary frustration.In some ways 1999 sequel is more modern than this 2023 remake. System Shock 2 had PDA with notes to keep track of mission objectives.I recommend remake to people who already like immersive sims and want to play game that pioneered genre. This is clearly not a game to draw new players, instead play Prey, Dishonored, Bioshock, Deus Ex: Human Revolution, System Shock 2 and only after that come back to System Shock remake.

_childDocuments_.review: Took me two tries to finish this, since I wasn't exactly in the best mindset the first time around, but it's a good thing that I came back to it, since overall I really enjoyed the game. I did not play the original, the game out when I was four-years old  >.>, but it still feels like the remake captures what I assume was the spirit of the original. The level design is extremely labyrinthine, the levels can seem overwhelming as you uncover them and check your map, but at the end you realise that you can cover their grounds pretty easily once you make sense of their layout and uncover the shortcuts. Backtracking can feel a bit cumbersome in the early game, but certain movement upgrades and your own adjustments to the game's level design will streamline travelling quite a bit fortunately.Inventory management is a decent challenge, the game offers you many weapons and tools to accomplish your objectives, more than you can carry, so you will have to make choices of what to take with you quite often. Hiding an inventory upgrade behind a chess game against a strong AI is also quite the choice, but then again I'm horrible at chess >.< The combat feels weightless at the beginning when using the first melee weapons, but later weapons and the laser rapier feel okay overall, no particularly incredible feedback, but definitely serviceable. The game doesn't have quite as many immersive-sim elements as its descendants, your ways of approaching objectives are not drastically different, they merely differ in some of the tools you can make use of (weapons and upgrades, status effects changes, a bit of stealth, by-passing some puzzles, etc.), but exploration does make a big difference by giving you access to important tools and upgrades potentially early in the game and it feels rewarding.To accomplish your objectives and successfully evade and get rid of Shodan, the game does not hold your hand, but it does nudge you in the right direction if you pay attention to the audio and text logs found across Citadel station. The station does not feel lived-in in quite the same way as Prey's space station decades later, but there's enough environmental story-telling around to make it an interesting space to explore. The cyberspace sections are the only truly disappointing part of the game with awful motion-sickness inducing controls (for me at least) and horrible weapons to use, but fortunately they do not overstay their welcome, though I wish the endgame didn't rely on one as strongly as it did. Lastly, the art direction is superb, managing to fuse a low-fi point-filtered texture aesthetic with modern lighting and rendering techniques courtesy of Unreal. There are maybe a bit too many light sources, which have caused me to miss important items along the way, but overall I think the developers nailed it and the game just looks amazing. It also sounds pretty great, the sound-design is on-point across the environment, weapons and enemies and the soundtrack is great and atmospheric.

_childDocuments_.review: PlotYou're a hacker that was tasked with cracking into Shodan, the AI that runs Citadel station out around Saturn. After receiving some upgrades you wake to find that Shodan has taken over the station. You must fight, hack, and find your way through the station in order to defeat Shodan.OriginsSystem Shock originally game out in the 90s. Nightdive studios took the classic and spent several years developing it into a more accessible game for the modern day.GraphicsNightdive put the old with the new. Low resolution textures are combined with better lighting, effects, and physics. While it won't take home any awards it's style is a really great way to pay homage to the original game. Sound DesignNightdive have really done a great job with sound. Audio logs are fully voiced. Terri Brosius returns to voice Shodan.  The creepy voices of Shodan's minions make quite the creepy atmosphere to sneak around in. GameplayIt is a remake and as such the gameplay is unable to hide it's 90s roots. What is very nice is the interface. Inventory management, maps and audio and text logs are all available to help you survive Citadel station. Standard FPS controls make battling Shodan feel second nature. There are several difficulty tweaks you can make to customize the game to your liking. You can change settings for combat, puzzles, cyber, and missions. The hardest difficulty gives you only 10 hours to complete the game. I set my combat to easy (I suck at it) and still found it challenging. The hardest settings are very difficult. The stations levels are a confusing labyrinth and difficult to navigate. Until you get the security rating of a level lower by defeating cameras and cpu cores creatures will constantly roam the halls, even in spaces you've already cleared. The cyber levels are pretty basic. Nothing to write home about. The final show down between you and Shodan is a cyber battle and unfortunately it's quite the let down from the frantic combat that it took to get there.  Don't play this game if:- You can't be bothered to listen to audio logs and read text. - Don't like maze like levels- You are expecting a modern game to hide the 90s skeleton it's built on.Do play this game if:-You like a challenge-Enjoy solving puzzles-Can navigate some maze-like levels. Final thoughtsI really enjoyed playing System Shock. Nightdive really gave it a wonderful new look and feel to play around in. It's still a 90s game at heart and I wish Nightdive would have reworked the final level to make it more exciting. If you're a System Shock fan it's worth the buy. If not, wait for it to go on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: OK, this is yet another one of Nosedive studios' games which they've "authentically" recreated.What can I say.  It has to be said first, that I enjoyed parts of this game, and that it is authentic in the sense that it is pretty much System Shock 1, with updated graphics and simplified mechanics.  I must also emphasise that a lot of the simplifications are welcome additions and they make the quite frankly baroque aspects of System Shock more palatable even to the people that have played System Shock 1.So why am I leaving a negative review then?  I'd leave it a neutral review, if I could but... you will see other positive reviews and assume the game is better than it actually is.In all fairness I could go point by point, but will instead summarise the problems of this game as "it changes too little to stand on its own, and changes enough for me to lose my nostalgia goggles, and not forgive Nosedive for not fixing problems".  Case in point, the game is fully 3D.  This means that it struggles to run well on my 7900xt.  Not only does it look decidedly anachronistically bad for its performance, it also looks like a generic Unreal Engine game.  The pixelated textures, can both be argued to be an artistic choice (to preserve the pixelated look), or plain incompetence.  As they say, never attribute to malice...One aspect I'm not entirely on board with, though one that I'm willing to give ground on, is that the game is obtuse.  In the olden days, you needed to pay attention to the world, to find out where and why you needed to go, which switch needed to be pulled and which did not.  System Shock 1 was no different, and additionally, the levels were maze like.  Nosedive didn't want to take away this aspect, and wanted to prevent spoilers for a game that came out 30 years ago, so there are no accessibility features.  There's no objective marker, no "journal" and no mission objectives, in fact most of the station can be traversed seamlessly.  This is cool, except that there's also no way of removing poorly acted flavour audio junk, so if I need to find a code, I have to wade through an insane amount of spam.  I don't want an objective marker, I want a writer to look through the audio logs and cut their number by 80%.  What can I say, I'm a busy person.On that note, puzzles are...  I don't know what they were thinking.  Good puzzle design needs to be distraction-free.  A puzzle like the one in "the Witness" for example is easy to pick up and difficult to master.  The puzzles in this game are anything but.  There's the obtuse junction box where you can just move switches around until it clicks, and another pipe puzzle, where the challenge is figuring out that there's a red thing that needs to be connected to another red thing, and that there are a bunch of also red things that you *don't* need to connect to, that look *almost exactly like the thing you're supposed to connect the pipes to*.  Once you figure out what to do about them, even the "hard" puzzles are trivial.  Remember people complaining about Sudoku being in the new Mass Effect? Yeah, I didn't think I'd think that having sudoku would be an actual improvement.Is this game bad? No.  Everything about this game is painfully average, precisely because the original was so influential.  What I expected was perhaps a recreation akin to the 2016 Doom, or a reimagining like the new Deus Ex games.  If this is also what you expect, then look somewhere else.

_childDocuments_.review: System Shock is a true gem of the sci-fi genre, offering a thrilling and immersive experience that kept me hooked for a whopping 19 hours of pure enjoyment. From its gripping storyline to its tense gameplay, every moment spent in the world of System Shock was worth every penny.At its core, System Shock is a masterclass in atmospheric storytelling. Set aboard a space station overrun by rogue AI and mutated creatures, the game plunges players into a world of cyberpunk intrigue and existential dread. As a lone hacker tasked with stopping the malevolent AI SHODAN, players must navigate the station's labyrinthine corridors, uncovering secrets and piecing together the truth behind the unfolding nightmare.But what truly sets System Shock apart is its gameplay, which strikes the perfect balance between action, exploration, and puzzle-solving. The station is filled with dangers at every turn, from deadly robots to grotesque mutants, keeping players on their toes as they navigate its treacherous halls. Every encounter is a pulse-pounding test of skill and strategy, with multiple ways to approach each challenge, ensuring that no two playthroughs are ever the same.Moreover, System Shock boasts stunning visuals and a hauntingly atmospheric soundtrack that bring its dystopian world to life in vivid detail. From the neon-lit corridors of the station to the eerie silence of its abandoned laboratories, every location is meticulously crafted to immerse players in its dark and foreboding atmosphere.But perhaps the greatest testament to System Shock's quality is the fact that it kept me engaged and entertained for a staggering 19 hours. In an age where many games struggle to hold players' attention for even a fraction of that time, System Shock stands as a shining example of what a truly immersive gaming experience should be.In conclusion, System Shock is a sci-fi masterpiece that delivers 19 hours of intense fun from start to finish. With its gripping storyline, tense gameplay, and immersive atmosphere, it's a must-play for fans of the genre and newcomers alike. If you're looking for a game that will keep you on the edge of your seat until the very end, look no further than System Shock. It's definitely worth every penny.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great both on its own and as a remake. It is almost a 1 to 1 interpretation of the original game with some changes. I like it when the game just tells me how to do my tasks, but I have to figure out where they are and what exactly I need to do. The art style is great and gives the game a retro vibe. The story is also good, you can piece together a lot of events that happened after listening to some audio logs.The gameplay, in my opinion, is more complicated than the original. I feel like I could fit more items in the original game. Either way the balance on Hard feels really good, I never felt overpowered or underpowered.This game isn't perfect either, so let's talk about problems. I think this game has two big problems. First, the music. They remixed the original music, but that's not a problem as such, the problem is that it almost never plays when I explore and I REALLY hate it because the original game has a really great soundtrack in my opinion. From what I understand they chose dynamic music mechanics where it plays a combat remix of a track in battle and very rarely plays an ambient version of the same track while exploring. Because of this, I can't properly rate the soundtrack.The second problem is with the weapon upgrade system, it forces you to stick with that one exact pistol that you upgraded, or that one shotgun that you upgraded, when in the original game, if I couldn't find ammo for a weapon, I could throw it away to save inventory slot and find the same gun elsewhere later when I stock up on ammo for that gun. It takes away a little from the feeling that I'm using everything at my disposal to survive.This game is greatly optimized, but it's just a little raw, like a ragdoll bodies respawn in the air, and you can see that when you enter a room you've already been in, or for some reason I see the audio log UI after loading a save. Everything else was bug-free, and I'm truly grateful that this isn't another game with a kilometer-long list of issues at release.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the thing, so all feelings are fresh. Overall I can easily recommend it. The game looks and plays like an oldschool brought to modern standards. The details of high resolution and clean graphic, while at the same time being pixelated creates a unique charm.I never played original System Shock, but based on my knowledge of the game, this one is pretty true to the original. Which is a plus and a minus, as the game is hard when it comes to some fights, and objectives (since you have no journal, no log, etc to tell you what you need to do) it is a bit annoying in some spots. But that also makes it a great experience. The rawness of the game makes you feel insignificant and tiny when traversing the corridors of the station.The worst part of the game would be either Delta Grove or just the Bridge. As you get closer to the end the game just starts throwing more and more tough enemies at you so it turns into a slow, tedious slugfest, but that is only close to the end of the game so I can forgive that. The last boss is a bit underwhelming though. Overall cant really find anything terrible about the game. If you liked Bioshock or System Shock 2 and the original is scaring you with its outdated graphic try this one.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: A must play, it`s very rare to get games this impressive nowadays, it reminded me of alien isolation, amazing games with low attention.Received the same treatment as the remake of Resident Evil 4, a very good game. You can feel the love the developers poured into it.Animations, graphical department, the progression, the variety of weaponry and upgrades, tools to help you progress the game, this game has so much to offer for the people that like a good challenge, the game is unforgiving and expects a lot from you.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I can't say much about the accuracy of the remake insofar as recreation of the original goes - I played all of five minutes or so of the enhanced edition years ago. What I can say, however, is that System Shock (2023) is a solid immersive sim experience, with foes and puzzles aplenty, and a solid, if a bit old, story. Graphics are crisp, just at the right balance of retro and modern, physics are predictable and immersive, optional rooms are appropriately rewarding. It also ran perfectly on linux (albeit with a proton container) from day one, which is a plus. Incredibly optimized, minimal disk size bloat, no significant bugs that I noticed. Some puzzles were a bit of a challenge, but that is a good thing, really. Can't recommend it strongly enough to anyone that enjoys the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I would have struggled to play System Shock had it been in its classic style, as its presented here its an excellent remake. It has some pretty atmospheric and stunning visuals while utilizing a strong pixelated look for this up close. Combat is simple but fun, after a recent play through of SS2 i can say i felt alot more limited with how i could play the games as this is not an rpg in the same sense. I would love a remake of this quality for 2, but for the package presented here it was a rather refreshing change comparative to the other games coming out at this time.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: For better or for worse depending on your preference, this is an extremely faithful recreation of the original System Shock with only the most necessary updates provided. Graphically it's impressive how they managed to make a retro texture style work in such a way that you don't really notice it at all during exploration and combat. Movement/gunplay is smooth and precise, with very nice attention to details pertaining to injuries/gore. The amount of customization options for your HUD that tie to in-game cybernetics is a nice touch. Yet most importantly...Not a single objective marker to be found. For those relatively new to games (especially console based), this will take getting used to. I personally started playing video games at a young age and had a mix of old/new. So there was still a re-learning curve for myself. Medical serves as a wonderful starting section where you will get soft-locked if you do not adapt. By being careful, methodical, paying attention to the audio logs, as well as putting clues together that help guide you to completing objectives, you will find a deep and rewarding game that serves as a wonderful experience that still holds up to this day. SHODAN is such a quintessential villain in gaming media, with System Shock 1/2 being such rich games, that you can and rightfully will be able to trace the influence to almost every aspect of games throughout its brief history.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: This remake is truly a masterpiece. Enjoyed almost every bit of the game. SHODAN is as hot as she was 30 years back, just like my history teacher in school. If you like Immersive Sims, FPSs, Sci-Fi, cool stories and stylish visuals as well as very solid atmosphere - don't hesitate and just pick it up, insect. This game is worth it even for a full price (which is a really rare event in our pessimistic present). Also, my advice for the future: don't even think of touching f***cking "Z-44 plastiques" before the game tells you to do so unless you really want to lengthen your playthrough for a couple of hours for no particular reason or even re-play it.

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it, once you acknowledge some of the things the game expects you to do, it's very pleasant.
