If you're tempted by this game, don't be fooled, it will not hold your hand.This is a game for people who don't expect every single game to guide them around like toddlers and place markers everywhere to tell "go there go there", the original System Shock and this remake both expect you to pay attention. If you can do that, go for it 100% :)
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Faithful to the original, brutal as ♥♥♥♥ and completely unforgiving as you try to fight your way to saving yourself when a game is out to beat you at every possible turn.The atmosphere has such palpable tension you literally find yourself leaning forward almost touching your screen most of the time. When you aren't, you're probably watching the death cutscene. And with all of that said, this was one of the best gaming experiences I've had in a long time. This was well worth the painful wait!

_childDocuments_.review: Do I recommend this game? Yes, but with one caveat: this game absolutely does not hold your hand. Be prepared to get your ass kicked over and over again. If you're not into punishing games, System Shock is most likely not your cup of tea.(It's 100% MY cup of tea, though)Had a fantastic time with it and I hope the second game gets a remake as well

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely faithful, well polished, well done remake of System Shock.Hackers back, SHODANs back, Cyberspace is coherent. The only thing missing is the OG music but honestly that helps a lot to keep me terrified while I dodge a Cortex Reaver.Issues: -Melee is lackluster, but I drop it by the time I get a shotgun. -Kleptomaniacs/Loot goblins will spend a lot of time scrapping all misc items. (You don't need that many credits)-Dead Enemy Models will flop a bit when you re enter an area, might spook ya but it doesn't hinder game play-NEW PLAYERS to System Shock, Faithful recreation means lots of big corridors and rooms with no objective markers please, unless you enjoy problem solving by reading and paying close attention to audio logs, glance a guide when your not sure what you need to do.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I finished the game after almost 40 hours and... OK, it's not a perfect game, but it's a perfect remake of a 1994 game. I experienced something that I can't get from 2023 games. Confusing locations with tons of hidden paths, ambushes, no task tracker, no waypoints on the map, just your mind, map and notes. The inventory system constantly pushes you to make decisions. What's more important: patches or extra ammo packs, trash to recycle to make some money, or new weapons? It may not be smooth expirience, but it feels like you are really playing and your decisions have an impact. I also like visual effects, but not everyone likes pixels.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Some shooters guide you through their story and mission if you ever get lost. System Shock is aggressively obtuse and its levels and objectives are designed to hinder your progress.That's kind of the point. You spend about five minutes with a voice in your ear telling you what to do...and then SHODAN decides that's enough of that. SHODAN is in total control, you are alone in a hostile environment, and you need to figure out for yourself how to fight back.This game is great. The levels and music are incredibly atmospheric. The visuals are a unique blend of modern and retro. The entire station is a tightly designed labyrinth with a perfect balance of fights and puzzles.Its a masterpiece, remastered perfectly and faithfully.

Having played the OG and the EE, this remake is impressive from the first minute!The visuals, a mix of realistic and comiclike, pixelated look works so brilliantly well!The sound, eargasm inducing. Weapons sound very impactfull, something many games get it done wrong.And that lovely dark ambient soundtrack...Btw, bring paper and pen with you, this game doesn´t hold your hand and writes everything down (THANKFULLY, i hate this), and there are many codes and numbers to write down!
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: The Rules are simple;You have 10 hours to beat the game.You only got the taser gun for a long distance attack.Only thing after that is a Pipe used as a back-up plan(the only plan).Ok, to say it simply just play and buy this game. This game is a slam dunk every single time. However, this game is hard. Not as in "damn these guys are tough! i ought to get better at the game!" No: this game will tell what you need to do via AUDIO LOGS. So do it like me and write down everything, or remember the pertinent audio logs when the time comes. There are no way points. There are no objective markers or logs. This is every ones' father game. No hand holding. At all. You must figure it out. Even if you do you still might stumble a little bit because the game doesnt give you anything....and neither does Shodan. she will kill you and ambush you and trap you at ANY turn. You will die. That's ok, because if you did your job, youll come back. However, if you dont...game over. start from the last save....No, there is no autosave. So you must save often. However once you understand this game's loop it is by far the most engaging, action packed, horrifying and immersive experience you can sink your teeth into until Nightdive finally drops the System shock 2 rework.This game is a home run every time. It is a rainfall after a very, very long dry spell. It is a breath of fresh and a blast from the past in all its beautiful and dated details; Make no mistake though, even on easy difficulty (or the equivalent) expect no quarter. No mercy. Shodan is ALWAYS watching and unless youre careful she will kill you and the entire human race for something as trivial as a god making something or UNmaking something. Good luck, Hacker.

_childDocuments_.review: So, for me the remake is already pretty ace, I haven't ventured far enough into citadel station yet to find anything that's awful compared to the original, it's mostly all the same or straight improvements, it's awesome seeing all these old areas with a completely new coat of paint.So far my biggest complaint is that I first played through System Shock before the original release date, nearly 7 years ago (I think, might be 6), since then I've played through it multiple times but considering the struggled development, it seems to have turned out pretty great.Now for SS2EE.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: The main remake is amazing! It's and actual remake, not a falsely-advertised crap re-imagining like, say, FFVII. Everything about the station, from controls to graphics to puzzles are like improved versions of the original game's, a lot of fun, and (after the patch) seemingly bug-free. I'd give the main part of the remake a 9 or 10 out of 10!  Then, there's cyberspace... Cyberspace SUCKS!!! I mean, in the original, cyberspace wasn't great, but there was more to do, as well as software upgrades to help with increasingly difficult combat, so in the worst of cases, you could come back and muscle your way through. In other words, while a low point in the game, it was interesting and feasible. After seeing how great the rest of the remake is, cyberspace doesn't even seem complete. All you do is fight and hope you don't take damage - it's rather difficult to even tell what's going on at any given moment.In short, a great and professional remake, except for cyberspace.  Hopefully, we'll get a patch to bring it up to the standards of the rest of the game. I definitely recommend the game, as most of it is amazing, and in the end, cyberspace isn't a huge part of it.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Nightdive Studios is pretty much just a retro necromancer and this game is their magnum opus. No longer are you playing an operating system like you were in 1994. Now the game feels (mostly) intuitive, combat has some weight to it, and Citadel Station has never looked better. My only gripe is that the game is perhaps a little too faithful of a remake. Citadel Station is the labyrinth to end all labyrinths. Despite all your rage, you are very much a rat in a cage. Oddly enough, a walkthrough doesn't hurt a first-time playthrough too badly, but it's also because every objective in this game is randomized, save for a handful of key missions. Codes will be different, locations will change, leading to a rather schizophrenic experience where you make some progress only for the game's mechanics to bring it to a screeching halt. A particularly egregious example is repairing relay 428. The location is randomized amongst three maintenance mazes and it is very easy to miss what your supposed to be repairing. Hard to recommend to people who aren't already hardcore fans of the immersive sim genre, and a tough pill to swallow for people who thought they loved immersive sims.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is brutal and it's amazing. It's drawing you into its thick atmosphere when you go around check every inch of the station, scrapping for supplies, being afraid getting shot by a hopping laser drill. It's a bit buggy, but also in its weirdly unique way. Brings a lot of memories of the original system shock 2
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I had the pleasure playing through! System Shock was one of the first PC games I remember from the  original floppy disk version and I even bought the original CD version a few years later.For me the story and environment was always something that was rarely accomplished by other games that followed over the years. It's up there with the DeusEx series, Bioshock, Prey, Dishonored, ... and it amazes me how far System Shock was ahead of it's time back then and still is.However - while I had good memories of the original and even tried to get back into with the Enhanced Edition, the gameplay mechanics and engine just did not age very well.The remake however managed to take the complete original storyline and environment, putting it into a modern game engine and adding gameplay mechanics and functions that the games coming after System Shock established and refined.For me it was the perfect experience - a dungeon crawler in space that did not hold my hands every few minutes and just allowed me to explore a space station taken over by SHODAN on my own time and at my own pace.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: [Also known as "System Shock Remake"] You're a renowned hacker, the most notorious cyberspace thief in the corporate world. Caught during a risky break-in, you become indentured to a greedy TriOptimum executive. After six months in a healing coma, you awaken to the twisted aftermath of a terrible disaster. Where are the surgeons? Why is the station in such disrepair? Slowly, the chilling realization that something is very wrong creeps over you. Once a prime corporate research facility, Citadel Station now teems with mindless cyborgs, robots and terribly mutated beings, all programmed to serve SHODAN, a ruthless A.I. There's scarcely time to think before it unleashes the first terror...

name: GTFO
detailed_description: FINAL EDITION Rundown 8.0 – Duality brings the story of the prisoners in the Complex to its riveting culmination. With all rundowns available in GTFO: Final Edition you and your team have more than 80 nail-biting challenges to suffer through. More than most people ever will be able to endure. About the Game Your team of prisoners is dropped into the Rundown when a new Work Order is issued by The Warden, the mysterious entity holding you captive. The Rundown is a series of expeditions, each one taking you deeper into a decayed research facility called The Complex. You descend level by level, scavenging tools and resources that help you survive in a perilous network of tunnels where gruesome creatures lurk in every shadow. Complete all the expeditions to fulfill the Work Order and clear the Rundown. GTFO is designed for prisoner teams of four, putting cooperation at the core of the experience. Bots can fill your lineup if you’re short one or two players. They’ll follow you through expeditions, sneak when you sneak, collect resources, and fight alongside you. They’re a good fallback, but the level of communication and tactical combat in GTFO means it’s best to play with people. A strategy is necessary to clear the Rundown. Before you drop into The Complex, your team needs to decide what gear, boosters, and weapons to bring. You must also balance the team, identifying the function of each prisoner so that you know what to do when things go wrong. And they will. They always do. Stealth and coordination are necessary to survive as you maneuver through The Complex. Many of the creatures of GTFO are suspended in a state of hibernation, so light, noise, and vibrations can easily wake up these Sleepers. And if one of them knows you’re there, they all know. That’s when things get messy. You’ll need heavy weaponry and a clear mind when the shit hits the fan. Check your line of fire, force them through bottlenecks, set up your kill zones and reload every chance you get. These creatures stop at nothing, and neither should you. Once the mayhem starts, you have no choice but to put every last one of them down. Clearing expeditions and Rundowns will reward you with new cosmetic gear. Wear it with pride, as it proves to your peers you’ve been to hell and back. The Sleepers, on the other hand, will not care for a second.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start off by saying this game has made me more stressed than any final exam could. My 2 friends and I have just successfully completed our first 2 missions after more than 10 hours of gameplay. GTFO is a game that requires a great deal of stealth, patience, and teamwork. The rooms are pitch black, the monsters hit hard, and you will die many times. I have been watching this game for over a year now and picked it up the day it dropped, and I do not regret it at all. Here are a few things to consider before you buy however:1. GTFO is in early access and there may need to be bug fixes and balancing updates. So far after 20 hours, I have only encountered 1 minor glitch2. You will need a team of 3-4 players. I highly recommend getting this game with friends, but if you want to jump in without them, the GTFO discord can be used to match players together until they release matchmaking in game3. This is a team of 10 or so developers, if you want to support this game (Which you should if you like this genre), consider dropping the 30-35 dollars for this game so it can be improved even more.4. Teamwork and voice chat is a must. If you have a potato for a mic, consider getting an upgrade. There is nothing worse than losing a round after hours of gameplay because of miscommunication.5. Prepare to be uneasy. There is not enough ammo or med-packs to fight every monster. You WILL have to stealth your way through dark foggy rooms filled with hostiles that will obliterate you with the slightest misstep. Take your time and plan with your teamTL:DR - Overall I would say this is the best CO-OP experience I have ever had and GTFO really captures the essence of fear and unease. I would recommend this game to any horror/stealth enthusiast.

_childDocuments_.review: Very happy with the investment so far!This game has no publisher so the devs are doing this by themselves. I get that £30 is expensive for a game in its current state but this is clearly a small development team who have limited resources. Seeing people say it should cost £10, I don't understand how they expect the game to improve with such a pitiful investment. At this stage matchmaking is imminent if you look at the roadmap, which I get is essential for solo players with no immediate friends available. It is strange why they released it so suddenly if matchmaking is so close to being complete. However, it runs really well apart from the odd frame drop or stuttery enemies. This is just optimisation issues and with time will be ironed out. The game looks good too as you can see for yourself. This is also why the game will be expensive in its current state. Creating a game with a high end engine will be more costly to develop. I for one am happy they are willing to take a risk and go for a AAA feel despite being a small budget team.This is not a review as others have detailed the gameplay aspects already. I just wanted to put this opinion out there against those who I feel are being naive and short sighted. Look at videos on youtube, read their roadmap, see what they are offering and when and decide if you are willing to invest and help them make a game that is looking really promising.

_childDocuments_.review: : GTFO (Yes, get the ♥♥♥♥ out, this game will ruin you. Jk, it's great) is a 4-person cooperative, stealth based, tactical shooter with horror elements, developed and published by  At game start, you pick your load out for you and your team (Or solo, if you're a madman), and you are sent down into an underground complex by a mysterious entity called “The Warden”, to explore your subterranean prison and complete objectives, or fetch quests for the said Warden. Which from what we can gather, you're prisoners who are expendable, hence being sent down to the long abandoned complex that's now filled with these grotesque mutants that will eat your face off to do the Wardens bidding. GTFO has a HUGE emphasis on stealth, exploration and strategy, and if those aren't you're forte, you're not going to have a good time on this.: I love how streamlined all the assets are. The game is beautifully designed, and how  manages their assets is honestly amazing and will never cease to impress me. Each level, despite using the same assets in a lot of places to streamline how well the game runs, each level always feel unique enough to be completely separate to one another, whilst still being part of the same facility. : Eerie, unsettling, and then battle music when you know you've f*cked up. It works, it doesn't need anything more, anything less. Every sound in the game is so well done, crisp sounding and in your face when it needs to be. One sound I need to specifically highlight and give extra credit to is; Chargers. OHMYGOD, they sound horrific and I absolutely love it! Their movement sounds, breathing, it's so unsettling even when you've heard them a 100 times before. I love them so much.I also feel like I need to add context; Creatures will essentially give you a warning with “flashing” (a glow on certain parts of their body whilst they're sleeping, as a warning that they are aware of you), and a “beating” sound, when they are now quite aware of you moving/making noises/flashing your torches at them. You get the 2 stage warning before they scream and wake themselves and everyone else around.: Extremely clean, great intro into the game and honestly sets the tone extremely well. A nice array of settings to fiddle with, and they give you every option you could want to add friends into your game. Copying lobby code, invite through steam and/or matchmaking which is still in it's early stages.: I finally owed writing a review for this game, considering it is in my 10 top favorite games of all time. GTFO, does not care for your incompetence, if you cannot learn from your mistakes, learn how to deal with the enemies that are presented to you, maps, tactical placements of your gear, you will not win. I like to annoy people with calling this “The Dark Souls of Shooters”, and honestly whilst I started that as a meme, It's fairly true. GTFO is difficult, and it takes pride in being that. It takes pride in the fact you will spend up to 4 hours on a run, to make one mistake and have to restart the whole thing, but somehow, it's never punishing enough that you don't want to play it, you see exactly where you went wrong, and how to correct it when you try again.. Not many games have that, and it's one of my favorite parts of this game that shines above most.Further things I want to highlight; no perks, no cosmetics, no DLC's (they update the game with new rundowns and get rid of the old level packs as time goes by, so you have a constant variation of levels to play through), the whole game stands well enough on it's own and has solid gunplay, gameplay and even just that smidge of story hidden amongst the cracks to make it a well rounded, fun, engaging experience. Nothing beats that “Expedition Survived” screen though, and once you've triumphed through it all, that screen is the best thing you will ever see.Now with all that aside, this game definitely isn't for everyone, and it genuinely plays and feels better when you have a consistent team. You build new strats together, communication flows better, I can't imagine this being fun with randoms, but they have a tone of servers for players looking for people to join them, and now they have matchmaking through popular demand. I understand that having 3-4 people to play with isn't an easy thing to have.Also something else to note; GTFO does NOT scale. It is the same difficulty all the way through (They have added even more content and challenge with extra higher difficulties and areas to explore and complete). Enemies also are partly randomly generated, but levels will have specific caps and requirements (e.g 1 scout, 1 titan, 20 sleepers) so enemies will not be in the same place, unless it's one of the level specific mutants, even then it can still be in a different area. Whilst I've seen this game get a lot of flack over not scaling to less players, it honestly would not work, and it would not be the game they have wonderfully crafted to this point. It needs that brutal, cooperative experience, that will probably start arguments with your friends.This is a labor of love, you can tell. I can't praise the developers enough for making an early access game feel more polished and be one of the best co-op games I've played to date (Which by the way, there are (last I checked) 9 developers working on this game. 9!!!) GTFO honestly deserve so much more praise and love than it gets and I highly recommend it to anyone who likes tactical shooters that offer a challenge with friends!

_childDocuments_.review: GTFO is an fantastic evolution of the fps genre...! But...PROS!- 4 player coop - challenging but fair- retro ideas re-imagined - lore rich that isn't shoved in your face!!!CONS...- Derpy coop AI- some levels are too long- hard to convince friends to play (lol)I gotta say that this is by far the most criminally underrated game, at least that I've ever played. Too long has the fps genre been trying to add ideas and features that are either niche, trendy, or at worst damaging to its roots. Here? We have a game that doesn't hold back any punches, mixing the adrenaline filled firefights with the oddly satisfying resource management and computer terminal interactions that happens along the way. The weapon selection is some of the best I've seen with pros and cons to your choices to really encourage a mixed loadout approach for all players to go in as prepared as possible. Shall I elaborate? Nah! Experimentation is more fun anyway! Plus the devs are adding back new to toys each rundown update so there's a little something new to try out.Mostly great so far right? NOT SO FAST! There are a few quirks to keep in mind that cannot be overlooked... It pains me to say that a majority of these missions, are not for the faint of heart, if you don't have an hour at minimum to play at a time then you won't accomplish much, That's right, a whole hour. That can be a rather tall ask if I do say so myself. Especially when a few of the expeditions don't have checkpoints... Ouch...Its because of this, I can't recommend this to solo players, sure you can get some of the rundowns done with the bots, but they suffer from the odd... quirkiness... making them at best glorified meatbags. They try their best to ration resources but they do this automatically at will prioritize the player above all else, sounds great before you realize that they will often give you too much and waste it, or use it when the situation REALLY does not call for it. ie, Heal you in the middle of combat instead of shooting the thing attacking you, disinfect you while in the middle of poisonous fog that you cannot see in or steal resources you don't want them taking. Another odd quirk is their random points of being down right stupid, running through a door you wanna close and getting stuck, getting in front of your line of fire, or not placing their tools when you tell them to. I could go on and on but in all honesty? This is a game that you play with 3 of your friends so... whatever right? The game is great, tell your friends, bribe or guilt trip them to play with you because good gravy it is fun and rewarding. (don't actually do that but for real convince them to try it at least)

_childDocuments_.review: Challenging co-op in a dark, lo-fi sci-fi world. Emphasis on stealth, problem solving and teamwork.THE GOODFuture industrial aesthetic similar to Blade Runner or Alien.Satisfying stealth gameplay and puzzle solving.Command line interfaces that feel immersive and reward mastery.Potential for speedrunning and self-imposed challenges (solo, duo runs etc.)While you may wipe often it's almost always clear why you failed and what could be done better on the next attempt.Creative enemy design, a disgusting parasitic spore/deep sea/puppeteer infection with body horror.The rundown model is novel and should prevent the meta ever becoming stale or 'solved'.Gunplay feels satisfying.No stat-tracking, definitely reduces the pressure and stress when it comes to repeated fails.NO microtransactions of any sort (and the devs have pledged to avoid anything that would lead to any in-game advantage).THE BADNo matchmaking yet: although the community discord is friendly and mostly patient with new players.Rundowns (at least for early access) aren't there in their turnaround speed just yet.P2P servers makes desync and lag a serious issue, especially with both stealth and shooting; making enemies warp around in combat and making you feel unfairly seen when you thought you were safe.YOU. WILL. DIE. A lot. Don't buy this if you get frustrated easily with fail states.No stat-tracking! This might be an issue if you're the type who wants to show off.Some serious interface bugs (e.g. don't trust the overlaid HUD for teammate's health/ammo readouts! Use the map screen!).Some immersion breaking bugs/exploits which can trivialise some encounters.Speaking of which, once you grok the game mechanics the horror and tension is dispelled (though this is true of ALL survival horror games)In summary though I highly recommend the game, the negatives are all fixable and likely if you enjoy the central premise and what is here now you won't regret a purchase. I would only say avoid for sure if as I said, you hate failing a lot. This game doesn't ♥♥♥♥ about!

_childDocuments_.review: The game is really fun, but it has some key details that hold me back from recommending it. See below:-Very scary and atomspheric. The fog to the ambient noises, this game is really creepy and has a cinematic vibe to it unlike anything I've ever played.-Great sound effects and voice acting. The character VAing, or what little there is, is very well done and the sound effects of the monsters are bone-chilling.-Very unique menu and intro. I usually don't make the menu a pro in my reviews, but the menu and opening cutscene to this game perfectly illustrates what type of game it is, and sets the mood perfectly.-Gets updated frequently. This should really be a given with most EA titles, but here it is present moreso. Weapons, levels, and enemies are updated pretty frequently and they have a lengthy list of features they will add to the game and if it all gets added, this will certainly be worth the price.-New Rundowns come fast and are completely new levels. The Devs tailor make new batches of levels and release them depending on what levels people have finished. Each are pretty unique to eachother and offer an amazing challenge.-Long levels. Each level takes an half hour to sometimes an hour and half to finish, especially the harder levels.-VERY challenging and it takes careful planning and communication to finish each level. The levels here are extremely tough and make each person a necessity to carefully plan and finish levels using the right tools, as well as careful communication. Voice Chat is a NECESSITY to beat levels here.-Little to no bugs. In my entire time playing (which isn't too long but I will still keep this on here), I have encountered only one bug which is miraculous for an early access game (monster got stuck in the corner of a door). They clearly worked hard on optimizing the game, which most EA developers put in the backlog so they can roll out more P2P content.-NO MATCHMAKING!!! Fanboys may defend this by saying to use discord, which you need to find others to play with, but asking people to download another program to match with other players is absurd. If you have friends however you should be fine, but no MMing really hurts this game's playerbase as well. It is coming in the future, but as of now not having it is devastating.-No unlockables. I hear this is coming in the future so I might change my review then, but as of now there really isn't a reason to keep playing after you beat all the levels (which are long, but there are roughly 8 atm that are updated every few months.-Barely any enemy types. There are like 4 in total right now, but some levels have only like 2 types show up in TOTAL. Some variety could really help here.-No way to play old levels. Once a rundown ends (even if it was up for quite a while) you cannot play those levels again, which is a shame if people really like levels from the first rundown and wanna play them. I'm not really seeing this in their plans anytime soon either, so I don't think this will be added.In conclusion, GTFO is certainly interesting, but I would wait a few months for more essential features to be added before buying into this game. However, if you have some friends and want a fun game to jump into, this can be a fun time. Just be aware some major features are missing, and that you are buying this to help the developers finish their game.

If the answer is no then do not purchase. The game is way to difficult as a single player game and is not designed to work well solo. So in conclusion buy this game if you have long periods of time without major interruption, horror games, and most importantly, have people to play with.TLDR:  TRADITIONAL FRENCH CASSOULET1 pound (454g) dried cannellini beans3 tablespoons (27g) Diamond Crystal kosher salt; for table salt, use half as much by volume or the same weight5 cups (1.2L) homemade or store-bought unsalted chicken stock, divided (see notes)3 packets unflavored gelatin (3/4 ounce; 21g), such as Knox (optional, see notes)2 tablespoons (30ml) duck fat (optional)8 ounces (227g) salt pork, cut into 3/4-inch cubes (about 1 1/4 cups)8 ounces (227g) boneless pork shoulder, cut into 1-inch cubes4 skin-on, bone-in chicken thighs, 4 fresh duck legs, or 4 prepared duck confit legsFreshly ground black pepper1 pound (454g) garlic sausage (divided into 2-4 segments, if sausage is large)1 large onion (12 ounces; 340g), finely diced (about 1 1/2 cups)1 carrot (4 ounces;113g), unpeeled and cut into 3-inch sections2 ribs celery (6 1/2 ounces; 188g), cut into 3-inch sections1 whole head garlic (2 3/4 ounces; 80g)4 sprigs flat-leaf parsley2 bay leaves6 clovesSTEPS1) In a large bowl, cover beans with 3 quarts (2.8L) water and add salt. Stir to combine, then let stand at room temperature overnight. Drain and rinse beans; set aside.2) Adjust oven rack to lower-middle position and preheat oven to 325°F (160°C). Place 4 cups (946ml) stock in a large liquid measuring cup and sprinkle gelatin, if using, over top. Set aside. In a large Dutch oven, heat duck fat (if using), salt pork, and pork shoulder and cook over high heat, stirring occasionally, until browned all over, about 9 minutes (if not using duck fat, cook pork with no additional fat). Using a slotted spoon, transfer to a large bowl, leaving rendered fat in Dutch oven, and set aside.3) Season chicken thighs or duck confit with pepper (do not add salt) and place skin side down in Dutch oven. Cook without moving until well-browned, 6 to 8 minutes. Transfer to a plate and let cool to room temperature.4) Add sausages to Dutch oven and cook, turning occasionally, until well-browned, about 2 minutes per side. Transfer to bowl with salt pork. Drain all but 2 tablespoons fat from pot.5) Add onions to Dutch oven and cook, stirring and scraping up browned bits from bottom of pot, until onions are translucent but not browned, about 4 minutes. Add drained beans, carrot, celery, garlic, parsley, bay leaves, cloves, and stock/gelatin mixture. Bring to a simmer over high heat. Reduce to low, cover Dutch oven, and cook until beans are slightly softened but retain a bite, about 20 minutes.6) Cover cooled chicken or duck and transfer to refrigerator. Using tongs, remove carrots, celery, parsley, bay leaves, and cloves from pot and discard. Add pork and sausages to pot and stir to incorporate. Beans should be almost completely submerged. Transfer to oven and cook, uncovered, adding remaining 1 cup (237ml) stock halfway through by pouring it carefully down side of pot as necessary to keep beans mostly covered, until a thin crust forms on top, about 1 hour 30 minutes.7) Break crust with a spoon and shake pot gently to redistribute. Nestle chicken or duck into the Dutch oven, skin side up. Return to oven and continue cooking, stopping to break and shake crust every 30 minutes, until crust is deep brown and thick, an additional 1 hour 30 minutes. Serve immediately.

_childDocuments_.review: GTFO is an initially enticing, but ultimately superficial game which encourages a slow, cautious, exploratory playstyle, but does little to reward or incentivize it. It seems like an honest and genuine effort to make something that is approachable, while also being "hardcore" enough for gamers who don't want to be treated like idiots. They seem to have meant well and have had a clear idea in mind. I'm especially glad they tried to make a cooperative game in an era where PVP still seems to be the big ticket. Relatively short sessions that don't require too much involvement, but punish players for being mindless or not working together. I think that the game may have needed a little more time on the drawing board though. Unfortunately, where the game prides itself as being complicated, it ends up being more simply tedious, with sort of arbitrary padding and repetitive objectives requiring similar, slightly fiddly interactions making up the bulk of play time. THe use of command line terminals in games as a means of interacting with the world is interesting as a diegetic interaction, but it feels overused here. Most levels consist of some variation of 1. Pick up large item that prevents one player from firing or interacting. 2. Proceed to terminal for instructions on what to do with item. 3. Terminal out of range of objective. Proceed to area XX for terminal. 4. Zone XX inaccessible. Proceed to zone XY for terminal to find keycard. 5. Keycard out of range. Proceed to zone XZ. 6. Find terminal in XZ. 7. Locate keycard and bring it back to the first important door. Find terminal. 8. Terminal inaccessible. Proceed to zone YX to find keycard. Rinse, repeat.  I don't know that it's overall a bad idea, per se, but to me it feels like command line terminals in video games are to tension, as jumpscares are to horror. They feel artificial and they are frustrating for the wrong reason. Everything feels arbitrarily tedious and there is not a lot of narrative reward in return for this tedium. The game isn't really a thinking game either as so many describe it. The solution to every problem I've encountered in four hours is crouch with your light off, don't move when enemies are glowing or making noise, use charged melee weapons to quickly eliminate them if you have to, and save your ammo and sentry turrets for alarmed doors. I will try again during the next rundown and may revise this if the levels are more interesting. But right now most of the fun seems like it's meant to come from social interactions facilitated by the game, rather than the game itself.

_childDocuments_.review: This has become my most beloved game in my Steam Library. I can't recommend it enough to those who like a slow paced, cooperative, thrilling, hardcore experience. I'm gonna go into some Pros, Cons, and things that could be improved with this game that I've found, which will be updated as the game is significantly updated in the future.-=Pros=-- The graphics, designs, atomsphere, fog, and lighting are all impeccable; some of the best I've seen from an Indie Dev. (Although better Entity/Player shadows would be appreciated)- Sound design is amazing and immerses you instantly.    - Music as well really makes you feel calmed, on edge, or panicked depending on what's happening.- Pacing is solid, and doesn't rush you along when you don't have to. You can prepare accordingly and feel prepared enough to handle security doors (alarms).- All these come together to provide a truly exciting and terrifying experience, even at its slow pace.-=Cons/Things to be Improved=-- Sleepers (the monsters) animations are a bit jumpy and inconsistent. They can be hard to follow, as they sometimes jump a few frames in their animation and can look a bit rough. This may be due to connection or latency, but it needs to be addressed.- Gunplay feels a bit clunky and unsatisfying. It's an artificial recoil feel, and doesnt feel punchy in the slightest. Some of the gun sounds can be adjusted too to make the gun just feel better to shoot.-=Matchmaking/Partying Up=-This gets its own category because it's not really a pro or con for me personally, just something to address in the review.There currently is no implemented matchmaking or voice chat in the game, and it's not something that bothers me after taking a critical look at it.1. This game REQUIRES cooperation. If the matchmaking hadn't been implemented right at launch, arguably this would have made the game worse overall.2. The Discord usage for matchmaking and finding groups is really solid currently. It encourages people to be serious about what they're getting into and find people they want to party with, and I've made a few friends in my adventures this way, as Discord is high quality and easy to use.3. VOIP is hard to correctly implement! With a dev team of 9, I'm happy they're taking the time to do it right. (It should be directional though, if you're reading this devs! Just take your time!)-=Conclusion=-Overall this game is THE most solid early access game I've purchased. So few bugs, so much challenge, high fidelity, and a great foundation for this game to grow. Plus with their Rundown System and everything I've heard in interviews and in their AMAs, this game is shaping up to be one of the best coop experiences out here, albeit hardcore. At its current state: 8.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: GTFO is a game that definitely could have been good -- great, even, but I really don't think it's worth your time or money. Despite a strong first few hours, as you acquaint yourself with the game systems and enemies, the experience of actually sitting down to the game becomes a repetitive chore extremely quickly. The approach to absolutely every problem is nearly identical, the weapons are hit-and-miss (as far as feel goes), and what little context you're provided with is not only very poorly presented, with voice-acting straight from 'The Scenery Chewer's Guide to Overdoing It', but also has little-to-no reflection in the environment, which given its anonymous aesthetic and lack of integration with the telling of the story, feels procedurally generated, even though I'm given to understand that it was not.If you can sustain yourself through the repetitive trudge of the primary loop with nothing but the barest mechanical escalation and piss-weak context that roundly fails to tie it all together, there is a solid foundation here. Once you've found a gun that feels right for you, the shooting usually feels good, and the atmosphere is, for the first few levels you play, consistently oppressive and really rather solid. But GTFO only has one mood -- oppressive. Were it a single player game, it might feel genuinely horrifying, and legitimately desperate.But the multiplayer barrier to entry, and the episodic nature of the mission-based format, gives rise to my main issue -- you never feel genuinely trapped. Because of the episodic nature of the missions within the rundowns, we leave at the end of every mission and go back in at the start of the next one, and any sense of hopeless isolation is irretrievably lost. That episodic, mission-based framing doesn't work as well here as it does in an aesthetically grim game mission-based multiplayer shooter like Darktide, though, because Darktide is in fact a very silly game with a great deal of humour in its world, even if it is only sporadically successfully funny. GTFO has no such tonal contrast in its presentation, and the inherent sense of detachment the format is therefore catastrophic to the intended oppressive tone for me.Ultimately, it's the sort of thing that would benefit from a sequel or remake -- add some even halfway-decent story context, and integrate it with the environment in a way that is meaningful, and you could have something genuinely special. But GTFO is ultimately extremely unspecial, with nothing really to recommend it other than "it's very difficult and acceptably passes the time between cradle and grave".

_childDocuments_.review: Each update seems to introduce features that the vast majority of the player base seems to find either frustrating (respawn rooms), unenjoyable (stamina), or takes away from the learning curve (hammers now have 5x stagger and can 1 shot stun all giant enemies). Let's go through some history.R1 was release. The game was "spooky" at best but it was fun.R2 released a ~ 3 months later. It stepped up the game's mechanics, introducing infection and environmental hazards like spitters. It also introduced the "E Tier" levels where difficulty is at it's peak. Great rundown, though quite dated now.R3 releases just 2 1/2 months later. Referred to as "baby's first R2" as it was basically just R2 but the levels were easier. Massive downgrade in quality of content. The rundown was out for 4 months and was so bad that it spawned the GTFO Modding community because it was so unenjoyable.R4 releases and introduces "optional difficult content" except it's not optional and progression is actually locked behind this content, so they weren't able to actually make the optional content hard like it was promised to be. This update also introduced the "precision" system, which allows different guns to deal different headshot multipliers. They used this system to... nerf every single gun in the game by setting all of the guns below 1.0x headshot damage. Cool.R5 releases and adds an enemy that can be created in quite literally 30 seconds with no interesting new content, but serves as effectively a "level pack" as a rundown does. "Respawn sacks" were shoehorned in to try to force a new game play mechanic that prevents backtracking. The mechanic's tell is that there are cocoons on the ceiling. There is no audio or visual effect tied to these to suggest that they respawn enemies, and new players often think that the enemies respawning is actually a bug and not an intended feature. This rundown was out for 8 months. You read that correctly.R6 releases and adds a stamina system that the community simply tolerates because it's impossible to enjoy and doesn't truly solve the issues that it was meant to solve. It simply makes the game play slower, which doesn't make it play any better. The skill ceiling of melee was massively gutted in this rundown (see: solo gameplay of R5 vs R6 for melee comparison). Sledgehammer becomes a mindless instant stunlock monster but not very great against small enemies? Somehow this is backwards from what it was prior. Broken checkpoint system added that bricks runs, and might as well not be introduced until it's actually working properly. Massive enemy position desync bug added in a hotfix, massively complained about, but not reverted. This is important (bug introduced January 27th 2022 via hotfix).R7 releases as a free weekend. The enemy position desync bug has not properly been acknowledged or addressed in any capacity. Steam reviews plummet with free weekenders complaining about bugs (most of which are actually long standing bugs) and getting objective items stuck in their hands, ending their run. The developers finally after many months publicly address the enemy desync issue and checkpoint objective stuck bugs that make the game extraordinarily unfun to play before they go on vacation.So where does this leave us? The game has long since started to go down hill long ago. New features added are not great, often unfinished, or straight up broken (host migration). If you couldn't tell by my hours, I obviously enjoy this game a lot more than I should. It might be worth mentioning that a lot of my hours are actually just me on the rundown screen with VSCode open creating custom modded content to not have to tolerate very lengthy content droughts. This game has an absolutely incredible core structure, but the devs seem to introduce interesting mechanics in the most unfun possible ways. R7 is probably even their best rundown to date in terms of quality of content, but the state of the game itself is absolutely at it's worst it's ever been since public release. I want to, but I can not recommend GTFO in the current state. At this point, I blow through their 6 months worth of content in a day or two depending on how much attention to the lore I give, then exclusively mod the game for the rest of my play time.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game that only seems to be getting better, and is better than any AAA title I have played in years. It is a difficult coop shooter that requires communication, cooperation and using your brain. Great eerie atmosphere, a bit of a learning curve. Prepare to die, over and over. And then over again. The game punishes you for your mistakes, sometimes more than others. There is a steep learning curve, especially as you progress into later tiers.There are many areas where stealth is essential, and having someone alert the wrong room by accident can be a huge problem sometimes, and depending on the skill of the group this may be able to recover, or they can wipe. There are still plenty of moments where you are shooting, running and gunning, or just embracing hammertime. The better you get with melee, the more supplies you can potentially conserve when things go loud.Guns are decently balanced, each with their own strengths and weakness. Coordinating loadouts with your group is also essential to survive. Melee weapons are essentially all the same currently though.I'm a big fan of how they are doing the story personally, and from what I can tell, the devs are taking the time to develop a fascinating story over time as well.Only 2 major downsides are Bunnyhop stealthing, which both looks silly and breaks the immersion a little. You shouldnt be able to sprint jump around and make as much noise as a croucher, or even less. That just doesnt make sense.Cheesing(the common term used in the community), which is basically cheating. This is where you can sit in a spot where no enemies, or most enemies cannot attack you, but you are able to strike them. Sometimes even with just your melee weapon, using no supplies whatsoever. That's just a blatant abuse of an obvious bug to complete content some players would be otherwise incapable of. I'm sure these will be addressed over time though.

_childDocuments_.review: Time to update this from my previous 40 hour review to present 1.0 release time.Played since April 2020 (rundown 2).First I want to mention that the game does state you cannot play the previous rundowns, however you can still play the previous via Google shared files that are bundled with VRMODs if you wish to try. Not only do you have the oppotunity to play the current rundown but the previous have been archived. You cannot get banned or lose your copy of the game, the devs are fair with mods in private instances and in total you will have 6 whole rundowns available of time of buying as of this review! 200+ hours into this game and I still have yet to personally finish every level from each rundown, if that isn't content for people who are the next potential fans of the game, I don't what is.Now the actual review:An all time favourite game of mine to date. A solid hardcore team based PvE FPS, lots of replayability, each mission attempt is always slightly different from the last.  Challenging objective based missions now with a variety of objectives and tasks that will have a drastic effect on the entire level. Example: Poisonous fog spread throughout the level, optional objective available to go complete that will then remove the fog from the main objective. A high risk, high reward for doing the optional as they will be more slightly more challenging than the main mission itself but never necessary to complete.Gameplay loop: It's consistently the same throughout the game, stealth is a requirement, run n gun is possible but will punish you unless it's a mission that is mayhem from the start with constant mobs being spawned to attack you periodically. Simple loop: Stealth -> strategic wave defense -> objective -> stealth/ chaotic madness.I've always found the game to be decently optimized from my experience and others i've played with on low-mid range PCs. I.E i7700k with GTX 970 and still capable of getting 120+ fps consistently on medium graphics.Difficulty: The game will always be optimized for 4-player coop, there is now bots with 1.0 release. I cannot comment on the bots as I'll probably never use them but levels can be solo'd with a great deal of time and effort + high level fundamental understanding of the game. I do not recommend solo play for new players.There is matchmaking via player hosted lobbies, just like every game, your teammates skillset will be varied and can lead to either a great or not so fun experience. HOWEVER, the GTFO discord has LFG (looking for group) channels that are regionally separated if you want to jump straight in with some randoms who are eager to progress throughout the game! Highly recommend this, there is a short guide on the discord how to properly advertise your lobby if you choose to host than join others yourself.This review can easily go on and on but GTFO is 100% worth every penny especially when it's discounted. Anyone in small gaming communities that enjoy working together to achieve the same goal, this game is made for FPS enthusiasts or the coop lovers. Your aim may be great but is your strategy and problem solving skills equally as good. GTFO over the last 2 years has only got better and better with time, very easy game to pick up and play, put and down and come back to whenever. It does not force you to commit every day of your life to it so enjoy it to your hearts content.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; 7/10 decent game if you get a group.Review: It's a pretty good co-op FPS game that blends stealth, resource management, and teamwork. The atmosphere is great and the level of polish is up there. The mindset is hardcore, and it's necessary because GTFO is not a 1,2, or 3 player game(unless you're godlike). So naturally the hardest thing about GTFO is convincing 3 of your friends to also purchase and play with you and hope they enjoy it too. Or if you don't have friends then the discord is active.  There is also an in game matchmaking system, but the majority of the community playing uses the integrated discord matchmaking system. The developers add features and redo the levels every couple of months, so its like a new 10-40 hour game every time they update it.Suggestions: More interactions with the environment (things you might knock over by accident, traps, distraction mechanics?). Maybe some more of those run and gun sections where you mow down monsters for our more smooth brained teammates so they don't get bored of stealth, like maybe a clear the elevator drop zone or fight room to room down a more linear path between levels A1 and A2 or something.

_childDocuments_.review: The most beautifully challenging game I have ever played. I have been playing this game since Rundown 3, and we are now in version 1.0, Rundown 6, and every second I have spent playing this game, both with friends and solo has given me a truly lovable challenge. Never has a game made me want to win, or simply accomplish a goal so badly. The first time I beat a few levels filled me with more joy than anything I can remember in all my years of gaming. I then learned the game, closely studied it's mechanics, and took on Rundown 4, level A1 Extreme solo, and after many attempts, and multiple strategies, I beat it, and experienced pure, concentrated ecstasy. Looking back on it, that level was child's play, and that's one of the beauties of GTFO, it gets harder. It forces you to get better. The fun, for me, more than anything in this game, is this exact relationship, of learning how overcome such a daunting challenge, learning to make no mistakes, and winning, not because you got lucky, but because of you and your team's newfound skill, and knowledge. It has it's rough patches, some bugs, some mechanics that are a bit much for my taste, a few sections throughout the game since Rundown 3 that I considered to be unfair, or simply annoying, but all in all, the game seems to be heading in a good direction, the aspects I've loved are finally being fleshed out, and most importantly, what I love about this game still hasn't faded, the beautiful challenge of it all.

_childDocuments_.review: You walk down a staircase. It's almost pitch black, but you know you saw something glow for a moment. You know you heard something clicking. You turn on your flashlight for a moment. You catch four figures in your light. They might have been human once, but whatever they are now you know they'll kill you if you aren't careful. One of your allies ask what's going on, and you tell them. They coordinate with you to take to positions to stealth kill these creatures, stopping every now and then when one of the creatures starts gyrating and glowing in time with their heartbeat, hoping nobody alerts them. Eventually, they all get as close they can to one of these creatures, and one of them says something like this: "Okay, on my mark. Three. Two. One. Charge."You raise your mallet above your head, preparing to bring it down through the head and into the chest of the thing in front of you.Some time later, you're standing next to a set of two doors. You've closed one off and put a turret next to the other. It doesn't have many rounds in it, but neither do you, or your friends. They've managed to clear most of the next room while you were checking a computer, so you leave the fallback point you set up and try and sneak over to your allies. Halfway there, you hear something scream, one of your allies cussing, and music starting. You run back to the door without a turret, pinging the control panel so your allies can see it through the dark. You call to them to head through this one. As the last of them comes through, the awakened sleepers giving chase, you hit the panel and close the door. You toss a c-foam grenade at the closed door, and it goes off. The foam quickly expands between the door's slats and hardens, sealing it shut. Your turret chimes a small warning before firing off a burst at the sleepers that came in through the other door. Your allies use the last of their rounds to pick off any sleepers that run out of the turret's detection radius while you level your combat shotgun towards the door you sealed off. Some of them are banging on the other side, slowly breaking down the foam, and then the metal. The slats bend towards you like a busted ribcage as they try and pour through the opening. You empty your shotgun into the mass.Moments like these cover two parts of the average GTFO experience. It still has a ways to go, and games can take quite some time, but moments of tension in cooperation like these that make it an experience unlike any other I've had for a while.

_childDocuments_.review: (Updated review for Rundown 7) I really really like this game, but in its  state i just simply cannot reccomend it to anyone at all, so here's some of the good & bad things about the game in my own opinion. • Rewarding play from both mechanical skill & game knowledge. As in knowing how certain mechanics work really rewards you, and from observing your surroundings rather than just walking into rooms of sleeping enemies with no care in the world. So you get rewarding for paying attention a lot.• The tense feeling and atmosphere. Even if the games atmosphere has regressed, that doesn't stop it from being incredibly tense and makes you feel on edge (at least when starting out with the game).• Level design. The level design is quite thought through now in Rundown 7 and good, over all the level designs are nice and good. Only a plus from me.• MASSIVE performance issues compared to prior versions of the game, which makes this game feel incredibly awful to play. (i. e. playing on a consistent almost never dropping 60+ FPS in prior versions, to then have massive dips in FPS during normal gameplay. And even more severely going down to half of your FPS in certain scenarios (which would never happen prior))• Atmospherically the game has regressed majorly. From its dreadfully cold feeling of traversing the complex prior, to what can only be explained as a fever dream in the current version of the game. (besides some few levels feeling at the very least, slightly like the older levels atmospherically.• The lack of replayability. You can argue that this is a game you're supposed to 'play' once new content release, and then wait for new content after finishing it. As in the 'Rundown' Concept is cool and all, but it just doesn't cut it if the levels are not replayable  with stuff such as more substantially major optional objectives to do. Then 6-7 months inbetween major content drops just doesn't sit well.• Bugs as 'Features'. By this i mean the sheer amount of game breaking bugs that have become rather easy to encounter through normal gameplay. This includes bugs and major exploits that have persisted since much older versions of the game.• Checkpoints >:( Checkpoints overall in Rundown 7 are well placed and used generally speaking in the game. They however are still riddled with as many bugs as before, so still not a quality addition for the game in their current state.There's lots of other things I'd like to list, both good & bad, including rather bad things that have happened in the community and how communication and certain parts of the game is being handled between Devs and players. Well anyhow, i think this is comprehensive enough to get my opinion across.But I am giving this game a negative rating due to aforementioned issues heavily outweighting the positives as of now. I am hoping for Rundown 7 to at the very least adress the current performance issues, as they make the game borderline unenjoyable and unplayable for an FPS title of this type. Hopefully they give me enough of a reason to give this review a positive rating in the future.This game has massive amounts of potential, and has already shown us so much incredible stuff. I just hope they step up their game and start developing the game. Might just be me, but oh well. Additionally i want to divert the people that are really interested in GTFO as a whole, over to another community members video on the game that can be found , and why in its current state is simply unacceptable. Big shout out and thanks to Khepri.

_childDocuments_.review: GTFO is exactly what it says it is. A 4 player horror shooter, you are 4 humans armed with as much ammo as you can carry on your vest IRL in an area full of monsters that will happily and quickly kill you. Some times you an objective or the layout of spawns in a room makes it your best option to go loud so dont believe reviews that this game only lets you stealth. There is a decent amount of stealth if you want to play efficiently but if your a good shot you can make your ammo go a long way. Body shots do next to nothing, these things are zombies, they dont need a body to survive so if your spraying and praying then you run out of rounds and your a goner. But when you complete a map the feeling of satisfaction you get is wonderful. I have not tried the matchmaking and would highly recommend playing with friends or finding guys on the subreddit who want to actually play to win.

_childDocuments_.review: Heart-Pounding Cooperative Horror Experience - 8/10GTFO, developed by 10 Chambers Collective, is an intense cooperative first-person shooter that pushes players to their limits in a harrowing and atmospheric underground world. With its focus on teamwork, strategic gameplay, and unforgiving challenges, this game offers a unique and adrenaline-pumping horror experience that will leave you on the edge of your seat.From the moment you step into the eerie underground complex, GTFO sets a tense and foreboding atmosphere that never lets up. The game excels at building an oppressive ambiance, with dimly lit corridors, grotesque enemies lurking in the shadows, and an ominous soundscape that keeps you constantly on guard. The attention to detail and atmospheric design make every step a nerve-wracking experience.At the core of GTFO lies its cooperative gameplay, where communication and coordination are essential. Playing with a team of four, you must work together to overcome the deadly threats and solve complex objectives. Each player has a specific role with unique abilities and tools, emphasizing the importance of teamwork and strategic planning. The cooperative mechanics are finely tuned, rewarding players who communicate effectively and adapt to the ever-evolving challenges.The gameplay in GTFO is unforgiving and demands precision. Combat encounters are intense and require careful resource management and decision-making. Ammo and supplies are scarce, forcing players to prioritize targets and strategize their approach. The enemies, known as "sleepers," are formidable and will punish reckless play. The thrill of survival and the sense of accomplishment that comes with overcoming overwhelming odds make each successful mission a truly exhilarating experience.The level design in GTFO is intricate and masterfully crafted. Each expedition into the underground complex presents a unique set of challenges, ranging from navigating labyrinthine corridors to deciphering cryptic puzzles. The game encourages exploration, rewarding players who uncover hidden caches and secrets. The sense of progression and discovery adds depth and replayability to the overall experience.While GTFO excels in many areas, it's worth noting that the game's difficulty can be overwhelming for some players. The steep learning curve and the relentless nature of the challenges may deter those seeking a more casual or relaxed experience. However, for those seeking a thrilling cooperative horror adventure that pushes them to their limits, GTFO delivers in spades.In terms of visuals and audio, GTFO impresses with its gritty and atmospheric presentation. The dark and claustrophobic environments, combined with the haunting musical score, create a sense of dread that permeates every moment of gameplay. The attention to detail in both the visuals and sound design contributes to the immersive and chilling atmosphere.GTFO is a must-play for fans of cooperative shooters and horror enthusiasts. Its challenging gameplay, emphasis on teamwork, and atmospheric world create a pulse-pounding experience like no other. If you're ready to face your fears and test your mettle in a relentless and immersive underground nightmare, GTFO is waiting to deliver an unforgettable cooperative horror adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: There is or might have previously been a good game here, but best of luck finding it. I've played multiple stages of this game for several hours: the beta, early adopter/early access and release phase. The game plays at having a slew of loadout options, with unique pros and cons to each, a unique terminal/computer interaction system and a healthy mixture of stealth and gunplay.The reality is far more boring. The instant that you realize that you can clump up, sprint your way through rooms as a group and mow down enemies with your melee weapons before they can scream for help, and that you can bypass almost everything that makes the terminal system engaging with a few simple shortcut commands, it will shatter any illusion you had that this game is supposed to be difficult. Matches will take an extremely long time to finish the way the game was "meant" to be played, actively encouraging you to  slide down the slippery slope into banality.This is a game where the enjoyment is supposed to be derived from overcoming its difficult through teamwork; no difficulty, no enjoyment.. no fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you have great memories of Left 4 Dead? AND atmospheric horror like Alien Isolation? Well GTFO is the perfect blending of atmospheric horror and mad, horde-smashing action. You and your band of merry convicted friends will have heart-stopping moments as you try to sneak your way past the slumbering monsters, contrasted with frantic firefights as you try to hold off wave after wave of these terrifying beasts with your favourite lead-pumper. The Good:- For a very early version of the game it is extremely stable, smooth and bug-free. At 35 hours playtime I've had no crashes, and seen no game-play affecting glitches. - The gameplay is a lot of fun. Seriously, it's just a mechanically pleasing game. The Devs are continuing to roll-out new content that surprises and impresses. Even in it's first version they showed a lot of creativity in level design and making seemingly minor features into real challenges. If you're like me and don't enjoy looking up full playthroughs, you will have a great time finding all the ways things can work together. - It's only the beginning! Normally I'd always say be wary of early access but in this case that is a plus. Version 0.1 was a fully functional, enjoyable game. The fact that there is a lot more to look forward to before full release is a massive plus at this stage. The Bad:- This game is not really single-player accessable. You can start a level 1p and I've seen comments to suggest that it's possible. I don't consider myself a scrub but you would need to be a god-tier gamer to solo this game. If you don't have 3 friends, this game will probably feel like you're bashing your head against a wall. - You MUST have a stable internet connection. This is a game of high-level coordination and someone experiencing lagspikes or dropping out is probably going to cause a mission failure. It's not so much a fault of the game as it is a reality of the kind of experience they have created, but keep this in mind when considering your puchase. That's about it folks. Get out there and smoosh some monster heads with a sledge-hammer!

_childDocuments_.review: The actual game is fine. The gun play is fine. The graphics are good enough. The game-play loop is entertaining for the first bit.That's all the positives I had to say. This game is not "bad" per se, but it is full of so many small gripes that I legitimately think they all add up to make this game completely overshadowed by doing literally anything else with my time. I'll just list my gripes with no particular order.- The graphics are "over-rendered" with so many effects, fog, lighting artifacts, and motion sickness movements that instead of looking really pretty and impressive it just feels like a headache in a box with such little visibility I actually felt like I'd have better vision with a normal fps without all these annoying "dark moody" lighting systems on a 144p video. - The menus require click-and-hold on everything. EVERYTHING. From changing settings, selecting missions, quitting the game, inviting friends, it seems like everything in this game is just meant to feel clunky and annoying.- The enemies are not very varied. I mean, there is plenty of enemy variety but all of them are the same thing essentially. Fleshy person you shoot at and kill as fast as a L4D zombie. The special infected type monsters completely blend in with the rest of the enemies both literally and figuratively.- The game is incredibly simple in its complexity while entirely being so lacking in info to the players that you can't easily just do what you need to do. Our first game had us running in circles completely not having fun, and when we did figure out what to do, we just kinda though "Oh. That's it?"- This game is one of those games that builds itself up to be very skilled, complex, and strategic, but in actual gameplay, it's nothing like that. You just walk into area, shoot, and move on. The only thing that's "hard" about it is that you have as much health as a tissue box and resources are scarce.- The health system sucks. You don't really have a lot, which doesn't work in this game full of hits you couldn't avoid from how hard it is to see due to the way it's rendered as well as weird instances of friendly fire and other quirks that make you lose your health pretty unavoidably. The medkits are rare and don't even heal you fully. With how easily you lose health, there's basically no reason to heal. It's such a rare resource that you lose so easily, it's practically worthless. Made doubly true by the fact that once you're less than 20% health, you just auto-regen health. So We spent 90% of our game just at 20% and regen health which is not fun to do but also there's really no alternative. I really wanted to like this game. The Free Weekend I got to try it on was exciting at first, but we were with no exaggeration so bored out of our minds that we just all quit the game early before even playing longer than an hour. Does that make my review unfair since I haven't really experienced much of the game? Most definitely.Does the fact that this game I was interested in before is so boring that I didn't even care to play it long enough to form a fair opinion show pretty clearly how lack luster / clunky the game is? Most definitely.

_childDocuments_.review: GTFO is an amazing concept done very poorly.  I cannot see how anyone would have fun playing this game due to the massive amount of problems it has.  If these were all fixed or worked around, however, I think this could be a very enjoyable experience.  Pros- Visuals are quite good, even though I was playing with every single graphic setting on the lowest possible option.  - Horror is present but takes a sideline to stealth, action, and exploration, which seems to be intentional.  There is a small amount of actual fear, but the game seems to more be going for spooky or gloomy, which it succeeds in nicely.  - Resource management discourages combat, which sounds like a bad thing, but is again what the game is going for.  You are supposed to sneak around, with combat being a last resort or a fail safe.  If you shoot everything, you will die.  - The bio scanner only marking moving targets is a well designed way to balance out how strong the item is.  This system provides opportunities for players to work together, following the instructions of the scanner player to avoid monsters.  - Small details here or there really make the atmosphere that much more real.  Little splatters of enemy juice on your face from close range kills and the visual effect when shining a long range flashlight directly into someone's face make you feel like you are really in the facility.  Another example of this is the heavy breathing during the deployment cutscene at the beginning of each mission.  Truly masterful set dressing.  Cons- The tutorial is awful.  It doesn't teach you many of the button prompts needed to progress, provides no guidance on typing commands into consoles, and gives unclear instructions.  I spent a good 2 minutes trying to figure out what the correct command for the console was, and at the point where I was told to place a turret, I placed it facing the large obvious door instead of the much smaller door I just came through.  If this is just me being an idiot, fine, but the tutorial, which is designed to teach you the game, shouldn't just let me be an idiot.  It should teach me how to do what it wants me to do correctly, which it fails miserably in.  - The stealth isn't fun.  Stopping whenever a creature is pulsating is cinematic and cool, but not fun.  After the initial shock of "wuh oh, I gotta stop now!" the stealth ceases to be engaging, which is very unfortunate for a game that emphasizes stealth so heavily.  - The guns aren't great either.  There is no feedback for when your bullets connect or when something has died.  Amidst all the creatures running and crawling at you and the gunshots and exclamations of your friends, any visuals or audio indicating damage or a kill is lost.  I have stopped shooting at monsters several times believing them dead, only to be wrong.  - Friendly fire makes the game worse.  There are games where friendly fire forces you to use caution and its presence improves the gameplay experience.  This is not one of them.  When my friends and I just started, we tested if there was friendly fire with melee weapons and deduced there was not.  Because of this, we didn't worry about shooting each other.  Color us surprised when not only do guns have friendly fire, which isn't too bad, but turrets do as well.  The inconsistency of friendly fire alone is bad, but GTFO is not the type of game to benefit from friendly fire.  - Melee weapons are not fun.  The slow swinging and slow charging of melee weapons makes them unfun to use.  In a horror game, this makes sense.  Making the player feel weak by giving them weak defense options enhances the horror.  This is why Lethal Company lets you buy a shovel as a weapon, not a sword.  GTFO doesn't benefit from this design decision because it does empower you with firearms, turrets, and explosives, and because the horror takes a backseat to other things the game focuses on more.  - Navigation is unintuitive.  On our first run, my friends and I always took the doors whose numbers were closer to our target number.  Doing so for about 15 minutes led us to a dead end, where we then backtracked to the beginning and got on the real path towards the objective through a door that, through its number, told us was the wrong way.  The game seems to want you to go in the wrong direction.  I think it is good that these wrong directions exist, as sneaking around while checking doors for the most optimal path sounds like a good gameplay loop, but this only functions when the doors accurately relay information.  - Combat is both too punishing and not punishing enough.  Every time combat began, at least one of us, though usually two, went down.  This is far too punishing.  Yes, I'm sure we just suck, but going down to every single encounter just because we suck is not fun.  I am aware this game is designed to be difficult, but difficulty can be fun.  Elden Ring is fun difficulty.  Cuphead is fun difficulty.  Skul the Hero Slayer is fun difficulty.  GTFO's difficulty feels cheap and unfun.  That being said, combat is also not punishing enough.  While we do lose multiple people during each encounter, unlimited revives make this trivial.  As long as one of us is still standing, there is no punishment for the rest of us dropping, which doesn't disincentive combat as the other design choices of the game are trying to do.  - The game does not function.  I had to open the game six times just to turn down the graphics settings in the menu before I could play the game.  The game crashed five times before this happened, just during the intro cutscene.  If I were using a potato computer, sure, that would be tolerable, but I have a very good computer that is able to run other games typically thought of as requiring a good computer with no difficulty whatsoever.  For this reason, over anything else I have written in this review, I cannot recommend this game.  Steam is very nice and will provide a full refund if you have played less than two hours and have owned it for less than two weeks.  That is great, but when it took me 30 minutes just to begin the tutorial, and then another 15 or so to beat it, I wouldn't risk losing track of time and being unable to get a refund if you didn't like it with only an hour and change to experience the game. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a mixture of stealth and strategy. Of course, most mechanics are already decided for the player and won't be changing anytime soon.MECHANICS:-Light is used to see in dark spaces, but it can also be a double-edged sword when shining it onto enemies as you will alert them of you presence.-Weaponry consists of a Primary, Special, Equipment, and you can pick up tools or medical items in-game.There are varying levels of enemies that are all quite a handful at opportune times, but you'll manage.All-in-all I'd say to just check out the game and give it a try yourself with some friends or if your crazy attempt it alone. Whenever I play alone I am not bothered by other and take the time to learn the mechanics of the game and look for any exploits. Au Revoir, Hasta Luego y, Have a Good Time Running For Your LIFE!
