_childDocuments_.review: Yo! I'm here for my steam badge biyaash!!!Kidding aside, I highly recommend GTFO for anyone who's into a dark sci-fi procedural first-person dungeon crawler.You may notice that I did not mention the game being a horde shooter like Left 4 Dead or Vermintide because it's not. I DO NOT recommend this game to people who expect a horde shooter from it. Contrary to what most early marketing of GTFO and Youtuber let's plays make it out to be, GTFO is more about slowly and methodically clearing rooms in stealth than gunning down hordes of Naruto-running aliens/mutants.Unnecessary gunfights will deplete your resources. First Aid kits and Ammo packs don't necessarily fill up your status. There are no crowd control melee attacks or secondary weapons which means that every encounter with a horde will significantly drain either your health or ammo so the only good time to engage a horde is when you're forced to engage a horde. Resupplies are so rare that any significant expenditure early on will cost you and means the difference between actually finishing a level. Runs in GTFO also take a significant amount of time compared to horde shooters. Where clearing a level in L4D or Vermintide can happen within 20 minutes at the most, first time runs can take up to an hour and a half for new players and still around 45 minutes to an hour for more experienced players which does not include deciding to tackle side-vaults. It's easy to shrug off a bad run in other horde shooters when things go sour and try again. In GTFO, you end up wasting an hour or two of effort in your life. I remember the days when failing a run meant starting from the very beginning. They have since implemented checkpoints to the game, but you still need to set the expectation that runs still take a significant amount of time to accomplish. Progression in GTFO is also different from the norm. All equipment are available to the players from the start with no need to unlock them via levels, experience, or challenges. Variety is achieved via some of the more specialized equipment rotating in and out every season/rundown. The only unlockables you can expect from GTFO are cosmetic items for your character. I think this is apt for the game as it highlights the game loop of successfully clearing each "dungeon" and not unlocking equipment for unlocking equipment's sake.Before you get this game, make sure to consider first if you have anyone else in your friend group interested in it. If not, you should ask yourself if you're willing to go into the GTFO official discord and find other players there. While the game does have public matchmaking, it's still filled mostly of players who picked the game up thinking they were getting some sort of sci-fi Left 4 Dead and have no patience in actually playing the game for what it is. These kind of people will waste your time. You'll be a couple of minutes into a mission when they snap and decide to go Rambo and you never get close to actually finishing any level. Looking for a group in the official discord cuts down the amount of players who go into the game with the wrong expectations and you're most likely to find like-minded people there. If you go into GTFO understanding that it's not anywhere near a horde shooter like Left 4 Dead, where communication is important, where the goal and satisfaction comes from beating the game's "dungeons" and not having the most number of kills among your team, you will have a good time in GTFO. TLDR: The best advice I can give to people who are interested in this game: THIS IS NOT A HORDE SHOOTER. DO NOT PLAY THIS GAME WITH PEOPLE WHO DO NOT RESPECT YOUR TIME.

This game knows what it wants to be, and it has achieved that vision, still in early access. The new optional objectives in the rundown also bring this update up to par, adding not only replay value, but act as a difficultly gate for newer players, and added challenge for veteran ones. The map system allowing you to denote things to other players, as well as its small cosmetic update really make it very nice to use, even before it looked as good as it does now.  Progress is entirely based on skill and teamwork here, there are no in between run upgrades or progression, which may put some people off, but to me it allows me, on this new steam profile, to pick up almost exactly where I left off without having to grind, or waste anytime. The community in this game is great, although expect there to be about as many Russians as in CSGO, which can make communicating in some lobbies hard. Overall this is a very solid game, especially for early access.

Level designs are streamlined into prefixed rooms to arrange just in different order, which leads to further repetition in going through the same rooms upon rooms, and that takes away any possible unique story telling in the environment and memorability. Because of the unrecognizable layout of each rundown levels, it will make certain players lost, bored, or not even  remember any of the levels, alongside feeling no worth in coming back to re-experience them. The simplification of level designs might have been done to code the ai's pathfinding easier and to allow modders to design their own levels.Right out of the bat, GTFO is immersive from booting it as it loads information about the player being set as a prisoner getting loaded into the cortex. The atmosphere and the graphics are immersive too alongside the soundtracks.The story telling is done through each following. In level selection as the warden displaying minimal information allowed for the expendable prisoners. objectives that follows through each rundown that kind of tells the motives of the warden and the prisoners. And stored logs in the terminals of the Santonian Mining Industries, some added with audio that brings the characters to life, which are well done by the actors.It is all done in ways that the story is not enforced into the players time away from gameplay, and allowing them to seek it out on their own time and interest intrigued by the secrets laid in the whole scenario of the GTFO.Players are locked to each other as the majority of the game requires team scans, stripping players from allowing them to strategize in splitting their forces. The gameplay revolves around combat and working towards in how to deal with it better, through equipment and weapons, layout of the level and enemy types. With the following challenges laid bear, they require the players to work together and strategize with what they can get and could think of. GTFO is very punishing as it has been designed for a full team of four players and to make it challenging for them. It would be acceptable to improve upon set failures if the levels weren't dragged very long to average 2 hours each attempt, but most fall down to requiring even more brute force. In some cases, such cruelty works as it is satisfying when a strategy works in overcoming challenges.Weapons and equipment varies in good enough size that don't lack in any particular or dilutes any of them. Melee combat sucks as they have been coded as guns, striking a dot needle into a single spot instead of various forms like slicing and wider hitbox for bigger melee weapons.No matter the flaws GTFO has in variety, gameplay, coding, missing files, mismatched files, corrupt texture, unfinished in some overlooked stuff, cut contents such as voicelines, the game is fun to play with friends.Mods are exceptional in everyway the main game lacks, and are therefore the reason I have sunken many hours upon the mods.

_childDocuments_.review: -Press and hold buttons in the UI instead of just clicking it. I play on PC, why would you do that on PC? Minor, but annoying.-Textures are terrible. Washed out, blurry, nothing feels crisp.-Weapon handling is bad compared to any other high quality shooter I played. Recoil feels bad. Distance to sight feels bad. -Recoil probably feels bad because not the weapon model/sight moves upwards, but the entire screen moves upwards. It should be the exact opposite: Eye sight (=screen) is stable and the weapon moves. This goes for the Y axis of the recoil movement.Then again, the z-axis recoil of most guns is just completely over the top. Here, the gun moves, but the gun model and sight move so much, it feels they hit you right in the face when shooting. -Getting-Hit feedback feels bad. Never have a feeling how hard I got hit and from what angle.-Hitting-enemies feedback feels bad. -Shots don't feel like they connect.-Tactical shooter without any "lean" functionality.-You cannot drop equipment for your mates (e.g. dropping a large flashlight), but have to find a locker to exchange equipment.-When opening a secure door, a percentage number rised from 0% to 100%. During that process, hordes attack, and red markers appear that you have to stand on for the door to continue it's process to 100% (open). Next to questioning the design decision of this mechanic...(just why? it makes no sense, stand here, then stand over there, then stand over there again...for a door to open? Why?)...the markers are hardly visible in all the fog and blurry scene. It's a pretty frustrating experience. -Enemies shoot "flying yellow glowing balls" at you that neither make a sound when they are fired, don't make a sound when they approach, nor make a sound when they impact you.Sound feedback is such an essential, that feels underdeveloped in this game.Anyhow, enemies sending yellow glowing little orbs at you just feels underwhelming and unemotional. What kind of "fearsome attack" for a horror shooter is that?-Stealth is based on a binary system that is really rigid and getting stale fast. No dynamic. You are allowed to move freely, and you must stand still when the enemy glows. ->ON/OFF. ->Yes/No. No "stealth game indicator that rises" no "visibility indicator that changes". Nothing that would make you feel "the edge" of being close to being detected. That feeling of rising suspense, that you know from other good stealth games.Here, if you move while the enemy starts glowing, it is instant combat. Someone called it "Green light / Red light" mechanic, like at a traffic light. I think that sums it up pretty good.So clearing a room of "sleepers" (as they are called) has zero dynamic. It feels like work, because there is no movement, no change, just a room full of enemies that stand still and periodically glow, which translates to: Stop. Just wait. Then move some meters, then wait. Move some meters, wait. If you ask me, the concept idea as a baseline could be really interesting, but it's just way too basic in it's current form to create any kind of dynamic gameplay.-Ammo: Now stealth wouldn't be such an issue, if the game would allow more of the shooter gameplay. Though it is clearly intended to stealth A LOT, EVERYWHERE, as balancing for ammo-supply is very scarce, so that you are pressed to conserve ammo whereever you can. In turn, promoting the "stale and undynamic" stealth system to a mandatory experience.-Melee attacks can be quick or strong attacks, by holding down the mouse button longer before release. For whatever reason, devs decided that preparing a strong strike automatically is released after a while. Completely stupid, cause this is not street fighter where such a mechanic is needed. When I pull my hammer back to swing, it should't automatically do the swing after 5 seconds for no reason.-The best part about the game are the voice-overs. Actors sound real, intonation is good. There are not that many lines they speak, but they are delivered very very well.Overall, at the standard pricepoint, I cannot recommend this game in good faith. It's just not up there in terms of FPS weapon handling, shooter feeling, stealth dynamics or equipment unlocks.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like slow, methodical, and challenging co-op games with your friends, this game right here is about is good as you are going to find.  GTFO often plays like a puzzle game that you and your teammates have to solve through trail and error tactics.  This is a niche game in my opinion, in that I think a majority of people who play first person shooter games would not enjoy the slow grind and pacing of this game.  Part of the game is conserving ammo and avoid conflict, so it isn't a Call of Duty game where you are constantly and relentlessly forced into action.  I would definitely not recommend this game for someone who doesn't have friends to play with or is willing to join a discord server.  The game has bugs here and there, but over time they are less and less frequent.  Overall, I think this is a unique game that does exactly what it sets out to do.  For my friends and me, this game has given us lots of enjoyment and stress.  P.S. This game is hard, do not play if you want to relax.  4.5/5

_childDocuments_.review: Shipped out with three other lads to approx. 600m.Brought a shotgun for close quarters, and a sidearm to be practical, along with shaped charges.Couldn't even deploy with as much as we could carry because Requisitions are cheap bass turds. The other three brought regular kit, one with foam, one with a sentry, one with Bio tracker.The one with the tracker wouldn't shut up and kept yelling at the tracker like it was a person.  Also, didn't trust the tracker.Should have given him the foam gun.Was advised to keep flash lights off, but trying to see in the dark is for chumps.No hostiles upon arrival.  Just some left behind meds, some ammo, glowsticks, and conveniently, lock melters.Whoever manned this joint bounced in a hurry and didn't maintain their gear.  Med kits have holes in em.We pillaged about until we found a door.  Then another door.  Etc.  Opened up terminal to "query" for objective.Apparently ipconfig doesn't work for IPv11 endpoints.  Found some logs.  Bounced between a few terminals and discovered that they don't just  use a networked share drive.  Typical.Came across a couple interesting files about the pandemic, ate some pizza while the lads putz'd about.  Bio tracker kept mumbling to himself about "seeing lots of contacts" and "I don't trust this thing."  We began to get quite annoyed with him.Read some alarms about room temp alerts.  You'd think after 10 they'd just suspend the alert and save the log space.  Oh well.Terminal also had info about which room the objective was in, but was too far away to be of much help anyway.Proceeded into another alpha-numerically labelled room.  Whole place was foggy and dark with some red lighting.And some weirdos hunched over.  Suddenly one of them seemed to react to the flash light and became irritable.Turned off the flashlight and it calmed down.  Proceeded in the opposite direction, dead end.Tucker remained quiet for the most part until he decided to shout "WE NEED TO BE QUIET OR WE WILL WAKE THEM!!!"Voice echoed off every surface in the cave.  Hunched weirdos took issue with that, so we administered sedatives.*Cough* sledgehammers.Did a quick self-check after the confrontation, then proceeded to pillage more lockers, make loud noises by whacking locks and beeping the hacker, and felt a wee bit more confident in our supplies.  Apparently the doors are sound proof because the next room had more weirdos who were undisturbed.  Administered sedatives again.Trudged around in the darkness until we found a key that went to another door.  Good thing we didn't try to go through that door in the beginning.Returned to main cavern to go through said door.  We did musical chairs with the security system until a flood of weirdos decided to join the fun.Became heavily harassed, so we played king of the hill until they got tired.  Decided firearms were underrated.Went through the next door and took inventory.  All the goods we took the time to pillage were practically eradicated.Bio tracker Tom continued mumbling to himself.Administered first aid to a few scrapes that looked like a bad time, but it was dark so we pretended they were topical lacerations.  Somehow Bishop got shot, but we weren't aware the opposition had firearms, so we chalked it off to poor weapons handling.Continued down the maze of chambers via ladders and more locked doors.  Only encountered small numbers of weirdos at the time so we administered sedatives sternly but also inconspicuously.Finally closed in on our objective. Slightly larger weirdos were taking a nap in that room.  Decided to administer sedatives.Unfortunately, they have a tolerance for sledgehammers.  Somehow Bio Tracker Tom remained unscathed, but the rest of us came out... damaged.Came to a big door.  Had the lads lay out welcoming party gifts for playing musical chairs.It was a complete success.Picked up a large capacitor-looking thing.  Unfortunately, we ran out of supplies for musical chairs from the last encounter, so we made do with leftovers.The leftovers did not last long...9/10 Recommend.  Hopefully Bio Tracker Tom develops more topics to discuss and Tucker stops screaming about being quiet.Bishop was a real trooper and I hope to have more ops with him.  Literally gave me the shirt of his back.And some ammo.TL;DR: It was dark.  We bonked some things.  They bonked back.  So we brought guns.  But they brought their bigger friends.  With Guns.

You and your team need to plan your route, use the very neat terminal system to find your supplies and your way. You have to think logistically, always thinking ahead. _childDocuments_.review: NOT RECOMMENDED FOR ALL PLAYERSIf you hate : -  Horror themed games with infected type mobs- Working with other players at the cost of winning/losing the game- Commitment for an hour long run where the most basic mistake can make you start the whole rumble over again for the 56th timeThen this game ain't for you. I wouldn't recommend buying this game on your own, matchmaking is now live but communication always works best with some buddy of yours. The level design is on point; with the recent updates each mission has multiple difficulties unlocking different parts of the map if you're feeling up to the challenge, keeping things freshRapid fire for that last part, this is now a run on review- Music by Simon Viklund AKA Payday franchise composer- Excellent gunplay, very tight & responsive- Props to lighting and world building, very immersive, giving you that "wow" moment when opening a new door- Communication is essential and will be the make or break factor in most of your games- 1 guy in 10,000 made it through every single map. If you like the idea of a game that will send you back to the menu 99% of the time, only to push to you git gud until you beat said mission, making you feel like you actually crawled your way through all these sleepers yourself to type in a single line of code in a terminal, you know what to do

_childDocuments_.review: I wrote my initial review when I had 41 hours in the game. At that time, this game bugs rivaled those of Bethesda games, and it was a little un-balanced. But in the year that's gone by since my last review, 10 Chamber has exceeded the expectations of me, and 200,000+ other people. And in the year, they have managed to not only better balance the enemies and guns, but they tried a really unique objective based system, allowing players that aren't as good to manage better, and hopefully become pros quicker. And if you are already a pro, they have harder options to make it more interesting. They have put so much thought, and care into the mechanics of this game, it almost feels like you are there, doing the missions. They constantly add new "unique" enemies that you cant find on any other game. And my personal favorite, with their most recent set of mission, Rundown 4, I think they have found an amazing balance between needing to stealth, and having to go as loud as possible.15/10I lost my mind somewhere in the Rundown, and I can't find itShut up Woods...

_childDocuments_.review: Early adopters were left in the dust with this game's full release. It wasn't finished, and lacked a lot of content that was originally promised during early access. Moreover, the biggest broken promise, early adopters were told that the "rundowns" (sets of levels you can only play for a few months before the next update brings a new set) would never return, and rundowns would be replaced with permanent levels in the full release. They lied. Ever since the full release, they have brought back each old rundown periodically which is "good" for new players but bulldozes any reason for early supporters to play the game. It's clear that reusing old levels was significantly less work for the dev team than appeasing both old and new players.I'll repeat, this game wasn't finished, and when I heard it was getting a 1.0 release I knew it was over for the game. I have been patiently waiting for an excuse to play the game and still haven't touched it a year later.

_childDocuments_.review: As a big horror junkie, this game is something I've been wanting to get my hands on for a while, but honestly for how many redundancies there are in the core mechanics and how little much they've done to improve upon them since this game came out, I'm a little disappointed.There is a good amount of this game I do enjoy. The terminals, the 'don't tell your story, show it' vibe, the melee and gun range, and the minimalist out of game menu is all neat stuff that stands this game out from the rest, as for the mechanics this game  to be known for, it strangely just feels like they all shoot each other in the foot, not allowing anyone of them to fully flourish-Stealth-A big promoted part of GTFO is the urgency to be stealthy, never to get ahead of yourself and stay cautious. I can say that the mechanic works, and I haven't encountered any technical problems so far but its no where near being a unique and well thought out part of this game. It is essentially crouch->move->stop for 10 seconds->move->slap or stab depending on your melee->repeat, and when having to slap hundreds of tape worm riddled sleepy heads again and again, it can get very repetitive, very fast.The game also offers no alternative for this other than to avoid the room they're all in entirely or move past them (either which often isn't an option). Eventually, you'll start to get impatient and just cause a slap fest, making stealth null-Horde shooting-If at any point you have a ♥♥♥♥♥ wucky with the above mechanic, you'll trigger this phase. This is supposedly not an ideal situation  That being said, you will soon discover horde triggering is an utterly unavoidable part of this game. Visibility by design is abysmal, so having to accurately spot, shoot and stab hundreds of angry naked worm people (plus the fact that a would-be satisfying head-shot doesn't always kill them) is a massive head-ache. Unlike stealth however, you are given a variety of tools to help you in this situation; C-foam and mines to slow down enemies, sentries to hold choke points, and bio scanners to help you keep track of what your dealing with, all of which are designed to minimise you having to interact with the horde. Seems like there are two progressive paths away from this; A) give players an option to avoid hordes entirely in some scenarios or B) make hordes a fun shooting range event like most other horde-shooters, this game however is sadly stuck in the awkward mid ground.-Horror-Why I got this game, the big spook that sends adrenaline through you, perhaps (arguably) one of the biggest promotional features of this title, a feature that it sadly, like so many that have a horror-tag before it, falls so very far of.Now I know I sound like a gate-keeping bum, but lets just look at what two things mechanically make a  horror game.- Vulnerability Feeling unarmed even when you are anything but is what a great horror game accomplishes. This pressure can amplify the feeling to get anything that needs to be done 'done now' and greatly increases the rewarding feeling of completing a task. Whilst the above paragraph about 'Hordes' makes it seem like they accomplish this, the one further up about 'Stealth' shows that you are hunting these things, not the other way around. Similar to games like 'Dead-Space' or 'Evil Within', why should be afraid of something that you've already killed a hundred of? Answer is: you shouldn't- UnpredictabilityNot knowing is a defining feature of fear, its why most horror movies and games are far more horrifying mid way through then near the end. It can be done through RNG or even out of place events, both not too hard to implement. Whilst honestly I haven't witnessed all of what this game has to offer, It felt pretty predictable a few missions in.Whilst this games atmosphere and creatures seem perfect fits for horror, it fails to exaggerate both of these defining tid-bitsIn the end, the attempted stealth ruins the horror, the attempted horror ruins the horde-shooting and the attempted horde-shooting ruins the stealth, and we're left with just a hard game that's just not fun.I'll continue to play it a bit more and see If I can prove myself wrong but in the meantime  its actually very fun and knows exactly what it wants to be, plus the cosmetics don't suck ass.I give this game a 5/10

_childDocuments_.review: For the record: This is an incredible game. It has an amazing atmosphere, very unique intelligence gathering system relative to every other game out there, the gunplay is in a much better spot than in the closed tech test, and the enemy placement and item placement randomisation means most playthroughs of every level will be different every time. On the whole, the game is severely impressive. This is a negative review for several reasons, despite the praise I just gave the game, because I'm analysing it from a layman buyers perspective. This game is incredibly niche for one. The fact that your progression through each level is bound to commands into a console, although not complicated, would and will be enough to persuade buyers to refunding the game. Alongside that, no integral matchmaking meaning you have to LFG in friend groups or on discord servers (bonus points to the fact that the company is hosting their own official server, and other games like Deep Rock Galactic taking similar stances, although this shouldn't be necessary to enjoy the game) and the fact that despite being able to drop into the game single player, the game being vehemently tuned for a co op group of more than two and the steep learning curve can make this game severely displeasing, understandably so, never mind the very hefty price tag for an early access game. I very much feel like this game will do good though. It'll just take time, and it will always be a niche market. With further development I'll probably convert this to a positive review. But at this point, I'll list mine as a negative one to attract the attention of a reader who may benefit from this take. Happy hunting, and GTFO.

_childDocuments_.review: This is some of the best cooperative gameplay you can ask for.  This is not a drop into a session and coast to the end of a level with music blasting type game.  This is get your three best pals into a discord call, plan out equipment, and dynamically plan/debate defensive/stealth strategies to survive each section by the skin of your teeth.  With 1.0, they brought welcome additions like scarce checkpoints (No longer infuriating when one minor mistake ends the run but also doesn't hand hold you through the level), cosmetics earned only through successful expeditions, a more direct inclusion of story material, extra features like a artifact/perk system and more.  This game is also one of the most atmospheric games I've played in a long time.  With challenging enemies, complex but understandable level design, and little supplies to go around, this game makes it clear that you are as expendable as the Warden says you are.  This is what makes the game so gratifying.  The circumstances given dictate that you shouldn't make it far but with competent teamplay and good resource conservation, there is just enough of a chance for you and your fellow prisoners to barely slip out.In terms of negatives, some checkpoints through the few levels I've played so far will be placed before a resupply area so if you fail the section, you have to resupply again which for the tougher levels means you will be doing this quite a few times.  Game also is still a little buggy in terms of AI stealth detection and objectives on the hud not updating when you need the info on your hud progress (An example is needing the hud to tell you to type a specific command into a specific terminal to activate the next stage of the mission).  Luckily these are not game breaking and will definitely be adjusted and fixed as the dev team is quick to issue patches for any glaring issues.Overall, this is a must buy if you want an intense cooperative experience to enjoy with friends and I am so excited for what this game and dev team has in store for us.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hard, borderline frustrating at times, game that requires a lot of careful planning, teamwork, and sheer tenacity to make it to the extraction. However, this is what makes it so fun and rewarding. If you're looking for a simple point-and-shoot horror game, this isn't for you. But if you have some pals that live for the challenge and grind, you'll have oodles of fun trying to clear rooms, do the objective, and deal with new threats the deeper you descend into the Complex. I do admit the game play can feel a smidge repetitive trying to sneak and defend security scans, but the tension offsets that because just one screw-up can mean ruining a run after you're an hour deep. Some might hate this sort of mechanic because it does mean it throws all your progress out the window. I think it's great because poses actual stakes-- a real sweaty, butt-clenching, heart-racing drive not to screw up.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: also I'd like to pre-emptively stop any smoothbrains' possible ad hominem if they disagree with my below assessment: I am a better player than 95% of the people who play this game, and that's a conservative estimate. My complaints do not arise from a lack of skill.I can only speak to my own experience here. The core of what's here is good: it has a ton of potential and it could easily become the best hardcore co-op game there is. That isn't what it is right now, and it is NOT because it's feature incomplete, it's because of the design philosophy. A game is built on the ideas the developers wish to use, their concepts for how their game should play. In the previous set of missions, there were questionable design decisions, but they were only here and there and could be improved on. Now, with the Infection rundown release, this new set of missions shows them doubling down on these decisions. The game design is heading down a road I consider bad design, and so I cannot recommend it.My brother and I played the alpha over and over until we beat it with just the two of us, a mission that was balanced for four people. We beat half of the first rundown the same way after we had beaten every mission a dozen times each. We learned the mechanics inside and out, and any game change spurs us to do more testing to see how things work now. I have 150+ hours in the game. I know what I'm talking about.Right now, the game missions are designed by hand. Anything randomized (container locations, items in the containers, objective locations, enemy and light spawns, etc.) is only pseudo-randomized within a preset allowed margin. What this translates to in practice is that your success or failure on any given mission is heavily, heavily contingent on how you know the mission is going to play out. It makes a huge difference knowing whether the mission contains invisible enemies, and when or where they spawn. It makes a huge difference knowing which objective locations can change, and which ones of those options are far easier than the other(s). This is a massive design flaw, because everything now comes down to trial and error, forcing players to memorize the mission by dying to something they couldn't predict until getting killed by it. Skill factors in only in terms of maintaining stealth and shooting enemies accurately; no amount of skill will allow you to win a mission if it has invisible enemies while no one on the team has a tracker (which is the least useful of the tools, so most team loadouts do not include a tracker). Your success on a mission is determined far less by actual skill and adapting on the fly to changing situations, and much more to do with memorization of what will happen when, and what to do to counter it. This is terrible. In rundown 1, there was really only one mission in which this rule held irrefutably true, and so this flaw was prevalent at a lesser degree; in this current rundown it exists in spades.Missions last 2-3 hours now. No respect for player's time. Incredibly irritating and noticeable issues haven't been changed despite being some of the first things you notice, like the EAR BLAST of the gasp that happens before you drop. Easy fix, hasn't been changed, it's like the devs don't know or care and don't play their own game. Enemies can still get aggroed/alerted at extreme range by stealth kills if they're glowing a hundred feet away; if it's a bug, it still isn't fixed, and if it's intentional, it's horrendous design. The new bursting cysts are a terrible mechanic that don't add to the gameplay and only create yet more busywork and tedium. I could go on. This review will change to positive if these issues and the fundamental concept of design philosophy takes another direction, but I doubt it, and I was really, really looking forward to the future of this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of the best games I've played in a while. GTFO is a Hardcore-Shooter about 4 men who have been imprisoned and sent to an underground facility to accomplish different types of tasks.  GTFO is all about teamwork. Having bad teammates is your doom so make sure you start off with a team which knows what they're doing (or are euqal to your game experience). You should like stealthing if you decide to buy GTFO - Stealthing past enemies and patience to not wake them up is also important. So if you don't like stealthing or if you are inpatient, don't buy this game since you can't always charge into a room and kill the enemies all at once, lol. You should buy this game if you are up for teamplay and lots...and lots...and lots of shooting, don't forget to use your Melee tho ;). (Also the lore is pretty neat.)There isn't really anything I don't like about that game, it's just really - freaking - hard but that just makes it more fun to play and rage because your teammate triggered an entire room and kills the whole team in no less than two minutes hehe. _childDocuments_.review: This game has done everything right so far.I'd grown somewhat weary of cooperative shooters, because none of them seemed to truly rely on supporting and complementing one another, became repetitive very quickly, didn't offer a challenge (outside of frustratingly difficult hordes or something) and also tended to lack atmosphere.I have yet to play with complete strangers, but even playing in a full group of friends, you still feel utterly alone in the darkness if you allow the scenery to sink in a bit. All weapons and tools have their place and use, and unlike many other co-op's, you will respect enemies, regardless of how well kitted you are at any point.Replayability is ensured by additional challenges that prepare you for harder levels, and the difficulty curve is well paced, once you understand your own fighting power in the context of the game.I'm very excited to see where this goes in the future, but even as it is, I'm loving what I got. Well worth the investment!

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest, deciding whether to recommend this game or not is one of the hardest decisions I've done this month.If you're one of those people who would get annoyed at people for restarting the moment the guards got alerted in Payday 2, this game is probably for you. Stealth until someone or something ♥♥♥♥♥ up. Rinse and repeat.There's a very good concept here at its core, and it's balanced beautifully, but hitting a game breaking bug 40 minutes into an expedition is really deflating - thankfully it will get fixed relatively quickly. You'll definitely want to play with people, the bots are decent, but they can't really help you much when trying to stay quiet, only prevent a wipe when things go wrong.This brings me to the next issue, which is one of pricing - yes, developers deserve to get paid, but it's really hard three friends to drop €40 on a game each blindly, especially one which up front says you might not like it! Keeping an eye on a two hour timer doesn't make for a good experience either.Something that could help here would be a demo version that lets you complete a fixed expedition with a fixed loadout with bots, or even just the "evaluation" that was introduced with this rundown (rundown 7). Let friends get a feel for the game, and if it's worth the money, because when there isn't a free weekend going on, those player numbers worry me. You'll pretty much always be able to play with friends since it's peer to peer, but developers can't justify working on a game that doesn't make them money.Get this game with at least one other friend, set a timer on your phone for an hour and 50 minutes, and try it out together. See if you like it or not. If you like it, it's probably gonna be one of the best games you've played. If you don't like it, you can always get a refund.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I liked this game. I wish I got to see more of this game. I don't and I didn't.This is a suicide note and I'm getting creative. Suicide by cop is so last year. I'm committing suicide by l33t gamer SoMe posse. Buh-bye, cruel world! Here we go...The idea of the game is brilliant, a pure co-op with slight assymetry between team members (you can't be everything, so you pick a role, with strenghts and vulnerabilities, a role you all agree on, not some dull template). I love it! The ambience of the game is brilliant too. It's a pure gloom and despair festival! I just think it's a shame the developer is so uncompromising and made the game so hard and thus inaccessible to many players. A prestige contest? I dunno, I just don't get it. We're outta prestige ourselves. It all just seems like a bad financial decision to me. It would have reached a wider audience with a little more accessibility. Call it something humiliating, a "l2p n00b" mode or whatever, we don't care.So we are this group of old gamers. We are so OG our teeth are beginning to fall out (hair is already way gone). We were there at the birth of pro gaming (QW), we were there at the birth of MMORPG's with hard content (long before pansy WoW). But we are too old these days to keep up with the hardgames (now you know what's coming, zoomer). It's just that GTFO isn't even like Dark Souls or something. There you have a comeback mechanism at least. Here you don't. You spend an evening trying to crack a level. You're cautious. You discuss. You devise a plan. You deal with situations. It takes time. And then towards the end of the level you wipe anyway. And all your efforts are down the drain but it's too late in the evening for another go. Try again from scratch next week. And then next week you wipe again at the end of the level. And the week after. You need the patience of a Buddah, all of you in the team. You also need a lot of time, for back to back sessions. _childDocuments_.review: To learn a game, you replay the sections you fail until you understand it. This is a core learning loop, and is a big part of what makes a game fun and engaging.GTFO has very long missions, often over two hours a pop. Multiple times in this game, we've cleared the first 1.5 hours of a mission with relatively minor pain, only to fail at the 11th hour. To replay the final section, we'd need to replay the entire 2 hour mission, which feels like a massive waste of time.Games address this problem using checkpoints, which allow players to progress through a piece of content gradually. Checkpoints allow developers to dictate the pace at which their players experience their game's core learning loop. They allow games like GTFO to have long missions, with non-uniform difficulty throughout.GTFO has checkpoints...but it might as well not. The checkpoints in GTFO are too far apart, often well over an hour. They are also confusingly inconsistent - in one mission, we got a checkpoint after 15 minutes (after ~one big fight), and then no checkpoint for 2 hours (after ~four big fights).This game is fantastic for those who want to grind out a mission for dozens of hours. The gameplay is pretty good. Melee feels weak (but on purpose), ammo is scarce (but on purpose), turrets and foam and mines and setup in general seem strong (also on purpose). It offers some incredible highs, and is an awesome base platform for future updates. It's easy to see the developers adding new weapons, new tools, new enemies, etc.But the checkpoints are too far apart. The game did not respect my time, and it won't respect yours. If that's okay with you, great, you can find a lot of enjoyment here. But there's a lot of games out there my group of 4 can enjoy. We'll likely gravitate towards those other games, at least for the moment.

_childDocuments_.review: GTFO's horror atmosphere is good but I didn't particularly enjoy any aspect of the gameplay.Guns feel unsatisfying to use and you're constantly pressured into using them as little as possible, instead being pushed to use the melee weapons for stealth kills. The melee weapons don't really feel any better and there's a distinct lack of feedback when blows connect, in a floaty way which reminds me of melee in The Elder Scrolls games.The goals of each map differ yet they progress in almost the same way, namely creeping around in the dark whacking things until a door mandates that you face waves of enemies, checking a terminal for resupplies, and then continuing onward to the objective. Ultimately, it felt more tedious than scary to be slowly moving through these maps making melee attacks in sync with the rest of the team.The idea of using a command line interface when you encounter a terminal is perhaps cooler in concept than it is in practice. In the end it's just typing in a couple of commands on occasion and optionally reading a few tidbits of lore.The artifact/booster system which awards buffs that you can activate for a mission is pretty unsatisfying, and lacks impact; so much so that they could remove it from the game entirely and it wouldn't be any worse off.The bots are competent enough to fill out a team if you're missing someone or playing in a duo but playing with them solo is frustrating; if you're looking for a game to play alone then you'd best give this a miss.If the moment to moment gameplay weren't so tedious I could see the atmosphere being immersive enough to overlook some of the game's shortcomings but as it stands I can't recommend GTFO.

Every "Rundown" or "mission" offers a new experience, a new way to play and experience the game. Make no mistake, this is one of the best example of game design to come on sale in many years. If you don't have the team to get through it with, you're not going to have a good time.In my opinion the developers would do well to create some new, much easier Rundowns of a more casual nature. These Rundowns wouldn't need to change every "season" like the current ones do, but could be there as a consistent "game mode" with matchmaking. These simple Rundowns would provide an ideal training ground in which to learn the game, experience a semi-skimmed version, and meet people to play the full fat version with.

_childDocuments_.review: I've finally managed to finish this game, so here's my review:I've been playing this game since it was in early access, and I find the style, lore, and characters really cool. However, I can't fully recommend this game for one simple reason: IT'S INSANELY UNBALANCED.Yes, I said "unbalanced" and not "difficult" because Dark Souls is difficult. It means you can defeat a boss or another type of difficulty with a lot of effort, a good strategy, and farming/better items. Here in G.T.F.O., no, you can be a korean pro player, but you will fail no matter what you do.1) Enemies are too many.2) Enemies are too fast.3) Enemies deal a lot of damage.4) You are always low on ammo.5) Levels are pitch black, and the only good flashlight is the big one.6) Enemies sometimes "respawn" due to a glitch, so you have to face the same enemies more and more times.7) There's a lot of (toxic) fog (toxic for you, not for the monsters, obviously), and this will also further compromise your vision.In order to succeed in an expedition, you need tons of luck, especially for the ammo packs, tool refill packs, and medkits, and an excellent team combined with a lot of patience and trial and error.Difficulty aside, the levels are all the same with just a little bit of tweaks here and there. I mean, come on, be more creative! I don't want to downvote this title, but it's a 6/10; I can't give more than this.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend purchasing GTFO despite it being a decent game. As of recently, it was announced that GTFO has entered the end stages of development and will be releasing one more rundown some time in 2023. After this, the game will be "completed" and 10 Chambers will begin to focus on other efforts. This is shocking news to me, mainly because this game has several glaring issues regarding multiplayer connectivity and quality of life discrepancies that seem odd to run across in a "nearly completed product". This is disappointing and I cannot stress how annoying it is when obvious issues of quality exist in a product and people accept it as "just another modern gaming experience".The positive aspects of this game largely revolve around visual appeal, sound design (gunfire is distinct among the various firearms players can equip, and many of the guns sound extremely powerful), and difficulty. This game is quite difficult upon starting out, but once the player completes a few missions (or has to retry the same mission over and over again), they will be able to grasp many of the game's nuances and begin to speed up their in-game actions, making smarter moves with each obstacle they encounter.  Even some of the more tedious actions within the game (like typing on terminals) become second nature once a player has dealt with them a few times. Unfortunately, the negatives far outweigh the benefits of buying this game now that we have a clearer picture of what GTFO's "finished" form will be. GTFO (much like 10 Chambers lead Ulf Andersson's previous game "PAYDAY") is filled with fixable yet ignored bugs and quality of life issues that range from "annoying to deal with" all the way to "my friends and I just wasted 2 hours of our night because someone's game crashed mid-door scan". It's painful to see how much potential this game has and how wasted it is due to what feels like a flat-out refusal to add features that are commonplace now in games. For example, GTFO's matchmaking system does not include a lobby list that players can choose available games from, rather it merely has the ability to select what mission a player wants to play, what languages the player speaks, and if they have a microphone. While this sounds like enough, a player using matchmaking will often sit for literal hours trying to find other players to cooperate with. Out of the 87 or so hours I have on this game, about half of those hours have been spent in the mission select lobby waiting in vain for another player to join. Additionally, 10 Chambers has removed many of the rundowns that were once freely playable. This is virtually cutting off access to over half the game and while these rundowns are slowly coming back with the final Rundown addition releasing soon, it should not be the case where new players (or veterans who just took a break for a period of time) simply cannot access features that were in the game a year ago. That is classic user manipulation to artificially inflate the active player base. This is likely to hide the fact that GTFO truthfully has an active player base of just under 1000 people, which is not good. For reference, Left 4 Dead 2 (a game that launched in 2009) registered over 27,000 active players for November 2022.Finally, if one chooses to play the game with the 3 AI-controlled bots, it is very likely that players will never complete the more advanced levels as the AI is terrible in a fight and is basically a detriment to the team regarding certain objectives. Bots are generally regarded as "useless except for using their tools". They miss almost every shot they fire (seriously, watch any video of a player running a mission solo and it's likely the player will be merely using the bots for their tools and not their presence in a fight). So, in order to really experience the game and fully complete rundowns, a solo player will have to find other solo players to team up with if they do not have personal friends to schedule with.Which comes to my biggest complaint regarding GTFO and a large reason why I am not recommending this game for purchase; the community (for the most part) willingly accepts this matchmaking SNAFU as "just a small side effect of an early access game" while they chide you to "simply use the GTFO Discord server" if you wish to play GTFO with strangers/as a solo player. While there isn't any major issue with this in a vacuum, the more prominent members of the player base are... quite picky when it comes to who they partner up with for a mission. Because this game's "shortest mission" is around 30 real life minutes, many players want guaranteed completion of the mission when entering the lobby and/or Discord call because most people do not have the patience to run through these missions more than once or twice. One of my biggest issues is the feeling of wasted time while playing this game, and this feeling is most prevalent when failing a mission at the final obstacle (which will probably happen a lot) because there is no checkpoint system (sans Rundown 7, which does have checkpoints on certain levels). It's all or nothing and many players from my experience simply are not good enough to jump into a match with 3 other random players and coordinate effectively enough to succeed. This is especially so now, since the game has had an influx of newer players since it went on sale.The GTFO Discord creates a somewhat stark cultural divide in game availability for the average player, with older players who have had GTFO since Alpha projecting a sense of inflated ego onto newer players when they match up together (talking about the kids who offer to be "coaches"). Those newer players looking to complete harder levels will likely go through what feels like a high-level job interview with the average older player, being peppered with probing questions to assess your skill level. While it is understandable to want the best teammates available, it is also apparent that many players are willing to spend an unreasonable amount of time nitpicking you on your playtime or your choice of weapons, more time than it takes to simply play through the mission and call out incoming issues to said new players.A majority of the regular "Discord" experiences a player with live through will be one member of the party (usually a "veteran of the game") trying to control every movement the party makes in-game. Marine drill instructors give more leeway than the average GTFO veteran player will, every small error resulting in a cacophony of condescending comments and rude diatribe. Many players you encounter will have a "my way or the highway" attitude, resulting in lots of passive-aggressive commentary from your team. The only mistakes die-hard fans are willing to accept with grace are the game design failures from 10 Chambers.  Any legitimate criticism of this game's flaws in forum posts or discussions usually results in a loyal squad of fanboys rushing to defend the laziness of the developers regarding fixing these issues. Stockholm Syndrome be damned, I refuse to be a sheep and just accept mandatory usage of the Discord as a customer because the game should effectively matchmake for me if that system exists in the game. I should not have to make a strictly-formatted post on a third-party service and wait around for some weird Europeans to join my game and harass me at every turn just to screw up the mission for everyone at the end because  got cocky and assumed  couldn't make mistakes themselves. There is almost no progression system involved in this game. Players looking to "earn" something will only be able to grind out clothing options which are mostly randomized, meaning you can spend weeks playing through the game staring at the same helmet or chest piece. There is also no weapon customization, which feels like a huge miss considering this is an obvious factor of PAYDAY 2's success.In conclusion, do not buy. Game's dead.

_childDocuments_.review: Good idea with horrible execution.The core idea of the game is rather good, the graphics looks good but the way it plays is flat and lame.A lot of the enemies are just copy-paste of each other with more health and more damage. Even with the bosses, the game have a sum of 5 (five!) unique enemy, and 11 (Eleven!) that is mere copy-paste of the 5 base enemy, of which only 1 have an extra unique skill. The rest is just The gunplay is absolute garbage. Scopes moves your camera to an offset from your character's origo of rotation (essentially shifting left and right). The weapons have no synergy. They don't complete each other, some are basically a better version of another. Which is rather funny as all weapons are unlocked by default. You have absolute no reason to chose around 80% of the weapon selection as the rest is the same, just better. Sometime in every aspect possible.Map design is fine. R1 to R5 was rather generic, as the maps was constructed from copy-paste modules. R6 finally brought some variety to the environment.This is the worst point of all. Either you only want to play stealthy or bang bang shooter, this game repeatedly forces you into situations out of your control. This is  a stealth game, this is a shooter game with absurdly low ammo count and enemies with stupid skills. You  play stealth for like 5 minutes until the game tosses an  alarm in your face. That's where the game shows it's teeth. Despite trying to act like a stealth game, it provides you no option to skip / avoid bang bang sections. There are no submissions to bypass an alarm, no longer routes to skip a blood door. The devs are stuck on the creativity level of a toddler. At some points, it even has the face to throw you into an  alarm that begins to spawn infinite enemies  the RNG dropped enemies in the alarm zone until you find the objective and . I haven't had the nerve to finish this rundown, but R5 had a blood door that had a scout behind next to a cocoon room. For anyone who haven't played this game yet: You was forced to begin blasting, that woke up the scout who screamed and spawned X new enemies. While you were clearing them out, the cocoon room began respawning enemies you already cleared before that was  got woken up by the shootings. To "fix" this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, players began to  in the cocoon room to prevent it from respawning sleepers. (Note: as I know, R6 "fixed" scouts behind shooty shooty doors).The second worst part of the game. As said before: the game does  let you play fully stealth. This would make you think at least it provides you all the necessary tools and ammo. Well: nope. It RNG drops enemies, RNG drops loots, RNG drops the mission locations. As an example, in R5B2 (or B3?) we straight up restarted the mission if the starting mission wasn't behind a specific door, as the other 2 options was absurdly harder. Lexical example of how to make your game harder when you lack of  creativity: RNGesus.  behind the infinite error alarms the enemy types and locations are RNG. You can't just orchestra your way through it, you gotta pray for RNGesus it didn't drop 3 charger right behind the door. Enemies are also anything but interesting. One of them shoots HOMING MISSILES. The other one has HOMING TONGUE and another does HOMING RAMMING. The scout becomes invulnerable during screaming. the devs ticked every single point on the "How to make the stupidest, least interesting enemies of all time" checklist. Did I mention the all-time-invincible spitters? Did I mention they are RNG dropped all around a room (even the walls and ceiling)? They can be  neutralized by glowing your flashlight on them. Ohh, did it RNG spawn above a charger that will wake up from the flashlight? . A good stealth game lets you learn the map, control the events, be one step ahead of the enemies. GTFO is the exact opposite.This game has a lot of good ideas in it, and exactly the same amount of bad ideas. And even those are not meshed together well, rather just tossed into a sack and sold as a product. it have a serious identity crisis between being a stealth and being a bang bang shooter. It have way too much RNG for the genre it wants to be, and the enemies are extremely uncreative. For the time, it seems this is not an intermediate state, but a design choice. Typical game that looks good from the outside but heavily shallow on the inside.If you love unfair hard games, GTFO is for you. Not games that plays good, that you got to learn or you can control with enough invested time. It's  hard and there is nothing else. The  way you could become better in this game if you learnt kiting, that is officially considered an exploit and is being fought, or if you began exploiting each system of the engine, like enemy spawning or pathfinding. _childDocuments_.review: This game absolutely rocks. It is extremely intense and very difficult. It's described as going from tense stealth to extreme action in a heartbeat and that's absolutely true, one ♥♥♥♥-up easily results in a horde of enraged monsters rushing you down.The missions also have a great arc to them, in terms of the progression of tension. You start at half ammo so you're already a little haggard, but I can't tell you how many times my friends and I have barely survived an encounter with almost no supplies, only to open the door to the next room and see something even worse that we somehow have to get through. The missions are full of tense, skin-of-your teeth moments and surprises that are extremely unpleasant, in a pleasant sort of way, such as opening a door with an alarm that can only be turned off on the other side, only to realize that in order to do so you need to find a keycard to open another security door while being hounded by swarms of deadly enemies.The game absolutely requires serious planning and impeccable teamwork. It basically never feels like you have enough resources to keep going,  yet somehow you manage, to the point where when you do find supplies it's almost suspicious. You're certain something worse is around the corner and it usually is. While this is unquestionably the game's greatest strength, it's also a bit of a weakness. This game NEEDS teamwork, and while there is a helpful community discord, I still wouldn't recommend this game without a couple friends to play it with. If you do though, prepare for one hell of a ride.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, for the amount of time I've played, this game is amazing! Though this game is better with friends, at least 4 players. Practically impossible with 1-2 players and manageable with 3. Though for the full experience, I recommend 4 players. Even if you don't have friends that own this game, you can go on the GTFO discord, the community is very accepting and because this game is early access, everyone is new and not extremely experienced yet. So mostly everyone is going through the same experience together. Now looking at the game play aspect, it really deserves credit for the intensity it puts you through and the heart stopping moments when you open a door and a creature is right in front of you. You have to take things slow and steady and if you screw up, than you may have just failed the expedition. Its not a run and gun, hack and slash, when you first spawn in, you start with a very small amount of ammo in your weapons. Most of the time, the attempt is to go sneak up on a monster and take it out with stealth, which in his case you'd use your melee weapon. You also don't regen health, the only way to do that is to find loot, like a med kit. To obtain more ammo, you'd have to find ammo packs. And the ambience and setting of the game is just perfect. There are some rooms that are just completely dark and foggy, others with flickering lights. In cases where you can't see the monsters, you'll have to hear them and make sure not to trigger them, if you trigger one, you trigger all of them, and trust me that gets messy and drains supplies for your whole team.In the end, I 100% recommend this game if you like games that are more strategic, scary, intense and not just hack and slash at all time. Also if you are able to get a squad of at least 3-4 players.

This review does not highlight pro strats or take into account what happens when you sink 900 hours into this game min-maxing your whole life.What you should bring:- You are comfortable joining discords to find teammates or have friends who want to play with you.- You are capable of being a patient team player for up to two hours without breaks.- You are capable of dealing with difficulty and overcoming skill and rng-issues, sometimes retrying levels many times.- You can deal with others ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ up once in a while and you are not a prick.- The occasional bug that ruins your run does not mentally destroy you.- You are capable of preserving ammo.- You are able to control yourself and not panic the instant you see something move.- For the love of god bring a mic, your voice is not as bad as you think. _childDocuments_.review: I have played 23 hours of this game so far. I have completed exactly 3 runs without dying. We have been stuck on floor B1 for a long time now. We live, we stuggle, we live a little longer, we die, we mourn our lost prisoner characters, we go back in because we are definitely going to beat it this time, the cycle begins anew.Honestly, this is such a solid game. We go in knowing full well that we are likely to die after spending 1.5 hours working through the rooms to achieve our goal. But it is just such a fun atmosphere. Everything from the level design, to the sound, to the mechanics and environment are all so well put together that it makes it worth it to keep going back in just to die. The developers truly put a lot of soul into these rundowns. Now, a warning for the masses. This game is hard. Brutally hard at some points. You will feel moments where there can't possibly beat the floor you are on. You need to have a cool head, work together, and go back in with an updated plan. This is the key to getting better. Me and my friends are not great at this game. But planning ahead from what we know has been able to get us further and further in these floors. The euphoric feeling of beating a floor you have been stuck on is why you play.Would I recommend this to people? Yes, 100x over. You won't regret this game if you love good co-ops

_childDocuments_.review: Originally a positive review, but things do change. As much as it's sad to me, I cannot recommend GTFO right now. There is a number of reasons for it. However, just to make it clear from whom this review is coming from: a long-time player (been here since R1), a co-creator of arguably the most complex single-source guide for this game, ex-member of the bug hunt program (even though I was far from being extremely useful there due to time limitations at that period of my life to be fair), also enjoyer of challenging games and someone genuinely passionate about GTFO (you can tell based on my hrs on record).Coming back to the game and what are the major problems with it. I'm not going to list all of them, just because it has no sens, but I will do my best to go through the most outstanding ones.1. Lack of vision.Probably not something most would expect to go as the 1st point, but GTFO used to be a pretty unique game at certain point of its life. Hence, lost of direction is by miles the biggest problem. The game is advertised as a hardcore co-op game, where counting bullets and crystal clear communication with your team are vital for survival. A number of elements contributed to achieve it. However, the studio lost it somewhere around adding bots (remember statements that bots never get here?), boosters (looking at you, supply efficiency for endless piu piu), checkpoints (which encourage a brainless moron-style of a gameplay in public matches "we screwed up, lets reset guys"), return of the old rundowns (even though it was supposed to be a value of a sort to complete a time-limited content, no? I don't rly care about them being available or not, it's about what game tries to be and attempts to deliver). These, and other factors contribute to the game generally becoming significantly easier, while there is no incentive to so something objectively harder, e.g. beating the entire rundown without checkpoints or boosters. As a result, sense of accomplishment, or so called "GTFO feeling" are gone provided that you have at least a couple of dozens of hours.2. Lack of transparency.Studio is trying to be extremely mysterious about the future of the game and its state. Okay, I perfectly understand that studios never disclose all the info about what's in development, but being honest to your community is a must. This also comes down to game rulings. This is a topic to be discussed for hours, but rules in the public discord are something close to ruzzian red lines - they do move sometimes depending on the mood.3. Tech issues and acknowledging them.Many games have bugs, poor optimization and such - it isn't something unique for GTFO. However, narrowing poor optimization down to "your PC is probably ain't good enough" is very cheap. Fyi, R6D1 boss fight was a power struggle even for GFN machines :DOnes again, not going to specifics, bugs always were and always will be to this or another extent, but approach to how studios deal with them is something else.4. Modding community.GTFO has one of the best small communities I've ever seen. Sure, GTFO isn't a game where one can do a lot of cosplays, or different arts, but people here are friendly and there is always someone willing to help newer player, and such. We can all agree that modding community is usually the best part of any game? These are the most passionate people about a given game, they are willing to build up and develop content in their free time. I believe 10CC is the 1st studio in my experience which actively fought against mods. Sure thing, not all games are open for mods, but usually it's coming from publishers. Here modding community was illegal (literally) at the certain stage of the game, even with EULA threats popping up. If you are interested, check reddit for community purity topics.5. Recycling.Ones again, something done by many games, but in GTFO it's everywhere: room layouts, enemies, etc.In case you care about more, this man did a nice breakdown of exactly the same topic. If you have an hour of your life to spare - check it out.

_childDocuments_.review: After reconsidering my previous review, I have decided to recommend this game, but with caveats and some decent changes.TL;DR Devs have rescinded on previous stances that overall make the game better, and I have decided that my hopes for this game outweigh the bugs and desync. FPS Stealth horde shooter with limited resources and very difficult content. Great game, unless you don't like insane difficulty.The Jist:Chamber12 is creating truly a unique FPS experience. A stealth horde shooter with limited resources and a very hands-off objective system. The missions in rundowns start easy and then get difficult, with a D. The joy of this game is in being able to complete all the D and E missions as well as their Prisoner Efficiency objs. Beating this game with a well-juiced team that you trust is insanely satisfying. Despite the bugs and the other issues I keep coming back each rundown because this game is just that promising. Cons:- Bugs that were present at early access launch are still present and have had not fixes as well as some newer bugs. The biotracker red dots, checkpoint ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in general, occasional bad enemy hitboxes, fall damage when running down stairs, melee reticles bigging even when at range and others.- Desync is a major issue. sniper melee, teleporting, terminal ghost resources upon reconnect, map fog of war reset on reconnect, sometimes resetting to default ammo on reconnect, earlier mentioned hitbox issues and others. Supposedly devs are on record saying they can't fix it but that is not enough of an excuse in my opinion. Even if it is not in your skill set if you are a game dev you have an obligation to provide a stable multiplayer. If you don't know how to fix desync, someone else does.- The devs introduce systems that hurt intermediate players while not actually challenging solo players. Stamina is just honestly a load of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.- This game is almost friend-mandatory. Matchmaking and bots sucks tbh. Discord is thankfully pretty large for finding groups.Pros:- Devs have lessened their iron fist stance on mods. They allow to some extent, but they don't have a hard-on for shutting them down now.- Devs have rescinded their previous stance on gone-forever rundowns. In my opinion this is for the better. If you want to do some Unnus Annus/FOMO ♥♥♥♥ in a video game, it is not going to go well. Revisiting the previous content allows for more people to play and stay interested. That simple.- Guns feel great- The story is pretty interesting once you filter through the logs on terminals and stuff. - Decent gun balance for the most part- Cosmetics are a nice touch. Weapon skins could be cool.- The adrenaline from scout killing. - The mission format and how you have to get intel on each mission and make simple or complex plans.- me and the bois out at 2am looking for BEANS

"innovative gameplay".After that *yawning* experience Im rewarded with an apparel style that ads a red stripe to my clothes *yawn*.Most of the games from bigger studios during these times are so bad, that not having microtransactions, grindy mechanics (you own everything from the very beginning) unoptimized visuals put this game into a "very positive" state but the gameplay itself is mediocre at best, tedious at its worst.I may give this game a positive review if I really wanted to persuade my friends to play this with me, and i didn't want to look like a sucker for spending 30E on a horde shooter with 4 enemy types that all look like a raw chicken that ate a flashlight.TLDR: fun for the first couple hours with its Intriguing atmosphere of being a prisoner sent to industrial hell and plenty of cool guns to switch around, then it turns into a reptetive, tedious, yawning simulator

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not L4D. If you are going into this expecting the just run-n-gun your way through the enemy, you will not get far. If you are going into this expecting to beat it on your first try solo, you will quickly realize the error of your ways. In GTFO, your teammates are as much a part of your arsenal as your weapons and tools. Stealth is not a suggestion, it is a prayer that will lead you through the dark catacombs of the Rundown. And when that unearthly roar echoes through the complex, you and your team will have to work as one living, breathing entity if you want to survive...Pros;-Atmosphere: The atmosphere in this game is truly terrifying. The complex is pitch black most of the time, only illuminated by your glowsticks and flashlights... and of course the glowing heartbeats of the monsters that live there. Subtle sounds like water dripping from pipes overhead, coupled with the occasional sound of muffled movement makes you look over your shoulder constantly as you descend deeper into the unknown.-Cooperation: The core mechanic of this game is teamwork. Without your team, your chances of survival are minimal. The forces arrayed against you are hard to kill, hit like a freight train, and are too many to count. Things like timing your stealth attacks to avoid waking the entire room, setting up fallback positions while some of your team prepare to take out enemies too dangerous to kill silently, and calling out enemy positions instantly will become second nature to you.-Enemies: The enemies in the game are varied, and I will avoid too many spoilers in this review, but trust me when I say they are disturbing to look upon and horrifying to fight. These things can be ripped almost in half and still keep coming, but that is not their most terrifying trait. No, that title is held by the way they all perk their heads up and their bioluminescent hearts beat when you open a door leading into their chosen resting place, as if they are waiting for you. Of course, there are worse things awaiting you further down...-Navigation: I know what you're thinking. Navigation? Really? How is navigating your way through a tunnel complex so good as to be a selling point? Well, let me tell you. The in-game map is generated dynamically as you move through the complex, allowing you to easily see where you have and have not been. You can draw on the map to indicate preferred paths, enemy locations, and just to draw amusing images while discussing your plan with your team. However, the true joy of navigating the world comes form the terminals. With these, you have to find the in-game ID of an object you are searching for (medipacks, for example) and then query it to find out what zone it is in. Once you navigate to that zone, you must then find a terminal within said zone to ping the same object, allowing you get more exact details on its whereabouts. This system, while seemingly obtuse, actually means that quests for supplies become their own mini-game in a way, forcing you to take detours and go through areas that otherwise you may not enter.Cons;-Early Access: As the game is in early access, bugs abound. I've seen enemies spawn under floors where they are inaccessible, foes detect you when you could not have done anything to alert them and various visual bugs. A few of my teammates have experienced crashes and massive framerate drops, although I have yet to witness these myself. If you expect a flawless experience, I would recommend waiting until it fully releases.-Matchmaking and VOIP: Neither of these things exist. There is no matchmaking system in-game currently, nor any voice communications. The only way to join a lobby is to either join a Steam friend, or to copy a special lobby code to your clipboard (provided by the individual hosting the lobby). Thankfully the devs have 200+ voice channels on their Discord, but these tend to become unreliable during prime time hours due to heavy traffic. Both of these issues will be addressed in the future, but so far Discord is a requirement.-Lack of Clarity: Something I have personally noticed is the lack of basic instructions for new players. Regardless of level, your are always dropped straight into the map with no briefing on how the enemies function, how the stealth mechanics work, what various items do, things like that. Obviously this can be easily remedied with a quick Google search or with an experienced teacher, but such basic information should probably be provided somewhere in-game for those just starting out. If you do buy this game, I recommend searching through the Discord to find someone willing to show you the ropes.All in all, I highly recommend this game. Despite its current flaws, I have absolutely gotten my money's worth of enjoyment out of the game in its current state. Most of the flaws can be easily worked around via the Discord (you can find an invite link to it on their website) and those that cannot are issues that I suspect will be remedied shortly. I am very excited to see where the game goes once they fully introduce the Rundown system, as well as what new challenges await me and my team in the darkness below!

_childDocuments_.review: After playing for several hours I can honestly say this is the best co-op game I've ever played. High intensity and a good variety of challenges forces you to work as a team if you want to survive. The graphics look great and the atmosphere is palpable. I don't think i'll ever forget the first encounter with a scout. The game does very little to show you how to play. There's no objective points, nothing to show you exactly what the thing you're looking for looks like, and no aim assist. This works exceptionally well as it fully immerses you in the game. As you progress you learn how to play smarter, and with each rundown the game gets more and more interesting. If you don't have any friends with the game, don't fret, there is a very helpful player base on discord who is more than happy to help you learn. The game rewards you with new outfits for customization with each successful mission, so there's plenty of gear to keep you coming back. Finally, the game gets lots of support and constant updates with new rundowns, gear, new enemies, bosses, etc.  I highly recommend getting a group of friends to buy this together as it will give you hundreds of hours of fun and is well worth full price.
