_childDocuments_.review: Initial Review (Rundown 4):I bought this fully expecting to fail very hard.I did not only just fail extremely hard, but had fun playing.Having a team of friends to play with makes this so much more enjoyable.And for those people who don't have friends to play with, the discord community is quite active and it is easy to find people to play with or potentially become friends with.It has a lot of room for learning, once you get to beating the more difficult levels, you realize you have much more to learn in the iceberg known as GTFO.Edit (Rundown 5): So the new rundown released, here are my thoughts. It. Is. Difficult. If you're picking this game up for the first time, good luck. It is more challenging than the last rundown and you do have to be more mindful of your resources. If you feel like your flashlight is obscuring your vision, that is intentional. That's all I can say without spoiling anything else in the game for newcomers.If you haven't already, I also recommend joining the GTFO discord server where you can find other players to play with.Good luck out there.Edit 2 (1.0 release / Rundown 6):So this rundown has brought upon some new features and balancing. Here's my thoughts on it. They added bots! For those of you that don't have any friends, it is now possible to have bots fill in as teammates. I mean, they get the job done. You can tell them to use their utility or follow you, as far as I know.This rundown also seems a bit easier for the first levels of each 'tier'.. They seem to have decided to pack a bunch more story/lore into this rundown.One thing I noticed, you can no longer infinitely sprint as doing so will raise your pulse and inevitably you'll become as slow as a snail trying to run away. Having a maximized pulse means you will not regenerate health and will have a walk speed/sprint speed de-buff.Jumping, Sprinting, Swinging your melee weapon, will raise your pulse.This rundown has also added a checkpoint system where you are able to start from a checkpoint if you get to one when you fail. Mixed feelings about that so far as it seems to break *some* objectives. Mostly the secondary ones.The level design definitely improved this rundown. That's all I'd like to say to not spoil anything about the levels.Good luck and happy exploring.

Is it perfect? No but it's improved so much I can only feel excited for more in the future. The games unforgiving nature is still there but where it felt like the game actively hated you before, not it feels like it respects teams who communicate and work together. The AI is nothing short of moronic which will be an issue for solo-players but me and 2 friends have managed to enjoy the challenge (one insisting on using a gamepad!) and although we wipe a lot we can always recognise the mistakes we made rather than feeling the game boned us, so I don't feel a full 4 person team is a must.The atmosphere in the game is awesome, it really feels oppressive and intimidating, as you progress you really get a feel for how horrible things are and how doomed the world seems to be. The enemies default nature of sleeping or aimlessly wandering is yet to feel not creepy to me too. This isn't a 'scary' game, but it's a creepy one and does it perfectly.Oh and not really related to the game, but the voice actor in the 1.0 trailer is amazing. I don't think I've heard someone convey utter soul crushing fear without having to express in words their emotions before!

Alot of the weapons have unique traits, for example: The sniper rifle, while useless against hordes is key to clear a room of a scout, who goes invulneral as soon as you hit it with a weaker weapon, while the sniper rifle dispatches him immediately. _childDocuments_.review: This game is what would happen if you put Payday: The Heist, Resident Evil, and Neon Genesis Evangelion in a blender. It's not an exaggeration to say that the entry barrier is a brick wall, but the game does give you the sledgehammer you'll need to batter it down. Keep at it and you'll go from being crippled by simple mistakes to quickly mitigating the consequences of colossal screw-ups, but don't get too complacent because it will eventually throw a curve ball at you.If you're wondering WHY you're crawling around a foggy underground hell hole you're about on the same page as the people you're playing as. Those pods they get pulled out of at the start of every mission damage their memories so they have only the faintest idea of who they are and what they're doing, so don't worry too much about it.Matchmaking is a bit FUBAR as I'm writing this, so you might have to go poking around the game's discord to get a full group if you don't have friends to play with already. You can play alone with bots and probably manage to complete at least Rundown 1 if you equip them properly. They do make extremely stupid decisions sometimes though so be prepared for that. On the bright side: With the right weapons they can be relied on to hit their targets. Just avoid giving them low capacity guns and you should be okay.

_childDocuments_.review: At first I laughed when someone told me this game is considered a heist game, but then I thought about it more and realized how damn right that is. It's a heist game except you're heisting from unbelievable nightmares lurking in the darkness, only visible when it's too late or you've made a mistake and they're listening for you. GTFO does insanely well at immersing you, from the UI effects, terminal system for finding objectives that demands ACTUAL learning of its commands and inner workings, to learning the way the different enemies can be defeated or outmaneuvered. In the end, it always comes down to this- you're intruding, and you WILL have to activate an alarm at some point.Unfortunately, the only downside to this wonderful game is that... it takes so damn long to do the harder missions. It makes sense, and is satisfying the whole way through, but damn do I struggle to play 3 hours of one mission. Mods can help clean up the sloppy place of checkpoints so at least failing partway through doesn't mean over an hour lost, but... oof.★★★★☆/★★★★★ - Masterpiece, but long mission durations make short sessions unlikely

_childDocuments_.review: Wanna start by saying I'm looking at this from a post-beta play standpoint.TLDR; Overall a pretty fun game that's just not worth the full price right now. Had they kept the beta price, I would absolutely say get it, but at $40USD, I can't truly say yes. Once more cosmetics and new, (hopefully) longer rundowns come out, definitely get this game.- Overall, WAAAAAY easier than the beta, and I'm not sure how I feel about that. Managed to clear A1, B1 and C1 solo with bots, where as in EXP4, I couldn't get past B1 with 2 other friends without having quite a bit of trouble. I liked the difficulty, not the tedium. Now, both seem to be removed.- The game is beautiful, daunting, and atmospheric as all hell. It's got a very 'Alien' vibe to the facility, feeling much like a concrete Nostromo. While the game isn't scary in the slightest, the tense atmosphere is killer when it counts. GTFO covers all of its design bases with nice wide sounds, foggy and dark environments, foreboding festering caverns, and mossy machinery concrete structures reclaimed by nature. Very,  nice to look at and listen to.- The new melee weapons are very cool, and I'm in def love with the spear and knife. However, there's not much else to say about the melee, since really you only have 2 attacks; the good one, and the bad one.- GTFO is VERY well optimized, and it's a blessing. At maxed out settings (aside from fog resolution) on my test rig (GTX2060, r7-3700x @3.6, 16gb DDR4 RAM), this game runs at a smooth 144FPS with drops no lower than 120 during crazy scenes. On a weaker test rig at the same settings (GTX1650, i5-2500 @2.5, 16GB DDR4 RAM), it ran at a solid 75FPS, dropping no lower than 50 during intense fights (60 with low shadows and contact shadows), so it was still very playable on a far less than budget rig.- The feel of the gunplay and animations are much better than in the beta, but still not good enough to make me  to shoot. Shooting probably shouldn't feel like a hassle in an FPS, but hey, I'm no game dev.It's very jumpy, super unsatisfying, and feels like I'm missing at point blank, while nearly barrel stuffing enemies. Normally that would immediately shut me off to a game, but really, your melee is the primary here, so while not a huge deal, it could still use some tweaking. The only weapon I've yet to experience this with are the shotguns, merely because they cover such a large spread.- The character customization is pretty basic right now but very nice to have! Letting you choose your mask, torso, pants, backpack and color palette, it seems like they have quite a bit planned.The problem is that the cosmetics at the moment are some of the most ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ atrocious apparel choices I've ever seen in my life. The main characters look so awesome and bad ass! SO WHY ARE ALL THE UNLOCKABLE COSMETICS JORTS WITH PANTYHOSE UNDERNEATH THE SAME COLOR AS MY GRANDMOTHERS SOUP FROM WHEN I WAS 6 YEARS OLD, OR CRUSTY LONG SLEEVED SHIRTS FROM THE BOTTOM OF THE LAUNDRY BASKET. We don't need crazy flashy cosmetics like CoD, but give us something that we wanna wear for heavens' sake. Until I unlock much more gear, I'm sticking to the base cosmetics and the B1 pants.- While I personally don't have a problem with no party matchmaking, I do understand that's a huge turnoff to a lot of players. YOU CAN SOLO MATCHMAKE, TO BE CLEAR; but yeah if you wanna play with a friend and randoms, you'll need to join the GTFO Discord or something. Also, they're adding party match making, so you could also just wait ig

Carefully crafting a plan, you execute through the darkness, until you've reached *the spot*.Everyone is anxious. There's no checkpoint around, ammo is running a bit lower than you'd like. Maybe we didn't prep right?"Wth even is a M Class alarm anyway?"You open the door.Shots get fired. "I'm down!"Mines go off.That one guy runs around, and all you can hear is a total stampede around your dying body.He somehow pulls it off, rinsing an entire wave with his Heavy Assault Rifle. Everyone cheers!And beyond the door is wast amounts of health and ammo, and suddenly a sense of dread fills you. _________Absolutely love this game. Play it with friends. Rundowns offer a type of seasonal content, swapping out gear and missions, giving the game a lot of longevity.10 Chambers are working actively on the title, and they've made something that's truly worth supporting. The atmosphere is brilliant. Although the visceral horro feeling might wear off, you will be anxious moving around in the shadows, worried about having missed that one enemy, that will trigger certain doom for everyone. It's not a game for everyone, but I have a feeling more people would enjoy this game a lot more than they would think.

_childDocuments_.review: This game's whole atmosphere is insane, the UI, gameplay, and storyline are very detailed and immersive and match the tense, yet entertaining gameplay. The gameplay is focused around stealth (optional) but there are parts of very chaotic, stressful fights that you have to keep focused on what you are doing which creates a very unique experience. The amount of content in this game is very large as there are currently 7 rundowns which have many missions inside of them, rundown 1 has 6 missions and it took me 18 hours to complete rundown 1, and the later rundowns are larger with 12 missions and some missions has up to 2 optional objectives along with the main objective per mission. The gameplay is quite hard, but not enough to be annoying. I would like an in-game server browser to play with others, but currently it is heavily relied on Discord, which isn't bad, it just breaks the immersion. While there is a system for matchmaking, no one uses it and its not great. The weapons in GTFO are very unique and there is at least 2 guns for how you like to play and are very balanced. How enemies have very realistic bodies that break apart as you hit them is very unique. You have to manage resources wisely and efficiently as there are not many resources so melees are very helpful. You have to communicate with teammates, establish plans, and execute them with little room for error. I would recommend this game to people who like horror, cooperative, risky, and atmospheric shooters.

_childDocuments_.review: A while ago, I made a review ranting about the confusing actions of the devs/moderators against their own playerbase, as well as the STEEP learning curve to moderately succeed, and the absolutely terrible endgame.I can safely say, as of 1.0, GTFO is definitely better now. They have made the game generally more accessible through checkpoints and have MUCH more community transparency. By implementing systems like pulse, the game is a lot more grounded. The Hardcore aspect still exists at the core of it, you will still be greatly challenged no matter what.Before, I ranted about the confusing actions of the devs and moderators that actively punished their own playerbase (modding, accusations of datamining, etc). Now, I can say that all of that is gone. They are okay with dataming, they are okay with mods, generally the game has never been better, and I can't stop gushing how good this current rundown is.A1 is an amazing tutorial, there are many brand new mechanics and changes, and overall, it feels like a much more polished game. Before, this game was like terrible spicy food. You'd get something simple absolutely covered with spicy powder just to make it hot. Now though, the game is spicy without the powder. The difficulty doesn't feel artificial and unplaytested anymore, the levels all have a unique aspect to them. I can honestly say I'm excited for the future of the game.It's a great game made even better, and you should probably play it.Turns out I was proven wrong.OLD REVIEW:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Great Game, don't play it. The first few hours are amazing, it truly captures co-op stealth perfectly, but after being in this game for a while, I can't recommend it for 90% of people considering trying it out. The endgame is the complete opposite of starting out, where run and gun with hammers ONLY is meta and effectively forced on harder levels. I don't like the direction the game is going, because it seems each rundown gets harder and stealth is less and less incentivized. Most Importantly though, the devs actively seek out loyal fans and threaten them with DMCA and legal stuff. I'll elaborate:A dedicated player was able to find exact damage points for each weapon, an estimate for enemy health, and much more useful information about the game in general. They got the damage numbers by shooting teammates, and lots of time and dedication went into it. Soon after it was posted they got a message from a specific dev through discord threatening legal action for datamining, which is against the game's EULA, which you agree to when you buy the game. They manged to calm them down, and keep the numbers up, but given the vibe in the screenshots they feel generous for giving the benefit of a doubt.That's not all.Modding was essentially forbidden, until recently they went lighter on it. They still hold the firm opinion that they don't care as long as it doesn't harm other players' experience, which is very understandable. However, Modded screenshots were banned before and strict rules were put on modding in general. This led to essentially a "underground" community of multiple modding discords, with the organizers getting threatened with legal stuff whenever they were caught.Summary:The first hours are great. You have no idea what to expect, the atmosphere is spooky, and you slowly learn more and more and go deeper and deeper. However, it quickly devolves into kiting and hammer meta, and guns only being used in alarms or specific situations. If you don't git good at holding shift, bhopping, and only using hammer to take out many enemies, you WILL NOT get far. The new rundown's levels are even worse at this than the last, having constant alarms in regular B levels, which heavily punishes regular gun usage. The new levels are also difficult, to the point where I doubt 70% of new players get past A tier this rundown. There are many other points I could make, but if you are questioning buying it, you are best just moving on and either waiting for it to get better or ditching it entirely.I want to be proven wrong in the future.Important Sources:(Veteran player's EULA experience and reason for leaving)(Spreadsheet creator's current opinion of the devs)(Edit)(Dev Screenshots, EULA threats)

_childDocuments_.review: This game has an identity crisis. They wanted to create a game where tactics, planning, and stealth take center stage instead of a shear guns blazing approach. Scarce supplies in an unknown environment facing a threat that can kill you and your team quickly really serve to drive this point home that GTFO is meant to be a difficult, challenging game where careful thought and planning are preferable to anything else. This sounds like an interesting experience on paper, but then the developers decided it was a good idea to throw this formula out the window and force you into situations where you have to stay in one location fighting a large group of enemies that can and will overwhelm you faster than you can fight them, and you will not have the ammunition or resources to handle this onslaught. This is done through alarmed security doors that not only break the flow of the intense environment and swift and decisive planning, but is a complete 180 from the very core of what this game was marketed as. Whoever thought it was a good idea force the players into an open combat scenario in a game that wasn't designed for that to begin with probably should have taken more time to reconsider. GTFO could have been great, but when it comes to that part of this game, all I can say is "people, pick a lane and stay in it."

_childDocuments_.review: About:If you enjoyed R6 Seige or Dying Light, GTFO is sure to please. There is a strong teamwork element as this is meant for 4 player coop, and you will need to communicate and work together to GTFO of each level. The gameplay and guns are really well done and there is some melee involved if you want to save ammo and be stealthy. There are a variety of monsters you will encounter in the depths. The difficulty can be immersive, and you must pay attention to the team's resource management to survive.Comments, Concerns, Suggestions:  Matchmaking can be hit or miss. You can fill in the team with bots which work ok, and you can give them orders, but for the best experience I recommend finding a group on discord server or dragging your friends in. The terminals can be cumbersome. They don't take too long to learn, but I feel the accessibility can detract from the gameplay. When your resources are depleted, sometimes you have to use a terminal to list items to find out what is available that hasn't been looted, then query them to find what zone they are in, go back to the zone, then ping them from that zone. It can be a little time consuming. Given that hordes will often approach from narrow passages, friendly fire can be very annoying, but it can be mitigated with good prep and planning before sounding an alarm. It takes a while to experiment with the different loadouts, so it would be nice if you could swap your weapon loadout during a mission.

_childDocuments_.review: GTFO is an immersive, teamwork-oriented, coop survival horror where you and up to 3 other unfortunates are sent into the depths of abandoned underground facility with an important mission... And they don't actually expect you to come back.Now, let me get this clear: don't think of this as another L4D or B4B or whatever else.This is different.How do i even explain this... Think "SWAT" meets "The Thing" meets "Aliens".The loud shooting sections only make up like 1/3 of the game, with majority of time being spent on stealth, exploration and trying to figure what is even your objective.Each mission has its own unique set of objectives. Usually its something related to keeping Complex operational, or making progress on whatever the hell Warden is up to. The gameplay generally consists of 2 sections: stealth and loud. Stealth is NOT optional. Most of the time, anyway. Ammo and other supplies are scarse and it's preferable to avoid any unnecessary spendings.This is where most of playtime goes into. You'll be crawling through dark rooms, smacking sleeping monsters on the head, until eventually you'll run into one of alarm events.This is where loud section begins.The alarm will keep blaring, sending waves of monsters your way, until you do something to stop it. If you even can, that is: some alarms are permanent and will continue until the very moment you extract.During loud gameplay the rest of game's mechanics come into play.Not only prisoners have access to a variety of firearms, each with their own strengths, weaknesses and roles, but also to tactical tools: automated sentries, mines, construction-grade foam and even an Alien-style biotracker. Bringing correct tools for the job and using them appropriately is the key to success. You won't get away with just shooting things yourself - not with this limited ammo supply.You stealth to conserve bullets, you shoot to survive, you survive to get ♥♥♥♥ done, and you get ♥♥♥♥ done to get your extraction point and GTFO.It must be noted that there is no progression system in this game.All the gear is available from the start and there's nothing new to unlock, not even a new aiming sight or anything - all the guns come completely pre-baked.You do, however, receive random cosmetic items for your character upon successful expedition clears. Better than nothing i suppose.

_childDocuments_.review:
GTFO is a 4 player action/horror cooperative first-person shooter for hardcore gamers looking for a real challenge. Players get to play as a team of prisoners, forced to explore and extract valuable artifacts from a vast underground complex that has been overrun by terrifying creatures. Gather weapons, tools, and resources to help you survive - and work to unearth the answers about your past and how to escape.

KEY FEATURES

* 4 player cooperative PvE gameplay that puts you and your teammates through the ultimate cooperation and communication test.
* Explore a massive underground complex with a dense and dark atmosphere.
* Plan your expedition, equip and operate tools, combine your firepower, communicate and coordinate as a team - every detail counts if you are to survive the nightmare.
* Search the complex for information and resources to help you and your team solve your objectives and come back alive.
* The Rundown: New expeditions released regularly that always replaces the old expeditions. Our goal is to invent new ways of challenging you and your teammates in new and interesting ways.
* Nightmarish atmosphere accompanied by music from acclaimed composer Simon Viklund.

detailed_description: WISHLIST MEOW! 😻 Accolades About the Game Martha Is Dead is a dark first-person psychological thriller, set in 1944 Italy, that blurs the lines between reality, superstition and the tragedy of war. As conflict intensifies between German and Allied forces, the desecrated body of a woman is found drowned… Martha! Martha is dead, and her twin sister Giulia, the young daughter of a German soldier, must alone deal with the acute trauma of loss and the fallout from her murder. The hunt for the truth is shrouded by mysterious folklore and the extreme horror of war that draws ever closer. What will prevail? FEATURES Unashamedly authentic voice acting in Italian The first Indie game to launch using the native Italian language as the default setting – for full immersion into the story and the characters. From the creator of The Town of Light The second game from LKA, the award-winning developer of “The Town of Light” and specialists in reality-based narrative games focused on tough subjects. Deep and dark multi-layered narrative Martha Is Dead is an exploration of loss, relationships, and the psychological undertones of a dark period of history through the eyes of a young woman who seeks the truth, but who also has secrets of her own to hide. Explore a detailed recreation of the Italian countryside Freely explore the breathtakingly realised Tuscany countryside on foot, by boat, or by bike. Grounded in reality, Martha Is Dead’s setting and historical context are inspired by real facts and places that have been faithfully reconstructed in true LKA fashion. Play with dolls Play with numerous marionette sequences in the puppet theatre to remember repressed memories. Mixing folklore with superstition Unlock symbols and use tarot cards to unveil new aspects of the game and summon the spirit of The Lady. A backdrop of War Collect newspapers, and telegrams and listen to the radio to keep updated on what is occurring in the world during the war. Virtual photographic greatness Take pictures for the sheer pleasure of doing so, and also to progress through the story and discover more about the game world. A simulator will guide you through 1940s photography, where you’ll be able to develop your actual photos through a fully working in-game darkroom! Authentic Italian music of the era Immerse yourself in a deeply evocative and atmospheric soundtrack containing underwater music specialists Between Music and their Aquasonic project; The Town of Light composer Aseptic Void and his moody yet spinetingling tones; and held together in true vintage style featuring reimagined versions of classic tracks including Schubert's Ave Maria, O Bella Ciao, with original tracks written and sung by Francesca Messina, AKA 90s disco star, Femina Ridens.

_childDocuments_.review: I am giving a recommendation to play it as a HORROR GAME ONLY, but with the following warnings:1. This game begins with a crisis information website. There's a reason for it. Trust me on this. 2. The game is filled with triggering images and disturbing scenes/themes/topics. It covers everything from homicide to war crimes to miscarriage to animal abuse to child abuse to suicide. If you are a survivor of any of those types of severe traumas or may still have PTSD from combat or abuse, I would highly suggest you consider finding a game that isn't this one. It's likely to bring up some very negative memories and feelings that could re-traumatize you. Better to be safe than sorry. Lots of games out there are horror that don't go this deeply into extremely disturbing topics like these, especially in the detail you'll experience them if you play this game. It is TRIGGERING to an extreme. Just a warning on that.3. There's a LOT of Nazi imagery in the game. This could be upsetting for some people. 4. I work for a suicide/crisis hotline. This game was mentioned to me because of its triggering nature. I played it mainly to see what it was about. As a person who works in the field of mental health, I am very cognizant that a game of this type, portraying these types of images, and immersing the player in a lot of horrible situations...may be extremely difficult for many people. If you are suffering from any severe mental health disorder, especially depression or anxiety, I would suggest again that you consider playing something different. This game would likely make you feel worse. You don't need that.And if you play this game and feel like you're having a hard time coping with the game or its topics, please stop playing it. If it is damaging to you (and you should know what that feels like) or puts you in a sense of mental health crisis, PLEASE turn the game OFF, uninstall it, and then...reach out to a friend, a loved one, your doctor, your therapist, etc. You can also contact one of the many crisis/suicide hotlines available worldwide. Some even allow you only to talk via text.So, if you are inured to violence and none of the topics I mentioned above are something you have personally dealt with (or have been traumatized by in your past), the game itself is beautiful, mesmerizing in many ways, and the story is very engaging (almost too much so). The soundtrack is really great, too.  With all this said, on the basis of it being a HORROR GAME ONLY with its strong story, great soundtrack and gorgeous visuals, I can recommend it. However, PLAYER BE WARNED....that's all I have left to say about it.

_childDocuments_.review: 1944. Italy is ravaged by the misery of war, with Allied forces moving up towards the Tuscany region while Axis troops mount a desperate defense. Protagonist Giulia K. is the daughter of a high-profile Nazi officer, but even this privileged position doesn’t save her from tragedy. One day, her twin sister Martha is found dead in a lake - an overwhelming loss. She always was her parents’ favorite, unlike Giulia, so the latter decides to take her identity, pretending to be her from that moment forward, to gain the love so far denied to her.MiD mostly takes place in and around a countryside villa outside the village of San Casciano, Tuscany. There’s a remarkable attention to detail in the realization of each location, from the interiors of a typical upper-class 1940 Italian household, with luxuries such as electric power and a phone line, to the verdant woods and sun-beaten dirt paths commonly seen in the rural areas of the region even today. The marked contrast between these idyllic landscapes and the brutality of war, or the horrifying visions in Giulia’s mind, creates a rollercoaster of varied atmospheres that works out very well.Apart from the protagonist, there’s a small roster of relevant characters that, however, never happen to dialogue directly with you at any point: a consequence of the recent events, and of the pretense Giulia decided to put up. You’ll hear conversations, read missives, listen to telephone calls, but never engage in active dialogues save for some phone calls at specific points. The writing feels plausible, with an Italian voiceover that accounts for the different mannerisms and speech patterns of the time. Most situations feel plausible and realistic, even if (probably by design) you’ll end up questioning the veracity of some of them as the game progresses. The story plays out through a number of days, each having a primary objective related to the events at hand, and a series of optional activities as well. Generally, you’ll be able to explore the world freely at any time, with the primary areas being the villa and its courtyard, the nearby forest and the lake. Some places will be locked until specific events happen, or certain quests are triggered by your findings. Your trusty camera will be of paramount importance, as it will not only allow you to collect evidence in order to shed light on your sister’s death, but also to use filters (such as infrared) to reveal the unseen. There are a vast number of interactable objects that reveal more about the family’s past, the general lore or the people related to you in some way, each of them is voice-narrated by Giulia. Those looking to do everything will find much information in these optional interactions, they’re definitely worth the extra time spent.While your focus remains finding the truth about Martha’s death, there will be other things to do as well. For instance, hidden riddles can be found by photographing specific objects in the world, optional points of interest that reveal dark stories, or trigger quests altogether. These missions may be optional, but contain a good chunk of unique content, such as puzzles, minigames and sub-storylines regarding parallel ongoing events. Some of these elements also can be missed, since the game progresses in a series of days alongside the main quest’s evolution: after certain events unfold, some areas may not be accessible anymore, thus locking the quests out forever (unless you reload an earlier save). Going just for the main story is something I wouldn’t recommend, as these secondary missions, even if a tad annoying in pacing at times, prove overall interesting and expand on the narrative considerablyThe most frequent type of puzzle will be associated with photography: relevant items to frame, both primary and secondary, will be highlighted on your HUD, and it will be up to you to use the right camera accessories, such as filters, and set the right zoom level, exposure and focus to get the perfect shot. Not only that, but photos also need to be developed in a dark room, which involves a simple button-pressing prompt as QTE. Other than that, you’ll eventually be decoding telegraph ciphers, finding items such as keys to unlock doors, boxes and passages containing critical items, or figure out the right things to say in a phone call to extract information. There are also a few quick-time events here and there, but they’re fairly simple and not demanding in skill or reflexes at all, in line with the genre’s expectations.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? After a brief flashback from your childhood (1929), a 15 year time jump without any remembrance of the time between, the game begins in mid-1944 and you find your (deaf) twin sister Martha floating dead in a lake. Was she killed? Why is she wearing your clothes? Why can't you remember anything? After pulling her out, your parents think you are Martha, and so you switch identities. For reasons only known to yourself, you do not tell anybody that you are Martha's sister, Guliana. While your father always loved you (Guliana), your mother loved Martha, but not you. The game takes place in Tuscany, a region in Central Italy around the beautiful town of Florence. Your mother is Italian, but your father is a General in the German army. Quite an interesting (and strange) setting, for a supernatural horror game. Or is it a thriller? Or just an adventure?The controls work a bit like in Heavy Rain or the newer Vertigo. Press a mouse button and move the mouse in a direction to start actions. The game plays in first person perspective and makes heavy use of head bobbing and focusing/defocusing  to create suspense. In my case this mostly creates nausea and hurting eyes. Items in your inventory are used automatically (at the right spot). You carry a camera around with you and have to take pictures at certain spots. I hope you understand a bit of photography (in the pre-mobile phone days), because the game expets you to control aperture, exposure, focus, use different lenses, filters, films, flashes and whatever on your camera. After taking pictues, you have to go in the darkroom to develop them. At least this process has been considerably simplified compared to real life developement. I mean, I am playing a psychological horror game, and I am not taking a historical photographer course. Most of the game consists of walking around and examining your sourroundings, using items at the right spot. There are also some action sequences, when you fail one, you start again at the beginning - until you pass it. Or quit. The game is saved automatically at certain checkpoints, or you can save manually. You can always access a map, your objectives, an album of the photos you made or a log of the text read so far. Using a controller is possible. The story is told by a (rather good) narrartor. The graphics are close to photorealistic. And the environement is detailled. Really detailled, I have never seen such a realistic environment in a game. They stutter a bit on my PC (GTX 1070) when I move too fast, though. The houses and everything really look (and sound) like in real life, not something that has been made just for a game. Not even the visuals in "The Vanishing of Ethan Carter" came close to that. Really nice. At least the visuals are certainly a masterpiece.Graphically superior psychological thriller taking place in rural war-torn Central Italy of 1944.

_childDocuments_.review: On paper, this game is awesome. In practice, it falls short in almost every department. Before you call me a 'hater' please understand I spend my own cash playing this type of game to then list them as part of the only '' fan club i know of on Steam. So I have a lot of experience with these games: what makes a good experience or a bad one. This one has been terribly mediocre. I rarely complain about performance because I have a great rig and i regularly repaste it. But here, The graphics are good  without being great , yet they come at the price of strange, unwarranted performance cost (something the the developers are aware of). On a machine that can play CP77 at 70 FPS on ultra with DLSS set to 'quality @5k in SUW mode of all things, here I'm struggling to get 20fps in 'high performance' while locked at 1440p (so SUW option). I even had to drop the quality setting to 'high' to make the game playable. Objects pop into view (a clear sign of VRAM swapping despite having a card with 8GB of GDDR6 and 64 gig of RAM matched to a socketed i9900k). This is not acceptable. And the framerate drops constantly even if you drop the graphics to medium, meaning the problem is not rendering but elsewhere.I can't even imagine what the people who usually complain about framerate will say about this one! In addition, there are numerous crashes, geometry locks, and other annoyances that will force you to reload. So save often, no quick save is available however.None of this would really matter if the story was captivating - but it's just an awfully complicated, strange mess that initially give you the illusion of an open world only to place you on rails and never letting you go . At some point, you're given a chance to dial phone numbers. That opportunity is taken away from you and never given back if you 'trigger' an even by 'walking' in the 'wrong' place. Likewise, the game give you this amazing camera with TONS of options. They get used twice in the game, and the myriad of options are just an in-game toy to take neat screenshots. How disappointing. Imagine someone telling you 'hey i have this special filter that can see... ghosts' so you go around and take pictures of all the graves and nothing happens. But walk on the right 'trigger' and suddenly the same graves that didn't give out ghostly pictures will suddenly do so. Everything is on rails.Everything is scripted, and badly so. There are weird running labyrinth were you have to proceed by trial and error. There are underwater scenes where you can't go to the surface because it's a hidden boundary but you could in the previous scene. There are elements that are extremely hard to locate and I overall I felt I spent more time working around all this than actually playing a game.I would only recommend this game sub $10 AFTER they fix all the patches. It's short, it's clunky, and quite frankly we have so many alternatives in the walking simulator genre today, we have the right to demand the best. Look at Observer: System Redux if you don't believe me. Look at games like the Stanley Parable ultra deluxe. Heck - even the aged "Ethan Carter" still feel more modern than this.I feel about about giving the game a thumb down because some elements are really well done and conceptually, the idea was neat. But numerous technical issues, a lack of flexibility forcing people to reload old save to complete 'side missions' and a general feeling that the game is not finished stop me from recommending this title. Better luck next time.

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost, DO NOT play this game if you are squeamish to gore or sensitive to topics such as abuse, self-harm, and the like. Martha is Dead has multiple trigger warnings, some people chose to ignore those warnings and then had the audacity to complain when they witness something graphic. It’s laughable but I digress…Martha is Dead tells the story of…well, how Martha died. Going any deeper than that will probably spoil but I can definitely vouch for this game's story. It takes place in 1944 Italy and it’s not just about a young girl's internal struggle. It also portrays the tragedy involving World War ll and how people were affected by it. It’s like a historical-psychological-thriller mixed genre and I am all for that.  Gameplay mostly involves walking, biking, taking photographs, and developing those photos in the darkroom. There are different dialogue choices you make and you can explore the semi-open world, which is gorgeous by the way. The performance was not that great. There were a bunch of bugs and the stuttering was so bad I had to wait a couple of weeks for the game to be patched by the devs and they did. It now runs much smoother compared to its first week of release. They were on top of it, listening to everyone's requests/issues, and now the game is playable with some minor issues I’m sure they’ll fix with some future patches. This game is not for everyone. There are some scenes where even I, a horror lover, was shocked to see but no way would I wish for it to be censored (like it was on ps). The devs were kind enough to give people who bought it on ps steam keys if they didn't want to play the censored version of the game. I applaud them for doing that and for not playing it safe by sugar coating how brutal the war and people's ideologies were like back then.

_childDocuments_.review: is a psychological horror game heavily driven by its story. LKA Studio is tackling mental health issues and disorders and is doing it so brilliantly. The game takes place in Italy near the end of World War II. You will play Giulia K, the daughter of Nazi General Erich K, and while on a routine walk near the lake you find the floating body of your dead twin sister and embark on a journey to make sense of it and explain her death.We should start this review by saying that I would not recommend this game for whoever doesn’t like the sight of more graphic content, some scenes are disturbing, shocking, and not something you will typically see anywhere. With some pretty heavy trigger warning sounds, you will know when something is about to happen. With that in mind, Martha is Dead will not leave you indifferent on that aspect for better or for worse while exploring the world through Giulia’s perspective and her camera lenses.This was a truly horrifying experience, in the good sense of the term, without much context and not knowing the extent of what I was getting into, I expected ghosts, terror, jump scare, even zombies at some point. Instead, I got to go through this adventure with my imagination as my worse enemy. Not knowing what was going to happen, even trying to stop my character to do things at times but just being powerless and watching as everything unfolds.Throughout our investigation, Martha is Dead feels like an adventure-walking simulator with impeccable graphics, design, atmosphere, and an amazing system to immerse ourselves into it. Some sort of open-world is offered to us in the confine of our map, to find more elements of the story, more context, and details to read, analyze, think about to piece it all together. On top of that, we are free to take pictures with our camera as we please and go and develop them in the black room. This feature was really enjoyable with tons of different variations, lenses, and extra components added to the camera as we progress through the story. Photography is the hobby/passion of Giulia, an extensive amount of work was put into making it a core element of gameplay. Furthermore, the game is graphically stunning and will leave you in awe with the level of details. It contributes to a lot of the immersion and when most of your job is to take pictures, having some sense of artistic freedom and realism just seems natural. I was not expecting such high-quality work done on that front. The story is extremely well-written, the plot gets only better with time and some choices will have to be made during the journey. Whether it is through discussing with other characters of impact or for deciding your future actions on your own. It is unclear whether these have any impact on the story but it added some extra content to a game that can feel somewhat short to play without it.The ambiance is really well made and the exploration is rewarded, from the music, radio, pictures, paintings, everything has their own part to play in the world of Giulia and every room, corridor, and conversation mean something.The voice acting was really well-made, but only in Italian. It was pretty mediocre in English, the translations were accurate enough but had some mistakes, do yourself a favor and play the game in Italian with English subtitles, you will not regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Martha Is Dead

_childDocuments_.review: Martha Is Dead is a truly fantastic looking game with some great multilingual audio and an intriguing story to boot.While not extremely heavy on the scares, the game does a great job at building atmosphere and dread as the story progresses. Set against the harrowing backdrop of WW2, you'll play as Giulia, adopting your dead sister's identity after a misunderstanding. From there, Giulia will begin living a lie as she tries to discover who (or what) killed her sister. There will be many opportunities for you take different paths and make different choices. Some are meaningless, but others might have dire consequences. For a couple of examples - now that you're Martha, will you wear her clothes or you own? If you find secret information, will you keep it to yourself or tell the authorities?If you're a fan of vintage photography, this game will certainly scratch that itch, allowing you access to many accessories, lenses and a full-fledged dark room for you to use. Taking photos is an integral part of the game so you'll want to keep an eye out for little camera icons along your journey. It's an in-depth and intricate part of the game which I enjoyed using.This version is the uncensored one, so it does include some rather gruesome and unsettling scenes, so you have been warned.The game will likely last you at least around 4-5 hours. If you decide to investigate everything and try different paths, then I wouldn't be surprised if that number nears 10.

_childDocuments_.review: I waited a really long time to play this.  I am one of the patient (cheap) gamer crew, so I waited for an eternity for this to go on sale.  I’m glad I did because its pretty pricey for what it is.  It still gets the thumbs up though because it is a pretty good slow burn horror game that has virtually no jump scares and relies more on narrative and a visceral feeling of being in the shoes of the character to make you feel uneasy. I am glad I finally got to play this.  I think it is too much of an asking price and definitely recommend on a sale.  If you are in the mood for a dark walking sim with some puzzles then its pretty good.  As I mentioned before, there are horror elements to the game but it doesn’t have a single jumpscare.  It is creepy because it immerses you in the life of the protagonist and it does a good job of keeping you engaged in the story.

_childDocuments_.review: Martha is Dead is without doubt something that doesn't pop out from every corner - and for a reason because it is one of if not even the most terrifying psychologically challenging game I've played. Through the game the player is pushed to situations and visions that no sane person would like to watch too long. I mean that there is more than a handful of something caught from the worst nightmares and I'm not only talking about how gruesome they are but they stimulate almost too well of human mind which can snap in the wrong position in the most fatal way. Martha is Dead is the most miserable tale of how monstrous one can become if the current environment and the past direct so.The game takes place in the small villa in Italy's countryside near the end of WW2 where Allies are pushing forth and the country is more or a less in chaos reigned by National Socialists' Germany. Without spoiling too much of the remarkable story I cover the beginning where Guilia find's her twin sister Martha's corpse in the lake and as terrified she is she is also righteous and wants to find out who killed her twin. Nevertheless through fast twists and turns she also becomes anxious and haunted by the happened events and constantly falls deeper and deeper into state where both player and Guilia question what is actually true and what is not.Thus it is enough to say that the game is story rich and so rich that the layers within form a stack so huge that it is actually meant impossible to make any proper conclusions for protagonist's morals, fate, visions and past are left open. When I completed the game I watched a couple of analysis and I found out that there might be as many theories that there are players. But that much I know that the feelings I had changed from pure pity to utter rage towards the main character - there was a tiny moment I felt that I had to actually close the game, maybe uninstall it for I barely could watch this circus any longer.Martha is Dead isn't just psychological creep show though because there is some simple, but entertaining learning matter as well. The biggest feature is gorgeous WW2 era camera, which player uses to proceed in their objects but can use it freely to take pictures whenever and wherever they like and these pictures are developed in old fashioned way in a darkroom with thin red light and devices. The procedure is documented in detail from the beginning to the end also underlining the parts where it would take longer in real life. The telegraph is another thing which is used few times and I definitely know better now how to write Morse code if I ever need to. There is also lot of walking in the small but nice looking area and sometimes the game can feel rather a walking sim than a psycological horror/thriller, which it is but the more peaceful parts work as a good variation at least.  The icing on the cake is default Italian voice-overs and I do recommend to play it with those and English subtitles to fill the immersion. English voice-over is available option though.Even when I had played LKA's previous game 'The Town of Light', other controversial game still giving me creeps, Martha is Dead delivered something unforgettable. The most hawk eyed players have even seen some connections between the games. However, I hold no shame of playing this although  I would never recommend this to everyone because Martha is Dead is not for everyone. Period. It is an honest, uncensored and merciless ride into twisted and despaired human mind and I can't judge who is going to 'like' it or not, but for me it was dancing in the nonexistent line of sick taste, art and documentary finally making it over the finish line.If you should start this game, be honest with yourself and listen to your feelings. If any worse vibes emerges take care of yourself, refund the game and hug some of your loved ones.

_childDocuments_.review: "Martha Is Dead" is a psychological thriller set in 1944 Italy amidst the Second World War.Not really a jump-scare game, it is rather a look into the darkness of a troubled mind using horror and macabre, unsettling imagery.The story is very well written and the plot intelligently developed.  It has the feel of a "who-dunnit?" novel.I decided to play the game using the Italian voice acting (with English subtitles), which for me enhanced the experience from a historical location point of view.FPS drops in a few areas forced me to lower the graphics settings, because it resulted in your character being instantly turned around, going back the way you came from instead of continuing on to your goal.Overall, the game was well worth experiencing.

_childDocuments_.review: I really did a step out of my comfort zone with this game but it was nothing but worth it. The last week I was on vacation leave from work. I wanted to play a story game to have something to do my initial plan was to replay one of my favourite games in Witcher 3. While traveling through the world I intended to watch my favourite German Youtuber, Gronkh, again like in the good old days. When I stumbled over his playthrough of Martha is Dead I remembered hearing quite a lot about this little game. After 5 minutes of gameplay plus looking at the store page, I decided to play it myself. Coming into the game I didn’t know what to expect. I hoped it to be atmospheric but not so scary that I would ♥♥♥♥ my pants (I am very easy to scare…) and holy hell it was atmospheric. The game came out in a time where we have a new war on the European continent so everything was to be handled with care, this in combination with the game talking about topics in a way a triple A production would never dare to was a supreme combination. The trigger-warning at the beginning and in the middle of the game made the promise for this game to be graphic and so it was. However, this was nothing short of a brilliant way of supporting the story. In general, the game design was brilliant, between beautiful landscapes a scary but also awesome forest and the beautiful yet scary mansion and the morgue in a very sharp graphic the game also offered something more cartoonish which did still not break the dark atmosphere. They really found a perfect balance. I believe for everyone who usually plays horror games this will be nothing… but the game never wanted to be a horror game it wants you to feel unpleasant and this it achieved it for me in nearly all situations of the playthrough. This is also accomplished by the brilliant use of music, not good music in particular, though the game offers some good tracks via radios which are always turned on within the main area of the game those are nothing more than some background noises. I am referring to the music and sounds used when we get to the scarier parts of the game. For example, the use of only a very wrong and shrill played violine while doing something ethically not right did have me shivering. The sounds of the world in general are well done and good used. Well placed wild life noises could make you turn around one more time than you would like because you feel unpleasant. Gameplay wise this game has more to offer than I would have thought going into this adventure. Generally speaking, I like those so called walking simulators but this game had some fresh takes I rarely saw within other games. If it is to develop photos with the description how it would have been done historical speaking or the use of a morse code. Taking photos never was something annoying to me. The game offers a docent of different lenses and other shenanigans to use which gives you a nearly unlimited amount of possibilities and simulates the art of taking pictures back in the 1940s quite well. Story, wise I don’t want to say much, but the story is very winding and makes many turns. As the daughter of a top German General in 1944s Italy, close to the ever more progressing Allies we see the world through the eyes of someone who neither has much to do with the war nor understand it. However as always, we are forced to make decisions based on our hearts. However, this is not our most important task, because we try to solve the murder of our twin sister. We have to deal with beings whose existence we can't understand, and we have to process the new information we receive, while someone seems to be trying to kill us. Everything is under the question Martha or Giulia or is there another possibility?This game did catapult itself into one of my all-time favourites almost immediately. LKA wrote a great story with well thought out characters, side quest, one of the best atmospheres I ever experienced, a great plot and good-looking game, which at the same time doesn’t lose out on the gameplay side of things. The formula to go for such open and no taboo approach, by LKA and Wired production, is brave to say the least, but it was worth a 100%.The game wants you to think about your actions and sayings. Everything you say might have more effect on a person than you could imagine. It is very deep in telling you to watch more for your doings. I want to close this review with what I take away from this piece of art of a game. My learnings are to watch more on my behaviour and not put people into boxes and come to conclusions to fast. Not every one is in a healthy state of mind or feeling as good as I am. Some people have to deal with ♥♥♥♥ far greater than you could ever imagine. It is nothing short of unimaginable what the human brain can do to shield one from what it believes to be dangerous. This can come in an unthinkable amount of different signs and symptoms we might never be able to understand the full function and capacity of the human anatomy. Thus, all I want to say is that “We are nothing but a puppet of our mind” Thank you and if you need help, please reach out for it. You are never alone.~sincerely SVPPweeB

_childDocuments_.review: DISTURBING BUT ERRATIC JOURNEYIf you want to play "Martha is dead", don't expect a horror game, it's a mixture of different simulators with a creepy premise. Despite being a bigger game than their previous "The town of light", "Martha" shouldn't cost 30 euros, because as an experience it cannot rival other AA games."Martha is dead" includes: - Countryside simulator: ✓- Walking and running simulator: ✓- Photography simulator: ✓- Puppeteer simulator: ✓- Tarot reader simulator: ✓- Telegraph simulator: ✓- Bicycle and boat simulators: ✓Apart from that, I would urge the devs to eliminate all "running scared" scenes (especially the ones with words in them) cause they don't add anything at all to an otherwise serious, deeply disturbing tale. Get rid of these fake Alan Wake sentences, and the silly Lady in the lake scares, cause the core of the plot is much more important and disturbing than any horror nonsense. Devs could have created a really memorable mixture of WWII and psychological insanity by relying on the strong aspects of their plot: child abuse, insanity, violence, war, vengeance. Instead, they wanted to explain many films at once:- A half-arsed war story- A half-arsed family drama- A half-arsed ghost story- A half-arsed tarot reader story- A half-arsed love story- A half-arsed asylum storyIt's way too much. By the end, none of the simulators nor none of the stories seems developed enough to leave a lasting impression. On the bright side, each and every one of these ideas, stories and simulators is really interesting and fun, but together they don't make much sense. I would love for the devs to develop in depth seven different stories and games instead of this convoluted mess..As it stands, "Martha is dead" doesn't make much sense and doesn't scare much, in spite of all the gorey scenes that, to be honest, never stroke me as crucial to the plot. I'll play more games by you, LKA. But you can still fix this one! It shows so much promise and it crumbles under the weight of its own ambition! Don't add so much, but instead develop and explore the possibilities of one idea. Explore layers of one idea, go deep into the madness, just like Bloober Team and Frictional Games and Red Barrels and Red Candle do. I know that you can do it cause you've got the vision, the talent and the knowledge.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely beautiful, I love the attention to detail in it. I also can't remember a game where I've ridden such a real looking bicycle in first person (too bad I can't cycle on many paths).The story is very interesting so far and I'm interested to see how it unfolds. I do have some weird lag sometimes where my character gets completely turned around and especially in the forest that's quite annoying, but I'm sure that will be fixed.The voice acting sounds very good and the music is also nice (and some creepy) to listen to. I am very much a scaredy cat when it comes to horror games but this one isn't scary (so far) but just giving a creepy feeling.Edit: After continuing the story more I kind of realize how calling this game "beautiful" may seem a bit weird. I meant the environment and all, lol! The story is sinister to say the least.

_childDocuments_.review: My main complaint is the game-play. It has no real choices and it doesn't make you feel immersed until the end. Someone else in the reviews put it perfectly as a "Walking Simulator". Being a semi choose-your-own-adventure is misleading; most of the time it feels like you're just in the backseat rather than making choices as the character Martha.I Also couldn't tell if the intentional language setting was to be Italian or English. Both didn't sync to the characters models, and never pulled the weight of what exactly they are saying. Martha at moments has some dead-pan, emotionless voice acting. And some of Martha's dialogue could've been cut as well, with it being the trope of "Telling the audience instead of showing it" most of the time. Most of all this game feels like something you should watch a Youtuber or Streamer to react to. The empty game-play gives me the impression that it was ment to be commented over; for a Streamer and their audience.

_childDocuments_.review: Review Updated: March 4, 2022Do I recommend this game? Short answer: Is this game for everyone? No.  ...but if you want a reality-slap about your mental health, go play it.If you are like me, who has been searching for a good game with dark/heavy themes... this game is for you. In its core, Martha is dead delivers an authentic experience. The ambiance and the music perfectly encompass each scene.  The voice acting is splendid! I played through the whole game with the default Italian audio and it does not disappoint. The minor characters are pretty forgettable... But the way they frame the main character is hauntingly realistic. She's perfect. The devs have been working hard to push updates and fixes the past week. The game runs much better now and ray-tracing finally works now. As a general update: This game really hit hard. Remember: It's not too late to ask for help. I applaud the devs. They've succeeded in their message of mental health awareness. Thank you, LKA and Wired.

_childDocuments_.review: I just completed Martha Is Dead today, after less than 6 hours of gameplay. I took my sweet time exploring most options (finished 79% though). Overall, it was a disturbing visual novel with very few actual mechanics to make it feel like a video game. That's fine, but for $30 I expected a bit more enjoyment. And once you've completed the story, there's no real reason to delve back in...unless you're a completionist (which I'm not). If you have a weak stomach or get triggered easily by extreme violence and self-harm, steer clear. If you're a horror fan who likes this subgenre, and you can snag it at a deep discount, it's worth a look.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished it. Wow! Just wow!!! I cried. This is the most sinister game I’ve ever played, and just the raw reality of severe mental illness that it portrayed is absolutely mind-blowing. I dunno if it’s because I’m an IRL mental health therapist with a passion for it, but as gory, gruesome, and triggering that this game is, it was utterly fascinating to me. _childDocuments_.review: (Steam says I have 50+ hours in the game.  This is incorrect.  The game apparently failed to exit properly more than once.)I really wanted to like this game.  I love story games, I'm okay with minimalist game play while being led through a story with no branching.  I'm good with an unreliable narrator.  But Martha is Dead really just falls flat.  The attempts to add game-play elements makes the game frustrating (the telegraph made me want to scream, being forced to do click-drag type actions to mutilate a dead body more than once instead of just watching a cut-scene).  There are too many points where trying to figure out where to go and what to do made me bored with the game. I got stuck on a telephone pole, unable to get down, unable to figure out why, until I happened to _look in the right direction_ at something completely unrelated to my reason for being on the pole.  If you delay certain actions, you get locked out of completing them by story events.  The puppet show was torture... again, making you click and drag and push your way through multiple cut-scenes.  It would have been _less_ tedious if it hadn't been interactive.The sets are well-developed, with a large amount of detail.  The English voice acting is great.  The main character has a beautiful voice and listening to her for hours is easy.  And the story started out as very engaging... but then it all fell apart and it lost my interest, and the ending told me there was no point to trying to figure out what happened, as it was all meaningless.And despite all the poor game-play, that wasn't what ultimately put me off.  The story itself was confused and confusing, and in the end, I disconnected from the main character and _stopped caring_ about her because the unreliable narrator had become so unreliable I wasn't sure about any of the events that had been portrayed, and I just wanted to get the game over with because I hate not finishing a game.

_childDocuments_.review: It was not easy for me to make a decision on how to rate the game and what to write about it (and I've been sitting here for quite a long time, changing parts of the text again and again, rereading it and changing it again and so on. ..).- I really wanted to play the game and my decision to give a thumbs up is based on the fact that I found the game to be quite good despite the later following things. - For someone unfamiliar with the genre or these types of games, the ~$30 could well be a waste of money, so I'd have to give it a thumbs down.- For a concrete recommendation, I would actually prefer a neutral rating, because in my opinion it really depends, for example, on whether you because you could say that the game is more like an interactive audio book novel that comes with lots of text and voice-over. I didn't buy the game on Steam and the $10 i have paid, I think it's still ok. Anyone who knows such or similar games can roughly guess what to expect. As for the differing opinions on playability, it seems that the game actually performs better at some setups and worse on others.  In this context, I cannot say whether it is due to the hardware used, the game settings or what else is done on the side. I also had stutters and frame drops during the game, but I have to say that I played the game in windowed mode due to the situation and used a lot of ALT+TAB, which this game doesn't like at all. Maybe it's due to bad or missing optimization, I don't know.As the brief description on the store page says, the game is a ““, and it is. .  The horror in this game only relates to the "coming" war. But nothing more.If you decide to play the game, , but also bring a good portion of patience with you, since the game is not (yet) completely error-free. It can happen that you often have to reposition yourself in the game before you can interact with something or have to load a save game because you get stuck somewhere. It's not tragic, but can be a bit annoying at times. By the way, there is no jump button, you just walk (run) or ride a bike.I played through the game as much as possible in one go and would also recommend it because of the atmosphere, even if it can be "tiring" at times. I would say the playtime is somewhere between 6 and 10 hours. But it simply depends on whether you complete all (side) tasks and the associated achievements or not. Getting lost and wandering included.If you get involved in the game and the emotional, sometimes confusing and bizarre story, it can be quite captivating and exciting.The game design and the mood it captures is really great and you can see the love for detail on every corner. Graphically, the game is a real eye-catcher. When it comes to the story, it's more up to you to decide whether it's satisfying for you or not.✅ stunning (level) design ✅ great mood captured✅ lovely details✅ bizarre story❌ too expensive ❌ some bugs ❌ possible performance problems
_childDocuments_.name: Martha Is Dead

_childDocuments_.review: Martha is Dead, begins with a heavy disclaimer and rightfully so. The game covers ethically heavy topics such as war crimes, child trauma, pregnancy and mental health. Should you as a player, in any time or point, experienced any form of severe trauma, do please reconsider playing this game. This game excels at story telling and it provides stunning graphics. The narrative is driven and doesn’t feel boring. Thus, you are constantly engaged with the story. As an amateur photographer I loved the mechanics behind old school photography, I have never come across developing photos manually so I loved it. I managed to beat it under 6 hours, would have preferred a longer story. Coming from a medical background, it didn’t seem all too disturbing to me but please do heed the warnings. Maybe I’m just too desensitized due to work. Quick takes:+ Story is great and it provides a few plot twists,+ Graphics is absolutely stunning once you crank up the settings, the game looks okey on medium settings but I did encounter a few visual bugs. Perhaps due to the lower setting. + Taking photos can result in you grabbing a many stunning photos. + The tasks in the game is at period, difficult until you get the hang of it. + You must complete some morse code puzzle, in which was a fun experience. It too took me a while to figure out how to read the morse code map thingy. +/- The soundtrack is on-point but does become "meh" at times. - Walking can be tedious between locations.- It wasn’t scary to play the game and horror aspect of it is lacking. - The story is rather short  Overall, I recommend this game and perhaps we will see a similar game from this game studio in the future? I rate this game 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Martha Is Dead

_childDocuments_.review: A few things to know before you buy:1. It’s short. I don’t rush my games but I still finished it in about 3 sessions of play.2. Don't let the beautiful rural surroundings and old-timey photography and telephones fool you: this is a very gruesome, morbid, tragic and miserable story. And there is a lot of gore, violence and other unpleasantness. This is not a subtle game. It keeps getting in your face, like it’s determined to find some way to upset you.3. There isn’t much interactivity, and what’s there often feels pointless. Like, you’re directed to make the character do something but there’s no way to mess it up, so why make you do it at all? Only, it seems, to make you feel complicit in her actions. There is also a long-ish sequence where you need to uncover the story through controlling a puppet show, which is just incredibly cumbersome and annoying.4. The camera stuff is cool but a lot of the equipment you’re given is superfluous. The photo developing process is boring. And there really isn’t enough to take pictures of that will have any effect on the game.5. The world is small and claustrophobic. You only have the house and the grounds in which to manoeuvre, beautiful as they are.I did finish the story, but only out of a desire for completeness. I was really willing it to end for the last hour or so. All in all, disappointing. Glad it was on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Martha Is Dead

_childDocuments_.review: Martha is Dead was an incredible journey. I went into the game extremely excited from the trailers that I had previously seen before release. I highly recommend this game. Now, let's get into the pros and cons.The developers weren't scared of delving into incredibly dark topics that normally most developers will avoid like the plague, . This can be a turn off to some, and that's okay. That just means the game isn't for you. The soundtrack and atmosphere were both magnificent and well-done. The story that was told in this game is probably one of the best stories I have ever experienced. I found myself crying, almost to the point of an uncontrollable sob when watching the ending and having the credits roll. I found myself to be somewhat relatable to the main character and it just hit very different. If you're looking for a game with a great story, this game is for you. Just be warned, there are some very gruesome scenes.The game definitely needs to be optimized. The developers are aware of the problems that everyone is experiencing and are working on it, as far as I know (per Steam Discussions/Forums). There also appears to be a form of a memory leak when having the game running for several hours at a time. Simply restart the game and it'll be working again. When utilizing the camera to take pictures, any movement with the camera can cause it to jump or stutter, which kind of got annoying but I got used to it. I didn't really encounter any game breaking bugs or glitches.All in all, this was an incredibly fascinating game with a beautiful story to tell. Do I recommend it? 100% yes. But, I recommend waiting until an optimization patch is released, which should hopefully be soon. Thanks for reading! 🥰  🥰
