_childDocuments_.review: ‘Martha is Dead’ is a game created by LKA Studios (authors of the excellent ‘Town of Light’) and was released in February 2022. It tells the story of Giulia K., a young girl who is trying to find out who killed her twin sister Martha. The game is 7/8 hours long and the plot is truly intriguing from the start as we quickly realize that something’s wrong here. Really, really wrong.The game is a walking simulator in a semi-open world: we’re playing as Giulia (in FPP view) and we’re spending most of the time at exploring and looking for objects that are crucial to the story. We can also gather additional informations about some events or characters by reading notes and newspapers and sometimes we have to take photos of certain things to advance the plot. Gameplay-wise it’s just a typical walking-sim, so if you have played games like ‘Firewatch’ or ‘The Vanishing of Ethan Carter’ you know what to expect. There are also few QTE in the game, but they are very simple and almost impossible to fail, so they are not annoying.The in-game world is quite large (list of locations includes the house, the forest, the lake and several other interesting and sometimes also quite surprising places), but navigating through it is easy, because Giulia has access to the map and her diary, so we always know where we are and what to do next. It’s also worth mentioning that there are few optional side-quests available. They allow us to get a better understanding of certain events, but we also can completely ignore them and focus just on the main plot - it’s totally up to us. The game is set at the Italian countryside during World War II and the protagonist is a daughter of an Italian woman and a Nazi general. This alone gives quite an unusual (and basically unseen in video games) perspective, but there’s more - as it turns out, Giulia seemingly has absolutely no idea that Italian fascist and the Nazis are the bad guys (!) and she’s genuinly surprised that partisans are constantly fighting the Axis armies. Developers did a really good job here showing not only the girl's different (and ridiculous) perspective, but also how blind to the facts she is, because there’s enough evidence lying around to know what Mussolini’s and Hitler’s people really do. This whole thing is basically a detail always subtly appearing somewhere in the background and it’s really easy to miss if we’re not exploring carefully enough, but it is really well done. And now it's time to talk about the best thing about ‘Martha is Dead’ - absolutely fantastic story. I'll write it right away to make it clear – this is NOT a normal story about solving Martha's murder. The plot is really dark, heavy and reaches into the deepest, darkest parts of our minds making us wonder what's real and what's not. We’ll witness a lot of strong and very violent scenes (and I woudn’t be surprised if some people call them shocking or disgusting), but all of them make sense and are justified by the story the developers are telling. The story that at some point turns into the absolutely fascinating and messed up journey that keeps us hooked to the screen the entire time and does not disappoint at the end of the game. On top of that devs treat us like adults, so there is not just one simple explanation to everything and we should pay attention to details as some of them can totally change the way we’re understanding some events. Moreover, the atmosphere throughout the entire gameplay is simply incredible, because developers are revealing next layers of the story in very smart way and we know something unexpected is going to happen sooner or later.There’s also one thing that should be mentioned: even though the game is not a horror, it has some jump-scares in it. There are literally few of them, but I know some people hate them, so I think it should be mentioned. As for the technical stuff – ‘Martha is Dead’ looks stunning, especially on the ultra graphic settings: the textures are razor sharp, the lights and shadows work just like they should and some of the views are simply gorgeous. It’s basically one of those games where we can just go from place to place and spend hours taking screenshot after screenshot. The same thing can be said about the soundtrack as the music is simply phenomenal and complements what we see on the screen in an incredible way. I played the game with the Italian voice acting (it’s really solid) and English subtitles and I think it’s the best way to do it, but English voice acting is available as well (can’t say anything about its quality though). And it’s also worth mentioning that we can save game anytime we want plus there’s also an autosave feature.Now the complains and luckily the list is not long. First and foremost - ‘Martha is Dead’ was released 2,5 years ago and the technical state of the game is still.... Well, disastrous. Regardless of the graphic settings and DirectX version (we can choose between DX11 or DX12) I was experiencing constant stuttering, freezes, FPS drops, texture pop-ups and a whole bunch of other problems, such as camera jumps, crashes or the fact that sometimes after closing the game it turned out that I have to manually kill the process in the task manager because it was still running in the background. I have really decent PC that allows me to comfortably play games like ‘Cyberpunk 2077’ or ‘Elden Ring’, so it's not a hardware problem on my end and there’s a lot of topics about it on the Steam forums and it’s constantly mentioned here in the reviews. It’s kind of surprising to be honest, because previous LKA game (‘Town of Light’) worked like a charm and I had no technical issues with it whatsoever. Obviously I know every game is different, but I just didn’t expect that ‘Martha is Dead’ could be THAT messed up technically.Apart from that I can complain about literally two little things. First – sometimes during the exploration ambient music just stops and restarts only after saving and reloading the game. Not a big deal, but still an issue. Second – backtracking is a little bit annoying sometimes. Developers seem to be aware of it, because there’s a bike available in the game, but because of the technical problems I described earlier it becomes completely useless, mostly due to the sudden camera jumps as they make it impossible to drive straight even just a few meters. To sum up this review – ‘Martha is Dead’ is really a great game. Dark, thought-provoking, incredibly intriguing and sometimes simply fascinating. And yes, it’s a mess on the technical side, but in my opinion the story makes up for everything. Give it a shot, I’m pretty sure you won’t regret it.-----TL;DR? Here's the short version.Pros:+ Fascinating story with many unexpected twists+ Creepy and disturbing atmosphere+ Graphics are absolutely stunning+ Beautiful soundtrack and really solid voice acting+ Manual saving system (and there's also autosaving feature)Cons:- Constant stuttering and framedrops- Random freezing and crashes- Backtracking can be kind of annoyingIt's a great game with a lot of technical problems, but the story IMHO makes up for everything. Is it worth giving a shot? Totally.

_childDocuments_.review: *Slight spoilers to follow so be warned but if you want my immediate takeaway, this is one of my least favorite gaming experience of all time. - In it's short play time Martha is Dead juggles themes of child abuse, animal abuse, familicide, suicide, mental illness, fascism, and more - all with the most superficial depth and subtlety of a sledgehammer.- The first 4-5 hours are a tedious slog through walking sim exposition with the clunkiest controls and slowest movement to pad out the run time as it spoon feeds you unreliable narration that hardly ties it's plot points together. - To pad out even more time none of the dialogue or constant monologue is skippable. If you read fast, you'll spend a third of this game waiting for it catch up with you. - The final hour or so amplifies the previous problems just by bathing the story in unpleasantness and a marionette play that despite looking kind of clever, manages to slow exposition down even further. - All plotlines are explained away as mental illness with a shrug - Incredibly weird this game cuts to black to hide gun violence several times, gives you the option to censor a scene of self harm YET makes you partake in a lengthy QTE minigame where you undress the corpse of a teenager and cut a deformed fetus out of her with a pair of scissors a'la Inside. - All the constant grief and trauma in this game leads up to a suicide that quite honestly feels earned for the pain it's endured and given to others - but this the game has the audacity end on a "suicide is never the answer - good things are always around the corner" message right after staring into the dead eyes of it's truly horrendous protagonist. I don't know there's a ton more technical stuff pertaining to the awkward movement, the inconsistent lighting, and the fact that despite looking dated and mid it somehow put my PC thru the wringer but still the tone deaf ending that never seems to end just had me screaming "OH FFS..." as it stumbled towards the finish. Absolutely hated this experience and would not recommend for even a "hate watch" playthru.

_childDocuments_.review: Potentially one of the most disturbing games of the year, Martha is Dead unfolds as a slow-burn, first-person, psychological thriller. The main premise of the game entails Martha, the identical sibling to Giulia, of course, dying; and the rest is comprised of how people in her vicinity are affected by this, which is also interjacent to your eventual descent into madness. It certainly does surprise you with more than what seems plausible on the surface.The controls are easy enough to grasp, being mostly point-and-click interactive with movements assisted by a WASD keyboard format. You, obviously, can use different layouts or a controller if you please, and you can play the game in a multitude of languages—Italian being both the innate choice and possibly the best one. The game includes a log for missed dialogue and subtitles, and while some documents in-game might be in English, they're mainly in Italian, so it isn't completely immersion shattering. There are also extra details that I appreciate, such as the daily tarot divinations.Regardless of whatever technical choice you make, you will eventually assume the role of a twin sister situated in the Italian countryside of the 1940s, who is engrossed in a web of war, abuse, grief, and psychotic delusion. You are simply a victim of circumstance. This game definitely requires quite a heavy trigger warning prior to playing it, as there are a few pop-up messages preceding specific scenes. Martha is Dead is an ordeal that is RIFE with both realistic & gratuitous gore. The experience is heavy on atmosphere and accompanied by an eerie soundtrack, and the graphics are the icing on the cake. With that being said, the character models, along with environmental textures, can sometimes look wonky up close. Still, the game is capable of everyone's favorite buzzword, a.k.a. "ray tracing," and can easily result in your system heating up to some extent (it's probably necessary to mention here that I am playing on a laptop with an i7-9700 Intel Core, 16GB of RAM, and an RTX 2070.) In addition to that, it's worth saying that my playthroughs were significantly glitched, with me being unable to proceed with certain quests despite my position in the story. There were many occasions when I'd fly through the map after trying to do something as simplistic as riding my bicycle over a dirt hump. While hunting for the last two achievements, I would have to close out my game just to reset the location of my bike. As you'd guess, this ultimately became very draining after figuring out that these problems were not unique to a single condition and would recurrently show up. My game would, on occasion, have somewhat of a stuttering problem as well.Martha is Dead begins with a view of a bedroom window, amongst a doting nanny retelling the story of a local cryptid: a homicidal wraith who slays a young woman every time fog descends upon the lake nearby. The reason for this stems from a traumatic event involving the drowning of the "White Lady" during a domestic situation regarding her and her significant other.Although you may interpret this as the main focus of the game, the White Lady is predominantly made available in fleeting moments and photographs, most of which you have to actively try to discover. The other times she appears are within metaphors and coincidences parallel to the story; an eternally repetitive imprint on reality, i.e., "The house was a place of suffering."One of the teeming questions that plague this game is having you navigate between major parts of the story through either the lens of a camera or from the audience of a puppeteer show at the theatre. Some of the first items & areas you're presented with either involve or consist of being gifted a camera, alongside your own personal darkroom to develop whatever tokens of interest you capture with it. If you're confused about how to progress, all you really have to do is keep an eye out for the hand-shaped button prompts, which routinely fill up with red. There are also collectibles, requiring you to pick up rolls of film and camera modifications that you find in and around your family's estate. This feature leads me to reminisce a lot about Fatal Frame and its mechanics with picture taking.(Spoiler warnings from this point forward.)Overall, Martha is Dead was an encounter I mostly enjoyed, as long as I wasn't forced to figure out how to progress through game-breaking bugs. Luckily, the developers seem to be pretty focused on staying on top of patches and updates, so I doubt that any of these hiccups will survive for very long. It's a gripping adventure that will at best make you uncomfortable and at worst cause you to be confused, depressed, and sick to your stomach. I'd recommend it to anybody who isn't particularly sensitive to these things.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic horror tale that’s bound to sit with you. One that feels like it’s using the medium to tell a story, not just to shoehorn in the usual suspects of video game tropes and slapdash mechanisms. At times, it actually comes off more like something you’d experience in 70’s horror cinema: A slow-burn that starts out more akin to a social drama, but carefully turns into something more sinister and makabre during the latter part. In fact, one of the things that make Martha Is Dead stand out is how it’s a little bit less concerned with giving nods to the player. It’s not a game that fits the modern mold of streamer-friendly gargle -- even though there’s no clear elevator pitch here that would convince you otherwise. There’s just something about how no one’s trying to impress or scare you for the sake of scares alone. No one’s monitoring your heart rate. No one’s using algorithms to inject jumpscares. Instead, gore and horror feel more like a natural, deliberate extension of the storytelling.It’s a confidently produced and directed game; laser focused in its mission to create a believable and chilling atmosphere. And the setting really is one of the highpoints for me here. It’s beautiful. Especially how the whole WWII-backdrop looms in the background, grounding it. Also, how the environments and attention to details manage to transport you into this beautiful European period piece. I wish more developers would allow themselves to use their native language as the default spoken one. It’s a huge part of why Martha is Dead works for me -- and why I’m in Tuscany and not at home in front of my computer.Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Martha Is Dead is a one of a kind experience.As a psychological horror fan, I went in with certain expectations. I said "one of a kind," because what I got to experience is something I haven't in any video game before. It is not afraid to push the ladder a bit further than you're used to in games or even movies. It gives you a fair amount of warnings - for a good reason. But the true horrors of this game are not those in jumpscares and disturbing imaginery, they are those within mental illnesses (trauma, self-harm, abuse) and war (I would like to put an ephasis on drug usage during WW2). The unspoken, beneath the surface horrors. And that is where it succeeds the most. The game is running on UE4 and despite of being made on an Indie budget, the visuals are stunning - partly photorealistic.It is set during the late years of World War 2 in a small fictional town in Tuscany. The attention to details representing this time period is fantastic. From the landscapes to the house interiors and decorations, everything was crafted with the utmost care. The title also uses "metahuman technology," which made it possible to render pretty realistic character models. Attention was also paid to the lighting of specific scenery, which I consider an important aspect of a good horror game. But what ties everything together and makes it complete is the soundtrack. And it's great. It fits the game's environment perfectly and was well incorporated to add tension when needed.The gameplay itself is consisting more or less of puzzle and mystery solving, exploration, and has a really extensive photography mechanic that was fun to use. But the gameplay and some other issues are where this title falls a bit short for me. Walking as a whole was kind of clumsy. Later on you can unlock a bike to travel longer distances with, although I chose to walk rather than ride it due to its riding mechanics. It also felt a bit repetitive at times. Some chapters felt like there wasn't much going on. Now, Personally, I like slow burns so I didn't mind it that much, but I can understand why it might be a problem for some players. Just remember - in the end, it will all make sense. Everything, is building up to it. The optimization is just simply, bad and could have been polished. Randomly dropping frames, stuttering, getting stuck in objects on the ground, game crashing after loading a save file, cutscene not loading properly forcing you to reload.. Final verdict : I enjoyed the game and don't think I'm gonna forget about it for quite some time. Through all it's flaws "Martha Is Dead" is a piece of art, and I recommend it to anyone who isn't overly sensitive or is a fan of psychological horror. Special thanks to LKA and Wired Productions for bringing us and allowing us to experience this unique game.

_childDocuments_.review: FULL REVIEW --->  Not in the typical jump-scare sense we see all too much today though. There were many moments during Martha is Dead where I truly gasped in horror. There were things the game requires you to do, that you DO NOT WANT to do in the game. There are several moments of truly graphic visual horror that many people will not get past.It is a true psychological horror that will get in your head. Days after finishing, I continue to reflect on the game. It sticks with you.All serious elements are dealt with respectfully and tastefully and are there for developing the story (although you may not realize it yet), not just a gore ‘shock effect’. They help place you into the character and doing these extreme actions in a game will push your own mental boundaries. Again, this game will NOT be for everyone. I personally feel exploring these topics respectfully in a video game is a step in the right direction. Much respect to the developers for bringing light to and allowing people to experience the torment of these issues in the safety of a game, that many people experience every day in their real life.

_childDocuments_.review: Martha is Dead is an indie walking simulator set at the end of World War II (1945), Italy, where you play as Julia (Giulia) whose identical twin, Martha, is mysteriously killed. The protagonist fakes as her sister and you will see her journey of finding out the truth behind the death. This game has some good ideas in terms of gameplay and an obscure yet unexpected story, however, falls short because of the execution and technology implementation, making it kind of a niche experience where you must endure lots of clunkiness before you can see a story that may or may not appeal to you.For most walking simulators today, the story is moved forward by the change of space. The course of walking and the interactions in between are the gameplay, which makes this genre tend to have weak playability. I think the dev of this game saw this weakness, so instead of walking, they designed the gameplay around exploration in one big map. It is a very good idea and supposedly makes the game more interesting with higher playability. Unfortunately, the execution is not there.The assistive designs around exploration, such as map design and movement are very poor, further disincentivizing players to explore. It is a result of poor implementation of technology.The interactions are unnecessarily complicated. For example, to open the camera, you need to do almost everything you need in real life, all of which are followed by a set of interactions. Some of the interactions give a good opportunity for internal monologue to happen, but more of them are just filler contents – to make you do a series of button pressing for the sake of having more things to do.There is one puzzle session in the entire game, which is to translate morse code. Daymare 1998 also has the same translation puzzle and I criticized it for the same reason – making a real-life implementation as a video game puzzle is just lazy, and morse code translation is just too complicated and uninteresting. I had to google a tutorial to translate the puzzle.This game keeps reminding me of The Beast Inside, another walking simulator that uses similar exploration as gameplay design. That game has its own problems, but in terms of gameplay, it has genuinely good puzzles and some interesting map interconnectivity for exploration. By comparison or not, Martha is Dead is just a very underwhelming experience.The storytelling, on the other hand, is much better than gameplay. Martha is Dead uses a non-continuous narrative method that jumps from scene to scene, similar to montage in movie. You might find it difficult to understand the story due to the jumping, but with this, the story is able to simplify unnecessary plots and more importantly, works really well in creating mystery and smoothing the transition. Speaking of, I think the scriptwriting is pretty good. It is one of those stories that is unexpected but also perfectly makes sense, as the mystery is well set up and leaves small hints in different sessions if you are able to notice them. The story also leaves some ambiguity smartly, allowing players to have two different but interesting interpretations of the story.I do think the good and bad of the story come in the same form, which is obscurity. Because of the scene jumping and using inner monologue as narrative (hence the very limited perspective in viewing the entire event), the story takes effort to understand. On top of that, the gameplay can greatly distract players from sorting out the information they gather. Therefore, I think only a certain group of people will appreciate the story.As for the presentation, the game has good sound design that enhances the atmosphere very well, but the visual design is kind of a mixed bag. The interior design of the house is very detailed and believable as a house of the 1940s, but outside the house, the game doesn’t look so good. The environment seems to be designed with assets from Unreal Engine Marketplace, hence they come in low resolution, look particularly bad up close, and have no environmental effects (like the leaves don’t move with wind), yet the optimization is atrocious with lots of random frame drop (frame rate cut in half with RTX on but visual difference is minimal). Also, the FOV is kind of uncomfortable and needs lots of time to get used to (motion sick warning). I played the game in mid-March and there were many bugs (I had the game on Day One but a game-breaking bug prevented me from advancing until a patch came out). To their credit, the dev released patches that fix bugs and optimize the game quite frequently.In conclusion, the story of Martha is Dead is not for the majority yet can attract people who enjoy psychological horror and obscure storytelling. But as a video game, the story is not enough to redeem the unexciting and disappointing gameplay. I really wish it is a movie instead of a video game.

_childDocuments_.review: Spoiler free!Initially, this game was a big yes. At least as far as the story goes. But ultimately, Martha is Dead makes for an interesting story that really lacks any fun gameplay elements, is optimized horribly, and goes on for just a bit too long. - StoryReally the majority of the story is very interesting. You're often wanting to know what happens next and occasionally scratching your head over certain puzzling elements. However, there's times when the writing doesn't make sense in areas where maybe I missed a small piece of it, but certain dialogue choices don't make sense. There's some twists and turns and some of them are neat, but holy Shyamalan Batman, I was left rolling my eyes at yet another "twist." By the last few twists, I just didn't care anymore. The clunky gameplay also gets in the way of the story to the point where by the end of it, I just wanted the story to be over. - Audio The voice acting is mostly superb. The main character is voiced beautifully. There's maybe a few heightened emotional moments that didn't really sound great, but overall, it was great. Some of the supporting characters are lifeless, but you'll spend most of your time listening to the main character's voice which is great. The music in this game tries way too hard. I'm also of the opinion that vocals in music in games are often distracting and out of place and this is no different. Like this follows the trope of the *violin intensifies* and it's really just obnoxious especially when the scene doesn't warrant THAT much tension. - GameplayMy biggest gripe with this game is that it tries so hard to be a complex game and add all these little mini games, but it doesn't do any of them well or it over complicates things for no reason. The camera is the main part of the "gameplay" and it really just throws all kinds of film, lenses, and accessories at you and allows you to adjust focus, aperture, and exposure which you would think means you're going to be taking some super Instagram worthy shots, but really any story elements are locked to a particular exposure, focal length, and lens to the point where there is indeed a wrong way to take a photo. Not only that, but the incredibly tedious and boring task of developing photos is slow and not engaging at all. You have to do it correctly, so no framing shots in a way you think looks cool. And the game over explains everything and wants to tell you how developing photos was REALLY done back in the day, but it's simplified for the game. I can respect the game is trying to be educational, but the task is still tedious and talking to the players directly takes me out of the immersion. There's all sorts of mini games like this, but I don't want to write an actual novel here so I'll move on. -VisualsThis game looks beautiful...when it works. Let me preface this by saying I have a Ryzen9 5900x and a 3080. There's very little my PC struggles to run. However, this game in 1440p on ultra is literally unplayable. I know I know, there's some games that just aren't meant to run maxed out, but even with some settings turned down, my PC struggled to keep up with it. To the point where there were large frame rate drops and stutters as the game loaded sections in. But the BIGGEST problem is the Morse Code mini game. You'll have to press your mouse with long and short sequences...neat right? Nope. Not if the game isn't running smoothly. One message was fine, but then another just would not work. I was getting so frustrated, I literally held up my mouse to my microphone for chat to hear a long press, followed by short, only to be met with an error telling me I was doing it wrong. I was going to lose my mind. I had to quickly jab the mouse like it was too hot to touch. The stuttering frames meant the game wasn't reading my input correctly either. After noticing the audio kept cutting out, I realized it may be because of the game's poor performance that it was doing this. Finally the last bit here. Horror.So this game isn't really horror. At least not in the traditional sense. I see it's tagged as psychological horror which...I mean...that doesn't seem to be entirely accurate either. It's just gore. Very gory. I don't mind gore, but this was just shock value gore. There's sections of the game that just seems to throw in gore and nudity for no real reason. It was just a bit over the top and though some parts served the story, I felt like most of it was just a bit much. TLDR; Martha is Dead is a beautifully horribly optimized game with tedious and boring gameplay mechanics and excessive gore for shock value. The story was questionably worth it, but by the time it was done, I was just relieved to be done with it.

_childDocuments_.review: I was very excited to play this game. The idea of playing as an Italian woman living in the Toscana region during the 1940s (a very particular time period for Italy history wise!) was very attractive. Taking that and mixing it with a very suspenseful premise for the main plot and very ominous title (you know, Martha is Dead). And even more, adding a very strong analog photography element and even a little bike ride (not just any bike, but an old big bike, like the ones your grandpa may have lying around).Going in I think there were a lot of things that are recognizable in one way or another to a lot of people around the world in this game.Indeed this game has a lot of good things going on for it, first one is: the attention to detail and the graphical fidelity are amazing. Not just from a technical standpoint of view but from a craft and artistic one too. Waking up for the first time in your room, looking at things, the rest of the house as well and the nearby woods is like transporting to another place, and another era.The dialogues in Italian with subtitles (if you play the original audio) is very well done and helps a lot getting you immersed.The initial premise for the story, is very attractive and promises a lot.Sadly, the game then fails to meet many of these promises or at least falls short of the enormous potential it does have.The photography element, which is one of the main points of interest in the game, does look very well, (your camera, your accessories, you have a lot of them) they all look and feel great, but in execution..... that's where it kind of falls short... taking the picture, you do have your manual focus for example, but the game tells you then with a big red message when your picture is in focus. A the very beginning of the game you do have a special "precise” focus tool in your camera, but you never really use it after that. The same can be said about exposure (aperture, speed) You do have manual controls for that too, but the game camera shows you how the picture will end up looking, and a big red sign lights up telling you when it is well exposed or not enough... which kind of makes the whole point of having the manual controls not really necessary in the end... It is a shame really, the tools are there, but the implementation does not really favours you trying, making experiments, because its really difficult seeing your manual focus on screen without a focus tool like the one in the beginning and then using the filters. At least the “Dark Room” part in which you develop and print your images is a little better, and you can play with longer exposures if you choose to do so, while still advancing the main story.But I’m going on a tangent about photography perhaps, you'll have to excuse me as I was at some point a photographer, and all these things ring very near to me. Perhaps, most people won't even notice many of these things.Moving on, the bicycle is another great touch to the game, which gets terribly underused. You'll probably ride your bike once or twice in the whole game, unless you just want to go in circles around the house. And it is a shame because the bike mechanics are very good (at least the few times I spent with trying them) Specially the sounds, I love the sound the bike makes when you’re going at full speed downhill, you hear the chain roll, just like a real old bike, you can just let go off the pedal, and the bicycle will go on alone without you doing anything, which of course doesn't happen when going up. Little beautiful touches that make all these interactions so special.And then there's the story... the ominous title, your sister's mystery, the historical political context surrounding everything, can it be related? Your German father with its Nazi affiliations and your mother.Without spoiling the story, I would say that I personally didn't like the way the story went, or at least, how it went in the later parts of the game, especially in the end. It could have been so much more. All the elements are there, it just feels like a wasted opportunity.The game also makes some narrative decisions (as to how the story is told) specially towards the end which left me wandering if maybe they ran out of resources, and they just had to resort to a very minimalistic (and frankly poor way) of telling certain key elements of the story while at the beginning of the game it was done much better with maybe less crucial scenes (which were beautifully told) but still, all that effort put there, and all the immersive historical elements too, and then what happened to the story?In a way, having all these beautiful visual achievements, photography mechanics and historical accuracy showed to us at each step, undermines how little the actual story in the game makes use of all of this.As much as I like all the comfort food, the story should have been more predominant, the player more involved with it. However the main character sees to it of course. Doesn't matter how radical the story gets in the end. IT should FEEL more as a road taken. Not just something that appears suddenly and that's that. Tell us more. Make us understand more our main character. However improbable.   One thing is certain, I like LKA game worlds, they tell us (imperfect) interesting stories and I think the potential for a great well told story is there, latent, like a photograph taken on film, just waiting to see the world one day.This very inflammatory but respectful review is

_childDocuments_.review: Martha Is Dead is an absolutely remarkable psychological thriller. If you appreciate games with complex unravelling narratives and strong emotional content, you will probably really enjoy this game. It is set in Italy in 1944. You are Giulia, a young woman. Your twin sister Martha is deaf. Your father is a German general overseeing the war in Italy. Your Italian mother despises you. She adores Martha but has been profoundly abusive to you throughout your life. Your father did love you and try to protect you from your mother, but he was increasingly absent because of the war. It begins as you are gathering film in the forest near the lake. You had set up cameras on timers and want to develop the photos. As you are focusing one of the cameras, you realise that there is a body in the water. You frantically swim to it. It is Martha. You drag her to shore and just sit with your dead twin. Impulsively you remove her locket and place it around your neck. Your parents find the two of you. But they believe that it is Giulia who has drowned. It is at that moment that you decide to live as Martha. It's one of the best narrative hooks that I've ever encountered in a game. As you live as Martha, you begin investigating her death. Giulia knows that she's psychologically damaged and is working to overcome that. She wants to know that truth. What unfolds is a series of revelations, some of which are very powerful. The game has some really strong moments andI don't think that I'll forget it. This is an excellent game. _childDocuments_.review: Length <5hrMartha is Dead is a strange game, on the box it seems like a horror game set in World War 2. I saw the trailers and thought, Wow this is going to be some occult horror of a monster in the lake. Nope! The game is completely Psychological Horror, with random and at times what feels like over the top horror scenes glued on. Do not come into the game with the expectation to be scared, the horror visuals are few and spaced out. The game is more about the player understanding what is actually going on, and the player will only realise this later into the game.I would say the game is closer to The Remains of Edith Finch and The Vanishing of Ethan Carter, than a full horror game.Most of Martha is Dead is a Simulation game, the player will be completing random actions in Giulia’s daily life. While later the player will support the war effort, this gameplay is mainly fetch quests or go to set locations.The player will also have to complete some morse code puzzles, which was a fun experience. It took me a while to work out how to read the morse code map, as I attempted to read it from the bottom at first, till I learned it was a branching path from the top. The rest of the game is exploration or narrative plot, you are not going to find any real action in the game out of a few moments. At times the player will also need to make use of their camera to take pictures asked of them, this is a little tedious as you need to find the perfect angle and use the correct lenses and focus. The player can also find items to take pictures of in the environment that will reveal more. Once the player has taken pictures they will need to develop them, which is done through a little mini game. Now the visuals are amazing, especially the horror moments, they stand out and definitely worth the time to see them. They out match a lot of horror moments in games, and would be scenes I would expect to see in the original Texas Chainsaw Massacre.Before Spoilers I just want to say Martha is Dead is a good game for people who just want to experience a game, it is closer to a walking simulator-esque game, go in expecting that and you will enjoy the game. I did not, I saw the game marketed as an over the top horror game, and thought that what I was buying with countless times being told of how dark horror is.. Sadly this was a tiny amount of my gameplay and I feel a lot of the horror moments are not really needed for the narrative and are only there to make visual stand out set pieces.Martha is Dead is solely reliant on its story and we perceive the story through Giulia, the only problem is, she is an unreliable narrator. This extends into the whole game, everything you see, everything you hear has a high chance of being her false reality, and as such the game is completely subjective to what the player thinks is real. I am not even sure if any aspect can be perceived as real.So my best guess, Martha is dead, she has been dead since birth. Your mother had pains during pregnancy and only one child was born. I believe this is the case as Giulia says that her family is cursed with twins, and is seen in the fetus. (Your Mother also states you were alone at the lake, having a breakdown).This led her mother to have mental problems post birth where she abused Giulia, but also treated Giulia as two people declaring her as Martha and may be the origin of Martha as an identity, this can be seen in the puppets where each time punishment was dealt it was to solely one child. Your Mother also refers to this later during your confrontation. This caused Giulia to create Martha as a separate personality, one that cannot talk to her mother, and in doing so did not receive further abuse. It was Giulia who was blamed for problems and received the abuse instead. You were taken away from your mother when she was meant to be in a mental ward, you can hear that in the ending when the mother talks to the priest. It also explains why you were alone with Nanny, as there was no abuse removing the need for Giulia to rely on Martha to protect herself. This leads to the start of the game, where your mental state further deteriorates after your miscarriage and Giulia wants to become Martha to avoid the pain she is in. Also potential on meeting your mother again.You could also perceive that your Mother preferred Martha as a personality because she could not answer back, meaning your Mother rewarded the Martha part of Giulia. While other characters only interact with Giulia, such as Nanny and your Father. This can also be reinforced when people can not identify the difference between Martha and Giulia because there is not one, it solely what personality is dominant, with no physical change.Now if I was to take my theory as real, then so much of the game is probably just Giulia’s reality and never happened, to the scope of this who knows. It might be everything, she may have not done anything but walked around talking to herself. Core moments like being shot, the injury just disappearing, all newspapers she reads mentioning Martha, conversation you hear from soldiers or even the doctor. The phone call with Nanny, and any picture that you had taken. None may be real, this also renders all horror scenes as part of her delusion and not being real. There is even a chance that all actions you do for the war were not real, as did you even receive the first note from your lover as that also mentions Martha. I just don’t know.This really comes to light in the endings, where you are effectively having to piece together your reality. What you submit at the end is Giulia’s reality.Here are some more points for you, the White Lady (Ghost in the lake), a fairytale from your nanny that you do when you play with your puppets. Any scene she is in is probably a delusion. Why Martha had a bed and clothes, I have no clue. Why you are restricted from your old room, I am still not sure, really on this one I think I missed some context for all I know the roof was leaking. You may enjoy the game, but to me, the game leaves a foul aftertaste where it feels like I am going to have to fully break down all moments, just to find out that nothing makes any sense because Giulia throughout the whole game can not perceive reality. This has been so annoying. I have thought over the game repeatedly, I wrote this review on release and have redrafted it endlessly. The story of Martha is Dead, is confusing solely on the fact that you cannot build a grounded reality from anywhere because everything you perceive is potentially unreal.Here’s the last thing, did your Mum and Dad die, did your Nanny die? You carry your Mum’s head under the bridge but was this reality? Your Dad is killed but his body is taken, and there is nothing left on the floor to prove he was even there. The moment plays off fast in the story and the only visible sign of it can be seen as the injury to Martha’s face. Your Nanny’s death is told through exposition, exposition that directly references Martha.I would not recommend the game unless you want to just experience the game. Really experience the game for what it is. Now I have a headache and need to leave this game in the past, it’s been a long time writing this and now, I’m free. Still lots of cool moments, it’s worth buying for those.If you want to have a look at the game here is the start of my playthrough:For some good horror games check out my Curator Page:

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a game meant for everyone. If you are a fan of The Town of Light you will likely enjoy this entry. Something I enjoyed about both games is the way in which it depicts and explores mental illness. It is not taken lightly, and the game designers clearly have a deep empathy for people who endure mental health issues. Game play  is limited, but given the nature of the game itself this is not an issue. They do a good job of exploiting the medium to tell an effective story. There were some elements that I found needlessly complicated, but these are optional. Taken as a whole everything serves to move the story forward, or immerse you in the narrative until you feel as one with the protagonist. The last part is crucial for me. I haven't felt like this since I first saw the film Session 9. The way in which the narrative unfolds leaves you questioning what exactly happened until the very end. The denouement is touching and a great send off. Performance wise I feel like this could have been optimized a little better. For being a limited narrative experience it really made my computer chug at times. There were some texture loading anomalies, and some inconsistent pop-in. Nothing super extreme, but it's worth mentioning. 8/10 would strongly recommend.  Definitely play it alongside Town of Light as they link together in a sort of meta-narrative.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay spoilers follow, no substantial plot spoilers. This is a strange game, but, unfortunately, it is not strange in an a particularly interesting or thoughtful way. It's less a traditional "horror game" and more an unfocused mash-up of early-00s era adventure games like Nancy Drew, the modern first-person narrative "walking simulator," and a historical drama with psychological horror/thriller elements. There's also a weirdly (kind of hilariously) detailed camera simulator for some reason, which the developers take great pains to explain is similar too, but not exactly like, the way a real camera works. The main problem is that it is full of half-executed ideas and mechanics, as it jumps between these influences abruptly and without warning. After a promising start, the game quickly loses steam. The long middle of the game is largely just wandering the environment looking for stuff and taking pictures as the story unfolds. The story is interesting but not exactly exciting or unique (unless you are new to any psychological horror tropes). There are some places where you make "choices" but if those choices have any consequences for the story itself, I'm not sure. As is often the case with psychological horror, you quickly realize your player character is not a reliable narrator, and what you seem to be doing might not be what is actually happening. Unfortunately the game wastes the productive narrative tension and gameplay dissonance from this most basic trope of psychological horror. Instead, you walk through the woods for the umpteenth time to look for a thing to do a thing, etc. It's very tedious and strange.To the earlier Nancy Drew comparison, I wish this game was half as cozy or well-designed as those games, which, are under-appreciated puzzle masterpieces. Unfortunately this game consists of a few Nancy Drew-esque puzzles (including an incredibly frustrating telegraph machine) that ultimately seem to be optional or at least have no bearing on the story as experienced by the player.There are a lot of bizarre choices and elements in this game. One is a bike, which you gain access to sometime in the first half of the game, but is basically unusable because riding it feels like bobsledding while drunk and wearing binoculars. The other is the camera -- introduced as a main item for our character, a part of her characterization, and also as a portal into the narrative drama and horror elements. As I mentioned before, the camera simulator is laughably complex, and was pretty clearly someones labor of love. Unfortunately this game really fails to deliver on any of this. You forgot you have the camera until you need it to advance the story. And you only really need to use it a few times. You're given a ton of camera accessories (lenses, tripods, flash, camera skins, etc) for pretty much no reason at all. I think there was a version of this game that was about capturing paranormal things on camera, which may have been an interesting concept, but got pushed to the side in favor of more (half-baked) ideas.In terms of the scares, they aren't really there. The horror element opens the game, and then disappears until the final act. There are two or three memorable, macabre scenes, that I actually admire the developers for including. This would be fine if the game spent that long, ponderous, middle section actively building tension or atmosphere, but it simply does not. Instead you are just checking boxes and solving pointless puzzles.If you're really into the psychological horror walking-sim thing, like, be my guest and buy this game. But definitely not for more than $10. Just don't expect good puzzles, any scares, or a finished, thoughtful project.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, I definitely wasn’t expecting this one. Then again I normally don’t have expectations going into horror games since I tend to avoid any real context on what it is about, so I was quite pleasantly surprised with this being a different kind of horror.ProsA well crafted slow burn tale of grief, trauma and mental illnessWhile normally irrelevant in horror, this is a different kind of horror game and the good graphics enriches the experienceWell executed atmosphere with music, radio broadcasts and news articles that help you feel you are in 1940s Italy and feel the somber tone of what Gulia is going throughIn depth explanations as to how actual photography at the time worked despite the simplified methods used for the game playNeat little puzzle involving the use and deciphering of Morse codeConsThis game gets really dark with its theme, so if you are sensitive to the subject matter the game presents then this is probably not going to be for youSome tones of the voice acting, particularly with the father, feel like they may have been lost a little in translation, recommend playing in the default Italian language with subtitles for the best experienceSo would I recommend this? Absolutely! This is a well crafted experience, however as I said previously this is not going to be for everyone especially. While not really a con, there is almost no replay value for this game outside of achievement hunting or maybe wanting to revisit the story sometime long down the road. Though that’s not what this game sets out to do, it sets out to give you an experience that will linger with you long after the credits roll. That being said this one will be sticking with me for a long time and I rate this game 4 GO HUG YOUR PETS, YOUR FAMILY, YOUR FRIENDS, ALL YOUR LOVED ONES RIGHT F***ING NOW out of 5

_childDocuments_.review: On paper this seems exactly like my type of game: a scary, narrative heavy, messed up story with critical acclaim. How could this not be a hit? I ended up playing this game twice because initially I felt that my conflicted opinion stemmed from the fact that in my first playthrough I thought this was going to be a ghost story. While there is an element of this, it only makes up a small portion of the story. This game is more of a dramatic story about struggle with mental illness, which is fine, it was just not what I was expecting from watching the trailer. I did find it frustrating though as the initial hook is so unique and interesting I found the premise wasted on what the game actually ends up being. I am not a fan of discussing spoilers in reviews, but the ending has to be discussed in order to provide the context for the entirety of the game and thus my review of it. So warning - heavy spoilers ahead:While the ending is vague it is essentially explained that your twin sister does not exist and she was a manifestation of your character's imagination as a result of a traumatic upbringing with an abusive mother. I think. The ending certainly leaves room for interpretation, but despite me playing this twice, reading the wiki, and watching youtube interpretations, it is not overtly clear what part of this game actually happened. Some people maintain that the game happened but your character created this elaborate “fake twin” plot to deal with the trauma of the actual narrative, but I disagree with this take - the game leans heavy into the “there was no twin” plot twist towards the end, essentially leaving two spins on what the ending is. 1) None of this game happened and your character was just in a mental hospital the whole time. Or 2) Your character never had a twin, she was a manifestation of your character’s trauma. For the sake of breaking down the plot I interpret the game’s ending to indeed suggest that your character’s twin was imaginary, and that most of the game is the result of an unreliable narrator presenting false events to the player. The game does commit to this ending the most, so let's talk about why it is horrible. Quick plot point to provide context: The twins in this game are Gulia and Martha. In the beginning of the game it is Martha who “dies”, with Gulia then pretending to be Martha, so your parents and the community actually think it is Gulia who died.If Martha is imaginary, somewhere like 90% of this game did not actually happen. The first few chapters are about dealing with Gulia’s (but actually Martha’s) funeral: there is a body in a casket and a funeral your character makes preparations for. You listen to your parent’s deal with the grief of losing a child. Multiple other character’s acknowledge that in some capacity you had a sister. All of this has to be hand-waved away as just straight up lying to the audience. The “twins” have their own rooms and own clothes in the house - an argument could be made that your parents were trying to maintain the facade of your character having a twin - but then why later on are they surprised when Gulia reveals to everyone that it was in fact Martha who died. What difference does this make as they only have one child? A portion of this game also deals with Gulia discovering that her boyfriend actually slept with Martha and got her pregnant. Again, fantastic plot point, but this is of no consequence because Martha and Gulia are the same person. This is the recurring theme, the game will present some plot point that may or may not be intriguing, but regardless of what this point is, it ultimately doesn’t matter because it never really happened to begin with. I love a good unreliable narrator twist ending. A great example is “Braid”, where the ending changes your entire perspective on the game up to that point, yet the story still makes sense in this new light. Braid is a terrific case of the unreliable narrator technique being used constructively. Martha Is Dead uses the unreliable narrator technique destructively. So much of the game’s ending is impossible to reconcile with literally every character's behaviour. On my second playthrough I kept an eye out to see if there was clever wording that hints at the ending - but no, every character behaves in a way that is contradictory to the “twist” with no attempt made to explain this contradiction. And at the very end you get a cinematic where your character explains that she recovered and is fine after “everything”. That’s great: what did she recover from? What arc in the story led to this recovery? Moving past the story you are left with some very basic gameplay elements. When not dealing with the plot, the gameplay will consist of:- Dialing the phone (yep…)- Riding a janky bicycle (which is frustrating and got my character stuck a couple of times resulting in my having to reload an earlier save)- Sending and interpreting telegraph Morse-code sequences, where your character deciphers the code by just looking at a piece of paper - Taking and developing photos with your cameraYeah, gameplay is light. Usually I can forgive this if a game’s story can make up for it, but that is not the case here. Now I actually liked the photograph gameplay component of the ones listed above. There was something fun about setting up a shot, using the right attachments, and spending the time to develop the photo. It was mostly automatic but it was cool going through the whole process and seeing the final result (and the photo’s did look very nice once developed). The telegraph quest is by far the worst offender - it is so boring and as much as I hate to admit it, I just turned to a walkthrough guide to quickly get the interpretations. The worst part of all of this is the wasted potential of this game. This is my 2-cents on how to fix the narrative: Commit to the twins existing. Commit to the mistaken identity of which twin actually died. Use this plot point to justify the existence of ghosts and layer this game with creepy ghost sequences and haunted house moments. Use the unreliable narrator technique to confuse the player into which twin you are playing as and which twin died. Throughout the game it can bounce back and forth, and you the character discover things that make you question who you are and why your twin died. Commit to everything in the game happening, we just don’t know which twin it is happening to. This makes the boyfriend plot more interesting (did he cheat on you, did he ever love you to begin with) and the mother plot more interesting (I personally would use this as the ending of the game, your mother meant to kill Gulia but ended up killing Martha - her favourite daughter). This naturally cycles back into the game’s premise of your mother being a terrible person. You then sacrifice your mother to the White-Lady ghost (I didn’t talk much about her as this review is getting long enough as is, but she exists…) and you, your twin’s ghost, and White-Lady reconcile over the similar grief you have felt and the trauma you endured, healing together and allowing everyone to be at peace. This leads to your character’s recovery and justifies her ending monologue about her being ok now. Boom - a satisfying narrative with actual character arc’s and the perfect playground for this game to deliver creepy moments.A couple quick positives: visually the game looks quite nice (not amazing, but definitely nice). There are a number of graphic moments you play through that do hit hard (but are wasted on the game's ending of “not really happening”). The house design is cool, and is complemented by great sound design (and a wonderful soundtrack as well).I am surprised by the overwhelmingly positive reviews for this game. I love these types of games and I did not enjoy my experience with this one at all.

_childDocuments_.review: was a unique horror game that caught my interest when I first heard it was getting censored on the PS4 due to  current stance on censorship. I, of course, love horror games and I wanted to see what kind of game this would be, there is also a disclaimer that the game gives as soon as you boot it up. This is not for the faint of heart and definitely not for the squeamish, I myself like to explore these types of games so my interest was definitely caught. The game also had some really high ratings on other review websites, so I was expecting something amazing.However, when I played it, I got something else, and I am honestly quite disappointed by the shallow experience that I have gotten, which is what made me put the game down. I will be going into all of this in the review and why I personally think that  is not a horror game.I should also probably make this clear, but I do not play , however, I will not be giving this game a negative review simply because it is one. I am someone who will play any game as long as it’s fun. The only game that I have played that is part of this genre is  and that was an enjoyable experience. I am judging this game with the experience that I have had and nothing more.The story starts out in the year 1944 in , with , who is at a lake taking photos when she sees a lifeless body floating in the river. She swims out to go and rescue the person for her to only find that it’s her sister  and she is dead. However, when her parents come to see her, they mistake the dead body for  and think that  herself, who is alive, is . assumes the role of  so she can feel the love that she never got, as she was abused by her mother, and her father is a soldier who is working with the  in .  will try her best to find the truth as to why her sister died, while she deals with trauma and the loss of war.The story of  had a very interesting start and then it turned into something that I was honestly disappointed with. There will be segments where you can choose how to progress through the story, like one of those choose your own adventure kind of things. However, none of the choices you make matter in the grand scheme of things. If a story allows you to choose your own path, the story should reflect on that and divide different outcomes and endings. You don’t get that in this game, and you only get one ending where nothing you do matters. Also, for some reason,  likes to leave the front door open whenever she leaves. Perfect for any person or demon to walk in and haunt the house. I did like the segment where we enact a recap of the story so far with this grim reaper puppet. The overall design and layout of the segment are really interesting, and I liked it overall. he one thing I will give praise for is the voice acting, it’s really well done, and I even hear that one of the voice actresses is being nominated for an award for their performance. The entire game takes place in  so you will be hearing everything in Italian while you read the subtitles.Now, there is not a whole lot to talk about in terms of gameplay for . That’s not to say that is a bad thing as the game is a walking sim. There is a camera that you will have to use to progress through the story- you will use it to take photos and then you will have to develop those photos by going into the photographic darkroom. Which is rather cool, I liked this feature as it showed us how to develop them.Although that’s all of the positives I can think of in terms of  gameplay. The game has these on-rail moments that make you choose certain words to progress, however, if you choose the wrong one, you must redo the entire segment again. There also are other on-rail moments and none of these feel fun. The issue I have with the gameplay is that there is no failure, even the moments that you think have failure don’t. I don’t feel vulnerable at all in certain situations or threatened. For a horror game like this, I think a sense of dread should be included to make the ghosts you come across threatening.However, the worst aspect of the game is the lack of actual horror elements. It relies on jump scares; these are not considered horror in my opinion unless done correctly. The content is more of a thriller than horror which leaves the feeling that something is not right. The game is disturbing on some levels with the gore, but it is not presented in any new or interesting way. With this said, everyone may not be as used to gore as I, so be cautious with what the game does have in store.The graphics are honestly really beautiful, and I would have loved to spend time admiring the clear-like fields if my experience wasn't affected by a few performance issues.First, I will mention gaming performance, mainly low FPS issues. Even after lowering the graphic settings the problems persist. Draw distance is another issue, it is absolutely horrible; I can stand a few feet away from something and you can see the low resolution with the screenshot I provided.One last issue worth mentioning is the camera movement can end up in pretty awkward positions when panning around with a mouse. I should note that the developers are aware of these problems and plan on fixing them.I tested the game on an NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1060 3GB, AMD Ryzen 5 1500X Quad-Core Processor 3.50, with 16 GB of RAM. is an interesting idea on paper, but the execution didn't pan out. I think the experience would be different if they are able to iron out some of the issues that currently break the experience.I ended up putting the game down due to all of these issues and the fact that I was also locked into progressing at a certain point. I know I could have just reset the game to resolve this, but I simply didn't have enough interest in the game's current state. If you truly do want to play it yourself, I recommend getting it when it’s on sale, as the current price of 33.89 CDN with only four hours of content is just not worth the asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: While the historical accuracy of the game is spot on and the lack of censorship is commendable, the side quests relating to the war as well as the developers focus on realistic fascists of life in WW2 Italy, (telegrams, red room development of pictures, and decoding morse) lead to tedious tasks that detract from the main horror theme and eliminates any suspense through long periods of unrelated and boring game play. At its best points the game is a atmospheric and shocking horror with interesting character dynamics and shocking imagery. At it's worst, which takes up most of the game, it is a scatterbrained camera developing and rusty-ass bike riding simulator.

_childDocuments_.review: This game had a lot of good and bad things. Starting with the good.It had a great story line. interesting with small twists here and there. It showed difficult topics in a respectful way. Meaning, any difficult topic that was shown was done for story purposes and not to overly upset or intimidate the viewer. It even had trigger warnings on the most intense part and offers a selection to censor it. I enjoyed the story enough to want to play it again. The Bad. It honestly should have been a movie. There is a lot of "gameplay" where youre just sitting and watching and not really controlling much. When you did have control, the game tended to be a bit glitchy and difficult to interact with the enviroment. It had fun minigames, but the tediousness in which the minigames were carried out took away any fun that was had. For instance there is an optional quest where you must send a telegram with morse code. The first part of sending the message was fun and easy. but you then have to decode the telegram and it becomes a little bit more frusterating. Each of the situations like this alone are not too bad and would be minor if every mini game and quest turned into this annoying chore simulator. Even the picture taking mechanic was fun at first and so was developing the photos but it turned into a chore when you had to do this for every single photo you took. overall i would play the game again if there was some of the bugs fixed and the games changed a little bit. Maybe making photos in batch, or what have you.

A lot of budget seems to have gone into cloth physics and the player model but not into NPC facial animations. If this game is striving to be artistic, then it has a pretty funny idea of what that looks like. Yeah it's art. The art of hiding characters from the player while trying to sell this immersive tale all at the same time.Had they cut out one or two thirds of this game the pacing and overall quality would've been better for it. Aside from that... The Town of Light is easily the developer's better experience with a much more iconic atmosphere. I care about atmosphere and presentation a lot when approaching the horror genre. And this just made me feel nothing more than what I could've gotten out of a random WWII Italian drama.

_childDocuments_.review: I waited for such a long time for this game to come out. So much so I had planned on scheduling this game entirely around the launch.I am a full time horror streamer, and have been passionate about horror and stories revolving deep topics since my childhood.This in short, is one of the most massive misses I have EVER experienced. I would much rather play one of those god awful off brand $2 horror thrown together messes than ever giving this a second thought, and my god have I played some pretty AWFUL games. Both laughable, and in taste.You all had so much opportunity to tell such a beautiful story, to touch our hearts with something we could relate to, and even wrap it up in a really interesting time piece. It could have been meaningful. All you did was use trauma as a crutch and not only that but continuously shoved it down our throats until we got sick and tired of looking. I had to literally close your game during the stream in the middle of one of the scenes as the only place it was going, was down. I kept pushing through about 7 hours just in hope that there would be some point to it all.To top all of that off, the mechanics were absolutely AWFUL. It was broken, and beyond poorly optimised.I'm extremely disappointed in you guys, to my absolute core.Next time, please take a lighter touch with trauma.Edit: This is specifically referencing shoving the dog in a boiling pot of water and forcing her daughter to eat it, and slapping her until she did. This has nothing to do with the setting of war, or the undoing of her mental state because of it. The plot was understood and I was on board with it from the beginning, until we hit that part of the game. As it was completely irrelevant to me and unnecessary.So when I say "a lighter touch" I mean stick to what's relevant in telling the story. I'm not sure boiling dogs and forcing kids to eat it...pushes that..

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely, this is a horror game. But this is not a screamers case. I tell you about suspense and feeling of approaching something horrible. Also, powerful subtext won't leave you indifferent. Moving through the story, you'll feel uncomfortable and uneasy. Difficult to describe without spoilers what this game is about. Summer of 1944, Italy. A girl, Martha drowned in the river. Her sister Giulia doesn't believe that was an accident because of many suspicious moments. She starts her own investigation to find the truth. The game is not for everybody because of disturbing content. The developers say about that everywhere. Even it the game there is a title before last scene where they suggest you to watch it censored. It is a slow-burned adventure where you shouldn't rush and enjoy views of living in a distant Italian villa. Very slow. So, the opposite side of the medal is boring gameplay. You may bore before the final credits.The graphics are stunning. The realistic environment easily makes you dive into the Italian countryside with their vineyards and hot sun. But it affects on the performance. Freezes, lags may escort you through the whole game. And don't even dare use alt+tab   combination. It cuts your performance twice until restart the game.Photography lovers can be pleased with photo mechanics here. Yes, it is simplified, but still interesting. Anyway, you have a lot of attachments to your camera to make a good shot.I liked the game for its vibes, skillful storytelling and deep social subtext. Everything looks natural and makes you to believe without efforts.But remember, this is a very grim game. Not for sensitive people.P.s. You can find all my short reviews .

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR A walking simulator with an overall weak plot sold on "MUCH DISTURBING, VERY EDGE" marketing.Pretty much what it says on the "TL;DR". Most of the "disturbing" moments within the game are, quite frankly, neither disturbing nor meaningful, but rather tasteless and exploitative; the game's plot consists entirely of these scenes and an ending twist, which I assume everyone over 18 saw coming from a mile away.The only saving grace consists of a few moments with interesting imagery, especially near the end. _childDocuments_.review: Last night I started Martha is Dead, streaming some of it on BEAM. Today, I had a feeling that it wasn't the best sort of game to stream, due to the subject matter: Mental health.Today I finished it, and I have to say that I am glad I didn't stream the rest. It covered some horrific issues and didn't shy away from any of them.Martha is Dead is a walking simulator with some simple exploration puzzles, but nothing that proves too difficult.Everything in the game is designed to push the story forward, allowing you to make certain choices (most of which still push you into the direction of the main plot) that range from the banal chores of everyday life, to the gruesome triggering horror that seems all the more disturbing because it's based around the mental health of the main character.After you find your twin sister Martha dead in a local lake you are taken on a trip in a stunning Italian landscape in the grip of World War II. Your family tries to carry on as the world around falls apart and as you progress through the story you get hit with one shocking twist after another.I thought I had the story figured out pretty quickly, but as is the case with well-told tales, I was wrong. The darkest thoughts in my head - the ones that should never see the light of day - are what this tale is about. The taboo of a person's mental health deteriorating at a drastic pace, when it was probably never great to begin with. I've played a lot of harrowing tales, but this is only the second time that I felt horrified at the things that can happen to people (the first being another Italian game called The Town of Light) when they really have nowhere to turn for help.All of this torment is covered with a veneer of a stunningly realised rural Italy, with a soundtrack and environmental audio to match. Walking in the woods, you could close your eyes and swear you were there. Walking through their rustic home, you can hear clocks in another room and floorboards creaking as your weight bears down on them.Little touches like realistic fabric physics on your character's clothes are something you rarely see, but if you look at her shadow whilst walking, you can see the flow of the material. There is so much love poured into this game.But there is one caveat to all this.There are performance issues galore in Martha is Dead. The longer you play, the worse they get, leading me to think there are memory bleed issues (and I had one crash with an error code that said as much). The odd thing is that whilst in the dense woodlands, the frame-rate was better than inside the house.If you can persevere, it's a tale worth being part of.Another word of warning though. There are scenes of graphic self-harm and stuff that is much darker, so if you are in a fragile state of mind, you may find it hard to stomach.If you are okay with that, and the performance drops, I'd say give it a go. It's not happy, but it's a story that has a lot of heart and hard work behind it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be frank about the game. Do I recommend it? Surprisingly yes. But only to people who were fine with narrative games like Hideo Kojima's Death Stranding.To me the game narrative was amazing and the gruesome interactive sequences did make me squeamish and uncomfortable. But the game also heavily advertised on horror and paranormal folklore as much as it did on the mystery narrative. To me that was a mistake and feels almost clickbait-y. I bought the game excited for the horror sequences after playing the demo but the horror and gruesome moments occurred very solemnly and spanned across hours of gameplay between one another. I took maybe 16 hours to complete the game and I think I could count all the gruesome scenes on one hand where maybe only 2 of those moments were actually interactive if I remember correctly. As a narrative and story driven game it's fantastic, as an exploration game the scenery and audio is mesmerizing. But the game falls flat for me on the horror.I was expecting something like the game Layers of Fear, a game that will keep you on your toes with tension while being capable of finding a way to either release that suspense without cheap jump scares or a game capable of building off it. But anytime the game seemed like it would pick up horror wise, it'd soon find myself back to walking around and photographing/locating things that would help continue the murder solving narrative. This honestly made the game come off as boring at times. There wasn't enough interactive gruesome bits and the white lady of the lake while frequently mentioned is barely interacted with.10/10 narrative plot10/10 sceneric/audio visuals7/10 on the horror. And this is me being modest because of how well the few scenes that were scary were delivered. There are better horror games for cheaper, and at this price I seriously only recommend this game if you're interested in a narrative, almost cinematic experience because that is the only thing this game manages to deliver amazingly on

_childDocuments_.review: Even though I would not recommend the game, I will start with elements I liked about it, as I do appreciate the massive effort going into such productions even if the end result is not something to my liking.I think the setting was done very well, and it was an interesting choice. In general I do not enjoy war-themed stories that much, but it was used here as a background rather than a focal point. I really liked seeing the general's house and what kind of standards were considered as being well off in those times. I played with Polish subs and Italian voiceovers and the voices were done really well I thought. I cannot understand the language, apart maybe from a few words, but I enjoyed the voiceovers a lot still.When it comes to why I would not recommend, I want to start with gameplay side - which was very scarce. There were a lot of moments where interactiveness did not seem needed, and was even annoying (like the marionnettes). Tons of scenes could have been cutscenes really and at the end I felt maybe it would have been better as a movie than trying to be a game.The graphics are very nice, but the game isn't optimised too well, even after few patches made since the release. The bicycle riding was quite unpleasant, so I barely used it, and saw in some other reviews people were getting stuck and needed to reload.How the menu UI works isn't very intuitive and simple actions like objectives checking was an annoying task as a result.Taking and developing photos mechanic was kind of nice to start with, but I did not enjoy that much repeating it too many times. I was glad some parts of it were skippable.I had some trouble with the telegraph puzzle, it's possible Polish subs were not optimal to make it fully cohesive.The plot was intriguing and I liked a bit of uncertainty whether paranormal was the actual activity in teh setting, or just the character's imagination. However, at the end I felt robbed of conclusion and understanding what has really happened.

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful game that unfortunately didn't stick the landing, especially given the 30 dollar price tag. 5/10This game has a lot of fantastic ingredients- An interesting camera mechanic, some beautiful art, a few novel ways to convey a story. But it just doesn't pull them together well enough in the end for anything to really stick with me. Ends up falling into some unsatisfying psychological horror cliches that left the story lacking for the substance needed to carry the dull gameplay loop. The last minute of the game gave me tonal whiplash, feels like the devs realized the ending they'd cornered themselves into wasn't something they weren't comfortable subjecting the general public to (fair enough, I can definitely see where they were coming from given one of this game's major themes is trauma) so they had to quickly make a U-turn.Ultimately the game ended up being 'meh' for me. But I'll also likely buy the studio's next game, as I genuinely believe they're capable of something great.
