_childDocuments_.review: Martha is Dead is not a horror game. If you are looking for jumpscares and the likes, look elsewhere. Martha is Dead is not a shooter, not a RPG, not an action game. If you want to 360 No Scope, talk to a lot of NPC's or smash buttons, look elsewhere. It is also not for the faint of heart. It's not without reason the developers have put a warning at the beginning of the game, provide a  for those that feel the need to seek help and have censored certain parts of the game. The game deals with some very serious topics, not in the least child/animal abuse. So please, heed these warnings before you play!So what is Martha is Dead? In my humble opinion only one of the best games ever made. It tells you a psychological story. A story about a young woman (Giulia) in 1944 Tuscany. A story about her mind and what goes on inside of it while she tries to find out what happened to her twin sister (Martha). You are taken on a trip deep into her mind and at the end you're left wondering what was real and what wasn't. What really happened to Martha and if she was even real in the first place. Personally, I couldn't help but feel for Giulia at the end. For everything she had gone through in her life and what that had done to her mentally.The game is visually stunning. The devs have really captured the feel of Tuscany during summer. I love how you walk around the area and really feel like you're there. The music is absolutely beautiful and fits every scene. The implementation of the camera into the gameplay is one I found very interesting. Taking pictures, developing them to further the story is a very nice touch. A few collectables to get, a couple of side quests, but these aren't too difficult. All in all you can play through and get all achievements in about 6 to 8 hours. I'd recommend to play without a guide the first time to really immerse yourself into Giulia's mind.Seriously, play this game!10/10 (I've just started to play this on Steam. I have 40+ hours on Xbox in this game)

_childDocuments_.review: While the advertising focuses a lot on the shocking and horrific elements, it would be more accurate to describe this game as a mystery thriller set against the backdrop of Nazi-occupied Italy during WWII (which is a bit of a mouthful so I guess psychological horror works too). The story is the game's greatest strength, focused on the journey of Giulia as she uncovers the mystery of her sister, Martha's, death. It really manages to hook you from the opening once you find her body in the lake, and as you discover more details related to the event it pulls you deeper in until the very end where all becomes clear, relatively speaking. Honestly given the themes and topics this game tackles it makes sense that the ending is unclear, as well as the events that transpired; it allows the player to fully process the story as a whole and it opens up to repeat playthroughs to appreciate how the greater reveal works as you play with the ending in mind. The way it handles mental illness and struggling with trauma is both haunting and sad, and the time period is incredibly important in making this work when you look at certain details (like the prescription drugs found all over the house). Even as I type this I'm still thinking about it and trying to understand what is real and what isn't, but with Guilia as our narrator we truly won't know will we? And as she accepts her actions in the end, neither will she. But the hope that she has grown and moved past those events is the light at the end of an otherwise bleak narrative. I genuinely appreciate games like this that bring to light struggles that comparitively few people face in order to have the majority reach a wider understanding. If I had to compare this to another game it would be Hellblade in that it uses a genre (psychological horror/action-adventure) as a vehicle to tell a deeper narrative.Although the gameplay isn't the focus of these games, I unfortunately must mention how the gameplay in Martha is Dead is pretty straightforward and poorly optimized. I don't have the current top of the line rig, but an i9 and 3070 gtx should be more than enough to have this game running smoothly. And yet I would have egregious frame drops as the map still has to load in, times where dialogue would run over a game running 5 frames a second until its all loaded and it starts to play catch-up, and multiple times where I would see the map loading in real time from a blurry mess to the gorgeous graphics it touts. Make no mistake, the game is beautiful, but it needs a few more minutes after it's done loading to actually be done loading, if you know what I mean. Also, performance issues aside, as I mentioned the game doesn't ask much of you as a player to do. It's a walking sim through and through where most of the time you're exploring an environment to find the next piece needed to progress. For the story it wants to tell this is more than fine, but for it to have performance issues when it doesn't demand that much? It does bring the game down a bit for me.All in all, if this game does interest you, I would advise to wait for a sale, solely because two years after its release it still has performance issues. But I do believe if you push through it you will find a good, unique story here that is well worth the time to invest in.

_childDocuments_.review: 'Martha is Dead' is an incredibly well written story with a few twists down the line, some more predictable than others, all the while diving deep into the human mind and how it could lead us down a twisted path. The game had some choppy frames, buggy music and effects that were mostly fixed with the recent patches. I was waiting for this title since the trailer was released and it delivered for sure. There were a lot of unique elements that I've never seen in a horror game before and were used up to perfection to present the story at hand. Some of the quests felt like chores but they didn't take away from the overall experience. Played the entire game in Italian and I was surprised how good the voice actors did, certainly added a lot. The dialogue/monologue is interesting and keeps you invested the entire time. There is a lot of explicit and gory scenes that I feel were needed to explain what the human mind can conjure up. The graphics look amazing and a lot of detail and attention was poured into small things that you don't often see in most indie titles. Definitely recommend picking it up.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a walking simulator and it's a little bit slow at first but the descent into insanity will hit you hard. One of the very few actual "psychological horror" games. That is to say it is the actual psyche of the character that turns on itself. Rather than most games were some external source is being applied to the character causing insanity or some other issue. The gameplay is about uncovering a mystery and it consists of mainly walking around and interacting with various objects. The story of the game is the focus here so actual gameplay takes a backseat, but that is ok for games like this. There were alot of warnings when you start up the game about "graphic scenes" that will upset some people and apparently this game got media coverage for some graphic scenes or something but I dunno to me this game was very lax in terms of graphic depictions. It does have some pretty messed up things happen in the game but if you can watch a standard R rated movie im sure nothing in this game is going to upset you. The story is really good and dives into actual mental illness as well as how war can directly affect innocent people that have nothing to do with said war. I read some reviews saying the game length doesn't justify the price and that is completely insane to me. This game has actual heart and soul put into it, and for 6+ hours of entertainment with a story that you WILL be thinking about for weeks to come the price is worth every penny.

_childDocuments_.review: Martha is Dead follows a new yet familiar take on horror games, staying away from cliche jump scares and predictable plots.The game combines puzzle-solving, semi-open world exploration, and even QTE (Quick-Timed Events) sequences.The story told throughout the game was phenomenal. This aspect of unraveling the unknown is what I genuinely love about the genre of horror and mystery, may it be through movies or video games. The game tells its story in memories that the main character can remember. This writing and storytelling style is a genius way of sparking the curiosity from players, leaving them with the itch to play more.For a non-triple A title, the graphics were top-notch. Everything seems polished from the beginning of the game up to the free-roaming segment. The details and lighting are crisp, clean, and well presented. There are parts of the game where I was like, "This looks realistic as heck."Martha Is Dead's sound design is one of the game's best aspects for me. It presents constant tension throughout the game when it's needed (i.e., exploring the woods at night.). With the birds' melodic chirping to the ravens' harsh grating sounds, the game truly feels alive even during day time.The atmosphere provides a safe yet constant feeling of distraught through certain game moments. When that continuous feeling of distraught is about to break, it doesn't bring out cliche moments like jumpscares to burst the bubble per se. The game does an outstanding job of not opting for a jumpscare; instead, it goes for a more creepy and memorable horror moment.Martha Is Dead is an excellent psychological-horror game with its unique tackle on the horror and mystery genre. It's sure to deliver a great and memorable experience to horror fans out there.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I was looking forward to this game, I can't recommend it.Graphically the game is beautiful. I ran into a few places where elements of the terrain didn't line up properly and grey light shone through, I had to disable Ray Tracing after day 2 because the reflective surfaces became super-luminous, and despite playing on my GFs i7/3060 PC on a 4k TV the only resolution option I was given was 720p even with RT and DLSS disabled. But the level of detail is amazing and the world is well crafted and completely believable. Exploration can be frustrating. Walking speed is comparable to other games crouch speed and sprinting is comparable to other games walking. There is a bike that is supposed to allow you to cover long distances faster but it's barely faster than your sprint speed and can only really be used for two short sections nearer the end of the game. There are also many invisible walls that impede exploration that can make navigating the woods were most of the game takes place incredibly frustrating.Many objectives are missing markers or waypoints and interactive elements in the environment can be very finicky to position for the contextual prompt to activate. On the positive side, the camera and telegraph mechanics are actually really well done and were some of my favourite parts of the game. Whilst the game starts out seeming as if it will be dealing with more classic spooky horror, this mostly falls away within the first 20 minutes or so and largely deals with shock and gore horror, either relating to the characters mental health or the horrors of war. Whilst this is a great concept and something I was aware of before purchasing, the game seems to lose it's direction about half way through and becomes increasingly incoherent in its story telling. There are a couple of "side quests" whose progress is locked out until new areas become accessable but this is never communicated to the player leaving you wandering around until you give up and return to the main quest. Things do greatly improve in the last 20 minutes or so, but doesn't have the intended impact due to the previous half the game, as well as a couple of side quests which if incomplete, the game assumes they weren't started leading to characters saying things that don't make sense given the objectives that you have completed.*MINOR SPOILER WARNING* The end sequence is also slightly ruined by a pop up content warning advising of scenes of self harm, which seems completely pointless when the game has already showed execution by hanging, shooting, death from explosion and several graphic scenes of corpse mutilation.*END SPOILER*If you really want to check this out, I'd recommend waiting for a hefty discount.

Before the latest patches I was unable to play the game on my system (RTX 2060, R5 3600, 32 ram) due to terrible lagging and poor FPS and so I refunded it.After the updates I decided to re-purchase the game today to give it one more try, and with my surprise I can finally run the game nicely on 2560*1080 res with medium master quality and DLSS on (I'm above 100 FPS with such settings).I have to say that the developers commitment to their game is without doubt commendable. Martha Is Dead is not yet 100% perfect, but the gain in performance is certainly big enough to make the game enjoyable. I still feel that some chapters are better optimized than others: for example in the second chapter (if I remember correctly) I still experienced some lags in the same environments that didn't have any noticeable lag in later chapters. Anyway, we are on the right track now.As for the game itself, I'm enjoying its dark story so far although some tasks are a bit of an annoyance (yes telegram machine, I'm referring to you!). _childDocuments_.review: I liked the gameplay aspects, the graphics were gorgeous and it really did evoke a sense of being in Tuscany in 1944. I do think some things were missed that added a lot of context; for instance, the medication her mother was using is methamphetamine. Which explained so much about the mother, but unless you know that or google it, it's lost on the player. Similarly, seeing it beside Martha's bed on the floor and in the box. This has implications which are potentially lost to the unaware which could provide more context for character actions.Pros: Beautiful graphicsGood voice over (highly recommend keeping it in Italian)Fun gameplay mechanics - camera, Morse code.Very time capsule like - It's like stepping into the time period, a lot of love was put into ensuring this was accurate.Haunting atmosphere without the need for jump scares - refreshing in a jumpscare-tastic gaming industry.Cons:Some parts dragged on a bit too much, the puppets for example.The area is far too big with not enough to do in it. - The woods are sprawling and beautiful, but there is not that much to do within, so it made the woods seem a bit lifeless in terms of it just...being there to walk around in and admire the graphics.It seems to villainize mental health disorders - It surely seems like a cause to be celebrated; greater representation in the media of mental illnesses and mental health. But. despite warnings and links to mental health sites, the game does, at least in my opinion, villainize mental health disorders, namely DID and/or schizophrenia/Paranoia etc. I didn't feel like it was telling a poignant story about the struggles of mental health and what that entails, but more that it was leaning toward the cliche of 'mental health disorders turn people into raging murderers with delusions'. The focus seemed more on the gore, rather than what abuse and living through a horrific war did to the main character and the fear that must have come with being the daughter of a high ranking German official (It was touched on, but not much and the game says nothing on this fact other than showing us a lot of Nazi flags when in reality, it could have served as being much more thought provoking. It lacked any underlying substance). I think, if it had been accompanied by more concrete evidence rather than hearsay, it would have been more thought-provoking and shined a much better light on mental health. Instead it seemed to skim over the abuse and trauma for the main character to remind us that she was 'crazy'.As it stands, it's following a classic media trope of stigmatizing mental health disorders into simply 'this character is mad/insane'. I do not feel that the game shed much light on the complexity and fragility of the mind with regard to the subjects in the game. A lot of mainstream media show various mental health conditions personified as evil and I feel Martha Is Dead has, unfortunately, leaned into this trope. For decades, horror films and games have used 'madness' and 'psychotic' as their variation on evil and horror and falsely perpetuated the notion that mental conditions commonly lead to violence against others. Something Martha Is Dead leans heavily into.Martha Is Dead also seems to perpetuate the continuing confusion about the relationship between schizophrenia and dissociative identity disorder, as the game seemingly teeters between the two with its implications and hearsay, with a lack of solid evidence and research. Compared to games like Hell blade, who put in a lot of research to ensure Schizophrenia was portrayed accurately, I feel as if Martha Is Dead pulled a trope from a hat and simply went with it. It feels like little thought was put into the consequences of trying to depict mental illness without enough research backing it up. This is not to say that it was done on purpose, more that it feels like a smaller team with a large idea perhaps didn't put in as much thought as they could have with regard to what they were trying to portray. Sadly, at least in my opinion, Martha Is Dead is continuing a stigma on mental illness. As a result, I feel the story, while starting off strongly with a lean toward the supernatural, fell short and could leave people feeling frustrated. There is no real satisfactory ending, rather one which makes you feel like what you did was meaningless while you try and piece together a story with parts missing or without context. People with schizphrenia or DID or severe mental health disorders, don't flip between types of symptomatic behavior like a rolodex and the fact that mental health is the big reveal at the end of the game is really disappointing.Quite frankly, I was disappointed that it didn't stick more with the mother and her addiction or just go full supernatural. Dramatization of mental health may serve as entertainment for many, but the impact of that is far reaching and harmful. Do I recommend this game if you're looking for something impactful about mental health? No. Do I reccommend this game if you're just looking for gore with little substance and/or reasoning behind said gore? Haunting music and atmosphere and beautiful scenery? Yes!

_childDocuments_.review: ★½Let me start this review by stating that I truly enjoy the walking simulator genre. My favourite game of all time is Death Stranding, which obviously isn't your conventional walking simulator, but I also love games like Layers of Fear or Firewatch. Now, this game has some incredible graphics, an unbelievably realistic art style, and one of the most hauntingly beautiful soundtracks that I've heard in a video game. The setting is also interesting and allows for some interesting character backgrounds and motivations. However, that is about where my praise for the game ends. This game was seriously exhausting and excruciatingly boring. Firstly, similar to many other reviewers, I experienced horrible optimization issues and was plagued by low FPS throughout my entire playthrough. I also experienced multiple instances where I had to close and reload the game because it either completely froze or questlines would break and would not allow me to progress. To relate back to my original comment about walking simulators, I think many of the gameplay aspects of this game should have been left out of the game (and allowed it to only be a walking simulator), as many of these mechanics were either inconsequential or excruciatingly tedious. There are game components that I do not think that you should have the player do, and should just perform them for the player. The camera was an interesting mechanic for the first few times, but is only used 4-5 times throughout the entire story, but the worst mechanic was the telegraph. You had to fully code and decode morse code messages, which took an incredible amount of time and was not fun as a gameplay mechanism at all. I also played the game in the native Italian language and I thought the voice acting was subpar, where the main actress did not feel emotionally invested and provided emotion and enthusiasm in the wrong places. Furthermore, I feel as though the story is more akin to an audiobook than playing a video game. The main story beats are told through text on a black screen and major plot points are either told in this method or skipped over so quickly you are not given enough time to emotionally process them. Similarly, I don't think the story itself is meaningful, powerful, or important in any way. The story is terribly shallow and told in  way that does not properly emphasize or draw importance to . Finally, the ending is probably the worst part of the entire game. The last ~30 minutes are probably one of my least favourite video games moments ever. The entire story is poorly summarized in a puppet show (telling the story that we have already seen and telling it in a really poor medium). The ending itself does not pack the deep emotional punch that they think it does or that it should based on the subject matter. Moreover, the gore and extreme visuals feel as though they're added just for the sake of having them present rather than beginning importance to the story or themes. Ultimately, I expected a lot more from this game and felt like it severely underdelivered and was definitely disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: While everything below are things I stand by, I finished the game today and it actually got way, way better. Even though those small issues that annoy me are still there, the story is absolutely worth it. The puzzles are good, the story got me intrigued, the atmosphere is superb. So wonky gameplay aside, I like this game. 7.5/10This game confuses me...POSSIBLE SPOILERS AHEAD, READ THE REVIEW WITH CAUTIONThe game does some things well and some things not so well. But the thing is that the things it does well, it does really well, but the things that it does poorly it does atrociously bad.Take for instance the morse code section; when developing photos, the game tells you at least 4 times, if not more, that it's more complicated in real life but they toned it down in the game for the sake of the player. Then about 45 minutes later you have to communicate using morse code, and you actually have to decipher and decode the messages you get back. So, they "dumb down" one part of the game to make it less tedious for the player, but they keep another part as real as possible which just really made me want to refund the game instantly because that section was painfully boring and annoying.Also, the majority of the cutscenes are way longer than they need to be. Instead of just saying "Hmm, maybe I should go to the shed", your character might say "Me and my sister used to spend so much time at the old shed. If I should go anywhere, it's there. The shed is the obvious place for me to look at. Yes, I should go there. To the shed, I go" in an unskippable cutscene, and she also talks very slowly so it all takes way, way longer than it needs to.On the other hand, the story is really interesting, the graphics are well made, the game is very beautiful and intriguing, and it makes me want to come back for more. And like I said, the gameplay mechanics they got right, they absolutely nailed! It's just that the bad parts are sooooo bad, it's almost undescribable.I don't know if I recommend this game. If you like a game with a fantastic story that keeps you interested and you don't mind a sea full of terrible flaws, then this is a game for you. Otherwise, maybe not.

It's not for everyone, it's hard to even say you enjoyed a game like this, but the overall message is an important one to hear and I have the utmost respect for the developers. As a video game though, it's mainly a slog unfortunately. Everything is very slow and tedious, you crawl around at a snails pace and there just isn't much there from a gameplay mechanics perspective. Would have liked to see more puzzles such as the morse code bit. The game is also very beautiful but even on top tier hardware(rtx3080,12900k, 32gbb ddr5, m.2 ect) I experienced stuttering and frame drops throughout much of the game, very immersion breaking. _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Check the price first. If you find it at a discount or desperately want a psychological horror game that feels very grounded, go for it.I will try not to spoil this one for anyone interested.MiD is about a sister (Giulia) who finds her twin sister (Martha) dead in the lake and, at first, by sheer shock, agrees to say that she is indeed Martha (who was deaf). What slowly unfolds is a tale of psychological horror that sticks with you for one reason or another. The game is set in late 1984, you are part of an Italian family that supports Nazi Germany.Before that though, let's delve into not so serious issues.Gameplay wise, the game is more of a walking simulator, and I mean that in a good way. Your "quests" so to speak are rather rudimentary; Go there, do this, come back. Giulia has a camera at her disposal that allows her to not only document things that she sees in her daily life, but also uncover the truth behind the events that occur throughout the 6 hours it takes to finish the game. The camera manipulation was surprisingly accurate, including different lenses, manipulation of focus, aperture and shutter speed and choosing the right ISO film. The most interactive bit of the game I would say comes from a quest that involves using Morse Code; sending a message is rather easy, but decoding it makes the ordeal much more challenging. In gameplay terms, my biggest gripe is how some of the quests are handed out; you will be given a task that involves say opening a door, but the solution to it is way further ahead within the story, which can lead to frustration. Overall, I think I can describe the gameplay to feel like an artisan craft. Technically, it feels as if it's one scripted scene away from being broken, but never really does.Graphics and sound wise, MiD has its ups and downs. I'd wager the game makes heavy use of photogrammetry to capture some of the landscape, as it all looks and feels great to the eye overall. It's not a technical wonder by any means, but it works well. What doesn't work well however, is performance; the average FPS is not the problem, but rather the stuttering. You would think that using the Unreal Engine for so long, someone would just find a proper solution for it, but it seems not. Add the framedrops, and the abhorrent performance when enabling Ray Tracing (which tbh, I had a hard time finding a proper difference), and you will just have to learn to deal with it. Sound design also has its issues; While the voices are well acted (and I appreciate being able to have the original italian VO with English subs - perfect practice), they would oftentimes get muffled by some other sound in the background, or be played offset to the location that they are in, relative to your perspective. These aspects were not gamebreakers, but they did not help.The story is where MiD shines, yet also trips. The game tells the story of a VERY unreliable narrator, where choices SEEM to matter, but really they do not. What's mostly gripping about the story however is when you realize just how twisted Giulia is, and why that occurs. Sadly though, it resorts to gore and macabre to do so, which I felt was a bit cheap when the story doesn't necessarily need the shock factor to hit home. That said, do be aware that mental illness is at the forefront of this game and pulls no punches in that regard.So, in the end what we have is a game that feels handcrafted, with a slow burner of a story that ends up hitting home when it needed it the most.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a really hard game to finish because it made me feel so messed up for most of it! It's a very personal story that touches on family abuse, mental health, child trauma's, human perversions, body gore, symbolism and much more. This game requires you to witness every messed up part that you can imagine and interact with it the whole time making you part of the action like no other game that I've seen or heard of before... What's also interesting is that this game doesn't depict these topics freely or without merit! Everything is done in a very realistic and necessary way that works with the story and it left me speechless and uneasy which is a very hard thing to do because I've gotten used to a lot as a video game consumer. I've played countless horror experiences and nothing came to be as traumatizing and as memorable as this game was and I'm really greatful for it! Another main reason why this game is so effective is because it puts you in plausible scenarios and forces you to do the exact thing that you don't want to do making it scary and uncomfortable where most games would use metaphors or background text describing what happened to ease the experience and therefore making it less impactful. This game will remain in my memory for a long time and, for what it's worth, I believe that its an amazing game in all the right ways! If you're still wondering if this game is for you then I'll ask you one question: If you had to feel and see some of the worst that mankind has to offer, would you be happy that you were able to experience that feeling from the comfort of your home and not by living it as some people have or are currently living it? If your answer is yes than this is probably your kind of psychological horror and you should consider this title. If this question made you uncomfortable or you're looking for any other type or intensity of horror experience than don't play this game! Lastly, if someone offers to show you this game for fun, don't do it! This game can mess you up if you're not a mentally strong person!

_childDocuments_.review: Intensely immersive and thought-provoking psychological horror.I will compare it to two titles. First, this game is superficially extremely similar to LKA's previous release, . Both games explore madness associated with sexual promiscuity and volatile mother-daughter relationships in the context of World War II fascism, and both take place in a building surrounded by rural nature in Italy. In many ways  can be understood as a remake and a rewrite of , a new attempt to tackle the same topic. Indeed it feels quite different: 's plot occurs during the descent, not after it, and is far more visceral and immediate. It wants you to be inside the deeply troubled mind of the protagonist, and not just to observe it as was the case in .I would also compare this game to Guillermo del Toro's film, . There, too, is an attempt at penetrating the trauma of life under fascism through the psychotic fantasies of a young woman. But in this comparison  falls short as it ambitiously forwards an unconvincing equivalence between the Nazis and the Italian Partisans, portraying them as indistinguishable twin siblings emerging from mutual trauma. It's an interesting academic exercise, but it's not unproblematic to portray sympathy towards Nazis. Unfortunately, 's writing isn't deft enough to deal with this challenge and disturbingly dangling questions remain as to what it says or fails to say about Nazism.The writing is also not deft enough to deal constructively with mental illness. It seems that Sony forced LKA to include warnings and triggers, and so like in a lot of "psychological horror" the beams get crossed. On the one hand we are asked to treat sickness with sympathy and respect. On the other hand the game gratuitously sensationalizes and even glorifies it for our entertainment. Let's be honest: horror is not the right genre to tackle mental illness. So, don't even try, because the result is always accompanied by insincerity.Let's talk about what works. The visual design is gorgeous. Play with raytracing if you can and lose yourself in this idyllic, atmospheric countryside cottage by a lake. Much of the game is about taking photos and developing them in a dark room, and the attention to the details of the process is delightful. There are also telegraph decryption and tarot reading mini-games that are likewise satisfyingly detailed without being tedious. What works less well is the quest design. Some poorly placed cues and map bugs make it seem like you're supposed to go looking for things when you can't, or they point you in the wrong direction.  suffered from this, too, so it's definitely something LKA needs to work on.Writing is also hit and miss. Some poorly edited scenes diminish the grandeur of the best ones. And the voice acting, at least in English, is somewhat mediocre. It doesn't seem like the actors were getting proper direction, if at all.Despite the flaws, the sum totality of this game's storytelling is devastating. I won't soon forget what I saw and will continue to second guess myself as to what really happened.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall,  is a fantastic example of a psychological thriller. It achieves horror in clever and sinister ways that linger in the player’s mind, avoiding tropes such as jump scares. The narrative is dark and layered and there is a kind of disturbed pleasure afforded by exploring it that is not found in many other games. Similarly, the visual and audio elements are beautiful and immersive, even in the most unsettling and gory parts.Spanning a range of gameplay and narrative genres, Martha is Dead has wide appeal, it is stunning and horrific and will haunt players long after they finish playing. It will take around 6-8 hours to complete but has some replayability in terms of choices made in-game, missable quests and achievements. As the content warnings suggest, this game may not be for everyone but I heartily recommend this game to fans of dark emotional interactive fiction and cleverly scary horror games.My full review of this game., where I go into detail about gameplay,. narrative and styling can be found on .

_childDocuments_.review: A decent game with a good story. Totally recommended. It is not perfect however, but more on that below.Good:- Story. It is actually a very well-written one with a good ending and good atmosphere. People who say that it is too violent or gross are, probably, people who never experienced things similar to what is displayed in the game - but I did (including self-harm and child abuse), and I think that dialogues, thoughts of the main character and overall presentation are very real and natural. Puppet shows are amazing in terms of how bluntly they express childhood traumas - and I also could relate to this, with the only exception being that I do not need to remember because I never forget.- Some interesting mechanics such as using the telegraph, developing photos, or using camera accessories. They do a great job of immersing yourself into the game.- Little details which show how much attention was put into the game. There are a lot of them, but the one which surprised me the most is the black stain on the front tooth of the main character during just a few of the cutscenes which had a close-up of her face. Might not sound like much, but the game is full of things like this and it really helps with believing the story.Not so good:- Stuttering. I am starting to hate UE more and more, and this game was another example of why. No matter what I did - it stuttered from start to finish, and it would not be such a big deal if it was not accompanied with cases of mouse skipping.- Texture issues. For some reason, the wall textures of the house got broken starting with the second chapter and remained like this until the end of the game. Again, ♥♥♥♥ UE.- Some mechanics which I talked about positively above are not really utilized that often. On the one hand it is good that they do not become stale, but I would still like to play around with them more.- Some interactions are more or less hard to figure out due to small icons and sometimes strange gameplay constraints (like you cannot enter a church without the lighter being lit up, even though there is plenty of light around)- The advice to visit professional help which is always around is a good one. Except, like always, the website they provide does not provide help in many countries, including mine (Ukraine, in my case). Which is actually laughable, considering that, again, people who are advised to get help are mostly located in the countries where they can easily get it.Overall a solid experience, which might not suit everyone, but hey: you have your warnings about the game content. Read them.

The major strength of this game is its story telling and the plot twists. However, be warned: you must cope with death, violence and (self-)mutilation. _childDocuments_.review: While this game is beautiful and has some unique elements to it (the photography and personal journey) it falls flat for me. This is another psychological horror game where a character has a mental illness and is a murderer because of it. I wish we could get horror games that throw away the trope of demonizing mental disorders. (Hellblade is an example of an indie game which took on a huge research effort to accurately portray schizophrenia and mental illness to their players.) The devs try to take the time to illustrate how horrible "mental asylums" were back in the day, and even the medications people were put on, but they don't lend the physical experience to players---it's all done in exposition diary-entry style narration---which is a real missed opportunity.This game really isn't scary. It's a walking simulator with an unraveling narrative given to the player by the protagonist. However, I did not experience any bugs and I feel that the developers did try to have heart in the right places, but the execution focused on high-intensity gore and confusion. If you like spending time in a slower paced environment, this game is worth a try. Otherwise I'd get it on sale or look elsewhere for your tension-string needs.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the performance issues, the story did keep me captivated long enough to finish. While it wasn't a long game, it was indeed performative. Gameplay was indeed minimal and i would be lying if i said otherwise. The gameplay is merely a vehicle for which the developers allow the progression of the story they wished to tell.A story of deceit, sadness, self reflection, and of course realization. The game starts off as quite a mystery, and as the story progresses you are left with more and more questions. By the end everything is seemingly answered. A few are left for subjective interpretation.I will give this games story a solid 8/10. However due to performance issues i will have to give an overall score of 6/10. Still above average and after a couple updates this game will be easily an 8 or 9. Graphics are of course very well detailed and you can tell a lot of work went into it. Sound was fairly well done. Voice acting was done fairly well. Some of the animation could have used a bit of work, but they were so minor that it didn't really detract from the overall experience. This kinda of game isn't really about the gameplay but instead the delivery of a captivating story. They did a fairly good job. The ending was filled with twists and more twists, but kept along a fairly straight and easy to discern path.Should you play this? At the moment it's hard to say yes, but the story is done well enough for one. You will want a decent PC if you wanna run at 4k. I ran the game at 4k ultra 30fps locked with no DLSS no Ray Tracing. Had a Ryzen 5600x and RTX 3060Ti. Something about how the ray tracing is done makes it nearly impossible for a 3060Ti to run about 15fps which is not playable. For a cinematic game like this you can get away with 30fps if it is a mostly constant framerate. Though even then i still had occasional drops to 20fps. Like i said, there are substantial performance issues.

_childDocuments_.review: Martha Is Dead is advertised as a "dark first-person psychological thriller" from the creator of The Town of Light. Set in 1944 Italy, and with an Italian language set as default, the game is designed to get into the mind of the player.You play as Giulia, and start off as a young girl, with her grandmother reading a rather unsuitable story to her, the story of a White Lady in a lake, a ghost who lost her partner, trapped in the lake until there is fog upon which she can wonder the surrounding forest, and as is often the case, will murder young women. Lovely bedtime reading. Once the seemingly never-ending intro is finished, you fast forward in time, and get some control of your character, you find yourself setting up a camera by the lake, to try and get photos of wild animals, you then have to go through a rather tedious effort of changing the film on the camera, and since this is 1944, it is one of those very old cameras. After you put the new film in, you check to make sure you have the focus right, but upon doing this you spot a body in the lake. You run down, and by run down, you press one button and the character runs automatically, you dive in, after pressing one button, recover the body and drag to lakeside. But wait the body is your identical twin sister Martha who for some reason is wearing one of Giulia's dresses. Upon this terrible discovery, Giulia takes off Martha's necklace and puts it on herself. Your parents spot you, come to your aid, but your mother who despises you, assumes you are your deaf sister Martha and comforts you. And so, the lie begins, Martha is dead, but now you have become Martha, destined to not only pretend to be her, but also learn more about her mysterious death.Ok that enough spoilers of the game, since that is the opening chapter.The game itself has plenty of warnings on it for disturbing content. The PlayStation release has been censored heavily, and some scenes have been removed completely. Suffice to say this is not a kid's game. For those of you who have played The Town of Light, you might have a general idea of what to expect, but no this is much more disturbing.There are options to skip the disturbing scenes, but then what is the point of playing if you take out the most powerful bits.The rest of the game will have you exploring the woods and the area around the family home, the stunning Italian countryside and of course trying to contact the White Lady.The game can be very disturbing as I mentioned, there are some horrific scenes that not only do you have to watch, but you actively take part in. You will quickly understand why the warnings were needed.Think of the game more as a walking simulator, something that the person sitting next to you watching, will get as much out of it as you would playing, there is a lot of going backwards and forwards between the same locations, which can become tedious too. Giulia moves annoyingly slow, and although the atmosphere of the game is great to start with, it soon loses its impact with repetition.There are a few puzzles to complete in the game, but most of the interactivity involves you collecting things or looking at things. Dolls, Puppets etc which help unlock memory sequences. As this is set in 1944 there are plenty of references to the war, radio news alerts, newspapers and so on.And of course, just as you started, taking and developing photos is a big part of the game.Now I originally played this on Xbox and I was not keen. But I thought I would give it another shot now I knew the general gameplay better, and I must say my opinion has changed a bit.My issues are still there, but I do think there is a story to be told here for you the view to "enjoy" if within the horror realm.Is it perfect? no, but it is not bad either. Better second time around for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: SPOILERS AHEAD:I initially had heard about this game from my best friend. He told me about how it was going to be censored on PlayStation and about the graphic nightmare close to the beginning where the player is forced to skin the face off of her sister and then proceeds to wear it. I was IMMEDIATELY interested seeing as it's rare that a game has that sort of depiction of violence and I wanted to know more about the story. I personally am a sucker for psychological horror/thrillers and horror all around so this so far has been perfect for me.DISCLAIMER: At this time I've only played about 3 hours so far.Although I've only logged a few hours so far, the graphics run very well on my computer for it being a low-end PC and the soundtrack is absolutely breath-taking. I've adored the gorey symbolism that's taken place so far and the addition of tarot card usage. The atmosphere is very chilling in some spots, like when we head down to the cellar for the first time or tend to our sister's corpse. The music especially is what truly makes it worth everything. There's so much going on in the best way that leaves me wondering what it means and what could happen next. The throw in of puppetry (although not IRL stuff) was so fresh to see and it made me really intrigued to know more about the character, Death, and their role.My only negative to the game is how the bike is practically useless and a bit wonky to control (very stiff). If you do activate the bike pump task, that also was VERY difficult for me to find. That might have been because I haven't rode a bike in years but I wasn't expecting it to be on the other bikes. I do wish our character also ran a bit faster but it's not that big of an issue where it would hinder game play. It also can seem like a lot at times, especially when it comes to new information but once you start using it, it's truly not as bad as I've seen in other games. Mechanically it's a really great game from what I've played so far and I can't wait to delve further into it!

_childDocuments_.review: The game starts incredibly well. The story seems intriguing and the horror omnipresent.But you quickly come to complete objectives one after another, with slow movements and repetitive actions.Yes, the game was very graphical and disturbing at times. But that doesn’t make it a good game that I would recommend.Moreover, the store page description is misleading in many ways. “Freely explore the breathtakingly realized Tuscany countryside on foot, by boat, or bike.”There are at most 3 or 4 paths around the main house that you can take. That’s all.The character is extremely slow to move, as is the bike which is more than completely useless.As for the boat, it is used only in 2 very scripted sequences.So much for “freely explore”.“Play with numerous marionette sequences”Yes. You’ll play with marionettes like… 2 or 3 times at the very end of the game.Why even advertise something that’s nearly absent from the game…There are so many boring, slow, and repetitive sequences (the telegraph, the phone, the photography, and the darkroom) along with the endlessly walking around everywhere only to complete objectives that this game wasn’t that enjoyable at the end of the day.Oh, and the game took me less than 7 hours to complete.If you really want to give it a try nonetheless, wait for some Steam Sales. It is not worth 30$.

Normally this wouldn't be that big of an issue, but so much of the dialogue in the game just felt like flavor text.3) Half the game feels like it is retelling you parts of the story that you've already heard before ()4) It was never really clear which objectives would cause time to progress and which ones were completely missable. As a result, near the end of the game I found that one of the objectives that I had really been wanting to do was now completely blocked off.

_childDocuments_.review: Martha Is Dead is a first-person horror game set in 1940’s Italy that manages to be both lovely and horrifying at the same time. I won’t give any spoilers. The only kind of spoiler I’ll say is that “Martha Is Dead” (as the game’s name implies). The protagonist you control is named Giulia and her twin sister is Martha, who is found dead at the beginning of the game. Giulia uses the tools available to her such as her camera to figure out who killed Martha. The premise is simple, but with all of the characters thrown in and without spoiling any plotlines, the plot becomes a lot more complex very quickly.The game is set in 1940’s Italy during World War 2 and Giulia lives with her parents. The game really does showcase the tragedy of war and it’s very respectfully done. It doesn’t glorify war at all. My heart sank when I read through the newspapers in the game, who tried to pin Martha’s murder as something political when it likely wasn’t. It’s not a good idea to rush through this game because Giulia’s house is full of interesting objects to examine and the developers put a lot of creativity into making her house feel like a real house someone would live in for the time period.The graphics of the game are very decent for a game of this scope and the art direction is top-notch. It’s trying to be realistic for the time period and it really does a good job. Another example of a game that did a good job with the art direction in a similar way was A Plague Tale: Innocence, though that was set in 1358 in what would be present-day France. In Martha Is Dead, the nearby forest, the lake, the bridge, the farm and its animals are all beautiful and juxtapose the horror parts of the game that I’ll get more into soon.The gameplay is in first-person view and involves moving Giulia around and examining objects. During certain game segments you’ll need to press combinations of buttons or analog stick directions to proceed, such as through setting up her camera. Some of them are quick-time events where you need to press the sequence of buttons within a few seconds while being chased.There are also scenes where Giulia is flying through the air and has to choose paths with words to complete a sentence for a plot event that happened (it’s like the Psyche Taxi minigame in the Danganronpa series). You’ll restart these sections if you put in an incorrect word, but they’re short and easy for the most part and serve as a good refresher for the plot events that happened.The game has a hint feature that you can activate to highlight all examinable objects in the area. In addition, there’s also a journal to view your objectives. There are both main and optional story objectives in the journal and it does provide hints in the text if you’re stuck in the game.Some of the items needed to progress the game can be a little tricky to find, but if you read the journal and take the game slowly you can find everything without issue. During the early story I had to find a bicycle pump, which was attached on another bicycle by another side of the house’s exits. I was also able to collect scissors and a tripod for Giulia’s camera. If you really get stuck, the journal will provide a hint, such as it explaining that the camera tripod is downstairs.The best thing to remember is that there are 3 elements of the photo you can change, including the exposure, aperture and focus and each of these can be turned up or down by using a control, left analog stick, right analog stick, and left/right directional pad, respectively. You don’t need to change them all at once, you can do it one-by-one and when you get more practice it’s pretty simple, it’s just that it looks intimidating.Sometimes you’ll need to search the house to find special kinds of attachments for the camera such as a flash to allow it to take pictures at night. This does add another layer of complexity because you’ll now have to select your attachments and then take the picture correctly as usual, but it’s not bad at all.I would recommend playing this game with a controller, it makes the game much easier to play and I can’t imagine using the camera with a keyboard. There are scenes where you need to use the camera to take a picture to progress, but you can also use the camera for fun. The house has a farm nearby with many loveable animals and I took a picture of a goat and her kid.The game does a great job of juxtaposing between horrifying moments and happy life moments. I haven’t mentioned it in great detail until now, but horror is certainly present in this game and the game does have very gruesome moments, such as one scene where you play as someone cutting off a human face from a dead body and wearing it. I liked the horror elements of Martha Is Dead because I grew up with slasher movies full of gore, but at the same time I know that it’s not for everyone and I wouldn’t force it on someone who’s not into it. But as someone who has played and watched both horror movies and video games for over 30 years, there is a lot of nasty scenes and the developers aren’t afraid to take risks which I can really appreciate in the modern era. The horror scenes are not distasteful in this game either, they’re meant to convey what it’s like going through a terrible experience and there are significant meanings behind the scenes in the game.The game is organized into days, and progressing the main story mission usually results in major plot events happening and the day progressing, so it’s a good idea to have backup saves because often I’ve accidentally progressed the plot even though I wanted to do side content first.The game is very linear for the first few days, but as you progress you will be able to unlock many side objectives and the world becomes more open. My only criticism is that the days can get repetitive after a while, and as I was finishing my playthrough of the preview build it was getting boring because you’re waking up and exploring the same house again until you do the main mission.One interesting side objective involved finding the pack of tarot cards that was confiscated from you. It’s a really neat game mechanic where once a day Giulia will shuffle her deck, pick 3 random cards, and do a tarot card reading on herself.Eventually you get access to the house’s telephone. There’s a list of contacts your family has written down, such as the police number, family friends, the doctor, etc. You can also keep track of important numbers you come across in the game not present on that list of contacts. When you have free time you can call them and get access to a lot of interesting information. One interesting conversation you can have is actually with a rebel group and it leads to an extremely interesting side quest chain. I’ve explained earlier that Giulia’s father is a German general even though Giulia’s living in Italy. You can help the rebels with their efforts by thwarting the Germans’ plans, or alternatively you can even tell your father about it.I chose to help the rebels, and it lead me sending and receiving their messages in Morse code. It was a very fun side quest and actually taught me how to use Morse code. The game had a translation sheet to convert words to Morse code and back, and that made the process easy even though it looked daunting at first. In fact, I wouldn’t even mind if the whole game was like that because helping the rebels felt like a historical movie.It’s genuinely fun to explore Giulia’s Italian household and learn the rich culture of the 1940’s and when you begin playing I guarantee you’ll want to solve the mystery of what really happened to Martha on that eventful night.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredibly well made. The map, the sound, the characters/objects...everything is fantastic. However, the story is incredibly slow. Incredibly. The story involved in the game is interesting, but progressing through the game is extremely tedious and boring. Having to inspect dozens of items, sometimes to meet an objective (like reading the newspaper every day, letters, etc), or completing objectives that are just really boring in general. There are also bugs in the game that should be addressed as well. I picked up a letter and was unable to put it back down, I was just stuck there; I had to load one of my saves in order to continue. I also thought it was very annoying when I had the lighter in my hand to see around the house, and then if I were to do anything I had to select it from my bag again.The breaking point for me was when the game spawns you in the forest after Martha's funeral, and naturally you think to go down to the lake to meet the White Lady because the main character talked about it. I got down there and realized that I had to walk all the way back to the house to find an item, then go all the way back in order to continue. Very annoying; I just quit the game at that point. It felt more like an open world adventure game rather than a horror.Overall the game was very boring to me, which is disappointing because every other aspect of the game is flawless. I like everything about it except for some small bugs/game mechanics, and how incredibly slow the story is. Sometimes games can be slow, tedious, or boring at certain parts, but I played for 2.5 hours and nothing changed. Sorry devs.Edit: Another major complaint that I have is that the game is not really optimized. I don't have the best computer, but I can play some really resource intensive games on high settings with little to no issues. On this game I had to lower everything to medium, which made the once beautiful-looking game to meh looking, otherwise the lag I got made the game unplayable.

_childDocuments_.review: This is yet another title where I would have preferred a middle option. I'm gonna go with not recommended due to its somewhat insensitive handling of mental health and - disorders subject matters.It looks ASTOUNDING though, I love everything visual about it, and some scenes and sections are truly great, like a scene in the woods where the backdrop and setting suddenly hits you in a remarkably poignant way (I don't wanna spoil it as it was the true highlight for me).I enjoyed the photographing and photo development, and sending morse code via the telegraph (a completely optional side quest, but come on, you miss basically half the game not doing it, though I appreciate the option to be more or less active in the war). Several gamers on forums took issue with how the morse code puzzle worked, but I found it actually very smart and realistic, in a gamified way of course. The game does not hold your hand when it comes to coding and decoding these messages but if you figure it out you feel like a champ, and the girl you play as would have had to figure this out the same way you do. Or not, depending.There are several of these little instances where you can opt to take steps to figure things out, like getting hold of numbers to call and pretend to be other people say, to gain information, but the game doesn't outright tell you this is an option as I recall. Then again, you can ignore that completely and bascially never touch the phone at all and go about the games main storyline. I love that.You have all these realistic settings and mechanics in a stunningly beautiful realised world, with superb leading voice actress Annie Warburton, all conveying what could have been a very interesting and engaging story, but then they have to attempt to shock for shock values sake alone. It is pretentious and at the same time insensitive and therefor disingengious to the story they are trying to tell.There was some controversy regarding the game being censored for certain releases, and what it meant was making a cutscene out of a short game play mechanic in which you simply moved the mouse according to prompts. I can't say I understand the reasoning behind that, and also I would stress that the scene in question is meant to be taken metaphorically. The scene didn't bother me and it was a legit part of the story. However, when we later in the game are to believe we can cut a body set in rigor mortis open with normal fricking scissors as if it was made out of butter, I was taken out of it completely and had to laugh to myself. Well I don't know, I'm no expert, maybe dead bodies do turn to butter after a some days, but it came across comedic as presented in game, and I just felt like it was one ”dark for darkness sake” scenario too many and it tips over into splatter farce rather than psychological horror.

_childDocuments_.review: It's difficult to give a verdict. Many pro's and con's. The setting and time period was a fantastic idea as it has a certain charm that you won't find anywhere else. The protagonist is engaging and you really delve into it all. The journey down the rabbit hole and finding the "truth" was quite thrilling, BUT. The big con of Martha is Dead is that despite its few and short horror bits, it lacks overall intensity. It's not hardcore enough to make you fall out of your seat. Yes it is a psychological horror, but it mostly is psychological and only little horror. Would have been great to see one fall into a nightmare (blair witch / the evil within 2).

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, the graphics in this game are beautiful. If you didn't know it was a horror game, you def wouldn't know by looking at the scenery. The story, overall was pretty good, however, I do have to go back and google or rewatch my gameplay to understand a few questions I have that were not clearly answered. I do wish there was an option to go back and complete it 100% without starting over. When the game concluded I apparently completed only 70ish % of the objectives. There is a morse code part in the game that I highly suggest googling a morse decoder because looking at the chart in the game was like a foreign language. My only BIG complaint is that I would have liked to see loss of a child, child abuse, and animal abuse as part of the warnings. I love gore, and honestly there was a LOT LESS of it than I anticipated. Nothing was really "scary" about the game in my opinion, however, I would have liked a warning about those 3 trigger warnings mentioned. Honestly, I think those few scenes messed with me more than anything. Luckily I was prepared for the loss of a baby because I read a twitter trigger warning. The other two, I was blindsided by. Overall, I do recommend checking out. The graphics and game mechanics alone make it a really interesting game.

_childDocuments_.review: Totally not worth the price.Some stupid examples:You see you can pick up cutters, your character says nope.You move, see a window where the object you desire is, character comments that how to get it. Be a clever and go check if you can now pick up the cutters. Nope.Go back, see the door with lock, character comments that hmm I wonder how I can open this. Go back to cutters, Ohh ofc NOW I CAN PICK THEM UP.Another example, you see a sewer hole in a side quest marked on map. You want to go there. But your character refuses to use a boat, can't walk up the beach or through a forest. Have to check some main quest ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ to get the boat to run. name: HYPERCHARGE: Unboxed
detailed_description: HELP SGT. MAX AMMO TO DEFEAT MAJOR EVIL AND SAVE THE HYPERCORE! There was once an ancient line of action figures, who created a magical power source that would allow humans to keep their favourite childhood memories of their toys. This ancient power source is known as the Hypercore. Inside the Hypercore are the beloved memories of our favorite toys. If Major Evil destroys it, these memories will disappear forever. Defend it with everything you've got, or see our cherished toys turn into lost treasures of the past! Key Features 1-4 player online/local co-op. Full split-screen support including online/local. Single player/offline play with player bots. Difficulty scales based on the number of players. Wave-based shooter with story campaign. Classic PvP game modes. (up to eight players) First and third-person camera modes. PLAY CO-OP WITH YOUR FRIENDS Work together as a team to defend the Hypercore. Grab a friend, break out of your toy packaging, and get ready to fight waves of classic toys. Prepare for each wave by searching for weapons, resources, and even hidden secrets. OFFLINE PLAY FOR SOLO PLAYERS Not everybody likes to play online. Hypercharge supports Offline, Split-Screen and Local play. You can progress and unlock everything in-game while playing solo. PLAYER BOTS Don’t have a team to play with? Don’t worry, we’ve got you solo players covered. Player bots listen to your commands, collect resources, and even help to build defences. UNLOCK ACTION FIGURES Earn unlocks the old school way, in-game with hard work! No Pay-to-Win nonsense. PLAYER VERSUS PLAYER MODES Go head-to-head against other action figures as you fight to become top of the scoreboard! Classic PvP modes include Deathmatch, Team Deathmatch, Capture the Battery, Infection, and King of the Hill.

_childDocuments_.review: Hypercharge: Unboxed is a game that reminded me of the Toy Story movies with the references to the Green Army Men from the movie dropping in with their parachutes and tank trucks. It also has that Tower Defense vibe in the adventure mode, but does kind of fall short in the multiplayer department in terms of match making and servers.MY VIDEO  REVIEW LINK: Written Review coming to Weebly soonSCORE: 7/10PROS: - Love the customization option. I just wished there was a little more to it - Reminds me of my childhood with toys beating up other toys - Cool and catchy soundtrack CONS: - Matchmaking can sometimes lead to bot lobbies - Servers created by other players shut down when they shut them down. -I think they could have added other things in gameplayI think the game is worth it for sure when it comes to kids. I like the enemy variety and what they are trying to accomplish, but I just think it needed something to push the score higher, especially in the gameplay / mechanic department. Overall, a 7 out of 10. Do I recommend it? Yes in terms of fun times and nostalgic stuff

_childDocuments_.review: If you're the type of person who enjoyed Small Soldiers, and Toy Story this game will suit you well. If you're the type of person who enjoyed toy stores, arcades, and cartoons in the 90's you'll probably enjoy this game too.Mechanically, this game is crisp. Shooting enemies, and building a defense for your power cores feels rewarding. Graphically, the game is gorgeous. It feels like you're dropped right in the heart of a Pixar scene, and i found myself spending the first few minutes of every new map ignoring the objective and exploring. Just when you think you've found all the hidden nooks, you find a box you didn't know you could jump on, and suddenly an entire area of the map you previously though was inaccessible is made available to you. I'm excitedly waiting this games full release, and to see how other game modes are introduced. I'll be updating this review as the game develops, but for now this game is a wonderfully priced way to spend a few hours a week.

_childDocuments_.review: From what I've played so far I absolutely love this game, I've been waiting for a silly toy themed game like this for years and the time has finally come.If you're just wanting a "is it worth the price or not", definitely. I got this on sale for £7.74 and feel bad I got it for this cheap, as so much went into this game.I do have some small nit picks that I want to mention to the devs that I feel could improve the game (and just other tiny nit picks that are mostly silly).- The movement.The movement in this game feels a bit off, for example I feel the ledge grabbing is very inconsistent. I feel having the game grab ledges automatically as long as you're in the air and you're going in a forward motion should have the game look for ledges to grab in front of you. Tapping or holding space whilst looking at a ledge to climb over a lot of the time does not work half of the time.I also feel like the game doesn't let you have much air control. A lot of the times I go and try and jump up somewhere, but a lot of the time I'm fighting against the small amount of air control you're allowed to maneuver with, I feel a game like this should definitely allow for some more freedom in movement in terms of air control, but I could just be malding here, as it's just something that bugged me a little when playing.Another thing is I feel that even if toggle sprinting is off, when running you should still be running when letting go off the sprint button by default, it feels a bit clunky when you're expecting your character to still be running, but actually you're suddenly walking and you die from it or you don't make the jump you're trying to make. Toggle sprint is a good counter to this issue, but I feel it still should be a present feature of normal sprinting.The thing that bugged me the most about the movement is just how inconsistent the ledge grabbing felt.- Visual indicators.There were times I had no idea what was hurting me, or that I was being hurt. I feel like the visual indicator on screen that is showing where you got hurt form could maybe be improved slightly, in the form of make it more obvious that it's there or something, because I feel it's hard to notice HUD elements sometimes amongst all the chaos.Now saying this I could just be blind and everyone is fine with how it is, but I know there's people out there who would judge an entire game based off the fact they didn't know where they were getting hit from, so It's just something to keep in mind.- The silly stuff.Now like I said before, I've been waiting for a silly toy game like this of this quality for a long time. That being said, I personally believe there could be a few changes done to make it feel more silly and "toy like".For example, the foot step sounds right now make me feel like i'm playing a super serious world war 2 battlefield game, and the guns sounds (and shoot) like they're real guns. So as a suggestion of something to at least have a think about, is have the foot step sounds sound more "plastic" if that makes sense, so you actually feel like you're an action figure just running around the bed room or whatever, and make the guns feel more "toy like" if that's even possible.Obviously I'm not a developer of this game, maybe all this was already trialed and it just felt like crap, or some other reason, I'm not sure, but again these are just tiny nit picks that I feel would make this game even better and make what it's going for more of a thing. It's just these small tweaks to make what the game is going for be more present, and to just constantly remind you you're playing as an action figure running around the bed room or the garden or whatever doing action figure things.And one last thing, I don't often make a review with much thought into it, it feels funny being a 21 year old doing a serious critique on a game about action figures and toys. Thank you for making a game that is making me a man child.

Cosmetics are great too, with your action figure able to go from G.I. Joe, to dino-men, ninjas, robots, and bug-men.A special note:Not only is this game an incredibly enjoyable mix of FPS and Tower Defense, but the entire release shows just how much the devs care.  On day 1 of release:-Almost no bugs-Full controller support-Online AND splitscreen support, in 2020-A decent sized demo, in 2020-Tons of cosmetics with no microtransactions, in 2020-A quality game for $15-$20, in 2020Day 2, 3, and 5:-Fixed the only bug-Added Steam Trading Cards.-Added more dedicated serversI also need to mention the insane amount of accessibility options:-Separate FOV for game and weapon-Night mode options (disabling blue light)-Screen shake intensity-Weapon sway intensity-Button prompts for Xbox, PlayStation, and Nintendo Switch controllers-Separate HUD and UI scaling from 50%-150%-Customizable splitscreen options like quality, vertical or horizontal split, and if third screen is top or bottom-Separate control customization between splitscreen players, including KB/MTo top this all off: cheat codes, all of which are yet to be discovered and aren't on the internet yet.  In 2020.  'Nuff said.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall this is a genuinely terrific game. While it won't have the 4K shine of an AAA title, it looks incredible (especially given it's install size) and has tons of little details to appreciate. The levels are decently varied in terms of size, aesthetics, and design. When playing with friends lower difficulty levels are easy enough, but the harder difficulties can be tough. Players start a level with a set amount of "Build points" (currency) and use those to construct defenses to protect a number of Hypercores (the number varies based on the leval) from swarms of enemy toys that attack in waves. Killing enemy toys provides you with more build points, to build more defenses, to kill more enemies the next wave, etc. Build points are also scattered around the levels for players to run around and collect. This not only provides incentive for exploring each level, but helps teach newer players the layout of the levels and can highlight some good spots to defend from once the attack phase starts. Waves are split into a Build phase and Attack phase.Hypercharge: Unboxed supports four player co-op locally, online, or a combination of the two. While it's more fun (and more fair) to play with friends, it's entirely possible and enjoyable to play single player.Probably my biggest complaint is that I'm not really a fan of the Buildables unlock system. That said, it's a small team, it's still being updated, and what IS there is more or less terrific.If you like FPS, or First Person Tower Defense games Hypercharge: Unboxed is an excellent game overall. It looks great, it sounds great, the weapons feel solid and varied, the platforming is quite good, the levels are diverse, and it feels like playing a war game set inside of Toy Story.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a lot to like about Hypercharge unboxed, but there is also a lot to dislike.Likes- Graphically excellent. Great use of primary colour and cartoonish textures to have you expecting to see a spaceman and a cowboy toy popping up somewhere.- Cute story, voiceover and music. So wholesome and innocent :)  - Well designed levels. The layouts have been lovingly crafted and remind me of an old Sega Saturn game called 'Clockwork Knight', with plenty to explore.Dislikes- Tedious platform hopping nonsense. Oh you think you can make that jump because the physics let you do the same thing earlier? Nope. Have a long fall and spend another 30 seconds getting back to the jump point to try again.- Crap weapons. Yay! I finally got a flamethrower, but it takes 10 seconds to kill a bad guy with it. The 'railgun' needs to be charged up and takes 2 shots to kill things. Your starting weapon is just as effective.- Sequenced collectables. There are lots of nooks and crannies to search, but some things don't appear until you've completed a wave, or collected something else. You're going to have to be REALLY dedicated to pick up everything.Overall, the frustration outweighs the pleasure with this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I played with a friend of mine through all of the levels on casual difficulty and earned gold or higher on each of them.this is by far my favorite game to come to steam in 2020 thus far, i never got the chance to play Toy Soldiers when i was a child but this feels like a way for me to experience it in the modern gaming space while also taking me back to my fantasies while playing with action figures in my childhood home.the graphic fidelity is STUNNING. the attention to detail and the love poured into each miniscule scratch and smudge brings the entire world to life, the subtlest of movement in the animations that show you these are indeed 80s/90s action figures is breathtaking. the batteries have fingerprints on them, the character models have seams in their plastic, the store tiles have scratches and subtle dips from years of wear. every inch of this game world deserves to be admired.It should also be stated. VERY IMPORTANT. I can tell that the artistic portion was so much fun for these devs to work on, because after the first few minutes me and my friend had decided that if there were legible words on objects in the environment.. WE WERE READING THEM! so many fake products that have such incredible meta humor and silliness had us catching our breath for minutes at a time, do yourself a favor and simply walk up to any old box or household object and read the labels. you will not be dissapointed!as for the gameplay, its quick enough to get your blood pumping, but not so fast-paced that it stresses you out, the gun mechanics are more solid than most indie shooters i have seen, with some unique recoil patterns on the automatic powerhouse weapons and some pinpoint accuracy for the sniper options, though it becomes a little obvious this game was not intended to be a hyper-accurate shooter, many starting rifles have very unruly kick to them that make it impossible for newcomers to reliably track targets.the buildable defense mechanics are a lot of fun to play with and strategize, carfully choosing where to place those walls and anti-air turrets to better thwart the waves of incoming toys trying to whack your hyper cores, the more you play a certain stage, the more familiar you become with the best defense strategy to employ.the character customization has consistently put a smile on my face no matter which model of figure i decide to play as, my current favorite being the undead knight figure, Wraith. The name system is also a blast to mess around with, unlocking more titles, nouns, adjectives, etc to mix and match into the perfect pre-2000s action hero name, and the randomization button has given me a ton of laughs as i wonder how my friends might react to seeing what the system has decided to name me.and this may or may not be important to some people, but it sure put the final digital cherry on top when i discovered that each and every one of the customization and buildable card options will be earned through gameplay and skillful challenge completions! no in-game micro-transactions of any kind! it actually blew my mind!this game could have been double the original price and still be far beyond worth the money, please support this wonderful development team, such a small studio deserves your praise and adoration for crafting this plastic-smashing work of art and i cant wait to see what sort of content will become available in the future.
