_childDocuments_.review: Updated review.  I'd recommend this game to folks now who are looking for a "fun in short bursts" co-op game to play with their buddies.  It's not the best FPS tower defense game out there, but it also has enough charm and does enough right to warrant a purchase - especially on a sale.  It's not something that's going to hold a group's attention for a long time, and the game doesn't have much staying power thanks to forcing you and your friends into replaying the same levels over and over to get your unlocks (since hidden items that give you the unlocks disappear for everyone once one person gets them), but there is fun to be had here in smaller play sessions.The dev fixed all the camera issues that caused extreme nausea, which my first review below touched on, so full props to them for fixing the issues that made the game all but unplayable for quite a few people and as such, I'm adjusting this review to recommend the game now.---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------OLD REVIEW HERE---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------If you are prone to any sort of nausea when playing FPS games, you may want to be careful here.I can handle most games, but there are some VR games that put me in a bad state.  This game makes me feel like I played a bad VR game due to the following reasons:- The entire camera shakes when you shoot your gun, instead of just the gun itself.  This may not be so bad if it were subtle, but it's not subtle at all; the whole screen shakes violently.- The camera tilts at an angle when strafing.  This makes it appear like the camera is locked to the player model's head and the player model leans when it strafes.  Can't say for sure, but this is how it appears.  This is also the most nauseating thing... eyes to do not do this when you move side to side in real life or tilt your head.  When you combine this with the camera shake, it's a recipe for that bad VR feel.- Motion blur that cannot be disabled.  This isn't nearly as bad as the other two, but it still sucks.Can't recommend this game in its current state, and since it doesn't look like there's any way to disable all this camera WTFery (it almost seems like the devs have never played a shooter before), I'm probably going to have to refund this.Sucks too, because the premise seems super awesome and tearing out of a toy package as an action figure on a shelf was such a great start.

_childDocuments_.review: is a pretty simple tower-defense FPS with a fantastic "retro toy" aesthetic and decent replay value. Built by a passionate dev team that cares  about the game they're making, it's worth the price of admission (which is usually $15-20). Unfortunately, the community is extremely small, and finding a game with other humans can be hard. Versus modes Deathmatch, Team Deathmatch, and Infection are available to play with up to 8 players, but they offer limited entertainment without a full party of human players. Customization options look great, but lack diversity and uniqueness. The retro toy aesthetic shouldn't exclude more varied body shapes and design concepts, but embrace and allow for them instead. I'd like to see this game spread its wings a little bit in that regard. The DLC is reasonably priced, after all. Gimme some Gorgonites for my Commando Elites, you know?While I do recommend it for the fun it's given me,  doesn't seem to have much more than 10 hours of actual game. Unlocks are rewarded through tedious hunts for hidden shinies in each stage. The devs like to call their unlock mechanics "play-to-win," calling back to the gaming days of yesteryear when content was unlocked via gameplay. I don't disagree with the principle (given the pay-to-win MTX addiction grinder  the big-name devs are all dragging us into), but scouring every in' stage for shinies is in' exhausting.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a bona fide children's wonderland. What a gem; truly, this game will bring you back to playing war with your mismatched assortment of toys as a kid. Though, it's not only the charm of it's characters and settings that elevate this game, but it's variety of play. The maps, guns (plus their modifications), and enemy hordes are unique and numerous, which drastically change the flow of the game and your approach to fighting against the toy invaders. There are a myriad of challenges which will truly test your prowess of the game and it's mechanics, including gathering collectables scattered around each map that require epic parkour to acquire as well as high ranks on the many maps. The rewards are fantastic, too, with some delightful cosmetics that allow you to customize your toy soldier as well as have access to creative new buildable defenses. This game is fantastic and while there is much to praise, I think that the trailer speaks for itself; if you have even an inkling of interest after watching it, then I encourage you to buy. You will not regret it. The only major negative I have is the game's lack of singleplayer content. The game does not scale very well and you quickly feel overwhelmed when playing by yourself, especially on the game's more expansive maps. I almost exclusively play this game with one other friend of mine. And even with that extra support, we've found it near impossible to get anything higher than a gold rank (have all towers still standing on either easy or normal difficulty) on Garden of Evil, the game's largest map. We have put in arduous effort to earn a diamond rank--that is, a perfect score with no damage done to any of the towers on hard difficulty--on a handful of other maps. I've also frequently experienced a bug where my mouse clicks don't always register in the game, so I'll be vigorously clicking and not shooting at all at random points. It's more of a minor annoyance, however, it does become an issue on the air hockey map in particular if you're shooting for that challenging diamond rank, as every shot is crucial. Not everyone experiences this glitch, though I know of some others that have from the game's discord. Thankfully, the singleplayer issue is being addressed in the next major update, which is adding a new game mode (along with a brilliant pirate's playground map) and bots to help pull some weight when low on friends to play with. And yes, the creator's do continue to pour their hearts into this game and are excellent at communicating with the playerbase. I look forward to the future of this game and hope that it gains some more players, as it's well deserving of the attention. It has easily become one of my favorite shooters.9/10 (only gets better with every update)

_childDocuments_.review: I don't generally enjoy leaving reviews, as a matter of fact this is my very first steam review to any of the games that I own. However with this game being in early access I felt that I should at least do my part and tell anyone having doubts whether they should buy this game or wait until its full release - just as I was. And let me tell you that you absolutely should buy it now if this is the type of game that you enjoy. And here is why:CONTENT:The game is full of it - The principle is simple enough, you have to defend your cores. But it's how you do it that will really keep you going - which traps to lay down and in which position, where should you position yourself for quick access to all cores, where should you invest your coins - a trap, a jumping platform or a weapon upgrade. These strategies will lead you to a gold or even platinum medal (standard difficulty) if you are able to use your resources appropriately. tl;dr - If you are concerned with content I can assure you that it isn't lacking and you will have as much fun as any other fully released game in this genera. MAPS: Because the game is in early access and more maps may be added I will not say exactly how many are currently available, but it's the same quantity and size than any other AAA FPS game. The maps are very cleverly laid out and really make you plan and outline a way to get to all cores in time for a quick response.SINGLE V MULTI-PLAYERI have played in both modes and honestly I felt no difference between the two modes, both are very fun and because the game balances the difficult of the level based on you being solo or paying with a friend it never feels unfair.PERFORMANCE: The games runs very smoothly and it never crashed on me once, I run this game at a consistent 144fps and I never had a dip even in intensive battles where a lot of enemies are in one location, if you are especially picky with the performance of your games then I can assure you that this game won't let you down.WILL YOU HAVE FUN?:OBVIOUSLY! If you love fast paced and action filled games then this game is loads of fun!FINALLY:Massive thanks to the devs -  the artwork is absolutely amazing and the game runs buttery smooth and you can tell by a mile that this game had and still has a lot of love put into it. With the amount of crappy games coming out its great to see such a good title being on steam.FINALLY FINALLY - Please to the devs if they are listening - please don't take an epic exclusive for your full release, without steam I couldn't even be writing this review!

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game from my best friend some time back, and after having gone in to thoroughly play it, it is a demanding title with a variety of fun gameplay modes. Pros: 1: Nostalgia for toy movies such as Toy Story, and Small Soldiers. If you grew up with movies like these, you're gonna start off on a good vibe!2: Classic shooter style gameplay. Nothing fancy, no "slide cancel", no "Advanced techs" or any of that! It's RAW!3: Simplified weapon system! Your entire weapon loadout is 2 weapons, and you can pick them up as you go. They change based on what weapons you pick up in each stage, and each has it's own ammo. 4: Fun character designs. The playable characters and enemies by majority have a humanoid shape. 5: Single Player and Multiplayer modes a plenty! From the campaign/story mode, to the VS modes. 6: Loads of player customization! You unlock a LOT of stuff to work with to make your ideal figure! From base body, to matching heads, to the weapon color, EVEN THE BOX! I was impressed by the attention to detail with the way all of these details came together!7: You can play with up to 7 friends for 8-player online play! This means a fairly light load on your PC if you happen to host a game online!8: Peer to Peer connection: No worry about servers shutting down if the devs decide they're done with this game and move on to their next project if it proves profitable.9: Unique "Tower Defense" action gameplay! It incorporates tower defense mechanics into the game, making it a whole new vibe. Totally different from every other action shooter game I've EVER played to this point!Cons: 1: Only 10 maps (And they're used in both single player and multiplayer)... THIS is a bit crippling to me, as I remember my old FPS and TPS titles having more than 10 maps. The only difference is that the hypercores are not present in most multiplayer modes. I would appreciate some Multiplayer exclusive maps or arena maps designed for multiplayer. Something like an "Overhead display" map, or "Collector's room", or for a MASSIVE map, a Gymnasium from a local High School with stuff like Bleachers as a MASSIVE symmetrical multiplayer map. 2: Bot AI... This is one of those cases where AI bots will start to focus on you if you start to get good or start climbing the heap, even if they're all set to the easiest setting. 3: Limited multiplayer mode options. You have the Campaign/story whhich can be played split-screen, or online, or run a LAN network, which is a big plus for up to 4-players co-op. But the multiplayer modes are the usual batch. Deathmatch, Team Deathmatch, Capture the Flag, and a mode I never thought I'd see outside of free to play garbage First Person Shooters with gross balance issues (Such as overpowered sniper rifles that instant-kill in one shot with explosives nerfed to be useless), the "Infection" mode. There is one more mode, but I forgot what it was... Would be nice if they could make a differentiation between Free For All, and Team modes. 4: Sessions max out up to 8 players in VS modes. I get this is to accommodate players with older PCs, which hits me in nostalgie for old 8-player Starcraft matches. But as an action and shooter game, personally it feels like they could crank up the player and bot numbers. Just a small gripe honestly. I'm used to VS matches with 16 and even 32, sometimes even 64 players at a time killing each other.5: Loadout limitations. Some weapons take 2 slots, and as powerful as they are, the biggest problem with these is the fact that some weapons have substantially more recoil. The minigun for example has crazy high recoil, and you need minigun specific parts to add to your gun.All things considered, despite the cons, the Pros more than outweigh them. I hope this game gets some updates soon to add more to it. It's a good solid game to play, and it could always stand to get more support. A Gymnasium level would be so awesome though.  And a stage where the entire house is a MASSIVE open world including the back yard. An alley map with pipes and lumber situated for a symmetrical map would be cool too. Adding symmetrically designed maps for multiplayer would be a great step forward.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely recommend this game to pretty much anybody: The price point is incredible, the attention to detail in-game is stunning, the references are endless and universally heartwarming, the soundtrack is BANGIN, and the game is just good clean fun. The gameplay cycle in co-op mode is basically as follows:Platform for resources, build defenses, fight, repeat. It's good fun, especially with friends. There's also free roam, where you can explore the levels and collect secrets without a time crunch, a competitive mode where you can murder your friends, and a couple party games, too. It's quite a bit of content for a low price.Try out the demo to get an idea of what's going on in the game, but be aware that it's tame compared with what you'll normally come up against in-game. Each level is unique, and they change quite a bit with each difficulty level. There's a surprisingly large amount of content.

_childDocuments_.review: After a bad review with my first encounter of the game, I would like to sweep off the table..I was unable to play online due to my AV/firewall was blocking, I tried whitelisting which didn't help, at last I disabled my AV/firewall and ran the game and steam as adminstrator and then it worked.... And booooy! I'm so glad it works, what a fun game!First of all, I love the concept and the whole idea. The way the developers use humor is next level :-DThe graphics goes perfect with the environment. I stopped several times fighting, just to admire the maps. All the maps I've tried so far, are really carried out well, and you really get the feeling of being a little sized figure in a really big world, which in perspective, is just a garden or a childsroom. It's simply just brilliant, and I'd really really wish this game just had a "id*ot-proof" matchmaking system, like... Overwatch, or something... That would guarantee more players filling up the game modes, and make it way easier for newcomers, unfamiliar with creating/searching for game-lobbies. I know there is a "automatic finder"-function, but that's not what I mean, I would like to see a queue-system, where you can optional choose to host the game, and get a bit more XP, or something like that, you could also then easy implement ranked.Score:Graphics - 9/10 - The graphics blend almost perfect with the whole idea of the game.Mechanics (Only played co-op) - 8/10 - Nothing that you haven't seen before, but they took the best parts of other co-op games and blend it together.Sound - 8/10 - Really blends well with the environment, I personally turned down music, but that's just me.Animations/level design - 10/10 - The only thing I miss, which is totally unnecessary for the gameplay, is the possibility to interact with the objects/toys in the surroundings, like moving them or such, everything is just static objects. I'm thinking straight out of the box here, but you could maybe even make it possible to use some of the objects for your advantage. As an example, in the kitchen, there is abit of objects you can interact with, like vegetables and stuff, but what if I could use my grenade launcher to shoot at a carrot which goes into a horde, or push a book down the shelf, to a massive plastic crowd? ---------------Overall: 9/10 - Would easily get a + point if they added queue system and ranked etc. and fixed the progression not being a locale save file, your profile should have some Cloudsync or server hosting.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of, if not, the most innovative and fun tower defense game that I ever played. It's very creative and rich in detail with its guns, weapon attachments, map variety, enemy types and game modes.   It functions pretty much like a regular strategic tower defense game, but the strong and unique aspect of this game is the freedom to explore, climb and jump around the map to find collectibles (and very well hidden secrets) and to gather coins to expend on defenses, guns, weapon attachments and even to try your luck on a slot machine.  Depending on your match performance, you'll unlock customization options for your character and buildables for strong and sturdier defenses. It's easier and even in its best when played with friends or by a company of randoms in public matches, but it can be really challenging depending on the difficulty that's being played on, so it requires team synergy and strategic thinking. Really fun and very creative game.tl;dr: It's a tower defense game that's really creative and fun to play with friends, can be really challenging and it's very rewarding, detailed and addicting. Highly Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I spent most of my playtime in the newly updated single-player campaign/waves mode.- Map Design is astounding. Each map is fun to explore for collectibles, with plenty of jokes and easter-eggs to find. You can spend hours exploring a single map, free roam mode lets you do just that.- The combat tech is very engaging. There's a lot to learn using weapons, from the current gun build you're making to reload swapping.(Swapping weapons/Melee does not cancel previous reload.)- Lots of cosmetic customization. Tons of things to unlock to make your character feel unique.- Versus and other modes are great. No complaints aside from semi-empty lobbies. If you got friends (I don't) it's super fun (I'd think).- The game has incredible charm It's one of the most imaginative and fun games to run around in. Reminds me of the old 3DO Army men games in the best ways possible. They really captured the aesthetic they were aiming for here.- Optimization is insanely great Load times are near instant and framedrops are non-existent. It's amazing how smooth the game runs even with so many toy corpses near the end of a mission.- The devs are devoted and compassionate for their work.Doing free content updates and listening to their fans for so long earns some mad respect from me, no matter what. Excited to see how the game evolves further. Again this is from my personal experience in single-player campaign/waves mode that was released literal days before I installed. - The actual Tower Defense feels limited.The tower-defense part of this game is a bit restricting. Very few placement tiles on early maps and easier difficulties. The turrets are very expensive and feel too situational to rely on. On single-player expect being overrun often, as bots abandon posts frequently, meaning the 1,500 credit defenses gets shredded by 2 meanbots and a spinner cause you were busy with the other 98% of the wave.Trying to juggle defending every hypercore personally makes getting Platinum/Diamond rank (no core damage) a pain on big maps.Batteries drain incredibly fast and sometimes the map spawns too few to sustain a good defense, there's a battery charger you can unlock for build phase to help with this, but it unlocks from Platinum clears, making it obsolete on Casual/Regular.- Some enemy encounters are VERY annoying.There are a few "player hunter" enemies that are too strong, usually killing you before you realize they're there, Brobots and mini-bosses in particular.Drones aren't very tanky but their raw numbers in some maps will demolish you, and they usually kill you in just a few hits. Anti Air is basically required to help mitigate this.Jets are the epitome of annoying. Fast flying, hard to hit enemies that send homing rockets to hit you and your defense. Not terribly lethal to you but it will knock you around (and off high ground) and shred defenses. In my experience, antiair usually miss shots on them because they're just too fast.Dead Army Men sometimes land upright, making you think they're still alive.- Movement feels a bit jankPlatforming is a bit floaty and vaulting is inconsistent. It helps if you have a grenade launcher or jetpack, but I've lost about a half-dozen Platinum games because I couldn't get up to the core from missing a vault and falling down at critical moments.I know I just criticized the game for the past few paragraphs but I had actual, genuine fun while playing. I'd still recommend it even if you'll only ever do the single-player stuff. I know the developers read and respond to reviews so hopefully they use my feedback/complaining however they need. It was a lot of fun to do the campaign and I'll keep trying to solo Diamond rank every level.p.s. flamethrower turrets would be pretty neat, just sayin :^)

_childDocuments_.review: It's a beautiful game that's very well polished; just needs a little bit of work on certain aspects in regards to bug fixes and tweaks. It's genuinely surreal to be running around in almost identical environments you've likely ran around in as a kid, from toy stores stacked up like military installments I used to make out of dumb Legos and the million assortment of toys/household items around me, to a garden, a garage, and even a familiar bedroom! The customization is super on point too and it genuinely feels like you're making your own action figure. My only gripes with the game are some of the current standing bugs that'll definitely be fixed I'm sure, along with the inability to 'pick' a general starting weapon. It's not a -huge- deal but I do wish you could opt to go into the game with a certain weapon and deal with its drawbacks rather than just having to hope for RNG to give you what you're looking for.Some enemies definitely need tweaking as well, notably the bomber versions of enemies. They feel a little bit cheap when they just plow through an entire line of defenses without issue, then totally nuke one of your points because there's so many of them. Maybe just reduce their rate of spawn a touch? I dunno.This game has a -LOT- of potential though and could go very far with what it has. I genuinely hope to see so much more content for this game, because what's there is genuinely amazing, and is so much fun to play around with. If I had any suggestions as a shot in the dark, maybe an elf action figure or a dwarf, though I know the latter might be more unlikely due to possible funky behavior with the camera and platforming mechanics. New buildables though, new enemies-- honestly just everything the game has now but expanded upon! It has an amazing base to work from, and just generally more of what we've got would be a massive chef's kiss. Thank you guys for the cool game, definitely will be keeping up with it as time goes on.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a very Good First/Third person Tower defense.Pros- Can play single player not just a multiplayer Game! (Though Multiplayer is more preferred) - The graphics are very well done and the art style is great.- The sound track is great and puts you in that retro style mood.- Every toy in the game is just such a throw back to childhood. - Lots of collectables hope to see more!- Good Maps From Small to Large. (There's about 11 Maps I believe so far, which isn't bad but looking forward to seeing more with updates!)- Movement and controls are pretty solid (The climbing up can be a bit tricky with certain secrets but its not overly difficult to get them)- Gun play is pretty well done! (Not to compare with other games but I get a Very "Doom" or "Halo" vibe with it and in my opinion, that's great for this type of game)- The customizing your Gun during Gameplay is pretty cool (Really like that idea Especially when you can switch out to any type of weapon that you need or want quickly. Hope to see more Weapon parts be added!)- split-screen/Local Multiplayer always nice to see in a game like this! Gives a lot of the older multiplayer vibes.- Customization is simple and very pleasing to switch what Action-Figure you want play as and give them a unique title and Symbol. (hope to see more with updates!)- Like that you can have different defense towers and unlocking new ones over time- plenty of replayability and mindless enjoyment (I've Completed most maps on gold and a few on platinum) Haven't done higher difficulty then regular yet so far but plan on doing it all!- Lots of little Easter eggs/references and such, which is fantastic.- So far no bugs or glitches that I have encountered, one crash though, which isn't bad, over the course of my Game Time and its well optimized as well. Cons- There are very little cons with this game which is great but there are improvements that can be done and additions that can be added!- Not alot of PvP or Main Game Modes! (I assume there will be more but it is a bit disappointing there is only the few Main choices you have which is Death match, plague and the Wave based mode. The mini games are cool, Spinners and tanks but I don't count these as main modes because there fairly quick but all modes are decent and have lots of replayability!)- The Bot AI is a bit wonky and simple. (just needs some fixes and tweaks)- Waves do become a bit tedious and no differences between the enemies each wave (at least on regular difficulty) it's usually the same enemies for each map in order then random.- No Campaign is a bummer but it is planned in the future updates.Other Stuff- Unfortnately not a lot of online players and servers so expect to play mostly with friends then random people which isn't a bad thing, you'll probably have a better time with friends then randoms anyway but its personal preference.- Was hoping to see more pvp game modes, maybe a tug of war mode. its a 4v4 and you have to defend your own hyper core while your minion toys attack the other team or something of the sort. Maybe even a capture the flag mode. where the flag is a battery instead and you have to charge your own core or something. Just more other modes in general really. (I just hope too see a few more main modes really, which are planned in the road map and I am very looking forward to.)- Good Design and types of enemies, just hope to see more as well in updates.- Movement is smooth but just needs the slightest tweak with a few things but really it's pretty minor in my opinion and doesn't hinder gameplay at all.-This game has just alot of potential to be better (It's already good) but it can be better and improve with more over time, respectfully in my opinion, of course especially with continuous updates. It is impressive that this is a Fairly Small development team that has made such a good quality game as well so I don't expect things too be pumping out constantly and super fast. So as long as the quality is the same as the game itself with dlc and updates, Im pretty happy with buying this game and the packs to support it.-I don't review a lot of games but this is an under the radar game, and I think this game deserves more attention and notice and believe every review helps to keep this game going and noticed especially when it is a very fun and enjoyable experience, I wish the developers luck and look forward too seeing further updates with this solid game! I hope to see more in the future and look forward to the games that they develop next!

_childDocuments_.review: Game is well made with a lot of style.--Gameplay--PVE: Pretty much defend the points against waves of enemy toys using map exploration to find weapon attachments and currency to put down traps and bolster your defences. This works very well but does have a level of RNG with drops etc.PVP: I haven't really played much of this but it seems like a simple and effective arena shooter with a few modifier game-modes like zombies which is cool.Freeroam: Exactly what it says on the tin. This mode is mainly to get used to the maps and find collectables for character unlocks which is a good touch and appreciated.--Controls--The controls are pretty standard for an FPS aside from the more floaty feeling during jumps.You have a standard jog and sprint along with a standard jump, double jump and vault/climb when holding down the spacebar to allow for easier traversal. Shooting is a standard sort of FPS thing with damage, recoil, accuracy and reloads that can be slightly buffed through attachments but if you are stuck between reloads you can also melee to deal damage. You have a basic weapon reticle that varies between weapons for aiming and the ability to zoom in with right click (If you have a sniper scope attachment you can scope in proper too).--Graphical design--The whole game reminds me of playing the toy story 2 video game on PS1 or army men on PS2 and I like that a lot!The maps have very good attention to detail even down to the small ones like the trash strewn about on the ground with great modelling, textures and scaling. In a word, the game is very TOYETIC if that's a thing.--Enemies--The base enemies are very well made with their own unique attack/movement animations and variations depending on difficulty. The explosions can be a bit too much at times however.The bosses, be it end of the level or mid wave mini-bosses, are all pretty fun to fight with each having their own designs, abilities and weaknesses. Very nice.--Customisation--The player gets a whole lot of customisation options that are unlocked in various ways on top of 2 payed for DLC packs that add some new character options to chose from which are pretty good.One interesting thing you can give your character a name from a set of unlockable preset words which have a good amount for creativity.The player character starts with a type that has different heads, colour schemes and weapons colours too which gives a pretty good amount of things to tweak and change.There is a bunch more I could say but I'll keep it simple. Overall there aren't really any aspects I HATE at all and the small dev team is constantly working hard to push new content and general updates for the future, props to them.An easy recommend for me and there is also a demo to try for you to check if this game is for you!

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played much Hypercharge yet, but I can already tell that this game has the potential to become something very, very special. The developers have done something really difficult here in managing to capture a true childhood-like experience of just playing with our toys and upscaling it into a grand battle that is both beautiful and funny. Kudos.Stuff that I love about this game:- No microtransactions. Thank you for not being evil.- Map design and variety. - Tons of stuff to unlock. Buildables, skins, maps, even new names in the name generator.- The name generator itself is a delight. - The off-brands. Just reading the labels on all of the various props around has been cracking me up. I wish my speed stick had 24 hour Hodor protection.- The music. Great soundtrack with a perfect 80's vibe. I hope more tracks continue to be added!- The level of nostalgia that this game sets off is incredible.- Challenges and Collectibles for added objectives each map. Things that need improvement:- As I write this, only one game mode exists. Coop defense vs waves of enemies. It's fun, but I could see it getting stale after a while, especially once you've collected all of the unlockables. But considering a drop-down menu for game modes exists in the menu, I have to assume that more modes are planned for the future.- The weapon system could use improvement. Attachments are unclear as how they effect you (ex: different optics simply say things like +1 accuracy, but in a game where there is no aiming down sights and only a zoom-in-effect, I have no idea if accuracy means an improved zoom effect, decreased spread, recoil reduction, sway, or what. There's also no indicator for how much +1 is vs nothing or +2, or any comparison with a currently equipped attachment of the same slot). Weapon variety itself is a bit low, but a new weapon was just patched in today, so again my hope is that this is being worked on already.- The machine gun is awful. If it's going to be less accurate and do less damage than the regular rifle, it can't also have a smaller mag. Give that thing at least 60 rounds.- Enemy variety. I absolutely love the enemies that exist (the spinning crossfire death discs might be a bit too strong) but I would love to see more knock-offs of different toys coming in to attack. A bit of randomization to some waves might be nice as well.- Shop inventories. While I love the way that shops are set up as attachments that come in the toy's box, it's a little awkward trying to mouse over every little object to see if it's anything useful or not. I think a shopping menu that you can access at the boxes might be more intuitive. It could also let us sell unwanted attachments for more cash/building coin.

_childDocuments_.review: started off to be a fresh and unique take on the tower defense genre, not necessarily redefining it by any means but it definitely stands out from the crowd. The idea of being a toy soldier defending Hypercores against a multitude of various toys was a charming experience. However the further that you progress into this title, the more obvious it became that some core mechanics were either overlooked completely or restricted compared to other tower defense games.• A variety of different enemies with different variations• Each level is well designed with a lot of attention to detail and secrets• The majority of weapons were decent and fun to use• The idea of being a toy fighting against different enemy toys was quite a charming factor• Lot of replay value if you have a full team• PVP is also available if you’re interested in that• Lacks and restricts basic tower defense mechanics • Games difficulty doesn’t scale with the number of team members, solo players won’t survive• There are fixed positions where you are forced to build towers, with little to freedom• Sometimes the game feels too RNG based, sometimes you’ll get OP weapons that spawn and other times you won’t get anything worthwhile• The range of turrets is represented by a number but it never shows how much a unit is in the map• Sometimes towers to me were damaged but to other players, they weren’t damaged at all• An instance happened where the wave wouldn’t end so we were forced to restartLike any tower defense game your main objective is to protect your base of operation, in this case you’ll be defending Hypercores. Depending on which map you play on, there can be anywhere between one to four Hypercores to protect. It isn’t necessary to protect them all though it does affect your rating on the level which can unlock new towers.Upon starting a level you’ll be given three minutes to explore the map, collect money, build defenses and find batteries. Exploring these maps was always enjoyable the first few times, though some maps were more platform heavy than others, there was still a lot of secrets and collectibles to find as well as references and jokes scattered around the map. Three minutes barely seemed like enough time for a team of two and we usually fell short on time to do all the necessary preparations for the upcoming wave.This title definitely brings new mechanics to the tower defense genre that makes it unique. Whilst your defenses primarily slow down and shoot nearby enemies, the majority of the firepower will come from the weapons that you acquire. There’s a decent amount of weapons that you can find that can mow down most of the enemies, though some were clearly more superior than others. Unfortunately finding these weapons comes down to luck whether they spawn in a shop or around the map.In order to progress through the game you’ll need to obtain medals to unlock other levels. Depending on how many Hypercores you protect will depend on what medal you will get. On expert difficultly, it can be very challenging to get the diamond medal and it got to a point where it felt impossible to progress with just a team of two.As you progress through the game you’ll undoubtedly encounter a lot of different enemies from different toy sets. You’ll be fighting against toy soldiers, robots, spinners, bouncy balls and various other enemies along with different variations of them on the harder difficulties. Some defenses were more effective against specific enemies (for example fire traps were good against spinners) but it was more of a trial and error system to find out which ones were best against what enemy. Spinners were a primary concern if you built walls since the walls were hollow if the spinner could get inside then it would destroy the wall in seconds and leave your Hypercore exposed.However,  seems to overlook some of the most basic tower defense mechanics or make them more restricted. One of the more annoying restrictions is the fixed positions that you build your defenses on, there’s little freedom to where you can place your towers, and although the harder difficulties give you more places to build it still felt rather restrictive.To add more frustration there isn’t any indication as to were your enemies will be coming from. This becomes problematic since you don’t know which Hypercores to protect with more defenses and which ones you don’t have to bother with on that wave. It punishes the player despite not giving information that they need to effectively spend their money and choose which defenses would be the most effective.One of the more noticeable flaws with  is the fact that it doesn’t seem to scale its difficultly depending on how many players are on your team. Solo players will definitely have a hard time getting through the more difficult levels because of the sheer amount of enemies spawning or because of the size of the maps. It seems that  was definitely created with a full team in mind, punishing solo players or teams below four in a number of ways. You can join random people through servers however, you do need a level of communication that doesn’t seem possible when playing with random people.Another overlooked mechanic is yet again more information that is withheld from the player, being able to know what enemies will be attacking on what wave is vital to keeping the Hypercores alive.  doesn’t seem to have this basic feature, on more than one occasion we had to restart because we didn’t have the defenses required to effectively take care of the enemies on that wave. This would usually result in a Hypercore being destroyed or heavily and having no choice but to restart since it would affect our rating for that level.Playing in the perspective of a toy soldier was very appealing, being able to climb the familiar environments of the bedroom, kitchen and gardens was a joy. Every map has a lot of detail both in the textures and references that you’ll find by exploring the maps. Enemies are all designed to be just like classic toys and some are obviously plain knock offs of classic toys from your childhood that adds to the charm of the game. definitely brought some interesting mechanics to the table, its just unfortunate that it forgot about some of the more basic ones. Playing this game solo is practically impossible up to a certain point and even with another friend you won’t be able to get through the entire game without a full team. If you and some friends can team up and play this game together then I would definitely recommend this title. If not then I would wait for an update until it balances some of these issues so it can be possible to play solo or with a friend.

_childDocuments_.review: After viewing the steam page I was pleasantly surprised by how much I actually enjoy playing this game. It is a similar to a tower defense game, but it encourages/requires exploration between waves of enemies. A timer appears between each wave for you to explore and collect credits or collectibles and build up your defenses. Different strategies are needed for different maps and yes, even different waves. I have played exclusively Co-op so I can't speak for the other game modes, but it is extremely engaging and requires communication and teamwork. Each map brings different challenges. My team and I played several maps, unlocked skins and immediately began customizing our action figures. Then pressed to unlock more. It is fun and addicting and has a lot of playable hours in it making it well worth the money. I can see this as a base game with more maps/unlocks being added in the future as I feel that this game definitely is "beatable" and once all the items are unlocked there won't be much point in playing anymore. The appearance is charming and brings back childhood memories and sparks the imagination in a very Toy Soldier like atmosphere. There are unlock-able characters and skins for your little action figure and your weapon.There is a lot of parkour to collect credits or collectables. These challenges of a different taste than the fast beat shoot'em up during each wave really breaks the game up in a refreshing way. I find it keeps me engaged as basic shooters tend to leave me bored after only a few rounds. I only wish it gave you a little more time during each round for these exploration stages. I end up turning the difficulty to easy for the first few times on each map in order to get all the collectibles as easy mode gives you roughly 4 mins between waves to try to figure out some of the parkour puzzles and try and fail at them a few times while still giving you time to build your defenses. The only thing I found to be disappointing right off the bat was that there were no female versions of each action figure type. It has nothing to do with the game play, just a purely cosmetic thing, but as a girl, its nice to play as a girl character. Especially since the entire game is centered around unlocking customizables for your character. But this doesn't take away anything from this games value or the fun to be had. So i don't see this as a negative, just a little disappointment. There are a few issues I have found. Though none of them are game breaking or even irritating on a level to cause more than a fleeting, mild annoyance.  One of which, is the short tutorial leaves a lot to be desired. I came out of it having no idea how to do a melee attack. Either the words flashed by on the screen too fast for me to catch or I just missed it amidst my panic as I tried to fight little robot action figures.I still have no idea what order the medals are in. I believe it is bronze, silver, gold, platinum, diamond, then emerald? I have also heard rumors that there is a ruby, but I could be wrong and perhaps diamond is the highest? I only know of some of the rewards because the skins require an emerald or diamond score to unlock them. Otherwise, I would have no idea there was even an emerald.And there are options in the host co-op menu that are unclear. There are some things that aren't explained clearly. Navigating the menu can be a little confusing. When first trying to figure out how to play co-op I stumbled around in the menu for a minute as I was expecting a large CO-OP button. Instead, there is a play online and I am still unclear if your friends can just join you as I have had to invite them every time because we can't figure out how to join friends games from the in game menu, so we use steam invites instead. Using the menu I am still unclear and it is a little confusing.In game there are upgrades for your weapons that add to things like accuracy. I have collected a lot of them, but never noticed a difference. I don't know if they do anything at all. If there is a difference, it isn't noticeable during battle.Overall, it is a great game. I enjoy playing and highly recommend it. It is worth the price and I see a lot of potential for dlc's or expansions for this game, continuing the fun. I hope the developers do add new levels, each with their assortment of new maps/challenges. It is really fun. And is some of the most fun I have had with fam/friends on a game in a long time. Seriously, if you are here at the steam page and giving it a look, just buy it. You will get your money's worth and have a blast.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to recommend this game. The devs are great people that care about their game. They've released a slew of free updates and are on top of fixing bugs. The base game looks and runs great, is a unique twist on the genre, and has some fun combat. Still, the game just doesn't have much replay value. You don't have to take my word for it, though; even the reviews that recommend the game only have 5-10 hours in the game on average. If that's all you're looking for, then this game will be a fun time. If you want to be able to play a game for more than an afternoon or two as I do, then this game is not for you.Devs, I know you are working on making that campaign, but I think there are much better uses of your time and energy than something that will most likely only be played once. After you finish that, I think you need to work on making the base game more random and varied as well as some medium to long term goals for people to keep working towards. As of now, each map is basically the same experience each time. Once you find all the collectibles, why play it again? I recommend taking a page from other games that spawn random waves with a rare chance of special waves (like maybe an alien invasion or a ton of green military figures or something). The Gardens and Graveyards game mode of Plants vs. Zombies Garden Warfare does this well. On top of making each session more fun, players need a reason to keep playing/something to work towards. Yes, there already is a ton of different skins to unlock and better versions of placeable defenses, but there is a not a clear path to earning them. It just kinda...happens every once in a while. Players need to be able to target earning what they want to.

_childDocuments_.review: [Disclaimer: I have only played the campaign for 2 hours so my impression *could* change with more play-time]I saw a reel for this game on Instagram and had to buy it!It looked like a realisation of my childhood, playing with action figures with my brothers, in the wake of films like Toy Story and Small Soldiers (from which I'm sure the developers took some inspiration).After my first play-through I can say its great! The nods to all sorts of things from the 90s (from toy stores to the toys themselves) are great and I can't tell you how much I love it when games entice you to explore with the promise of unseen collectables. Something that is often lacking from most modern games.That being said, I can't shake the feeling that as it is it's fallen short of its potential in two critical areas.1. PvE/StoryHaving not played the original, multiplayer mode of the game I can't really comment on it, but from what I've read it appears that the campaign essentially draws completely from it, but adds a string of narrative.I like the route they've gone with the narrative, and the comic strips are really well done, but it feels like a bit of a cop-out for a single player mode to just be a version of MP with bots. They could have done a little more and created a more fully fledged story mode, with some of those MP elements but with a narrative that evolves as you play each level.Like I said before (and has been echoed by many other reviews) the game gives me Small Soldier/Toy Story vibes. It would be great if they capitalised on that more and brought in more of what makes those two special.2. MapsThe maps have been brilliant so far, each further drawing on what it felt like as a child with their favourite action figure in any given environment. The toy stores have been my particular faves, giving you plenty to explore while also providing lots of ways to take out at the enemy...I just wish they were bigger. I know there are limits and what makes sense given the mechanics of the game, but my urge to explore and find other vantage points always lead me to the doors or the end of the aisle where I'm left disappointed to see the (almost) invisible wall. I want to run around the whole house!! I've seen mention of some bigger maps, maybe I've just not got to them yet, but I just feel like there should be more room.(As an aside to the subject of maps, how about this for an idea? A MP mode a bit like Planetside where you have various teams in battle for control of a whole house/store. It could work much like I imagine MP currently does, with points being captured and defended, but each battle contributes to the overall control of the region.)As I previously admitted, I've not played the MP aspect of this game but I think I know what I'm going to say about it based on the little I've read. I'll reserve my judgement on it for now, and come back once I've played it.So yeah, so far I'd give it a 6.5/10, but it could be even better with some more additions.[Edit #1] Oh, and I really wish I could choose to only use 3rd person. The point in this game is to see that you're a toy. you can't do that in 1st and I have to switch camera modes in every level and with every respawn...

_childDocuments_.review: This game is already truly excellent. I've just been seeing adverts for Grounded and getting excited about a game on a small scale, and then this drops into my lap. I've played about 10 hours so far, and myself and my friends that have played it all agree that you can DEFINITELY see that this was made by a group of friends, because it's just... fun, which is the highest compliment I can give any game. The environments are stunning, particularly all the easter eggs; the music is fantastic; the enemy models are perfect; the naming style for your character is GENIUS and not something I would have ever thought of; the controls are intuitive.From reading the developer responses to other reviews, I was very happily surprised to learn that the game is still being updated and changes will still be made. I was already extremely pleased with the game as is, but to hear new game modes might be added in has me very excited. A singleplayer mode would be very useful I think, as some people have mentioned the difficulty is a tad high when there's only 1 of you since you're stretched defending 3 hypercores at once, and depending on the map that can be very difficult to manage. I would add though that I wouldn't want the solution to be what so many games do, whereby you ALWAYS have 4 people on your team, and if there's less than 4 players it just fills the rest with AI. I think one of the dev responses mentioned adding 1 AI bot to help you in singleplayer, which I'd be very happy with, but I wouldn't want the AI to outnumber me 3:1 at that scale.The limitations on where you can build defences makes a lot of sense to me - I would say my only issue so far has been that a lot of the more static defences don't feel dynamic enough to me. Glue traps are fantastic, actively slowing the enemies down and giving you more time to deal with them, but I find walls to end up not being that useful as a couple of solid hits and they're gone. On top of that, it makes them feel like a bad investment as when they're destroyed you have to pay for a brand new one at full price. To use the castle walls as an example in the bedroom map (Dawn of the Toys I think?), I would quite like it if the base price for a wall is something like 15 build credits (or however much it is right now as I recall it being a sensible price), if it's damaged but not destroyed it's 5 to repair, but then if it's destroyed rather than just falling down and vanishing maybe the enemy could bust THROUGH, and then charge you 10 to repair it? That may go against the toy feeling, however, so I would totally get it if that's not the direction artistically the devs wanted to go.One final thing that might help would be either in each level, or maybe only in levels you've already played at least once, before each wave comes maybe it could give you a hint of where the enemies will spawn? I know in some levels, e.g. No 2, you can basically just leave one of the hypercores until later as it won't be attacked directly until wave 3 or 4. Knowing where the enemy will come from, and therefore which hypercores will be most vulnerable in a given wave, might allow players to think more tactically, and maybe destroy defences around 1 core to get the credits to reinforce one that's about to be hit hard.Honestly, if nothing I've said above gets implemented or anything close to it, this would still be one of my favourite games I've played this year. As I've said above, this game is just FUN, I can kick back with a controller and shoot little green army men, and what else do you want in life?Oh, and on a final note, THANK YOU FOR HAVING SPLITSCREEN. I feel like a lot of game developers have forgotten that splitscreen exists over the years, and it sucks because this sort of game is meant for the old days of 4 friends sitting spread across sofas, bean bags and floor in a living room, a few bottles of fizzy drinks, and laughing and yelling as they play together. Kudos to the developers.

_childDocuments_.review: I’d been watching this game on Steam for some time because I’m big fan of toy games like the original Army Men and the Toy Soldiers games and this looked right up my alley. I think it’s the nostalgia thing that gets me, the fond memories of playing with toys as a kid and setting up big elaborate battle scenes. For some reason I never got around to buying it though, then one day my 10-year-old son saw it on the Nintendo Switch eShop and really liked the look of it and kept asking me to buy it. I thought it would be better on PC, so I stalled him. Fast forward to the 2020 Steam Winter/Summer sale and I noticed it was in sale and showed my son who so excited about it that he used his leftover birthday money to buy it. I’m so glad he did, as we have been having a blast playing it ever since and even my 8 year-old-son has now joined in for 3 player split-screen action. I literally have to stop them from playing as the 3 of us would happily sit there and play it all day if we could, we’re totally obsessed, curse you responsible parenting! I’m using my keyboard and the boys are both using controllers (Xbox One and Xbox 360) and the controls work perfectly. The game’s main mode is a first-person shooter/tower defence hybrid. The levels are a mix of everyday rooms in a house and in a toyshop where you have a set time to explore to collect money to use to build your defences around the “Hypercores” that you need to defend. One of the things that always sucks me into games in unlockable content and goals/achievements and this game has heaps of them. Each level, on top of the hidden coins, coin packs and gear you need to find, there are also well-hidden collectable items. Your money can also be used to buy weapon upgrades in shops or you can take a risk and gamble with a slot machine, which is unlocked after finishing a level over a certain rating for awesome loot (strangely, both my boys get obsessed with these machines and spend far too much money on them). It’s a lot of fun jumping around the level searching for stuff, especially as the developers have added a heap of little details and jokes throughout each level. The level of detail is impressive, for example on the back of some of the toy boxes there’s full readable text. Your character can only build 3 different defence structures at a time, which you can change and customise before you start a game. As with most things in this game your choice of 3 structures is very limited at the start as you need to unlock more as you progress. This also helps when playing co-op to make sure everyone has a good combination of defences at their disposal. The other unlockables in the game are various characters and cosmetics for them. I also like how you unlock a custom title for you character using 4 different slots that have various names you can combine to make you own 3 word title that appears above you in-game, mine is currently: “Sir Mighty Eagle”. There are a couple of other game modes, including a Deathmatch and an Infected style mode, which I have only played briefly. They’re good, but just not as fun as the tower defence co-op mode in my opinion.Everyone starts with a basic rifle weapon, which, depending on the level, will start with one function. You can often find weapon attachments scattered throughout the level and in the in-game shop and slot machine. You are limited to 2 weapon types to change between at once and in some cases with the more powerful and rare weapons like the flamethrower and minigun, only one. The other attachments are items that add accuracy to you weapon, like sights, bipods, and stocks. There is a decent enough variety of weapons, like shotguns, grenade launchers, lasers and machine guns and you soon discover that some weapons are more suited to killing certain enemies that others. This once again comes into co-op strategy as it works well if your team has a good mix of weapons to help take out certain enemies quicker and easier. Speaking of enemies, they are a cool mix of old-school and newer toys that attack you in waves. There’s classic army men, bouncy balls, robots, zombies, and Beyblades just to name a few. They each have different ways of moving and attacking and once you learn their strategies it is a lot easier to dispatch them. And there’s even larger bosses on some levels that take a fair amount of damage before you kill them.You can play this game by yourself and it is still fun, if not a bit harder to defend the cores all by yourself, but this game shines playing co-op with friends without a doubt. The lasting appeal of this game is redoing all the levels and trying to find all the collectables and then increasing the difficulty to try and get some more unlockables. I’m really excited to see what the developers have planned for the future of this game, some more content and DLC packs would be amazing. Great retro theme, awesome level of detail, great couch co-op, tonnes of unlockable content, great for split-screen  Could use some more levels and modes (which it looks like the dev’s will add in at some stage), not as much fun by yourselfEDIT: Since I posted this review the dev's have added so much more free content and they continue to do so, making an awesome game even better!

_childDocuments_.review: This game has never been any fun to play (as you can infer from the fact that I gave up on trying to find a way to enjoy it after only 3 hours) and I don't think it ever will be because rather than listen to player feedback on how to improve the game (namely by adding worthwhile content rather than microtransactions) the devs instead seem to focus on the worst possible form of PR management by attempting to censor negative user-reviews for their microtransactions and banning people who write them.Save your money. I actually gave this game a timid recommendation back when it was still in Early Access because although it wasn't good, I liked the concept and hoped it would eventually become good if the devs could just improve the core gameplay...My sincere apologies to anyone who might have bought the game based on my review because rather than actually make the game good, the devs added MICROTRANSACTIONS in the form of "DLC" skins.After I posted a negative review for a bundle of those, the devs flagged my review with Steam which temporarily resulted in my review being banned. (As you can see above it's back up now because Steam Support found that it was wrongly banned)One of the devs even ADMITTED on discord that they had flagged my review for because it referred to his skin bundles as microtransactions.This is especially absurd since "microtransaction" is literally the same terms used b Eurogamer and other publications to refer to the cosmetic "DLC" in "So Borderlands 3 will indeed have in-game microtransactions, but these will be cosmetic-only..."So to summarize, these devs literally believe that THEY are entitled to decide what the word "microtransactions" means and then flag reviews that use the term in the same way as major gaming publications... Literally minutes after telling me that they flagged my review and WOULD FLAG any other reviews that mentioned their microtransactions, they banned me from the Steam forum literally without even listing a reason, citing an old post that literally read: "Thanks I'm looking forward to it!" in response to one of the devs describing plans for future content.The game works, it looks great, and it's a nice concept.HOWEVER, it isn't nearly as interesting as I hoped it would be because the tower defense aspect is kind of broken (you never actually seem to get enough money to build any of the more interesting defenses) and as a result, the game is kind of dull to play.This game could be great with more dramatic battles and enough money to actually build interesting bases.Timid recommendation because it works and what is here is good but it could be so much more.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: This game is pure fun and a nostalgic overflow.It has several modes. PvE tower-defense with 14 levels and a stylish art-book like story telling campaign. S mall-to-medium replayability factor. (But it will get better when endless mode becomes a thing). PVP modes like Team Deathmatch, Free-for-All and Infection.(Can be played with bots too and friends in private lobbies) Split-Screen mode. 4 difficulty stages.Intuitive gunplay and high level of customization with a little bit of grind required to unlock some parts. (Just like in the 90's!)Flawless performance. Stable FPS, no lag or crashing.Only gets better with friends and family.Recommended with reasonable expectations, as this is an indie team of 5 people.     With a total of 13+ hrs on record, trying to explain how nostalgic this game is , would be an understatement of a century.With every new level you discover or rediscover a part of your childhood and that distant, long forgotten memory that unlocks with an audible 'clink', when you see your favorite toy come to life again. A straight definition of a 'core memory unlocked'. In short, I adore this game. But as anything game-related, I will always try to criticize it without prejudice and provide an actual experience in a form of a review.     First of all, game-play. I would consider it to be good with room for growth. The gunfight is enjoyable and responsive. Each weapon feels as it should feel and packs enough damage as one would expect it to. The idea that you create your own weapon with each session/level, based on your needs at a time, seems like a healthy choice for a tower-defense/shooter. (Although I would like to see an in-game vending machine, where your pre-built weapon could be purchased.) Luckily enough, that is not an issue in almost any level. Throughout said level, you can still create a weapon of your choosing, even when playing with friends.     And perhaps you remember the good old days, when you and your friends gathered at their place and played on a single TV or Screen, using Split-Screen mode? Well, I'm happy to report that this game has this too. One that can be customized to your own preference.    The level design is great with a clear inspiration from Toy Story or Small Soldiers.(From a child's bedroom, where toys come to life to a garden and the toy store.) Presenting a healthy array of jumping-puzzles, collectibles, points of interest and Easter eggs. Almost anyone could find their preferred play style when it comes to weapons. Those few who enjoy a melee based combat, will be disappointed as there are no blades, axes or daggers, just a good old fashioned knuckle sandwich.    Secondly, performance. Geforce RTX 3070 / AMD Ryzen 5/3600 6-core. / 16 gb RAM = 99% 125 FPS. || 200 FPS. I think the result speaks for itself. I have not experienced a drastic dip in FPS or have any lag when playing with friends. Don't remember a single crash either. But again, that is my experience.     And lastly, content. From what I know, the game is being developed by a small indie team. Ever since 2020, the game received several major updates. Introducing campaign, maps, enemies, guns, fixes and more. They are not frequent but they are great. Sometimes there are major updates back to back and sometimes several months pass without much happening. And as of this moment, they are working on an endless tower-defense mode. Which will only enhance the grand experience of this game.     And if you will ever get bored of the campaign and its repetitiveness? The game also offers actual PVP modes such as: free-for-all and Team Deathmach. Infection. (Essentially Zombie survival).Sadly they don't seem to be as populated as one would want them to be. At least in some cases. Some days better than others.One thing is certain. The developers love this game. They love their past and they introduce us to our own nostalgia without looking like greedy corpos thirsting for a quick cash grab. Their DLC's are straightforward. A support package and a couple of action figures.I recommend this game at this stage as it may as well be on par with Deep Rock Galactic, just not as fleshed out. (yet).

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing this game on the Nintendo Switch since launch, and was absolutely blown away by the level of detail and care that they (the developers Digital Cybercherries) put into it. This was even BEFORE I had joined their community on Discord (which is great btw)With that said - reviewing this PC version is straight forward. The game is rock solid, runs fantastically, looks exponentially better than the Nintendo Switch version (which in itself was a feat to get running and looking well). I came in knowing the baseline of what to expect, but even that was exceeded by just simply playing it. The first major difference I noticed was the additional details with regards to lighting and particle effects. Just absolutely gorgeous. It also runs easily at 60 fps on my aging Dell XPS 9550 (with a eGPU GTX 970). There is also 4-player (up to) spit-screen mode - which is in itself a lost art. Playing with my buddies just threw me back 15 years to Halo days. There are modes for all to play - and even little 'party game' style games (Spinners mode and Tank battles).The online mode is solid - there will no doubt be more servers playing up as this launch happens. Hypercharge seriously makes me feel like my 80's kid self. I don't normally 'double-dip' into games on multiple platforms, but something compelled me to just do it. With the 1.0 official launch happening - it's an absolute MUST-HAVE game to own. It's a true sleeper-hit waiting in the wings.

_childDocuments_.review: Even in it's early state, this is seriously one of my new favorite games. Just a really solid co-op shooter. I love being able to mow down waves of killer Beyblades and tiny green army men with a minigun that shoots airsoft pellets. I love how giant and detailed the maps are, they are waaay more beautiful than they have any right to be, and have easter eggs and collectables scattered around to reward exploration. With a little bit of extra content and balance changes, I also think the PVP could be worth the price of admission alone, if that's your thing. But most of all, being an immature manchild who has a thing for old toys, I absolutely love the theme. It's kind of like if Microvolts was a tower defense game, and, you know, not complete garbage.The only real issues I can think of with the gameplay are the weird floaty movement, which isn't too bad but it can take a bit of getting used to and could use some tweaking, and the surprising spikes in difficulty. Even on the lower difficulty levels, the later maps can be brutal without an experienced teammate or two, especially if you're going for higher ranks like Platinum and above.If what you've seen has peaked your interest at all, I implore you, buy it now. Buy it for a friend too, because the worst thing about this game right now is the lack of players, and it's a damn shame that a hidden gem like this is being overlooked. DCC has created something special here.

_childDocuments_.review: There is Early Access and then there is development hell Early Access.  Currently this could easily be released today and be 100% better than some other full games out there.  I would put this in the category with Deep Rock Galactic early access run.  The only thing it lacks is more of it. That being said this isn't barebones with ten levels, multiple enemies, and lots of unlockable cosmetics.Short Review: If it looks fun to you I would say get it.  I bought it on a whim (mainly due to the aesthetics) and I have been having fun.  If you like horde/tower defense gameplay as well as exploring huge rooms as an action figure then give it a shot.Gushing Long Review: All I can say, #1 is the art style is 1000% on point.  There is so much attention to detail everywhere!  All of the plastic looks like molded plastic.  I ran into a random garlic clove in the bedroom and I spent a minute just looking over the details.  So many games in the last few years have tried to do the nostalgia of old toys, but they never get the idea right.  Two examples that work so well here is when you spawn in, you burst out of your packaging.  Additional weaponry is even attached to these boxes.  The other example is players don't have player names, they have toy names, like Dr. Punch Man. Which is all selectable in the customization screen.It would be one thing to have a level full of cool details everywhere, but have no reason to look at it.  Some games (I'm thinking of For Honor right now) have loads of detail but all of the gameplay is hyper focused in a small area.  Hypercharge is different because each building round you need to get money that is littered around the room.  So each new round you will want to explore new shelves, around boxes, and in the rafters for all the money and unlockables.  More money means better defenses and more unlockables means more customization.Levels are large, but (as far as I have gotten) not hard to manage. Typically there is one defense point that is out in the open, another one that is slightly less visible, and one that is usually out of the way with less defenses. Most fights start with a focus on the main one, then bump up to the first two, and by the third round you are getting sneaky enemies attacking the third.  I have been playing solo and it's doable but the garage was the first mission I just gave up on one node to focus on the other two.  The game can be soloed but there are definitely advantages to having more players.I'm sort of blathering on at this point so here are my two major highlights so far.  In the second story level the game spawned in green army men.  Here is what I'm talking about with aesthetics.  The army men aren't green soldiers, they are army men with flat mountings on their feet, so to approach you they have to hop!  It's kind of horrifying in a way, even more so because these are the first enemies that have ranged attacks.  So the round starts and I hear a weird diesel engine sound.  Must be an ambient truck noise (I forgot to mention there is some good sound design too).  Then I see one of those classic green tanks that usually come with green army men.  This is followed by out of control green jeeps and finally a huge bomber flying overhead.  The floor is littered with still army men and the bomber is dropping parachute men.  It's chaos, but I'm having a blast.The other moment is just the simple joy that the action playset (with clearly defined "Battle Damage TM" window) is something you can actually use for cover.  Cons: MOAR everything!  The game is great, but more stuff would just make it better. My only other criticism is I think it would be cool if you could interact with the environment.  Like stepping on the keyboard changes the screen or if you step on that plate in the playset the "Battle Damage TM" window blows out.  Maybe things like that could be triggered to do damage to enemies or block paths.Can't wait to see what will be next for HYPERCHARGE: Unboxed!

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't put a ton of time into this game, but I can assure you it is worth way more than the 15$ you are going to spend. The update that it recently received could be considered a new game in itself with only the feel of the original lingering in the air.HyperCharge: Unboxed is best played with friends but is completely enjoyable just by yourself.it is an incredibly cool take on the original tower defense games, and while this genre has been done before. The dev team has out done themselves by making this game a unique experience for the player.The graphics are an amazing. first off, while they are pretty realistic you will still get this feeling that you’re just a plastic doll running around the map. a lot of the things you can jump on and identify throughout the map push that art choice. That allows you to get extremely immersed in the game; even before you start the tower defense aspect of it.The defense aspect of it isn't anything too new at least on the surface, each character before playing can select 3 cards to take with them to build with. each card is a defense which will impede or attack enemies before they reach the core. The main difference from other games is that you also get your own weapon which can have at least two different gun types attached to it. this setup allows for a lot of customization between players.this leads into the gameplay, which is an incredible mix of strategy and just plain fun when playing with your friends. For each level there are 3 different difficulties with 3 different medals for each that you can earn. Medals are achieved by how many objectives are left standing by the end. My only grip right now with the gameplay is that it needs a mode where the waves don’t end for each level. that would make playing levels over again more enjoyable.

In addition to the bugs, i feel like more guns and gun attachments would increase the variety and replayability the game has to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game right now, but it needs work. PROS- Nostalgic- Beautiful graphics- Fun gameplay- Lots of potential (maybe bigger maps?)- Amazingly designed maps (seriously, some of my favourite I've seen in a game)- Passionate DevsCONS- . SEE UPDATE- Some weapons feel unbalanced, particularly the sniper (doesn't do enough damage imo). - AI can be a little finicky and can get stuck. Also, AI which only shoot more accurately as difficulty increases and nothing else (such as smartness and strategy) are a little underwhelming. And if there is a increased AI smartness already implemented, I haven't noticed. I'm not saying AI are not fun, they are, but I think to give them bit of a "human element" to them would be awesome. When I play against AI I want to be able to strategize and coordinate, not find loopholes in their logic. Obviously that'd be a huge undertaking, but my points still stand. - Enemies are slightly hard to see, and makes playing sometimes a bit of a strain on the eyes.- Something to give the game some replayability. Nostalgia and beautiful graphics can only keep me in a game for so long. I don't have any ideas personally, and I trust the devs to think of something great, but I do feel something is missing here and hope to see some new game modes added. Overall, a great game I will continue playing but I hope some of the issues I addressed here are heard. Also thank you for porting this game to GNU/Linux/Steam Deck!UPDATE TO REVIEW:- The new lobby is great and much easier to host with a friend. Thanks! However, typing in a code all the time to switch a game mode is annoying!- After playing the game a bit more, the minigun recoil is terrible and hardly worth being used, ever. So I'd buff the minigun a little bit.- Some achievements are not working, even after the hotfix, namely the Unlockables and Collectable achievements.
