_childDocuments_.review: Big note: My playtime being 37 hours is from me randomly deciding to go back and get SOME stuff, and playing out of boredom. The real playtime, if you're just going once through is probably around 4-6 hours, if you can actually get through it with the bots or get graced with the right online party.Welp... Here we are at campaign's debut, which may as well be 1.0, and... Wow.-The menus have been overcomplicated and downgraded in a previous update (you have to back out from the singleplayer menu with a specific button now in order to get back to the choice screens, tabbing three or four times to go back to be able to choose Online instead of the previous 1-and-set-to-private, but you can also still exit the menu like normal with one button press, leaving you in the menu you wanted to get out of by pressing said button, too, so... was that change really necessary...?)-The maps shown in said menus will bug out and not show you the correct amounts of anything in that level, instead it'll show you the values for the PREVIOUS map you looked at.-Enabling Vsync crashes the game-Hidden collectibles do nothing but give certain awful one-color skins. Objectives also do nothing, unless it's the single one on Adventure Dunes that gets you some more build credits.-All cosmetics are still locked behind random requirements, and buildables are behind medal levels on certain maps. This includes name options, meaning you might have do do all levels on expert and nightmare, then have your hypercores never take any damage before you get the skin or name/adjectives or buildables you like... Except, if you're at that point, you're already about to leave the game anyway due to it being too hard or not playing with friends, so... Why?-The bobbleheads to get different voices/heads for characters are hidden in some really mean spots, I recommend looking up the guides to find them all, cause, no, you're not finding them all on your own. Some can only be shot from exactly 1 angle and it's just plain annoying to get them. Also look up the guide for getting pleb/max ammo, cause, yeah no, you probably didn't even realize they were unlockable til now.-The comics do almost nothing. It basically just shows Max Ammo going through the different areas with no continuity or explanation of what happens to introduced characters, or acknowledgement of the player. In fact, the ending takes the punch out of YOU defeating/exploding Major Evil by saying "oh no! Max Ammo did it, except Major Evil decided to jump off a ledge and a dog actually is just using him as a chewtoy now lol!!!" Basically, we're just stand-ins for Max Ammo the whole time, which would be better if everyone actually started with him, instead of him being unlockable as a super-secret... Oh, and the final bit to the narrator's dialogue is a sequel bait, but, I get the distinct feeling that nothing will come of it...-Bots STILL don't care about hypercores. They can literally all be at the same hypercore, have that hypercore be swarmed by 8 enemies, and they'll shoot something far away from it, so, good luck soloing. They also like to build stuff that doesn't do much of anything helpful.-Online lobbies are practically nonexistant, because everyone else already went through every map, did every difficulty they wanted to, and unlocked everything THEY COULD (remember the earlier point). Thus, you have to rely on the terrible bots to get through solo, or force your friends to go through it with you, or somehow get lucky on the browser, or brave the discord...-Certain enemies are still tanky, annoying, and just... Bad. T-rex, Major Evil, Demolisher, Mothership, Cargo Plane, Fighter Jet, Ninja Joes... All of those, for different reasons. Two practically instakill, all have too much health, and all of them except Cargo, Demo and Mothership speed around extremely fast (or in the case of Major, literally randomly teleport while firing homing explosives at you...), with Demo and Major having the unique ability to ignore all your defenses hp and destroy them in one hit (and you, if you get hit by their attacks, which is worse on the Demolishers because they can only be shot with lasers or in the back of the head with bullets... While they always either fire a fast instakill laser themselves, or continually stare at you.-Hypercores can have their batteries removed, and can have their shields bursted to hp damage quickly, invalidating most high-medal runs simply from "oops nobody could deal with those 9 enemies all at once lol". This is most seen on Airhockey Shuffle. Worst map next to Funderdome, fyi...The concept is still as nice as it was years ago, but, the end product just... There's no real freedom until after you're done with the game, and even then, you have to do the hardest stuff just to unlock some things you might actually like, so, you won't get what you might want, and you'll feel bad about it. The enemies, too, just... Ugh. Soloing this game sucks, and online is a die-roll. Even then, all the enemies and terrible bot AI are gonna just annoy you til you're done with the game. It's still completeable, yes, but, not very satisfyingly given the medals and what it takes to do so...

_childDocuments_.review: This one feels like a hidden gem on Steam. Fun cooperative (or competitive) game based around the realm of toys. Even as an adult this is one fun game, and add the fact its local split screen simply adds the cherry on top. In short, would recommend a purchase on sale (and especially if friends are picking up a copy).HYPERCHARGE: Unboxed (HU)'s  is straight forward and simple. The game allows the player to switch between first person and third person, with a double jump and ledge climbing ability that is integral to the game's mechanics. The movement is smooth and doesn't feel janky. In the defence type game mode player's are challenged to collect a variation of secrets (from gap jumps, finding collectables, and tagging) in addition to collecting coins. As the player collects coins they are allowed to build a preset defence around coloured "towers". Around the map the player can purchase or find weapon upgrades. Two weapons are allowed to be equipped at once (such as shotgun and rifle), but bigger weapons such as a rocket launcher or mini-gun take up both slots. Eliminating enemies also gives the player credit to use towards defence. The enemies themselves are varied, fun, and challenging. From BeyBlades, to toy robots, to drones, to toy planes and jets, to tanks, to jeeps, etc... Each enemy adds a new challenge, and the game throws mini-bosses and large bosses the player's way. The better the player performs in levels means more game unlocks. This is an underrated feature in games as most games require some sort of pay to play. It is rewarding to play and be able to unlock levels, skins, or characters. The  are spot on and absolutely immerse the player into the environment. Being a tiny toy in a giant room and navigating obstacles that a every day room would pose to such a small character is a fun universe to play in. The game does a good job notifying players of possible jumps, and the more familiar a player feels with the level - the more fun it is to jump from location to location. Animations are well done, especially when BeyBlades explode and when the toy robots get punched by the player causing a 360 spin. I also think majority of the level designs were extremely well done. The  are also suitable to the game's environment. Every little sound (from building to moving about the map) is included, and the music switches between some fun themes.Overall, would highly recommend a purchase on sale (and especially with friends). It's a fun simple game I feel anyone can get into - and even appropriate enough if you're playing with kids. One major down side to the game is the inability to throw grenades. Beyond that - well done Devs.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute blast to play and a awesome nostalgic trip to 80's and 90's toys, beautiful environments, and great gameplay. One feature that this game has that I think is amazing and that is lost from modern games is four-player split screen couch coop. Literally an amazing feature to play with your family or friends. The game itself has platforming aspects that are fun and enjoyable, and for a game with as much freedom as this one in the environments I expected to get a lot of clipping or stuck in weird places, this is not the case here, excellent design. The game is a four player shooter where you defend HyperCores from waves of evil toys, but can be played solo with surprisingly intelligent AI bots. There is the ability to place buildables and turrets, but these are more to complement the shooting than actual tower defense. There are collectables and unlockables in every map and toy solider skins and outfits which are a great progression goal. Also there is quite a bit of extra things to do stuffed in here, with a diorama sets, party games, and multiplayer, more than a lot of triple AAA games. The developers have shown to be absolutely invested into making this a great game and every update makes it even better. For problems with this game, the online seen is hard to find games, but I never had a problem with it as I normally play with bots or my friends locally. I feel like this game was made to be played with families or friends in the same room. Other issues are the occasional  bug, not game breaking but annoying. A good example is the Tank party game included which lets you play as tanks in a top down arena mode, it sadly does not have functioning controls when used with a gamepad controller, but really not a big deal as the party game itself was just a bonus. Overall, 10/10 for games, and with the gradual updates even better. I do wish there was some melee weapons, like a He-man sword or battleaxe, as many of the enemies can overwhelm or group up and I would love to just have a mace and smash those toys! Also more types of guns as well for even more types of shooting (There is a lot already, but I crave MOAR!). The gun modulation is great, attachments are fun and the game is packed full of humor and references (I noticed a certain M41A Pulse scope which was amazing). As you may already tell I love this game, and highly recommend it and hope to see even more from it.But remember!*THIS IS NOT A FLYING TOY* (Unless, of course, you have the Jetpack).

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the premise, but sadly the game feels less Tower Defense and more like a wave based shooter. Traps are extremely limited to a select few specific spots on the map and are extremely costly to build while feeling incredibly weak as well. To get money to build things, you need to run around the map between waves grabbing coins, and while I loved the idea of doing so, winds up leaving you very little time to actually build the traps since money isn't shared between players. Weapon types seem to be just upgrades you find or buy during a map, also scattered about. From what I saw, there was only a machine gun and shot gun variant, and of course each one needs to be recollected during the map.Overall, I really enjoyed the basic concept, but the execution I found very lacking. Was hoping for something closer to an actiony TD game like OMD, and instead got something closer to a wave based hold out game with heavy parkour elements. If you enjoy that sorta thing though, this would definitely be the game to play.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Awesome game for both newcomers and veterans to FPS games. Highly recommended!I got this game because my 7 year old son wanted to play a FPS and I wanted to find something that (1) wasn't gory, (2) wouldn't be too punishing for him, and (3) I could play with him. This game hits all the marks with the added bonus of being a total blast for me, too. My son gets a huge kick out of the fact that we're fighting toys; we have a bucket of the little green army guys so this game has more-or-less brought our play battles to life. The local multiplayer option is great, but I quickly decided to just get a second copy so we could both go full screen and KB+M.The game handles very well and the weapon upgrades and strategy behind placing buildables between waves gives a nice cadence to a round. My son is always psyched to unlock a new character skin and there are plenty of them to go after. The difficulty is such that on the lowest setting, the two of us can do quite well on pretty much any map. There is a good variety there, too, from a frenetic, close-quarters map on an air hockey table to an open kitchen with multiple attack lines.I can tell we'll be playing this for a long time. I have a lot of games in my Steam library but I've never bothered to write a review before -- but I wanted to give a shout out to this small development team. Thanks for making a great game for me and my son!

_childDocuments_.review: Initially my buddy bought this for me and to be honest, I wasn't completely sold at first just playing through the tutorial. The shooting feels nice, the jumping and in air control was pretty decent, and the soundtrack felt a little lackluster but still fit the theme so it never felt too out of place. Getting further into it recently with friends, I discovered this game has alot to offer. The maps are fun and masterfully made with an insane amount of set dressing that makes it an absolute joy to traverse. Gameplay doesn't feel sluggish and eve with bots you can chew through everything with some pretty decent success. The only thing I'm not a fan of is the vaulting system when holding space near a ledge. Sometimes it works perfectly, sometimes you drop back down and look up and ask...."Why me God?". Also the tower defense aspect is super fun especially unlocking new towers to experiment with.The characters are all designed perfectly, giving you a real sense of "Small Soldiers" when playing and to me that just scratches a nostalgic itch I never new I had. Also having a good sized roster of characters and unlockable characters to customize and play with is just icing on the cake. All in all, the maps are beautiful with a ton of unlocks and hidden secrets to find, the characters have some awesome customization to unlock through getting higher scores in maps and finding secrets, and the soundtrack fits really well even though it's nothing to write home about.If you're looking for a neat little game that hearkens back to the 90's, this game is a fun little romp to goof off with friends and I absolutely suggest getting this.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, do I have much time in this game? No, not yet but I'm on my way.Edit: This game jumped to the front of my mind since it's releasing on Xbox with cross-play to PC soon, and I'm loving it every bit as much as I did before.However, it takes no time at all to see all the tender love and care the developers have put into this game. There are details everywhere that will make you smile. The environments are colorful, vivid, and contain all the details you'd expect to find if you were walking around them in real life. The models of everything from the characters to the weapons to the enemies are so beautifully rendered. The animations are somehow lifelike even though they perfectly match how you'd expect the toys to move. I've seen other reviews mentioning this, but the game feels as though the developers behind the Toy Story 2 Action Game had the budget of a AAA release and the modeling/animation knowhow of modern AAA game devs.I don't have a single complaint I can think of to state against this game because I think it is beyond evident that this game is exactly the game it wants to be, and that is a simply fun game that inherits all the best qualities from the old arcade shooters a lot of people used to play on consoles like the Nintendo 64 and OG Xbox, and it expands upon all of them with the quality of life features you'd want from a game that came out in the past few years while also having gorgeous visuals.The gameplay itself is simplistic, but that's not a bad thing. It's masterfully executed:- the weapons all feel unique and impactful- the attachments make the difference you would expect- enemy types are numerous to the point you think you've seen them all but then realize there's more than you remember- enemy AI is unique between the types, and the AI works fluidly in tandem with the unique animations that fit the toy they appear asHonestly the enemy variety is one of my favorite things about this game. The difference in behavior keeps things fresh between every wave of every match, and this element of the game feels inspired by Doom Eternal, the only other game I can think of where I constantly forget about a specific enemy type and am then pleasantly surprised to be reminded of an enemy I forgot about.Don't be deceived. While the gameplay is and looks simple, it is SOLID, and extremely enjoyable.Do not go into this game expecting Deep Rock Galactic, Evolve, Rainbow Six Siege, or anything else that requires a ton of tactical thought. Go into this game expecting Halo: CE, Army Men: Sarge's Heroes, Toy Story 2: Action Game, and clearly identifiable love for this artistic medium.Should you buy this game? If you want something that's stupid fun and good to play with friends absolutely yes. If you like supporting dedicated artists, absolutely yes. I was initially drawn by the aesthetics in the trailers and gameplay I saw, and then I was floored by the aesthetics I saw when I played it, and then I was hooked by how much fun the game actually turned out to be. I guarantee you'll find something about this game that puts a stupid grin on your face.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve spent over 24 hours of my life playing this game and haven’t even owned it for 4 days. It takes me back to being a kid. Reminds me of Hot Wheels Stunt Track Driver. You’re a toy in a huge house, a kid with a huge imagination. Nostalgia spills from every bit in this game. And not only the feeling of being thrown back to a kid playing with toys in their bedroom, but the gameplay, the PvE and PvP are fun as hell and addicting. Either waves of bad toys trying to destroy nodes you must protect or running into a launch pad and jumping 20 feet in the air as you shoot a grenade at an enemy underneath you as their character explodes into different pieces everywhere. The gameplay sticks, feels like quake but as a toy. Zero micro transactions- the 5 man dev team wanted their game like the old school games. You want something you grind your butt off for it and let me tell you. It’s rewarding as hell. So many secrets hidden all over various maps you have to go back and look for a badass skin or head to show off in game. The soundtrack is a mix of everything. Reminds me of retrowave sometimes and rock at others. It’s all over the place but in a good way with the song suiting what going on. I love it and honestly debating about spending 10 bucks just for the soundtrack alone. Normally I turn the music off in any shooter or grinding game I play to play my own, but this game has me clicking pause on spotify and turning music volume in game all the way up. Some tracks even giving chills at times gripping you in the moment as you shooting down multiple toy planes defending your precious node. This game is a breath of fresh air to me in a era of dying good games riddled with micro transactions and the company’s goal being more for money than the community. This is not the case with hypercharge. I highly recommend this game. Grab a friend, play alone, or play online with randoms cause this game has an amazing community. Join the discord too. This game already has so much to offer in it’s current state and has so much more to offer in the coming future updates. Give it a chance. Whether you’re returning to your childhood memories or want a cool fun co-op/ pvp game to play and chill with. This game is perfect for just that. And at 20 dollars that’s nothing to scoff at. It’s worth so so soooo much more than 20 dollars in my opinion. I played it off my friend’s library and not long after a couple of hours in total I had to own it. Buy it. You won’t regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: This was my first "tower-defense" type game, and I'm very glad I started with this. I don't think I would normally be in to this genre, but the design is so tight here it is very enjoyable. This is absolutely dripping with late 80's-90's nostalgia, but not in a lazy, cash-grabby way. It is clear the devs put a lot of love and energy into it's design and have a deep respect for the toys they've represented. This is the perfect manifestation of what we were imagining as kids playing with action figures and it just feels SO DAMNED GOOD to play it out here. There are so many tiny details that no one would have blamed them for not including, but stumbling onto them after your 10th match on a level is so satisfying. And don't let the toy theme fool you - this is not an easy game. Normal difficulty can still throw you some curve balls, and you might breeze through the first and second rounds, and by the last you're just happy you made it out alive. One issue I have is the limited customization options you start out with. Granted they are all unlockable - and you don't have to pay for them - but many of the smaller unlockables are stuck behind very difficult challenges, like perfect scoring some of the levels, which is not easy. I'm happy with this system, I just wish there was a bit more open in the beginning, and perhaps challenges that were a bit more forgiving (read: I need to get good).Overall, this is a small but tight game, made by a small but passionate dev team. There is seemingly endless fun to be had here, and bonus points for local split-screen! 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Hoo boy, got a lot to say about this one! First off, and this is something I truly feel the developers put their main focus on: Attention to detail. There is SO much detail to every little thing you can see in this game. From the single color plastic fortifications, the little missiles you see in missile launching toys (I actually had one of those growing up and its clear these guys did too) from the way the army men move to the way the toys fall apart into glorious messes that poor mom probably has to clean up. You can read those little blurbs they put on the backs of action figure packages that explain the lore and world behind them, and every match starts with you breaking out of your packaging! I could go on, but suffice to say they really nailed the toy acstetic. Its incredible. Now onto the gameplay itself: Its main mode is tower defence, where you have multiple (Some maps just one) Hypercore to defend from waves of enemies. Even the smallest map is huge for a toy, so there is a lot of verticallitity in how you jump, climb and avoid enemy fire. You'll need to jump and climb all over the maps too, since your currency is scattered all over the map as collectables. In between waves thats your cue to get as many collectables, repair, construct defences and upgrade your weaponry. Every map has hidden collectables and hard to find bobbleheads which unlock new customatization parts for your action figure. Every hypercore has a shield and health, and its shield will only recharge if it is powered by a battery, a pickup that can spawn between waves. The battery is essential not only for keeping your hypercores protected, but also powering automated defences like turrets. Plus, to get the highest reward grade post match, all power cores need to have not taken any health damage, which is easier said then done! Teamwork is key in this game, but don't worry, singleplayer lets you play with bots and does not lock you out of any unlockables. I myself managed to do Garden of Evil: The longest biggest map by myself with just one bot (But only after many failed attempts and nailing what defences to pick and where to pick them, plus learning the optimum routes to traverse the map and getting as many credits as I could between rounds.) Last note on this mode, its recommended to clear all maps on regular or casual with Platinum before moving onto expert mode, as getting platinum unlocks the battery charger on a map (where applicable, some maps do not have it) which allows you to recharge your precious batteries and keep them around. The second mode is free roam, which allows you to run jump and climb the maps to your hearts content, and also lets you find each level's secret collectables and bobble heads without any timed pressure. I wish I could speak for the pvp modes, but I'm not huge into pvp so I cannot speak for them sadly. I'll leave you with a tip that will hopefully help: Bots can be very helpful for not making you have to do everything yourself, but remember the more bots you have, the more enemies spawn! Good luck Soldier!

_childDocuments_.review: Great Fun little Arcade Game.... Only Really 3 Modes you can play. 2 Pvp Modes and 1 PVE A Great idea of a game bringing Retro Toys back to life with this game, sadly still feels like a work in progress to me. I feel this game could really kick off if some more work was put into it and expanded a bit with more game modes and fine tuning. Customization options are really amazing especially the Glow in the Dark features on some of the skins. Imagine if they put in Actual Licensed Retro Toys in the game (Masters of the Universe, Toy Story, GI Joe, classic Toys) but then again would it be weird if they were shooting toy guns?A Downside i feel is the Name Customization where you pick out a generated name tag for your character which i think is in place to Disguise the bots that most likely always in your match because of the lack of players ( i even played on the weekend)-Plague Mode - which is a variant of a "Infected" game mode which has you scoring points by standing in a zone to capture points and avoiding infected players (you can only score points by being on the zone, most players don't know that). Downside to this mode is if you are not infected you'll be always marked on the HUD with a Red skull so the infected know where you are regardless if you find a great hiding spot or not.-Deathmatch - PVP Free-for-all Game Mode , score points by killing other players where you can pick up weapons off the ground and attatchments.-Waves - PVE Defend zones and collect coins or kill enemies to buy buildables to place around the zone to defend from waves or hordes of enemies which vary from game to game. Not 1 wave is the same from match to match, or game to game. You can buy weapons, attachments around the map with the points you have collected. Survive and keep you base in tip top shape and you will be awarded with a Shiny medal at the end based on your performance. Some levels have hidden collectibles you can grab if you can find them during the match.I Recommend this game if you're the kind of player who likes to try a new game or looking for a new Co-operative game to play with your friends, I also think the game is kid friendly.

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing yet small game, Hypercharge: Unboxed gives massive nostalgia for anybody whom fondly remembers the Army Men series or the Small Soldiers movie of the 90's. Playing as your own customizable action figure and battling classic toys of yesteryear's youth, you will scale entire rooms, vault through gardens, and reach the heights of a massive garage in an attempt to find coins, unlock more weapons, and upgrade defenses in order to protect a series of objective 'hypercores'. There's only four things I can imagine that would make this game even better; an open-world level combining the garden and all rooms of the house into one level, toy combat vehicles to help you move around quicker and battle enemies, an in-depth RPG-like skillpoint system to upgrade your weapon profiency, and finally heavy buildables based around real-sized human technology, like desk fans to chop enemies or hair-dryers to melt them or mannable golf-ball shooting turrets (Basically really creative ways small toys would use human-made objects to destroy enemies.)I personally love this game, but for now it's so small and has limited re-playability. I'm eagerly keeping up on the news the Devs are dishing out, and looking forward to the new survival mode they have planned. If they keep up their hard work, Hypercharge is a game that should be mandatory in any game-lovers library!

_childDocuments_.review: I Buy things on purchase, I Dont watch reviews and ponder my decision because I want to see what the game is like for myself, And im Truly surprised, The game has been fun to play with in CO-OP that is typically what i normally play these daysBut the Deathmatch mode gave me feelings of DM17 from back in the Quake 3 days using the jump pads to traverse and get pickups, Movement is probably more like a blend between Quake and UT but if you played the Toyroom mods for either game this is basically a game dedicated to that sort of gamestyle, The movement system is on point even though some people might want it to be faster, It works well either way.Dont be put off that yes, the game has toys and actionfigues if you wanted a different style, Everything is crafted in such a nice way, Like reading the labels on the back of a liquor bottle that is behind the recycling bin The Devs probably know that you have other things to do and dont have loads of free time these days, so the game modes dont waste your time doing pointless things its quick to have a few games and go and do other stuff, and then you probably want to hop back on when you can anyway, No messing about just easy to jump in and play.Obviously the graphics are amazing with the amount of detail that is put into the game, The text not only makes the place feel alive and believable but you are gonna read that text, because the fine detail in the game is amazing, And also the fact that you can use battery chargers for the batteries that power your defences in CO-OP.The CO-OP itself is great with just enough things to place to defend your cores without getting overwhelmed, you need to keep playing to progress, but i mean just finish matches and you are rewarded, no bull, just do stuff and you get new skins and stuff when you keep playing, and you will want to keep playing its just so enjoyable followed by fantastic weapon sound effects that means these are proper high quality action figures with FLAC weapon sounds.the game is never too relaxing on the casual difficulty setting, its just right for everyone that they actually need to at least put some effort into shooting things, and thats key, as long as you can point and shoot and at least like shooters in that regard then you will be fine and will have a fun time.So there is a small playerbase, on this game, you can wait and play with bots online if you want but i dont think it will be that hard to get a match for most as there is an active discord and you only need 3 others for co-op, When the game is on sale it will be populated for a while but how many will stay i cant tell, a couple will most likely sure, but provided this keeps getting regular updates every now and then and a sale to help, i can see this being popular even if it has a couple of hundred regulars online, It has the potential to be MASSIVE IMO but that will probably affect the general direction of the game if i were a developer, Im pretty sure the Devs know what they can and cant do with the game and they do treat it like its their baby, So show them some respect even if the game isnt for you, Its so easy to visually see all the love and effort they have put into this game.After the recent sale i purchased the Complete edition to support the devs, But also the fact that this is giving me a lot of value for my money and i support any developer that does that.PS Im not good with TL:DR's and thanks for those who read my feelings on the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great little Team Shooter in which you basically have couple of minutes to build defences around your 3 Power Nodes and once the timer runs out you have to defend them against waves of enemies. The fact you are an action figure fighting against various types of other toys is AWESOME! e.g.  Army Men, Spinners, Robots to name a few.  Visually this game is stunning and the gameplay is smooth and hectic.  The levels are really well laid out as well with Nooks and Crannies to find coins and other hidden unlockables.  I highly recommend this game and it's best with other players although you can play with bots.   Jump in, have fun and re-live your action figure days :)

_childDocuments_.review: In a time long forgotten, there existed an ancient line of action figures imbued with sentience and bound by a sacred purpose: preserving the joy of childhood. These figures, known as the Guardians of Imagination, foresaw a day when humanity's connection to its most precious memories—those of favorite toys and the adventures shared with them—would fade. To prevent this tragedy, they created a magical artifact known as the Hypercore.The Hypercore was no ordinary object. Forged from the purest fragments of nostalgia and wonder, it became a living reservoir of childhood memories. Every child’s laughter, every whispered secret, every epic battle reenacted in bedrooms and backyards was absorbed into its glowing core. It became a source of unending power, ensuring that the bond between humans and their cherished toys could never be broken.But peace would not last. A dark figure arose: Major Evil, a tyrannical force born from forgotten and discarded toys who had grown bitter in their neglect. Fueled by resentment, Major Evil vowed to obliterate the Hypercore, erasing the memories stored within it forever. Without those memories, humanity would lose its connection to the joy and creativity that toys inspire, and the Guardians of Imagination would be reduced to lifeless relics.Now, the fate of the Hypercore—and all the cherished memories it holds—rests in your hands. Major Evil’s armies of corrupted playthings march ever closer, seeking to extinguish the light of the Hypercore. Will you stand with the Guardians of Imagination, wielding the spirit of play and creativity as your weapon?Defend the Hypercore with everything you’ve got, or see the treasures of our past turn to dust. The battle for nostalgia begins now.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good CO-OP tower defense game with interesting FPS elements, this game is also good looking and has great attention to detail in its level design. Some buildables are over-powered while others are under-powered, however, that is to be expected of an early access game.But I would like to bring attention to some serious game/connectivity issues me and a friend have been having online, for example, the game enemies sometimes go very fast and instantly attack the cores within a few seconds and a game over occurs, or they go so slow that it makes an Expert difficulty match extremely easy to complete with a Diamond award.Other game/connectivity issues include randomly not being able to jump, jump pads not being interactive and randomly disconnecting from the server.Another issue is that the Beyblade style enemies are very powerful and hard to stop. When all goes well on a cohesive Expert playthrough of a map, these Beyblade enemies spawn and instantly melt your core's shields and damages health without giving you much of a chance to react. The main problem is that they can glitch through buildable walls and drop from vents directly on top of a core, instantly damaging them before you could even destroy them. They spawn in too many numbers and they are the only enemy in this game that feels truly unfair. Another problem is the dropship, their turrets like to shoot down one particular core, melting their shield down in no time preventing you from getting a Diamond award. This is a problem because you and your friends cannot kill one fast enough before they do that. However the dropships only tend to be a problem on the garden map with the red core.On the plus side though, this game is very fun and completely unique. There is not another game of this kind. If you like rats style maps on CSS/CSGO or TF2 or you have played one of those old Tower Defense flash games, then do yourself a favour and play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Did you ever watch Toy Story or Small Soldiers as a kid and think 'man I wish they made a videogame about that but with guns and explosions?' well then Hypercharge is the game for you!Lots of love and detail has clearly been put into this game and it shows in the character of the maps, flavor text and toy designs. Very well optimized, easy to set up a game and play with friends. Lot of cool cosmetics and collectibles to explore and unlock. Love the ability to swap between first and 3rd person mode seamlessly.The generousness of the jumping, double jumping, vaulting and ledge grabbing means you can parkour to some insane and unthinkable places(wink wink).Most of the classic 90s shooter weapon archetypes are represented here. In an amusing twist that I quite like, have for the most part realistic firing sounds but they all launch little plastic bb pellets that, when you reload fall on the floor.Speaking of weapon sounds, the sound design is very good. You can tell special care was taken on weapons. They all sound satisfying to fire and the explosions sound deep and bassy without being too loud. It's a good thing in the normal CoOp modes ammo is unlimited because you'll want to mag-dump just to feel like toy Rambo.The actual original sound track for the game is also pretty good.The building system has a bunch of fun traps, sentries and, I don't know how best to describe them but Crowd control? oriented structures to unlock and experiment with.Has that very 90s early 2000s Saturday morning toy commercial vibe nailed down. A few suggestions I would give for the devs is. 1. Custom maps. You guys have clearly put a lot of effort and love into crafting all the assets in this game, If would be great if you could somehow look into making a in-game custom map making mode where the community could take all those assets and remix and rearrange them to make infinite new maps to play on like one big toy box. These maps don't necessarily need to support all the specially placed collectibles and achievement based cosmetic progression you have baked into the developer made ones, but It would be super cool if we had the tools to make map setups for any room scenario we could imagine.2. A slightly more robust ping system for working with the player bots when playing solo or in a not full multiplayer lobby. Being able see the bots build cards and request they put specific structures on specific build nodes would greatly enhance the experience when playing with them.3. Add are few more weapon types namely a 2 slot Quake/TeamFortress style rocket launcher, kinda slow projectile but with good AOE damage, some sort of auto or semi-auto bolt gun/crossbow than can impale/collateral multiple enemies or pin them to walls, and finally a full sword of some kind for either a full melee or hybrid build would be super cool.My personal wishlist aside, at the end of the day Hypercharge is a very fun, nostalgic coop or pvp toy shooter and it definitely has my recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: All the down-votes are just wrong.Let me explain. This is a $20 game. There is no grift here. Stop judging a labor of love against COD. Not every game needs to give you 100+ hours of investment. Its fun and polished. Combining a platforming exploration with a firefight wave game. The multiplayer works just fine. Never once had an issue. I play with my 5 year old and we have a blast. I play with my older boys and we have fun turning up the difficulty but the 5 year old can still play. And you can add bots to your team to help if you are playing with a 5 year old. If you can't admit that there might be a place for a $20 party game where the replay value is "that was fun with you" and "find everything" and "now try it on harder," then I'm sorry this isn't for you. Go play God of War or Counterstrike and go curb stop the plebs. But if you and your friends or kids or GF want to have fun protecting a toy from the bad guys like, parachuting green army men that come up to your knees and just tip over when you snipe them from overwatch position on the toilet in the bathroom map, then try it out. Its fun. Its loved by the devs. There is NONE of the toxic mechanics invading games. And its better with friends but not heroin. We need more games made in the spirit of the Mario Party version of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely amazing game with a ton of content and great atmosphere brought to life by the  beautiful and cute visual design!In no way did this game leave me with a feeling of "early access" because of how lush and rich in content it feels. Still though, if the devs plan on releasing more quality content like this in the future, I would definitely not refuse!Ever wanted to play a first person, horde-mode (or pvp) shooter with platforming elements, but set in a universe reminicent to Toy Story or Small Soldiers (god I feel old now)? Well, this game has you covered!From the funny references to the cleanly flowing gameplay to the deliciously dripping toy theme, this game delivers in many more ways than I anticipated and I personally cant wait what the devs might add in the future. I do have 2 little pieces of constructive critisism though if the devs are interested. 1. I think the game is doing itself a disservice with the game's title. Even though I like the idea of there beijg a toyline called "Hypercharge", I don't really think it reaches out to the (right) target audience. I, for one, have been looking for a game like this for a long time, but found this one merely by accident and excessively digging through steam's library of games. I guess "Hypercharge" isn't really a tag that pops quickly on people's radar. 2. I love playing the game and enjoy unlocking the plentiful amount of cosmetic content, but I do think the game is a bit overly restrictive on the "unlockables" department. You dont really start out with any options to customize your character and I think that could potentially scare way players who just want to jump in and immediately have a fun casual time with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: I never review games, like, ever, I play them, and then I talk to them with my friends, but I never feel like my review would be worth it in the sea of other reviews. I have also never really heard of this game before purchasing it. I had the spare cash, I liked the visuals and the trailer, I figured this might be another one of those games I'd play for two hours and then never play again. Boy, was I wrong. This game feels like they took a beloved PS2-era game and slapped modern graphics to it. Other than the "supporter pack" DLC, there is no form of microtransaction in this game, and yet, LOADS of unlockables, all unlocked through normal playthrough in various different ways. The devs have hidden SO many small, funny, cheeky details and references in this game, it just shows this game is a labour of love.On to gameplay, it kind of feels to me like CoD Zombies meets tower defence, you have 3 or 4 nodes to defend through several waves of enemies, each with different ways of attacking you. Speaking of enemies, I expected something similar to CoD Zombies, where there are maybe 2-3 types of enemies, all with similar functions, but nah, there are about a dozen types of enemies in this game, with varying degrees of annoyance and danger, along with a couple "minibosses". Every stage has several difficulties to play it in, and trust me, you don't want to start playing the maps on expert right away, you're going to get your ass kicked. This game relies on the cooperation of every teammate, and it has honestly given me some of the best gaming nights with my buddies.Only downside I can find right now, is that it's almost impossible to get a diamond rank while playing solo in some of the maps, but this game is enjoyed the most with friends anyways. If you do end up getting the game, check out their discord, it's full of helpful people, and it seems like a generally nice place.Oh, and about the DLC, as of right now, there is only one DLC, the "supporter pack" DLC, which gives you more skins and an additional character. It's very much not needed, but it's worth it for the fact that you're giving more money to the devs, who truly deserve it.So yes, I wholeheartedly recommend this game, you get a LOT of content for the small amount they ask for the game.Honestly

_childDocuments_.review: Holy hell is this game fun! It isn't insanely difficult nor is it stupidly easy. Boss waves are plenty difficult, and so far only the air hockey stage is really the only one I'd say is too easy (but hey, its a gimmick stage so who really cares). There aren't many people online, though that's something that I can't complain about too much since the game is pretty niche. The graphics are actually significantly better than what I expected from a low price title. The stages also have ridiculous detail, going so far as to stock the shelves and containers with objects that look like they could be found in real life toy stores. Ever since I saw the first post about this game on imgur, its always been in the back of my mind. It seemed fun and interesting. Though I haven't used it yet, couch co-op is always, ALWAYS, a welcome addition to any game. Glad the devs implemented it.I only have a few complaints that I really hope get fixed, though they don't change my mind on whether or not to recommend this game.Weapon types are like, really rare. Of all my gameplay I think I only got a secondary weapon twice, and I've only repeated one level.Lack of content. There are plenty of maps under development at the map selection screen, so this will for sure be fixed very soon. PvP would also be a neat addition, just remove the hypercores and let players shoot each other.Vehicles are ridiculously bulky. It takes so long to wear down a tank or a jeep, even when they stand absolutely still. I'm fine with boss vehicles like the plane being stupidly bulky, but regular ones shouldn't take multiple full clips to take down.This game is still extremely fun and well worth the $15. My only regret with this purchase is waiting so long to get it. I saw the first couple posts about it on imgur back whenever that was, but I didn't bite for whatever reason until recently. I'm glad I did. Now I just have to convince my friends to buy it....

_childDocuments_.review: Updated Review:Came back to the game after a recent update. Congratulations on the full launch of the game Joe, and other members of the Dev team. It's fairly smooth, with a bit of jank I expect to be ironed out in future via more updates.Some of the problems I had with the game have been alleviated somewhat, although i'm still not entirely onboard with the unlock system, especially so since I still feel base models (Eg, Dinosaur, Bug, etc - should be there from go, like the original early access. But, oh well.)Easy is easy, and hard can be nightmarish if you aren't running around grabbing batteries for turrets or switching between modes on your weapon to maximize dps. The moment your DPS slows down, is the moment you lose.Tweaks i'd like to see - Increased movement speed, the jump pads help somewhat - but when you're in a hurry with a brain fart, all you want to do is run.- Better indicators for what is being attacked, it's okay where it is now, but could definitely be aided with color coding text, or a minimap with flashing. - Less RNG - Longer battery life- Rocket Jeep, why- I haven't looked into it, but an easier to use block feature would be very appreciated. Had a match the other day with someone repeatedly spamming sorry, while knocking me and other players off tabletops in the kitchen level (I think it was a kitchen?) with melee. Got frustrating, very quickly. I'll maybe update this review as I play, but for now I feel this is a good place to leave it. The game is enjoyable. Lots of content, a range of cosmetics for characters and weapons, nice weapon variety complimented with the weapon swapping, and modes for all types of players such as PvE/Co-Op and Multiplayer Deathmatch, or the Zombie mode (Which I haven't tried yet, since I auto disconnect before the match loads, or I load into an empty match despite selecting a map sitting at 6/8 people.)Old Review:I enjoyed this game quite a bit when it first released, not so much now. "Why?" the reasons I bought the game are now locked behind requirements that are near impossible to achieve as a Solo player. "Just get someone to help", I just did and we got ranked LOWER than when I was doing matches Solo. Both of us were doing well, but got overwhelmed at the last level. Too many enemies, not enough time to reload while they swarm over the protect items. As a primarily Solo player, I cannot recommend this game.For any of the devs reading this, your requirements for base cosmetics and maps is far too high.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun co-op horde shooter. It does have PvP modes, but my friends and I have yet to play those. All of my experience is either single-player or co-op. It's got a good campaign with varied level/enemy design. The core loop is you and three buddies hold off waves of enemy toys advancing to destroy your little battery-powered brains in jars around the map, while trying to find cash and loot along the way. Typically you have 3 OBJs you have to defend and a sizable map with plenty of secrets to help you stand up to the tyrannical toys attacking you. Guns include things like lasers, miniguns, shotguns, grenade launchers, and probably more I don't remember. You can also buy attachments during the level to upgrade stats on your guns. Levels include things like bedrooms, bathrooms, backyards, kitchens, etc. and it makes for a good variety of different environments to fight in with notably more verticality than I expected when going in. All of your progress contributes to your customization options for your character. Maybe my favorite part of the game is to engage with is making my little action figure and assembling an absurd name from unlocked keywords. My friends and I have tons of fun making silly characters between levels, diving in to unlock more options, and doing it all over again. It gives me a feeling of nostalgia similar to walking down the toy isle as a kid and looking at all the various things on the wall my parents would never get me. Action figures were always pretty cheap though, so I got to take one home with me now and again. For 25$ I think you could do a lot worse. If you lack friends to play it with it might be worth considering a sale first. I think the game has a nice and friendly community though it is small. LFG will probably get you better results than matchmaking, but it requires actually interacting with people you don't know. Scary right? Anyways, good game. I do give it the Steam thumbs up.

_childDocuments_.review: A Nostalgic mood game, based in your childhood home, with a well designed wave-based tower-defense mode that stays fun for hours. An abundance of character customization options that caters to the collector type, unlocked through gameplay, not bs.I consider a games worth, by how many hours I spend enjoying it versus how much I spent. I’m still avidly enjoying, it still is a favorite in my friend group, and the game says I’m 70% through it (all game difficulties, unlocks, etc). I spent $20, well worth it. Or try the free demo. It’s what convinced me!The Waves ModeThere are several game modes to play, but my favorite is the Waves mode. I’ve seen ppl complain that it’s confusing. The tutorial they provide is done in 10 mins, and more than explains all the basics you need to know.Essentially, you defend towers from waves of enemies. In-between waves, you have limited time, to collect weapon upgrades, and credits to spend on defenses. This is the best part. Strategizing your defenses with your friends, unlocking new turrets and traps, failing miserably and then returning with more wisdom to crush the next time. Character CustomizationYou start with several base characters, but as you play you unlock more characters, and a host of different skin options for each of them. The customization menu is so fun to use, and keeps me entertained even when I’m just looking at stuff lol. Because the theme is action figures from your childhood, there’s a satisfying feeling to the fantasy of it all.Level DesignTruly inspired designs to each of their levels. Each level could be somewhere from your home. You can tell that the devs are speaking from their heart when they made each one. Complete with boss levels, special defense modes, and free roam options to give you time to really enjoy it all. For the $20 price tag, they provided a solid base of content to enjoy, with honestly satisfying replayability. Edit: As of April 2023, it seems that the devs are close to finished with the updates on this game. There may be a few more, but most their content seems to be out. This game is a steal. And what's more, most all my gripes with the game have been fixed and/or improved. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: I came across this game years ago when it first came out. I was looking for a couch coop fps game and this pretty much ticks all the boxes. But I'm glad they never gave up and have made an amazing game. It has come a long way and all the changes and additions made were all for the better. They deserve recognition and I hope they receive multiple awards for this labour of love, and continue to produce more games.Onto the game itself. In essence it is a tower defence game meets wave shooter set in a world where you play as action figures fighting against weaponised toys. If you have ever watched films like "Toy story", "Small Soldiers" or played with certain toys at one point in your life, this game will bring you so much nostalgia. _childDocuments_.review: Probably among the best purchases you could make on this platform. Hypercharge is a fun parody of 80s and 90s toys while also drawing a lot of inspiration from films like Toy Story and Small Soldiers. However, even more than that what it sets out to do it does perfectly. Pros:-The art design is absolutely flawless. Not only does it perfectly replicate the genuine look and design of a toy from the 80s and 90s, the figure designs look like real toys I would have played with as a kid. There is not a single enemy type, player skin, or environmental detail that does not ring a bell with me, I mean even the grenade launcher is a spring loaded missile. Despite none of these toys actually existing there is an amazing amount of thought and detail put into them that makes them feel like toys that would actually be produced.-Sound design is equally good with weapons packing a very satisfying punch despite being BBs.-Weapon variety is wide and very entertaining to swap between different gun combos. Some weapons are admittedly harder to find than others, like the laser or railgun, but when you do manage to get the fun weapons they do not disappoint. It all comes back to that satisfying sound design giving the weapons life and the balancing that makes them feel nice and chunky. You can also add other attachments to your gun such as scopes, stocks, and underslung equipment like a flashlight or stand (the stand is merely cosmetic though, and doesn't setup)-I didn't think much of the music at first, but when I actually paused to take a listen there are some really good tracks in the game's OST. The ones that stood out to me the most were Highway to Heaven, Arcade of Death, and Electrify This just being three that come off the top of my head that could not possibly fit any better in this game. Lots of synthesizers, electric guitars, and every once in a while you'll get more ambient tracks in between all the chaos. This is one of the few games where I'd say picking up the soundtrack is well worth it.-Secrets are sprinkled throughout all of the maps and I could not be any happier with this. They are both challenging to collect without being unfair, and they bring back the novel idea of actually playing the game to unlock cool cosmetics instead of paying for 15 or so DLCs on the storepage. Having to earn those cosmetics provides a true sense of accomplishment for mastering the game's parkour and map layouts, and that accomplishment can then be shown to other players in multiplayer. Really brings back those old memories in Halo 3's multiplayer.-The game pulls no punches, which is why you really need to learn the maps you're playing on and find as many tokens as quickly as possible. The game is challenging, and will get intense, but it never feels unfair or cheap.Cons:-Might be a little entitled, but I don't feel there are still enough unlocks for each figure. Some have less than others, like the space marine or warrior chick. That can be improved through content updates, but that depends entirely on the developers.-The parkour is fine once you get used to it, but it's really jarring figuring out what you can climb on and what you can't. The collision can also be weird so you might think you landed a jump but you bounce off the terrain instead.-Bots can be worse than real players when playing offline. They often wait around the slot machine to take your items, so that jet pack you were throwing precious tokens away for gets snatched up by the bot waiting right behind you. It's incredibly frustrating.-Once again, more more more. I don't feel there are enough maps even with the updates to this game. There are certainly plenty to play on so it's not like you will be bored in the first 4 hours, but variety is never a terrible thing. Maps like a literal sandbox, or a dollhouse, or even kid rooms in different nations would be fun, like in a Japanese kid's room full of Kaiju. There are so many creative ways to play with this concept and I hope the devs run wild with it.Aside from those cons, you can't go wrong buying this game. If you enjoyed tower defense games when those were hitting it big in the mid 2010s, or like wave based shooters the game is for you. It also features other game modes like PVP, but those aren't as heavily populated. If you insist on playing PVP then definitely join the Discord.With all of that said, 10/10, $10 bucks well spent.

_childDocuments_.review: Tl;DR: HyperCharge: Unboxed is a decent Rat-Map Shooter with a lot of potential in it's ball joints.My friends and I picked this game up a few days ago, and have managed to do all the maps on Regular difficulty, getting Gold or better ranking on all of them. All and all it's a solid, if a bit flawed experience I'd still recommend. The premise is simple; You're a bunch of custom made action figures brought to life Toy Story-style (even a few references to that in game) and tasked with defending several Brain-in-a-jar Hypercores from varying waves of enemies, using a few Tower Defense-Style turrets, traps, and walls.I hasten to say this isn't a Tower Defense game.The idea of a Rat-map always makes for interesting environments to jump and shoot in. Instead of a standard gray military base or an open field, you instead jump around a messy kitchen or a room of a kid who couldn't be bothered to tidy up before he went out. this concept provides colorful and varied maps to explore and fight in.This game is far from perfect, and my friends and I have a handful of things we'd like to see changed. I'm going to note them here, since DCC seems to pay attention to Steam Reviews as well.1: Reloads. A good shooter can be made into a great shooter based simply on how the guns feel to use. Now, I'm not expecting toy guns to feel as powerful as a hand-cannon or anything... But when your reload is simply lowering a gun off screen and bringing it back up again, it doesn't make for satisfying gunplay. We do like that if you start a reload and then swap weapons, reload won't stop. it keeps the pace up and allows for little downtime in a situation where downtime can prove fatal. What I'll suggest instead is maybe giving the player two different moddable guns with Proper reloads. We're already suspending our disbelief over toys going to war, so keeping the reload when holstered mechanic is still fine with two guns.2: Power Consumption: I get the in game joke of the "Ultra-Volt" brand batteries not having nearly enough power to be remotely useful in-world. The problem we've come across, however, is that the turrets, which use the battery's energy to fire, simply cost too much power to be useful. I'd like to see the capacity of the batteries upgraded, or the power costs of the turrets reduced. I'll also voice here my concerns about the Battery Recharger. If you limit access to this station by making sure the player(s) have to have first beaten a map with a Platnium medal (Perfect victory, no health damage to any of the Hypercores), why prevent a player wanting to go back and just have fun with the map from using it on the difficulty they've earned it? Why limit it's use to Expert or Nightmare only? (Edited note: Apparently it is on some maps' Normal and Easy difficulties, just not all of them. It's not on Dawn of the Toy's Normal, for example.)3: The Air Hockey Map: This one's a fun one. Now, A map with no turrets, traps, or map specific defenses is not a bad idea. It challenges the players on their skills with the guns and their own wits. The problem is the choice in enemy type. Beyblades (called Spinners in game) dive at the core relentlessly, and can shove players off the map into the kill zone below. Doing this map perfectly on Expert (Diamond Medal) is the only way to get the upgraded anti-infantry turret, and can seem honestly impossible for any less than 4 players in perfect sync. maybe even with that. I'd like to see the Spinner count cut down by a lot, and add a few more basic melee enemies, like Meanbots, to give some diversity as well as make it more possible for people to win perfectly, if you insist on putting something like a Turret behind that achievement.4: Customization: As I said, the action figures you play as are custom made. This means you can make your own Action figure, name them, and have something that's you. I'd like to see this expanded upon. Being able to swap parts from different types around would be interesting. For example, what I'd personally make is a Knight with a Dino's head, and a Cyborg arm from the Cyber Fury type. Clothing would also be nice, one of my friends would love to have his Dino with Solider style vests, straps and cargo pants over the dinosaur legs.As I said, this is a decent game that has promise. We're likely to keep playing this for weeks to come. More, if the Devs keep updating the game. Maybe give some mod support too. Either way, I hope you all can enjoy this game the way we have.

This game to me feels like a love letter to the time when gaming was a passion and people wanted to get their ideas out to the world instead of catering to whatever fad is currently out. Games are a form of entertainment for people to escape and unwind from the stresses of their lives, and I for one thoroughly enjoy what this game has to offer. This is a fun game to sink plenty of hours into, and I look forward to what it holds in the future. Thanks for the amazing game so far, Digital Cybercherries~!

_childDocuments_.review: I would never refer to myself as someone who enjoys shooter games. I'm a MOBA player to my core. However, my partner recommended that we get this game to try together, and I've fallen for it hard. Hypercharge: Unboxed is a unique combination of childhood nostalgia + horde shooters that has a beautifully bright atmosphere to set it apart from games like L4D2. As someone who has struggled to get into shooting games for years, I'm captivated by the ability to play as toy defenders in home and store environments, spaces that recall imagery from the Toy Story movies. Unlike most games, Hypercharge: Unboxed allows you to acquire skins and titles by just playing and meeting certain goals on levels - gathering all the coins and collectibles, reaching a particular level rating (gold, plat, diamond...), etc. It also features the ability to switch between first-person and third-person to fit your personal favorite shooter style. Combine this with the extremely satisfying sound of breaking out of your box at the beginning of the level, the building and repair noises, and the overall toy-like sound effects of the players and enemies, and you've got a fantastic game. I hope the devs continue to pour love into this game, because so much of their enthusiasm already shines through. I highly recommend that anyone who is feeling uncertain about this game to give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: HYPERCHARGE: UNBOXED is  probably the only fps/tower defense hybrid game that has held my interest and I believe could be a couch co-op staple if more people knew about it. Reasons you might like this game:-The game looks pretty impressive and if you like toy story you may feel some nostalgia playing it.-The game has multiple game modes ranging from co-op to vs to a top down tank brawler giving it added replayability with other players although the main gamemode includes singleplayer should you prefer to play alone.-The game heavily encourages and rewards exploration not only by having useful weapons/powerups/parts scattered around the maps but also through  unlockable cosmetics hidden throughout.- There are Several  difficulty levels allowing for players of varied skill levels to play/enjoy the game.- The vast majority of levels can be traversed with no/few invisible walls allowing players to scale the entirety of most maps using skillful use of jumps/ grenade jumps. -The developers are continuing to add new content to the game and are listening to feedback to improve the experience. Reasons you  might not like this game:-Some players dislike the movement in this game and believe it is difficult to respond to threats fast enough(personally I haven't had this issue as I find climbing obstacles to be fairly fluid and allows one to cover ground quickly)- Defenses can only be built in set locations on each map- Most guns are fairly inaccurate making combat at long ranges difficult.For it's price I think HYPERCHARGE is well worth the price and i'd highly recommend it to anyone who enjoys the fps/tower defense genre, people who are looking for a fun co-op game for both offline and online play and really anyone who doesn't find the downsides l've listed dealbreakers as I personally think the game is fantastic. If you're still unsure whether this game is for you be sure to check out the demo and try it for yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: 21:9 Ultrawide video review: HyperCharge: Unboxed is a Coop First person shooting wave defense game where you take on the role of an action figure and you have to defend your hyper cores from being destroy by an invasion of evil toys. The gameplay is your standard shooter type with the addition of some platforming elements and base building. The game splits between 2 phases, one for building and setting up your defenses like lego barricades, plastic posion ivy, hot glue and more. During the build phase your able to collect coins used for constructing these defenses as well as fine hidden collectibles that require quite a bit of platforming to reach. The second phase is the action phase where you will be fighting of hordes of various toys each with their own strength, weakness, and behaviors. Right clicking allows you to zoom in but there is no aim down sights in this game. There are attachments that appear at random through your mission that can give you an alternate fire or an addon for your gun to provide a stat bonus. At the end of a mission you will be awarded with XP and a rank based on how much health the cores were left with. My only real complaint with the gameplay was that the climbing can act up at times and cause you to work your way back up to where you fell off.Hypercharge Unboxed also features quite a bit outside of native ultra wide support. It has up to 4 player local split screen coop, private matches, a server browser, and tons of customization options to unlock like character skins, gun skins, and different playable action figures. The game is currently in early access and includes a good amount of missions with the promise of more to come, the developers have also stated they plan on adding a PVP game mode and more PVE content down the line.Visually the game is beautiful, the graphics and art style look amazing and I did have someone walk by quickly taking a look at the game thinking it was a toy story trailer. The variety in enemy toys really is a great addition because of the nostalgia factor it gave me, a lot of the toys where things i played with in my child hood. The audio works great and shooting the robots has a very pleasing shut down sound play when they get destroyed. Environments of each level are different and unique with my favorite having to be the toy isle. There's a lot of great jokes and references to be found littered throughout like the pc master race subreddit opened up in the bedroom, or the zerg rush deodorant in the bathroom. Performance wise i had no issues playing and no graphical issues from playing in ultra-wide either. The UI and menus can be scaled but does not have full customization in terms of placementOver all I enjoyed my time with HyperCharge: Unboxed, Its easy to see the developers at Digital Cybercherries put a lot of work into making this game and cared about their product. Its not perfect and could certainly use some more levels but for its asking price I would say it fulfills in giving enough content with the promise of more to come and offers a good amount of replay ability. If you dont take my word for it feel free to check out the stream review section with lots of players who feel the same way. My biggest gripe with the game was not being able to find enough players online off peak hours and thats saying something.

_childDocuments_.review: Hypercharge:unboxed is a fun game. It needs co-op with voice to get the most enjoyment if you want to be successful. There are a range of well designed and ascetically pleasing maps although the Garden of Death needs some work on being able to pick out enemies.On the waves mode which is what I've played the most, you defend 3-4 terminals from attack by AI forces. You gather construction points to build defences, with the type of enemy and defences making some differences e.g. there are airborne enemies in some maps and you can build anti-air defences.For gameplay, some changes I'd like to see are: - another player not being able to destroy your defences- a shorter ready time option, 3:30 minutes between maps is a long time to wait on someone else, as is the construction phase if one player isn't coming out of it but they have no points anyway - more balancing between AI attacks on different terminals, it tends to focus on 1-3 and mostly ignores 4 e.g. the attic level, the players can build a gun turret at green and pretty much leave it while red is under constant attack.- an anti-air weapon that can be carried by playersI hope more players find the game over time and play it, I think some more maps for longevity would help.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this game for maybe 3 days and already have 10 hours into it. The design is obviously the hook, and it's as good as you think it is. The gameplay is good as well, there are multiple guns and attachments as well as defensive builds you can choose from. The stages themselves might be my favorite, there are so many secret areas to find and little details that make this game really special.For me personally, there is one drawback. I am by no means a completionist. It does not bother me in the slightest that I don't have the highest rank on the hardest difficulty for each stage. If you don't really play with friends like myself, you may feel you've run out of content pretty early on. I've played every stage on normal difficulty, and most on expert. After beating the last couple stages on expert, it will be hard for me to return to Hypercharge very often. This does not make it a bad game- if you are a completionist you'll easily put 50-100 hours into it. I just don't see myself getting over 20. (which, again, is not bad).Overall, the game is a very fair price, and what I have played I have enjoyed. The aesthetic is top tier. I give HYPERCHARGE: Unboxed a 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was my Christmas gift from a friend. I like the game, but I hate seeing not many people playing it. It should be a powerhouse of players like Garry's mod or at least, Hades, but after spend a few moment playing it, I realize the devs can attract much much more players if:_They add a better gun system, & more guns. Pls allow people to upgrade their guns or diversify their weapon of choice, or have more inventory slots, not just two & buying crazily expensive & useless weapon mods. People should be freely exploring their firepower, not limiting them into just a few choices. Add an option to store different grenade types, too, like molotovs, flash bang, freeze grenades, electric, C4, mines, etc. People play CS 1.6, call of duty, payday & killing floor because their arsenal they can possess. Let them unleash these power of theirs, in toy mode!_They add melee weapons, like those Left 4 Dead 2 melee weapons. Come on, what's the point of playing toys when your action figure can't hold a big sword or a massive hammer? There're even a guy in a kungfu outfit in the game, & he cant even have melee weapons except punching? Give them extra power melee moves, add a mana bar, give them horrendous magic skills so they can at least perform some mystical katana slashes at that gigantic armored T-rex, not just getting slapped off the ring by its long tail like a bunch of wimp losers. If you're forcing the players to lose, at least earn their respect & make them lose honorably, not insta-killing them with a dumb-ass boss that they barely respect, including that insta kill laser boss or that nuke flying from the sky. Confusing af, bro._I really like the toys in the game but, somehow they feel repetitive, probably lacking of model variation among the same type of enemy. Pls add more variation towards the army men, too, not just the same dude who holding the same gun. If you ever own an army men bucket, they have 50 cal, flame thrower, medic, etc. Just add like 3 more variations to these army men & it will be freaking awesome. & pls get rid of those annoying tornado fidget spinner that keep bashing people unless players jump up & down like a bunch of clowns. if u guys are keeping 'em, pls add some tiny spinning Ryu like model on top so he can spin kick his iconic kungfu move so at least players know they're gettin kick in the face, and might burst out flames when fidgets glow red, or laser rings when they grow purple like starwars. These spinners in real life are super colorful, not just in only red & blue. Make these monsters as variable as possible, not only adding a bunch of skins for player customization but to the enemies as well. The enemy variations are also the reason why people love playing games. Just look at Left 4 Dead, & Vampire survivors. They don't have to produce so many types of enemies. They only need to recycle & reskin 'em with a few tweaks. Lazy, yes, but efficient? Maximum. Cuz with 1 enemy type, you can do lots of stuff with 'em, like pulling their guts off their bodies, & spamming hundreds of 'em without gettin bored._Players are weak af. Take 2 punches to kill a brain-dead bot. Guns are horrendously weak. If you want the players to easily die, at least, give them extra power so they can at least mow a bunch of morons down with them. Allow them to strap explosives around them & when they die, they can explode with glory. & if the players get too overpowered? Simply make the enemies more powerful with more skills & weapons & strategies, not just increasing their health. Increasing the enemy's health should be the last step. Spam more weak enemies & make them die easily, so players can feel a bit more.. powerful? Give 'em some variation of power up for them to choose in the beginning of the match, like extra melee power, extra jumps, extra running speed, & allow them to choose 2 of them every run._The narration is really boring. That captain price looking guy keeps screaming while the enemies barely talk. Enemies only screech a little, no lore, no story, no nothing. In Left 4 Dead, hearing the screeches of the enemies enough to give people heart attacks. You guys have like... a laser shooting robot boss? an alien mothership? At least, give them some annoying voice lines, like "I'm from Zion world & Im here to harvest black gold from your government!", so they can show off how powerful they are, and tell them to laugh whenever they manage to finish off a player, to make sure the dude who die is humiliated lol like those amusing COD kids that keep telling people they have intercourse with other people's mothers. Give the battle more awesome narrative, like why do we have to defend these cores? Why are these cores here? And what the enemies want with it? What type of beef does this commander has with the other toys? Did he stole their ice cream maker or something? You can tell a great story with just a few voice lines if you pick the right word, or the right sound. Try Portal series. That's a perfect example superior intimidation. Right now I barely know why Im in a freaking garage blasting alien mothership for no reason. There should be a purpose for every run, like in the beginning level of L4D Louis has a line "The subway can take us straight to Mercy hospital!" - this is what makes people comeback & remember the game for whatever it is._Effects are kinda... meh. If it is super hard to optimize your game with a huge load of effects, try some stylized effects like imaginative comic graphics, "boom!", "pow!", or pixelated 8 bit type of damage audio or muzzle flare, or even pixelated gun smoke. Be creative, add a 8bit coin drop sound when there's a coin drop, give those army men some more funny screams with 8 bit greenish blood. If u guys think this is too much & out of theme, allow this as a feature so people can turn on & off, & if u guys wanna make more money, sell these effects for like quarter or something.
